title:1/2: The undisputed representative work of director F. Fellini. Film director Guido dreams one day of his body falling through the air. To heal the various mental and physical fatigue associated with his daily life, he goes to a spa for rest and recuperation, but even there he cannot escape from work and life. And finally, he begins to hallucinate that he is among the elderly spending their remaining years at the spa... This film is an autobiographical work by Fellini himself, and its depiction is superb, portraying reality and fantasy in parallel! A must-see!!
title:100 METERS: Togashi, born with natural speed, has always used it to gain friends and a place to belong. Meanwhile, transfer student Komiya runs recklessly, trying to forget his painful reality. Togashi teaches Komiya how to run faster, and after school the two practice together. Finding something to devote himself to, Komiya greedily chases new records. Gradually, through the 100-meter dash, their relationship grows into something between rivals and best friends.
title:100,000年後の安全: Once the waste reaches a certain level, the facility will be sealed, never to be opened again. But who can guarantee that? Is there a way to reliably warn the people living there 100,000 years from now of the danger? They might mistake it for ruins or tombs of our era, or a place where treasures are hidden. Will those people of the future even understand
title:1975年のケルン・コンサート: A music youth film that goes behind the scenes of the concert given by world-famous jazz pianist Keith Jarrett at the Cologne Opera House in Germany on January 24, 1975, centering on the then-18-year-old female promoter. Vera Brandes, a music-loving high school student living in Cologne, Germany, starts a part-time job booking tours for musicians visiting Germany, partly as an act of rebellion against her strict father. Just as her work begins to gain momentum thanks to her innate vitality, she visits the Berlin Jazz Festival and is stunned by the performance of American piano genius Keith Jarrett. Determined to make Keith's Cologne concert happen, she overcomes numerous difficulties to arrange the event, but on the day, a problem arises: a different type of piano than the one Keith had requested is provided. As the start time approaches, Keith refuses to play, putting the concert in jeopardy... Based on historical facts, this film adapts the little-known true story of how the legendary concert, also known as the live album masterpiece "The Köln Concert," was nearly cancelled due to a last-minute crisis but was saved by the quick thinking and resourcefulness of an 18-year-old female promoter. German rising star Mala Emde plays Vera, and John Magaro, known for "First Cow" and "Past Lives," plays Keith Jarrett.
title:2045 FILMS WORKSHOP vol.1:
This short film omnibus marks the first independent project from "2045," a label comprised of next-generation creators from BABEL LABEL—a content studio behind numerous films and dramas. The collection features three works directed by young filmmakers belonging to the label.

"24 Frames of Nonsense" (directed by Ren Akiba) is a fantasy love story that weaves together fiction and non-fiction to depict a film director struggling with the script for their commercial feature debut while confronting their own past and present. "For My Grief" (directed by Hitomi Tatsumura) is an ensemble drama that follows four couples who love in their own ways and choose to part for their own reasons, portraying the act of cherishing the people and the time that were undeniably there. "Yomosugara" (directed by Mikumo Yoshimura) is a human drama about a young person who, despite turning their passion into a career, is driven to the brink by the gap between ideal and reality, chronicling a single night they spend in a mysterious cafe they happen to stumble upon.

The directors include Ren Akiba, who made his feature debut with "Tokyo Escape"; Hitomi Tatsumura, who is also an actor known for her lead role in "Angels"; and Mikumo Yoshimura, a prolific creator of short films and music videos who gained recognition for her Nihon University College of Art graduation project "The Last Train." title:2046: A sci-fi love story written and directed by Hong Kong master Wong Kar-wai, starring Asian superstars Tony Leung, Takeshi Kaneshiro, and Zhang Ziyi. Set in the 1960s, following "Days of Being Wild" and "In the Mood for Love," it weaves in episodes from those films. In 1967, during Hong Kong's turbulent era, writer Chow, unable to forget a past love and engaging in fleeting relationships with women, begins writing a near-future sci-fi novel titled "2046" at his hotel. The novel's characters board a train where androids serve as stewardesses, heading toward "2046," a place where lost love can be found. Chow reflects his own daily life in the novel, projecting himself onto the male protagonist as he writes. It won Best Actor (Tony Leung) and Best Actress (Zhang Ziyi) at the 24th Hong Kong Film Awards in 2005, and the New York Film Critics Circle Award for Best Foreign Language Film. In 2022, a 4K restored version was screened as part of "WKW4K" at theaters including Cinemart Shinjuku, Grand Cinema Sunshine, and Cinema City.
title:20th Century Women: From director Mike Mills, who drew on his own gay father for "Beginners," comes a story now centered on his mother. Set in Santa Barbara in 1979, it depicts a special summer for 15-year-old Jamie, his single mother Dorothea, and the people around them. Dorothea, a single mother struggling with how to raise her adolescent son Jamie, asks her roommate, photographer Abbie, and Jamie's childhood friend Julie, who lives nearby, to help him out. Starring as the mother Dorothea, Annette Bening was nominated for the Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy. Elle Fanning ("Maleficent") plays Julie, and Greta Gerwig ("Frances Ha") plays Abbie.
title:20センチュリー・ウーマン: From director Mike Mills, who drew on his own gay father for "Beginners," comes a story now centered on his mother. Set in Santa Barbara in 1979, it depicts a special summer for 15-year-old Jamie, his single mother Dorothea, and the people around them. Dorothea, a single mother struggling with how to raise her adolescent son Jamie, asks her roommate, photographer Abbie, and Jamie's childhood friend Julie, who lives nearby, to help him out. Starring as the mother Dorothea, Annette Bening was nominated for the Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy. Elle Fanning ("Maleficent") plays Julie, and Greta Gerwig ("Frances Ha") plays Abbie.
title:2部／3部)濱⼝⻯介監督特集上映突然、偶然、必然: Akari, Sakurako, Fumi, and Jun, now in their late 30s, believed they were close friends who could share anything—until they discovered Jun's secret. Born from a citizen-participation improvisational acting workshop in Kobe, this three-part film features mostly first-time actors and was created through unprecedented methods. It won the Best Actress award at the 68th Locarno Film Festival.
title:361 White and Black: Director Koichiro Oyama, who received high praise for his 2020 feature debut "The Murders of Oiso," directs this human drama centered on the game of Go. Masato Kamijo, living in a port town, happens to see a press conference on television where the world Go champion, Park Han-myeong, declares, "I have a rival in Japan." While everyone assumes the rival is Sara Yonehara, 7th dan, expectations soar for a direct showdown between Park and his rival at an upcoming tournament in Japan with a total prize pool of 100 million yen. Meanwhile, Masaki Kosaka, a production director for the tournament's broadcast, meets Masato during his research and discovers that he is a childhood friend of both Park and Sara. title:361 – White and Black –: Masato Kamijo (Ryota Nagano), living in a port town, happens to see a press conference on television where the world Go champion, Park Han-myeong (Park Yu-chun), declares, "I have a rival in Japan." While everyone assumes the rival is Sara Yonehara, 7th dan (Nao Hoshino), anticipation grows as Park enters a tournament in Japan with a total prize pool of 100 million yen, sparking hope for a direct showdown with this mysterious rival. Meanwhile, Masaki Kosaka (Koudai Matsuoka), a director for the tournament’s television coverage, meets Masato during his research and discovers that Masato is a childhood friend of both Park and Sara. Upon learning that Masato is an online Go champion, Masaki encourages him to enter the tournament, only to find that Masato is traumatized by a past event that makes him unable to play Go face-to-face. Through Masaki’s unconventional plan, Masato eventually enters the competition and faces off against formidable opponents. What was the tragic event that occurred between Masato, Park, and Sara in the past? What is the secret hidden within the tournament? Through his matches, Masato arrives at a single truth...
title:365DAYs＋2彷徨う大人たち:
In the documentary "365DAYs+," director Hiroyuki Kitaura chronicled the year leading up to his retirement. This sequel serves as a personal record of his daily life and inner struggles starting from his second year after leaving the workforce. After 36 years as a corporate "salaryman," Kitaura transitioned into life as a househusband and documentary filmmaker. His first year of retirement was a whirlwind of activity, from visiting the public employment office to enrolling in graduate school.

By his second year, as the initial dust settled, Kitaura had finally attained the "free and unconstrained life" he had dreamed of during his corporate days. Yet, he noticed a faint, lingering sense of unease beginning to stir deep within him. To uncover the source of this feeling, he once again began filming with his smartphone. Through his graduate studies, travels across Japan and Asia, and interviews with friends and former colleagues, he searches for the true nature of this restlessness. During a month-and-a-half stay in Manila to obtain a Philippine retirement visa, Kitaura spent his time reflecting while staring at his hotel ceiling, eventually arriving at a conclusion he presents as "My Personal Formula for Happiness."

Like its predecessor, the film is constructed from a vast archive of footage captured daily on a smartphone. It offers a raw look at the reality of life for a retiree while exploring the fundamental meaning of "working" and "continuing to work" through candid interviews.
title:404 Still Remain: Set in early 2000s South Korea, when Japanese pop culture was restricted, this coming-of-age drama tenderly follows a shy transfer student and a popular class president who bond over J-Pop. In 2001, Gyung-hwan transfers to a high school in Daegu, Korea's most conservative city. A huge fan of then-taboo Japanese music and anime, he secretly listens to Japanese songs on his MP3 player during lunch. Teased as an 'otaku' by classmates, he discovers that his deskmate, class president Jae-min, also secretly loves Japanese culture. Sharing earphones on the bus after school while listening to J-Pop, they gradually grow closer. One day, Gyung-hwan confesses a secret to Jae-min, but afterward, Jae-min's attitude suddenly changes. Making his feature debut, director Eom Ha-nul wrote the script based on his own teenage experiences as a fan of Japanese culture, weaving in diverse Japanese pop culture from the 1990s. Shim Hyun-seo, a child actor known for 'The King of Pigs', plays transfer student Gyung-hwan, and Hyun Woo-seok, from 'The School Nurse Files', plays class president Jae-min. Gong Min-jung ('Kim Ji-young: Born 1982') and Lee Dong-hwi ('The Roundup: Punishment') co-star.
title:47系統: Screening at EU Film Days 2026 (Tokyo: May 16–29, 2026 at Theater Image Forum, May 19–24 at the National Film Archive; Nagoya: June 6–19 at Nagoya Kinema Noi; also to be held in Hiroshima, Kyoto, and Fukuoka).
title:5 Centimeters per Second: A live-action film adaptation of Makoto Shinkai's 2007 theatrical anime "5 Centimeters Per Second," directed by Shinkai of "Your Name." and "Suzume," starring Hokuto Matsumura of SixTONES. Spring 1991. Takaki Tono and Akari Shinohara, who meet at an elementary school in Tokyo, connect through their shared loneliness, but Akari moves away upon graduation. In the winter of their first year of middle school, they reunite on a snowy night in Iwafune, Tochigi, and promise beneath a cherry tree standing in the snow to meet again at the same place on March 26, 2009. Time passes to 2008. Takaki, now working as a systems engineer in Tokyo and approaching 30, realizes a part of himself remains left behind in a distant time. Akari, too, lives her quiet daily life with those memories. Mitsuki Takahata plays Akari Shinohara, the heroine who connects with Takaki; Nana Mori plays Kanae Sumita, a high school classmate who has feelings for Takaki; Yuzu Aoki plays Takaki in high school; and Asa Kimura plays Risa Mizuno, Takaki's coworker. Also starring Aoi Miyazaki and Hidetaka Yoshioka. Directed by visual artist and photographer Yoshiyuki Okuyama, who gained attention with "At the Bench," with a screenplay by Fumiko Suzuki of "Love At Least."
title:501号室の男 ある作家の記録: A Korean suspense thriller about floor noise and a cult religion, depicting the fate of a female writer who strives to uncover the truth behind the noise coming from the upstairs neighbor. Eun-su, an aspiring writer living in apartment 401, has been applying to numerous writing contests but faces a string of rejections. Meanwhile, for about a month, she has been tormented by unbearable noise coming from unit 501 above. Deciding to use this situation as material for her work, Eun-su, along with her friend Ji-seong, begins observing Ho-gyeong, a middle-aged man living in 501. Even after he notices her excessive stalking, she relentlessly pursues him for the sake of her writing. Eventually, Eun-su arrives at a shocking truth hidden behind the noise, but at the same time, she finds herself backed into a dangerous situation. Director Kim Jeong-uk, who has crafted many stories candidly depicting the human psyche, portrays with intense suspense the psychological anxiety born from trivial troubles lurking in daily life. Ryu Hwa-young, known as a former member of the K-pop group T-ARA, stars in her first lead film role, passionately playing Eun-su, a writer whose obsession with writing blurs the line between reality and delusion. Veteran actor Park Jin-woo, known for the Netflix drama "Squid Game," plays the mysterious upstairs resident Ho-gyeong.
title:5時から7時までのクレオ: Cleo (Corinne Marchand) is a beautiful blonde woman. Lately, however, Cleo is troubled. She feels unwell. The thought that it might be cancer makes her restless. Recently, she underwent a thorough examination at the hospital. The results are due this evening. Cleo is terrified of that moment. Five o'clock. Cleo sits down before a female fortune teller. The fortune teller sees through her illness.
title:8½: The undisputed representative work of director F. Fellini. Film director Guido dreams one day of his body falling through the air. To heal the various mental and physical fatigue associated with his daily life, he goes to a spa for rest and recuperation, but even there he cannot escape from work and life. And finally, he begins to hallucinate that he is among the elderly spending their remaining years at the spa... This film is an autobiographical work by Fellini himself, and its depiction is superb, portraying reality and fantasy in parallel! A must-see!!
title:90 Meters: Yū, a high school senior, is on the verge of giving up his dreams to support his mother, who suffers from a serious illness. Torn by his inability to confess his hope of pursuing higher education... A heart-wrenching human drama about the bonds between parent and child and the journey toward independence.
title:90メートル: Yū, a high school senior, is on the verge of giving up his dreams to support his mother, who suffers from a serious illness. Torn by his inability to confess his hope of pursuing higher education... A heart-wrenching human drama about the bonds between parent and child and the journey toward independence.
title:9月のアル・ラシード通り: On September 9, 2025, the Israeli military called on all residents of Gaza City to evacuate via Al-Rashid Street to Al-Mawasi in the south, through social media and leaflets dropped from the air.
title:A Balloon's Landing: A road movie set in Hong Kong and Taiwan, depicting a midsummer miracle connected by a single letter. Against the beautiful, shimmering landscapes of Taiwan, it portrays a time-spanning bond between a wounded writer and a lonely young man. Tianyu, a popular Hong Kong writer, faces fierce public backlash after accusations of plagiarism. Deeply hurt, he travels alone to Taiwan in search of the 'Whale's Vanished Cove,' a place said to lead to heaven, which a boy he once corresponded with told him about. After being cheated in an unfamiliar country and getting drunk in the bustling streets of Taipei, Tianyu is helped by Ashang, a local thug. When Tianyu reveals the purpose of his journey, Ashang, claiming to know the 'Whale's Vanished Cove,' offers to take him there, and their summer journey begins... Terence Lau, known for 'Twilight Warriors: Final Battle in the Kowloon Walled City,' delicately portrays the gentle and pure writer Tianyu, while Fandy Fan, from 'Destiny Matchup,' co-stars as the thug Ashang.
title:A Bride for Rip Van Winkle: Nanami Minagawa, a temporary teacher in Tokyo, meets Tetsuya on social media and marries him. She hires Amaru, a jack-of-all-trades, to provide stand-in guests for the wedding ceremony. However, Tetsuya's affair soon comes to light. Then Nanami is accused by her mother-in-law of having an affair herself and is forced to leave the house. Amaru introduces Nanami to jobs as a stand-in wedding guest and as a live-in maid with a monthly salary of 1 million yen. There she meets her fellow maid, the unconventional and free-spirited Mashiro Satonaka.
title:A Comedy in Front of the Station:: The 15th installment of the 'Ekimaé Series,' which produced 24 films starring Frankie, Morishige, and Bando. Riding the unprecedented manga boom, this film features Frankie as a manga artist and is a legendary oddity, with appearances by 'Obake no Q-taro' and 'Osomatsu-kun' within the story.
title:A Confucian Confusion: A youth ensemble drama from 1994 by the renowned Taiwanese master Edward Yang, known for "A Brighter Summer Day" and "Yi Yi." Set in Taipei in the early 1990s, amidst rapid Westernization and economic development. Molly, who runs a business, is struggling both with her company's finances and her relationship with her fiancé Akin. Qiqi, Molly's friend who works at her company, is at the mercy of Molly's work habits and constantly fights with her boyfriend Ming. Centering on Molly and Qiqi, the film depicts the intertwining lives of ten men and women—classmates, lovers, and colleagues—over the course of two and a half days, showing them searching for what they truly seek amidst their inner emptiness. The film won awards for Best Screenplay, Best Supporting Actor, and Best Supporting Actress at the 1994 Golden Horse Awards and was officially selected for the 47th Cannes Film Festival. A 4K restoration premiered at the 79th Venice International Film Festival and was revived in theaters in 2023.
title:A DOCUMENTARY FILM OF LOSTAGE -ひかり:
What is life? What does it mean to make a living through music? What, exactly, is a rock band?

LOSTAGE is a three-piece rock band based in Nara that continues to tour live houses across Japan. Their work is never reflected in the hit charts—they deliberately chose a path outside of major distribution and sales channels. Yet, every one of their releases has sold over 5,500 copies, and their back catalog continues to be repressed, with sales figures steadily climbing to this day.

Now in their 40s, they are a rare active band with a devoted following that transcends age and gender, recently completing a sold-out 47-prefecture tour and a successful solo performance at the Hibiya Open-Air Concert Hall. Now in their 25th year, the three members have each built families in Nara and run community-based businesses, continuing their musical activities as a direct extension of their daily lives.

Once expected to "make it big" as a rock band, they even experienced a major label debut. However, with 2011 serving as a turning point, they have navigated a path of twists and turns, buffeted by the whims of reality.

While "deified" by countless fellow musicians, the three members remain firmly grounded in their daily lives. This intimate documentary explores the mystery and allure of LOSTAGE in their truest form—a band that continues to pursue a dream-like existence while remaining rooted in the reality of home and family.
title:A DOCUMENTARY FILM OF LOSTAGE ひかりの: A documentary exploring the enigma and allure of the alternative rock band LOSTAGE as they mark their 25th anniversary. Formed in 2001 and based in Nara, the three-piece band continues to perform at live houses across Japan. Despite choosing a path that avoids major distribution and the hit charts, every one of their releases has sold over 5,500 copies, with sales of their back catalog continuing to grow. Now in their 40s, the three members have built families in Nara and run community-based businesses, maintaining a musical career that is inextricably linked to their daily lives. Once burdened by the expectation to "make it big" and having experienced a major label debut, they reached a turning point in 2011, navigating a winding path through the shifting realities of life ever since. Directed by filmmaker MINORxU, who shares a 20-year history with the band, the film depicts the trajectory of three men who are revered by fellow musicians yet live grounded lives as everyday people.
title:A Desirable Marriage: Mieko, a widow running a pawnshop, tries to arrange a favorable marriage for her only daughter Non, but Non pretends to be in a relationship with her coworker Kawata to avoid it. However, the two unexpectedly fall in love and decide to marry for real, only for various incidents to arise between both families surrounding the wedding. This home drama explores what it means to have a happy marriage.
title:A Foggy Tale: Directed by Taiwan's Yu-Hsun Chen, known for "The Girl Who Leapt Through Time" and "The Tropical Fish," this is a story of hope and rebirth set against the backdrop of the "White Terror" era in 1950s Taiwan, when many citizens were arrested and executed on suspicion of being anti-government. In the 1950s, under martial law in Taiwan. A young girl named A-Yue, living in Chiayi, learns that her brother, captured as an anti-government element, has been executed in Taipei. With a small amount of money and her brother's keepsake watch in hand, she heads to Taipei alone, only to find that a hefty fee is required to claim his body. At her wit's end, she is tricked by a suspicious man and nearly sold into a brothel, but is rescued by a rickshaw puller named Zhao Gongdao. Originally from Guangdong, China, he came to Taiwan as a soldier for the Nationalist army and has been unable to return home, living hand-to-mouth ever since. Having lost his army comrades to the White Terror and finding no direction in life, Gongdao is moved by A-Yue's determination and decides to lend her a hand. Caitlin Fang ("A Girl from America") plays A-Yue, Will Or ("The Staggering Girl") plays Zhao Gongdao, and popular Taiwanese singer and actor 9m88 co-stars. The film won four awards, including Best Feature Film, at the 62nd Golden Horse Awards in 2025.
title:A Foreign Affair: Set in the ruins of post-war Berlin, this film depicts a romantic rivalry involving a playboy American officer. An American female politician heading to Germany is entrusted by a woman with a gift for Captain Pringle. The woman is one of the captain's girlfriends, but upon receiving it, he immediately trades it for a mattress on the black market—so he can flirt with a German woman he has a crush on. Marlene Dietrich plays a Nazi singer, and composer Frederick Hollander, who handled the music, appears as a pianist.
title:A Future History Of: The Elephant: A music documentary that uncovers the truth behind the mysterious music collective 'Elephant 6,' born in the late 1980s American South and sparking a unique movement in the 90s indie scene. In the late 1980s, a group of high school friends in Ruston, Louisiana, began experimenting with home recordings using whatever instruments they could find. Sharing a love for psychedelic music, they eventually moved to Denver, Colorado, and Athens, Georgia, sticking to their DIY ethos by lining cheap apartments with aluminum foil to create studios. From this emerged bands like 'The Apples in Stereo,' 'Neutral Milk Hotel,' and 'Olivia Tremor Control,' which formed the core of 'Elephant 6,' later joined by many others. What started as a friendship-driven project, fueled by a rebellious spirit against the mainstream music of the time, grew in support and sparked an unprecedented movement in the American music scene. Director Chad Stockfress, a friend of Robert Schneider from 'The Apples in Stereo,' spent about ten years interviewing participants and fans. Elijah Wood (from 'The Lord of the Rings') and David Cross (from 'Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind') appear as commentators. This long-anticipated title, known early on to some Japanese fans through connections with Keigo Oyamada and Kahimi Karie, will be released in Japan on July 31, 2026, in a version with added live footage.
title:A Little Girl's Dream: A documentary film adaptation of a 26-year chronicle following one girl's dream from its beginning to the present day, originally produced by TeNY Television Niigata, a local TV station in Niigata Prefecture. The story gained attention when it was featured on Nippon Television network programs such as "Zoom In!! Morning!" and "NNN Documentary." In 1987, three calves arrive at a small elementary school in the mountains of Niigata. A third-grade girl at the time dreams of becoming a "cow doctor" through caring for the calves. After parting with the cows she had grown attached to, and with support from her family and those around her, she overcomes difficult hurdles to become a veterinarian for "livestock," not pets. Through her continued dedication to invaluable lives every day—now as a married mother—the film explores the importance of having dreams, as well as themes of family, hometown, work, and the harshness of reality. Yui Yokoyama of AKB48 takes on her first narration role.
title:A Missing Part: A drama directed by Guillaume Senez, who also teamed up with Romain Duris in 'Our Struggles,' with Duris starring. Set primarily in Japan, it depicts the changing forms of modern families under the universal themes of parent-child bonds and love, against the backdrop of the differences between Japanese and French social systems. Jay, a Frenchman working as a chef in Tokyo, marries a Japanese woman but divorces her. Due to differences in the joint custody systems of Japan and France, he is separated from his beloved daughter Lily. Unable to give up hope, he becomes a taxi driver, wandering the city while searching for traces of his daughter. Nine years later, just as Jay decides to return to France, his daughter Lily, now a grown girl, coincidentally gets into his taxi. Without Lily knowing the driver is her real father, and Jay unable to reveal himself, they spend a brief moment together. The cast includes Judith Chemla, known for 'A Woman's Life' and 'Our Arias for Mother,' Tsu Yu from 'TAXi (2),' Yumi Narita from 'Don't Stop the Camera!' and 'Mari's Story,' as well as Shinnosuke Abe, Toshihiro Yashiba, Moro Agata, and Haruko Uchida.
title:A Missing Part また君に会えるまで: A drama directed by Guillaume Senez, who also teamed up with Romain Duris in 'Our Struggles,' with Duris starring. Set primarily in Japan, it depicts the changing forms of modern families under the universal themes of parent-child bonds and love, against the backdrop of the differences between Japanese and French social systems. Jay, a Frenchman working as a chef in Tokyo, marries a Japanese woman but divorces her. Due to differences in the joint custody systems of Japan and France, he is separated from his beloved daughter Lily. Unable to give up hope, he becomes a taxi driver, wandering the city while searching for traces of his daughter. Nine years later, just as Jay decides to return to France, his daughter Lily, now a grown girl, coincidentally gets into his taxi. Without Lily knowing the driver is her real father, and Jay unable to reveal himself, they spend a brief moment together. The cast includes Judith Chemla, known for 'A Woman's Life' and 'Our Arias for Mother,' Tsu Yu from 'TAXi (2),' Yumi Narita from 'Don't Stop the Camera!' and 'Mari's Story,' as well as Shinnosuke Abe, Toshihiro Yashiba, Moro Agata, and Haruko Uchida.
title:A Naughty Angel: An unconventional home drama depicting the daily life of a new father (Frankie), who works from home and is run ragged by his mischievous toddler yet raises him with abundant love. His chemistry with his on-screen wife Ikeuchi is excellent, and Bando and Miki are amusing as hopeless fathers.
title:A New Dawn: This animated film marks the feature directorial and screenwriting debut of Yoshitoshi Shinomiya, who has worked across genres primarily as a Nihonga (Japanese-style) painter. It is a Japan-France co-production with the cutting-edge French studio Miyu Productions. The 330-year-old Tategami Fireworks Factory, nestled in the woods, is facing eviction due to town redevelopment. Keitaro Tategami, who grew up there, has barricaded himself in the factory for four years, striving to complete the legendary "Shuhari" firework in place of his missing father, Eitaro. Meanwhile, Keitaro's childhood friend Kaoru Shikimori left their hometown for Tokyo after a past incident. Contacted by Keitaro's older brother Sentaro, who works at the city office, Kaoru visits the Tategami family on the last day of summer, the day before the eviction deadline, reuniting with Keitaro for the first time in four years. As they clash, trying to reclaim lost time and broken bonds, they hatch a surprising plan to uncover the secret of the phantom firework. The key lies in a beautiful blue pigment called "hanaryokusei" (copper acetoarsenite). Actors Rihito Noda and Kotone Furukawa make their voice acting debuts as Keitaro and Kaoru respectively, with voice actor Miyu Irino as Keitaro's brother Sentaro and actor Takashi Okabe as their father Eitaro. The film was selected for the Competition section of the 78th Berlin International Film Festival in 2026.
title:A New Love in Tokyo: Ray is an actress in a small theater troupe. By day, she devotes herself to rehearsals with her friends, and by night, she works as a dominatrix at an SM club in Shibuya. One evening, Ray becomes friendly with Ayumi, a hotel escort girl she occasionally sees in the elevator of the building where the club is located. Ayumi is a shrewd girl living with Kenji, a ronin studying for medical school entrance exams. The two hit it off and head out into the nightlife. After drinking, dancing, and partying, they part ways, promising to go see the sea at dawn together someday. Finally, the day of Ray's theater troupe's performance arrives. With Ayumi and Ray's client Sawatari watching, Ray's play is a success, met with thunderous applause. Ray is moved by the satisfaction of accomplishing something. Ayumi is also moved seeing Ray like this. The two head out to the coast at dawn in a car driven by a man they picked up.
title:A Private Life: Oscar-winning actress Jodie Foster, known for 'The Accused' and 'The Silence of the Lambs', stars in her first French-language film in this mystery. Lilian, a successful American psychoanalyst practicing in Paris, receives news that Paula, a long-time patient, has died. Suspicious of Paula's death, Lilian suspects murder but cannot involve the police due to patient confidentiality. She decides to uncover the truth herself. Meanwhile, since learning of Paula's death, Lilian has been troubled by uncontrollable crying, regardless of the situation, and visits her ex-husband Gabriel, an ophthalmologist. Though the cause of her tears remains unclear, Gabriel agrees to help Lilian investigate Paula's case. As she embarks on a detective-like investigation, Lilian delves into dangerous truths. Foster plays the protagonist, psychoanalyst Lilian, entirely in French. Daniel Auteuil, known for 'La Belle Époque', plays her ex-husband and investigative partner Gabriel. Virginie Efira from 'Suddenly Sick' and Mathieu Amalric from 'Quantum of Solace' co-star. The film is directed by Rebecca Zlotowski, known for 'Grand Central' and 'Planetarium'.
title:A Samurai in Time: A period comedy depicting a late-Edo period samurai who time-travels to a modern-day period drama studio and struggles as a sword-falling extra. In Kyoto at the end of the Edo period, Kosaka Shinzaemon, a retainer of the Aizu domain, receives a secret order from the chief retainer to kill a Choshu domain samurai, but at the moment his blade meets his target's, he is struck by lightning and loses consciousness. When he wakes up, he finds himself in a modern period drama studio. Shinzaemon causes commotions wherever he goes, and is stunned to learn that the Tokugawa shogunate fell 140 years ago. Resigned to death at first, he is helped by kind-hearted people and regains his will to live. Eventually, relying only on his polished swordsmanship, he knocks on the studio's door and decides to live as a sword-falling extra. Starring Makiya Yamaguchi, who has appeared in numerous period dramas including the TV series "Kenkaku Shobai," with Norimasa Tomiya and Yuno Sakura co-starring. Directed and written by Junichi Yasuda ("Gohan," "Kenju to Medamayaki"), it was completed with special cooperation from Toei Kyoto Studio despite being an independent production. Released exclusively at Ikebukuro Cinema Rosa on August 17, 2024 (a "Deluxe Version" with added scenes began screening at Kawasaki Cinecitta from August 30), word of mouth spread, and from September 13 of the same year, with Gaga as co-distributor, it expanded to over 100 theaters nationwide including Shinjuku Piccadilly and Toho Cinemas Hibiya. It became an unprecedented hit for an independent film and achieved the feat of winning the Best Picture award at the 48th Japan Academy Film Prize.
title:A Separation: Nader is in divorce negotiations with his wife, who wants to leave Iran for the sake of their daughter. He hires a woman named Razieh to care for his father, who suffers from dementia and lives with him, but an unexpected incident sets off a chain of events... An exquisite drama that intertwines a mystery with Iran's divorce issues.
title:A Summer at Grandpa's: Taiwanese master Hou Hsiao-hsien crafts a masterpiece drama that vividly portrays the beauty of nature and childhood friendship through the story of a young brother and sister spending a summer in their grandfather's countryside home. After graduating from elementary school in Taipei, Tongtong's mother is hospitalized, so he and his little sister spend summer vacation at their grandfather's house in the countryside. They quickly become friends with the neighborhood children, and Tongtong enjoys a fun summer running through the fields. Meanwhile, his sister Tingting struggles to join the group and passes the time by playing pranks on her brother and his friends, until their father eventually comes from Taipei to pick them up. The father of the siblings is played by filmmaker Edward Yang, known for "The Terrorizers" and "Yi Yi." First released in Japan in 1990. Digital remastered versions were re-released in 2016 and 2025.
title:A Sun-Tribe Myth from the Bakumats: Saheiji, left penniless at a Shinagawa pleasure quarter at the end of the Edo period... A masterpiece by Kawashima and Frankie, and a classic in Japanese film history. In this ensemble comedy where late-Edo period patriots and courtesans mingle, Frankie's light and agile movements as he navigates through the chaos are the film's core.
title:A Useful Ghost: In Bangkok, Thailand, where dust pollution is severe, March (Wisarut Himmarat) spends his days in grief after losing his beloved wife Nat (Davika Hoorne) to a respiratory disease. One day, Nat's soul returns, inhabiting a vacuum cleaner, and the two reaffirm their love. Meanwhile, at the factory run by March's family, the spirit of a deceased employee possesses the machinery, bringing operations to a halt. Rejected by family troubled by the spirit and by society, Nat tries to prove her true love for her husband and her own existence as a 'useful ghost' by helping with the factory's exorcism...
title:A Window of Memories: A "listening-and-writing film" that makes you remember someone and want to talk about them—the eagerly awaited latest work from director Yui Kiyohara, whose "Our House" and "Remembering Every Night" were acclaimed both in Japan and abroad. Selected for the International Competition at the Yamagata International Documentary Film Festival 2025.
title:A Woman Called Sada Abe: "The outside light bothers me" "His smell is soaked into the futon too..." Sadame closes the storm shutters to keep Kichizō's scent from escaping. How long has it been since the two of them were alone in the small room of the teahouse? Their union seeks ever more unknown pleasures. Sadame, choking Kichizō, says happily, "Kichi-san is twitching inside me." But when Kichizō, whose health is beginning to fail, suggests returning home for a while, Sadame's pure love for him becomes directly linked to pure desire. "I won't let anyone else touch you anymore. No one..."
title:A Woman Is a Woman: This is Jean-Luc Godard's third feature film, following "Breathless," and a romantic comedy created based on the idea of a "musical comedy in which the characters do not sing." Angela, a cabaret dancer, tells her live-in lover Émile that she wants a child right now. Émile cannot hide his bewilderment at her request. Then a young man named Alfred, who has feelings for Angela, appears... Following Godard's previous film "Le Petit Soldat," Anna Karina plays the heroine, with Jean-Paul Belmondo of "Breathless" as Alfred and Jean-Claude Brialy of "Les Cousins" as Émile. The music is by Michel Legrand, the renowned composer of "The Umbrellas of Cherbourg" and other films.
title:A pátý jezdec je Strach: Set in Nazi-occupied Czechoslovakia, this drama portrays the terror of an informant society during wartime. Dr. Braun, a Jew living in Nazi-occupied Czechoslovakia, is forbidden from practicing medicine. The elderly man seems to have already accepted the fate of the Jews. Then one day, a neighbor asks him to treat a wounded political fugitive, and he reluctantly provides care. Eventually confronting his inner self, Dr. Braun decides to continue illegal treatment for the resistance to reclaim his identity. He wanders the streets of Prague in search of the morphine needed for this, but... Through the various people Dr. Braun meets and the wartime cityscape, the film depicts a society decaying and collapsing under war with hallucinatory visual beauty. In Japan, it will have its theatrical premiere in April 2026 as part of "Czech Film Masterpieces," a series featuring classics of the Czech New Wave.
title:AALTO: Alvar Aalto (1898-1976), Finland's representative architect and designer. He created outstanding designs and numerous masterpieces of architecture, including the timeless classic "Stool 60," the iconic "Aalto Vase," and the "Maison Louis Carré" with its exquisite harmony with nature. What drove Alvar Aalto's life as a designer was a single woman—
title:AMRUM: In 1945, at the end of World War II, the island of Amrum in northern Germany remained in a strange, paradise-like stillness even as bombers flew overhead toward the mainland. Naning, a 12-year-old boy evacuated there, supports his pregnant mother and family by helping with farm work in place of his father, who has not returned from the front. However, when his mother Hille, who is devoted to Hitler, collapses both mentally and physically upon receiving news of his death, Naning's daily life is transformed. Hille, drained of vitality and refusing food, desires only one thing: white bread generously spread with butter and honey.
title:ARCO アルコ: The adventure of Iris, a girl living in a near future devastated by climate change, and Arco, a rainbow-colored boy who 'fell from the sky.' A poetically rich animation by a rising French director, depicted in vivid colors.
title:ARCO／アルコ: The adventure of Iris, a girl living in a near future devastated by climate change, and Arco, a rainbow-colored boy who 'fell from the sky.' A poetically rich animation by a rising French director, depicted in vivid colors.
title:ATEEZ : LIGHT THE WAY IN CINEMAS: A concert film that reconstructs the immersive live experience of the popular K-pop group ATEEZ for theaters. Following their 2025 theatrical release "ATEEZ WORLD TOUR [TOWARDS THE LIGHT : WILL TO POWER] IN CINEMAS," this is their second theatrical release, based on the immersive experience that toured various locations from 2025 by the VR concert platform AMAZE, reconfigured in native 8K resolution and 5.1ch surround sound. One day, a mysterious message arrives for ATEEZ, who are spending a peaceful time at their hideout. From that moment, everything begins to change, and their fans "ATINY" disappear. As if under a spell, ATEEZ wander through a dreamlike wilderness, a world engulfed in flames and collapsing, and a "Dark City" shrouded in deep fog. While pursued by an unidentified force, they launch a counterattack to find ATINY. Featuring Hongjoong, Seonghwa, Yunho, Yeosang, San, Mingi, Wooyoung, and Jongho, the film brings performances of hit songs like "INCEPTION," "BOUNCY (K-HOT CHILLI PEPPERS)," and "Ice On My Teeth" to the big screen. It also includes 20 minutes of unreleased behind-the-scenes footage.

title:Aa!! Hana no Ouendan: The first film adaptation in 20 years of the hit 1976 series "Aa!! Hana no Ōendan." At the Minami Kawachi University cheerleading squad, an annual alumni gathering is planned, but they discover a hole in their precious team flag. The members hurriedly take part-time jobs to earn repair money, but the workplace is run by yakuza who refuse to pay and threaten them. However, Sekidō Aota appears and beats the yakuza to a pulp. Ken'ichi Nagira reprises his role as senior Yakutsuji from the previous series, and Junko Miyashita also appears.
title:Aalto: Alvar Aalto (1898-1976), Finland's representative architect and designer. He created outstanding designs and numerous masterpieces of architecture, including the timeless classic "Stool 60," the iconic "Aalto Vase," and the "Maison Louis Carré" with its exquisite harmony with nature. title:About Us But Not About Us: A Filipino film that unfolds as a witty, single-setting dialogue piece between a lonely literature professor and a young man aspiring to be a writer, revolving around the secrets of a deceased lover. Directed and written by Jun Robles Lana of 'Die Beautiful' fame, it weaves themes of losing a loved one, LGBTQ+ issues, sexual abuse, and the precariousness of the social media generation, exposing the ailments and love-hate dynamics of modern Philippines. In pandemic-era Manila, Eric, a literature professor grieving the recent death of his lover Marcos, a renowned novelist, agrees to meet his student Lance at a long-established restaurant. Despite his sense of loss, Eric looks forward to time with Lance, who admires him. The two grow closer over talk of apple pie and Daft Punk, but the atmosphere shifts when a story about Marcos comes up. Gazing into Lance's eyes, Eric uncovers a startling truth about Marcos. Elijah Canlas, known from the Japanese-hit drama 'Gameboys,' plays the handsome young Lance, while veteran Filipino actor Romnick Sarmenta portrays Professor Eric.
title:Abunai Deka Forever The Movie: Yokohama Port Police detectives Takayama and Oshita, a duo, once arrest Jojima, a member of the internationally wanted terrorist group 'NET,' but Jojima escapes from the police hospital, and the detectives pursue him. One day, an incident occurs where Jojima and his comrades attack a transport vehicle carrying firearms seized by the police, attempting to steal the weapons. Ignoring orders to stay off the case, Takayama and Oshita return to the scene, thwarting Jojima's gang's scheme, but the group's leader Date is advancing an even larger plan.
title:Ace in the Hole: Billy Wilder parted ways with his long-time screenwriting partner Charles Brackett and brought in a new writer for this film. Jack, kicked out of a New York newspaper, witnesses a man buried alive in a cave. Desperate to return to a top-tier paper, he manipulates information using the scoop. A journalist who stops at nothing for his own ambition is ultimately judged by public opinion, making for a compelling watch. There is also an anecdote that the studio changed the title from 'Ace in the Hole' to 'The Big Carnival' due to poor public reception.
title:Adam's Sake: The second feature from Belgian director Laura Wandel, who gained attention with her 2021 debut 'Playground', is a human suspense drama depicting one night's events surrounding a 4-year-old boy hospitalized in a pediatric ward and his mother, told from the perspective of a nurse trying to support them. Four-year-old Adam is admitted to a pediatric center with a broken left arm. Malnourished and underdeveloped, his bones are brittle. The court rules that Rebecca, an immigrant single mother, has not been providing Adam with proper nutrition and issues an order restricting her visits. Nurse manager Lucie, herself a single mother, tries to support Rebecca, who fears losing custody and being separated from her son. But Rebecca's reckless actions and pressure from superiors and colleagues push Lucie into a corner. Léa Drucker ('Close') plays nurse Lucie, torn between her desire to save the mother and child and the judicial system the hospital must follow. Anamaria Vartolomei ('Happening') plays isolated single mother Rebecca. The film is produced by Belgian masters Jean-Pierre and Luc Dardenne. It opened the Critics' Week at the 2025 Cannes Film Festival.
title:Affeksjonsverdi: Swedish director Joachim Trier, who gained international attention with "The Worst Person in the World," crafts a family drama centered on the tangled bonds of love and hate inherent in the parent-child relationship. Nora, an actress thriving in Oslo, and her sister Agnes, who chose family life and lives quietly with her husband and son. One day, their father Gustav, a film director who abandoned the family when they were young and has been out of contact for years, reappears and offers Nora the lead role in his first autobiographical film in 15 years. Filled with anger and disappointment toward her father, Nora firmly refuses, and soon the popular young American actress Rachel is cast instead. When Nora learns that the film will be shot at the family's old home, a place filled with memories, uncontrollable emotions surge within her once again. Renate Reinsve, who also starred in "The Worst Person in the World," plays the protagonist Nora, with acclaimed actor Stellan Skarsgård as her father Gustav. Inga Ibsdotter Lilleaas plays sister Agnes, and Elle Fanning plays the popular American actress Rachel. The film won the Grand Prix at the 78th Cannes Film Festival in 2025. At the 98th Academy Awards, it received nine nominations across eight categories, including Best Picture, and won the award for Best International Feature Film.
title:After Life: A fantasy drama by Hirokazu Kore-eda of "Maborosi" fame, depicting the seven days between death and reaching heaven. Twenty-two deceased people arrive at a facility shrouded in mist. The staff waiting for them instruct them to choose the single most important memory from their lives within the seven days before they go to heaven. Some choose a memory immediately, while others struggle to decide. But the final day, when a screening will be held, steadily approaches. Starring ARATA in his film debut.
title:After the Storm: Director Hirokazu Kore-eda of "Our Little Sister" and "Like Father, Like Son" teams up with Atsushi Abe for the third time, following "Still Walking" and "I Wish," in this human drama centered on a man who can't grow up and his aging mother, portraying a family living a present different from the future they once dreamed of. Ryota is a middle-aged man who won a literary prize 15 years ago but hasn't been successful since, still chasing his dream of becoming a writer. He currently works at a detective agency to make ends meet, but makes excuses to himself and others that it's "research for his novel." Still hung up on his ex-wife, Kyoko, he is shocked to discover she has a new boyfriend while "staking out" her apartment. One day, Ryota, Kyoko, and their 11-year-old son Shingo gather at the apartment of his mother, Toshiko, who lives alone in a housing complex. Stranded by a typhoon, they end up spending the night together. Kirin Kiki delivers a wonderful performance as the protagonist's mother, with a stellar supporting cast including Yoko Maki, Satomi Kobayashi, and Lily Franky.
title:Afternoon Breezes: Mitsu's birthday. Natsuko buys matching Virgo necklaces and a rose. However, a white handkerchief is hanging in the apartment window. It's the signal that Mitsu's lover, Hideo, is there. Natsuko, who has secretly fallen in love with Mitsu, approaches Hideo in order to have Mitsu all to herself... On a midsummer afternoon, a shocking ending that will shake the world.
title:Aftersun: A human drama that recounts a summer vacation spent with a father, 20 years later from the perspective of the daughter who has now reached the same age her father was then, as she discovers a new side of her father she never knew at the time. During the summer when she was 11, adolescent Sophie visits a rustic Turkish resort with her 31-year-old father Calum, from whom she lives apart. Under the blazing sun, they point a video camera Calum obtained at each other, spending intimate time together. 20 years later, Sophie, now the same age as Calum was then, looks back at the nostalgic footage shot at that time, reviving memories of her beloved father. Paul Mescal, who broke out with the TV drama "Normal People," plays the loving yet sensitive father Calum, earning a nomination for the 95th Academy Award for Best Actor. The role of Sophie is played by newcomer Frankie Corio, selected through auditions. The director and screenwriter is Scottish newcomer Charlotte Wells, making her feature-length debut with this film.
title:Agatha and the Limitless Readings: French writer Marguerite Duras, known for 'The Lover,' adapts her own book 'The Malady of Death / Agatha' into a film. Set in a dilapidated seaside hotel, this experimental work depicts the forbidden love between a brother and sister through lyrical imagery and Duras's own narration. Agatha, reuniting with her brother after eight months at the winter seaside villa Villa Agatha, decides to leave the next morning and part from him forever. The two reminisce about their forbidden love. The brother is played by Yann Andréa, Duras's lover who was 38 years her junior. In Japan, the film had its first theatrical release in 2003, 23 years after its 1981 release. It was re-released in 2012.
title:Agatha et les lectures illimitées: French writer Marguerite Duras, known for 'The Lover,' adapts her own book 'The Malady of Death / Agatha' into a film. Set in a dilapidated seaside hotel, this experimental work depicts the forbidden love between a brother and sister through lyrical imagery and Duras's own narration. Agatha, reuniting with her brother after eight months at the winter seaside villa Villa Agatha, decides to leave the next morning and part from him forever. The two reminisce about their forbidden love. The brother is played by Yann Andréa, Duras's lover who was 38 years her junior. In Japan, the film had its first theatrical release in 2003, 23 years after its 1981 release. It was re-released in 2012.
title:Ah Special Attack Corps: A war film depicting the fleeting youth of kamikaze pilots who perished in vain at the end of the Pacific War. This is the directorial debut of Yoshio Inoue, based on a script by Kimiyuki Hasegawa (known for "The Squirrel and the American: Gunshot in the Ruins"). Yoshio Inoue was born in Tokyo in 1926, graduated from Urawa High School's humanities track, joined Daiei in February 1938, and studied under Seiji Hisamatsu, Kon Ichikawa, and Yasuzo Masumura. Cinematography by Toru Watanabe (known for "The White Path Across the River").
title:Aikatsu Stars! The Movie: The theatrical film of the TV anime 'Aikatsu Stars!', which began airing in April 2016 as a new series following the popular idol anime 'Aikatsu!'. It depicts the struggles of girls, including the protagonist Yume Nijino, who enrolls at Yotsusei Gakuen aiming to become the top idol. In this first theatrical film of 'Aikatsu Stars!', the story is set on a southern island where the characters come for an event. It revolves around the rumored 'Legendary Dress' said to be sleeping on the island, and depicts the friendship between Yume and Laura Sakuraba, as well as the school's top four-idol unit 'S4' taking the stage together. The short film 'Aikatsu! The Targeted Magical Aikatsu! Card' is shown simultaneously.
title:Air Doll: Based on a short manga by Yoshiie Gouda, this allegorical work uses the love story of a sentient love doll to lead viewers into philosophical contemplation about the emptiness and life of modern people. With cinematographer Mark Lee Ping-bing and art director Yohei Taneda on board, the fictional setting is brilliantly visualized using analog special effects.
title:Akko-chan's Got a Secret! – The Se: Elementary school student Kagami Atsuko can transform into any appearance she desires using a magical mirror. This is the first theatrical film in the second series of "Himitsu no Akko-chan," which captures the transformation wishes of young girls. The story depicts the interaction between "Taishō," who opposes the construction of a building on the children's playground, and his father, who works in construction. Akko transforms into a baton twirler who leads the protest. Kanemori Yoshinori's four-heads-tall characters move energetically across the screen.
title:Al-Rashid Street in September: On September 9, 2025, the Israeli military called on all residents of Gaza City to evacuate via Al-Rashid Street to Al-Mawasi in the south, through social media and leaflets dropped from the air.
title:Alakazam the Great!: A rousing entertainment masterpiece based on Osamu Tezuka's "My Son Goku," bringing together the energy of young artists during the first golden age of Toei Animation. It is noteworthy that Osamu Tezuka himself took the lead in drawing the storyboards, and the on-site staff included a large number of talented individuals who would later carry the future of Japan's animation industry. In other words, it is one of the origins of Japanese animated films, a monumental work that greatly envisioned the future of the medium from an entertainment perspective. Winner of the Special Grand Prize at the Venice International Children's Film Festival.
title:Ali Baba and the Forty Thieves: Alibaba XXXIII, descendant of the original Alibaba and now king, indulges in pleasure and uses the lamp's genie to oppress his people. The descendant of a thief, Al-Hack, teams up with one mouse and 38 cats, riding a flying carpet into the castle. Akira Daikuhara's challenge is evident in the round, deformed characters. Hack is voiced by Nobuyo Oyama, and the shadow-puppet flashback scenes were handled by the theater troupe Kakashiza. This was the last film credited to Toei president Hiroshi Okawa, who passed away suddenly that year.
title:All About Lily Chou-Chou: In a provincial city, middle school student Yuichi becomes close with the honor student Hoshino, but a summer trip changes the dynamics among their friends. When the new semester begins, Hoshino defeats the class's worst delinquent in a fight and gradually turns into a tyrant himself. As his actions escalate—assault, shoplifting, and forcing classmates into prostitution—Yuichi, who has become a target of bullying, is also made complicit. Turning his eyes away from reality, Yuichi creates a fan site for his idolized artist, Lily Chou-Chou.
title:All Around Us: "Unforgettable masterpieces" return to the screen! Since his directorial debut with "A Touch of Fever" (1993), Ryosuke Hashiguchi—known as a "master of few works" eagerly awaited by film fans both in Japan and abroad—has delivered acclaimed films including "Like Grains of Sand" (1995), which won the Grand Prix at the 25th Rotterdam International Film Festival; "Three Stories of Love" (2015), which swept various film awards including the Kinema Junpo Best Ten Japanese Films No. 1; and his latest work "Motherhood" (2024), released nine years after "Three Stories of Love." "Hush!" depicts a gay couple and a woman—three people who had given up on connecting with others—forming a "new kind of family." "All Around Us" portrays the hope that arises between people through ten years in the life of a married couple. Both films are often cited as "all-time best films" and are known as "unforgettable masterpieces." Now, these two works will be revived in 4K remastered versions! "All Around Us" returns 18 years after its June 2008 release, while "Hush!" returns 25 years after its production in 2001 (released April 2002)—a full quarter-century later. "All Around Us" follows a wife who falls into depression due to her overly serious nature and her husband, a courtroom sketch artist who supports her, tracing their inseparable bond over ten years against the backdrop of various shocking events from the 1990s. The film was screened in the Panorama section of the 2009 Berlin International Film Festival.
title:All Shall Be Well: A drama depicting a long-term lesbian couple facing various problems after one partner's sudden death. Director Ray Yeung, who previously explored the issues of elderly gay couples in "Suk Suk," turns his gaze to the current state of Hong Kong, where prejudice against homosexuality remains deeply rooted, while also highlighting social issues such as severe housing shortages, employment difficulties, and economic disparity. Pat and Angie, a lesbian couple in their 60s, are enjoying a stable and peaceful life both publicly and privately. However, Pat suddenly dies. Angie was close with Pat's relatives, but they clash over the funeral arrangements. Furthermore, under Hong Kong law, Pat's brother, as her relative, inherits her estate. This is an unacceptable reality for Angie, who considered the apartment, filled with memories of Pat, to be their final home. Meanwhile, Pat's financially struggling brother, his wife, and their children also grapple with their own circumstances. The film won the Teddy Award for outstanding LGBTQ cinema at the 74th Berlin International Film Festival in 2024 and received high praise, including five nominations at the 43rd Hong Kong Film Awards, including Best Film. Patra Au, who won the Hong Kong Film Award for Best Supporting Actress for "Suk Suk," plays Angie, earning a Best Actress nomination for this film. Maggie Li, returning to the screen after about 30 years, plays Pat.
title:All of Tokyo!: A youth ensemble drama featuring all fourth-generation members of the popular idol group Hinatazaka46. Directed by the renowned Kumakiri Kazuyoshi, known for 'My Man' and '#Manhole,' it follows eleven unique high school girls on a school trip to Tokyo as they race through the big city to enjoy everything it has to offer. High school student Ikezono, visiting Tokyo on a school trip, meticulously plans a perfect itinerary to tour famous spots, intending to lead her group. However, on the long-awaited free day, the group inexplicably splits up, and Ikezono finds herself alone at the base of Tokyo Skytree. Determined to complete her plan, she sets out to explore Tokyo, but unbeknownst to her, her group members each have their own agendas for being in Tokyo. Shogenji Yoko, who served as center for Hinatazaka46's single 'Kimi wa Honeydew,' stars as the protagonist Ikezono, with all eleven fourth-generation members appearing. The screenplay is by Fukuda Shohei of the 'HiGH&LOW THE MOVIE' series and Tsuchiya Ryoichi of the film 'Osomatsu-san.' From the planning stage, they directly interviewed all eleven members, gathering memories from their school days, pre-idol stories, and feelings about Tokyo, crafting an original script woven from their real-life stories.
title:All of a Sudden: Director Ryusuke Hamaguchi ("Drive My Car," "Evil Does Not Exist") portrays the spiritual encounter of two women with the same-sounding name in Paris. Based on the exchange of 20 letters between philosopher Makiko Miyano, who survived cancer metastasis, and anthropologist Maho Isono, titled "Suddenly Feeling Ill," the film depicts the connection between two women who meet by chance and their confrontation with the world. Marie-Lou Fontaine, director of the care facility "Garden of Freedom" on the outskirts of Paris, struggles with staff shortages and misunderstanding while striving for humane care. She meets Japanese stage director Mari Morisaki, who is battling cancer, and draws courage from her theater work. Guided by the coincidence of their similar-sounding names, Marie-Lou and Mari begin a friendship. But one day, Mari suddenly falls ill. As her illness progresses, their bond deepens, and their souls connect. Virginie Efira ("Benedetta") plays Marie-Lou, and Tao Okamoto, a global fashion model who has appeared in Hollywood films like "The Wolverine," plays Mari. Kyozo Nagatsuka ("Enemy") plays Goro Seimiya, an actor in Mari's play, and Koyo Kuroki ("The Generation of the Looking-Ahead") plays Tomoki Kubodera, Goro's grandson. Screened in the Competition section of the 79th Cannes Film Festival in 2026, Virginie Efira and Tao Okamoto jointly won the Best Actress award. Okamoto became the first Japanese person to win the Cannes Best Actress award.
title:Along the Sea: This is the second feature film by director Akiro Fujimoto, whose first feature 'Where I Belong'—a Japan-Myanmar co-production—won the Grand Prize in the 'Asian Future' section of the 30th Tokyo International Film Festival and received high acclaim both in Japan and abroad. Following his previous film, which dramatized the true story of a Myanmar family torn between Japan and Myanmar, this work again tackles the realities of Asian residents in Japan, depicting the plight of young women who come to Japan as technical intern trainees. Three Vietnamese women, who fled their workplaces after being mistreated, become undocumented. Relying on brokers to find new jobs, they end up in a snowy northern port town... Fujimoto met a female technical intern trainee online who later disappeared after grueling daily labor; he interviewed women in similar situations and wrote an original script.
title:Alpine Fire: A 1985 film by the master Fredi M. Murer, known as a pioneer of New Swiss Cinema, which won the Golden Leopard, the top prize at the Locarno International Film Festival. A family of four lives a nearly self-sufficient life surrounded by the majestic Alps. The teenage younger brother, who is deaf-mute, grows up healthily, sometimes frustrated by his disability but loved by his parents and older sister. One day, angered by a broken lawnmower, he throws it away, incurring his father's wrath. Running away from home, he begins living alone in a mountain hut. His worried sister brings him food, and they spend happy times together around a campfire on the mountain peak. Eventually, the sister's pregnancy is discovered... The film was first released in Japanese theaters in 1986. A digitally remastered version was revived in February 2020.
title:Amrum: In 1945, at the end of World War II, the island of Amrum in northern Germany remained in a strange, paradise-like stillness even as bombers flew overhead toward the mainland. Naning, a 12-year-old boy evacuated there, supports his pregnant mother and family by helping with farm work in place of his father, who has not returned from the front. However, when his mother Hille, who is devoted to Hitler, collapses both mentally and physically upon receiving news of his death, Naning's daily life is transformed. Hille, drained of vitality and refusing food, desires only one thing: white bread generously spread with butter and honey.
title:Amélie et la métaphysique des tube: An animated film set in 1960s Kobe, depicting the growth of Amélie, a Belgian girl born in Japan. Based on the autobiographical novel "Tube Metaphysics" by Belgian writer Amélie Nothomb, it portrays a world rich in emotion, seen through the eyes of the two-year-old protagonist Amélie, woven with life, color, and her witty words. In 1960s Kobe, Amélie, a Belgian girl born into a diplomat's family, is unresponsive until age two and a half, but then enters an invincible childhood, believing herself to be a god and living in a magical world. Her days with her beloved housekeeper Nishio and her family are adventures full of new discoveries. One day, she learns the kanji for "rain," which suits her perfectly. Then, on her third birthday, an event occurs that changes everything. Directed by Myriam Ballard and Liang-Cho Han, who worked on "Long Way North," with music by Japanese composer Mari Fukuhara. It won the Audience Award at the 2025 Annecy International Animated Film Festival and was nominated for Best Animated Feature at the 98th Academy Awards.
title:An Actor's Revenge: This adaptation of the same-named period novel by Otaguro Mikami was scripted by Daisuke Ito and Teinosuke Kinugasa, with a screenplay by Natsuto Wada, and directed by Kon Ichikawa. Kazuo Hasegawa, who starred in the 1935 version, again plays the dual roles of Yukinojo Nakamura and Yami Taro. The cast also includes Fujiko Yamamoto, Ayako Wakao, Raizo Ichikawa, and Shintaro Katsu, among other luminaries. This film commemorates Hasegawa's 300th appearance. In Edo, Yukinojo Nakamura, a female-role actor of Kamigata kabuki performing in the city, spots Sanzai Tsuchibe and Kaimiya, the men who framed his father on false charges and drove him to suicide. Sanzai's daughter, Namiji, falls in love with Yukinojo, and he uses her to avenge his father. Kawaguchiya, who had been hoarding rice during the Edo famine, is thwarted by Kaimiya—instigated by Yukinojo—and goes bankrupt, after which Kaimiya sets fire to his shop. Enraged, Kaimiya strangles Kawaguchiya but is stabbed by Namiji, whom he had tried to abduct.
title:An Cailín Ciúin: Set in early 1980s Ireland, this human drama depicts a special summer vacation experienced by a 9-year-old girl. It won the Grand Prix in the International Generation section for films starring children at the 72nd Berlin International Film Festival and was nominated for the International Feature Film Award at the 95th Academy Awards. In 1981, in a rural Irish town, a quiet girl named Cott, who lives silently within a large family, spends her summer vacation at the lush green farm of the Kinsella couple. Initially confused by the unfamiliar life, Cott receives abundant love from Sean and Eileen and, as she carefully experiences each moment, comes to feel a joy in living she had never known before. Catherine Clinch, in her debut role, delicately portrays the protagonist Cott with overwhelming transparency and presence, winning the IFTA Award (Irish Film & Television Academy Award) for Best Actress at the youngest age of 12. Based on the novel "Foster" by Irish writer Claire Keegan, this is the first feature-length fiction film directed and written by Colm Bairéad, who has previously focused on children's perspectives and family bonds in his documentary works.
title:An Island Drifts: Winner of both Best Director and Best Drama at the USC First Look Awards. Andrew is a boy attending a private elementary school in modern Singapore, where the pressures of an academic meritocracy swirl around him. One day, a minor accident during a physical education class causes matters to escalate far beyond what is necessary... ■Ticket price: Flat 1,000 yen. *Free tickets, invitation tickets, and various other discount services cannot be used. Information on discounts available only at the box office on the day: Present a ticket for another film on the same day and receive 100 yen off. *Applicable only when purchasing tickets at the box office on the day. Making movie theaters a more casual option. '20 Minute Cinema' is a new initiative screening short films of 15-20 minutes in theaters. A 20-minute interlude you can drop into casually like a café, between shopping or after work. Masterpieces from around the world you won't find on streaming services will vividly color your everyday life.
title:Animal Treasure Island: Young Jim, who dreams of foreign lands and sailing, is left to mind the old inn Benbow Tavern in a port town tonight. But a suspicious cat captain shows up and leaves behind a mysterious map. It seems to indicate the location of treasure hidden by the famous pirate Captain Flint. Jim sets out to sea with his best friend, a mouse named Gran, in his homemade barrel ship, the Pioneer. Their destination: the legendary Treasure Island on the map! However, the Pioneer is sunk by a pirate ship, and the two are quickly taken prisoner. The pirate ship is named the Pork Sauté. Its captain, Silver, was once one of Flint's men, and he too has his eye on the treasure of Treasure Island. Jim and Gran escape and land on Pirate Island. But they are caught by Silver's gang, have the map stolen, and are sold off to slave traders. In the stone prison where they are confined, they find a girl named Cathy already there. It turns out Cathy is Captain Flint's granddaughter and is also looking for the map. Jim and Cathy initially clash but eventually open their hearts to each other and decide to cooperate and head for Treasure Island. Now, the curtain rises on a great adventure across the sea!
title:Anita: A documentary depicting the tumultuous life of Anita Pallenberg, known as the muse of the British rock band The Rolling Stones. Anita Pallenberg, an Italian-German model, actress, and fashion icon, embodied her era through her persona and creativity, becoming a symbolic figure in the rock culture of the 1960s and 70s. In 1965 she fell in love with Rolling Stones leader Brian Jones, and after his death had three children with Keith Richards, also captivating Mick Jagger, with whom she appeared in films. Anita became the source of their creativity, transformed fashion, engaged with the music itself, and lived her own life without being overshadowed by anyone. The film uses words from an unpublished memoir discovered after Anita's death, home movies, and family photographs, while her son Marlon, daughter Angela, and their father Keith Richards reveal intimate family secrets. Furthermore, Marianne Faithfull, Mick's lover and Anita's close friend, and model Kate Moss, who adored Anita, speak about the magnitude of her influence. Scarlett Johansson lends her voice to the words of Anita's memoir. Anita's son Marlon Richards serves as executive producer.
title:Another Home: Set in a small diner on Cheung Chau, an outlying island of Hong Kong, this documentary observes a changing world through the islanders who gather there. Located about 30 minutes southwest of Hong Kong Island by ferry, Cheung Chau is a small island known as a fishing village, where colorful boats bob in the harbor and time flows gently. The 'Yat Tai' diner on the island is always bustling with locals who gather to play cards and mahjong with a beer in hand. However, societal changes and the fervor of citizens reach this island far from Hong Kong, and the diner's regulars cannot remain indifferent. From the owner staring at the TV to young people eagerly seeking information, each person grapples with the tides of the era from their own perspective and distance. Eventually, the pandemic that engulfs the world also has a major impact on this diner. The director is Frankie Shin, for whom this is his first feature-length documentary. Shin, a native of Cheung Chau who was also a regular at the Yat Tai diner, carefully captures how the people he treated like family faced the changing times and continued their daily lives. The film won the Best Documentary Award at the 29th Busan International Film Festival in 2024.
title:AnyMart: At a convenience store called AnyMart in a corner of Tokyo, the assistant manager Sakai (Sosuke Ikematsu) has spent most of his twenties working there since his student days. Register work. Stocking shelves. Disposal. Mobile games. Dating apps. Just repeating the same things every day. The owner (Masahiko Nishimura) rules the store within the convenience store system, allowing no deviation. However, the arrival of a new part-time worker, Ogawa (Erika Karata), begins to quietly disrupt the store's equilibrium. Eventually, this distortion silently and surely transforms the convenience store into an extreme space.
title:Arabian Nights: The Adventures of: Toei Animation's first departure from traditional Japanese or Chinese settings follows a young sailor's romantic voyage. The screenplay was an unusual collaboration between Morio Kita, a recent Akutagawa Prize winner with experience as a ship's doctor, and Osamu Tezuka. Staff went to great lengths to depict waves, sometimes painting as many as 300 polka dots on a single cel, and the resulting animation—over 10,000 drawings—imbues the ocean adventure with remarkable realism.
title:Arco: The adventure of Iris, a girl living in a near future devastated by climate change, and Arco, a rainbow-colored boy who 'fell from the sky.' A poetically rich animation by a rising French director, depicted in vivid colors.
title:Asako I & II: The commercial film debut of director Ryusuke Hamaguchi, who gained attention for "Happy Hour," a film that meticulously depicted the daily lives and friendships of four women over more than five hours and won major awards at numerous international film festivals including Locarno and Nantes. This film was entered into the Competition section of the 71st Cannes International Film Festival. It is an adaptation of the award-winning love novel of the same name by Akutagawa Prize-winning author Tomoka Shibasaki, starring Masahiro Higashide and Erika Karata. Asako, a 21-year-old living in Osaka, meets Baku and falls into a fateful love, but one day, Baku suddenly disappears from her life. Two years later, having moved from Osaka to Tokyo, Asako meets Ryohei, who has a face identical to Baku's. Unable to forget Baku, Asako tries to avoid Ryohei, but he develops feelings for her. Despite her hesitation, Asako finds herself drawn to Ryohei. Higashide plays the dual roles of Baku and Ryohei, while Karata plays Asako.
title:At the Triangle Intersection: A documentary observing a 99-year-old woman and her son and daughter-in-law, who were affected by the Great East Japan Earthquake and the Fukushima Daiichi nuclear disaster and live in disaster recovery public housing, over a three-year period from 2018 to 2021. Seven years after the 2011 Great East Japan Earthquake and Fukushima Daiichi nuclear disaster, a family forced to evacuate from Namie Town, Fukushima, wavers between returning to their hometown and choosing a new life. Having closed their long-running printing business due to the disaster and living in disaster recovery public housing in Iwaki City, the roles and relationships within the family quietly change. Tetsu, the 99-year-old mother, clings to memories of her birthplace, Okuma Town, even as her memory fades. Her taciturn son Takemasa respects his mother but leaves most of her care to his wife Shigeko. Shigeko, who has continued to bear this role, begins to reexamine her taken-for-granted position within the family and her own way of living. Through the family's daily life in flux, the film questions what "home" is and what "I" is. Directed by Toru Yamada, who has continued making films in Fukushima since the Great East Japan Earthquake.
title:Au Hasard Balthazar: The 7th feature film by master director Robert Bresson, known for "L'Argent," "Pickpocket," and "The Trial of Joan of Arc," released in 1966. Inspired by an episode from Dostoevsky's novel "The Idiot," it portrays the strange fate of a donkey and a young girl. In a small Pyrenean village, little Marie names a newborn donkey Balthazar and cherishes him. Ten years later, Balthazar is used for hard labor by a blacksmith but escapes the suffering and returns to Marie. The grown Marie rejoices at their reunion and takes Balthazar with her, but Gérard, who has feelings for her, becomes jealous and torments the donkey. Through the silent perspective of the donkey, the film calmly depicts human folly and ugliness, winning the Special Jury Prize at the Venice International Film Festival and earning acclaim as a masterpiece. Starring Anne Wiazemsky, who later appeared in many Godard films including "La Chinoise," in her film debut. First theatrically released in Japan in 1970, and again in 1995 distributed by France Eigasha. Revived in October 2020 in a 4K restored digital remaster. Also revived in 2026 as part of "Robert Bresson Masterpiece Selection."
