title:Au pan coupé: The second feature film by Guy Gilles, a director re-evaluated since the 2000s as a 'forgotten master of the French New Wave,' depicting a woman living with the memory of her lover who chose death. The present is shown in black-and-white, and fragments of recollection in color, delicately and melancholically portraying the memory of love and the pain of absence. Jeanne lives with the memory of her deceased lover Jean. Jean rejected social order and the bourgeois world, found no place in the Beat generation, and chose death. Unaware of his death, Jeanne feels him always by her side, existing like a ghost. Masha Meril, known for 'A Time for Loving' and 'Belle de Jour,' plays the protagonist Jeanne, and Patrick Jouané, an actor who met Guy Gilles during the filming of 'Le Rempart des Béguines' and became an irreplaceable presence in his life and work, plays the deceased lover Jean. The film was released in Japanese theaters in April 2026.
title:BE:the ONE START BEYOND DREAMS:
The third installment in the "BE:the ONE" documentary series follows the popular dance and vocal group BE:FIRST on their first-ever world tour, held from April to July 2025.

Spanning 12 cities across Asia, Europe, and North America, the "BE:FIRST World Tour 2025 Who is -BE:FIRST?-" transcended language and culture to captivate audiences worldwide. This film features not only their stunning live performances but also the moments of inspiration the members found in various cities and their brief moments of downtime. Furthermore, because the members themselves took turns behind the camera, the film offers an even more authentic, true-to-life look at the group.

The documentary also focuses on RYOKI, who went on hiatus (and subsequently left the group) following the Singapore performance on July 5. It portrays the feelings of each member and their experiences on the ground, capturing their final performance as a seven-member group and their interactions backstage. Additionally, the film includes brand-new interviews capturing the raw emotions of the members after returning home, delving deep into where they stand today.
title:BREAK SHOT: A short black comedy written and directed by Kuruma Takahira of the comedy duo 'Reiwa Roman' as his directorial debut. It depicts an incident that occurs on a congested highway late at night, entirely from the perspective of dashcams. Six cars are driving on the highway. Inside each vehicle, excuses, pride, probing, work anxiety, someone being chased, reckless challenges to boost video views, and trivial conversations unfold. Only the dashcams inside the cars record everything. Tomohiro Kodama of the comedy duo 'Sarugorira' stars, with a stellar supporting cast including Joe Odagiri, Kengo Kora, Aoi Morikawa, and Oshiro Maeda. It was released in theaters after a special screening at 'Short Shorts Film Festival & Asia 2026'. A making-of documentary titled 'KURUMA: The Road to BREAK SHOT' was also produced, delving into the behind-the-scenes production.
title:BREATHLESS: Jean-Luc Godard's first feature-length directorial work. Produced with techniques that broke the conventions of theatrical cinema at the time, such as improvisational direction and handheld street shooting, it is a landmark film of the French New Wave that greatly influenced the later film industry. The original idea was by François Truffaut, and Claude Chabrol also participated as a technical advisor. Michel, a car thief who kills a policeman and flees to Paris, enjoys a free relationship with Patricia, an American student selling newspapers. To test Michel's love, Patricia informs the police of his whereabouts and tells Michel what she has done... A digitally remastered version with a new translation by Jiro Terao was released in 2016. In 2022, a 4K restored version created to commemorate the 60th anniversary of its release was shown. In 2026, a 4K restored version will be revived in conjunction with the release of Richard Linklater's film 'Nouvelle Vague,' which depicts the production process of 'Breathless.'
title:BRING HER BACK: After their father dies, brother Andy and his visually impaired sister Piper come to live with foster mother Laura. Also living there is a boy named Oliver who does not speak. Andy feels uneasy about Laura's seemingly excessive affection, but a new life for the siblings begins under her care. From a certain day onward, unsettling events begin to occur one after another in the house. Furthermore, there are mysterious circular motifs scattered around the house, and the presence of Oliver. When these seemingly unrelated elements all connect, Laura's hidden 'terrifying wish' is revealed.
title:BURN: Director Makoto Nagahisa, known for "We Are Little Zombies" and "And So We Put Goldfish in the Pool," casts Nana Mori in a drama set in Shinjuku's Kabukicho, depicting a "flame war" incident started by a girl. Born into a family of cult followers, Kobayashi Kurie is raised under strict discipline alongside her younger sister. The sisters pray to God daily for their painful days to end and for their education-obsessed father to disappear. Years later, their prayers are answered when their father dies, but their mother continues the harsh upbringing. Unable to bear it any longer, Kurie runs away from home, leaving her sister behind. Following a message on social media, she arrives at a square in Kabukicho where young people gather. There, she is given the name "Juju," a place to sleep, food, a smartphone, and a job. Experiencing the world for the first time and meeting various people, she finally begins to develop her own will. She dreams of taking her sister away from their mother and living together, but... Nagahisa wrote the original script and filmed on location in Kabukicho, capturing the raw reality of the neighborhood and the young people living there. Mori plays the protagonist Kurie, with Aoi Yamada ("Perfect Days"), Ryosuke Soda ("The Liar and His Lover"), and Wataru Ichinose (Netflix's "Sanctuary") co-starring.
title:Badlands: The feature directorial debut of Terrence Malick, director of "Days of Heaven" and "The Thin Red Line," released in 1973. Based on a series of real murders that occurred in the late 1950s in America, it vividly and poetically depicts the flight of a young couple who commit a series of unplanned crimes. In 1959, in a small town in South Dakota. Holly, a 15-year-old girl who is not very noticeable at school, meets Kit, a young garbage collector, and falls in love. However, when Kit shoots and kills Holly's father, who disapproves of their relationship, the two embark on a aimless journey of escape. They live a reckless life, staying carefree in a treehouse and breaking into a rich man's mansion. Holly can only watch as Kit kills people one after another... Martin Sheen, known for "Apocalypse Now," plays Kit, and Sissy Spacek, known for "Carrie," plays Holly. In Japan, it was broadcast on TV in 1980 under the title "Jigoku no Tōhikō," and was released in theaters for the first time in March 2025 under the title "Badlands."
title:Balance: Starring Kumi Takiuchi of 'A Balance' and directed by Yujiro Harumoto of 'To the Ends of the Earth,' this drama confronts the problems and contradictions of the information society head-on. Yūko, a documentary filmmaker, pursues the truth behind a high school girl's suicide due to bullying that occurred three years ago. She is committed to shedding light on issues that need to be brought before the public, even if it means clashing with the production side. Meanwhile, she helps run the cram school managed by her father, Masashi, and has lived happily with him, working as a team. However, an unexpected action by Masashi forces Yūko into an ultimate choice that shakes her convictions. Takiuchi plays the protagonist Yūko, and Ken Mitsuishi plays her father Masashi, with supporting roles by Tomohiro Umeda and Yūmi Kawai. The film was screened in the Panorama section of the 71st Berlin International Film Festival in 2021.
title:Ball of Fire: At the Totten Foundation in New York, eight scholars are putting the finishing touches on an encyclopedia, but when grammar professor Potts overhears a slang term, he realizes their work has been isolated from the real world and ventures into the city to investigate. There, he seeks the help of O'Shea, a nightclub singer... Although the film was a hit in the U.S. upon release, it was never imported due to the times. Billy Wilder contributed to the script on the condition that he be allowed to observe Hawks' direction. He made his directorial debut the following year, having used this as preparation.
title:Band of Outsiders: A masterpiece from Jean-Luc Godard's early period, this melodrama is based on an American crime novel and depicts in comedic fashion the love triangle and criminal scheme involving two men and one woman. Winter in Paris. Franz and Arthur, best friends with completely opposite personalities, both fall in love at first sight with Odile, a beautiful and shy woman from Scandinavia. One day, they learn that a large sum of money is hidden in Odile's aunt's house, and the three plot to steal it, but the plan takes unexpected twists and turns... This was the first production from "Anouchka Films," the production company founded by Godard and actress Anna Karina, who played Odile and were married at the time. Music by Michel Legrand of "The Umbrellas of Cherbourg." It went unreleased in Japanese theaters for many years before finally premiering in 2001.
title:Bande à part: A masterpiece from Jean-Luc Godard's early period, this melodrama is based on an American crime novel and depicts in comedic fashion the love triangle and criminal scheme involving two men and one woman. Winter in Paris. Franz and Arthur, best friends with completely opposite personalities, both fall in love at first sight with Odile, a beautiful and shy woman from Scandinavia. One day, they learn that a large sum of money is hidden in Odile's aunt's house, and the three plot to steal it, but the plan takes unexpected twists and turns... This was the first production from "Anouchka Films," the production company founded by Godard and actress Anna Karina, who played Odile and were married at the time. Music by Michel Legrand of "The Umbrellas of Cherbourg." It went unreleased in Japanese theaters for many years before finally premiering in 2001.
title:Be Pretty and Shut Up!: The only feature-length directorial work by actress Delphine Seyrig, known for films like 'Last Year at Marienbad' and 'Jeanne Dielman, 23 quai du Commerce, 1080 Bruxelles', released in 1976. This documentary interviews 23 actresses active in Hollywood and Paris. Seyrig herself serves as the interviewer, asking two questions: 'If you were a man, would you still have chosen this profession?' and 'Have you ever played a friendly scene with another actress?' The film features a range of women—from famous film actresses like Jane Fonda ('Julia'), Shirley MacLaine ('The Apartment'), Juliet Berto ('Céline and Julie Go Boating'), Anne Wiazemsky ('La Chinoise'), and Maria Schneider ('Last Tango in Paris'), to TV actresses and unknowns—speaking frankly, intimately, and sometimes humorously about gender questions that were risky to answer in the male-dominated film industry of the time. The original title 'Sois belle et tais-toi!' (Be beautiful and shut up) is said to have been a phrase used against women in French film and theater, and is now a cliché symbolizing gender discrimination in English-speaking countries. In Japan, it will have its first theatrical release in July 2026 to commemorate the 50th anniversary of its production.
title:Be a Man!! Samurai School: Depicts the extreme training and battles at 'Otokojuku,' a school that raises men among men. Invited to the 'Big Battle August' tournament where representatives from around the world compete for supremacy during summer vacation, the first-year students fight their way through Hawaii, Niagara Falls, Alaska, and New York, culminating in a decisive battle against the American team. The appeal lies in the massive physiques and dynamic storytelling.
title:Beyond the Fire: The Life of Japan: A documentary depicting the life of activist Teishiro Minami, who organized Japan's first Pride Parade in 1994. Today, Pride Parades are held in over 40 locations in Japan, and partnership systems are spreading nationwide. At the starting point of this progress were the grassroots activities of pioneers who forged a path from "zero" to "one." Born in Karafuto (Sakhalin) in 1931 and raised in Akita Prefecture, Teishiro Minami moved to Tokyo at age 22, constantly searching for a way to live authentically. In 1984, he began the gay liberation movement, immersing himself in activism and following his passion. Then, in 1994, he launched Japan's first Pride Parade. The activities Minami spearheaded became the foundation of the pride movement in Japan, but he gradually became fixated on his own beliefs, deepening the rift with those around him. By the third parade, he faced significant backlash and was forced to step back from the front lines of the movement. What did Minami, driven by justice and swept along by the times, find in the end of his fervor? Tracing his tumultuous path through his own testimony, interviews with people involved at the time, news reports, photos, and videos, the film depicts the origins of the pride movement in Japan. Directed by Hiroaki Matsuoka ("Okinawa Coming Out Story").
title:Beyond the Game: Samurai 2026 WORL: A documentary providing an intimate behind-the-scenes look at Samurai Japan, the Japanese national baseball team, during the 6th World Baseball Classic (WBC) held in March 2026. Having vowed to "discard admiration and surpass it" to win the world championship in a hard-fought battle at the 2023 WBC, the team entered this tournament under the immense pressure of being the reigning champions, facing the inescapable burden of "having to remain the winning champions." The film explores what the players felt and how they fought during their quest to remain on top, and how they came to terms with the result of losing in the quarterfinals. Through the lens of the only camera granted exclusive access to the team for this tournament, the documentary gets to the heart of the action behind the scenes. The director is Shintaro Miki, who has previously made documentaries closely following Samurai Japan, such as "Unity, Beyond: The Warriors' Anguish and Hope" and "The Samurai Who Surpassed Admiration: Record of Becoming World No. 1." Narration is provided by Kazunari Ninomiya, and the theme song is performed by Koshi Inaba. It began streaming on Netflix on April 20, 2026, and had a limited theatrical release nationwide in Japan starting August 14, 2026, including at Aeon Cinema Itabashi.
title:Beyond the Infinite Two Minutes: This is the first original feature-length film by the popular theater troupe 'Europe Kikaku,' known for works like 'Summer Time Machine Blues,' rebooting their short film 'Howling.' On the second floor of a certain mixed-use building, Kato hears a voice from the TV and looks at the screen to see his own face. The Kato on the screen speaks to him, saying 'I'm you from two minutes in the future.' It seems that the second-floor room where Kato is and the first-floor café are connected with a two-minute time difference. The friends who learn of the 'Time TV' become desperate to find out more about the future by facing two TVs towards each other... The film stars troupe members including Kazunari Tosa as the protagonist Kato, along with Aki Asakura and Riko Fujitani. The original concept and screenplay are by the troupe's leader, Makoto Ueda, and the director is the troupe's video director, Junta Yamaguchi.
title:Billy Elliot: A coming-of-age drama set in a 1980s British mining town, following a boy's struggle to become a ballet dancer and the bonds of family. In 1984, in a mining town in northeast England, 11-year-old Billy, who has lost his mother, is forced by his coal miner father to attend boxing classes. One day, intrigued by a ballet class he stumbles upon, he joins the girls in their lessons. Ballet teacher Mrs. Wilkinson discovers Billy's talent as a dancer, and under her passionate guidance, he improves rapidly. Jamie Bell, chosen from over 2,000 auditionees, delivers a powerful performance as Billy. Julie Walters of "Educating Rita" plays Mrs. Wilkinson, earning an Academy Award nomination for Best Supporting Actress. Gary Lewis of "My Name Is Joe" plays Billy's father. World-renowned ballet dancer Adam Cooper makes a special appearance. The film marks the feature directorial debut of stage director Stephen Daldry, who later helmed "The Hours."
title:Bis ans Ende der Welt: A film that Wim Wenders nurtured for about 13 years before completing. Blending sci-fi elements, it combines a road movie and love story set in a world facing apocalypse. In the winter of 1999, the predicted crash of a nuclear satellite casts the world into anxiety. Claire, traveling by car from Venice, meets Trevor, who is being chased by someone. Though they part ways, she can't stop thinking about him and, with the help of her ex-lover (a writer) and a private detective, follows him to Lisbon, Moscow, and Beijing. Reuniting with Trevor in Tokyo, Claire learns the purpose of his journey.
title:Black Ox: A visual poem co-produced by Japan, Taiwan, and the United States, inspired by the "Ten Ox Herding Pictures," which depict the path to enlightenment in Zen using ten images of oxen. Directed and written by Tetsuichiro Tsuta, who gained domestic and international attention for "The Ravine of Goodbye," the film took eight years to complete. A hunter, forced to wander as he loses his mountain home in a rapidly changing era, encounters a majestic black ox in the mountains. He forcibly brings the resisting ox back and begins living with it in a remote house. The man and the ox till the land to survive, but they cannot see eye to eye in the face of nature's fury. However, an encounter with a Zen monk gradually brings the man and the ox to understand each other. Taiwanese acclaimed actor Lee Kang-sheng, known for his frequent roles in Tsai Ming-liang's films like "Stray Dogs," stars, with dancer Min Tanaka, also active as an actor, co-starring as the Zen monk. The entire film was shot on film, with some portions using 70mm film, a first for a Japanese feature film. The music uses compositions by Ryuichi Sakamoto, who had expressed his intention to participate in the project before his death. After its premiere at the "Asian Future" section of the 37th Tokyo International Film Festival in 2024, it won the top prize, the Firebird Award, at the 49th Hong Kong International Film Festival in 2025.
title:Black Rain: Shizuma Shigematsu, living with his family in a village near Fukuyama City, was in Hiroshima with his wife and niece. The atomic bombing was a tragedy that mercilessly took the lives of thousands and forever etched the harsh existence of the survivors.
title:Blood Flower: Set in Malaysia, this demon-combining exorcism gore horror film takes on the Islamic exorcism rites of the state religion and Southeast Asia's most enigmatic flower, the titan arum. A boy apprentice exorcist, who inherited spiritual powers from his mother, engages in a deadly struggle against the forbidden curse dwelling within the "corpse flower." Iqbal, raised under the wing of Norman, a Muslim exorcist, possesses rare spiritual abilities inherited from his mother Dina. One day, Dina is possessed and killed by an evil spirit while shielding Iqbal, who was targeted because of the strength of his powers. Grief-stricken, Iqbal resents his own overwhelming power, and his father Norman, worried about his son's future, seals away part of his abilities. Crawling toward the wounded family are a series of tragedies brought by the curse of the "corpse flower." Can Iqbal overcome his sorrow and exorcise a curse steeped in mystery and taboo?
title:Blood Relatives: A police inspector from the Montreal Police Department solves a murder case using clues obtained from the victim's diary.
title:Blood of My Blood: A Gothic fantasy film by Italian master Marco Bellocchio, released in 2015 and winner of the FIPRESCI Prize at the 72nd Venice International Film Festival. The story intertwines the 17th century and the modern era, depicted with eerily beautiful imagery. In 17th-century Bobbio, northern Italy, young soldier Federico visits an old monastery to uncover the truth behind the death of his twin brother Fabrizio, a priest. It is said that Fabrizio was seduced by a nun named Benedetta, betrayed his faith, and lost his life. Seeking to restore his brother's honor, Federico tries to make Benedetta confess her guilt, but gradually becomes captivated by her, even as she is accused of witchcraft. The story then shifts to the modern day, centuries later. The former monastery lies in ruins, and a sale to a wealthy Russian is being negotiated. A man appears, but the ruins are haunted by a mysterious old count who only shows himself at night. Benedetta is played by Lidia Lieberman, Federico (living in both past and present) by Pier Giorgio Bellocchio, and the mysterious old count by Roberto Herlitzka. A cover of Metallica's "Nothing Else Matters" is used prominently in the film.
title:Blue Lock: A live-action film adaptation of the soccer manga 'Blue Lock', serialized in Kodansha's 'Weekly Shonen Magazine' since 2018, which has gained popularity both domestically and internationally for its innovative premise, unique and egotistical characters, and unpredictable story development. To overcome the Japanese national team's chronic lack of goal-scoring ability, a top-secret project, the 'Blue Lock (Blue Prison)', is launched. Three hundred high school strikers are gathered and subjected to numerous trials, with only the final survivor earning the right to become the world's greatest striker. However, there's a cruel condition: those eliminated are permanently banned from ever representing Japan. Yoichi Isagi, an unknown high school player who dreams of becoming the national team's ace striker and winning the World Cup, decides to participate to change his life. Lacking the outstanding physical abilities of the other 299 participants, Isagi relies on his exceptional spatial awareness to survey the entire pitch and his strong will to pursue the goal, taking on the fierce survival battle. Takahashi Fumiya stars as Yoichi Isagi. The cast includes Sakurai Kaito as Meguru Bachira (Team Z), Takahashi Kyohei (Naniwa Danshi) as Hyoma Chigiri, Nomura Kota as Rensuke Kunigami, K (&TEAM) as Seishiro Nagi (the undefeated champion Team V), Tsunahiro Keito as Reo Mikage, Kubota Masataka as Jinpachi Ego (the project's supreme leader), and Hatakeyama Mei as Anri Teieri (Ego's right hand). The Japan Football Association and J.League fully cooperated with the filming, and former Japanese national team player Matsui Daisuke served as soccer supervisor.
title:Blue Moon: From director Richard Linklater, known for the 'Before' trilogy beginning with 'Before Sunrise' and the six-time Oscar-nominated 'Boyhood,' this conversation piece stars his longtime collaborator Ethan Hawke and depicts a night spent at a party attended by legendary Broadway lyricist Lorenz Hart. On the evening of March 31, 1943, the night of the premiere of the musical 'Oklahoma!,' created by his longtime composing partner Richard Rodgers with a new collaborator, Lorenz Hart—the lyricist behind hits like 'The Lady Is a Tramp' and 'My Funny Valentine'—was invited to a party at the Broadway restaurant Sardi's. Over the course of that night, Hart confronts his own swirling emotions of love, jealousy, anxiety, and longing. Ethan Hawke plays Lorenz Hart, alongside Margaret Qualley as Elizabeth, the woman Hart pines for; Andrew Scott as his former partner Richard Rodgers; and Bobby Cannavale as Eddie, the bartender Hart trusts as a confidant. The film was screened in the competition section of the 75th Berlin International Film Festival in 2025, where Andrew Scott won the Silver Bear for Best Supporting Actor. It was nominated for Best Original Screenplay and Best Actor (Ethan Hawke) at the 98th Academy Awards.
title:Blue Spring: At an all-boys high school. Kyujo (Ryuhei Matsuda) and his five friends, now third-years in the new term, stand outside the railing on the rooftop, playing the 'Balcony Game'—competing to see who can clap the most times before falling. Kyujo sets a new record in this game, where failure means a straight drop to the schoolyard, and as the winner, gains the right to rule the school. But for him, both the 'game' and 'ruling the school' are meaningless and trivial. As Kyujo and the others drift through their aimless days, lost about where they belong, the reality of choosing their future paths is eventually thrust upon them...
title:Bluebeard's 8th Wife: At a department store in the French resort of Riviera, American businessman Michael Brandon (Gary Cooper) insists on buying only the top half of a pair of pajamas. Conveniently appearing to take just the bottoms is Nicole (Claudette Colbert), the daughter of a poor aristocrat. Instantly smitten by her spirited nature, Brandon pursues her relentlessly and secures an engagement. However, on their wedding day, Nicole discovers Brandon has been married seven times and flies into a rage. They manage to marry only on the condition that Brandon pays Nicole a huge alimony if they divorce. Naturally, the relationship fails, and frustrated by his wife's indifference, Brandon resorts to a desperate measure.
title:Bodacious Space Pirates: Abyss of: The theatrical film version of the TV anime "Mouretsu Pirates," which aired from January to June 2012, based on Yuichi Sasamoto's popular SF light novel "Mini-Skirt Space Pirates." Marika Kato, a high school girl who is a legitimate space pirate holding a government-issued "privateer's license," leads a busy life juggling her studies, club activities in the space yacht club, a part-time job at a café, and her role as captain of the space pirate ship "Bentenmaru." One day during spring break, just before she is about to advance to her third year, Marika takes on a pirate business job aboard a luxury liner and meets Kanata Mugen, the son of the renowned subspace diver, Dr. Mugen. The opening theme, following the TV series, is "Mouretsu Uchuu Koukyoukyoku Dainanagakushou 'Mugen no Ai'" by Momoiro Clover Z. The director is Tatsuo Sato, known for "Martian Successor Nadesico."
title:Bohemian Rhapsody: A biographical drama depicting Freddie Mercury, the vocalist of the world-famous rock band Queen, who passed away in 1991 at the young age of 45. Queen's current members Brian May and Roger Taylor served as music producers, and the film's soundtrack primarily uses Freddie's own vocals. It recreates the moments of birth of classics like "Bohemian Rhapsody" and "We Will Rock You," as well as legendary performances in music history such as the stunning performance at "Live Aid," the largest charity concert of the 20th century, while also portraying the untold stories behind his glamorous career. Rami Malek, known for "Night at the Museum," delivers a passionate performance as Freddie. Bryan Singer, known for the "X-Men" series, is credited as director, but he left during production, and Dexter Fletcher, known for "Sunshine on Leith" and "Eddie the Eagle," completed the film, handling the remaining shooting and post-production. Despite the production troubles, it was embraced by audiences worldwide, and in Japan, it became a massive hit, surpassing 13 billion yen at the box office, the highest for a film released in 2018. It won Best Motion Picture – Drama and Best Actor – Drama at the 76th Golden Globe Awards. It was nominated for five Academy Awards at the 91st Academy Awards, including Best Picture, and won four, including Best Actor.
title:Bonne Chance: A road movie written and directed by Shin Adachi, known for scripting the NHK morning drama "Boogie Woogie" and films like "Zako-domo yo, Taishi o Idake" and "Theater Version: Still, I Want to Be with My Wife," set in Bungo-Ono, Oita Prefecture, depicting a small journey of a man and woman lost in life. Taro Oyama, approaching 30, calls himself a film director but is actually supported by the woman he lives with. He is selected for a film festival in Oita Prefecture but receives harsh criticism from the female organizer. The next day, heartbroken, Taro heads to neighboring Chikugo-Ono and meets a mysterious woman named Miki Sunahara. Miki, who says she saw Taro's film at the festival, and Taro embark on a small one-night, two-day trip. Miki is of unknown identity but has a frank personality. Taro, baring his lack of confidence in filmmaking to her, gradually develops a faint romantic feeling... Taro, the struggling film director protagonist, is played by Hiroki Sano from "SUPER HAPPY FOREVER," and Miki, the mysterious woman he meets on his journey, is played by Hana Amano from "Chime." The supporting cast includes Saki Kato, Ryo Shinoda, Ayame Gouriki, and Yuka Itaya.
title:Boy Meets Girl: The feature debut of French maverick Leos Carax, released in 1983. It depicts the encounter of two lonely souls wandering through the Paris night in beautiful black-and-white imagery, winning the Youth Prize at the 37th Cannes Film Festival and generating buzz at festivals worldwide. Alex, a young man whose best friend stole his girlfriend, has a fateful encounter with Mireille, a woman who just fought with her lover. Alex falls in love with Mireille at first sight, but they soon meet with an unexpected tragedy. The roles of Alex and Mireille were played by then-newcomers Denis Lavant and Mireille Perrier. The protagonist Alex, played by Lavant, later reappeared in transformed forms in 'Bad Blood' and 'The Lovers on the Bridge', forming what is known as the 'Alex Trilogy' along with this film. Jean-Yves Escoffier handled the cinematography and continued as cinematographer for the subsequent two films. In Japan, it was first theatrically released in July 1988, following the release of 'Bad Blood' in February of the same year. A 4K restored version was re-released in January 2026.
title:Boyfriends and Girlfriends: The sixth film in Éric Rohmer's "Comedies and Proverbs" series. Set in a new town on the outskirts of Paris, it lightly depicts the romantic affairs of four men and women. Blanche, a shy woman working at city hall, and Léa, a pragmatic female student, hit it off and become friends. Léa lives with her boyfriend Fabien, but their relationship isn't going well. Meanwhile, Blanche develops feelings for Alexandre, a playboy and friend of Fabien's, but her timid nature prevents her from confessing. Eventually, Fabien finds himself drawn to Blanche... The colorful 1980s fashion is also a highlight.
title:Brand New Landscape: Set in rapidly redeveloping Tokyo's Shibuya, this drama portrays the relationship between a father and son left behind after the mother's death. It marks the film debut of Koyo Kurozaki, who gained attention for his acting debut in the NHK morning drama "Boogie Woogie." This is the feature debut of Yuiga Dansuka, based on his original script; he previously directed the short "I Want to Go Far Away" as part of the Agency for Cultural Affairs' young filmmaker development project "ndjc (New Directions in Japanese Cinema)." Ren, a young man working as a Phalaenopsis orchid delivery driver in Shibuya, became estranged from his father, Hajime, a landscape designer, after losing his mother, Yumiko, as a child. One day, Ren coincidentally meets his father during a delivery and tells his sister Emi, but she remains indifferent, quietly preparing for her own wedding. Amidst this, Ren tries to reassess his distance from his family. Kurozaki plays the protagonist Ren, Kenichi Endo (an indispensable supporting actor in Japanese cinema) plays his father Hajime, Haru Ikewaki (active as an actress and model) plays the deceased mother Yumiko, and Maso Kuryu (a talented actress from "Chrysanthemum and Guillotine" and "The Lies of the Suzuki Family") plays his sister Emi. The film was selected for the Directors' Fortnight at the 78th Cannes Film Festival in 2025.
title:Breathless: Jean-Luc Godard's first feature-length directorial work. Produced with techniques that broke the conventions of theatrical cinema at the time, such as improvisational direction and handheld street shooting, it is a landmark film of the French New Wave that greatly influenced the later film industry. The original idea was by François Truffaut, and Claude Chabrol also participated as a technical advisor. Michel, a car thief who kills a policeman and flees to Paris, enjoys a free relationship with Patricia, an American student selling newspapers. To test Michel's love, Patricia informs the police of his whereabouts and tells Michel what she has done... A digitally remastered version with a new translation by Jiro Terao was released in 2016. In 2022, a 4K restored version created to commemorate the 60th anniversary of its release was shown. In 2026, a 4K restored version will be revived in conjunction with the release of Richard Linklater's film 'Nouvelle Vague,' which depicts the production process of 'Breathless.'
title:Bright Future: Yuji Nimura spends a quiet, monotonous daily life with his coworker Mamoru Arida at the same moist towel factory. Yuji is reckless and struggles to get along with others. Seeing this, Mamoru one day proposes two signals that only the two of them can understand and tries to enforce them. Around that time, Yuji begins to take an interest in the highly venomous 'sea wasp' jellyfish that Mamoru keeps. One day, Mamoru entrusts the jellyfish to Yuji and suddenly disappears. Mamoru is imprisoned as a suspect in the murder of the factory owner and his wife. From then on, Yuji, though bewildered, begins caring for the jellyfish as if possessed by something.
title:Bring Her Back: After their father dies, brother Andy and his visually impaired sister Piper come to live with foster mother Laura. Also living there is a boy named Oliver who does not speak. Andy feels uneasy about Laura's seemingly excessive affection, but a new life for the siblings begins under her care. From a certain day onward, unsettling events begin to occur one after another in the house. Furthermore, there are mysterious circular motifs scattered around the house, and the presence of Oliver. When these seemingly unrelated elements all connect, Laura's hidden 'terrifying wish' is revealed.
title:Broker: A road movie that won two awards at the 75th Cannes Film Festival, featuring a Korean production team and cast. Two male brokers who kidnap an infant from a 'baby hatch' and the mother who once abandoned her child. Bound by a strange sense of solidarity, they journey to find adoptive parents, quietly pursued by two female detectives. This film returns to Kore-eda's signature theme of 'quasi-family,' depicting certain hope beyond the moral dilemmas surrounding the salvation of unwanted lives.
title:Bugonia: The eccentric genius Yorgos Lanthimos, known for 'Poor Things' and 'The Favourite', directs this kidnapping suspense film starring Emma Stone in their fifth collaboration. Ari Aster, director of 'Welcome to Eddington' and 'Midsommar', serves as producer. It is a remake of the 2003 Korean film 'Save the Green Planet!'. Michelle, the charismatic CEO of a globally renowned pharmaceutical company, is kidnapped by Teddy, a conspiracy theorist who firmly believes she is an alien set on invading Earth, and his devoted cousin Don. They imprison her in a basement and demand she abandon her plans for Earth. Michelle dismisses their absurd demands and tries to talk her way out, but the tug-of-war takes unexpected turns. As Teddy's hidden past comes to light, the absurd kidnapping plot veers in unforeseen directions. Emma Stone appears with a shaved head, passionately playing Michelle. Jesse Plemons and newcomer Aiden Delvis, cast through auditions, play the two kidnappers. The film was presented in the competition section of the 82nd Venice International Film Festival in 2025 and was nominated for four Academy Awards at the 98th ceremony, including Best Picture and Best Actress.
title:By the Stream: Korean master Hong Sang-soo directs an ensemble drama set at a women's university in Seoul, depicting the romantic entanglements of students and adults surrounding a theater festival. At a women's university in Seoul, with the theater festival approaching, textile artist Jon-hee, who works as a lecturer, invites her uncle Si-on, a famous actor and stage director, as a temporary director to fill a gap caused by a love scandal on campus. As they begin creating a short play for the festival, various events unfold over ten days, including the aftermath of the students' love affairs and the budding romance between a senior professor and Si-on. Actress Kim Min-hee, Hong Sang-soo's partner in both public and private life, stars as Jon-hee and won the Best Performance Award at the 77th Locarno International Film Festival in 2024. The cast also includes regulars from Hong Sang-soo's films: Kwon Hae-hyo as Jon-hee's uncle Si-on, Cho Yun-hee as the professor who admires Si-on, and Ha Seong-guk as the fired director who was dating three people. In Japan, it was screened under the title 'Suyuchon' at the 25th Tokyo Filmex in 2024. It was theatrically released in 2025 as the second film in the 'Monthly Hong Sang-soo' project, a series of five consecutive monthly new releases celebrating the director's 30th debut anniversary.
title:By the Window: A love story directed by Rikiya Imaizumi (known for "Ai ga Nanda") starring Goro Inagaki, based on an original screenplay. Freelance writer Shigeki Ichikawa realizes that his wife, editor Sae, is having an affair with the popular young writer she handles, but he can't bring himself to confront her. At the same time, Shigeki is troubled by a certain feeling that sprouted within him when he learned of the affair. One day, at a literary award ceremony, Ichikawa meets high school writer Rea Kubo and is drawn to the content of her award-winning novel "La France." He asks if there is a real-life model for the story and if he can meet them. Sae, Ichikawa's wife, is played by Yuri Nakamura; high school writer Kubo by Tina Tamashiro; Shigeki's friend Masatsugu Arisaka by Ryuya Wakaba; Arisaka's wife Yukino by Mirai Shida; and Sae's lover Madoka Arakawa by Shion Sasaki.
title:B面の夏: A man whose lover was stolen by his best friend (Kazama), a woman who loved a man for whom she felt no affection (Henmi), and a woman who longs to be alone but cannot (Ishibashi). The lives of these three individuals, each standing at a crossroads, gently intersect in a town by the sea. Because the original source material is a haiku collection by Madoka Mayuzumi, the connecting screenplay was developed entirely from scratch. Despite the unique nature of its production and release—created as a promotional video for Meiji Life Insurance to be distributed to its customers—the film boasts a cast and crew on par with any major theatrical feature.
title:CATCHFIRE: Ann (Jodie Foster), a contemporary artist in Los Angeles, accidentally witnesses a mafia murder. Her boyfriend Bob (Charlie Sheen) is killed, and Ann goes into hiding. Professional hitman Milo (Dennis Hopper), hired by the mafia, pursues Ann but inexplicably begins to fall in love with her. Milo gives Ann an ultimatum: "Die or become my woman." Forced to comply, Ann gradually finds herself drawn to Milo's pure feelings... <Screening Overview> Period: Friday, July 17 – Thursday, July 23, limited one-week screening. Admission: Flat rate of 1,300 yen (no discounts applicable, no complimentary tickets or T-tickets accepted). *Screening material is DVD.
title:CJ7: Ti, who lost his wife to illness, works at a construction site to send his only son Dicky to a prestigious private elementary school. While retrieving a pair of sneakers Dicky wanted from the garbage dump, Ti finds a green ball. Dicky begins keeping the creature (or is it an object of unknown nature?) that is born from the ball Ti brought home, naming it Miracle 7.
title:CLIMAX クライマックス: One night in 1996, 22 dancers selected by a famous choreographer gather in a remote, ruined building. After finishing their final rehearsal for a US tour, they start an after-party. The dancers, moving to blasting music and drinking sangria like water, unknowingly consume sangria laced with LSD. They gradually lose their senses and descend into a trance-like state. The dance floor becomes a paradise for some but a hell for most. What kind of ending awaits this mad feast of people who have lost their reason? A 97-minute pseudo-trance experience from Gaspar Noé, who has provoked and captivated film fans worldwide with themes of love, violence, and sex. This film, which can be considered the culmination of his work to date, offers a completely new and unprecedented cinematic experience.
title:CRAZY PETE: Freedom! Provocation! Headlong rush! A dizzying flood of quotations and colors. Loquacious poetry and suffocating romanticism. Karina, Godard's muse but recently divorced from him, and Belmondo, who became a huge star in 'Breathless' and would part ways with Godard through this film. A miraculous masterpiece where each burned out at the critical point of their careers! [STORY] Ferdinand is bored with his life with his wealthy wife and driven by an urge to escape. One night, a babysitter arrives for their young daughter as the couple heads to a party. She turns out to be his former lover, Marianne. Ferdinand slips out of the party, returns home alone, drives her home, and spends the night with her. Waking up the next morning, he finds a dead man with scissors stuck in his neck in her apartment. In contrast to his shock, Marianne calmly makes breakfast and sings. Ferdinand, leaving Paris with only the clothes on his back, follows her as she promises to explain later, heading to the south of France where her brother lives...
title:CROSSING 心の交差点: Lia, a retired teacher living in Georgia, sets out for Istanbul, Turkey, alongside Achi, a young man who claims to know her missing transgender niece, Tekla. However, finding Tekla, who has vanished without a trace, proves more difficult than they ever imagined. Eventually, Lia crosses paths with Evrim, a lawyer fighting for transgender rights, and enlists her help. Why did Tekla leave Georgia? Set in Istanbul—a city where East and West converge in an evocative cultural tapestry—the journey to find Tekla becomes a path that slowly brings Lia, Achi, and Evrim closer together.

The latest film from Levan Akin, director of *And Then We Danced*.
A journey of the heart connecting past and future, woven in Istanbul—a city where encounters and farewells intertwine.
title:CURE: A masterpiece of psychological suspense in Japanese film history, directed by the brilliant Kiyoshi Kurosawa and starring Kōji Yakusho. A series of bizarre murders occur one after another. While the perpetrators of each case have no connection, the victims all have an X-shaped cut from their neck to their chest, all the assailants are arrested near the crime scene immediately after the incident, and none of the killers had a clear intent to murder just before the act. Detective Takabe, whose wife suffers from a mental illness, is assigned to the investigation but struggles to find a common thread among the perpetrators. Around the same time, a murder with the same modus operandi occurs on a beach near Tokyo, and a young man named Mamiya, who has no memory of being near the scene, is taken into custody. Takabe discovers that Mamiya is a former medical student and realizes he has been using hypnosis to trigger the series of events, but...
title:Call Me Dragon: In the late Qing dynasty, the villainous Im Kun-ho rules over Gold Sand Village, a place rife with all kinds of crime and violence, including drugs and human trafficking. The Dragon group, traveling while punishing evil, and at the same time, the legendary female martial artist Eagle, arrive in this village. They are both searching for a treasure called the 'Silver Pearl', said to have been stolen from a Tibetan temple. Then, the ruthless killer karate practitioner Black Jaguar also appears, and fierce battles unfold among the powerful fighters over the Silver Pearl. This is the Japan comeback film for Yasuaki Kurata, who was active primarily in Hong Kong.
title:CatVideoFest（キャットビデオフェスト）:
CatVideoFest is a globally beloved festival held annually since 2016, now screened in over 350 theaters worldwide, including the United States, Canada, and Europe. The festival features a carefully curated selection of the latest and greatest cat videos from across the globe. Cute, hilarious, and sometimes deeply moving—you can experience the full charm of these feline stars all at once on the big cinema screen!

As a theater-exclusive event, the festival has become a massive hit in the U.S., with attendance growing every year. Last year, it surpassed $1 million at the box office, proving that the unique experience of "watching cat videos together" continues to draw crowds to the cinema. These 73 minutes, filled with smiles and comfort, are truly a "dream come true for cat lovers."

Furthermore, the festival is built on a foundation of compassion: the act of watching the films directly supports cats in need. A portion of ticket proceeds is donated to animal welfare organizations. Since 2019, screenings around the world have raised over $150,000, saving the lives of countless cats. For the screenings in Japan, a portion of the proceeds will also be donated to local rescue groups to fund medical care, foster programs, and other essential support for cats in need.

Help cats just by watching. CatVideoFest is a celebration of feline wonder filled with kindness. Welcome to a "Kitty World" that fills the entire screen! This winter, treat yourself to the ultimate heartwarming cat video experience.
title:Catchfire: Ann (Jodie Foster), a contemporary artist in Los Angeles, accidentally witnesses a mafia murder. Her boyfriend Bob (Charlie Sheen) is killed, and Ann goes into hiding. Professional hitman Milo (Dennis Hopper), hired by the mafia, pursues Ann but inexplicably begins to fall in love with her. Milo gives Ann an ultimatum: "Die or become my woman." Forced to comply, Ann gradually finds herself drawn to Milo's pure feelings... <Screening Overview> Period: Friday, July 17 – Thursday, July 23, limited one-week screening. Admission: Flat rate of 1,300 yen (no discounts applicable, no complimentary tickets or T-tickets accepted). *Screening material is DVD.
title:Catching Fire: The Story of Anita: A documentary depicting the tumultuous life of Anita Pallenberg, known as the muse of the British rock band The Rolling Stones. Anita Pallenberg, an Italian-German model, actress, and fashion icon, embodied her era through her persona and creativity, becoming a symbolic figure in the rock culture of the 1960s and 70s. In 1965 she fell in love with Rolling Stones leader Brian Jones, and after his death had three children with Keith Richards, also captivating Mick Jagger, with whom she appeared in films. Anita became the source of their creativity, transformed fashion, engaged with the music itself, and lived her own life without being overshadowed by anyone. The film uses words from an unpublished memoir discovered after Anita's death, home movies, and family photographs, while her son Marlon, daughter Angela, and their father Keith Richards reveal intimate family secrets. Furthermore, Marianne Faithfull, Mick's lover and Anita's close friend, and model Kate Moss, who adored Anita, speak about the magnitude of her influence. Scarlett Johansson lends her voice to the words of Anita's memoir. Anita's son Marlon Richards serves as executive producer.
title:Catching the Stars of This Summer: A drama based on the award-winning novel by Mizuki Tsujimura, depicting the complex emotions of junior high and high school students during the COVID-19 pandemic, set in Tokyo's Shibuya Ward, Tsuchiura City in Ibaraki Prefecture, and Goto City in Nagasaki Prefecture. In 2020, with school attendance and club activities restricted due to the pandemic, Aya Tanimoto, a second-year student in the astronomy club at Ibaraki Prefectural Sunaura High School, proposes an 'Online Star Catch Contest'—a competition using remote meetings to conduct simultaneous astronomical observations across different locations. The activity, joined by students from the Goto Islands in Nagasaki and central Tokyo, eventually spreads nationwide and sparks a miracle. Hiyori Sakurada, known for 'The Fake Diary,' stars as Aya. Rinataro Mizusawa plays her classmate; Arisa Nakano and Ikoi Hayase play students from Nagasaki; Soiya Kurokawa and Anna Hoshino play students from Tokyo; and Takashi Okabe plays the astronomy club advisor. Tamaki Yamamoto, who gained attention for the 2019 short film 'One Night After' and the streaming drama 'Today You're Restless, You're Burning,' makes his feature-length commercial film debut as director. Mash Morino, known for the drama 'Keke no Hi no Kekeke,' writes the screenplay. Haruka Nakamura, known for 'Look Back,' provides the music.
title:Chaser Game W: A Match Made in Hea: A film version serving as a sequel to the TV dramas 'Chaser Game W: My Ex-Girlfriend is My Harassing Boss' and 'Chaser Game W2: The Beautiful Celestial Maidens,' which delicately portrayed the realities of the game industry and a romance between women. Set seven years after the drama, it depicts the relationship evolving over time and the two women confronting life choices. Itsuki and Fuyu live in Ito City, Shizuoka Prefecture, with their daughter Tsuki, now a middle school student. As they become consumed by housework, childcare, and work, their time together becomes routine. Over the seven years, their relationship shifts from lovers to family, and they gradually begin to drift apart. Though they maintain a peaceful home while being disturbed by each other's casual words and attitudes, their daughter Tsuki senses the unease between her parents. One day, Tsuki gets into trouble and is helped by a taxi driver named Kozue. This encounter prompts Itsuki and Fuyu to confront each other's true feelings for the first time and re-examine the form of love they have lost sight of. Continuing from the drama series, Sugai Yuka stars as Itsuki, Nakamura Yurika as Fuyu, Okamoto Mirai as their middle-school-aged daughter Tsuki, Ito Ayumi as taxi driver Kozue, and Kurotani Tomoka as Department Chief Ro. Directed by Ota Isamu, who also worked on the drama series, with a screenplay by Asada Atsushi.
title:Chiikawa the Movie: The Secret of: Based on the original manga serialized on X (formerly Twitter) since 2020 by illustrator Nagano, the massively popular "Chiikawa" franchise—winner of the Japan Character Grand Prix three times, with its 2022 TV anime's catch-up streams on YouTube surpassing 400 million views—gets an animated film adaptation. Under the complete supervision of creator Nagano, the film adapts the particularly popular long-form "Siren Arc" from the original manga series, depicting a grand adventure of Chiikawa and friends on a mysterious island through epic music and powerful visuals. One day, while Chiikawa and Hachiware are relaxing in the square, a rabbit with a flyer stuck to its face appears. Hachiware reads the flyer, which turns out to be an invitation to a "special island." Tempted by promises of "easy monster subjugation on the island for 100x rewards" and "limited island ramen, limited sweets—sweet and spicy stuff all practically free," Chiikawa and friends decide to join the island camp. Along with a skeptical otter, they board a ship and land on the island, but... CygamesPictures, known for "Umamusume: Pretty Derby - Beginning of a New Era," handles the animation production.
title:Chikamatsu Monogatari: A commentary: Osan, the young wife of a Kyoto paper merchant, is suspected of adultery with the clerk Mohei due to a chance incident... Based on a Chikamatsu puppet play, this celebrated film depicts a man and woman who awaken to true love through a life-or-death escape, rendered with rigorous yet flowing brushstrokes. The dignified beauty of Kagawa as Osan is not to be missed.
title:Children Who Chase Lost Voices: Makoto Shinkai, the animation artist known for delicate psychological portrayals and meticulous visual beauty in works like 'Voices of a Distant Star' and 'The Place Promised in Our Early Days,' returns with his first original feature in five years since '5 Centimeters per Second.' This juvenile animation follows a girl named Asuna who, triggered by mysterious music heard through a mineral radio left by her father, embarks on a grand adventure. The familiar staff supporting Shinkai's works, including art director Takumi Tanji and composer Tenmon, come together for this film.
title:Chimney Town: Frozen in Time: The sequel to the 2020 anime film 'Poupelle of Chimney Town,' based on the picture book of the same name by Akihiro Nishino. Based on the 2019 picture book 'Tick Tock: The Promised Clock Tower,' it is adapted on a much larger scale, depicting the story of the boy Rubitch meeting his dear friend Poupelle, who went far away in the previous film, once again. One year has passed since the miracle night when Chimney Town was enveloped in a starry sky. The boy Rubitch, who lost his dear best friend Poupelle, continued to believe in their reunion but eventually gives up to move forward. One day, Rubitch wanders into a mysterious otherworld that controls time, the 'Millennium Fortress.' In this world, clocks that no longer tell time are disposed of, but there is a mysterious clock tower that, though not broken, has stopped at 11:59. The mission Rubitch is given to return to his original world is to get this stopped clock tower moving again. Rubitch meets a man who has kept a promise and waited for 100 years, and regains the courage to believe. Continuing from the previous film, Akihiro Nishino serves as executive producer, original creator, and screenwriter, Yusuke Hirota directs, and STUDIO4°C handles the animation production. Yuzuna Nagase, a child actor known for the TV drama series 'Asa ga Kita,' voices the protagonist Rubitch, and Masataka Kubota, who voiced Poupelle in the previous film, reprises his role.
title:Chronicle of Anna Magdalena Bach: The life of Johann Sebastian Bach as seen through the eyes of his second wife, Anna Magdalena Bach. Directed and written by the duo Jean-Marie Straub and Danièle Huillet, with cinematography by Ugo Piccone, Saverio Diamante, and Giovanni Canfarelli, and music by Leo Leonius. Starring Gustav Leonhardt and Christiane Lang-Drewanz. The film is composed of just over one hundred shots. Only the musicians performing appear on screen, while Anna Magdalena's (Christiane Lang-Drewanz) narration recounts Bach's (Gustav Leonhardt) life from age 35 until his death. The Bach works performed on screen include the Brandenburg Concerto No. 5 BWV 1050, 1st movement Allegro; Prelude No. 8 BWV 854 from the Clavier-Büchlein for Wilhelm Friedemann Bach; Minuet from French Suite No. 1 BWV 812; Viola da Gamba Sonata No. 2 BWV 1028, 1st movement Adagio; Organ Trio No. 2 BWV 526, 2nd movement Largo; Magnificat BWV 243, movements 11 and 12; Tempo di Gavotta from Partita No. 6 BWV 830; Cantata BWV 205 "Zerreißet, zersprenget, zertrümmert die Gruft," movements 2 and 3 (Bass Recitative and Aria); Cantata BWV 198 "Trauer-Ode," final chorus; Funeral Music for Prince Leopold BWV 244a, Soprano Aria; St. Matthew Passion BWV 244, opening chorus; Cantata BWV 42 "Am Abend aber desselbigen Sabbats," opening Sinfonia and Tenor Recitative; and 24 other pieces. In 1722, Anna Magdalena is taken in as Bach's second wife. Over the 29 years until her death in 1756, Bach's creative struggles and his attitude towards Anna and their children at home are narrated in the order the music was composed.
title:Chronik der Anna Magdalena Bach: The life of Johann Sebastian Bach as seen through the eyes of his second wife, Anna Magdalena Bach. title:Chuckle Chuckle: A fusion of individuality from promising young creators. Directed by Yuka Nishida, a graduate of Kyoto University of the Arts, who now belongs to STARDUST CREATORS as a screenwriter. This film is her graduation project, made when she was 22. It has been nominated for the SKIP City International D-Cinema Festival 2025, the 23rd Ueda Castle Town Film Festival Independent Film Competition, and the 28th Kyoto International Student Film Festival. Lead actor Mao Yoshino passionately plays dual roles: Ichitaro Sahara and his 'ideal self' Sahara. After this film, Yoshino was cast as a main host in 'Love and Rumors Last Seventy-Five Days' (2023, directed by Ririko Shinjo). Satoru Murayama, playing Junji Setoguchi who forms a duo 'Geki Amazu Buta' with Yoshino, portrays his partner while carrying a difficult-to-share secret, and was selected as a main cast member from about 700 applicants for the 2026 film 'Hello My Friend' (2026, directed by Masahide Ichii). Nanami Kitano, playing Sahara's neighbor Suzuka Murii, expresses a delicate distance with Sahara through a transparent performance, and has appeared in many films since. Distribution is handled by GeneHeart, which operates 'GeneTheater,' a streaming service curating only high-quality Japanese short films that stir emotions.
title:Chungking Express: A stylish ensemble love story set in Hong Kong that depicts the intersecting romantic entanglements of young people, catapulting director Wong Kar-wai to international fame. Cop 223, heartbroken on April Fool's Day, buys a can of pineapple every day until his birthday a month later. Determined to forget his lover by falling for a woman he meets that night, he encounters a blonde woman in sunglasses at a bar he stumbles into. Meanwhile, fast-food worker Faye is given a letter by her boss for regular customer Cop 633. It's a letter from Cop 633's ex-girlfriend, containing the key to his apartment. Faye, harboring a crush on him, uses the key to sneak into his room... Cop 223 is played by Takeshi Kaneshiro, and Cop 633 by Tony Leung. It won three awards including Best Picture at the 14th Hong Kong Film Awards. First released in Japan in 1995. In 2022, a 4K restored version was screened as part of 'WKW4K' (from August 19, 2022, at Cine Mart Shinjuku, Grand Cinema Sunshine, Cinema City, etc.).
title:Citizen Kane: A human drama produced, directed, co-written, and starring the 25-year-old prodigy Orson Welles, hailed as a masterpiece in film history. Based on real-life newspaper magnate William Randolph Hearst, it depicts the tumultuous life of a wealthy tycoon through innovative visual techniques and narrative structure. The wealthy newspaper magnate Kane dies, leaving behind the mysterious word "Rosebud." A newsreel editor assigned to investigate the meaning of the word interviews people who knew Kane in life, including his ex-wife and business partners. What emerges is the lonely life of a man who had everything. The film won the Academy Award for Best Original Screenplay at the 14th Academy Awards in 1942.
title:Climax: One night in 1996, 22 dancers selected by a famous choreographer gather in a remote, ruined building. After finishing their final rehearsal for a US tour, they start an after-party. The dancers, moving to blasting music and drinking sangria like water, unknowingly consume sangria laced with LSD. They gradually lose their senses and descend into a trance-like state. The dance floor becomes a paradise for some but a hell for most. What kind of ending awaits this mad feast of people who have lost their reason? A 97-minute pseudo-trance experience from Gaspar Noé, who has provoked and captivated film fans worldwide with themes of love, violence, and sex. This film, which can be considered the culmination of his work to date, offers a completely new and unprecedented cinematic experience.
title:Climbing for Life: This drama marks Sayuri Yoshinaga's 124th film appearance and is modeled after Junko Tabei, the first woman to successfully summit the world's highest peak, Mount Everest. It portrays a female mountaineer who staked her entire life on reaching the 'top.' In 1975, as deputy leader and climbing captain of the Japanese Women's Everest Expedition, Junko Tabe became the first woman in the world to summit Everest. Her achievement astonished the world and brought light to herself, her friends, and her family, but it also cast a deep shadow. Her challenges as a mountaineer continued, and in her later years, even while battling illness and after being given a terminal diagnosis, Junko continued to smile, involve those around her, and climb mountains. The cast includes Yoshinaga as Junko Tabe, a character based on Junko Tabei; Koichi Sato as her husband Masaaki; Yuki Amami as Etsuko Kitayama, Junko's ally and Everest climbing partner; and Non as the young Junko. The film is directed by Junji Sakamoto, who previously directed Yoshinaga in 'The Light of the North' and reunites with her after 13 years.
title:Close to the Bone: A documentary following Ryusho Gushiken, who has spent over 40 years collecting the remains of those who died in the Battle of Okinawa. It is said that nearly 3,000 sets of remains—of local residents, former Japanese soldiers, American soldiers, and people from the Korean Peninsula and Taiwan—still lie in southern Okinawa Island, the site of fierce fighting. Gushiken, now 70, began collecting remains at age 28 and has found approximately 400 sets. From fragments he gathers—crushed and scattered small bones, pieces of teacups, shrapnel, and traces of flamethrowers—he infers whether the remains are those of soldiers or civilians, how they met their end, and offers his thoughts and prayers. Film director Katsuya Okuma, who himself lost a great-aunt in the Battle of Okinawa, accompanies Gushiken on his collection efforts, searching for traces of his great-aunt's life. Interweaving archival footage of the Battle of Okinawa, the film illuminates Okinawa's history and present.
title:Cléo de 5 à 7: Cleo (Corinne Marchand) is a beautiful blonde woman. Lately, however, Cleo is troubled. She feels unwell. The thought that it might be cancer makes her restless. Recently, she underwent a thorough examination at the hospital. The results are due this evening. Cleo is terrified of that moment. Five o'clock. Cleo sits down before a female fortune teller. The fortune teller sees through her illness.

title:Coffee After All: A humorous yet slightly poignant conversation piece chronicling the two months leading up to the closure and relocation of a real small coffee shop called "Kohaze Coffee" in Tokyo's Shimokitazawa. Responding to the shop manager Ryuji Tanigawa's wish to preserve on film the old shop he ran for 18 years before moving to a new location in May 2025, actor-director Jun Hosoi wrote the script and directed the film. Long beloved in Shimokitazawa, "Kohaze Coffee" is preparing to move, but manager Tanigawa, veteran part-timer Shimada, and new part-timer Sudo keep things running at their own leisurely pace. Regular customer Aoki makes it a routine to spend his work breaks there alone. Other regulars and staff—Takeda, Tsukamoto, Ito—develop slightly strange and varied relationships, which in turn cause some things in Aoki to change while others remain the same. Starring Sakura Fujiwara as Aoki, Tokio Emoto as the manager, Jun Hosoi, Tatsuya Yamawaki, and Ryohei Higashi as regulars, Nanami Hidaka and Riko Seto as part-timers, with special appearances by Yūki Isomura and Yoshinori Okada. Koichi Sogawa, closely associated with Shimokitazawa, wrote the new theme song "Ending."
title:Cranko: A film about the life of genius choreographer John Cranko, who elevated the Stuttgart Ballet from a small regional company in Germany to world-class status, made with the full cooperation of the ballet company. It depicts the untold story behind the creation of his masterpiece "Onegin" and his true face, cut short by an untimely death at the age of 45, all colored by spectacular dance performances by current star dancers. John Cranko, an up-and-coming choreographer active in England, is prosecuted for homosexual acts after a police sting operation. Forced to leave London in 1960, he becomes a guest artist with the Stuttgart Ballet through connections. Finding a place in the company that accepts him without prejudice, he becomes artistic director the following year in 1961, creating works and a company that express beauty and passion with free-thinking ideas. In 1969, the ballet company is invited to the Metropolitan Opera House in New York and rises to the top of the world overnight. Sam Riley, known for "Maleficent" and "Control," stars, passionately portraying Cranko, a man overflowing with passion and innovative talent but who sometimes hurts others due to being too pure in his pursuit of art. Directed and written by Joachim A. Lang, known for "The Man Who Produced Hitler" and who has covered the Stuttgart Ballet for many years.
title:Cruel Story of Youth: High school girls Makoto and Yoko always hitch rides home from town with men who have cars, getting them to drive them home. But one day, a middle-aged man in a foreign car tries to take Makoto to a hotel. A college student named Kiyoshi appears, knocks the man down, and saves Makoto, but their encounter leads them toward destruction... The shocking intensity of the love scenes and raw depictions gave rise to the term 'Shochiku Nouvelle Vague,' and this second feature film by director Nagisa Oshima was a huge box office hit.
title:Cruising: A crime suspense film directed by William Friedkin, who won an Academy Award for "The French Connection" and had a worldwide hit with "The Exorcist," released in 1980, set against the backdrop of New York City's underground gay culture at the time. A series of murders targeting only gay men occurs in New York at night. Police detective Burns, given a secret mission, goes undercover in S&M clubs frequented by gay men, pretending to be homosexual. Wandering the depths of male sexuality night after night, Burns wears himself down both physically and mentally, finally finding a clue to the killer... Based on actual murders of gay men that occurred between 1973 and 1979, Friedkin wrote the script after experiences including meeting with a suspect who had also appeared in "The Exorcist." Considered the first Hollywood film to openly depict male same-sex S&M sex, it faced protests from the time of its announcement through its release for allegedly promoting homophobia, and was not a commercial success. However, since the 2000s, it has been re-evaluated as a valuable record of gay culture before the global spread of HIV.
title:Cry Out: A mystery drama based on the acclaimed novel by best-selling author Kanae Minato, considered her magnum opus, directed by Takahisa Zeze ('The Last 10 Years', 'Those Who Were Not Protected'). Shinomiya Mayuko fulfills her grandmother's expectations and becomes a teacher despite her complicated family background. One day, her student Saeki Akiko receives a letter from someone claiming to be 'Me, 20 years from now'. Half-doubtful, Akiko writes back, enduring the grief of losing her father and the lonely days with her withdrawn mother. But violence from her mother's boyfriend, bullying, and an unbelievable truth push her to the edge. In deep despair, Akiko and her only friend Arisa hatch a forbidden plan: 'kill the parents'. Mayuko tries to save Akiko, reaching out even as she herself is crushed by society's injustices. Yuna Kuroshima plays Mayuko, the teacher who tries to support children despite her own complicated past. Nanami Yamazaki plays Akiko, the girl struggling to survive harsh reality. Tori Matsuzaka and Kitagawa Keiko play Akiko's parents Ryota and Fumino. Ryuta Bando plays Mayuko's lover Haruki Yuki. Kanata Hosoda and Hana Kondo play Hirota Higuchi and Shinju Morimoto, who deeply influence the lives of Mayuko and Akiko.
title:Cure: A masterpiece of psychological suspense in Japanese film history, directed by the brilliant Kiyoshi Kurosawa and starring Kōji Yakusho. A series of bizarre murders occur one after another. While the perpetrators of each case have no connection, the victims all have an X-shaped cut from their neck to their chest, all the assailants are arrested near the crime scene immediately after the incident, and none of the killers had a clear intent to murder just before the act. Detective Takabe, whose wife suffers from a mental illness, is assigned to the investigation but struggles to find a common thread among the perpetrators. Around the same time, a murder with the same modus operandi occurs on a beach near Tokyo, and a young man named Mamiya, who has no memory of being near the scene, is taken into custody. Takabe discovers that Mamiya is a former medical student and realizes he has been using hypnosis to trigger the series of events, but...
title:Cyborg 009 and the Monster Wars: During the early days of TV anime, orders were unstable, so to secure steady theatrical commissions, a medium-length film series called "B Works" was planned (conventional feature-length films were called "A Works"). Based on Shotaro Ishinomori's popular sci-fi manga, the film employed TV anime staff such as Keiichiro Kimura, the animation director of "Rainbow Sentai Robin," and utilized TV production efficiency techniques. While there were changes from the original manga, such as turning one of the characters into a child, the battles unfold across land, sea, and air, offering high entertainment value, and the composition shows awareness of widescreen framing.
title:DANS LA VILLE DE SYLVIA: This film follows a young aspiring painter wandering through places of memory, searching for traces of Sylvia, a woman he loved six years ago. It constructs an obsessive love story reminiscent of Alfred Hitchcock's 'Vertigo' (1958) with meticulously calculated sound and imagery, resulting in a groundbreaking work unlike anything seen before. The film was shot entirely on location in Strasbourg, France, an ancient city where medieval streetscapes and cutting-edge railways coexist without dissonance, creating a stateless atmosphere. The masterful sound design, which orchestrates the city's noises—the murmur of people, the passing of trams—like a symphony, and the beautiful, luminous chain of images captured through glass reflections and tram windows, transport the viewer into an unknown, otherworldly space.
title:DEAD OR ZOMBIE:
Set in a city overrun by zombies, this unconventional drama depicts the quiet survival of individuals struggling with the burdens of life. Originally released as the 2022 short film *DEAD OR ZOMBIE: Even if Zombies Appear, We Won't Change Our Self-Esteem*, the project was expanded with prequels and sequels to form a single feature-length film consisting of four episodes.

A zombification phenomenon breaks out in a regional Japanese city. Saki, a high school girl who had been a shut-in in her room, remains in the quarantine zone to care for her zombified family, carving out a life of survival (Episode 1: "Even if Zombies Appear, We Won't Change Our Self-Esteem").

An ancient virus is discovered in samples collected from an asteroid by a Japanese unmanned space probe, and analysis begins at the National Space Research Institute... (Episode 0: "The Origin of Life").

With the Japanese government’s response lagging, the U.S. Forces Japan take control of the quarantine zone. Meanwhile, China sends in a research institution to investigate the zombies (Episode 2: "The Will of the Universe").

title:DIE MY LOVE: Director Lynne Ramsay ("We Need to Talk About Kevin," "You Were Never Really Here") presents a psychological drama starring Jennifer Lawrence and Robert Pattinson, depicting a couple torn between love and madness. It was screened in the Competition section of the 78th Cannes Film Festival and nominated for the Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Drama. Grace, a writer who moves to a countryside town with her husband Jackson, begins a new life. Peaceful days are shattered after childbirth: her writing stalls, and the pressure and loneliness of childcare, along with fragmentary hallucinations, gradually distort her reality. As the boundary between reality and fantasy blurs, Grace's mind quietly but surely collapses. Jennifer Lawrence, who won the Academy Award for Best Actress for "Silver Linings Playbook," plays Grace and also serves as a producer, drawing on her own childbirth experience to embody the loneliness and anxiety of a postpartum woman. Robert Pattinson ("The Batman") plays Jackson. The film is based on the novel "Die, My Love" by Ariana Harwicz, with Martin Scorsese as a producer.

title:DISTANCE: Four men and women, all family members of the perpetrators of a murder case committed by a cult three years earlier, meet once a year to pay their respects at the lake where the ashes were scattered. That year, their car goes missing as they try to return from the lake. Stranded, they end up spending the night at a lodge where the cult members once lived, along with a former cult member who also lost his motorcycle. Directed by Hirokazu Kore-eda of "After Life" fame. Starring ARATA, Yusuke Iseya, Susumu Terajima, Tadanobu Asano, and others.

title:DOPPEL:
Director Kenji Tani, known for *Reminiscence Journey Reenact*, helms this drama depicting the life of a young rookie actor set within a popular theater troupe. Troupe Byakuya, which enjoys a cult following, shifts its creative direction to cater to a new fan base after a stage adaptation of a manga becomes a massive hit. Noboru Mitsui, a newcomer to the troupe, feels frustrated and anxious that the current style is preventing him from honing his craft. With the support of the troupe’s star actor, Miyabayashi, Noboru appeals to the leader, Terada, expressing his desire to perform the kind of edgy plays they once did, and is subsequently cast as the lead in their next production. Tasked with playing an "emotionless killer," Noboru undergoes extreme character preparation as Terada’s demands during rehearsals grow increasingly severe. Eventually, Noboru begins to feel a growing anger toward himself for being unable to discard the very desire to "act."

Daisuke Morisaki, formerly of the global boy group BLANK2Y, makes his film debut as the lead, Noboru Mitsui. He is joined by Shohei Hashimoto, a veteran of numerous "2.5D" stage plays, as the troupe’s star Yosuke Miyabayashi; Yusuke Hino from the tokusatsu drama *Kamen Rider Gavv* as Tomoyuki Sotodate, a former member who holds the key to the story; voice actor and actor Shintaro Asanuma, also an active playwright and director, as the troupe leader Nao Terada; and Taro Hasegawa, the film’s screenwriter and an actor/director himself, as theater writer Harumitsu Fujimaki.
title:DOPPEL 舞台挨拶１:
Daisuke Morisaki’s First Starring Role as a Rookie Theater Member
Co-starring Shohei Hashimoto, Yusuke Hino, and Shintaro Asanuma
The film *DOPPEL* is set for a limited one-week screening at Cinemart Shinjuku from April 17 (Fri) to April 23 (Thu)!

Director Kenji Tani—whose previous work *Reminiscence Journey Re-enact* began as a crowdfunding project before gaining widespread acclaim across 30 theaters nationwide in 2024—returns with his latest film, *DOPPEL*. It has been officially confirmed for a special one-week run at Cinemart Shinjuku from April 17 (Fri) to April 23 (Thu).

2025 | Blu-ray | Color | 46 min | *DOPPEL* Film Partners

This project marks another collaboration between Kenji Tani and Cast Corporation, the agency of Ryo Matsuda (star of *Reminiscence Journey Re-enact*). Featuring Daisuke Morisaki in his first leading role and Shohei Hashimoto as his co-star, this film presents a new story set in the world of theater, following in the footsteps of *Reminiscence Journey Re-enact*.

**■ Main Trailer and Poster Visual Unveiled**
The main trailer begins with the protagonist, rookie actor Noboru Mitsui (Daisuke Morisaki), declaring, "I am an actor," providing a glimpse into the film's narrative.
The footage introduces the challenges faced by Noboru as he is cast as an "emotionless killer," alongside the troupe’s star actor Yosuke Miyabayashi (Shohei Hashimoto), whom Noboru looks up to. We also see the troupe’s director, Nao Terada (Shintaro Asanuma), appearing visibly enraged, and former member Tomoyuki Sotodate (Yusuke Hino), who exudes an unsettling aura. Theater writer Harumichi Fujimaki (Taro Hasegawa) is also shown, seemingly unable to stop writing.
The inclusion of a bloody scene midway through suggests that this is far more than a simple coming-of-age story about a rookie actor.

Furthermore, the theme song "End of the Chosen Path" (Eranda Michi no Hate) is performed by Mai Sato. Having felt a sense of disconnect with female school uniforms since junior high, Sato’s life changed after a pivotal encounter, leading her to become the center of a men’s dance-vocal group. She currently creates and shares work on YouTube as a VTuber.
The narration is provided by Takuya Masunaga, known for his roles in *Hypnosis Mic -Division Rap Battle- Rule the Stage* and *The Prince of Tennis* musicals.

The main poster visual features Daisuke Morisaki as Noboru in the center, flanked by Shohei Hashimoto as Miyabayashi on the left and Shintaro Asanuma as Terada—sporting striking sunglasses—on the right.
The background features cuts from the film, leaving viewers to wonder what they represent... a mystery to be solved at the theater. The visual perfectly captures the tagline: "Reality or fiction? This is the story of an actor burdened by karma," depicting a world where reality and illusion intertwine.
Witness the life of a young rookie actor on the big screen!

**■ Video Message from Daisuke Morisaki and Shohei Hashimoto Expressing "Panai" Joy over the Theatrical Release**
A video has arrived from Daisuke Morisaki (Noboru Mitsui) and Shohei Hashimoto (Yosuke Miyabayashi) celebrating the theatrical release! Experience the "Panai" (incredible) energy in the film itself.

**● Project Overview**
**【Introduction】**
The latest work from Director Kenji Tani, whose film *Reminiscence Journey Re-enact* became a sensation after starting as a crowdfunding project and screening in 30 theaters nationwide.
The protagonist, Noboru Mitsui, is played by Daisuke Morisaki in his first-ever starring film role. Morisaki debuted in 2022 as part of the K-POP Japan-Korea-China global boy group "BLANK2Y" and later served as the leader of "Celest1a," produced by Eunhyuk of SUPER JUNIOR, garnering significant attention from Gen Z.
In this film, Morisaki takes on a new challenge as an actor, playing Noboru Mitsui, a rookie in the popular "Troupe Byakuya" who is suddenly cast in the lead role of an "emotionless killer" for their next production.

Shohei Hashimoto plays Yosuke Miyabayashi, the star of Troupe Byakuya. Hashimoto has appeared in numerous "2.5D" stage productions, including *Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba* and *Ensemble Stars! THE STAGE*. While he plays Mitsui’s senior in the story, he is also his actual senior at the same talent agency.
