title:DOPPEL 舞台挨拶２:
Daisuke Morisaki’s First Starring Role as a Rookie Theater Member
Co-starring Shohei Hashimoto, Yusuke Hino, and Shintaro Asanuma
The Film "DOPPEL" Confirmed for a Limited One-Week Screening at Cinemart Shinjuku from Friday, April 17th to Thursday, April 23rd!

The latest work from director Kenji Tani—whose previous film *Reminiscence Journey: Re-enact* began as a crowdfunding project before gaining significant buzz during its 2024 release in 30 theaters nationwide—has been announced. The film *DOPPEL* will hold a limited one-week screening at Cinemart Shinjuku from Friday, April 17th to Thursday, April 23rd.

2025 | Blu-ray | Color | 46 min | ©DOPPEL Film Partners

For this project, director Kenji Tani once again teams up with Cast Corporation, the agency of *Reminiscence Journey: Re-enact* star Ryo Matsuda. The film features Daisuke Morisaki in his first starring role, with Shohei Hashimoto co-starring. This marks a new story set in the world of theater, following in the footsteps of *Reminiscence Journey: Re-enact*.

■ Main Trailer and Poster Visual Unveiled
The main trailer begins with the protagonist, rookie actor Noboru Mitsui (Daisuke Morisaki), declaring, "I am an actor," providing a glimpse into the film's narrative.
The footage introduces Yosuke Miyabayashi (Shohei Hashimoto), the star actor of the troupe whom Noboru admires, as Noboru is given the challenging task of playing an "emotionless killer." We also see the troupe’s leader, Nao Terada (Shintaro Asanuma), appearing visibly enraged; former troupe member Tomoyuki Sotodate (Yusuke Hino), who exudes an unsettling atmosphere; and theater writer Harumitsu Fujimaki (Taro Hasegawa), who seems unable to stop writing.
A mid-trailer shot featuring blood suggests that this is more than just a simple coming-of-age story about a rookie theater member.

Furthermore, the theme song "End of the Chosen Path" (Eranda Michi no Hate) is performed by Mai Sato. Sato, who felt a sense of disconnect with female school uniforms since junior high, eventually became the center of a men’s dance and vocal group following a fateful encounter. She currently releases work on YouTube as a VTuber.
The narration is provided by Takuya Masunaga, known for his roles in *Hypnosis Mic -Division Rap Battle- Rule the Stage* and *The Prince of Tennis* musicals.

The main poster visual features Daisuke Morisaki as Noboru in the center, flanked by Shohei Hashimoto as Miyabayashi on the left and Shintaro Asanuma as Terada—sporting impressive sunglasses—on the right. Background cuts from the film add to the mystery... please see what they represent for yourself at the theater. The visual perfectly captures the theme: "Reality or fiction? This is the story of an actor burdened by karma," appearing as a blend of reality and illusion.
Witness the way of life of a young rookie actor on the big screen!

■ A "Panai" Joyful Video Message from Daisuke Morisaki and Shohei Hashimoto
A video has arrived from Daisuke Morisaki (Noboru Mitsui) and Shohei Hashimoto (Yosuke Miyabayashi) expressing their excitement for the theatrical release! Please look forward to experiencing the "Panai" (incredible) energy in the film itself.

● Work Overview
【Introduction】
The latest film from director Kenji Tani, whose crowdfunding-born hit *Reminiscence Journey: Re-enact* was released in 30 theaters nationwide.
Starring in his first film role as the protagonist Noboru Mitsui is Daisuke Morisaki. Morisaki debuted in 2022 as a member of the K-POP global boy group "BLANK2Y" and later gained attention among Gen Z as the leader of "Celest1a," produced by Eunhyuk of SUPER JUNIOR.
In this film, marking his challenge in the new field of acting, Morisaki plays Noboru Mitsui, a rookie in the popular "Troupe Byakuya" who is suddenly cast in the lead role of an "emotionless killer" for their next production.

Playing Yosuke Miyabayashi, the star actor of Troupe Byakuya, is Shohei Hashimoto. Hashimoto has appeared in numerous "2.5D" stage productions, including *Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba* and *Ensemble Stars! THE STAGE*. While he plays Mitsui’s senior in the story, he is also Morisaki’s senior at the same talent agency in real life.
The key character Tomoyuki Sotodate, who is fired from the troupe, is played by Yusuke Hino, who is currently gaining popularity as Hanto Karakida/Kamen Rider Valen in *Kamen Rider Gavv*.
The leader of Troupe Byakuya, Nao Terada, is played by Shintaro Asanuma
title:DREAMS:
Norwegian director Dag Johan Haugerud—a former bestselling author and librarian—presents a drama exploring the lives of three generations of women with differing values, centered on a young girl’s candid memoir about her love for a female teacher. Set in the Norwegian capital of Oslo, the film is the final installment of Haugerud’s trilogy chronicling three perspectives on "sex," "love," and "desire." At the 75th Berlin International Film Festival in 2025, it became the first Norwegian film ever to win the Golden Bear, the festival's top honor.

Seventeen-year-old Johanne, experiencing her first love for her teacher Johanna, records her yearning and exhilaration in a personal memoir. Hoping to share her feelings, Johanne shows the writing to her grandmother, a poet, but the situation takes an unexpected turn. While the grandmother is reminded of her own history of struggle as a woman, Johanne's mother attempts to categorize the work through a modern lens as a "feminist novel documenting a lesbian awakening."

The film will be released in theaters in September 2025 as part of the special screening series "Oslo: Three Landscapes of Love," alongside the trilogy’s previous two installments, *SEX* and *LOVE*.
title:Daisies: A landmark film of the 1960s Czech New Wave, this work portrays the wild antics of two uninhibited girls, both named "Marie," using a boldly experimental array of techniques including color shifts, coloring, optical effects, innovative sound design, and abrupt scene transitions. The older sister, with a blonde bob and a daisy wreath, and the younger sister, with dark brown hair in two pigtails, both call themselves "Marie" and pretend to be siblings. They live freely, tricking men into buying them meals only to fake-cry and run away. At home, they do whatever they please—bathing in milk, burning paper, cutting out magazine photos, slicing up bed sheets, and eventually cutting each other's bodies, until the screen itself fragments. Directed and written by Věra Chytilová, a pioneering Czech filmmaker and the most prominent female director of the Czech New Wave. The two leads were played by non-professional actresses selected through auditions: Jitka Cerhová and Ivana Karbanová. Other roles were also filled by non-actors, such as composers and designers. The film had its first official theatrical release in Japan in 1991 at Kichijoji Baus Theater, where it ran for an extended period through word of mouth. It has since gained a cult following, and in March 2026, a 4K restored version will be re-released to commemorate the 60th anniversary of its production and the 35th anniversary of its Japanese release.
title:Das Versprechen - Architekt BV Dos: A documentary about the world-renowned Indian architect Balkrishna Doshi. Balkrishna Vithaldas Doshi, who in 2018 became the first Indian to win the Pritzker Prize, considered the Nobel Prize of architecture, passed away in 2023 at the age of 95. Beginning his career under Le Corbusier in Paris in the 1950s, he oversaw the implementation of Corbusier's projects in Ahmedabad, western India, and later collaborated with Louis Kahn after India's independence. Influenced by Corbusier and Kahn, Doshi incorporated sustainable and ecological ideas into his architecture early on, establishing a unique style that fused modernism with Indian tradition, climate, and spirituality. He aimed for architecture that contributes to society and the environment, a 'people's architecture' rooted in daily life. This film delves into Doshi's inner world in his final years, visiting the buildings he collaborated on with Corbusier and Kahn, as well as his own works, as he discusses his architectural philosophy, creative process, and career spanning 70 years. Screened as part of the special program 'Le Corbusier and Doshi: Indian Modernism' (starting May 1, 2026, at Eurospace in Tokyo and other theaters nationwide).
title:Das geschriebene Gesicht: This film approaches Kabuki actor Bandō Tamasaburō and, through the existence of the onnagata (female-role specialist), brings into relief a traditional Japanese feminine ideal as a construct of fiction. An unconventional work that blends fiction and reality and depicts its subject in a fantastical manner.
title:David Byrne's American Utopia: A live performance film directed by Spike Lee, capturing the legendary Broadway show based on David Byrne's 2018 album American Utopia. All 21 songs, including tracks from the album plus his signature songs from the Talking Heads era, are performed in a stunning showcase by David Byrne and 11 musicians all dressed in matching gray suits.
title:Days of Being Wild: Director Wong Kar-wai's second feature film from 1990, this youth ensemble drama depicts the romantic entanglements of young people in 1960s Hong Kong with a sense of rushing visual beauty, catapulting Wong Kar-wai to international fame. Yuddy approaches Su, who works as a vendor at a soccer stadium, and they fall in love. However, Yuddy is troubled by not knowing his biological mother. After breaking up with Su, Yuddy spends a night with Mimi, a dancer at a nightclub. Leaving the room, Mimi encounters Yuddy's best friend Zeb, who falls in love with her at first sight. Tide, a policeman on night patrol, has feelings for Su, but she cannot forget Yuddy. The cast features Hong Kong cinema's biggest stars, including Leslie Cheung, Maggie Cheung, Carina Lau, Tony Leung, Andy Lau, and Jacky Cheung. First released in Japan in 1992. A digital remastered version was released in February 2018 at Bunkamura Le Cinema and other venues. A 4K restored version was released in December 2023 as part of the special screening "Wong Kar-wai: The Beginning."
title:Dead Man's Wire: Tony Kiritsis (Bill Skarsgård), a middle-aged single man living in Indianapolis, believing he was swindled out of his entire life savings by the mortgage company Meridian Mortgage, breaks into their office and takes the president's son and executive, Dick Hall (Dacre Montgomery), hostage. Using a device called a "dead man's wire"—a shotgun and wire rigged to his and the hostage's necks so that any sudden movement would trigger the gun—he demands an apology and compensation from the company. With the local police completely unable to act, Tony calls a popular radio show to expose Meridian Mortgage's wrongdoing, involving the show's DJ Fred Temple (Coleman Domingo) to broadcast his claims. The mortgage company's representative issues a statement on TV accepting Tony's demands, but Tony refuses, insisting that the president, M.L. Hall, must apologize in person first. As the situation shows no sign of improvement, the FBI arrives and begins profiling Tony, while police prepare for a raid. Suspicion of a bomb on the scene brings in a bomb squad, tightening the net around Tony. Meanwhile, Tony's next move is to call in the three major US networks and other media to the scene, holding a press conference with the dead man's wire still pointed at Dick. Tony's appeal through the media divides public opinion and throws America into chaos.
title:Deaf: A Spanish film that delicately portrays the story of a woman living in a world without sound and her family. Ángela, who is deaf, and her husband Héctor, who gently supports her, communicate through the irreplaceable language of sign language. Ángela works in a pottery workshop, surrounded by the comforting smell of clay and trusted colleagues, living a quiet and peaceful life. However, a certain 'happy event' begins to gradually shatter her daily life. As she wavers in her sense of alienation, Ángela tries to grasp the 'true happiness' that flickers between the silent world and the world outside... Directed by emerging filmmaker Eva Libertad, who also works as a playwright and sociologist, this film is based on her highly acclaimed 2021 short film 'Sorda.' Starring Miriam Garlo, a deaf actress and Libertad's real sister, the film reflects the director and her sister's long-standing personal experiences, capturing the subtle misunderstandings between deaf and hearing people and the different feelings of alienation each holds. It won the Panorama Audience Award and the Art Cinema Award at the 75th Berlin International Film Festival in 2025, as well as the Golden Biznaga (Best Film), Audience Award, Best Actress, and Best Actor at the 28th Málaga Film Festival in Spain.
title:Deathstalker: From Steven Kostanski, the mad genius director of "Psycho Goreman" (2020) and member of Canada's notorious effects collective Astron-6, who has contributed special effects to Hollywood blockbusters like "Resident Evil: Retribution" (2012) and "Pacific Rim" (2013). His two latest films, "Frankie Freako" and "Deathstalker," will be released sequentially in Japan starting July 3rd at Cinemart Shinjuku and other theaters nationwide. Kostanski, who wrote and directed both films, is known for his unique creature designs reminiscent of classics like "E.T." (1982), "Gremlins" (1984), and "The Goonies" (1985), blending 80s-style monster panic with absurdist black humor, creating a devoted fanbase. These new films bring his signature style to Japan. "Deathstalker" is a reboot of the 1984 cult classic "Deathstalker" (executive produced by Roger Corman). It reconstructs the sword-and-sorcery world with Kostanski's signature nightmarish horror and gore, infused with comedy and darkness. Daniel Bernhardt ("The Matrix Reloaded," "John Wick") stars as the titular Deathstalker. Slash, guitarist of Guns N' Roses, contributes to production and music. Synopsis: In a chaotic world ruled by sword and sorcery, the kingdom of Abraxion suffers under attacks from the sudden appearance of the crimson knight order, the Dread Knights, and is in decline. Unsettling rumors spread that this war is a precursor to the resurrection of the ancient sorcerer Necromemnon. Amidst this, the insolent wandering warrior Deathstalker comes into possession of a cursed amulet, making him a target for the Dread Knight's assassins. To break the curse and repel the approaching evil, Deathstalker embarks on a perilous journey, eventually being drawn into a battle that will decide the fate of the world.
title:Decision to Leave: From Park Chan-wook, director of 'Oldboy' and 'The Handmaiden', comes a suspense drama about a detective investigating a murder and the victim's wife, a suspect to whom he finds himself drawn. When a man falls to his death from a mountain peak, Detective Hae-joon suspects it may be murder rather than an accident. He focuses on the victim's mysterious wife, Sore, but she has an alibi. As the investigation proceeds, Hae-joon finds himself attracted to Sore, and she develops special feelings for him too. Just when a lead emerges and the case seems solved... Park Hae-il plays Hae-joon, Tang Wei plays Sore, with Lee Jung-hyun and Go Kyung-pyo in supporting roles. The film won the Best Director award at the 75th Cannes Film Festival in 2022.
title:Deep Red: The splendid murder aesthetics of Dario Argento, the emperor of Italian horror, explode throughout the film. In Japan, after the huge success of 'Suspiria' (1977) with the clever tagline 'Never watch it alone,' this film was given a Japanese title to ride on that wave and was released in theaters, but it is actually unrelated in content and was made before that film. A shocking work that weaves the mystery of a series of gruesome murders with Argento's signature gorgeous and shocking visual beauty. Starring David Hemmings from 'Blow-Up' and Daria Nicolodi, Argento's good partner both publicly and privately. At the European Parapsychology Conference held in Rome, a telepathic woman named Helga, while demonstrating her abilities on stage, senses someone's murderous intent and becomes hysterical. She declares that a person who has committed brutal murders is in the audience. Later, Helga is brutally murdered in her room. Mark, a British pianist who happens to arrive at the scene and witnesses the murder and a suspect, teams up with journalist Jenna to investigate the mystery, but the truth they ultimately uncover is beyond imagination.
title:Den sidste viking: Danish director Anders Thomas Jensen, known for writing "Riders of Justice," "The Good Life," and "After the Wedding," delivers a human drama starring his frequent collaborator Mads Mikkelsen. After serving time for a robbery, Anker is released and reunites with his brother Manfred, who hid a large sum of money during the heist, for the first time in 15 years. However, Manfred not only has forgotten the hiding place but also believes he is John Lennon. The two set out on a journey to find the bag of hidden money, but the trip gradually transforms into a journey of self-reflection for both of them. Mikkelsen plays Manfred, who has lost his memory and believes he is John Lennon, embodying this eccentric and unique character. Anker is played by Nikolaj Lie Kaas, another frequent collaborator of Jensen's. The film had its world premiere in the Out of Competition section of the 2025 Venice International Film Festival and became a massive hit in its native Denmark, breaking the country's all-time box office record for a live-action film.
title:Der Himmel über Berlin: A masterpiece fantasy film directed by Wim Wenders ('Paris, Texas'), who took the helm in his home country of Germany for the first time in a decade, winning the Best Director award at the 40th Cannes Film Festival in 1987. Set in Berlin before the fall of the Wall, it poetically and beautifully depicts the fate of an angel who falls in love with a human. Damiel, an angel who listens to the inner voices of humans and comforts their sorrows, meets Marion, a trapeze artist performing in a circus. Strongly drawn to her loneliness, Damiel decides to descend from the heavenly realm to the human world. Bruno Ganz stars, and Peter Falk ('Columbo') appears as himself. The screenplay was contributed by Peter Handke, who would later win the Nobel Prize in Literature. A sequel, 'Faraway, So Close!,' was produced in 1993.
title:Desert of Namibia: A youth drama written and directed by Yoko Yamanaka, highly acclaimed for her directorial debut 'Amiko,' which made her the youngest director ever invited to the Forum section of the Berlin International Film Festival. Starring Yuumi Kawai from 'The Girl in the Photograph,' it sharply portrays the love lives and struggles of contemporary Japanese youth. It won the FIPRESCI Prize at the Directors' Fortnight of the 77th Cannes Film Festival in 2024. For 21-year-old Kana, thinking about the future is too boring, and she doesn't even know what she wants out of life. She has no passion for anything, and even love is just a way to kill time. Her live-in boyfriend Honda tries to please her by paying rent and cooking, but as Kana grows closer to the confident creator Hayashi, she begins to feel Honda is a burden. Daikei Kaneko from 'See You at the Jogasaki Cart' and 'Summer Film' plays Hayashi, and Kanichiro from 'Okiku and the World' and 'Promised Land' plays Honda. The cast also includes Yuzumi Shintani, Ayumu Nakajima, Erika Karata, and Shiku Shibuya.
title:Detective Conan: Fallen Angel of t: The 29th theatrical film in the nationally hit series "Detective Conan", based on the manga by Gosho Aoyama. Conan, Ran, Sonoko, and Kogoro, along with motorcycle enthusiast Sera Masumi, encounter a mysterious black motorcycle speeding out of control while on their way to the "Kanagawa Motorcycle Festival" in Yokohama's Minato Mirai district. Kanagawa Prefectural Police traffic officer Hagiwara Chiharu chases the black bike but narrowly misses catching it. Conan and the others arrive at the festival venue, where a new white motorcycle called "Angel" equipped with cutting-edge technology is being unveiled. News then arrives that the runaway black bike has appeared in Tokyo. After evading the Metropolitan Police Department's pursuit, the black bike, whose body closely resembles the "Angel", is dubbed the "Black Angel" or "Lucifer", and the chase continues. In Chiharu's mind, memories of her younger brother Hagiwara Kenji and his colleague Matsuda Jinpei flash by. Hagiwara Chiharu, praised by Ran as the "Goddess of the Wind" for her driving skills, makes her first appearance in a theatrical film, engaging in intense motorcycle action against the mysterious black bike "Lucifer". Chiharu is voiced by Miyuki Sawashiro, who took over the role from Atsuko Tanaka, who passed away in August 2024. Guest voice actors Ryusei Yokohama and Mei Hata make their voice acting debuts. Directed by Takahiro Hasui, who handled direction for "Detective Conan: Black Iron Submarine".
title:Detective Story: This was a highly anticipated comeback film for Yakusho, who had taken a break from acting to prepare for university entrance exams after the massive hit of her starring movie "Sailor Suit and Machine Gun" (1981). The story follows a pampered college girl, played by Yakusho, who is bodyguarded by a private detective played by Matsuda. Director Negishi Kichitaro and the staff devised various strategies to help Yakusho grow as an actress, and she rose to the occasion. It was first released as a double feature with "The Girl Who Leapt Through Time" starring Harada Tomoyo. College student Arai Naomi is set to leave for America, where her father awaits, in one week. Invited by her admired senior Nagai, she heads to a hotel, but a man claiming to be her uncle bursts in and drives Nagai away. The man is a private detective named Tsujiyama Shuichi, hired by her father's former secretary to protect her until her departure. One day, Tsujiyama's ex-wife Sachiko shows up at his apartment, saying she is suspected of stabbing Kazuya, the heir to the Okazaki gang, at a hotel. Naomi suggests to Tsujiyama that they search for the real culprit together.
title:Detective vs. Sleuths: A suspense action film starring Lau Ching-wan of 'Burning Down' fame, which was a huge hit in China. It depicts a former detective once called the 'God of Detectives' taking on a series of murders that shocks Hong Kong. A sequel to the 2007 film 'Mad Detective' co-directed by Johnnie To and Wai Ka-fai, this installment is directed solely by Wai Ka-fai. It won awards for Best Director, Best Actor, Best Screenplay, and Best Cinematography at the 41st Hong Kong Film Awards in 2023. It was also screened in the Gala Selection section at the 35th Tokyo International Film Festival in 2022. Screened at the 'Unseen Zone Films 2024' event held at Human Trust Cinema Shibuya and Cine Libre Umeda.
title:Devara: Part 1: A sea battle entertainment film starring NTR Jr. from "RRR." In 1996, on the eve of the Cricket World Cup, the Indian police headquarters, under high alert, receives intelligence about a sabotage plot by a massive criminal organization. Special investigation officer Shivam pursues the organization's leader to Ratnagiri in South India. A settlement of four villages in the region known as the "Red Sea" is feared as a den of vicious smugglers. Disguising himself as a smuggler to gather information, Shivam learns from the elder Singappa about a brutal conflict that began 12 years ago and the bloody legend of the Red Sea's hero, Devaraj, and his son Vara. NTR Jr. plays dual roles as the legendary hero Devaraj and his son Vara. Saif Ali Khan from "Vikram Vedha" plays Devaraj's nemesis Bhaira, and Janhvi Kapoor from "Gunjan Saxena: The Kargil Girl" plays the heroine. The film is directed and written by Koratala Siva, known for "Mirchi" and "Janatha Garage."
title:Die Büchse der Pandora: A sensual melodrama based on the play of the same name by F. Wedekind, which gave L. Brooks, who moved from Hollywood to Germany, the nickname 'Lulu' after her character. Lulu, a dancer in a seedy dive, becomes the mistress of Dr. Schön, a newspaper publisher, through the skills of her foster father Schigolch. She rises to perform in top theaters, and when Schön tries to break up with her, she turns the tables and forces him to marry her. Schön has a son of marriageable age, Alwa, who is also his secretary, and Lulu seduces him as if enjoying tearing the father and son apart. When Schön learns of her numerous affairs and the decisive truth, he threatens to kill Lulu and then himself, but in the struggle, she shoots him. Although captured, she escapes during the trial with the help of her foster father and Alwa. She lives a life of pleasure on a gambling ship in a port town, introduced by her lover, the strongman Rodrigo. But when Rodrigo sells her, a fight breaks out over her, and Lulu, her foster father, and Alwa secretly enter London. Reduced to extreme poverty in the slums, Lulu decides to become a prostitute, bringing a man into her room while the two men wait outside, unaware that the effeminate man is the infamous Jack the Ripper...
title:Die My Love: Director Lynne Ramsay ("We Need to Talk About Kevin," "You Were Never Really Here") presents a psychological drama starring Jennifer Lawrence and Robert Pattinson, depicting a couple torn between love and madness. It was screened in the Competition section of the 78th Cannes Film Festival and nominated for the Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Drama. Grace, a writer who moves to a countryside town with her husband Jackson, begins a new life. Peaceful days are shattered after childbirth: her writing stalls, and the pressure and loneliness of childcare, along with fragmentary hallucinations, gradually distort her reality. As the boundary between reality and fantasy blurs, Grace's mind quietly but surely collapses. Jennifer Lawrence, who won the Academy Award for Best Actress for "Silver Linings Playbook," plays Grace and also serves as a producer, drawing on her own childbirth experience to embody the loneliness and anxiety of a postpartum woman. Robert Pattinson ("The Batman") plays Jackson. The film is based on the novel "Die, My Love" by Ariana Harwicz, with Martin Scorsese as a producer.
title:Digimon Adventure: The first theatrical film in the "Digimon" series. From a midnight computer screen, a strange creature named "Botamon" is born! While Tai is uneasy, his little sister Kari is overjoyed. Botamon evolves into Agumon! Suddenly, the Digital World, home to digital monsters, appears. A bird-like monster charges at Agumon. But then, another change occurs in Agumon's body... Evolution into the giant monster "Greymon" begins! Two colossal monsters clash—what will be the outcome of this fierce battle?
title:Distance: Four men and women, all family members of the perpetrators of a murder case committed by a cult three years earlier, meet once a year to pay their respects at the lake where the ashes were scattered. That year, their car goes missing as they try to return from the lake. Stranded, they end up spending the night at a lodge where the cult members once lived, along with a former cult member who also lost his motorcycle. Directed by Hirokazu Kore-eda of "After Life" fame. Starring ARATA, Yusuke Iseya, Susumu Terajima, Tadanobu Asano, and others.
title:Doggie March: A puppy named Rock rises up with stray dogs to defeat Killer the tiger, who killed his mother. Drawing on 'Chushingura' and Sazanami Iwaya's children's literature 'Koganemaru,' this film more consciously adopts Disney's style compared to earlier feature-length works. The stateless urban depictions and the action in a snow-covered amusement park, inspired by an idea from Osamu Tezuka, exude a chic and modern sensibility.
title:Dogville: An experimental work by the Danish maverick Lars von Trier, who won the Grand Prix for 'Breaking the Waves' and the Palme d'Or for 'Dancer in the Dark' at the Cannes Film Festival. Inspired by the song 'Pirate Jenny' from Brecht's 'The Threepenny Opera,' and referencing Dashiell Hammett's 'Red Harvest' and Kafka's 'Amerika,' he describes this as depicting an 'imaginary America.' The director himself also participated in the filming using a DV camera.
title:Donnie Darko: As the second installment of THE RIVER's original program 'REVIVAL by THE RIVER,' which brings back beloved Western films from the 2000s for revival screenings, the legendary cult film 'Donnie Darko' will be screened once again. An emergency revival screening will take place at Human Trust Cinema Shibuya for a limited weekend on August 22 (Sat) and 23 (Sun), 2026. It returns to Japanese screens to mark the 25th anniversary of its U.S. release. Middlesex, Massachusetts. Donnie Darko, 17. Ever since a plane engine fell onto his house, a silver rabbit has appeared before him. The rabbit tells him [28:06:42:12]. The beautiful transfer student, Dr. Hawking, the basement door... Everything surrounding him is telling him about "it." What awaits him in the world 28 days later? Flat rate of 1,600 yen (various discount services not applicable).
title:Double Clutch: Centered on the bond between a young man (Go) who dreams of becoming a racer and his older sister (Matsuzaka), who works as a station vendor by day and a hostess by night to support him and fulfill his dream. The story also unfolds a passionate love affair between the sister and a teacher (Chii), as well as a gentle romance between the young man and the teacher's sister-in-law (Morishita). However, one day, a tragic event strikes the close-knit siblings. The teacher, whom the sister trusted, turns out to be married; he impregnates her and ultimately murders her. Enraged for his sister, the young man seeks revenge, double-clutching his car into a deadly car chase against the teacher.
title:Double Indemnity: An early work by Billy Wilder and a masterpiece of film noir suspense. Insurance salesman Walter is approached by a married woman who wants to take out an accident insurance policy on her husband without his knowledge. Sensing something amiss, he initially refuses, but captivated by the beautiful wife, he descends into becoming an accomplice in the husband's murder. The murder scene creates indirect realism by holding on the expressions of those present. The supporting characters surrounding the pair are also superb.
title:Dragon Ball Z: Fusion Reborn: At Enma's palace, where he usually manages heaven and hell, a young psychedelic demon forgets to replace the tank of the spirit laundering device that purifies souls bound for hell. Evil energy leaks from the now-full tank, and using the psychedelic demon's body as a medium, it transforms into the monster Janemba. At the same time, Enma's palace is sealed off by a barrier, throwing the order of the afterlife and the living world into chaos. In the living world, villains previously defeated, such as Frieza, are revived, causing great turmoil. Son Gohan, Son Goten, and Trunks fight back, but they are at a loss for a fundamental solution. Around the same time, during the finals of the Other World Tournament being held again as a rematch of the previous one, a mysterious crystal suddenly appears. Sensing something wrong in the Enma realm, Goku and Pikkon head to Enma's location and attempt to destroy the barrier, but fail. Enma tells them that the one who created the barrier is Janemba, who is above, and with Janemba himself calling him out, Goku takes on the fight. Janemba looks foolish at first glance, but he freely manipulates magical, bizarre techniques and is skilled at reading his opponent's movements, so Goku struggles somewhat. Finally, Goku transforms into Super Saiyan 3 for the second time since his battle with Majin Buu and lands a full-force blow on Janemba. However, Janemba, who seemed to have been killed, instantly regenerates his body and, now in a more combat-oriented form, attacks Goku. Janemba's power is too much even for Goku's Super Saiyan 3, and Goku finds himself in dire straits. Just then, Vegeta, who has regained his original body due to the disturbance in the afterlife's order, rushes to Goku's aid. Vegeta fights bravely on his own, but he cannot match Janemba, and after being shown the clear difference in power, he realizes that even in death, he still falls short of Goku, and is disheartened. Then, Goku proposes the fusion technique as a last resort. To restore the order of the afterlife and the living world, Goku and Vegeta attempt to fuse in the face of the powerful enemy Janemba.
title:Drive My Car: Inheriting the original story of a man's loss and hope after losing his wife, this is a remarkable narrative where the story and the play within the film resonate contrapuntally, boldly incorporating theatrical elements from timeless works like 'Uncle Vanya' and 'Waiting for Godot.' It won four awards including Best Screenplay at the 74th Cannes Film Festival and won the Academy Award for Best International Feature Film at the 94th Academy Awards.
title:Driving Madeleine: A human drama about a taxi driver who, while driving an elderly lady preparing for the end of her life, gets swept up in a journey across Paris exploring her past. Charles, a grumpy taxi driver on the verge of losing his license with no money or days off, is in the biggest crisis of his life. Then he agrees to drive 92-year-old Madeleine to the opposite side of Paris. Madeleine, who is preparing for her final affairs, asks Charles to make one detour after another. The streets of Paris where she lived her life hold many secrets, and with each detour, Madeleine's surprising past is revealed. This drive gradually transforms both their lives. Dany Boon plays Charles, and French chanson legend Line Renaud plays Madeleine. The film is directed and written by Christian Carion.
title:Dynamite Don-Don: Set in 1950, in Kokura, Northern Kyushu, under U.S. occupation just after the war. To resolve the escalating yakuza conflict between the Okagen and Hashiden gangs, the police chief proposes a peaceful solution: a yakuza baseball tournament instead of a turf war. The protagonist, Kasuke of the Okagen gang, uses his wits to suppress Hashiden's offense, but the impatient Hashiden brings in their secret weapon, Ginji. A pitcher who became a yakuza after having his fingers severed over a woman, his magical pitches turn the tide, putting Okagen in a tough spot.
An immortal masterpiece of sci-fi human drama directed by Steven Spielberg, depicting the bond between an alien left behind on Earth and a group of children. A spaceship arrives in an American forest to study the planet's plant life. When human searchers close in, the ship flees, but in the chaos, one alien is left behind. Ten-year-old Elliot, who lives near the woods, encounters the alien and hides him in his home. Drawing in his older brother and younger sister, Elliot deepens his connection with the alien they name E.T., but... Henry Thomas, active as a child actor, plays the lead role of Elliot, and Drew Barrymore, also a child actor at the time, plays his sister Gertie. The special effects and E.T.'s design were handled by Carlo Rambaldi, who previously teamed with Spielberg on 'Close Encounters of the Third Kind,' earning the film an Academy Award for Visual Effects. The score by John Williams, who also composed for 'Jaws' and 'Star Wars,' accompanies iconic scenes like the bicycle soaring through the night sky, along with countless famous lines and moments. In January 2025, the film received its first IMAX screening as part of the 'Steven Spielberg IMAX Film Festival.'

title:ENHYPEN [WALK THE LINE SUMMER EDIT:
A concert film capturing the first-ever stadium performance in Japan by the seven-member global boy group from South Korea, ENHYPEN.

As part of ENHYPEN's world tour in Japan, the dome tour "ENHYPEN WORLD TOUR ‘WALK THE LINE’ IN JAPAN" was held from November 2024 to January 2025. As an encore to that tour, "ENHYPEN WORLD TOUR ‘WALK THE LINE’ IN JAPAN SUMMER EDITION" took place on July 5 and 6, 2025, at Tokyo's Ajinomoto Stadium, and on August 2 and 3 at Osaka's Yanmar Stadium Nagai.

This film captures the full performance from the July 6 show at Ajinomoto Stadium. In addition to the passionate performances delivered on the group's largest-ever stage, the film brings to the screen behind-the-scenes rehearsals, candid moments from their daily lives while traveling, and the overwhelming energy of ENGENE (ENHYPEN's fandom) that filled the stadium with excitement.

The film will be screened in a variety of formats, including standard 2D, the three-sided multi-projection ScreenX, the immersive 4DX, and ULTRA 4DX, which combines both ScreenX and 4DX.
title:ENZO: Set in sun-drenched Southern France, this is a fresh and vivid youth drama about the inner conflicts and love of an adolescent boy living in the complex modern era. Enzo, a 16-year-old raised in a wealthy family in Southern France, struggles to fit in at school and works at a construction site. He becomes drawn to Vlad, a young Ukrainian man he meets there, but Vlad must go to war for his military service. Distrust towards his seemingly comfortable family, anxiety about the future, and the reality of war taking away those close to him. Unable to control his emotions, Enzo's summer passes quietly. Originally a project launched by director Laurent Cantet, known for "The Class," his ally Robin Campillo, known for "BPM (Beats Per Minute)," took over and completed the film after Cantet passed away in 2024 while battling cancer. Newcomer actor Eloi Poy, a former competitive swimmer, delicately portrays Enzo's inner turmoil. Pierfrancesco Favino, known for "The Traitor," and Élodie Bouchez, known for "The Dreamed Path," co-star as Enzo's parents. Amateur actor Maxime Slivinsky, who actually worked on construction sites, was cast as Vlad, the worker Enzo has a faint crush on.
title:EPiC / エピック エルヴィス・プレスリー・イン・コンサート: A visual work by director Baz Luhrmann, who helmed the 2022 biographical film "Elvis," using cutting-edge technology to revive Elvis Presley in the modern era. Elvis Presley, hailed as the "King of Rock and Roll" for his innovative music and charismatic stage performances, lived a 42-year life as a darling of the times. During the production of the biopic "Elvis," director Baz Luhrmann and his team discovered a treasure trove in Warner Bros.' vault: footage shot for "Elvis: That's the Way It Is" (covering his August 1970 Las Vegas engagement) and "Elvis on Tour" (recording his 1972 nationwide tour), as well as unreleased 8mm film and unheard audio of Elvis discussing his career. This film centers on the legendary Las Vegas shows and iconic performances from the nationwide tour, restoring countless precious images over more than two years using state-of-the-art restoration/remastering technology. Using over 70 songs including hits like "Can't Help Falling in Love" and "Suspicious Minds" as well as rare performances like "Oh Happy Day," it synchronizes Elvis's overwhelming vocals with his own words, delicately and boldly reconstructing the footage for an immersive cinematic experience.

title:EPiC／エピック エルヴィス・プレスリー・イン・コンサート: An overwhelming 97-minute immersive experience that invites you to a stage where a superstar poured out his heart and soul! The film’s opening races through the first half of Elvis’s life—from his childhood and his debut performances met with high-pitched screams to his television appearances and his time in the service—utilizing abundant footage from his starring roles in films like *G.I. Blues* and *Blue Hawaii*. Accompanied by his own voice reflecting on his musical awakening and his true feelings about his film career, the experience is, in essence, Elvis telling the story of his own life. Then, putting an end to his Hollywood era, Elvis makes his comeback to the stage, fueled by a burning passion for the music he loves. Centered on his 1970 and 1972 Las Vegas residency performances, rehearsals, and press conferences, the narrative of Elvis’s life continues, interweaving footage from his 1970 and 1972 US tours and personal home videos from Graceland.
title:Easy Rider: A quintessential work of American New Cinema, depicting two hippies who hide a large sum of money from marijuana sales in a gas tank and set off on a motorcycle road trip in search of the true America. Originally conceived as a modern Western with horses replaced by motorcycles, what it ultimately portrays is drug culture, intense xenophobia, and the hollow promise of "freedom" in contemporary America.
title:Eddington: From Ari Aster, director of 'Midsommar', and following 'Beau Is Afraid', this thriller stars Joaquin Phoenix and depicts how a local election in a small town locked down during the COVID-19 pandemic escalates into a nationwide crisis. In 2020, the small town of Eddington, New Mexico, USA. Forced into a suffocating quarantine due to the pandemic lockdown, residents' frustration and anxiety are about to explode. Amidst this, town sheriff Joe clashes with ambitious Mayor Ted, who wants to save the town by attracting an IT company, over a minor dispute about wearing masks, and suddenly declares his candidacy for mayor. The fire of Joe and Ted's quarrel spreads, and social media erupts with fake news and hatred. Meanwhile, Joe's wife Louise becomes captivated by the inciting videos of cult leader Vernon, sinking into conspiracy theories. As suspicion, controversy, and rage swirl, violence begets violence, and criticism and conspiracy shroud the truth, the town of Eddington hurtles toward the brink of destruction. Joaquin Phoenix plays Sheriff Joe, Pedro Pascal plays Mayor Ted, Emma Stone plays Joe's wife Louise, and Austin Butler plays cult leader Vernon. Screened in the Competition section of the 78th Cannes Film Festival in 2025.
title:Eleanor the Great: Actress Scarlett Johansson makes her feature directorial debut with this lighthearted drama about the friendship between a powerful elderly woman and a motherless student, sparked by a lie, set against the backdrop of her own Jewish cultural roots. Based on a script by first-time feature screenwriter Tory Kamen, drawing on her own grandmother's and family history, Johansson directs with humor and wit. Eleanor, an elderly woman living in New York, feels a void after losing her longtime friend Bessie. One day, intending to attend a tea party, she accidentally wanders into a support group for Holocaust survivors. There, she improvises a story about Bessie's life, recounting her Holocaust memories. Inspired by the dramatic story, journalism student Nina approaches Eleanor, and a new friendship blossoms. But Eleanor's lie takes on a life of its own, sparking a major uproar. June Squibb ("Thelma") plays the unconventional Eleanor, and Erin Kellyman ("Solo: A Star Wars Story") plays Nina. Rita Zohar, herself a Holocaust survivor, plays Eleanor's late friend Bessie.
title:Eno: Brian Eno is a legendary artist who has continuously embodied the very concept of "innovation" in music and art. As a musician, producer, visual artist, and activist, he has remained ahead of his time in every field—a truly unparalleled presence who has presented a clear vision for over 50 years. Now, *Eno*, the world’s first fully generative documentary that delves into the essence of the man himself, arrives in Japan. Directed by Gary Hustwit, the film combines extensive interviews with Brian Eno and over 500 hours of rare archival footage, utilizing "Brain One" (an anagram of Brian Eno), an automated generation system co-developed with artist Brendan Dawes. This groundbreaking work defies cinematic conventions to create a completely new experience where the structure and content change with every screening. Just like the ever-evolving Eno, do not miss this once-in-a-lifetime viewing experience!

title:Eric Clapton: Across 24 Nights: A selection of the best performances from Eric Clapton's 42 concerts at London's Royal Albert Hall in the early 1990s, screened on the big screen. Clapton's 18 concerts at the venue in January-February 1990 were monumental, featuring various elaborate arrangements from a four-piece band to a 13-piece ensemble with a horn section, and collaborations with an orchestra. Furthermore, in February-March of the following year, 1991, he successfully completed 24 consecutive performances, including a blues night with guests Albert Collins and Buddy Guy, and evenings featuring the Royal Philharmonic Orchestra conducted by Michael Kamen. A total of 17 songs, including 13 previously unreleased tracks, are revived on screen with supreme sound and 4K imagery, including an orchestral prologue based on the classic "Layla." Directed by David Barnard, director of "Eric Clapton: Lockdown Sessions."
title:Erica: A psycho-horror film self-remade by director Taro Miyaoka, known for "The Fallen" and "Last Summer Wars," based on his own independent film "Chain"—which won the Special Jury Prize at the 21st Tokyo Student Film Festival—after more than 15 years. Exploring the boundary between love and obsession, it thrillingly depicts human madness. Tatsuki, a 23-year-old who has never had a girlfriend, meets Erica, a beautiful woman working at a café, and is captivated by her kindness. Their relationship deepens, but Erica's suggestive words and actions, along with inexplicable events around Tatsuki, gradually cast an unsettling shadow over his daily life. Eventually, Erica's abnormal obsession and madness are revealed, dragging Tatsuki into an inescapable fate. Starring Ayumu Mochizuki, who rose to fame with the two-part film "Solomon's Perjury." The heroine Erica is played by Mei Hayashi, who has worked as a model since elementary school and made her acting debut in the 2024 drama "Goodbye, Teacher." The cast also includes Hayato Takao, Kurea Hatsuki, Moeka Koizumi, and Itsuki Fujiwara. The screenplay was written by Tete Inoue of "Initiation Love."

title:Eu e Meu Avô Nihonjin: An animated film based on the novel 'Nihonjin' by Oscar Nakazato, which won the 'Jabuti Prize' in 2012, the most prestigious literary award in Brazil's publishing world, depicting the rich human drama of three generations of Japanese immigrants living in Brazil. Inspired by the visual world of contemporary artist Oscar Oiwa, who expresses sweeping, allegorical perspectives with meticulous detail, it was brought to the screen by the Brazilian animation studio PINGUIM CONTENT. Noboru, a 10-year-old boy who is a third-generation Japanese-Brazilian, is given a school assignment to research his cultural identity and visits his grandfather Hideo. The taciturn Hideo has avoided confronting his past, but begins to tell his life story to Noboru. In the 1920s, 20-year-old Hideo arrived in Brazil after a two-month voyage and struggled daily on an unfamiliar coffee plantation. As Noboru delves deeper into his family's history, he learns of an uncle, Haruo, whom he has never met. Ken Kaneko, a painter and first-generation Japanese immigrant from Yokohama, voices the grandfather Hideo, and Pietro Takeda, an 11-year-old with several years of voice acting experience, voices the grandson Noboru.

title:Eureka: Directed by Kiyoshi Aoyama of 'Helpless,' this human drama depicts the journey of recovery for people traumatized by a bus-jacking incident. It won the FIPRESCI Prize and the Ecumenical Jury Prize at the 53rd Cannes International Film Festival in 2000. A bus-jacking occurs in a regional city in Kyushu, and many passengers are killed. The only survivors are the driver, Sawai, and two siblings: junior high school student Naoki and elementary school student Kozue. All three are deeply scarred. Two years later, Sawai, who had disappeared leaving his family behind, returns to town. Around the same time, a series of murders occur in the area, and suspicion falls on Sawai. Learning that the siblings are living alone, Sawai visits their home and begins living with them. Joined by the siblings' cousin, Akihiko, the four set out on a journey in a bus driven by Sawai... Kōji Yakusho plays Sawai, while real-life siblings Shō Miyazaki and Aoi Miyazaki play Naoki and Kozue. Following director Kiyoshi Aoyama's death in March 2022, a digital master complete version was released in theaters that May as a memorial screening.
title:Eva: Bestselling author Tyvian Jones is living a leisurely life in Venice, Italy. But his life is turned upside down when he unexpectedly meets the bewitching French woman Eva Olivier. Despite being already engaged to Francesca Ferrara, he loses his heart to Eva at first sight. However, winning Eva's love is no easy task—she is more interested in money than love. Still, Tyvian cannot let go of his obsession, pursuing Eva with a passion that threatens to destroy his life.
title:Evil Does Not Exist: In Mizuhiki Town, Nagano Prefecture, blessed with abundant nature. Takumi and his only daughter Hana have lived modestly there for generations, but one day a plan emerges to build a glamping site nearby, and its repercussions gradually reach their lives. A feature film born alongside "GIFT," a silent live concert film by Eiko Ishibashi, who composed the music for "Drive My Car." Winner of the Silver Lion (Grand Jury Prize) at the 80th Venice International Film Festival.
title:Ex Libris – The New York Public Li: A documentary by director Frederick Wiseman capturing the behind-the-scenes world of the New York Public Library, one of the world's greatest temples of knowledge and a dream destination for librarians everywhere. The New York Public Library, boasting a collection of 60 million items in its main Beaux-Arts building from the early 19th century and 92 branches, is also known for its thorough service to local residents and researchers. Wiseman, a documentary master who received an Academy Honorary Award in 2016, handled direction, sound, editing, and production, recording the librarians and volunteers working with pride and love for the materials and activities, as well as the behind-the-scenes areas tourists never see. By showing why the library is the most famous in the world, the film illuminates what the public sphere means and what democracy supporting American society is. Numerous celebrities appear, including Dr. Richard Dawkins, Elvis Costello, and Patti Smith. Winner of the International Critics' Week Award at the 74th Venice International Film Festival.
