title:Exist Within: A Korean suspense thriller about floor noise and a cult religion, depicting the fate of a female writer who strives to uncover the truth behind the noise coming from the upstairs neighbor. Eun-su, an aspiring writer living in apartment 401, has been applying to numerous writing contests but faces a string of rejections. Meanwhile, for about a month, she has been tormented by unbearable noise coming from unit 501 above. Deciding to use this situation as material for her work, Eun-su, along with her friend Ji-seong, begins observing Ho-gyeong, a middle-aged man living in 501. Even after he notices her excessive stalking, she relentlessly pursues him for the sake of her writing. Eventually, Eun-su arrives at a shocking truth hidden behind the noise, but at the same time, she finds herself backed into a dangerous situation. Director Kim Jeong-uk, who has crafted many stories candidly depicting the human psyche, portrays with intense suspense the psychological anxiety born from trivial troubles lurking in daily life. Ryu Hwa-young, known as a former member of the K-pop group T-ARA, stars in her first lead film role, passionately playing Eun-su, a writer whose obsession with writing blurs the line between reality and delusion. Veteran actor Park Jin-woo, known for the Netflix drama "Squid Game," plays the mysterious upstairs resident Ho-gyeong.
title:FEVER ビーバー！: A unique action-entertainment spectacle depicting a life-or-death struggle between a hunter and countless mascot-suit beavers in a surreal black-and-white world, garnering acclaim at fantastic film festivals worldwide. After losing his job as an apple cider salesman, a man turns to hunting forest animals. When he meets the woman of his destiny at a fur trading post, he realizes he needs hundreds of beaver pelts to win her father’s approval for their courtship. The hunter sets various traps to catch his prey, but the beavers aren't about to go down without a fight. Set against the backdrop of a sub-zero forest, the curtain rises on an epic battle between the hunter and an army of beavers. Directed, written, and produced by Mike Cheslik, who is also a prominent YouTuber with over 1.6 million subscribers.
title:FRIDAY: A music documentary chronicling a legendary live house with a 40-year history in Chojamachi, Naka-ku, Yokohama. Tucked away on the third floor of a multi-tenant building, "FRIDAY" is a venue with a capacity of only 50 seats. It is widely known as the home base for Crazy Ken Band, who have performed there since their days of obscurity and continue to hold monthly shows there even after their major breakthrough. Managed by its 80-year-old proprietor, Junichi Isohara, the club has long been beloved by a roster of illustrious musicians, including George Yanagi, Ryudo Uzaki, Crystal King, and Haruo Chikada. Centered on interviews and live footage of artists who adore the venue and its master—such as Ken Yokoyama, Show, Hiroaki Yamazaki, Monsieur Yoshizaki, Haruo Chikada, Ryudo Uzaki, and Aya Nakano—this film explores the enduring allure of FRIDAY and Junichi Isohara. The documentary is directed by Shikai Kyodai, whose previous works include "Ima o Ureu Kimi mo Haru ni Nareba" and "Boku to, Kare to."
title:FUJIKO: Set in Shizuoka during the 1970s and 80s, this human drama portrays a single mother navigating a turbulent era, searching for her own way to live while walking forward with strength. In 1977, during a fierce storm that causes a blackout at the hospital, Fujiko gives birth to her daughter Mari. But her joy as a new mother is short-lived; she suffers unreasonable treatment from her husband's family, and her infant daughter Mari is taken away by her mother-in-law and sister-in-law. With the help of her own mother Chiyo, Fujiko manages to get Mari back and, defying opposition from those around her, decides to raise Mari as a single mother. Buffeted by the waves of the times, she refuses to be defeated by society, seeks freedom, and desperately fights to survive with the support of those around her. Yuki Katayama ('The Burning of the Crimson') stars as Fujiko. YOU plays the spiteful mother-in-law Toshiko, Lily Franky plays Sasaki, whom Fujiko meets through her insurance sales job, Tsuyoshi Ujiki plays Fujiko's ailing father, Keiko Takeshita plays Hatayama, the director of the daycare center Fujiko turns to, Issey Ogata plays Oishi, an old friend of Fujiko's father who runs a soba shop, Kayoko Kishimoto plays Fujiko's mother Chiyo, and MEGUMI plays Nagura, the owner of the coffee shop where Fujiko works. Directed and based on an original story by Taichi Kimura, who has directed numerous music videos and commercials and gained attention with his 2023 feature debut 'AFTERGLOWS'. MEGUMI handled planning and production.
title:Fallen Angels: Director Wong Kar-wai of 'Chungking Express' crafts a pop-infused ensemble drama about the poignant romantic entanglements of five men and women in the neon-lit streets of Hong Kong. This film completes an episode originally planned as part of 'Chungking Express' as an independent work. A lonely hitman and the woman who acts as his agent. Their rule is to keep personal feelings out of work, but their relationship begins to waver. Meanwhile, a mute young man named Mo sneaks into other people's shops every night and runs them without permission. One day, Mo meets a woman who has just been heartbroken and falls for her. The hitman is played by Leon Lai of 'The City of Sadness,' the agent by Michelle Lee of 'Flowers of Shanghai,' and Mo by Takeshi Kaneshiro of 'Chungking Express.' Cinematography is by Christopher Doyle, who worked on many of Wong Kar-wai's films. First released in Japan in 1996. In 2022, a 4K restored version was screened as part of 'WKW4K' (from August 19, 2022, at Cine Mart Shinjuku, Grand Cinema Sunshine, Cinema City, etc.).
title:Falling Angels: Set in Shinjuku's Kabukicho, this film portrays two girls working at a girls' bar alongside women from various backgrounds. As they continue to sell their youth and perform the roles demanded of them, they gradually lose sight of what they truly want. The film won the Movie.com Award at the 18th Tanabe Benkei Film Festival, a gateway for new directors. Naru, 19, starts working at a girls' bar after high school to leave her parents' home. Maria, 21, works at the same bar while attending university to repay her student loans. Bathed in the neon lights of the night town, Naru wishes to become someone special, while Maria longs to be a normal college student. One day, Naru meets a host on the streets of Kabukicho, and Maria is approached by a customer for an off-the-books deal. The director and screenwriter is Naima Kimura, for whom this is her second directorial work and first feature film. Kimura drew inspiration from her own experience working at a girls' bar as a student. The film was screened in theaters as part of the "Tanabe Benkei Film Festival Selection 2024" (May 9–June 5, 2024 at Theatre Shinjuku; June 20–26, 2024 at Theatre Umeda).
title:Farewell My Concubine: An epic saga depicting the tumultuous lives of two Peking opera actors, this was the first Chinese-language film to win the Palme d'Or at the Cannes Film Festival. It portrays the love, hatred, and lives of two Peking opera performers who play the classic 'Farewell My Concubine,' set against the backdrop of China's turbulent history from 1925 under the Nationalist government through the Cultural Revolution and into the late 1970s. Directed by Chen Kaige, who gained attention with his debut 'Yellow Earth' and became a leading figure of China's Fifth Generation directors with this film's success. In 1925 Beijing, Douzi, abandoned by his prostitute mother, is sent to a Peking opera training school. Shitou protects him like a younger brother and becomes his strong support through harsh training. As they grow up, they become major stars in the Peking opera world... Leslie Cheung plays Cheng Dieyi, a male dan actor who clings to love despite being tossed by the times, and Gong Li appears as a high-class courtesan who becomes his love rival. A 4K version was released in 2023, marking the 30th anniversary of the film's production and 20 years after Leslie Cheung's death.
title:Fargo: An unconventional crime suspense film by the Coen Brothers, laced with black humor. In snow-covered Fargo, Minnesota, car salesman Jerry, drowning in debt, plots to have his wife Jean kidnapped to extort a ransom from her wealthy father. But when the two hired kidnappers shoot a police officer and a witness, the case spirals out of control. Winner of multiple film awards, including the Academy Awards for Best Original Screenplay and Best Actress.
title:Film Socialisme: A visual poem by French master Jean-Luc Godard, depicting modern Europe with overwhelming visual beauty and masterful editing. It is Godard's first feature film shot entirely in digital, his first in six years since 'Our Music.' Set on a luxury cruise ship touring the Mediterranean, it consists of three movements: the first movement 'Such Things' depicts human drama over gold lost during the Spanish Civil War; the second movement 'Where to, Europe' is a political comedy about a family living in the French countryside; and the third movement 'We Humans' explores history and culture across six locations related to human history, using countless quotations and collages. Utilizing various video formats and freely incorporating images, words, sounds, and even digital noise, it is depicted with overwhelming density and speed, full of rebellious spirit. Musician Patti Smith, guitarist Lenny Kaye, and philosopher Alain Badiou appear as themselves. Screened as part of the special screening series 'Jean-Luc Godard in the 21st Century: Our Films 2001-2010' (starting June 20, 2026, at Theater Image Forum Shibuya and other locations nationwide).
title:Fires on the Plain: An anti-war film adapted from Shōhei Ōoka's novel of the same name, scripted by Kazuo Wada and directed by Kon Ichikawa. Abandoned by both the hospital and his unit, Tamura wanders the island of Leyte on the Philippine front. He reunites with fellow retreating soldiers in front of a hospital, but when the hospital comes under shelling, Tamura flees alone. With no food and having lost his comrades, Tamura survives by eating grass. Eventually he reunites with his former comrades Nagamatsu and Yasuda, who had been separated from him. The two call the soldiers they killed 'monkeys' and have been eating their flesh...
title:Fireworks, Should We See It from t: Summer vacation. Norimichi, an elementary school student, is invited by his classmate Nazuna—who is set to transfer schools after the summer due to her parents' divorce—to go to the fireworks festival with her that night. However, Nazuna is planning to run away from home, and Norimichi finds himself being dragged along. Meanwhile, Norimichi's friends, including Junichi, have decided to go to the festival to see for themselves whether fireworks look round or flat when viewed from the side. Nazuna remains determined to carry out her plan to run away.
title:Fish Story: Directed by Yoshihiro Nakamura, who helmed the film adaptation of Kotaro Isaka's "A Duck and a Coin Locker," this film adapts another of Isaka's short stories of the same name. It's an ensemble drama depicting how a song that received almost no attention upon its release transcends time to save the world from extinction. In the 1970s, the ahead-of-its-time punk band "Gekirin" disbanded, leaving behind the song "FISH STORY," which was not understood by the world. Years later, in the 1980s, a timid college student who happens upon the record takes desperate action to save a woman attacked by thugs. Further in time, in the 2000s, a ferry cook aspiring to be a hero saves a high school student caught up in a sea-jacking during a school trip. And in 2012, as humanity faces extinction from a comet collision, a record shop owner also holds "FISH STORY" in his hands. Ito Atsushi and Kora Kengo play the members of the band "Gekirin," Hamada Gaku plays the timid college student, Tabe Mikako plays the high school student caught in the sea-jacking, Moriyama Mirai plays the cook, and Omori Nao plays the record shop owner. The screenplay is by Tamio Hayashi, who later worked with Nakamura on "Golden Slumber." Music production was handled by Kazuyoshi Saito. In 2026, 17 years after its 2009 release, it will be digitally re-released.
title:Five Graves to Cairo: A rare action thriller from Billy Wilder, depicting British soldiers fighting to survive. After the British army suffers defeat at the hands of Rommel's German forces, Corporal Bramble, who escaped death, disguises himself as a hotel waiter who died the previous day and attempts to make contact with German soldiers. Fortunately, the deceased waiter was a German spy, allowing him to leak classified information to the Allies. Erich von Stroheim, a director Wilder had long admired, appears in the role of a general.
title:Flames of Blood: The turbulent life of gambler Senkichi, who continues to love one woman. Set in Kyoto at the end of the Edo period, this powerful portrayal of unadorned love between a man and a woman stands as Tai Kato's final, crowning live-action film.
title:Flowers of Mold: An unconventional romance film starring Kim Jae-kyung, former leader of the South Korean girl group RAINBOW who now works as an actress. Based on the short story 'Flowers of Mold' by Ha Seong-nan, an award-winning author in Korean literary circles, the film depicts a woman who tries to understand others through 'trash,' the most private and defenseless traces of a person. Ji-su, who carries deep romantic trauma, secretly collects and files away other people's trash, believing that 'one's true self appears in what they throw away.' One day, she finds a trash bag that has been carefully sorted and discarded, and upon discovering it belongs to her neighbor, a man named U-je, she approaches him using fragmentary information gleaned from the trash. The two gradually open their hearts to each other, but one night, U-je witnesses Ji-su entering her apartment with a trash bag and discovers her secret. Kim Jae-kyung passionately portrays the protagonist Ji-su, who cannot trust others due to past relationship experiences, with Hyun-woo from the TV drama 'Law School' co-starring as the neighbor U-je. Directed by Sim Hye-jung, who gained attention for her previous work 'A Bedsore,' the film won the CGV Award and the Watcha's Pick Feature Film Award at the Jeonju International Film Festival 2023.
title:Forte フォルテ: A music horror film by director Gimbo Kim, known for numerous music videos and short films. Set in the music industry, it depicts a young person possessed by the desire for success and obsession with creation. Yeong-ji, who moved to the city believing in her musical talent, is hired by the composing studio "Forte," which she had admired. However, the actual work turns out to be behind-the-scenes labor as a "ghost composer" whose name never appears publicly. While working with a sense of suffocation, the mysterious death of a colleague reveals unsettling rumors about the studio and the existence of a "cursed grand piano." Yeong-ji, who has been continuously suppressed, gradually becomes consumed by obsession and madness for creation. Officially invited to the 27th Bucheon International Fantastic Film Festival and the 2024 Busan International Film Festival. Released theatrically as part of the "Hangeul New Wave Film Festival 2026," a special screening of Korean indie genre films.
title:Four Nights of a Dreamer: Jacques, an aspiring painter, saves a young woman named Marthe from throwing herself into the Seine one night. She had a lover who left for America a year ago, and that very night was when they had promised to reunite. Jacques finds her, sunk in anguish, beautiful. Driven by a fierce impulse of love, he forces himself to remain calm, hoping her heart will drift away from her lover, while feeling guilt over this. Like the 1957 version, this is a modern adaptation of Dostoevsky's famous tragic love story, a poignant work revealing Bresson's awakened worldview. Visconti's romanticism is absent here; the young man's blind love is brutally exposed as he pours out his feelings into a mini tape recorder, a habit of his, making it painful to watch.
title:Four Trails: The Hong Kong Four Trails Ultra Challenge, commonly known as HK4TUC, requires runners to consecutively complete four trail courses in Hong Kong and reach the finish line within a time limit of 72 hours (3 days). The total course length is 298 km, comparable to the distance between Tokyo and Nagoya, with a cumulative elevation gain of 14,500 m, equivalent to seven full marathons or two ascents of Mount Everest. Furthermore, participants must procure their own water and food from shops along the way, and strict rules prohibit the use of poles or portable music players, which would be advantageous on the undulating mountain paths. It is an event of extreme physical and mental challenge. This film captures 18 runners who took on the HK4TUC pushing their limits, set against the beautiful natural landscapes of Hong Kong, rarely seen before. The director is Robin Lee, a British director born and raised in Hong Kong. The film began a limited release in Hong Kong at the end of 2024, but word-of-mouth spread rapidly and the number of screens increased sharply. It gained further attention when the major star Chow Yun-fat, known for the 'A Better Tomorrow' series and 'Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon', highly praised it, saying 'every Hong Kong person should watch it'. Supported not only by sports enthusiasts but also by general film fans, it became the biggest surprise hit of 2025, attracting 150,000 viewers. Additionally, it has won numerous awards, including the Best New Director Award at the 43rd Hong Kong Film Awards, the Audience Award at the 22nd Hong Kong Asian Film Festival, the Recommended Film Award at the 31st Hong Kong Film Critics Society Awards, and the Jury Special Award at the 2025 Hong Kong Directors' Guild Awards, earning high praise as a documentary.
title:Fragments of the Last Will: A biographical drama starring Kazunari Ninomiya as real-life Japanese prisoner of war Yamamoto Hanao, held in a Siberian labor camp (Laguerre). Based on Jun Henmi's nonfiction novel "The Last Letter from the Laguerre," directed by Takahisa Zeze, known for "Those Who Were Not Protected" and "The Thread." In 1945, after World War II, Japanese POWs in Siberian camps faced brutal conditions—temperatures dropping to -40°C, minimal food, and forced heavy labor, with many dying. Amid this, Yamamoto Hanao believes he will return to his wife and children in Japan, encouraging those around him. His selfless actions and strong faith ignite a flame of hope in many prisoners' hearts. Kitagawa Keiko plays Yamamoto's wife Mojimi, with a star-studded cast including Matsuzaka Tori, Nakajima Kento, Kiryū Kentarō, and Yasuda Ken as fellow prisoners.
title:Frankie Freako: From Steven Kostanski, the mad genius director of "Psycho Goreman" (2020) and member of Canada's notorious effects collective Astron-6, who has contributed special effects to Hollywood blockbusters like "Resident Evil: Retribution" (2012) and "Pacific Rim" (2013). His two latest films, "Frankie Freako" and "Deathstalker," will be released sequentially in Japan starting July 3rd at Cinemart Shinjuku and other theaters nationwide. Kostanski, who wrote and directed both films, is known for his unique creature designs reminiscent of classics like "E.T." (1982), "Gremlins" (1984), and "The Goonies" (1985), blending 80s-style monster panic with absurdist black humor, creating a devoted fanbase. These new films bring his signature style to Japan. "Frankie Freako" is a monster freak comedy that extensively uses unique puppets to achieve a visual style straight out of a comic book, bursting with Kostanski's unique worldview. The cast includes fellow Astron-6 members Conor Sweeney and Adam Brooks. Synopsis: Connor, a workaholic, has a dilemma: he is respected by neither his boss, his colleagues, nor his wife. One night, he sees a commercial on a shady late-night show for a party hosted by Frankie Freako and impulsively calls the number. Suddenly, a goblin-like creature named Frankie and his troublesome friends invade his home, trashing the place. Connor struggles to stop Frankie and the rampaging monsters. However, this chaos unexpectedly leads him on a journey of self-discovery.
title:Frankie the Milkman: A cheerful young man moves to Tokyo to help at a relative's milk shop and struggles to outdo his business rivals. A film adaptation of a popular radio drama, this is an early representative work of Frankie Sakai, known as a hidden gem of slapstick comedy.
title:Fujiko: Set in Shizuoka during the 1970s and 80s, this human drama portrays a single mother navigating a turbulent era, searching for her own way to live while walking forward with strength. In 1977, during a fierce storm that causes a blackout at the hospital, Fujiko gives birth to her daughter Mari. But her joy as a new mother is short-lived; she suffers unreasonable treatment from her husband's family, and her infant daughter Mari is taken away by her mother-in-law and sister-in-law. With the help of her own mother Chiyo, Fujiko manages to get Mari back and, defying opposition from those around her, decides to raise Mari as a single mother. Buffeted by the waves of the times, she refuses to be defeated by society, seeks freedom, and desperately fights to survive with the support of those around her. Yuki Katayama ('The Burning of the Crimson') stars as Fujiko. YOU plays the spiteful mother-in-law Toshiko, Lily Franky plays Sasaki, whom Fujiko meets through her insurance sales job, Tsuyoshi Ujiki plays Fujiko's ailing father, Keiko Takeshita plays Hatayama, the director of the daycare center Fujiko turns to, Issey Ogata plays Oishi, an old friend of Fujiko's father who runs a soba shop, Kayoko Kishimoto plays Fujiko's mother Chiyo, and MEGUMI plays Nagura, the owner of the coffee shop where Fujiko works. Directed and based on an original story by Taichi Kimura, who has directed numerous music videos and commercials and gained attention with his 2023 feature debut 'AFTERGLOWS'. MEGUMI handled planning and production.
title:Full Moon in Paris: The fourth film in Éric Rohmer's 'Comedies and Proverbs' series. Louise, an interior designer, lives with her architect boyfriend Rémi in a suburban Paris apartment. The serious Rémi and the free-spirited Louise are constantly bickering. Feeling stifled in her life with Rémi, Louise rents her own room in Paris and starts going out with her married best friend Octave... The film delicately portrays a woman's emotions as she wavers between two men and two homes. Lead actress Pascale Ogier won the Best Actress award at the Venice Film Festival for this role, but tragically died shortly after at the young age of 25. The cast also includes Fabrice Luchini from 'Claire's Knee' and Tchéky Karyo from 'Nikita.'
title:G.I. Samurai: Led by Lieutenant Yoshiaki Iba, 21 members of the Japan Ground Self-Defense Force, armed with modern weapons, suddenly time-slip along with their supply depot to the Sengoku period while en route to an exercise. As they stand bewildered, Nagao Heizo Kagetora arrives with his retainers to meet them. Upon first seeing Iba, Kagetora takes an instant liking to him, calling him "a kindred spirit," and is drawn to their unfamiliar clothing and weapons, hoping to recruit them. Iba and his soldiers struggle to accept the reality of their time slip. However, after encountering Kagetora and being attacked by guerrilla forces of a rival feudal lord—resulting in a comrade's death—and witnessing Kagetora's battle firsthand, they are forced to come to terms with having arrived in the Sengoku period.
title:GEMNIBUS vol.2: The second installment of "GEMNIBUS," an omnibus film featuring up-and-coming directors, created as part of Toho's talent support project "GEMSTONE Creative Label." The collection consists of six films: "Blue Bird," a road movie by photographer and director Sara Masuda, who explores her own impulses and struggles with the act of "capturing images" through overwhelming visual beauty set against the vast nature of Hokkaido; "Influencer Ghost," a stylish creature horror film by director Masaki Nishiyama (noted for his short "Sumahora!") who teams up with Shoichiro Sato, a VFX artist for "Godzilla Minus One"; "The Faceless City," an SF psychological horror by director Riko Murakami (of "MIRRORLIAR FILMS") that vividly depicts a near-future dystopia based on the Grand Prize winner of the "Toho x World Maker Short Film Contest" co-hosted by Shueisha’s "Shonen Jump+" and Toho; "Sonic Beat," a youth story by director Shunta Seki (highly acclaimed for his graduation film "Bowl Meets Girl") who mirrors his own journey into his first commercial work through a protagonist in a high school track club; "You Cannot Be Serious!", a comedy by award-winning director Satsuki Okawa that portrays the struggles of a woman with an unexpected pregnancy in a realistic yet pop style; and "If We Are to Be Born," an animated work by director Asuka Dokai that uses the theme of "ten months and ten days" to fantastically chronicle twins waking up on a mysterious planet and embarking on a journey to meet the mother they have never seen.
title:GO: High school senior Sugihara has South Korean nationality, but usually doesn't think about it. He starts dating a girl named Sakurai and thinks he must confess his nationality to her someday, when a tragedy befalls a close friend of the same nationality. Based on the Naoki Prize-winning novel "GO" by Kinichi Kaneshiro. Directed by Isao Yukisada, who won the International Critics' Award at the previous year's Busan Film Festival for "Himawari." Screenplay by Kankuro Kudo of the TV series "Ikebukuro West Gate Park." Co-starring popular young actors including Yosuke Kubozuka from that show and Ko Shibasaki from "Battle Royale."
title:GOOD BOY／グッド・ボーイ: 'Something is wrong...' The one who notices the anomaly is not a human, but a pet dog named Indie. Staring intently at a corner of an empty room. Barking in response to something. The fear that lies beyond these mysterious behaviors of pet dogs, which everyone can relate to, is depicted by director Ben Leonberg in his feature debut, after a three-year production period. It premiered at SXSW (South by Southwest Film Festival) in 2025 and won the Best Dog Acting Award. It garnered attention as an innovative horror film told from a dog's perspective, and as soon as the trailer was released, it became a hot topic on social media. Originally scheduled for a limited release, it was hastily expanded to 1,650 screens and achieved a 90% rating on Rotten Tomatoes. Praised as 'one of the most moving horror films of 2025', it made the US top 10 for two consecutive weeks. At the 2026 Astra Film Awards in the 'Horror or Thriller' category, Indie (the dog), the star of this film, achieved the historic feat of winning the Best Performance Award for an animal actor, defeating a stellar lineup including Alfie Williams ('28 Years Later'), Ethan Hawke ('The Black Phone 2'), and Alison Brie ('Together'). Indie is a retriever dog living with his owner Todd in an apartment. Recently, Todd's health has been poor, and one day he vomits blood. Todd's sister Vera, who happens to visit the apartment, rushes him to the hospital. After being discharged, Todd takes Indie and moves into his grandfather's house, which has been vacant since his grandfather's mysterious death. Todd borrows a backup generator from a neighbor and spends his time with a little light and watching old home videos of his grandfather, but Indie senses something strange in the house. On the phone with Vera, Todd wonders if there is a curse on the house and his grandfather. Of course, Indie doesn't understand, but he feels something is wrong, hears strange noises, and senses a shadow drifting from the corner of the room. The evil presence worsens Todd's condition, and Indie desperately tries to protect Todd from the eerie something...
title:GO（2001）: High school senior Sugihara has South Korean nationality, but usually doesn't think about it. He starts dating a girl named Sakurai and thinks he must confess his nationality to her someday, when a tragedy befalls a close friend of the same nationality. Based on the Naoki Prize-winning novel "GO" by Kinichi Kaneshiro. Directed by Isao Yukisada, who won the International Critics' Award at the previous year's Busan Film Festival for "Himawari." Screenplay by Kankuro Kudo of the TV series "Ikebukuro West Gate Park." Co-starring popular young actors including Yosuke Kubozuka from that show and Ko Shibasaki from "Battle Royale."
title:GRIT バレーボール男子日本代表 栄光への始発点: A documentary film documenting the 2025 challenge of the Japan Men's National Volleyball Team. Despite their valiant efforts at the 2025 World Volleyball Championship—the culmination of the 2025 season—the team failed to reach the final tournament and was eliminated in the preliminary round. This film follows the team closely throughout the season, from the national team call-up in May
title:Ga, Ga. Chwała bohaterom: One of four dark sci-fi works by Piotr Szulkin, a pioneer of dystopian science fiction in Poland, created under the strict censorship of the socialist regime in the late 1970s and 1980s. With a style blending fierce satire and extreme surrealism, the film depicts the miserable existence of people living under corrupt power and bureaucracy. A man trapped on a giant space station is forced, like other prisoners, to volunteer for exploration of a distant planet. Landing on Planet Australia 458, he is welcomed as a hero, but soon realizes that freedom comes at a high price. His violent life is broadcast live for the entertainment of the planet's inhabitants. The film had its Japanese theatrical premiere in 2026 as part of the special screening series "Polish Dark Sci-Fi: The End of Civilization Tetralogy" (starting February 21, 2026, at Theater Image Forum).
title:Ga-ga: Glory to the Heroes: One of four dark sci-fi works by Piotr Szulkin, a pioneer of dystopian science fiction in Poland, created under the strict censorship of the socialist regime in the late 1970s and 1980s. With a style blending fierce satire and extreme surrealism, the film depicts the miserable existence of people living under corrupt power and bureaucracy. A man trapped on a giant space station is forced, like other prisoners, to volunteer for exploration of a distant planet. Landing on Planet Australia 458, he is welcomed as a hero, but soon realizes that freedom comes at a high price. His violent life is broadcast live for the entertainment of the planet's inhabitants. The film had its Japanese theatrical premiere in 2026 as part of the special screening series "Polish Dark Sci-Fi: The End of Civilization Tetralogy" (starting February 21, 2026, at Theater Image Forum).
title:Galaxy Express 999: The Movie: The first theatrical film in the classic sci-fi anime series "Galaxy Express 999," based on Leiji Matsumoto's manga of the same name. Based on the "Andromeda Arc" from the original manga, it features character designs different from the TV series. In a future where humans can achieve eternal life by replacing their bodies with machines, the mechanical bodies are expensive and unaffordable for the poor. Rumors spread that riding the Galaxy Express 999 can take you to a planet where you can get a free mechanical body. The boy Tetsurō Hoshino heads to the metropolis Megalopolis, where the 999 stops, with his mother, but they are attacked by the Mechanical Count's human hunt, and his mother is killed. Living in the slums of Megalopolis, Tetsurō one day receives a pass for the 999 from the mysterious beauty Maetel and embarks on a journey into space with her. The theme song by Godiego was also a huge hit.
title:Game of Seduction: An erotic film directed by Roger Vadim, based on the sensual novel 'Les Liaisons Dangereuses'. Set in 19th-century France, it depicts the affair between a playboy count and a married woman. The bewitching performances of two charismatic actresses are captivating.
title:Gattaca: A sci-fi suspense film starring Ethan Hawke, Uma Thurman, and Jude Law. In a near future where 'valids' born through genetic engineering dominate society, Vincent, born naturally, lives a life of discrimination as an 'invalid.' He has dreamed of becoming an astronaut since childhood, but it is a profession only permitted for valids. One day, through a DNA broker, Vincent purchases the valid identity of Jerome, a former swimmer now paralyzed from the waist down. Posing as Jerome, Vincent joins the space corporation 'Gattaca' and, through sheer effort, is eventually selected as an astronaut for a Titan exploration mission, but... This is the directorial and screenwriting debut of Andrew Niccol.
title:Ghost of Ueno: Set in Ueno Park in Tokyo, this human mystery, a Japan-China-Korea co-production, explores human connections while focusing on "disappearance" as a way of life. A homeless man known as "Gojo" in Ueno has died. No one knows his real name, what he did in life, or why he ended up in a tent in the park. Satsuki, a social worker, with the help of Toshi, a man living in the park after losing his wife, searches through the homeless network to uncover Gojo's identity, using his diary as a clue. Eventually, the existence of a woman comes to light, and it's revealed that Gojo had cut ties with his family. This fact also profoundly shakes Satsuki's own life. Kadowaki Mugi stars as Satsuki, a social worker carrying a certain loss from her own past, and Takenaka Naoto co-stars as Toshi, a homeless man who accompanies Satsuki. The director and screenwriter is Wang Qii, who spent his childhood in Japan and studied filmmaking in the UK. Wayne Wang, known for directing "Smoke" and "The Joy Luck Club," is credited as co-writer and project planner.
title:Gimtinė: Set in Lithuania just after its independence, this drama quietly observes memories, conflicts, and the lives of people caught between shifting eras through the eyes of an American-born boy visiting the country with his Lithuanian mother. Director Tomas Vengris, making his feature-length debut, draws on his own experience growing up as the son of Lithuanian immigrants in Washington, D.C., to delicately portray the reality of people tossed about by changes in territory and political systems. In 1992, mother and son Victoria and Kovas arrive from America to Lithuania, which has just gained independence from the Soviet Union. As a child, Victoria was separated from her family under Soviet occupation and lost her home and land. In Lithuania, where control shifted from Nazi Germany to the Soviet Union, people's freedom continued to waver under different regimes. Returning to her homeland after 20 years, Victoria seeks to reclaim her lost family land and start a new life with her son, but finds a Russian family already living there. Faced with the harsh reality that reclaiming the land is not easy, her ideal of a fresh start in Lithuania begins to quietly unravel. Martas Metlevskis, an American-born actor of Lithuanian descent, plays the boy Kovas, and renowned Lithuanian actress Sevilija Janušauskaitė plays his mother Victoria.
title:Glasses: On a break from life, Taeko visits a southern seaside town and stays at a strange inn called Hamada. However, in a small beach town with nothing to see or do, she is pushed around by the overly laid-back residents and, unable to bear it, leaves Hamada—but... From the director Naoko Ogigami and star Satomi Kobayashi of "Kamome Diner," the hit film about slow-living daily life set in a Japanese restaurant in Finland, comes a gentle portrayal of people re-examining their lives, this time set on a southern beach.
title:Gloaming in Luomu:
Winner of the Best Film Award in the Competition Section of the 30th Busan International Film Festival.

The traces of a lost lover, and a path that recedes the more you search—another time flowing through Luomu, an ancient town in Sichuan Province.

A postcard arrives from Wang, a lover who vanished without a trace three years ago, bearing only the words "Twilight in Luomu." Bai, who worked as a dancer in a theater troupe, follows this single clue to an inn in the ancient town of Luomu, Sichuan. There she meets Liu, the inn's proprietress; Huang, who has harbored feelings for Liu for twenty years; and a stream of passing travelers. In this town, once prosperous from trade and now flowing with quiet time, what she encounters is not Wang himself, but the traces of the time he left behind. The faint sound of a distant whistle echoes, and before Bai, who wanders the ancient town, Wang appears and disappears like a phantom. One day, Bai learns that a man resembling Wang was reportedly seen at a mountain temple—

Released simultaneously with its sister film "Chunshu," shot with the same cast prior to this work.
title:Godai - The Wunderkind: A historical ensemble drama starring Haruma Miura, depicting the life of Tomoatsu Godai, a visionary who built the foundations of modern Japan's economy and was hailed as a 'Tengaramon' (a person of extraordinary talent). Written by Eriko Komatsu and directed by Mitsutoshi Tanaka, the film presents an original story. In the late Edo period, Japan is shocked by Perry's arrival. Young samurai Saisuke Godai (later Tomoatsu), sensing the dawn of a new era, ignores internal conflicts over expulsion or opening of the country and looks to the world. After meeting the courtesan Haru, he is driven by the desire for 'free dreams' and joins forces with Ryoma Sakamoto, Yataro Iwasaki, Hirobumi Ito, and others to build a nation where everyone can dream. Shohei Miura plays Ryoma Sakamoto, Godai's ally; Takanori Nishikawa plays Yataro Iwasaki, who later founded the Mitsubishi conglomerate; Yuki Morinaga plays a young Hirobumi Ito, who becomes the first Prime Minister; and Mei Nagano plays the courtesan Haru.
title:Godzilla: A landmark tokusatsu kaiju film produced and released by Toho in 1954. Ships are sinking one after another in the Pacific Ocean. The few survivors report sightings of a giant monster. An investigation team formed by paleontologist Dr. Yamane, his daughter and assistant Emiko, and her fiancé Hideto Ogata, head of a salvage company, is dispatched to Odo Island near the incident site, where the monster eventually appears. Named "Godzilla" after an old island legend, the monster is believed to be an ancient creature that survived in secret, awakened by the radiation from repeated hydrogen bomb tests, and countermeasures are devised. However, humans are helpless against its immense power, and Godzilla lands in Tokyo, turning the city into a sea of fire. Meanwhile, Dr. Yamane's beloved student, scientist Serizawa, has realized a terrible invention that could be effective against Godzilla. Fearing its future misuse, Serizawa hesitates to use it... A Hollywood version directed by Roland Emmerich was also produced in 1998. To commemorate the 60th anniversary in 2014 and the production/release of the second Hollywood version "GODZILLA" (directed by Gareth Edwards), this original film was revived as the "Godzilla 60th Anniversary Digital Remastered Version."
title:Golden Kamuy: Assault on Abashiri: The second film in the live-action adaptation of Satoru Noda's popular manga "Golden Kamuy," serving as a sequel to the 2024 film and the WOWOW drama series "Golden Kamuy: The Hunt of the Tattooed Prisoners in Hokkaido." Former soldier Saichi Sugimoto, known as "Immortal Sugimoto," learns of a vast gold hoard stolen from the Ainu people. The mysterious culprit, "Noppera-bo," hid the gold before his capture, tattooing the locations on the bodies of prisoners and engineering their escape. The tattoos form a single code when combined across 24 men. Sugimoto meets Ainu girl Asirpa, whose father was killed by the gold thief, and they join forces. Meanwhile, Lieutenant Tsurumi of the Imperial Japanese Army's 7th Division, who aims to conquer Hokkaido, and Toshizo Hijikata, who should have died in the Boshin War, also seek the gold, sparking a fierce battle for the tattooed prisoners. The stage moves to Abashiri Prison, where Noppera-bo is incarcerated. Returning cast members include Kento Yamazaki as Sugimoto and Anna Yamada as Asirpa, with new additions: Yu Inaba as Private Usami of the 7th Division, Sohma Wada as Chief Guard Kadokura, and Jun Kunimura as Navy Rear Admiral Heiji Koido, father of "Satsuma's Prince" Otonoshin Koido. Directed by Kenji Katagiri, who helmed episodes 3 and 5-8 of the drama series.
title:Good Boy: 'Something is wrong...' The one who notices the anomaly is not a human, but a pet dog named Indie. Staring intently at a corner of an empty room. Barking in response to something. The fear that lies beyond these mysterious behaviors of pet dogs, which everyone can relate to, is depicted by director Ben Leonberg in his feature debut, after a three-year production period. It premiered at SXSW (South by Southwest Film Festival) in 2025 and won the Best Dog Acting Award. It garnered attention as an innovative horror film told from a dog's perspective, and as soon as the trailer was released, it became a hot topic on social media. Originally scheduled for a limited release, it was hastily expanded to 1,650 screens and achieved a 90% rating on Rotten Tomatoes. Praised as 'one of the most moving horror films of 2025', it made the US top 10 for two consecutive weeks. At the 2026 Astra Film Awards in the 'Horror or Thriller' category, Indie (the dog), the star of this film, achieved the historic feat of winning the Best Performance Award for an animal actor, defeating a stellar lineup including Alfie Williams ('28 Years Later'), Ethan Hawke ('The Black Phone 2'), and Alison Brie ('Together'). Indie is a retriever dog living with his owner Todd in an apartment. Recently, Todd's health has been poor, and one day he vomits blood. Todd's sister Vera, who happens to visit the apartment, rushes him to the hospital. After being discharged, Todd takes Indie and moves into his grandfather's house, which has been vacant since his grandfather's mysterious death. Todd borrows a backup generator from a neighbor and spends his time with a little light and watching old home videos of his grandfather, but Indie senses something strange in the house. On the phone with Vera, Todd wonders if there is a curse on the house and his grandfather. Of course, Indie doesn't understand, but he feels something is wrong, hears strange noises, and senses a shadow drifting from the corner of the room. The evil presence worsens Todd's condition, and Indie desperately tries to protect Todd from the eerie something...
title:Good Luck: A road movie written and directed by Shin Adachi, known for scripting the NHK morning drama "Boogie Woogie" and films like "Zako-domo yo, Taishi o Idake" and "Theater Version: Still, I Want to Be with My Wife," set in Bungo-Ono, Oita Prefecture, depicting a small journey of a man and woman lost in life. Taro Oyama, approaching 30, calls himself a film director but is actually supported by the woman he lives with. He is selected for a film festival in Oita Prefecture but receives harsh criticism from the female organizer. The next day, heartbroken, Taro heads to neighboring Chikugo-Ono and meets a mysterious woman named Miki Sunahara. Miki, who says she saw Taro's film at the festival, and Taro embark on a small one-night, two-day trip. Miki is of unknown identity but has a frank personality. Taro, baring his lack of confidence in filmmaking to her, gradually develops a faint romantic feeling... Taro, the struggling film director protagonist, is played by Hiroki Sano from "SUPER HAPPY FOREVER," and Miki, the mysterious woman he meets on his journey, is played by Hana Amano from "Chime." The supporting cast includes Saki Kato, Ryo Shinoda, Ayame Gouriki, and Yuka Itaya.
title:Good Morning: In a suburban housing complex, several families live side by side like in a row house. The Hayashi family's sons Minoru (Kōji Shidō) and Isamu (Masahiko Shimazu) beg their parents for a television, but their request is denied. The children go on strike, refusing to speak until their demand is met, and eventually, their parents give in and buy one.
title:Good Valley Stories: A new feature film from director José Luis Guerín, who captivated the world with 'In the City of Sylvia' (2007) and was called 'the most outstanding filmmaker in contemporary Spain' by fellow Spanish director Víctor Erice. Despite his sparse output, Guerín continues to create masterpieces that lightly transcend the boundaries between fiction and documentary. This is his long-awaited new film, his first in ten years since 'The Academy of Muses' (2015), now arriving in Japan. To commemorate the release of 'The Good Valley Story,' the beautiful masterpiece 'In the City of Sylvia' will also be revived. Please enjoy Guerín's world on the big screen. The Vallbona district, located on the outskirts of Barcelona, Spain. This place, named 'The Good Valley,' is surrounded by rivers and railway tracks, an isolated land left behind by development, yet it also seems like an ideal paradise blessed with nature so rich it's hard to believe it's near a big city. Here, families who moved in from the mid-20th century live together with a new generation of immigrants who have arrived recently. Although their cultures and lifestyles differ, the children play together in the river, and everyone eats, drinks, sings, and dances well, finding a moment of peace. A new railway expansion plan is proposed for this urban oasis. A residents' information meeting is held, and some people are forced to relocate...
title:Good-for-Nothing: Toshio, a university student, drives a luxury car through the office district. Together with his friends Jun, Morishita, and Fujieda, he forces his father's company secretary, Ikuko, into the car and robs her. After savoring a brief thrill, they return the money and let her go, but days later they contact her again and forcibly take her to a party.
title:Goodbye My Car: A comedy starring Hiroshi Tachi, depicting a 70-year-old movie star caught up in a major uproar over surrendering his driver's license. Nanjo Hiroshi, who has enjoyed a smooth acting career and recently won numerous film awards for art films, secretly longs to appear in action movies. When his longtime actor friend Ozaki Makoto gets into a motorcycle accident, Nanjo is asked by the media for comment as a fellow actor of the same generation. His remarks admonishing Ozaki unexpectedly attract public attention, and the narrative takes on a life of its own, involving his manager and family, and being interpreted in ways far from his original intent. Although Nanjo wants to continue performing action scenes with cars and motorcycles, those around him expect him to surrender his license, plunging him into the biggest crisis of his life. Hiroshi Tachi comically plays actor Nanjo Hiroshi, the same name as the character he played in the 1994 film "License!". Nishino Nanase plays his manager Kawauna Mai, who is thrown into chaos by Nanjo; Kurokawa Sooya plays young man Kugami Ryo, whose life changes dramatically after meeting Nanjo; Yoshida Kotaro plays Mita Atsushi, the president of Nanjo's talent agency; and Uzaki Ryudo plays Ozaki Makoto, an actor friend who built an era alongside Nanjo. Directed by Kawai Yuji of "Kaguya-sama: Love Is War" fame, with screenplay by Hayashi Tamio of "From the Land of Love to the Land of Sorrow".
title:Goodbye, My Loved Ones!: The third installment in the human comedy series that explores family dynamics and second chances through the theme of "shukatsu" (end-of-life planning), following "Oshukatsu: Jukushun! Jinsei, Hyakunen Jidai no Sugoshikata" and "Oshukatsu: Saishun! Jinsei Rhapsody." Aya, the eldest daughter of Shinichi and Chikako Ohara, finally decides to marry her fiancé Ryota. However, just before the wedding, a casual remark from Aya causes a rift in their relationship, escalating into a major commotion involving both families. Meanwhile, Shinichi's junior colleague Kato struggles to accept his mother Toyoko's progressing dementia, speaking harshly to her. Chikako gently tells Kato, "Even with dementia, the heart doesn't forget." Continuing from the previous two films, director Hideyuki Kazuki helms this installment, incorporating the latest end-of-life planning trends and knowledge while depicting family bonds with light humor and a warm perspective. The cast reunites familiar faces from the series, including Tsurube Shofukutei as Shinichi Ohara, Junko Takahata as his wife Chikako, Ayame Goriki as their daughter Aya, along with Yuki Matsushita, Masahiko Nishimura, Norika Fujiwara, Renji Ishibashi, Kumiko Fujiyoshi, LiLiCo, Kunikazu Katsumata, and Yoshihiko Hakamada. Guest stars include Keiko Mita as Toyoko, who has dementia, and Fumiyo Kohinata as her son Kato, who supports her despite his own inner conflict.
title:Grim Reaper Barber: A human fantasy set in a mysterious beauty salon run by Death, where a woman who must spend her final days there reexamines her life through various encounters and farewells. Based on a proposal by Yoichi Umeki submitted for a Nihon University College of Art class assignment, with a screenplay by Kohei Taniguchi ('This Video Cannot Be Played THE MOVIE') and directed by Shinji Imaoka ('Reiko Iruka'). Hairdresser Miho Saeki, frustrated by troubles at work and in her private life, slips on stairs. Waking up, she is led by rookie Death Sakuma to a suspicious salon 'Meikup' (Makeup), where Death hairdressers touch up the deceased to connect them with loved ones for one last day. However, Miho's actual death is days away, and Sakuma jumped the gun. She stays at the salon until her death. Hinako Sakurai plays Miho, KANON from dance & vocal group STARGLOW plays Sakuma. Okabe Dai (comedy trio Hanako) plays the salon owner, Hirai Amon plays Miho's boyfriend, Inuzuka Kenta plays her salon manager, and Miho Jun plays her mother.
title:Gulliver's Travels Beyond the Moon: Toei Animation's first sci-fi feature. It is also the first feature-length film solely directed by Kuroda Yoshiro, whose highly designed compositions and musical style highlight the allegorical world. Ambitious meta-cinematic structures are employed, marking a breakthrough for a new generation at Toei Animation. The princess's secret revealed at the end carries a critique of civilization, an idea proposed by then-animator Hayao Miyazaki.
title:HAPPYEND: Directed by Neo Sora, known for "Ryuichi Sakamoto | Opus," in his feature fiction film debut, this youth film depicts the precariousness of friendship in a possible future, using unique sound and emotional visual beauty. In Japan, XX years from now. Yuta and Ko, childhood best friends, spend their days listening to music and goofing around with their friends. One night in their senior year of high school, they sneak into school, and Yuta comes up with a crazy prank. The next day, the principal, enraged upon discovering the prank, escalates the situation by introducing an AI surveillance system into the school. This event prompts Ko, who is about to go to university, to think deeply about his future and identity, creating a rift between him and Yuta, who just wants to keep having fun. Sōta Kurihara and Yukito Hidaka, both cast through auditions and making their screen debuts, play the protagonists Yuta and Ko respectively. Yūta Hayashi from "Lost Summer" and Kirara Inori from "Summer Film ni Notte" co-star. The film was screened in the Orizzonti Competition section at the 81st Venice International Film Festival in 2024.
title:HUG! PreCure Futari wa Pretty Cure: Cure Black, Cure White, and Shiny Luminous defeat a monster rampaging through the city. However, a mysterious monster named Miden appears and transforms Luminous into a child. Miden steals memories from all the previous Pretty Cures and turns them into baby Cures. Miden also appears before Hana and the others, and Hana fights alongside Black and White, who rush to help, but Cure Ange, Cure Etoile, Cure Macherie, Cure Amour, and even White are all reduced to toddlers. Hana, sinking into grief and despair before her young companions who have forgotten everything about themselves, and Nagisa, who cannot transform into a Pretty Cure without Honoka, find themselves in an utterly desperate crisis.
title:Hallan: Based on the 'Jeju April 3 Incident,' a massacre in which nearly 30,000 people are said to have been killed but which was covered up for a long time, this drama depicts the flight of a mother and daughter desperately trying to survive while being driven into a corner by unreasonable violence. On April 3, 1948, the 'Jeju April 3 Incident' began when some islanders on Jeju Island, opposed to interference by foreign forces, staged an armed uprising. From October of the same year, the government designated areas more than 5 kilometers from the coastline as 'hostile zones' and issued a proclamation stating, 'Anyone entering or leaving will be shot without condition.' To escape disaster, the villagers head for Hallasan Mountain, which rises in the center of Jeju Island. A-jin, a woman who has to leave the village temporarily, is extremely worried about her 6-year-old daughter Hye-sen, whom she left behind. Meanwhile, in the village, the South Korean army is mercilessly shooting the elderly. Surviving, Hye-sen heads into the mountains alone to find her mother. After miraculously reuniting, the mother and daughter embark on a life-or-death escape to survive. Directed and written by Ha Myeong-mi, who built her career as a screenwriter for commercial films, it vividly portrays the nameless people tossed about by state power. Kim Hyang-gi, known for 'Along with the Gods' and 'Innocent Witness,' stars as A-jin.
title:Hamnet: A drama by Chloé Zhao, director of "Nomadland," that blends fiction with the tragic love story behind the creation of Shakespeare's classic play "Hamlet." Based on the 2020 novel of the same name by Northern Irish author Maggie O'Farrell, which won the Women's Prize for Fiction and the National Book Critics Circle Award. In a small 16th-century English village, Agnes Shakespeare, who possesses knowledge of herbs and mysterious powers, lives with her three children while her husband William works as a writer in London. Agnes struggles to protect her children during a plague outbreak, but tragedy strikes when her 11-year-old son Hamnet dies, plunging the family into deep grief. Jessie Buckley ("Women Talking") plays Agnes, and Paul Mescal ("Aftersun") plays William, with Emily Watson ("Breaking the Waves") and Joe Alwyn ("The Brutalist") co-starring. Steven Spielberg and Sam Mendes are among the producers. Nominated for eight Academy Awards at the 98th ceremony, including Best Picture, Jessie Buckley won the Best Actress award.
title:Hamtaro: Adventures in Ham-Ham Lan: It's Laura's birthday. Hamtaro has prepared a present, but Laura ignores him, and in frustration he runs away from home. Seeing this, the Ham-Hams are about to help Hamtaro run away when a mysterious fairy hamster appears and takes everyone to Ham-Ham Land, a dream world where only hamsters live. But Hamtaro can't stop thinking about Laura. Hearing from the fairy hamster about 'magic sunflower seeds' that allow hamsters to talk to humans, Hamtaro sets out on an adventure to find them. But what awaits?
title:Hamtaro: The Captive Princess: Hamtaro had a dream. It was a dream of a beautiful hamster princess... 'Help me... Please... Come here quickly...' The princess was trapped inside a soap bubble, tears in her eyes. Even after waking up, Hamtaro can't stop worrying about the princess from his dream. So, he and the Ham-Hams decide to go rescue her. They arrive at the 'Hamja Kingdom,' the homeland of hamsters with a history of 8686 in the Ham Calendar, surrounded by desert. The sky is dark, and the hamsters living there seem downcast. No wonder—Princess Shera of the Hamja Kingdom, who was engaged to Prince Hamuha of the neighboring country, has been kidnapped by a mysterious cat that suddenly appeared and trapped her just like in Hamtaro's dream. That cat wants to marry Princess Shera and take over the kingdom! At this rate, the princess and the kingdom are in danger! Can Hamtaro and the Ham-Hams save the princess and protect the hamsters' homeland? An adventure of love and courage begins now.
title:Hana: In the 15th year of the Genroku era. A young samurai (Okada) burdened by the duty to avenge his father travels from Shinshu to Edo and hides out in a tenement slum. The film depicts how his resolve begins to waver as he interacts with the residents of the tenement. While weaving the story of the Ako Ronin's raid into the background, director Kore-eda turns it on its head, aiming for 'a story where the weak are affirmed as they are.' This ambitious work marks Kore-eda's first deep dive into a narrative world, having previously been conscious of the distance between fiction and nonfiction in his live-action films.
title:Hanging Garden: 'Conceal nothing, create no taboos, and share everything as much as possible.' That is the rule of the Kyobashi family, decided by Eriko as a reaction against her mother Satoko, who never did anything motherly—Eriko is determined to maintain a smiling, happy household. But contrary to Eriko's wishes, each family member harbors secrets. Her husband Takashi shuttles between two lovers, Asako and Mina; her daughter Mana refuses to go to school; and her son Ko, a shut-in with an interest in architecture, unknowingly hires Mina—his father's lover—as his tutor. One day, Eriko throws a joint birthday party for Satoko and Mina. However, thanks to a drunken Mina, the family's secrets are exposed one after another, and the home Eriko built crumbles. Yet on her own birthday, a birthday call from Satoko dissolves her resentment, and Eriko is able to be reborn, warmly welcoming her family home with gifts in hand.
title:Happiness: One of the representative works of Agnès Varda, a leading female director of the French New Wave, this human drama depicts the ironic fate that befalls an ordinary couple in search of happiness. François lives a peaceful and happy life surrounded by his beautiful wife Thérèse and their adorable children. One day, while visiting a nearby town, François meets Émilie, a woman who works at the post office, and falls in love with her. At the same time, François truly loves his wife Thérèse. One day, while on a picnic with his family, François confesses his infidelity to Thérèse... The film won the Silver Bear at the 1965 Berlin International Film Festival.
title:Happy Hour: Starring four women with no acting experience, this film portrays the anxieties and worries of ordinary women in their late 30s through a tense 317-minute drama. Directed by Ryusuke Hamaguchi, known for challenging works like the 4-hour-plus epic "Intimacies" (using film school students) and the Tohoku documentary trilogy ("The Sound of the Waves," "Voices from the Waves," "Singing in the Dark"), the film won the Best Actress award for its four leads at the 68th Locarno International Film Festival in Switzerland. Akari, Sakurako, Fumi, and Jun, all in their late 30s, thought they were best friends who could tell each other anything. However, it is revealed that Jun had been hiding her year-long divorce negotiations. Shaken by this, the four women take a trip to Arima Onsen for a brief escape and enjoy a fun time together, but...
title:Happy Together: A love story directed by Wong Kar-wai of 'Days of Being Wild,' starring Leslie Cheung and Tony Leung as lovers, depicting the poignant romance and human relationships between two men set in Argentina. Ho Po-wing and Lai Yiu-fai, who have loved intensely but repeatedly broken up, head to Iguazu Falls to repair their relationship, but get lost, argue, and part on bad terms. Later, a wounded Ho Po-wing shows up at the apartment of Lai Yiu-fai, who is working as a doorman at a tango bar in Buenos Aires. Lai Yiu-fai reluctantly lets him stay, but after recovering, Ho Po-wing starts going out while Lai Yiu-fai is away. Meanwhile, Lai Yiu-fai changes jobs to work at a Chinese restaurant and becomes close with a young coworker named Chang. It won the Best Director award at the 50th Cannes International Film Festival. Released in theaters in 1997. In February 2018, it had a special screening at Bunkamura Le Cinema to coincide with the release of the digital remaster of Wong Kar-wai's 'Days of Being Wild.' In 2022, a 4K restored version was screened as part of 'WKW4K' (from August 19, 2022, at Cine Mart Shinjuku, Grand Cinema Sunshine, Cinema City, etc.).

In Japan, XX years from now. Yuta and Ko, childhood best friends, spend their days listening to music and goofing around with their friends. One night in their senior year of high school, they sneak into school, and Yuta comes up with a crazy prank. The next day, the principal, enraged upon discovering the prank, escalates the situation by introducing an AI surveillance system into the school. This event prompts Ko, who is about to go to university, to think deeply about his future and identity, creating a rift between him and Yuta, who just wants to keep having fun. Sōta Kurihara and Yukito Hidaka, both cast through auditions and making their screen debuts, play the protagonists Yuta and Ko respectively. Yūta Hayashi from "Lost Summer" and Kirara Inori from "Summer Film ni Notte" co-star. The film was screened in the Orizzonti Competition section at the 81st Venice International Film Festival in 2024.
title:Harmagedon: The destroyer of the universe, "Genma," was approaching Earth. Luna, a princess of Transylvania and an esper, received a message from the cosmic consciousness "Froi" and began a battle to protect Earth alongside Vega, a cyborg soldier also fighting Genma. Luna decided to gather psychics from around the world to counter Genma. Among them was high school student Azuma Higashi, who was unaware of his own abilities until Vega's provocations awakened his psychic powers. However, emotionally immature, he closed his heart to Luna's pleas to join the fight to save the universe. Even so, the enemy appeared before him without mercy.
title:Harum Malam: Set in Malaysia, this demon-combining exorcism gore horror film takes on the Islamic exorcism rites of the state religion and Southeast Asia's most enigmatic flower, the titan arum. A boy apprentice exorcist, who inherited spiritual powers from his mother, engages in a deadly struggle against the forbidden curse dwelling within the "corpse flower." Iqbal, raised under the wing of Norman, a Muslim exorcist, possesses rare spiritual abilities inherited from his mother Dina. One day, Dina is possessed and killed by an evil spirit while shielding Iqbal, who was targeted because of the strength of his powers. Grief-stricken, Iqbal resents his own overwhelming power, and his father Norman, worried about his son's future, seals away part of his abilities. Crawling toward the wounded family are a series of tragedies brought by the curse of the "corpse flower." Can Iqbal overcome his sorrow and exorcise a curse steeped in mystery and taboo?
title:Harà Watan: Directed by Akio Fujimoto, who has garnered international attention for "Where I Belong" and "The Girls at the Seashore," this road movie is based on the testimonies of the Rohingya, often called "one of the most persecuted ethnic groups in the world." It depicts a young refugee brother and sister, driven from their homeland, risking their lives to cross borders in search of their family. Blending unrelenting reality with fantastical imagery, the film portrays the harrowing journey of refugees smuggling themselves across borders from a child's perspective. Five-year-old Shafi and his nine-year-old sister Somiir, living in a refugee camp, set out with their aunt for distant Malaysia, hoping to reunite with their family. Unable to obtain passports, they are led by smugglers onto a fishing boat, and despite facing the fury of nature, pursuit by security forces, and the threat of human trafficking, they desperately overcome the grueling journey. The cast includes over 200 Rohingya people, led by the siblings Somiir and Shafi in the lead roles. Their voices and gazes, as people who have themselves been driven from their homeland, lend the film a powerful realism despite their lack of acting experience. The film received high praise at film festivals worldwide, including winning the Special Jury Prize in the Orizzonti section at the 82nd Venice International Film Festival in 2025, the first time a Japanese director has won this award.
title:Heldin: A social human drama that depicts the relentless hard work and unexpected troubles constantly falling on nurses in an understaffed, full hospital ward, which became a huge hit in Switzerland. Directed by Swiss screenwriter and filmmaker Petra Volpe, it realistically and thrillingly portrays the urgent, universal problem of hospital realities. Florie, a dedicated and highly professional nurse working in a state hospital, faces an even busier late shift than usual because a colleague is out sick. The ward is full, and she also has to train nursing students. Despite the situation, Florie treats patients with anxiety and loneliness sincerely, but she falls into an unmanageable situation and eventually faces a major trial. Leonie Benesch, known for 'The Teachers' Lounge' and 'September 5,' stars.
title:Her Brother: Set in Mukojima, Tokyo, during the Taisho era. Siblings Gen and Aoiro live with their writer father and stepmother. Gen takes care of Aoiro, covering for their sick stepmother, but Aoiro starts hanging out with a bad crowd. They protect each other at times and have big fights at others, living together as siblings, until Aoiro falls ill with tuberculosis.
title:Hero's Island: A documentary by Guillaume Brac, director of 'A Summer's Tale' and 'The Gentle Ones,' capturing a summer at the leisure facility 'Leisure Island' in Cergy-Pontoise, a suburb of Paris. Known as the setting for Éric Rohmer's 'My Girlfriend's Boyfriend,' and a place Brac himself frequently visited as a child, Leisure Island is filled with vacationers but has no flashy attractions, only expanses of water and greenery. Under beautiful sunlight, the film captures the natural moments of various people: boys trying to sneak into the facility, young men hitting on women, an elderly man reminiscing about the past, and employees managing and guarding the place.
title:Heso no taisho: Set in a slum along the Hirano River in eastern Osaka. A fine human drama depicting the interactions between the so-called 'Apache tribe,' who make a living by stealing scrap metal, and a town doctor (Frankie) who strives to stand by them. Michiyo Aratama, playing his wife, also delivers a remarkable presence.
title:Hidden Blade: Set in Shanghai during World War II, this spy noir depicts the back-and-forth battle of nameless spies among the Chinese Communist Party, the Kuomintang, and the Japanese military. Starring Hong Kong superstar Tony Leung, who won the Best Actor award at the 53rd Cannes International Film Festival for 'In the Mood for Love' (2000) and has recently gained attention from younger generations for his role in 'Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings' (21). The other lead is Wang Yibo, who debuted as a member of the China-Korean joint unit 'UNIQ' and later broke out as an actor in the TV drama 'The Untamed' (19), now one of the most sought-after young actors in China. This film marks his first leading role in a movie, and he has since starred in multiple films, winning the Best Actor award at the 20th Film Channel Media Awards for his second lead role in 'Born to Fly' (23) alongside this film. The intense, stunt-free action sequences performed by the two leads captivate with overwhelming tension and unparalleled beauty. Directed by Chen Er, who previously helmed 'Once Upon a Time in Shanghai' (16). Chen also wrote and edited this film, and Tony Leung was so impressed by the script—only Chen's fourth feature—that he agreed to star. Nominated for eight awards including Best Picture and Best Actor at the 36th China Film Golden Rooster Awards, the highest honor in Chinese cinema, held in November last year. Wang Yibo, making his film debut, was nominated for Best Supporting Actor. Tony Leung won Best Actor, and director Chen Er won Best Director and Best Editing, achieving a triple crown.
title:Hiroshima: A high school in Hiroshima. In the third-year class taught by Kitagawa, student Michiko Oba collapses with a nosebleed. It is caused by leukemia from the atomic bomb. In this class, a full one-third of the students are hibakusha (atomic bomb survivors). On that day, Yukiko's sister was exposed to the bomb while working on evacuation duties and died in a river. Endo Yukio's father could not save his wife, who was trapped under a building and engulfed in flames. When radish sprouts appeared in Hiroshima, where it was said no grass would grow for 75 years after the bombing, people found hope in those sprouts.
title:Hiroshima Mon Amour: An actress, once condemned for having an affair with an enemy soldier in a French village under German occupation, visits Hiroshima for a film shoot and indulges in a one-day affair with a Japanese architect. Through this, she learns of Hiroshima's tragedy. The date is August 6th. Against the backdrop of the anti-nuclear movement, their lonely conversation continues. The city, miraculously rebuilt from the ashes, can never forget the shadow of death.
