This place, named 'The Good Valley,' is surrounded by rivers and railway tracks, an isolated land left behind by development, yet it also seems like an ideal paradise blessed with nature so rich it's hard to believe it's near a big city. Here, families who moved in from the mid-20th century live together with a new generation of immigrants who have arrived recently. Although their cultures and lifestyles differ, the children play together in the river, and everyone eats, drinks, sings, and dances well, finding a moment of peace. A new railway expansion plan is proposed for this urban oasis. A residents' information meeting is held, and some people are forced to relocate...
title:Hit the Road: A car races across the desolate landscape of Iran. In the back seat, the father entertains his exuberant younger son; in the passenger seat, the mother sways to an old pop song; and in the driver's seat, the eldest son stares silently ahead. While the younger son, unaware of the purpose of the trip, frolics innocently, the family arrives near the Turkish border...
title:Hito wa Naze Love Letter wo Kaku n: A young man died in a train derailment in the year 2000. Twenty-four years later, a letter from a woman who was in love with him arrives for his father... A story depicting the bonds between people carrying loss.
title:Hodonaku, Owakare Desu: Based on the bestselling novel of the same name by Amone Nagatsuki, winner of the Shogakukan Bunko Novel Award Grand Prize, starring Minami Hamabe and Ren Meguro, directed by Takahiro Miki ("Ao Haru Ride," "Tomorrow I Will Date Yesterday's You"). It depicts a heroine who joins a funeral company and, together with her supervising funeral planner, aims to create the "best possible funeral." Misu Shimizu, struggling with job hunting, has a secret she can't tell anyone: she can hear the voices of the deceased. A fateful encounter changes her life when Reiji Urushibara, a funeral planner who notices her ability, invites her into the world of funeral planning. Guided by something, Misu becomes an intern at the funeral company "Bando Kaikan." Teaming up with Urushibara, she confronts the question "What is a funeral that satisfies not only the surviving family but also the deceased?" through various families' funerals, including a husband who lost his pregnant wife and a couple who lost their young daughter. Eventually, Misu comes to admire Urushibara's sincere dedication to the deceased and their families, and decides to pursue a career as a funeral planner herself. Hamabe plays Misu, Meguro plays Urushibara, with a stellar cast including Mochika Yamada, Ken Mitsuishi, Mirai Shida, Keisuke Watanabe, Kotone Furukawa, and Takumi Kitamura. The script is by Takuro Honda (drama "Lion's Snack"), supervised by Yoshikazu Okada, known for various hit works.
title:Hold Your Breath Like a Lover: This is the graduation work from Kohei Igarashi's master's program at Tokyo University of the Arts. Igarashi, who studied under Nobuhiro Suwa and Kiyoshi Kurosawa, received high international praise for his first feature film, "The Voice of Wind and Rain," made while he was still a student. It is December 30, 2017, about two years before the Tokyo Olympics, and the constitution has been revised and a National Defense Force established. A stray dog wanders into a garbage processing plant. Tani-chan, who works in the office, searches for the dog but can't find it. Ken, who finished his night shift, plays video games with Go, who is off duty that day. Adachi-san refuses to go home, while Yan-san is busy putting up New Year's decorations. The workers at the plant each grapple with similar problems: pregnancy, infidelity, family, and friends who died in the war. Amidst this, Tani-chan, troubled by her affair with Adachi-san, begins to feel that her late father, the former plant manager, might be present in this place.
title:Holding Liat: A documentary depicting an Israeli-American family's desperate efforts to rescue their daughter abducted by Hamas, crossing divides. On the morning of October 7, 2023, the agricultural community of Nir Oz in southwestern Israel was attacked by Hamas militants, with a quarter of its roughly 400 residents killed or taken hostage. Yehuda, the father of hostage Liat Beinin Atzili and her husband Aviv, along with his family, begins a frantic mission to save them. Because Liat holds American citizenship, Yehuda travels to the US as part of a delegation urging the American government to secure the hostages' release, but is shocked to realize that the hostages' plight is being used to justify the Israeli government's continuation of the war. While Yehuda, critical of Netanyahu's administration, accuses the prime minister of prolonging the war to avoid imprisonment, some family members and associates push back, arguing that rescue should take priority over criticism. Through the urgent perspective of those longing for the safe return of their loved ones, the film illuminates the complex interplay of politics, history, and divided values. The production includes Darren Aronofsky, director of 'Black Swan,' among its team. It won the Best Documentary Award at the 75th Berlin International Film Festival in 2025.
title:Homework: A documentary by internationally acclaimed Iranian director Abbas Kiarostami ('Where Is the Friend's Home?'), focusing on homework and school education. Feeling that Iranian children are always overwhelmed by homework, Kiarostami himself acts as interviewer, asking elementary school students and their parents a series of questions about 'homework.' Through the interviews, the complex family circumstances of each child emerge, revealing the problems within Iran's education system. Kiarostami vividly captures the children's diverse expressions and words while sounding an alarm to society. A digital remastered version was screened as part of the special program 'And Kiarostami Continues' (from October 16, 2021, at Eurospace in Tokyo and other venues).
title:Honey and Clover: Takemoto (Sakurai Sho), a student at Hama Art University, one day finds himself falling for Hagumi (Aoi Yu), a girl who paints with complete absorption. She is a transfer student rumored to be a prodigy and a relative of university professor Hanamoto (Sakai Masato). Takemoto cannot get Hagumi out of his head, but the presence of the extraordinary senior Morita (Iseya Yusuke), who also cares for her, stirs up Takemoto's feelings.
title:Hoodlum Soldier: An entertainment film based on Arima Yorichika's original work "Kisaburo Ichidai," adapted by Kikushima Ryuzo and directed by Masumura Yasuzo. Its success led to a series of nine films. The dynamic duo of the outrageous protagonist played by Katsu Shintaro and the intellectual officer played by Tamura Takahiro are the highlight.
title:Horus: Prince of the Sun: Director Isao Takahata's feature-length debut, made in 1968 during his time at Toei Animation. Based on the puppet play 'The Sun on the Spring Elm' by Kazuo Fukazawa, it depicts the brave boy Hols, entrusted with the Sun Sword, confronting a demon. Hols lives with his father in a remote natural setting. Rescued from a wolf attack by the rock giant Moog, Hols receives the Sun Sword embedded in Moog's shoulder. After losing his father, Hols follows his father's dying wish and sets out for a village where people live, but is captured by the terrifying demon Grunwald and thrown off a cliff. Washing up in a village, Hols defeats a giant pike that has been plaguing the villagers and becomes a hero. One day, he meets a lonely girl named Hilda in a ruined village and brings her back, but... Scene design, art design, and key animation were handled by Hayao Miyazaki, animation direction by Yasuo Otsuka, and key animation by Koji Mori. It was released as part of the 'Toei Manga Parade' (Toei Manga Festival) in the summer of 1968.
title:Hour of the Star 4K: "I am a typist, a virgin, and I like Coke and hot dogs." Based on the novel by Clarice Lispector, known as 'Brazil's Virginia Woolf,' this film shines with an unforgettable brilliance in the history of Brazilian cinema. After 40 years, it receives its first theatrical release in Japan.
title:Humanity and Paper Balloons: The final work of renowned early Showa period director Tomu Uchida, who died of illness at just 28, this is a humanistic period drama. In the Edo period, Shinzo, a barber living in a poor tenement, runs a gambling den and catches the eye of yakuza. Strapped for cash, he tries to pawn his barber tools but is refused. Meanwhile, Matajuro, a ronin living in the same tenement, seeks employment with a samurai his father once served, but is completely ignored. One day, Shinzo accidentally kidnaps the pawnshop owner's daughter and brings her back to the tenement... An adaptation of Kawatake Mokuami's kabuki play "Kamiyui Shinzo."
title:Hush!: "Unforgettable masterpieces" return to the big screen! Since his directorial debut with "Twenty Years' Micro Heat" (1993), Ryosuke Hashiguchi—a "master of few works" eagerly awaited by film fans worldwide—has won the Grand Prix at the 25th Rotterdam International Film Festival for "Like Grains of Sand" (1995), swept various film awards including the Kinema Junpo Best Ten Japanese Films No. 1 for "Three Stories of Love" (2015), and released his latest film "Motherhood" (2024) nine years after "Three Stories of Love." "Hush!" depicts a gay couple and a woman who proposes having a child through sperm donation—"not dating or marriage, but I want a child"—and the "new form of family" the three of them create. "All Around Us" portrays the hope that arises between people over the course of a decade in a married couple's life. Both films are often cited as "all-time best movies" and are known as "unforgettable masterpieces." Now, these two works are getting a revival release in 4K remastered versions! "All Around Us" returns 18 years after its June 2008 release, and "Hush!" returns a full quarter-century after its production in 2001 (released April 2002). "Hush!" was screened at the 2001 Cannes Film Festival Directors' Fortnight.
title:Höhenfeuer: A 1985 film by the master Fredi M. Murer, known as a pioneer of New Swiss Cinema, which won the Golden Leopard, the top prize at the Locarno International Film Festival. A family of four lives a nearly self-sufficient life surrounded by the majestic Alps. The teenage younger brother, who is deaf-mute, grows up healthily, sometimes frustrated by his disability but loved by his parents and older sister. One day, angered by a broken lawnmower, he throws it away, incurring his father's wrath. Running away from home, he begins living alone in a mountain hut. His worried sister brings him food, and they spend happy times together around a campfire on the mountain peak. Eventually, the sister's pregnancy is discovered... The film was first released in Japanese theaters in 1986. A digitally remastered version was revived in February 2020.
title:I Want to Be a Shellfish: A small-town barber who has returned from the war unexpectedly finds himself put on trial as a war criminal. This film version, directed by screenwriter Hashimoto himself, is based on a television drama that won an Art Festival Award. A legendary work that portrays the absurdity and cruelty of war, with Frankie's heartfelt performance that shakes the soul.
title:I Was a Stranger: An ensemble drama inspired by the reality that 14 million people were forced to flee abroad to escape the long devastation of the Syrian civil war, depicting families torn apart by conflict and those around them from multiple perspectives. Set across four countries—Syria, Turkey, Greece, and the United States—the story unfolds in five chapters, intersecting the lives of five families. As the civil war between government forces and rebel groups intensifies in Syria's dictatorship, Syrian doctor Amira decides to cross dangerous borders with her daughter to reach safety. Syrian border guard Mustafa distrusts the brutal government forces and struggles between being a soldier who follows orders and a human with a conscience. Turkish smuggler Marwan seeks to earn money by loading refugees onto boats bound for Greece to move his sick son to America. Poet Fathi boards that boat with his wife and child, facing mortal danger. Greek coast guard Stavros discovers refugees navigating stormy seas and strives to save lives. Film producer and humanitarian activist Brandt Andersen, who made the 2020 short film "Refugee" as his starting point, makes his feature directorial, screenwriting, and producing debut with this meticulously researched work. Yasmin Al-Masri reprises her role as doctor Amira from the short, and Omar Sy returns as smuggler Marwan.
title:I Wish: Director Hirokazu Kore-eda of "Nobody Knows" and "Air Doll" depicts a family drama set in Kyushu, which is buzzing with excitement over the full opening of the Kyushu Shinkansen line in March 2010. Starring the comedy brother duo Maeda Maeda's Koki Maeda and Koshiro Maeda. The story follows two brothers, separated by their parents' divorce to live in Kagoshima and Fukuoka respectively, who strive to reunite their broken family, spurred on by the full opening of the bullet train line. Co-stars include regulars from Kore-eda's films such as Yui Natsukawa, Atsushi Abe, Yoshio Harada, and Kirin Kiki.
title:IAI: A horror film directed by Yoshizo Sakai of "Fictional" and "Counselor," planned and produced by Tokio Omori, a TV Tokyo producer who brought forth "The Missing Exhibit" and "Searching for Kikue Ishinaga." Rio Yamashita, who starred in the 2025 long-running hit "Yukiko a.k.a." primarily in mini-theaters over about a year, plays the lead role of a woman tormented by paranoid fear through caring for her mother. After her father's death, Kana returns to her childhood home and begins caring for her mother, who has dementia. She devotes herself to caregiving as if trying to reclaim time with her mother, but her mother's inexplicable behavior gradually becomes increasingly bizarre, and Kana begins to feel uneasy about strange occurrences around her. Eventually, possessed by the sensation that something has entered her mother's inner being, Kana is driven mad by the presence of an unearthly "something." In addition to Rio Yamashita as the protagonist Kana, An Ogawa, who has starred in successive films including "There Is a Stone" and "Song of the Beyond," plays Kana's younger sister Anri, who rushes to the family home after hearing Kana's pleas, and Sports Makita plays psychiatrist Kumagai, who becomes acquainted with Kana and Anri's family through a certain incident.
title:Ice Blood: Minoru (Hiromitsu Kitayama) and Yuki (Chihiro Kato) move with their young son Akira to Minoru's family home in a heavy snowfall area. The couple wishes for a peaceful life, but Minoru's father Shigeru, who has dementia, is inexplicably terrified of Yuki and calls out his deceased wife's name. One morning, Shigeru dies grotesquely in an abnormal state. From that moment on, the family is plagued by suspicion and fear. Soon, eerie 'white women' begin appearing in the house one after another, encroaching on their daily lives. Minoru, as if losing his mind, keeps drawing pictures of the 'white woman,' while young Akira's view of his mother gradually begins to reflect 'something else.' One by one, the family members break down. Minoru, captivated by snowflakes and losing his reason; Yuki, being eroded; and Akira, placed in danger. Is this a curse, an illusion, or reality? When the snowy plains are stained with fresh blood, an unknown 'white terror' appears and runs amok with brutality.
title:Ichi the Killer: A violent action film based on the popular manga of the same name by Hideo Yamamoto, directed by Takashi Miike. Set in a yakuza apartment building in Shinjuku's Kabukicho district, it depicts a surreal battle between insane men with thorough violence. The boss of the Anjo-gumi yakuza group, based in Kabukicho, suddenly disappears. Kakihara, a masochist who loved the violence given by the boss, persistently searches the city. Eventually, he learns of a hitman named Ichi, and upon witnessing his deranged killing style, feels an excitement akin to love. Tadanobu Asano plays Kakihara, with bleached hair and a face full of scars, and Nao Omori plays Ichi, a weak-willed man who turns into a crying killing machine. The cast includes Shinya Tsukamoto, Suzuki Matsuo, SABU, and Jun Kunimura. The screenplay is by Sakichi Sato, known for 'The Golden Grasslands.' A 4K remastered version will be re-released in May 2026.
title:Il Buco: Director Michelangelo Frammartino, whose "Four Lives" depicting the cycle of life earned high praise at the Cannes Film Festival, questions the meaning of humanity's venture into the unknown against the historical context of Italy's economic boom. This film won the Special Jury Prize in the Competition section of the 78th Venice International Film Festival in 2021. Young explorers descend 683 meters underground without maps, using acetylene lamps to measure and map the cave structure. Above ground, an elderly shepherd on the Pollino Plateau prepares for a quiet death amidst vast nature, suffering from illness. The shepherd's death coincides with the explorers reaching the deepest abyss, creating a grand cycle of life and death, time and space. The cinematographer is the renowned Renato Berta, known for collaborations with masters like Jean-Luc Godard, Éric Rohmer, Daniel Schmid, and Manoel de Oliveira. In Japan, it screened under the title "Cave" in the World Focus section of the 34th Tokyo International Film Festival. It will have its theatrical premiere in Japan in 2026 under the title "Journey to the Depths of the Earth" as part of the special screening series "The Amazing World of Michelangelo Frammartino."

title:Il deserto rosso: The first color film by Italian master Michelangelo Antonioni, this psychological drama won the Golden Lion at the 25th Venice International Film Festival in 1964. In Ravenna, an industrial coastal city lined with sterile factories, Giuliana lives with her husband and son but remains unable to recover from the shock of a car accident years earlier, spending her days in emotional instability. One day, her husband introduces her to his friend Corrado. Giuliana is drawn to Corrado, who carries a loneliness similar to her own, and gradually the two grow closer... Monica Vitti, known as Antonioni's muse, plays Giuliana, with British star Richard Harris as Corrado. A 4K restored version will be released in August 2026 as part of the retrospective program "Michelangelo Antonioni Retrospective: Arid Love, Wandering Souls," featuring five of Antonioni's early works.
title:Imaginary Line: After graduating from film school, Fumiko continues making films with her best friend, Mohamed Yume, but one day she discovers that Yume does not have legal residency status... A drama that delves into the realities of the immigration system.
title:Immediate Family: A music documentary tracing the journeys and bonds of four session musicians who supported the American West Coast sound. In the early 1970s, musicians Danny Kortchmar (guitar), Waddy Wachtel (guitar), Leland Sklar (bass), and Russ Kunkel (drums) participated in recordings for artists like Carole King, James Taylor, Jackson Browne, and Linda Ronstadt, who lived around Laurel Canyon in Los Angeles. Later called the supergroup "The Immediate Family," their solid playing and musical understanding contributed to the birth of many classic songs, continually supporting the artists' expressions. Through interviews with the four musicians themselves and the renowned artists they made music with, the film reveals moments of creation in the studio's closed space and the deep bonds between musicians. It also explores projects each participated in solo, depicting their rise to becoming popular musicians. Directed by Denny Tedesco, who also directed the music documentary "The Wrecking Crew" about the session musicians who supported the American music scene of the 1960s and 70s.
title:In Our Day: The 30th feature film by Korean master Hong Sang-soo, who continues to release works in his unique style, distanced from large-scale commercial cinema. It depicts a day in the lives of a resting actor and an elderly poet living in seclusion, whose paths almost cross but never quite do. Sang-won, an actor on hiatus staying at a friend's house, and Hong Ui-ju, an elderly poet living alone in a small apartment, receive visits from young guests burdened with anxiety about the future, who ask various questions: What is necessary for acting? How does one become an actor or poet? Why did you start writing poetry? The topics the young people raise gradually develop into important conversations about life. Meanwhile, a friend's cat suddenly goes missing... Through two alternating locations and times, and the comedic dialogue that unfolds, the film discovers dramatic moments hidden in everyday life. Kim Min-hee, an indispensable presence in Hong Sang-soo's works, plays the actor Sang-won, and Ki Joo-bong, who won the Best Actor award at the Locarno International Film Festival for "Hotel by the River," plays the poet Hong Ui-ju. The film will be released in theaters in 2026 as the fourth installment of "Monthly Hong Sang-soo," a project screening new works for five consecutive months to commemorate the director's 30th debut anniversary.
title:In Praise of Love: A drama by Jean-Luc Godard, the master who led the French New Wave, centered on the theme of 'love.' Edgar, a young artist in Paris, conceives a new work depicting four moments related to love—'encounter, passion, separation, reconciliation'—using three couples. The heroine Edgar considers ideal for this project is a woman he met two years ago. She is the granddaughter of an elderly couple who were once involved in the Resistance, whom Edgar met while researching the history of the Resistance in Brittany. Searching for her, Edgar revives his memories of Brittany two years ago. The first half depicts present events in richly shaded black-and-white 35mm film, while the second half shows protagonist Edgar's flashbacks in vivid color using digital video. The 4K restored version will be screened in Japan for the first time as part of the special screening series 'Jean-Luc Godard in the 21st Century: Our Films 2001-2010' (starting June 20, 2026, at Theater Image Forum Shibuya and other locations nationwide).
title:In The Grey: To confront the dictator Salazar, who vanished after stealing one billion dollars, sharp lawyer Rachel hires two professionals: the brilliant Sid (Henry Cavill), a former Royal Marine, and Bronco (Jake Gyllenhaal), a fighting machine from the U.S. Navy. The team uses strategic warfare to bring down the dictator's empire, but just as the mission is about to succeed, Rachel is kidnapped by Salazar. Sid and Bronco infiltrate the isolated island controlled by Salazar and face a dangerous battle—.
title:In Their Own Words: The Women of K: A documentary that investigates the reality of sexual violence euphemistically called "entertainment" inflicted on the women of the Kurokawa settlement group in Manchuria during wartime. As part of the Japanese government's national policy in the 1930s-40s, the Manchuria-Mongolia settlement groups were sent from across Japan to Manchuria, China. As Japan's defeat became imminent, the Soviet army invaded Manchuria in August 1945, plunging the settlers into dire circumstances. To survive and return to Japan, the Kurokawa settlement group from Gifu Prefecture offered 15 women aged 18 and older (by traditional count) as sexual partners to the enemy Soviet army in exchange for help. After returning to Japan, the women faced discrimination and prejudice. Their voices, physically and mentally scarred, were silenced, and the truth was concealed for many years. However, about 70 years after the war, in 2013, the women of Kurokawa joined hands and began to speak publicly about the layers of harm they suffered. Director Fumie Matsubara, known for "Hama no Don," carefully weaves together these women's oral stories. Actress Shinobu Otake provides narration.
title:In die Sonne schauen: Four girls from different eras, spanning from the 1910s to the present day, experience inexplicable events on a farm in northern Germany. A century-spanning visual epic where their anxieties resonate with one another.
title:In the Grey: To confront the dictator Salazar, who vanished after stealing one billion dollars, sharp lawyer Rachel hires two professionals: the brilliant Sid (Henry Cavill), a former Royal Marine, and Bronco (Jake Gyllenhaal), a fighting machine from the U.S. Navy. The team uses strategic warfare to bring down the dictator's empire, but just as the mission is about to succeed, Rachel is kidnapped by Salazar. Sid and Bronco infiltrate the isolated island controlled by Salazar and face a dangerous battle—.
title:In the Mood for Love: A romantic drama directed by Wong Kar-wai of 'Days of Being Wild' and 'Happy Together,' starring Tony Leung and Maggie Cheung, depicting the adulterous love between a married man and woman. Hong Kong, 1962. Chow, a newspaper editor, and Chan, a secretary at a trading company, move into the same apartment building on the same day and become neighbors. They soon discover their respective spouses are having an affair and begin spending time together. Hesitant yet strongly drawn to each other, Chow and Chan... Some settings and the worldview are carried over from 'Days of Being Wild,' and the story connects to the 2004 film '2046.' It won the Best Actor award and the Technical Grand Prize at the 53rd Cannes Film Festival. Released in Japanese theaters in 2001. In February 2018, it had a special screening at Bunkamura Le Cinéma alongside the digital remastered release of Wong Kar-wai's 'Days of Being Wild.' In August 2022, the 4K restored version was screened as part of 'WKW4K: Wong Kar-wai 4K.' In May 2026, a revival release titled 'In the Mood for Love 25th Anniversary Special Edition' is scheduled, screened simultaneously with the short film 'In the Mood for Love 2021.'
title:In the Realm of the Senses: In the 11th year of the Showa era (1936). Sadako, a maid at a Japanese inn, becomes infatuated with the inn's master and begins an affair. When the affair is discovered by the man's wife, the two decide to elope. As they indulge in days of pleasure, Sadako becomes unwilling to ever let him go, and eventually strangles him to death to keep him for herself, then cuts off his genitals.
title:Inheritence: A humorous drama about the inheritance disputes that erupt within a once-close family after the death of their elderly mother. The Suzuki family mourns the loss of their mother, but soon, arguments break out over her estate: the eldest and second daughters insist on selling the family home and splitting the proceeds, the younger brother and his wife claim the land and house as their inheritance as the family successor, and the widow of the deceased eldest son joins the fray, souring their previously warm relationships. When a later-discovered will surfaces, objections arise, worsening the rifts. The conflict escalates to the point of litigation, but... Nene Otsuka plays the eldest daughter Reiko, Yami Yumiko plays the second daughter Satomi, and Shinobu Nakayama plays Sanae, the widow of the late eldest son. Akiko Matsumoto takes on the role of a consultant offering inheritance advice from a legal standpoint, while Yota Kawase plays Reiko's husband Seiichi. The film is directed and written by Fujimura Mamiya, known for scripting the 'Care Nin' series, which depicted the realities of nursing care.
title:Inside Llewyn Davis: The Coen brothers, directors of "No Country for Old Men" and "True Grit," won the Grand Prix at the 66th Cannes Film Festival in 2013 with this film. Loosely based on the life of Dave Van Ronk, a musician who represented the 1960s folk scene, it humorously depicts a week in the life of a struggling young folk singer. In the winter of 1960s New York, singer-songwriter Llewyn keeps performing at live houses but can't seem to make it big. On the verge of giving up on making a living through music, he still manages to get by with the help of his friends. Oscar Isaac, who appeared in "Robin Hood" and "Drive," plays Llewyn and also performs the songs. The music is by T Bone Burnett of "O Brother, Where Art Thou?" and "Crazy Heart."
title:Into the Belly of the Beast: A crime suspense film depicting a man consumed by a desire for cannibalism as he descends into the abyss of ruin. It won the Grand Prize at the 19th Tanabe-Benkei Film Festival, a first for a suspense film in the festival's history. Satō, a young man working as a host at a cabaret club, harbors a secret desire to eat people. One day, he finds a smartphone at work, which leads to him being threatened by a mysterious duo and forced into a dark side job as a courier. After making a large sum of money from the illegal but lucrative work, Satō begins to use his earnings to satisfy his hidden desires. Shun Tohari stars in his film debut as Satō. The film will be screened theatrically as part of the 'Tanabe-Benkei Film Festival Selection 2026.'
title:Is This Thing On?: A couple whose smooth-sailing life takes a turn and their marriage falls apart. The disheartened husband, Alex, finds a new purpose in life by turning their marital woes into comedy at a comedy club.
title:Ishibumi: A theatrical release version re-edited from a special 70th post-war anniversary program broadcast on Hiroshima TV in August 2015. It reveals the portraits of 321 first-year students of the former Hiroshima Prefectural Hiroshima Second Middle School, who lost their lives in the atomic bombing and for whom a memorial stone was erected along the Motokawa River, based on the writings of their bereaved families. While building on a reading drama broadcast on the same station in 1969, composed by Matsuyama Zenzo, it adds original elements such as projection performances using wooden boxes and interview footage by Ikezawa Akira.
title:It Was Just an Accident: A suspense thriller by Iranian master Jafar Panahi, winner of the Palme d'Or at the 78th Cannes Film Festival in 2025. It thrillingly and humorously depicts people wrongfully imprisoned seeking revenge. Vahid, once unjustly imprisoned, accidentally encounters a man he believes was his torturer guard. He forcibly restrains the man and digs a hole in the wilderness to bury him, but the man's ID card shows a different name. The man claims it's a case of mistaken identity. Blindfolded during imprisonment, Vahid never saw his torturer's face. Unsure if this is the right man, Vahid pauses revenge and visits a friend who was also tortured by the same guard. Panahi, banned from filmmaking by the Iranian government for opposition activities, drew inspiration from his own two imprisonments and the real voices of cellmates. Having won the Golden Lion at Venice for 'The Circle' and 'No Bears', and the Golden Bear at Berlin for 'Taxi', Panahi achieved the feat of winning top prizes at all three major festivals with this film. A French co-production, it was France's entry for Best International Feature Film at the 98th Academy Awards and received a nomination.
title:JAWAN/ジャワーン: A thrilling action film from the 'King of Bollywood', Shah Rukh Khan, in his first collaboration with a young Tamil film crew. It depicts the righteous struggle of subway hijackers who steal a ransom from arms dealers.
title:JAWAN／ジャワーン: A thrilling action film from the 'King of Bollywood', Shah Rukh Khan, in his first collaboration with a young Tamil film crew. It depicts the righteous struggle of subway hijackers who steal a ransom from arms dealers.
title:JOTARO: Novelist Jotaro Izumi (Sojiro Yoshimura) made a spectacular debut after winning the Bungei Prize. However, his success was short-lived; now, he spends his days in depravity, borrowing money from his editor, Eiji Matsumura (Kohshu Hirano), on the condition that he write. Pursued relentlessly by photographer Ranko Kijima (Aika Yukihira), he drifts into a relationship and moves into her home, yet the twisted desires writhing within him remain unfulfilled. It is then that Matsumura introduces him to a research subject: Anna Unabara (Suika Yamasaki), a woman once dubbed the "Beautiful Criminal" for swindling 30 million yen through sugar dating. Beneath her quiet and submissive facade lurks an inexplicable strangeness—and Jotaro begins to feel that she may be the one who can finally satisfy his desires.
title:JUST ANOTHER: A documentary following the punk band "the Genbaku Onanies" as they reached their 38th anniversary in 2020. Formed in Nagoya in 1982, the group centered on EDDIE, formerly of THE STAR CLUB, and TAYLOW, known locally as the "Punk Doctor." Through numerous lineup changes, the band is also known for having included members such as Tatsuya Nakamura (who later joined BLANKEY JET CITY) and Ken Yokoyama of Hi-STANDARD. Remaining committed to their home base in Aichi, they have held steady jobs rather than aiming for professional status, and continue to play punk rock today even after turning 60. In this film—the first documentary of their career—the members themselves reveal internal truths about the band that have never been told before. It is directed by Michiko Oishi, the filmmaker who created "MOTHER FUCKER," a documentary about the music label "Less Than TV."
title:Jack and the Witch: Directed by Yasuji Yabushita with animation direction by Akira Daikuhara for Toei Animation's 10th anniversary film. Based on the heroic epic 'Beowulf,' this version features Jack driving a car, a witch arriving by helicopter, and a struggle to rescue comrades turned into demons in the witch's castle. Seiichiro Uno's cheerful music won the Mainichi Film Concours Music Award.
title:Japan's Longest Day: The film depicts the 24 hours from noon on August 14, 1945 (Showa 20), when the Showa Emperor and cabinet ministers decided to surrender at an Imperial Conference, to noon on August 15, when the acceptance of the Potsdam Declaration was announced to the public via the radio broadcast of the Emperor's Jewel Voice (Gyokuon-hoso) through NHK.
title:Jawan: A thrilling action film from the 'King of Bollywood', Shah Rukh Khan, in his first collaboration with a young Tamil film crew. It depicts the righteous struggle of subway hijackers who steal a ransom from arms dealers.
title:Jeanne Dielman, 23, quai du Commer: A masterpiece drama by Belgian female director Chantal Akerman, who left many works earnestly examining women's lives in society and daily life, carefully capturing a housewife's frustrations and details while tracing how cracks emerge in ordinary routine. Jeanne lives alone with her adolescent son in a Brussels apartment. Boiling water, peeling potatoes, going shopping—she leads an "ordinary" life, but... Starring Delphine Seyrig, known for "Last Year at Marienbad" and "The Discreet Charm of the Bourgeoisie." Screened at the "Chantal Akerman Film Festival" (April 29 - May 12, 2022, Human Trust Cinema Shibuya).
title:Jeunes mères: An ensemble drama by Belgian masters Jean-Pierre and Luc Dardenne, known for "The Child" and "The Kid with a Bike," depicting five young mothers living in a mother-child support facility. The five girls—Jessica, Perla, Ariane, Julie, and Naima—live together in a facility that supports women who became pregnant young. Without anyone to rely on and facing various problems like poverty and violence, they become mothers while confused, troubled, and unable to find a model for the family they should aim for. Struggling not to be swallowed by the overwhelming loneliness, the girls who still wish "to love" sometimes lean on others and choose their own paths to follow. Lukas Dhont, director of "Close," is listed as a co-producer. Screened in the Competition section of the 78th Cannes Film Festival in 2025, it won the Best Screenplay Award and the Ecumenical Jury Prize.
title:Jin-Roh: The Wolf Brigade: A film adaptation of Mamoru Oshii's manga "Kerberos Panzer Cop," part of the "Kerberos Saga" that also includes Oshii's live-action films "The Red Spectacles" and "StrayDog: Kerberos Panzer Cops." Set in an alternate 1960s Japan, it depicts the love, hatred, and tragic romance between an elite special forces officer and a guerrilla girl. In the Tokyo metropolitan area, emerging from post-war chaos, the "Capital Police" is formed to combat escalating armed conflicts. Kazuki Fuse, a member of the Special Assault Team, encounters a girl carrying a bomb during a riot suppression. Hesitating to pull the trigger, the girl detonates the bomb and kills herself. Fuse is sent back to training school for failing his mission, but one day he meets a woman who looks exactly like the girl. This is the directorial debut of animator Hiroyuki Okiura, known for key animation on "Akira" and "Patlabor," and it received high praise at the Berlin International Film Festival. In March 2026, a 4K remastered and Dolby Atmos version will be released for revival screenings and home video to mark the 25th anniversary.
title:Johatsu - Die sich in Luft auflöse: A documentary co-directed by German filmmaker Andreas Hartmann and Berlin/Tokyo-based video artist Arata Mori, exploring the Japanese phenomenon of "evaporation" (disappearance). In Japan, approximately 80,000 people go missing each year, with thousands vanishing completely. Known as "evaporated people," their reasons range from relationship troubles and debt to yakuza threats. Some, with the help of so-called "night escape artists," abandon all ties and start new lives elsewhere. "Evaporation," intersecting deep loss and the hope of starting over, has been a motif in literature and film. This work uses immersive imagery to delve into the unknown work of "night escape artists" and the emotional conflicts and paths to reconciliation for both the disappeared and those left behind. It garnered attention at film festivals worldwide, winning Best Documentary at the 39th Munich International Documentary Film Festival.

title:John Cranko: A film about the life of genius choreographer John Cranko, who elevated the Stuttgart Ballet from a small regional company in Germany to world-class status, made with the full cooperation of the ballet company. It depicts the untold story behind the creation of his masterpiece "Onegin" and his true face, cut short by an untimely death at the age of 45, all colored by spectacular dance performances by current star dancers. John Cranko, an up-and-coming choreographer active in England, is prosecuted for homosexual acts after a police sting operation. Forced to leave London in 1960, he becomes a guest artist with the Stuttgart Ballet through connections. Finding a place in the company that accepts him without prejudice, he becomes artistic director the following year in 1961, creating works and a company that express beauty and passion with free-thinking ideas. In 1969, the ballet company is invited to the Metropolitan Opera House in New York and rises to the top of the world overnight. Sam Riley, known for "Maleficent" and "Control," stars, passionately portraying Cranko, a man overflowing with passion and innovative talent but who sometimes hurts others due to being too pure in his pursuit of art. Directed and written by Joachim A. Lang, known for "The Man Who Produced Hitler" and who has covered the Stuttgart Ballet for many years.
title:Journey to the West: Conquering th: Young monster hunter Xuanzang uses his "Three Hundred Nursery Rhymes" as a weapon to try to awaken the good hearts of monsters, but always fails. One day, in a riverside village attacked by a half-fish, half-beast monster, he works with the villagers to haul the creature ashore, where it transforms into human form. The nursery rhymes Xuanzang sings have no effect at all, and when he is attacked instead, he is saved by a female monster hunter named Duan.
title:Jules: A human drama starring the acclaimed actor Ben Kingsley, humorously depicting a lonely elderly man who, after getting caught up in a bizarre commotion with his neighbors, rediscovers the joy of life. Milton, a 79-year-old man living in a small town in western Pennsylvania, continues to live alone despite his daughter Denise worrying about his early symptoms of dementia. One night, an unidentified flying object from the sky crashes into Milton's yard, shaking his peaceful daily life. When no one around him takes him seriously, Milton shares the secret of the flying object with his neighbors Sandy and Joyce, who are around his age and also witnessed it. The three, each carrying their own loneliness, rediscover the forgotten joys of life and face their futures. Harriet Sansom Harris ("The Bodybuilder") plays Sandy, Jane Curtin ("Coneheads") plays Joyce, and Zoe Winters (series "Succession") plays Milton's daughter Denise. The director is Mark Turtletaub, known as a producer for "Little Miss Sunshine" and "Loving."
title:KATSEYE: WILD HEARTS: KATSEYE: WILD HEARTS offers an intimate look at the group's bold new era and serves as a tribute to the fans who have supported their journey. Through never-before-seen footage, fan videos created by the fandom EYEKONS, and candid interviews with the members, the film portrays the strong bond between KATSEYE and their global fandom. A love letter to the EYEKONS who have helped build the KATSEYE movement, the film reflects that this group's story is only just beginning. The documentary also captures the highs, setbacks, sacrifices, and breakthrough moments KATSEYE experienced on their path to becoming global pop stars—from the intense pressure of the HYBE and Geffen Records audition program The Debut: Dream Academy to topping the charts. Praised by media outlets including The New York Times, Vogue, Rolling Stone, and Billboard, KATSEYE has solidified its global presence as one of the most exciting new-generation global acts in pop through relentless effort and stunning live performances. The team behind Netflix's documentary series Pop Star Academy: KATSEYE returns for this film, produced by Interscope Films and Boardwalk Pictures in partnership with HYBE x GEFFEN. Nadia Hallgren, who also directed the series, serves as director.
title:KEEPER キーパー: A horror film directed by Osgood Perkins of "Longlegs" fame, depicting extreme terror closing in on a woman brought to a mountain lodge by her lover, rendered in a mysterious, nightmarish world. Liz, an artist living in the city, is invited to a mountain lodge owned by her boyfriend Malcolm. Malcolm is a wealthy but somewhat enigmatic doctor, and for Liz, who wants to confirm his true feelings, this weekend trip to mark their first anniversary is supposed to be special. The lodge, reached by car driven by Malcolm, is in a remote area surrounded by dense forest. Nearby is another lodge owned by Malcolm's cousin Darren, who visits with his young lover Minka, but Liz feels repulsed by Darren's crude and intrusive manner. Encouraged by Malcolm, Liz eats a chocolate cake said to be a gift from the caretaker, and is plagued by strange nightmares and hallucinations. The next day, Malcolm is called away to the hospital for an emergency, leaving Liz alone at the lodge. Gripped by a vague unease, Liz is beset by one abnormal event after another, losing the boundary between reality and nightmare, and is threatened by the presence of something unknown stirring within the lodge. Tatiana Maslany, who also appeared in Perkins' previous film "The Monkey," plays the protagonist Liz, and Rossif Sutherland from "Orphan: First Kill" plays her boyfriend Malcolm.

title:KIDS キッズ: Photographer Larry Clark, known for his photo book "Tulsa" and for continuously capturing the real lives of teenagers, made his directorial debut with this 1995 film. It vividly depicts the reality of teenagers living on the streets in the 1990s—sex, drugs, violence, HIV—in a documentary-like style, sparking nationwide controversy in America. On a hot summer afternoon in New York, Telly is hanging out with his friends as usual, bragging about having bagged a virgin girl. Meanwhile, at Ruby's house, Jenny and four other girls are also talking only about sex. Ruby, who enjoys experienced and unprotected sex, gets excited sharing her own stories. Jenny is angry at Telly, who took her virginity and then never contacted her again. Worried about HIV infection, Ruby suggests Jenny get tested and goes with her to hear the results. Jenny had only ever had sex with Telly, and the test result is positive. Having received a death sentence from just one sexual encounter with one person, Jenny tries to tell Telly the truth. But Telly, unaware that he is an HIV carrier, is out having fun luring a new virgin. The screenplay was written by Harmony Korine, then 19 years old. Cinematography is by Eric Edwards, the renowned cameraman of "My Own Private Idaho." Music is by Lou Barlow of the alternative rock band Dinosaur Jr. Gus Van Sant served as executive producer. Chloë Sevigny, who had no acting experience at the time, played Jenny, and Rosario Dawson played Ruby.

title:KNEECAP ニーキャップ: A semi-autobiographical drama tracing the birth of KNEECAP, a hip-hop trio from Northern Ireland who rap in Irish—a language not officially recognized in the region until 2022—and draw attention with their radical lyrics and performances, set against the backdrop of protests demanding official status for the Irish language. With humor and stylish direction, it portrays working-class youth in West Belfast, still scarred by the Northern Ireland conflict. Nisha (MC name: Móglaí Bap), a drug dealer born and raised in Belfast, and his childhood friend Liam (MC name: Mo Chara) are caught in a drug deal. Liam refuses to speak English and remains defiant. Music teacher JJ (MC name: DJ Próvai), sent as an interpreter, sees Irish lyrics in Liam's notebook and recognizes his talent. The three start rapping in Irish to reclaim their suppressed identity and linguistic rights... The three KNEECAP members make their acting debut playing themselves, with Michael Fassbender co-starring. The film won numerous awards worldwide, including the Audience Award in the NEXT section at the 2024 Sundance Film Festival.

title:KUBO AND THE TWO STRINGS: Long ago in Japan. A boy named Kubo, who lost his left eye, lives with his ailing mother. Playing a magical shamisen inherited from his mother, he earns a living by telling the story of a samurai named Hanzo in the village. On the night of the Bon festival, two 'Sisters of the Dark' who claim to be his mother's sisters appear and attack Kubo, but his mother tells him to gather his father's 'sword, armor, and helmet' and magically sends Kubo far away. Beginning his journey, Kubo makes allies of a female monkey and a male stag beetle while searching for the 'sword, armor, and helmet'.

title:Kabei: Our Mother: In the 15th year of the Showa era, as global tensions rise, German literature scholar Shigeru (Mitsugoro Bando) is arrested for advocating against the war. His grieving mother Kayo (Sayuri Yoshinaga) and two daughters (Mirai Shida, Mirai Sato) are supported by his former students, relatives, and neighbors, and strive to live brightly and strongly.
Kamen Rider Decade, aka Kadoya Tsukasa, arrives in a "certain world." In this world, for some reason, the photos Tsukasa takes do not distort the image. Suddenly, a certain Western-style mansion comes to mind. Following faint memories, Tsukasa reaches the mansion, where he meets a girl who calls herself his sister, Kadoya Sayo. Tsukasa becomes convinced this is his own world. However, even in this world, the "collapse of worlds" is progressing. Sayo's servant, Tsukikage Nobuhiko, claims that the cause of the world's collapse lies in the Riders born in each world, and declares that to stop it, they must decide on a single "strongest Rider."
title:Kamen Rider Hibiki The Movie: Hibi: In present-day Japan, the giant demonic monster Orochi appears on a coast. Hibiki and Asumu rush to fight it, but Hibiki is defeated by Orochi and falls into a coma. Asumu seeks clues to save Hibiki in the Takeshi's ancient documents describing Orochi, but there he finds the name "Asumu," the same as his own, along with the stories of Oni... The ancient document tells of a village in the Sengoku period. There, Orochi demanded a human sacrifice every year. When Asumu's acquaintance Hitoe is chosen as the sacrifice, Asumu consults Tobei Tachibana to find a way to save her. Following the idea of asking an Oni for help, Asumu and the others set out to search for an Oni.
title:Kamikaze Girls: A youth comedy set in Shimotsuma City, Ibaraki Prefecture, depicting the friendship between two girls with completely opposite values: a Lolita and a Yankee. Based on the novel of the same name by Novala Takemoto, directed and adapted by Tetsuya Nakashima. In Shimotsuma City, Ibaraki, surrounded by endless rice fields, 17-year-old Momoko is a super laid-back girl who adores Rococo-era France. She dresses in her beloved Lolita fashion and commutes to Daikanyama, where the flagship store of her worshipped brand is located. One day, she starts selling counterfeit famous brands to earn money for clothes, and a girl her age named Ichigo, a member of a local biker gang, appears before her. Ichigo takes a liking to the gutsy Momoko and begins frequently visiting her home. Momoko the Lolita girl is played by Kyoko Fukada, and Ichigo the Yankee girl is played by Anna Tsuchiya. In 2024, marking the 20th anniversary of its release, it was converted to Digital Cinema Package (DCP) and screened in revival.
title:Kamome Diner: A drama depicting the peaceful daily lives of three Japanese women set in a small restaurant in Helsinki, the capital of Finland. Based on the novel of the same name by author Yōko Mure, adapted and directed by Naoko Ogigami, who gained attention with her feature directorial debut "Barber Yoshino." Japanese woman Sachie opens a small restaurant called "Kamome Diner" on a street corner in Helsinki, but no customers come. One day, Sachie happens to meet a Japanese tourist named Midori and asks her to help out at the restaurant. Soon, a variety of colorful characters start coming to Sachie's shop one after another... Satomi Kobayashi, Hairi Katagiri, and Masako Motai play the three Japanese women, with Markku Peltola from "The Man Without a Past" co-starring.
title:Kaneko Fumiko: This biographical drama centers on Fumiko Kaneko, a nihilist and anarchist who fiercely resisted Japan's state power about 100 years ago, depicting the 121 days from her death sentence to her suicide in prison. Directed by female filmmaker Sachi Hamano (known for "Yukiko-san no Ashioto"), the film draws on tanka poems that convey Kaneko's own voice to portray her solitary struggle. Born in 1903, Kaneko grew up as a "non-registered person" because her father never filed her birth registration. At age nine, she was sent to live with her grandmother and aunt in Korea, where she suffered abuse akin to slavery from a family that exploited the colonized Korean villagers. In 1919, she witnessed the March First Independence Movement in Korea. Sent back to her mother's home in Yamanashi at 16, she later struggled through poverty in Tokyo, moving ideologically from Christianity to socialism, anarchism, and finally nihilism. She eventually met Park Yeol, a Korean independence activist who had fled to Japan. Becoming comrades and lovers, they campaigned against Japanese imperialism and colonialism, but were arrested during the 1923 Great Kanto Earthquake and sentenced to death. After her sentence was commuted to life imprisonment through amnesty, Kaneko was sent to Tochigi Women's Prison, where she continued her solitary fight behind bars. Nanana stars as Kaneko, embodying the soulful cry of a woman who defied state power to the end. Katsuya Kobayashi plays Park Yeol, with supporting performances by Masaki Miura, Yoko Horaguchi, and Kazuko Yoshiyuki.
title:Kantara: A legendary suspense-action film set in South India, centered on the ancient ritual of 'Bhuta Kola' (spirit worship). It powerfully depicts the strange fate of a land protected by divine grace and became a long-running hit in India. About 170 years ago, a vast forest was granted to the indigenous people by the oracle of the god Panjuruli. The village of Kadu Bettur has long performed the Bhuta Kola ritual and maintained peace through divine protection, even when landlords tried to reclaim the land. However, the newly appointed forest officer Murali attempts to incorporate the villagers' land into a state-designated protected forest. As the village faces a crisis of survival, Shiva, a buffalo race champion whose father was a Bhuta Kola performer, opposes the forest department to protect the village's peace, leading to an incident. Rishab Shetty, who has an unusual background of juggling jobs in water vending and real estate before entering the film industry, directed, wrote, and starred in the film, passionately playing Shiva, the village's biggest rogue.

title:Killer of Sheep: The feature debut of Charles Burnett, a filmmaker who quietly revolutionized American cinema by depicting the daily lives and humanity of African Americans, released in 1977. It portrays the everyday existence of African American workers living on the fringes of Los Angeles with a realistic gaze and poetic visual beauty. Set in the Watts district of Los Angeles in the early 1970s, still bearing the scars of the Watts riots. Stan works at a sheep slaughterhouse to support his wife and two children, living an empty daily life. Exhausted physically and mentally by labor and poverty, he withdraws into himself, while his wife grows increasingly lonely. Directed by Burnett as his graduate thesis film while a student at UCLA Film School, it was shot in Watts using a mostly amateur cast of people he knew. Long unreleased due to music copyright issues, it finally had a theatrical release in the US in 2007. The 4K restoration completed in 2025 replaces the music in the final scene with Dinah Washington's "Unforgettable," as Burnett originally intended. It won the FIPRESCI Prize at the Forum section of the 31st Berlin International Film Festival in 1981. In Japan, it will have its first theatrical release in the 4K restored version as part of the special screening series "Charles Burnett: Everyday Blues" (starting February 7, 2026, at Theater Image Forum).
title:Kin-dza-dza!: A deadpan sci-fi comedy made in Soviet-era Georgia in 1986, which became a huge hit in the USSR at the time. One day, a student named Gedevan asks construction engineer Mashkov for help, looking troubled, saying, 'There are some men over there who claim to be aliens.' Mashkov, who doesn't believe in aliens, presses a button on a space travel device the men were holding, and in the next instant, Mashkov and Gedevan are warped to the planet Pluke in the Kin-Dza-Dza Nebula, far from Earth. There, for some reason, Earth matches are extremely valuable, and the two try to use the value of matches to somehow return to Earth... Culturally popular in Japan as well, it was first introduced at the 'Soviet SF Film Festival' held in Tokyo in 1989, later released in a new print in 2001 and a digital remaster in August 2016. In May 2021, to coincide with the release of the animated version 'Ku! Kin-Dza-Dza,' the live-action film had its fourth theatrical release.
title:Kind Hearts and Coronets: A suspense comedy that follows the trail of a serial murder spree by a young man burning with ambition and a thirst for revenge, laced with biting black humor. One of the 'Ealing Comedies,' a series of comedy films produced at Ealing Studios in the UK from the late 1930s to the mid-1950s, directed by Robert Hamer, known for 'It Always Rains on Sunday.' The story is told in flashback form as Louis, a young man of aristocratic blood from the D'Ascoyne family, writes his memoirs in his prison cell, recounting how he systematically murders his relatives to avenge his mother's disownment and reclaim his status. The renowned actor Alec Guinness, known for his role as Obi-Wan Kenobi in 'Star Wars' and 'The Bridge on the River Kwai,' plays all eight members of the D'Ascoyne family who are killed by Louis. Dennis Price plays the protagonist Louis, and Joan Greenwood leaves a strong impression as the cold, calculating heroine. This film is part of the special screening series 'The Golden Age of British Ealing Comedies' (June 20–July 17, 2026, at Shinjuku K's Cinema).
title:Kingdom 5: Set during China's Spring and Autumn period, this is the fifth live-action film adaptation of Yasuhisa Hara's popular manga series 'Kingdom,' depicting the grand story of Shin, a boy who dreams of becoming the world's greatest general, and the young king Ying Zheng, who aims to unify China. This film adapts the beloved 'Coalition Army Arc' from the original manga, where Qin clashes with the six other states. Three years after the Battle of Mayang, where Qin lost the great general Wang Qi, Shin, who has inherited Wang Qi's will and continued to grow, has been promoted to commander of a thousand men. Meanwhile, under the strategy of Zhao's prime minister Li Mu, all states except Qin unite to form a 'Coalition Army' of 500,000 troops, launching an invasion of Qin. At the capital city of Xianyang's palace, Ying Zheng and his court scramble to respond, but faced with an unprecedented force, Qin is pushed to the brink of national collapse. Shin, along with fellow young generals Meng Tian and Wang Ben, heads to Hangu Pass, the gateway to Qin, where representative Qin generals such as Biao Gong, Meng Wu, Teng, Wang Jian, and Huan Qi gather. On the other side, the Coalition Army, led by Lord Chunshen of Chu, assembles powerful warriors from various states, including the fierce Zhao general Wan Ji, who harbors a grudge against Qin for trampling his homeland. Familiar series cast members return, including Kento Yamazaki as Shin, Ryō Yoshizawa as Ying Zheng, and Shun Oguri as Li Mu. New additions to the lavish cast include Jun Shison as Meng Tian, Fūju Kamio as Wang Ben, Kenji Sakaguchi as Huan Qi, and Takumi Saitō as Lord Chunshen. Director Shinsuke Sato, who has helmed all previous films in the series, returns, and original manga author Yasuhisa Hara, who has been involved in the script since the first film, also wrote the screenplay for this installment.
title:Kiss Me Deadly: One night, private detective Mike Hammer picks up a woman named Christina and lets her into his car, but is suddenly attacked by three men and loses consciousness. When he comes to, Mike finds himself in a hospital bed. According to his secretary Velda, Mike and Christina were driven into a river along with the car, and Christina died. Sensing something behind it all, Mike begins to investigate Christina's background.
title:Kneecap: A semi-autobiographical drama tracing the birth of KNEECAP, a hip-hop trio from Northern Ireland who rap in Irish—a language not officially recognized in the region until 2022—and draw attention with their radical lyrics and performances, set against the backdrop of protests demanding official status for the Irish language. With humor and stylish direction, it portrays working-class youth in West Belfast, still scarred by the Northern Ireland conflict. Nisha (MC name: Móglaí Bap), a drug dealer born and raised in Belfast, and his childhood friend Liam (MC name: Mo Chara) are caught in a drug deal. Liam refuses to speak English and remains defiant. Music teacher JJ (MC name: DJ Próvai), sent as an interpreter, sees Irish lyrics in Liam's notebook and recognizes his talent. The three start rapping in Irish to reclaim their suppressed identity and linguistic rights... The three KNEECAP members make their acting debut playing themselves, with Michael Fassbender co-starring. The film won numerous awards worldwide, including the Audience Award in the NEXT section at the 2024 Sundance Film Festival.
title:Koenji Cinema Club Vol. 7:
