An inspired film based on the classic song "12-gatsu no Ame no Hi" (December Rain) from Happy End's self-titled debut album released in 1970. Marin, a girl searching for her birthplace, travels through her hometown in an attempt to recover paintings. An "inner-world road movie."

Director, Screenplay, Editor: Sawa Kawakami
Cast: Marin Hidaka, Jun Hosoi, Yuriko Tanaka, Ayu (Taro Monogatari), Kanon (Taro Monogatari), Yui Nishide, Konnichi Hakase (Nankyoku), Tomomi Nakai (Voice)
title:MOOSIC LAB2026:
【super໒꒱cute໒꒱fragile — Sawa Kawakami Director Special】
"December Rain" (23 min) ©︎ "December Rain" Film Partners

An inspired film based on the classic song "December Rain," originally released in 1970 on Happy End's self-titled debut album. An "inner world road movie" following Marin, a girl searching for her birthplace, as she travels through her hometown attempting to recover paintings.

Director, Screenplay, Editor: Sawa Kawakami
Cast: Marin Hidaka, Jun Hosoi, Yuriko Tanaka, Ayu (Taro Monogatari), Kanon (Taro Monogatari), Yui Nishide, Konnichi Hakase (Nankyoku), Tomomi Nakai (Voice)
title:MOTHERLAND: Set in Lithuania just after its independence, this drama quietly observes memories, conflicts, and the lives of people caught between shifting eras through the eyes of an American-born boy visiting the country with his Lithuanian mother. Director Tomas Vengris, making his feature-length debut, draws on his own experience growing up as the son of Lithuanian immigrants in Washington, D.C., to delicately portray the reality of people tossed about by changes in territory and political systems. In 1992, mother and son Victoria and Kovas arrive from America to Lithuania, which has just gained independence from the Soviet Union. As a child, Victoria was separated from her family under Soviet occupation and lost her home and land. In Lithuania, where control shifted from Nazi Germany to the Soviet Union, people's freedom continued to waver under different regimes. Returning to her homeland after 20 years, Victoria seeks to reclaim her lost family land and start a new life with her son, but finds a Russian family already living there. Faced with the harsh reality that reclaiming the land is not easy, her ideal of a fresh start in Lithuania begins to quietly unravel. Martas Metlevskis, an American-born actor of Lithuanian descent, plays the boy Kovas, and renowned Lithuanian actress Sevilija Janušauskaitė plays his mother Victoria.
title:MOTHERS’ INSTINCT: In 1960s America, best friends Celine and Alice live next door to each other in a suburban neighborhood. Both come from wealthy families and each has an only son the same age, living a perfect, happy life. But one day, Celine's son is involved in a tragic accident, and their relationship changes completely. Consumed by loss, Celine gradually begins to grow close to Alice's son, Theo. Alice starts to grow suspicious. Is she trying to take my family away? Or is it all just a misunderstanding... Alice's behavior escalates step by step, and soon both women are swallowed into a vortex of madness and delusion.
title:MOULIN ROUGE: A biographical film by master filmmaker John Huston, known for 'The Maltese Falcon' and 'The African Queen,' depicting the short life of the late 19th-century French painter Toulouse-Lautrec. Paris, Montmartre, at the end of the 19th century. The painter Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec frequents the cabaret 'Moulin Rouge,' symbolized by the red windmill on its roof, spending his days sketching the dancers and drunk patrons. Born into an aristocratic family, his leg growth stopped due to the effects of consanguineous marriage and a childhood accident. He finds purpose in life by leaving his stifling home to live in Montmartre and painting its scenes. One night, Henri helps a prostitute named Marie and begins living with her, but their relationship gradually falls apart. Based on the biographical novel 'Moulin Rouge' by Pierre La Mure, the screenplay was co-written by Huston and Anthony Veiller, known for 'The Night of the Iguana' and 'The Killers.' José Ferrer, of 'The Caine Mutiny,' stars, playing both Toulouse-Lautrec and his father in a dual role. The film won the Academy Awards for Best Art Direction and Best Costume Design at the 25th Academy Awards in 1953.
title:Maborosi: Having witnessed grief work in his TV documentary 'However... In an Age of Welfare Cuts,' Kore-eda tackles this theme head-on in his first theatrical feature, based on the novel of the same name by Teru Miyamoto. Yumiko (Esumi), who carries childhood trauma, loses her husband to suicide in the midst of a happy marriage. Years later, she lives a peaceful life with a new family, but a lingering unease never fully fades. Against the backdrop of Noto's nature captured in long shots, the quiet rebirth of a woman's heart is depicted with a serene gaze.
title:Made in Abyss: Dawn of the Deep So: A theatrical film based on the TV anime 'Made in Abyss', which itself is adapted from Akihito Tsukushi's manga of the same name. The Abyss is the only remaining unexplored chasm in a world that has been thoroughly explored. This deep, massive vertical hole is home to numerous strange creatures and contains countless precious relics that modern humanity cannot create. Riko, an orphan girl living in the town of Orth, built on the edge of the Abyss, decides to descend into its depths after the discovery of her mother's White Whistle, a legendary cave raider. Along with Reg, a robot boy who has lost his memory, she overcomes various hardships and continues her adventure. At the Fourth Layer, they are joined by Nanachi, a 'Hollow' they encounter. They then venture into the Fifth Layer, where Bondrewd awaits, and there they meet a girl named Prushka.
title:Magic Boy: The second feature-length animation produced against the backdrop of the flourishing Toei period drama genre. For the sword-fighting scenes, Reijiro Adachi, a top action choreographer at Toei Kyoto Studio, was brought in, and Daikuhara Akira, known for dynamic action, handled both direction and key animation. Newcomers including Isao Takahata, Hiroshi Ikeda, Masao Kuroda, and Yoichi Kotabe participated in production for the first time. It is also Japan's first feature-length animation in CinemaScope.
title:Magical Secret Tour: A crime drama about three women who have drifted through life, who deepen their bond through gold smuggling and reclaim their respective lives. Director Chihiro Amano ("Mrs. Noisy") was inspired by a real 2017 incident in which housewives were arrested for gold smuggling at Chubu Centrair International Airport. She co-wrote the original script with Madoka Kumagai, with whom she also worked on "Sato-san and Sato-san." Large-scale location shooting was conducted in Singapore, depicting the glamorous yet perilous journey of gold smuggling. Wakako, a mother of two living a peaceful life, learns that her husband has been fired from his company for embezzlement. To pay off her husband's debts, she becomes involved in gold smuggling in Singapore, where she meets Kiyoe, a non-regular researcher struggling with student loan repayments, and Mayu, an unmarried pregnant woman with zero savings. After successfully smuggling gold and getting a taste for it, the three decide to start smuggling on their own. For the first time, they gain money, freedom, and the joy of living authentically, spending a magical time together—but... Kasumi Arimura plays Wakako, the mother of two who learns of her husband's embezzlement; Haru Kuroki plays Kiyoe, the indebted researcher; Sara Minami plays Mayu, the unmarried pregnant woman; Akihisa Shiono plays Wakako's husband Takashi; Yuzu Aoki plays Kiyoe's colleague Shiina; and Takumi Saito plays Takashi's boss Tanoue.
title:Mahjong Horoki: In Ueno just after Japan's defeat in the war. One day, a young man named Tetsu unexpectedly runs into Joshu Tora, who once taught him how to gamble. Led by Tora into the Chinchiro slums, Tetsu bets his last bit of money on a game run by Dosa Ken, a professional gambler. He wins a considerable amount, but most of it is taken by Dosa Ken as a coaching fee.
title:Main Theme: Ogasawara Shibuki meets Daito Shima Ken, who is training in magic, and decides to go on a trip in his car. Shibuki's destination is Osaka, and Ken's is Okinawa. The two don't get along and argue constantly during the trip. In Hamamatsu, Ken's uncle has a magic show, and Shibuki ends up helping out. However, during the show, Ken meets with a jazz singer named Ise Masayo. Seeing Ken so smitten with Masayo, Shibuki feels jealous. The car arrives in Osaka, and the two part ways. But Shibuki can't stop thinking about Ken and sets off for Okinawa, where her sister and brother-in-law live.
title:Malpaís: The feature directorial debut of Terrence Malick, director of "Days of Heaven" and "The Thin Red Line," released in 1973. Based on a series of real murders that occurred in the late 1950s in America, it vividly and poetically depicts the flight of a young couple who commit a series of unplanned crimes. In 1959, in a small town in South Dakota. Holly, a 15-year-old girl who is not very noticeable at school, meets Kit, a young garbage collector, and falls in love. However, when Kit shoots and kills Holly's father, who disapproves of their relationship, the two embark on a aimless journey of escape. They live a reckless life, staying carefree in a treehouse and breaking into a rich man's mansion. Holly can only watch as Kit kills people one after another... Martin Sheen, known for "Apocalypse Now," plays Kit, and Sissy Spacek, known for "Carrie," plays Holly. In Japan, it was broadcast on TV in 1980 under the title "Jigoku no Tōhikō," and was released in theaters for the first time in March 2025 under the title "Badlands."
title:Man: I'll make you a good man. Identity unknown. Purpose unknown--- A suspense comedy about being devoted to by a mysterious man. Directed by Koji Maeda, who has won numerous awards for films like "Before Marriage" ('11) and "Just Remembering" ('21), this suspense comedy stars Yohei Uno. Oda is a young man who is a member of a car theft ring and has turned to crime. One night, at a crime scene, he is suddenly abducted by a stranger. "From now on, don't waste your time; live an honest life," the man tells him, handing him the keys to an apartment. Thus begins the bizarrely strange cohabitation of an unidentified man and a young criminal. The man persistently imposes lessons and goodwill on Oda, trying to make him a "good man." Who on earth is he? What is his true purpose? Devoted to and pushed around by a mysterious man. A startling 94 minutes.
title:Marcel the Shell with Shoes On: A talked-about film that adapts short films sequentially released by amateur filmmaker Dean Fleischer-Camp into a feature-length movie. It depicts the adventures of Marcel, a small shell, in a mockumentary style combining live-action and stop-motion animation.
title:Mark Antony: This Indian sci-fi action film comically and eccentrically depicts a gangster's son who obtains a phone that allows him to talk to people in the past and tries to rewrite fate. In 1975, mad scientist Chiranjeevi invents a telephone that can call people in the past. Using it, he can avert disasters about to befall his past self or loved ones, or make choices that lead to profit. However, Chiranjeevi gets caught in a gang war at a bar while celebrating, and the phone goes missing. Twenty years later, auto mechanic Mark stumbles upon the phone and learns its special abilities and how to use it. This phone eventually sparks a massive upheaval involving Mark's foster father, gang boss Jackie; Jackie's son Madan; and Mark's deceased father, Antony. In Japan, Vishal plays dual roles as mechanic Mark and his gangster father Antony, while S. J. Surya, known for "Jigarthanda Double X," co-stars as Antony's partner Jackie.
title:Marty Supreme: A drama starring Timothée Chalamet, set in 1950s New York, inspired by the life of real-life table tennis player Marty Reisman. Marty Mauser, who dreams of becoming the world's number one table tennis player in America where the sport has low popularity, works at a relative's shoe store to raise funds to participate in the World Championships. After losing to Japanese player Endo at the World Championships held in London, Marty aims to compete in the next World Championships in Japan. With his mistress Rachel pregnant, his player eligibility revoked by the table tennis association, and his funds running out, Marty tries every possible way to raise money for the trip... Gwyneth Paltrow plays Kay, a retired famous actress; Grammy-winning artist Tyler Okonma, known as Tyler, The Creator, plays Marty's friend; Odessa A'zion plays Marty's girlfriend; Kevin O'Leary plays Milton, Kay's husband and president of an ink company; and Japanese Deaflympics table tennis representative Kōto Kawaguchi plays Japanese player Endo. Directed by Josh Safdie ("Uncut Gems," "Good Time"), the film was nominated for nine Academy Awards at the 98th ceremony, including Best Picture, Best Director, and Best Actor.
title:Martyrs:
Pain and salvation. Rejection and worship. Despair, and then ecstasy. The world's fastest theatrical release—you will become a "witness" to film history. Since its French release in 2008, 'Martyrs' has sparked controversy with its brutally intense depictions, while leading audiences to an unpredictable conclusion that borders on the sublime, igniting fierce debate worldwide. The pinnacle of the "French horror" movement that dominated an era, and the masterpiece of the eccentric genius director Pascal Laugier, now revived in the Reiwa era with a 4K digital remaster in the world's fastest theatrical release. The origin of Laugier's consistent portrayal of women with the conviction to face despair, this film pushes terror and philosophical depth to their absolute limits, venturing into realms beyond human comprehension. Even 18 years later, it remains undimmed, continuing to exert immense influence on contemporary French filmmakers including Coralie Fargeat's 'The Substance' and Julia Ducournau's 'TITANE'. What awaits beyond the pain swirling with conflicting emotions is an unknown realm no other film has ever reached. *Please note: This theater will screen the 2K version.
France in the early 1970s. A missing girl named Lucie is found wandering the streets, battered and emaciated. She had been imprisoned, tortured, and abused by someone for a long time, and escaped on her own. However, there were no signs of sexual abuse, and the motive for the crime remained unknown... 15 years later, one morning, a doorbell suddenly rings at a peaceful family home surrounded by forest. When the homeowner opens the door, Lucie (Mylène Jampanoï) stands there with a hunting rifle. Convinced she has finally found the person who abused her, she pulls the trigger of revenge. Anna (Morjana Alaoui), Lucie's best friend, receives a phone call from her and rushes to the house, turning away in horror at the carnage. The two set about disposing of the bodies and preparing to leave. But then, they are confronted with an unimaginable truth.
Admission: General/Student/Senior 1,700 yen, HC discount 1,000 yen. *Other discounts, various invitation and courtesy tickets, and T-tickets cannot be used.
title:Masters of the Universe: A new live-action film adaptation of the popular "Masters of the Universe" series, based on the action figures created by Mattel in 1981, which have been expanded across comics, animation, and other media, and previously adapted into the 1987 live-action film "Masters of the Universe" starring Dolph Lundgren. Prince Adam of the planet Eternia is sent to Earth as a child to protect him from war, and grows up hiding his identity. Fifteen years later, guided by the legendary Power Sword he accidentally discovers, he returns to his homeworld and learns that Eternia is under the control of his archenemy Skeletor. To save Eternia and its people, Adam transforms into the warrior He-Man and plunges into a deadly battle against the forces of evil. Directed by Travis Knight ("Bumblebee", "Kubo and the Two Strings"), with a screenplay by Chris Butler ("Missing Link"). Nicholas Galitzine, who has gained attention for roles in "Red, White & Royal Blue" and "The Idea of You", plays the lead role of Adam/He-Man. Camila Mendes ("The Revenge Swap", "Upgraded") plays the warrior Teela, who fights alongside He-Man; Jared Leto ("Tron: Ares") plays the villain Skeletor; and Idris Elba plays Man-At-Arms, a father figure to He-Man, in a star-studded cast.
title:Materialists: A love story directed and written by Celine Song of 'Past Lives,' set in the modern marriage market, depicting a love triangle with beautiful imagery. Lucy, a matchmaker at a New York dating agency, is a professional at matching clients' high ideals and detailed conditions, and a materialist who judges love not only by emotion but also by asset value. Leading a busy, work-focused life, she receives a passionate approach from Harry, a wealthy investor she meets at the wedding of a couple she matched. Meanwhile, at the same reception, Lucy reunites with her ex-boyfriend John, who was working as a waiter. They had loved each other, but she couldn't endure the poor life with John, who was drifting between part-time jobs while pursuing his dream of becoming an actor. Lucy begins a relationship with Harry, who is perfect in family background, personality, and education, but her feelings for John, who hasn't given up on his dream, are rekindled. When a client gets involved in an incident, Lucy finds herself at a crossroads in both work and love. Dakota Johnson of the 'Fifty Shades' series plays protagonist Lucy, Chris Evans of the 'Captain America' series plays struggling actor John, and Pedro Pascal of 'Welcome to Eddington' plays investor Harry.
title:Mazinger Z vs The Great Dark Gener: A theatrical version of the TV anime "Mazinger Z," featuring a piloted giant robot as the protagonist. Director Nobutaka Nishizawa heightened the drama by entrusting the robot with the protagonist's worries and pain, depicting the invincible Mazinger Z fighting while battered and broken. The surprise appearance of the successor Great Mazinger, ahead of the TV series, astonished children. "Mazinger Z" achieved strong revenue from merchandise licensing, sparking a trend of incorporating merchandising into projects from the planning stage onward.
title:Medea: Directed by Pier Paolo Pasolini, the Italian polymath known as a poet, writer, and filmmaker, this film adapts the Greek tragedy 'Medea' starring Maria Callas, the iconic 20th-century soprano. Jason, the orphaned son of the King of Iolcus, demands the return of the throne from his uncle Pelias, who usurped it. Pelias sets the condition that Jason must retrieve the Golden Fleece from the barbaric land of Colchis. On his journey, Jason wins the heart of Medea, the daughter of the King of Colchis, and brings back the fleece. However, the promise of the throne is broken, and Jason flees with Medea to neighboring Corinth. There, favored by the king, Jason abandons Medea and becomes engaged to the king's daughter. Betrayed, Medea vows revenge. In March 2022, the film had a revival screening as part of the special program 'Pasolini Film Speciale 1 & 2' (at Human Trust Cinema Yurakucho, Shinjuku Musashino Hall, and others).
title:Melody: A coming-of-age love story about the first love of an 11-year-old boy and girl, which became a huge hit in Japan along with the theme song 'Melody Fair' by the Bee Gees. Daniel, a shy boy attending a London public school, is best friends with his rambunctious classmate Tom, and they always play together. One day after school, while peeking at the girls' ballet practice, Daniel's heart is captured by a girl named Melody. They are drawn to each other and eventually promise to get married... The screenplay was written by Alan Parker, who later directed films such as 'Midnight Express' and 'Mississippi Burning.' A digital remastered version was re-released in June 2019.
title:Memories of Origin: Hiroshi Sugimo: A documentary that provides the first long-term, in-depth look at Hiroshi Sugimoto, a world-renowned photographer and artist who has won numerous awards in Japan and abroad. The film follows Sugimoto as he works across borders, from his home base in New York to Japan, the South of France, and Sydney. It reveals his true character and what he strives for in his art. Originally broadcast on WOWOW in 2010 as "The Memory of Origins: Contemporary Artist Hiroshi Sugimoto," this theatrical version incorporates newly filmed footage.
title:Memorizu: Starring Tasuku Emoto, this drama explores themes of family memory and records. Yuta, who lives with his wife and daughter in Tokyo, travels to a rural town in Kyushu to care for his father-in-law Makoto, who has broken his leg, until he recovers. While helping out at Makoto's old-fashioned photo studio, Yuta exchanges videos taken on his smartphone with his wife and daughter back in Tokyo. Even without major events, the accumulation of daily trivial records and memories quietly and vividly reveals the long span of a family's life. Moka Kamishiraishi ("Shōgun," "Girl Encounters") plays Yuta's wife Yuki, who continues working and raising their child in Tokyo. Issey Ogata plays Makoto, the taciturn father-in-law, and Yū Kashii plays a character symbolizing precious family memories. Director Miu Sakanishi, who gained attention for short films while at Kyoto University of Art and Design and later worked as an assistant director for Yūya Ishii and a making-of cameraman for Yūichirō Doi, makes her feature-length directorial debut.
title:Memory Door: A human drama that portrays the pure love between a woman facing early-onset dementia and a young man who has lived his life obeying his parents, while incorporating social themes such as dementia, young caregivers, and human dignity. Kazuya, a 27-year-old office worker, is a so-called obedient child who always listens to his parents. He lives a stable life meeting their expectations, but feels a sense of emptiness somewhere in his heart. One day, he happens to visit a "dementia café" and meets Reiko, a woman 20 years his senior. Despite suffering from early-onset dementia, Reiko's smile lights up those around her, and Kazuya is captivated. Witnessing Reiko facing her loneliness, he is drawn to her strength and human vulnerability. This encounter frees Kazuya from the rails laid by his parents, and for the first time in his life, he discovers true love. Directed and written by Etsuo Kato, whose 2023 film "Three Souls" was screened and won awards at numerous film festivals including the Tanabe-Benkei Film Festival. Minehiro Kinomoto and Shinobu Tsuji, who also appeared in "Three Souls," play Kazuya and Reiko respectively. Winner of the Grand Prix at the 20th Nakajima Film Festival.
title:Merrily We Roll Along: A filmed recording of the Broadway musical 'Merrily We Roll Along,' which won four Tony Awards, screened in theaters. Based on the play of the same name by George S. Kaufman and Moss Hart, this musical, which premiered in 1981, features music by the legendary Stephen Sondheim, creator of numerous masterpieces including 'Sweeney Todd.' The story depicts the tumultuous 30-year relationship between Frank, a successful Hollywood producer; Mary, a former best-selling author; and Charlie, a Pulitzer Prize-winning playwright, told in reverse chronological order. This recording captures the 2023–24 Broadway production starring Maria Friedman, which was a huge hit. Jonathan Groff, known for the Netflix series 'Mindhunter' and as the voice of Kristoff in Disney's 'Frozen,' plays producer Frank; Daniel Radcliffe of the 'Harry Potter' series plays playwright Charlie; and Lindsay Mendez, a veteran of numerous Broadway musicals, plays former best-selling author Mary. At the 2024 Tony Awards, the production won Best Revival of a Musical, Best Actor in a Musical (Jonathan Groff), Best Featured Actor in a Musical (Daniel Radcliffe), and Best Orchestrations.
title:Message from Space: A bandwagon film made by Kinji Fukasaku during the Star Wars boom. Though the story is simplistic, borrowing from the Tale of the Eight Dog Warriors, it generated buzz with the casting of Vic Morrow and the construction of a full-scale replica of the Riave ship. While the special effects fall short compared to Star Wars, the chase scenes created without compositing were highly praised overseas. The planet Jirusia in the Andromeda Galaxy has been transformed into a "Planet Fortress" by the invading Gabanas Empire, led by Emperor Roxeia XII. Jirusia's Great Chief Kido seeks a hero of miraculous salvation, releasing eight "Sacred Riave Fruits" into space and instructing his granddaughter Emeralida and two warriors, Urokko, to pursue the fruits and retrieve the hero. However, Roxeia launches pursuit warships without delay. The Riave fruits reach five individuals on the Earth Federation colony planet Miraseria: Galda, a former general who resigned in disillusionment; Shiro and Aron, young space bikers; Jack, a thug; and Meia, a wealthy heiress. The youths find Emeralida's damaged ship while collecting "Space Fireflies" and rescue her and Urokko, but are bewildered by their mission. Galda returns the fruit and declines to join. Shiro and the others, keeping Meia in the dark, lie about introducing other heroes and sell Emeralida to an old woman seeking a bride for her son. The old woman and Emeralida are later captured by Gabanas pursuit forces. Meia, furious upon learning of their actions, inspires the repentant youths to prepare for Jirusia's rescue. They modify Meia's space boat to carry Shiro and Aron's small craft and head for Jirusia. Along the way, they are joined by Hans, a Gabanas man who holds a Riave fruit and is the rightful heir to the Gabanas throne, usurped by Roxeia. Meanwhile, Gabanas, captivated by Earth's beauty, demands unconditional surrender from the Earth Federation. Amid the chaos, Shiro and his six companions, now reunited with Galda, infiltrate the Gabanas fortress to destroy the planet fortress and rescue Emeralida. Gathering the remaining two allies, the eight confront Roxeia.
title:Michael: A biographical film depicting the life of Michael Jackson, the "King of Pop," beloved across eras and borders for his overwhelming vocal ability and innovative dance performances. Directed by Antoine Fuqua of "Training Day" and "The Equalizer" series, it portrays Michael's story—how he transcended music to greatly impact the world—alongside his many hit songs. Michael Jackson, under his ambitious father Joseph's strict training, achieved early success as a member of the Jackson 5. Meeting legendary producer Quincy Jones, he created numerous historic hits as a solo artist and quickly became the darling of his era. But behind the glory lay the loneliness of a precocious genius, the shackles of his authoritarian father, and the struggle between his love for his family and the visions overflowing within him. The film stars Michael's real-life nephew Jaafar Jackson as Michael, with Juliano Krue Valdi as young Michael, Colman Domingo as father Joseph, Nia Long as mother Katherine, Kendrick Sampson as Quincy Jones, and Miles Teller as longtime lawyer John Branca. The screenplay was written by John Logan of "Gladiator," and the film was produced by Graham King of "Bohemian Rhapsody."

title:Mid-August Commotion: On August 6, 1945, the atomic bomb was dropped on Hiroshima, and Japan's defeat became all but certain. The Prime Minister's secretary, Nakajima, sounds out senior statesmen about accepting the Potsdam Declaration. But this peace faction's moves provoke the resistance-minded military officers. Unable to persuade the army and out of options, the Prime Minister petitions for an Imperial Conference to be held.
title:Millennium Actress: Director Satoshi Kon of 'Perfect Blue' crafts an original feature-length animation depicting an actress who has cherished a man for decades, transcending time and space. Tachibana, the president of a small video production company, visits the secluded estate of Chiyoko Fujiwara, a legendary Showa-era actress who once dominated the silver screen, to produce a documentary about her. Chiyoko, who vanished from cinema thirty years ago and has lived in seclusion, begins to recount her memories upon seeing a single key Tachibana brings. Her narrative soon blurs the lines between reality and film episodes, unfolding into a tumultuous tale. At the 5th Agency for Cultural Affairs Media Arts Festival, it won the Grand Prize in the animation division alongside Hayao Miyazaki's 'Spirited Away.' It also received the Best Asian Film award at the 33rd Sitges Film Festival, earning high acclaim domestically and internationally, and was distributed worldwide by DreamWorks.
title:Milton Bituca Nascimento: Called the 'Voice of Brazil,' Milton Nascimento, affectionately known as Bituca, led MPB (Brazilian popular music post-bossa nova) alongside contemporaries Gilberto Gil, Caetano Veloso, and Chico Buarque, and collaborated with countless international musicians. This documentary film traces Milton's life and music while following his global farewell concert tour, announced upon turning 80 in 2022. In the first half, Milton's troupe tours Europe and the Americas, receiving ecstatic welcomes. Pat Metheny, Spike Lee, Quincy Jones, and Wayne Shorter speak about Milton, and there are scenes of collaboration with Esperanza Spalding and Herbie Hancock. Milton reflects on his childhood raised as an adopted son, converses with his own adopted child on the road, and shares memories of his benefactor, singer Elis Regina. The second half begins with the landscapes of Minas Gerais, the highland region of inland Brazil that is Milton's home and musical origin. Friends like Chico, Caetano, and Gil, collaborating poets like Márcio Borges and Ronaldo Bastos, and younger musicians who admire Milton, discuss the appeal and depths of his music. Inescapable negative histories, such as racism and Brazil's 20-year military dictatorship starting in 1964, are also revealed. Then, the farewell concert finale approaches: the concert at Mineirão, the football stadium in Belo Horizonte, the capital of Minas Gerais. Members of Clube da Esquina (Corner Club), the title of a landmark 1972 album and the name for the family of Minas musicians centered around Milton—Lô Borges, Beto Guedes, Wagner Tiso, and Toninho Horta—share behind-the-scenes stories and perform together.
title:Minions & Monsters: The third installment in the 'Minions' animated film series, an adventure comedy featuring the popular characters born from Illumination's 'Despicable Me' franchise as the main protagonists. The Minions, continuing their quest for the most powerful and evil boss, arrive in Hollywood, the city of dreams. Getting into a movie studio by chance, they eagerly decide to make their own monster movie and attempt to summon a real monster. The first to appear is an unexpectedly small green monster, but soon, extremely dangerous monsters are unleashed upon the city one after another, throwing Hollywood into chaos. Adding to the mayhem, a rift forms among the Minions themselves, putting them in an unprecedented crisis. Directed by Pierre Coffin, known for the 'Minions' and 'Despicable Me' series. The screenplay is co-written by Brian Lynch, who worked on Illumination's 'Pets' series, and Coffin. In the Japanese dub, Matsudaira Ken voices film director Max, Chiba Yudai voices the new boss candidate Dott, Suzuki Airi voices Debbie, who falls in love with Dott, and Yamadera Koichi voices the mysterious monster Goomy. Comedy duo 'Batterys' members Ace and Ie are cast as the unique monsters Phillips and Howard, marking their voice acting debut. Additionally, singer LiSA joins the dub cast as a Hollywood actress.
title:Mirai 運命の戦士: Released in India in September 2025, this film stunned audiences with its phenomenal VFX quality and unprecedented action sequences incorporating the ancient Indian staff martial art 'Karra Saamu', sparking a social phenomenon across India. In ancient times, Emperor Ashoka, having experienced the tragic Kalinga War, sealed forbidden wisdom capable of transforming humans into god-like beings within the 'Nine Scriptures (Grantha)'. Fearing their misuse, the king ordered that these immensely powerful scriptures be secretly protected through the shadows of history by nine chosen nameless warriors. Fast forward to the present day. Mahavir Rahma, known as 'Black Sword', the most sinister enemy and leader of an evil cult plotting to shroud the world in eternal darkness 'Eclipse', begins to move. He eliminates guardians one after another to gain immortality and seizes the scriptures. As the world teeters on the brink of despair, guided by the threads of destiny as the last hope, is Veda—a lonely young man living in the underworld. Unaware of the secret of his own birth, he meets loved ones and confronts harsh truths, beginning to awaken as the legendary warrior 'Super Yoda', destined to protect the scriptures. Armed with the godly bow 'Kodanda' and wielding ancient Indian staff techniques and supernatural abilities, can Veda shatter the ambitions of the overwhelmingly powerful Black Sword? The mysteries of history transcending time and space, and the fierce battle for the fate of the world, now begin. The awakening of the guardian, the start of a legend.
title:Miss Oyu: A commentary: The man who is a match for the younger sister becomes drawn to the older sister who sits in on the arranged meeting... This is Mizoguchi's first film at Daiei, which produced numerous masterpieces during its golden age. Collaborating for the first time with the renowned cinematographer Miyagawa, it delicately depicts the shifting love triangle between two beautiful sisters and one man with a dreamlike visual beauty.
title:Moana: A musical adventure that is a live-action adaptation of the 2016 Disney animated feature 'Moana', which follows the journey of a young girl named Moana who shares a special bond with the ocean as she sets out on an adventure to save the world. On the mystical South Pacific island of Motunui, 16-year-old Moana, who loves the ocean and her people more than anyone and was raised as the pride of her family, is told by her grandmother Tala the truth of the legend passed down on the island and her destiny. With an evil darkness approaching, Moana, entrusted with a mission as 'the one chosen by the ocean', sets sail on a small canoe across the vast ocean to find the legendary hero Maui and return the heart of the goddess Te Fiti. The role of Moana is played by newcomer Australian actress Catherine Laga'aia, who showcases a powerful singing voice. The role of the demigod hero Maui is reprised by Dwayne Johnson, who voiced the same role in the animated version. Directed by Thomas Kail, who brought the acclaimed Broadway musical 'Hamilton' to the screen, the film uses the immersive visuals unique to live-action cinema and exquisite music to tell the story.
title:Mobuko's Love: Director Taichi Kazama, known for the TV drama "Silent," adapts manga artist Akari Tamura's comic into a live-action film, a love story about the first crushes of "supporting characters" who have quietly lived on the fringes of society. Shy and reserved college student Nobuko Tanaka identifies with the term "mob," meaning crowd, extra, or non-major character, and has lived her life watching from afar as other protagonists shine. Then, she notices Hiroki Irie, a young man working part-time at the same supermarket. Touched by Irie's natural thoughtfulness, Nobuko gradually becomes drawn to him. Through her encounter with Irie, she begins to struggle to break free from the shell that has bound her, and while sometimes confronted with harsh realities, she perseveres with the support of her coworkers. Meanwhile, Irie also notices Nobuko's quiet kindness and looks straight at her. The accumulation of small, everyday moments eventually gives them both the strength to take a step forward. Hiyori Sakurada ("The Diary of a Substitute Lie") plays Nobuko, aka Mobuko, and Taisei Kido ("Yukite Kaeranu") plays Hiroki Irie, the object of her first love. The cast also includes Ikoi Hayase as Nobuko's junior coworker Abe, Erika Karata as senior coworker Shinozaki, Takuya Kusakawa as fellow part-timer and Irie's friend Kaneko, Tsubasa Araki as new part-timer Ono, and Kanji Furutachi as store manager Orihara.
title:Modern Times: A classic comedy masterpiece by Charles Chaplin, who directed, wrote, produced, composed the music for, and starred in it, offering a scathing satire of industrial civilization and capitalist society. Charlie, working in a large factory, goes mad from performing monotonous tasks with the same machine every day and is sent to a hospital. After being discharged, he is mistaken for the leader of a protest march and imprisoned. When proven innocent and freed, he starts working at a shipyard but is quickly fired, leading him to consider ways to return to prison. Eventually, he is arrested for eating without paying and meets a young girl who stole bread in the police van. The heroine is played by Paulette Goddard, Chaplin's partner at the time. This was the first film in which Chaplin spoke on screen and sang his own composition, "Titina." The famous song "Smile" played during the final scene also leaves a lasting impression.
title:Money Kisses: A massive hit released in Vietnam in 2025, drawing approximately 2.56 million viewers and earning around 1.2 billion yen at the box office, ranking among the country's top 10 highest-grossing films of all time. Its universal themes of love, money, family, and life choices resonated with audiences across generations. To reclaim a lost family home filled with memories, Van reluctantly follows a plan devised by her sister Kieu and best friend Thien, approaching two wealthy suitors who are pursuing her. One is a man with calm, mature charm and warmth. The other is young, unconventional, and a playboy. Van eventually discovers her true feelings, but also learns that both men have their own hidden motives for approaching her. Thu Tran, who has been active as a Vietnamese actor and producer, makes her directorial debut while also starring and producing.
title:Monk in Pieces: A documentary exploring the creative life of 83-year-old legendary New York-based artist Meredith Monk. Living in a TriBeCa loft with a turtle, the woman with trademark braids, Meredith Monk, was born on November 20, 1942, and raised in New York. She has worked as a composer, singer, director, choreographer, and performance artist creating various music-theatre works, films, and installations, influencing many musicians. A pioneer of contemporary artistic expression, she treats her voice—spanning over three octaves—as an instrument, continuously pursuing original, genre-transcending expression. The film weaves together extensive archival footage of Monk's stage and performance works with interviews from admirers like Björk and David Byrne, connecting fragments of her 60-year career like a concept album to depict her unique expression and life. It highlights her strong, resilient, and charming persona, having started her career in the male-dominated 1960s and continued her own path despite occasional critical scorn.
title:Monkey Business: The Adventures of: A documentary about Hans and Margret Rey, the couple who created the beloved children's book series "Curious George," cherished worldwide. Hans and Margret, originally from Hamburg, Germany, were living in Paris and creating children's books when they invented the character Curious George, who would become the protagonist of their future bestseller. When World War II began, the Jewish couple fled Paris on bicycles to escape the Nazi invasion, carrying the original illustrations for "Curious George" with them. After the war, they continued their writing careers in New York, protecting the character of George for the rest of their lives. The film portrays their tumultuous lives using a wealth of archival footage, precious original artwork, and handwritten animation. This is the feature-length directorial debut of Ema Yamazaki, acclaimed in Japan and abroad for works like "Elementary School: A Small Society" and "Koshien: Field of Dreams," completed in 2017. It was released in theaters in 2018 as part of the Shinjuku Cinema Qualite special program "Caricolle 2018 / Qualite Fantastic! Cinema Collection 2018." A Japanese dubbed version with narration by Yuuimi Kawai is scheduled for release in 2026.
title:Mononoke the Movie: Chapter III -: The concluding chapter of the theatrical trilogy based on the TV anime "Mononoke," itself a spin-off from the "Bakeneko" segment of the 2006 Fuji TV Noitamina omnibus anime "Ayakashi." It delves into the greatest secret long hidden within the Ooku (the shogun's harem) and depicts the fierce battle between the protagonist, the Medicine Seller, and the most fearsome mononoke of all, the Serpent God, which threatens to shake the Ooku to its foundations. After a deadly struggle with the Medicine Seller, who carries a exorcism sword, and a Tengu umbrella, followed by a decisive battle with the Fire Rat, peace finally seems to have returned to the Ooku. However, the Medicine Seller senses a lingering presence and remains on guard. Around this time, the shogun's official wife, Sachiko, gives birth to a long-awaited son, but the infant soon dies. Sachiko, who had hoped to change her formal marriage to the shogun by bearing an heir, is physically and emotionally exhausted and becomes entangled in a conspiracy that could overturn the Ooku's very existence. Hokuto Mizorogi, the priest of the "Mizusama" faith within the Ooku, watches the events unfold with a solemn expression. At the same time, unnatural earthquakes, as if a giant creature is crawling, occur frequently within the Ooku, and bizarre incidents happen where maids are twisted and crushed to death. Before the Medicine Seller, who rushes to the scene, appears the mononoke Serpent God, taking the form of a giant snake.
title:Monster: Directed by Hirokazu Kore-eda, winner of the Palme d'Or at the Cannes Film Festival for "Shoplifters," this human drama is based on an original screenplay by Yuji Sakamoto, the popular screenwriter known for films like "We Made a Beautiful Bouquet" and the TV drama "The Days of Natsume." The music was composed by Ryuichi Sakamoto, who became the first Japanese to win an Academy Award for Best Original Score for "The Last Emperor" and passed away in March 2023. In a suburban town by a large lake, a single mother who loves her son, a caring schoolteacher, and innocent children live peaceful daily lives. One day, a fight breaks out at school. It seems like an ordinary scuffle between kids, but the accounts of those involved conflict, gradually escalating into a major incident that draws in society and the media. Then, on a stormy morning, the children suddenly vanish. What is the "monster"? This collaboration among leading Japanese creators—Hirokazu Kore-eda, Yuji Sakamoto, and Ryuichi Sakamoto—depicts the conclusion reached through a search for the "monster" from each character's perspective. Alongside Soya Kurokawa and Hinata Hiiragi, who play the two central boys, the film features a stellar cast including Sakura Ando, Eita Nagayama, Mitsuki Takahata, Akihiro Kakuta, Shido Nakamura, and Yuko Tanaka. It was screened in the Competition section of the 76th Cannes Film Festival in 2023, winning the Best Screenplay Award. It also received the Queer Palm, awarded to films dealing with LGBT and queer themes.
title:Monterey Pop: A music documentary recording the 'Monterey International Pop Festival' held in 1967. In June 1967, in the midst of the hippie movement, the 'Monterey International Pop Festival,' which would usher in a new era of rock and roll, was held in Monterey, California. The festival launched the careers of Jimi Hendrix, Janis Joplin, and Otis Redding, and featured numerous artists including Jefferson Airplane, Simon & Garfunkel, The Mamas & the Papas, and The Who, serving as a pioneer of large-scale rock festivals. Directed by D. A. Pennebaker, known for numerous music documentaries such as 'Don't Look Back' and 'Ziggy Stardust,' the film captures legendary moments including Pete Townshend smashing his guitar, Jimi Hendrix burning his guitar, and Cass Elliot being overwhelmed by Janis Joplin's performance.

title:Monument to the Girl's Corps: A war drama depicting the tragedy of the 'Himeyuri Student Corps,' mobilized as nursing staff during the Battle of Okinawa at the end of the Pacific War. Director Toshio Masuda brings together Nikkatsu's golden couple Sayuri Yoshinaga and Mitsuo Hamada to adapt Keiichiro Ishino's novel of the same name. In 1943, in Okinawa, still untouched by the shadow of war, Yonamine Kazuko, a student at the Okinawa Normal School for Girls, enjoys a sports day with her classmates and meets Nishizato Junichiro, a student from the men's normal school. By 1944, the war situation worsens. As Okinawa itself is about to become a battlefield, Kazuko and Junichiro, now engaged in building fortifications, begin to develop feelings for each other. Soon, Saipan falls. Kazuko's mother Hatsu, an elementary school teacher, boards a transport ship to accompany the schoolchildren who have been ordered to evacuate to the mainland, but the ship is sunk and she never returns. In October, the air raids finally begin. A state of total emergency is declared across the island. Female students are sent to the Haebaru Army Hospital as temporary nurses, while male students join the army as part of the Blood and Iron Student Corps.
title:Moon: Sam takes a job that requires him to stay alone on the moon for three years to mine a necessary energy source for Earth. Direct communication with Earth is not permitted, and his only conversation partner is a single artificial intelligence computer. But one day, with only two weeks left until the end of his mission, Sam encounters a person with the same face as his own.
title:Motherland: Set in Lithuania just after its independence, this drama quietly observes memories, conflicts, and the lives of people caught between shifting eras through the eyes of an American-born boy visiting the country with his Lithuanian mother. Director Tomas Vengris, making his feature-length debut, draws on his own experience growing up as the son of Lithuanian immigrants in Washington, D.C., to delicately portray the reality of people tossed about by changes in territory and political systems. In 1992, mother and son Victoria and Kovas arrive from America to Lithuania, which has just gained independence from the Soviet Union. As a child, Victoria was separated from her family under Soviet occupation and lost her home and land. In Lithuania, where control shifted from Nazi Germany to the Soviet Union, people's freedom continued to waver under different regimes. Returning to her homeland after 20 years, Victoria seeks to reclaim her lost family land and start a new life with her son, but finds a Russian family already living there. Faced with the harsh reality that reclaiming the land is not easy, her ideal of a fresh start in Lithuania begins to quietly unravel. Martas Metlevskis, an American-born actor of Lithuanian descent, plays the boy Kovas, and renowned Lithuanian actress Sevilija Janušauskaitė plays his mother Victoria.
title:Mothertongue:
Winner of the Best Director Award and Best Actor Award in the Competition Section of the 38th Tokyo International Film Festival.

A woman who has lost her mother tongue returns home. Dreams, love, memories, and the time of cinema gently unravel—

Chunshu, 37, has lost her way as an aspiring actress and is stuck in her love life. Returning to Chengdu, her former hometown she left twenty years ago, she visits her old acting instructor, Zhang Mei. But Zhang Mei has dementia and is gradually losing her speech. Unable to find a place anywhere, Chunshu is quietly accompanied by Dongdong, Zhang Mei's son who has returned from Shanghai to care for his mother. Like the decaying national film studio that remains in ruins, past glories, teachings, and lessons are gradually forgotten in the flow of time, and days pass quietly beside people stuck in stagnation.

Released simultaneously with its sister film "Twilight in Luomu," shot consecutively with the same cast.
title:Mouchette: Master filmmaker Robert Bresson's eighth feature, made right after his masterpiece "Au Hasard Balthazar." Based on a novel by French author Georges Bernanos, it starkly and realistically depicts the tragic fate of a young girl through rigorous framing and the actors' minimally restrained performances. 14-year-old Mouchette lives in the French countryside, forced to run the household for her alcoholic father and ill mother, while being cruelly treated by classmates and teachers at school. The unfortunate girl's fate takes a turn for the worse when, one rainy night, she encounters a poacher in the forest, sending her spiraling into further misery and ruin. Nadine Nortier, discovered for this role, plays the protagonist Mouchette, a girl standing on the brink of despair yet harboring a rebellious spirit. Produced in 1967, it was first released in Japan in 1974 by Equipe de Cinema, and again in 1995 by France Eiga Sha. A 4K restored digital remastered version had a revival release in October 2020. Another revival release is scheduled for 2026 as part of the "Robert Bresson Masterpiece Selection."
title:Mrs. Warren's Profession: One of the National Theatre Live series, which films and screens selected acclaimed stage productions from the UK's Royal National Theatre in cinemas. This recording captures 'Mrs. Warren's Profession', featuring five-time Laurence Olivier Award winner Imelda Staunton performing alongside her real-life daughter Bessie Carter. Vivie Warren is a young woman with progressive ideas. Her mother, however, while upholding the old patriarchal system, has built a fortune by exploiting that very system. But a heavy price lies hidden behind it all. This play by Irish playwright George Bernard Shaw, known for 'Pygmalion' and a Nobel laureate in Literature, is directed by Dominic Cooke, who has also worked on screen productions such as the BBC series 'The Hollow Crown' and the film 'The Memory of Justice'. The cast also includes Kevin Doyle from 'Downton Abbey' and Robert Glenister from 'Into the Sky'.
title:My Brother's Wedding: A director's cut, completed in 2007 through re-editing, of Charles Burnett's second feature film from 1983. Burnett, an influential figure in American independent cinema who consistently depicts the daily lives and humanity of African Americans, presents a tragicomedy of a working-class young man torn between family, friendship, and identity. It quietly reveals class differences within the Black community, psychological gaps between generations, and the frustration of young people left behind by social success, all from the gaps in everyday life. Pierce, a 30-year-old helping his parents run their dry-cleaning shop, drifts aimlessly through his days with no clear future. His childhood friends are either in prison or already dead. When his brother, a lawyer, marries a woman from a wealthy family, Pierce's discomfort and feelings of inferiority grow. Around this time, Pierce reunites with his best friend Soldier, just released from prison, and finds himself caught between his sense of duty to his family and his loyalty to his friend, forced to make a choice. In Japan, this 4K restored version will have its theatrical premiere at the special screening series 'Charles Burnett: Everyday Blues' (from February 7, 2026, at Theater Image Forum).
title:My God, My God, Why Hast Thou Fors: A near-future drama by director Shinji Aoyama of "EUREKA," depicting people striving to find hope for the future in a world ravaged by a mysterious deadly virus, through the symbol of hope—"sound"—and beautiful imagery. In 2015, "Lemming Disease," which is transmitted through images and inevitably leads to death, has spread worldwide, and people live in despair. Amid this, the only method to suppress the onset of the disease is discovered: listening to the "sound" performed by Mizui and Asuhara. One day, a wealthy man appears before them, asking them to save his granddaughter Hana, who has been infected with Lemming Disease. Mizui is played by Tadanobu Asano, Hana by Aoi Miyazaki, Asuhara by musician Masaya Nakahara, and Hana's grandfather by author Yasutaka Tsutsui. The title "Eri Eri Rema Sabakutani" refers to the last words of Jesus Christ, Hebrew for "My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?" Screened in the Un Certain Regard section at the 58th Cannes Film Festival in 2005.
title:My Grandfather Is a Nihonjin: An animated film based on the novel 'Nihonjin' by Oscar Nakazato, which won the 'Jabuti Prize' in 2012, the most prestigious literary award in Brazil's publishing world, depicting the rich human drama of three generations of Japanese immigrants living in Brazil. Inspired by the visual world of contemporary artist Oscar Oiwa, who expresses sweeping, allegorical perspectives with meticulous detail, it was brought to the screen by the Brazilian animation studio PINGUIM CONTENT. Noboru, a 10-year-old boy who is a third-generation Japanese-Brazilian, is given a school assignment to research his cultural identity and visits his grandfather Hideo. The taciturn Hideo has avoided confronting his past, but begins to tell his life story to Noboru. In the 1920s, 20-year-old Hideo arrived in Brazil after a two-month voyage and struggled daily on an unfamiliar coffee plantation. As Noboru delves deeper into his family's history, he learns of an uncle, Haruo, whom he has never met. Ken Kaneko, a painter and first-generation Japanese immigrant from Yokohama, voices the grandfather Hideo, and Pietro Takeda, an 11-year-old with several years of voice acting experience, voices the grandson Noboru.
title:My Mind Is Always Racing: A film themed around the 'quarter-life crisis,' a psychological state common among people in their late twenties to thirties who feel vague anxiety and restlessness about the future, unable to live the life they imagined. Directed by and starring Reimi Miyamori, it won the Actor Award at the 18th Tanabe Benkei Film Festival, a gateway for independent films. Nozomi, a 25-year-old woman who moved to Tokyo to become a novelist, is struggling and going nowhere. In her mind, 18-year-old Nozomi, living a rural high school life, asks her if she has truly followed through on her words and made it big in Tokyo. While resisting a frustrating life where she wants to change but cannot, the 25-year-old Nozomi confronts her 18-year-old self and begins to notice various things she had never faced before. This is the debut feature film of Reimi Miyamori, a graduate of the Nihon University College of Art's Film Department who began making films during the COVID-19 pandemic. She served as director, screenwriter, producer, and lead actress. It was screened in theaters as part of the 'Tanabe Benkei Film Festival Selection 2024' (May 9 – June 5, 2024 at Theatre Shinjuku / June 20–26, 2024 at Theatre Umeda).
title:My Own Private Idaho: A youth road movie directed early in the career of Gus Van Sant, one of American cinema's leading masters, and notable for the collaboration of River Phoenix and Keanu Reeves. Mike, who suffers from narcolepsy and suddenly loses consciousness when tense, was abandoned by his mother at age 12 and left his hometown of Idaho to live on the streets of Portland, selling his body. Scott, raised without want as the son of Portland's mayor, grew disgusted with his superficial family and ran away from home. After meeting on the streets, the two head to Mike's hometown of Idaho to search for his missing mother, but eventually their paths diverge. River Phoenix, who played Mike, won the Volpi Cup (Best Actor) at the 48th Venice International Film Festival. The film is inspired by William Shakespeare's plays "Henry IV, Part 1," "Henry IV, Part 2," and "Henry V."
title:Mysterious Skin: A youth drama depicting the fates of two boys deeply scarred by childhood sexual abuse. Based on the novel "Mysterious Skin" by Scott Heim, which draws from his own experiences, the film was directed and written by Gregg Araki of "The Doom Generation." In the small Kansas town of Hutchinson. In the summer of 1981, 8-year-old Brian and Neil, teammates on a Little League team, have their lives drastically warped by their coach, who habitually sexually abuses children. Brian, suffering from psychological shock, loses his memory and is plagued by aftereffects, becoming convinced he was abducted by aliens. Neil, on the other hand, believes there was "love" between him and the coach, and spends his life selling his body to older men while searching for a shadow of the coach. Brian, trying to recover his lost memories, discovers that the boy who repeatedly appears in his dreams is Neil... A pre-breakout Joseph Gordon-Levitt plays Neil, and Brady Corbet, who later became a director known for "The Brutalist," plays Brian. The film was not released in Japanese theaters for a long time, finally premiering in April 2025.
title:NEW GROUP: The second theatrical release from director Yuta Shimotsu, who gained attention for his 2024 commercial film debut "May the Lord Be with You". It comically and seriously explores the underlying psychology of human behavior in group activities, specifically through the lens of group gymnastics, with a unique worldview. High school girl Ai, who has family problems, is shy and unable to assert her own opinions. Transfer student Yu, who has returned from overseas, is the type to speak her mind clearly and struggles to fit into the group-oriented, harmony-focused activities of Japanese schools. Ai is interested in Yu, but Yu grows frustrated with Ai's inability to express herself. One day, a student in the schoolyard freezes on all fours. Soon, other students begin lining up beside him in the same position, forming a massive human pyramid. Strangely, the school encourages participation in the human pyramid as a "good thing," and the stacked students all wear serene expressions. As students gather one after another and obey without a word, Ai herself becomes dazed and nearly joins the pyramid. The situation eventually escalates into a collective supernatural phenomenon engulfing the entire region. Anna Yamada (from the "Golden Kamuy" series) plays the protagonist Ai, and Yuzu Aoki (from "5 Centimeters per Second") plays the transfer student Yu. Pierre Taki delivers a bizarre performance as the principal who leads the group. The film won the Special Jury Prize at the 29th Fantasia International Film Festival in 2025.
title:NEWシネマ歌舞伎 四谷怪談: The 28th installment in the "Cinema Kabuki" series, which digitally screens kabuki stage performances in movie theaters. This recording captures the June 2016 performance of the 15th "Cocoon Kabuki," featuring Tsuruya Nanboku's "Tokaido Yotsuya Kaidan" in a new direction and composition by Kushida Kazumi. The production originated in 1994 at Shibuya's Theater Cocoon, led by Nakamura Kanzaburo XVIII, and this was the first program in that series. Iemon, who lives faithfully to his own desires; Naosuke Gonbei; the fleeting moments of men. Osode and Oiwa, toyed with by men; the sorrow of women. Kushida's interpretation of "Yotsuya Kaidan" as a story of instinct and desire that still resonates today is recreated with footage emphasizing the unique sense of presence of a live theater. Nakamura Shido plays Iemon, Nakamura Kankuro plays Naosuke Gonbei, Nakamura Shichinosuke plays Osode, and Nakamura Senjaku plays Oiwa. Along with regular "Cocoon Kabuki" actors like Kataoka Kamezo and Sasano Takashi, the cast also features unconventional choices for kabuki, including Omori Hiroshi and ballet dancer Shuto Yasuyuki.
title:Nagasaki: Memories of My Son: On August 9, 1948, at a midwife's home in Nagasaki, Nobuko is visited by her son Koji, who she had lost three years earlier in the atomic bombing. Stunned by the impossibility, she watches as her already-dead son begins to appear frequently. Koji, who had been aiming to become a doctor, had a fiancée named Machiko with whom he had promised a future.
title:Nameless: A film adaptation of the psycho-violent manga "Nanashi" by Sato Jiro—who is active not only as an actor but also as a screenwriter and film director—marking his first work based on a manga. Sato stars and wrote the script, with Hideo Shijo of "Bad Summer" directing. A brutal murder occurs at a family restaurant in the afternoon. Security cameras capture a bald middle-aged man who appears to be the culprit, but he holds no weapon. The footage records the bizarre sight of people spurting blood and collapsing just from the man approaching and lightly touching them. Investigating police identify the bald man as "Taro Yamada," who was questioned for shoplifting 11 years earlier. When investigators rush to Yamada's home address, they find a decomposed female corpse. Sato plays the protagonist, serial killer Yamada. Takaya Kamikawa plays Teruo, the patrol officer who becomes the namesake for the nameless orphaned young Yamada. MEGUMI plays Hanako Yamada, who grew up with Yamada in the same children's home and lives with him. Kuroudo Yashima plays Detective Kunieda, who works tirelessly to stop Yamada.
title:National Theatre Live: Hamlet: One of the 'National Theatre Live' productions, where the UK's Royal National Theatre films selected acclaimed stage performances for cinema screenings. This recording features 'Hamlet' starring Sri Lankan-born actor Hiran Abeysekara, who won the Laurence Olivier Award for Best Actor for his performance in 'Life of Pi' at the Royal National Theatre. Surrounded by power and privilege, the young Prince Hamlet wavers between duty and doubt. He confronts the ultimate question: 'To be, or not to be.' Directed by Robert Hastie, who became Associate Artistic Director of the Royal National Theatre in January 2025, offering a contemporary perspective on Shakespeare's masterpiece. Co-stars include Alistair Petrie, known for 'The Bank Job' and 'Rush,' Ayesha Dharker, known for 'Star Wars: Episode II – Attack of the Clones,' and Francesca Mills, known for the Netflix series 'The Witcher: Blood Origin.'
title:National Theatre Live: The Fifth S: Part of the 'National Theatre Live' series, which films and screens selected acclaimed stage productions from the UK's Royal National Theatre in cinemas. This recording captures 'The Fifth Step' by David Ireland, directed by Finn den Hartog, performed at the @sohoplace theatre in London's West End. James, who has long worked on the '12 Steps' alcohol recovery program, becomes the sponsor for newcomer Luca. They drink black coffee, share their stories, and build a fragile friendship through shared experiences. But as Luca approaches the fifth step, the 'moment of confession,' a dangerous truth emerges that threatens the very 'trust' that has been the foundation of both their recoveries. Starring Jack Lowden (known for the film 'Dunkirk' and the series 'The Spy') and Martin Freeman (from 'Sherlock,' 'The Hobbit,' and 'Black Panther' series).
title:Nenette and Boni: In the port city of Marseille in southern France. Young Boni works at a pizzeria, spending his days belonging nowhere. One day, his long-estranged younger sister Nenette suddenly appears and crashes at his place. Having nowhere to go, Nenette carries a secret: she is pregnant. But she never reveals this fact to Boni. In their awkward cohabitation, the two spend time maintaining a distance they cannot cross. Boni develops feelings for a woman who works at a bakery, but cannot turn those feelings into reality. Nenette confronts her own body and tries to choose her future. In a cruel world, desire and tenderness quietly transform their relationship. Unspoken emotions slowly seep through.
title:Never Give Up: A massacre occurs deep in the Tohoku mountains, killing most of a village's residents. A self-defense force special unit member, Misawa, who was training in the mountains, happens upon the scene, kills the perpetrator, and rescues the sole survivor—a village girl named Yoriko. Later, after retiring, Misawa adopts Yoriko and works as an insurance salesperson. One day, he rescues a female journalist named Tomoko from an attacker, but she is being targeted because she tried to expose the corruption of a local businessman, Oba. Meanwhile, Detective Kitano, who suspects Misawa of being the massacre killer, continues to shadow him.

title:News from Home: A documentary by Belgian director Chantal Akerman, who revolutionized cinema with 'Jeanne Dielman, 23 quai du Commerce, 1080 Bruxelles,' a portrait of an ordinary housewife's daily routine. In this film, she reads letters from her mother over footage capturing the landscapes of 1970s New York. By layering her mother's affectionate words over the bleak cityscapes of New York—alleyways, cars on avenues, people waiting for trains on station platforms, and underground passages—the film highlights the alienation of urban life and the distance from family far away. In Japan, it received its theatrical premiere at the 'Chantal Akerman Film Festival 2023' (April 7–27, 2023, Human Trust Cinema Shibuya), screened together with 'Saute ma ville.'
title:Nico, 1988: A musical biopic depicting the later years of Nico, the German-born chanteuse of the American rock band The Velvet Underground and muse of pop art pioneer Andy Warhol, who dominated the 1960s scene. Focusing on the two years before her death in 1988 at age 49, it interweaves her stage presence with personal struggles, realistically portraying the loneliness and rebirth behind the glamorous legend. In 1986, Nico, in her late 40s and living alone in England, distances herself from past fame and embarks on a European tour with her new manager Richard and her band. But the journey is harsh, forcing her to confront her unstable psyche, drug addiction, and conflicts with those around her. Burdened by regret and conflict as a mother, she retrieves her son Ari, who is in a French rehabilitation facility for drug addiction and a suicide attempt, and brings him along on tour... Trine Dyrholm (from "Into Eternity") stars as Nico and performs the songs herself. John Gordon Sinclair ("Gregory's Girl") plays manager Richard, and Anamaria Marinca ("4 Months, 3 Weeks and 2 Days") plays violinist Sylvia. Directed by Italian filmmaker Susanna Nicchiarelli, known for "Miss Marx." It won the Best Film award in the Orizzonti section at the 74th Venice International Film Festival in 2017.
title:Night Flower: A human suspense film directed by Eiji Uchida ("Midnight Swan"), starring Keiko Kitagawa. Uchida also wrote the original story and screenplay. It thrillingly depicts a mother, hounded by debt collectors, who steps into a dangerous world to make her children's dreams come true. Natsuki Nagashima, who fled to Tokyo with her two children to escape debt collectors, works desperately day and night but still struggles to afford food for the next day. One day, she witnesses a drug deal in the nightlife district and decides to become a dealer herself. She meets Tamae Yoshii, a fighter carrying deep loneliness, who offers to be her bodyguard. Teaming up, they venture into even more dangerous transactions. However, the death of a female college student sends Natsuki and Tamae's fates spiraling in an unexpected direction. Tomochi Morita (live-action "City Hunter") plays Tamae, the female fighter who becomes Natsuki's bodyguard. Daisuke Sakuma (from the idol group Snow Man) plays Tamae's childhood friend, Kaito Ikeda. Ryuta Shibuya (from the rock band SUPER BEAVER) plays Sato, the drug trafficking boss. The cast also includes Kiyohiko Shibukawa, Rena Tanaka, Hiroyuki Ikeuchi, and Ken Mitsuishi.
title:Night Is Short, Walk On Girl: An animated film adaptation of "The Night is Short, Walk on Girl," an early bestseller by popular author Tomihiko Morimi, known for "The Tatami Galaxy" and "Uchoten Kazoku," which humorously depicts the story of an unremarkable university student who pines for a black-haired maiden. Directed by Masaaki Yuasa, popular for his uniquely expressive animation works including the TV anime "The Tatami Galaxy," "Mind Game," and "Ping Pong The Animation." The screenplay is by Makoto Ueda of the theater troupe Europe Kikaku, who also worked on "The Tatami Galaxy." Singer-songwriter and actor Gen Hoshino, also popular for his role in the drama "We Married as a Job," voices the protagonist. The university student "Senpai," who harbors feelings for "the black-haired maiden," a junior in his club, spends his days executing the "Nakame Strategy" aimed at "getting her to notice him as much as possible." The seasons turn as he gets swept up in strange incidents caused by his colorful friends, but his relationship with the black-haired maiden only progresses around the edges without making real headway...
title:Ninja Wars: Kashin Koji, a mysterious man who appears during the Sengoku period, is a master of various mystical arts, and tales of his sightings and experiences are told in many places. He is summoned by the warlord Matsunaga Hisahide. Hisahide harbors a desire for Miyoshi Yoshiyuki's wife, Ukon no Tsubone, and plots to have his way with her. Kashin proposes a plan to create an "lust stone"—an aphrodisiac capable of melting any woman's heart. It is made by having seven ninja monks under Kashin's command rape women and boiling down the resulting fluids. The sheer horror of this plan leaves the assembled Sen no Rikyū and Yagyū Shinzaemon trembling in fear.
title:Ninomiya Kinjirou: A biographical drama depicting the little-known half-life of Ninomiya Kinjiro, famous for the statue of a boy reading a book while carrying firewood that once stood in many elementary school grounds. Ninomiya Kinjiro lost his parents and spent his childhood living apart from his siblings. As a young man, Kinjiro is entrusted with the restoration of the Sakurama domain (present-day Moka City, Tochigi Prefecture) by the Odawara domain. Kinjiro works on village restoration using his own original methods, but faces strong opposition from conservative villagers. Meanwhile, the Odawara domain dispatches the samurai Toyoda Shosaku, who begins various acts of obstruction against Kinjiro's measures, claiming "Kinjiro is destroying order." Kinjiro is played by Masahito Goda, known for the drama "Mito Komon," with a cast including Misato Tanaka, Riri Narita, Vino Inuyama, Takaaki Enoki, Shingo Yanagisawa, Min Tanaka, Ikkei Watanabe, Kenjiro Ishimaru, and Katsuhiko Watabiki. Directed by Takumi Saitoh, known for "Sayonara, Mine" and "Five for Freedom."
title:Ninotchka: A romantic comedy featuring the divinely beautiful Greta Garbo in a comedic performance. The Soviets try to sell jewels confiscated from aristocrats, while the aristocrats are determined to stop them. The man and woman who become their respective agents end up falling in love.
title:Niñxs: A documentary by transgender director Kani Lapuerta, recording eight years in the life of a transgender elementary school student in Mexico as she grows into a teenager. In Tepoztlán, a town south of Mexico City, 15-year-old Carla talks with director Kani Lapuerta in a secret cocoon. They discuss what kind of film they want to make, and begin to look back on Carla's life chronologically from her elementary school days. The schoolyard where she couldn't line up with either the 'boys' or 'girls,' the bedroom where she endlessly practiced makeup, the morning school reopened during the pandemic, the city hall where she officially changed her name, the slogans she shouted at the Pride March, and the baton club she admired. Watched over by her punk and hippie chef parents, her friends, director Lapuerta, the queer community, and the sacred rocky mountain, Carla encounters various versions of herself. Director Kani Lapuerta also appears in the film, gradually sharing her inner thoughts with Carla like an exchange diary. With comedic touches, it portrays the struggles and fluctuations of adolescence growing up in a small town with strong gender stereotypes.
title:No Other Choice: Korean master filmmaker Park Chan-wook, winner of the Grand Prix at Cannes for "Oldboy" and Best Director for "Decision to Leave," directs this suspense drama laced with irony and black humor about a salaryman whose life is turned upside down by a sudden layoff. Park reunites with Lee Byung-hun, who starred in his breakthrough film "Joint Security Area," for the first time in 21 years. Man-su, an ordinary salaryman at a paper company, lives with his wife, two children, and two dogs, believing he has everything he could want. But his life changes drastically when he is suddenly fired from the company he has worked for for 25 years. His job search drags on for over a year, and he is forced to sell his beloved home. Desperate, Man-su walks into a rapidly growing paper company with his resume, only to be flatly rejected. Convinced he is the most qualified person for the company, he makes a decision: if there's no opening, he'll have to create one himself. The film is based on the novel "The Ax" by Donald E. Westlake, which was also adapted into a film by Costa-Gavras. Lee Byung-hun plays the increasingly cornered Man-su, and Son Ye-jin of "Crash Landing on You" plays his wife Mi-ri, who grows stronger as the crisis deepens. The film was selected for the competition section of the 82nd Venice International Film Festival in 2025 and won the newly established International Audience Award (for non-North American films) at the 50th Toronto International Film Festival.
title:Nobody Knows: Keiko (YOU) and four children, including Akira (Yagira), live in a single apartment room under false pretenses. When Keiko eventually stops coming home, the children are left to fend for themselves, but their financial situation gradually becomes dire. Inspired by a real-life child abandonment case, the film delicately portrays modern social issues such as neglect, young carers, and those who fall through the cracks of the welfare system, earning high international acclaim.
title:Nothing But Bones: In the late Meiji period, a poor farmer's daughter is sold as a prostitute to the Suzaki pleasure quarters. A fierce masterpiece of women's cinema by Tai Kato, depicting the sorrow and resilience of women exploited to the bone.
title:Notre Musique: A feature film by French master Jean-Luc Godard, shot in the war-torn city of Sarajevo as a prayer for world peace. Based on Dante's epic poem 'The Divine Comedy,' it is structured in three parts: 'Hell,' 'Purgatory,' and 'Paradise.' Visiting Sarajevo for a lecture, Godard finds a historical crossroads in the rebuilding city, which is also a history of human conflict and massacre. Using the asymmetry between Israel and Palestine, and Judaism and Islam as examples, Godard discusses the dominant structures of conflict in the world. 'Hell' is composed of montages of war footage; 'Purgatory' depicts the interaction between Godard, invited to Sarajevo for a lecture, and a female student named Olga; and 'Paradise' shows the peaceful world Olga reaches after her death. Godard appears as himself, along with Palestinian poet Mahmoud Darwish and Spanish novelist Juan Goytisolo, who appear under their real names. The 4K restored version will be screened in Japan for the first time as part of the special screening series 'Jean-Luc Godard in the 21st Century: Our Films 2001-2010' (starting June 20, 2026, at Theater Image Forum Shibuya and other locations nationwide).

title:Nouvelle Vague: From the director of "Boyhood" and the "Before" series, Richard Linklater, comes a film that goes behind the scenes of Jean-Luc Godard's "Breathless"—a landmark work of the French New Wave, the revolutionary film movement that emerged in the late 1950s. It depicts the young people who sparked a revolution in film history, along with their vibrant interactions with the leading filmmakers of French cinema. In 1959, France. Jean-Luc Godard, a 28-year-old critic writing for the film magazine "Cahiers du Cinéma," begins production on his feature directorial debut, "Breathless," starring French up-and-coming actor Jean-Paul Belmondo and American starlet Jean Seberg. Those around him are thrown off by Godard's innovative and freewheeling shooting methods, but the set, fueled by a shared passion for filmmaking, is filled with energy. Following the style of "Breathless," the film is shot in black and white in the Academy ratio (1:1.37), almost entirely in French, and the cast, except for Zoey Deutch as Jean Seberg, is made up of mostly unknown actors. Guillaume Marbeck, who worked as a photographer and model, was cast as the protagonist Godard. The film was selected for the Competition section of the 78th Cannes Film Festival in 2025.

Nenette confronts her own body and tries to choose her future. In a cruel world, desire and tenderness quietly transform their relationship. Unspoken emotions slowly seep through.
title:Nụ Hôn Bạc Tỷ: A massive hit released in Vietnam in 2025, drawing approximately 2.56 million viewers and earning around 1.2 billion yen at the box office, ranking among the country's top 10 highest-grossing films of all time. Its universal themes of love, money, family, and life choices resonated with audiences across generations. To reclaim a lost family home filled with memories, Van reluctantly follows a plan devised by her sister Kieu and best friend Thien, approaching two wealthy suitors who are pursuing her. One is a man with calm, mature charm and warmth. The other is young, unconventional, and a playboy. Van eventually discovers her true feelings, but also learns that both men have their own hidden motives for approaching her. Thu Tran, who has been active as a Vietnamese actor and producer, makes her directorial debut while also starring and producing.
title:O-Bi, O-Ba: The End of Civilizatio: One of four dark sci-fi works by Piotr Szulkin, a pioneer of dystopian science fiction in Poland, created under the socialist regime in the late 1970s and 1980s. With a style blending fierce satire and extreme surrealism, the film explores the theme of "escape from totalitarianism." In a world devastated by nuclear war, the planet is frozen, and radiation kills anyone who ventures outside the dome. A man who controls the last surviving humans walks among the crowds, preventing morale from collapsing, seducing prostitutes, suppressing rebellions, and occasionally feeding the hungry. But as the true evil nature of the dome becomes clear, he begins to question whether humanity is worth saving. The film had its Japanese theatrical premiere in 2026 as part of the special screening series "Polish Dark Sci-Fi: The End of Civilization Tetralogy" (starting February 21, 2026, at Theater Image Forum).
title:O-bi, o-ba. Koniec cywilizacji: One of four dark sci-fi works by Piotr Szulkin, a pioneer of dystopian science fiction in Poland, created under the socialist regime in the late 1970s and 1980s.
