title:OBSESSION: The film 'Obsession: Disaster Love' has been sweeping film festivals around the world and generating fervent buzz on social media even before its release. It had its world premiere in the 'Midnight Madness' section of the 50th Toronto International Film Festival, winning second place in the Audience Award. It subsequently achieved three awards at the Sitges International Fantastic Film Festival, quickly becoming a hot topic among genre film fans. The trailer has been viewed over 1.7 million times on social media, and it holds a 95% Fresh rating on Rotten Tomatoes (as of May 25, 2026). After its US release, with a production budget of under $1 million, it grossed over $17 million in its opening weekend. Furthermore, in its second week, it rose in the rankings to second place, just behind 'Star Wars: The Mandalorian & Grogu' released that week, achieving an extraordinary hit with a cumulative box office (May 15-24) of over $50 million.
title:OXANA 裸の革命家・オクサナ:
2002, Khmelnytskyi, Western Ukraine. Oksana lives with her alcoholic father and her mother who devotedly supports him, earning a living for the family by painting icons. However, unable to endure the unfair treatment from the church and the deep-seated misogyny of an irrational society, she flees her home.

In 2008, she forms the feminist activist group "FEMEN" alongside comrades she met during street debates. Their activities expand, beginning with a protest against the death of a female patient due to medical malpractice. In 2009, while campaigning to eradicate sex tourism in the capital city of Kyiv, Oksana strips to the waist to garner attention, arriving at a mode of expression that utilizes the body as "combat gear."

Before long, their activism crosses borders. In 2011, she is detained and tortured for protesting the Alexander Lukashenko regime in Minsk, Belarus, and later sustains serious injuries during a protest against Vladimir Putin in Moscow. As surveillance and suppression of FEMEN intensify, Oksana is forced to make the decision to flee to Paris as a political refugee...
title:OXANA／裸の革命家・オクサナ: 2002, Khmelnytskyi, Western Ukraine. Oksana lives with her alcoholic father and her mother, who devotedly supports him. She helps provide for the family by painting icons, but unable to endure the unfair treatment from the church and the injustices of a deeply patriarchal society, she flees her home. In 2008, alongside comrades she met at street debates, she co-founds the feminist activist group "FEMEN." Their activities expand, beginning with a protest against the death of a female patient caused by medical malpractice. In 2009, while campaigning to eradicate sex tourism in the capital, Kyiv, Oksana strips to the waist to draw attention, arriving at a form of expression that uses the body as "combat gear." Their activism eventually crosses borders. In 2011, she is detained and tortured while protesting the Alexander Lukashenko regime in Minsk, Belarus, and later suffers serious injuries during a protest against Vladimir Putin in Moscow. As surveillance and suppression of FEMEN intensify, Oksana is forced to make the decision to flee to Paris as a political refugee...
title:Occult: Kōji Shiraishi, the horror master known for "Noroi" and "Kuchisake-onna," delivers an ambitious work depicting the thrills and terrors of people producing an occult documentary program. Director Kiyoshi Kurosawa of "Akarui Mirai" and "Tokyo Sonata," and manga artist Peco Watanabe make special appearances. Film director Shiraishi, intrigued by a random murder that occurred at a tourist spot three years earlier, conducts an interview with Eno, the sole survivor of the incident, who is now a net café refugee.
title:Oldboy: Oh Dae-su, a man living an ordinary life, regains consciousness to find himself locked in a small, confined room. After 15 years of imprisonment without knowing why, he is suddenly released. Who did this?! For what purpose?! With the help of a young woman named Mi-do, Dae-su vows revenge. A mysterious man named Woo-jin appears before him and proposes a deadly "game": Dae-su must uncover the reason for his imprisonment within five days, with both their lives at stake. An unimaginable and terrifying scheme lies behind it all...
title:On Falling: This human drama depicts the loneliness and division in modern society through the daily life of an immigrant woman working in a massive logistics center in Scotland, ultimately finding a faint glimmer of hope. Aurora, a Portuguese immigrant, works as a picker in a huge logistics center on the outskirts of Scotland. Her days are mostly spent walking through countless aisles following scanner instructions and retrieving items from shelves. Conversations with colleagues are limited to brief breaks, and after her shift, she drags her tired body back to a shared house for immigrant workers. Interactions among residents are superficial, relationships never deepen, and her rootless days continue monotonously. One day, Aurora accidentally breaks her smartphone. Losing this modern necessity—her means of workplace communication and her "companion" for passing time—slowly but surely begins to change her daily life. Portuguese-born, Scotland-based Laura Carreira wrote and directed her first feature film based on her own experiences as an immigrant, winning the Best Director Award at the 72nd San Sebastián International Film Festival in 2024.
title:Once We Were Us: Summer 2008, Seoul. University students Uno and Jeong-won meet fatefully on a long-distance bus. Uno, who dreams of becoming a game creator, and Jeong-won, who aspires to be an architect. Supporting each other through their urban days filled with dreams and anxieties, they eventually fall in love, deeply and truly. However, faced with the harshness of reality that youth cannot resist, they choose to part ways. Ten years later, in the summer of 2024, they coincidentally reunite on a flight to Seoul. As they look back on their memories, Uno asks Jeong-won a question he has kept buried deep in his heart: 'What if, back then...'
title:One Last Throw: This film traces the life of former professional baseball player Shintaro Yokota, who was drafted second by the Hanshin Tigers and expected to have a bright future, but was forced to retire at age 21 after being diagnosed with a brain tumor. It stars Taya Matsutani and Kyoka Suzuki. In the 2013 draft, 18-year-old Shintaro Yokota was selected second by the Hanshin Tigers. In the opening game of 2016, he was chosen as a starter for the first team and recorded his first hit, with everyone holding great expectations for his future. However, soon after, Shintaro began experiencing double vision. The doctor's diagnosis was a brain tumor, a harsh reality for a 21-year-old. Nevertheless, supported by his family, mentors, and teammates, Shintaro fought against his illness. At his retirement game in September 2019, he performed a miraculous throw home, moving the stadium to tears. But Shintaro's story didn't end there. Matsutani, a former high school baseball player, plays Yokota, and Suzuki plays his mother, Manami. The director is Jun Akiyama of "20 Years Old Soul."
title:One, Two, Three: A slapstick comedy filmed in Germany. McNamara, the head of Coca-Cola's Berlin branch, is tasked by a company executive with babysitting his daughter. However, this girl is a troublesome handful who defies easy handling. The protagonist's mindset of doing anything for career advancement echoes Billy Wilder's previous film "The Apartment." The rapid-fire exchange of gags in the dialogue is quintessentially Wilder. The film also showcases the full comedic charm of James Cagney, who also worked as a director.
title:Osaka Elegy: Synopsis: Ayako (Yamada), a telephone operator, enters into a lover's contract with a married company president to cover her father's debts after he loses his job due to embezzlement suspicions... Considered one of Mizoguchi's masterpieces from before the war, the lively streets of Osaka and Yamada's modern fashion are also highlights.
title:Oslo, 31. august: The second feature film by director Joachim Trier (known for "The Worst Person in the World"), released in 2011. A bold adaptation of Pierre Drieu La Rochelle's novel "Le Feu Follet" (also the basis for Louis Malle's film "The Fire Within"), it sensitively portrays the pain and despair of a young man addicted to drugs, set in modern-day Oslo. Anders, undergoing a drug addiction treatment program at a facility in the suburbs, is plagued by suicidal thoughts. As his rehabilitation nears its end, he receives a leave pass and returns to his hometown of Oslo to reunite with friends. However, conversations are strained, and a job interview goes poorly. Eventually, he goes to a party but fails to fit in, and after a long period of abstinence, he starts drinking alcohol and then turns to drugs. This is the second film in what is called the "Oslo Trilogy," which includes Trier's 2006 debut "Reprise" and his 2021 film "The Worst Person in the World." Anders Danielsen Lie, who also starred in "Reprise," plays the protagonist Anders. The film was screened in the Un Certain Regard section at the 64th Cannes Film Festival in 2011. It received its first Japanese theatrical release as part of the special program "Joachim Trier: The Oslo Trilogy" (from February 13, 2026, at Bunkamura Le Cinéma Shibuya Miyashita in Tokyo and other venues).

title:Our Little Sister: A story spanning one year in the lives of three sisters (Ayase, Nagasawa, Kaho) who, after the death of their father who left home 15 years ago and with whom they had lost touch, come to live with their half-sister Suzu (Hirose), who has lost her own family. Based on the best-selling manga by Yoshida Akimi, it carefully depicts the town of Kamakura, where the story is set, and the changing seasons, while bringing to light the love and sorrows of women of different generations.
title:Over the Town: Arakawa Ao (Ryuya Wakaba), who works at a vintage clothing store in Shimokitazawa, can't forget his ex-girlfriend who cheated on him and dumped him. His life, mostly spent alone—occasionally going to live shows or his usual bar—is self-contained within the Shimokitazawa area. One day, a female director attending art school invites him to appear in her independent film.
title:P. P. Rider: Jojo, Bruce, and Jisho, a trio of middle schoolers, are constantly bullied by the neighborhood bully Debnaga. Determined to get revenge on Debnaga today, the three are psyched up, but right before their eyes, Debnaga is kidnapped. From there, the three are drawn into a yakuza conflict involving stimulant drugs...
title:PATHAAN パターン: A spy action film starring Indian cinema superstar Shah Rukh Khan, known for films like "My Name Is Khan" and "Om Shanti Om." When the Indian government revokes the autonomy of the Kashmir region spanning India and Pakistan, an enraged Pakistani General Qadir teams up with former Indian soldier Jim to plan a terrorist attack. Pathaan, an agent of India's intelligence agency RAW (Research and Analysis Wing), moves to stop Jim's planned biological weapon attack. However, it is discovered that a biological weapon has been planted on a plane flying over Delhi. With only six minutes left in a desperate situation, Pathaan, India's top agent, fights to protect his homeland. It has become a talking point that Tiger, the spy played by Salman Khan in the film "Tiger: The Legendary Spy"—which also features the same Indian intelligence agency RAW—is set as a colleague of the protagonist Pathaan in this film. Directed by Siddharth Anand of "War" and "Bang Bang!" Deepika Padukone, who has co-starred with Shah Rukh Khan in films like "Om Shanti Om" and "Chennai Express," plays the heroine Rubai.
title:PATHAAN／パターン: A spy action film starring Indian cinema superstar Shah Rukh Khan, known for films like "My Name Is Khan" and "Om Shanti Om." title:PAW Patrol: The Dino Movie: The third theatrical film in the popular North American children's animated series "PAW Patrol," affectionately known as "Paupato." It depicts the adventures of the boy Kent and his team of unique puppies, the PAW Patrol, as they strive to save Dino Island, home to gentle dinosaurs, from a crisis. On Dino Island, where dinosaurs live, Mayor Rival uses dynamite to excavate the island's diamonds, causing a massive explosion. This triggers a volcanic eruption, putting the dinosaurs in grave danger. The Japanese voice cast includes Megumi Han as Kent, Shizuka Ishigami as Chase, Mako Komatsu as Marshall, Shiori Izawa as Skye, Sōma Saitō as Rubble, Miyuki Kobori as Rocky, and Sayuri Yahagi as Zuma, all reprising their roles from previous series. Guest voice actors include Yūko Ōshima and the comedy duo "Rainbow" members Takao Jumbo and Naoto Ikeda. The theme song is a new track written by the Backstreet Boys titled "Bottle Up."
title:PEACOCK ／ピーコック: A perfect son, a cultured lover, a thug for those who want to play hero on a date—'My Companion' is an agency that provides ideal individuals for any situation. Matthias, their top performer, perfectly plays the required roles, living through various personalities every day. However, when his girlfriend Sofia tells him 'I don't feel the real you' and they break up, his perfect mask begins to quietly peel away. Furthermore, an unexpected incident with a client causes Matthias's gears to gradually start grinding, and eventually the boundary between reality and fiction becomes blurred...
title:PEACOCK／ピーコック: The perfect son, a cultured lover, a thug for hire for those who want to play hero on a date—Matthias is the top performer at "My Companion," an agency that provides ideal personas for any situation. He flawlessly plays the roles demanded of him, living out various personalities every day. However, triggered by a sudden breakup with his girlfriend Sofia and an unexpected incident with a client, Matthias's gears begin to slowly grind out of alignment, and the boundary between reality and fiction gradually blurs...
title:PEAK END: A feature film directed, planned, and starring Korean-born filmmaker Shin Chae-rin, created as her graduation project from the Kyoto University of Arts Film Department. Shot with a minimal production setup and incorporating documentary elements, it was screened at various film festivals, including being an invited work at the 21st Osaka Asian Film Festival and selected for the 47th Pia Film Festival. Rin, who came to Kyoto from Seoul, and Sora, who came to Kyoto from Okinawa, meet at university and aspire to make films. They give form to the impulses and desires that arise in their daily lives through the act of 'making a film.' Their relationship, which seeks to know each other through actions like sending jam sandwiches flying into the sky or tracing roots in Okinawa, continues to change. Shin Chae-rin plays Rin, and Sora Itami from Okinawa plays Sora, both also participating in the production. The film was made by a small team of five staff members, including the two actresses.
title:PERFECT BLUE 4Kリマスター版:
[Admission Fee] 1,600 yen flat rate
*No discounts applicable. Complimentary tickets and free passes cannot be used.

The 1998 debut feature of animation director Satoshi Kon, who received high acclaim both in Japan and abroad for works such as "Paprika" and "Millennium Actress." Based on Yoshikazu Takeuchi's novel "Perfect Blue: Complete Metamorphosis," the film depicts the nightmare-like events that befall a woman transitioning from a pop idol to an actress.

Mima Kirigoe leaves her idol group to pursue a career as an actress. While bewildered by a series of provocative jobs that shatter her previous image—including a rape scene in a TV drama and a nude photo book—she steadily gains recognition. Meanwhile, a series of murders targeting those close to her occurs. An individual posing as Mima begins posting detailed diary entries online, and she gradually becomes terrified by the shadow of a stalker.
title:PLAYLIST アジアの才能: An omnibus film collecting works from five young directors from Japan, South Korea, China, Taiwan, and Vietnam. Selected from short films screened at the 20th and 21st Osaka Asian Film Festival, these five works showcase next-generation talent, arranged like a music album under the 'PLAYLIST' concept. Though each piece differs in setting and style, they capture universal emotions—love, growth, loss, identity—through the eyes of today's youth. The lineup includes: 'Boxing Day' by China's Zhang Xiaoyi, depicting a nurse who develops feelings for a discharged boxer and is led into a strange dream; 'Suzuki' by South Korea's Ahn Jung-min, following a middle schooler who loves Western music and grows through admiration and unexpected loss after meeting someone in a chat room; 'Rooftop Lempicka' by Vietnam's Nguyen Luong Hang, showing a 10-year-old girl glimpsing the adult world through a Tamara de Lempicka art book found in a bookstore and interactions with a waitress; 'Black Dog' by Taiwan's Yang Lin, exploring family through a girl's attempt to solve the mystery of strange howling from her father's room at night; and 'Melting in the Street' by Japan's Nako Komiyama, depicting queer children who are drawn to each other as they share secrets, along with their struggles and a small escape.
title:POCA PON ポカポン: Living in poverty, bothered by noisy neighbors. Frustrated with an absurd reality, middle school student Kenta struggles to support his mother Asako and younger brother Yuji. And then there's the mysterious "pokapon" sound echoing around him. Watching over this family quietly is the housing complex manager, Shunichi. Eventually, Kenta and Shunichi begin to understand each other, but rumors start to circulate that the perpetrator of a series of child murders that once shocked the nation is hiding in this housing complex...
title:POPEYE THE SLAYER MAN: A horror film based on the popular cartoon character 'Popeye,' created by American cartoonist Elzie Crisler Segar in 1929. Produced after the original copyright expired in January 2025, entering the public domain, it depicts the righteous sailor Popeye awakening as a brutal murderer, armed with his familiar can of spinach and powerful forearms. College student Dexter is making a documentary about a local legend in a small port town: a sailor who wanders the docks every night in search of prey. One night, Dexter brings along Olivia, whom he has long had a crush on, and their friends to sneak into an abandoned factory near the port for investigation. As they proceed in a somewhat playful mood, the smell of pipe tobacco begins to drift from somewhere, and soon the legendary sailor emerges from the darkness. As his companions are brutally killed one after another, Dexter and Olivia desperately flee, following clues left in the factory to uncover the sailor's true identity.
title:PRETTY CRAZY: A romantic comedy from director Lee Sang-geun, who previously scored a massive hit in Korea with 'EXIT' and reunites with Im Yoon-ah. It follows a woman possessed by a demon who shows completely different faces by day and night, and the kind-hearted young man who falls for her. On leave from work, Gil-gu falls in love at first sight with Seon-ji, a baker who moves in downstairs. But when he encounters her late that night, she is entirely different. Her father Jang-su explains that Seon-ji is gentle and bright by day, but at 2 AM a demon awakens, transforming her. Gil-gu agrees to Jang-su's odd request to watch over Seon-ji at night. She drags him out every night, running wild and selfishly bossing him around. Im Yoon-ah, a Girls' Generation member known for films like 'EXIT' and drama 'The King's Chef', plays Seon-ji. Ahn Bo-hyun, from the drama 'Spring Fever', plays Gil-gu. Song Dong-il, known for the 'Reply' series, plays Seon-ji's protective father Jang-su.
title:PRIMITIVE WAR: A survival action film depicting a deadly battle between dinosaurs that suddenly appear in the jungles of the Vietnam War and the U.S. military. In 1968, amidst the intense Vietnam War, the elite 'Viper Squad' of the U.S. Army Green Berets, on a special mission, goes missing in the jungle. The U.S. 'Vulture Platoon,' dispatched to search for them, encounters deep in the jungle a horde of dinosaurs, including Tyrannosaurus and Triceratops. Facing attacks from land, river, and air, the Vulture Platoon members engage in a fierce battle against the dinosaurs. Directed by Luke Sparke, an up-and-coming Australian filmmaker who single-handedly handled the script, production, editing, and art direction. Dale Dye, a retired Marine who served in the Vietnam War and appeared in 'Platoon' and 'Saving Private Ryan,' supervised the script, adding realism to the war film.
title:Pale Blue Dot 君が微笑めば、: 'Pale Blue Dot: If You Smile' (2024 / Japan / 97 min / 5.1ch / 16:9) Director: Koji Nishijima Narration: Yayako Uchida Cast: Rumiana Tsenkova, Shogo Shigeoka, Mikinosuke Kakisaka, Masataka Kakisaka, Haruo Saji Ending Theme: EPO 'Glory' (eponica Record) Organized by: 'Pale Blue Dot: If You Smile' Office
title:Panda! Go Panda!: This animation was planned following the panda boom in Japan sparked by China's gift of pandas to Ueno Zoo in 1972 as part of Japan-China friendship. Mimiko sends her grandmother off to a memorial service and will be living alone for a while. But when she returns home, there is a child panda who understands human speech. Then the father panda also appears. This panda father and child were lured by the bamboo grove near Mimiko's home. Mimiko treats the father panda, Papanda, as her own father and the child panda, Pan, as her child, and begins living together with them. One day, a policeman visiting Mimiko's house is startled to see the panda pair. In fact, Papanda and Pan had escaped from the zoo. The zoo director, alerted by the police, tries to take them back, but Pan gets lost, and a search begins. Pan is found swept away in a river, with a sluice-gate waterfall beyond—a major crisis. Can they rescue Pan? And can Mimiko and the panda pair live together again?
title:Panda! Go Panda!: Rainy Day Circus: Mimiko-chan, Pan-chan, and Papanda lived happily together every day. Then, one day, while Mimiko-chan and the others were out, two suspicious characters showed up... When Mimiko-chan returned, she was delighted, saying, "It's my first time seeing burglars!" but the pair ran away in a flash. Mimiko-chan was a little disappointed that the seemingly interesting guests had gone, but Pan-chan noticed that his food had been eaten. Pan-chan sniffed around the house searching. Crawling into Pan-chan's bed and sleeping soundly was... a tiger cub! Both of them were so surprised they ran around the house making a huge commotion...
title:Pandora's Box: A sensual melodrama based on the play of the same name by F. Wedekind, which gave L. Brooks, who moved from Hollywood to Germany, the nickname 'Lulu' after her character. Lulu, a dancer in a seedy dive, becomes the mistress of Dr. Schön, a newspaper publisher, through the skills of her foster father Schigolch. She rises to perform in top theaters, and when Schön tries to break up with her, she turns the tables and forces him to marry her. Schön has a son of marriageable age, Alwa, who is also his secretary, and Lulu seduces him as if enjoying tearing the father and son apart. When Schön learns of her numerous affairs and the decisive truth, he threatens to kill Lulu and then himself, but in the struggle, she shoots him. Although captured, she escapes during the trial with the help of her foster father and Alwa. She lives a life of pleasure on a gambling ship in a port town, introduced by her lover, the strongman Rodrigo. But when Rodrigo sells her, a fight breaks out over her, and Lulu, her foster father, and Alwa secretly enter London. Reduced to extreme poverty in the slums, Lulu decides to become a prostitute, bringing a man into her room while the two men wait outside, unaware that the effeminate man is the infamous Jack the Ripper...
title:Paprika: Director Kon Satoshi, known for "Perfect Blue" and "Millennium Actress," boldly adapts Tsutsui Yasutaka's science fiction novel of the same name into this animated feature film. The "DC Mini," a revolutionary device developed at the Institute for Psychiatric Research, allows users to share dreams. Chiba Atsuko, a psychotherapist at the institute, enters her clients' dreams as Paprika, a dream detective with a completely different appearance and personality, conducting secret therapy sessions. One day, the DC Mini is stolen from the institute, and staff members begin to have strange dreams and suffer psychological damage. Paprika investigates and dives into dreams contaminated by mad imagery, but a terrifying trap awaits her there. Megumi Hayashibara voices the protagonist Paprika. Madhouse handles the animation, and musician Hirasawa Susumu provides the music. The film was screened in the competition section of the 63rd Venice International Film Festival in 2006. Director Kon passed away in 2010 after this film, which became his final feature-length work. In 2026, a 4K remastered version will be revived nationwide to commemorate the 20th anniversary.
title:Parasite: The fourth collaboration between director Bong Joon-ho ('Memories of Murder,' 'The Host,' 'Snowpiercer') and lead actor Song Kang-ho, this film won the Palme d'Or at the 72nd Cannes Film Festival in 2019, the first for a Korean film. It also garnered global attention by winning four awards at the 92nd Academy Awards, including Best Picture—the first for a foreign language film—as well as Best Director, Best Original Screenplay, and Best International Feature Film. The Kim family is all unemployed and living in poverty, scraping by day to day. One day, the eldest son, Ki-woo, goes to the lavish home of IT CEO Mr. Park for a tutoring job interview. Following him, his sister Ki-jeong also sets foot in the mansion. The encounter between these two families from opposite worlds accelerates into a tragicomedy beyond imagination at breakneck speed... Co-starring Lee Sun-kyun ('A Hard Day'), Cho Yeo-jeong ('The Concubine'), and Choi Woo-shik ('Train to Busan').
title:Paris ni Saku Étoile: Set in early 20th-century Paris, this animated film delicately and vividly portrays the struggles of two Japanese girls pursuing their dreams in a foreign land. In Paris at the turn of the century, two girls who came from Japan live there. One is Fujiko, who dreams of becoming a painter despite being expected to become a good wife supporting her husband. The other is Chizuru, born into a samurai family and a master of the naginata, but drawn to ballet. The two, who met once in Yokohama, reunite after five years when Chizuru helps Fujiko out of trouble. Learning of Chizuru's dream, Fujiko discovers that Olga, the mother of a young man named Ruslan living in the same apartment building, is a former Russian ballerina and arranges lessons for Chizuru. Meanwhile, Fujiko's guardian uncle goes missing. Ami Touma voices the protagonist Fujiko, who dreams of being a painter; Rina Arashi voices Chizuru, who aspires to be a ballerina; and Taichi Saotome voices Ruslan, the young man who meets Fujiko. Directed by Goro Taniguchi of "ONE PIECE FILM RED" and the "Code Geass: Lelouch of the Rebellion" series, with original character designs by Katsuya Kondo, who worked on character design and key animation for Studio Ghibli films like "Kiki's Delivery Service." The screenplay is by Reiko Yoshida of "The Colors Within" and "Violet Evergarden."
title:Paris vu par…: An omnibus film of short works, each directed by one of six leading directors of the French New Wave, all set against the backdrop of Paris. The six episodes are: "Saint-Denis Street" (directed by Jean-Daniel Pollet), about a timid man who brings a prostitute he met in a red-light district back to his apartment; "North Station" (Jean Rouch), about a woman living with her lover in an apartment far from the station who encounters an unexpected incident on her way to work after arguing with him; "Saint-Germain-des-Prés" (Jean Douchet), depicting the romantic entanglements of young people in a student quarter; "Place de l'Étoile" (Éric Rohmer), about a man heading to work through the Place de l'Étoile who faces a series of troubles; "Montparnasse and Levallois" (Jean-Luc Godard), about a woman who writes love letters to two different men but accidentally mails the wrong ones; and "La Muette" (Claude Chabrol), depicting a tragedy that strikes a bourgeois family in an upscale neighborhood from the son's perspective. The cast includes Joanna Shimkus from "The Adventurers," Stéphane Audran from "Babette's Feast," and Barbet Schroeder, who also produced this film, among others.
title:PascaLs しあわせのようなもの: A documentary about the acoustic orchestra band "Pascals," led by Rocket Matsu. Formed in 1995, the group has garnered popularity for their unique, euphoric sound. They have composed numerous scores for films, television dramas, and stage productions—including *The Fish Child* and *Riverside Mukolitta*—and have received high acclaim internationally, particularly in France. While the band had performed with the same lineup for approximately 25 years, cellist Kota Miki passed away suddenly in April 2020. Focusing on memorial concerts held in the spring of 2021 and 2022 during the pandemic, the film captures their music as they grapple with "a presence defined by absence." Directed by Shinichi Ise, the documentary filmmaker behind *Nao-chan* and *Now is Past: My Father, Java & the Phantom Films*.
title:Passage of Life: Set in Japan and Myanmar, this drama is based on a true story about a Myanmar family living in Japan. Kane lives in a small Tokyo apartment with her two young sons. After her husband Aise is detained by immigration authorities, Kane must support the family alone. Since her children grew up in Japan and cannot speak their native language, Kane pours all her love into them using her imperfect Japanese, but the brothers, stressed by their father's absence, fight daily. Growing anxious about their future, Kane increasingly longs to return to Myanmar, where she was born and raised. This is director Akiro Fujimoto's feature-length debut. The film was screened in the 'Asian Future' section of the 30th Tokyo International Film Festival in 2017, where it won both the section's Best Picture Award and the Japan Foundation Asia Center Special Prize.
title:Pastoral: To Die in the Country: An autobiographical work written and directed by Shuji Terayama, adapting his own poetry collection of the same name. In a village at the foot of Mount Osore in Aomori Prefecture, a young boy, 'I', lives with his mother in an old house after losing his father. The boy's only solace is having an itako (a spirit medium) summon his father's spirit to talk to him. A beautiful woman who marries into the neighboring house and a circus troupe that comes to the village tempt the boy to run away from home. Later, 'I' grows up, moves to Tokyo, becomes middle-aged, and makes a film. Before this 'I' appears the boy he once was... Kantaro Suga, known for 'Thirteen Assassins' and others, plays the lead, and Kaoru Yachigusa plays the neighbor's wife.
title:Pathaan: A spy action film starring Indian cinema superstar Shah Rukh Khan, known for films like "My Name Is Khan" and "Om Shanti Om." When the Indian government revokes the autonomy of the Kashmir region spanning India and Pakistan, an enraged Pakistani General Qadir teams up with former Indian soldier Jim to plan a terrorist attack. Pathaan, an agent of India's intelligence agency RAW (Research and Analysis Wing), moves to stop Jim's planned biological weapon attack. However, it is discovered that a biological weapon has been planted on a plane flying over Delhi. With only six minutes left in a desperate situation, Pathaan, India's top agent, fights to protect his homeland. It has become a talking point that Tiger, the spy played by Salman Khan in the film "Tiger: The Legendary Spy"—which also features the same Indian intelligence agency RAW—is set as a colleague of the protagonist Pathaan in this film. Directed by Siddharth Anand of "War" and "Bang Bang!" Deepika Padukone, who has co-starred with Shah Rukh Khan in films like "Om Shanti Om" and "Chennai Express," plays the heroine Rubai.
title:Patlabor EZY: File 2: During an internal audit at headquarters, Kurumi from the maintenance team notices that one live round for the revolver cannon is missing. She consults Kikkyo, and one by one, the other squad members get drawn into the situation. Unaware of this, Towa and Saki begin to suspect the attitudes of Kikkyo and the others...
title:Pauline at the Beach: The third film in Éric Rohmer's "Comedies and Proverbs" series. It depicts the romantic entanglements of six men and women at a seaside villa, seen through the eyes of adolescent girl Pauline. Fifteen-year-old Pauline comes to Normandy for a vacation with her older cousin Marion. When they go to the beach, they meet Marion's ex-boyfriend Pierre. Pierre still harbors feelings for Marion, but Marion falls for Henri, a playboy acquaintance of Pierre's. Meanwhile, Pauline grows close to Sylvain, a boy windsurfing at the beach... The film won the Silver Bear and the FIPRESCI Prize at the Berlin International Film Festival.
title:Pauline à la plage: The third film in Éric Rohmer's "Comedies and Proverbs" series. It depicts the romantic entanglements of six men and women at a seaside villa, seen through the eyes of adolescent girl Pauline. Fifteen-year-old Pauline comes to Normandy for a vacation with her older cousin Marion. When they go to the beach, they meet Marion's ex-boyfriend Pierre. Pierre still harbors feelings for Marion, but Marion falls for Henri, a playboy acquaintance of Pierre's. Meanwhile, Pauline grows close to Sylvain, a boy windsurfing at the beach... The film won the Silver Bear and the FIPRESCI Prize at the Berlin International Film Festival.
title:Pelikan Blue: An animated film that visualizes an astonishing true story from 1990s Hungary in Eastern Europe, incorporating documentary materials. In 1990s Hungary, after the fall of the Iron Curtain opened the door to Western Europe, foreign travel was liberalized, and many people turned their eyes to the outside world. However, international train tickets were expensive and out of reach for ordinary people. Amidst this, three young men—intellectual Akos, fearless Pecha, and swimming enthusiast Laci—find a way to forge tickets. They dissolve the blue carbon ink "Pelikan Blue" from the company Pelikan, used on the tickets, with household detergent and rewrite the destinations. After enjoying overseas trips with forged tickets, they decide to distribute "tickets to freedom" to other young people in similar situations. The plan seems to go smoothly, but eventually, a police investigation begins, escalating into a major uproar that shakes the nation. Directed by László Csáki, known for his distinctive animation style, who conducted meticulous research over ten years and blends documentary materials like archival footage and interview audio with hand-drawn animation.
title:Penguin Highway: An animated film adaptation of the novel that won the Japan SF Award, written by popular author Tomihiko Morimi, known for works like "The Night is Short, Walk on Girl" and "The Eccentric Family." This is the first feature-length film from Studio Colorido, the studio behind the shorts "Shiranpuri" and "Typhoon Noruda." It is directed by the emerging talent Hiroyasu Ishida (of "Shiranpuri" fame), with character designs by Yojiro Arai ("Typhoon Noruda"). Aoyama-kun, a studious fourth grader who diligently records everything he learns in a notebook, is close friends with the young woman at his dental clinic. She, in turn, dotes on the slightly cheeky and precocious Aoyama-kun. One day, a penguin suddenly appears in their residential town, which has no ocean nearby. Why would a penguin show up in a mere housing district? Aoyama-kun begins his research to solve the mystery, but then witnesses the young woman's discarded cola can transform into a penguin. Kana Kita, known for the TV drama "Byplayers," voices Aoyama-kun in her voice acting debut, while Yu Aoi, who has voice acting experience in "Tekkonkinkreet" and "The Case of Hana & Alice," plays the role of the young woman.
title:Peppermint Candy: A human drama that traces twenty years in the life of a man against the backdrop of modern Korean history, winning five major awards including Best Picture at the Grand Bell Awards, South Korea's equivalent of the Oscars. This is the second feature film by director Lee Chang-dong, made in 1999, known for "Oasis" and "Secret Sunshine." Spring, 1999. Kim Yeong-ho, at the depths of despair after losing his job and family, shows up at a picnic with old friends wearing an out-of-place suit. It is the same place he visited twenty years earlier with his first love, Sunim. Standing on the railroad tracks, Yeong-ho shouts "I want to go back!" at an oncoming train, and his life begins to rewind. We see his self-destructed marriage to his wife Hong-ja, his love for Sunim that drew them together but was never fulfilled, and the Gwangju Uprising he witnessed as a soldier. Yeong-ho's journey through memory eventually arrives at the time twenty years ago when his life was most beautiful and pure. The film was released in a 4K-restored digital remaster in 2019 to coincide with the release of Lee Chang-dong's "Burning." A 4K restoration was also screened in 2023 as part of the special retrospective "Lee Chang-dong Retrospective 4K."
title:Perfume - \"Cold Sleep\" –25 years: A documentary depicting the 25-year culmination of the three-member music unit 'Perfume,' which announced a 'cold sleep' (hiatus) in 2025. Formed in Hiroshima in 1999, Perfume gained attention not only in Japan but worldwide after the huge breakout success of their 2007 single 'Polyrhythm.' Having raced through 25 years, they announced a hiatus from 2026, termed a 'cold sleep,' on September 21, 2025, the 20th anniversary of their major debut. This film looks back at their journey from formation to the present, including live performances—especially their last concert before the cold sleep and first Tokyo Dome show in five years, 'Perfume ZO/Z5 Anniversary "Nebula Romance" Episode TOKYO DOME' held on September 22 and 23—along with unreleased footage. It also closely follows the behind-the-scenes after the cold sleep announcement and features exclusive interviews with the three members. The three, who have grown both as artists and as people over 25 years, explore what has changed and what remains constant, as well as their feelings about the cold sleep. The director is Taketoshi Sado, who also directed the 2015 Perfume documentary film 'WE ARE Perfume WORLD TOUR 3rd DOCUMENT.'

title:Petite Maman: Directed and written by Céline Sciamma of "Portrait of a Lady on Fire," this film weaves a story of loss and healing connecting three generations: daughter, mother, and grandmother. Eight-year-old Nelly, grieving her beloved grandmother, is taken by her parents to clean out the forest house where her grandmother lived. But her mother, who spent her own childhood there, is overwhelmed by memories at every turn and eventually leaves. Left behind, Nelly wanders the woods and meets another eight-year-old girl who calls herself Marion—the same name as Nelly's mother. The girl invites Nelly to her home, which turns out to be "grandma's house." Sisters Joséphine and Gabrielle Sanz, making their film debut, play Nelly and Marion. Nina Meurisse ("A Woman's Life") and Margot Abascal ("Sagan") co-star. The film was presented in the competition section of the 71st Berlin International Film Festival in 2021.
title:Pfau - Bin ich echt?: A perfect son, a cultured lover, a thug for those who want to play hero on a date—'My Companion' is an agency that provides ideal individuals for any situation. Matthias, their top performer, perfectly plays the required roles, living through various personalities every day. However, when his girlfriend Sofia tells him 'I don't feel the real you' and they break up, his perfect mask begins to quietly peel away. Furthermore, an unexpected incident with a client causes Matthias's gears to gradually start grinding, and eventually the boundary between reality and fiction becomes blurred...
title:Piccola felicita(ピッコラ・フェリチタ)～小さな幸せ: An ensemble drama depicting the lives of three couples at crossroads in life. A former restaurant manager facing mandatory retirement after 25 years and grappling with loneliness, a painter struggling under his father's shadow and on the verge of divorce, and a young man captivated by a mysterious hotel guest. When their seemingly unrelated daily lives intersect, heartwarming "little miracles" unfold alongside unexpected events.
title:Piccola felicità 〜小さな幸せ〜: An ensemble drama depicting the lives of three couples at crossroads in life. A former restaurant manager facing mandatory retirement after 25 years and grappling with loneliness, a painter struggling under his father's shadow and on the verge of divorce, and a young man captivated by a mysterious hotel guest. When their seemingly unrelated daily lives intersect, heartwarming "little miracles" unfold alongside unexpected events.
title:Piccola felicità（ピッコラ・フェリチタ） 小さな幸せ: The fourth feature film directed by actor Yutaka Mizutani, familiar from the "Aibou" series. Mizutani also handles planning, script, production, and lead acting, as unpredictable stories intertwine involving three couples in their 60s, 40s, and 30s. Sato, retiring after 25 years at a restaurant, divorced and unable to see his daughter, feels his life is over. A small miracle brings him unexpected joy. Fujio, who runs a painting class, struggles under his painter father's shadow, drowning in alcohol and women daily. Divorce from his estranged wife Miki seems inevitable, but Fujio's final confession changes everything. Reo, working at a hotel, falls in love at first sight with Aoi, whom he meets at a café, and they quickly fall for each other. But Reo learns a secret about Aoi. The human dramas of these three couples are depicted with a theme color set for each story. Alongside Mizutani, the cast includes Nobue Iketani, Nanahana, Gamon Kaiga, Shuri, and Jun Hashimoto. This film marks the first parent-child co-starring role for Mizutani and Shuri. Cinematography is by Masahiro Aida, who also worked on the "Aibou" series, and music by Yoshiki Yamamoto from Mizutani's previous film "Taiyo to Bolero."
title:Pickpocket: Michel, a poor university student, discovers by chance that he has a talent for pickpocketing. Though once caught by a detective, he is released due to lack of evidence and soon targets others' wallets again. Eventually, his methods become organized as he brings in accomplices. In 'A Man Escaped,' Bresson realistically and thrillingly depicted a prison break; here, he turns his focus to pickpocketing, introducing actual techniques while portraying a lonely young man distrustful of others. A gripping masterpiece where the realism born from amateur actors and the suspense created by various pickpocketing scenes blend seamlessly.
title:Pierrot le Fou: A masterpiece by Jean-Luc Godard, released in 1965 and revered as a cornerstone of the French New Wave. Ferdinand, called 'Pierrot,' is driven by an urge to escape his boring married life and spends a night with his former lover Marianne, whom he meets by chance. The next morning, finding a dead stranger, the two go on the run, but Marianne eventually tires of Ferdinand and betrays him by colluding with gangsters. A digitally remastered version with a new translation by Jiro Terao was released in 2016. A 2K restored version was released in 2022 and 2026.
title:Pierrot le fou: A masterpiece by Jean-Luc Godard, released in 1965 and revered as a cornerstone of the French New Wave. Ferdinand, called 'Pierrot,' is driven by an urge to escape his boring married life and spends a night with his former lover Marianne, whom he meets by chance. title:Play it, Boogie-Woogie: Goro and Sachino first met on the Third Keihin Expressway. Sachino, thrown out of a white Mustang, was rescued by Goro, who was riding a motorcycle. The two begin living together. Meanwhile, the middle-aged man who was driving the Mustang is also leading a strange cohabitation. Sachino starts working at a snack bar called Queen Elizabeth. Goro gets into a fight and quits his part-time job. When Goro leaves home, Sachino decides to meet the middle-aged man.
title:Playback: A drama captured in beautiful monochrome cinematography, following an actor at a crossroads in life as he moves between the past and present to take a new step forward. The film is the second feature from up-and-coming director Sho Miyake. Haji, an actor on the verge of turning 40, finds himself at a professional standstill, burdened by a mounting series of personal struggles including failing health and a separation from his wife. It is then that Bon, a high school friend he hasn't seen in years, appears and invites him to their hometown for the wedding of another old friend, Yuji. While traveling to his hometown in Bon’s car, Haji drifts off to sleep, only to wake up and find himself transported back to his high school days twenty years ago—yet still in his adult body. Led by Jun Murakami, the film features a talented ensemble cast including Kiyohiko Shibukawa, Masaki Miura, Makiko Watanabe, and Shun Sugata.
title:Poca Pon: Living in poverty, bothered by noisy neighbors. Frustrated with an absurd reality, middle school student Kenta struggles to support his mother Asako and younger brother Yuji. And then there's the mysterious "pokapon" sound echoing around him. Watching over this family quietly is the housing complex manager, Shunichi. Eventually, Kenta and Shunichi begin to understand each other, but rumors start to circulate that the perpetrator of a series of child murders that once shocked the nation is hiding in this housing complex...
title:Point Blank: A hard-boiled action film directed by British master John Boorman in 1967, early in his career, starring Hollywood legend Lee Marvin ('The Dirty Dozen,' 'The Professionals'). Based on Richard Stark's crime novel 'The Hunter' (featuring the character Parker), it depicts a man's revenge against his betrayers, blending avant-garde New Wave techniques with the psychedelic culture of the American West Coast. Walker, at the request of his friend Reese, robs a criminal organization's deal at the abandoned Alcatraz prison and steals a large sum of money. However, Reese betrays Walker, shooting him and fleeing with his $93,000 share and Walker's wife, Lyn. As his consciousness fades, memories and fantasies swirl through Walker's mind. Surviving, Walker sets out to recover his share and exact revenge, tracking Reese down. Marvin delivers a powerful performance as the ruthless avenger Walker, with Angie Dickinson ('Rio Bravo') and John Vernon ('Dirty Harry') co-starring.
title:Pola X: The fourth feature film by French wunderkind Leos Carax, released eight years after 'The Lovers on the Bridge.' An adaptation of the novel 'Pierre' by 19th-century American author Herman Melville, written the year after his masterpiece 'Moby-Dick.' Shifting the setting to modern-day Paris, it uses emotional imagery and sound to depict the intense, racing love of a man and woman swept up by fate and drawn into despair. Pierre, a young novelist living in a Norman castle, enjoys a wealthy, contented rural life with his mother Marie and fiancée Lucie. One day, Isabelle, a Bosnian refugee claiming to be Pierre's half-sister, appears. Drawn to Isabelle's charm, Pierre abandons everything and heads to Paris with her. Guillaume Depardieu, son of Gérard Depardieu, passionately plays Pierre, and Katerina Golubeva, known for 'Paris at Night,' plays Isabelle. Catherine Deneuve co-stars as Pierre's mother Marie. Cinematography is by Éric Gautier, known for 'My King,' and music is by singer-songwriter Scott Walker. A 4K restored version will be re-released in February 2026.
title:Popeye the Slayer Man: A horror film based on the popular cartoon character 'Popeye,' created by American cartoonist Elzie Crisler Segar in 1929. Produced after the original copyright expired in January 2025, entering the public domain, it depicts the righteous sailor Popeye awakening as a brutal murderer, armed with his familiar can of spinach and powerful forearms. College student Dexter is making a documentary about a local legend in a small port town: a sailor who wanders the docks every night in search of prey. One night, Dexter brings along Olivia, whom he has long had a crush on, and their friends to sneak into an abandoned factory near the port for investigation. As they proceed in a somewhat playful mood, the smell of pipe tobacco begins to drift from somewhere, and soon the legendary sailor emerges from the darkness. As his companions are brutally killed one after another, Dexter and Olivia desperately flee, following clues left in the factory to uncover the sailor's true identity.

title:Pornostar: Kamijo struggles to scrape together tribute money for the yakuza while harboring ambitions of one day surpassing them. Then, a man named Koya appears—a man who kills yakuza without so much as a flicker of expression. Koya fills a sports bag with knives and goes around stabbing anyone who calls himself a yakuza, one after another.
title:Postcard: Near the end of the war, 100 middle-aged soldiers are called up. Their postings are decided by their superior officer's lottery. Realizing he won't return alive after being assigned to the Philippines, Morikawa Teizo asks Matsuyama Keita to deliver a postcard to his wife, Tomoko, and tell her he read it. After the war ends, only six soldiers, including Keita, survive. Based on the postcard, they visit Tomoko's house, but...
title:Pretty Crazy: A romantic comedy from director Lee Sang-geun, who previously scored a massive hit in Korea with 'EXIT' and reunites with Im Yoon-ah. It follows a woman possessed by a demon who shows completely different faces by day and night, and the kind-hearted young man who falls for her. On leave from work, Gil-gu falls in love at first sight with Seon-ji, a baker who moves in downstairs. But when he encounters her late that night, she is entirely different. Her father Jang-su explains that Seon-ji is gentle and bright by day, but at 2 AM a demon awakens, transforming her. Gil-gu agrees to Jang-su's odd request to watch over Seon-ji at night. She drags him out every night, running wild and selfishly bossing him around. Im Yoon-ah, a Girls' Generation member known for films like 'EXIT' and drama 'The King's Chef', plays Seon-ji. Ahn Bo-hyun, from the drama 'Spring Fever', plays Gil-gu. Song Dong-il, known for the 'Reply' series, plays Seon-ji's protective father Jang-su.
title:Pretty Cure All Stars DX3: Deliver: Childhood friends Hibiki Hojo and Kanade Minamino, along with the fairy Hummy, visit a massive shopping mall on its opening day, but they lose sight of Hummy along the way. They manage to find her, but end up crashing into a fashion show hosted by Erika Kurumi. Amidst this, buildings and residents from other worlds, such as the Toy Kingdom and the Dessert Kingdom, suddenly appear. Furthermore, powerful enemies who once tormented the Pretty Cures are revived by the dark power of a black hole, plotting to wither the miracle flower connecting worlds, the "Prism Flower," and plunge the world into darkness. The Pretty Cures are sent to different worlds by the enemies' scheme, separated from their usual partners and allies, and each is invited into the worlds created by their formidable foes.
title:Priest of Darkness: To save the daughter of an amazake shop owner from a dire situation, two rogues throw themselves into the fray. A masterpiece showcasing perfect chemistry between the renowned actors of Zenshinza and director Yamanaka. The beauty of a 15-year-old Setsuko Hara is captivating.
title:Primavera: A drama based on the true story of composer Vivaldi's appointment as a violin teacher at the Ospedale della Pietà in Venice in the early 18th century, depicting the growth of a lonely girl whose talent blossoms under his guidance, and Vivaldi's inner ambition, craving recognition for his own genius. Venice, 1716, at the Ospedale della Pietà. Cecilia, raised without knowing her mother's presence or love, secretly slips out of bed every night to write letters to her mother with no address. To leave the Pietà and live in the outside world, her mother must come for her, or she must marry a nobleman. Amidst this, Antonio Vivaldi, arriving as a violin teacher, discovers Cecilia's exceptional violin skill and appoints her as the leader of the first violins. Under Vivaldi, Cecilia endures rigorous practice, hones her violin skills, and they gradually grow close. However, the officer the Pietà has chosen as Cecilia's husband returns from war, and an incident soon occurs. Tekla Insolia, noted for the Italian TV drama 'The Art of Joy,' plays Cecilia, and Michele Riondino of 'The Sleeping Beauty' plays Vivaldi. The film is directed and written by Damiano Michieletto, a leading Italian opera director who served as creative director for the opening and closing ceremonies of the Milan Cortina Winter Olympics.
title:Primitive War: A survival action film depicting a deadly battle between dinosaurs that suddenly appear in the jungles of the Vietnam War and the U.S. military. In 1968, amidst the intense Vietnam War, the elite 'Viper Squad' of the U.S. Army Green Berets, on a special mission, goes missing in the jungle. The U.S. 'Vulture Platoon,' dispatched to search for them, encounters deep in the jungle a horde of dinosaurs, including Tyrannosaurus and Triceratops. Facing attacks from land, river, and air, the Vulture Platoon members engage in a fierce battle against the dinosaurs. Directed by Luke Sparke, an up-and-coming Australian filmmaker who single-handedly handled the script, production, editing, and art direction. Dale Dye, a retired Marine who served in the Vietnam War and appeared in 'Platoon' and 'Saving Private Ryan,' supervised the script, adding realism to the war film.
title:Princess Arete: The time is the Middle Ages. A princess is confined to a small room at the top of a high tower, never showing her face to the people. Her mission is to remain pure until the day her future husband appears. But she, Princess Arete, gazes down from the tower window at the people living in the castle town below and ponders the meaning of life. One day, deciphering an ancient document, she discovers a secret passage and escapes the castle to go into town. The castle town is a world of artisans. The way each of their hands creates meaningful objects is like watching magic. If human hands hold such potential, then surely there must be something my hands can do...
title:Princess Yang Kwei-fei: A commentary: Emperor Xuanzong of Tang, grieving the loss of his beloved consort, sets his sights on a young woman... Mizoguchi's first color film, a co-production with Hong Kong, is a courtly tapestry portraying the love and tragic fate of Yang Guifei, the beauty who toppled an empire. The restrained color palette that highlights the exotic costumes and art direction is striking.
title:Profondo rosso: The splendid murder aesthetics of Dario Argento, the emperor of Italian horror, explode throughout the film. In Japan, after the huge success of 'Suspiria' (1977) with the clever tagline 'Never watch it alone,' this film was given a Japanese title to ride on that wave and was released in theaters, but it is actually unrelated in content and was made before that film. A shocking work that weaves the mystery of a series of gruesome murders with Argento's signature gorgeous and shocking visual beauty. Starring David Hemmings from 'Blow-Up' and Daria Nicolodi, Argento's good partner both publicly and privately. At the European Parapsychology Conference held in Rome, a telepathic woman named Helga, while demonstrating her abilities on stage, senses someone's murderous intent and becomes hysterical. She declares that a person who has committed brutal murders is in the audience. Later, Helga is brutally murdered in her room. Mark, a British pianist who happens to arrive at the scene and witnesses the murder and a suspect, teams up with journalist Jenna to investigate the mystery, but the truth they ultimately uncover is beyond imagination.
title:Project Hail Mary: A film adaptation of the bestselling science fiction novel by Andy Weir, author of "The Martian" (the basis for the Oscar-nominated "The Martian"). It depicts a middle school science teacher entrusted with the fate of Earth on the brink of extinction, who encounters an unknown life form with the same purpose at the edge of the universe, and together they risk their lives to save their home planets. An unexplained anomaly occurs where the sun's energy is being drained. If this continues, Earth will freeze and humanity will perish. It is discovered that the same phenomenon is happening not only to the sun but to countless stars scattered across the universe, and a single intact star is found 11.9 light-years away. Humanity's only remaining option is to travel to that star in a spaceship and solve the mystery to save the sun and humanity. Sent into space for this "Hail Mary" project is Grace, a brilliant scientist who left academia and now works as a humble middle school teacher. Alone in the vastness of space far from Earth, he relies on his scientific knowledge to tackle the mission, where he meets Rocky, an alien also struggling to save his home planet. Despite their different forms and languages, the two use science as a common language to face challenges, developing a friendship along the way. Ryan Gosling of "La La Land" and "Barbie" plays the protagonist middle school teacher Grace, with Sandra Hüller of "Anatomy of a Fall" and "The Zone of Interest" co-starring. Drew Goddard, who also worked on "The Martian," wrote the screenplay, and Phil Lord & Christopher Miller, known for producing and writing the "Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse" series, directed.
title:Proof of the Man: A black man is murdered in an elevator at a luxury hotel in Tokyo, leaving behind the word 'Stoha' and a poetry collection by Saijo Yaso. Fashion designer Kyoko Yasugi and her son appear and disappear along the investigative trail. Detective Muneyori travels to the United States to trace the black man's past. The unexpected relationship between Kyoko and the black man, as well as the connection between the American detective and Detective Muneyori, comes to light.
title:Puella Magi Madoka Magica the Movi: The first part of a two-part theatrical film reconstruction of the 12-episode TV anime 'Puella Magi Madoka Magica,' which aired from January to April 2011. One day, a mysterious transfer student named Homura Akemi arrives at the middle school attended by Madoka Kaname, an ordinary girl living a mundane life. After school that day, guided by a mysterious voice, Madoka encounters a strange creature calling itself Kyubey, who tells her, 'I want you to make a contract with me and become a magical girl.' The staff from the TV series, who built its unique worldview, including chief director Akiyuki Shinbo, screenwriter Gen Urobuchi (Nitroplus), and the otherworldly space design team Gekidan Inu Curry, have reunited for this film.

The second part of a two-part theatrical film reconstruction of the TV anime 'Puella Magi Madoka Magica,' which aired in 2011, created a huge sensation, and won numerous awards including the 16th Animation Kobe Award for TV Series, the 11th Tokyo Anime Award at Tokyo International Anime Fair 2012, and the Grand Prize in the Animation Division at the 15th Japan Media Arts Festival. Sayaka, who became a magical girl for the sake of her beloved Kyosuke, becomes consumed by despair upon learning the truth about magical girls and ultimately transforms into a witch. Madoka accepts Kyoko's proposal to try and save Sayaka, but... A dark fantasy depicting the harsh fate of five girls who chose to fight as magical girls in exchange for having just one wish granted.

The third film in the theatrical series of "Puella Magi Madoka Magica," which aired on TV from January to April 2011 and received high acclaim and popularity, including winning the Grand Prize in the Animation Division at the 15th Agency for Cultural Affairs Media Arts Festival. Following the "Beginning Story" and "Eternal Story" films, which recompiled the 12-episode TV series, this is a completely new feature-length work with newly written script and animation. In a new world where Madoka Kaname freed magical girls from the chain of cruel fate, Homura Akemi, left behind unable to fulfill her feelings for Madoka, continues to fight alone, believing she can meet Madoka again. New magical girl Nagisa Momoe appears as a new character alongside Madoka and Homura.
title:Pusher: Frank, a highly skilled drug pusher, makes money with his partner Tony by carrying out jobs for drug kingpin Milo. After taking a huge loan from Milo for a large deal, a police raid causes the deal to fail, and Frank loses the money, facing relentless pressure from his boss to repay the debt. A crime action drama that depicts a man spiraling into a hellish debt trap in the underworld of rampant drug trafficking, pushed to his absolute limits, all rendered in dark, stylish visuals. This is Nicolas Winding Refn's landmark debut film, hailed as the Danish film that first achieved worldwide success as a gangster movie.
title:Pusher II: The second film in the 'Pusher' trilogy, an early crime drama by Danish director Nicolas Winding Refn, who gained global attention with 'Drive.' It centers on drug dealer Tonny, the sidekick of protagonist Frank from the first film, depicting the struggles and battles of a man returning from prison. Released from prison, drug dealer Tonny starts helping his gangster father, who is connected to Copenhagen's underworld, but fails repeatedly. One day, he learns that an acquaintance, Charlotte, has given birth to his child, and decides to go straight. However, unable to refuse, he helps with a drug deal that goes wrong, saddling him with a huge debt and dragging him back into the underworld. Mads Mikkelsen reprises his role as drug dealer Tonny, winning the Robert Award (Denmark's Academy Award) for Best Actor. The trilogy, including 'Pusher' and 'Pusher 3,' had its first theatrical release in Japan in 2013. In May 2026, the trilogy will be revived in 4K digitally restored versions as a special program for the 'Nordic Treasure: Mads Mikkelsen's 60th Birthday Festival.'
title:Pusher III: The concluding chapter of director Nicolas Winding Refn's crime drama "Pusher" trilogy, which he made in his native Denmark early in his career, before gaining international acclaim with "Drive." It depicts the loneliness and decline of power of Milo, the drug lord who appeared throughout the series. Copenhagen drug lord Milo is busy preparing for his beloved daughter's birthday party while also trying to close a heroin deal. However, due to a mix-up, what arrives is not heroin but a large quantity of ecstasy tablets. Milo, who had planned to use the heroin money to pay off his debts, reluctantly orders his subordinate Muhammad to sell the ecstasy, but Muhammad disappears along with the drugs. Cornered, Milo is gradually consumed by madness and takes unexpected action. Zlatko Buric, who played Milo in the previous two films, reprises the role. The trilogy was first released theatrically in Japan in 2013. In May 2026, the trilogy will be revived in 4K digitally restored versions as a special program within the "Nordic Treasure: Mads Mikkelsen 60th Birthday Festival."
title:Puss 'n Boots Travels Around the W: Péro, a restaurant waiter in a certain town, gets into an argument with the arrogant Lord Groumon and makes a bet: "I'll travel around the world in eighty days. If I fail, I'll become Groumon's slave." Pursued by time, Péro continues his arduous journey with a father-and-son mouse duo and Carter, the restaurant's cook, but is obstructed by Dr. Garigari, Lord Groumon's henchman, and the mysterious beauty Susanna.
title:Quatre nuits d'un rêveur: Jacques, an aspiring painter, saves a young woman named Marthe from throwing herself into the Seine one night. She had a lover who left for America a year ago, and that very night was when they had promised to reunite. Jacques finds her, sunk in anguish, beautiful. Driven by a fierce impulse of love, he forces himself to remain calm, hoping her heart will drift away from her lover, while feeling guilt over this. Like the 1957 version, this is a modern adaptation of Dostoevsky's famous tragic love story, a poignant work revealing Bresson's awakened worldview. Visconti's romanticism is absent here; the young man's blind love is brutally exposed as he pours out his feelings into a mini tape recorder, a habit of his, making it painful to watch.
title:REDLINE:
Based on an original story by Katsuhito Ishii (director of *Shark Skin Man and Peach Hip Girl* and *The Taste of Tea*), director Takeshi Koike—who helmed the "World Record" segment of the omnibus *The Animatrix*—brings this vision to life as an animated feature with a relentless commitment to hand-drawn techniques. The film depicts daredevil racers competing in "REDLINE," a race held once every five years to determine the fastest in the universe, brought to life through overwhelming visuals that took seven years and 100,000 hand-drawn frames to produce.

The cool protagonist JP, sporting a pompadour and leather jacket, is actually a shy and pure-hearted man. To win the heart of his first love, Sonoshee, he decides to enter "REDLINE," an anything-goes car race held in the military nation of "Roboworld." He enters the race in the ultimate machine customized by his childhood friend and genius mechanic, Frisbee, but the car has been rigged with a trap for match-fixing.

The film features a star-studded voice cast, including Takuya Kimura as JP, Yu Aoi as Sonoshee, and Tadanobu Asano as JP’s partner and mechanic, Frisbee. The screenplay was co-written by original creator Ishii alongside Yoji Enokido (*Neon Genesis Evangelion*) and Yoshiki Sakurai (*Ghost in the Shell: Stand Alone Complex*). Animation production was handled by Madhouse (*Summer Wars*).

Originally produced and released in 2010, the film saw a revival screening in February 2021 for its 10th anniversary. In December 2025, it will be screened as part of the special feature "Katsuhito Ishii World 30th Anniversary," celebrating the 30th anniversary of Ishii’s directorial debut.
title:RIP SLYME THE MOVIE 25th ANNIVERSA:
A live performance and documentary film featuring RIP SLYME, the pioneering group credited with pushing Japanese hip-hop into the mainstream. Following their major debut in 2001, the group made history with their 2002 sophomore album *TOKYO CLASSIC*, which became the first hip-hop album in Japan to achieve one million copies in sales. Producing a string of hits such as "One," "Rakuen Baby," and "Nettaiya," they paved the way for a generation of artists who followed in their footsteps. In April 2025, the five original members reunited for a limited time leading up to March 22, 2026, the 25th anniversary of their major debut. The release of their new song "Do ON" in May of that year garnered massive attention from both long-time fans and the "Reiwa generation" discovering them for the first time. 

The film captures RIP SLYME’s past and present, blending recent live performances and backstage footage with archival clips, a special New Year’s shrine visit filmed specifically for this project, and interviews with those close to the group. It is directed by Hiro Kanai, the acclaimed director behind hit TV dramas such as *The Confidence Man JP* and *HERO*, who shares a long-standing bond of trust with the members.
title:RRR: From S.S. Rajamouli, director of the "Baahubali" series, which was a huge hit and had a long theatrical run in Japan, comes this spectacular action entertainment set in the turbulent era of British colonial India, depicting the clash of friendship and duty between two men. In 1920, during British rule in India, Bheem rises to save a young girl kidnapped by the British army, while Rama becomes a police officer for the British government for a greater cause. Though they are on opposing sides, driven by their own passionate beliefs, fate brings them together without knowing each other's true identities, and they become inseparable friends. However, an incident forces them to choose between friendship and their missions. N.T. Rama Rao Jr., known for "Baadshah," plays Bheem, and Ram Charan, who starred in Rajamouli's "Magadheera," plays Rama. The title "RRR" is derived from the initials of "Rise," "Roar," and "Revolt." It became the first Indian film to gross over 1 billion yen at the Japanese box office. The song "Naatu Naatu" also became a sensation, winning the Academy Award for Best Original Song at the 95th Academy Awards, a first for an Indian film.
title:Ready or Not 2 : Here I Come: The sequel to the survival horror "Ready or Not," in which bride Grace, targeted for death in a traditional wedding-night game, flees the mansion of a wealthy family. The stage expands further, depicting Grace being drawn into a power struggle among the ultra-rich who secretly control the world. Grace survived the blood-soaked game, but the nightmare wasn't over. Her survival catches the attention of the rulers who secretly manipulate the world, and she is once again chosen as a target. The stage is the forbidden realm known as the Council, where chosen noble families vie for supremacy. Representatives of six noble families, bound by a pact with the demon Le Bail, attack Grace with their ancestral weapons, tasked with killing her by dawn. Her only ally is her long-estranged sister Faith, but the two are chained together and unable to move freely. In this extreme situation, their family bond is put to the test as they fight to survive. Samara Weaving reprises her role as Grace. Kathryn Newton ("Abigail") joins as sister Faith, along with new cast members Sarah Michelle Gellar, David Cronenberg, and Elijah Wood. As with the previous film, directing duties were handled by Matt Bettinelli-Olpin and Tyler Gillett of the filmmaking unit Radio Silence.
