title:Rear Window: After breaking his leg, photographer Jeff is confined to a wheelchair and bed rest. To stave off boredom, he makes a daily habit of watching the residents of the apartment building across the way through his window. One day, however, he notices that the bedridden wife who had been arguing with her salesman husband has disappeared. Enlisting the help of his girlfriend Lisa and his nurse Stella, he begins his investigation through the rear window. Piece by piece, he gathers circumstantial evidence suggesting the man murdered his wife, and his suspicion gradually hardens into certainty…
title:Red Desert: The first color film by Italian master Michelangelo Antonioni, this psychological drama won the Golden Lion at the 25th Venice International Film Festival in 1964. In Ravenna, an industrial coastal city lined with sterile factories, Giuliana lives with her husband and son but remains unable to recover from the shock of a car accident years earlier, spending her days in emotional instability. One day, her husband introduces her to his friend Corrado. Giuliana is drawn to Corrado, who carries a loneliness similar to her own, and gradually the two grow closer... Monica Vitti, known as Antonioni's muse, plays Giuliana, with British star Richard Harris as Corrado. A 4K restored version will be released in August 2026 as part of the retrospective program "Michelangelo Antonioni Retrospective: Arid Love, Wandering Souls," featuring five of Antonioni's early works.
title:Red Peony Gambler: Flower Cards Ga: The third film in the "Red Peony Gambler" series. In the mid-Meiji period, Oryu (Sumiko Fujiwara), traveling to learn the ways of the world, joins the Nishinomiya family, Nagoya's top gambling clan, ahead of the Atsuta Shrine Festival's charity gambling. However, she gets caught in a merciless conflict between the gambler Hanooka (Ken Takakura), who owes a debt to the Kimbara family aiming for the position of gambling boss, and both sides.
title:Rendezvous in Paris: Three stories about love and chance, all centered around a date in Paris.
title:Rental Family: Brendan Fraser, winner of the Academy Award for Best Actor for "The Whale," stars in this human drama shot entirely in Japan. Directed by Japanese filmmaker HIKARI, who gained attention for her feature debut "37 Seconds" and the drama series "Beef," the film follows a down-on-his-luck actor living in Tokyo who rediscovers himself through working for a rental family service. Philip, an American actor who once dominated toothpaste commercials but has since been largely forgotten, lives in Tokyo, eking out a living in the acting world and blending into the city. One day, he is hired by Tada, who runs a rental family company. The job involves playing the role of a cherished "family member" for clients in exchange for payment. Initially hesitant about delving into others' lives, Philip begins to change as he interacts with the people he meets through his work. Takehiro Hira plays Tada, the rental family company owner; Mari Yamamoto plays Aiko, an actress working for the company; and Akira Emoto plays Kikuo, an aging actor.
title:Reprise: The feature directorial debut of Joachim Trier, a Danish director distantly related to Lars von Trier who studied film in Denmark and England, released in 2006. This is the first work of the "Oslo Trilogy," which also includes his later films "Oslo, August 31st" and "The Worst Person in the World." Philip and Erik are childhood friends who have dreamed of becoming writers since they were kids. One day, they both send manuscripts to a publisher, but only Philip's is accepted. Philip becomes a suddenly famous author, but soon begins to suffer mental instability. Meanwhile, Erik continues writing novels without giving up... Anders Danielsen Lie, who stars in all three films of the "Oslo Trilogy," plays Philip. Selected as Norway's entry for the 79th Academy Awards for Best Foreign Language Film, it received high praise, winning the Grand Prix (Best Film), Best Director, and Best Screenplay at the Amanda Awards, Norway's equivalent of the Academy Awards. It received its first theatrical release in Japan as part of the special screening series "Joachim Trier: The Oslo Trilogy" (starting February 13, 2026, at Bunkamura Le Cinéma Shibuya Miyashita and other venues in Tokyo).
title:Return to My Blue: A short documentary following a boy on a ventilator as he takes on an adventure to a deserted island. Ten-year-old Sota Yoshihara, who requires advanced medical care, and his mother Sumiyo decide to join a tour that takes children with disabilities to a remote island in Okinawa. For Sota, who relies on a ventilator and needs electricity and medical care daily, a trip to an island with no electricity or water is far from safe—one wrong step could be life-threatening. Doctors initially say the tour is too difficult, but Sota's earnest wish to 'go on an adventure to a deserted island' ultimately moves a doctor to accompany the tour himself, making the journey possible. On the day of the tour, with the help of many people, Sota crosses the sea on a small fishing boat and sets foot on the deserted island. The film captures how one boy's small courage and challenge move those around him to fulfill his wish, and reveals moments that remind everyone of what is truly important in their own lives. Directed by Takehiro Noguchi, known for directing NHK's morning drama 'Anpan' and 'Yell' as well as the taiga drama 'What Will Ieyasu Do?', in his documentary directorial debut.
title:Returnees（リターニーズ） 元こども兵 それぞれの再起: Set in Uganda, East Africa, this documentary follows former child soldiers struggling to reclaim their lives and the efforts of a Japanese NPO supporting them. For over 20 years, Uganda was gripped by conflict between the government and the Lord’s Resistance Army (LRA), an anti-government insurgent group. During the civil war, the LRA abducted more than 30,000 children, forcing boys into combat and girls into forced marriages with soldiers. The LRA continues to operate from neighboring countries, where they still carry out child abductions. In 2023, approximately 140 former child soldiers and their families escaped from these active conflict zones. Known as "returnees," these individuals were kidnapped as children, deeply traumatized, and robbed of their futures. Having grown up in brutal conditions, they lack formal education and struggle to meet even their most basic needs. Shingo Ogawa, a director of the NPO Terra Renaissance, has developed a three-year training program to support their reintegration, standing by them as they work to regain their self-esteem and find a place in society. Recording these efforts over a period of two years, the film captures the former child soldiers as they take their first courageous steps toward a new life.
title:Rhapsody, Rhapsody: Actor Tsuyoshi Rishu, who has directed films such as 'Chloe' and 'Goodbye Debussy', takes the director's chair for a feature film for the first time in 13 years, with Issei Takahashi in the lead role. This human drama humorously depicts a man who has avoided social interactions, whose life takes an unexpected turn when he discovers he has been unknowingly registered as married to a woman he doesn't know. Mikio Natsuno, a slightly naive man who never gets angry, goes to get a copy of his family register to renew his passport and is shocked to find the words 'Relationship: Wife' for a woman he has absolutely no memory of. Learning that a woman named 'Shigeko' has registered herself as his wife without his knowledge, Mikio begins searching for this mysterious woman. He eventually finds Shigeko at a small flower shop on a street corner, but she is an unconventional woman who destroys everything she touches. Though Mikio is tossed around by Shigeko, this strange encounter gradually brings unexpected changes to both their lives. Issei Takahashi plays the kind-hearted and sensitive protagonist Mikio, and Kumi Goshima (NHK morning drama 'Manpuku') plays the enigmatic heroine Shigeko who bewilders everyone around her. Okihiko Serizawa and Chizuru Ikewaki co-star, and director Rishu also appears as a key character. World-renowned jazz pianist Junko Onishi provides the music.
title:Riceboy Sleeps: Set in 1990s Canada, this drama weaves the bond between a Korean immigrant mother and her son through beautiful 16mm film imagery. Soyoung, who became an unwed mother after losing her lover, moves with her infant son Donghyun to a suburb of Vancouver, Canada. Starting work at a factory, Soyoung faces language and cultural barriers as well as racial discrimination, but raises her son with determination. When Donghyun turns 16, he goes by the English name "David" and has fully adapted to life in Canada, but deep down he yearns to know his roots and the father he has never met. Then one day, receiving shocking news, the mother and son return to Korea for the first time, confronting a painful past. Director and screenwriter Anthony Shim, who himself immigrated from Korea to Canada at age eight, powerfully yet delicately portrays the fluidity of immigrant identity and the conflict and renewal between parent and child. Choi Seung-yoon, active in Korea as a dancer, choreographer, and actor, plays mother Soyoung, and Ethan Hwang of the drama "The Umbrella Academy" plays the teenage Donghyun.
title:Riceboy ライスボーイ: Set in 1990s Canada, this drama weaves the bond between a Korean immigrant mother and her son through beautiful 16mm film imagery. title:Rich Flu: A thriller dripping with black humor that depicts the collapse of capitalist society following the outbreak of a mysterious disease called "Rich Flu" that only infects the wealthy. Directed and written by Galder Gaztelu-Urrutia of the "The Platform" series, which sharply depicted social inequality, it thrillingly portrays the chaos brought about by a reversal of values. Laura, a high-ranking producer at a streaming platform company, prioritizes her career over her family and is on the verge of success in the glamorous film industry. But just then, a mysterious disease called "Rich Flu" suddenly spreads worldwide, killing wealthy people one after another. As wealth transforms from a symbol of success into a "mark of elimination," capitalist society collapses and the world descends into chaos. In this extreme situation, Laura makes a decision. Mary Elizabeth Winstead, known for films like "Gemini Man" and "Birds of Prey," plays the career-driven Laura who neglects her family. Raf Spall, who has appeared in major works like "Life of Pi" and "Jurassic World: Fallen Kingdom," plays Tony, her husband who is exasperated with her yet gets caught up in the unprecedented pandemic alongside her. Timothy Spall, known for the "Harry Potter" series and "Mr. Turner," plays the billionaire Sebastian Snail.
title:Ring: Reiko Asakawa, a TV station director, is investigating an urban legend when she notices that a man and woman rumored to have been involved with a 'cursed videotape' that kills viewers within a week died at the exact same date and time as her niece, Tomoko Oishi, who had died strangely a few days earlier. As her investigation progresses, Reiko discovers that Tomoko and the other three who died simultaneously were acquaintances, that they had stayed at a rental villa in Izu called 'Izu Pacific Land' a week prior, and that the faces of the four in film photos taken at that time are eerily distorted. Seeking to uncover the mystery of their deaths, Reiko visits the villa in question, watches the suspicious tape that was rented there, and immediately receives an eerie silent phone call. From that point on, Reiko's own photos also begin to show her face distorted, just like the four deceased.
title:River: The second original feature film by the popular theater troupe Europe Kikaku, led by Makoto Ueda. Following their acclaimed first feature "Droste no Hate de Bokura," Ueda writes the original story and script, with the troupe's video director Junta Yamaguchi directing. This ensemble comedy depicts the chaos of people trapped in a repeating two-minute time loop set in winter at Kibune, Kyoto. Mikoto, a waitress at the long-established inn Fujiya in Kibune, is called back to work by the landlady while standing by the Kibune River behind the annex. But two minutes later, she finds herself in the same spot. Not only Mikoto, but also the head clerk, waitresses, chefs, and guests all realize time is looping. After two minutes, time rewinds and everyone returns to their original positions, but their memories carry over. They work together to find the cause of the loop, but Mikoto alone harbors complicated feelings. Filmed in winter at Kibune with full cooperation from Kibune Shrine and the inn Fujiya. Starring Riko Fujitani as Mikoto, along with many Europe Kikaku actors, Yuki Torigoe, Manami Honjo, Saoi, and Yoshimasa Kondo. Shiori Kubo of Nogizaka46, who has ties to Ueda and Europe Kikaku through stage productions, makes a guest appearance in a key role.
title:Robot Carnival: Produced during the mid-1980s when original video animation was booming, this omnibus work pushes forward the director's individuality. Katsuhiro Otomo handles the opening and ending, packing the essence of his animation into a short time. The English title logo features a building drawn in meticulous detail so its structure is discernible. The composition of it running as a machine, and the imagery of a toy-box-like, amusement-park-like interior collapsing carefully step by step, truly feels like a microcosm of 'Steamboy'. While other directors develop unique worlds around the theme of 'robots', Otomo creates a short film that is more relaxed and visually driven.
title:Robot Dreams: The first feature-length animated film by Spanish director Pablo Berger, known for 'Blancanieves.' Based on the graphic novel of the same name by American author Sara Varon, it depicts the friendship between a dog and a robot in 1980s New York, where anthropomorphic animals live, entirely without dialogue or narration. In Manhattan, New York. Dog, deeply lonely, builds a robot to be his friend, and they deepen their bond. In summer, Dog and Robot go to the beach, but Robot rusts and becomes immobile. Dog tries everything to repair Robot, but the beach closes for the off-season with Robot left behind, and the two are separated. Nominated for Best Animated Feature at the 96th Academy Awards in 2024.
title:Rochelle:
Winner of the Best Short Film Award at the 2025 New Zealand Screen Awards. Reckless young Mac decides to give his late friend's beat-up car, "Rochelle," one last moment in the spotlight. He heads to the local junk car race. At first his friends are exasperated, but soon they are moved by Mac's dream and begin to cheer him on in earnest...
■ Ticket price: 1,000 yen flat rate (Free tickets, invitation tickets, and other discounts are not applicable.)
■ Same-day discount at the box office: Present a ticket for another film viewed on the same day to receive 100 yen off. (Limited to tickets purchased at the box office on the day.)
Making movie theaters a more casual option. "20 Minute Cinema" is a new initiative screening short films of 15–20 minutes in theaters. A 20-minute stop you can drop into like a café between shopping or after work. Masterpieces from around the world you won't find on streaming services will add vibrant color to your daily life.
title:Rokkoku Kitchen: A documentary that observes people's lives and the present state of Fukushima through the dining tables of those living along National Route 6, commonly known as "Rokkoku," where areas still remain designated as difficult-to-return zones.
title:Romance Express: Aboard an express train from Tokyo to Osaka, waitress Sayoko (Dan) pressures kitchen assistant Kiichi (Frankie) to marry her. An adaptation of a popular novel by Bunroku Shishi, this ensemble comedy depicts the chaos stirred up by a group of eccentric passengers sharing the dining car.
title:Room for Let: In a large rundown house overlooking the Tsutenkaku Tower in Osaka, a group of eccentric lodgers live... Frankie, in his famous partnership with Kawashima, plays a laid-back jack-of-all-trades who works as a ghostwriter and konnyaku maker. With unique supporting actors like Naniwa and Ozawa, this is a brilliant ensemble comedy that leaves a lasting impression.
title:Rosetta: A film by the Dardenne brothers, directors of 'The Promise,' portraying a woman who tenaciously survives despite adversity. Rosetta lives with her alcoholic mother in a trailer at a campground. One day, she is fired from her job for no apparent reason. Rosetta, confronting the harsh realities of society, desperately continues searching for new work... Winner of the Palme d'Or and Best Actress award at the 1999 Cannes Film Festival.
title:Roujin Z: In the near future, to cope with an aging society, the Ministry of Health and Welfare develops a sixth-generation computer with self-replicating functions, the elderly care machine 'Unit Z001.' However, this computer absorbs the elderly selected as samples and goes on a rampage, causing a huge uproar involving volunteer female college students and the media.
title:Ryuichi Sakamoto | Playing the Orc: Ryuichi Sakamoto performed with a full orchestra in Japan for the first time in 16 years at the acclaimed concert "Playing the Orchestra 2013." As an updated version, the 2014 Tokyo concert, which he conducted himself, became "Ryuichi Sakamoto | Playing the Orchestra 2014." At this concert, Sakamoto played the piano while conducting all pieces, performing a diverse repertoire—from YMO-era classics to masterpieces like "Merry Christmas, Mr. Lawrence" and "The Last Emperor," as well as his film scores—with the Tokyo Philharmonic Orchestra.
title:Ryuichi Sakamoto | Trio Tour 2012:
World-renowned musician Ryuichi Sakamoto’s "Trio Tour 2012"—a concert series performed in a trio arrangement of piano, cello, and violin—comes to the big screen. In 1996, Sakamoto released the album *1996*, a work that achieved peak musical expression through a simple trio configuration, leading to a highly acclaimed world tour. In 2012, he produced the long-awaited trio album *THREE* and embarked on a 12-show tour of Japan and South Korea alongside long-time collaborator Jaques Morelenbaum (cello) and Judy Kang (violin), who was selected through an online audition. 

The repertoire includes classics from his YMO days, iconic film scores such as "Merry Christmas Mr. Lawrence" and "The Last Emperor," and the new piece "Shizen no Koe." Furthermore, reflecting the tour’s visit to the Tohoku region just one year after the Great East Japan Earthquake, the performance also features the charity song "Kizuna World" and "Yae no Sakura," the main theme for the Taiga drama set in Fukushima. This film captures the complete performance at Tokyo’s Akasaka ACT Theater, a show where a sense of tension and intimacy quietly coexisted. The audio has been specially reconstructed for the cinema to faithfully recreate the atmosphere of the venue to the fullest extent.
title:SAGRADA: El misteri de la creació: A documentary about the Sagrada Família, the century-spanning architectural project conceived by Catalan architect Antoni Gaudí, under construction since 1882 for over 130 years. Registered as a World Heritage Site in 2005, the Sagrada Família continues to captivate over three million visitors annually from around the world. As construction continues towards a projected completion in 2026, computers have been introduced on site, and staff repeatedly experiment to determine how to best reproduce Gaudí's vision with current technology. Incorporating footage from inside the site, inaccessible to outsiders, and interviews with architectural staff, the film unravels the project surrounding the Sagrada Família, including how the construction period, once said to require '300 years until completion,' has been shortened to a projected completion in 2026.
title:SAKAMOTO DAYS: A live-action film adaptation of the hit comic by Yuto Suzuki, serialized in Shueisha's "Weekly Shonen Jump", starring Ren Meguro of "Snow Man". It comically depicts a legendary retired hitman running a small shop who throws himself into battle to protect his beloved family and peaceful daily life. Sakamoto Taro, once feared as the "strongest ever," falls in love at first sight with a woman named Aoi who works at a convenience store, and promptly retires from being a hitman. After marrying and having a daughter, he becomes the manager of a small shop called "Sakamoto Store" and enjoys a happy family life, having grown so fat that he no longer resembles his former self. One day, a 10 billion yen bounty is suddenly placed on Sakamoto, and assassins from all over the world attack him. With his former subordinate, the esper Shin, as his partner, Sakamoto rises to protect his peaceful daily life. Meguro uses special makeup to portray two contrasting versions of Sakamoto: a plump one weighing an estimated 140 kg and a sleek one who rapidly loses weight when he gets serious, and also takes on full-fledged action scenes. Takahashi Fumiya plays Sakamoto's partner Asakura Shin; Ueto Aya plays Sakamoto's wife Aoi; Yokota Mayuu plays Lu Shaotang, a tai chi expert working at Sakamoto Store with Shin; Tozuki Junki plays Masumo Heisuke, a skilled sniper; Kitamura Takumi plays Nagumo, a member of the hitman world's highest force "ORDER"; Yagi Yusei plays Kamigami; and Nemu Yumemi plays Daibutsu. Directed and written by Yuichi Fukuda of the "Gintama" series.
title:SAYAMA みえない手錠をはずすまで: This documentary follows Kazuo Ishikawa and his wife, Sachiko. Ishikawa was convicted of the 1963 "Sayama Incident"—the murder of a high school girl in Sayama City, Saitama—through a forced confession and fabricated evidence, and he continues to maintain his innocence to this day. Having endured 32 years in prison and 19 years on parole, Ishikawa has lived with the stigma of being a murderer for over half a century. Despite his petitions for a retrial being repeatedly rejected, he and Sachiko continue their fight for justice. Through their unwavering journey and their perspective that they were "unlucky, but not unhappy" despite a lifetime of hardship, the film conveys universal messages about the beauty of life, happiness, love, friendship, and justice.
title:SEX:
The first installment in a trilogy by Norwegian director Dag Johan Haugerud—a former bestselling author and librarian—this film explores three perspectives on "romance," "love," and "sex" set in the Norwegian capital of Oslo. With a comedic touch, it depicts two married men as they reconsider their "masculinity" following unexpected experiences.

The two men, both chimney sweeps with families, find their lives disrupted. One discovers a new sense of excitement after an unexpected sexual encounter with a male client; however, his relationship with his wife becomes strained when he tells her about the experience without a hint of remorse. The other begins to wonder how his own identity is shaped by the gaze of others after dreaming that David Bowie perceives him as a woman. Having lived as "good fathers" and "good husbands," both men must now confront their own sense of masculinity and identity.

The film won three awards at the 74th Berlin International Film Festival in 2024, including the Ecumenical Jury Prize. In Japan, it will be released in theaters in September 2025 as part of the special screening series "Oslo: Three Landscapes of Love," alongside the other entries in the trilogy, "LOVE" and "DREAMS."
title:SHIBOYUGI: Playing Death Games to: A sequel to the 2026 TV anime 'Death Game de Meshi o Kū,' based on the popular light novel by Yūshi Ukai, this theatrical anime adapts the original 'Cloudy Beach' arc. A deadly murder game where survival earns you prize money. Allies you encouraged yesterday can become enemies today, and even with full preparation, you can lose your life. The girl Yūki aims to clear this life-or-death game 99 times, making a living from the prize money she wins. Overcoming the 'Wall of Thirty'—a jinx where player survival rates drop drastically—she continues forward and takes on her 44th game, 'Cloudy Beach.' Among the eight players gathered on a remote island, Yūki spots a familiar veteran. Continuing from the TV anime, Sōda Ueno of 'Stepsister Life' directs, with animation production by Studio Deen.
title:SPh: Director Macoto Tezka’s first feature-length 16mm film. "Sph" is an abbreviation for "Spiritual Phenomenon" (fairy phenomenon). Moe Imai plays the heroine, a fairy.
title:SUPER HAPPY FOREVER: On August 19, 2023, Sano and Miyata visit a seaside resort hotel in Izu. Sano had recently lost his wife Nagi, whom he had met and fallen in love with there five years earlier. Miyata, as a friend, tries to advise Sano, who is clinging to memories of his wife and becoming self-destructive, but Miyata's words, steeped in a certain seminar he is devoted to, do not reach Sano. Exchanging few words, the two visit the now-closed restaurant and sightseeing boat filled with memories, and begin searching for the red hat that was lost long ago.
title:SUPER HAPPY FOREVER《2周年アンコール上映》: On August 19, 2023, Sano and Miyata visit a seaside resort hotel in Izu. Sano had recently lost his wife Nagi, whom he had met and fallen in love with there five years earlier. Miyata, as a friend, tries to advise Sano, who is clinging to memories of his wife and becoming self-destructive, but Miyata's words, steeped in a certain seminar he is devoted to, do not reach Sano. Exchanging few words, the two visit the now-closed restaurant and sightseeing boat filled with memories, and begin searching for the red hat that was lost long ago.
title:Sabrina: A romantic comedy directed by Billy Wilder, starring Audrey Hepburn in the year following "Roman Holiday." Sabrina, the daughter of a chauffeur serving the wealthy Larrabee family, falls in love with the family's younger son. To make her forget this hopeless love, her father and fellow servants send Sabrina to Paris. Two years later, Sabrina returns as a refined lady, and her transformation is so complete that the younger son and his brother fail to recognize her as the chauffeur's daughter. In 2013, a digitally remastered version was released as part of the special screening series "Screen Beauties Vol. 1: Audrey Hepburn."
title:Sai: Disaster: A psychological suspense film directed, written, and edited by Yutaro Seki and Kentaro Hirase of the filmmaking collective "May," who gained domestic and international attention for their 2022 feature debut "Miyamatsu to Yamashita." It stars Kōji Yakusho, who also collaborated with them on that previous film. This is the theatrical version of the WOWOW drama series "Wazawai" (Disaster), broadcast from April to May 2025. It boldly restructures the six-episode series into a single film, depicting the calamity brought by a single man who infiltrates the everyday lives of six unrelated people. A high school girl troubled by family and her future, a deliveryman with a past, a shopping mall cleaner and a barber, the manager of a debt-ridden inn, and an ordinary housewife. The modest daily lives of these six people are suddenly struck by inexplicable disasters. The police dismiss them all as suicides or accidents, but Detective Dōmoto senses something strange and pursues the truth. Lurking around the edges of these six disasters is a single man. Changing his personality and appearance, he appears before the six as completely different people, bringing calamity upon them. Detective Dōmoto is played by Anne Nakamura, his colleague by Pistol Takehara and Kaito Miyakuni, and the people struck by disaster by Sena Nakajima, Ryuhei Matsuda, Megumi Uchida, Shunki Fujiwara, Jiro (Shisonne), and Maki Sakai.
title:Sailor Suit and Machine Gun: The boss of a small yakuza gang called Medaka-gumi, who has only four underlings, dies leaving a will stating that his successor must be a blood relative. Around the same time, high school girl Izumi Hoshi is saying her final goodbye at the crematorium to her father Takashi, who died after being hit by a car in front of Narita Airport. Izumi's mother passed away long ago, leaving her truly alone. When Izumi returns to her apartment, a woman named Mayumi is there, carrying a letter from her father that says, 'If I die, please take care of Izumi.' The next day, a crowd of men in black suits lines up in front of her school. Ignoring her friends Tomoki, Tetsuo, and Shuhei, who try to stop her, Izumi heads toward the school gate. The man from the crematorium steps forward and says, 'You're Izumi Hoshi, right?' This man, named Sakuma, takes her to a shabby office and asks her to succeed as the fourth-generation boss of the Medaka-gumi.
title:Saint Seiya: Legend of Crimson You: The third theatrical film. The immensely powerful sun god Abel is resurrected, and his sister Athena abandons the protagonists who have fought alongside her to leave with Abel. The scene where the usually energetic protagonist sheds tears emphasizes the boy's purity and fragility. The revival of the five "Gold Saints" who died in the TV anime is also a highlight. As part of the 20th anniversary of "Weekly Shōnen Jump," this was released as a 75-minute extended version, double-billed with "Sakigake!! Otokojuku."
title:Saint Seiya: The Heated Battle of: Warriors clad in constellational armor, the 'Saints,' fight for the goddess Athena. With beautifully exaggerated bodies designed by Shingo Araki and Michi Himeno, special moves accompanied by lavish screen effects like transmitted light, fast-paced action, emotional direction, and an orchestral score, it became a representative action anime of the 1980s. The first theatrical film was directed by TV series director Toshio Morishita and depicts the resurrection of the evil god Eris.
title:Sakamoto Days: A live-action film adaptation of the hit comic by Yuto Suzuki, serialized in Shueisha's "Weekly Shonen Jump", starring Ren Meguro of "Snow Man". It comically depicts a legendary retired hitman running a small shop who throws himself into battle to protect his beloved family and peaceful daily life. Sakamoto Taro, once feared as the "strongest ever," falls in love at first sight with a woman named Aoi who works at a convenience store, and promptly retires from being a hitman. After marrying and having a daughter, he becomes the manager of a small shop called "Sakamoto Store" and enjoys a happy family life, having grown so fat that he no longer resembles his former self. One day, a 10 billion yen bounty is suddenly placed on Sakamoto, and assassins from all over the world attack him. With his former subordinate, the esper Shin, as his partner, Sakamoto rises to protect his peaceful daily life. Meguro uses special makeup to portray two contrasting versions of Sakamoto: a plump one weighing an estimated 140 kg and a sleek one who rapidly loses weight when he gets serious, and also takes on full-fledged action scenes. Takahashi Fumiya plays Sakamoto's partner Asakura Shin; Ueto Aya plays Sakamoto's wife Aoi; Yokota Mayuu plays Lu Shaotang, a tai chi expert working at Sakamoto Store with Shin; Tozuki Junki plays Masumo Heisuke, a skilled sniper; Kitamura Takumi plays Nagumo, a member of the hitman world's highest force "ORDER"; Yagi Yusei plays Kamigami; and Nemu Yumemi plays Daibutsu. Directed and written by Yuichi Fukuda of the "Gintama" series.
title:Sana: Play with Me: Directed by Takashi Shimizu of the "Ju-On" series, this school horror film stars Suzuka Chinzei of the idol group FRUITS ZIPPER in the lead role. A secret rumor circulates among young people about a forbidden game: if you record a date and name onto a cassette tape on the 13th step of an empty school staircase, that person will die. High school students casually try the game, and their daily lives begin to warp. One by one, those whose names were recorded on the tape die mysteriously on the specified dates. The school takes the situation seriously and asks psychological counselor Koharu Hirase to provide mental care for the students. Koharu counsels a student who witnessed the incidents, but among those who played the game is her younger sister, Nanami. As students are attacked by strange phenomena one after another, Koharu and Nanami are dragged into a chain of terror. Suzuka Chinzei takes on her first solo lead film role and first horror role as counselor Koharu; Anna Hoshino (from "Gold Boy") plays Koharu's sister Nanami; Riku Onishi (from "Water Flows Toward the Sea") plays classmate Jotaro Chiba who looks out for Nanami; and Shota Sometani plays a young man who holds the key to the story.
title:Sangue del mio sangue: A Gothic fantasy film by Italian master Marco Bellocchio, released in 2015 and winner of the FIPRESCI Prize at the 72nd Venice International Film Festival. The story intertwines the 17th century and the modern era, depicted with eerily beautiful imagery. In 17th-century Bobbio, northern Italy, young soldier Federico visits an old monastery to uncover the truth behind the death of his twin brother Fabrizio, a priest. It is said that Fabrizio was seduced by a nun named Benedetta, betrayed his faith, and lost his life. Seeking to restore his brother's honor, Federico tries to make Benedetta confess her guilt, but gradually becomes captivated by her, even as she is accused of witchcraft. The story then shifts to the modern day, centuries later. The former monastery lies in ruins, and a sale to a wealthy Russian is being negotiated. A man appears, but the ruins are haunted by a mysterious old count who only shows himself at night. Benedetta is played by Lidia Lieberman, Federico (living in both past and present) by Pier Giorgio Bellocchio, and the mysterious old count by Roberto Herlitzka. A cover of Metallica's "Nothing Else Matters" is used prominently in the film.
title:Sans toit ni loi: A film by renowned French filmmaker Agnès Varda, tracing the steps of a young girl who freezes to death after wandering, which won the Golden Lion, the top prize, at the 42nd Venice International Film Festival in 1985. In winter in southern France, the body of an 18-year-old girl, Mona, is found frozen to death in a roadside ditch in the countryside. The film traces Mona's journey over the final weeks of her life as she hitchhikes aimlessly and continues a solitary journey, through the testimonies of the people she met on the road. Starring Sandrine Bonnaire (from "The Hairdresser's Husband"), with co-stars Macha Méril (from "Belle de Jour"), Stéphane Freiss (from "The Five Senses"), and Yolande Moreau (from "Séraphine"). It recorded over one million admissions in France at the time, becoming Varda's biggest hit.
title:Sansho the Bailiff: Commentary: In the Heian period, Zushio and Anju, separated from their parents, are sold into slavery... A film adaptation of Ogai's short story based on a medieval folktale, this timeless masterpiece won the Silver Lion at the Venice International Film Festival. The visual beauty captured by the renowned cinematographer Miyagawa is also awe-inspiring.
title:Sarvam Thaala Mayam: A youth music film about a young man's struggle to become a player of the mridangam, a traditional Indian percussion instrument. Peter, the son of a mridangam craftsman living in Chennai, India, is inspired to become a player himself after seeing a master perform on a mridangam his father made. Apprenticing under the master and training diligently, Peter faces various challenges including caste discrimination, conflicts over preserving traditional arts, and generational differences, but confronts them with passion and respect. The music is composed by A. R. Rahman, who won an Academy Award for 'Slumdog Millionaire.' G. V. Prakash Kumar, Rahman's nephew and a renowned film music composer, plays the protagonist Peter. Screened under the title 'The World Is Full of Rhythms' in the World Focus section of the 31st Tokyo International Film Festival in 2018. For its theatrical release in October 2022, the film was distributed by 'Nandori,' a South Indian restaurant in Tokyo's Arakawa Ward that fell in love with the film.
title:Sasuke and His Comedians: Director Takashi Kato presents an unconventional period action film depicting the story of the Sanada Ten Braves, who fought in the Winter and Summer Sieges of Osaka, with fantastical fun and excitement! Affected by the radiation of a meteorite that fell from space, the Warring States street urchin Sasuke gains mysterious abilities. Growing up, he calls himself Sarutobi Sasuke and, along with the flying squirrel Okiri, becomes a subordinate of the cool commander Sanada Yukimura, rampaging through the rigged Winter and Summer Sieges of Osaka!
title:Satoshi: A Move for Tomorrow: Murayama Takashi, who suffered from a serious illness since early childhood, discovers shogi during repeated hospitalizations and, at age 15, becomes a disciple of Mori Nobuo. Ten years later, Takashi moves to Tokyo to fulfill his dream of becoming a Meijin champion. Supported by those around him, he devotes himself fully to shogi, and after reaching the rank of 7-dan, he develops a fierce rivalry with Habu Yoshiharu, who won the Meijin title in the same generation. Takashi immerses himself even deeper in shogi, but cancer gradually consumes his body...
title:Scarborough: A Canadian drama that captures the lives of people on the fringes of society with an honest gaze, following three children living in harsh circumstances as they form bonds at a local community education center. In Scarborough, a diverse, multicultural neighborhood in eastern Toronto. Bing, a Filipino boy who fled his mentally ill father's violence to come to this town; Sylvie, a girl of Indigenous heritage living in a shelter with her family of four; and Laura, a girl neglected and tossed about by her parents—these three find a safe haven at the education center run by social worker Hina. Despite their difficult circumstances, they nurture a small but meaningful bond... The lead roles are played by three children making their film debut, and the supporting cast includes non-professional actors from Scarborough. The film is based on Canadian author Catherine Hernandez's debut novel "Scarborough," which she adapted from her own experiences. Directors Shasha Nakai and Rich Williamson, highly acclaimed in the documentary field, made their narrative feature debut with this film. It won eight awards, including Best Picture and Best Director, at the 10th Canadian Screen Awards in 2022.
title:Scarface: A violent action film starring Al Pacino from 'The Godfather' series, depicting the rise and fall of a man climbing Miami's criminal underworld in the 1980s, with extreme violence. Directed by Brian De Palma, written by Oliver Stone, it is a modern remake of Howard Hawks' classic gangster film 'Scarface'. In 1980, many criminals flood into America among Cuban refugees. Tony Montana, an anti-Castro exile arriving in Miami, takes on a hit at a refugee camp for Frank, a Miami drug lord. Tony gains trust through drug deals and murders for Frank, while also falling for Frank's mistress Elvira. As Tony rises in the underworld, his arrogance and insatiable greed drive him toward destruction. Al Pacino embodies Tony's madness and desire with intense performance. Steven Bauer plays Tony's right-hand man Manny, Robert Loggia plays drug lord Frank, and Michelle Pfeiffer plays Frank's mistress Elvira. With domestic screening rights ending at the end of June 2026, a 4K revival screening is held.
title:Scrap Heaven: The third feature film by director Sang-il Lee, made in 2005, based on his original screenplay. It depicts young people carrying aimless anger and loneliness as they attempt small acts of rebellion against an unreasonable society. Shingo, who became a police officer dreaming of being a "hero of justice," is fed up with days spent doing only desk work and after-the-fact paperwork. One day, he encounters a bus-jacking incident. On the bus are a young man, Tetsu, and a woman in sunglasses, Saki. For Shingo, it should have been the perfect situation, but the incident ends without him laying a finger on the culprit. Three months later, Shingo coincidentally meets Tetsu again, and prompted by Tetsu's words, "This world lacks imagination," the two begin a game of "revenge proxy," fulfilling the wishes of people who have despaired of society. Requests for revenge pour in one after another, and dragged along by the free-spirited Tetsu, their game escalates. Meanwhile, Saki, working as a pharmacist, conducts secret experiments in her room. Tetsu and Shingo's game heats up further, and things begin to spiral in unexpected directions. Ryo Kase plays Shingo, Joe Odagiri plays Tetsu, and Chiaki Kuriyama plays Saki. The rock band Fujifabric provides the ending theme. Scheduled for a revival screening in April 2026.
title:Sedmikrásky: A landmark film of the 1960s Czech New Wave, this work portrays the wild antics of two uninhibited girls, both named "Marie," using a boldly experimental array of techniques including color shifts, coloring, optical effects, innovative sound design, and abrupt scene transitions. The older sister, with a blonde bob and a daisy wreath, and the younger sister, with dark brown hair in two pigtails, both call themselves "Marie" and pretend to be siblings. They live freely, tricking men into buying them meals only to fake-cry and run away. At home, they do whatever they please—bathing in milk, burning paper, cutting out magazine photos, slicing up bed sheets, and eventually cutting each other's bodies, until the screen itself fragments. Directed and written by Věra Chytilová, a pioneering Czech filmmaker and the most prominent female director of the Czech New Wave. The two leads were played by non-professional actresses selected through auditions: Jitka Cerhová and Ivana Karbanová. Other roles were also filled by non-actors, such as composers and designers. The film had its first official theatrical release in Japan in 1991 at Kichijoji Baus Theater, where it ran for an extended period through word of mouth. It has since gained a cult following, and in March 2026, a 4K restored version will be re-released to commemorate the 60th anniversary of its production and the 35th anniversary of its Japanese release.
title:Seek: Shane Kosugi, son of action star Sho Kosugi who sparked the ninja boom in Hollywood and brother of Kane Kosugi, makes his feature directorial debut with this action film themed around ninjas believed to be extinct. Chinese martial arts world champion Kansuke Asano, who became a world champion in his teens, stars and produces, with Kane Kosugi also appearing. Ninjas living in modern-day Japan have changed their names and appearances, secretly carrying out missions as agents of the non-governmental organization 'Shiju-ku (49)'. Kyōhei Aizawa, one of the most skilled agents in history, loses his beloved lover, the only person he truly trusted, in a plane crash. As he contemplates the meaning of life in solitude, Kyōhei is assigned an infiltration mission into the Japanese yakuza group Takatsuki-gumi. After Kyōhei successfully completes the mission, the Takatsuki-gumi, learning of his existence, begins eliminating people around him by any means necessary for a certain purpose. Realizing that his loved ones are disappearing because of him, Kyōhei confronts the Takatsuki-gumi alone. Asano plays the protagonist Kyōhei, with Seiki Miura and Nanana among the cast.
title:Sentimental Value: Swedish director Joachim Trier, who gained international attention with "The Worst Person in the World," crafts a family drama centered on the tangled bonds of love and hate inherent in the parent-child relationship. Nora, an actress thriving in Oslo, and her sister Agnes, who chose family life and lives quietly with her husband and son. One day, their father Gustav, a film director who abandoned the family when they were young and has been out of contact for years, reappears and offers Nora the lead role in his first autobiographical film in 15 years. Filled with anger and disappointment toward her father, Nora firmly refuses, and soon the popular young American actress Rachel is cast instead. When Nora learns that the film will be shot at the family's old home, a place filled with memories, uncontrollable emotions surge within her once again. Renate Reinsve, who also starred in "The Worst Person in the World," plays the protagonist Nora, with acclaimed actor Stellan Skarsgård as her father Gustav. Inga Ibsdotter Lilleaas plays sister Agnes, and Elle Fanning plays the popular American actress Rachel. The film won the Grand Prix at the 78th Cannes Film Festival in 2025. At the 98th Academy Awards, it received nine nominations across eight categories, including Best Picture, and won the award for Best International Feature Film.
title:Seven Days War: At Aoba Junior High, where strict discipline is enforced, eleven boys and girls rise up in pursuit of freedom. They bring food and barricade themselves in an abandoned factory, while the teachers try to disband them strictly according to school rules. The students fend off the teachers using various means, but... A lighthearted youth drama based on the original novel by So Munetari. Screened simultaneously with "Flower's Asuka Gang!".
title:Sgt. Frog: As part of the 20th-anniversary project for the TV anime "Sergeant Keroro," based on the manga by Mine Yoshizaki serialized in "Monthly Shonen Ace" since 1999, this theatrical anime is the first in 16 years since "Keroro Gunso the Super Movie: Creation! Ultimate Keroro, Wonderous Time-Space Island!!" in 2010. It depicts the Keroro Platoon, who were supposed to invade Earth, fighting to protect the planet from a new invader. Sergeant Keroro and his platoon members, who came to Earth to invade but now spend their days idly at their host family's home, encounter mysterious phenomena occurring across the country. Feeling a sense of crisis, the Keroro Platoon rises to the challenge, putting their pride as invaders on the line, but they encounter mysterious letters wherever they go. The screenplay and general direction are handled by Yuichi Fukuda, known for directing the live-action "Gintama" series. The staff includes key members who have supported the series, with Satoshi Ozaki as director, Satoshi Koike as character designer, and BN Pictures handling animation production. Jesse from SixTONES voices the theatrical original characters, the brothers Aruru and Deruru, playing both roles.
title:Shadow of Fire: Director Shinya Tsukamoto, known for "Fires on the Plain" and "Killing," depicts the lives of people carrying despair and darkness in the black market just after the end of the war. A woman living alone in a small, surviving izakaya is forced into selling her body and spends her days without the will to resist, overwhelmed by despair. One day, a child who lost their family in an air raid sneaks into the woman's izakaya to steal food. From then on, the child begins to frequent the place, and through her interaction with the child, the woman begins to find a faint glimmer of light. Hikari Mitsushima, known for "Just Remembering," delivers a delicate yet bold performance as the protagonist, the woman. Mirai Moriyama plays a mysterious man with a paralyzed arm, Sōga Tsukao, a child actor known for "The Last 10 Years," plays a war orphan, and Hironori Kōno, known for "Special Actors," plays a young repatriated soldier. It was screened in the Orizzonti section of the 80th Venice International Film Festival in 2023 and won the NETPAC Award (Best Asian Film Award).
title:Shall We Dance?: Directed by Masayuki Suo of "Sumo Do, Sumo Don't" fame, this heartwarming comedy became a huge hit by depicting a middle-aged man rediscovering his life through ballroom dancing. Shohei Sugiyama is an ordinary salaryman with no complaints about his work or family life, yet he feels a vague emptiness. One day, on the train home from work, he spots a woman standing by the window of a dance studio and is captivated by her beauty. Later, he begins learning ballroom dancing at that very studio and becomes deeply absorbed in the world of dance through interactions with a colorful group of fellow students. Koji Yakusho plays the protagonist Sugiyama, while ballerina Tamiyo Kusakari plays Mai. In 2004, the film was remade in Hollywood starring Richard Gere and Jennifer Lopez.
title:Shall We ダンス？: Directed by Masayuki Suo of "Sumo Do, Sumo Don't" fame, this heartwarming comedy became a huge hit by depicting a middle-aged man rediscovering his life through ballroom dancing. Shohei Sugiyama is an ordinary salaryman with no complaints about his work or family life, yet he feels a vague emptiness. One day, on the train home from work, he spots a woman standing by the window of a dance studio and is captivated by her beauty. Later, he begins learning ballroom dancing at that very studio and becomes deeply absorbed in the world of dance through interactions with a colorful group of fellow students. Koji Yakusho plays the protagonist Sugiyama, while ballerina Tamiyo Kusakari plays Mai. In 2004, the film was remade in Hollywood starring Richard Gere and Jennifer Lopez.

title:Sheep in the Box: A feature film directed by Hirokazu Kore-eda ("Monster", "Shoplifters"), starring Haruka Ayase and Daigo (from the comedy duo "Chidori"), based on an original script about a couple who welcome a humanoid in the form of their deceased son. Set in the near future. Architect Kōmoto Oto and her husband Kensuke, the second-generation president of a construction company, take in a humanoid resembling their son Sho, who died two years ago. On the day the humanoid arrives, Oto joyfully welcomes him with Sho's same smile and voice, while Kensuke hides his bewilderment behind a stiff expression. Family time gradually begins, but an unexpected event occurs, revealing the couple's hidden feelings about their son's death. Meanwhile, the humanoid Sho secretly starts connecting with other humanoids. The role of the deceased son Sho and his humanoid counterpart is played by Kuwaki Rito, chosen from over 200 auditionees. Kiyono Yasho plays Oto's younger sister Kotaki Arisu; Kanichiro plays Nikawa Gen, an employee at Kensuke's construction company Tamaken; Yo Kimiko plays Oto's mother Nishimura Nobuyo; and Tanaka Min plays Yamagata Akio, a skilled worker at Tamaken. The title "The Sheep in the Box" is derived from a passage in Antoine de Saint-Exupéry's classic novel "The Little Prince". The film was selected for the Competition section of the 79th Cannes Film Festival in 2026.
title:Shinpei: A brother who cannot fit into society, a father who has given up on the future, and a sister bound to the home. This is a story of the small steps the three of them take forward. One day, the Great East Japan Earthquake suddenly upends their peaceful daily lives. Not only the earthquake and tsunami, but also the nuclear accident forced many people to lose their homes and jobs, leaving Fukushima behind. This is the story of a family living in the aftermath, three years later, in a deeply scarred Fukushima.

title:Shoplifters: Directed by Hirokazu Kore-eda of "The Third Murder" and "Our Little Sister," this human drama portrays human connections through the lens of a family that engages in petty crimes together. At the 71st Cannes Film Festival in 2018, it won the Palme d'Or, the top prize, for the first time for a Japanese film since "The Eel" in 1997. It also earned high praise overseas, including a nomination for Best Foreign Language Film at the 91st Academy Awards, the first for a Japanese film in a decade. At the 42nd Japan Academy Film Prize, it won eight awards, including Best Picture. In a working-class district of Tokyo, in an old one-story house seemingly left behind among high-rise apartments, live the homeowner Hatsue, the couple Osamu and Nobuyo, their son Shota, and Nobuyo's younger sister Aki, all dependent on Hatsue's pension. They make ends meet by shoplifting, living on the fringes of society, yet their days are filled with laughter. One winter day, Osamu brings home a little girl shivering on the balcony of a nearby apartment complex, and Nobuyo decides to raise her as a daughter. Triggered by an incident, the close-knit family begins to fall apart, revealing the secrets and desires each of them harbors. Alongside regular Kore-eda collaborators Lily Franky as the father Osamu, who repeatedly shoplifts with his son, and Kirin Kiki as Hatsue, the film marks the first Kore-eda works for Sakura Ando as Nobuyo and Mayu Matsuoka as Aki, Nobuyo's sister.
title:Shot the Voice of Freedom: A documentary recording the daily struggles of women who continue to seek freedom in Afghanistan under Taliban rule. In August 2021, the Taliban seized control of nearly all of Afghanistan, collapsing the two-decade democratic government. With the Taliban's return to power, women were once again barred from working outside the home, deprived of educational opportunities, and girls were forced into marriages with much older men and confined to their houses. Sisters Rashmin and Nastaran, along with other women, take to the streets to raise their voices against countless inequalities. Undaunted even by armed men, they hide smartphones under their scarves to film and broadcast the current situation in Afghanistan. They continue their resistance while moving from one relative's home to another, but in a patriarchal society, their father despises the women participating in demonstrations, and they are forced to live in fear of neighbors informing on them. Despite such harsh circumstances, Rashmin, driven by the desire not to make the next generation experience the same suffering, rushes out into the streets. The director is Zainab Entezar, an Afghan-born female filmmaker, producer, and writer who, while living in exile, continues to broadcast the voices of the women of her homeland to the world.
title:Sing Street: A semi-autobiographical work by director John Carney of "Begin Again" and "Once," this youth drama depicts the love and friendship of a boy who forms a band to impress a girl he likes, set to 1980s British sounds. In 1985 Dublin, Ireland, struggling through a severe recession, 14-year-old Conor is forced to transfer to a rough public school after his father loses his job. At home, his parents constantly fight, pushing the family to the brink of collapse. Conor's only solace in his miserable days is watching music videos from neighboring London on TV with his music-obsessed older brother. One day, captivated by the mature charm of a girl named Raphina he sees on the street, Conor invites her to appear in a music video for his band. Hurriedly forming a band, Conor begins intense training to create a video that will amaze the London music scene...
title:Sinners: A survival thriller directed by Ryan Coogler ('Black Panther,' 'Creed'), starring Michael B. Jordan, with whom Coogler has frequently collaborated on feature films. In the 1930s, in a devout small town in the American South, twin brothers Smoke and Stack open a dance hall in their former hometown, serving illegal alcohol and music in pursuit of a fortune. On opening night, the crowd revels in a night of swirling desires, but the arrival of uninvited guests changes everything. The dance hall is consumed by senseless despair, and a night of chaos beyond human comprehension begins. Jordan plays the dual role of the twin brothers. The cast includes Hailee Steinfeld ('Bumblebee'), Jack O'Connell ('Ferrari'), and Delroy Lindo ('Da 5 Bloods'). Coogler also wrote and produced the film, reuniting the 'Black Panther' team including production designer Hannah Beachler, composer Ludwig Göransson, and costume designer Ruth E. Carter. At the 98th Academy Awards, it received a record-tying 16 nominations, including Best Picture and Best Director, winning four awards: Best Actor (Michael B. Jordan), Best Original Screenplay, Best Cinematography, and Best Original Score.
title:Sinsin and the Mouse: A human drama based on a story from Banana Yoshimoto's short story collection 'Mitten and Fubin', co-produced by Japan and Taiwan. It quietly depicts a woman carrying loss who, through encounters in a foreign land, gradually finds renewal. Chizumi is a woman living each day with deep grief after losing her mother. As time passes without filling the void in her heart, she is invited by a friend to visit Taiwan. There, she meets Shin-shin, a young man with a Taiwanese mother and a Japanese father. The unfamiliar cityscapes and the accumulation of casual conversations slowly begin to move her frozen heart, and Chizumi, while still carrying her lingering sense of loss, discovers small warmth. Yukino Kishii ('Small, Slow but Steady', 'Just the Two of Us') plays the protagonist Chizumi, and popular young Taiwanese actor Tseng Jing-hua (known for 'The Soul of the Prisoner', 'Your Name Engraved Herein') plays Shin-shin, the young man she meets in Taiwan. The cast also includes Tokio Fujiwara, Seina Nakata, Tokio Emoto, Kayo Ise, Kisuke Iida, and Kimiko Yo. Directed and scripted by Yukinori Makabe ('I Am a Monk.', 'Scoop!').
title:Sirat: This road movie, blending a fantastical story with cool dance music, follows a father and son's journey through a desert rave party in search of a missing daughter, sparking buzz across Spain and Europe. Luis drives with his son Esteban from the Moroccan mountains deep into the desert to find his daughter, who disappeared after attending a desert rave. They reach an outdoor rave site where reality and hallucination blur, but she is not there. The father and son chase a group of ravers, heading to the next rave site where they believe she went. Sergi López ("Pan's Labyrinth") plays father Luis. Directed and written by Oliver Laxe ("Fire Will Come"), the film is produced by renowned Spanish master Pedro Almodóvar. The title "Siraat" means "path" in Arabic and, in a religious sense, symbolizes the narrow bridge over heaven and hell on Judgment Day. Screened in the Competition section of the 78th Cannes Film Festival in 2025, it won four awards including the Jury Prize. It was nominated for the Academy Awards for Best International Feature Film and Best Sound at the 98th Academy Awards.
title:Siren and Life – ウクライナで続く、戦争と日常。: In late May 2026, at a theater in Tokyo, the first feature-length documentary film *Siren and Life* by filmmaker and street photographer Kaito Tada was screened. Director Tada made his debut as a film director at the 2022 Zushi Film Festival with the short documentary *Our Beautiful Playground*. His second work, the documentary *Siren and Life*, which depicts the reality of everyday life in Ukraine, garnered significant attention, drawing an audience of 156 people over just two days of screenings. Now, a special screening with a talk event has been scheduled for July 20 (Monday, public holiday) at Uplink Kichijoji. On the day, in addition to Director Tada, three panelists will take the stage: art director Marina Takahashi, who handled the visual design, and Dante Kuwajima, who served as the interviewer in the film. They will speak at length in an interview-style format, including a Q&A session, about topics related to the film and the attention to detail in the book production.
