title:The Long Walk: The first-ever film adaptation of Stephen King's first novel, "The Long Walk," written while he was in college in the 1960s and published under the pseudonym Richard Bachman in 1979. In a near-future America divided by war, a national competition called "The Long Walk" is held as a beacon of hope for a struggling society. Fifty selected teenage boys challenge this contest, where the only requirement is to keep walking. The prize is a staggering sum of money and the fulfillment of one wish. The rules are simple: maintain a pace of 4.8 km/h, receive a warning if you slow down, be executed after three warnings, and keep walking until only one person remains. Surrounded by armored vehicles and under the threat of guns, the boys desperately continue walking in extreme conditions with no rest or sleep allowed... Starring Cooper Hoffman ("Licorice Pizza") and David Johnson ("Alien: Romulus") as the young participants, and Mark Hamill ("Star Wars" series) as the Major who oversees the competition. Directed by Francis Lawrence ("The Hunger Games" series) with a screenplay by J.T. Molner ("Strange Darling").
title:The Longing: A human drama about a young man who could only feel himself through committing crimes, and how he finds meaning in life through his encounter with a couple running an okonomiyaki restaurant. Directed and written by Toshizo Fujiwara, who has acted in films such as "A Scene at the Sea," the film was selected for the Panorama section of the 75th Berlin International Film Festival in 2025. Hiroyuki and Sonoko Kiuchi, a couple running an okonomiyaki shop, hire former prisoners and juvenile detention center graduates to help them reintegrate into society. However, since an incident involving a former employee a year ago, they have been plagued by online harassment. During an interview at a juvenile detention center, the Kiuchis meet 18-year-old Yuto Nishimura, who pleads to start his life over, and they hire him as a new employee. Yuto begins working earnestly, but after a certain event, he reconnects with his old friends and becomes strongly drawn to Yukiha, a dancer he meets at a club. The script was written based on extensive research at various sites, including an okonomiyaki shop in Osaka that actually supports the employment of former prisoners and juvenile detainees, and incorporates Fujiwara's own experiences. Daiki Ido stars in his first leading role as Yuto, Fujiwara plays Hiroyuki, Rino Tsuneishi plays Sonoko, with supporting roles by Tomoko Fujita and Jiei Kabira.
title:The Lost Weekend: A serious drama acclaimed worldwide, winning four Academy Awards and the Grand Prix at the Cannes Film Festival. Don, a struggling writer living in New York, drowns his days in alcohol. Desperate for drink money, he steals from his brother and even tries to sell his typewriter. Ray Milland delivers a powerful performance as Don wandering the depths of despair, earning him an Oscar for Best Actor. Director Wilder met his second wife, Audrey Young, during the making of this film.
title:The Love That Remains: In a small rural town in Iceland, artist Anna lives with her responsible eldest daughter Ida, her mischievous twin sons Grímur and Þorgils, and her dog Panda, while searching for her path as an artist. Though she married young and is supposedly "no longer a couple" with her ex-husband Magnús, he can't seem to cut ties, constantly finding excuses to visit, share meals, and even join picnics. Before she knows it, they slip back into a daily life as if they were "still a family"—but what comes next?
title:The Major and the Minor: Billy Wilder's second directorial work, which was never theatrically released in Japan. This was his highly anticipated first Hollywood film, successfully casting the era's star Ginger Rogers. To save money on train fare to Iowa, Susan disguises herself as a 12-year-old girl. A faint affection begins to blossom between her and Colonel Philip, who happens to be on the same train... Although the film touches on the theme of attraction to a minor, it was produced 12 years before the publication of the bestselling novel "Lolita."
title:The Man in the White Suit: A social satire comedy that depicts the fate of a scientist obsessed with developing a 'miracle fiber' that never gets dirty, delving into the fundamental contradictions of capitalism. One of the 'Ealing Comedies,' a series of comedy films produced at Ealing Studios in the UK from the late 1930s to the mid-1950s, directed by Alexander Mackendrick, known for 'The Ladykillers.' Sidney, a scientist working in the British textile industry, spends his days experimenting to develop a fiber that never gets dirty and never frays, no matter how much it's washed. He builds strange contraptions in a corner of the factory, remaining expressionless and unfazed by the lack of understanding around him. With the backing of the company president and his daughter Daphne, Sidney finally completes the 'miracle fiber,' but... The lead role of the scientist Sidney is played by the renowned actor Alec Guinness, known for 'Star Wars' and 'The Bridge on the River Kwai.' This film is part of the special screening series 'The Golden Age of British Ealing Comedies' (June 20–July 17, 2026, at Shinjuku K's Cinema).
title:The Metropolitan Opera: El Último: The eighth installment of the 2025-26 season of "MET Live Viewing," which records and screens the latest opera performances at the Metropolitan Opera House in New York. Based on Mexican painters Frida Kahlo and Diego Rivera, this production reverses the setting of the classic Italian opera "Orfeo ed Euridice," depicting a deceased wife returning from the underworld to her husband for just one day in "Frida and Diego: The Last Dream" (recording of the performance staged on May 30, 2026). In 1957, on Mexico's Day of the Dead. Diego, who lost his wife Frida three years earlier, is tormented by age and grief, longing to reunite with her. Meanwhile, Frida, freed from suffering in the underworld, is told by La Catrina, the guardian of the dead, that she should accompany Diego at the end of his life, and reluctantly agrees to return to the earthly world for only 24 hours. Diego and Frida have a moving reunion, but Frida is bound by a rule that she must not touch the living.
title:The Moment: A film conceived by global musician Charli XCX, who also stars, depicting the turbulent behind-the-scenes world of show business involving top stars and industry insiders. In 2024, pop star Charli XCX became a global sensation with her album "brat," sparking a social phenomenon called "Brat Summer" and becoming an icon of the era. Bold and unapologetic, she daily pursues her authentic self. However, her music label, manager, and social media handlers, using the slogan "Brat Summer Forever," try to forcibly prolong the movement, intervening in live performances and promotions with backing from Amazon, pushing Charli into a clichéd star image. Overwhelmed by her busy schedule, Charli escapes to Ibiza for a vacation just days before a live show, throwing the production into chaos. Directed by Aidan Zamiri, who has directed music videos for Billie Eilish and others. The cast includes Alexander Skarsgård, Rosanna Arquette, and Kylie Jenner.
title:The Monkey King 2: Five hundred years after the violent Son Goku was imprisoned under Five Elements Mountain, he is freed from his seal by the monk Sanzo, who is heading to India, and joins the journey as Sanzo's bodyguard. Along the way, the group gains new companions, but they are confronted by the demoness Hakukotsu-fujin, who seeks to kill Sanzo in order to maintain her own eternal beauty. Using various schemes, Hakukotsu-fujin finally captures Sanzo.
title:The Monkey King 3: Continuing their westward journey to India, Sanzo and his companions Son Goku, Cho Hakkai, and Sha Gojyo are attacked by a giant fish while traveling by boat on a river. The four are swept through a mysterious hole in the sky and land in a strange land—the "Land of Women," where only women live. The queen and Sanzo develop mutual affection. Soon, the four are sentenced to execution under the land's laws, but they manage to escape thanks to the queen's intervention. However, they have no idea how to return from the Land of Women to their original world...
title:The Mountain: A film adaptation of the novel "Iwaiyama" by Nanami Kamon, an author known for works on folklore and the occult, based on her own experiences, starring Ai Hashimoto. Directed and written by Shingo Takeda, a filmmaker who has won awards at film festivals for his horror works, marking his feature-length theatrical debut. Horror novelist Minami Kano, suffering from writer's block, receives a letter from her middle school classmate Asako Yaguchi. The letter describes unexplainable phenomena that have been occurring ever since she went on a dare to visit a ruin known as a haunted spot. Seeking material for her new work, Minami reunites with Asako and their old friends, and becomes entangled in mysterious events. As the investigation progresses, it emerges that behind the series of strange occurrences lies the forbidden mountain "Iwaiyama" they once set foot on. Ai Hashimoto plays the protagonist Minami Kano, marking her first horror film role in ten years since "Zan: The Haunted Room." The cast also includes Ren Ishikawa, Sayu Kubota, Takuya Kusakawa, Yuya Matsuura, and Go Riju.
title:The Mouths: A film adaptation of the bestselling novel 'A Survey About the Mouth' by author Senkin, who sparked the mockumentary horror boom with 'About a Certain Place in the Kinki Region.' Published in 2024, the palm-sized, 60-page story became a huge sensation on social media for delivering a solid scare in such a short format. Directed by Takashi Shimizu of the 'Ju-On' series, it marks Rihito Itagaki's first solo lead role in a live-action film. A group of university students hear a rumor about a 'cursed tree' in a cemetery known as a haunted spot and visit it for a test of courage. The next day, one of the group members mysteriously disappears. Since then, inexplicable phenomena begin to occur around the students who visited the cemetery, and they are gradually driven into a corner. Guided by the baffling testimonies of the five students, a terrifying truth emerges. Rihito Itagaki plays Shota Murai, one of the university students. The cast also includes Keito Tsuna as Tatsuya, Ai Yoshikawa as An, MOMONA (ME:I) as Mirei, Shuto Mori (BUDDiiS) as Horita, a student who visits the cemetery for fun, Tomoki Nishiyama (TAGRIGHT) as Kawase, who is forcibly taken to the cemetery by Horita, Shido Nakamura as Detective Kusabe, who pursues the missing student, and Tokio Emoto as journalist Nishi.
title:The Naked Spur: Like 'The Naked Spur,' this is a Technicolor Western directed by Anthony Mann and starring James Stewart, produced by William H. Wright of 'Violent Behavior' in 1953. The screenplay was written by up-and-coming radio and TV writing team Sam Rolfe and Harold Jack Bloom, cinematography by William C. Mellor of 'Cross Missouri,' and music by Bronisław Kaper of 'The Wolf of the North.' Co-stars include Janet Leigh of 'Blood Fight,' Robert Ryan of 'The Three Bad Men of the Wilderness,' newcomer Ralph Meeker of 'The Four Jeeps,' and Millard Mitchell of 'Singin' in the Rain.'
title:The New King of Comedy: Mo dreams of becoming a movie actress. But she remains a perpetual extra, and the only roles that come her way are bit parts where her face never even appears, or corpse roles. One day, her minor cosmetic surgery for a role catches the eye of a staff member, and she is selected for the blockbuster "Snow White: Bloody Chinatown," starring former star actor Ma. But Ma is the absolute worst in both acting and personality—a troublemaker clinging to past glory. A washed-up actor Ma, and Mon, fighting to climb out from the bottom. Before long, this encounter will drastically change both of their lives—!!
title:The Ninth Configuration: The directorial debut of William Peter Blatty, known as the author of 'The Exorcist,' who adapted his own novel. Blatty wrote, directed, produced, and scripted this unique human drama set in an old castle used as a psychiatric hospital. In a remote mountain castle serving as a sanatorium, soldiers driven insane by the Vietnam War are gathered and treated. Among them is astronaut Billy Cutshaw, who was committed after going mad just before a rocket launch. One day, Navy psychiatrist Hudson Kane arrives at the facility. Kane listens sympathetically to the patients, but Cutshaw is defiant, and Kane soon begins to be plagued by nightmares. Won the Golden Globe for Best Screenplay. Stars Stacy Keach of 'Roadgames' and 'Escape from L.A.' Although never theatrically released in Japan, it will have its first theatrical screening in 2026 as part of the 'Shinjuku Hardcore Masterpiece Selection 2' special screening (April 17 - May 21, 2026, at CineMart Shinjuku).
title:The Old Oak: British master Ken Loach delivers the final chapter of his 'North East England Trilogy', following 'I, Daniel Blake' and 'Sorry We Missed You'. Set in a former mining town in Northern England, 'The Old Oak' is the last remaining pub cherished by locals. About 30 years after the town's vibrant heyday, it now faces harsh times, but owner TJ Ballantine struggles to keep it going through trial and error. However, when the town begins accepting Syrian refugees, the pub—once a place of solace—turns into a battleground for belonging. Wrestling with the pub's uncertain future, TJ meets Yara, a Syrian woman with a camera, and unexpectedly forms a friendship. Scripted by Paul Laverty, Loach's longtime collaborator, the film is portrayed with warmth and realism. Dave Turner, who appeared in 'I, Daniel Blake' and 'Sorry We Miss You', plays pub owner TJ. Winner of the Audience Award at the 2023 Locarno Film Festival, and screened in competition at the 76th Cannes Film Festival.
title:The Orphan Brother: Summoned by Toei's top brass seeking a weighty drama, screenwriter Sumie Tanaka was brought on board. The story follows aristocratic siblings reduced to slavery, overcoming their suffering through social advancement. Animators strongly objected to the narrative's obliviousness to societal power structures, yet the breathtakingly beautiful Yamato-e style visuals, where backgrounds and characters harmonize perfectly, captivate the viewer.
title:The Outside Man: A crime suspense film co-produced by France, Italy, and the United States, starring the renowned French actor Jean-Louis Trintignant, known for "A Man and a Woman" and "The Conformist." Lucien, a French hitman, arrives at Los Angeles International Airport. Checking into a Beverly Hills hotel and concealing a pistol, Lucien drives to the upscale residential area where his target, a crime boss, lives. After efficiently eliminating the target, Lucien returns to the hotel only to find that someone has checked him out and his passport and plane ticket are gone. As Lucien becomes paranoid, a hail of bullets suddenly rains down on him from an unknown assassin. Alongside Trintignant as Lucien, the film features a cast of distinctive French, Italian, and American actors including Ann-Margret from "The Hunter" and Roy Scheider from "The French Connection." Directed by Jacques Deray, known for the two "Borsalino" films and "Flic Story." The screenplay is by Jean-Claude Carrière, who worked on numerous masterpieces such as "The Unbearable Lightness of Being" and "The Discreet Charm of the Bourgeoisie." After more than half a century since its production in 1972, it receives its first Japanese release in 2026 in a 4K remastered version.
title:The Outwaters: A found footage horror film that uses avant-garde visuals and storytelling to depict four men and women visiting a desert who encounter unimaginable terror. Three memory cards are discovered in the Mojave Desert, containing horrifying footage. One day, Robbie, Angela, Scott, and Michelle come to the Mojave Desert in California to shoot a music video. But when night falls, strange sounds, lights, and inexplicable phenomena begin to occur. Soon, the four are swallowed by a rift in reality, and the camera captures the nightmare that befalls them. Robbie Banfitch, a multi-talented filmmaker, screenwriter, actor, and musician from New Jersey, makes his feature-length directorial and screenwriting debut, also starring in the lead role.
title:The Panda's Great Adventure: In 1972, two pandas were gifted from China, and Japan was swept by an unprecedented panda boom. Released amid that frenzy, this film is a coming-of-age tale of Ron Ron, a panda prince of the Bear Kingdom, who faces numerous trials to become king. The animation director was Nobuya Takahashi, who designed many characters in the Toei Magical Girl series. It is also the last Toei Animation film in which Koji Mori participated.
title:The Peanut Butter Falcon: A human drama depicting the adventure of three people—a down-on-his-luck fisherman, a young man with Down syndrome who escapes from a care facility, and a nurse from the facility—as they journey to fulfill the young man's dream. Zack, a young man with Down syndrome living in a group home, escapes to enroll in a professional wrestling school, a dream he has had since childhood. Tyler, a fisherman living a lonely life after the death of his brother, tries to flee on his boat after being caught stealing someone else's catch. Zack happens to meet Tyler, and Eleanor, the nurse who came looking for Zack, joins them. The three head to a destination for Zack's sake. Shia LaBeouf plays Tyler, Dakota Johnson plays Eleanor, and Zack Gottsagen, who inspired the film's creation, plays Zack. John Hawkes and Thomas Haden Church round out the supporting cast. The film marks the feature directorial debut of Tyler Nilson and Michael Schwartz.
title:The Place Promised in Our Early Da: Makoto Shinkai, who rose to prominence with his fully digital personal animation "Voices of a Distant Star" in 2002, makes his feature-length directorial debut. Set in post-war Japan divided north and south by the Tsugaru Strait, it depicts boys struggling to save a girl burdened with the world's mysteries. In Japan under US military rule, middle school students Hiroki Fujisawa and Takuya Shirakawa in Aomori admire a giant tower standing across the strait in Hokkaido, and secretly work on assembling an airplane at an abandoned station site, dreaming of one day reaching that tower. One summer vacation, they confide their airplane secret to their classmate Sayuri Sawatari, another object of their admiration. The three share the dream of reaching the tower together, enjoying a brief period of happiness, but in the summer of their third year of middle school, Sayuri transfers away without explanation. The dream of reaching the tower by plane fades, and three years pass. Hiroki and Takuya, having gone their separate ways, reunite when dark clouds gather over the world situation and the tower's secrets gradually come to light. Voice cast includes actors Hidetaka Yoshioka and Masato Hagiwara.
title:The Power of Utopia: Living with L: A documentary about Chandigarh, the planned city built in India by Le Corbusier, the master of modernist architecture who left behind numerous legendary buildings. In 1947, India and Pakistan gained independence, and Punjab was divided between the two countries. With the state capital Lahore belonging to Pakistan, India needed to build a new capital. Prime Minister Nehru wanted a city symbolizing faith in the future and democracy, entrusting Le Corbusier with designing the planned city of Chandigarh. Born in the wilderness at the foot of the Himalayas, the "Shining City" of Chandigarh aimed to be a human-centered utopia where natural order and modern technology were in perfect harmony, symbolizing a new India. How has this city transformed 70 years after its birth? The film traces the buildings and their history, while residents—architects, urban activists, and artists—discuss the challenges Chandigarh faces and its enduring charm. Screened as part of the special program "Le Corbusier and Doshi: Modernism in India" (from May 1, 2026, at Eurospace in Tokyo and other theaters nationwide).
title:The President's Cake: Lamia, chosen as the 'honorable' cake maker, goes out to town with her grandmother and friend the rooster to search for cake ingredients──
title:The Professor and the Burlesque Qu: At the Totten Foundation in New York, eight scholars are putting the finishing touches on an encyclopedia, but when grammar professor Potts overhears a slang term, he realizes their work has been isolated from the real world and ventures into the city to investigate. There, he seeks the help of O'Shea, a nightclub singer... Although the film was a hit in the U.S. upon release, it was never imported due to the times. Billy Wilder contributed to the script on the condition that he be allowed to observe Hawks' direction. He made his directorial debut the following year, having used this as preparation.
title:The Promise, Architect BV Doshi: A documentary about the world-renowned Indian architect Balkrishna Doshi. Balkrishna Vithaldas Doshi, who in 2018 became the first Indian to win the Pritzker Prize, considered the Nobel Prize of architecture, passed away in 2023 at the age of 95. Beginning his career under Le Corbusier in Paris in the 1950s, he oversaw the implementation of Corbusier's projects in Ahmedabad, western India, and later collaborated with Louis Kahn after India's independence. Influenced by Corbusier and Kahn, Doshi incorporated sustainable and ecological ideas into his architecture early on, establishing a unique style that fused modernism with Indian tradition, climate, and spirituality. He aimed for architecture that contributes to society and the environment, a 'people's architecture' rooted in daily life. This film delves into Doshi's inner world in his final years, visiting the buildings he collaborated on with Corbusier and Kahn, as well as his own works, as he discusses his architectural philosophy, creative process, and career spanning 70 years. Screened as part of the special program 'Le Corbusier and Doshi: Indian Modernism' (starting May 1, 2026, at Eurospace in Tokyo and other theaters nationwide).
title:The Quiet Girl: Set in early 1980s Ireland, this human drama depicts a special summer vacation experienced by a 9-year-old girl. It won the Grand Prix in the International Generation section for films starring children at the 72nd Berlin International Film Festival and was nominated for the International Feature Film Award at the 95th Academy Awards. In 1981, in a rural Irish town, a quiet girl named Cott, who lives silently within a large family, spends her summer vacation at the lush green farm of the Kinsella couple. Initially confused by the unfamiliar life, Cott receives abundant love from Sean and Eileen and, as she carefully experiences each moment, comes to feel a joy in living she had never known before. Catherine Clinch, in her debut role, delicately portrays the protagonist Cott with overwhelming transparency and presence, winning the IFTA Award (Irish Film & Television Academy Award) for Best Actress at the youngest age of 12. Based on the novel "Foster" by Irish writer Claire Keegan, this is the first feature-length fiction film directed and written by Colm Bairéad, who has previously focused on children's perspectives and family bonds in his documentary works.
title:The Reality Behind What We See - T: The film opens with footage of the tsunami from the Great East Japan Earthquake (courtesy of the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism). The new work by Gozo Yoshimasu, 'A Water Tree Stands on the Planet,' born at the climax of this film, was completed after the poet's long struggle. Yoshimasu had been unable to write poetry since the 2011 Great East Japan Earthquake. 'At the beginning of human life, there is amniotic fluid and bathwater; at the end, there is the water of the dying that moistens the lips,' says Yoshimasu. 'Water,' the source of life for humanity, has been an important theme for poets throughout history. However, the poet who directly witnessed the scars of the great tsunami lost his words to the impact of water that strips everything away. Instead of writing poetry, Yoshimasu began daily copying the poems of the Showa-era philosopher Takaaki Yoshimoto in rice-grain-sized characters, like a sutra transcription. The camera captures this strange and fascinating scene. 'Beside the Poem,' written over four years and which he calls 'Monster-kun,' is a massive work of nearly 700 pages. Within it, the actual voice of the representative Japanese poet Akiko Yosano (1878–1942) resounds, sanukite stones ring, and finally, an eerie scene unfolds as he flings ink onto paper like Jackson Pollock (USA, 1912–1956), the founder of action painting. Deviating from the act of writing, time accumulates on a single sheet of paper, creating an object-like state. This becomes a 'practice writing book' over a long period, leading to the gestation of a new work. One day, learning that Kyoto has as much groundwater as Lake Biwa (Japan's largest lake), the poet seeks a new path for poetic creation in Kyoto's water veins. The poet's tentacles begin to reach the water of Kyoto, which holds a giant cradle of water. Then, before Yoshimasu appears the phantom of Yasunari Kawabata, winner of the Nobel Prize in Literature. Resonating with the talent of seeing phantoms in Kawabata, who stayed in Kyoto and devoted himself to creative work, the poet gropes for the thread of his own poetic creation. What the poet's senses finally touch is the great Eastern spirit, the water god, the dragon. Yoshimasu hears the voice of water's destiny and takes up his brush. The story of Gozo Yoshimasu depicted in this film shows the path of a poet, standing at the abyss of creative despair, 'gaining new life.' The backdrop, like Kawabata's masterpiece 'The Old Capital' which earned him the Nobel Prize, is vividly colored by Kyoto's four seasons, Zen temples, and karesansui (dry landscape gardens).
title:The Resurrection of the Golden Wol: Legendary popular actor Yusaku Matsuda stars as a lone wolf with two faces—a salaryman and an outlaw—in this hit Kadokawa action film based on the novel of the same name by Haruhiko Oyabu, which was a huge success upon its release. Following his explosive popularity in the pioneering TV drama 'Taiyo ni Hoero!', Matsuda teams up again with director Tohru Murakawa and cinematographer Seizo Sengen—who also worked with him on the 'Game' film series and the drama 'Daitokai PARTII'—to break new ground in domestic hard-action cinema. A must-see film, Matsuda enhanced his wild charisma by experiencing live-fire shooting abroad for his role. Murakawa's signature long-take cinematography brings unique intensity to the gunfight scenes, and the final line is said to be an ad-lib by Matsuda himself, not in the script. Tetsuya Asakura appears to be an ordinary salaryman by day, but by night he trains his body and plots to take over a massive corporation. One day, he uses drugs he obtained to seduce his boss's mistress, Kyoko Nagai. Soon after, he discovers that a man named Sakurai is blackmailing company executives over an embezzlement scandal. Asakura skillfully manipulates Sakurai and the company to successfully become engaged to the president's daughter, Eriko. Meanwhile, burning with jealousy, Kyoko makes a fateful decision.
title:The Samurai and the Prisoner: Acclaimed director Kiyoshi Kurosawa ("Wife of a Spy," "Creepy") takes on his first period film, adapting the mystery novel of the same name by Honobu Yonezawa, which won both the 166th Naoki Prize and the 12th Yamaneko Prize. Murashige Araki rebels against Nobunaga Oda's tyrannical methods and holes up in Arioka Castle. Surrounded by the Oda army and isolated, Murashige struggles to control his hot-blooded retainers while relying on his wife, Chiyo, for emotional support, striving to protect the castle and its people. Amidst this, a boy is murdered inside the castle, followed by a series of strange incidents. With the suspects being the retainers and family members trapped inside the sealed-off castle, and the enemy outside, everyone falls into suspicion and paranoia. Cornered, Murashige seeks help from the genius military strategist Kanbei Kuroda, who was imprisoned after being sent as Nobunaga's envoy to persuade him, and sets out to solve the case. Starring Masahiro Motoki as Lord Murashige Araki, Masaki Suda as the genius strategist Kanbei Kuroda, Yuriko Yoshitaka as Murashige's wife Chiyo, Takao Aoki as Murashige's trusted retainer Kyusaemon Araki, Ryota Miyate (Snow Man) as the young retainer Saburo Inui, Tasuku Emoto as the skilled sniper Sagari Saika who witnesses the events, and Joe Odagiri as Juemon Kori, who operates in the shadows as Murashige's hidden blade. The film was selected for the Cannes Premiere section at the 79th Cannes Film Festival in 2026.
title:The Second Is a Christian: Kyoko, a nun at St. Saffron Church on Mount Rokko, plays hymns on the organ. Haruhiko Tenryu, the second-generation head of the Tenryu-gumi yakuza clan, is deeply in love with Kyoko because of her refined beauty, and has even forced his underlings to be baptized as Christians. Also harboring feelings for Kyoko is Detective Jindai, whose family runs a Tendai sect temple, presenting another formidable obstacle. However, Kyoko herself secretly harbors feelings for Eiji, whom she met fatefully one stormy day. As the feelings of those around her intertwine, Kyoko's destiny begins to move in an unexpected direction.
title:The Secret Battlefield: Four months before the attack on Pearl Harbor—what they saw was the conclusion: 'Japan's inevitable defeat.' In April 1941, there existed an organization called the 'Total War Research Institute,' where elites from across Japan were secretly gathered. The 'best and brightest' of the next generation, selected from bureaucrats, the military, and the private sector, were tasked with 'predicting' the outcome of a war with the United States and other foreign powers. After accumulating vast amounts of data and repeatedly running simulations with anguish and passion, what they saw was a shocking scenario of Japan's 'overwhelming defeat'—one that predicted almost everything except the atomic bombings. Not a single bullet is fired. But here lies the harshest battlefield, where the mind is the weapon. Why did Japan charge into a war it knew it would lose? Now, the 'inconvenient truth' buried in history bares its fangs on the screen.
title:The Seven Year Itch: A sexy comedy adapted by Billy Wilder from a hit stage play, following "Stalag 17." In a sweltering New York apartment, Richard is enjoying a temporary bachelor lifestyle while his wife and children are on vacation. A beautiful woman from the upstairs apartment comes down seeking air conditioning. The scene of Marilyn Monroe's white skirt billowing up as she stands over a subway grate is famously iconic. Tom Ewell, who also played the lead role on stage, reprises the role of Richard in the film version.
title:The Shadow's Edge: A battle action film starring Jackie Chan, depicting the fight between a police force led by a tracking expert and a cybercrime group led by a former assassin. In Macau, a series of clever heists by an elusive cybercrime group occur. With the surveillance system hijacked and the investigation stalled, the police seek help from Huang Dezhong, a retired tracking expert, as their trump card. Teaming up with young elite police officers, Huang Dezhong uses old-school investigative techniques and the latest technology to pursue the cybercrime group led by a former assassin known as 'Shadow.' Leon Ka-Fai, known for 'The Lover' and 'Cold War,' plays the former assassin leader of the criminal group, reuniting with Jackie Chan for the first time in about 20 years since 'The Myth.' JUN, a member of the popular K-POP group SEVENTEEN who also works as an actor, takes on his first villain role as a member of the criminal group. Zhang Zifeng, from 'Sister Summer's Farewell,' and Zusha, from the TV drama 'Mountain and River Shadows,' also appear. The film is directed and written by Larry Yang, who previously worked with Jackie Chan on 'Ride On.'
title:The Sheep Detectives: An unconventional mystery film starring Hugh Jackman, depicting sheep whose beloved owner is murdered as they struggle to find the culprit. In a peaceful English countryside town, shepherd George lives alone surrounded by his beloved sheep. He reads detective novels to them every night, and the sheep actually understand the stories and look forward to this time. One day, George is found dead. The sheep refuse to believe it was an accident and, led by their smartest leader Lily, launch an investigation. As they follow clues, they discover George had a huge inheritance. Determined to avenge their beloved George, the sheep race to find the killer. Hugh Jackman plays the victimized shepherd George, with Oscar-winning actress Emma Thompson, Nicholas Galitzine from "The Idea of You," and Nicholas Braun from the TV series "Succession" co-starring. Julia Louis-Dreyfus, Patrick Stewart, and Bryan Cranston voice the sheep. Based on the 2005 bestselling novel of the same name by German author Leonie Swann, directed by Kyle Balda of the "Minions" series.
title:The Smashing Machine: The untold story of mixed martial artist Mark Kerr, who rose to fame during the early days of the "PRIDE" tournament that captivated all of Japan, is brought to film by Dwayne Johnson—also known as the wrestler The Rock—who stars and produces. Making his MMA debut in 1997, Mark Kerr rose undefeated to the top. After consecutive wins in the UFC, he also made a stunning run in Japan's PRIDE, becoming feared as "the strongest man in the hominidae family," but the pressure quietly eroded his mind. Kerr gradually became dependent on painkillers, and his relationship with his girlfriend Dawn deteriorated. After experiencing his first defeat, he finally confronts his own weakness and decides to step back into the ring to rebuild his life. Dwayne Johnson, inspired by the 2002 documentary of the same name, personally secured the film rights and carefully portrays the vulnerable side of a tough man. Emily Blunt plays Kerr's girlfriend Dawn, and Japanese actors including Tadanobu Asano, Satoshi Ishii, Yasuko Mitsuura, and Tomoyasu Hotei also appear. Benny Safdie, highly acclaimed for his co-directed works with his brother Josh such as "Uncut Gems," makes his solo directorial debut with this film, winning the Silver Lion for Best Director at the 82nd Venice International Film Festival in 2025. A team led by Japanese makeup artist Kazuhiro Tsuji handled the special effects makeup, earning a nomination for the Academy Award for Best Makeup and Hairstyling at the 98th Academy Awards.
title:The Son: The Dardenne brothers, directors of 'Rosetta' and 'The Promise,' sincerely and ambitiously tackle a profound motif that could be called humanity's eternal challenge in civilized society. They depict the extreme inner turmoil of a protagonist burdened with complex emotions in a stripped-down, understated style. Olivier Gourmet won the Best Actor award at the 2003 Cannes Film Festival. One day, a boy named Francis enters a vocational training center. He wants to join the woodworking class, but the instructor, Olivier, turns him away, saying he's too busy. Yet, Olivier finds himself strangely preoccupied with Francis. Eventually, Olivier accepts Francis into his class...
title:The Sparring Partner: A courtroom dark thriller based on the real 'Parents Murder and Dismemberment Case' that occurred in Tai Kok Tsui, Hong Kong in March 2013, and the subsequent trial. Henry Chong, a young man with deep resentment towards his parents, conspires with his friend Angus Tong to murder them, dismembering and disposing of their bodies. The two are soon arrested, and the crime seems certain, but when the trial begins, Angus denies the murder, testifying that Henry killed his parents and that he was threatened into dismembering the bodies. Henry, on the other hand, insists they killed them together, directly contradicting Angus's testimony. As everything begins to unravel, the trial descends into a labyrinth, with intense battles between defense and prosecution, and the jurors' ethics and emotions sway, until the time for the verdict arrives. The actual trial concluded in 2015, and the perpetrator is serving time. The film depicts this case, which is said to still hold lingering mysteries about whether the verdict was correct. Due to some graphic depictions, it received an R18 rating in Hong Kong (R15+ in Japan) but was a huge hit. It garnered attention, winning Best Actor at the Hong Kong International Film Festival and Best New Director and Best Editing at the Hong Kong Film Awards.
title:The Sting: A blockbuster hit from director George Roy Hill, who reunited with stars Paul Newman and Robert Redford after 'Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid.' Chicago in the 1930s. Young con man Hooker, whose partner was killed by a powerful gangster, teams up with gambler Gondorff to pull off the ultimate scheme for revenge. A brilliant crime drama with a twist-filled plot and crisp pacing. Won 7 Academy Awards in 1973, including Best Picture, the most of any film that year.
title:The Super Mario Galaxy Movie: The second film in the series of "The Super Mario Bros. Movie", which animated the world of Nintendo's "Super Mario" game series and became a massive hit in 2023, grossing over $13 billion worldwide. Twin plumbers Mario and Luigi, while helping Princess Peach in the Mushroom Kingdom, take care of the captured King Koopa and solve everyone's problems. One day, they meet a new partner, Yoshi. Then, triggered by Princess Peach's birthday party, they embark on a new adventure across space to thwart the evil ambitions of Koopa's son, Bowser Jr. In addition to familiar faces from the first film like Mario, Luigi, Princess Peach, Koopa, and Toad, new characters from the original game series appear, including Yoshi, Rosalina, and Bowser Jr. Produced jointly by Chris Meledandri of Illumination (known for the "Minions" and "Sing" series) and Nintendo's Shigeru Miyamoto. Directors Aaron Horvath and Michael Jelenic, and screenwriter Matthew Fogel return, along with the original voice cast including Chris Pratt, Anya Taylor-Joy, Charlie Day, and Jack Black, as well as the Japanese dub cast including Mamoru Miyano, Ayasa Shida, Yu Hatakeyama, Kenta Miyake, and Tomokazu Seki.
title:The Tale of the White Serpent: The white snake spirit Bai Niang, unable to forget Xu Xian who cared for her when she was young, appears before him as a beautiful woman. The fish spirit Shao Qing acts as their go-between. The two quickly fall in love. However, this soon comes to the attention of the monk Fa Hai, who, concerned for the life of the young man bewitched by a demon, decides to use his magical powers to obstruct their love. Yet their romance seems to be progressing smoothly, as they spend dreamlike moments strolling through the garden of a beautiful mansion in full bloom. Xu Xian's close friends, the panda and Mimi, also playfully roam the mansion with Shao Qing, eventually pulling down a decorative dragon from a pillar. The dragon moves on its own, capturing the panda, Mimi, and Shao Qing, flying through the night sky and dropping them into a treasure hall. Shao Qing gives the jewels she finds there to Xu Xian and Bai Niang, but this becomes the cause of their separation.
title:The Tasters: Based on the global bestseller "The Taster" written from the testimony of German woman Margot Wolk, this drama portrays the fate of women forced by the Nazis to be Hitler's food tasters. It captures the horrors of war from a female perspective and the shifting relationships among the women who share their daily lives as tasters. In 1943, near the end of World War II, Rosa flees the bombing of Berlin and waits for her husband's return from the front in a Polish village, close to the forest where Hitler's Wolf's Lair headquarters is located. One day, Rosa is ordered to taste Hitler's food before he eats, and along with other young women, she is forced under SS guard at gunpoint to consume the meals. They endure the torment of sampling the finest dishes prepared for Hitler in a life-threatening situation. In July 1944, a coup attempt to assassinate Hitler at the Wolf's Lair plunges the war into further chaos. Elisa Schlott, star of the Netflix series "The Empress," plays Rosa, with Max Riemelt of "The Matrix Resurrections" co-starring as an SS officer. Italian director Silvio Soldini, known for "Emma's Eyes" and "Love in Venice," directs.
title:The Terrorizers Digital remaster: With the release of 'A One and a Two (4K Restored)', the screening of Edward Yang's representative work 'A Brighter Summer Day (Digital Remastered)' has also been confirmed!
title:The Testament of Ann Lee: A biographical musical film chronicling the tumultuous life of Ann Lee, a real-life religious leader who founded the utopian "Shaker" sect in the 18th century, starring Amanda Seyfried of "Mamma Mia!" and "Les Misérables." Born into a poor blacksmith's family in 18th-century England, Ann grows up as a devout woman. After the heartbreaking experience of bearing four children, all of whom die, she receives a revelation that she is the female reincarnation of Christ. Her way of life, preaching equality of gender and race, attracts many followers but also invites persecution from those who resent or fear her. Eventually, she crosses to America with just eight followers, seeking a utopia where they can realize an ideal life based on gender and racial equality, but further hardships await her there. Co-stars include Lewis Pullman of "Top Gun: Maverick" and Thomasin McKenzie of "Last Night in Soho." Directed by Mona Fastvold, who co-wrote the script with her partner, director Brady Corbet of "The Brutalist." The film was presented in the competition section of the 82nd Venice International Film Festival in 2025.
title:The Third Murder: Lawyer Shigemori (Fukuyama) takes on the defense of Misumi (Yakusho), who has been arrested on suspicion of murdering the president of the company where he worked. Misumi had previously been sentenced to life imprisonment for a robbery-murder committed 30 years ago and was on parole. Misumi's testimony shifts back and forth repeatedly. Eventually, an unexpected connection emerges between the victim's daughter, Sakie (Hirose), and Misumi... This film, framed as a courtroom suspense, questions ethical issues that lie outside legal judgment.
title:The Three Musketeers in Boots: Pero, a cat targeted by a bumbling hitman for saving a mouse, fights villains in the American West! The second theatrical film in the beloved series featuring the cute cat that serves as the symbol of Toei Doga (now Toei Animation).
title:The Traveler: The feature-length debut of Iranian master Abbas Kiarostami, made in 1974, this human drama freshly depicts the funny yet poignant adventures of a boy struggling desperately to watch a soccer match. Gassem, a 10-year-old boy attending elementary school, is obsessed with soccer, often neglecting his homework and classes, earning constant scolding from his teacher and mother. Determined to go see an important match held in the capital, Tehran, he tries every trick to get money for transportation and a ticket, including stealing from home and deceiving his friends... A digital remastered version was screened as part of the special program "And Kiarostami Continues" (from October 16, 2021, at Eurospace in Tokyo and other venues).
title:The Triplets of Belleville: The feature directorial debut of bande dessinée artist and animator Sylvain Chomet, this animated film humorously depicts a grandmother's desperate quest to rescue her kidnapped grandson. Minimizing dialogue and featuring stylized characters on a jaunty jazz-infused soundtrack, this adventure earned high international acclaim, becoming the first French film nominated for the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature. The grandmother learns that her shy, lonely grandson, Champion, is interested in bicycles. To help him become a cyclist, the grandmother trains with him, and he eventually grows up to compete in the world's greatest bicycle race, the Tour de France. However, during the race, Champion is kidnapped by mysterious figures. The grandmother sets off on an adventure with her loyal dog Bruno to rescue her kidnapped grandson. With the help of three legendary triplet musician old ladies, and armed with her life experience, wisdom, and humor, she overcomes numerous obstacles. Besides Best Animated Feature, the film was also nominated for the Academy Award for Best Original Song. In Japan, it was praised by Isao Takahata of Studio Ghibli and was first released in theaters in 2004. A revival screening was held in 2021 as a pre-20th anniversary project.
title:The Truman Show: A comedy-drama depicting a man whose entire life is broadcast live on a reality TV show. Truman, a man born and raised on the isolated island town of Seahaven, works at an insurance company and lives a peaceful daily life with his dependable wife Meryl. However, there is a shocking fact that only he doesn't know. In reality, since his birth, every moment of Truman's life has been broadcast live 24 hours a day on the TV show 'The Truman Show.' The town he lives in is a massive set, and all the residents, including his wife and best friend, are actors. Beginning to feel that something is off about the world he lives in, he frantically tries to uncover the truth... Jim Carrey plays the protagonist Truman, and Ed Harris plays the show's producer. The film won Best Actor and Best Supporting Actor at the 56th Golden Globe Awards. Directed by Peter Weir ('Witness'), with a screenplay by Andrew Niccol ('Gattaca').
title:The Truth: Kore-eda's first international co-production. On the occasion of the publication of the memoir 'The Truth' by Fabienne (Deneuve), a grande dame of French cinema, her screenwriter daughter Lumir (Binoche) returns home with her actor husband and daughter. However, mother and daughter clash fiercely over the book's embellished contents. As they hurl their long-held feelings at each other, the differences in the 'truth' they each hold come to light. The film portrays a family where the memories and emotions of mother and daughter intertwine, eventually moving toward a new bond.
title:The Unfaithful Wife: Praised by many critics and hailed not only as one of Chabrol's best works but also as his own greatest confidence piece. Charles, an executive at an insurance company, lives happily with his wife Hélène and son, but one day discovers that Hélène is having an affair with a writer named Pegala. Visiting Pegala's house, Charles initially maintains his composure, but gradually succumbs to rage... A masterpiece thriller capturing Agnès Varda's 'Happiness', Jacques Demy's 'The Umbrellas of Cherbourg', and the sophisticated visual beauty of Jean Rabier, who shot all three films including this one, along with performances by renowned actors, exquisitely delicate psychological portrayal, and startling violence. (1969) *All films screened in digitally remastered versions.
title:The Unforgiven: The Zachary family runs a ranch on the Texas plains. Rumors spread that their adopted daughter, Rachel, is a Kiowa girl. Ben, the eldest son who manages the ranch, tries to uncover the truth. The facts eventually come to light through the mother, but the Zacharys become isolated, and the Kiowa attack to reclaim Rachel. Ben and his family fight back. This is Audrey Hepburn's first and only Western film.
title:The Usual Suspects: A crime suspense that depicts the outcome of a criminal plan by five ex-convicts through a clever story development. At a California pier, a drug smuggling ship explodes, killing 27 people and causing $91 million in cash to disappear. Customs special agent Kujan interrogates Kint, the sole survivor who escaped unscathed. Six weeks earlier, five 'usual suspects' arrested by New York police for a gun heist are released and later conspire to attack a corrupt cop and steal jewels. To sell the loot, they head to California, where a dealer offers them a new job... At the 68th Academy Awards, Kevin Spacey won Best Supporting Actor and Christopher McQuarrie won Best Original Screenplay. Director Bryan Singer was highly praised for this film, which became his breakthrough, leading to his selection as director of 'X-Men'.
title:The Vacation Begins: Satoshi Kimura, director of 'Strange Lovers from Another Planet' and 'The Melancholic After-School of Yoyogi Johnny', takes on the classic French genre of 'vacation film' with this dialogue-driven drama. At the start of summer, Yuka, freshly divorced from Haruki after three years together, visits a seaside town on vacation with her best friend Shina and Shina's boyfriend Dazai. Yuka and Dazai were once in love, and reuniting with him rekindles her feelings. Meanwhile, Shina finds herself drawn to Tenma, a poet living in the seaside town. The film creates '1:1' scenes where characters enter the frame in pairs, unfolding the story through a chain of different combinations. The emotion of 'liking' determines each character's formation, shifting relationships as they cross paths. Yu Imari ('Soirée', 'A Janitor') plays Yuka, Ei Adachi ('If Tokugawa Ieyasu Became Prime Minister') plays Dazai, Yuki Shinho ('YOUNG&FINE') plays Shina, Takeo Yamaguchi ('BADBOYS THE MOVIE') plays Tenma, and Ryo Igarashi ('Before Dawn') plays Haruki.
title:The Virgin Suicides: Sofia Coppola, daughter of the master Francis Ford Coppola, made her feature directorial debut with this 1999 film. Based on the novel "The Virgin Suicides" by American author Jeffrey Eugenides, it depicts the emotional fluctuations of adolescent girls harboring a sense of danger with fresh, vivid visual beauty. In a 1970s American suburban town. The Lisbon house has five sisters, aged 13 to 17, each born a year apart, and the neighborhood boys are infatuated with them. One June day when dragonflies are swarming, the youngest daughter, Cecilia, attempts suicide. A few days later, the family throws a party to cheer her up, but during the party, she throws herself out of a window... Kirsten Dunst, who gained attention in "Interview with the Vampire," plays the fourth daughter Lux, while James Woods and Kathleen Turner play the sisters' parents. The French electronic duo AIR composed the music. A 4K restored version was released in May 2025 as part of the "12 Months of Cinema Relay 2024-2025."
title:The Voice of Hind Rajab: January 29, 2024. Based on the true tragedy the world watched from the sidelines—a soul-shaking true-life drama. On January 29, 2024, a volunteer team from the Palestinian humanitarian organization Palestine Red Crescent Society receives an emergency call. It is from Hind Rajab, a 6-year-old girl trapped in a car under gunfire in the Gaza Strip. The Red Crescent volunteer team keeps the line open with Rajab and exhausts every possible means to rescue her— Directed and written by acclaimed Tunisian filmmaker Kaouther Ben Hania, who continues to explore the boundary between fiction and documentary.
title:The Voices of the Silenced: A documentary co-directed by Park Soo-nam, a second-generation Zainichi Korean filmmaker who turns 90 in 2025, and her daughter Park Ma-i, depicting the stories of the voiceless buried in history. Park Soo-nam, a second-generation Zainichi Korean born in Mie Prefecture in March 1935, gained attention for her correspondence with Lee Jin-woo, a second-generation Zainichi Korean juvenile death row inmate in the 1958 Komatsugawa Incident, published as "Sin, Death, and Love." She subsequently published collections of testimonies uncovering the voices of Zainichi Koreans forcibly conscripted under colonial rule and those exposed to the atomic bombs in Hiroshima and Nagasaki. Switching from pen to camera, she made her directorial debut in 1986 with the documentary "Another Hiroshima" about Korean A-bomb victims. She has since produced documentary works such as "Song of Ariran: Testimony from Okinawa," "Nuchigafu (Life's Blessing): Testimony from the Place of Mass Death," and "Silence: The Rising Comfort Women." This film refocuses on the realities and contemporary challenges of Korean A-bomb victims, a lifework for Park Soo-nam, and is based on 16mm film she has been shooting for about 40 years. It depicts the voiceless stories of Koreans affected by the atomic bombs in Hiroshima and Nagasaki, forced laborers taken to Nagasaki's Battleship Island (Gunkanjima), former Korean civilian employees in the Battle of Okinawa, and women forced into Japanese military sexual slavery.
title:The War of the Worlds: Next Centur: One of four dark sci-fi works by Piotr Szulkin, a pioneer of dystopian sci-fi in Poland, who created them during the late 1970s and 1980s under the socialist regime, navigating strict censorship. The film depicts the theme of 'escape from totalitarianism' with a style of intense satire and surrealism taken to its extreme. Martians have attacked Earth. A TV host has been telling people 'there is nothing to fear,' but his apartment is ransacked and his wife is kidnapped. The nightly TV script is also changed, and the reality he sees no longer matches what he tells people every night. The film will have its theatrical premiere in Japan as part of the special screening project 'Polish Dark Sci-Fi: The Four Films of Piotr Szulkin' (starting February 21, 2026, at Theater Image Forum).
title:The Way We Talk: A Hong Kong youth film vividly depicting the changes and growth of three young people with hearing impairments. Sophie, in her 20s, lost her hearing at age 3 and uses a cochlear implant to live a "normal" life as a "hearing person." Jason, born deaf, lives proudly as a sign language user. Alan, also a cochlear implant user, is bilingual in sign and spoken language. Jason and Alan met at a deaf school that banned sign language and promoted oral education; despite recognizing their different circumstances, they remained close friends into adulthood. When Alan and Sophie meet as ambassadors promoting cochlear implants, Jason becomes furious at Sophie's statement at a promotion event: "If science advances, there will be no deaf people in this world." John Shiuin, known for "Aspiring Lyricist" and "Kill the Twilight," plays Sophie and also wrote the lyrics for Panther Chan's theme song "What If." Directed by Adam Wong, highly acclaimed for "The Way We Dance" and "The Way We Keep Dancing." Won Best Leading Actress (John Shiuin) at the 61st Golden Horse Awards in 2024, and received a Special Mention at the 20th Osaka Asian Film Festival in 2025.
title:The Who: The Kids Are Alright: Alongside The Beatles and The Rolling Stones, The Who led the golden age of British rock and continued to innovate the genre as a superband. This rock documentary masterpiece features live performances of their greatest hits from 1964 to 1978—a period when they were unable to tour Japan at their peak—along with promotional films and interviews. Among the many historic scenes, the film notably features Keith Moon, the legendary genius drummer, in his final full-bodied performance, filmed at Shepperton Studios in May 1978 specifically for this production—a truly precious treasure.
title:The Whole Floor Is Like This: A drama about two women who are close friends but growing increasingly dissatisfied with their shared living situation, as they struggle to clean their filthy apartment over the course of one night. Yabuki Kotori is curious and takes long trips to the toilet, while Mimori Suzuka is a fermented food enthusiast who is bad at housework. The best friends share a house, but something feels off. One day, their dream man, Kurita-san, is coming to visit, but their apartment is unbelievably dirty. With a deadline of 10 a.m., Kotori and Suzuka start a big cleanup together, but... Created by the filmmaking unit "Shidoromodori," known for "Sumiko 22" and "I Still Don't Know You," consisting of Hamada Satsuki and Fukuoka Sawako, based on their own shared-house experiences. Hamada directs, and Fukuoka handles the script and editing. Seto Riko (from "Kekkyoku Kohi") stars as Yabuki Kotori, and Sono Rin (from "Otona ni Naritakunaremasu you ni") stars as Mimori Suzuka, with Matsuzaki Shohei, Shinpo Yuki, and Kudo Haruka in a special appearance supporting the cast. The project "chill the gambler" and "kiss the gambler" by singer-songwriter Kana-fan provides the music and theme song.
title:The Wild Swans: The only fairy tale adaptation directed by Nishizawa Nobutaka. What is the mission entrusted to the younger sister Elisa to turn her brothers, who were transformed into swans by a witch's daughter, back into humans? Elisa's pitiful yet steady hands as she weaves nettle shirts lend a powerful realism to this fantastical story. Miyazaki Kyōko, an actress also known as the wife of Nakadai Tatsuya, wrote the screenplay under the name Takaba.
title:The Woman in the Rumor: A commentary: A daughter returns to Kyoto's Shimabara pleasure district, wounded after a broken engagement, and strongly resists her mother, who runs the long-established geisha house "Izutsuya." This masterpiece centers on the mother-daughter conflict, portraying the sorrow of women who have no choice but to live in the flower and willow world. The art direction by Hiroshi Mizutani, who long supported Mizoguchi's films from before the war, is also stunning.
title:The Woman with Red Hair: Based on Kenji Nakagami's short story "Akagami" (Red Hair), with a screenplay by the young Haruhiko Arai, vividly brought to the screen by director Kōji Wakamatsu. A masterpiece passionately remembered as one of Nikkatsu Roman Porno's representative works. The story follows Kōzō, a dump truck driver at a construction company, and a red-haired woman he picks up on the street, depicting the sordid waves of lust, the stagnant relationship between a man and a woman unfolding in a closed-off town. And on the other side, a man and a woman who begin seeking an escape from it all...
title:The Wonderful World of Puss 'n Boo: Hundreds of years ago, in a certain country, lived a kind-hearted boy named Pierre and a brave cat named Pero who wore boots. Pierre was raised in a wealthy home, but after his father died, his greedy brothers, after his inheritance, drove him out. Pero was ostracized after helping a mouse. They became friends while taking shelter from the rain at the same farm one rainy day and decided to travel together. Crossing fields, mountains, rivers, and lakes, they arrived at a castle where Pierre was delighted to see a wonderful notice. It stated that the richest and most valiant young man in the world would become Princess Rosa's husband. However, princes and knights from all over the world flocked there, using every means to win the princess's favor, and even the demon king Lucifer tried to become her husband using his magic. But when Rosa refused his proposal, he turned the castle into ruins, transformed the king into a pig, and left, saying he would return for the princess on the night of the full moon. Sneaking into the hall and witnessing everything, Pero realized that if they defeated the demon king, Pierre would become the bridegroom. Around that time, Pero rescued a lost baby mouse. Grateful, the mice became Pero's loyal servants and helped him, allowing Pierre to meet the princess. On the night of the full moon, Pierre revealed his true identity, and the princess was captivated by this pure and gallant young man, but she was taken away by the demon king who appeared exactly on time. Pierre, along with Pero and the mouse servants, went to the demon king's castle. The demon king was in high spirits at his wedding feast with the princess. Flattered by Pero's compliments, he showed off by transforming into various animals. But when the demon king realized Pierre and the others were after his magic pendant, he trapped them in a cave. The princess, bargaining for everyone's lives by agreeing to become the demon king's queen, seized a moment to grab the pendant and throw it into the cave. Pierre escaped to the castle tower and held the pendant high. At that moment, the sun rose from behind the mountains, and the pursuing demon king disintegrated along with the castle. Thus, in the castle restored to peace, Pierre and the princess were wed, and they lived happily ever after with Pero.
title:The World of Hans Christian Anders: Inspired by Hans Christian Andersen's words, 'My life is a fairy tale,' this musical drama weaves together tales like 'The Red Shoes' and 'Thumbelina' while depicting Andersen's boyhood. The night sky sparkles with colorful stars, and the orchestra's melodies envelop the story. The art by Reiji Koyama and the music by Seiichiro Uno sweetly bring this fairy-tale world to life.
title:The Worst Person in the World: An unconventional love drama directed by Danish filmmaker Joachim Trier, known for "The Worst Person in the World" and "Thelma," which won the Best Actress award at the 74th Cannes Film Festival in 2021 and was nominated for two Academy Awards at the 94th ceremony in 2022—Best International Feature Film and Best Original Screenplay. Julie is approaching the milestone age of 30. Having already squandered several talents, she still hasn't found direction in life. Her older boyfriend Aksel, a successful graphic novelist, has been increasingly eager to settle down. One night, Julie crashes a party she wasn't invited to and meets the young and charming Eivind. Soon after, she leaves Aksel and throws herself into a new romance, hoping to find a new outlook on life—but... Renate Reinsve, who appeared in Trier's "Oslo, August 31st" and other works, plays Julie and won the Best Actress award at the Cannes Film Festival.
title:The Written Face: This film approaches Kabuki actor Bandō Tamasaburō and, through the existence of the onnagata (female-role specialist), brings into relief a traditional Japanese feminine ideal as a construct of fiction. An unconventional work that blends fiction and reality and depicts its subject in a fantastical manner.
title:The Zen Diary: A human drama starring Kenji Sawada, based on the culinary essay "Days of Eating Earth: My Twelve Months of Shojin" by writer Tsutomu Minakami. Directed and written by Yuji Nakae of "Nabi no Koi" fame, the film crafts an original story inspired by the rich worldview of the source material. Tsutomu, a writer living alone in a remote mountain cabin in Nagano, spends his days cooking wild berries, mushrooms, and vegetables from his garden, feeling the changing seasons as he writes. His editor and much younger lover, Machiko, occasionally visits him from Tokyo. For the two, cooking and eating seasonal ingredients together is a special time. Though Tsutomu lives a carefree life, he has been unable to enshrine the ashes of his wife, who passed away 13 years ago. Takako Matsu plays Tsutomu's lover Machiko. Cooking researcher Yoshiharu Doi created the many dishes that appear in the film.
title:Thelma: A comedy-drama about a 93-year-old grandmother's struggle against a grandparent scam, starring June Squibb, nominated for an Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress for 'Nebraska,' in her first leading film role at age 93. Thelma, 93, lives alone after losing her husband, lonely but carefree. One day, hearing that her beloved grandson Danny has caused an accident and is in jail, she sends $10,000 for bail to help him, but it's a classic scam. Determined to find the culprit and get her money back, Thelma drags her old friend Ben along and sets out on a great adventure on an electric scooter. Fred Hechinger, from 'Gladiator II,' plays the grandson Danny. The role of old friend Ben is played by Richard Roundtree, known for 'Shaft,' who passed away in October 2023. Additionally, Parker Posey from 'Beau Is Afraid' co-stars as Thelma's daughter Gail, and Clark Gregg from 'Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D.' plays Gail's husband Alan. Malcolm McDowell from 'A Clockwork Orange' plays a key figure who appears in the latter half of the story. The film is the feature debut of director and screenwriter Josh Margolin, based on his real-life experiences with his own grandmother, Thelma.
title:This Place: A Japan-Philippines co-produced drama set in Rikuzentakata City, Iwate Prefecture, over a decade after the Great East Japan Earthquake, portraying the emotional recovery and identity rebirth of two half-sisters of different cultures and races. Reina Hashimoto, a 20-year-old art student living in Rikuzentakata, suddenly loses her beloved father and is overwhelmed with grief. Then appears Ella, her half-sister seven years older, who arrives from the Philippines. Reina is confused and unable to understand why Ella, who has been out of contact for so long, suddenly shows up after their father's death. The sisters, differing in culture and race, repeatedly clash and seek understanding as they confront their emotional wounds and reconsider their feelings toward family and homeland. Starring Arisa Nakano as Reina, who won the Best Actress award at the 48th Gawad Urian Awards in the Philippines—the first foreign actor to do so—and Filipino actor Gabby Padilla as her sister Ella. The cast also includes Reiko Kataoka, Cheryl Ichikawa, Satoshi Nikaido, and Sho Yakumaru. Directed and written by Filipino filmmaker Jaime Pacena II, who has visited the Tohoku region as a visual artist since 2010 and maintained ties with local communities, in his feature-length directorial debut.
title:This Planet is not my Planet: At the time, many women resonated with Tanaka's sentiment, 'I want to live as myself, rather than living like a woman,' sparking the women's liberation movement across Japan. The women never backed down against the male media who mocked them as 'sour grapes of unpopular women,' retorting, 'The difficulty of women's lives is where lib breathes!' For Tanaka, lib was a world of one versus many. Now, as an acupuncturist facing patients one-on-one, Tanaka says, 'There is a place for that person within me, and there is a place for me within that person.'
title:Through the Olive Trees: A young couple who married a few days after the earthquake appeared in one scene of 'And Life Goes On.' However, the young man who played the husband had actually proposed to the woman playing the wife before and been rejected. When director Kiarostami learned of their past, he decided to make a film based on this episode.
title:Throw Away Your Books, Rally in th: A grandmother who is a habitual shoplifter, a father who is a war criminal, and a sister with an obsessive love for rabbits. Raised in a dysfunctional family, "I" am always thinking of running away from home, while "he" is placed in a privileged environment. Burdened by a restless, pent-up passion with nowhere to go, "I" encounters strange people and wanders through a city where fantasy and memory blend together.
title:Till We Meet Again: From Giddens Ko, director of "Mon Mon Mon Monsters!" and "You Are the Apple of My Eye," comes a pure love fantasy inspired by the Taiwanese folk deity "Yue Lao" (the God of Matchmaking) and the concept of reincarnation. After being struck by lightning and brought to the underworld, Xiao Lun, along with Pinky who also arrives there, returns to the mortal world as the Taiwanese matchmaking god "Yue Lao" to tie the fates of people together. One day, a dog appears before them, triggering Xiao Lun to recover his lost memories of his past life. He remembers a promise he made to his first love, Xiao Mi, which he was unable to fulfill due to his sudden death. Starring popular Taiwanese actors: Ku Chen-dong ("You Are the Apple of My Eye") as Xiao Lun, Vivian Sung ("Our Times") as Xiao Mi, and Wang Jing ("The Soul of the Banquet," "My Ghost Friend") as Pinky.
title:Till We Meet Again on the Starry H: The sequel and conclusion to the 2023 blockbuster 'Till We Meet Again on the Lily Hill', a live-action adaptation of Shiomi Natsue's best-selling novel, which depicted the poignant love between a high school girl who time-travels from the present to 1945 and a kamikaze pilot. Based on the sequel novel 'I Want to Meet You Again on That Starry Hill', it follows the story of Yuri, the protagonist, after she wakes up in the present day, having lost her beloved in a senseless manner. Seven years have passed since her parting with Akira, the kamikaze pilot. Yuri has become a high school teacher, a dream of Akira's, and leads a busy life, but her heart remains left behind on that lily-covered hill in 1945. A young man named Ryo, who bears a resemblance to Akira, appears before her. He is a temporary teacher assigned as the deputy homeroom teacher for Yuri's class. Yuri is swayed by Ryo's straightforward affection, but she cannot bring herself to embrace a new love, feeling it would betray Akira. Amidst her inner conflict, Yuri meets Chiyo, an elderly woman spending her peaceful final days in a hospice. It's another form of love that Chiyo walked after losing Ishimaru. And what Chiyo entrusts to Yuri is a book left by Akira just before his sortie, addressed to the future Yuri. The cast reunites members from the previous film, including Fukuhara Haru as Yuri, Deguchi Natsuki, and Ito Kentaro. Additionally, Hosoda Kanata plays Ryo, the young man with Akira's likeness, and Baisho Chieko plays the elderly Chiyo. Directed by Niinobe Katsuhiko of '366 Days', with the theme song performed by Fukuyama Masaharu, continuing from the previous film.
title:Till the Day I Can Laugh about My: Ayako Ando (Ann) is a lonely middle school student who doesn't fit in at school. Her only refuge is a dim, off-limits staircase. One day, she receives a magical kaleidoscope from a mysterious shop. When she looks into it, a forbidden door opens, and on the rooftop beyond, she finds another student, Aina, who also has the same kaleidoscope. The two quickly become friends and spend a dreamlike summer vacation together. However, there is a rumor that the ghost of a student who once jumped to their death haunts the rooftop. Despite harboring suspicions that Aina might be that ghost, they become irreplaceable to each other...
title:Tochka: An unconventional film that depicts the drama woven by a man and a woman who meet by chance, drawn to the darkness of the "pillbox group," war ruins built on the coast of Nemuro, Hokkaido for border defense at the end of World War II and still standing without being demolished, set almost entirely in a single location. Nemuro, Hokkaido, a town on the border with Russia at Japan's easternmost point. In the winter-barren wilderness, pillboxes built during World War II and now weathered are scattered. A man is staring intently at one of these pillboxes, and a woman inside the pillbox happens to see him. Guided by memories recounted by the man, the two trace back through hidden time. Starring Yoko Fujita from "Dog and Cat" and Shun Sugata from "The Last Samurai." Directed by Hiroyuki Matsumura, a native of Hokkaido. Screened in the "Japanese Cinema: A Different Perspective" section of the 22nd Tokyo International Film Festival in 2008. Theatrically released in 2009, with a revival release in 2026.
title:Tokijiro: Lone Yakuza: Tokijiro sets out on a journey with the wife and child of a man he killed out of obligation to the underworld. This eighth film adaptation of a classic play, directed by Tai Kato, crystallizes supreme lyricism into a poignant love story, resulting in a masterpiece.
title:Tokyo Burst: STORY: In the dark city of East Asia, Shinjuku's Kabukicho district. A man walks with a swagger, cutting through the wind: Aiba Shiro, a rookie detective at the Shinjuku Central Police Station. Born and raised in Kabukicho, Aiba, a former bōsōzoku gang leader, is always causing trouble due to his physical strength and hot-blooded nature. One day, Korean National Police Agency detective Choi Si-woo arrives in Japan, pursuing a heinous internationally wanted criminal syndicate. From day one, the two clash and are on the verge of conflict, but with information that the wanted criminals are hiding in Kabukicho, they form an impromptu partnership and begin a joint investigation. As they investigate while remaining at odds, a certain group robbery incident triggers a massive conflict between a violent yakuza group and Kabukicho's largest host club group. Furthermore, the criminal syndicate joins the fray, and Shinjuku, transformed into a battlefield, is enveloped in chaotic darkness. And lurking behind it all is a vast conspiracy involving state power.
title:Tokyo Melody: A legendary lost documentary of Ryuichi Sakamoto filmed in 1984. Featuring precious interviews, recording sessions, and footage of YMO's 'Open Rehearsal' concert, along with scenes of 1980s Tokyo.
title:Tokyo Nightfall: Set against the chaotic nightscape of Tokyo, this human drama delicately portrays young people living with loneliness and unspoken anguish on the fringes of the city, tackling the extreme subject of a mass suicide event held at a nightclub. Directed and written by Yuto Shimizu, who gained attention with his debut feature 'The Fireworks That Bloomed Inside Me.' A young man named Amenashi loses his sister Anna, who changed after witnessing a classmate's suicide in high school and later took her own life. Burdened by guilt over her death, Amenashi continues to chase her shadow. One night, he learns of a secret mass suicide event held in a corner of Tokyo's neon-lit streets and, drawn to it, steps into the nightclub venue. His friends Notsu and Hattori, suspicious of his actions, follow him and infiltrate the club. In this closed space filled with despairing youth, the three try to escape but are forced to confront the emotions buried deep within their hearts. Amenashi is played by Iori Abe, and his sister Anna by Utano Aoi, both reuniting with director Shimizu after 'The Fireworks That Bloomed Inside Me.' The cast also includes Kosuke Tanaka and Taiga Hironaka, with rappers Kan a.k.a. GAMI, Bontou, and Isaac among the diverse supporting roles. The producer is Ken Ochiai of 'Uzumasa Limelight.'
title:Tokyo Story: A timeless masterpiece by the master Yasujiro Ozu, this film depicts the changing family relationships in post-war Japan through the story of an elderly couple visiting their children in Tokyo. Using his signature "Ozu style"—characterized by low camera angles and static shots—he meticulously portrays the parent-child dynamic. Shukishi and Tomi, an elderly couple living in Onomichi, travel to Tokyo for the first time in a while to visit their children. However, their eldest son, Koichi, a doctor, and their eldest daughter, Shige, who runs a beauty salon, are both too busy with their own lives to pay much attention to their parents. Only Noriko, the widow of their second son who died in the war, shows them genuine kindness and consideration.
title:Tokyo Taxi: Master filmmaker Yoji Yamada, directing his 91st film, brings together Baisho Chieko and Kimura Takuya as leads in this human drama about the joys of life, based on the 2022 French film "A Taxi for Paris." Taxi driver Koji Usami is tasked with driving 85-year-old Sumire Takano from Tokyo's Shibamata to a nursing home in Hayama, Kanagawa. Sumire asks him, "For my last look at Tokyo, there are a few places I'd like to stop by," and Usami follows her instructions, driving her around various locations. As they share the journey, Sumire gradually opens up and reveals her surprising past. The chance encounter between a taxi driver and his passenger sets both their hearts and lives in motion. Alongside Baisho as Sumire and Kimura as driver Usami, Aoi Yu, making her sixth appearance in a Yamada film since "My Wife is a Rose: Family is Tough III," plays the young Sumire. Takaya Sakaguchi plays Sumire's fiancé Ogawa, and Yuka plays Usami's wife Kaoru. The cast also includes Runa Nakajima, Misuzu Kanno, Lee Jun-young, and Takashi Sasano.
title:Tokyo Trial: A feature-length documentary that records the proceedings of the International Military Tribunal for the Far East, which determined the course of Japan's future after its defeat in the Pacific War. Released 25 years after the trial, it was edited over a five-year period from over 500,000 feet of film footage provided by the U.S. Department of Defense.
title:Tomie: Tsukiko Izumisawa, a girl suffering from memory loss and insomnia due to an accident three years ago, attends a psychiatric clinic. Her doctor, Hosono, probes her memories through hypnotherapy and hears the name "Tomie." However, Tsukiko cannot recall who that name belongs to. Then, strange and terrifying events suddenly begin occurring in Tsukiko's life. One day, a detective from the Metropolitan Police visits Hosono. He is investigating a woman named Tomie Kawakami.
title:Tonnerre: A life-affirming drama by rising French director Guillaume Brac, known for 'A Summer's Tale,' depicting an aging, down-and-out musician struggling with a bleak future as he gradually discovers the true meaning of love. Starring Vincent Macaigne, a regular in Brac's films. Maxime, a musician now nearly forgotten by the world, returns to his hometown of Tonnerre in the Burgundy region of France. His single father Claude enjoys outdoor sports, has a vibrant love life, and revels in life, but Maxime, exhausted by city living, has lost his will to live. Then, a young female journalist named Mélodie from a local information magazine comes to interview Maxime. Drawn to her youth and smile, Maxime grows closer to her...
title:Tony Takitani: A love story adapted from Haruki Murakami's short story of the same name, directed by Jun Ichikawa of 'Tokiwa: The Manga Apartment' and 'Tsugumi,' starring Issey Ogata and Rie Miyazawa. Tony Takitani, born as the son of a trombonist, loses his mother shortly after birth and grows up carrying loneliness. After working at a design company, he becomes an independent illustrator, falls in love with a woman, and marries her. But their happy days are short-lived; his wife dies in an accident. Feeling his loneliness, he hires a woman who closely resembles his late wife as an assistant and tries to get used to her death by having the assistant wear the vast collection of clothes his shopaholic wife left behind... Issey Ogata plays the protagonist Tony Takitani and his father, Rie Miyazawa plays Tony's wife and the woman who resembles her, with Hidetoshi Nishijima providing narration. The music is composed by Ryuichi Sakamoto. The film won the Special Jury Prize, the FIPRESCI Prize, and the Youth Jury Award at the 57th Locarno International Film Festival in 2004. A 4K remastered version was re-released in 2026.
title:Top Gun: Maverick: The sequel to the worldwide hit "Top Gun" (1986) that shot Tom Cruise to stardom. Maverick, a legendary pilot, returns to TOPGUN, the U.S. Navy's elite pilot training school, as an instructor. He, who knows the harshness and beauty of the sky better than anyone, teaches the difficulty of protecting and the harshness of fighting, but the trainees are confused and resistant to his unconventional methods. Among them is Rooster, the son of Goose, Maverick's wingman who died during a training flight with him. Rooster resents Maverick and confronts him...
