title:ユマカウンティの行き止まり: The feature-length debut of up-and-coming director Francis Galluppi, this black comedy crime thriller depicts a series of unpredictable worst-case scenarios unfolding at a desert diner. In the 1970s, in the desert region of Yuma County, Arizona. A salesman visits a diner that serves as the last gas station. When the fuel truck doesn't arrive on time, the salesman passes the time chatting with a waitress. A vicious bank robber shows up, taking the salesman and waitress hostage. However, because there's no gasoline, the bank robber can't leave the diner either. Unaware of the situation, a steady stream of quirky customers arrives at the diner: an elderly couple, an Indian chief, a hapless sheriff, and a couple aspiring to be criminals. Jim Cummings of "The Thunder Road" plays the salesman, Jocelin Donahue of "The House of the Devil" plays the waitress, and Richard Brake of "Barbarian" plays the bank robber. The film won the Best Picture award in the ORBITA section at the 2023 Sitges International Film Festival, which selects the best thrillers, suspense, and action films, earning high praise.
title:ユリイカ: Directed by Kiyoshi Aoyama of 'Helpless,' this human drama depicts the journey of recovery for people traumatized by a bus-jacking incident. It won the FIPRESCI Prize and the Ecumenical Jury Prize at the 53rd Cannes International Film Festival in 2000. A bus-jacking occurs in a regional city in Kyushu, and many passengers are killed. The only survivors are the driver, Sawai, and two siblings: junior high school student Naoki and elementary school student Kozue. All three are deeply scarred. Two years later, Sawai, who had disappeared leaving his family behind, returns to town. Around the same time, a series of murders occur in the area, and suspicion falls on Sawai. Learning that the siblings are living alone, Sawai visits their home and begins living with them. Joined by the siblings' cousin, Akihiko, the four set out on a journey in a bus driven by Sawai... Kōji Yakusho plays Sawai, while real-life siblings Shō Miyazaki and Aoi Miyazaki play Naoki and Kozue. Following director Kiyoshi Aoyama's death in March 2022, a digital master complete version was released in theaters that May as a memorial screening.
title:ユージュアル・サスペクツ: A crime suspense that depicts the outcome of a criminal plan by five ex-convicts through a clever story development. At a California pier, a drug smuggling ship explodes, killing 27 people and causing $91 million in cash to disappear. Customs special agent Kujan interrogates Kint, the sole survivor who escaped unscathed. Six weeks earlier, five 'usual suspects' arrested by New York police for a gun heist are released and later conspire to attack a corrupt cop and steal jewels. To sell the loot, they head to California, where a dealer offers them a new job... At the 68th Academy Awards, Kevin Spacey won Best Supporting Actor and Christopher McQuarrie won Best Original Screenplay. Director Bryan Singer was highly praised for this film, which became his breakthrough, leading to his selection as director of 'X-Men'.
title:ユースフル・ゴースト: In Bangkok, Thailand, where dust pollution is severe, March (Wisarut Himmarat) spends his days in grief after losing his beloved wife Nat (Davika Hoorne) to a respiratory disease. One day, Nat's soul returns, inhabiting a vacuum cleaner, and the two reaffirm their love. Meanwhile, at the factory run by March's family, the spirit of a deceased employee possesses the machinery, bringing operations to a halt. Rejected by family troubled by the spirit and by society, Nat tries to prove her true love for her husband and her own existence as a 'useful ghost' by helping with the factory's exorcism...
title:ユートピアの力: A documentary about Chandigarh, the planned city built in India by Le Corbusier, the master of modernist architecture who left behind numerous legendary buildings. In 1947, India and Pakistan gained independence, and Punjab was divided between the two countries. With the state capital Lahore belonging to Pakistan, India needed to build a new capital. Prime Minister Nehru wanted a city symbolizing faith in the future and democracy, entrusting Le Corbusier with designing the planned city of Chandigarh. Born in the wilderness at the foot of the Himalayas, the "Shining City" of Chandigarh aimed to be a human-centered utopia where natural order and modern technology were in perfect harmony, symbolizing a new India. How has this city transformed 70 years after its birth? The film traces the buildings and their history, while residents—architects, urban activists, and artists—discuss the challenges Chandigarh faces and its enduring charm. Screened as part of the special program "Le Corbusier and Doshi: Modernism in India" (from May 1, 2026, at Eurospace in Tokyo and other theaters nationwide).
title:ライオンにいてほしい: To be screened at EU Film Days 2026 (Tokyo: May 16–29, 2026 at Theater Image Forum, May 19–24 at National Film Archive; Nagoya: June 6–19 at Nagoya Cinema Neu; also to be held in Hiroshima, Kyoto, and Fukuoka).
title:ライフセーバー！: A youth ensemble drama set on Wakasa Wada Beach in Takahama Town, Fukui Prefecture, the first beach in Asia to receive the international environmental certification "Blue Flag," depicting a young man lost and without dreams who meets lifeguards and grows through challenging trials. Yuki Otomo, a university junior, has no motivation for job hunting and is lost in life. Plagued by loneliness at being left behind by those around him and a sense of futility about the future, he is invited by his uncle to spend summer vacation in Fukui. One day, Yuki tries to save a drowning person but ends up drowning himself, and is rescued by members of the "Wakasa Wada Lifesaving Club." Witnessing their love for the sea and their courage to act for others, a passionate feeling begins to stir in the apathetic Yuki's heart. Deciding to become a lifeguard, Yuki trains hard alongside his peers, but... Model and actor Nose Rin, who made his screen debut in "About a Place in the Kinki Region," makes his film lead debut as Yuki. Satoshi Tokushige plays the leader of the Wakasa Wada Lifesaving Club, Hina Irei plays a club member, Toru Kazama plays Yuki's uncle, and Tokuma Nishioka plays the chairman of the Takahama Town Water Rescue Association. Directed and written by Yoshihisa Kodama, known for "Oshorin," with the ending theme performed by singer-songwriter Hana Sekitori.
title:ライフテープ:
This is the first documentary from director and actor Ryo Anraku, who has previously crafted feature films based on his own experiences, such as *Halfway Through a Dream* and *Dance of One*. The film tenderly captures the precious daily lives of Anraku’s close friend, street dancer and artist Ryuichi, his wife Ayaka, their son Haku—who lives with Menkes disease, a rare condition said to affect only one in 120,000 people—and their cat, Figaro.

In October 2022, after being asked by his childhood friend Ryuichi to "film my family," Anraku began documenting their lives. Their newborn son, Haku, has Menkes disease, a congenital metabolic disorder caused by a copper deficiency that leads to various health complications. While the life shared by the family and Figaro is filled with smiles, Ayaka’s diary—written between Haku's birth and his diagnosis—contains the raw, poignant words of a couple struggling to accept their reality. As they continue to weave their daily lives while confronting inescapable loneliness and anxiety, they reach a major turning point: the decision for Haku to undergo a tracheostomy. This theatrical version has been re-edited from the edition screened at the 16th Za-Koenji Documentary Festival in 2025.
title:ライブビューイング ミュージカル『⼑剣乱舞』 〜静かなる夜半の寝ざめ:
[Original Concept] Based on "Touken Ranbu ONLINE" (DMM GAMES/NITRO PLUS)
[Director] Isamu Kayano
[Script & Lyrics] Sayaka Asai
[Music Director] YOSHIZUMI
[Choreography & Staging] Shinnosuke Motoyama, TETSUHARU, Ryosuke Sakuragi, REX
[Presented by] Musical "Touken Ranbu" Production Committee (Nelke Planning, Nitro Plus, DMM GAMES, Euclid Agency)
title:ライヴ・アット・マディソン・スクエア・ガーデン2008: A concert film capturing the joint live performances by Eric Clapton and Steve Winwood at Madison Square Garden in New York from February 25 to 28, 2008. Eric Clapton and Steve Winwood, who performed together in the band Blind Faith, generously perform Blind Faith songs including "Can't Find My Way Home," along with tracks from their respective bands and solo careers, as well as covers of songs by Jimi Hendrix, Ray Charles, and J.J. Cale. The film captures the entire performance, bringing the excitement and power of the live concert to the big screen. In Japan, it was released in 2009 as the 90-minute "Eric Clapton & Steve Winwood Live from Madison Square Garden cine sound ver." In 2026, it will be released under the Japanese title "Live at Madison Square Garden 2008" with a 140-minute runtime as part of the "Clapton Festival," a series of Eric Clapton live and documentary screenings.
title:ラブ≠コメディ: A love story starring Nakajima Kento and Nagahama Neru as the heroine, set on the set of a romantic comedy drama. Popular actor Kanzaki Reiji, hailed as a '360-degree handsome man,' has starred in numerous romantic comedies. Turning 30, he yearns to be recognized as an actor in more serious works, but receives another offer for a typical rom-com. He resists upon learning his co-star is Minakaze Misato, a member of the idol group 'Pyon Pyon Fruits,' but this encounter will drastically change his life. The polar opposites, Reiji and Misato, are imperfect, leading them to hesitate and clash, yet they grow with the support of those around them. The cast includes Itaya Yuka as producer Shuto Asami, Shiono Akihisa as rival actor Fuchigami Soma, Honda Riki as director Nihei Sanpei, Mitsuishi Ken as senior actor Yamamura Kenji, Zaizen Naomi as veteran screenwriter Hashitani Kinako, and Mitsuishi Kotono as Misato's mother Mariko. Directed by Kamitani Kaede of the TV drama 'She Was Pretty,' with a screenplay by Okita Haruka of the 'Radiation House' series.
title:ラプソディ・ラプソディ: Actor Tsuyoshi Rishu, who has directed films such as 'Chloe' and 'Goodbye Debussy', takes the director's chair for a feature film for the first time in 13 years, with Issei Takahashi in the lead role. This human drama humorously depicts a man who has avoided social interactions, whose life takes an unexpected turn when he discovers he has been unknowingly registered as married to a woman he doesn't know. Mikio Natsuno, a slightly naive man who never gets angry, goes to get a copy of his family register to renew his passport and is shocked to find the words 'Relationship: Wife' for a woman he has absolutely no memory of. Learning that a woman named 'Shigeko' has registered herself as his wife without his knowledge, Mikio begins searching for this mysterious woman. He eventually finds Shigeko at a small flower shop on a street corner, but she is an unconventional woman who destroys everything she touches. Though Mikio is tossed around by Shigeko, this strange encounter gradually brings unexpected changes to both their lives. Issei Takahashi plays the kind-hearted and sensitive protagonist Mikio, and Kumi Goshima (NHK morning drama 'Manpuku') plays the enigmatic heroine Shigeko who bewilders everyone around her. Okihiko Serizawa and Chizuru Ikewaki co-star, and director Rishu also appears as a key character. World-renowned jazz pianist Junko Onishi provides the music.
title:ラベンダー・ヒル・モブ: A crime comedy that depicts, with ironic humor, how two men's gold bullion heist plan takes an unexpected turn. One of the 'Ealing Comedies,' a series of comedy films produced at Ealing Studios in the UK from the late 1930s to the mid-1950s, directed by Charles Crichton, who was later nominated for an Academy Award for Best Director for 'A Fish Called Wanda.' Henry, a serious man who has worked as a bank security guard for 20 years, conspires with his friend Pendlebury, a souvenir shop owner, to steal a shipment of gold bullion. After successfully pulling off the heist, they process the gold into miniature Eiffel Towers to smuggle it abroad, but in a lounge at the Eiffel Tower in Paris, they accidentally sell them to a group of schoolchildren on a trip from England... Alec Guinness of 'Star Wars' fame plays Henry, and Stanley Holloway of 'My Fair Lady' plays Pendlebury. A young Audrey Hepburn appears in a single scene. The film won the Academy Award for Best Original Screenplay at the 25th Academy Awards in 1953. This film is part of the special screening series 'The Golden Age of British Ealing Comedies' (June 20–July 17, 2026, at Shinjuku K's Cinema).
title:ラルジャン: The 13th feature film by French master director Robert Bresson, who left behind masterpieces such as "Resistance: From the Prisoner's Diary" and "Mouchette." Bresson, already over 80 at the time of filming, passed away in 1999, making this his final work. Based on the novella "The Forged Coupon" by Russian literary giant Leo Tolstoy, it depicts the life of Yvon, a young fuel delivery man who, after unknowingly using a counterfeit bill that falls into his hands, triggers a family massacre and spirals downward. The title "L'argent" means "money" in French. First released in Japan in 1986. Revived in 2011 as part of "Cinema Masterpiece Selection III: The Art of Robert Bresson" with new prints. In 2026, it will be revived again in a 2K restored version as part of "Robert Bresson Masterpiece Selection."
title:ラ・パロマ: At Madame Lily's brothel, life-or-death gambling takes place amidst decadent plumes of purple smoke. The patrons are intoxicated by the company of young prostitutes and beautiful boys. The brothel's celebrated chanteuse, Viola—also known as "La Paloma" (Ingrid Caven)—appears on stage singing "Shanghai." A male patron gazes intently at her alluring figure. This man, named Isidore (Peter Kern), visits La Paloma's dressing room day after day with a yellow rose, but is fiercely rejected by her, drowned in alcohol.
title:ラ・ラ・ランド: A musical film directed by Damien Chazelle, who gained attention with "Whiplash," starring Ryan Gosling and Emma Stone. It depicts the romance between a struggling actress and a jazz pianist through gorgeous and romantic song and dance reminiscent of classic musical films. Mia, an aspiring actress dejected after failing an audition, has a terrible first encounter with Sebastian, a pianist, at a jazz bar she enters drawn by the sound of piano. Later, Mia reunites with Sebastian at a party, where he's sullenly playing 80s pop by the poolside. Though they clash during their first conversation, they fall in love as they're drawn to each other's talents and dreams. J.K. Simmons, who won the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor for "Whiplash," also appears. Emma Stone won Best Actress at the 73rd Venice International Film Festival, and the film won a record seven awards at the 74th Golden Globe Awards including Best Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy. At the 89th Academy Awards, it received 14 nominations, tying the record for most nominations, with Chazelle becoming the youngest Best Director winner in history, and winning six Oscars total including Best Actress for Emma Stone.
title:ラーゲリより愛を込めて: A biographical drama starring Kazunari Ninomiya as real-life Japanese prisoner of war Yamamoto Hanao, held in a Siberian labor camp (Laguerre). Based on Jun Henmi's nonfiction novel "The Last Letter from the Laguerre," directed by Takahisa Zeze, known for "Those Who Were Not Protected" and "The Thread." In 1945, after World War II, Japanese POWs in Siberian camps faced brutal conditions—temperatures dropping to -40°C, minimal food, and forced heavy labor, with many dying. Amid this, Yamamoto Hanao believes he will return to his wife and children in Japan, encouraging those around him. His selfless actions and strong faith ignite a flame of hope in many prisoners' hearts. Kitagawa Keiko plays Yamamoto's wife Mojimi, with a star-studded cast including Matsuzaka Tori, Nakajima Kento, Kiryū Kentarō, and Yasuda Ken as fellow prisoners.
title:リアム・ギャラガー ライブ・アット・ネブワース2022: A live film documenting the solo outdoor concert performed by Liam Gallagher, the legendary voice of the British rock band Oasis, at Knebworth Park in 2022. Ever since Oasis drew 250,000 people there in 1996, Knebworth has been revered as the "holy ground" of the band. Having established himself as a solo artist following the group's 2009 split, Liam returned to the Knebworth stage for the first time in 26 years, performing for 170,000 ecstatic fans over two days. The film captures the 16-song set—featuring 10 Oasis anthems such as "Wonderwall," "Champagne Supernova," "Live Forever," and "Stand By Me"—alongside the liberating atmosphere and sense of pure joy unique to an outdoor festival. The encore also features a guest appearance by former Stone Roses guitarist John Squire.
title:リップヴァンウィンクルの花嫁: Nanami Minagawa, a temporary teacher in Tokyo, meets Tetsuya on social media and marries him. She hires Amaru, a jack-of-all-trades, to provide stand-in guests for the wedding ceremony. However, Tetsuya's affair soon comes to light. Then Nanami is accused by her mother-in-law of having an affair herself and is forced to leave the house. Amaru introduces Nanami to jobs as a stand-in wedding guest and as a live-in maid with a monthly salary of 1 million yen. There she meets her fellow maid, the unconventional and free-spirited Mashiro Satonaka.
title:リトル・ダンサー: A coming-of-age drama set in a 1980s British mining town, following a boy's struggle to become a ballet dancer and the bonds of family. In 1984, in a mining town in northeast England, 11-year-old Billy, who has lost his mother, is forced by his coal miner father to attend boxing classes. One day, intrigued by a ballet class he stumbles upon, he joins the girls in their lessons. Ballet teacher Mrs. Wilkinson discovers Billy's talent as a dancer, and under her passionate guidance, he improves rapidly. Jamie Bell, chosen from over 2,000 auditionees, delivers a powerful performance as Billy. Julie Walters of "Educating Rita" plays Mrs. Wilkinson, earning an Academy Award nomination for Best Supporting Actress. Gary Lewis of "My Name Is Joe" plays Billy's father. World-renowned ballet dancer Adam Cooper makes a special appearance. The film marks the feature directorial debut of stage director Stephen Daldry, who later helmed "The Hours."
title:リバー、流れないでよ: The second original feature film by the popular theater troupe Europe Kikaku, led by Makoto Ueda. Following their acclaimed first feature "Droste no Hate de Bokura," Ueda writes the original story and script, with the troupe's video director Junta Yamaguchi directing. This ensemble comedy depicts the chaos of people trapped in a repeating two-minute time loop set in winter at Kibune, Kyoto. Mikoto, a waitress at the long-established inn Fujiya in Kibune, is called back to work by the landlady while standing by the Kibune River behind the annex. But two minutes later, she finds herself in the same spot. Not only Mikoto, but also the head clerk, waitresses, chefs, and guests all realize time is looping. After two minutes, time rewinds and everyone returns to their original positions, but their memories carry over. They work together to find the cause of the loop, but Mikoto alone harbors complicated feelings. Filmed in winter at Kibune with full cooperation from Kibune Shrine and the inn Fujiya. Starring Riko Fujitani as Mikoto, along with many Europe Kikaku actors, Yuki Torigoe, Manami Honjo, Saoi, and Yoshimasa Kondo. Shiori Kubo of Nogizaka46, who has ties to Ueda and Europe Kikaku through stage productions, makes a guest appearance in a key role.
title:リプライズ: The feature directorial debut of Joachim Trier, a Danish director distantly related to Lars von Trier who studied film in Denmark and England, released in 2006. This is the first work of the "Oslo Trilogy," which also includes his later films "Oslo, August 31st" and "The Worst Person in the World." Philip and Erik are childhood friends who have dreamed of becoming writers since they were kids. One day, they both send manuscripts to a publisher, but only Philip's is accepted. Philip becomes a suddenly famous author, but soon begins to suffer mental instability. Meanwhile, Erik continues writing novels without giving up... Anders Danielsen Lie, who stars in all three films of the "Oslo Trilogy," plays Philip. Selected as Norway's entry for the 79th Academy Awards for Best Foreign Language Film, it received high praise, winning the Grand Prix (Best Film), Best Director, and Best Screenplay at the Amanda Awards, Norway's equivalent of the Academy Awards. It received its first theatrical release in Japan as part of the special screening series "Joachim Trier: The Oslo Trilogy" (starting February 13, 2026, at Bunkamura Le Cinéma Shibuya Miyashita and other venues in Tokyo).
title:リモート・コントロール: Screened at the 2nd Japan-Mongolia Film Festival (March 14–27, 2026, at K's cinema).
title:リリイ・シュシュのすべて: In a provincial city, middle school student Yuichi becomes close with the honor student Hoshino, but a summer trip changes the dynamics among their friends. When the new semester begins, Hoshino defeats the class's worst delinquent in a fight and gradually turns into a tyrant himself. As his actions escalate—assault, shoplifting, and forcing classmates into prostitution—Yuichi, who has become a target of bullying, is also made complicit. Turning his eyes away from reality, Yuichi creates a fan site for his idolized artist, Lily Chou-Chou.
title:リング: Reiko Asakawa, a TV station director, is investigating an urban legend when she notices that a man and woman rumored to have been involved with a 'cursed videotape' that kills viewers within a week died at the exact same date and time as her niece, Tomoko Oishi, who had died strangely a few days earlier. As her investigation progresses, Reiko discovers that Tomoko and the other three who died simultaneously were acquaintances, that they had stayed at a rental villa in Izu called 'Izu Pacific Land' a week prior, and that the faces of the four in film photos taken at that time are eerily distorted. Seeking to uncover the mystery of their deaths, Reiko visits the villa in question, watches the suspicious tape that was rented there, and immediately receives an eerie silent phone call. From that point on, Reiko's own photos also begin to show her face distorted, just like the four deceased.
title:リンダ リンダ リンダ: A refreshing youth drama set in high school, depicting the struggles of a girls' band. Starring Bae Doona of 'Barking Dogs Never Bite' and 'Tube', Aki Maeda of the 'Battle Royale' series, Yuu Kashii of 'Lorelei', and Shiori Sekine, bassist of the rock band Base Ball Bear. Directed by Nobuhiro Yamashita of 'A Gentle Breeze in the Village'. It delicately portrays the subtle emotional shifts and excitement in the hearts of teenage girls. At a local high school, an emergency strikes Kyoko, Megumi, and Nozomi of the same band. They had even prepared an original song for the school festival, but guitarist Moyu injured her finger, and the furious vocalist Rinko quit the band. However, after listening to 'Linda Linda' by The Blue Hearts, which they happen to hear, Kyoko and the others decide to form a cover band of The Blue Hearts. They invite Song, a Korean exchange student, to be the vocalist, and she agrees. The four practice hard toward the final day of the school festival, but...
title:リンダ リンダ リンダ 4K: A refreshing youth drama set in high school, depicting the struggles of a girls' band. Starring Bae Doona of 'Barking Dogs Never Bite' and 'Tube', Aki Maeda of the 'Battle Royale' series, Yuu Kashii of 'Lorelei', and Shiori Sekine, bassist of the rock band Base Ball Bear. Directed by Nobuhiro Yamashita of 'A Gentle Breeze in the Village'. It delicately portrays the subtle emotional shifts and excitement in the hearts of teenage girls. At a local high school, an emergency strikes Kyoko, Megumi, and Nozomi of the same band. They had even prepared an original song for the school festival, but guitarist Moyu injured her finger, and the furious vocalist Rinko quit the band. However, after listening to 'Linda Linda' by The Blue Hearts, which they happen to hear, Kyoko and the others decide to form a cover band of The Blue Hearts. They invite Song, a Korean exchange student, to be the vocalist, and she agrees. The four practice hard toward the final day of the school festival, but...
title:リー・ミラー 彼女の瞳が映す世界:
Starring and produced by Kate Winslet, this film dramatizes the extraordinary life of Lee Miller, the real-life figure who transformed from a top fashion model into one of the 20th century's most iconic photojournalists. In 1938, while vacationing in the South of France with a circle of artist friends, Lee meets and falls in love with the artist Roland Penrose. Before long, the looming threat of World War II changes their lives forever. Securing work as a photographer, Lee teams up with David Scherman, a photojournalist and editor for the American magazine *LIFE*. In 1945, serving as a war correspondent and photographer, Lee captures a series of historic scoops. On the day of Hitler's suicide, she signals the end of the war by photographing a portrait of herself in the bathtub of Hitler's Munich apartment. The sights she witnessed remained etched in her mind, haunting her for many years after the war.

Kate Winslet’s performance as Lee Miller earned her a Golden Globe nomination for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Drama. The film features a supporting cast including Marion Cotillard as Lee's friend Solange d'Ayen, Alexander Skarsgård as her lover Roland Penrose, and Andy Samberg as David Scherman. Ellen Kuras, the acclaimed cinematographer of *Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind*, makes her feature directorial debut.
title:ルオムの黄昏:
Winner of the Best Film Award in the Competition Section of the 30th Busan International Film Festival.

The traces of a lost lover, and a path that recedes the more you search—another time flowing through Luomu, an ancient town in Sichuan Province.

A postcard arrives from Wang, a lover who vanished without a trace three years ago, bearing only the words "Twilight in Luomu." Bai, who worked as a dancer in a theater troupe, follows this single clue to an inn in the ancient town of Luomu, Sichuan. There she meets Liu, the inn's proprietress; Huang, who has harbored feelings for Liu for twenty years; and a stream of passing travelers. In this town, once prosperous from trade and now flowing with quiet time, what she encounters is not Wang himself, but the traces of the time he left behind. The faint sound of a distant whistle echoes, and before Bai, who wanders the ancient town, Wang appears and disappears like a phantom. One day, Bai learns that a man resembling Wang was reportedly seen at a mountain temple—

Released simultaneously with its sister film "Chunshu," shot with the same cast prior to this work.
title:レオ ブラッディ・スウィート: Director Lokesh Kanagaraj (Kaithi, Vikram) reunites with superstar Vijay following their collaboration on Master for this high-octane crime action film. In the quiet North Indian town of Theog, Parthiban, a Tamil animal rescuer and cafe owner, lives a peaceful life with his wife and two children. However, their tranquility is shattered when a gang led by Shanmugam rampages through the town and breaks into his cafe. Though Parthiban initially tries to settle the matter by handing over the cash, he is forced to act when his daughter and female staff are threatened, taking down five attackers in an instant with extraordinary physical prowess. As the incident makes national headlines, various underworld factions begin to target him—including mysterious men who insist on calling him "Leo." Trisha Krishnan (Ponniyin Selvan: I & II) stars as Parthiban's wife, with Sanjay Dutt (K.G.F: Chapter 2, PK) appearing as the gangster hunting for Leo.
title:レッツ・ロック・アゲイン！: A documentary capturing the final days of Joe Strummer, former member of the quintessential London punk band The Clash, who passed away suddenly in December 2002. The film follows Strummer's band 'Joe Strummer & The Mescaleros' on their 2001 US tour and 2002 Japan tour, composed of live performances, backstage footage, promotional activities, and interviews from various tour stops. It includes scenes of him personally handing out handwritten flyers before shows, revealing a warm, human side of Strummer that contrasts with the tense, rebellious stance of his Clash days. Produced and released in 2004. To commemorate the 40th anniversary of The Clash's 'London Calling,' a digitally remastered version was revived in theaters in December 2019. Directed by Dick Rude, who had befriended Strummer and even appeared alongside him in Alex Cox's 'Straight to Hell.'
title:レディ・オア・ノット2: The sequel to the survival horror "Ready or Not," in which bride Grace, targeted for death in a traditional wedding-night game, flees the mansion of a wealthy family. The stage expands further, depicting Grace being drawn into a power struggle among the ultra-rich who secretly control the world. Grace survived the blood-soaked game, but the nightmare wasn't over. Her survival catches the attention of the rulers who secretly manipulate the world, and she is once again chosen as a target. The stage is the forbidden realm known as the Council, where chosen noble families vie for supremacy. Representatives of six noble families, bound by a pact with the demon Le Bail, attack Grace with their ancestral weapons, tasked with killing her by dawn. Her only ally is her long-estranged sister Faith, but the two are chained together and unable to move freely. In this extreme situation, their family bond is put to the test as they fight to survive. Samara Weaving reprises her role as Grace. Kathryn Newton ("Abigail") joins as sister Faith, along with new cast members Sarah Michelle Gellar, David Cronenberg, and Elijah Wood. As with the previous film, directing duties were handled by Matt Bettinelli-Olpin and Tyler Gillett of the filmmaking unit Radio Silence.
title:レネットとミラベル 四つの冒険: An omnibus of four short episodes by director Eric Rohmer, chronicling the curious encounters of two contrasting young women, Reinette and Mirabelle. In the first episode, "The Blue Hour," the two—who met after a flat bicycle tire—strive to experience the moment of absolute silence that occurs just before dawn. The second episode, "The Waiter," depicts their interactions with a peculiar cafe server after they begin living together in Paris. The third episode, "The Beggar, the Kleptomaniac, and the Swindler," features a series of dialogues concerning crime and conscience. The film concludes with the fourth episode, "Selling the Painting," in which they scramble to sell one of Reinette’s artworks to cover their rent. Rohmer conceived the project based on the personal anecdotes of Joëlle Miquel, who plays Reinette, and filmed it on 16mm with a minimal crew.
title:レンタル・ファミリー: Brendan Fraser, winner of the Academy Award for Best Actor for "The Whale," stars in this human drama shot entirely in Japan. Directed by Japanese filmmaker HIKARI, who gained attention for her feature debut "37 Seconds" and the drama series "Beef," the film follows a down-on-his-luck actor living in Tokyo who rediscovers himself through working for a rental family service. Philip, an American actor who once dominated toothpaste commercials but has since been largely forgotten, lives in Tokyo, eking out a living in the acting world and blending into the city. One day, he is hired by Tada, who runs a rental family company. The job involves playing the role of a cherished "family member" for clients in exchange for payment. Initially hesitant about delving into others' lives, Philip begins to change as he interacts with the people he meets through his work. Takehiro Hira plays Tada, the rental family company owner; Mari Yamamoto plays Aiko, an actress working for the company; and Akira Emoto plays Kikuo, an aging actor.
title:レンタル家族: Through the seemingly eccentric service of a rental family, the characters waver between 'acting' and 'true feelings,' eventually opening their hearts to one another. This human drama questions the nature of family and modern loneliness. Yoko Sakamoto, an office worker in Tokyo, leads a busy life but regularly returns to her hometown to care for her father Tadakatsu and her mother Chieko, who has dementia. Chieko's symptoms have been progressing rapidly, and she has forgotten that Yoko divorced years ago, asking about her ex-husband and daughter each visit. One day, a business contact introduces Yoko to a 'rental family' service and suggests she try it. Initially hesitant, Yoko decides to hire a rental husband as a housekeeper. She hits it off with the rental husband, Takeshi Matsushita, and confides in him about Chieko. Takeshi proposes that they play the roles of husband and daughter, with him as the husband and his acquaintance, child actress Akari Yasuda, as the daughter. Starring Yuri Ogino, a member of the theatrical company 'Seinenza' active in stage, film, TV, and commercials. Directed by Ryunosuke Uesaka, making his directorial debut with this independent film after working on TV programs and commercials. It won the Grand Prix at the 23rd Nakanoshima Film Festival.
title:ロストフォリア: An omnibus work depicting 'hearts carrying loss'. The title 'Lostphoria' is a coined term that regards 'loss (Lost)' as a state of mind. Through protagonists of different generations, this film portrays the loneliness and pain that everyone harbors, and the 'faint light' that lies beyond them. It was created with the aim of allowing audiences to touch the loneliness of others and feel that 'they are not alone'.
title:ロスバンド: A Norwegian youth music road movie. Grim, the drummer, who is heartbroken by his parents' discord, and his best friend Aksel, the guitarist and vocalist, practice daily to compete in a Norwegian rock competition. Grim is bothered by Aksel's lack of singing ability but can't bring himself to tell the truth. They manage to get tickets for the long-awaited competition, but they have no bassist, and the event is held in Tromsø, a town at the northern tip. They form "Los Band" after adding Tilda, a 9-year-old cello player who comes to the bassist audition, and set off on a journey in a car driven by their neighbor Mattin, a skilled driver... Director Kristian Land, known as a master of children's films, portrays their struggles and cooperation towards their dreams against the backdrop of rich Nordic nature.
title:ロゼッタ: A film by the Dardenne brothers, directors of 'The Promise,' portraying a woman who tenaciously survives despite adversity. Rosetta lives with her alcoholic mother in a trailer at a campground. One day, she is fired from her job for no apparent reason. Rosetta, confronting the harsh realities of society, desperately continues searching for new work... Winner of the Palme d'Or and Best Actress award at the 1999 Cannes Film Festival.
title:ロックンロウル: The first feature film directed by Yu Yamada, who gained attention with short films "An Exhibition of Your Substitute" and "Perry (Just Dropped In)." Set in the world of small-theater stage productions, this ensemble drama powerfully and forcibly depicts people overcoming various forms of loneliness. Four days before the performance, actors Mina and Kosei are suddenly told by director Atsuzawa to stop rehearsals. Anxious Mina unilaterally vents to her live-in lover Tatsunori, while Kosei, harshly criticized for his acting, is dumped by his fiancée. Assistant director Momiji seeks to be needed by someone, and lighting staff Sho feels distant from those around him. Director Atsuzawa continues revising the script while bearing responsibility for the work. Each carries loneliness and anxiety as the performance day approaches. Seina Otaku, who starred in Yamada's "An Exhibition of Your Substitute," plays protagonist Mina; Chihiro Kabaki, who starred in "Perry (Just Dropped In)," plays assistant director Momiji. Also appearing are Yuho Fukui and Kimihito Omae from the comedy unit "Suzume People," who shine in theater productions by Yamada's creative group "Shinagawa Shinashirazu," and Takuma Ishii, who actively performs mainly in small theaters.
title:ロックン・ロール・サーカス: A music film planned, produced, and hosted by The Rolling Stones with the aim of 'fusing rock and roll with the circus,' filmed in December 1968 but shelved until 1996 due to various circumstances. The Stones, having just released the historic album 'Beggars Banquet,' perform six songs including 'Sympathy for the Devil,' with Mick Jagger delivering an outstanding performance. Leader and guitarist Brian Jones died suddenly at the young age of 27 six months after filming, making this the Stones' final performance with him. Additionally, the film features a host of star musicians including The Dirty Mac, a band formed for this project by John Lennon with Eric Clapton and Keith Richards, as well as The Who and Marianne Faithfull. Directed by Michael Lindsay-Hogg, known for the film 'Let It Be.' A 4K restored version was produced in 2019 and received its first Japanese theatrical release in August 2022.
title:ロッコク・キッチン: A documentary that observes people's lives and the present state of Fukushima through the dining tables of those living along National Route 6, commonly known as "Rokkoku," where areas still remain designated as difficult-to-return zones.
title:ロビー！ 4000億円を懸けた仁義なき18ホール: Popular Korean actor Ha Jung-woo stars in and directs this comedy-drama depicting a young CEO’s struggle as he tackles his first-ever round of business golf to secure a massive national project. Chang-wook, the head of a small tech startup, begins lobbying efforts to save his company from the brink of bankruptcy. Although a brilliant engineer, he is clueless about the unwritten rules of the business world and a poor salesman. To get a piece of a 4-trillion-won national project, he finds himself playing a high-stakes game of golf with Director Choi, the man who holds the power over the bidding process. Chang-wook arrives fully prepared, even inviting Se-bin, a young pro golfer and Director Choi’s personal favorite. However, the day descends into total chaos when a rival CEO and the Minister—who happens to be both Choi’s boss and his wife—unexpectedly show up. The film features an ensemble cast including Kim Eui-sung (Train to Busan), Park Byung-eun (In Our Prime), Lee Dong-hwi (Extreme Job), Kang Mal-geum (Lucky Chan-sil), Choi Si-won of the boy band SUPER JUNIOR, and Kang Hae-lim (Netflix’s Somebody). Kim Kyung-chan (1987: When the Day Comes) co-wrote the screenplay alongside Ha Jung-woo.
title:ロブスター [プレ企画]シネマカリテと また逢える: "Singles" are detained and sent to a hotel. If they fail to find a partner within 45 days, they are transformed into an animal of their choosing and released into the woods. In such an era, David, having become single, is also sent to the hotel. There, a daily life of madness lay in wait.
title:ロボットカーニバル: Produced during the mid-1980s when original video animation was booming, this omnibus work pushes forward the director's individuality. Katsuhiro Otomo handles the opening and ending, packing the essence of his animation into a short time. The English title logo features a building drawn in meticulous detail so its structure is discernible. The composition of it running as a machine, and the imagery of a toy-box-like, amusement-park-like interior collapsing carefully step by step, truly feels like a microcosm of 'Steamboy'. While other directors develop unique worlds around the theme of 'robots', Otomo creates a short film that is more relaxed and visually driven.
