title:太陽（2005）: Russian visionary director Alexander Sokurov, known for *Spiritual Voices* and *Russian Ark*, presents this provocative film as the third installment in his tetralogy exploring 20th-century leaders, following *Moloch* (Hitler) and *Taurus* (Stalin). The film depicts the internal conflict of Emperor Showa, who was revered as a deity, leading up to his "Humanity Declaration" at the end of the war. Issey Ogata stars as the Emperor, alongside Kaori Momoi as the Empress and Shiro Sano as the Grand Chamberlain.
title:太陽（ティダ）の運命: Director Tadahiko Sako, known for "Kamejiro: The Man the U.S. Military Feared Most," delves into modern Okinawan history through the lives of two governors who fiercely confronted the national government. Masahide Ota (the 4th governor after Okinawa's reversion to Japan, serving 1990–98) and Takeshi Onaga (the 7th governor, serving 2014–18) held opposing political positions, yet both garnered broad support from the people and managed the prefecture by transcending the traditional conservative-liberal divide. Ota fought the state in court in 1995 over his refusal to sign for the forced use of military land, while Onaga did the same in 2015 regarding the revocation of the Henoko landfill approval; their battles brought to light the nature of democracy, local autonomy, and the contradictions of the nation. Incorporating testimonies from many who were involved in their lives, the film highlights their personal charisma and depicts the indomitable struggle of two men who lived by their convictions. The title "Tida" means "Sun" in the Okinawan dialect, a word that anciently referred to a chief or leader.
title:失われた週末: A serious drama acclaimed worldwide, winning four Academy Awards and the Grand Prix at the Cannes Film Festival. Don, a struggling writer living in New York, drowns his days in alcohol. Desperate for drink money, he steals from his brother and even tries to sell his typewriter. Ray Milland delivers a powerful performance as Don wandering the depths of despair, earning him an Oscar for Best Actor. Director Wilder met his second wife, Audrey Young, during the making of this film.
title:失楽園: Kuki, once a sharp editor at a publishing house but now relegated to a dead-end position, meets Rinko, a married woman who teaches calligraphy at a culture center run by a friend, and continues an adulterous affair with her. Their love only deepens, and Kuki eventually rents an apartment in Tokyo to serve as their love nest. But Rinko's husband hires a private detective and learns of her infidelity, while Kuki's wife pressures him for a divorce. Yet the more they are cornered by those around them, the more fiercely Kuki and Rinko's love burns.
title:奇跡: Director Hirokazu Kore-eda of "Nobody Knows" and "Air Doll" depicts a family drama set in Kyushu, which is buzzing with excitement over the full opening of the Kyushu Shinkansen line in March 2010. Starring the comedy brother duo Maeda Maeda's Koki Maeda and Koshiro Maeda. The story follows two brothers, separated by their parents' divorce to live in Kagoshima and Fukuoka respectively, who strive to reunite their broken family, spurred on by the full opening of the bullet train line. Co-stars include regulars from Kore-eda's films such as Yui Natsukawa, Atsushi Abe, Yoshio Harada, and Kirin Kiki.
title:女たちの庭: Soichiro Ishizuka, the head of Kikumaru Textiles—a venerable establishment in Nihonbashi—has three daughters, Hatsuko, Yuko, and Izumi, with his wife Ayako. Hatsuko has taken Yoshio as her husband to serve as the family heir, and the parents are now searching for a suitable match for Yuko. One day, Soichiro’s old schoolmate Furusawa arrives with news that another classmate, Mayama—a potter living in Imari, Kyushu—is rumored to be terminally ill with cancer...
title:女たちの証言 －「労働運動のなかの先駆的女性たち」: In 1982, under the sponsorship of socialist researcher Kiyomizu Ishidō, a roundtable discussion was held with pioneering female activists who had participated in the launch of the popular labor movement from the Taishō to Shōwa eras. Those gathered were Setsu Tanno (wife of Masanosuke Watanabe), Utako Nabeyama (wife of Sadachika Nabeyama), Misao Fukuoka (wife of Kyōji Koreeda), and Mina Yamauchi (wife of Naokazu Tachibana). Although they had once worked together in the movement, decades later, after the war, some held different positions, making such a gathering rare. At the request of the host, Mr. Ishidō, who said, 'I want to record this for posterity,' director Haneda filmed the discussion. Time passed without the footage being released, but driven by the director's strong desire to 'preserve the history of these women,' additional filming was done as much as possible to compile the work. In this film, the discrimination and subjugation experienced by these female activists are told in their own words. It is a work that quietly questions what true women's liberation really is.

title:女ともだち（1955）: The third feature film by Italian master Michelangelo Antonioni, known for the 'trilogy of arid love' including L'Avventura, La Notte, and L'Eclisse, made in 1955. Set in Turin, it depicts the unstable relationships of five women who meet by chance through his distinctive visual style, winning the Silver Lion at the 16th Venice International Film Festival. Clelia, who works at a high-end dress shop based in Rome, arrives in Turin as the manager of a new branch opening there. One night, in the hotel room next to her lodging, she discovers Rosetta unconscious after a suicide attempt. Through this incident, Clelia deepens her friendship with Rosetta and her friend Momina... Based on Cesare Pavese's novel "Among Women Only." Starring Eleonora Rossi Drago from "The Golden Coach," Gabriele Ferzetti from L'Avventura, and Valentina Cortese from "Day for Night," among others. First released in Japanese theaters in 1964. A 2K restored version will be shown in August 2026 at the retrospective "Michelangelo Antonioni Retrospective: Arid Love, Wandering Souls," featuring five of Antonioni's early works.
title:女と男のいる舗道: This is Jean-Luc Godard's fourth feature film, following "A Woman Is a Woman," and was shot starring Anna Karina, his partner both publicly and privately. Nana, who decides to part ways with her husband after discussing life with him at a café in Paris, falls into a life where she cannot even pay her rent. She begins to proposition men on the street and engage in prostitution. Eventually, Nana becomes numb to having relations with strangers. The music was handled by Michel Legrand, the renowned composer of "The Umbrellas of Cherbourg" and other films.
title:女は女である: This is Jean-Luc Godard's third feature film, following "Breathless," and a romantic comedy created based on the idea of a "musical comedy in which the characters do not sing." Angela, a cabaret dancer, tells her live-in lover Émile that she wants a child right now. Émile cannot hide his bewilderment at her request. Then a young man named Alfred, who has feelings for Angela, appears... Following Godard's previous film "Le Petit Soldat," Anna Karina plays the heroine, with Jean-Paul Belmondo of "Breathless" as Alfred and Jean-Claude Brialy of "Les Cousins" as Émile. The music is by Michel Legrand, the renowned composer of "The Umbrellas of Cherbourg" and other films.
title:女鹿: Directed by Claude Chabrol, a leading figure of the Nouvelle Vague known for films such as *Les Cousins* and *The Third Lover*, this suspense drama explores the mysterious relationship and the web of love and hate woven by two contrasting women. The story begins when Frédérique, a wealthy bourgeois woman, becomes infatuated with Why, a young woman she spots drawing on the pavement of the Pont des Arts over the Seine. Frédérique is assertive, flamboyant, and lives a life of leisure on her father’s inheritance; Why is a quiet, struggling aspiring artist. Despite their opposite natures, Why—weary of her impoverished life—accepts Frédérique’s invitation to live at her villa. However, when Why finds herself drawn to Paul, an architect attending one of their parties, Frédérique notices and decides to seduce him herself, sparking a tense affair. Frédérique is played by Stéphane Audran, who was married to Chabrol at the time, appearing here alongside her former husband Jean-Louis Trintignant. The film earned Audran the Silver Bear for Best Actress at the 18th Berlin International Film Festival.
title:妻の病 レビー小体型認知症: This documentary captures the ten-year journey and the profound bond between Dr. Koichi Ishimoto, a pediatrician in Nankoku City, Kochi Prefecture, and his wife, Yayoi, as they navigate her battle with dementia. After being diagnosed with schizophrenia in 2004, it was discovered three years later that Yayoi actually had early-onset Lewy body dementia. Since then, Dr. Ishimoto has meticulously recorded his wife’s daily life, utilizing the keen observational eye unique to a physician. Director Shinichi Ise, who first met Dr. Ishimoto during the production of his pediatric cancer documentary "Kaze no Katachi," provides a warm portrayal of the doctor caring for Yayoi with deep affection while supported by family and the local community. Through the story of a couple whose bond deepens through illness, the film asks what is truly important when a loved one—or oneself—is faced with dementia.
title:宇宙からのメッセージ: A bandwagon film made by Kinji Fukasaku during the Star Wars boom. Though the story is simplistic, borrowing from the Tale of the Eight Dog Warriors, it generated buzz with the casting of Vic Morrow and the construction of a full-scale replica of the Riave ship. While the special effects fall short compared to Star Wars, the chase scenes created without compositing were highly praised overseas. The planet Jirusia in the Andromeda Galaxy has been transformed into a "Planet Fortress" by the invading Gabanas Empire, led by Emperor Roxeia XII. Jirusia's Great Chief Kido seeks a hero of miraculous salvation, releasing eight "Sacred Riave Fruits" into space and instructing his granddaughter Emeralida and two warriors, Urokko, to pursue the fruits and retrieve the hero. However, Roxeia launches pursuit warships without delay. The Riave fruits reach five individuals on the Earth Federation colony planet Miraseria: Galda, a former general who resigned in disillusionment; Shiro and Aron, young space bikers; Jack, a thug; and Meia, a wealthy heiress. The youths find Emeralida's damaged ship while collecting "Space Fireflies" and rescue her and Urokko, but are bewildered by their mission. Galda returns the fruit and declines to join. Shiro and the others, keeping Meia in the dark, lie about introducing other heroes and sell Emeralida to an old woman seeking a bride for her son. The old woman and Emeralida are later captured by Gabanas pursuit forces. Meia, furious upon learning of their actions, inspires the repentant youths to prepare for Jirusia's rescue. They modify Meia's space boat to carry Shiro and Aron's small craft and head for Jirusia. Along the way, they are joined by Hans, a Gabanas man who holds a Riave fruit and is the rightful heir to the Gabanas throne, usurped by Roxeia. Meanwhile, Gabanas, captivated by Earth's beauty, demands unconditional surrender from the Earth Federation. Amid the chaos, Shiro and his six companions, now reunited with Galda, infiltrate the Gabanas fortress to destroy the planet fortress and rescue Emeralida. Gathering the remaining two allies, the eight confront Roxeia.
title:宇宙戦争 次の世紀: One of four dark sci-fi works by Piotr Szulkin, a pioneer of dystopian sci-fi in Poland, who created them during the late 1970s and 1980s under the socialist regime, navigating strict censorship. The film depicts the theme of 'escape from totalitarianism' with a style of intense satire and surrealism taken to its extreme. Martians have attacked Earth. A TV host has been telling people 'there is nothing to fear,' but his apartment is ransacked and his wife is kidnapped. The nightly TV script is also changed, and the reality he sees no longer matches what he tells people every night. The film will have its theatrical premiere in Japan as part of the special screening project 'Polish Dark Sci-Fi: The Four Films of Piotr Szulkin' (starting February 21, 2026, at Theater Image Forum).
title:安寿と厨子王丸: Summoned by Toei's top brass seeking a weighty drama, screenwriter Sumie Tanaka was brought on board. The story follows aristocratic siblings reduced to slavery, overcoming their suffering through social advancement. Animators strongly objected to the narrative's obliviousness to societal power structures, yet the breathtakingly beautiful Yamato-e style visuals, where backgrounds and characters harmonize perfectly, captivate the viewer.
title:安楽死特区:
What if a "Euthanasia Bill" were passed in Japan?

Following the passage of the bill in the Diet, a facility named "Hitorishizuka" is established as a National Strategic Special Zone. Designed for those seeking euthanasia to reside and receive care, the facility becomes a lightning rod for controversy at the intersection of ethics and politics.

Shotaro Sako (Katsuya Maiguma), a rapper suffering from an incurable disease with no hope of recovery, continues to weave words together, finding salvation in hip-hop even as his condition worsens. He lives with Ayumi Fujioka (Ayaka Onishi), a journalist he met in Tibet. Despite Shotaro being given only six months to live, the two remain opposed to euthanasia and enter "Hitorishizuka" with the intent of exposing the reality of the special zone from the inside.

The facility is home to various residents, each with their own story: Ikeda (Mitsuru Hirata), who is suffering from terminal cancer, and his wife Tamami (Mariko Tsutsui); and Shinya (Kimiko Yo), a former manzai comedian with dementia who wishes to die before she completely loses her sense of self.

As Shotaro’s physical strength rapidly declines and even speaking becomes a struggle, he abruptly changes his mind without consulting Ayumi, stating, "I want euthanasia." Ayumi is forced to confront the weight of life and death as she encounters the convictions of the specialized doctors—including Ikeda’s physician Torii (Eiji Okuda) and Shotaro’s physicians Ogata (Masaya Kato) and Miura (Yuka Itaya).
title:完全版 ザ・レンチキュラーズ a/b: "Rakkun" has a crush on his classmate "Sawaki-san." After a simple exchange of work gloves brings them closer together, Rakkun is walking on air—until he remembers a rumor that she had a boyfriend in middle school. Director Akira Amemiya of the SSSS.GRIDMAN series presents a relatable, slice-of-life youth romantic comedy.
title:宝島: A documentary by Guillaume Brac, director of 'A Summer's Tale' and 'The Gentle Ones,' capturing a summer at the leisure facility 'Leisure Island' in Cergy-Pontoise, a suburb of Paris. Known as the setting for Éric Rohmer's 'My Girlfriend's Boyfriend,' and a place Brac himself frequently visited as a child, Leisure Island is filled with vacationers but has no flashy attractions, only expanses of water and greenery. Under beautiful sunlight, the film captures the natural moments of various people: boys trying to sneak into the facility, young men hitting on women, an elderly man reminiscing about the past, and employees managing and guarding the place.
title:宝島（2019）: A documentary by Guillaume Brac, director of 'A Summer's Tale' and 'The Gentle Ones,' capturing a summer at the leisure facility 'Leisure Island' in Cergy-Pontoise, a suburb of Paris. Known as the setting for Éric Rohmer's 'My Girlfriend's Boyfriend,' and a place Brac himself frequently visited as a child, Leisure Island is filled with vacationers but has no flashy attractions, only expanses of water and greenery. title:実録阿部定: "The outside light bothers me" "His smell is soaked into the futon too..." Sadame closes the storm shutters to keep Kichizō's scent from escaping. How long has it been since the two of them were alone in the small room of the teahouse? Their union seeks ever more unknown pleasures. Sadame, choking Kichizō, says happily, "Kichi-san is twitching inside me." But when Kichizō, whose health is beginning to fail, suggests returning home for a while, Sadame's pure love for him becomes directly linked to pure desire. "I won't let anyone else touch you anymore. No one..."
title:実験映画集: "Dialogue with a White Shadow" is an experimental work created by Minao Kitamura—who has practiced "visual folklore" since the 1970s—during his university years. Set against the backdrop of the defeat of the Anpo protests, the film captures a man tormented by anxiety as he wanders through Tokyo. Featuring music by Takehisa Kosugi and art by Hi-Red Center, the work vividly reflects the atmosphere of its era. "A Kiss for Three" is the follow-up work by Akio Okumura, who formed the collective "Cinema Voyant" and produced a series of experimental films. His first work, "Hesitation, or the Man Who Caresses Shadows" (1967), won the Grand Prix at the legendary 1st Sogetsu Experimental Film Festival. Okumura also translated numerous books by Jean-Luc Godard.
title:宮古島物語ふたたヴィラ かんかかりゃの願い: The third chapter of the "Miyako Island Story: Futatavilla" series, a human drama exploring the bonds and rebirth of people set against the backdrop of a small hotel on Okinawa's Miyako Island. Directed, written by, and starring Yudai Uanishi (known for "Hitokuzu" and "Goro's 400 Million Yen"), the film centers on a small villa called "Futatavilla," where it is said that staying will grant the reunion one truly desires. A couple who lost their daughter to bullying, a man pursued by debt and guilt, and friends burdened by their pasts—each carrying their own pain and prayers—are drawn to the island as if guided by the wind, eventually discovering a glimmer of new hope. The cast includes Katsuya Shibayama, chairman of Resort Life Co., Ltd., which operates hotels in Miyako Island and throughout Japan, alongside returning regulars Yudai Uanishi, Chieko Matsubara, Ai Furukawa, Mika Tokutake, and Ruby Moreno. Guest stars include Ryo Tamura and Tamotsu Ishibashi.
title:家からの手紙: A documentary by Belgian director Chantal Akerman, who revolutionized cinema with 'Jeanne Dielman, 23 quai du Commerce, 1080 Bruxelles,' a portrait of an ordinary housewife's daily routine. In this film, she reads letters from her mother over footage capturing the landscapes of 1970s New York. By layering her mother's affectionate words over the bleak cityscapes of New York—alleyways, cars on avenues, people waiting for trains on station platforms, and underground passages—the film highlights the alienation of urban life and the distance from family far away. In Japan, it received its theatrical premiere at the 'Chantal Akerman Film Festival 2023' (April 7–27, 2023, Human Trust Cinema Shibuya), screened together with 'Saute ma ville.'
title:家族という病: Writer Shimojo Akiko's 2015 essay, which questioned the concept of 'family worship' and became a bestseller with 600,000 copies, is adapted into a film by director-screenwriter Oyama Chikako of 'My Name is Lucia.' This ensemble piece, laced with black humor, depicts the absurdity and madness of people clinging to normalcy. Bestselling mystery novelist Tahara Junichiro has his life controlled by his intense wife Mariko, leaving his true talent dormant. Former elite salaryman Matsubara Yuji, unable to betray his mother's expectations even after retirement, continues to play the role of a fake executive while dealing with his hikikomori son. High school girl Kuroki Maria is driven into a corner when rumors spread that her mother is an AV actress. Appearing before these three families is Fujita Shin, an up-and-coming writer who won a literary award for a work themed around nudity. Additionally, a homeless woman living freely in the park appears as a completely different presence. Starring Fujimoto Takahiro, Tomochika, Watanabe Eri, Koide Keisuke, Teraishi Ken, Sakakibara Ai, and Hiroi Wakana.
title:富江: Tsukiko Izumisawa, a girl suffering from memory loss and insomnia due to an accident three years ago, attends a psychiatric clinic. Her doctor, Hosono, probes her memories through hypnotherapy and hears the name "Tomie." However, Tsukiko cannot recall who that name belongs to. Then, strange and terrifying events suddenly begin occurring in Tsukiko's life. One day, a detective from the Metropolitan Police visits Hosono. He is investigating a woman named Tomie Kawakami.
title:富江 tomie: Tsukiko Izumisawa, a girl suffering from memory loss and insomnia due to an accident three years ago, attends a psychiatric clinic. Her doctor, Hosono, probes her memories through hypnotherapy and hears the name "Tomie." However, Tsukiko cannot recall who that name belongs to. Then, strange and terrifying events suddenly begin occurring in Tsukiko's life. One day, a detective from the Metropolitan Police visits Hosono. He is investigating a woman named Tomie Kawakami.
title:寝ても覚めても: The commercial film debut of director Ryusuke Hamaguchi, who gained attention for "Happy Hour," a film that meticulously depicted the daily lives and friendships of four women over more than five hours and won major awards at numerous international film festivals including Locarno and Nantes. This film was entered into the Competition section of the 71st Cannes International Film Festival. It is an adaptation of the award-winning love novel of the same name by Akutagawa Prize-winning author Tomoka Shibasaki, starring Masahiro Higashide and Erika Karata. Asako, a 21-year-old living in Osaka, meets Baku and falls into a fateful love, but one day, Baku suddenly disappears from her life. Two years later, having moved from Osaka to Tokyo, Asako meets Ryohei, who has a face identical to Baku's. Unable to forget Baku, Asako tries to avoid Ryohei, but he develops feelings for her. Despite her hesitation, Asako finds herself drawn to Ryohei. Higashide plays the dual roles of Baku and Ryohei, while Karata plays Asako.
title:寝ても覚めても濱⼝⻯介監督特集上映突然、偶然、必然: The commercial film debut of director Ryusuke Hamaguchi, who gained attention for "Happy Hour," a film that meticulously depicted the daily lives and friendships of four women over more than five hours and won major awards at numerous international film festivals including Locarno and Nantes. This film was entered into the Competition section of the 71st Cannes International Film Festival. It is an adaptation of the award-winning love novel of the same name by Akutagawa Prize-winning author Tomoka Shibasaki, starring Masahiro Higashide and Erika Karata. Asako, a 21-year-old living in Osaka, meets Baku and falls into a fateful love, but one day, Baku suddenly disappears from her life. Despite her hesitation, Asako finds herself drawn to Ryohei. Higashide plays the dual roles of Baku and Ryohei, while Karata plays Asako.
title:寝る映画:
A film featuring a screenplay generated by ChatGPT, with its ethereal visuals and music also brought to life through AI. As the characters experience a virtual world while asleep, they discover a profound connection to the film's core themes: "seeing with the heart" and "touching with sound."

Yuki is blind, and her husband Ken is deaf. Despite their bond, a certain distance lingers between them. One day, the couple joins a clinical trial premised on the idea that "disabilities can be overcome within an AI-generated virtual reality." While their bodies sleep in the physical world, they awaken in a virtual realm where their sight and hearing have been restored. Amidst the strange occurrences of this world, they begin to sense each other’s presence more deeply than ever before.

Positioned as "unconscious immersive cinema" designed to be experienced while the viewer sleeps, this experimental film attempts to reach the subconscious by layering poetic phrases, music, and subtitled imagery throughout. It is directed by Tsuyoshi Sone, widely known as the cinematographer of "One Cut of the Dead."
title:尋秦記 バック・トゥ・ザ・パスト: A historical sci-fi action film and sequel to the 2001 TV series 'A Step into the Past', based on a popular Hong Kong novel. After time-traveling to the Warring States period and deeply influencing history, former Hong Kong police VIP protection officer Xiang Shaolong lives quietly in seclusion with his wife and child. His former disciple, the King of Qin, whom Xiang helped ascend the throne, remains wary of his master, their conflict smoldering. Meanwhile in modern Hong Kong, Ken, the time machine inventor imprisoned for 20 years for Xiang's failure to return, is released. Having lost everything, he plots to seize the Qin throne and become the First Emperor himself, traveling back to the Warring States with his daughter Gary and others. Attacked by Ken, the King of Qin flees and ends up at Xiang Shaolong's refuge. Louis Koo and Raymond Lam, who also starred together in the 2024 hit 'Twilight of the Warriors: Walled In', reprise their roles as Xiang Shaolong and the King of Qin, also performing the theme song. Alongside original TV series cast members, the film features Michael Miu ('White Storm'), Bai Baihe ('Monster Hunt'), and Wu Yue ('Ip Man: The Finale'). Hong Kong action star Sammo Hung serves as action director.
title:小さな恋のメロディ: A coming-of-age love story about the first love of an 11-year-old boy and girl, which became a huge hit in Japan along with the theme song 'Melody Fair' by the Bee Gees. Daniel, a shy boy attending a London public school, is best friends with his rambunctious classmate Tom, and they always play together. One day after school, while peeking at the girls' ballet practice, Daniel's heart is captured by a girl named Melody. They are drawn to each other and eventually promise to get married... The screenplay was written by Alan Parker, who later directed films such as 'Midnight Express' and 'Mississippi Burning.' A digital remastered version was re-released in June 2019.
title:小屋番 八ヶ岳に生きる 劇場版: Yatsugatake is home to so many mountain huts that it is often referred to as “Koyagatake.” In this film, we journey through these peaks alongside mountain photographer Tetsuo Kikuchi to meet the individuals who, driven by various motivations, have chosen the path of the “hut keeper.” Why did they choose a harsh daily life with no convenience stores or cars—a life lived in direct confrontation with nature? The work of a hut keeper involves supporting those who enjoy mountaineering, while at times coming face-to-face with death. While life in a mountain hut may be defined by its inconveniences, it gently offers a new perspective on the nature of living and the essence of life itself to those of us living in a modern world—exhausted by a frantic information society and accustomed to having everything at our fingertips.

This documentary journeys through the Yatsugatake mountains alongside mountain photographer Tetsuo Kikuchi, capturing the untold stories of those who confront nature and life through stunningly beautiful cinematography. Based on "KOYABAN: Living in Yatsugatake," which premiered at the TBS Documentary Film Festival 2025, this theatrical release has been re-edited with new interviews and footage of the changing seasons. In a region so dense with mountain huts it is nicknamed "Koyagatake," the film turns its lens toward the "koyaban" (hut keepers) who have chosen this path. It explores why they embrace a harsh daily existence facing nature head-on without the comforts of cars or convenience stores, and delves into the gravity of their work—supporting climbers and, at times, encountering death.
title:小川のほとりで: Korean master Hong Sang-soo directs an ensemble drama set at a women's university in Seoul, depicting the romantic entanglements of students and adults surrounding a theater festival. At a women's university in Seoul, with the theater festival approaching, textile artist Jon-hee, who works as a lecturer, invites her uncle Si-on, a famous actor and stage director, as a temporary director to fill a gap caused by a love scandal on campus. As they begin creating a short play for the festival, various events unfold over ten days, including the aftermath of the students' love affairs and the budding romance between a senior professor and Si-on. Actress Kim Min-hee, Hong Sang-soo's partner in both public and private life, stars as Jon-hee and won the Best Performance Award at the 77th Locarno International Film Festival in 2024. The cast also includes regulars from Hong Sang-soo's films: Kwon Hae-hyo as Jon-hee's uncle Si-on, Cho Yun-hee as the professor who admires Si-on, and Ha Seong-guk as the fired director who was dating three people. In Japan, it was screened under the title 'Suyuchon' at the 25th Tokyo Filmex in 2024. It was theatrically released in 2025 as the second film in the 'Monthly Hong Sang-soo' project, a series of five consecutive monthly new releases celebrating the director's 30th debut anniversary.
title:小春日和 Indian Summer:
This human drama depicts a troubled and isolated nursing assistant searching for her own way of life through a series of encounters. The film was planned and produced by Tomoko Kusube, a psychiatrist and actress, who drew from her own experience battling cancer to convey the importance of living a positive life.

Koharu Sakaguchi, burdened by worries she cannot share with anyone, flees her home after a clash with her father. Unable to return due to her feelings of guilt, she begins working as a nursing assistant at a hospital. Through her interactions with patients facing their illnesses in their own ways—such as "The Cancers," a trio of women living brightly despite their battle with cancer, and Yuki Yamamoto, who chooses to be discharged to spend her remaining days at home—Koharu gradually begins to confront her own life. One day, she suddenly recalls a precious message from her beloved grandmother, Suzuko, and makes a firm resolution.

Misaki Mizumura (*Move Forward as You Are*) stars as Koharu Sakaguchi, with Yura Chihara as Hiyori Sakaguchi, Kaoru Yumi as Grandmother Suzuko, Rie Shibata as cancer patient Yuki Yamamoto, Kappa Kunikida as Yuki’s husband Takashi, and Shiro Sano as Dr. Hiroshi Ueda. The film is directed by Isao Matsumoto (*Let’s Meet at Angie’s Bar*).
title:少佐と少女: Billy Wilder's second directorial work, which was never theatrically released in Japan. This was his highly anticipated first Hollywood film, successfully casting the era's star Ginger Rogers. To save money on train fare to Iowa, Susan disguises herself as a 12-year-old girl. A faint affection begins to blossom between her and Colonel Philip, who happens to be on the same train... Although the film touches on the theme of attraction to a minor, it was produced 12 years before the publication of the bestselling novel "Lolita."
title:少女ムシェット: Master filmmaker Robert Bresson's eighth feature, made right after his masterpiece "Au Hasard Balthazar." Based on a novel by French author Georges Bernanos, it starkly and realistically depicts the tragic fate of a young girl through rigorous framing and the actors' minimally restrained performances. 14-year-old Mouchette lives in the French countryside, forced to run the household for her alcoholic father and ill mother, while being cruelly treated by classmates and teachers at school. The unfortunate girl's fate takes a turn for the worse when, one rainy night, she encounters a poacher in the forest, sending her spiraling into further misery and ruin. Nadine Nortier, discovered for this role, plays the protagonist Mouchette, a girl standing on the brink of despair yet harboring a rebellious spirit. Produced in 1967, it was first released in Japan in 1974 by Equipe de Cinema, and again in 1995 by France Eiga Sha. A 4K restored digital remastered version had a revival release in October 2020. Another revival release is scheduled for 2026 as part of the "Robert Bresson Masterpiece Selection."
title:少年ジャックと魔法使い: Directed by Yasuji Yabushita with animation direction by Akira Daikuhara for Toei Animation's 10th anniversary film. Based on the heroic epic 'Beowulf,' this version features Jack driving a car, a witch arriving by helicopter, and a struggle to rescue comrades turned into demons in the witch's castle. Seiichiro Uno's cheerful music won the Mainichi Film Concours Music Award.
title:少年猿飛佐助: The second feature-length animation produced against the backdrop of the flourishing Toei period drama genre. For the sword-fighting scenes, Reijiro Adachi, a top action choreographer at Toei Kyoto Studio, was brought in, and Daikuhara Akira, known for dynamic action, handled both direction and key animation. Newcomers including Isao Takahata, Hiroshi Ikeda, Masao Kuroda, and Yoichi Kotabe participated in production for the first time. It is also Japan's first feature-length animation in CinemaScope.
title:山の焚火: A 1985 film by the master Fredi M. Murer, known as a pioneer of New Swiss Cinema, which won the Golden Leopard, the top prize at the Locarno International Film Festival. A family of four lives a nearly self-sufficient life surrounded by the majestic Alps. The teenage younger brother, who is deaf-mute, grows up healthily, sometimes frustrated by his disability but loved by his parents and older sister. One day, angered by a broken lawnmower, he throws it away, incurring his father's wrath. Running away from home, he begins living alone in a mountain hut. His worried sister brings him food, and they spend happy times together around a campfire on the mountain peak. Eventually, the sister's pregnancy is discovered... The film was first released in Japanese theaters in 1986. A digitally remastered version was revived in February 2020.
title:山人（やまんど） 縄文の響きが木霊する: Director Masaki Haramura, who has produced numerous documentaries on the theme of agriculture, presents the final installment of his "Yamazato Trilogy," following "Young People Aim for Mountain Villages" and "Mountain Villages Were a Sustainable World." The film follows Toichi Kanke, born in 1953, who lives in a remote village in the Oku-Aizu region of Fukushima Prefecture. As a "Yamando" (mountain person) with an intimate knowledge of the wilderness, he enters the mountains throughout the four seasons, living off their bounty without destroying the natural environment. His way of life follows a code of conduct passed down since the Jomon period, offering clues for how we might realize a sustainable future. In spring, when a variety of wild plants sprout, he ensures a continuous harvest for years to come by never picking them all. A craftsman of traditional household goods made from mountain plants, Kanke is a successor to the ancestral wisdom of utilizing precious resources without exhausting them, and he speaks of sensing the presence of the divine within the mountains. While Kanke maintains that "hunting is culture," he is deeply pained by the indiscriminate killing of bears for pest control; fearing their potential extinction, he has ceased hunting them deep in the mountains. Before each hunting season begins, he never fails to perform memorial services for the wildlife. Through the life of Kanke, embraced by the blessings of the mountains, the film brings to light a vital message that modern society is losing sight of.
title:山口くんはワルくない: A youth romance live-action film adaptation of the shōjo manga of the same name by Yu Saiki, serialized in Kodansha's 'Bessatsu Friend,' starring Kyōhei Takahashi of the idol group 'Naniwa Danshi.' It depicts the romantic journey of Satsuki, an ordinary high school girl who dreams of love, and Yamaguchi-kun, a transfer student with a scary-looking face and a Kansai dialect. Yamaguchi-kun, who transfers to Satsuki's school, has blonde hair and piercings, giving him a menacing look, and rumors circulate that he's a yakuza. After a certain incident brings her close to Yamaguchi-kun, Satsuki learns about his shy and kind true nature and gradually becomes drawn to him. Satsuki tries to keep Yamaguchi-kun's hidden charms all to herself, but a handsome classmate, Ishizaki, who inexplicably has a grudge against Yamaguchi-kun, stands in her way. It turns out Ishizaki also harbors special feelings for Yamaguchi-kun, suddenly emerging as Satsuki's romantic rival. The love triangle of these three takes an unexpected turn. Kyōhei Takahashi plays Yamaguchi-kun, who has a kind and pure heart beneath his scary appearance; Hikaru Takahashi ('Romantic Killer') plays the heroine Satsuki, who grows close to Yamaguchi-kun; and Yōji Iwase ('The Girl and the Guard Dog') plays Ishizaki, the classmate who stirs up trouble between Yamaguchi-kun and Satsuki. The film is directed by Kentarō Moriya ('PRINCE OF LEGEND,' 'Seaside Motel').
title:山椒大夫: Commentary: In the Heian period, Zushio and Anju, separated from their parents, are sold into slavery... A film adaptation of Ogai's short story based on a medieval folktale, this timeless masterpiece won the Silver Lion at the Venice International Film Festival. The visual beauty captured by the renowned cinematographer Miyagawa is also awe-inspiring.
title:岡本万太: The protagonist, Manta Okamoto (Sojiro Sanada), is a 26-year-old part-timer. Plagued by mounting irritation over life’s minor inconveniences, he lives in constant fear of whether he can suppress his own impulses. For Manta is a man of uncontrollable rage. Once a month, his stress reaches a breaking point—his "Limit Day." To cope, he locks himself away at home, strapped to a bed with restraints. Because these days strike without warning, he frequently misses work, leading to a cycle of being fired and drifting from one job to the next. One day, Nakamura (Masaki Miura), a former senior colleague from a publishing house that let him go, approaches him with a new opportunity. The job is simple: store some cardboard boxes for a few days in exchange for a large sum of money. But...
title:工場 鉄西区 第一部: Part one of the documentary trilogy "Tie Xi Qu: West of the Tracks," a nine-hour epic by director Wang Bing ("The Ditch") that chronicles the decline of the Tiexi District, a heavy industrial zone in Shenyang, China. Originally established in Mukden, Manchuria, during the Japanese occupation, the district grew into a vital industrial hub of 20th-century China before its prosperity eventually faded with the changing times. The film takes its camera into three factories, capturing workers who once braved hazards like accidents and lead poisoning as they now idle in facilities slated for closure, as well as state-owned factory managers struggling with the pressures of privatization and failing operations. The trilogy won the Grand Prize at the 2003 Yamagata International Documentary Film Festival and received its first Japanese theatrical release in 2013 to coincide with the premiere of Wang Bing’s "Three Sisters."
title:左ききのエレン（3話先行上映）:
The first three episodes of the TV anime *Left-Handed Eren*, set to premiere in April 2026, will receive a limited one-week theatrical screening ahead of the television broadcast. Based on the manga of the same name by Kappi, the story is set in the advertising industry and depicts a youth ensemble drama of creators. It centers on two individuals: Koichi, an ordinary man dreaming of becoming "something" while struggling with the limits of his own talent, and Eren, a solitary genius who suffers due to her overwhelming gift.

High school student Koichi Asakura, who aspires to attend an art university to become a designer, is one day struck by graffiti scrawled on an art museum wall. The artist is Eren Yamagishi, a left-handed high school girl who had suppressed her talent following a certain incident. Eventually, the two come to acknowledge one another through the act of "creating," and while Koichi sets out to become a designer and Eren a painter, their paths take unexpected turns...

Shoya Chiba voices the role of Koichi, and Yumi Uchiyama voices Eren Yamagishi. The series is directed by Toshimasa Suzuki (*Fafner in the Azure: Heaven and Earth*), with series composition by Taku Kishimoto (*Haikyu!!*). Takayuki Goto (*Ghost in the Shell: S.A.C. 2nd GIG*) provides the original animation character drafts, while Yuka Fukuchi and Akane Tamai (*Platinum End*) serve as character designers and chief animation directors. Animation production is a joint effort by Signal.MD and Production I.G.
title:左利きの少女: Taipei, a night market noodle stall. Five-year-old Yi-jin (Nina Yeh), along with her single mother Shue-fen (Janel Tsai) who is burdened with debt, and her teenage sister Yi-an (Ma Shih-yuan), returns from the countryside to rebuild their lives. One day, her old-fashioned grandfather denounces her dominant left hand as the "devil's hand," and Yi-jin begins to feel guilt. That devil's hand, inadvertently, brings to light the "sins" that each family member has been hiding.
title:左撇子女孩: Taipei, a night market noodle stall. Five-year-old Yi-jin (Nina Yeh), along with her single mother Shue-fen (Janel Tsai) who is burdened with debt, and her teenage sister Yi-an (Ma Shih-yuan), returns from the countryside to rebuild their lives. One day, her old-fashioned grandfather denounces her dominant left hand as the "devil's hand," and Yi-jin begins to feel guilt. That devil's hand, inadvertently, brings to light the "sins" that each family member has been hiding.
title:市民ケーン: A human drama produced, directed, co-written, and starring the 25-year-old prodigy Orson Welles, hailed as a masterpiece in film history. Based on real-life newspaper magnate William Randolph Hearst, it depicts the tumultuous life of a wealthy tycoon through innovative visual techniques and narrative structure. The wealthy newspaper magnate Kane dies, leaving behind the mysterious word "Rosebud." A newsreel editor assigned to investigate the meaning of the word interviews people who knew Kane in life, including his ex-wife and business partners. What emerges is the lonely life of a man who had everything. The film won the Academy Award for Best Original Screenplay at the 14th Academy Awards in 1942.
title:帰って来たドラゴン: In the late Qing dynasty, the villainous Im Kun-ho rules over Gold Sand Village, a place rife with all kinds of crime and violence, including drugs and human trafficking. The Dragon group, traveling while punishing evil, and at the same time, the legendary female martial artist Eagle, arrive in this village. They are both searching for a treasure called the 'Silver Pearl', said to have been stolen from a Tibetan temple. Then, the ruthless killer karate practitioner Black Jaguar also appears, and fierce battles unfold among the powerful fighters over the Silver Pearl. This is the Japan comeback film for Yasuaki Kurata, who was active primarily in Hong Kong.
title:幕末ヒポクラテスたち: A period drama set at the end of the Edo period, when traditional Chinese medicine doctors and Western-trained Dutch medicine doctors coexisted, starring Kuranosuke Sasaki as the village Dutch medicine doctor Daisuke Okura. In a village on the outskirts of Kyoto at the end of the Edo period, Daisuke Okura is a tolerant, curious Dutch medicine doctor who saves common people regardless of wealth or status. He is constantly engaged in fierce arguments with the Chinese medicine doctor Gensai, his sworn enemy. One day, Okura saves a hot-tempered young man named Shinsa through surgery, an event that drastically changes both their lives. Director Kazuki Omori, known for the ensemble drama 'Hippocrates' about Kyoto medical students, conceived this film based on the 1960 film 'Fundoshi Doctor,' which depicted a warm-hearted doctor and his wife, setting it in Kyoto at the end of the Edo period to portray the dawn of modern Japanese medicine. When Omori passed away in 2022 while preparing for filming, the project nearly became a phantom, but Akira Ogata, director of 'The Independent Teenage Chorus' and a former assistant director to Omori, carried on his will and brought it to completion. Kuranosuke Sasaki plays Okura. Takeshi Naito, who made his film debut in 'Hippocrates,' plays Okura's rival Gensai, and Akira Emoto, who played a resident doctor in 'Hippocrates,' appears as the mysterious samurai Danzo. Additionally, Shizuka Muroi, who made her film debut in Omori's 'Hear the Wind Sing,' provides narration, and Takuya Nishioka, who has known Omori since the 1970s, wrote the screenplay, with many cast and crew members associated with Kazuki Omori participating.
title:幕末太陽傳: Saheiji, left penniless at a Shinagawa pleasure quarter at the end of the Edo period... A masterpiece by Kawashima and Frankie, and a classic in Japanese film history. In this ensemble comedy where late-Edo period patriots and courtesans mingle, Frankie's light and agile movements as he navigates through the chaos are the film's core.
title:平田雄己監督特集上映Lost in Images: One day, Ayano goes on a picnic with her boyfriend, Shuichi, and his daughter, Minato. However, the atmosphere between the three is slightly strained. Eventually, they drift apart. Minato immerses herself in memories of her late mother, Miho. Shuichi sees visions of his past family. And then, Miho appears before Ayano.
title:幸せの、忘れもの。: A Spanish film that delicately portrays the story of a woman living in a world without sound and her family. Ángela, who is deaf, and her husband Héctor, who gently supports her, communicate through the irreplaceable language of sign language. Ángela works in a pottery workshop, surrounded by the comforting smell of clay and trusted colleagues, living a quiet and peaceful life. However, a certain 'happy event' begins to gradually shatter her daily life. As she wavers in her sense of alienation, Ángela tries to grasp the 'true happiness' that flickers between the silent world and the world outside... Directed by emerging filmmaker Eva Libertad, who also works as a playwright and sociologist, this film is based on her highly acclaimed 2021 short film 'Sorda.' Starring Miriam Garlo, a deaf actress and Libertad's real sister, the film reflects the director and her sister's long-standing personal experiences, capturing the subtle misunderstandings between deaf and hearing people and the different feelings of alienation each holds. It won the Panorama Audience Award and the Art Cinema Award at the 75th Berlin International Film Festival in 2025, as well as the Golden Biznaga (Best Film), Audience Award, Best Actress, and Best Actor at the 28th Málaga Film Festival in Spain.
title:幸福（しあわせ）: One of the representative works of Agnès Varda, a leading female director of the French New Wave, this human drama depicts the ironic fate that befalls an ordinary couple in search of happiness. François lives a peaceful and happy life surrounded by his beautiful wife Thérèse and their adorable children. One day, while visiting a nearby town, François meets Émilie, a woman who works at the post office, and falls in love with her. At the same time, François truly loves his wife Thérèse. One day, while on a picnic with his family, François confesses his infidelity to Thérèse... The film won the Silver Bear at the 1965 Berlin International Film Festival.
title:幻の光: Having witnessed grief work in his TV documentary 'However... In an Age of Welfare Cuts,' Kore-eda tackles this theme head-on in his first theatrical feature, based on the novel of the same name by Teru Miyamoto. Yumiko (Esumi), who carries childhood trauma, loses her husband to suicide in the midst of a happy marriage. Years later, she lives a peaceful life with a new family, but a lingering unease never fully fades. Against the backdrop of Noto's nature captured in long shots, the quiet rebirth of a woman's heart is depicted with a serene gaze.
title:幻を見るひと: A documentary depicting Yoshimasu Gozo, a leading contemporary Japanese poet, as he visits Kyoto, a city rich with groundwater, questions the meaning of life through dialogue with 'water' and the changing seasons, and ultimately creates a poem. Witnessing the tsunami damage from the Great East Japan Earthquake in 2011, Yoshimasu was struck speechless by the impact of water that strips everything away. Seeking a new meaning for water, he visits Kyoto, known for its abundant groundwater. In Kyoto, a basin surrounded by deep mountains, Yoshimasu travels tracing the 'water' of the city, visiting places like Ryukyoin, where Kawabata Yasunari wrote 'The Old Capital,' as well as Daigo-ji, Myoshin-ji, Daitoku-ji, and Kifune Shrine. The film captures Yoshimasu's sensibility, which remains virginal even as he approaches 80, and his precious creative process.
title:幻を見るひと〜京都の吉増剛造〜: The film opens with footage of the tsunami from the Great East Japan Earthquake (courtesy of the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism). The new work by Gozo Yoshimasu, 'A Water Tree Stands on the Planet,' born at the climax of this film, was completed after the poet's long struggle. Yoshimasu had been unable to write poetry since the 2011 Great East Japan Earthquake. 'At the beginning of human life, there is amniotic fluid and bathwater; at the end, there is the water of the dying that moistens the lips,' says Yoshimasu. 'Water,' the source of life for humanity, has been an important theme for poets throughout history. However, the poet who directly witnessed the scars of the great tsunami lost his words to the impact of water that strips everything away. Instead of writing poetry, Yoshimasu began daily copying the poems of the Showa-era philosopher Takaaki Yoshimoto in rice-grain-sized characters, like a sutra transcription. The camera captures this strange and fascinating scene. 'Beside the Poem,' written over four years and which he calls 'Monster-kun,' is a massive work of nearly 700 pages. Within it, the actual voice of the representative Japanese poet Akiko Yosano (1878–1942) resounds, sanukite stones ring, and finally, an eerie scene unfolds as he flings ink onto paper like Jackson Pollock (USA, 1912–1956), the founder of action painting. Deviating from the act of writing, time accumulates on a single sheet of paper, creating an object-like state. This becomes a 'practice writing book' over a long period, leading to the gestation of a new work. One day, learning that Kyoto has as much groundwater as Lake Biwa (Japan's largest lake), the poet seeks a new path for poetic creation in Kyoto's water veins. The poet's tentacles begin to reach the water of Kyoto, which holds a giant cradle of water. Then, before Yoshimasu appears the phantom of Yasunari Kawabata, winner of the Nobel Prize in Literature. Resonating with the talent of seeing phantoms in Kawabata, who stayed in Kyoto and devoted himself to creative work, the poet gropes for the thread of his own poetic creation. What the poet's senses finally touch is the great Eastern spirit, the water god, the dragon. Yoshimasu hears the voice of water's destiny and takes up his brush. The story of Gozo Yoshimasu depicted in this film shows the path of a poet, standing at the abyss of creative despair, 'gaining new life.' The backdrop, like Kawabata's masterpiece 'The Old Capital' which earned him the Nobel Prize, is vividly colored by Kyoto's four seasons, Zen temples, and karesansui (dry landscape gardens).
title:幻愛 夢の向こうに:
STORY Is this love real, or an illusion?
Primary school teacher Lok (Li Chi-lok) manages to navigate his daily life while living with schizophrenia. One day, he falls in love at first sight with a woman named Yan Yan. The two are quickly drawn to one another, but Lok suffers in silence, unable to reveal the truth about his condition. As his symptoms worsen, their relationship begins to distort. Later, during a therapy session, Lok meets Ip Lam, a woman who looks exactly like Yan Yan. A graduate student majoring in psychology, Lam is researching "erotomania," a symptom of schizophrenia. Seeing Lok as the ideal subject for her research, she asks for his cooperation with her thesis. However, the two soon find themselves developing feelings that transcend the boundaries between researcher and patient—

Terence Lau (*Twilight of the Warriors: Walled In*) and Cecilia Choi star in this poignant love story depicting a man and woman wandering the boundary between reality and illusion.

Primary school teacher Lai Chi-lok manages to lead a functional life despite suffering from schizophrenia. He falls in love at first sight with a woman named Yan Yan, but as they grow closer, he is unable to confess his illness to her. As his symptoms worsen, it is eventually revealed that Yan Yan herself was a hallucination. During a therapy session, Lok meets Ip Lam, a woman who is the spitting image of Yan Yan. A graduate student majoring in psychology, Lam is researching "erotomania," a symptom of schizophrenia. Though she initially asks Lok to cooperate with her thesis as an ideal research subject, the two soon develop feelings that transcend the roles of researcher and patient.

The film is directed by Kiwi Chow (*Ten Years*, *Revolution of Our Times*). Terence Lau plays Chi-lok, a young man seeking love while struggling with schizophrenia, and Cecilia Choi plays both Yan Yan and Lam. Their performances won Best Actor and Best Actress, respectively, at the 26th Hong Kong Film Critics Society Awards.
title:幻魔大戦: The destroyer of the universe, "Genma," was approaching Earth. Luna, a princess of Transylvania and an esper, received a message from the cosmic consciousness "Froi" and began a battle to protect Earth alongside Vega, a cyborg soldier also fighting Genma. Luna decided to gather psychics from around the world to counter Genma. Among them was high school student Azuma Higashi, who was unaware of his own abilities until Vega's provocations awakened his psychic powers. However, emotionally immature, he closed his heart to Luna's pleas to join the fight to save the universe. Even so, the enemy appeared before him without mercy.
title:床一面こんな感じ: A drama about two women who are close friends but growing increasingly dissatisfied with their shared living situation, as they struggle to clean their filthy apartment over the course of one night. Yabuki Kotori is curious and takes long trips to the toilet, while Mimori Suzuka is a fermented food enthusiast who is bad at housework. The best friends share a house, but something feels off. One day, their dream man, Kurita-san, is coming to visit, but their apartment is unbelievably dirty. With a deadline of 10 a.m., Kotori and Suzuka start a big cleanup together, but... Created by the filmmaking unit "Shidoromodori," known for "Sumiko 22" and "I Still Don't Know You," consisting of Hamada Satsuki and Fukuoka Sawako, based on their own shared-house experiences. Hamada directs, and Fukuoka handles the script and editing. Seto Riko (from "Kekkyoku Kohi") stars as Yabuki Kotori, and Sono Rin (from "Otona ni Naritakunaremasu you ni") stars as Mimori Suzuka, with Matsuzaki Shohei, Shinpo Yuki, and Kudo Haruka in a special appearance supporting the cast. The project "chill the gambler" and "kiss the gambler" by singer-songwriter Kana-fan provides the music and theme song.
title:廃用身: Based on the debut novel by physician-author Yo Hisakabe published in 2003, this human suspense film stars Shota Sometani. At the daycare facility 'Ijinzaka Clinic,' an innovative treatment devised by director Kuranosuke Urushibara spreads quietly among the elderly. Aiming for cost-effective care, the treatment involves 'useless limbs' (paralyzed body parts with no hope of recovery), and unexpected 'favorable side effects' have appeared, such as 'feeling lighter in body and mind' and 'a harsh personality softening.' Hearing rumors, editor Yagura senses potential for a revolution in geriatric medicine and proposes publishing a book to Urushibara. However, everything takes a dark turn when an internal whistleblowing about the daycare leaks to a weekly magazine, and a shocking incident occurs at a patient's home. Sometani delivers a haunting performance as Urushibara, a doctor who, in pursuit of his ideals, steps into the gap between rationality and madness. The cast includes Yuki Kitamura as editor Yagura, Naomasa Rokudaira as elderly patient Iwagami who reclaims his life through Urushibara's treatment, and Kumi Takiuchi as Urushibara's wife Kikuko. The film is directed and written by Mitsuki Yoshida, who has gained international attention for works such as 'Family X' and 'Three Lights.'

title:從今以後: A drama depicting a long-term lesbian couple facing various problems after one partner's sudden death. Director Ray Yeung, who previously explored the issues of elderly gay couples in "Suk Suk," turns his gaze to the current state of Hong Kong, where prejudice against homosexuality remains deeply rooted, while also highlighting social issues such as severe housing shortages, employment difficulties, and economic disparity. Pat and Angie, a lesbian couple in their 60s, are enjoying a stable and peaceful life both publicly and privately. However, Pat suddenly dies. Angie was close with Pat's relatives, but they clash over the funeral arrangements. Furthermore, under Hong Kong law, Pat's brother, as her relative, inherits her estate. This is an unacceptable reality for Angie, who considered the apartment, filled with memories of Pat, to be their final home. Meanwhile, Pat's financially struggling brother, his wife, and their children also grapple with their own circumstances. The film won the Teddy Award for outstanding LGBTQ cinema at the 74th Berlin International Film Festival in 2024 and received high praise, including five nominations at the 43rd Hong Kong Film Awards, including Best Film. Patra Au, who won the Hong Kong Film Award for Best Supporting Actress for "Suk Suk," plays Angie, earning a Best Actress nomination for this film. Maggie Li, returning to the screen after about 30 years, plays Pat.
title:復活の日: In 1982, the deadly virus MM-88 is stolen from a research institute in East Germany. However, the plane carrying the spy who stole it crashes in the Alps, and the virus spreads across the Earth, wiping out humanity except for a small group of survivors in Antarctica. One of these survivors, earthquake researcher Yoshizumi, realizes an even greater danger is approaching: a massive earthquake could strike the eastern United States, potentially triggering the launch of nuclear missiles.
title:心と体と [プレ企画]シネマカリテと また逢える: A slaughterhouse on the outskirts of Budapest. Mária, who struggles to fit in at work, and Endre, her boss who takes an interest in her. Though the two are socially awkward and out of sync, they are drawn together when a company-wide counseling session reveals they have been sharing the exact same dream—but...
title:心のパズル:
A drama that explores the multifaceted nature of the human psyche through the lens of Dissociative Identity Disorder (multiple personality disorder). Former stage actor Kimihiko Yuasa, unable to control a violent "other self" within him, once struck the director he admired, Kiyoshi Yanagimoto, during a rehearsal. Now, while grappling with his own inner turmoil, Yuasa works as a private investigator. One day, he is approached by Takayama—who, like Yuasa, was a victim of Yanagimoto’s abuse of power—with a request: "He must have multiple personalities; find the evidence." As Yuasa begins his investigation, he encounters a version of Yanagimoto who seems like a completely different person.

The film marks the directorial debut of Shigeharu Kadowaki. Coming from the food and beverage industry, Kadowaki turned to filmmaking
title:心をつないで 思いを紡いで: Screening at EU Film Days 2026 (Tokyo: May 16–29, 2026 at Theater Image Forum, May 19–24 at National Film Archive; Nagoya: June 6–19 at Nagoya Kinema Noi; also to be held in Hiroshima, Kyoto, and Fukuoka).
title:心平、: A brother who cannot fit into society, a father who has given up on the future, and a sister bound to the home. This is a story of the small steps the three of them take forward. One day, the Great East Japan Earthquake suddenly upends their peaceful daily lives. Not only the earthquake and tsunami, but also the nuclear accident forced many people to lose their homes and jobs, leaving Fukushima behind. This is the story of a family living in the aftermath, three years later, in a deeply scarred Fukushima.
title:心平、【公開1周年記念 パンフレット付上映】: A brother who cannot fit into society, a father who has given up on the future, and a sister bound to the home. This is a story of the small steps the three of them take forward. One day, the Great East Japan Earthquake suddenly upends their peaceful daily lives. Not only the earthquake and tsunami, but also the nuclear accident forced many people to lose their homes and jobs, leaving Fukushima behind. This is the story of a family living in the aftermath, three years later, in a deeply scarred Fukushima.
title:心耳 耳を澄まさぬ表現者たち: This documentary focuses on "Sign Language Kyogen," a subject that Tetsuko Kuroyanagi has devoted over 40 years to, capturing the efforts of deaf individuals who take on classical performing arts through sign language. The Sign Language Kyogen project was initiated by Tetsuko Kuroyanagi in the 1980s with the "Japan Deaf Theatre Company." Over four decades, their performances have become so popular that tickets are constantly sold out, and they have also performed abroad, spreading Japanese traditional arts worldwide. Through rare footage of the overseas performance of "Uri Nusubito" (The Melon Thief), testimonies from those involved, scenes of rigorous training, and behind-the-scenes moments, the film explores the appeal of Sign Language Kyogen, its differences from traditional Kyogen, and how it is received globally. Interview footage features Tetsuya Izaki, a founding member of the troupe who has supported Sign Language Kyogen alongside Kuroyanagi; Satoshi Ezoe, the troupe's representative; and Chikashige Miyake, a Kyogen performer of the Izumi school who instructs the troupe using sign language. Tetsuko Kuroyanagi serves as executive producer, and director Shugo Fujii, known for "ONPAKU" and "Chō Gitaiteki Ningen," completed this as his first documentary work.
title:心耳～耳を澄まさぬ表現者たち: There are deaf people spreading Japanese traditional performing arts to the world. Driven by this fact, director Hidetake Fujii's impulse that "this must be conveyed to the world" became the catalyst for making this film. Tetsuko Kuroyanagi's passion, having devoted 40 years to sign language and sign language Kyogen. Through meeting her, the significance of sign language as a "language" comes into view. But the story does not end as a mere record of inspiration. What they arrive at is one pressing question. This film is by no means simply a movie to promote the appeal of sign language.
title:急に具合が悪くなる: Director Ryusuke Hamaguchi ("Drive My Car," "Evil Does Not Exist") portrays the spiritual encounter of two women with the same-sounding name in Paris. Based on the exchange of 20 letters between philosopher Makiko Miyano, who survived cancer metastasis, and anthropologist Maho Isono, titled "Suddenly Feeling Ill," the film depicts the connection between two women who meet by chance and their confrontation with the world. Marie-Lou Fontaine, director of the care facility "Garden of Freedom" on the outskirts of Paris, struggles with staff shortages and misunderstanding while striving for humane care. She meets Japanese stage director Mari Morisaki, who is battling cancer, and draws courage from her theater work. Guided by the coincidence of their similar-sounding names, Marie-Lou and Mari begin a friendship. But one day, Mari suddenly falls ill. As her illness progresses, their bond deepens, and their souls connect. Virginie Efira ("Benedetta") plays Marie-Lou, and Tao Okamoto, a global fashion model who has appeared in Hollywood films like "The Wolverine," plays Mari. Kyozo Nagatsuka ("Enemy") plays Goro Seimiya, an actor in Mari's play, and Koyo Kuroki ("The Generation of the Looking-Ahead") plays Tomoki Kubodera, Goro's grandson. Screened in the Competition section of the 79th Cannes Film Festival in 2026, Virginie Efira and Tao Okamoto jointly won the Best Actress award. Okamoto became the first Japanese person to win the Cannes Best Actress award.
title:怪奇タクシー 布告を知らぬ者達に: A live-action film adaptation of Tatsuya Morino's popular manga "Kaiki Taxi," created by the artist who studied under Shigeru Mizuki and specializes in yokai (supernatural creatures) stories. The film consists of three episodes: "Curve's Man-Eating Car," where a TV crew investigating rumors of a mysterious accident involving a couple's car on a hilltop date spot curve is drawn into a terrifying experience, guided by the enigmatic taxi driver Takerō Kiboku; "Illegal Parking Critic," which reveals the truth behind a tragedy where an ambulance couldn't reach the hospital in time due to traffic caused by illegally parked cars, resulting in a death; and "Mystery Tour," depicting various strange occurrences during a bus tour attended by a man with a secret. The cast includes Yumi Okada, Taisei Kido, Koji Matoba, Emiri Nakayama, Taiyo Sugiura, Seiji Chihara, Ryūya Nagayama, and Makoto Ogawa. Hideo Okamoto, who also wrote the screenplay for the film adaptation "Kaiki Taxi: Beware the Windy Night Road" and is known as a designer for various special effects and anime works, directed the film.
title:怪奇タクシー布告を知らぬ者達に: This film is a live-action adaptation of the cult-favorite work 'Kaiki Taxi' by yokai manga artist Tatsuya Morino. Screened at the Hiroshima International Film Festival 2025 and the Kyoto Machinaka Film Festival 2026, it has stirred the occult film scene and finally hits theaters. Three horror tales spanning genres like occult, urban legend, and human terror are woven together: 'Curve's Man-Eating Car,' where a TV crew investigating a curve prone to mysterious accidents encounters terror guided by an unidentified monstrous taxi driver named Takerō Kaiki; 'Illegal Parking Critic,' depicting the tragedy born from illegal parking and a further chilling truth; and 'Mystery Tour,' the nightmare of a man with a secret who joins a certain bus tour. The cast brings together a luxurious and diverse lineup, including Yumi Okada, Taisei Kido, Yu Kamimura, Dai Hirayama ('Curve's Man-Eating Car'), Koji Matoba, Emiri Nakayama, Taiyo Sugiura, Seiji Chihara ('Illegal Parking Critic'), Ryuya Nagayama, Makoto Ogawa, and Mirai Takikita ('Mystery Tour'). The director is Hideo Okamoto, who has long been active in special effects, anime, and design. Expanding the original work's worldview, it has been developed into a more layered, full-fledged horror. Occult? Human terror? Genre-defying, this eerie and exhilarating horror, where fantasy and reality intermingle, races through this summer!
title:怪奇！死肉の男: A full AI-produced film adaptation (with all dialogue in English) of horror manga artist Hino Hideshi's terrifying yet moving story 'Horror! The Man of Dead Flesh.' One day, a 'living corpse' suddenly appears in the city—his body is rotting and squishy, maggots crawl from his eyes, and his heart isn't beating, yet somehow he is alive! After being taken into police custody, the man is sent to a university hospital's isolation ward. Growing sick of the repeated human experiments, he finally attempts to escape... Who is he, and where is he headed? A poignant and sorrowful man of dead flesh. His fate begins with death. What awaits him beyond?
title:怪物: Directed by Hirokazu Kore-eda, winner of the Palme d'Or at the Cannes Film Festival for "Shoplifters," this human drama is based on an original screenplay by Yuji Sakamoto, the popular screenwriter known for films like "We Made a Beautiful Bouquet" and the TV drama "The Days of Natsume." The music was composed by Ryuichi Sakamoto, who became the first Japanese to win an Academy Award for Best Original Score for "The Last Emperor" and passed away in March 2023. In a suburban town by a large lake, a single mother who loves her son, a caring schoolteacher, and innocent children live peaceful daily lives. One day, a fight breaks out at school. It seems like an ordinary scuffle between kids, but the accounts of those involved conflict, gradually escalating into a major incident that draws in society and the media. Then, on a stormy morning, the children suddenly vanish. What is the "monster"? This collaboration among leading Japanese creators—Hirokazu Kore-eda, Yuji Sakamoto, and Ryuichi Sakamoto—depicts the conclusion reached through a search for the "monster" from each character's perspective. Alongside Soya Kurokawa and Hinata Hiiragi, who play the two central boys, the film features a stellar cast including Sakura Ando, Eita Nagayama, Mitsuki Takahata, Akihiro Kakuta, Shido Nakamura, and Yuko Tanaka. It was screened in the Competition section of the 76th Cannes Film Festival in 2023, winning the Best Screenplay Award. It also received the Queer Palm, awarded to films dealing with LGBT and queer themes.
title:怪速急行■■行き: A mystery horror from South Korea that follows the fate of a video creator investigating the truth behind a station rumored to make people disappear. Da-gyeong, a female horror content creator struggling with low view counts, posts a video about the urban legend of 'Gwangnim Station,' a subway station where people have been going missing, in a bid to turn things around. The video goes viral, skyrocketing to the top of the rankings overnight. Consumed by her desire for views, Da-gyeong steps into an inescapable darkness to uncover the truth behind the rumors. Directed by rising South Korean filmmaker Tak Seung, the film depicts how a familiar place like a subway station transforms into something terrifying. Ju Hyeon-yeong (known for dramas like 'A Gentle Woman' and 'Extraordinary Attorney Woo') makes her feature film debut as the protagonist Da-gyeong. Jung Bae-su (from 'Queen of Tears') plays the station master who tells Da-gyeong about the strange rumors, and Choi Bo-min (from 'Spirit Fingers') plays Woo-jin, the producer at the content production company Da-gyeong works for.
title:恋する惑星: A stylish ensemble love story set in Hong Kong that depicts the intersecting romantic entanglements of young people, catapulting director Wong Kar-wai to international fame. Cop 223, heartbroken on April Fool's Day, buys a can of pineapple every day until his birthday a month later. Determined to forget his lover by falling for a woman he meets that night, he encounters a blonde woman in sunglasses at a bar he stumbles into. Meanwhile, fast-food worker Faye is given a letter by her boss for regular customer Cop 633. It's a letter from Cop 633's ex-girlfriend, containing the key to his apartment. Faye, harboring a crush on him, uses the key to sneak into his room... Cop 223 is played by Takeshi Kaneshiro, and Cop 633 by Tony Leung. It won three awards including Best Picture at the 14th Hong Kong Film Awards. First released in Japan in 1995. In 2022, a 4K restored version was screened as part of 'WKW4K' (from August 19, 2022, at Cine Mart Shinjuku, Grand Cinema Sunshine, Cinema City, etc.).
title:恋文: From naval academy to the skies of the South Seas, and now having survived to set foot on his homeland's soil, Reikichi's only thought has been his beloved Michiko. Through rumors, he heard she had lost her husband to death and moved to Tokyo. Reikichi moves to Tokyo and stays in the apartment of his younger brother Yo, a book broker, and while working as a ghostwriter of love letters for mistresses through the help of his war comrade Yamaji, he searches for Michiko's whereabouts. The day that compressed five years into an instant finally arrives. Michiko comes to him to request ghostwriting of a love letter, just like any other 'panpan' girl. Reikichi, who had cherished the image of pure Michiko, lashes out with harsh words at the Michiko before him. From then on, Reikichi spends days of drunken agony torn between love and hatred for Michiko. Yo, who vaguely senses his brother's feelings, consults Yamaji and meets Michiko. After her husband's death in the war, unable to stay in her stepmother's home, she worked with the occupation forces in Yokohama, and out of loneliness began living with a kind foreign officer—but she was not living a dissolute life like so-called 'panpan' girls, and had since parted with that officer. Yo and Yamaji arrange for Michiko and Reikichi to meet, but Reikichi refuses. Knowing Reikichi's heart that will not forgive her, Michiko throws herself into oncoming traffic amid tangled headlights. Told by police of her serious injury, Reikichi realizes that regardless of her past mistakes, she is precious to him. In the car racing to the hospital, Reikichi sobs and prays to God for Michiko's life.

title:恐怖分子: With the release of 'A One and a Two (4K Restored)', the screening of Edward Yang's representative work 'A Brighter Summer Day (Digital Remastered)' has also been confirmed!
