title:犬王: A feature-length musical anime directed by Masaaki Yuasa (*Lu Over the Wall*), adapting Hideo Furukawa’s novel *Tales of the Heike: Inu-Oh*, which was modeled after the real-life Noh performer Inu-Oh who flourished during the Nanboku-cho and Muromachi periods. In the capital of Kyoto, a child is born into the Hiei-za family of Omi Sarugaku. This child would grow up to be the Noh performer Inu-Oh, who would later drive the masses into a frenzy, but his physical form is so bizarre that the adults cover his body in clothing and hide his face behind a mask. One day, Inu-Oh meets Tomona, a blind boy and biwa priest. Bound by a firm friendship as business partners to survive the world, the two unleash their respective talents and produce a string of hits. As Inu-Oh captivates audiences on stage, he transforms a part of his body with every performance, gradually attaining a singular beauty. The film features character designs by Taiyo Matsumoto, the manga artist of *Ping Pong* (which Yuasa previously adapted), and a screenplay by Akiko Nogi (*I Am a Hero*).
title:犬神家の一族: The will of the old family patriarch Saibee Inugami is made public, but it states that the heir to the vast fortune is the one who marries Tamayo Nonomiya, the granddaughter of Saibee's mentor. Saibee's three grandsons each scheme to claim Tamayo for themselves, but this soon escalates into a series of murders...
title:猫を放つ: A love story that interweaves past and present, depicting the current state of a drifting married couple and a reunion with a friend that stirs up past memories. This is the feature-length directorial debut of Daisuke Shigayuki, who gained attention for short films like "Haru Mitai da" and "Madotachi," completed after a seven-year production period. Mori, a musician, is troubled by the distance he feels from his wife Maiko, a photographer. One day, Mori unexpectedly reunites with a former friend, Asako, rekindling old feelings for her. Asako also remembers being attracted to Mori in the past. However, their memories, tinged with expectations and desires, appear blurry, distorted, and conveniently rewritten in each of their minds. After a long walk, Mori and Asako reexamine their two lives that have already gone off track and the present moment they each stand in. Actor Soma Fujii, who also works as singer-songwriter "soma," stars as Mori and also handles the music. Ran Taniguchi (from "Hold Your Breath") plays Mori's wife Maiko, and Yukiho Murakami (from "August My Heaven") plays Mori's former friend Asako. The film was selected for the competition section of the 30th Busan International Film Festival in 2025.
title:獨立時代: A youth ensemble drama from 1994 by the renowned Taiwanese master Edward Yang, known for "A Brighter Summer Day" and "Yi Yi." Set in Taipei in the early 1990s, amidst rapid Westernization and economic development. Molly, who runs a business, is struggling both with her company's finances and her relationship with her fiancé Akin. Qiqi, Molly's friend who works at her company, is at the mercy of Molly's work habits and constantly fights with her boyfriend Ming. Centering on Molly and Qiqi, the film depicts the intertwining lives of ten men and women—classmates, lovers, and colleagues—over the course of two and a half days, showing them searching for what they truly seek amidst their inner emptiness. The film won awards for Best Screenplay, Best Supporting Actor, and Best Supporting Actress at the 1994 Golden Horse Awards and was officially selected for the 47th Cannes Film Festival. A 4K restoration premiered at the 79th Venice International Film Festival and was revived in theaters in 2023.
title:王女メディア: Directed by Pier Paolo Pasolini, the Italian polymath known as a poet, writer, and filmmaker, this film adapts the Greek tragedy 'Medea' starring Maria Callas, the iconic 20th-century soprano. Jason, the orphaned son of the King of Iolcus, demands the return of the throne from his uncle Pelias, who usurped it. Pelias sets the condition that Jason must retrieve the Golden Fleece from the barbaric land of Colchis. On his journey, Jason wins the heart of Medea, the daughter of the King of Colchis, and brings back the fleece. However, the promise of the throne is broken, and Jason flees with Medea to neighboring Corinth. There, favored by the king, Jason abandons Medea and becomes engaged to the king's daughter. Betrayed, Medea vows revenge. In March 2022, the film had a revival screening as part of the special program 'Pasolini Film Speciale 1 & 2' (at Human Trust Cinema Yurakucho, Shinjuku Musashino Hall, and others).
title:甘い罠: Screened as part of "Eiga no Kuni Masterpiece Selection II: Claude Chabrol’s Unreleased Masterpieces," a series showcasing previously unreleased works in Japan by the French New Wave master who passed away in 2010. Based on American author Charlotte Armstrong’s *The Chocolate Cobweb*, this psychological crime drama explores the conflict between good and evil lurking in the depths of the human heart, set to the strains of classical masterpieces including Liszt’s piano piece "Funérailles."
title:田名網敬一作品集: A leading figure in Japan’s underground art scene, Keiichi Tanaami has worked prolifically across a wide range of genres, including painting, collage, sculpture, animation, experimental film, and installation. This program screens eight of his works that influenced Japanese experimental cinema, produced by drawing on the methodologies and techniques he cultivated as a designer.
title:田園に死す: An autobiographical work written and directed by Shuji Terayama, adapting his own poetry collection of the same name. In a village at the foot of Mount Osore in Aomori Prefecture, a young boy, 'I', lives with his mother in an old house after losing his father. The boy's only solace is having an itako (a spirit medium) summon his father's spirit to talk to him. A beautiful woman who marries into the neighboring house and a circus troupe that comes to the village tempt the boy to run away from home. Later, 'I' grows up, moves to Tokyo, becomes middle-aged, and makes a film. Before this 'I' appears the boy he once was... Kantaro Suga, known for 'Thirteen Assassins' and others, plays the lead, and Kaoru Yachigusa plays the neighbor's wife.
title:由宇子の天秤: Starring Kumi Takiuchi of 'A Balance' and directed by Yujiro Harumoto of 'To the Ends of the Earth,' this drama confronts the problems and contradictions of the information society head-on. Yūko, a documentary filmmaker, pursues the truth behind a high school girl's suicide due to bullying that occurred three years ago. She is committed to shedding light on issues that need to be brought before the public, even if it means clashing with the production side. Meanwhile, she helps run the cram school managed by her father, Masashi, and has lived happily with him, working as a team. However, an unexpected action by Masashi forces Yūko into an ultimate choice that shakes her convictions. Takiuchi plays the protagonist Yūko, and Ken Mitsuishi plays her father Masashi, with supporting roles by Tomohiro Umeda and Yūmi Kawai. The film was screened in the Panorama section of the 71st Berlin International Film Festival in 2021.
title:男子有情: In 1886, as the Freedom and People's Rights Movement surged once again, three spirited students, including Shimada (Oka), took to the streets of Tokyo to sing "Enka"—songs of resistance against the old shogunate system—to appeal to the common people. Their headmaster, seeing great promise in their futures, urged them to enter a newspaper’s essay contest as a stepping stone to success. However, in an attempt to save Shigeyo (Hanai), the woman he loves, Shimada becomes a suspect in a murder case and is put on trial. This entertaining film skillfully captures the spirit of the Meiji era and the rhythmic 7-5 meter of Enka. Presented in a new print from Toho’s original master.
title:異国の出来事: Set in the ruins of post-war Berlin, this film depicts a romantic rivalry involving a playboy American officer. An American female politician heading to Germany is entrusted by a woman with a gift for Captain Pringle. The woman is one of the captain's girlfriends, but upon receiving it, he immediately trades it for a mattress on the black market—so he can flirt with a German woman he has a crush on. Marlene Dietrich plays a Nazi singer, and composer Frederick Hollander, who handled the music, appears as a pianist.
title:発掘されたアニメーション映画: *Dental Health* is a live-action educational film that utilizes animation to explain the importance of dental hygiene. *Chiyogami Cartoon: The Dango’s Whereabouts* features Kabuki music, a rarity for an animated film. *Thumbelina* is a silhouette animation based on the Hans Christian Andersen fairy tale. *Weather School (Supervised by the Central Meteorological Observatory)* is a short film providing an accessible explanation of meteorology for children, with animation production subcontracted to Nihon Doga (now Toei Animation). *The Dull Sword* [New Longest Version] and *Fairy Tale: The Piggyback Ghost*—both of which premiered as new prints in the screening program "Excavated Films 2018"—have undergone their first digital restoration and conversion to DCP for this occasion.
title:発掘されたサイレント映画: "The Green Horseman" is a Fuji Eiga production starring Denmei Suzuki. Although only a small portion survives (the original was 10 reels), it is a rare contemporary drama centered on horse racing. "In Search of Mother" is the second film adaptation following Hiroshi Inagaki’s 1931 version, also starring Chiezo Kataoka. While the original film is in extremely poor condition and incomplete, it is a precious surviving work. These will be screened alongside the 16mm version of "A Straightforward Boy," which premiered at the 2023 "TIFF/NFAJ Classics."
title:発掘された教育劇映画: *Glory of the Village: Promotion of Side Jobs for Rural Revitalization* is an educational drama advocating patriotic frugality. After completing his military service, a young man named Okubo returns to his village; distressed by the moral decay of the inhabitants, he makes a success of a side business and becomes a model for the community. A key highlight is the restoration of the vibrant tinting and toning applied to the original film elements. *Patriotic Tale: Kimigayo*, based on an original story and screenplay by Chiaki Tsukuda, portrays the economic struggles of a farming village against the backdrop of the Russo-Japanese War.
title:白い車に乗った女:
A suspense thriller marking the first collaboration between Jung Ryeo-won (*My Lovely Sam Soon*) and Lee Jung-eun (*Parasite*). The film depicts the course of a mysterious murder case in a snow-covered rural town through an unpredictable and original narrative.

At dawn, a writer named Do-gyeong arrives at a hospital with an unconscious woman in her car. When police officer Hyeon-ju questions the distraught Do-gyeong, she claims the woman is her sister and that they were fleeing from her sister's violent fiancé. However, it is soon revealed that the two are complete strangers, and the man alleged to be the fiancé is found dead in the snow. As the credibility of Do-gyeong's testimony is called into question, Hyeon-ju struggles to uncover the truth behind the incident, but...

Jung Ryeo-won plays the writer Do-gyeong, who holds the key to the case, winning the Korean Fantastic Actor Award at the 26th Bucheon International Fantastic Film Festival in 2022 for her performance. Lee Jung-eun plays Hyeon-ju, a police officer who must confront her own trauma while conducting the investigation. The film marks the feature directorial debut of Ko Hye-jin.
title:白パンと独裁者: In 1945, at the end of World War II, the island of Amrum in northern Germany remained in a strange, paradise-like stillness even as bombers flew overhead toward the mainland. Naning, a 12-year-old boy evacuated there, supports his pregnant mother and family by helping with farm work in place of his father, who has not returned from the front. However, when his mother Hille, who is devoted to Hitler, collapses both mentally and physically upon receiving news of his death, Naning's daily life is transformed. Hille, drained of vitality and refusing food, desires only one thing: white bread generously spread with butter and honey.
title:白夜: Jacques, an aspiring painter, saves a young woman named Marthe from throwing herself into the Seine one night. She had a lover who left for America a year ago, and that very night was when they had promised to reunite. Jacques finds her, sunk in anguish, beautiful. Driven by a fierce impulse of love, he forces himself to remain calm, hoping her heart will drift away from her lover, while feeling guilt over this. Like the 1957 version, this is a modern adaptation of Dostoevsky's famous tragic love story, a poignant work revealing Bresson's awakened worldview. Visconti's romanticism is absent here; the young man's blind love is brutally exposed as he pours out his feelings into a mini tape recorder, a habit of his, making it painful to watch.
title:白夜（1971）:
Following his 1969 film "A Gentle Woman," French master Robert Bresson directed this drama, adapting a short story by the literary giant Dostoevsky. Jacques, a lonely young painter, spends his days fantasizing about meeting his ideal woman and recording his thoughts into a tape recorder. One night, on the Pont Neuf bridge over the Seine, he encounters Marthe, a beautiful woman with a look of despair. Marthe explains that her lover left to study in America a year ago, promising to meet her in a year's time once he was in a position to marry; however, a year has passed, and he has failed to appear. Harboring passionate feelings for Marthe, Jacques does everything he can to help her reunite with her promised lover, yet the man does not show. Before long, Marthe’s heart also begins to be drawn toward Jacques.

The setting has been moved from the 19th-century Petersburg of the original story to the Paris of the time of filming. In Japan, the film was first released in theaters in 1978, followed by a 35mm new print release in 2012. A 4K restored version will receive a revival release in 2025, with another revival scheduled for 2026 as part of the "Robert Bresson Masterpieces Selection."
title:白蛇伝: The white snake spirit Bai Niang, unable to forget Xu Xian who cared for her when she was young, appears before him as a beautiful woman. The fish spirit Shao Qing acts as their go-between. The two quickly fall in love. However, this soon comes to the attention of the monk Fa Hai, who, concerned for the life of the young man bewitched by a demon, decides to use his magical powers to obstruct their love. Yet their romance seems to be progressing smoothly, as they spend dreamlike moments strolling through the garden of a beautiful mansion in full bloom. Xu Xian's close friends, the panda and Mimi, also playfully roam the mansion with Shao Qing, eventually pulling down a decorative dragon from a pillar. The dragon moves on its own, capturing the panda, Mimi, and Shao Qing, flying through the night sky and dropping them into a treasure hall. Shao Qing gives the jewels she finds there to Xu Xian and Bai Niang, but this becomes the cause of their separation.
title:白衣の男: A social satire comedy that depicts the fate of a scientist obsessed with developing a 'miracle fiber' that never gets dirty, delving into the fundamental contradictions of capitalism. One of the 'Ealing Comedies,' a series of comedy films produced at Ealing Studios in the UK from the late 1930s to the mid-1950s, directed by Alexander Mackendrick, known for 'The Ladykillers.' Sidney, a scientist working in the British textile industry, spends his days experimenting to develop a fiber that never gets dirty and never frays, no matter how much it's washed. He builds strange contraptions in a corner of the factory, remaining expressionless and unfazed by the lack of understanding around him. With the backing of the company president and his daughter Daphne, Sidney finally completes the 'miracle fiber,' but... The lead role of the scientist Sidney is played by the renowned actor Alec Guinness, known for 'Star Wars' and 'The Bridge on the River Kwai.' This film is part of the special screening series 'The Golden Age of British Ealing Comedies' (June 20–July 17, 2026, at Shinjuku K's Cinema).
title:皇帝円舞曲: A musical film sprinkled with comedic elements, including a parody of trademarked dogs and Freudian psychoanalysis of a dog. An American phonograph salesman arrives in Vienna. His rare phonograph is mistaken for a bomb, and he falls in love at first sight with an aristocrat's daughter, dragging his pet dog into a series of mishaps. Bing Crosby's expansive singing voice is a delight to hear. However, this became Billy Wilder's only musical film, as he later said he lacked the talent to make musicals.
title:看我今天怎麼說: A Hong Kong youth film vividly depicting the changes and growth of three young people with hearing impairments. Sophie, in her 20s, lost her hearing at age 3 and uses a cochlear implant to live a "normal" life as a "hearing person." Jason, born deaf, lives proudly as a sign language user. Alan, also a cochlear implant user, is bilingual in sign and spoken language. Jason and Alan met at a deaf school that banned sign language and promoted oral education; despite recognizing their different circumstances, they remained close friends into adulthood. When Alan and Sophie meet as ambassadors promoting cochlear implants, Jason becomes furious at Sophie's statement at a promotion event: "If science advances, there will be no deaf people in this world." John Shiuin, known for "Aspiring Lyricist" and "Kill the Twilight," plays Sophie and also wrote the lyrics for Panther Chan's theme song "What If." Directed by Adam Wong, highly acclaimed for "The Way We Dance" and "The Way We Keep Dancing." Won Best Leading Actress (John Shiuin) at the 61st Golden Horse Awards in 2024, and received a Special Mention at the 20th Osaka Asian Film Festival in 2025.
title:真夜中の河: An independent film written and directed by actor Yusuke Nagumo, a native of Miyakojima, Okinawa, based on his own experiences as a sewage worker. Starring former child actor Hiroki Ida (now Kunihiko Ida), the film also features appearances by numerous well-known actors close to Nagumo. Uehara (Ida), who moved from Okinawa to Tokyo to pursue his dream of acting, scrapes by working as a film extra while supporting himself with a part-time job cleaning sewers. As he crawls through an underground world that stands in stark contrast to the city's hustle and bustle, Uehara begins to find hope through his interactions with a colorful cast of coworkers.
title:真実: Kore-eda's first international co-production. On the occasion of the publication of the memoir 'The Truth' by Fabienne (Deneuve), a grande dame of French cinema, her screenwriter daughter Lumir (Binoche) returns home with her actor husband and daughter. However, mother and daughter clash fiercely over the book's embellished contents. As they hurl their long-held feelings at each other, the differences in the 'truth' they each hold come to light. The film portrays a family where the memories and emotions of mother and daughter intertwine, eventually moving toward a new bond.
title:真田風雲録: Director Takashi Kato presents an unconventional period action film depicting the story of the Sanada Ten Braves, who fought in the Winter and Summer Sieges of Osaka, with fantastical fun and excitement! Affected by the radiation of a meteorite that fell from space, the Warring States street urchin Sasuke gains mysterious abilities. Growing up, he calls himself Sarutobi Sasuke and, along with the flying squirrel Okiri, becomes a subordinate of the cool commander Sanada Yukimura, rampaging through the rigged Winter and Summer Sieges of Osaka!
title:真空地帯: After serving two years in the army prison for stealing an officer's wallet, Kitani returns to his unit. Inside the unit, the squad leader and senior soldiers bully the new recruits. In particular, Private First Class Aita, a university graduate, is subjected to daily violence. Kitani, however, refuses to take part in the bullying. Aita grows fond of Kitani and they become close, but he learns that Kitani has been selected for frontline deployment. Both Kitani's imprisonment and his selection for the front lines were the result of factional infighting.
title:眩暈 VERTIGO: January 2020, just before the coronavirus envelops New York. Poet Gozo Yoshimasu traces the traces of his ally Jonas Mekas (1922–2019), the father of avant-garde cinema, in Manhattan and Brooklyn on the first anniversary of his death, a friendship that had continued since 1985. Wartime study notes left in the studio, a 1945 passport, personal effects arranged by his son Sebastian. In a corner of the bedroom, Yoshimasu becomes dizzy and collapses. Early in the morning of January 23rd, the anniversary of his death, a memorial poem is completed in an instant. Crossing the bridge to the office. Yoshimasu reads it aloud to the waiting Sebastian. Then, a long silence falls.
title:眩暈 Vertigo: January 2020, just before the coronavirus envelops New York. Poet Gozo Yoshimasu traces the traces of his ally Jonas Mekas (1922–2019), the father of avant-garde cinema, in Manhattan and Brooklyn on the first anniversary of his death, a friendship that had continued since 1985. Then, a long silence falls.
title:矛盾に抱かれて 音楽 建築 哲学 悲哀 循環:
Embraced by Contradiction: Watching works related to music, architecture, philosophy...
Minding the Gap
FLEE
The Biggest Little Farm
The Act of Killing
Navalny
Citizenfour

Documentary of Baby Assassins

title:石井ふく子 100歳 心のドラマの軌跡:
A documentary focusing on producer and director Fukuko Ishii, the visionary behind legendary TV dramas such as *Onna to Misoshiru*, *Kimottama Kaasan*, and *Wataru Seken wa Oni Bakari*, who will celebrate her 100th birthday in September 2026. By partnering with screenwriters like Sugako Hashida and Yumie Hiraiwa, Ishii produced a string of masterpieces and established the "home drama" genre in Japan.

As the world’s oldest active producer, Ishii continues to create new works to this day. In her own words, she shares the origins of her creativity, the untold stories behind her classic hits, and her life in the present as she remains at the forefront of the industry. Through an extensive interview and rare archival footage, the film explores her creative philosophy.

Directed by Daiki Sai (*Hinomaru: 40 Years After Shuji Terayama’s Provocation*, *Ride the Ark: The Truth of Jesus’ Ark 45 Years Later*). The film will be screened as part of the "3rd TBS Retrospective Film Festival: Fukuko Ishii Special" (starting May 22, 2026, at Morc Asagaya and other venues), a festival dedicated to the digital restoration and theatrical release of precious films from the TBS archives.
title:石炭の値打ち:
A two-part social drama produced in 1977 by British master Ken Loach for the BBC’s "Play for Today" anthology series. Scripted by Barry Hines following their 1969 collaboration *Kes*, the film is set in a coal mine—a workplace that symbolized British society at the time—and meticulously portrays the lives and struggles of those who live there.

Part 1, "Meet the People" (77 min), follows a mining town ahead of an official visit by the Prince of Wales. With humor and irony, it depicts the residents scrambling to perform "staged" cleaning and repairs, and workers being mobilized solely for the sake of appearances. Through the authorities demanding superficial decorum and the workers at their mercy, the film exposes the structural absurdity and inherent violence of a class-based society.

Part 2, "Back to Reality" (91 min), takes a sharp turn toward a hard-hitting, serious tone, poignantly depicting a tragic accident born from the disregard for workers' rights and a negligent management system. It offers a raw look at the reality of miners working on the brink of death and the families forced to face the aftermath of tragedy.

Long difficult to view in Japan due to the lack of home video or streaming releases, the film will receive its Japanese theatrical premiere in November 2025.
title:砂丘: Italian master Michelangelo Antonioni, who won top prizes at all three major film festivals (Berlin, Venice, Cannes) in the 1960s, made this film after moving to America in 1970. Set in Los Angeles and Death Valley, it depicts the psychological landscape of love between a man and a woman. In the late 1960s, amidst the peak of counterculture, with university protests raging and students clashing with armed police, Mark grows tired of futile debates at student gatherings. He grabs a gun and confronts the police officers cracking down on campus, but misses his chance to fire and flees. He then steals a Cessna at an airfield and takes to the sky. Meanwhile, Daria, a secretary at a Los Angeles real estate company, is driving across the vast desert to attend a meeting. The two meet by chance and arrive at Zabriskie Point, overlooking Death Valley... The leads are newcomers Mark Frechette and Daria Halprin, whom Antonioni scouted on the streets. The soundtrack effectively features music by Pink Floyd, Jerry Garcia of the Grateful Dead, Kaleidoscope, John Fahey, The Rolling Stones, and The Youngbloods. Released in Japan in 1970, it also had a late-show release in 1996. A revival release is scheduled for 2026, the first in 30 years.
title:破·地獄: A human drama reuniting Hong Kong comedy king Michael Hui, popular in Japan for the 'Mr. Boo!' series, and Dayo Wong, a top Hong Kong comedian and actor ('A Witness Out of the Blue'), after 32 years. It became a massive hit, breaking Hong Kong's all-time box office record. Set in Hong Kong's funeral industry, it carefully explores universal themes of family, tradition, and views on life and death. Wedding planner To-sang, burdened with debt from the pandemic, reluctantly switches to the funeral business but faces difficulties as weddings and funerals are vastly different. To-sang, focused on profit, constantly clashes with the strict Taoist priest Master Man, who values tradition. However, as To-sang interacts with Master Man and his daughter Man-yuet, his resentment gradually fades. He begins to understand the true meaning of the traditional Taoist ritual 'Breaking Hell' that Master Man performs at funerals. Dayo Wong plays funeral director To-sang, and Michael Hui plays Taoist Master Man. Director Anselm Chan, a screenwriter making his third feature, helmed the film. It won five awards at the 43rd Hong Kong Film Awards in 2025, including Best Actress (Michelle Wai). At the 37th Tokyo International Film Festival's World Focus section, a 126-minute version was screened under the title 'The Last Dance'. The theatrical release is a 140-minute director's cut.
title:祇園の姉妹: A commentary: A masterpiece that gazes with a penetrating eye at two contrasting geisha sisters living in Kyoto's Gion pleasure district. The older sister, old-fashioned and easily swayed by emotion, and the younger sister, modern and pragmatic... You can't take your eyes off the 19-year-old Yamada, who plays the younger sister rebelling against her submissive elder sibling and trying to toy with men, exuding a remarkable presence.
title:祝山: A film adaptation of the novel "Iwaiyama" by Nanami Kamon, an author known for works on folklore and the occult, based on her own experiences, starring Ai Hashimoto. Directed and written by Shingo Takeda, a filmmaker who has won awards at film festivals for his horror works, marking his feature-length theatrical debut. Horror novelist Minami Kano, suffering from writer's block, receives a letter from her middle school classmate Asako Yaguchi. The letter describes unexplainable phenomena that have been occurring ever since she went on a dare to visit a ruin known as a haunted spot. Seeking material for her new work, Minami reunites with Asako and their old friends, and becomes entangled in mysterious events. As the investigation progresses, it emerges that behind the series of strange occurrences lies the forbidden mountain "Iwaiyama" they once set foot on. Ai Hashimoto plays the protagonist Minami Kano, marking her first horror film role in ten years since "Zan: The Haunted Room." The cast also includes Ren Ishikawa, Sayu Kubota, Takuya Kusakawa, Yuya Matsuura, and Go Riju.
title:祝（ほうり）の島: Iwaishima, located in Kaminoseki, Yamaguchi Prefecture, is a beautiful island in the Seto Inland Sea with a population of approximately 500. In 1982, a plan emerged to build a nuclear power plant just four kilometers across from the island, sparking an opposition movement that the residents have maintained for 28 years. This documentary explores the fundamental nature of humanity and society through the daily lives of the islanders. Produced by Seiichi Motohashi, director of *Alexei and the Spring*, the film marks the theatrical debut of director Aya Hanabusa.
title:神と恩送り、:
Starring former AKB48 and HKT48 member Chiyori Nakanishi alongside Saeri Umehara, known for her work in stage plays such as *Assault Lily* and *Towatsugai*, this hopeful drama is set in Tokyo’s Adachi Ward and the town of Kyonan in Chiba Prefecture. It depicts the way people forge connections even amidst misunderstandings and heartache.

Saori, a 26-year-old temporary worker in Tokyo, feels increasingly suffocated by the pressures of her job and personal relationships. One day, while preparing a surprise gift for a loved one’s birthday, she is confronted by their betrayal. On the verge of an emotional breakdown, she stops by an izakaya and meets Miumi, a young woman working there part-time. This chance encounter begins to spark a gradual change in Saori’s life. Having been estranged from her family for years, Saori must confront deep-seated tensions; spurred by her mother’s illness, she begins to face her past and herself with Miumi by her side.

The film was created by actor and director Hayato Otoki, in collaboration with actor and choreographer Keiko Matsumoto and musician Yosuke Saigo. Conceived as a sequel to their short drama *Around 30 Woman, God, and a Roommate*, the work blends dance, drama, and music to weave a story that speaks to the pain and hope inherent in modern life.
title:神探大戦: A suspense action film starring Lau Ching-wan of 'Burning Down' fame, which was a huge hit in China. It depicts a former detective once called the 'God of Detectives' taking on a series of murders that shocks Hong Kong. A sequel to the 2007 film 'Mad Detective' co-directed by Johnnie To and Wai Ka-fai, this installment is directed solely by Wai Ka-fai. It won awards for Best Director, Best Actor, Best Screenplay, and Best Cinematography at the 41st Hong Kong Film Awards in 2023. It was also screened in the Gala Selection section at the 35th Tokyo International Film Festival in 2022. Screened at the 'Unseen Zone Films 2024' event held at Human Trust Cinema Shibuya and Cine Libre Umeda.
title:神探大戰: A suspense action film starring Lau Ching-wan of 'Burning Down' fame, which was a huge hit in China. It depicts a former detective once called the 'God of Detectives' taking on a series of murders that shocks Hong Kong. A sequel to the 2007 film 'Mad Detective' co-directed by Johnnie To and Wai Ka-fai, this installment is directed solely by Wai Ka-fai. It won awards for Best Director, Best Actor, Best Screenplay, and Best Cinematography at the 41st Hong Kong Film Awards in 2023. It was also screened in the Gala Selection section at the 35th Tokyo International Film Festival in 2022. Screened at the 'Unseen Zone Films 2024' event held at Human Trust Cinema Shibuya and Cine Libre Umeda.
title:神龍小虎闖江湖: In the late Qing dynasty, the villainous Im Kun-ho rules over Gold Sand Village, a place rife with all kinds of crime and violence, including drugs and human trafficking. The Dragon group, traveling while punishing evil, and at the same time, the legendary female martial artist Eagle, arrive in this village. They are both searching for a treasure called the 'Silver Pearl', said to have been stolen from a Tibetan temple. Then, the ruthless killer karate practitioner Black Jaguar also appears, and fierce battles unfold among the powerful fighters over the Silver Pearl. This is the Japan comeback film for Yasuaki Kurata, who was active primarily in Hong Kong.
title:私たちの一日: The 30th feature film by Korean master Hong Sang-soo, who continues to release works in his unique style, distanced from large-scale commercial cinema. It depicts a day in the lives of a resting actor and an elderly poet living in seclusion, whose paths almost cross but never quite do. Sang-won, an actor on hiatus staying at a friend's house, and Hong Ui-ju, an elderly poet living alone in a small apartment, receive visits from young guests burdened with anxiety about the future, who ask various questions: What is necessary for acting? How does one become an actor or poet? Why did you start writing poetry? The topics the young people raise gradually develop into important conversations about life. Meanwhile, a friend's cat suddenly goes missing... Through two alternating locations and times, and the comedic dialogue that unfolds, the film discovers dramatic moments hidden in everyday life. Kim Min-hee, an indispensable presence in Hong Sang-soo's works, plays the actor Sang-won, and Ki Joo-bong, who won the Best Actor award at the Locarno International Film Festival for "Hotel by the River," plays the poet Hong Ui-ju. The film will be released in theaters in 2026 as the fourth installment of "Monthly Hong Sang-soo," a project screening new works for five consecutive months to commemorate the director's 30th debut anniversary.
title:私たちの話し方: A Hong Kong youth film vividly depicting the changes and growth of three young people with hearing impairments. Sophie, in her 20s, lost her hearing at age 3 and uses a cochlear implant to live a "normal" life as a "hearing person." Jason, born deaf, lives proudly as a sign language user. Alan, also a cochlear implant user, is bilingual in sign and spoken language. Jason and Alan met at a deaf school that banned sign language and promoted oral education; despite recognizing their different circumstances, they remained close friends into adulthood. When Alan and Sophie meet as ambassadors promoting cochlear implants, Jason becomes furious at Sophie's statement at a promotion event: "If science advances, there will be no deaf people in this world." John Shiuin, known for "Aspiring Lyricist" and "Kill the Twilight," plays Sophie and also wrote the lyrics for Panther Chan's theme song "What If." Directed by Adam Wong, highly acclaimed for "The Way We Dance" and "The Way We Keep Dancing." Won Best Leading Actress (John Shiuin) at the 61st Golden Horse Awards in 2024, and received a Special Mention at the 20th Osaka Asian Film Festival in 2025.
title:私のすべて:
A French drama that delicately portrays the emotional and physical liberation of a woman who has devoted her life to her son. Mona, a single mother living in the suburbs of Paris, has raised her son Joel, who has developmental delays, alone since she was young. Now in his early 30s, Joel works at a vocational workshop for people with disabilities. Mona and Joel have spent their lives supporting and caring for one another, but their world is upended when Océane, a coworker at Joel’s facility, becomes pregnant with his child. Having known nothing of their relationship, Mona is shaken, and the bond between mother and son begins to waver.

Laure Calamy (*Only the Animals*) stars as Mona, while the roles of Joel and Océane are played by Charles Peccia-Gallet and Julie Froger, both of whom are actors with disabilities. The production employed the French film industry’s only accessibility coordinator to support the actors with disabilities on set. Directed by Anne-Sophie Bailly (co-writer of *Dog on Trial*) in her feature debut, the film won the Authors Under 40 Award for Best Director in the Orizzonti section at the 81st Venice International Film Festival in 2024.
title:私の男:
Director Kazuyoshi Kumakiri (*Sketches of Kaitan City*, *The End of Summer*) adapts the 138th Naoki Prize-winning novel by author Kazuki Sakuraba. Set against the majestic natural backdrop of Hokkaido, the film depicts an orphaned girl and the distant relative who takes her in as they live in close proximity, each harboring a profound inner emptiness. Starring Tadanobu Asano and Fumi Nikaido, the film features a stellar supporting cast including Kengo Kora and Tatsuya Fuji.

Hana, orphaned at the age of ten, is taken in by a distant relative named Jungo. Bound by their shared loneliness, the two live a quiet life in the rural town of Mombetsu, Hokkaido. However, their peace is shattered when news breaks of a murder committed on the drift ice. Upon hearing the report, the two flee the town as if pursued...
title:私の血に流れる血: A Gothic fantasy film by Italian master Marco Bellocchio, released in 2015 and winner of the FIPRESCI Prize at the 72nd Venice International Film Festival. The story intertwines the 17th century and the modern era, depicted with eerily beautiful imagery. In 17th-century Bobbio, northern Italy, young soldier Federico visits an old monastery to uncover the truth behind the death of his twin brother Fabrizio, a priest. It is said that Fabrizio was seduced by a nun named Benedetta, betrayed his faith, and lost his life. Seeking to restore his brother's honor, Federico tries to make Benedetta confess her guilt, but gradually becomes captivated by her, even as she is accused of witchcraft. The story then shifts to the modern day, centuries later. The former monastery lies in ruins, and a sale to a wealthy Russian is being negotiated. A man appears, but the ruins are haunted by a mysterious old count who only shows himself at night. Benedetta is played by Lidia Lieberman, Federico (living in both past and present) by Pier Giorgio Bellocchio, and the mysterious old count by Roberto Herlitzka. A cover of Metallica's "Nothing Else Matters" is used prominently in the film.
title:私は死にたくない:
Directed in 1958 by Robert Wise, the master behind *West Side Story* and *The Sound of Music*, this black-and-white social drama is based on the true story of Barbara Graham, a woman who maintained her innocence until the very end despite being sentenced to death for robbery and murder.

Barbara had left her life of prostitution behind after getting married. However, years later, struggling with poverty and her husband’s drug addiction while raising a child, she is forced back into the life to survive. When a robbery-homicide occurs, she is arrested as a suspected accomplice for being seen with the men involved. Interrogated under the presumption of guilt, Barbara desperately pleads her innocence, but her cries fall on deaf ears...

Susan Hayward (*Rawhide*, *I’ll Cry Tomorrow*) stars in a powerhouse performance that earned her the 31st Academy Award for Best Actress, among many other accolades. The film co-stars Theodore Bikel (*The Enemy Below*) and Simon Oakland (*Psycho*). It is featured in the special screening series "Shinjuku Hardcore Masterpieces" (July 18 – September 4, 2025, at Cinemart Shinjuku), a retrospective showcasing the masterpieces and unconventional works of America’s legendary directors.
title:私は貝になりたい: A small-town barber who has returned from the war unexpectedly finds himself put on trial as a war criminal. This film version, directed by screenwriter Hashimoto himself, is based on a television drama that won an Art Festival Award. A legendary work that portrays the absurdity and cruelty of war, with Frankie's heartfelt performance that shakes the soul.
title:秒速5センチメートル: A live-action film adaptation of Makoto Shinkai's 2007 theatrical anime "5 Centimeters Per Second," directed by Shinkai of "Your Name." and "Suzume," starring Hokuto Matsumura of SixTONES. Spring 1991. Takaki Tono and Akari Shinohara, who meet at an elementary school in Tokyo, connect through their shared loneliness, but Akari moves away upon graduation. In the winter of their first year of middle school, they reunite on a snowy night in Iwafune, Tochigi, and promise beneath a cherry tree standing in the snow to meet again at the same place on March 26, 2009. Time passes to 2008. Takaki, now working as a systems engineer in Tokyo and approaching 30, realizes a part of himself remains left behind in a distant time. Akari, too, lives her quiet daily life with those memories. Mitsuki Takahata plays Akari Shinohara, the heroine who connects with Takaki; Nana Mori plays Kanae Sumita, a high school classmate who has feelings for Takaki; Yuzu Aoki plays Takaki in high school; and Asa Kimura plays Risa Mizuno, Takaki's coworker. Also starring Aoi Miyazaki and Hidetaka Yoshioka. Directed by visual artist and photographer Yoshiyuki Okuyama, who gained attention with "At the Bench," with a screenplay by Fumiko Suzuki of "Love At Least."
title:秘密の森の、その向こう: Directed and written by Céline Sciamma of "Portrait of a Lady on Fire," this film weaves a story of loss and healing connecting three generations: daughter, mother, and grandmother. Eight-year-old Nelly, grieving her beloved grandmother, is taken by her parents to clean out the forest house where her grandmother lived. But her mother, who spent her own childhood there, is overwhelmed by memories at every turn and eventually leaves. Left behind, Nelly wanders the woods and meets another eight-year-old girl who calls herself Marion—the same name as Nelly's mother. The girl invites Nelly to her home, which turns out to be "grandma's house." Sisters Joséphine and Gabrielle Sanz, making their film debut, play Nelly and Marion. Nina Meurisse ("A Woman's Life") and Margot Abascal ("Sagan") co-star. The film was presented in the competition section of the 71st Berlin International Film Festival in 2021.
title:空中庭園: 'Conceal nothing, create no taboos, and share everything as much as possible.' That is the rule of the Kyobashi family, decided by Eriko as a reaction against her mother Satoko, who never did anything motherly—Eriko is determined to maintain a smiling, happy household. But contrary to Eriko's wishes, each family member harbors secrets. Her husband Takashi shuttles between two lovers, Asako and Mina; her daughter Mana refuses to go to school; and her son Ko, a shut-in with an interest in architecture, unknowingly hires Mina—his father's lover—as his tutor. One day, Eriko throws a joint birthday party for Satoko and Mina. However, thanks to a drunken Mina, the family's secrets are exposed one after another, and the home Eriko built crumbles. Yet on her own birthday, a birthday call from Satoko dissolves her resentment, and Eriko is able to be reborn, warmly welcoming her family home with gifts in hand.
title:空気人形: Based on a short manga by Yoshiie Gouda, this allegorical work uses the love story of a sentient love doll to lead viewers into philosophical contemplation about the emptiness and life of modern people. With cinematographer Mark Lee Ping-bing and art director Yohei Taneda on board, the fictional setting is brilliantly visualized using analog special effects.
title:空飛ぶゆうれい船／海底3万マイル: One night, Hayato rescues the chairman of Kuroshio Products Group and his wife from a car accident. Little does he know he will soon be drawn into an unexpected conspiracy... A social sci-fi work containing sharp criticism of capitalism, with the in-story commercial for the soft drink 'Boa Juice,' which holds the key to the plot, leaving a strong impression.
title:窓辺にて: A love story directed by Rikiya Imaizumi (known for "Ai ga Nanda") starring Goro Inagaki, based on an original screenplay. Freelance writer Shigeki Ichikawa realizes that his wife, editor Sae, is having an affair with the popular young writer she handles, but he can't bring himself to confront her. At the same time, Shigeki is troubled by a certain feeling that sprouted within him when he learned of the affair. One day, at a literary award ceremony, Ichikawa meets high school writer Rea Kubo and is drawn to the content of her award-winning novel "La France." He asks if there is a real-life model for the story and if he can meet them. Sae, Ichikawa's wife, is played by Yuri Nakamura; high school writer Kubo by Tina Tamashiro; Shigeki's friend Masatsugu Arisaka by Ryuya Wakaba; Arisaka's wife Yukino by Mirai Shida; and Sae's lover Madoka Arakawa by Shion Sasaki.
title:立てば転ぶ: Set in a supermarket after closing, this film depicts complex human relationships through a continuous stream of idle chatter. Actor Jun Hosoi planned, directed, and starred in the project, with Nanami Hidaka also serving as planner and co-star. They are joined by a talented supporting cast including An Ogawa, Ryohei Higashino, and Seiichi Kohinata. The film won the Audience Award in the Japanese Short Film Competition at the SKIP City International D-Cinema Festival 2024. Following a double Acting Award win (Jun Hosoi and Nanami Hidaka) and a positive reception at MOOSIC LAB 2025, the film has now been set for a one-week solo theatrical release.
title:竜宮の誘い: A crime suspense film depicting a man consumed by a desire for cannibalism as he descends into the abyss of ruin. It won the Grand Prize at the 19th Tanabe-Benkei Film Festival, a first for a suspense film in the festival's history. Satō, a young man working as a host at a cabaret club, harbors a secret desire to eat people. One day, he finds a smartphone at work, which leads to him being threatened by a mysterious duo and forced into a dark side job as a courier. After making a large sum of money from the illegal but lucrative work, Satō begins to use his earnings to satisfy his hidden desires. Shun Tohari stars in his film debut as Satō. The film will be screened theatrically as part of the 'Tanabe-Benkei Film Festival Selection 2026.'
title:笑え: A 43-minute mid-length film directed in 2009 by Masahiro Ota, director of "S." The film depicts a single night spent by actors on the eve of the final performance of a stage play about the Great Hanshin-Awaji Earthquake, with the cast performing entirely through improvisation. Summer 2008, Kobe. On the night before the closing performance of "Stage: The Great Hanshin-Awaji Earthquake," a conflict arises between the troupe leader, a survivor of the disaster, and Ota and other actors who did not experience it. The cast features Kenichi Takito, who rose to prominence in "Climber's High," among others. Originally released theatrically in Osaka in 2009, the film will receive its first Tokyo theatrical release in April 2026 to coincide with the release of Ota’s "S" (International Version).
title:笑えない世界でも:
I hope no one empathizes with this film.

When I found myself completely alone, I watched a certain TV drama (*Seija no Koushin*, written by Shinji Nojima) and wept, realizing that it was okay for me to be alive. From that moment, Atsushi Okamoto aspired to become a film director, driven by a desire to create and deliver works that could offer even the slightest solace to those who find life difficult to endure. This is his first original feature film, delicately tracing the inner lives of two young girls.

Ayaka, making her starring debut as a "loner" girl working without hope in a small factory, won the Best Actress Award at the 10th Kashikojima Film Festival for her performance. Playing the other protagonist—another isolated soul on the brink of despair—is Misaki Tanifuji, who graduated from an idol group in 2023 and appeared as the Hakata gal "Tamatchi" in the 2024 NHK morning drama *Omusubi*.
title:第6回ジーンシアタースタジアム: GeneHeart Co., Ltd. operates "GeneTheater," a Japanese subscription service specializing in short films, and the mini-theater and independent film information site "Japanese Cinema Online," in addition to its theatrical distribution business. Launched in October 2025, "GeneTheater Stadium" screens three independent short films as a single program for a limited one-week run. Under the banner "Movies aren't just for watching. It's time to nurture them!", the project implements a new form of film screening centered on three keywords: "Audience Participation," "Discovering Your Favorites," and "Short Films."
title:第五の騎士は恐怖: Set in Nazi-occupied Czechoslovakia, this drama portrays the terror of an informant society during wartime. Dr. Braun, a Jew living in Nazi-occupied Czechoslovakia, is forbidden from practicing medicine. The elderly man seems to have already accepted the fate of the Jews. Then one day, a neighbor asks him to treat a wounded political fugitive, and he reluctantly provides care. Eventually confronting his inner self, Dr. Braun decides to continue illegal treatment for the resistance to reclaim his identity. He wanders the streets of Prague in search of the morphine needed for this, but... Through the various people Dr. Braun meets and the wartime cityscape, the film depicts a society decaying and collapsing under war with hallucinatory visual beauty. In Japan, it will have its theatrical premiere in April 2026 as part of "Czech Film Masterpieces," a series featuring classics of the Czech New Wave.
title:第十七捕虜収容所: Based on a hit Broadway play set in a Nazi-guarded American POW camp. With everyone's cooperation, two prisoners attempting to escape are shot dead. Suspicions arise among the group that there is a traitor, and the lone wolf Sefton is immediately eyed with distrust. Sefton tries to clear his name by searching for the German spy... Lead actor William Holden joined the ranks of Oscar-winning actors with this film and went on to achieve remarkable success. However, he tragically died in an accident in 1981.
title:箱の中の羊: A feature film directed by Hirokazu Kore-eda ("Monster", "Shoplifters"), starring Haruka Ayase and Daigo (from the comedy duo "Chidori"), based on an original script about a couple who welcome a humanoid in the form of their deceased son. Set in the near future. Architect Kōmoto Oto and her husband Kensuke, the second-generation president of a construction company, take in a humanoid resembling their son Sho, who died two years ago. On the day the humanoid arrives, Oto joyfully welcomes him with Sho's same smile and voice, while Kensuke hides his bewilderment behind a stiff expression. Family time gradually begins, but an unexpected event occurs, revealing the couple's hidden feelings about their son's death. Meanwhile, the humanoid Sho secretly starts connecting with other humanoids. The role of the deceased son Sho and his humanoid counterpart is played by Kuwaki Rito, chosen from over 200 auditionees. Kiyono Yasho plays Oto's younger sister Kotaki Arisu; Kanichiro plays Nikawa Gen, an employee at Kensuke's construction company Tamaken; Yo Kimiko plays Oto's mother Nishimura Nobuyo; and Tanaka Min plays Yamagata Akio, a skilled worker at Tamaken. The title "The Sheep in the Box" is derived from a passage in Antoine de Saint-Exupéry's classic novel "The Little Prince". The film was selected for the Competition section of the 79th Cannes Film Festival in 2026.
title:約束の土地Ziemia obiecana / The Promise: A masterpiece by the legendary Andrzej Wajda, this epic portrays the shifting of eras and generations through a portrait of ambitious youth. Based on the novel by Władysław Reymont, Wajda depicts the rise and fall of three young men in a film that was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film and is considered one of the greatest landmarks in Polish cinema history. In the 19th-century industrial city of Łódź, Karol, Moryc, and Maks come from different backgrounds but share a common dream: to establish their own textile factory and seize control from the older generation. After a turbulent journey, they finally achieve success—only to find that the time has come to pay the price for their dreams...
title:結局珈琲: A humorous yet slightly poignant conversation piece chronicling the two months leading up to the closure and relocation of a real small coffee shop called "Kohaze Coffee" in Tokyo's Shimokitazawa. Responding to the shop manager Ryuji Tanigawa's wish to preserve on film the old shop he ran for 18 years before moving to a new location in May 2025, actor-director Jun Hosoi wrote the script and directed the film. Long beloved in Shimokitazawa, "Kohaze Coffee" is preparing to move, but manager Tanigawa, veteran part-timer Shimada, and new part-timer Sudo keep things running at their own leisurely pace. Regular customer Aoki makes it a routine to spend his work breaks there alone. Other regulars and staff—Takeda, Tsukamoto, Ito—develop slightly strange and varied relationships, which in turn cause some things in Aoki to change while others remain the same. Starring Sakura Fujiwara as Aoki, Tokio Emoto as the manager, Jun Hosoi, Tatsuya Yamawaki, and Ryohei Higashi as regulars, Nanami Hidaka and Riko Seto as part-timers, with special appearances by Yūki Isomura and Yoshinori Okada. Koichi Sogawa, closely associated with Shimokitazawa, wrote the new theme song "Ending."
title:絞首台からの生還: On November 22, 1975, the South Korean government arrested Zainichi Koreans studying in the country on "suspicion of spying." 160 people were detained, and nine were sentenced to "death." Half a century has passed since then.
title:給阿マ的情書 おばあちゃんへのラブレター【日本語字幕無し】: Ye, living a quiet old age in the southern Chinese town of Chaozhou, receives an unexpected visit. One day, her grandson Xiaowei, burdened with debt, secretly heads to Thailand without telling his grandmother. His goal is to find his grandfather, known as a 'legendary billionaire' who hasn't returned to his homeland in over 50 years, and borrow money from him. However, upon finally arriving, he learns that his grandfather has already passed away. Furthermore, the person with whom his grandmother had been exchanging love letters for decades turns out to be someone completely different. As Xiaowei pursues the truth, the family secrets sealed away for half a century gradually come to light.
title:絶倫!! 好色一代［『ニッポンの猥褻』改題版］＊: Known by its theatrical title, *Obscenity in Japan*, this film was produced to commemorate the 30th anniversary of Shintoho Eiga. Tetsu Hashimoto (Kubo), a self-proclaimed sexologist entering his later years, reflects on his life through the lens of his vivid sexual experiences. Shinji Kubo, hailed as the "Emperor of Porno" for his commanding presence in *pink* cinema, captivated audiences with a surging energy epitomized by his role as Ozaki in the *Widow's Boarding House* series (1974–1984).
title:緋牡丹博徒 花札勝負: The third film in the "Red Peony Gambler" series. In the mid-Meiji period, Oryu (Sumiko Fujiwara), traveling to learn the ways of the world, joins the Nishinomiya family, Nagoya's top gambling clan, ahead of the Atsuta Shrine Festival's charity gambling. However, she gets caught in a merciless conflict between the gambler Hanooka (Ken Takakura), who owes a debt to the Kimbara family aiming for the position of gambling boss, and both sides.
title:緑の光線: The fifth film in Éric Rohmer's "Comedies and Proverbs" series. Through lively dialogue and beautiful imagery, it depicts the journey of a lonely woman seeking love and happiness on vacation, winning the Golden Lion at the Venice International Film Festival. Delphine, who works as a secretary, is looking forward to a vacation in Greece, but her female friend who was supposed to go with her cancels at the last minute. She goes to the South of France with other friends but can't fit in and returns to Paris alone. Later, visiting the beach at Biarritz alone, Delphine hears about the "green ray" from a Jules Verne novel—a flash of light visible only for an instant just before sunset. Starring Marie Rivière of "The Aviator's Wife" and "Autumn Tale."
title:緑の山: A documentary by Swiss master director Fredi M. Murer, known for "Mountain Fire," investigating a planned radioactive waste disposal facility in the Alps. It follows both opponents and supporters among the residents trying to protect their roots and land. Murer dedicated this film "to the children and the children's children," posing questions to adults who should bear responsibility for the next generation. Along with "We Mountain People" and "Mountain Fire," it is considered part of the "Mountain Trilogy."
title:總輯版 天兵童子: Based on the children's novel by Eiji Yoshikawa, this grand and magnificent adventure spectacle depicts Tenpei Doji (So), a boy who boasts of having descended from the heavens, as he survives a turbulent era through the training imposed by Bodaiji (Hara) and battles against rampant villains. Although this version has had "lines glorifying feudalistic emperor-centrism" removed post-war, remnants of the wartime imperial view of history are still discernible. Director Shozo Kumita made his directorial debut under the name Kyoji Kumita with *Hungry Bushido* (1932). Following works such as the *Maboroshi-jo* (1940) trilogy, a serial action film starring Kensaku Hara, he went on to work on TV period dramas after the war.

Based on the children's novel by Eiji Yoshikawa, this grand and magnificent adventure spectacle depicts the life of Tenpei Doji (So), a boy who boasts of having descended from the heavens, as he survives a turbulent era through training imposed by Bodaiji (Hara) and battles against rampant villains. Although this version has had its "lines glorifying feudalistic Emperor-centrism" removed post-war, traces of the wartime Imperial View of History remain visible. Director Shozo Kumita made his directorial debut under the name Kyoji Kumita with *Hungry Bushido* (1932). Following works such as the three-part serial action film *Maboroshi-jo* (1940) starring Kensaku Hara, he went on to work on television period dramas after the war.
title:罗目的黄昏:
Winner of the Best Film Award in the Competition Section of the 30th Busan International Film Festival.

The traces of a lost lover, and a path that recedes the more you search—another time flowing through Luomu, an ancient town in Sichuan Province.

A postcard arrives from Wang, a lover who vanished without a trace three years ago, bearing only the words "Twilight in Luomu." Bai, who worked as a dancer in a theater troupe, follows this single clue to an inn in the ancient town of Luomu, Sichuan. There she meets Liu, the inn's proprietress; Huang, who has harbored feelings for Liu for twenty years; and a stream of passing travelers. In this town, once prosperous from trade and now flowing with quiet time, what she encounters is not Wang himself, but the traces of the time he left behind. The faint sound of a distant whistle echoes, and before Bai, who wanders the ancient town, Wang appears and disappears like a phantom. One day, Bai learns that a man resembling Wang was reportedly seen at a mountain temple—

Released simultaneously with its sister film "Chunshu," shot with the same cast prior to this work.
title:罠 ドナウ川の守り人: Screened at EU Film Days 2026 (Tokyo: May 16–29, 2026 at Theater Image Forum, May 19–24 at National Film Archive; Nagoya: June 6–19 at Nagoya Cinema Neue; also held in Hiroshima, Kyoto, and Fukuoka).
title:罪の棘: A human drama depicting the conflicts and redemption of people burdened by past sins. It portrays the intersecting fates of individuals living in harsh realities as they confront their own transgressions. Directed by Hisashi Ueda, known for 'The Last Theatrical Version of Tokumei Kakarichō Tadano Hitoshi.' Erika, a former female inmate who lost her father at a young age and grew up without love, struggles to form relationships, trapped in a cycle of dependency and loneliness. She tends to cacti, believing their thorns are a survival mechanism for the dry, harsh desert, reflecting her view that human society is equally dry and brutal. Her parole officer is Iwanaga, a man who served time for a robbery 25 years ago and carries regret for someone he once failed to protect. He tries to support Erika. Meanwhile, Detective Tōdō, who lost his father in that same incident 25 years ago, suspects a link between the old case and a new series of robberies, relentlessly pursuing Iwanaga. Their three fates become intricately intertwined. Model Yabin stars in her film debut as Erika, with Tomohiro Waki as Iwanaga and Katsuya as Tōdō. Mami Yamazaki and Koichi Miura round out the supporting cast.
title:罪人たち: A survival thriller directed by Ryan Coogler ('Black Panther,' 'Creed'), starring Michael B. Jordan, with whom Coogler has frequently collaborated on feature films. In the 1930s, in a devout small town in the American South, twin brothers Smoke and Stack open a dance hall in their former hometown, serving illegal alcohol and music in pursuit of a fortune. On opening night, the crowd revels in a night of swirling desires, but the arrival of uninvited guests changes everything. The dance hall is consumed by senseless despair, and a night of chaos beyond human comprehension begins. Jordan plays the dual role of the twin brothers. The cast includes Hailee Steinfeld ('Bumblebee'), Jack O'Connell ('Ferrari'), and Delroy Lindo ('Da 5 Bloods'). Coogler also wrote and produced the film, reuniting the 'Black Panther' team including production designer Hannah Beachler, composer Ludwig Göransson, and costume designer Ruth E. Carter. At the 98th Academy Awards, it received a record-tying 16 nominations, including Best Picture and Best Director, winning four awards: Best Actor (Michael B. Jordan), Best Original Screenplay, Best Cinematography, and Best Original Score.
title:美しき仕事: A film by French master Claire Denis, based on Herman Melville's novel "Billy Budd" (known for "Moby-Dick"), depicting the daily lives of the French Foreign Legion and the commander leading them against the backdrop of the blue, dazzling African coast. Galoup is writing his memoirs at his home in Marseille, France. A former senior sergeant in the Foreign Legion, he was stationed in Djibouti, Africa. While spending time in the hot, dry land, Galoup gradually becomes envious of the many qualities of his superior officer, Forestier. One day, a new recruit named Sentain arrives at the unit. Galoup feels jealousy and envy towards Sentain, who quickly becomes popular due to his sociable personality, and eventually wishes to destroy him. Starring Denis Lavant, known as a regular in Leos Carax's works such as "Bad Blood" and "The Lovers on the Pont Neuf." Long unreleased in Japan, it received its first theatrical release in 2024 in a 4K restored version.
title:美しく、黙りなさい: The only feature-length directorial work by actress Delphine Seyrig, known for films like 'Last Year at Marienbad' and 'Jeanne Dielman, 23 quai du Commerce, 1080 Bruxelles', released in 1976. This documentary interviews 23 actresses active in Hollywood and Paris. Seyrig herself serves as the interviewer, asking two questions: 'If you were a man, would you still have chosen this profession?' and 'Have you ever played a friendly scene with another actress?' The film features a range of women—from famous film actresses like Jane Fonda ('Julia'), Shirley MacLaine ('The Apartment'), Juliet Berto ('Céline and Julie Go Boating'), Anne Wiazemsky ('La Chinoise'), and Maria Schneider ('Last Tango in Paris'), to TV actresses and unknowns—speaking frankly, intimately, and sometimes humorously about gender questions that were risky to answer in the male-dominated film industry of the time. The original title 'Sois belle et tais-toi!' (Be beautiful and shut up) is said to have been a phrase used against women in French film and theater, and is now a cliché symbolizing gender discrimination in English-speaking countries. In Japan, it will have its first theatrical release in July 2026 to commemorate the 50th anniversary of its production.
title:老人Z: In the near future, to cope with an aging society, the Ministry of Health and Welfare develops a sixth-generation computer with self-replicating functions, the elderly care machine 'Unit Z001.' However, this computer absorbs the elderly selected as samples and goes on a rampage, causing a huge uproar involving volunteer female college students and the media.
title:聖の青春: Murayama Takashi, who suffered from a serious illness since early childhood, discovers shogi during repeated hospitalizations and, at age 15, becomes a disciple of Mori Nobuo. Ten years later, Takashi moves to Tokyo to fulfill his dream of becoming a Meijin champion. Supported by those around him, he devotes himself fully to shogi, and after reaching the rank of 7-dan, he develops a fierce rivalry with Habu Yoshiharu, who won the Meijin title in the same generation. Takashi immerses himself even deeper in shogi, but cancer gradually consumes his body...
title:聖闘士星矢 真紅の少年伝説: The third theatrical film. The immensely powerful sun god Abel is resurrected, and his sister Athena abandons the protagonists who have fought alongside her to leave with Abel. The scene where the usually energetic protagonist sheds tears emphasizes the boy's purity and fragility. The revival of the five "Gold Saints" who died in the TV anime is also a highlight. As part of the 20th anniversary of "Weekly Shōnen Jump," this was released as a 75-minute extended version, double-billed with "Sakigake!! Otokojuku."
title:聖闘士星矢 神々の熱き戦い: Warriors clad in constellational armor, the 'Saints,' fight for the goddess Athena. With beautifully exaggerated bodies designed by Shingo Araki and Michi Himeno, special moves accompanied by lavish screen effects like transmitted light, fast-paced action, emotional direction, and an orchestral score, it became a representative action anime of the 1980s. The first theatrical film was directed by TV series director Toshio Morishita and depicts the resurrection of the evil god Eris.
title:聖闘士星矢／聖闘士星矢 神々の熱き戦い: Warriors clad in constellational armor, the 'Saints,' fight for the goddess Athena. With beautifully exaggerated bodies designed by Shingo Araki and Michi Himeno, special moves accompanied by lavish screen effects like transmitted light, fast-paced action, emotional direction, and an orchestral score, it became a representative action anime of the 1980s. The first theatrical film was directed by TV series director Toshio Morishita and depicts the resurrection of the evil god Eris.
title:聴く隣人のいるところ: A documentary recording one year at a boarding high school. Christian Aishin High School, with a total student body of 34, is situated halfway up Mt. Asari Fuji in Gotsu City, Shimane Prefecture. In this secluded location, students live away from their parents, sharing their daily lives with their peers. While smartphones and the internet are absent from school life, they are surrounded by
title:肉屋（1970）: Directed by Claude Chabrol, a leading figure of the French New Wave known for numerous suspense and mystery masterpieces, this crime drama is set in a peaceful rural village. It quietly and sharply delves into the darkness of the human psyche through a series of murders committed by a lonely butcher and the female teacher who is loved by him. Hélène, a primary school teacher in a small village in southwestern France, meets Paul, a war veteran burdened with loneliness, and they gradually grow close. Meanwhile, a series of murders of women shakes the village's calm daily life. One day, during a picnic with her students, Hélène discovers a brutally murdered body; beside it lies a lighter identical to one she had given Paul. Stéphane Audran, who was married to Chabrol at the time, stars as Hélène, the same character name as in 'Les Biches'. Jean Yanne plays the butcher Paul. Although never theatrically released in Japan, the film will have its Japanese theatrical premiere as part of the 'Claude Chabrol Masterpiece Selection' (starting February 13, 2026, at Cinema Rise and Morc Asagaya, among others), featuring three of Chabrol's suspense films from the late 1960s to 1970.
title:脛擦りの森:
An original work from the creative duo behind the *Thus Spoke Kishibe Rohan* series, director Kazutaka Watanabe and star Issey Takahashi. Inspired by the "Sunekosuri" (shin-rubber) folklore of Okayama Prefecture, this film is set deep within a forest to tell a mysterious, beautiful, and cruel tale of love.

Deep in a forest far from civilization, a young man with an injured leg is led by a woman’s sweet singing voice to an ancient shrine. Living there are a mysterious man and his young, beautiful wife, Sayuri. Nursed back to health, the young man spends a dreamlike time where it feels as though time itself has stopped. These peaceful, repeating days seem as if they might last forever, but...

Director Watanabe personally visited the forests of Okayama, drawing inspiration from local legends to pen this original screenplay. Filming took place in the cities of Takahashi and Niimi in Okayama Prefecture. Issey Takahashi stars as the mysterious man, while rising star Nijiko Aoto, in her second film role, plays Sayuri, the mysterious woman living deep in the woods. Koudai Kurosaki, who garnered attention for his lead role in *The Miharashi Generation* (selected for the 78th Cannes Film Festival Directors' Fortnight), portrays the injured young man who wanders into the forest.
title:臆病者:
A drama by Indian master Satyajit Ray, based on a short story by writer Premendra Mitra, depicting the clash of new values in an Indian society standing at the crossroads of tradition and modernization. Amit, a screenwriter living in Kolkata, experiences a car breakdown while on a research trip in the countryside and ends up staying at the home of Bimal, a tea plantation owner he meets by chance. There, he is reunited with Karuna—the woman he once loved but left due to his own cowardice, and who is now Bimal’s wife. While Amit attempts to make amends for the past, Karuna remains composed, her true feelings unreadable. Before his departure, Amit tells Karuna to come to the station if she still loves him, but...

The film stars Ray regular Soumitra Chatterjee as Amit, with Madhabi Mukherjee, who also appeared alongside Chatterjee in Ray’s previous work *Charulata*, playing the role of Karuna. In its native India, the film was released as a double feature with Ray’s *The Holy Man*. In Japan, it will make its theatrical debut in July 2025 as part of the "Satyajit Ray Retrospective 2025," a special screening program commemorating the 70th anniversary of the director's debut.
title:臨時増発 ミルキー☆サブウェイ 各駅停車劇場行き: A version of the theatrical film "Galaxy Express Milky☆Subway: Local Train to the Theater" with new scenes added. "Galaxy Express Milky☆Subway: Local Train to the Theater" is the theatrical adaptation of the short anime "Galaxy Express Milky☆Subway," which gained popularity for its surreal and lively developments featuring unique characters aboard a runaway galaxy express. It was released in theaters in February 2026, re-editing all 12 episodes broadcast and streamed from July 2025 with new scenes added. In "Special Extra Edition: Milky☆Subway Local Train to the Theater," a new post-credits scene is added after the ending. In addition to the standard 2D version, a 4D version was also produced.
title:自然は君に何を語るのか: Korean master Hong Sang-soo, a multiple award-winner at the Berlin and Cannes film festivals, humorously and realistically depicts the irreparable failures caused by alcohol in this home drama centered on a young poet who ends up spending a day with his girlfriend's family. When poet Dong-ha escorts his girlfriend Juni home, he runs into her father at the front door and unexpectedly spends the day with her family. Initially awkward, Dong-ha gradually grows closer to Juni's family as they show him around their home and neighborhood and engage in conversation. Eventually, at dinner with the family, he drinks as urged, becomes intoxicated, and an uncomfortable atmosphere settles over the table. Ha Seong-guk, who previously played poets in Hong Sang-soo's "The Woman Who Ran" and "In Front of Your Face," takes on the role of Dong-ha, marking his first lead role in a Hong Sang-soo film. The parents welcoming their daughter's boyfriend are played by Hong Sang-soo regulars and real-life couple Kwon Hae-hyo and Cho Yun-hee. Kang So-yi ("In Front of Your Face," "By the Stream") plays Juni, and Park Mi-so ("Introduction") plays Juni's older sister. The film was selected for the competition section of the 75th Berlin International Film Festival in 2025. It will be released in theaters in 2026 as the fifth installment of "Monthly Hong Sang-soo," a project screening new works for five consecutive months to commemorate the director's 30th debut anniversary.
title:花よりもなほ: In the 15th year of the Genroku era. A young samurai (Okada) burdened by the duty to avenge his father travels from Shinshu to Edo and hides out in a tenement slum. The film depicts how his resolve begins to waver as he interacts with the residents of the tenement. While weaving the story of the Ako Ronin's raid into the background, director Kore-eda turns it on its head, aiming for 'a story where the weak are affirmed as they are.' This ambitious work marks Kore-eda's first deep dive into a narrative world, having previously been conscious of the distance between fiction and nonfiction in his live-action films.
title:花様年華: A romantic drama directed by Wong Kar-wai of 'Days of Being Wild' and 'Happy Together,' starring Tony Leung and Maggie Cheung, depicting the adulterous love between a married man and woman. Hong Kong, 1962. Chow, a newspaper editor, and Chan, a secretary at a trading company, move into the same apartment building on the same day and become neighbors. They soon discover their respective spouses are having an affair and begin spending time together. Hesitant yet strongly drawn to each other, Chow and Chan... Some settings and the worldview are carried over from 'Days of Being Wild,' and the story connects to the 2004 film '2046.' It won the Best Actor award and the Technical Grand Prize at the 53rd Cannes Film Festival. Released in Japanese theaters in 2001. In February 2018, it had a special screening at Bunkamura Le Cinéma alongside the digital remastered release of Wong Kar-wai's 'Days of Being Wild.' In August 2022, the 4K restored version was screened as part of 'WKW4K: Wong Kar-wai 4K.' In May 2026, a revival release titled 'In the Mood for Love 25th Anniversary Special Edition' is scheduled, screened simultaneously with the short film 'In the Mood for Love 2021.'
title:花様年華 25周年特別版:
Wong Kar-wai’s masterpiece *In the Mood for Love* (2000) earned Tony Leung the Best Actor award at the 53rd Cannes Film Festival and became a massive hit upon its Japanese theatrical release in 2001. This year, as the film celebrates its 25th anniversary on March 31st, *In the Mood for Love* will be screened alongside the legendary short film *In the Mood for Love 2001*—previously shown only at a masterclass during the 2001 Cannes Film Festival—as the "In the Mood for Love 25th Anniversary Special Edition."

*In the Mood for Love* was originally conceived under the title "THREE STORIES ABOUT FOOD," intended as a trilogy depicting three different eras. Within this concept, *In the Mood for Love 2001* was positioned as the "dessert." While the two stars, Tony Leung and Maggie Cheung, eventually saw *In the Mood for Love* evolve into a standalone feature film, *In the Mood for Love 2001* remained dormant, much like canned or frozen food.

Now, they "re-encounter each other across time, revealing a connection through this first meeting." The newly unveiled poster visual features Maggie Cheung from both films, contrasting her vermilion coat with a modern blue striped set-up. As the tagline "Drawn to each other, again and again" suggests, *In the Mood for Love* continues to captivate not only the original generation of fans but also younger audiences with every theatrical run. By encountering *In the Mood for Love 2001*, featuring the same cast, viewers can once again savor the story of two people drawn together by fate.

The accompanying trailer begins with the iconic image of Maggie Cheung turning toward the camera. It unfolds to the sound of Nat King Cole’s "Quizás, Quizás, Quizás," and just when it seems to end, a brief glimpse of *In the Mood for Love 2001* appears.

**【Film Overviews】**

**In the Mood for Love 4K**
A classical depiction of the emotional turmoil between a man and a woman, both married to others. 
Hong Kong, 1962. Chow, an editor for a local newspaper, and Chan, a secretary at a trading company, move into the same apartment building on the same day and become neighbors. Eventually, they realize their respective spouses are having an affair...
2000 / Hong Kong / Original Title: 花樣年華 / 98 min / 1.66:1 / Cantonese / 5.1ch / Japanese Subtitles: Sohei Okada

**In the Mood for Love 2001**
A postmodern tale capturing the moment love blossoms between a man and a woman. 
A convenience store owner finds himself drawn to a regular customer who often comes to buy cake to satisfy her hunger. A series of strange coincidences follow...
2001 / Hong Kong / Original Title: 花様年華2001 / 9 min / 1.66:1 / Cantonese / 5.1ch / Japanese Subtitles: Sohei Okada

Cast: Tony Leung, Maggie Cheung
Director, Writer, Producer: Wong Kar-wai
Cinematography: Christopher Doyle, Mark Lee Ping-bing
