Elle Fanning ("Maleficent") plays Julie, and Greta Gerwig ("Frances Ha") plays Abbie.
title_norm:2部／3部)濱⼝⻯介監督特集上映突然、偶然、必然: Akari, Sakurako, Fumi, and Jun, now in their late 30s, believed they were close friends who could share anything—until they discovered Jun's secret. Born from a citizen-participation improvisational acting workshop in Kobe, this three-part film features mostly first-time actors and was created through unprecedented methods. It won the Best Actress award at the 68th Locarno Film Festival.
title_norm:404 still remain: Set in early 2000s South Korea, when Japanese pop culture was restricted, this coming-of-age drama tenderly follows a shy transfer student and a popular class president who bond over J-Pop. In 2001, Gyung-hwan transfers to a high school in Daegu, Korea's most conservative city. A huge fan of then-taboo Japanese music and anime, he secretly listens to Japanese songs on his MP3 player during lunch. Teased as an 'otaku' by classmates, he discovers that his deskmate, class president Jae-min, also secretly loves Japanese culture. Sharing earphones on the bus after school while listening to J-Pop, they gradually grow closer. One day, Gyung-hwan confesses a secret to Jae-min, but afterward, Jae-min's attitude suddenly changes. Making his feature debut, director Eom Ha-nul wrote the script based on his own teenage experiences as a fan of Japanese culture, weaving in diverse Japanese pop culture from the 1990s. Shim Hyun-seo, a child actor known for 'The King of Pigs', plays transfer student Gyung-hwan, and Hyun Woo-seok, from 'The School Nurse Files', plays class president Jae-min. Gong Min-jung ('Kim Ji-young: Born 1982') and Lee Dong-hwi ('The Roundup: Punishment') co-star.
title_norm:47系統: Screening at EU Film Days 2026 (Tokyo: May 16–29, 2026 at Theater Image Forum, May 19–24 at the National Film Archive; Nagoya: June 6–19 at Nagoya Kinema Noi; also to be held in Hiroshima, Kyoto, and Fukuoka).
title_norm:5 centimeters per second: A live-action film adaptation of Makoto Shinkai's 2007 theatrical anime "5 Centimeters Per Second," directed by Shinkai of "Your Name." and "Suzume," starring Hokuto Matsumura of SixTONES. Spring 1991. Takaki Tono and Akari Shinohara, who meet at an elementary school in Tokyo, connect through their shared loneliness, but Akari moves away upon graduation. In the winter of their first year of middle school, they reunite on a snowy night in Iwafune, Tochigi, and promise beneath a cherry tree standing in the snow to meet again at the same place on March 26, 2009. Time passes to 2008. Takaki, now working as a systems engineer in Tokyo and approaching 30, realizes a part of himself remains left behind in a distant time. Akari, too, lives her quiet daily life with those memories. Mitsuki Takahata plays Akari Shinohara, the heroine who connects with Takaki; Nana Mori plays Kanae Sumita, a high school classmate who has feelings for Takaki; Yuzu Aoki plays Takaki in high school; and Asa Kimura plays Risa Mizuno, Takaki's coworker. Also starring Aoi Miyazaki and Hidetaka Yoshioka. Directed by visual artist and photographer Yoshiyuki Okuyama, who gained attention with "At the Bench," with a screenplay by Fumiko Suzuki of "Love At Least."
title_norm:501号室の男 ある作家の記録: A Korean suspense thriller about floor noise and a cult religion, depicting the fate of a female writer who strives to uncover the truth behind the noise coming from the upstairs neighbor. Eun-su, an aspiring writer living in apartment 401, has been applying to numerous writing contests but faces a string of rejections. Meanwhile, for about a month, she has been tormented by unbearable noise coming from unit 501 above. Deciding to use this situation as material for her work, Eun-su, along with her friend Ji-seong, begins observing Ho-gyeong, a middle-aged man living in 501. Even after he notices her excessive stalking, she relentlessly pursues him for the sake of her writing. Eventually, Eun-su arrives at a shocking truth hidden behind the noise, but at the same time, she finds herself backed into a dangerous situation. Director Kim Jeong-uk, who has crafted many stories candidly depicting the human psyche, portrays with intense suspense the psychological anxiety born from trivial troubles lurking in daily life. Ryu Hwa-young, known as a former member of the K-pop group T-ARA, stars in her first lead film role, passionately playing Eun-su, a writer whose obsession with writing blurs the line between reality and delusion. Veteran actor Park Jin-woo, known for the Netflix drama "Squid Game," plays the mysterious upstairs resident Ho-gyeong.
title_norm:5時から7時までのクレオ: Cleo (Corinne Marchand) is a beautiful blonde woman. Lately, however, Cleo is troubled. She feels unwell. The thought that it might be cancer makes her restless. Recently, she underwent a thorough examination at the hospital. The results are due this evening. Cleo is terrified of that moment. Five o'clock. Cleo sits down before a female fortune teller. The fortune teller sees through her illness.
title_norm:8½: The undisputed representative work of director F. Fellini. Film director Guido dreams one day of his body falling through the air. To heal the various mental and physical fatigue associated with his daily life, he goes to a spa for rest and recuperation, but even there he cannot escape from work and life. And finally, he begins to hallucinate that he is among the elderly spending their remaining years at the spa... This film is an autobiographical work by Fellini himself, and its depiction is superb, portraying reality and fantasy in parallel! A must-see!!
title_norm:90 meters: Yū, a high school senior, is on the verge of giving up his dreams to support his mother, who suffers from a serious illness. Torn by his inability to confess his hope of pursuing higher education... A heart-wrenching human drama about the bonds between parent and child and the journey toward independence.
title_norm:90メートル: Yū, a high school senior, is on the verge of giving up his dreams to support his mother, who suffers from a serious illness. Torn by his inability to confess his hope of pursuing higher education... A heart-wrenching human drama about the bonds between parent and child and the journey toward independence.
title_norm:9月のアル・ラシード通り: On September 9, 2025, the Israeli military called on all residents of Gaza City to evacuate via Al-Rashid Street to Al-Mawasi in the south, through social media and leaflets dropped from the air.
title_norm:aa!! hana no ouendan: The first film adaptation in 20 years of the hit 1976 series "Aa!! Hana no Ōendan." At the Minami Kawachi University cheerleading squad, an annual alumni gathering is planned, but they discover a hole in their precious team flag. The members hurriedly take part-time jobs to earn repair money, but the workplace is run by yakuza who refuse to pay and threaten them. However, Sekidō Aota appears and beats the yakuza to a pulp. Ken'ichi Nagira reprises his role as senior Yakutsuji from the previous series, and Junko Miyashita also appears.
title_norm:aalto: Alvar Aalto (1898-1976), Finland's representative architect and designer. He created outstanding designs and numerous masterpieces of architecture, including the timeless classic "Stool 60," the iconic "Aalto Vase," and the "Maison Louis Carré" with its exquisite harmony with nature. What drove Alvar Aalto's life as a designer was a single woman—
title_norm:about us but not about us: A Filipino film that unfolds as a witty, single-setting dialogue piece between a lonely literature professor and a young man aspiring to be a writer, revolving around the secrets of a deceased lover. Directed and written by Jun Robles Lana of 'Die Beautiful' fame, it weaves themes of losing a loved one, LGBTQ+ issues, sexual abuse, and the precariousness of the social media generation, exposing the ailments and love-hate dynamics of modern Philippines. In pandemic-era Manila, Eric, a literature professor grieving the recent death of his lover Marcos, a renowned novelist, agrees to meet his student Lance at a long-established restaurant. Despite his sense of loss, Eric looks forward to time with Lance, who admires him. The two grow closer over talk of apple pie and Daft Punk, but the atmosphere shifts when a story about Marcos comes up. Gazing into Lance's eyes, Eric uncovers a startling truth about Marcos. Elijah Canlas, known from the Japanese-hit drama 'Gameboys,' plays the handsome young Lance, while veteran Filipino actor Romnick Sarmenta portrays Professor Eric.
title_norm:abunai deka forever the movie: Yokohama Port Police detectives Takayama and Oshita, a duo, once arrest Jojima, a member of the internationally wanted terrorist group 'NET,' but Jojima escapes from the police hospital, and the detectives pursue him. One day, an incident occurs where Jojima and his comrades attack a transport vehicle carrying firearms seized by the police, attempting to steal the weapons. Ignoring orders to stay off the case, Takayama and Oshita return to the scene, thwarting Jojima's gang's scheme, but the group's leader Date is advancing an even larger plan.
title_norm:ace in the hole: Billy Wilder parted ways with his long-time screenwriting partner Charles Brackett and brought in a new writer for this film. Jack, kicked out of a New York newspaper, witnesses a man buried alive in a cave. Desperate to return to a top-tier paper, he manipulates information using the scoop. A journalist who stops at nothing for his own ambition is ultimately judged by public opinion, making for a compelling watch. There is also an anecdote that the studio changed the title from 'Ace in the Hole' to 'The Big Carnival' due to poor public reception.
title_norm:adams sake: The second feature from Belgian director Laura Wandel, who gained attention with her 2021 debut 'Playground', is a human suspense drama depicting one night's events surrounding a 4-year-old boy hospitalized in a pediatric ward and his mother, told from the perspective of a nurse trying to support them. Four-year-old Adam is admitted to a pediatric center with a broken left arm. Malnourished and underdeveloped, his bones are brittle. The court rules that Rebecca, an immigrant single mother, has not been providing Adam with proper nutrition and issues an order restricting her visits. Nurse manager Lucie, herself a single mother, tries to support Rebecca, who fears losing custody and being separated from her son. But Rebecca's reckless actions and pressure from superiors and colleagues push Lucie into a corner. Léa Drucker ('Close') plays nurse Lucie, torn between her desire to save the mother and child and the judicial system the hospital must follow. Anamaria Vartolomei ('Happening') plays isolated single mother Rebecca. The film is produced by Belgian masters Jean-Pierre and Luc Dardenne. It opened the Critics' Week at the 2025 Cannes Film Festival.
title_norm:affeksjonsverdi: Swedish director Joachim Trier, who gained international attention with "The Worst Person in the World," crafts a family drama centered on the tangled bonds of love and hate inherent in the parent-child relationship. Nora, an actress thriving in Oslo, and her sister Agnes, who chose family life and lives quietly with her husband and son. One day, their father Gustav, a film director who abandoned the family when they were young and has been out of contact for years, reappears and offers Nora the lead role in his first autobiographical film in 15 years. Filled with anger and disappointment toward her father, Nora firmly refuses, and soon the popular young American actress Rachel is cast instead. When Nora learns that the film will be shot at the family's old home, a place filled with memories, uncontrollable emotions surge within her once again. Renate Reinsve, who also starred in "The Worst Person in the World," plays the protagonist Nora, with acclaimed actor Stellan Skarsgård as her father Gustav. Inga Ibsdotter Lilleaas plays sister Agnes, and Elle Fanning plays the popular American actress Rachel. The film won the Grand Prix at the 78th Cannes Film Festival in 2025. At the 98th Academy Awards, it received nine nominations across eight categories, including Best Picture, and won the award for Best International Feature Film.
title_norm:after life: A fantasy drama by Hirokazu Kore-eda of "Maborosi" fame, depicting the seven days between death and reaching heaven. Twenty-two deceased people arrive at a facility shrouded in mist. The staff waiting for them instruct them to choose the single most important memory from their lives within the seven days before they go to heaven. Some choose a memory immediately, while others struggle to decide. But the final day, when a screening will be held, steadily approaches. Starring ARATA in his film debut.
title_norm:after the storm: Director Hirokazu Kore-eda of "Our Little Sister" and "Like Father, Like Son" teams up with Atsushi Abe for the third time, following "Still Walking" and "I Wish," in this human drama centered on a man who can't grow up and his aging mother, portraying a family living a present different from the future they once dreamed of. Ryota is a middle-aged man who won a literary prize 15 years ago but hasn't been successful since, still chasing his dream of becoming a writer. He currently works at a detective agency to make ends meet, but makes excuses to himself and others that it's "research for his novel." Still hung up on his ex-wife, Kyoko, he is shocked to discover she has a new boyfriend while "staking out" her apartment. One day, Ryota, Kyoko, and their 11-year-old son Shingo gather at the apartment of his mother, Toshiko, who lives alone in a housing complex. Stranded by a typhoon, they end up spending the night together. Kirin Kiki delivers a wonderful performance as the protagonist's mother, with a stellar supporting cast including Yoko Maki, Satomi Kobayashi, and Lily Franky.
title_norm:afternoon breezes: Mitsu's birthday. Natsuko buys matching Virgo necklaces and a rose. However, a white handkerchief is hanging in the apartment window. It's the signal that Mitsu's lover, Hideo, is there. Natsuko, who has secretly fallen in love with Mitsu, approaches Hideo in order to have Mitsu all to herself... On a midsummer afternoon, a shocking ending that will shake the world.
title_norm:aftersun: A human drama that recounts a summer vacation spent with a father, 20 years later from the perspective of the daughter who has now reached the same age her father was then, as she discovers a new side of her father she never knew at the time. During the summer when she was 11, adolescent Sophie visits a rustic Turkish resort with her 31-year-old father Calum, from whom she lives apart. Under the blazing sun, they point a video camera Calum obtained at each other, spending intimate time together. 20 years later, Sophie, now the same age as Calum was then, looks back at the nostalgic footage shot at that time, reviving memories of her beloved father. Paul Mescal, who broke out with the TV drama "Normal People," plays the loving yet sensitive father Calum, earning a nomination for the 95th Academy Award for Best Actor. The role of Sophie is played by newcomer Frankie Corio, selected through auditions. The director and screenwriter is Scottish newcomer Charlotte Wells, making her feature-length debut with this film.
