title_norm:agatha and the limitless read: French writer Marguerite Duras, known for 'The Lover,' adapts her own book 'The Malady of Death / Agatha' into a film. Set in a dilapidated seaside hotel, this experimental work depicts the forbidden love between a brother and sister through lyrical imagery and Duras's own narration. Agatha, reuniting with her brother after eight months at the winter seaside villa Villa Agatha, decides to leave the next morning and part from him forever. The two reminisce about their forbidden love. The brother is played by Yann Andréa, Duras's lover who was 38 years her junior. In Japan, the film had its first theatrical release in 2003, 23 years after its 1981 release. It was re-released in 2012.
title_norm:agatha et les lectures illimi: French writer Marguerite Duras, known for 'The Lover,' adapts her own book 'The Malady of Death / Agatha' into a film. Set in a dilapidated seaside hotel, this experimental work depicts the forbidden love between a brother and sister through lyrical imagery and Duras's own narration. Agatha, reuniting with her brother after eight months at the winter seaside villa Villa Agatha, decides to leave the next morning and part from him forever. The two reminisce about their forbidden love. The brother is played by Yann Andréa, Duras's lover who was 38 years her junior. In Japan, the film had its first theatrical release in 2003, 23 years after its 1981 release. It was re-released in 2012.
title_norm:ah special attack corps: A war film depicting the fleeting youth of kamikaze pilots who perished in vain at the end of the Pacific War. This is the directorial debut of Yoshio Inoue, based on a script by Kimiyuki Hasegawa (known for "The Squirrel and the American: Gunshot in the Ruins"). Yoshio Inoue was born in Tokyo in 1926, graduated from Urawa High School's humanities track, joined Daiei in February 1938, and studied under Seiji Hisamatsu, Kon Ichikawa, and Yasuzo Masumura. Cinematography by Toru Watanabe (known for "The White Path Across the River").
title_norm:aikatsu stars! the movie: The theatrical film of the TV anime 'Aikatsu Stars!', which began airing in April 2016 as a new series following the popular idol anime 'Aikatsu!'. It depicts the struggles of girls, including the protagonist Yume Nijino, who enrolls at Yotsusei Gakuen aiming to become the top idol. In this first theatrical film of 'Aikatsu Stars!', the story is set on a southern island where the characters come for an event. It revolves around the rumored 'Legendary Dress' said to be sleeping on the island, and depicts the friendship between Yume and Laura Sakuraba, as well as the school's top four-idol unit 'S4' taking the stage together. The short film 'Aikatsu! The Targeted Magical Aikatsu! Card' is shown simultaneously.
title_norm:air doll: Based on a short manga by Yoshiie Gouda, this allegorical work uses the love story of a sentient love doll to lead viewers into philosophical contemplation about the emptiness and life of modern people. With cinematographer Mark Lee Ping-bing and art director Yohei Taneda on board, the fictional setting is brilliantly visualized using analog special effects.
title_norm:akko chans got a secret! – th: Elementary school student Kagami Atsuko can transform into any appearance she desires using a magical mirror. This is the first theatrical film in the second series of "Himitsu no Akko-chan," which captures the transformation wishes of young girls. The story depicts the interaction between "Taishō," who opposes the construction of a building on the children's playground, and his father, who works in construction. Akko transforms into a baton twirler who leads the protest. Kanemori Yoshinori's four-heads-tall characters move energetically across the screen.
title_norm:al rashid street in september: On September 9, 2025, the Israeli military called on all residents of Gaza City to evacuate via Al-Rashid Street to Al-Mawasi in the south, through social media and leaflets dropped from the air.
title_norm:alakazam the great!: A rousing entertainment masterpiece based on Osamu Tezuka's "My Son Goku," bringing together the energy of young artists during the first golden age of Toei Animation. It is noteworthy that Osamu Tezuka himself took the lead in drawing the storyboards, and the on-site staff included a large number of talented individuals who would later carry the future of Japan's animation industry. In other words, it is one of the origins of Japanese animated films, a monumental work that greatly envisioned the future of the medium from an entertainment perspective. Winner of the Special Grand Prize at the Venice International Children's Film Festival.
title_norm:ali baba and the forty thieve: Alibaba XXXIII, descendant of the original Alibaba and now king, indulges in pleasure and uses the lamp's genie to oppress his people. The descendant of a thief, Al-Hack, teams up with one mouse and 38 cats, riding a flying carpet into the castle. Akira Daikuhara's challenge is evident in the round, deformed characters. Hack is voiced by Nobuyo Oyama, and the shadow-puppet flashback scenes were handled by the theater troupe Kakashiza. This was the last film credited to Toei president Hiroshi Okawa, who passed away suddenly that year.
title_norm:all about lily chou chou: In a provincial city, middle school student Yuichi becomes close with the honor student Hoshino, but a summer trip changes the dynamics among their friends. When the new semester begins, Hoshino defeats the class's worst delinquent in a fight and gradually turns into a tyrant himself. As his actions escalate—assault, shoplifting, and forcing classmates into prostitution—Yuichi, who has become a target of bullying, is also made complicit. Turning his eyes away from reality, Yuichi creates a fan site for his idolized artist, Lily Chou-Chou.
title_norm:all around us: "Unforgettable masterpieces" return to the screen! Since his directorial debut with "A Touch of Fever" (1993), Ryosuke Hashiguchi—known as a "master of few works" eagerly awaited by film fans both in Japan and abroad—has delivered acclaimed films including "Like Grains of Sand" (1995), which won the Grand Prix at the 25th Rotterdam International Film Festival; "Three Stories of Love" (2015), which swept various film awards including the Kinema Junpo Best Ten Japanese Films No. 1; and his latest work "Motherhood" (2024), released nine years after "Three Stories of Love." "Hush!" depicts a gay couple and a woman—three people who had given up on connecting with others—forming a "new kind of family." "All Around Us" portrays the hope that arises between people through ten years in the life of a married couple. Both films are often cited as "all-time best films" and are known as "unforgettable masterpieces." Now, these two works will be revived in 4K remastered versions! "All Around Us" returns 18 years after its June 2008 release, while "Hush!" returns 25 years after its production in 2001 (released April 2002)—a full quarter-century later. "All Around Us" follows a wife who falls into depression due to her overly serious nature and her husband, a courtroom sketch artist who supports her, tracing their inseparable bond over ten years against the backdrop of various shocking events from the 1990s. The film was screened in the Panorama section of the 2009 Berlin International Film Festival.
title_norm:all of a sudden: Director Ryusuke Hamaguchi ("Drive My Car," "Evil Does Not Exist") portrays the spiritual encounter of two women with the same-sounding name in Paris. Based on the exchange of 20 letters between philosopher Makiko Miyano, who survived cancer metastasis, and anthropologist Maho Isono, titled "Suddenly Feeling Ill," the film depicts the connection between two women who meet by chance and their confrontation with the world. Marie-Lou Fontaine, director of the care facility "Garden of Freedom" on the outskirts of Paris, struggles with staff shortages and misunderstanding while striving for humane care. She meets Japanese stage director Mari Morisaki, who is battling cancer, and draws courage from her theater work. Guided by the coincidence of their similar-sounding names, Marie-Lou and Mari begin a friendship. But one day, Mari suddenly falls ill. As her illness progresses, their bond deepens, and their souls connect. Virginie Efira ("Benedetta") plays Marie-Lou, and Tao Okamoto, a global fashion model who has appeared in Hollywood films like "The Wolverine," plays Mari. Kyozo Nagatsuka ("Enemy") plays Goro Seimiya, an actor in Mari's play, and Koyo Kuroki ("The Generation of the Looking-Ahead") plays Tomoki Kubodera, Goro's grandson. Screened in the Competition section of the 79th Cannes Film Festival in 2026, Virginie Efira and Tao Okamoto jointly won the Best Actress award. Okamoto became the first Japanese person to win the Cannes Best Actress award.
title_norm:all of tokyo!: A youth ensemble drama featuring all fourth-generation members of the popular idol group Hinatazaka46. Directed by the renowned Kumakiri Kazuyoshi, known for 'My Man' and '#Manhole,' it follows eleven unique high school girls on a school trip to Tokyo as they race through the big city to enjoy everything it has to offer. High school student Ikezono, visiting Tokyo on a school trip, meticulously plans a perfect itinerary to tour famous spots, intending to lead her group. However, on the long-awaited free day, the group inexplicably splits up, and Ikezono finds herself alone at the base of Tokyo Skytree. Determined to complete her plan, she sets out to explore Tokyo, but unbeknownst to her, her group members each have their own agendas for being in Tokyo. Shogenji Yoko, who served as center for Hinatazaka46's single 'Kimi wa Honeydew,' stars as the protagonist Ikezono, with all eleven fourth-generation members appearing. The screenplay is by Fukuda Shohei of the 'HiGH&LOW THE MOVIE' series and Tsuchiya Ryoichi of the film 'Osomatsu-san.' From the planning stage, they directly interviewed all eleven members, gathering memories from their school days, pre-idol stories, and feelings about Tokyo, crafting an original script woven from their real-life stories.
title_norm:all shall be well: A drama depicting a long-term lesbian couple facing various problems after one partner's sudden death. Director Ray Yeung, who previously explored the issues of elderly gay couples in "Suk Suk," turns his gaze to the current state of Hong Kong, where prejudice against homosexuality remains deeply rooted, while also highlighting social issues such as severe housing shortages, employment difficulties, and economic disparity. Pat and Angie, a lesbian couple in their 60s, are enjoying a stable and peaceful life both publicly and privately. However, Pat suddenly dies. Angie was close with Pat's relatives, but they clash over the funeral arrangements. Furthermore, under Hong Kong law, Pat's brother, as her relative, inherits her estate. This is an unacceptable reality for Angie, who considered the apartment, filled with memories of Pat, to be their final home. Meanwhile, Pat's financially struggling brother, his wife, and their children also grapple with their own circumstances. The film won the Teddy Award for outstanding LGBTQ cinema at the 74th Berlin International Film Festival in 2024 and received high praise, including five nominations at the 43rd Hong Kong Film Awards, including Best Film. Patra Au, who won the Hong Kong Film Award for Best Supporting Actress for "Suk Suk," plays Angie, earning a Best Actress nomination for this film. Maggie Li, returning to the screen after about 30 years, plays Pat.
title_norm:along the sea: This is the second feature film by director Akiro Fujimoto, whose first feature 'Where I Belong'—a Japan-Myanmar co-production—won the Grand Prize in the 'Asian Future' section of the 30th Tokyo International Film Festival and received high acclaim both in Japan and abroad. Following his previous film, which dramatized the true story of a Myanmar family torn between Japan and Myanmar, this work again tackles the realities of Asian residents in Japan, depicting the plight of young women who come to Japan as technical intern trainees. Three Vietnamese women, who fled their workplaces after being mistreated, become undocumented. Relying on brokers to find new jobs, they end up in a snowy northern port town... Fujimoto met a female technical intern trainee online who later disappeared after grueling daily labor; he interviewed women in similar situations and wrote an original script.
title_norm:alpine fire: A 1985 film by the master Fredi M. Murer, known as a pioneer of New Swiss Cinema, which won the Golden Leopard, the top prize at the Locarno International Film Festival. A family of four lives a nearly self-sufficient life surrounded by the majestic Alps. The teenage younger brother, who is deaf-mute, grows up healthily, sometimes frustrated by his disability but loved by his parents and older sister. One day, angered by a broken lawnmower, he throws it away, incurring his father's wrath. Running away from home, he begins living alone in a mountain hut. His worried sister brings him food, and they spend happy times together around a campfire on the mountain peak. Eventually, the sister's pregnancy is discovered... The film was first released in Japanese theaters in 1986. A digitally remastered version was revived in February 2020.
title_norm:amrum: In 1945, at the end of World War II, the island of Amrum in northern Germany remained in a strange, paradise-like stillness even as bombers flew overhead toward the mainland. Naning, a 12-year-old boy evacuated there, supports his pregnant mother and family by helping with farm work in place of his father, who has not returned from the front. However, when his mother Hille, who is devoted to Hitler, collapses both mentally and physically upon receiving news of his death, Naning's daily life is transformed. Hille, drained of vitality and refusing food, desires only one thing: white bread generously spread with butter and honey.
title_norm:amélie et la métaphysique des: An animated film set in 1960s Kobe, depicting the growth of Amélie, a Belgian girl born in Japan. Based on the autobiographical novel "Tube Metaphysics" by Belgian writer Amélie Nothomb, it portrays a world rich in emotion, seen through the eyes of the two-year-old protagonist Amélie, woven with life, color, and her witty words. In 1960s Kobe, Amélie, a Belgian girl born into a diplomat's family, is unresponsive until age two and a half, but then enters an invincible childhood, believing herself to be a god and living in a magical world. Her days with her beloved housekeeper Nishio and her family are adventures full of new discoveries. One day, she learns the kanji for "rain," which suits her perfectly. Then, on her third birthday, an event occurs that changes everything. Directed by Myriam Ballard and Liang-Cho Han, who worked on "Long Way North," with music by Japanese composer Mari Fukuhara. It won the Audience Award at the 2025 Annecy International Animated Film Festival and was nominated for Best Animated Feature at the 98th Academy Awards.
title_norm:an actors revenge: This adaptation of the same-named period novel by Otaguro Mikami was scripted by Daisuke Ito and Teinosuke Kinugasa, with a screenplay by Natsuto Wada, and directed by Kon Ichikawa. Kazuo Hasegawa, who starred in the 1935 version, again plays the dual roles of Yukinojo Nakamura and Yami Taro. The cast also includes Fujiko Yamamoto, Ayako Wakao, Raizo Ichikawa, and Shintaro Katsu, among other luminaries. This film commemorates Hasegawa's 300th appearance. In Edo, Yukinojo Nakamura, a female-role actor of Kamigata kabuki performing in the city, spots Sanzai Tsuchibe and Kaimiya, the men who framed his father on false charges and drove him to suicide. Sanzai's daughter, Namiji, falls in love with Yukinojo, and he uses her to avenge his father. Kawaguchiya, who had been hoarding rice during the Edo famine, is thwarted by Kaimiya—instigated by Yukinojo—and goes bankrupt, after which Kaimiya sets fire to his shop. Enraged, Kaimiya strangles Kawaguchiya but is stabbed by Namiji, whom he had tried to abduct.
title_norm:an cailín ciúin: Set in early 1980s Ireland, this human drama depicts a special summer vacation experienced by a 9-year-old girl. It won the Grand Prix in the International Generation section for films starring children at the 72nd Berlin International Film Festival and was nominated for the International Feature Film Award at the 95th Academy Awards. In 1981, in a rural Irish town, a quiet girl named Cott, who lives silently within a large family, spends her summer vacation at the lush green farm of the Kinsella couple. Initially confused by the unfamiliar life, Cott receives abundant love from Sean and Eileen and, as she carefully experiences each moment, comes to feel a joy in living she had never known before. Catherine Clinch, in her debut role, delicately portrays the protagonist Cott with overwhelming transparency and presence, winning the IFTA Award (Irish Film & Television Academy Award) for Best Actress at the youngest age of 12. Based on the novel "Foster" by Irish writer Claire Keegan, this is the first feature-length fiction film directed and written by Colm Bairéad, who has previously focused on children's perspectives and family bonds in his documentary works.
title_norm:an island drifts: Winner of both Best Director and Best Drama at the USC First Look Awards. Andrew is a boy attending a private elementary school in modern Singapore, where the pressures of an academic meritocracy swirl around him. One day, a minor accident during a physical education class causes matters to escalate far beyond what is necessary... ■Ticket price: Flat 1,000 yen. *Free tickets, invitation tickets, and various other discount services cannot be used. Information on discounts available only at the box office on the day: Present a ticket for another film on the same day and receive 100 yen off. *Applicable only when purchasing tickets at the box office on the day. Making movie theaters a more casual option. '20 Minute Cinema' is a new initiative screening short films of 15-20 minutes in theaters. A 20-minute interlude you can drop into casually like a café, between shopping or after work. Masterpieces from around the world you won't find on streaming services will vividly color your everyday life.
title_norm:animal treasure island: Young Jim, who dreams of foreign lands and sailing, is left to mind the old inn Benbow Tavern in a port town tonight. But a suspicious cat captain shows up and leaves behind a mysterious map. It seems to indicate the location of treasure hidden by the famous pirate Captain Flint. Jim sets out to sea with his best friend, a mouse named Gran, in his homemade barrel ship, the Pioneer. Their destination: the legendary Treasure Island on the map! However, the Pioneer is sunk by a pirate ship, and the two are quickly taken prisoner. The pirate ship is named the Pork Sauté. Its captain, Silver, was once one of Flint's men, and he too has his eye on the treasure of Treasure Island. Jim and Gran escape and land on Pirate Island. But they are caught by Silver's gang, have the map stolen, and are sold off to slave traders. In the stone prison where they are confined, they find a girl named Cathy already there. It turns out Cathy is Captain Flint's granddaughter and is also looking for the map. Jim and Cathy initially clash but eventually open their hearts to each other and decide to cooperate and head for Treasure Island. Now, the curtain rises on a great adventure across the sea!
title_norm:anita: A documentary depicting the tumultuous life of Anita Pallenberg, known as the muse of the British rock band The Rolling Stones. Anita Pallenberg, an Italian-German model, actress, and fashion icon, embodied her era through her persona and creativity, becoming a symbolic figure in the rock culture of the 1960s and 70s. In 1965 she fell in love with Rolling Stones leader Brian Jones, and after his death had three children with Keith Richards, also captivating Mick Jagger, with whom she appeared in films. Anita became the source of their creativity, transformed fashion, engaged with the music itself, and lived her own life without being overshadowed by anyone. The film uses words from an unpublished memoir discovered after Anita's death, home movies, and family photographs, while her son Marlon, daughter Angela, and their father Keith Richards reveal intimate family secrets. Furthermore, Marianne Faithfull, Mick's lover and Anita's close friend, and model Kate Moss, who adored Anita, speak about the magnitude of her influence. Scarlett Johansson lends her voice to the words of Anita's memoir. Anita's son Marlon Richards serves as executive producer.
title_norm:another home: Set in a small diner on Cheung Chau, an outlying island of Hong Kong, this documentary observes a changing world through the islanders who gather there. Located about 30 minutes southwest of Hong Kong Island by ferry, Cheung Chau is a small island known as a fishing village, where colorful boats bob in the harbor and time flows gently. The 'Yat Tai' diner on the island is always bustling with locals who gather to play cards and mahjong with a beer in hand. However, societal changes and the fervor of citizens reach this island far from Hong Kong, and the diner's regulars cannot remain indifferent. From the owner staring at the TV to young people eagerly seeking information, each person grapples with the tides of the era from their own perspective and distance. Eventually, the pandemic that engulfs the world also has a major impact on this diner. The director is Frankie Shin, for whom this is his first feature-length documentary. Shin, a native of Cheung Chau who was also a regular at the Yat Tai diner, carefully captures how the people he treated like family faced the changing times and continued their daily lives. The film won the Best Documentary Award at the 29th Busan International Film Festival in 2024.
title_norm:anymart: At a convenience store called AnyMart in a corner of Tokyo, the assistant manager Sakai (Sosuke Ikematsu) has spent most of his twenties working there since his student days. Register work. Stocking shelves. Disposal. Mobile games. Dating apps. Just repeating the same things every day. The owner (Masahiko Nishimura) rules the store within the convenience store system, allowing no deviation. However, the arrival of a new part-time worker, Ogawa (Erika Karata), begins to quietly disrupt the store's equilibrium. Eventually, this distortion silently and surely transforms the convenience store into an extreme space.
title_norm:arabian nights the adventures: Toei Animation's first departure from traditional Japanese or Chinese settings follows a young sailor's romantic voyage. The screenplay was an unusual collaboration between Morio Kita, a recent Akutagawa Prize winner with experience as a ship's doctor, and Osamu Tezuka. Staff went to great lengths to depict waves, sometimes painting as many as 300 polka dots on a single cel, and the resulting animation—over 10,000 drawings—imbues the ocean adventure with remarkable realism.
title_norm:arco: The adventure of Iris, a girl living in a near future devastated by climate change, and Arco, a rainbow-colored boy who 'fell from the sky.' A poetically rich animation by a rising French director, depicted in vivid colors.
title_norm:arco アルコ: The adventure of Iris, a girl living in a near future devastated by climate change, and Arco, a rainbow-colored boy who 'fell from the sky.' A poetically rich animation by a rising French director, depicted in vivid colors.
title_norm:arco／アルコ: The adventure of Iris, a girl living in a near future devastated by climate change, and Arco, a rainbow-colored boy who 'fell from the sky.' A poetically rich animation by a rising French director, depicted in vivid colors.
title_norm:asako i & ii: The commercial film debut of director Ryusuke Hamaguchi, who gained attention for "Happy Hour," a film that meticulously depicted the daily lives and friendships of four women over more than five hours and won major awards at numerous international film festivals including Locarno and Nantes. This film was entered into the Competition section of the 71st Cannes International Film Festival. It is an adaptation of the award-winning love novel of the same name by Akutagawa Prize-winning author Tomoka Shibasaki, starring Masahiro Higashide and Erika Karata. Asako, a 21-year-old living in Osaka, meets Baku and falls into a fateful love, but one day, Baku suddenly disappears from her life. Two years later, having moved from Osaka to Tokyo, Asako meets Ryohei, who has a face identical to Baku's. Unable to forget Baku, Asako tries to avoid Ryohei, but he develops feelings for her. Despite her hesitation, Asako finds herself drawn to Ryohei. Higashide plays the dual roles of Baku and Ryohei, while Karata plays Asako.
title_norm:at the triangle intersection: A documentary observing a 99-year-old woman and her son and daughter-in-law, who were affected by the Great East Japan Earthquake and the Fukushima Daiichi nuclear disaster and live in disaster recovery public housing, over a three-year period from 2018 to 2021. Seven years after the 2011 Great East Japan Earthquake and Fukushima Daiichi nuclear disaster, a family forced to evacuate from Namie Town, Fukushima, wavers between returning to their hometown and choosing a new life. Having closed their long-running printing business due to the disaster and living in disaster recovery public housing in Iwaki City, the roles and relationships within the family quietly change. Tetsu, the 99-year-old mother, clings to memories of her birthplace, Okuma Town, even as her memory fades. Her taciturn son Takemasa respects his mother but leaves most of her care to his wife Shigeko. Shigeko, who has continued to bear this role, begins to reexamine her taken-for-granted position within the family and her own way of living. Through the family's daily life in flux, the film questions what "home" is and what "I" is. Directed by Toru Yamada, who has continued making films in Fukushima since the Great East Japan Earthquake.
title_norm:ateez light the way in cinema: A concert film that reconstructs the immersive live experience of the popular K-pop group ATEEZ for theaters. Following their 2025 theatrical release "ATEEZ WORLD TOUR [TOWARDS THE LIGHT : WILL TO POWER] IN CINEMAS," this is their second theatrical release, based on the immersive experience that toured various locations from 2025 by the VR concert platform AMAZE, reconfigured in native 8K resolution and 5.1ch surround sound. One day, a mysterious message arrives for ATEEZ, who are spending a peaceful time at their hideout. From that moment, everything begins to change, and their fans "ATINY" disappear. As if under a spell, ATEEZ wander through a dreamlike wilderness, a world engulfed in flames and collapsing, and a "Dark City" shrouded in deep fog. While pursued by an unidentified force, they launch a counterattack to find ATINY. Featuring Hongjoong, Seonghwa, Yunho, Yeosang, San, Mingi, Wooyoung, and Jongho, the film brings performances of hit songs like "INCEPTION," "BOUNCY (K-HOT CHILLI PEPPERS)," and "Ice On My Teeth" to the big screen. It also includes 20 minutes of unreleased behind-the-scenes footage.
title_norm:au hasard balthazar: The 7th feature film by master director Robert Bresson, known for "L'Argent," "Pickpocket," and "The Trial of Joan of Arc," released in 1966. Inspired by an episode from Dostoevsky's novel "The Idiot," it portrays the strange fate of a donkey and a young girl. In a small Pyrenean village, little Marie names a newborn donkey Balthazar and cherishes him. Ten years later, Balthazar is used for hard labor by a blacksmith but escapes the suffering and returns to Marie. The grown Marie rejoices at their reunion and takes Balthazar with her, but Gérard, who has feelings for her, becomes jealous and torments the donkey. Through the silent perspective of the donkey, the film calmly depicts human folly and ugliness, winning the Special Jury Prize at the Venice International Film Festival and earning acclaim as a masterpiece. Starring Anne Wiazemsky, who later appeared in many Godard films including "La Chinoise," in her film debut. First theatrically released in Japan in 1970, and again in 1995 distributed by France Eigasha. Revived in October 2020 in a 4K restored digital remaster. Also revived in 2026 as part of "Robert Bresson Masterpiece Selection."
title_norm:au pan coupé: The second feature film by Guy Gilles, a director re-evaluated since the 2000s as a 'forgotten master of the French New Wave,' depicting a woman living with the memory of her lover who chose death. The present is shown in black-and-white, and fragments of recollection in color, delicately and melancholically portraying the memory of love and the pain of absence. Jeanne lives with the memory of her deceased lover Jean. Jean rejected social order and the bourgeois world, found no place in the Beat generation, and chose death. Unaware of his death, Jeanne feels him always by her side, existing like a ghost. Masha Meril, known for 'A Time for Loving' and 'Belle de Jour,' plays the protagonist Jeanne, and Patrick Jouané, an actor who met Guy Gilles during the filming of 'Le Rempart des Béguines' and became an irreplaceable presence in his life and work, plays the deceased lover Jean. The film was released in Japanese theaters in April 2026.
title_norm:badlands: The feature directorial debut of Terrence Malick, director of "Days of Heaven" and "The Thin Red Line," released in 1973. Based on a series of real murders that occurred in the late 1950s in America, it vividly and poetically depicts the flight of a young couple who commit a series of unplanned crimes. In 1959, in a small town in South Dakota. Holly, a 15-year-old girl who is not very noticeable at school, meets Kit, a young garbage collector, and falls in love. However, when Kit shoots and kills Holly's father, who disapproves of their relationship, the two embark on a aimless journey of escape. They live a reckless life, staying carefree in a treehouse and breaking into a rich man's mansion. Holly can only watch as Kit kills people one after another... Martin Sheen, known for "Apocalypse Now," plays Kit, and Sissy Spacek, known for "Carrie," plays Holly. In Japan, it was broadcast on TV in 1980 under the title "Jigoku no Tōhikō," and was released in theaters for the first time in March 2025 under the title "Badlands."
title_norm:balance: Starring Kumi Takiuchi of 'A Balance' and directed by Yujiro Harumoto of 'To the Ends of the Earth,' this drama confronts the problems and contradictions of the information society head-on. Yūko, a documentary filmmaker, pursues the truth behind a high school girl's suicide due to bullying that occurred three years ago. She is committed to shedding light on issues that need to be brought before the public, even if it means clashing with the production side. Meanwhile, she helps run the cram school managed by her father, Masashi, and has lived happily with him, working as a team. However, an unexpected action by Masashi forces Yūko into an ultimate choice that shakes her convictions. Takiuchi plays the protagonist Yūko, and Ken Mitsuishi plays her father Masashi, with supporting roles by Tomohiro Umeda and Yūmi Kawai. The film was screened in the Panorama section of the 71st Berlin International Film Festival in 2021.
title_norm:ball of fire: At the Totten Foundation in New York, eight scholars are putting the finishing touches on an encyclopedia, but when grammar professor Potts overhears a slang term, he realizes their work has been isolated from the real world and ventures into the city to investigate. There, he seeks the help of O'Shea, a nightclub singer... Although the film was a hit in the U.S. upon release, it was never imported due to the times. Billy Wilder contributed to the script on the condition that he be allowed to observe Hawks' direction. He made his directorial debut the following year, having used this as preparation.
title_norm:balloons landin: A road movie set in Hong Kong and Taiwan, depicting a midsummer miracle connected by a single letter. Against the beautiful, shimmering landscapes of Taiwan, it portrays a time-spanning bond between a wounded writer and a lonely young man. Tianyu, a popular Hong Kong writer, faces fierce public backlash after accusations of plagiarism. Deeply hurt, he travels alone to Taiwan in search of the 'Whale's Vanished Cove,' a place said to lead to heaven, which a boy he once corresponded with told him about. After being cheated in an unfamiliar country and getting drunk in the bustling streets of Taipei, Tianyu is helped by Ashang, a local thug. When Tianyu reveals the purpose of his journey, Ashang, claiming to know the 'Whale's Vanished Cove,' offers to take him there, and their summer journey begins... Terence Lau, known for 'Twilight Warriors: Final Battle in the Kowloon Walled City,' delicately portrays the gentle and pure writer Tianyu, while Fandy Fan, from 'Destiny Matchup,' co-stars as the thug Ashang.
title_norm:band of outsiders: A masterpiece from Jean-Luc Godard's early period, this melodrama is based on an American crime novel and depicts in comedic fashion the love triangle and criminal scheme involving two men and one woman. Winter in Paris. Franz and Arthur, best friends with completely opposite personalities, both fall in love at first sight with Odile, a beautiful and shy woman from Scandinavia. One day, they learn that a large sum of money is hidden in Odile's aunt's house, and the three plot to steal it, but the plan takes unexpected twists and turns... This was the first production from "Anouchka Films," the production company founded by Godard and actress Anna Karina, who played Odile and were married at the time. Music by Michel Legrand of "The Umbrellas of Cherbourg." It went unreleased in Japanese theaters for many years before finally premiering in 2001.
title_norm:bande à part: A masterpiece from Jean-Luc Godard's early period, this melodrama is based on an American crime novel and depicts in comedic fashion the love triangle and criminal scheme involving two men and one woman. Winter in Paris. Franz and Arthur, best friends with completely opposite personalities, both fall in love at first sight with Odile, a beautiful and shy woman from Scandinavia. One day, they learn that a large sum of money is hidden in Odile's aunt's house, and the three plot to steal it, but the plan takes unexpected twists and turns... This was the first production from "Anouchka Films," the production company founded by Godard and actress Anna Karina, who played Odile and were married at the time. Music by Michel Legrand of "The Umbrellas of Cherbourg." It went unreleased in Japanese theaters for many years before finally premiering in 2001.
title_norm:be a man!! samurai school: Depicts the extreme training and battles at 'Otokojuku,' a school that raises men among men. Invited to the 'Big Battle August' tournament where representatives from around the world compete for supremacy during summer vacation, the first-year students fight their way through Hawaii, Niagara Falls, Alaska, and New York, culminating in a decisive battle against the American team. The appeal lies in the massive physiques and dynamic storytelling.
title_norm:be pretty and shut up!: The only feature-length directorial work by actress Delphine Seyrig, known for films like 'Last Year at Marienbad' and 'Jeanne Dielman, 23 quai du Commerce, 1080 Bruxelles', released in 1976. This documentary interviews 23 actresses active in Hollywood and Paris. Seyrig herself serves as the interviewer, asking two questions: 'If you were a man, would you still have chosen this profession?' and 'Have you ever played a friendly scene with another actress?' The film features a range of women—from famous film actresses like Jane Fonda ('Julia'), Shirley MacLaine ('The Apartment'), Juliet Berto ('Céline and Julie Go Boating'), Anne Wiazemsky ('La Chinoise'), and Maria Schneider ('Last Tango in Paris'), to TV actresses and unknowns—speaking frankly, intimately, and sometimes humorously about gender questions that were risky to answer in the male-dominated film industry of the time. The original title 'Sois belle et tais-toi!' (Be beautiful and shut up) is said to have been a phrase used against women in French film and theater, and is now a cliché symbolizing gender discrimination in English-speaking countries. In Japan, it will have its first theatrical release in July 2026 to commemorate the 50th anniversary of its production.
title_norm:beyond the fire the life of j: A documentary depicting the life of activist Teishiro Minami, who organized Japan's first Pride Parade in 1994. Today, Pride Parades are held in over 40 locations in Japan, and partnership systems are spreading nationwide. At the starting point of this progress were the grassroots activities of pioneers who forged a path from "zero" to "one." Born in Karafuto (Sakhalin) in 1931 and raised in Akita Prefecture, Teishiro Minami moved to Tokyo at age 22, constantly searching for a way to live authentically. In 1984, he began the gay liberation movement, immersing himself in activism and following his passion. Then, in 1994, he launched Japan's first Pride Parade. The activities Minami spearheaded became the foundation of the pride movement in Japan, but he gradually became fixated on his own beliefs, deepening the rift with those around him. By the third parade, he faced significant backlash and was forced to step back from the front lines of the movement. What did Minami, driven by justice and swept along by the times, find in the end of his fervor? Tracing his tumultuous path through his own testimony, interviews with people involved at the time, news reports, photos, and videos, the film depicts the origins of the pride movement in Japan. Directed by Hiroaki Matsuoka ("Okinawa Coming Out Story").
title_norm:beyond the game samurai 2026: A documentary providing an intimate behind-the-scenes look at Samurai Japan, the Japanese national baseball team, during the 6th World Baseball Classic (WBC) held in March 2026. Having vowed to "discard admiration and surpass it" to win the world championship in a hard-fought battle at the 2023 WBC, the team entered this tournament under the immense pressure of being the reigning champions, facing the inescapable burden of "having to remain the winning champions." The film explores what the players felt and how they fought during their quest to remain on top, and how they came to terms with the result of losing in the quarterfinals. Through the lens of the only camera granted exclusive access to the team for this tournament, the documentary gets to the heart of the action behind the scenes. The director is Shintaro Miki, who has previously made documentaries closely following Samurai Japan, such as "Unity, Beyond: The Warriors' Anguish and Hope" and "The Samurai Who Surpassed Admiration: Record of Becoming World No. 1." Narration is provided by Kazunari Ninomiya, and the theme song is performed by Koshi Inaba. It began streaming on Netflix on April 20, 2026, and had a limited theatrical release nationwide in Japan starting August 14, 2026, including at Aeon Cinema Itabashi.
title_norm:beyond the infinite two minut: This is the first original feature-length film by the popular theater troupe 'Europe Kikaku,' known for works like 'Summer Time Machine Blues,' rebooting their short film 'Howling.' On the second floor of a certain mixed-use building, Kato hears a voice from the TV and looks at the screen to see his own face. The Kato on the screen speaks to him, saying 'I'm you from two minutes in the future.' It seems that the second-floor room where Kato is and the first-floor café are connected with a two-minute time difference. The friends who learn of the 'Time TV' become desperate to find out more about the future by facing two TVs towards each other... The film stars troupe members including Kazunari Tosa as the protagonist Kato, along with Aki Asakura and Riko Fujitani. The original concept and screenplay are by the troupe's leader, Makoto Ueda, and the director is the troupe's video director, Junta Yamaguchi.
title_norm:billy elliot: A coming-of-age drama set in a 1980s British mining town, following a boy's struggle to become a ballet dancer and the bonds of family. In 1984, in a mining town in northeast England, 11-year-old Billy, who has lost his mother, is forced by his coal miner father to attend boxing classes. One day, intrigued by a ballet class he stumbles upon, he joins the girls in their lessons. Ballet teacher Mrs. Wilkinson discovers Billy's talent as a dancer, and under her passionate guidance, he improves rapidly. Jamie Bell, chosen from over 2,000 auditionees, delivers a powerful performance as Billy. Julie Walters of "Educating Rita" plays Mrs. Wilkinson, earning an Academy Award nomination for Best Supporting Actress. Gary Lewis of "My Name Is Joe" plays Billy's father. World-renowned ballet dancer Adam Cooper makes a special appearance. The film marks the feature directorial debut of stage director Stephen Daldry, who later helmed "The Hours."
title_norm:bis ans ende der welt: A film that Wim Wenders nurtured for about 13 years before completing. Blending sci-fi elements, it combines a road movie and love story set in a world facing apocalypse. In the winter of 1999, the predicted crash of a nuclear satellite casts the world into anxiety. Claire, traveling by car from Venice, meets Trevor, who is being chased by someone. Though they part ways, she can't stop thinking about him and, with the help of her ex-lover (a writer) and a private detective, follows him to Lisbon, Moscow, and Beijing. Reuniting with Trevor in Tokyo, Claire learns the purpose of his journey.
title_norm:black ox: A visual poem co-produced by Japan, Taiwan, and the United States, inspired by the "Ten Ox Herding Pictures," which depict the path to enlightenment in Zen using ten images of oxen. Directed and written by Tetsuichiro Tsuta, who gained domestic and international attention for "The Ravine of Goodbye," the film took eight years to complete. A hunter, forced to wander as he loses his mountain home in a rapidly changing era, encounters a majestic black ox in the mountains. He forcibly brings the resisting ox back and begins living with it in a remote house. The man and the ox till the land to survive, but they cannot see eye to eye in the face of nature's fury. However, an encounter with a Zen monk gradually brings the man and the ox to understand each other. Taiwanese acclaimed actor Lee Kang-sheng, known for his frequent roles in Tsai Ming-liang's films like "Stray Dogs," stars, with dancer Min Tanaka, also active as an actor, co-starring as the Zen monk. The entire film was shot on film, with some portions using 70mm film, a first for a Japanese feature film. The music uses compositions by Ryuichi Sakamoto, who had expressed his intention to participate in the project before his death. After its premiere at the "Asian Future" section of the 37th Tokyo International Film Festival in 2024, it won the top prize, the Firebird Award, at the 49th Hong Kong International Film Festival in 2025.
title_norm:black rain: Shizuma Shigematsu, living with his family in a village near Fukuyama City, was in Hiroshima with his wife and niece. The atomic bombing was a tragedy that mercilessly took the lives of thousands and forever etched the harsh existence of the survivors.
title_norm:blood flower: Set in Malaysia, this demon-combining exorcism gore horror film takes on the Islamic exorcism rites of the state religion and Southeast Asia's most enigmatic flower, the titan arum. A boy apprentice exorcist, who inherited spiritual powers from his mother, engages in a deadly struggle against the forbidden curse dwelling within the "corpse flower." Iqbal, raised under the wing of Norman, a Muslim exorcist, possesses rare spiritual abilities inherited from his mother Dina. One day, Dina is possessed and killed by an evil spirit while shielding Iqbal, who was targeted because of the strength of his powers. Grief-stricken, Iqbal resents his own overwhelming power, and his father Norman, worried about his son's future, seals away part of his abilities. Crawling toward the wounded family are a series of tragedies brought by the curse of the "corpse flower." Can Iqbal overcome his sorrow and exorcise a curse steeped in mystery and taboo?
title_norm:blood of my blood: A Gothic fantasy film by Italian master Marco Bellocchio, released in 2015 and winner of the FIPRESCI Prize at the 72nd Venice International Film Festival. The story intertwines the 17th century and the modern era, depicted with eerily beautiful imagery. In 17th-century Bobbio, northern Italy, young soldier Federico visits an old monastery to uncover the truth behind the death of his twin brother Fabrizio, a priest. It is said that Fabrizio was seduced by a nun named Benedetta, betrayed his faith, and lost his life. Seeking to restore his brother's honor, Federico tries to make Benedetta confess her guilt, but gradually becomes captivated by her, even as she is accused of witchcraft. The story then shifts to the modern day, centuries later. The former monastery lies in ruins, and a sale to a wealthy Russian is being negotiated. A man appears, but the ruins are haunted by a mysterious old count who only shows himself at night. Benedetta is played by Lidia Lieberman, Federico (living in both past and present) by Pier Giorgio Bellocchio, and the mysterious old count by Roberto Herlitzka. A cover of Metallica's "Nothing Else Matters" is used prominently in the film.
title_norm:blood relatives: A police inspector from the Montreal Police Department solves a murder case using clues obtained from the victim's diary.
title_norm:blue lock: A live-action film adaptation of the soccer manga 'Blue Lock', serialized in Kodansha's 'Weekly Shonen Magazine' since 2018, which has gained popularity both domestically and internationally for its innovative premise, unique and egotistical characters, and unpredictable story development. To overcome the Japanese national team's chronic lack of goal-scoring ability, a top-secret project, the 'Blue Lock (Blue Prison)', is launched. Three hundred high school strikers are gathered and subjected to numerous trials, with only the final survivor earning the right to become the world's greatest striker. However, there's a cruel condition: those eliminated are permanently banned from ever representing Japan. Yoichi Isagi, an unknown high school player who dreams of becoming the national team's ace striker and winning the World Cup, decides to participate to change his life. Lacking the outstanding physical abilities of the other 299 participants, Isagi relies on his exceptional spatial awareness to survey the entire pitch and his strong will to pursue the goal, taking on the fierce survival battle. Takahashi Fumiya stars as Yoichi Isagi. The cast includes Sakurai Kaito as Meguru Bachira (Team Z), Takahashi Kyohei (Naniwa Danshi) as Hyoma Chigiri, Nomura Kota as Rensuke Kunigami, K (&TEAM) as Seishiro Nagi (the undefeated champion Team V), Tsunahiro Keito as Reo Mikage, Kubota Masataka as Jinpachi Ego (the project's supreme leader), and Hatakeyama Mei as Anri Teieri (Ego's right hand). The Japan Football Association and J.League fully cooperated with the filming, and former Japanese national team player Matsui Daisuke served as soccer supervisor.
title_norm:blue moon: From director Richard Linklater, known for the 'Before' trilogy beginning with 'Before Sunrise' and the six-time Oscar-nominated 'Boyhood,' this conversation piece stars his longtime collaborator Ethan Hawke and depicts a night spent at a party attended by legendary Broadway lyricist Lorenz Hart. On the evening of March 31, 1943, the night of the premiere of the musical 'Oklahoma!,' created by his longtime composing partner Richard Rodgers with a new collaborator, Lorenz Hart—the lyricist behind hits like 'The Lady Is a Tramp' and 'My Funny Valentine'—was invited to a party at the Broadway restaurant Sardi's. Over the course of that night, Hart confronts his own swirling emotions of love, jealousy, anxiety, and longing. Ethan Hawke plays Lorenz Hart, alongside Margaret Qualley as Elizabeth, the woman Hart pines for; Andrew Scott as his former partner Richard Rodgers; and Bobby Cannavale as Eddie, the bartender Hart trusts as a confidant. The film was screened in the competition section of the 75th Berlin International Film Festival in 2025, where Andrew Scott won the Silver Bear for Best Supporting Actor. It was nominated for Best Original Screenplay and Best Actor (Ethan Hawke) at the 98th Academy Awards.
title_norm:blue sprin: At an all-boys high school. Kyujo (Ryuhei Matsuda) and his five friends, now third-years in the new term, stand outside the railing on the rooftop, playing the 'Balcony Game'—competing to see who can clap the most times before falling. Kyujo sets a new record in this game, where failure means a straight drop to the schoolyard, and as the winner, gains the right to rule the school. But for him, both the 'game' and 'ruling the school' are meaningless and trivial. As Kyujo and the others drift through their aimless days, lost about where they belong, the reality of choosing their future paths is eventually thrust upon them...
title_norm:bluebeards 8th wife: At a department store in the French resort of Riviera, American businessman Michael Brandon (Gary Cooper) insists on buying only the top half of a pair of pajamas. Conveniently appearing to take just the bottoms is Nicole (Claudette Colbert), the daughter of a poor aristocrat. Instantly smitten by her spirited nature, Brandon pursues her relentlessly and secures an engagement. However, on their wedding day, Nicole discovers Brandon has been married seven times and flies into a rage. They manage to marry only on the condition that Brandon pays Nicole a huge alimony if they divorce. Naturally, the relationship fails, and frustrated by his wife's indifference, Brandon resorts to a desperate measure.
title_norm:bodacious space pirates abyss: The theatrical film version of the TV anime "Mouretsu Pirates," which aired from January to June 2012, based on Yuichi Sasamoto's popular SF light novel "Mini-Skirt Space Pirates." Marika Kato, a high school girl who is a legitimate space pirate holding a government-issued "privateer's license," leads a busy life juggling her studies, club activities in the space yacht club, a part-time job at a café, and her role as captain of the space pirate ship "Bentenmaru." One day during spring break, just before she is about to advance to her third year, Marika takes on a pirate business job aboard a luxury liner and meets Kanata Mugen, the son of the renowned subspace diver, Dr. Mugen. The opening theme, following the TV series, is "Mouretsu Uchuu Koukyoukyoku Dainanagakushou 'Mugen no Ai'" by Momoiro Clover Z. The director is Tatsuo Sato, known for "Martian Successor Nadesico."
title_norm:bohemian rhapsody: A biographical drama depicting Freddie Mercury, the vocalist of the world-famous rock band Queen, who passed away in 1991 at the young age of 45. Queen's current members Brian May and Roger Taylor served as music producers, and the film's soundtrack primarily uses Freddie's own vocals. It recreates the moments of birth of classics like "Bohemian Rhapsody" and "We Will Rock You," as well as legendary performances in music history such as the stunning performance at "Live Aid," the largest charity concert of the 20th century, while also portraying the untold stories behind his glamorous career. Rami Malek, known for "Night at the Museum," delivers a passionate performance as Freddie. Bryan Singer, known for the "X-Men" series, is credited as director, but he left during production, and Dexter Fletcher, known for "Sunshine on Leith" and "Eddie the Eagle," completed the film, handling the remaining shooting and post-production. Despite the production troubles, it was embraced by audiences worldwide, and in Japan, it became a massive hit, surpassing 13 billion yen at the box office, the highest for a film released in 2018. It won Best Motion Picture – Drama and Best Actor – Drama at the 76th Golden Globe Awards. It was nominated for five Academy Awards at the 91st Academy Awards, including Best Picture, and won four, including Best Actor.
title_norm:bonne chance: A road movie written and directed by Shin Adachi, known for scripting the NHK morning drama "Boogie Woogie" and films like "Zako-domo yo, Taishi o Idake" and "Theater Version: Still, I Want to Be with My Wife," set in Bungo-Ono, Oita Prefecture, depicting a small journey of a man and woman lost in life. Taro Oyama, approaching 30, calls himself a film director but is actually supported by the woman he lives with. He is selected for a film festival in Oita Prefecture but receives harsh criticism from the female organizer. The next day, heartbroken, Taro heads to neighboring Chikugo-Ono and meets a mysterious woman named Miki Sunahara. Miki, who says she saw Taro's film at the festival, and Taro embark on a small one-night, two-day trip. Miki is of unknown identity but has a frank personality. Taro, baring his lack of confidence in filmmaking to her, gradually develops a faint romantic feeling... Taro, the struggling film director protagonist, is played by Hiroki Sano from "SUPER HAPPY FOREVER," and Miki, the mysterious woman he meets on his journey, is played by Hana Amano from "Chime." The supporting cast includes Saki Kato, Ryo Shinoda, Ayame Gouriki, and Yuka Itaya.
title_norm:boy meets girl: The feature debut of French maverick Leos Carax, released in 1983. It depicts the encounter of two lonely souls wandering through the Paris night in beautiful black-and-white imagery, winning the Youth Prize at the 37th Cannes Film Festival and generating buzz at festivals worldwide. Alex, a young man whose best friend stole his girlfriend, has a fateful encounter with Mireille, a woman who just fought with her lover. Alex falls in love with Mireille at first sight, but they soon meet with an unexpected tragedy. The roles of Alex and Mireille were played by then-newcomers Denis Lavant and Mireille Perrier. The protagonist Alex, played by Lavant, later reappeared in transformed forms in 'Bad Blood' and 'The Lovers on the Bridge', forming what is known as the 'Alex Trilogy' along with this film. Jean-Yves Escoffier handled the cinematography and continued as cinematographer for the subsequent two films. In Japan, it was first theatrically released in July 1988, following the release of 'Bad Blood' in February of the same year. A 4K restored version was re-released in January 2026.
title_norm:boyfriends and girlfriends: The sixth film in Éric Rohmer's "Comedies and Proverbs" series. Set in a new town on the outskirts of Paris, it lightly depicts the romantic affairs of four men and women. Blanche, a shy woman working at city hall, and Léa, a pragmatic female student, hit it off and become friends. Léa lives with her boyfriend Fabien, but their relationship isn't going well. Meanwhile, Blanche develops feelings for Alexandre, a playboy and friend of Fabien's, but her timid nature prevents her from confessing. Eventually, Fabien finds himself drawn to Blanche... The colorful 1980s fashion is also a highlight.
title_norm:brand new landscape: Set in rapidly redeveloping Tokyo's Shibuya, this drama portrays the relationship between a father and son left behind after the mother's death. It marks the film debut of Koyo Kurozaki, who gained attention for his acting debut in the NHK morning drama "Boogie Woogie." This is the feature debut of Yuiga Dansuka, based on his original script; he previously directed the short "I Want to Go Far Away" as part of the Agency for Cultural Affairs' young filmmaker development project "ndjc (New Directions in Japanese Cinema)." Ren, a young man working as a Phalaenopsis orchid delivery driver in Shibuya, became estranged from his father, Hajime, a landscape designer, after losing his mother, Yumiko, as a child. One day, Ren coincidentally meets his father during a delivery and tells his sister Emi, but she remains indifferent, quietly preparing for her own wedding. Amidst this, Ren tries to reassess his distance from his family. Kurozaki plays the protagonist Ren, Kenichi Endo (an indispensable supporting actor in Japanese cinema) plays his father Hajime, Haru Ikewaki (active as an actress and model) plays the deceased mother Yumiko, and Maso Kuryu (a talented actress from "Chrysanthemum and Guillotine" and "The Lies of the Suzuki Family") plays his sister Emi. The film was selected for the Directors' Fortnight at the 78th Cannes Film Festival in 2025.
title_norm:break shot: A short black comedy written and directed by Kuruma Takahira of the comedy duo 'Reiwa Roman' as his directorial debut. It depicts an incident that occurs on a congested highway late at night, entirely from the perspective of dashcams. Six cars are driving on the highway. Inside each vehicle, excuses, pride, probing, work anxiety, someone being chased, reckless challenges to boost video views, and trivial conversations unfold. Only the dashcams inside the cars record everything. Tomohiro Kodama of the comedy duo 'Sarugorira' stars, with a stellar supporting cast including Joe Odagiri, Kengo Kora, Aoi Morikawa, and Oshiro Maeda. It was released in theaters after a special screening at 'Short Shorts Film Festival & Asia 2026'. A making-of documentary titled 'KURUMA: The Road to BREAK SHOT' was also produced, delving into the behind-the-scenes production.
title_norm:breathless: Jean-Luc Godard's first feature-length directorial work. Produced with techniques that broke the conventions of theatrical cinema at the time, such as improvisational direction and handheld street shooting, it is a landmark film of the French New Wave that greatly influenced the later film industry. The original idea was by François Truffaut, and Claude Chabrol also participated as a technical advisor. Michel, a car thief who kills a policeman and flees to Paris, enjoys a free relationship with Patricia, an American student selling newspapers. To test Michel's love, Patricia informs the police of his whereabouts and tells Michel what she has done... A digitally remastered version with a new translation by Jiro Terao was released in 2016. In 2022, a 4K restored version created to commemorate the 60th anniversary of its release was shown. In 2026, a 4K restored version will be revived in conjunction with the release of Richard Linklater's film 'Nouvelle Vague,' which depicts the production process of 'Breathless.'
title_norm:bride for rip van winkle: Nanami Minagawa, a temporary teacher in Tokyo, meets Tetsuya on social media and marries him. She hires Amaru, a jack-of-all-trades, to provide stand-in guests for the wedding ceremony. However, Tetsuya's affair soon comes to light. Then Nanami is accused by her mother-in-law of having an affair herself and is forced to leave the house. Amaru introduces Nanami to jobs as a stand-in wedding guest and as a live-in maid with a monthly salary of 1 million yen. There she meets her fellow maid, the unconventional and free-spirited Mashiro Satonaka.
title_norm:bright future: Yuji Nimura spends a quiet, monotonous daily life with his coworker Mamoru Arida at the same moist towel factory. Yuji is reckless and struggles to get along with others. Seeing this, Mamoru one day proposes two signals that only the two of them can understand and tries to enforce them. Around that time, Yuji begins to take an interest in the highly venomous 'sea wasp' jellyfish that Mamoru keeps. One day, Mamoru entrusts the jellyfish to Yuji and suddenly disappears. Mamoru is imprisoned as a suspect in the murder of the factory owner and his wife. From then on, Yuji, though bewildered, begins caring for the jellyfish as if possessed by something.
title_norm:bring her back: After their father dies, brother Andy and his visually impaired sister Piper come to live with foster mother Laura. Also living there is a boy named Oliver who does not speak. Andy feels uneasy about Laura's seemingly excessive affection, but a new life for the siblings begins under her care. From a certain day onward, unsettling events begin to occur one after another in the house. Furthermore, there are mysterious circular motifs scattered around the house, and the presence of Oliver. When these seemingly unrelated elements all connect, Laura's hidden 'terrifying wish' is revealed.
title_norm:broker: A road movie that won two awards at the 75th Cannes Film Festival, featuring a Korean production team and cast. Two male brokers who kidnap an infant from a 'baby hatch' and the mother who once abandoned her child. Bound by a strange sense of solidarity, they journey to find adoptive parents, quietly pursued by two female detectives. This film returns to Kore-eda's signature theme of 'quasi-family,' depicting certain hope beyond the moral dilemmas surrounding the salvation of unwanted lives.
title_norm:bugonia: The eccentric genius Yorgos Lanthimos, known for 'Poor Things' and 'The Favourite', directs this kidnapping suspense film starring Emma Stone in their fifth collaboration. Ari Aster, director of 'Welcome to Eddington' and 'Midsommar', serves as producer. It is a remake of the 2003 Korean film 'Save the Green Planet!'. Michelle, the charismatic CEO of a globally renowned pharmaceutical company, is kidnapped by Teddy, a conspiracy theorist who firmly believes she is an alien set on invading Earth, and his devoted cousin Don. They imprison her in a basement and demand she abandon her plans for Earth. Michelle dismisses their absurd demands and tries to talk her way out, but the tug-of-war takes unexpected turns. As Teddy's hidden past comes to light, the absurd kidnapping plot veers in unforeseen directions. Emma Stone appears with a shaved head, passionately playing Michelle. Jesse Plemons and newcomer Aiden Delvis, cast through auditions, play the two kidnappers. The film was presented in the competition section of the 82nd Venice International Film Festival in 2025 and was nominated for four Academy Awards at the 98th ceremony, including Best Picture and Best Actress.
title_norm:burn: Director Makoto Nagahisa, known for "We Are Little Zombies" and "And So We Put Goldfish in the Pool," casts Nana Mori in a drama set in Shinjuku's Kabukicho, depicting a "flame war" incident started by a girl. Born into a family of cult followers, Kobayashi Kurie is raised under strict discipline alongside her younger sister. The sisters pray to God daily for their painful days to end and for their education-obsessed father to disappear. Years later, their prayers are answered when their father dies, but their mother continues the harsh upbringing. Unable to bear it any longer, Kurie runs away from home, leaving her sister behind. Following a message on social media, she arrives at a square in Kabukicho where young people gather. There, she is given the name "Juju," a place to sleep, food, a smartphone, and a job. Experiencing the world for the first time and meeting various people, she finally begins to develop her own will. She dreams of taking her sister away from their mother and living together, but... Nagahisa wrote the original script and filmed on location in Kabukicho, capturing the raw reality of the neighborhood and the young people living there. Mori plays the protagonist Kurie, with Aoi Yamada ("Perfect Days"), Ryosuke Soda ("The Liar and His Lover"), and Wataru Ichinose (Netflix's "Sanctuary") co-starring.
title_norm:by the stream: Korean master Hong Sang-soo directs an ensemble drama set at a women's university in Seoul, depicting the romantic entanglements of students and adults surrounding a theater festival. At a women's university in Seoul, with the theater festival approaching, textile artist Jon-hee, who works as a lecturer, invites her uncle Si-on, a famous actor and stage director, as a temporary director to fill a gap caused by a love scandal on campus. As they begin creating a short play for the festival, various events unfold over ten days, including the aftermath of the students' love affairs and the budding romance between a senior professor and Si-on. Actress Kim Min-hee, Hong Sang-soo's partner in both public and private life, stars as Jon-hee and won the Best Performance Award at the 77th Locarno International Film Festival in 2024. The cast also includes regulars from Hong Sang-soo's films: Kwon Hae-hyo as Jon-hee's uncle Si-on, Cho Yun-hee as the professor who admires Si-on, and Ha Seong-guk as the fired director who was dating three people. In Japan, it was screened under the title 'Suyuchon' at the 25th Tokyo Filmex in 2024. It was theatrically released in 2025 as the second film in the 'Monthly Hong Sang-soo' project, a series of five consecutive monthly new releases celebrating the director's 30th debut anniversary.
title_norm:by the window: A love story directed by Rikiya Imaizumi (known for "Ai ga Nanda") starring Goro Inagaki, based on an original screenplay. Freelance writer Shigeki Ichikawa realizes that his wife, editor Sae, is having an affair with the popular young writer she handles, but he can't bring himself to confront her. At the same time, Shigeki is troubled by a certain feeling that sprouted within him when he learned of the affair. One day, at a literary award ceremony, Ichikawa meets high school writer Rea Kubo and is drawn to the content of her award-winning novel "La France." He asks if there is a real-life model for the story and if he can meet them. Sae, Ichikawa's wife, is played by Yuri Nakamura; high school writer Kubo by Tina Tamashiro; Shigeki's friend Masatsugu Arisaka by Ryuya Wakaba; Arisaka's wife Yukino by Mirai Shida; and Sae's lover Madoka Arakawa by Shion Sasaki.
title_norm:call me dragon: In the late Qing dynasty, the villainous Im Kun-ho rules over Gold Sand Village, a place rife with all kinds of crime and violence, including drugs and human trafficking. The Dragon group, traveling while punishing evil, and at the same time, the legendary female martial artist Eagle, arrive in this village. They are both searching for a treasure called the 'Silver Pearl', said to have been stolen from a Tibetan temple. Then, the ruthless killer karate practitioner Black Jaguar also appears, and fierce battles unfold among the powerful fighters over the Silver Pearl. This is the Japan comeback film for Yasuaki Kurata, who was active primarily in Hong Kong.
title_norm:catchfire: Ann (Jodie Foster), a contemporary artist in Los Angeles, accidentally witnesses a mafia murder. Her boyfriend Bob (Charlie Sheen) is killed, and Ann goes into hiding. Professional hitman Milo (Dennis Hopper), hired by the mafia, pursues Ann but inexplicably begins to fall in love with her. Milo gives Ann an ultimatum: "Die or become my woman." Forced to comply, Ann gradually finds herself drawn to Milo's pure feelings... <Screening Overview> Period: Friday, July 17 – Thursday, July 23, limited one-week screening. Admission: Flat rate of 1,300 yen (no discounts applicable, no complimentary tickets or T-tickets accepted). *Screening material is DVD.
title_norm:catching fire the story of an: A documentary depicting the tumultuous life of Anita Pallenberg, known as the muse of the British rock band The Rolling Stones. Anita Pallenberg, an Italian-German model, actress, and fashion icon, embodied her era through her persona and creativity, becoming a symbolic figure in the rock culture of the 1960s and 70s. In 1965 she fell in love with Rolling Stones leader Brian Jones, and after his death had three children with Keith Richards, also captivating Mick Jagger, with whom she appeared in films. Anita became the source of their creativity, transformed fashion, engaged with the music itself, and lived her own life without being overshadowed by anyone. The film uses words from an unpublished memoir discovered after Anita's death, home movies, and family photographs, while her son Marlon, daughter Angela, and their father Keith Richards reveal intimate family secrets. Furthermore, Marianne Faithfull, Mick's lover and Anita's close friend, and model Kate Moss, who adored Anita, speak about the magnitude of her influence. Scarlett Johansson lends her voice to the words of Anita's memoir. Anita's son Marlon Richards serves as executive producer.
title_norm:catching the stars of this su: A drama based on the award-winning novel by Mizuki Tsujimura, depicting the complex emotions of junior high and high school students during the COVID-19 pandemic, set in Tokyo's Shibuya Ward, Tsuchiura City in Ibaraki Prefecture, and Goto City in Nagasaki Prefecture. In 2020, with school attendance and club activities restricted due to the pandemic, Aya Tanimoto, a second-year student in the astronomy club at Ibaraki Prefectural Sunaura High School, proposes an 'Online Star Catch Contest'—a competition using remote meetings to conduct simultaneous astronomical observations across different locations. The activity, joined by students from the Goto Islands in Nagasaki and central Tokyo, eventually spreads nationwide and sparks a miracle. Hiyori Sakurada, known for 'The Fake Diary,' stars as Aya. Rinataro Mizusawa plays her classmate; Arisa Nakano and Ikoi Hayase play students from Nagasaki; Soiya Kurokawa and Anna Hoshino play students from Tokyo; and Takashi Okabe plays the astronomy club advisor. Tamaki Yamamoto, who gained attention for the 2019 short film 'One Night After' and the streaming drama 'Today You're Restless, You're Burning,' makes his feature-length commercial film debut as director. Mash Morino, known for the drama 'Keke no Hi no Kekeke,' writes the screenplay. Haruka Nakamura, known for 'Look Back,' provides the music.
title_norm:chaser game w a match made in: A film version serving as a sequel to the TV dramas 'Chaser Game W: My Ex-Girlfriend is My Harassing Boss' and 'Chaser Game W2: The Beautiful Celestial Maidens,' which delicately portrayed the realities of the game industry and a romance between women. Set seven years after the drama, it depicts the relationship evolving over time and the two women confronting life choices. Itsuki and Fuyu live in Ito City, Shizuoka Prefecture, with their daughter Tsuki, now a middle school student. As they become consumed by housework, childcare, and work, their time together becomes routine. Over the seven years, their relationship shifts from lovers to family, and they gradually begin to drift apart. Though they maintain a peaceful home while being disturbed by each other's casual words and attitudes, their daughter Tsuki senses the unease between her parents. One day, Tsuki gets into trouble and is helped by a taxi driver named Kozue. This encounter prompts Itsuki and Fuyu to confront each other's true feelings for the first time and re-examine the form of love they have lost sight of. Continuing from the drama series, Sugai Yuka stars as Itsuki, Nakamura Yurika as Fuyu, Okamoto Mirai as their middle-school-aged daughter Tsuki, Ito Ayumi as taxi driver Kozue, and Kurotani Tomoka as Department Chief Ro. Directed by Ota Isamu, who also worked on the drama series, with a screenplay by Asada Atsushi.
title_norm:chiikawa the movie the secret: Based on the original manga serialized on X (formerly Twitter) since 2020 by illustrator Nagano, the massively popular "Chiikawa" franchise—winner of the Japan Character Grand Prix three times, with its 2022 TV anime's catch-up streams on YouTube surpassing 400 million views—gets an animated film adaptation. Under the complete supervision of creator Nagano, the film adapts the particularly popular long-form "Siren Arc" from the original manga series, depicting a grand adventure of Chiikawa and friends on a mysterious island through epic music and powerful visuals. One day, while Chiikawa and Hachiware are relaxing in the square, a rabbit with a flyer stuck to its face appears. Hachiware reads the flyer, which turns out to be an invitation to a "special island." Tempted by promises of "easy monster subjugation on the island for 100x rewards" and "limited island ramen, limited sweets—sweet and spicy stuff all practically free," Chiikawa and friends decide to join the island camp. Along with a skeptical otter, they board a ship and land on the island, but... CygamesPictures, known for "Umamusume: Pretty Derby - Beginning of a New Era," handles the animation production.
title_norm:chikamatsu monogatari: A commentary: Osan, the young wife of a Kyoto paper merchant, is suspected of adultery with the clerk Mohei due to a chance incident... Based on a Chikamatsu puppet play, this celebrated film depicts a man and woman who awaken to true love through a life-or-death escape, rendered with rigorous yet flowing brushstrokes. The dignified beauty of Kagawa as Osan is not to be missed.
title_norm:children who chase lost voice: Makoto Shinkai, the animation artist known for delicate psychological portrayals and meticulous visual beauty in works like 'Voices of a Distant Star' and 'The Place Promised in Our Early Days,' returns with his first original feature in five years since '5 Centimeters per Second.' This juvenile animation follows a girl named Asuna who, triggered by mysterious music heard through a mineral radio left by her father, embarks on a grand adventure. The familiar staff supporting Shinkai's works, including art director Takumi Tanji and composer Tenmon, come together for this film.
title_norm:chimney town frozen in time: The sequel to the 2020 anime film 'Poupelle of Chimney Town,' based on the picture book of the same name by Akihiro Nishino. Based on the 2019 picture book 'Tick Tock: The Promised Clock Tower,' it is adapted on a much larger scale, depicting the story of the boy Rubitch meeting his dear friend Poupelle, who went far away in the previous film, once again. One year has passed since the miracle night when Chimney Town was enveloped in a starry sky. The boy Rubitch, who lost his dear best friend Poupelle, continued to believe in their reunion but eventually gives up to move forward. One day, Rubitch wanders into a mysterious otherworld that controls time, the 'Millennium Fortress.' In this world, clocks that no longer tell time are disposed of, but there is a mysterious clock tower that, though not broken, has stopped at 11:59. The mission Rubitch is given to return to his original world is to get this stopped clock tower moving again. Rubitch meets a man who has kept a promise and waited for 100 years, and regains the courage to believe. Continuing from the previous film, Akihiro Nishino serves as executive producer, original creator, and screenwriter, Yusuke Hirota directs, and STUDIO4°C handles the animation production. Yuzuna Nagase, a child actor known for the TV drama series 'Asa ga Kita,' voices the protagonist Rubitch, and Masataka Kubota, who voiced Poupelle in the previous film, reprises his role.
title_norm:chronicle of anna magdalena b: The life of Johann Sebastian Bach as seen through the eyes of his second wife, Anna Magdalena Bach. Directed and written by the duo Jean-Marie Straub and Danièle Huillet, with cinematography by Ugo Piccone, Saverio Diamante, and Giovanni Canfarelli, and music by Leo Leonius. Starring Gustav Leonhardt and Christiane Lang-Drewanz. The film is composed of just over one hundred shots. Only the musicians performing appear on screen, while Anna Magdalena's (Christiane Lang-Drewanz) narration recounts Bach's (Gustav Leonhardt) life from age 35 until his death. The Bach works performed on screen include the Brandenburg Concerto No. 5 BWV 1050, 1st movement Allegro; Prelude No. 8 BWV 854 from the Clavier-Büchlein for Wilhelm Friedemann Bach; Minuet from French Suite No. 1 BWV 812; Viola da Gamba Sonata No. 2 BWV 1028, 1st movement Adagio; Organ Trio No. 2 BWV 526, 2nd movement Largo; Magnificat BWV 243, movements 11 and 12; Tempo di Gavotta from Partita No. 6 BWV 830; Cantata BWV 205 "Zerreißet, zersprenget, zertrümmert die Gruft," movements 2 and 3 (Bass Recitative and Aria); Cantata BWV 198 "Trauer-Ode," final chorus; Funeral Music for Prince Leopold BWV 244a, Soprano Aria; St. Matthew Passion BWV 244, opening chorus; Cantata BWV 42 "Am Abend aber desselbigen Sabbats," opening Sinfonia and Tenor Recitative; and 24 other pieces. In 1722, Anna Magdalena is taken in as Bach's second wife. Over the 29 years until her death in 1756, Bach's creative struggles and his attitude towards Anna and their children at home are narrated in the order the music was composed.

Directed and written by the duo Jean-Marie Straub and Danièle Huillet, with cinematography by Ugo Piccone, Saverio Diamante, and Giovanni Canfarelli, and music by Leo Leonius.
