Numerous celebrities appear, including Dr. Richard Dawkins, Elvis Costello, and Patti Smith. Winner of the International Critics' Week Award at the 74th Venice International Film Festival.
title_norm:exist within: A Korean suspense thriller about floor noise and a cult religion, depicting the fate of a female writer who strives to uncover the truth behind the noise coming from the upstairs neighbor. Eun-su, an aspiring writer living in apartment 401, has been applying to numerous writing contests but faces a string of rejections. Meanwhile, for about a month, she has been tormented by unbearable noise coming from unit 501 above. Deciding to use this situation as material for her work, Eun-su, along with her friend Ji-seong, begins observing Ho-gyeong, a middle-aged man living in 501. Even after he notices her excessive stalking, she relentlessly pursues him for the sake of her writing. Eventually, Eun-su arrives at a shocking truth hidden behind the noise, but at the same time, she finds herself backed into a dangerous situation. Director Kim Jeong-uk, who has crafted many stories candidly depicting the human psyche, portrays with intense suspense the psychological anxiety born from trivial troubles lurking in daily life. Ryu Hwa-young, known as a former member of the K-pop group T-ARA, stars in her first lead film role, passionately playing Eun-su, a writer whose obsession with writing blurs the line between reality and delusion. Veteran actor Park Jin-woo, known for the Netflix drama "Squid Game," plays the mysterious upstairs resident Ho-gyeong.
title_norm:fallen angels: Director Wong Kar-wai of 'Chungking Express' crafts a pop-infused ensemble drama about the poignant romantic entanglements of five men and women in the neon-lit streets of Hong Kong. This film completes an episode originally planned as part of 'Chungking Express' as an independent work. A lonely hitman and the woman who acts as his agent. Their rule is to keep personal feelings out of work, but their relationship begins to waver. Meanwhile, a mute young man named Mo sneaks into other people's shops every night and runs them without permission. One day, Mo meets a woman who has just been heartbroken and falls for her. The hitman is played by Leon Lai of 'The City of Sadness,' the agent by Michelle Lee of 'Flowers of Shanghai,' and Mo by Takeshi Kaneshiro of 'Chungking Express.' Cinematography is by Christopher Doyle, who worked on many of Wong Kar-wai's films. First released in Japan in 1996. In 2022, a 4K restored version was screened as part of 'WKW4K' (from August 19, 2022, at Cine Mart Shinjuku, Grand Cinema Sunshine, Cinema City, etc.).
title_norm:falling angels: Set in Shinjuku's Kabukicho, this film portrays two girls working at a girls' bar alongside women from various backgrounds. As they continue to sell their youth and perform the roles demanded of them, they gradually lose sight of what they truly want. The film won the Movie.com Award at the 18th Tanabe Benkei Film Festival, a gateway for new directors. Naru, 19, starts working at a girls' bar after high school to leave her parents' home. Maria, 21, works at the same bar while attending university to repay her student loans. Bathed in the neon lights of the night town, Naru wishes to become someone special, while Maria longs to be a normal college student. One day, Naru meets a host on the streets of Kabukicho, and Maria is approached by a customer for an off-the-books deal. The director and screenwriter is Naima Kimura, for whom this is her second directorial work and first feature film. Kimura drew inspiration from her own experience working at a girls' bar as a student. The film was screened in theaters as part of the "Tanabe Benkei Film Festival Selection 2024" (May 9–June 5, 2024 at Theatre Shinjuku; June 20–26, 2024 at Theatre Umeda).
title_norm:farewell my concubine: An epic saga depicting the tumultuous lives of two Peking opera actors, this was the first Chinese-language film to win the Palme d'Or at the Cannes Film Festival. It portrays the love, hatred, and lives of two Peking opera performers who play the classic 'Farewell My Concubine,' set against the backdrop of China's turbulent history from 1925 under the Nationalist government through the Cultural Revolution and into the late 1970s. Directed by Chen Kaige, who gained attention with his debut 'Yellow Earth' and became a leading figure of China's Fifth Generation directors with this film's success. In 1925 Beijing, Douzi, abandoned by his prostitute mother, is sent to a Peking opera training school. Shitou protects him like a younger brother and becomes his strong support through harsh training. As they grow up, they become major stars in the Peking opera world... Leslie Cheung plays Cheng Dieyi, a male dan actor who clings to love despite being tossed by the times, and Gong Li appears as a high-class courtesan who becomes his love rival. A 4K version was released in 2023, marking the 30th anniversary of the film's production and 20 years after Leslie Cheung's death.
title_norm:fargo: An unconventional crime suspense film by the Coen Brothers, laced with black humor. In snow-covered Fargo, Minnesota, car salesman Jerry, drowning in debt, plots to have his wife Jean kidnapped to extort a ransom from her wealthy father. But when the two hired kidnappers shoot a police officer and a witness, the case spirals out of control. Winner of multiple film awards, including the Academy Awards for Best Original Screenplay and Best Actress.
title_norm:fever ビーバー！: A unique action-entertainment spectacle depicting a life-or-death struggle between a hunter and countless mascot-suit beavers in a surreal black-and-white world, garnering acclaim at fantastic film festivals worldwide. After losing his job as an apple cider salesman, a man turns to hunting forest animals. When he meets the woman of his destiny at a fur trading post, he realizes he needs hundreds of beaver pelts to win her father’s approval for their courtship. The hunter sets various traps to catch his prey, but the beavers aren't about to go down without a fight. Set against the backdrop of a sub-zero forest, the curtain rises on an epic battle between the hunter and an army of beavers. Directed, written, and produced by Mike Cheslik, who is also a prominent YouTuber with over 1.6 million subscribers.
title_norm:film socialisme: A visual poem by French master Jean-Luc Godard, depicting modern Europe with overwhelming visual beauty and masterful editing. It is Godard's first feature film shot entirely in digital, his first in six years since 'Our Music.' Set on a luxury cruise ship touring the Mediterranean, it consists of three movements: the first movement 'Such Things' depicts human drama over gold lost during the Spanish Civil War; the second movement 'Where to, Europe' is a political comedy about a family living in the French countryside; and the third movement 'We Humans' explores history and culture across six locations related to human history, using countless quotations and collages. Utilizing various video formats and freely incorporating images, words, sounds, and even digital noise, it is depicted with overwhelming density and speed, full of rebellious spirit. Musician Patti Smith, guitarist Lenny Kaye, and philosopher Alain Badiou appear as themselves. Screened as part of the special screening series 'Jean-Luc Godard in the 21st Century: Our Films 2001-2010' (starting June 20, 2026, at Theater Image Forum Shibuya and other locations nationwide).
title_norm:fires on the plain: An anti-war film adapted from Shōhei Ōoka's novel of the same name, scripted by Kazuo Wada and directed by Kon Ichikawa. Abandoned by both the hospital and his unit, Tamura wanders the island of Leyte on the Philippine front. He reunites with fellow retreating soldiers in front of a hospital, but when the hospital comes under shelling, Tamura flees alone. With no food and having lost his comrades, Tamura survives by eating grass. Eventually he reunites with his former comrades Nagamatsu and Yasuda, who had been separated from him. The two call the soldiers they killed 'monkeys' and have been eating their flesh...
title_norm:fireworks, should we see it f: Summer vacation. Norimichi, an elementary school student, is invited by his classmate Nazuna—who is set to transfer schools after the summer due to her parents' divorce—to go to the fireworks festival with her that night. However, Nazuna is planning to run away from home, and Norimichi finds himself being dragged along. Meanwhile, Norimichi's friends, including Junichi, have decided to go to the festival to see for themselves whether fireworks look round or flat when viewed from the side. Nazuna remains determined to carry out her plan to run away.
title_norm:fish story: Directed by Yoshihiro Nakamura, who helmed the film adaptation of Kotaro Isaka's "A Duck and a Coin Locker," this film adapts another of Isaka's short stories of the same name. It's an ensemble drama depicting how a song that received almost no attention upon its release transcends time to save the world from extinction. In the 1970s, the ahead-of-its-time punk band "Gekirin" disbanded, leaving behind the song "FISH STORY," which was not understood by the world. Years later, in the 1980s, a timid college student who happens upon the record takes desperate action to save a woman attacked by thugs. Further in time, in the 2000s, a ferry cook aspiring to be a hero saves a high school student caught up in a sea-jacking during a school trip. And in 2012, as humanity faces extinction from a comet collision, a record shop owner also holds "FISH STORY" in his hands. Ito Atsushi and Kora Kengo play the members of the band "Gekirin," Hamada Gaku plays the timid college student, Tabe Mikako plays the high school student caught in the sea-jacking, Moriyama Mirai plays the cook, and Omori Nao plays the record shop owner. The screenplay is by Tamio Hayashi, who later worked with Nakamura on "Golden Slumber." Music production was handled by Kazuyoshi Saito. In 2026, 17 years after its 2009 release, it will be digitally re-released.
title_norm:five graves to cairo: A rare action thriller from Billy Wilder, depicting British soldiers fighting to survive. After the British army suffers defeat at the hands of Rommel's German forces, Corporal Bramble, who escaped death, disguises himself as a hotel waiter who died the previous day and attempts to make contact with German soldiers. Fortunately, the deceased waiter was a German spy, allowing him to leak classified information to the Allies. Erich von Stroheim, a director Wilder had long admired, appears in the role of a general.
title_norm:flames of blood: The turbulent life of gambler Senkichi, who continues to love one woman. Set in Kyoto at the end of the Edo period, this powerful portrayal of unadorned love between a man and a woman stands as Tai Kato's final, crowning live-action film.
title_norm:flowers of mold: An unconventional romance film starring Kim Jae-kyung, former leader of the South Korean girl group RAINBOW who now works as an actress. Based on the short story 'Flowers of Mold' by Ha Seong-nan, an award-winning author in Korean literary circles, the film depicts a woman who tries to understand others through 'trash,' the most private and defenseless traces of a person. Ji-su, who carries deep romantic trauma, secretly collects and files away other people's trash, believing that 'one's true self appears in what they throw away.' One day, she finds a trash bag that has been carefully sorted and discarded, and upon discovering it belongs to her neighbor, a man named U-je, she approaches him using fragmentary information gleaned from the trash. The two gradually open their hearts to each other, but one night, U-je witnesses Ji-su entering her apartment with a trash bag and discovers her secret. Kim Jae-kyung passionately portrays the protagonist Ji-su, who cannot trust others due to past relationship experiences, with Hyun-woo from the TV drama 'Law School' co-starring as the neighbor U-je. Directed by Sim Hye-jung, who gained attention for her previous work 'A Bedsore,' the film won the CGV Award and the Watcha's Pick Feature Film Award at the Jeonju International Film Festival 2023.
title_norm:foggy tale: Directed by Taiwan's Yu-Hsun Chen, known for "The Girl Who Leapt Through Time" and "The Tropical Fish," this is a story of hope and rebirth set against the backdrop of the "White Terror" era in 1950s Taiwan, when many citizens were arrested and executed on suspicion of being anti-government. In the 1950s, under martial law in Taiwan. A young girl named A-Yue, living in Chiayi, learns that her brother, captured as an anti-government element, has been executed in Taipei. With a small amount of money and her brother's keepsake watch in hand, she heads to Taipei alone, only to find that a hefty fee is required to claim his body. At her wit's end, she is tricked by a suspicious man and nearly sold into a brothel, but is rescued by a rickshaw puller named Zhao Gongdao. Originally from Guangdong, China, he came to Taiwan as a soldier for the Nationalist army and has been unable to return home, living hand-to-mouth ever since. Having lost his army comrades to the White Terror and finding no direction in life, Gongdao is moved by A-Yue's determination and decides to lend her a hand. Caitlin Fang ("A Girl from America") plays A-Yue, Will Or ("The Staggering Girl") plays Zhao Gongdao, and popular Taiwanese singer and actor 9m88 co-stars. The film won four awards, including Best Feature Film, at the 62nd Golden Horse Awards in 2025.
title_norm:foreign affair: Set in the ruins of post-war Berlin, this film depicts a romantic rivalry involving a playboy American officer. An American female politician heading to Germany is entrusted by a woman with a gift for Captain Pringle. The woman is one of the captain's girlfriends, but upon receiving it, he immediately trades it for a mattress on the black market—so he can flirt with a German woman he has a crush on. Marlene Dietrich plays a Nazi singer, and composer Frederick Hollander, who handled the music, appears as a pianist.
title_norm:forte フォルテ: A music horror film by director Gimbo Kim, known for numerous music videos and short films. Set in the music industry, it depicts a young person possessed by the desire for success and obsession with creation. Yeong-ji, who moved to the city believing in her musical talent, is hired by the composing studio "Forte," which she had admired. However, the actual work turns out to be behind-the-scenes labor as a "ghost composer" whose name never appears publicly. While working with a sense of suffocation, the mysterious death of a colleague reveals unsettling rumors about the studio and the existence of a "cursed grand piano." Yeong-ji, who has been continuously suppressed, gradually becomes consumed by obsession and madness for creation. Officially invited to the 27th Bucheon International Fantastic Film Festival and the 2024 Busan International Film Festival. Released theatrically as part of the "Hangeul New Wave Film Festival 2026," a special screening of Korean indie genre films.
title_norm:four nights of a dreamer: Jacques, an aspiring painter, saves a young woman named Marthe from throwing herself into the Seine one night. She had a lover who left for America a year ago, and that very night was when they had promised to reunite. Jacques finds her, sunk in anguish, beautiful. Driven by a fierce impulse of love, he forces himself to remain calm, hoping her heart will drift away from her lover, while feeling guilt over this. Like the 1957 version, this is a modern adaptation of Dostoevsky's famous tragic love story, a poignant work revealing Bresson's awakened worldview. Visconti's romanticism is absent here; the young man's blind love is brutally exposed as he pours out his feelings into a mini tape recorder, a habit of his, making it painful to watch.
title_norm:four trails: The Hong Kong Four Trails Ultra Challenge, commonly known as HK4TUC, requires runners to consecutively complete four trail courses in Hong Kong and reach the finish line within a time limit of 72 hours (3 days). The total course length is 298 km, comparable to the distance between Tokyo and Nagoya, with a cumulative elevation gain of 14,500 m, equivalent to seven full marathons or two ascents of Mount Everest. Furthermore, participants must procure their own water and food from shops along the way, and strict rules prohibit the use of poles or portable music players, which would be advantageous on the undulating mountain paths. It is an event of extreme physical and mental challenge. This film captures 18 runners who took on the HK4TUC pushing their limits, set against the beautiful natural landscapes of Hong Kong, rarely seen before. The director is Robin Lee, a British director born and raised in Hong Kong. The film began a limited release in Hong Kong at the end of 2024, but word-of-mouth spread rapidly and the number of screens increased sharply. It gained further attention when the major star Chow Yun-fat, known for the 'A Better Tomorrow' series and 'Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon', highly praised it, saying 'every Hong Kong person should watch it'. Supported not only by sports enthusiasts but also by general film fans, it became the biggest surprise hit of 2025, attracting 150,000 viewers. Additionally, it has won numerous awards, including the Best New Director Award at the 43rd Hong Kong Film Awards, the Audience Award at the 22nd Hong Kong Asian Film Festival, the Recommended Film Award at the 31st Hong Kong Film Critics Society Awards, and the Jury Special Award at the 2025 Hong Kong Directors' Guild Awards, earning high praise as a documentary.
title_norm:fragments of the last will: A biographical drama starring Kazunari Ninomiya as real-life Japanese prisoner of war Yamamoto Hanao, held in a Siberian labor camp (Laguerre). Based on Jun Henmi's nonfiction novel "The Last Letter from the Laguerre," directed by Takahisa Zeze, known for "Those Who Were Not Protected" and "The Thread." In 1945, after World War II, Japanese POWs in Siberian camps faced brutal conditions—temperatures dropping to -40°C, minimal food, and forced heavy labor, with many dying. Amid this, Yamamoto Hanao believes he will return to his wife and children in Japan, encouraging those around him. His selfless actions and strong faith ignite a flame of hope in many prisoners' hearts. Kitagawa Keiko plays Yamamoto's wife Mojimi, with a star-studded cast including Matsuzaka Tori, Nakajima Kento, Kiryū Kentarō, and Yasuda Ken as fellow prisoners.
title_norm:frankie freako: From Steven Kostanski, the mad genius director of "Psycho Goreman" (2020) and member of Canada's notorious effects collective Astron-6, who has contributed special effects to Hollywood blockbusters like "Resident Evil: Retribution" (2012) and "Pacific Rim" (2013). His two latest films, "Frankie Freako" and "Deathstalker," will be released sequentially in Japan starting July 3rd at Cinemart Shinjuku and other theaters nationwide. Kostanski, who wrote and directed both films, is known for his unique creature designs reminiscent of classics like "E.T." (1982), "Gremlins" (1984), and "The Goonies" (1985), blending 80s-style monster panic with absurdist black humor, creating a devoted fanbase. These new films bring his signature style to Japan. "Frankie Freako" is a monster freak comedy that extensively uses unique puppets to achieve a visual style straight out of a comic book, bursting with Kostanski's unique worldview. The cast includes fellow Astron-6 members Conor Sweeney and Adam Brooks. Synopsis: Connor, a workaholic, has a dilemma: he is respected by neither his boss, his colleagues, nor his wife. One night, he sees a commercial on a shady late-night show for a party hosted by Frankie Freako and impulsively calls the number. Suddenly, a goblin-like creature named Frankie and his troublesome friends invade his home, trashing the place. Connor struggles to stop Frankie and the rampaging monsters. However, this chaos unexpectedly leads him on a journey of self-discovery.
title_norm:frankie the milkman: A cheerful young man moves to Tokyo to help at a relative's milk shop and struggles to outdo his business rivals. A film adaptation of a popular radio drama, this is an early representative work of Frankie Sakai, known as a hidden gem of slapstick comedy.
title_norm:fujiko: Set in Shizuoka during the 1970s and 80s, this human drama portrays a single mother navigating a turbulent era, searching for her own way to live while walking forward with strength. In 1977, during a fierce storm that causes a blackout at the hospital, Fujiko gives birth to her daughter Mari. But her joy as a new mother is short-lived; she suffers unreasonable treatment from her husband's family, and her infant daughter Mari is taken away by her mother-in-law and sister-in-law. With the help of her own mother Chiyo, Fujiko manages to get Mari back and, defying opposition from those around her, decides to raise Mari as a single mother. Buffeted by the waves of the times, she refuses to be defeated by society, seeks freedom, and desperately fights to survive with the support of those around her. Yuki Katayama ('The Burning of the Crimson') stars as Fujiko. YOU plays the spiteful mother-in-law Toshiko, Lily Franky plays Sasaki, whom Fujiko meets through her insurance sales job, Tsuyoshi Ujiki plays Fujiko's ailing father, Keiko Takeshita plays Hatayama, the director of the daycare center Fujiko turns to, Issey Ogata plays Oishi, an old friend of Fujiko's father who runs a soba shop, Kayoko Kishimoto plays Fujiko's mother Chiyo, and MEGUMI plays Nagura, the owner of the coffee shop where Fujiko works. Directed and based on an original story by Taichi Kimura, who has directed numerous music videos and commercials and gained attention with his 2023 feature debut 'AFTERGLOWS'. MEGUMI handled planning and production.
title_norm:full moon in paris: The fourth film in Éric Rohmer's 'Comedies and Proverbs' series. Louise, an interior designer, lives with her architect boyfriend Rémi in a suburban Paris apartment. The serious Rémi and the free-spirited Louise are constantly bickering. Feeling stifled in her life with Rémi, Louise rents her own room in Paris and starts going out with her married best friend Octave... The film delicately portrays a woman's emotions as she wavers between two men and two homes. Lead actress Pascale Ogier won the Best Actress award at the Venice Film Festival for this role, but tragically died shortly after at the young age of 25. The cast also includes Fabrice Luchini from 'Claire's Knee' and Tchéky Karyo from 'Nikita.'
title_norm:future history of the elephan: A music documentary that uncovers the truth behind the mysterious music collective 'Elephant 6,' born in the late 1980s American South and sparking a unique movement in the 90s indie scene. In the late 1980s, a group of high school friends in Ruston, Louisiana, began experimenting with home recordings using whatever instruments they could find. Sharing a love for psychedelic music, they eventually moved to Denver, Colorado, and Athens, Georgia, sticking to their DIY ethos by lining cheap apartments with aluminum foil to create studios. From this emerged bands like 'The Apples in Stereo,' 'Neutral Milk Hotel,' and 'Olivia Tremor Control,' which formed the core of 'Elephant 6,' later joined by many others. What started as a friendship-driven project, fueled by a rebellious spirit against the mainstream music of the time, grew in support and sparked an unprecedented movement in the American music scene. Director Chad Stockfress, a friend of Robert Schneider from 'The Apples in Stereo,' spent about ten years interviewing participants and fans. Elijah Wood (from 'The Lord of the Rings') and David Cross (from 'Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind') appear as commentators. This long-anticipated title, known early on to some Japanese fans through connections with Keigo Oyamada and Kahimi Karie, will be released in Japan on July 31, 2026, in a version with added live footage.
title_norm:g.i. samurai: Led by Lieutenant Yoshiaki Iba, 21 members of the Japan Ground Self-Defense Force, armed with modern weapons, suddenly time-slip along with their supply depot to the Sengoku period while en route to an exercise. As they stand bewildered, Nagao Heizo Kagetora arrives with his retainers to meet them. Upon first seeing Iba, Kagetora takes an instant liking to him, calling him "a kindred spirit," and is drawn to their unfamiliar clothing and weapons, hoping to recruit them. Iba and his soldiers struggle to accept the reality of their time slip. However, after encountering Kagetora and being attacked by guerrilla forces of a rival feudal lord—resulting in a comrade's death—and witnessing Kagetora's battle firsthand, they are forced to come to terms with having arrived in the Sengoku period.
title_norm:ga ga glory to the heroes: One of four dark sci-fi works by Piotr Szulkin, a pioneer of dystopian science fiction in Poland, created under the strict censorship of the socialist regime in the late 1970s and 1980s. With a style blending fierce satire and extreme surrealism, the film depicts the miserable existence of people living under corrupt power and bureaucracy. A man trapped on a giant space station is forced, like other prisoners, to volunteer for exploration of a distant planet. Landing on Planet Australia 458, he is welcomed as a hero, but soon realizes that freedom comes at a high price. His violent life is broadcast live for the entertainment of the planet's inhabitants. The film had its Japanese theatrical premiere in 2026 as part of the special screening series "Polish Dark Sci-Fi: The End of Civilization Tetralogy" (starting February 21, 2026, at Theater Image Forum).
title_norm:ga, ga. chwała bohaterom: One of four dark sci-fi works by Piotr Szulkin, a pioneer of dystopian science fiction in Poland, created under the strict censorship of the socialist regime in the late 1970s and 1980s. With a style blending fierce satire and extreme surrealism, the film depicts the miserable existence of people living under corrupt power and bureaucracy. A man trapped on a giant space station is forced, like other prisoners, to volunteer for exploration of a distant planet. Landing on Planet Australia 458, he is welcomed as a hero, but soon realizes that freedom comes at a high price. His violent life is broadcast live for the entertainment of the planet's inhabitants. The film had its Japanese theatrical premiere in 2026 as part of the special screening series "Polish Dark Sci-Fi: The End of Civilization Tetralogy" (starting February 21, 2026, at Theater Image Forum).
title_norm:galaxy express 999 the movie: The first theatrical film in the classic sci-fi anime series "Galaxy Express 999," based on Leiji Matsumoto's manga of the same name. Based on the "Andromeda Arc" from the original manga, it features character designs different from the TV series. In a future where humans can achieve eternal life by replacing their bodies with machines, the mechanical bodies are expensive and unaffordable for the poor. Rumors spread that riding the Galaxy Express 999 can take you to a planet where you can get a free mechanical body. The boy Tetsurō Hoshino heads to the metropolis Megalopolis, where the 999 stops, with his mother, but they are attacked by the Mechanical Count's human hunt, and his mother is killed. Living in the slums of Megalopolis, Tetsurō one day receives a pass for the 999 from the mysterious beauty Maetel and embarks on a journey into space with her. The theme song by Godiego was also a huge hit.
title_norm:game of seduction: An erotic film directed by Roger Vadim, based on the sensual novel 'Les Liaisons Dangereuses'. Set in 19th-century France, it depicts the affair between a playboy count and a married woman. The bewitching performances of two charismatic actresses are captivating.
title_norm:gattaca: A sci-fi suspense film starring Ethan Hawke, Uma Thurman, and Jude Law. In a near future where 'valids' born through genetic engineering dominate society, Vincent, born naturally, lives a life of discrimination as an 'invalid.' He has dreamed of becoming an astronaut since childhood, but it is a profession only permitted for valids. One day, through a DNA broker, Vincent purchases the valid identity of Jerome, a former swimmer now paralyzed from the waist down. Posing as Jerome, Vincent joins the space corporation 'Gattaca' and, through sheer effort, is eventually selected as an astronaut for a Titan exploration mission, but... This is the directorial and screenwriting debut of Andrew Niccol.
title_norm:ghost of ueno: Set in Ueno Park in Tokyo, this human mystery, a Japan-China-Korea co-production, explores human connections while focusing on "disappearance" as a way of life. A homeless man known as "Gojo" in Ueno has died. No one knows his real name, what he did in life, or why he ended up in a tent in the park. Satsuki, a social worker, with the help of Toshi, a man living in the park after losing his wife, searches through the homeless network to uncover Gojo's identity, using his diary as a clue. Eventually, the existence of a woman comes to light, and it's revealed that Gojo had cut ties with his family. This fact also profoundly shakes Satsuki's own life. Kadowaki Mugi stars as Satsuki, a social worker carrying a certain loss from her own past, and Takenaka Naoto co-stars as Toshi, a homeless man who accompanies Satsuki. The director and screenwriter is Wang Qii, who spent his childhood in Japan and studied filmmaking in the UK. Wayne Wang, known for directing "Smoke" and "The Joy Luck Club," is credited as co-writer and project planner.
title_norm:gimtinė: Set in Lithuania just after its independence, this drama quietly observes memories, conflicts, and the lives of people caught between shifting eras through the eyes of an American-born boy visiting the country with his Lithuanian mother. Director Tomas Vengris, making his feature-length debut, draws on his own experience growing up as the son of Lithuanian immigrants in Washington, D.C., to delicately portray the reality of people tossed about by changes in territory and political systems. In 1992, mother and son Victoria and Kovas arrive from America to Lithuania, which has just gained independence from the Soviet Union. As a child, Victoria was separated from her family under Soviet occupation and lost her home and land. In Lithuania, where control shifted from Nazi Germany to the Soviet Union, people's freedom continued to waver under different regimes. Returning to her homeland after 20 years, Victoria seeks to reclaim her lost family land and start a new life with her son, but finds a Russian family already living there. Faced with the harsh reality that reclaiming the land is not easy, her ideal of a fresh start in Lithuania begins to quietly unravel. Martas Metlevskis, an American-born actor of Lithuanian descent, plays the boy Kovas, and renowned Lithuanian actress Sevilija Janušauskaitė plays his mother Victoria.
title_norm:glasses: On a break from life, Taeko visits a southern seaside town and stays at a strange inn called Hamada. However, in a small beach town with nothing to see or do, she is pushed around by the overly laid-back residents and, unable to bear it, leaves Hamada—but... From the director Naoko Ogigami and star Satomi Kobayashi of "Kamome Diner," the hit film about slow-living daily life set in a Japanese restaurant in Finland, comes a gentle portrayal of people re-examining their lives, this time set on a southern beach.
title_norm:gloaming in luomu:
Winner of the Best Film Award in the Competition Section of the 30th Busan International Film Festival.

The traces of a lost lover, and a path that recedes the more you search—another time flowing through Luomu, an ancient town in Sichuan Province.

A postcard arrives from Wang, a lover who vanished without a trace three years ago, bearing only the words "Twilight in Luomu." Bai, who worked as a dancer in a theater troupe, follows this single clue to an inn in the ancient town of Luomu, Sichuan. There she meets Liu, the inn's proprietress; Huang, who has harbored feelings for Liu for twenty years; and a stream of passing travelers. In this town, once prosperous from trade and now flowing with quiet time, what she encounters is not Wang himself, but the traces of the time he left behind. The faint sound of a distant whistle echoes, and before Bai, who wanders the ancient town, Wang appears and disappears like a phantom. One day, Bai learns that a man resembling Wang was reportedly seen at a mountain temple—

Released simultaneously with its sister film "Chunshu," shot with the same cast prior to this work.
title_norm:go: High school senior Sugihara has South Korean nationality, but usually doesn't think about it. He starts dating a girl named Sakurai and thinks he must confess his nationality to her someday, when a tragedy befalls a close friend of the same nationality. Based on the Naoki Prize-winning novel "GO" by Kinichi Kaneshiro. Directed by Isao Yukisada, who won the International Critics' Award at the previous year's Busan Film Festival for "Himawari." Screenplay by Kankuro Kudo of the TV series "Ikebukuro West Gate Park." Co-starring popular young actors including Yosuke Kubozuka from that show and Ko Shibasaki from "Battle Royale."
title_norm:godai the wunderkind: A historical ensemble drama starring Haruma Miura, depicting the life of Tomoatsu Godai, a visionary who built the foundations of modern Japan's economy and was hailed as a 'Tengaramon' (a person of extraordinary talent). Written by Eriko Komatsu and directed by Mitsutoshi Tanaka, the film presents an original story. In the late Edo period, Japan is shocked by Perry's arrival. Young samurai Saisuke Godai (later Tomoatsu), sensing the dawn of a new era, ignores internal conflicts over expulsion or opening of the country and looks to the world. After meeting the courtesan Haru, he is driven by the desire for 'free dreams' and joins forces with Ryoma Sakamoto, Yataro Iwasaki, Hirobumi Ito, and others to build a nation where everyone can dream. Shohei Miura plays Ryoma Sakamoto, Godai's ally; Takanori Nishikawa plays Yataro Iwasaki, who later founded the Mitsubishi conglomerate; Yuki Morinaga plays a young Hirobumi Ito, who becomes the first Prime Minister; and Mei Nagano plays the courtesan Haru.
title_norm:godzilla: A landmark tokusatsu kaiju film produced and released by Toho in 1954. Ships are sinking one after another in the Pacific Ocean. The few survivors report sightings of a giant monster. An investigation team formed by paleontologist Dr. Yamane, his daughter and assistant Emiko, and her fiancé Hideto Ogata, head of a salvage company, is dispatched to Odo Island near the incident site, where the monster eventually appears. Named "Godzilla" after an old island legend, the monster is believed to be an ancient creature that survived in secret, awakened by the radiation from repeated hydrogen bomb tests, and countermeasures are devised. However, humans are helpless against its immense power, and Godzilla lands in Tokyo, turning the city into a sea of fire. Meanwhile, Dr. Yamane's beloved student, scientist Serizawa, has realized a terrible invention that could be effective against Godzilla. Fearing its future misuse, Serizawa hesitates to use it... A Hollywood version directed by Roland Emmerich was also produced in 1998. To commemorate the 60th anniversary in 2014 and the production/release of the second Hollywood version "GODZILLA" (directed by Gareth Edwards), this original film was revived as the "Godzilla 60th Anniversary Digital Remastered Version."
title_norm:golden kamuy assault on abash: The second film in the live-action adaptation of Satoru Noda's popular manga "Golden Kamuy," serving as a sequel to the 2024 film and the WOWOW drama series "Golden Kamuy: The Hunt of the Tattooed Prisoners in Hokkaido." Former soldier Saichi Sugimoto, known as "Immortal Sugimoto," learns of a vast gold hoard stolen from the Ainu people. The mysterious culprit, "Noppera-bo," hid the gold before his capture, tattooing the locations on the bodies of prisoners and engineering their escape. The tattoos form a single code when combined across 24 men. Sugimoto meets Ainu girl Asirpa, whose father was killed by the gold thief, and they join forces. Meanwhile, Lieutenant Tsurumi of the Imperial Japanese Army's 7th Division, who aims to conquer Hokkaido, and Toshizo Hijikata, who should have died in the Boshin War, also seek the gold, sparking a fierce battle for the tattooed prisoners. The stage moves to Abashiri Prison, where Noppera-bo is incarcerated. Returning cast members include Kento Yamazaki as Sugimoto and Anna Yamada as Asirpa, with new additions: Yu Inaba as Private Usami of the 7th Division, Sohma Wada as Chief Guard Kadokura, and Jun Kunimura as Navy Rear Admiral Heiji Koido, father of "Satsuma's Prince" Otonoshin Koido. Directed by Kenji Katagiri, who helmed episodes 3 and 5-8 of the drama series.
title_norm:good boy: 'Something is wrong...' The one who notices the anomaly is not a human, but a pet dog named Indie. Staring intently at a corner of an empty room. Barking in response to something. The fear that lies beyond these mysterious behaviors of pet dogs, which everyone can relate to, is depicted by director Ben Leonberg in his feature debut, after a three-year production period. It premiered at SXSW (South by Southwest Film Festival) in 2025 and won the Best Dog Acting Award. It garnered attention as an innovative horror film told from a dog's perspective, and as soon as the trailer was released, it became a hot topic on social media. Originally scheduled for a limited release, it was hastily expanded to 1,650 screens and achieved a 90% rating on Rotten Tomatoes. Praised as 'one of the most moving horror films of 2025', it made the US top 10 for two consecutive weeks. At the 2026 Astra Film Awards in the 'Horror or Thriller' category, Indie (the dog), the star of this film, achieved the historic feat of winning the Best Performance Award for an animal actor, defeating a stellar lineup including Alfie Williams ('28 Years Later'), Ethan Hawke ('The Black Phone 2'), and Alison Brie ('Together'). Indie is a retriever dog living with his owner Todd in an apartment. Recently, Todd's health has been poor, and one day he vomits blood. Todd's sister Vera, who happens to visit the apartment, rushes him to the hospital. After being discharged, Todd takes Indie and moves into his grandfather's house, which has been vacant since his grandfather's mysterious death. Todd borrows a backup generator from a neighbor and spends his time with a little light and watching old home videos of his grandfather, but Indie senses something strange in the house. On the phone with Vera, Todd wonders if there is a curse on the house and his grandfather. Of course, Indie doesn't understand, but he feels something is wrong, hears strange noises, and senses a shadow drifting from the corner of the room. The evil presence worsens Todd's condition, and Indie desperately tries to protect Todd from the eerie something...
