title_norm:killer of sheep: The feature debut of Charles Burnett, a filmmaker who quietly revolutionized American cinema by depicting the daily lives and humanity of African Americans, released in 1977. It portrays the everyday existence of African American workers living on the fringes of Los Angeles with a realistic gaze and poetic visual beauty. Set in the Watts district of Los Angeles in the early 1970s, still bearing the scars of the Watts riots. Stan works at a sheep slaughterhouse to support his wife and two children, living an empty daily life. Exhausted physically and mentally by labor and poverty, he withdraws into himself, while his wife grows increasingly lonely. Directed by Burnett as his graduate thesis film while a student at UCLA Film School, it was shot in Watts using a mostly amateur cast of people he knew. Long unreleased due to music copyright issues, it finally had a theatrical release in the US in 2007. The 4K restoration completed in 2025 replaces the music in the final scene with Dinah Washington's "Unforgettable," as Burnett originally intended. It won the FIPRESCI Prize at the Forum section of the 31st Berlin International Film Festival in 1981. In Japan, it will have its first theatrical release in the 4K restored version as part of the special screening series "Charles Burnett: Everyday Blues" (starting February 7, 2026, at Theater Image Forum).
title_norm:kin dza dza!: A deadpan sci-fi comedy made in Soviet-era Georgia in 1986, which became a huge hit in the USSR at the time. One day, a student named Gedevan asks construction engineer Mashkov for help, looking troubled, saying, 'There are some men over there who claim to be aliens.' Mashkov, who doesn't believe in aliens, presses a button on a space travel device the men were holding, and in the next instant, Mashkov and Gedevan are warped to the planet Pluke in the Kin-Dza-Dza Nebula, far from Earth. There, for some reason, Earth matches are extremely valuable, and the two try to use the value of matches to somehow return to Earth... Culturally popular in Japan as well, it was first introduced at the 'Soviet SF Film Festival' held in Tokyo in 1989, later released in a new print in 2001 and a digital remaster in August 2016. In May 2021, to coincide with the release of the animated version 'Ku! Kin-Dza-Dza,' the live-action film had its fourth theatrical release.
title_norm:kind hearts and coronets: A suspense comedy that follows the trail of a serial murder spree by a young man burning with ambition and a thirst for revenge, laced with biting black humor. One of the 'Ealing Comedies,' a series of comedy films produced at Ealing Studios in the UK from the late 1930s to the mid-1950s, directed by Robert Hamer, known for 'It Always Rains on Sunday.' The story is told in flashback form as Louis, a young man of aristocratic blood from the D'Ascoyne family, writes his memoirs in his prison cell, recounting how he systematically murders his relatives to avenge his mother's disownment and reclaim his status. The renowned actor Alec Guinness, known for his role as Obi-Wan Kenobi in 'Star Wars' and 'The Bridge on the River Kwai,' plays all eight members of the D'Ascoyne family who are killed by Louis. Dennis Price plays the protagonist Louis, and Joan Greenwood leaves a strong impression as the cold, calculating heroine. This film is part of the special screening series 'The Golden Age of British Ealing Comedies' (June 20–July 17, 2026, at Shinjuku K's Cinema).
title_norm:kingdom 5: Set during China's Spring and Autumn period, this is the fifth live-action film adaptation of Yasuhisa Hara's popular manga series 'Kingdom,' depicting the grand story of Shin, a boy who dreams of becoming the world's greatest general, and the young king Ying Zheng, who aims to unify China. This film adapts the beloved 'Coalition Army Arc' from the original manga, where Qin clashes with the six other states. Three years after the Battle of Mayang, where Qin lost the great general Wang Qi, Shin, who has inherited Wang Qi's will and continued to grow, has been promoted to commander of a thousand men. Meanwhile, under the strategy of Zhao's prime minister Li Mu, all states except Qin unite to form a 'Coalition Army' of 500,000 troops, launching an invasion of Qin. At the capital city of Xianyang's palace, Ying Zheng and his court scramble to respond, but faced with an unprecedented force, Qin is pushed to the brink of national collapse. Shin, along with fellow young generals Meng Tian and Wang Ben, heads to Hangu Pass, the gateway to Qin, where representative Qin generals such as Biao Gong, Meng Wu, Teng, Wang Jian, and Huan Qi gather. On the other side, the Coalition Army, led by Lord Chunshen of Chu, assembles powerful warriors from various states, including the fierce Zhao general Wan Ji, who harbors a grudge against Qin for trampling his homeland. Familiar series cast members return, including Kento Yamazaki as Shin, Ryō Yoshizawa as Ying Zheng, and Shun Oguri as Li Mu. New additions to the lavish cast include Jun Shison as Meng Tian, Fūju Kamio as Wang Ben, Kenji Sakaguchi as Huan Qi, and Takumi Saitō as Lord Chunshen. Director Shinsuke Sato, who has helmed all previous films in the series, returns, and original manga author Yasuhisa Hara, who has been involved in the script since the first film, also wrote the screenplay for this installment.
title_norm:kiss me deadly: One night, private detective Mike Hammer picks up a woman named Christina and lets her into his car, but is suddenly attacked by three men and loses consciousness. When he comes to, Mike finds himself in a hospital bed. According to his secretary Velda, Mike and Christina were driven into a river along with the car, and Christina died. Sensing something behind it all, Mike begins to investigate Christina's background.
title_norm:kneecap: A semi-autobiographical drama tracing the birth of KNEECAP, a hip-hop trio from Northern Ireland who rap in Irish—a language not officially recognized in the region until 2022—and draw attention with their radical lyrics and performances, set against the backdrop of protests demanding official status for the Irish language. With humor and stylish direction, it portrays working-class youth in West Belfast, still scarred by the Northern Ireland conflict. Nisha (MC name: Móglaí Bap), a drug dealer born and raised in Belfast, and his childhood friend Liam (MC name: Mo Chara) are caught in a drug deal. Liam refuses to speak English and remains defiant. Music teacher JJ (MC name: DJ Próvai), sent as an interpreter, sees Irish lyrics in Liam's notebook and recognizes his talent. The three start rapping in Irish to reclaim their suppressed identity and linguistic rights... The three KNEECAP members make their acting debut playing themselves, with Michael Fassbender co-starring. The film won numerous awards worldwide, including the Audience Award in the NEXT section at the 2024 Sundance Film Festival.

title_norm:kokuho: A human drama depicting the tumultuous life of a man born into a yakuza family who dedicates his life to the path of art as a Kabuki actor. A talked-about sensation that has taken the Japanese film world by storm, finally screening!
title_norm:kono basho: A Japan-Philippines co-produced drama set in Rikuzentakata City, Iwate Prefecture, over a decade after the Great East Japan Earthquake, portraying the emotional recovery and identity rebirth of two half-sisters of different cultures and races. Reina Hashimoto, a 20-year-old art student living in Rikuzentakata, suddenly loses her beloved father and is overwhelmed with grief. Then appears Ella, her half-sister seven years older, who arrives from the Philippines. Reina is confused and unable to understand why Ella, who has been out of contact for so long, suddenly shows up after their father's death. The sisters, differing in culture and race, repeatedly clash and seek understanding as they confront their emotional wounds and reconsider their feelings toward family and homeland. Starring Arisa Nakano as Reina, who won the Best Actress award at the 48th Gawad Urian Awards in the Philippines—the first foreign actor to do so—and Filipino actor Gabby Padilla as her sister Ella. The cast also includes Reiko Kataoka, Cheryl Ichikawa, Satoshi Nikaido, and Sho Yakumaru. Directed and written by Filipino filmmaker Jaime Pacena II, who has visited the Tohoku region as a visual artist since 2010 and maintained ties with local communities, in his feature-length directorial debut.
title_norm:kraft der utopie – leben mit: A documentary about Chandigarh, the planned city built in India by Le Corbusier, the master of modernist architecture who left behind numerous legendary buildings. In 1947, India and Pakistan gained independence, and Punjab was divided between the two countries. With the state capital Lahore belonging to Pakistan, India needed to build a new capital. Prime Minister Nehru wanted a city symbolizing faith in the future and democracy, entrusting Le Corbusier with designing the planned city of Chandigarh. Born in the wilderness at the foot of the Himalayas, the "Shining City" of Chandigarh aimed to be a human-centered utopia where natural order and modern technology were in perfect harmony, symbolizing a new India. How has this city transformed 70 years after its birth? The film traces the buildings and their history, while residents—architects, urban activists, and artists—discuss the challenges Chandigarh faces and its enduring charm. Screened as part of the special program "Le Corbusier and Doshi: Modernism in India" (from May 1, 2026, at Eurospace in Tokyo and other theaters nationwide).
title_norm:kubo and the two strings: Long ago in Japan. A boy named Kubo, who lost his left eye, lives with his ailing mother. Playing a magical shamisen inherited from his mother, he earns a living by telling the story of a samurai named Hanzo in the village. On the night of the Bon festival, two 'Sisters of the Dark' who claim to be his mother's sisters appear and attack Kubo, but his mother tells him to gather his father's 'sword, armor, and helmet' and magically sends Kubo far away. Beginning his journey, Kubo makes allies of a female monkey and a male stag beetle while searching for the 'sword, armor, and helmet'.
title_norm:kubo／クボ 二本の弦の秘密: Long ago in Japan. A boy named Kubo, who lost his left eye, lives with his ailing mother. title_norm:kung fu: A wuxia fantasy action film directed by Taiwanese director Giddens Ko of 'The Secrets in the Lattice' and 'You Are the Apple of My Eye,' starring Ko Chen-tung, who collaborated with Ko on those two previous films. Director Giddens Ko, also active as a novelist, adapts his own internet-published novel 'Kung Fu' for the screen, weaving in homages to Hong Kong and Taiwanese wuxia films from the 1980s and 90s throughout. Underachieving high school student Yuan Zai and his best friend A Yi encounter a mysterious drifter, Huang Jun, who has awakened from a 500-year slumber. Witnessing Huang Jun's overwhelming martial arts prowess as a kung fu master, Yuan Zai and A Yi become his disciples. Their classmate Yi Jing, on whom Yuan Zai has a secret crush, also joins their training. They soon learn of the centuries-old feud between Huang Jun and his junior disciple Lan Jin, and uncover a momentous secret hidden within 'kung fu' that could shake heaven and earth. Ko Chen-tung plays Yuan Zai, Berant Zhu of 'Black Education' plays A Yi, Wang Jing of 'The Secrets in the Lattice' and 'The Return of the Condor Heroes' plays Yi Jing, veteran actor Tai Li-len plays the mysterious kung fu master Huang Jun, and Liu Kuan-ting of 'The Girl Who Robbed Time' plays Huang Jun's nemesis Lan Jin.
title_norm:kyoto hippocrates: A period drama set at the end of the Edo period, when traditional Chinese medicine doctors and Western-trained Dutch medicine doctors coexisted, starring Kuranosuke Sasaki as the village Dutch medicine doctor Daisuke Okura. In a village on the outskirts of Kyoto at the end of the Edo period, Daisuke Okura is a tolerant, curious Dutch medicine doctor who saves common people regardless of wealth or status. He is constantly engaged in fierce arguments with the Chinese medicine doctor Gensai, his sworn enemy. One day, Okura saves a hot-tempered young man named Shinsa through surgery, an event that drastically changes both their lives. Director Kazuki Omori, known for the ensemble drama 'Hippocrates' about Kyoto medical students, conceived this film based on the 1960 film 'Fundoshi Doctor,' which depicted a warm-hearted doctor and his wife, setting it in Kyoto at the end of the Edo period to portray the dawn of modern Japanese medicine. When Omori passed away in 2022 while preparing for filming, the project nearly became a phantom, but Akira Ogata, director of 'The Independent Teenage Chorus' and a former assistant director to Omori, carried on his will and brought it to completion. Kuranosuke Sasaki plays Okura. Takeshi Naito, who made his film debut in 'Hippocrates,' plays Okura's rival Gensai, and Akira Emoto, who played a resident doctor in 'Hippocrates,' appears as the mysterious samurai Danzo. Additionally, Shizuka Muroi, who made her film debut in Omori's 'Hear the Wind Sing,' provides narration, and Takuya Nishioka, who has known Omori since the 1970s, wrote the screenplay, with many cast and crew members associated with Kazuki Omori participating.
title_norm:kék pelikan: An animated film that visualizes an astonishing true story from 1990s Hungary in Eastern Europe, incorporating documentary materials. In 1990s Hungary, after the fall of the Iron Curtain opened the door to Western Europe, foreign travel was liberalized, and many people turned their eyes to the outside world. However, international train tickets were expensive and out of reach for ordinary people. Amidst this, three young men—intellectual Akos, fearless Pecha, and swimming enthusiast Laci—find a way to forge tickets. They dissolve the blue carbon ink "Pelikan Blue" from the company Pelikan, used on the tickets, with household detergent and rewrite the destinations. After enjoying overseas trips with forged tickets, they decide to distribute "tickets to freedom" to other young people in similar situations. The plan seems to go smoothly, but eventually, a police investigation begins, escalating into a major uproar that shakes the nation. Directed by László Csáki, known for his distinctive animation style, who conducted meticulous research over ten years and blends documentary materials like archival footage and interview audio with hand-drawn animation.
title_norm:köln 75: A music youth film that goes behind the scenes of the concert given by world-famous jazz pianist Keith Jarrett at the Cologne Opera House in Germany on January 24, 1975, centering on the then-18-year-old female promoter. Vera Brandes, a music-loving high school student living in Cologne, Germany, starts a part-time job booking tours for musicians visiting Germany, partly as an act of rebellion against her strict father. Just as her work begins to gain momentum thanks to her innate vitality, she visits the Berlin Jazz Festival and is stunned by the performance of American piano genius Keith Jarrett. Determined to make Keith's Cologne concert happen, she overcomes numerous difficulties to arrange the event, but on the day, a problem arises: a different type of piano than the one Keith had requested is provided. As the start time approaches, Keith refuses to play, putting the concert in jeopardy... Based on historical facts, this film adapts the little-known true story of how the legendary concert, also known as the live album masterpiece "The Köln Concert," was nearly cancelled due to a last-minute crisis but was saved by the quick thinking and resourcefulness of an 18-year-old female promoter. German rising star Mala Emde plays Vera, and John Magaro, known for "First Cow" and "Past Lives," plays Keith Jarrett.
title_norm:la femme infidèle: Praised by many critics and hailed not only as one of Chabrol's best works but also as his own greatest confidence piece. Charles, an executive at an insurance company, lives happily with his wife Hélène and son, but one day discovers that Hélène is having an affair with a writer named Pegala. Visiting Pegala's house, Charles initially maintains his composure, but gradually succumbs to rage... A masterpiece thriller capturing Agnès Varda's 'Happiness', Jacques Demy's 'The Umbrellas of Cherbourg', and the sophisticated visual beauty of Jean Rabier, who shot all three films including this one, along with performances by renowned actors, exquisitely delicate psychological portrayal, and startling violence. (1969) *All films screened in digitally remastered versions.
title_norm:la fiebre de los ricos: A thriller dripping with black humor that depicts the collapse of capitalist society following the outbreak of a mysterious disease called "Rich Flu" that only infects the wealthy. Directed and written by Galder Gaztelu-Urrutia of the "The Platform" series, which sharply depicted social inequality, it thrillingly portrays the chaos brought about by a reversal of values. Laura, a high-ranking producer at a streaming platform company, prioritizes her career over her family and is on the verge of success in the glamorous film industry. But just then, a mysterious disease called "Rich Flu" suddenly spreads worldwide, killing wealthy people one after another. As wealth transforms from a symbol of success into a "mark of elimination," capitalist society collapses and the world descends into chaos. In this extreme situation, Laura makes a decision. Mary Elizabeth Winstead, known for films like "Gemini Man" and "Birds of Prey," plays the career-driven Laura who neglects her family. Raf Spall, who has appeared in major works like "Life of Pi" and "Jurassic World: Fallen Kingdom," plays Tony, her husband who is exasperated with her yet gets caught up in the unprecedented pandemic alongside her. Timothy Spall, known for the "Harry Potter" series and "Mr. Turner," plays the billionaire Sebastian Snail.
title_norm:la la land: A musical film directed by Damien Chazelle, who gained attention with "Whiplash," starring Ryan Gosling and Emma Stone. It depicts the romance between a struggling actress and a jazz pianist through gorgeous and romantic song and dance reminiscent of classic musical films. Mia, an aspiring actress dejected after failing an audition, has a terrible first encounter with Sebastian, a pianist, at a jazz bar she enters drawn by the sound of piano. Later, Mia reunites with Sebastian at a party, where he's sullenly playing 80s pop by the poolside. Though they clash during their first conversation, they fall in love as they're drawn to each other's talents and dreams. J.K. Simmons, who won the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor for "Whiplash," also appears. Emma Stone won Best Actress at the 73rd Venice International Film Festival, and the film won a record seven awards at the 74th Golden Globe Awards including Best Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy. At the 89th Academy Awards, it received 14 nominations, tying the record for most nominations, with Chazelle becoming the youngest Best Director winner in history, and winning six Oscars total including Best Actress for Emma Stone.
title_norm:la paloma: At Madame Lily's brothel, life-or-death gambling takes place amidst decadent plumes of purple smoke. The patrons are intoxicated by the company of young prostitutes and beautiful boys. The brothel's celebrated chanteuse, Viola—also known as "La Paloma" (Ingrid Caven)—appears on stage singing "Shanghai." A male patron gazes intently at her alluring figure. This man, named Isidore (Peter Kern), visits La Paloma's dressing room day after day with a yellow rose, but is fiercely rejected by her, drowned in alcohol.
title_norm:la promesse: Fifteen-year-old Igor works in an auto repair shop, helping his father who trades in illegal foreign workers. One day, a worker named Amidou causes an accident. Fearing the police will discover his illegal labor, Igor's father refuses to take Amidou to the hospital. Amidou dies, entrusting Igor with a message for his wife and children. Igor's father makes him help bury the body and lies to Amidou's wife, Assita...
title_norm:la vérité: Kore-eda's first international co-production. On the occasion of the publication of the memoir 'The Truth' by Fabienne (Deneuve), a grande dame of French cinema, her screenwriter daughter Lumir (Binoche) returns home with her actor husband and daughter. However, mother and daughter clash fiercely over the book's embellished contents. As they hurl their long-held feelings at each other, the differences in the 'truth' they each hold come to light. The film portrays a family where the memories and emotions of mother and daughter intertwine, eventually moving toward a new bond.
title_norm:lady in the lake: A beautiful female editor visits private detective Philip Marlowe, asking him to find the missing wife of a magazine publisher. This experimental film is shot entirely from Marlowe's point of view, using the camera as his eyes.
title_norm:lady jane 終幕式「破の刻」 final stag:
A documentary capturing the four-night final event held after the closure of LADY JANE, a venerable Shimokitazawa jazz bar that brought the curtain down on its 50-year history in April 2025.

Since its founding in 1975, LADY JANE served as a cornerstone of Shimokitazawa’s cultural scene. Visited by a multitude of artists and intellectuals—including Seitaro Kuroda, Ryuichi Sakamoto, Yusaku Matsuda, Kotaro Sawaki, and Miyuki Nakajima—the bar was a crucible where encounters between diverse talents sparked countless cultural and artistic movements. The live performances held every weekend transcended genres and career levels, serving as a beacon for aspiring artists and a space for new connections and creativity for veterans.

Though the bar closed to much regret on April 13, 2025, a final event titled "LADY JANE 50th Anniversary: 'Ha no Toki' Closing Ceremony" began just a few days later on April 17 at Shimokitazawa The Suzunari. The theater featured a recreation of the bar's interior, and the stage brought together a stellar lineup of performers connected to the establishment, including a twin-drum set by Takeo Moriyama and Tatsuya Nakamura, as well as Yoshihide Otomo, Akira Sakata, Eiko Ishibashi, Jim O'Rourke, Mariko Hamada, and actors Tomoko Nakajima and Kyoko Koizumi. From the audience, leading figures in theater, film, music, and literature, along with many supporters and associates, looked on. This film captures the essence of those four nights and brings them to the silver screen.
title_norm:lady jane 終幕式破の刻〜 final stage:
LADY JANE: the legendary Shimokitazawa jazz bar that stood for 50 years. This documentary captures the four nights of final live performances held following its closure.

Founded in 1975, LADY JANE was a legendary establishment loved by actor Yusaku Matsuda and immortalized in song by Miyuki Nakajima. A cultural crossroads where music, film, literature, and theater intersected
title_norm:lady vengeance: Director Park Chan-wook's final installment of his "Revenge Trilogy," following "Sympathy for Mr. Vengeance" and "Oldboy," is a suspense drama about a woman wrongfully imprisoned who exacts revenge. Lee Geum-ja is imprisoned after a man takes her daughter hostage and forces her to take the blame for his child kidnapping and murder. During her sentence, she never loses her gentle smile, earning the nickname "Kind Geum-ja." After serving 13 years, she is released and begins her revenge against the true culprit who framed her. She retrieves her daughter, who was adopted abroad, and with the help of former inmates who have already been released, corners the man. Starring Lee Young-ae ("JSA," "Last Present") and co-starring Choi Min-sik ("Oldboy"), with cameos by Kang Hye-jung, Yoo Ji-tae, Song Kang-ho, and Shin Ha-kyun.
title_norm:lami de mon amie: The sixth film in Éric Rohmer's "Comedies and Proverbs" series. Set in a new town on the outskirts of Paris, it lightly depicts the romantic affairs of four men and women. Blanche, a shy woman working at city hall, and Léa, a pragmatic female student, hit it off and become friends. Léa lives with her boyfriend Fabien, but their relationship isn't going well. Meanwhile, Blanche develops feelings for Alexandre, a playboy and friend of Fabien's, but her timid nature prevents her from confessing. Eventually, Fabien finds himself drawn to Blanche... The colorful 1980s fashion is also a highlight.
title_norm:largent: The 13th feature film by French master director Robert Bresson, who left behind masterpieces such as "Resistance: From the Prisoner's Diary" and "Mouchette." Bresson, already over 80 at the time of filming, passed away in 1999, making this his final work. Based on the novella "The Forged Coupon" by Russian literary giant Leo Tolstoy, it depicts the life of Yvon, a young fuel delivery man who, after unknowingly using a counterfeit bill that falls into his hands, triggers a family massacre and spirals downward. The title "L'argent" means "money" in French. First released in Japan in 1986. Revived in 2011 as part of "Cinema Masterpiece Selection III: The Art of Robert Bresson" with new prints. In 2026, it will be revived again in a 2K restored version as part of "Robert Bresson Masterpiece Selection."
title_norm:late shift: A social human drama that depicts the relentless hard work and unexpected troubles constantly falling on nurses in an understaffed, full hospital ward, which became a huge hit in Switzerland. Directed by Swiss screenwriter and filmmaker Petra Volpe, it realistically and thrillingly portrays the urgent, universal problem of hospital realities. Florie, a dedicated and highly professional nurse working in a state hospital, faces an even busier late shift than usual because a colleague is out sick. The ward is full, and she also has to train nursing students. Despite the situation, Florie treats patients with anxiety and loneliness sincerely, but she falls into an unmanageable situation and eventually faces a major trial. Leonie Benesch, known for 'The Teachers' Lounge' and 'September 5,' stars.
title_norm:lavventura: Sandro, his lover Anna, and her friend Claudia go sailing on a yacht. When they land on a certain island, Anna suddenly disappears. Sandro and Claudia search for her, but gradually find themselves drawn to each other, giving in to their desires despite their guilt.
title_norm:le assaggiatrici: Based on the global bestseller "The Taster" written from the testimony of German woman Margot Wolk, this drama portrays the fate of women forced by the Nazis to be Hitler's food tasters. It captures the horrors of war from a female perspective and the shifting relationships among the women who share their daily lives as tasters. In 1943, near the end of World War II, Rosa flees the bombing of Berlin and waits for her husband's return from the front in a Polish village, close to the forest where Hitler's Wolf's Lair headquarters is located. One day, Rosa is ordered to taste Hitler's food before he eats, and along with other young women, she is forced under SS guard at gunpoint to consume the meals. They endure the torment of sampling the finest dishes prepared for Hitler in a life-threatening situation. In July 1944, a coup attempt to assassinate Hitler at the Wolf's Lair plunges the war into further chaos. Elisa Schlott, star of the Netflix series "The Empress," plays Rosa, with Max Riemelt of "The Matrix Resurrections" co-starring as an SS officer. Italian director Silvio Soldini, known for "Emma's Eyes" and "Love in Venice," directs.
title_norm:le bonheur: One of the representative works of Agnès Varda, a leading female director of the French New Wave, this human drama depicts the ironic fate that befalls an ordinary couple in search of happiness. François lives a peaceful and happy life surrounded by his beautiful wife Thérèse and their adorable children. One day, while visiting a nearby town, François meets Émilie, a woman who works at the post office, and falls in love with her. At the same time, François truly loves his wife Thérèse. One day, while on a picnic with his family, François confesses his infidelity to Thérèse... The film won the Silver Bear at the 1965 Berlin International Film Festival.
title_norm:le boucher: Directed by Claude Chabrol, a leading figure of the French New Wave known for numerous suspense and mystery masterpieces, this crime drama is set in a peaceful rural village. It quietly and sharply delves into the darkness of the human psyche through a series of murders committed by a lonely butcher and the female teacher who is loved by him. Hélène, a primary school teacher in a small village in southwestern France, meets Paul, a war veteran burdened with loneliness, and they gradually grow close. Meanwhile, a series of murders of women shakes the village's calm daily life. One day, during a picnic with her students, Hélène discovers a brutally murdered body; beside it lies a lighter identical to one she had given Paul. Stéphane Audran, who was married to Chabrol at the time, stars as Hélène, the same character name as in 'Les Biches'. Jean Yanne plays the butcher Paul. Although never theatrically released in Japan, the film will have its Japanese theatrical premiere as part of the 'Claude Chabrol Masterpiece Selection' (starting February 13, 2026, at Cinema Rise and Morc Asagaya, among others), featuring three of Chabrol's suspense films from the late 1960s to 1970.
title_norm:le fils: The Dardenne brothers, directors of 'Rosetta' and 'The Promise,' sincerely and ambitiously tackle a profound motif that could be called humanity's eternal challenge in civilized society. They depict the extreme inner turmoil of a protagonist burdened with complex emotions in a stripped-down, understated style. Olivier Gourmet won the Best Actor award at the 2003 Cannes Film Festival. One day, a boy named Francis enters a vocational training center. He wants to join the woodworking class, but the instructor, Olivier, turns him away, saying he's too busy. Yet, Olivier finds himself strangely preoccupied with Francis. Eventually, Olivier accepts Francis into his class...
title_norm:le quattro volte: Italian filmmaker Michelangelo Frammartino tells the story of four lives that are born and die. Based on the Pythagorean concept of "four transmigrations," the film presents humans, animals, plants, and minerals with equal weight from a fundamentally egalitarian perspective that does not center the human world. After an elderly shepherd quietly dies in a mountain village in Calabria, southern Italy, his young goat dies beside a large fir tree. The tree is cut down for a village festival and eventually becomes charcoal. With no dialogue and long takes, the film captures nature as it is. In Japan, it screened in the natural TIFF section of the 23rd Tokyo International Film Festival in 2010 and was released theatrically in 2011. It will be released in 2026 as part of the special screening series "The Amazing World of Michelangelo Frammartino."
title_norm:le rayon vert: The fifth film in Éric Rohmer's "Comedies and Proverbs" series. Through lively dialogue and beautiful imagery, it depicts the journey of a lonely woman seeking love and happiness on vacation, winning the Golden Lion at the Venice International Film Festival. Delphine, who works as a secretary, is looking forward to a vacation in Greece, but her female friend who was supposed to go with her cancels at the last minute. She goes to the South of France with other friends but can't fit in and returns to Paris alone. Later, visiting the beach at Biarritz alone, Delphine hears about the "green ray" from a Jules Verne novel—a flash of light visible only for an instant just before sunset. Starring Marie Rivière of "The Aviator's Wife" and "Autumn Tale."
title_norm:le silence de lorna: The Dardenne brothers, directors of 'The Son' and 'The Child,' craft a moving human love story centered on an immigrant woman who enters a sham marriage to obtain citizenship. With a bold structure, they suspensefully portray the conflict that arises when unexpected feelings develop within the false marriage, and the protagonist's growing desperation as she is cornered by her inescapable ties to the criminal underworld. Starring newcomer Arta Dobroshi, with Jérémie Renier from 'The Child.' Lorna, a woman from Albania, comes to Belgium. Dreaming of opening a bar with her fellow countryman lover, she enters a sham marriage with a drug-addicted young man, Claudy, arranged by a shady broker, Fabio, to gain citizenship. Initially finding him annoying, Lorna gradually develops special feelings for Claudy as he struggles to quit drugs and earnestly seeks her affection...
title_norm:leave the cat alone: A love story that interweaves past and present, depicting the current state of a drifting married couple and a reunion with a friend that stirs up past memories. This is the feature-length directorial debut of Daisuke Shigayuki, who gained attention for short films like "Haru Mitai da" and "Madotachi," completed after a seven-year production period. Mori, a musician, is troubled by the distance he feels from his wife Maiko, a photographer. One day, Mori unexpectedly reunites with a former friend, Asako, rekindling old feelings for her. Asako also remembers being attracted to Mori in the past. However, their memories, tinged with expectations and desires, appear blurry, distorted, and conveniently rewritten in each of their minds. After a long walk, Mori and Asako reexamine their two lives that have already gone off track and the present moment they each stand in. Actor Soma Fujii, who also works as singer-songwriter "soma," stars as Mori and also handles the music. Ran Taniguchi (from "Hold Your Breath") plays Mori's wife Maiko, and Yukiho Murakami (from "August My Heaven") plays Mori's former friend Asako. The film was selected for the competition section of the 30th Busan International Film Festival in 2025.
title_norm:left handed girl: Taipei, a night market noodle stall. Five-year-old Yi-jin (Nina Yeh), along with her single mother Shue-fen (Janel Tsai) who is burdened with debt, and her teenage sister Yi-an (Ma Shih-yuan), returns from the countryside to rebuild their lives. One day, her old-fashioned grandfather denounces her dominant left hand as the "devil's hand," and Yi-jin begins to feel guilt. That devil's hand, inadvertently, brings to light the "sins" that each family member has been hiding.
title_norm:legend of the eight samurai: Kinji Fukasaku directs this adaptation of Toshio Kamata's legendary novel "Shin Satomi Hakkenden," a fresh take on Bakin Takizawa's classic "Nanso Satomi Hakkenden." Starring the glamorous duo Hiroko Yakushimaru and Hiroyuki Sanada, it became a massive hit characteristic of Kadokawa Films, which dominated the era and breathed new life into Japanese cinema. Tamazusa, who once married into the Hikita domain and indulged in debauchery and tyranny before being destroyed by the Satomi clan, returns as a demon queen to exact revenge. She orders her son Motofuji Hikita and his retainers to attack the Satomi's Tateyama Castle. The Satomi clan is annihilated, but Princess Shizu and a few retainers escape, pursued by Tamazusa's forces. The eight warriors, each possessing a jewel inscribed with one of the virtues—benevolence, righteousness, propriety, wisdom, loyalty, faith, filial piety, and brotherly love—scattered from Princess Fuse's body, live their separate lives. Guided by fate, they gather around Princess Shizu and rise to battle, aiming to crush Tamazusa's ambitions.
title_norm:lenfant: 18-year-old Sonia (Déborah François) and 20-year-old Bruno (Jérémie Renier) have a son. After returning from the hospital, Sonia asks Bruno, who has no steady job and lives day-to-day through shady dealings, to get serious about working.
title_norm:les biches: Centering on the intense and mysterious relationship between two women—one dominant, one submissive, almost like doppelgängers—this masterpiece from Chabrol's 'peak period' exudes a powerful allure with the film itself baring love and hatred. One day, Frédérique, a bourgeois woman, spots Hoïe, a girl drawing on the pavement of the Pont des Arts bridge over the Seine. Hoïe comes to live at Frédérique's mansion and is drawn to Paul, a guest, but Paul also has a relationship with Frédérique... A sensual work filled with the complex and ambiguous hearts of women. In this film, Stéphane Audran, who was already Chabrol's wife, co-stars with her former husband Jean-Louis Trintignant. (1968) *All films screened in digitally remastered versions.
title_norm:les liens de san: A police inspector from the Montreal Police Department solves a murder case using clues obtained from the victim's diary.
title_norm:les nuits de la pleine lune: The fourth film in Éric Rohmer's 'Comedies and Proverbs' series. Louise, an interior designer, lives with her architect boyfriend Rémi in a suburban Paris apartment. The serious Rémi and the free-spirited Louise are constantly bickering. Feeling stifled in her life with Rémi, Louise rents her own room in Paris and starts going out with her married best friend Octave... The film delicately portrays a woman's emotions as she wavers between two men and two homes. Lead actress Pascale Ogier won the Best Actress award at the Venice Film Festival for this role, but tragically died shortly after at the young age of 25. The cast also includes Fabrice Luchini from 'Claire's Knee' and Tchéky Karyo from 'Nikita.'
title_norm:les rendez vous de paris: Three stories about love and chance, all centered around a date in Paris.
title_norm:les triplettes de belleville: The feature directorial debut of bande dessinée artist and animator Sylvain Chomet, this animated film humorously depicts a grandmother's desperate quest to rescue her kidnapped grandson. Minimizing dialogue and featuring stylized characters on a jaunty jazz-infused soundtrack, this adventure earned high international acclaim, becoming the first French film nominated for the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature. The grandmother learns that her shy, lonely grandson, Champion, is interested in bicycles. To help him become a cyclist, the grandmother trains with him, and he eventually grows up to compete in the world's greatest bicycle race, the Tour de France. However, during the race, Champion is kidnapped by mysterious figures. The grandmother sets off on an adventure with her loyal dog Bruno to rescue her kidnapped grandson. With the help of three legendary triplet musician old ladies, and armed with her life experience, wisdom, and humor, she overcomes numerous obstacles. Besides Best Animated Feature, the film was also nominated for the Academy Award for Best Original Song. In Japan, it was praised by Isao Takahata of Studio Ghibli and was first released in theaters in 2004. A revival screening was held in 2021 as a pre-20th anniversary project.
title_norm:let him rest in peace: After learning that his old friend Sakaguchi had attacked the president of Shimogata Construction and been arrested, Shindo returned to a small port town in Okinawa. Shimogata Construction was in charge of the town's redevelopment and had been harassing and threatening Sakaguchi to force him to sell his hotel. Shindo stayed at the hotel, the "Free Inn," and began investigating the incident. Meeting Shimogata's development chief Takabatake and Detective Tokuda, who was colluding with Shimogata, Shindo uncovered the truth: Sakaguchi had stormed Shimogata Construction to rescue his kidnapped son, Ryuta. Shindo also learned that Sakaguchi was suffering from cancer and had only a few months to live.
title_norm:let the right one in: Oscar, a 12-year-old in the prime of playfulness but with not a single friend, falls in love for the first time with Eli, who moves in next door. With messy black hair and a pale face, Eli only ever appears at night, and the more Oscar learns about her, the more mysterious she becomes. Though she claims to be the same age as Oscar, she doesn't even know her own birthday. Around the same time Oscar meets Eli, gruesome murders begin occurring in succession, casting an uneasy air over the town. In the midst of this, Oscar discovers a grave secret: the shocking truth that Eli has been 12 years old for a very long time. Eli is a vampire who has survived for 200 years, moving from town to town and drinking human blood.
title_norm:lets go karaoke!: Okasatomi, the choir club president, is suddenly invited to karaoke by yakuza member Narita Kyoji, who asks for singing lessons. To avoid the 'terror' that awaits whoever comes in last at the gang's karaoke contest, Kyoji must improve at all costs. His chosen song is X JAPAN's 'Kurenai.' Satomi reluctantly agrees to coach him, but in time, their relationship begins to change... What fate awaits Satomi? And can Kyoji escape the bottom spot?
title_norm:life, and nothing more…: In 1990, a massive earthquake in northern Iran mercilessly struck the village where the 1987 film "Where Is the Friend's Home?" was shot, as well as its residents. After the earthquake, film director Kiarostami, accompanied by his son, heads to the disaster-stricken area to check on the safety of the two brothers who appeared in the film.
title_norm:like father, like son: Ryota (Fukuyama) is a company employee who has carved out his own life and enjoys smooth sailing. One day, a call from the hospital informs him that the son he has raised with love for six years is actually another couple's child, switched at birth. Through interactions with the family who raised his biological son, his values gradually begin to waver, and he grapples with what family and blood ties truly mean. Winner of the Jury Prize at the 66th Cannes Film Festival.
title_norm:linconnu de la grande arche: The Grande Arche, a monumental cube-shaped building in the La Défense district west of Paris, stands on the "Paris historical axis" stretching straight from the glass pyramid of the Louvre. Behind its completion lies the unknown story of an anonymous architect whose fate was shaken. Based on historical fact, this human drama immerses viewers in the bizarre life of an architect who challenged a national project while being tossed about by ideals and political maneuvering. An ensemble of talented actors lends the film credibility, earning it a selection in the Un Certain Regard section of the 78th Cannes Film Festival and eight César Award nominations. This architectural drama resonates with debates surrounding Japan's National Stadium and the Osaka Expo. In 1983 Paris, President Mitterrand envisioned a new monument to celebrate the bicentennial of the French Revolution. The international design competition selected the unknown Danish architect Johan Otto von Spreckelsen. His bold plan—a cube-shaped arch of Italian Carrara marble with a cloud-like roof floating at its base—captured the president's heart and made him an overnight sensation. However, budget constraints, political pressure, and the expectations of those around him stood in the way of his pursuit of perfection. Should he stick to his ideals or compromise with reality? Caught in the vortex of a massive project, what "certain decision" will one architect make?
title_norm:linda linda linda: A refreshing youth drama set in high school, depicting the struggles of a girls' band. Starring Bae Doona of 'Barking Dogs Never Bite' and 'Tube', Aki Maeda of the 'Battle Royale' series, Yuu Kashii of 'Lorelei', and Shiori Sekine, bassist of the rock band Base Ball Bear. Directed by Nobuhiro Yamashita of 'A Gentle Breeze in the Village'. It delicately portrays the subtle emotional shifts and excitement in the hearts of teenage girls. At a local high school, an emergency strikes Kyoko, Megumi, and Nozomi of the same band. They had even prepared an original song for the school festival, but guitarist Moyu injured her finger, and the furious vocalist Rinko quit the band. However, after listening to 'Linda Linda' by The Blue Hearts, which they happen to hear, Kyoko and the others decide to form a cover band of The Blue Hearts. They invite Song, a Korean exchange student, to be the vocalist, and she agrees. The four practice hard toward the final day of the school festival, but...
title_norm:lintérêt dadam: The second feature from Belgian director Laura Wandel, who gained attention with her 2021 debut 'Playground', is a human suspense drama depicting one night's events surrounding a 4-year-old boy hospitalized in a pediatric ward and his mother, told from the perspective of a nurse trying to support them. Four-year-old Adam is admitted to a pediatric center with a broken left arm. Malnourished and underdeveloped, his bones are brittle. The court rules that Rebecca, an immigrant single mother, has not been providing Adam with proper nutrition and issues an order restricting her visits. Nurse manager Lucie, herself a single mother, tries to support Rebecca, who fears losing custody and being separated from her son. But Rebecca's reckless actions and pressure from superiors and colleagues push Lucie into a corner. Léa Drucker ('Close') plays nurse Lucie, torn between her desire to save the mother and child and the judicial system the hospital must follow. Anamaria Vartolomei ('Happening') plays isolated single mother Rebecca. The film is produced by Belgian masters Jean-Pierre and Luc Dardenne. It opened the Critics' Week at the 2025 Cannes Film Festival.
title_norm:little amélie or the characte: An animated film set in 1960s Kobe, depicting the growth of Amélie, a Belgian girl born in Japan. Based on the autobiographical novel "Tube Metaphysics" by Belgian writer Amélie Nothomb, it portrays a world rich in emotion, seen through the eyes of the two-year-old protagonist Amélie, woven with life, color, and her witty words. In 1960s Kobe, Amélie, a Belgian girl born into a diplomat's family, is unresponsive until age two and a half, but then enters an invincible childhood, believing herself to be a god and living in a magical world. Her days with her beloved housekeeper Nishio and her family are adventures full of new discoveries. One day, she learns the kanji for "rain," which suits her perfectly. Then, on her third birthday, an event occurs that changes everything. Directed by Myriam Ballard and Liang-Cho Han, who worked on "Long Way North," with music by Japanese composer Mari Fukuhara. It won the Audience Award at the 2025 Annecy International Animated Film Festival and was nominated for Best Animated Feature at the 98th Academy Awards.
title_norm:little girls dream: A documentary film adaptation of a 26-year chronicle following one girl's dream from its beginning to the present day, originally produced by TeNY Television Niigata, a local TV station in Niigata Prefecture. The story gained attention when it was featured on Nippon Television network programs such as "Zoom In!! Morning!" and "NNN Documentary." In 1987, three calves arrive at a small elementary school in the mountains of Niigata. A third-grade girl at the time dreams of becoming a "cow doctor" through caring for the calves. After parting with the cows she had grown attached to, and with support from her family and those around her, she overcomes difficult hurdles to become a veterinarian for "livestock," not pets. Through her continued dedication to invaluable lives every day—now as a married mother—the film explores the importance of having dreams, as well as themes of family, hometown, work, and the harshness of reality. Yui Yokoyama of AKB48 takes on her first narration role.
title_norm:little remi and famous dog ca: Based on 'Nobody's Boy.' Even after being sold by his stepfather to traveling performers, young Remi never loses heart. The background art incorporates elements from diverse European masterpieces by Millet and Monet, while Yugo Serikawa's masterful use of dramatic pauses heightens the arduous journey. Frankie Sakai's voice performance as Remi's sidekick Capi, with his playful demeanor, offers a refreshing respite amid the relentless tragedy.
title_norm:living corpse: A full AI-produced film adaptation (with all dialogue in English) of horror manga artist Hino Hideshi's terrifying yet moving story 'Horror! The Man of Dead Flesh.' One day, a 'living corpse' suddenly appears in the city—his body is rotting and squishy, maggots crawl from his eyes, and his heart isn't beating, yet somehow he is alive! After being taken into police custody, the man is sent to a university hospital's isolation ward. Growing sick of the repeated human experiments, he finally attempts to escape... Who is he, and where is he headed? A poignant and sorrowful man of dead flesh. His fate begins with death. What awaits him beyond?
title_norm:local reporter: A pollution issue arises in a town in the Tohoku region, and the media war heats up... An excellent film in which Frankie plays a newspaper reporter, depicting the struggles of journalists who, while grappling with the difficulties of maneuvering in a rural setting, burn with passion for producing community-focused articles.
title_norm:lornas silence: The Dardenne brothers, directors of 'The Son' and 'The Child,' craft a moving human love story centered on an immigrant woman who enters a sham marriage to obtain citizenship. With a bold structure, they suspensefully portray the conflict that arises when unexpected feelings develop within the false marriage, and the protagonist's growing desperation as she is cornered by her inescapable ties to the criminal underworld. Starring newcomer Arta Dobroshi, with Jérémie Renier from 'The Child.' Lorna, a woman from Albania, comes to Belgium. Dreaming of opening a bar with her fellow countryman lover, she enters a sham marriage with a drug-addicted young man, Claudy, arranged by a shady broker, Fabio, to gain citizenship. Initially finding him annoying, Lorna gradually develops special feelings for Claudy as he struggles to quit drugs and earnestly seeks her affection...
title_norm:lost land: Directed by Akio Fujimoto, who has garnered international attention for "Where I Belong" and "The Girls at the Seashore," this road movie is based on the testimonies of the Rohingya, often called "one of the most persecuted ethnic groups in the world." It depicts a young refugee brother and sister, driven from their homeland, risking their lives to cross borders in search of their family. Blending unrelenting reality with fantastical imagery, the film portrays the harrowing journey of refugees smuggling themselves across borders from a child's perspective. Five-year-old Shafi and his nine-year-old sister Somiir, living in a refugee camp, set out with their aunt for distant Malaysia, hoping to reunite with their family. Unable to obtain passports, they are led by smugglers onto a fishing boat, and despite facing the fury of nature, pursuit by security forces, and the threat of human trafficking, they desperately overcome the grueling journey. The cast includes over 200 Rohingya people, led by the siblings Somiir and Shafi in the lead roles. Their voices and gazes, as people who have themselves been driven from their homeland, lend the film a powerful realism despite their lack of acting experience. The film received high praise at film festivals worldwide, including winning the Special Jury Prize in the Orizzonti section at the 82nd Venice International Film Festival in 2025, the first time a Japanese director has won this award.
