title_norm:nenette and boni: In the port city of Marseille in southern France. Young Boni works at a pizzeria, spending his days belonging nowhere. One day, his long-estranged younger sister Nenette suddenly appears and crashes at his place. Having nowhere to go, Nenette carries a secret: she is pregnant. But she never reveals this fact to Boni. In their awkward cohabitation, the two spend time maintaining a distance they cannot cross. Boni develops feelings for a woman who works at a bakery, but cannot turn those feelings into reality. Nenette confronts her own body and tries to choose her future. In a cruel world, desire and tenderness quietly transform their relationship. Unspoken emotions slowly seep through.
title_norm:never give up: A massacre occurs deep in the Tohoku mountains, killing most of a village's residents. A self-defense force special unit member, Misawa, who was training in the mountains, happens upon the scene, kills the perpetrator, and rescues the sole survivor—a village girl named Yoriko. Later, after retiring, Misawa adopts Yoriko and works as an insurance salesperson. One day, he rescues a female journalist named Tomoko from an attacker, but she is being targeted because she tried to expose the corruption of a local businessman, Oba. Meanwhile, Detective Kitano, who suspects Misawa of being the massacre killer, continues to shadow him.
title_norm:new dawn: This animated film marks the feature directorial and screenwriting debut of Yoshitoshi Shinomiya, who has worked across genres primarily as a Nihonga (Japanese-style) painter. It is a Japan-France co-production with the cutting-edge French studio Miyu Productions. The 330-year-old Tategami Fireworks Factory, nestled in the woods, is facing eviction due to town redevelopment. Keitaro Tategami, who grew up there, has barricaded himself in the factory for four years, striving to complete the legendary "Shuhari" firework in place of his missing father, Eitaro. Meanwhile, Keitaro's childhood friend Kaoru Shikimori left their hometown for Tokyo after a past incident. Contacted by Keitaro's older brother Sentaro, who works at the city office, Kaoru visits the Tategami family on the last day of summer, the day before the eviction deadline, reuniting with Keitaro for the first time in four years. As they clash, trying to reclaim lost time and broken bonds, they hatch a surprising plan to uncover the secret of the phantom firework. The key lies in a beautiful blue pigment called "hanaryokusei" (copper acetoarsenite). Actors Rihito Noda and Kotone Furukawa make their voice acting debuts as Keitaro and Kaoru respectively, with voice actor Miyu Irino as Keitaro's brother Sentaro and actor Takashi Okabe as their father Eitaro. The film was selected for the Competition section of the 78th Berlin International Film Festival in 2026.
title_norm:new group: The second theatrical release from director Yuta Shimotsu, who gained attention for his 2024 commercial film debut "May the Lord Be with You". It comically and seriously explores the underlying psychology of human behavior in group activities, specifically through the lens of group gymnastics, with a unique worldview. High school girl Ai, who has family problems, is shy and unable to assert her own opinions. Transfer student Yu, who has returned from overseas, is the type to speak her mind clearly and struggles to fit into the group-oriented, harmony-focused activities of Japanese schools. Ai is interested in Yu, but Yu grows frustrated with Ai's inability to express herself. One day, a student in the schoolyard freezes on all fours. Soon, other students begin lining up beside him in the same position, forming a massive human pyramid. Strangely, the school encourages participation in the human pyramid as a "good thing," and the stacked students all wear serene expressions. As students gather one after another and obey without a word, Ai herself becomes dazed and nearly joins the pyramid. The situation eventually escalates into a collective supernatural phenomenon engulfing the entire region. Anna Yamada (from the "Golden Kamuy" series) plays the protagonist Ai, and Yuzu Aoki (from "5 Centimeters per Second") plays the transfer student Yu. Pierre Taki delivers a bizarre performance as the principal who leads the group. The film won the Special Jury Prize at the 29th Fantasia International Film Festival in 2025.
title_norm:new love in tokyo: Ray is an actress in a small theater troupe. By day, she devotes herself to rehearsals with her friends, and by night, she works as a dominatrix at an SM club in Shibuya. One evening, Ray becomes friendly with Ayumi, a hotel escort girl she occasionally sees in the elevator of the building where the club is located. Ayumi is a shrewd girl living with Kenji, a ronin studying for medical school entrance exams. The two hit it off and head out into the nightlife. After drinking, dancing, and partying, they part ways, promising to go see the sea at dawn together someday. Finally, the day of Ray's theater troupe's performance arrives. With Ayumi and Ray's client Sawatari watching, Ray's play is a success, met with thunderous applause. Ray is moved by the satisfaction of accomplishing something. Ayumi is also moved seeing Ray like this. The two head out to the coast at dawn in a car driven by a man they picked up.
title_norm:news from home: A documentary by Belgian director Chantal Akerman, who revolutionized cinema with 'Jeanne Dielman, 23 quai du Commerce, 1080 Bruxelles,' a portrait of an ordinary housewife's daily routine. In this film, she reads letters from her mother over footage capturing the landscapes of 1970s New York. By layering her mother's affectionate words over the bleak cityscapes of New York—alleyways, cars on avenues, people waiting for trains on station platforms, and underground passages—the film highlights the alienation of urban life and the distance from family far away. In Japan, it received its theatrical premiere at the 'Chantal Akerman Film Festival 2023' (April 7–27, 2023, Human Trust Cinema Shibuya), screened together with 'Saute ma ville.'
title_norm:newシネマ歌舞伎 四谷怪談: The 28th installment in the "Cinema Kabuki" series, which digitally screens kabuki stage performances in movie theaters. This recording captures the June 2016 performance of the 15th "Cocoon Kabuki," featuring Tsuruya Nanboku's "Tokaido Yotsuya Kaidan" in a new direction and composition by Kushida Kazumi. The production originated in 1994 at Shibuya's Theater Cocoon, led by Nakamura Kanzaburo XVIII, and this was the first program in that series. Iemon, who lives faithfully to his own desires; Naosuke Gonbei; the fleeting moments of men. Osode and Oiwa, toyed with by men; the sorrow of women. Kushida's interpretation of "Yotsuya Kaidan" as a story of instinct and desire that still resonates today is recreated with footage emphasizing the unique sense of presence of a live theater. Nakamura Shido plays Iemon, Nakamura Kankuro plays Naosuke Gonbei, Nakamura Shichinosuke plays Osode, and Nakamura Senjaku plays Oiwa. Along with regular "Cocoon Kabuki" actors like Kataoka Kamezo and Sasano Takashi, the cast also features unconventional choices for kabuki, including Omori Hiroshi and ballet dancer Shuto Yasuyuki.
title_norm:nico, 1988: A musical biopic depicting the later years of Nico, the German-born chanteuse of the American rock band The Velvet Underground and muse of pop art pioneer Andy Warhol, who dominated the 1960s scene. Focusing on the two years before her death in 1988 at age 49, it interweaves her stage presence with personal struggles, realistically portraying the loneliness and rebirth behind the glamorous legend. In 1986, Nico, in her late 40s and living alone in England, distances herself from past fame and embarks on a European tour with her new manager Richard and her band. But the journey is harsh, forcing her to confront her unstable psyche, drug addiction, and conflicts with those around her. Burdened by regret and conflict as a mother, she retrieves her son Ari, who is in a French rehabilitation facility for drug addiction and a suicide attempt, and brings him along on tour... Trine Dyrholm (from "Into Eternity") stars as Nico and performs the songs herself. John Gordon Sinclair ("Gregory's Girl") plays manager Richard, and Anamaria Marinca ("4 Months, 3 Weeks and 2 Days") plays violinist Sylvia. Directed by Italian filmmaker Susanna Nicchiarelli, known for "Miss Marx." It won the Best Film award in the Orizzonti section at the 74th Venice International Film Festival in 2017.
title_norm:night flower: A human suspense film directed by Eiji Uchida ("Midnight Swan"), starring Keiko Kitagawa. Uchida also wrote the original story and screenplay. It thrillingly depicts a mother, hounded by debt collectors, who steps into a dangerous world to make her children's dreams come true. Natsuki Nagashima, who fled to Tokyo with her two children to escape debt collectors, works desperately day and night but still struggles to afford food for the next day. One day, she witnesses a drug deal in the nightlife district and decides to become a dealer herself. She meets Tamae Yoshii, a fighter carrying deep loneliness, who offers to be her bodyguard. Teaming up, they venture into even more dangerous transactions. However, the death of a female college student sends Natsuki and Tamae's fates spiraling in an unexpected direction. Tomochi Morita (live-action "City Hunter") plays Tamae, the female fighter who becomes Natsuki's bodyguard. Daisuke Sakuma (from the idol group Snow Man) plays Tamae's childhood friend, Kaito Ikeda. Ryuta Shibuya (from the rock band SUPER BEAVER) plays Sato, the drug trafficking boss. The cast also includes Kiyohiko Shibukawa, Rena Tanaka, Hiroyuki Ikeuchi, and Ken Mitsuishi.
title_norm:night is short, walk on girl: An animated film adaptation of "The Night is Short, Walk on Girl," an early bestseller by popular author Tomihiko Morimi, known for "The Tatami Galaxy" and "Uchoten Kazoku," which humorously depicts the story of an unremarkable university student who pines for a black-haired maiden. Directed by Masaaki Yuasa, popular for his uniquely expressive animation works including the TV anime "The Tatami Galaxy," "Mind Game," and "Ping Pong The Animation." The screenplay is by Makoto Ueda of the theater troupe Europe Kikaku, who also worked on "The Tatami Galaxy." Singer-songwriter and actor Gen Hoshino, also popular for his role in the drama "We Married as a Job," voices the protagonist. The university student "Senpai," who harbors feelings for "the black-haired maiden," a junior in his club, spends his days executing the "Nakame Strategy" aimed at "getting her to notice him as much as possible." The seasons turn as he gets swept up in strange incidents caused by his colorful friends, but his relationship with the black-haired maiden only progresses around the edges without making real headway...
title_norm:ninja wars: Kashin Koji, a mysterious man who appears during the Sengoku period, is a master of various mystical arts, and tales of his sightings and experiences are told in many places. He is summoned by the warlord Matsunaga Hisahide. Hisahide harbors a desire for Miyoshi Yoshiyuki's wife, Ukon no Tsubone, and plots to have his way with her. Kashin proposes a plan to create an "lust stone"—an aphrodisiac capable of melting any woman's heart. It is made by having seven ninja monks under Kashin's command rape women and boiling down the resulting fluids. The sheer horror of this plan leaves the assembled Sen no Rikyū and Yagyū Shinzaemon trembling in fear.
title_norm:ninomiya kinjirou: A biographical drama depicting the little-known half-life of Ninomiya Kinjiro, famous for the statue of a boy reading a book while carrying firewood that once stood in many elementary school grounds. Ninomiya Kinjiro lost his parents and spent his childhood living apart from his siblings. As a young man, Kinjiro is entrusted with the restoration of the Sakurama domain (present-day Moka City, Tochigi Prefecture) by the Odawara domain. Kinjiro works on village restoration using his own original methods, but faces strong opposition from conservative villagers. Meanwhile, the Odawara domain dispatches the samurai Toyoda Shosaku, who begins various acts of obstruction against Kinjiro's measures, claiming "Kinjiro is destroying order." Kinjiro is played by Masahito Goda, known for the drama "Mito Komon," with a cast including Misato Tanaka, Riri Narita, Vino Inuyama, Takaaki Enoki, Shingo Yanagisawa, Min Tanaka, Ikkei Watanabe, Kenjiro Ishimaru, and Katsuhiko Watabiki. Directed by Takumi Saitoh, known for "Sayonara, Mine" and "Five for Freedom."
title_norm:ninotchka: A romantic comedy featuring the divinely beautiful Greta Garbo in a comedic performance. The Soviets try to sell jewels confiscated from aristocrats, while the aristocrats are determined to stop them. The man and woman who become their respective agents end up falling in love.
title_norm:niñxs: A documentary by transgender director Kani Lapuerta, recording eight years in the life of a transgender elementary school student in Mexico as she grows into a teenager. In Tepoztlán, a town south of Mexico City, 15-year-old Carla talks with director Kani Lapuerta in a secret cocoon. They discuss what kind of film they want to make, and begin to look back on Carla's life chronologically from her elementary school days. The schoolyard where she couldn't line up with either the 'boys' or 'girls,' the bedroom where she endlessly practiced makeup, the morning school reopened during the pandemic, the city hall where she officially changed her name, the slogans she shouted at the Pride March, and the baton club she admired. Watched over by her punk and hippie chef parents, her friends, director Lapuerta, the queer community, and the sacred rocky mountain, Carla encounters various versions of herself. Director Kani Lapuerta also appears in the film, gradually sharing her inner thoughts with Carla like an exchange diary. With comedic touches, it portrays the struggles and fluctuations of adolescence growing up in a small town with strong gender stereotypes.
title_norm:no other choice: Korean master filmmaker Park Chan-wook, winner of the Grand Prix at Cannes for "Oldboy" and Best Director for "Decision to Leave," directs this suspense drama laced with irony and black humor about a salaryman whose life is turned upside down by a sudden layoff. Park reunites with Lee Byung-hun, who starred in his breakthrough film "Joint Security Area," for the first time in 21 years. Man-su, an ordinary salaryman at a paper company, lives with his wife, two children, and two dogs, believing he has everything he could want. But his life changes drastically when he is suddenly fired from the company he has worked for for 25 years. His job search drags on for over a year, and he is forced to sell his beloved home. Desperate, Man-su walks into a rapidly growing paper company with his resume, only to be flatly rejected. Convinced he is the most qualified person for the company, he makes a decision: if there's no opening, he'll have to create one himself. The film is based on the novel "The Ax" by Donald E. Westlake, which was also adapted into a film by Costa-Gavras. Lee Byung-hun plays the increasingly cornered Man-su, and Son Ye-jin of "Crash Landing on You" plays his wife Mi-ri, who grows stronger as the crisis deepens. The film was selected for the competition section of the 82nd Venice International Film Festival in 2025 and won the newly established International Audience Award (for non-North American films) at the 50th Toronto International Film Festival.
title_norm:nobody knows: Keiko (YOU) and four children, including Akira (Yagira), live in a single apartment room under false pretenses. When Keiko eventually stops coming home, the children are left to fend for themselves, but their financial situation gradually becomes dire. Inspired by a real-life child abandonment case, the film delicately portrays modern social issues such as neglect, young carers, and those who fall through the cracks of the welfare system, earning high international acclaim.
title_norm:nothing but bones: In the late Meiji period, a poor farmer's daughter is sold as a prostitute to the Suzaki pleasure quarters. A fierce masterpiece of women's cinema by Tai Kato, depicting the sorrow and resilience of women exploited to the bone.
title_norm:notre musique: A feature film by French master Jean-Luc Godard, shot in the war-torn city of Sarajevo as a prayer for world peace. Based on Dante's epic poem 'The Divine Comedy,' it is structured in three parts: 'Hell,' 'Purgatory,' and 'Paradise.' Visiting Sarajevo for a lecture, Godard finds a historical crossroads in the rebuilding city, which is also a history of human conflict and massacre. Using the asymmetry between Israel and Palestine, and Judaism and Islam as examples, Godard discusses the dominant structures of conflict in the world. 'Hell' is composed of montages of war footage; 'Purgatory' depicts the interaction between Godard, invited to Sarajevo for a lecture, and a female student named Olga; and 'Paradise' shows the peaceful world Olga reaches after her death. Godard appears as himself, along with Palestinian poet Mahmoud Darwish and Spanish novelist Juan Goytisolo, who appear under their real names. The 4K restored version will be screened in Japan for the first time as part of the special screening series 'Jean-Luc Godard in the 21st Century: Our Films 2001-2010' (starting June 20, 2026, at Theater Image Forum Shibuya and other locations nationwide).
title_norm:nouvelle vague: From the director of "Boyhood" and the "Before" series, Richard Linklater, comes a film that goes behind the scenes of Jean-Luc Godard's "Breathless"—a landmark work of the French New Wave, the revolutionary film movement that emerged in the late 1950s. It depicts the young people who sparked a revolution in film history, along with their vibrant interactions with the leading filmmakers of French cinema. In 1959, France. Jean-Luc Godard, a 28-year-old critic writing for the film magazine "Cahiers du Cinéma," begins production on his feature directorial debut, "Breathless," starring French up-and-coming actor Jean-Paul Belmondo and American starlet Jean Seberg. Those around him are thrown off by Godard's innovative and freewheeling shooting methods, but the set, fueled by a shared passion for filmmaking, is filled with energy. Following the style of "Breathless," the film is shot in black and white in the Academy ratio (1:1.37), almost entirely in French, and the cast, except for Zoey Deutch as Jean Seberg, is made up of mostly unknown actors. Guillaume Marbeck, who worked as a photographer and model, was cast as the protagonist Godard. The film was selected for the Competition section of the 78th Cannes Film Festival in 2025.
title_norm:nénette et boni: In the port city of Marseille in southern France. Young Boni works at a pizzeria, spending his days belonging nowhere. One day, his long-estranged younger sister Nenette suddenly appears and crashes at his place. Having nowhere to go, Nenette carries a secret: she is pregnant. But she never reveals this fact to Boni. In their awkward cohabitation, the two spend time maintaining a distance they cannot cross. Boni develops feelings for a woman who works at a bakery, but cannot turn those feelings into reality. Nenette confronts her own body and tries to choose her future. In a cruel world, desire and tenderness quietly transform their relationship. Unspoken emotions slowly seep through.
title_norm:nụ hôn bạc tỷ: A massive hit released in Vietnam in 2025, drawing approximately 2.56 million viewers and earning around 1.2 billion yen at the box office, ranking among the country's top 10 highest-grossing films of all time. Its universal themes of love, money, family, and life choices resonated with audiences across generations. To reclaim a lost family home filled with memories, Van reluctantly follows a plan devised by her sister Kieu and best friend Thien, approaching two wealthy suitors who are pursuing her. One is a man with calm, mature charm and warmth. The other is young, unconventional, and a playboy. Van eventually discovers her true feelings, but also learns that both men have their own hidden motives for approaching her. Thu Tran, who has been active as a Vietnamese actor and producer, makes her directorial debut while also starring and producing.
title_norm:o bi, o ba the end of civiliz: One of four dark sci-fi works by Piotr Szulkin, a pioneer of dystopian science fiction in Poland, created under the socialist regime in the late 1970s and 1980s. With a style blending fierce satire and extreme surrealism, the film explores the theme of "escape from totalitarianism." In a world devastated by nuclear war, the planet is frozen, and radiation kills anyone who ventures outside the dome. A man who controls the last surviving humans walks among the crowds, preventing morale from collapsing, seducing prostitutes, suppressing rebellions, and occasionally feeding the hungry. But as the true evil nature of the dome becomes clear, he begins to question whether humanity is worth saving. The film had its Japanese theatrical premiere in 2026 as part of the special screening series "Polish Dark Sci-Fi: The End of Civilization Tetralogy" (starting February 21, 2026, at Theater Image Forum).
title_norm:o bi, o ba. koniec cywilizacj: One of four dark sci-fi works by Piotr Szulkin, a pioneer of dystopian science fiction in Poland, created under the socialist regime in the late 1970s and 1980s. title_norm:obsession: The film 'Obsession: Disaster Love' has been sweeping film festivals around the world and generating fervent buzz on social media even before its release. It had its world premiere in the 'Midnight Madness' section of the 50th Toronto International Film Festival, winning second place in the Audience Award. It subsequently achieved three awards at the Sitges International Fantastic Film Festival, quickly becoming a hot topic among genre film fans. The trailer has been viewed over 1.7 million times on social media, and it holds a 95% Fresh rating on Rotten Tomatoes (as of May 25, 2026). After its US release, with a production budget of under $1 million, it grossed over $17 million in its opening weekend. Furthermore, in its second week, it rose in the rankings to second place, just behind 'Star Wars: The Mandalorian & Grogu' released that week, achieving an extraordinary hit with a cumulative box office (May 15-24) of over $50 million.
title_norm:occult: Kōji Shiraishi, the horror master known for "Noroi" and "Kuchisake-onna," delivers an ambitious work depicting the thrills and terrors of people producing an occult documentary program. Director Kiyoshi Kurosawa of "Akarui Mirai" and "Tokyo Sonata," and manga artist Peco Watanabe make special appearances. Film director Shiraishi, intrigued by a random murder that occurred at a tourist spot three years earlier, conducts an interview with Eno, the sole survivor of the incident, who is now a net café refugee.
title_norm:oldboy: Oh Dae-su, a man living an ordinary life, regains consciousness to find himself locked in a small, confined room. After 15 years of imprisonment without knowing why, he is suddenly released. Who did this?! For what purpose?! With the help of a young woman named Mi-do, Dae-su vows revenge. A mysterious man named Woo-jin appears before him and proposes a deadly "game": Dae-su must uncover the reason for his imprisonment within five days, with both their lives at stake. An unimaginable and terrifying scheme lies behind it all...
title_norm:on fallin: This human drama depicts the loneliness and division in modern society through the daily life of an immigrant woman working in a massive logistics center in Scotland, ultimately finding a faint glimmer of hope. Aurora, a Portuguese immigrant, works as a picker in a huge logistics center on the outskirts of Scotland. Her days are mostly spent walking through countless aisles following scanner instructions and retrieving items from shelves. Conversations with colleagues are limited to brief breaks, and after her shift, she drags her tired body back to a shared house for immigrant workers. Interactions among residents are superficial, relationships never deepen, and her rootless days continue monotonously. One day, Aurora accidentally breaks her smartphone. Losing this modern necessity—her means of workplace communication and her "companion" for passing time—slowly but surely begins to change her daily life. Portuguese-born, Scotland-based Laura Carreira wrote and directed her first feature film based on her own experiences as an immigrant, winning the Best Director Award at the 72nd San Sebastián International Film Festival in 2024.
title_norm:once we were us: Summer 2008, Seoul. University students Uno and Jeong-won meet fatefully on a long-distance bus. Uno, who dreams of becoming a game creator, and Jeong-won, who aspires to be an architect. Supporting each other through their urban days filled with dreams and anxieties, they eventually fall in love, deeply and truly. However, faced with the harshness of reality that youth cannot resist, they choose to part ways. Ten years later, in the summer of 2024, they coincidentally reunite on a flight to Seoul. As they look back on their memories, Uno asks Jeong-won a question he has kept buried deep in his heart: 'What if, back then...'
title_norm:one last throw: This film traces the life of former professional baseball player Shintaro Yokota, who was drafted second by the Hanshin Tigers and expected to have a bright future, but was forced to retire at age 21 after being diagnosed with a brain tumor. It stars Taya Matsutani and Kyoka Suzuki. In the 2013 draft, 18-year-old Shintaro Yokota was selected second by the Hanshin Tigers. In the opening game of 2016, he was chosen as a starter for the first team and recorded his first hit, with everyone holding great expectations for his future. However, soon after, Shintaro began experiencing double vision. The doctor's diagnosis was a brain tumor, a harsh reality for a 21-year-old. Nevertheless, supported by his family, mentors, and teammates, Shintaro fought against his illness. At his retirement game in September 2019, he performed a miraculous throw home, moving the stadium to tears. But Shintaro's story didn't end there. Matsutani, a former high school baseball player, plays Yokota, and Suzuki plays his mother, Manami. The director is Jun Akiyama of "20 Years Old Soul."
title_norm:one, two, three: A slapstick comedy filmed in Germany. McNamara, the head of Coca-Cola's Berlin branch, is tasked by a company executive with babysitting his daughter. However, this girl is a troublesome handful who defies easy handling. The protagonist's mindset of doing anything for career advancement echoes Billy Wilder's previous film "The Apartment." The rapid-fire exchange of gags in the dialogue is quintessentially Wilder. The film also showcases the full comedic charm of James Cagney, who also worked as a director.
title_norm:osaka elegy: Synopsis: Ayako (Yamada), a telephone operator, enters into a lover's contract with a married company president to cover her father's debts after he loses his job due to embezzlement suspicions... Considered one of Mizoguchi's masterpieces from before the war, the lively streets of Osaka and Yamada's modern fashion are also highlights.
title_norm:oslo, 31. august: The second feature film by director Joachim Trier (known for "The Worst Person in the World"), released in 2011. A bold adaptation of Pierre Drieu La Rochelle's novel "Le Feu Follet" (also the basis for Louis Malle's film "The Fire Within"), it sensitively portrays the pain and despair of a young man addicted to drugs, set in modern-day Oslo. Anders, undergoing a drug addiction treatment program at a facility in the suburbs, is plagued by suicidal thoughts. As his rehabilitation nears its end, he receives a leave pass and returns to his hometown of Oslo to reunite with friends. However, conversations are strained, and a job interview goes poorly. Eventually, he goes to a party but fails to fit in, and after a long period of abstinence, he starts drinking alcohol and then turns to drugs. This is the second film in what is called the "Oslo Trilogy," which includes Trier's 2006 debut "Reprise" and his 2021 film "The Worst Person in the World." Anders Danielsen Lie, who also starred in "Reprise," plays the protagonist Anders. The film was screened in the Un Certain Regard section at the 64th Cannes Film Festival in 2011. It received its first Japanese theatrical release as part of the special program "Joachim Trier: The Oslo Trilogy" (from February 13, 2026, at Bunkamura Le Cinéma Shibuya Miyashita in Tokyo and other venues).

title_norm:our little sister: A story spanning one year in the lives of three sisters (Ayase, Nagasawa, Kaho) who, after the death of their father who left home 15 years ago and with whom they had lost touch, come to live with their half-sister Suzu (Hirose), who has lost her own family. Based on the best-selling manga by Yoshida Akimi, it carefully depicts the town of Kamakura, where the story is set, and the changing seasons, while bringing to light the love and sorrows of women of different generations.
title_norm:over the town: Arakawa Ao (Ryuya Wakaba), who works at a vintage clothing store in Shimokitazawa, can't forget his ex-girlfriend who cheated on him and dumped him. His life, mostly spent alone—occasionally going to live shows or his usual bar—is self-contained within the Shimokitazawa area. One day, a female director attending art school invites him to appear in her independent film.
title_norm:oxana 裸の革命家・オクサナ:
2002, Khmelnytskyi, Western Ukraine. Oksana lives with her alcoholic father and her mother who devotedly supports him, earning a living for the family by painting icons. However, unable to endure the unfair treatment from the church and the deep-seated misogyny of an irrational society, she flees her home.

In 2008, she forms the feminist activist group "FEMEN" alongside comrades she met during street debates. Their activities expand, beginning with a protest against the death of a female patient due to medical malpractice. In 2009, while campaigning to eradicate sex tourism in the capital city of Kyiv, Oksana strips to the waist to garner attention, arriving at a mode of expression that utilizes the body as "combat gear."

Before long, their activism crosses borders. In 2011, she is detained and tortured for protesting the Alexander Lukashenko regime in Minsk, Belarus, and later sustains serious injuries during a protest against Vladimir Putin in Moscow. As surveillance and suppression of FEMEN intensify, Oksana is forced to make the decision to flee to Paris as a political refugee...
title_norm:oxana／裸の革命家・オクサナ: 2002, Khmelnytskyi, Western Ukraine. Oksana lives with her alcoholic father and her mother, who devotedly supports him. title_norm:pale blue dot 君が微笑めば、: 'Pale Blue Dot: If You Smile' (2024 / Japan / 97 min / 5.1ch / 16:9) Director: Koji Nishijima Narration: Yayako Uchida Cast: Rumiana Tsenkova, Shogo Shigeoka, Mikinosuke Kakisaka, Masataka Kakisaka, Haruo Saji Ending Theme: EPO 'Glory' (eponica Record) Organized by: 'Pale Blue Dot: If You Smile' Office
title_norm:panda! go panda!: This animation was planned following the panda boom in Japan sparked by China's gift of pandas to Ueno Zoo in 1972 as part of Japan-China friendship. Mimiko sends her grandmother off to a memorial service and will be living alone for a while. But when she returns home, there is a child panda who understands human speech. Then the father panda also appears. This panda father and child were lured by the bamboo grove near Mimiko's home. Mimiko treats the father panda, Papanda, as her own father and the child panda, Pan, as her child, and begins living together with them. One day, a policeman visiting Mimiko's house is startled to see the panda pair. In fact, Papanda and Pan had escaped from the zoo. The zoo director, alerted by the police, tries to take them back, but Pan gets lost, and a search begins. Pan is found swept away in a river, with a sluice-gate waterfall beyond—a major crisis. Can they rescue Pan? And can Mimiko and the panda pair live together again?
title_norm:panda! go panda! rainy day ci: Mimiko-chan, Pan-chan, and Papanda lived happily together every day. Then, one day, while Mimiko-chan and the others were out, two suspicious characters showed up... When Mimiko-chan returned, she was delighted, saying, "It's my first time seeing burglars!" but the pair ran away in a flash. Mimiko-chan was a little disappointed that the seemingly interesting guests had gone, but Pan-chan noticed that his food had been eaten. Pan-chan sniffed around the house searching. Crawling into Pan-chan's bed and sleeping soundly was... a tiger cub! Both of them were so surprised they ran around the house making a huge commotion...
title_norm:pandoras box: A sensual melodrama based on the play of the same name by F. Wedekind, which gave L. Brooks, who moved from Hollywood to Germany, the nickname 'Lulu' after her character. Lulu, a dancer in a seedy dive, becomes the mistress of Dr. Schön, a newspaper publisher, through the skills of her foster father Schigolch. She rises to perform in top theaters, and when Schön tries to break up with her, she turns the tables and forces him to marry her. Schön has a son of marriageable age, Alwa, who is also his secretary, and Lulu seduces him as if enjoying tearing the father and son apart. When Schön learns of her numerous affairs and the decisive truth, he threatens to kill Lulu and then himself, but in the struggle, she shoots him. Although captured, she escapes during the trial with the help of her foster father and Alwa. She lives a life of pleasure on a gambling ship in a port town, introduced by her lover, the strongman Rodrigo. But when Rodrigo sells her, a fight breaks out over her, and Lulu, her foster father, and Alwa secretly enter London. Reduced to extreme poverty in the slums, Lulu decides to become a prostitute, bringing a man into her room while the two men wait outside, unaware that the effeminate man is the infamous Jack the Ripper...
title_norm:paprika: Director Kon Satoshi, known for "Perfect Blue" and "Millennium Actress," boldly adapts Tsutsui Yasutaka's science fiction novel of the same name into this animated feature film. The "DC Mini," a revolutionary device developed at the Institute for Psychiatric Research, allows users to share dreams. Chiba Atsuko, a psychotherapist at the institute, enters her clients' dreams as Paprika, a dream detective with a completely different appearance and personality, conducting secret therapy sessions. One day, the DC Mini is stolen from the institute, and staff members begin to have strange dreams and suffer psychological damage. Paprika investigates and dives into dreams contaminated by mad imagery, but a terrifying trap awaits her there. Megumi Hayashibara voices the protagonist Paprika. Madhouse handles the animation, and musician Hirasawa Susumu provides the music. The film was screened in the competition section of the 63rd Venice International Film Festival in 2006. Director Kon passed away in 2010 after this film, which became his final feature-length work. In 2026, a 4K remastered version will be revived nationwide to commemorate the 20th anniversary.
title_norm:parasite: The fourth collaboration between director Bong Joon-ho ('Memories of Murder,' 'The Host,' 'Snowpiercer') and lead actor Song Kang-ho, this film won the Palme d'Or at the 72nd Cannes Film Festival in 2019, the first for a Korean film. It also garnered global attention by winning four awards at the 92nd Academy Awards, including Best Picture—the first for a foreign language film—as well as Best Director, Best Original Screenplay, and Best International Feature Film. The Kim family is all unemployed and living in poverty, scraping by day to day. One day, the eldest son, Ki-woo, goes to the lavish home of IT CEO Mr. Park for a tutoring job interview. Following him, his sister Ki-jeong also sets foot in the mansion. The encounter between these two families from opposite worlds accelerates into a tragicomedy beyond imagination at breakneck speed... Co-starring Lee Sun-kyun ('A Hard Day'), Cho Yeo-jeong ('The Concubine'), and Choi Woo-shik ('Train to Busan').
title_norm:paris ni saku étoile: Set in early 20th-century Paris, this animated film delicately and vividly portrays the struggles of two Japanese girls pursuing their dreams in a foreign land. In Paris at the turn of the century, two girls who came from Japan live there. One is Fujiko, who dreams of becoming a painter despite being expected to become a good wife supporting her husband. The other is Chizuru, born into a samurai family and a master of the naginata, but drawn to ballet. The two, who met once in Yokohama, reunite after five years when Chizuru helps Fujiko out of trouble. Learning of Chizuru's dream, Fujiko discovers that Olga, the mother of a young man named Ruslan living in the same apartment building, is a former Russian ballerina and arranges lessons for Chizuru. Meanwhile, Fujiko's guardian uncle goes missing. Ami Touma voices the protagonist Fujiko, who dreams of being a painter; Rina Arashi voices Chizuru, who aspires to be a ballerina; and Taichi Saotome voices Ruslan, the young man who meets Fujiko. Directed by Goro Taniguchi of "ONE PIECE FILM RED" and the "Code Geass: Lelouch of the Rebellion" series, with original character designs by Katsuya Kondo, who worked on character design and key animation for Studio Ghibli films like "Kiki's Delivery Service." The screenplay is by Reiko Yoshida of "The Colors Within" and "Violet Evergarden."
title_norm:paris vu par…: An omnibus film of short works, each directed by one of six leading directors of the French New Wave, all set against the backdrop of Paris. The six episodes are: "Saint-Denis Street" (directed by Jean-Daniel Pollet), about a timid man who brings a prostitute he met in a red-light district back to his apartment; "North Station" (Jean Rouch), about a woman living with her lover in an apartment far from the station who encounters an unexpected incident on her way to work after arguing with him; "Saint-Germain-des-Prés" (Jean Douchet), depicting the romantic entanglements of young people in a student quarter; "Place de l'Étoile" (Éric Rohmer), about a man heading to work through the Place de l'Étoile who faces a series of troubles; "Montparnasse and Levallois" (Jean-Luc Godard), about a woman who writes love letters to two different men but accidentally mails the wrong ones; and "La Muette" (Claude Chabrol), depicting a tragedy that strikes a bourgeois family in an upscale neighborhood from the son's perspective. The cast includes Joanna Shimkus from "The Adventurers," Stéphane Audran from "Babette's Feast," and Barbet Schroeder, who also produced this film, among others.
title_norm:pascals しあわせのようなもの: A documentary about the acoustic orchestra band "Pascals," led by Rocket Matsu. Formed in 1995, the group has garnered popularity for their unique, euphoric sound. They have composed numerous scores for films, television dramas, and stage productions—including *The Fish Child* and *Riverside Mukolitta*—and have received high acclaim internationally, particularly in France. While the band had performed with the same lineup for approximately 25 years, cellist Kota Miki passed away suddenly in April 2020. Focusing on memorial concerts held in the spring of 2021 and 2022 during the pandemic, the film captures their music as they grapple with "a presence defined by absence." Directed by Shinichi Ise, the documentary filmmaker behind *Nao-chan* and *Now is Past: My Father, Java & the Phantom Films*.
title_norm:passage of life: Set in Japan and Myanmar, this drama is based on a true story about a Myanmar family living in Japan. Kane lives in a small Tokyo apartment with her two young sons. After her husband Aise is detained by immigration authorities, Kane must support the family alone. Since her children grew up in Japan and cannot speak their native language, Kane pours all her love into them using her imperfect Japanese, but the brothers, stressed by their father's absence, fight daily. Growing anxious about their future, Kane increasingly longs to return to Myanmar, where she was born and raised. This is director Akiro Fujimoto's feature-length debut. The film was screened in the 'Asian Future' section of the 30th Tokyo International Film Festival in 2017, where it won both the section's Best Picture Award and the Japan Foundation Asia Center Special Prize.
title_norm:pastoral to die in the countr: An autobiographical work written and directed by Shuji Terayama, adapting his own poetry collection of the same name. In a village at the foot of Mount Osore in Aomori Prefecture, a young boy, 'I', lives with his mother in an old house after losing his father. The boy's only solace is having an itako (a spirit medium) summon his father's spirit to talk to him. A beautiful woman who marries into the neighboring house and a circus troupe that comes to the village tempt the boy to run away from home. Later, 'I' grows up, moves to Tokyo, becomes middle-aged, and makes a film. Before this 'I' appears the boy he once was... Kantaro Suga, known for 'Thirteen Assassins' and others, plays the lead, and Kaoru Yachigusa plays the neighbor's wife.
title_norm:pathaan: A spy action film starring Indian cinema superstar Shah Rukh Khan, known for films like "My Name Is Khan" and "Om Shanti Om." When the Indian government revokes the autonomy of the Kashmir region spanning India and Pakistan, an enraged Pakistani General Qadir teams up with former Indian soldier Jim to plan a terrorist attack. Pathaan, an agent of India's intelligence agency RAW (Research and Analysis Wing), moves to stop Jim's planned biological weapon attack. However, it is discovered that a biological weapon has been planted on a plane flying over Delhi. With only six minutes left in a desperate situation, Pathaan, India's top agent, fights to protect his homeland. It has become a talking point that Tiger, the spy played by Salman Khan in the film "Tiger: The Legendary Spy"—which also features the same Indian intelligence agency RAW—is set as a colleague of the protagonist Pathaan in this film. Directed by Siddharth Anand of "War" and "Bang Bang!" Deepika Padukone, who has co-starred with Shah Rukh Khan in films like "Om Shanti Om" and "Chennai Express," plays the heroine Rubai.
title_norm:pathaan パターン: A spy action film starring Indian cinema superstar Shah Rukh Khan, known for films like "My Name Is Khan" and "Om Shanti Om." When the Indian government revokes the autonomy of the Kashmir region spanning India and Pakistan, an enraged Pakistani General Qadir teams up with former Indian soldier Jim to plan a terrorist attack. Pathaan, an agent of India's intelligence agency RAW (Research and Analysis Wing), moves to stop Jim's planned biological weapon attack. However, it is discovered that a biological weapon has been planted on a plane flying over Delhi. With only six minutes left in a desperate situation, Pathaan, India's top agent, fights to protect his homeland. It has become a talking point that Tiger, the spy played by Salman Khan in the film "Tiger: The Legendary Spy"—which also features the same Indian intelligence agency RAW—is set as a colleague of the protagonist Pathaan in this film. Directed by Siddharth Anand of "War" and "Bang Bang!" Deepika Padukone, who has co-starred with Shah Rukh Khan in films like "Om Shanti Om" and "Chennai Express," plays the heroine Rubai.
title_norm:pathaan／パターン: A spy action film starring Indian cinema superstar Shah Rukh Khan, known for films like "My Name Is Khan" and "Om Shanti Om." When the Indian government revokes the autonomy of the Kashmir region spanning India and Pakistan, an enraged Pakistani General Qadir teams up with former Indian soldier Jim to plan a terrorist attack. Pathaan, an agent of India's intelligence agency RAW (Research and Analysis Wing), moves to stop Jim's planned biological weapon attack. However, it is discovered that a biological weapon has been planted on a plane flying over Delhi. With only six minutes left in a desperate situation, Pathaan, India's top agent, fights to protect his homeland. It has become a talking point that Tiger, the spy played by Salman Khan in the film "Tiger: The Legendary Spy"—which also features the same Indian intelligence agency RAW—is set as a colleague of the protagonist Pathaan in this film. Directed by Siddharth Anand of "War" and "Bang Bang!" Deepika Padukone, who has co-starred with Shah Rukh Khan in films like "Om Shanti Om" and "Chennai Express," plays the heroine Rubai.
title_norm:patlabor ezy file 2: During an internal audit at headquarters, Kurumi from the maintenance team notices that one live round for the revolver cannon is missing. She consults Kikkyo, and one by one, the other squad members get drawn into the situation. Unaware of this, Towa and Saki begin to suspect the attitudes of Kikkyo and the others...
title_norm:pauline at the beach: The third film in Éric Rohmer's "Comedies and Proverbs" series. It depicts the romantic entanglements of six men and women at a seaside villa, seen through the eyes of adolescent girl Pauline. Fifteen-year-old Pauline comes to Normandy for a vacation with her older cousin Marion. When they go to the beach, they meet Marion's ex-boyfriend Pierre. Pierre still harbors feelings for Marion, but Marion falls for Henri, a playboy acquaintance of Pierre's. Meanwhile, Pauline grows close to Sylvain, a boy windsurfing at the beach... The film won the Silver Bear and the FIPRESCI Prize at the Berlin International Film Festival.
title_norm:pauline à la plage: The third film in Éric Rohmer's "Comedies and Proverbs" series. It depicts the romantic entanglements of six men and women at a seaside villa, seen through the eyes of adolescent girl Pauline. Fifteen-year-old Pauline comes to Normandy for a vacation with her older cousin Marion. When they go to the beach, they meet Marion's ex-boyfriend Pierre. Pierre still harbors feelings for Marion, but Marion falls for Henri, a playboy acquaintance of Pierre's. Meanwhile, Pauline grows close to Sylvain, a boy windsurfing at the beach... The film won the Silver Bear and the FIPRESCI Prize at the Berlin International Film Festival.
title_norm:paw patrol the dino movie: The third theatrical film in the popular North American children's animated series "PAW Patrol," affectionately known as "Paupato." It depicts the adventures of the boy Kent and his team of unique puppies, the PAW Patrol, as they strive to save Dino Island, home to gentle dinosaurs, from a crisis. On Dino Island, where dinosaurs live, Mayor Rival uses dynamite to excavate the island's diamonds, causing a massive explosion. This triggers a volcanic eruption, putting the dinosaurs in grave danger. The Japanese voice cast includes Megumi Han as Kent, Shizuka Ishigami as Chase, Mako Komatsu as Marshall, Shiori Izawa as Skye, Sōma Saitō as Rubble, Miyuki Kobori as Rocky, and Sayuri Yahagi as Zuma, all reprising their roles from previous series. Guest voice actors include Yūko Ōshima and the comedy duo "Rainbow" members Takao Jumbo and Naoto Ikeda. The theme song is a new track written by the Backstreet Boys titled "Bottle Up."
title_norm:peacock ／ピーコック: A perfect son, a cultured lover, a thug for those who want to play hero on a date—'My Companion' is an agency that provides ideal individuals for any situation. Matthias, their top performer, perfectly plays the required roles, living through various personalities every day. However, when his girlfriend Sofia tells him 'I don't feel the real you' and they break up, his perfect mask begins to quietly peel away. Furthermore, an unexpected incident with a client causes Matthias's gears to gradually start grinding, and eventually the boundary between reality and fiction becomes blurred...
title_norm:peacock／ピーコック: The perfect son, a cultured lover, a thug for hire for those who want to play hero on a date—Matthias is the top performer at "My Companion," an agency that provides ideal personas for any situation. He flawlessly plays the roles demanded of him, living out various personalities every day. However, triggered by a sudden breakup with his girlfriend Sofia and an unexpected incident with a client, Matthias's gears begin to slowly grind out of alignment, and the boundary between reality and fiction gradually blurs...
title_norm:peak end: A feature film directed, planned, and starring Korean-born filmmaker Shin Chae-rin, created as her graduation project from the Kyoto University of Arts Film Department. Shot with a minimal production setup and incorporating documentary elements, it was screened at various film festivals, including being an invited work at the 21st Osaka Asian Film Festival and selected for the 47th Pia Film Festival. Rin, who came to Kyoto from Seoul, and Sora, who came to Kyoto from Okinawa, meet at university and aspire to make films. They give form to the impulses and desires that arise in their daily lives through the act of 'making a film.' Their relationship, which seeks to know each other through actions like sending jam sandwiches flying into the sky or tracing roots in Okinawa, continues to change. Shin Chae-rin plays Rin, and Sora Itami from Okinawa plays Sora, both also participating in the production. The film was made by a small team of five staff members, including the two actresses.
title_norm:pelikan blue: An animated film that visualizes an astonishing true story from 1990s Hungary in Eastern Europe, incorporating documentary materials. In 1990s Hungary, after the fall of the Iron Curtain opened the door to Western Europe, foreign travel was liberalized, and many people turned their eyes to the outside world. However, international train tickets were expensive and out of reach for ordinary people. Amidst this, three young men—intellectual Akos, fearless Pecha, and swimming enthusiast Laci—find a way to forge tickets. They dissolve the blue carbon ink "Pelikan Blue" from the company Pelikan, used on the tickets, with household detergent and rewrite the destinations. After enjoying overseas trips with forged tickets, they decide to distribute "tickets to freedom" to other young people in similar situations. The plan seems to go smoothly, but eventually, a police investigation begins, escalating into a major uproar that shakes the nation. Directed by László Csáki, known for his distinctive animation style, who conducted meticulous research over ten years and blends documentary materials like archival footage and interview audio with hand-drawn animation.
title_norm:penguin highway: An animated film adaptation of the novel that won the Japan SF Award, written by popular author Tomihiko Morimi, known for works like "The Night is Short, Walk on Girl" and "The Eccentric Family." This is the first feature-length film from Studio Colorido, the studio behind the shorts "Shiranpuri" and "Typhoon Noruda." It is directed by the emerging talent Hiroyasu Ishida (of "Shiranpuri" fame), with character designs by Yojiro Arai ("Typhoon Noruda"). Aoyama-kun, a studious fourth grader who diligently records everything he learns in a notebook, is close friends with the young woman at his dental clinic. She, in turn, dotes on the slightly cheeky and precocious Aoyama-kun. One day, a penguin suddenly appears in their residential town, which has no ocean nearby. Why would a penguin show up in a mere housing district? Aoyama-kun begins his research to solve the mystery, but then witnesses the young woman's discarded cola can transform into a penguin. Kana Kita, known for the TV drama "Byplayers," voices Aoyama-kun in her voice acting debut, while Yu Aoi, who has voice acting experience in "Tekkonkinkreet" and "The Case of Hana & Alice," plays the role of the young woman.
title_norm:peppermint candy: A human drama that traces twenty years in the life of a man against the backdrop of modern Korean history, winning five major awards including Best Picture at the Grand Bell Awards, South Korea's equivalent of the Oscars. This is the second feature film by director Lee Chang-dong, made in 1999, known for "Oasis" and "Secret Sunshine." Spring, 1999. Kim Yeong-ho, at the depths of despair after losing his job and family, shows up at a picnic with old friends wearing an out-of-place suit. It is the same place he visited twenty years earlier with his first love, Sunim. Standing on the railroad tracks, Yeong-ho shouts "I want to go back!" at an oncoming train, and his life begins to rewind. We see his self-destructed marriage to his wife Hong-ja, his love for Sunim that drew them together but was never fulfilled, and the Gwangju Uprising he witnessed as a soldier. Yeong-ho's journey through memory eventually arrives at the time twenty years ago when his life was most beautiful and pure. The film was released in a 4K-restored digital remaster in 2019 to coincide with the release of Lee Chang-dong's "Burning." A 4K restoration was also screened in 2023 as part of the special retrospective "Lee Chang-dong Retrospective 4K."
title_norm:perfume cold sleep –25 years: A documentary depicting the 25-year culmination of the three-member music unit 'Perfume,' which announced a 'cold sleep' (hiatus) in 2025. Formed in Hiroshima in 1999, Perfume gained attention not only in Japan but worldwide after the huge breakout success of their 2007 single 'Polyrhythm.' Having raced through 25 years, they announced a hiatus from 2026, termed a 'cold sleep,' on September 21, 2025, the 20th anniversary of their major debut. This film looks back at their journey from formation to the present, including live performances—especially their last concert before the cold sleep and first Tokyo Dome show in five years, 'Perfume ZO/Z5 Anniversary "Nebula Romance" Episode TOKYO DOME' held on September 22 and 23—along with unreleased footage. It also closely follows the behind-the-scenes after the cold sleep announcement and features exclusive interviews with the three members. The three, who have grown both as artists and as people over 25 years, explore what has changed and what remains constant, as well as their feelings about the cold sleep. The director is Taketoshi Sado, who also directed the 2015 Perfume documentary film 'WE ARE Perfume WORLD TOUR 3rd DOCUMENT.'
