title_norm:petite maman: Directed and written by Céline Sciamma of "Portrait of a Lady on Fire," this film weaves a story of loss and healing connecting three generations: daughter, mother, and grandmother. Eight-year-old Nelly, grieving her beloved grandmother, is taken by her parents to clean out the forest house where her grandmother lived. But her mother, who spent her own childhood there, is overwhelmed by memories at every turn and eventually leaves. Left behind, Nelly wanders the woods and meets another eight-year-old girl who calls herself Marion—the same name as Nelly's mother. The girl invites Nelly to her home, which turns out to be "grandma's house." Sisters Joséphine and Gabrielle Sanz, making their film debut, play Nelly and Marion. Nina Meurisse ("A Woman's Life") and Margot Abascal ("Sagan") co-star. The film was presented in the competition section of the 71st Berlin International Film Festival in 2021.
title_norm:pfau bin ich echt: A perfect son, a cultured lover, a thug for those who want to play hero on a date—'My Companion' is an agency that provides ideal individuals for any situation. Matthias, their top performer, perfectly plays the required roles, living through various personalities every day. However, when his girlfriend Sofia tells him 'I don't feel the real you' and they break up, his perfect mask begins to quietly peel away. Furthermore, an unexpected incident with a client causes Matthias's gears to gradually start grinding, and eventually the boundary between reality and fiction becomes blurred...
title_norm:piccola felicita～小さな幸せ～: An ensemble drama depicting the lives of three couples at crossroads in life. A former restaurant manager facing mandatory retirement after 25 years and grappling with loneliness, a painter struggling under his father's shadow and on the verge of divorce, and a young man captivated by a mysterious hotel guest. When their seemingly unrelated daily lives intersect, heartwarming "little miracles" unfold alongside unexpected events.
title_norm:piccola felicità 〜小さな幸せ〜: An ensemble drama depicting the lives of three couples at crossroads in life. A former restaurant manager facing mandatory retirement after 25 years and grappling with loneliness, a painter struggling under his father's shadow and on the verge of divorce, and a young man captivated by a mysterious hotel guest. When their seemingly unrelated daily lives intersect, heartwarming "little miracles" unfold alongside unexpected events.
title_norm:piccola felicità（ピッコラ・フェリチタ）: The fourth feature film directed by actor Yutaka Mizutani, familiar from the "Aibou" series. Mizutani also handles planning, script, production, and lead acting, as unpredictable stories intertwine involving three couples in their 60s, 40s, and 30s. Sato, retiring after 25 years at a restaurant, divorced and unable to see his daughter, feels his life is over. A small miracle brings him unexpected joy. Fujio, who runs a painting class, struggles under his painter father's shadow, drowning in alcohol and women daily. Divorce from his estranged wife Miki seems inevitable, but Fujio's final confession changes everything. Reo, working at a hotel, falls in love at first sight with Aoi, whom he meets at a café, and they quickly fall for each other. But Reo learns a secret about Aoi. The human dramas of these three couples are depicted with a theme color set for each story. Alongside Mizutani, the cast includes Nobue Iketani, Nanahana, Gamon Kaiga, Shuri, and Jun Hashimoto. This film marks the first parent-child co-starring role for Mizutani and Shuri. Cinematography is by Masahiro Aida, who also worked on the "Aibou" series, and music by Yoshiki Yamamoto from Mizutani's previous film "Taiyo to Bolero."
title_norm:pickpocket: Michel, a poor university student, discovers by chance that he has a talent for pickpocketing. Though once caught by a detective, he is released due to lack of evidence and soon targets others' wallets again. Eventually, his methods become organized as he brings in accomplices. In 'A Man Escaped,' Bresson realistically and thrillingly depicted a prison break; here, he turns his focus to pickpocketing, introducing actual techniques while portraying a lonely young man distrustful of others. A gripping masterpiece where the realism born from amateur actors and the suspense created by various pickpocketing scenes blend seamlessly.
title_norm:pierrot le fou: A masterpiece by Jean-Luc Godard, released in 1965 and revered as a cornerstone of the French New Wave. Ferdinand, called 'Pierrot,' is driven by an urge to escape his boring married life and spends a night with his former lover Marianne, whom he meets by chance. The next morning, finding a dead stranger, the two go on the run, but Marianne eventually tires of Ferdinand and betrays him by colluding with gangsters. A digitally remastered version with a new translation by Jiro Terao was released in 2016. A 2K restored version was released in 2022 and 2026.
title_norm:play it, boogie woogie: Goro and Sachino first met on the Third Keihin Expressway. Sachino, thrown out of a white Mustang, was rescued by Goro, who was riding a motorcycle. The two begin living together. Meanwhile, the middle-aged man who was driving the Mustang is also leading a strange cohabitation. Sachino starts working at a snack bar called Queen Elizabeth. Goro gets into a fight and quits his part-time job. When Goro leaves home, Sachino decides to meet the middle-aged man.
title_norm:playlist アジアの才能: An omnibus film collecting works from five young directors from Japan, South Korea, China, Taiwan, and Vietnam. Selected from short films screened at the 20th and 21st Osaka Asian Film Festival, these five works showcase next-generation talent, arranged like a music album under the 'PLAYLIST' concept. Though each piece differs in setting and style, they capture universal emotions—love, growth, loss, identity—through the eyes of today's youth. The lineup includes: 'Boxing Day' by China's Zhang Xiaoyi, depicting a nurse who develops feelings for a discharged boxer and is led into a strange dream; 'Suzuki' by South Korea's Ahn Jung-min, following a middle schooler who loves Western music and grows through admiration and unexpected loss after meeting someone in a chat room; 'Rooftop Lempicka' by Vietnam's Nguyen Luong Hang, showing a 10-year-old girl glimpsing the adult world through a Tamara de Lempicka art book found in a bookstore and interactions with a waitress; 'Black Dog' by Taiwan's Yang Lin, exploring family through a girl's attempt to solve the mystery of strange howling from her father's room at night; and 'Melting in the Street' by Japan's Nako Komiyama, depicting queer children who are drawn to each other as they share secrets, along with their struggles and a small escape.
title_norm:poca pon: Living in poverty, bothered by noisy neighbors. Frustrated with an absurd reality, middle school student Kenta struggles to support his mother Asako and younger brother Yuji. And then there's the mysterious "pokapon" sound echoing around him. Watching over this family quietly is the housing complex manager, Shunichi. Eventually, Kenta and Shunichi begin to understand each other, but rumors start to circulate that the perpetrator of a series of child murders that once shocked the nation is hiding in this housing complex...
title_norm:poca pon ポカポン: Living in poverty, bothered by noisy neighbors. Frustrated with an absurd reality, middle school student Kenta struggles to support his mother Asako and younger brother Yuji. And then there's the mysterious "pokapon" sound echoing around him. Watching over this family quietly is the housing complex manager, Shunichi. Eventually, Kenta and Shunichi begin to understand each other, but rumors start to circulate that the perpetrator of a series of child murders that once shocked the nation is hiding in this housing complex...
title_norm:point blank: A hard-boiled action film directed by British master John Boorman in 1967, early in his career, starring Hollywood legend Lee Marvin ('The Dirty Dozen,' 'The Professionals'). Based on Richard Stark's crime novel 'The Hunter' (featuring the character Parker), it depicts a man's revenge against his betrayers, blending avant-garde New Wave techniques with the psychedelic culture of the American West Coast. Walker, at the request of his friend Reese, robs a criminal organization's deal at the abandoned Alcatraz prison and steals a large sum of money. However, Reese betrays Walker, shooting him and fleeing with his $93,000 share and Walker's wife, Lyn. As his consciousness fades, memories and fantasies swirl through Walker's mind. Surviving, Walker sets out to recover his share and exact revenge, tracking Reese down. Marvin delivers a powerful performance as the ruthless avenger Walker, with Angie Dickinson ('Rio Bravo') and John Vernon ('Dirty Harry') co-starring.
title_norm:pola x: The fourth feature film by French wunderkind Leos Carax, released eight years after 'The Lovers on the Bridge.' An adaptation of the novel 'Pierre' by 19th-century American author Herman Melville, written the year after his masterpiece 'Moby-Dick.' Shifting the setting to modern-day Paris, it uses emotional imagery and sound to depict the intense, racing love of a man and woman swept up by fate and drawn into despair. Pierre, a young novelist living in a Norman castle, enjoys a wealthy, contented rural life with his mother Marie and fiancée Lucie. One day, Isabelle, a Bosnian refugee claiming to be Pierre's half-sister, appears. Drawn to Isabelle's charm, Pierre abandons everything and heads to Paris with her. Guillaume Depardieu, son of Gérard Depardieu, passionately plays Pierre, and Katerina Golubeva, known for 'Paris at Night,' plays Isabelle. Catherine Deneuve co-stars as Pierre's mother Marie. Cinematography is by Éric Gautier, known for 'My King,' and music is by singer-songwriter Scott Walker. A 4K restored version will be re-released in February 2026.
title_norm:popeye the slayer man: A horror film based on the popular cartoon character 'Popeye,' created by American cartoonist Elzie Crisler Segar in 1929. Produced after the original copyright expired in January 2025, entering the public domain, it depicts the righteous sailor Popeye awakening as a brutal murderer, armed with his familiar can of spinach and powerful forearms. College student Dexter is making a documentary about a local legend in a small port town: a sailor who wanders the docks every night in search of prey. One night, Dexter brings along Olivia, whom he has long had a crush on, and their friends to sneak into an abandoned factory near the port for investigation. As they proceed in a somewhat playful mood, the smell of pipe tobacco begins to drift from somewhere, and soon the legendary sailor emerges from the darkness. As his companions are brutally killed one after another, Dexter and Olivia desperately flee, following clues left in the factory to uncover the sailor's true identity.
title_norm:pornostar: Kamijo struggles to scrape together tribute money for the yakuza while harboring ambitions of one day surpassing them. Then, a man named Koya appears—a man who kills yakuza without so much as a flicker of expression. Koya fills a sports bag with knives and goes around stabbing anyone who calls himself a yakuza, one after another.
title_norm:postcard: Near the end of the war, 100 middle-aged soldiers are called up. Their postings are decided by their superior officer's lottery. Realizing he won't return alive after being assigned to the Philippines, Morikawa Teizo asks Matsuyama Keita to deliver a postcard to his wife, Tomoko, and tell her he read it. After the war ends, only six soldiers, including Keita, survive. Based on the postcard, they visit Tomoko's house, but...
title_norm:pretty crazy: A romantic comedy from director Lee Sang-geun, who previously scored a massive hit in Korea with 'EXIT' and reunites with Im Yoon-ah. It follows a woman possessed by a demon who shows completely different faces by day and night, and the kind-hearted young man who falls for her. On leave from work, Gil-gu falls in love at first sight with Seon-ji, a baker who moves in downstairs. But when he encounters her late that night, she is entirely different. Her father Jang-su explains that Seon-ji is gentle and bright by day, but at 2 AM a demon awakens, transforming her. Gil-gu agrees to Jang-su's odd request to watch over Seon-ji at night. She drags him out every night, running wild and selfishly bossing him around. Im Yoon-ah, a Girls' Generation member known for films like 'EXIT' and drama 'The King's Chef', plays Seon-ji. Ahn Bo-hyun, from the drama 'Spring Fever', plays Gil-gu. Song Dong-il, known for the 'Reply' series, plays Seon-ji's protective father Jang-su.
title_norm:pretty cure all stars dx3 del: Childhood friends Hibiki Hojo and Kanade Minamino, along with the fairy Hummy, visit a massive shopping mall on its opening day, but they lose sight of Hummy along the way. They manage to find her, but end up crashing into a fashion show hosted by Erika Kurumi. Amidst this, buildings and residents from other worlds, such as the Toy Kingdom and the Dessert Kingdom, suddenly appear. Furthermore, powerful enemies who once tormented the Pretty Cures are revived by the dark power of a black hole, plotting to wither the miracle flower connecting worlds, the "Prism Flower," and plunge the world into darkness. The Pretty Cures are sent to different worlds by the enemies' scheme, separated from their usual partners and allies, and each is invited into the worlds created by their formidable foes.
title_norm:priest of darkness: To save the daughter of an amazake shop owner from a dire situation, two rogues throw themselves into the fray. A masterpiece showcasing perfect chemistry between the renowned actors of Zenshinza and director Yamanaka. The beauty of a 15-year-old Setsuko Hara is captivating.
title_norm:primavera: A drama based on the true story of composer Vivaldi's appointment as a violin teacher at the Ospedale della Pietà in Venice in the early 18th century, depicting the growth of a lonely girl whose talent blossoms under his guidance, and Vivaldi's inner ambition, craving recognition for his own genius. Venice, 1716, at the Ospedale della Pietà. Cecilia, raised without knowing her mother's presence or love, secretly slips out of bed every night to write letters to her mother with no address. To leave the Pietà and live in the outside world, her mother must come for her, or she must marry a nobleman. Amidst this, Antonio Vivaldi, arriving as a violin teacher, discovers Cecilia's exceptional violin skill and appoints her as the leader of the first violins. Under Vivaldi, Cecilia endures rigorous practice, hones her violin skills, and they gradually grow close. However, the officer the Pietà has chosen as Cecilia's husband returns from war, and an incident soon occurs. Tekla Insolia, noted for the Italian TV drama 'The Art of Joy,' plays Cecilia, and Michele Riondino of 'The Sleeping Beauty' plays Vivaldi. The film is directed and written by Damiano Michieletto, a leading Italian opera director who served as creative director for the opening and closing ceremonies of the Milan Cortina Winter Olympics.
title_norm:primitive war: A survival action film depicting a deadly battle between dinosaurs that suddenly appear in the jungles of the Vietnam War and the U.S. military. In 1968, amidst the intense Vietnam War, the elite 'Viper Squad' of the U.S. Army Green Berets, on a special mission, goes missing in the jungle. The U.S. 'Vulture Platoon,' dispatched to search for them, encounters deep in the jungle a horde of dinosaurs, including Tyrannosaurus and Triceratops. Facing attacks from land, river, and air, the Vulture Platoon members engage in a fierce battle against the dinosaurs. Directed by Luke Sparke, an up-and-coming Australian filmmaker who single-handedly handled the script, production, editing, and art direction. Dale Dye, a retired Marine who served in the Vietnam War and appeared in 'Platoon' and 'Saving Private Ryan,' supervised the script, adding realism to the war film.
title_norm:princess arete: The time is the Middle Ages. A princess is confined to a small room at the top of a high tower, never showing her face to the people. Her mission is to remain pure until the day her future husband appears. But she, Princess Arete, gazes down from the tower window at the people living in the castle town below and ponders the meaning of life. One day, deciphering an ancient document, she discovers a secret passage and escapes the castle to go into town. The castle town is a world of artisans. The way each of their hands creates meaningful objects is like watching magic. If human hands hold such potential, then surely there must be something my hands can do...
title_norm:princess yang kwei fei: A commentary: Emperor Xuanzong of Tang, grieving the loss of his beloved consort, sets his sights on a young woman... Mizoguchi's first color film, a co-production with Hong Kong, is a courtly tapestry portraying the love and tragic fate of Yang Guifei, the beauty who toppled an empire. The restrained color palette that highlights the exotic costumes and art direction is striking.
title_norm:private life: Oscar-winning actress Jodie Foster, known for 'The Accused' and 'The Silence of the Lambs', stars in her first French-language film in this mystery. Lilian, a successful American psychoanalyst practicing in Paris, receives news that Paula, a long-time patient, has died. Suspicious of Paula's death, Lilian suspects murder but cannot involve the police due to patient confidentiality. She decides to uncover the truth herself. Meanwhile, since learning of Paula's death, Lilian has been troubled by uncontrollable crying, regardless of the situation, and visits her ex-husband Gabriel, an ophthalmologist. Though the cause of her tears remains unclear, Gabriel agrees to help Lilian investigate Paula's case. As she embarks on a detective-like investigation, Lilian delves into dangerous truths. Foster plays the protagonist, psychoanalyst Lilian, entirely in French. Daniel Auteuil, known for 'La Belle Époque', plays her ex-husband and investigative partner Gabriel. Virginie Efira from 'Suddenly Sick' and Mathieu Amalric from 'Quantum of Solace' co-star. The film is directed by Rebecca Zlotowski, known for 'Grand Central' and 'Planetarium'.
title_norm:profondo rosso: The splendid murder aesthetics of Dario Argento, the emperor of Italian horror, explode throughout the film. In Japan, after the huge success of 'Suspiria' (1977) with the clever tagline 'Never watch it alone,' this film was given a Japanese title to ride on that wave and was released in theaters, but it is actually unrelated in content and was made before that film. A shocking work that weaves the mystery of a series of gruesome murders with Argento's signature gorgeous and shocking visual beauty. Starring David Hemmings from 'Blow-Up' and Daria Nicolodi, Argento's good partner both publicly and privately. At the European Parapsychology Conference held in Rome, a telepathic woman named Helga, while demonstrating her abilities on stage, senses someone's murderous intent and becomes hysterical. She declares that a person who has committed brutal murders is in the audience. Later, Helga is brutally murdered in her room. Mark, a British pianist who happens to arrive at the scene and witnesses the murder and a suspect, teams up with journalist Jenna to investigate the mystery, but the truth they ultimately uncover is beyond imagination.
title_norm:project hail mary: A film adaptation of the bestselling science fiction novel by Andy Weir, author of "The Martian" (the basis for the Oscar-nominated "The Martian"). It depicts a middle school science teacher entrusted with the fate of Earth on the brink of extinction, who encounters an unknown life form with the same purpose at the edge of the universe, and together they risk their lives to save their home planets. An unexplained anomaly occurs where the sun's energy is being drained. If this continues, Earth will freeze and humanity will perish. It is discovered that the same phenomenon is happening not only to the sun but to countless stars scattered across the universe, and a single intact star is found 11.9 light-years away. Humanity's only remaining option is to travel to that star in a spaceship and solve the mystery to save the sun and humanity. Sent into space for this "Hail Mary" project is Grace, a brilliant scientist who left academia and now works as a humble middle school teacher. Alone in the vastness of space far from Earth, he relies on his scientific knowledge to tackle the mission, where he meets Rocky, an alien also struggling to save his home planet. Despite their different forms and languages, the two use science as a common language to face challenges, developing a friendship along the way. Ryan Gosling of "La La Land" and "Barbie" plays the protagonist middle school teacher Grace, with Sandra Hüller of "Anatomy of a Fall" and "The Zone of Interest" co-starring. Drew Goddard, who also worked on "The Martian," wrote the screenplay, and Phil Lord & Christopher Miller, known for producing and writing the "Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse" series, directed.
title_norm:proof of the man: A black man is murdered in an elevator at a luxury hotel in Tokyo, leaving behind the word 'Stoha' and a poetry collection by Saijo Yaso. Fashion designer Kyoko Yasugi and her son appear and disappear along the investigative trail. Detective Muneyori travels to the United States to trace the black man's past. The unexpected relationship between Kyoko and the black man, as well as the connection between the American detective and Detective Muneyori, comes to light.
title_norm:puella magi madoka magica the: The first part of a two-part theatrical film reconstruction of the 12-episode TV anime 'Puella Magi Madoka Magica,' which aired from January to April 2011. One day, a mysterious transfer student named Homura Akemi arrives at the middle school attended by Madoka Kaname, an ordinary girl living a mundane life. After school that day, guided by a mysterious voice, Madoka encounters a strange creature calling itself Kyubey, who tells her, 'I want you to make a contract with me and become a magical girl.' The staff from the TV series, who built its unique worldview, including chief director Akiyuki Shinbo, screenwriter Gen Urobuchi (Nitroplus), and the otherworldly space design team Gekidan Inu Curry, have reunited for this film.

The second part of a two-part theatrical film reconstruction of the TV anime 'Puella Magi Madoka Magica,' which aired in 2011, created a huge sensation, and won numerous awards including the 16th Animation Kobe Award for TV Series, the 11th Tokyo Anime Award at Tokyo International Anime Fair 2012, and the Grand Prize in the Animation Division at the 15th Japan Media Arts Festival. Sayaka, who became a magical girl for the sake of her beloved Kyosuke, becomes consumed by despair upon learning the truth about magical girls and ultimately transforms into a witch. Madoka accepts Kyoko's proposal to try and save Sayaka, but... A dark fantasy depicting the harsh fate of five girls who chose to fight as magical girls in exchange for having just one wish granted.

The third film in the theatrical series of "Puella Magi Madoka Magica," which aired on TV from January to April 2011 and received high acclaim and popularity, including winning the Grand Prize in the Animation Division at the 15th Agency for Cultural Affairs Media Arts Festival. Following the "Beginning Story" and "Eternal Story" films, which recompiled the 12-episode TV series, this is a completely new feature-length work with newly written script and animation. In a new world where Madoka Kaname freed magical girls from the chain of cruel fate, Homura Akemi, left behind unable to fulfill her feelings for Madoka, continues to fight alone, believing she can meet Madoka again. New magical girl Nagisa Momoe appears as a new character alongside Madoka and Homura.
title_norm:pusher: Frank, a highly skilled drug pusher, makes money with his partner Tony by carrying out jobs for drug kingpin Milo. After taking a huge loan from Milo for a large deal, a police raid causes the deal to fail, and Frank loses the money, facing relentless pressure from his boss to repay the debt. A crime action drama that depicts a man spiraling into a hellish debt trap in the underworld of rampant drug trafficking, pushed to his absolute limits, all rendered in dark, stylish visuals. This is Nicolas Winding Refn's landmark debut film, hailed as the Danish film that first achieved worldwide success as a gangster movie.
title_norm:pusher ii: The second film in the 'Pusher' trilogy, an early crime drama by Danish director Nicolas Winding Refn, who gained global attention with 'Drive.' It centers on drug dealer Tonny, the sidekick of protagonist Frank from the first film, depicting the struggles and battles of a man returning from prison. Released from prison, drug dealer Tonny starts helping his gangster father, who is connected to Copenhagen's underworld, but fails repeatedly. One day, he learns that an acquaintance, Charlotte, has given birth to his child, and decides to go straight. However, unable to refuse, he helps with a drug deal that goes wrong, saddling him with a huge debt and dragging him back into the underworld. Mads Mikkelsen reprises his role as drug dealer Tonny, winning the Robert Award (Denmark's Academy Award) for Best Actor. The trilogy, including 'Pusher' and 'Pusher 3,' had its first theatrical release in Japan in 2013. In May 2026, the trilogy will be revived in 4K digitally restored versions as a special program for the 'Nordic Treasure: Mads Mikkelsen's 60th Birthday Festival.'
title_norm:pusher iii: The concluding chapter of director Nicolas Winding Refn's crime drama "Pusher" trilogy, which he made in his native Denmark early in his career, before gaining international acclaim with "Drive." It depicts the loneliness and decline of power of Milo, the drug lord who appeared throughout the series. Copenhagen drug lord Milo is busy preparing for his beloved daughter's birthday party while also trying to close a heroin deal. However, due to a mix-up, what arrives is not heroin but a large quantity of ecstasy tablets. Milo, who had planned to use the heroin money to pay off his debts, reluctantly orders his subordinate Muhammad to sell the ecstasy, but Muhammad disappears along with the drugs. Cornered, Milo is gradually consumed by madness and takes unexpected action. Zlatko Buric, who played Milo in the previous two films, reprises the role. The trilogy was first released theatrically in Japan in 2013. In May 2026, the trilogy will be revived in 4K digitally restored versions as a special program within the "Nordic Treasure: Mads Mikkelsen 60th Birthday Festival."
title_norm:puss n boots travels around t: Péro, a restaurant waiter in a certain town, gets into an argument with the arrogant Lord Groumon and makes a bet: "I'll travel around the world in eighty days. If I fail, I'll become Groumon's slave." Pursued by time, Péro continues his arduous journey with a father-and-son mouse duo and Carter, the restaurant's cook, but is obstructed by Dr. Garigari, Lord Groumon's henchman, and the mysterious beauty Susanna.
title_norm:pátý jezdec je strach: Set in Nazi-occupied Czechoslovakia, this drama portrays the terror of an informant society during wartime. Dr. Braun, a Jew living in Nazi-occupied Czechoslovakia, is forbidden from practicing medicine. The elderly man seems to have already accepted the fate of the Jews. Then one day, a neighbor asks him to treat a wounded political fugitive, and he reluctantly provides care. Eventually confronting his inner self, Dr. Braun decides to continue illegal treatment for the resistance to reclaim his identity. He wanders the streets of Prague in search of the morphine needed for this, but... Through the various people Dr. Braun meets and the wartime cityscape, the film depicts a society decaying and collapsing under war with hallucinatory visual beauty. In Japan, it will have its theatrical premiere in April 2026 as part of "Czech Film Masterpieces," a series featuring classics of the Czech New Wave.
title_norm:quatre nuits dun rêveur: Jacques, an aspiring painter, saves a young woman named Marthe from throwing herself into the Seine one night. She had a lover who left for America a year ago, and that very night was when they had promised to reunite. Jacques finds her, sunk in anguish, beautiful. Driven by a fierce impulse of love, he forces himself to remain calm, hoping her heart will drift away from her lover, while feeling guilt over this. Like the 1957 version, this is a modern adaptation of Dostoevsky's famous tragic love story, a poignant work revealing Bresson's awakened worldview. Visconti's romanticism is absent here; the young man's blind love is brutally exposed as he pours out his feelings into a mini tape recorder, a habit of his, making it painful to watch.
title_norm:ready or not 2 here i come: The sequel to the survival horror "Ready or Not," in which bride Grace, targeted for death in a traditional wedding-night game, flees the mansion of a wealthy family. The stage expands further, depicting Grace being drawn into a power struggle among the ultra-rich who secretly control the world. Grace survived the blood-soaked game, but the nightmare wasn't over. Her survival catches the attention of the rulers who secretly manipulate the world, and she is once again chosen as a target. The stage is the forbidden realm known as the Council, where chosen noble families vie for supremacy. Representatives of six noble families, bound by a pact with the demon Le Bail, attack Grace with their ancestral weapons, tasked with killing her by dawn. Her only ally is her long-estranged sister Faith, but the two are chained together and unable to move freely. In this extreme situation, their family bond is put to the test as they fight to survive. Samara Weaving reprises her role as Grace. Kathryn Newton ("Abigail") joins as sister Faith, along with new cast members Sarah Michelle Gellar, David Cronenberg, and Elijah Wood. As with the previous film, directing duties were handled by Matt Bettinelli-Olpin and Tyler Gillett of the filmmaking unit Radio Silence.

title_norm:rear window: After breaking his leg, photographer Jeff is confined to a wheelchair and bed rest. To stave off boredom, he makes a daily habit of watching the residents of the apartment building across the way through his window. One day, however, he notices that the bedridden wife who had been arguing with her salesman husband has disappeared. Enlisting the help of his girlfriend Lisa and his nurse Stella, he begins his investigation through the rear window. Piece by piece, he gathers circumstantial evidence suggesting the man murdered his wife, and his suspicion gradually hardens into certainty…
title_norm:red desert: The first color film by Italian master Michelangelo Antonioni, this psychological drama won the Golden Lion at the 25th Venice International Film Festival in 1964. In Ravenna, an industrial coastal city lined with sterile factories, Giuliana lives with her husband and son but remains unable to recover from the shock of a car accident years earlier, spending her days in emotional instability. One day, her husband introduces her to his friend Corrado. Giuliana is drawn to Corrado, who carries a loneliness similar to her own, and gradually the two grow closer... Monica Vitti, known as Antonioni's muse, plays Giuliana, with British star Richard Harris as Corrado. A 4K restored version will be released in August 2026 as part of the retrospective program "Michelangelo Antonioni Retrospective: Arid Love, Wandering Souls," featuring five of Antonioni's early works.
title_norm:red peony gambler flower card: The third film in the "Red Peony Gambler" series. In the mid-Meiji period, Oryu (Sumiko Fujiwara), traveling to learn the ways of the world, joins the Nishinomiya family, Nagoya's top gambling clan, ahead of the Atsuta Shrine Festival's charity gambling. However, she gets caught in a merciless conflict between the gambler Hanooka (Ken Takakura), who owes a debt to the Kimbara family aiming for the position of gambling boss, and both sides.
title_norm:rendezvous in paris: Three stories about love and chance, all centered around a date in Paris.
title_norm:rental family: Brendan Fraser, winner of the Academy Award for Best Actor for "The Whale," stars in this human drama shot entirely in Japan. Directed by Japanese filmmaker HIKARI, who gained attention for her feature debut "37 Seconds" and the drama series "Beef," the film follows a down-on-his-luck actor living in Tokyo who rediscovers himself through working for a rental family service. Philip, an American actor who once dominated toothpaste commercials but has since been largely forgotten, lives in Tokyo, eking out a living in the acting world and blending into the city. One day, he is hired by Tada, who runs a rental family company. The job involves playing the role of a cherished "family member" for clients in exchange for payment. Initially hesitant about delving into others' lives, Philip begins to change as he interacts with the people he meets through his work. Takehiro Hira plays Tada, the rental family company owner; Mari Yamamoto plays Aiko, an actress working for the company; and Akira Emoto plays Kikuo, an aging actor.
title_norm:reprise: The feature directorial debut of Joachim Trier, a Danish director distantly related to Lars von Trier who studied film in Denmark and England, released in 2006. This is the first work of the "Oslo Trilogy," which also includes his later films "Oslo, August 31st" and "The Worst Person in the World." Philip and Erik are childhood friends who have dreamed of becoming writers since they were kids. One day, they both send manuscripts to a publisher, but only Philip's is accepted. Philip becomes a suddenly famous author, but soon begins to suffer mental instability. Meanwhile, Erik continues writing novels without giving up... Anders Danielsen Lie, who stars in all three films of the "Oslo Trilogy," plays Philip. Selected as Norway's entry for the 79th Academy Awards for Best Foreign Language Film, it received high praise, winning the Grand Prix (Best Film), Best Director, and Best Screenplay at the Amanda Awards, Norway's equivalent of the Academy Awards. It received its first theatrical release in Japan as part of the special screening series "Joachim Trier: The Oslo Trilogy" (starting February 13, 2026, at Bunkamura Le Cinéma Shibuya Miyashita and other venues in Tokyo).
title_norm:return to my blue: A short documentary following a boy on a ventilator as he takes on an adventure to a deserted island. Ten-year-old Sota Yoshihara, who requires advanced medical care, and his mother Sumiyo decide to join a tour that takes children with disabilities to a remote island in Okinawa. For Sota, who relies on a ventilator and needs electricity and medical care daily, a trip to an island with no electricity or water is far from safe—one wrong step could be life-threatening. Doctors initially say the tour is too difficult, but Sota's earnest wish to 'go on an adventure to a deserted island' ultimately moves a doctor to accompany the tour himself, making the journey possible. On the day of the tour, with the help of many people, Sota crosses the sea on a small fishing boat and sets foot on the deserted island. The film captures how one boy's small courage and challenge move those around him to fulfill his wish, and reveals moments that remind everyone of what is truly important in their own lives. Directed by Takehiro Noguchi, known for directing NHK's morning drama 'Anpan' and 'Yell' as well as the taiga drama 'What Will Ieyasu Do?', in his documentary directorial debut.
title_norm:rhapsody, rhapsody: Actor Tsuyoshi Rishu, who has directed films such as 'Chloe' and 'Goodbye Debussy', takes the director's chair for a feature film for the first time in 13 years, with Issei Takahashi in the lead role. This human drama humorously depicts a man who has avoided social interactions, whose life takes an unexpected turn when he discovers he has been unknowingly registered as married to a woman he doesn't know. Mikio Natsuno, a slightly naive man who never gets angry, goes to get a copy of his family register to renew his passport and is shocked to find the words 'Relationship: Wife' for a woman he has absolutely no memory of. Learning that a woman named 'Shigeko' has registered herself as his wife without his knowledge, Mikio begins searching for this mysterious woman. He eventually finds Shigeko at a small flower shop on a street corner, but she is an unconventional woman who destroys everything she touches. Though Mikio is tossed around by Shigeko, this strange encounter gradually brings unexpected changes to both their lives. Issei Takahashi plays the kind-hearted and sensitive protagonist Mikio, and Kumi Goshima (NHK morning drama 'Manpuku') plays the enigmatic heroine Shigeko who bewilders everyone around her. Okihiko Serizawa and Chizuru Ikewaki co-star, and director Rishu also appears as a key character. World-renowned jazz pianist Junko Onishi provides the music.
title_norm:riceboy sleeps: Set in 1990s Canada, this drama weaves the bond between a Korean immigrant mother and her son through beautiful 16mm film imagery. Soyoung, who became an unwed mother after losing her lover, moves with her infant son Donghyun to a suburb of Vancouver, Canada. Starting work at a factory, Soyoung faces language and cultural barriers as well as racial discrimination, but raises her son with determination. When Donghyun turns 16, he goes by the English name "David" and has fully adapted to life in Canada, but deep down he yearns to know his roots and the father he has never met. Then one day, receiving shocking news, the mother and son return to Korea for the first time, confronting a painful past. Director and screenwriter Anthony Shim, who himself immigrated from Korea to Canada at age eight, powerfully yet delicately portrays the fluidity of immigrant identity and the conflict and renewal between parent and child. Choi Seung-yoon, active in Korea as a dancer, choreographer, and actor, plays mother Soyoung, and Ethan Hwang of the drama "The Umbrella Academy" plays the teenage Donghyun.
title_norm:riceboy ライスボーイ: Set in 1990s Canada, this drama weaves the bond between a Korean immigrant mother and her son through beautiful 16mm film imagery. Soyoung, who became an unwed mother after losing her lover, moves with her infant son Donghyun to a suburb of Vancouver, Canada. Starting work at a factory, Soyoung faces language and cultural barriers as well as racial discrimination, but raises her son with determination. Choi Seung-yoon, active in Korea as a dancer, choreographer, and actor, plays mother Soyoung, and Ethan Hwang of the drama "The Umbrella Academy" plays the teenage Donghyun.
title_norm:rich flu: A thriller dripping with black humor that depicts the collapse of capitalist society following the outbreak of a mysterious disease called "Rich Flu" that only infects the wealthy. Directed and written by Galder Gaztelu-Urrutia of the "The Platform" series, which sharply depicted social inequality, it thrillingly portrays the chaos brought about by a reversal of values. Laura, a high-ranking producer at a streaming platform company, prioritizes her career over her family and is on the verge of success in the glamorous film industry. But just then, a mysterious disease called "Rich Flu" suddenly spreads worldwide, killing wealthy people one after another. As wealth transforms from a symbol of success into a "mark of elimination," capitalist society collapses and the world descends into chaos. In this extreme situation, Laura makes a decision. Mary Elizabeth Winstead, known for films like "Gemini Man" and "Birds of Prey," plays the career-driven Laura who neglects her family. Raf Spall, who has appeared in major works like "Life of Pi" and "Jurassic World: Fallen Kingdom," plays Tony, her husband who is exasperated with her yet gets caught up in the unprecedented pandemic alongside her. Timothy Spall, known for the "Harry Potter" series and "Mr. Turner," plays the billionaire Sebastian Snail.
title_norm:rider: Jojo, Bruce, and Jisho, a trio of middle schoolers, are constantly bullied by the neighborhood bully Debnaga. Determined to get revenge on Debnaga today, the three are psyched up, but right before their eyes, Debnaga is kidnapped. From there, the three are drawn into a yakuza conflict involving stimulant drugs...
title_norm:rin: Reiko Asakawa, a TV station director, is investigating an urban legend when she notices that a man and woman rumored to have been involved with a 'cursed videotape' that kills viewers within a week died at the exact same date and time as her niece, Tomoko Oishi, who had died strangely a few days earlier. As her investigation progresses, Reiko discovers that Tomoko and the other three who died simultaneously were acquaintances, that they had stayed at a rental villa in Izu called 'Izu Pacific Land' a week prior, and that the faces of the four in film photos taken at that time are eerily distorted. Seeking to uncover the mystery of their deaths, Reiko visits the villa in question, watches the suspicious tape that was rented there, and immediately receives an eerie silent phone call. From that point on, Reiko's own photos also begin to show her face distorted, just like the four deceased.
title_norm:river: The second original feature film by the popular theater troupe Europe Kikaku, led by Makoto Ueda. Following their acclaimed first feature "Droste no Hate de Bokura," Ueda writes the original story and script, with the troupe's video director Junta Yamaguchi directing. This ensemble comedy depicts the chaos of people trapped in a repeating two-minute time loop set in winter at Kibune, Kyoto. Mikoto, a waitress at the long-established inn Fujiya in Kibune, is called back to work by the landlady while standing by the Kibune River behind the annex. But two minutes later, she finds herself in the same spot. Not only Mikoto, but also the head clerk, waitresses, chefs, and guests all realize time is looping. After two minutes, time rewinds and everyone returns to their original positions, but their memories carry over. They work together to find the cause of the loop, but Mikoto alone harbors complicated feelings. Filmed in winter at Kibune with full cooperation from Kibune Shrine and the inn Fujiya. Starring Riko Fujitani as Mikoto, along with many Europe Kikaku actors, Yuki Torigoe, Manami Honjo, Saoi, and Yoshimasa Kondo. Shiori Kubo of Nogizaka46, who has ties to Ueda and Europe Kikaku through stage productions, makes a guest appearance in a key role.
title_norm:robot carnival: Produced during the mid-1980s when original video animation was booming, this omnibus work pushes forward the director's individuality. Katsuhiro Otomo handles the opening and ending, packing the essence of his animation into a short time. The English title logo features a building drawn in meticulous detail so its structure is discernible. The composition of it running as a machine, and the imagery of a toy-box-like, amusement-park-like interior collapsing carefully step by step, truly feels like a microcosm of 'Steamboy'. While other directors develop unique worlds around the theme of 'robots', Otomo creates a short film that is more relaxed and visually driven.
title_norm:robot dreams: The first feature-length animated film by Spanish director Pablo Berger, known for 'Blancanieves.' Based on the graphic novel of the same name by American author Sara Varon, it depicts the friendship between a dog and a robot in 1980s New York, where anthropomorphic animals live, entirely without dialogue or narration. In Manhattan, New York. Dog, deeply lonely, builds a robot to be his friend, and they deepen their bond. In summer, Dog and Robot go to the beach, but Robot rusts and becomes immobile. Dog tries everything to repair Robot, but the beach closes for the off-season with Robot left behind, and the two are separated. Nominated for Best Animated Feature at the 96th Academy Awards in 2024.
title_norm:rochelle:
Winner of the Best Short Film Award at the 2025 New Zealand Screen Awards. Reckless young Mac decides to give his late friend's beat-up car, "Rochelle," one last moment in the spotlight. He heads to the local junk car race. At first his friends are exasperated, but soon they are moved by Mac's dream and begin to cheer him on in earnest...
■ Ticket price: 1,000 yen flat rate (Free tickets, invitation tickets, and other discounts are not applicable.)
■ Same-day discount at the box office: Present a ticket for another film viewed on the same day to receive 100 yen off. (Limited to tickets purchased at the box office on the day.)
Making movie theaters a more casual option. "20 Minute Cinema" is a new initiative screening short films of 15–20 minutes in theaters. A 20-minute stop you can drop into like a café between shopping or after work. Masterpieces from around the world you won't find on streaming services will add vibrant color to your daily life.
title_norm:rokkoku kitchen: A documentary that observes people's lives and the present state of Fukushima through the dining tables of those living along National Route 6, commonly known as "Rokkoku," where areas still remain designated as difficult-to-return zones.
title_norm:romance express: Aboard an express train from Tokyo to Osaka, waitress Sayoko (Dan) pressures kitchen assistant Kiichi (Frankie) to marry her. An adaptation of a popular novel by Bunroku Shishi, this ensemble comedy depicts the chaos stirred up by a group of eccentric passengers sharing the dining car.
title_norm:room for let: In a large rundown house overlooking the Tsutenkaku Tower in Osaka, a group of eccentric lodgers live... Frankie, in his famous partnership with Kawashima, plays a laid-back jack-of-all-trades who works as a ghostwriter and konnyaku maker. With unique supporting actors like Naniwa and Ozawa, this is a brilliant ensemble comedy that leaves a lasting impression.
title_norm:rosetta: A film by the Dardenne brothers, directors of 'The Promise,' portraying a woman who tenaciously survives despite adversity. Rosetta lives with her alcoholic mother in a trailer at a campground. One day, she is fired from her job for no apparent reason. Rosetta, confronting the harsh realities of society, desperately continues searching for new work... Winner of the Palme d'Or and Best Actress award at the 1999 Cannes Film Festival.
title_norm:roujin z: In the near future, to cope with an aging society, the Ministry of Health and Welfare develops a sixth-generation computer with self-replicating functions, the elderly care machine 'Unit Z001.' However, this computer absorbs the elderly selected as samples and goes on a rampage, causing a huge uproar involving volunteer female college students and the media.
title_norm:rrr: From S.S. Rajamouli, director of the "Baahubali" series, which was a huge hit and had a long theatrical run in Japan, comes this spectacular action entertainment set in the turbulent era of British colonial India, depicting the clash of friendship and duty between two men. In 1920, during British rule in India, Bheem rises to save a young girl kidnapped by the British army, while Rama becomes a police officer for the British government for a greater cause. Though they are on opposing sides, driven by their own passionate beliefs, fate brings them together without knowing each other's true identities, and they become inseparable friends. However, an incident forces them to choose between friendship and their missions. N.T. Rama Rao Jr., known for "Baadshah," plays Bheem, and Ram Charan, who starred in Rajamouli's "Magadheera," plays Rama. The title "RRR" is derived from the initials of "Rise," "Roar," and "Revolt." It became the first Indian film to gross over 1 billion yen at the Japanese box office. The song "Naatu Naatu" also became a sensation, winning the Academy Award for Best Original Song at the 95th Academy Awards, a first for an Indian film.
title_norm:ryuichi sakamoto playing the: Ryuichi Sakamoto performed with a full orchestra in Japan for the first time in 16 years at the acclaimed concert "Playing the Orchestra 2013." As an updated version, the 2014 Tokyo concert, which he conducted himself, became "Ryuichi Sakamoto | Playing the Orchestra 2014." At this concert, Sakamoto played the piano while conducting all pieces, performing a diverse repertoire—from YMO-era classics to masterpieces like "Merry Christmas, Mr. Lawrence" and "The Last Emperor," as well as his film scores—with the Tokyo Philharmonic Orchestra.
title_norm:sabrina: A romantic comedy directed by Billy Wilder, starring Audrey Hepburn in the year following "Roman Holiday." Sabrina, the daughter of a chauffeur serving the wealthy Larrabee family, falls in love with the family's younger son. To make her forget this hopeless love, her father and fellow servants send Sabrina to Paris. Two years later, Sabrina returns as a refined lady, and her transformation is so complete that the younger son and his brother fail to recognize her as the chauffeur's daughter. In 2013, a digitally remastered version was released as part of the special screening series "Screen Beauties Vol. 1: Audrey Hepburn."
title_norm:sagrada el misteri de la crea: A documentary about the Sagrada Família, the century-spanning architectural project conceived by Catalan architect Antoni Gaudí, under construction since 1882 for over 130 years. Registered as a World Heritage Site in 2005, the Sagrada Família continues to captivate over three million visitors annually from around the world. As construction continues towards a projected completion in 2026, computers have been introduced on site, and staff repeatedly experiment to determine how to best reproduce Gaudí's vision with current technology. Incorporating footage from inside the site, inaccessible to outsiders, and interviews with architectural staff, the film unravels the project surrounding the Sagrada Família, including how the construction period, once said to require '300 years until completion,' has been shortened to a projected completion in 2026.
title_norm:sai disaster: A psychological suspense film directed, written, and edited by Yutaro Seki and Kentaro Hirase of the filmmaking collective "May," who gained domestic and international attention for their 2022 feature debut "Miyamatsu to Yamashita." It stars Kōji Yakusho, who also collaborated with them on that previous film. This is the theatrical version of the WOWOW drama series "Wazawai" (Disaster), broadcast from April to May 2025. It boldly restructures the six-episode series into a single film, depicting the calamity brought by a single man who infiltrates the everyday lives of six unrelated people. A high school girl troubled by family and her future, a deliveryman with a past, a shopping mall cleaner and a barber, the manager of a debt-ridden inn, and an ordinary housewife. The modest daily lives of these six people are suddenly struck by inexplicable disasters. The police dismiss them all as suicides or accidents, but Detective Dōmoto senses something strange and pursues the truth. Lurking around the edges of these six disasters is a single man. Changing his personality and appearance, he appears before the six as completely different people, bringing calamity upon them. Detective Dōmoto is played by Anne Nakamura, his colleague by Pistol Takehara and Kaito Miyakuni, and the people struck by disaster by Sena Nakajima, Ryuhei Matsuda, Megumi Uchida, Shunki Fujiwara, Jiro (Shisonne), and Maki Sakai.
title_norm:sailor suit and machine gun: The boss of a small yakuza gang called Medaka-gumi, who has only four underlings, dies leaving a will stating that his successor must be a blood relative. Around the same time, high school girl Izumi Hoshi is saying her final goodbye at the crematorium to her father Takashi, who died after being hit by a car in front of Narita Airport. Izumi's mother passed away long ago, leaving her truly alone. When Izumi returns to her apartment, a woman named Mayumi is there, carrying a letter from her father that says, 'If I die, please take care of Izumi.' The next day, a crowd of men in black suits lines up in front of her school. Ignoring her friends Tomoki, Tetsuo, and Shuhei, who try to stop her, Izumi heads toward the school gate. The man from the crematorium steps forward and says, 'You're Izumi Hoshi, right?' This man, named Sakuma, takes her to a shabby office and asks her to succeed as the fourth-generation boss of the Medaka-gumi.
title_norm:saint seiya legend of crimson: The third theatrical film. The immensely powerful sun god Abel is resurrected, and his sister Athena abandons the protagonists who have fought alongside her to leave with Abel. The scene where the usually energetic protagonist sheds tears emphasizes the boy's purity and fragility. The revival of the five "Gold Saints" who died in the TV anime is also a highlight. As part of the 20th anniversary of "Weekly Shōnen Jump," this was released as a 75-minute extended version, double-billed with "Sakigake!! Otokojuku."
title_norm:saint seiya the heated battle: Warriors clad in constellational armor, the 'Saints,' fight for the goddess Athena. With beautifully exaggerated bodies designed by Shingo Araki and Michi Himeno, special moves accompanied by lavish screen effects like transmitted light, fast-paced action, emotional direction, and an orchestral score, it became a representative action anime of the 1980s. The first theatrical film was directed by TV series director Toshio Morishita and depicts the resurrection of the evil god Eris.
title_norm:sakamoto days: A live-action film adaptation of the hit comic by Yuto Suzuki, serialized in Shueisha's "Weekly Shonen Jump", starring Ren Meguro of "Snow Man". It comically depicts a legendary retired hitman running a small shop who throws himself into battle to protect his beloved family and peaceful daily life. Sakamoto Taro, once feared as the "strongest ever," falls in love at first sight with a woman named Aoi who works at a convenience store, and promptly retires from being a hitman. After marrying and having a daughter, he becomes the manager of a small shop called "Sakamoto Store" and enjoys a happy family life, having grown so fat that he no longer resembles his former self. One day, a 10 billion yen bounty is suddenly placed on Sakamoto, and assassins from all over the world attack him. With his former subordinate, the esper Shin, as his partner, Sakamoto rises to protect his peaceful daily life. Meguro uses special makeup to portray two contrasting versions of Sakamoto: a plump one weighing an estimated 140 kg and a sleek one who rapidly loses weight when he gets serious, and also takes on full-fledged action scenes. Takahashi Fumiya plays Sakamoto's partner Asakura Shin; Ueto Aya plays Sakamoto's wife Aoi; Yokota Mayuu plays Lu Shaotang, a tai chi expert working at Sakamoto Store with Shin; Tozuki Junki plays Masumo Heisuke, a skilled sniper; Kitamura Takumi plays Nagumo, a member of the hitman world's highest force "ORDER"; Yagi Yusei plays Kamigami; and Nemu Yumemi plays Daibutsu. Directed and written by Yuichi Fukuda of the "Gintama" series.
title_norm:samurai in time: A period comedy depicting a late-Edo period samurai who time-travels to a modern-day period drama studio and struggles as a sword-falling extra. In Kyoto at the end of the Edo period, Kosaka Shinzaemon, a retainer of the Aizu domain, receives a secret order from the chief retainer to kill a Choshu domain samurai, but at the moment his blade meets his target's, he is struck by lightning and loses consciousness. When he wakes up, he finds himself in a modern period drama studio. Shinzaemon causes commotions wherever he goes, and is stunned to learn that the Tokugawa shogunate fell 140 years ago. Resigned to death at first, he is helped by kind-hearted people and regains his will to live. Eventually, relying only on his polished swordsmanship, he knocks on the studio's door and decides to live as a sword-falling extra. Starring Makiya Yamaguchi, who has appeared in numerous period dramas including the TV series "Kenkaku Shobai," with Norimasa Tomiya and Yuno Sakura co-starring. Directed and written by Junichi Yasuda ("Gohan," "Kenju to Medamayaki"), it was completed with special cooperation from Toei Kyoto Studio despite being an independent production. Released exclusively at Ikebukuro Cinema Rosa on August 17, 2024 (a "Deluxe Version" with added scenes began screening at Kawasaki Cinecitta from August 30), word of mouth spread, and from September 13 of the same year, with Gaga as co-distributor, it expanded to over 100 theaters nationwide including Shinjuku Piccadilly and Toho Cinemas Hibiya. It became an unprecedented hit for an independent film and achieved the feat of winning the Best Picture award at the 48th Japan Academy Film Prize.
title_norm:sana play with me: Directed by Takashi Shimizu of the "Ju-On" series, this school horror film stars Suzuka Chinzei of the idol group FRUITS ZIPPER in the lead role. A secret rumor circulates among young people about a forbidden game: if you record a date and name onto a cassette tape on the 13th step of an empty school staircase, that person will die. High school students casually try the game, and their daily lives begin to warp. One by one, those whose names were recorded on the tape die mysteriously on the specified dates. The school takes the situation seriously and asks psychological counselor Koharu Hirase to provide mental care for the students. Koharu counsels a student who witnessed the incidents, but among those who played the game is her younger sister, Nanami. As students are attacked by strange phenomena one after another, Koharu and Nanami are dragged into a chain of terror. Suzuka Chinzei takes on her first solo lead film role and first horror role as counselor Koharu; Anna Hoshino (from "Gold Boy") plays Koharu's sister Nanami; Riku Onishi (from "Water Flows Toward the Sea") plays classmate Jotaro Chiba who looks out for Nanami; and Shota Sometani plays a young man who holds the key to the story.
title_norm:sangue del mio sangue: A Gothic fantasy film by Italian master Marco Bellocchio, released in 2015 and winner of the FIPRESCI Prize at the 72nd Venice International Film Festival. The story intertwines the 17th century and the modern era, depicted with eerily beautiful imagery. In 17th-century Bobbio, northern Italy, young soldier Federico visits an old monastery to uncover the truth behind the death of his twin brother Fabrizio, a priest. It is said that Fabrizio was seduced by a nun named Benedetta, betrayed his faith, and lost his life. Seeking to restore his brother's honor, Federico tries to make Benedetta confess her guilt, but gradually becomes captivated by her, even as she is accused of witchcraft. The story then shifts to the modern day, centuries later. The former monastery lies in ruins, and a sale to a wealthy Russian is being negotiated. A man appears, but the ruins are haunted by a mysterious old count who only shows himself at night. Benedetta is played by Lidia Lieberman, Federico (living in both past and present) by Pier Giorgio Bellocchio, and the mysterious old count by Roberto Herlitzka. A cover of Metallica's "Nothing Else Matters" is used prominently in the film.
title_norm:sans toit ni loi: A film by renowned French filmmaker Agnès Varda, tracing the steps of a young girl who freezes to death after wandering, which won the Golden Lion, the top prize, at the 42nd Venice International Film Festival in 1985. In winter in southern France, the body of an 18-year-old girl, Mona, is found frozen to death in a roadside ditch in the countryside. The film traces Mona's journey over the final weeks of her life as she hitchhikes aimlessly and continues a solitary journey, through the testimonies of the people she met on the road. Starring Sandrine Bonnaire (from "The Hairdresser's Husband"), with co-stars Macha Méril (from "Belle de Jour"), Stéphane Freiss (from "The Five Senses"), and Yolande Moreau (from "Séraphine"). It recorded over one million admissions in France at the time, becoming Varda's biggest hit.
title_norm:sansho the bailiff: Commentary: In the Heian period, Zushio and Anju, separated from their parents, are sold into slavery... A film adaptation of Ogai's short story based on a medieval folktale, this timeless masterpiece won the Silver Lion at the Venice International Film Festival. The visual beauty captured by the renowned cinematographer Miyagawa is also awe-inspiring.
title_norm:sarvam thaala mayam: A youth music film about a young man's struggle to become a player of the mridangam, a traditional Indian percussion instrument. Peter, the son of a mridangam craftsman living in Chennai, India, is inspired to become a player himself after seeing a master perform on a mridangam his father made. Apprenticing under the master and training diligently, Peter faces various challenges including caste discrimination, conflicts over preserving traditional arts, and generational differences, but confronts them with passion and respect. The music is composed by A. R. Rahman, who won an Academy Award for 'Slumdog Millionaire.' G. V. Prakash Kumar, Rahman's nephew and a renowned film music composer, plays the protagonist Peter. Screened under the title 'The World Is Full of Rhythms' in the World Focus section of the 31st Tokyo International Film Festival in 2018. For its theatrical release in October 2022, the film was distributed by 'Nandori,' a South Indian restaurant in Tokyo's Arakawa Ward that fell in love with the film.
title_norm:sasuke and his comedians: Director Takashi Kato presents an unconventional period action film depicting the story of the Sanada Ten Braves, who fought in the Winter and Summer Sieges of Osaka, with fantastical fun and excitement! Affected by the radiation of a meteorite that fell from space, the Warring States street urchin Sasuke gains mysterious abilities. Growing up, he calls himself Sarutobi Sasuke and, along with the flying squirrel Okiri, becomes a subordinate of the cool commander Sanada Yukimura, rampaging through the rigged Winter and Summer Sieges of Osaka!
title_norm:satoshi a move for tomorrow: Murayama Takashi, who suffered from a serious illness since early childhood, discovers shogi during repeated hospitalizations and, at age 15, becomes a disciple of Mori Nobuo. Ten years later, Takashi moves to Tokyo to fulfill his dream of becoming a Meijin champion. Supported by those around him, he devotes himself fully to shogi, and after reaching the rank of 7-dan, he develops a fierce rivalry with Habu Yoshiharu, who won the Meijin title in the same generation. Takashi immerses himself even deeper in shogi, but cancer gradually consumes his body...
title_norm:scarborough: A Canadian drama that captures the lives of people on the fringes of society with an honest gaze, following three children living in harsh circumstances as they form bonds at a local community education center. In Scarborough, a diverse, multicultural neighborhood in eastern Toronto. Bing, a Filipino boy who fled his mentally ill father's violence to come to this town; Sylvie, a girl of Indigenous heritage living in a shelter with her family of four; and Laura, a girl neglected and tossed about by her parents—these three find a safe haven at the education center run by social worker Hina. Despite their difficult circumstances, they nurture a small but meaningful bond... The lead roles are played by three children making their film debut, and the supporting cast includes non-professional actors from Scarborough. The film is based on Canadian author Catherine Hernandez's debut novel "Scarborough," which she adapted from her own experiences. Directors Shasha Nakai and Rich Williamson, highly acclaimed in the documentary field, made their narrative feature debut with this film. It won eight awards, including Best Picture and Best Director, at the 10th Canadian Screen Awards in 2022.
title_norm:scarface: A violent action film starring Al Pacino from 'The Godfather' series, depicting the rise and fall of a man climbing Miami's criminal underworld in the 1980s, with extreme violence. Directed by Brian De Palma, written by Oliver Stone, it is a modern remake of Howard Hawks' classic gangster film 'Scarface'. In 1980, many criminals flood into America among Cuban refugees. Tony Montana, an anti-Castro exile arriving in Miami, takes on a hit at a refugee camp for Frank, a Miami drug lord. Tony gains trust through drug deals and murders for Frank, while also falling for Frank's mistress Elvira. As Tony rises in the underworld, his arrogance and insatiable greed drive him toward destruction. Al Pacino embodies Tony's madness and desire with intense performance. Steven Bauer plays Tony's right-hand man Manny, Robert Loggia plays drug lord Frank, and Michelle Pfeiffer plays Frank's mistress Elvira. With domestic screening rights ending at the end of June 2026, a 4K revival screening is held.
title_norm:scrap heaven: The third feature film by director Sang-il Lee, made in 2005, based on his original screenplay. It depicts young people carrying aimless anger and loneliness as they attempt small acts of rebellion against an unreasonable society. Shingo, who became a police officer dreaming of being a "hero of justice," is fed up with days spent doing only desk work and after-the-fact paperwork. One day, he encounters a bus-jacking incident. On the bus are a young man, Tetsu, and a woman in sunglasses, Saki. For Shingo, it should have been the perfect situation, but the incident ends without him laying a finger on the culprit. Three months later, Shingo coincidentally meets Tetsu again, and prompted by Tetsu's words, "This world lacks imagination," the two begin a game of "revenge proxy," fulfilling the wishes of people who have despaired of society. Requests for revenge pour in one after another, and dragged along by the free-spirited Tetsu, their game escalates. Meanwhile, Saki, working as a pharmacist, conducts secret experiments in her room. Tetsu and Shingo's game heats up further, and things begin to spiral in unexpected directions. Ryo Kase plays Shingo, Joe Odagiri plays Tetsu, and Chiaki Kuriyama plays Saki. The rock band Fujifabric provides the ending theme. Scheduled for a revival screening in April 2026.
title_norm:sedmikrásky: A landmark film of the 1960s Czech New Wave, this work portrays the wild antics of two uninhibited girls, both named "Marie," using a boldly experimental array of techniques including color shifts, coloring, optical effects, innovative sound design, and abrupt scene transitions. The older sister, with a blonde bob and a daisy wreath, and the younger sister, with dark brown hair in two pigtails, both call themselves "Marie" and pretend to be siblings. They live freely, tricking men into buying them meals only to fake-cry and run away. At home, they do whatever they please—bathing in milk, burning paper, cutting out magazine photos, slicing up bed sheets, and eventually cutting each other's bodies, until the screen itself fragments. Directed and written by Věra Chytilová, a pioneering Czech filmmaker and the most prominent female director of the Czech New Wave. The two leads were played by non-professional actresses selected through auditions: Jitka Cerhová and Ivana Karbanová. Other roles were also filled by non-actors, such as composers and designers. The film had its first official theatrical release in Japan in 1991 at Kichijoji Baus Theater, where it ran for an extended period through word of mouth. It has since gained a cult following, and in March 2026, a 4K restored version will be re-released to commemorate the 60th anniversary of its production and the 35th anniversary of its Japanese release.
title_norm:seek: Shane Kosugi, son of action star Sho Kosugi who sparked the ninja boom in Hollywood and brother of Kane Kosugi, makes his feature directorial debut with this action film themed around ninjas believed to be extinct. Chinese martial arts world champion Kansuke Asano, who became a world champion in his teens, stars and produces, with Kane Kosugi also appearing. Ninjas living in modern-day Japan have changed their names and appearances, secretly carrying out missions as agents of the non-governmental organization 'Shiju-ku (49)'. Kyōhei Aizawa, one of the most skilled agents in history, loses his beloved lover, the only person he truly trusted, in a plane crash. As he contemplates the meaning of life in solitude, Kyōhei is assigned an infiltration mission into the Japanese yakuza group Takatsuki-gumi. After Kyōhei successfully completes the mission, the Takatsuki-gumi, learning of his existence, begins eliminating people around him by any means necessary for a certain purpose. Realizing that his loved ones are disappearing because of him, Kyōhei confronts the Takatsuki-gumi alone. Asano plays the protagonist Kyōhei, with Seiki Miura and Nanana among the cast.
title_norm:sentimental value: Swedish director Joachim Trier, who gained international attention with "The Worst Person in the World," crafts a family drama centered on the tangled bonds of love and hate inherent in the parent-child relationship. Nora, an actress thriving in Oslo, and her sister Agnes, who chose family life and lives quietly with her husband and son. One day, their father Gustav, a film director who abandoned the family when they were young and has been out of contact for years, reappears and offers Nora the lead role in his first autobiographical film in 15 years. Filled with anger and disappointment toward her father, Nora firmly refuses, and soon the popular young American actress Rachel is cast instead. When Nora learns that the film will be shot at the family's old home, a place filled with memories, uncontrollable emotions surge within her once again. Renate Reinsve, who also starred in "The Worst Person in the World," plays the protagonist Nora, with acclaimed actor Stellan Skarsgård as her father Gustav. Inga Ibsdotter Lilleaas plays sister Agnes, and Elle Fanning plays the popular American actress Rachel. The film won the Grand Prix at the 78th Cannes Film Festival in 2025. At the 98th Academy Awards, it received nine nominations across eight categories, including Best Picture, and won the award for Best International Feature Film.
title_norm:separation: Nader is in divorce negotiations with his wife, who wants to leave Iran for the sake of their daughter. He hires a woman named Razieh to care for his father, who suffers from dementia and lives with him, but an unexpected incident sets off a chain of events... An exquisite drama that intertwines a mystery with Iran's divorce issues.
title_norm:seven days war: At Aoba Junior High, where strict discipline is enforced, eleven boys and girls rise up in pursuit of freedom. They bring food and barricade themselves in an abandoned factory, while the teachers try to disband them strictly according to school rules. The students fend off the teachers using various means, but... A lighthearted youth drama based on the original novel by So Munetari. Screened simultaneously with "Flower's Asuka Gang!".
title_norm:sgt. fro: As part of the 20th-anniversary project for the TV anime "Sergeant Keroro," based on the manga by Mine Yoshizaki serialized in "Monthly Shonen Ace" since 1999, this theatrical anime is the first in 16 years since "Keroro Gunso the Super Movie: Creation! Ultimate Keroro, Wonderous Time-Space Island!!" in 2010. It depicts the Keroro Platoon, who were supposed to invade Earth, fighting to protect the planet from a new invader. Sergeant Keroro and his platoon members, who came to Earth to invade but now spend their days idly at their host family's home, encounter mysterious phenomena occurring across the country. Feeling a sense of crisis, the Keroro Platoon rises to the challenge, putting their pride as invaders on the line, but they encounter mysterious letters wherever they go. The screenplay and general direction are handled by Yuichi Fukuda, known for directing the live-action "Gintama" series. The staff includes key members who have supported the series, with Satoshi Ozaki as director, Satoshi Koike as character designer, and BN Pictures handling animation production. Jesse from SixTONES voices the theatrical original characters, the brothers Aruru and Deruru, playing both roles.
title_norm:shadow of fire: Director Shinya Tsukamoto, known for "Fires on the Plain" and "Killing," depicts the lives of people carrying despair and darkness in the black market just after the end of the war. A woman living alone in a small, surviving izakaya is forced into selling her body and spends her days without the will to resist, overwhelmed by despair. One day, a child who lost their family in an air raid sneaks into the woman's izakaya to steal food. From then on, the child begins to frequent the place, and through her interaction with the child, the woman begins to find a faint glimmer of light. Hikari Mitsushima, known for "Just Remembering," delivers a delicate yet bold performance as the protagonist, the woman. Mirai Moriyama plays a mysterious man with a paralyzed arm, Sōga Tsukao, a child actor known for "The Last 10 Years," plays a war orphan, and Hironori Kōno, known for "Special Actors," plays a young repatriated soldier. It was screened in the Orizzonti section of the 80th Venice International Film Festival in 2023 and won the NETPAC Award (Best Asian Film Award).
title_norm:shall we dance: Directed by Masayuki Suo of "Sumo Do, Sumo Don't" fame, this heartwarming comedy became a huge hit by depicting a middle-aged man rediscovering his life through ballroom dancing. Shohei Sugiyama is an ordinary salaryman with no complaints about his work or family life, yet he feels a vague emptiness. One day, on the train home from work, he spots a woman standing by the window of a dance studio and is captivated by her beauty. Later, he begins learning ballroom dancing at that very studio and becomes deeply absorbed in the world of dance through interactions with a colorful group of fellow students. Koji Yakusho plays the protagonist Sugiyama, while ballerina Tamiyo Kusakari plays Mai. In 2004, the film was remade in Hollywood starring Richard Gere and Jennifer Lopez.

Koji Yakusho plays the protagonist Sugiyama, while ballerina Tamiyo Kusakari plays Mai. In 2004, the film was remade in Hollywood starring Richard Gere and Jennifer Lopez.

Shohei Sugiyama is an ordinary salaryman with no complaints about his work or family life, yet he feels a vague emptiness. One day, on the train home from work, he spots a woman standing by the window of a dance studio and is captivated by her beauty. Later, he begins learning ballroom dancing at that very studio and becomes deeply absorbed in the world of dance through interactions with a colorful group of fellow students. Koji Yakusho plays the protagonist Sugiyama, while ballerina Tamiyo Kusakari plays Mai. In 2004, the film was remade in Hollywood starring Richard Gere and Jennifer Lopez.
title_norm:sheep in the box: A feature film directed by Hirokazu Kore-eda ("Monster", "Shoplifters"), starring Haruka Ayase and Daigo (from the comedy duo "Chidori"), based on an original script about a couple who welcome a humanoid in the form of their deceased son. Set in the near future. Architect Kōmoto Oto and her husband Kensuke, the second-generation president of a construction company, take in a humanoid resembling their son Sho, who died two years ago. On the day the humanoid arrives, Oto joyfully welcomes him with Sho's same smile and voice, while Kensuke hides his bewilderment behind a stiff expression. Family time gradually begins, but an unexpected event occurs, revealing the couple's hidden feelings about their son's death. Meanwhile, the humanoid Sho secretly starts connecting with other humanoids. The role of the deceased son Sho and his humanoid counterpart is played by Kuwaki Rito, chosen from over 200 auditionees. Kiyono Yasho plays Oto's younger sister Kotaki Arisu; Kanichiro plays Nikawa Gen, an employee at Kensuke's construction company Tamaken; Yo Kimiko plays Oto's mother Nishimura Nobuyo; and Tanaka Min plays Yamagata Akio, a skilled worker at Tamaken. The title "The Sheep in the Box" is derived from a passage in Antoine de Saint-Exupéry's classic novel "The Little Prince". The film was selected for the Competition section of the 79th Cannes Film Festival in 2026.
title_norm:shiboyugi playing death games: A sequel to the 2026 TV anime 'Death Game de Meshi o Kū,' based on the popular light novel by Yūshi Ukai, this theatrical anime adapts the original 'Cloudy Beach' arc. A deadly murder game where survival earns you prize money. Allies you encouraged yesterday can become enemies today, and even with full preparation, you can lose your life. The girl Yūki aims to clear this life-or-death game 99 times, making a living from the prize money she wins. Overcoming the 'Wall of Thirty'—a jinx where player survival rates drop drastically—she continues forward and takes on her 44th game, 'Cloudy Beach.' Among the eight players gathered on a remote island, Yūki spots a familiar veteran. Continuing from the TV anime, Sōda Ueno of 'Stepsister Life' directs, with animation production by Studio Deen.
title_norm:shinpei: A brother who cannot fit into society, a father who has given up on the future, and a sister bound to the home. This is a story of the small steps the three of them take forward. One day, the Great East Japan Earthquake suddenly upends their peaceful daily lives. Not only the earthquake and tsunami, but also the nuclear accident forced many people to lose their homes and jobs, leaving Fukushima behind. This is the story of a family living in the aftermath, three years later, in a deeply scarred Fukushima.
