title_norm:shoplifters: Directed by Hirokazu Kore-eda of "The Third Murder" and "Our Little Sister," this human drama portrays human connections through the lens of a family that engages in petty crimes together. At the 71st Cannes Film Festival in 2018, it won the Palme d'Or, the top prize, for the first time for a Japanese film since "The Eel" in 1997. It also earned high praise overseas, including a nomination for Best Foreign Language Film at the 91st Academy Awards, the first for a Japanese film in a decade. At the 42nd Japan Academy Film Prize, it won eight awards, including Best Picture. In a working-class district of Tokyo, in an old one-story house seemingly left behind among high-rise apartments, live the homeowner Hatsue, the couple Osamu and Nobuyo, their son Shota, and Nobuyo's younger sister Aki, all dependent on Hatsue's pension. They make ends meet by shoplifting, living on the fringes of society, yet their days are filled with laughter. One winter day, Osamu brings home a little girl shivering on the balcony of a nearby apartment complex, and Nobuyo decides to raise her as a daughter. Triggered by an incident, the close-knit family begins to fall apart, revealing the secrets and desires each of them harbors. Alongside regular Kore-eda collaborators Lily Franky as the father Osamu, who repeatedly shoplifts with his son, and Kirin Kiki as Hatsue, the film marks the first Kore-eda works for Sakura Ando as Nobuyo and Mayu Matsuoka as Aki, Nobuyo's sister.
title_norm:shot the voice of freedom: A documentary recording the daily struggles of women who continue to seek freedom in Afghanistan under Taliban rule. In August 2021, the Taliban seized control of nearly all of Afghanistan, collapsing the two-decade democratic government. With the Taliban's return to power, women were once again barred from working outside the home, deprived of educational opportunities, and girls were forced into marriages with much older men and confined to their houses. Sisters Rashmin and Nastaran, along with other women, take to the streets to raise their voices against countless inequalities. Undaunted even by armed men, they hide smartphones under their scarves to film and broadcast the current situation in Afghanistan. They continue their resistance while moving from one relative's home to another, but in a patriarchal society, their father despises the women participating in demonstrations, and they are forced to live in fear of neighbors informing on them. Despite such harsh circumstances, Rashmin, driven by the desire not to make the next generation experience the same suffering, rushes out into the streets. The director is Zainab Entezar, an Afghan-born female filmmaker, producer, and writer who, while living in exile, continues to broadcast the voices of the women of her homeland to the world.
title_norm:sing street: A semi-autobiographical work by director John Carney of "Begin Again" and "Once," this youth drama depicts the love and friendship of a boy who forms a band to impress a girl he likes, set to 1980s British sounds. In 1985 Dublin, Ireland, struggling through a severe recession, 14-year-old Conor is forced to transfer to a rough public school after his father loses his job. At home, his parents constantly fight, pushing the family to the brink of collapse. Conor's only solace in his miserable days is watching music videos from neighboring London on TV with his music-obsessed older brother. One day, captivated by the mature charm of a girl named Raphina he sees on the street, Conor invites her to appear in a music video for his band. Hurriedly forming a band, Conor begins intense training to create a video that will amaze the London music scene...
title_norm:sinners: A survival thriller directed by Ryan Coogler ('Black Panther,' 'Creed'), starring Michael B. Jordan, with whom Coogler has frequently collaborated on feature films. In the 1930s, in a devout small town in the American South, twin brothers Smoke and Stack open a dance hall in their former hometown, serving illegal alcohol and music in pursuit of a fortune. On opening night, the crowd revels in a night of swirling desires, but the arrival of uninvited guests changes everything. The dance hall is consumed by senseless despair, and a night of chaos beyond human comprehension begins. Jordan plays the dual role of the twin brothers. The cast includes Hailee Steinfeld ('Bumblebee'), Jack O'Connell ('Ferrari'), and Delroy Lindo ('Da 5 Bloods'). Coogler also wrote and produced the film, reuniting the 'Black Panther' team including production designer Hannah Beachler, composer Ludwig Göransson, and costume designer Ruth E. Carter. At the 98th Academy Awards, it received a record-tying 16 nominations, including Best Picture and Best Director, winning four awards: Best Actor (Michael B. Jordan), Best Original Screenplay, Best Cinematography, and Best Original Score.
title_norm:sinsin and the mouse: A human drama based on a story from Banana Yoshimoto's short story collection 'Mitten and Fubin', co-produced by Japan and Taiwan. It quietly depicts a woman carrying loss who, through encounters in a foreign land, gradually finds renewal. Chizumi is a woman living each day with deep grief after losing her mother. As time passes without filling the void in her heart, she is invited by a friend to visit Taiwan. There, she meets Shin-shin, a young man with a Taiwanese mother and a Japanese father. The unfamiliar cityscapes and the accumulation of casual conversations slowly begin to move her frozen heart, and Chizumi, while still carrying her lingering sense of loss, discovers small warmth. Yukino Kishii ('Small, Slow but Steady', 'Just the Two of Us') plays the protagonist Chizumi, and popular young Taiwanese actor Tseng Jing-hua (known for 'The Soul of the Prisoner', 'Your Name Engraved Herein') plays Shin-shin, the young man she meets in Taiwan. The cast also includes Tokio Fujiwara, Seina Nakata, Tokio Emoto, Kayo Ise, Kisuke Iida, and Kimiko Yo. Directed and scripted by Yukinori Makabe ('I Am a Monk.', 'Scoop!').
title_norm:sirat: This road movie, blending a fantastical story with cool dance music, follows a father and son's journey through a desert rave party in search of a missing daughter, sparking buzz across Spain and Europe. Luis drives with his son Esteban from the Moroccan mountains deep into the desert to find his daughter, who disappeared after attending a desert rave. They reach an outdoor rave site where reality and hallucination blur, but she is not there. The father and son chase a group of ravers, heading to the next rave site where they believe she went. Sergi López ("Pan's Labyrinth") plays father Luis. Directed and written by Oliver Laxe ("Fire Will Come"), the film is produced by renowned Spanish master Pedro Almodóvar. The title "Siraat" means "path" in Arabic and, in a religious sense, symbolizes the narrow bridge over heaven and hell on Judgment Day. Screened in the Competition section of the 78th Cannes Film Festival in 2025, it won four awards including the Jury Prize. It was nominated for the Academy Awards for Best International Feature Film and Best Sound at the 98th Academy Awards.
title_norm:siren and life – ウクライナで続く、戦争と: In late May 2026, at a theater in Tokyo, the first feature-length documentary film *Siren and Life* by filmmaker and street photographer Kaito Tada was screened. Director Tada made his debut as a film director at the 2022 Zushi Film Festival with the short documentary *Our Beautiful Playground*. His second work, the documentary *Siren and Life*, which depicts the reality of everyday life in Ukraine, garnered significant attention, drawing an audience of 156 people over just two days of screenings. Now, a special screening with a talk event has been scheduled for July 20 (Monday, public holiday) at Uplink Kichijoji. On the day, in addition to Director Tada, three panelists will take the stage: art director Marina Takahashi, who handled the visual design, and Dante Kuwajima, who served as the interviewer in the film. They will speak at length in an interview-style format, including a Q&A session, about topics related to the film and the attention to detail in the book production.
title_norm:sirāt: This road movie, blending a fantastical story with cool dance music, follows a father and son's journey through a desert rave party in search of a missing daughter, sparking buzz across Spain and Europe. Luis drives with his son Esteban from the Moroccan mountains deep into the desert to find his daughter, who disappeared after attending a desert rave. They reach an outdoor rave site where reality and hallucination blur, but she is not there. The father and son chase a group of ravers, heading to the next rave site where they believe she went. Sergi López ("Pan's Labyrinth") plays father Luis. Directed and written by Oliver Laxe ("Fire Will Come"), the film is produced by renowned Spanish master Pedro Almodóvar. The title "Siraat" means "path" in Arabic and, in a religious sense, symbolizes the narrow bridge over heaven and hell on Judgment Day. Screened in the Competition section of the 78th Cannes Film Festival in 2025, it won four awards including the Jury Prize. It was nominated for the Academy Awards for Best International Feature Film and Best Sound at the 98th Academy Awards.
title_norm:sisters of the gion: A commentary: A masterpiece that gazes with a penetrating eye at two contrasting geisha sisters living in Kyoto's Gion pleasure district. The older sister, old-fashioned and easily swayed by emotion, and the younger sister, modern and pragmatic... You can't take your eyes off the 19-year-old Yamada, who plays the younger sister rebelling against her submissive elder sibling and trying to toy with men, exuding a remarkable presence.
title_norm:six in paris: An omnibus film of short works, each directed by one of six leading directors of the French New Wave, all set against the backdrop of Paris. The six episodes are: "Saint-Denis Street" (directed by Jean-Daniel Pollet), about a timid man who brings a prostitute he met in a red-light district back to his apartment; "North Station" (Jean Rouch), about a woman living with her lover in an apartment far from the station who encounters an unexpected incident on her way to work after arguing with him; "Saint-Germain-des-Prés" (Jean Douchet), depicting the romantic entanglements of young people in a student quarter; "Place de l'Étoile" (Éric Rohmer), about a man heading to work through the Place de l'Étoile who faces a series of troubles; "Montparnasse and Levallois" (Jean-Luc Godard), about a woman who writes love letters to two different men but accidentally mails the wrong ones; and "La Muette" (Claude Chabrol), depicting a tragedy that strikes a bourgeois family in an upscale neighborhood from the son's perspective. The cast includes Joanna Shimkus from "The Adventurers," Stéphane Audran from "Babette's Feast," and Barbet Schroeder, who also produced this film, among others.
title_norm:small things like these: Starring Cillian Murphy of "Oppenheimer," this film adapts the bestselling novel "Small Things Like These" by Irish author Claire Keegan. Set against the backdrop of the real-life human rights abuses at Ireland's Magdalene laundries, it depicts the inner conflict and decision of a man who discovers a truth society has long ignored. In 1985, in a small Irish town, coal merchant Bill Furlong lives modestly with his family. One day before Christmas, while delivering coal to a local convent, a girl confined there begs him, "Please get me out of here." Confronted with the reality of young women suffering with no way out, Bill understands it would be wise to look the other way, but his conscience torments him, leading him to make a fateful decision. Emily Watson of "Breaking the Waves" plays the convent's Mother Superior, Sister Mary, winning the Silver Bear for Best Supporting Performance at the 74th Berlin International Film Festival in 2024. Eileen Walsh of "The Magdalene Sisters" plays Bill's wife, Eileen. Murphy, who fell in love with the original novel, personally pushed for the film adaptation and served as a producer for the first time. Directed by Tim Mielants of "Peaky Blinders," the film also features Matt Damon as a producer and Ben Affleck as an executive producer.
title_norm:snow as flowers niino’s snow: A documentary by filmmaker Shinkichi Noda, who continually explored the foundations of people's consciousness in rapidly changing Showa-era Japan. This film captures the "Niino Snow Festival" of Nagano Prefecture, seeking to find the enduring spirit of the people within this festival that has continued since medieval times. The Niino Snow Festival has been held since around the 13th century, centered around Izu Shrine and Suwa Shrine in Niino, Anan Town, Nagano Prefecture. People see the falling winter snow as rice flower blossoms, a harbinger of the harvest, and pray for abundant grain. Throughout the night-long festival, masked and costumed performances like "Kyoman" (horse racing), "Okina" (old man), and "Oni" (demon) appear one after another, and the crowd erupts when the spirit of bounty, "Saiho," makes its entrance. Director Noda attempts to read the everyday wishes of farmers for the coming year's production within this sacred festival space. This film is part of the special screening series "Shinkichi Noda Special: Snow is a Flower" (screening from December 6, 2025, at Pole Pole Higashi-Nakano and other theaters nationwide).
title_norm:solaris: When communication is lost with the space station Prometheus, which is exploring the ocean-and-cloud-covered planet Solaris, psychologist Kris is sent to investigate. Upon arriving at the Prometheus, Kris witnesses the suicide of a friend, traces of people who shouldn't be there, and a series of inexplicable phenomena caused by the sentient organic ocean.
title_norm:song sung blue: A musical drama starring Hugh Jackman and Kate Hudson in their first collaboration, based on the true story of a married couple who performed as a tribute band to American national singer Neil Diamond. Mike, who once dreamed of a music career, now can only get on stage by imitating someone else's singing, hitting rock bottom in life. One day, he meets Claire, a woman with the same passion, and they form a tribute band to their beloved Neil Diamond. Starting from a small garage, their voices gradually capture the hearts of the people in their town. But then, a sudden tragedy strikes them. Jackman and Hudson deliver powerful performances of Neil Diamond's classic songs, including 'Sweet Caroline.' The cast includes Michael Imperioli from 'The Sopranos,' Ella Anderson from 'The Glass Castle,' and singer-songwriter King Princess. Based on the 2008 documentary of the same name, Craig Brewer, director of 'Hustle & Flow,' wrote and directed the film. Hudson was nominated for Best Actress at the 98th Academy Awards.
title_norm:sorda: A Spanish film that delicately portrays the story of a woman living in a world without sound and her family. Ángela, who is deaf, and her husband Héctor, who gently supports her, communicate through the irreplaceable language of sign language. Ángela works in a pottery workshop, surrounded by the comforting smell of clay and trusted colleagues, living a quiet and peaceful life. However, a certain 'happy event' begins to gradually shatter her daily life. As she wavers in her sense of alienation, Ángela tries to grasp the 'true happiness' that flickers between the silent world and the world outside... Directed by emerging filmmaker Eva Libertad, who also works as a playwright and sociologist, this film is based on her highly acclaimed 2021 short film 'Sorda.' Starring Miriam Garlo, a deaf actress and Libertad's real sister, the film reflects the director and her sister's long-standing personal experiences, capturing the subtle misunderstandings between deaf and hearing people and the different feelings of alienation each holds. It won the Panorama Audience Award and the Art Cinema Award at the 75th Berlin International Film Festival in 2025, as well as the Golden Biznaga (Best Film), Audience Award, Best Actress, and Best Actor at the 28th Málaga Film Festival in Spain.
title_norm:sound of fallin: Four girls from different eras, spanning from the 1910s to the present day, experience inexplicable events on a farm in northern Germany. A century-spanning visual epic where their anxieties resonate with one another.
title_norm:soundtrack to a coup detat: A staggering documentary that delivers an unprecedented experience to audiences! A jazz rhapsody that digs into the darkness of history, built entirely from archival footage! Satchmo, Malcolm X, Gillespie, Khrushchev, Coltrane, Castro, Nina Simone, Nehru, Nasser, and Sukarno too... Witness a historical farce swirling with conspiracy!
title_norm:soundtrack to a coup d’etat: A staggering documentary that delivers an unprecedented experience to audiences! A jazz rhapsody that digs into the darkness of history, built entirely from archival footage! Satchmo, Malcolm X, Gillespie, Khrushchev, Coltrane, Castro, Nina Simone, Nehru, Nasser, and Sukarno too... Witness a historical farce swirling with conspiracy!
title_norm:soylent green: Directed by Richard Fleischer of "Fantastic Voyage" fame, this 1973 near-future sci-fi film adapts Harry Harrison's novel "Make Room! Make Room!" and depicts various social issues such as overpopulation, extreme weather, food shortages, resource depletion, ecological collapse, and poverty. In 2022, New York City is suffering from explosive population growth, leaving people homeless and food shortages commonplace, while rapid climate change has subjected the city to heat waves. In a world of extreme inequality, most people spend their days idly waiting for the weekly government ration of the nutrient food "Soylent." Amidst this, a murder occurs: Simonsohn, an executive of the Soylent Corporation who just announced the new product "Soylent Green" as the ultimate nutrition, is killed. Homicide detective Thorn takes on the investigation... Charlton Heston of "Ben-Hur" stars as Detective Thorn, with Edward G. Robinson of "Little Caesar" co-starring. A digitally remastered version was revived in theaters in May 2024.
title_norm:spalovač mrtvol: Set in Prague, Czechoslovakia on the eve of World War II, this dark comedy depicts how an ordinary citizen working at a funeral home is influenced by his pro-Nazi friend and the social climate, driving him toward a disastrous solution. Karel Kopfrkingl, who works as a cremator at a small Prague funeral home, is an ordinary man who loves his family. One day, he reunites with a war buddy from World War I, who has become a member of the Nazi Party. Persuaded by his friend to monitor the local Jewish community, Karel gradually becomes influenced by his friend and the social situation... The film portrays how an utterly ordinary person becomes a perpetrator, using beautiful yet eerie expressionistic imagery. This work, which exposes the terror of totalitarian ideology, was banned in its home country of Czechoslovakia and could not be shown until the fall of the communist regime in 1990. It won the Grand Prize at the 5th Sitges - Catalonian International Film Festival. In Japan, it will have its theatrical premiere in April 2026 as part of "Czech Film Masterpieces," a series featuring classics of the Czech New Wave.
title_norm:sph: Director Macoto Tezka’s first feature-length 16mm film. "Sph" is an abbreviation for "Spiritual Phenomenon" (fairy phenomenon). Moe Imai plays the heroine, a fairy.
title_norm:spider man 2: THE RIVER, one of Japan's largest overseas pop culture media outlets, celebrates its 10th anniversary in 2026. "REVIVAL by THE RIVER" is a new project expanding the community of online film fans into the real-world space of movie theaters. THE RIVER brings the films we once longed for back to the big screen. THE RIVER reunites films with their audiences! The commemorative first screening is 'Spider-Man 2'! Two years after the fierce battle with the Green Goblin, college student Peter Parker struggles with part-time jobs and classes while fighting for justice, leading a hectic life. Torn between his love for MJ and his friendship with Harry due to his identity as Spider-Man, Peter accepts his fate. A new enemy, Doctor Octopus, stands in his way. The most powerful action entertainment ever, surpassing its predecessor and achieving historic box office records. Flat rate of 1,600 yen (free tickets, invitation tickets, and various discount services not applicable). Online/TCG members: June 23 (Tue) 18:00~. General sale: June 23 (Tue) 21:00~. Box office sales begin June 24 (Wed). Screenings: July 3 (Fri) ~ July 9 (Thu), one screening per day at 18:10.
title_norm:spider man brand new day: The fourth installment of Tom Holland's 'Spider-Man' series, part of the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU). Set four years after the previous film 'Spider-Man: No Way Home,' it depicts a new battle for Peter Parker—Spider-Man—who has been erased from people's memories. To protect his loved ones, Peter Parker chose to erase all memory of his existence from the world. Living a lonely life in New York, where no one knows him, he spends his days fighting crime as Spider-Man and dedicating himself to protecting the city's people. But as public expectations of Spider-Man rise, the pressure threatens his very existence, causing life-threatening physical mutations. At the same time, mysterious crimes occur frequently in the city, and an unprecedented threat looms over Spider-Man. Co-stars include Zendaya as MJ, Jacob Batalon as Ned, and other familiar faces from the previous three films, plus Jon Bernthal as Frank Castle/The Punisher from the MCU series 'Daredevil' and 'The Punisher,' and Mark Ruffalo as Bruce Banner/The Hulk from 'The Avengers.' The director is Destin Daniel Cretton of 'Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings,' replacing Jon Watts, who directed the previous three films.
title_norm:spy game: Brad Pitt and Robert Redford, the duo from 'A River Runs Through It', reunite. A story of the passionate friendship between CIA spies and a desperate rescue mission.
title_norm:stalag 17: Based on a hit Broadway play set in a Nazi-guarded American POW camp. With everyone's cooperation, two prisoners attempting to escape are shot dead. Suspicions arise among the group that there is a traitor, and the lone wolf Sefton is immediately eyed with distrust. Sefton tries to clear his name by searching for the German spy... Lead actor William Holden joined the ranks of Oscar-winning actors with this film and went on to achieve remarkable success. However, he tragically died in an accident in 1981.
title_norm:star wars the mandalorian and: The first theatrical feature film in about seven years from the globally popular sci-fi saga "Star Wars". It depicts on a grand scale the story of the lone bounty hunter Mandalorian and the young Force-sensitive being Grogu, as portrayed in the drama series "The Mandalorian". Set in the galaxy after "Star Wars: Return of the Jedi", the era is chaotic, with the New Republic's rule incomplete and outlaws and Imperial remnants running rampant. Amidst this, the orphan Grogu, who possesses immense Force power, is pursued by those who covet his strength. The bounty hunter Din Jarin, aka the Mandalorian, decides to protect him, and as they travel through a dangerous galaxy, they gradually develop a father-son bond. The film shows a grown Grogu using the Force powers he honed under Luke Skywalker's training, and features intense, fast-paced battles against Imperial remnants, delivering the large-scale action unique to the "Star Wars" series. A new character, Colonel Ward, is played by the renowned actress Sigourney Weaver. Dave Filoni, Lucasfilm's Chief Creative Officer, serves as executive producer, and Jon Favreau directs, bringing together the creators behind "The Mandalorian" series.
title_norm:still walkin: Director Hirokazu Kore-eda of "Nobody Knows" and "Maborosi" quietly captures the scene of a family gathering at their elderly parents' home for the first time in a while, bringing out the joys and sorrows of life in this home drama. One summer day, the second son, Ryota, and the eldest daughter, Chinami, bring their respective families to the home where former doctor Kyohei Yokoyama and his wife Toshiko live alone. The Yokoyama family spends a casual time together, but this day happens to be the anniversary of the death of their eldest son, Junpei, who passed away 15 years ago.
title_norm:stop making sense: A live documentary of the rock band Talking Heads. Capturing their 1983 stage performance at the Pantages Theatre with various camera angles, it conveys the raw energy and excitement directly.
title_norm:storytellers: The third part of the Tohoku documentary trilogy co-directed by Ryusuke Hamaguchi ('PASSION') and Ko Sakai ('Home Sweet Home'). Following the first two works that collected dialogues of Great East Japan Earthquake survivors, this documentary records folk tales passed down in the Tohoku region. With folk tale researcher Kazuko Ono as the listener, three storytellers with richly inflected dialects perform their tales. The unique atmosphere that arises between storyteller and listener is brought to the screen through creative camerawork.
title_norm:stranger: In a corner of the city, Kawamura Kiriko lives a lonely life as a late-night taxi driver. Bound by a past with a criminal record, she continues to reject connections with others—until suddenly, someone targets her life. Who is the attacker? And what is the reason—!? A mysterious Land Cruiser, its driver unseen, roars as it attacks! But with the police refusing to take her seriously, she decides to fight alone. If she can do that, she can make a fresh start...
title_norm:stray kids the dominate exper:
A live documentary following the world tour of the globally renowned K-pop group Stray Kids.

Stray Kids is an eight-member South Korean boy group that debuted in March 2018 with the mini-album *I am NOT*. They have garnered significant attention as a highly talented group whose members write, compose, and produce their own music. With eight consecutive number-one albums on the U.S. Billboard 200 chart, they have built a massive following not only in Korea and Japan but across the entire globe.

From 2024 to 2025, the group embarked on their largest world tour to date, "dominATE," performing 56 shows across 35 countries and regions. This film follows the tour closely, centering on their electrifying performance at the massive SoFi Stadium in Los Angeles. It also features behind-the-scenes footage and exclusive interviews where the members speak candidly about their individual struggles and passions. From their overwhelming stage presence to their unfiltered moments backstage, the film captures the moments that define Stray Kids' identity. The documentary is directed by Paul Dugdale, who has previously worked on live concert films for world-class artists such as Adele and Taylor Swift.
title_norm:street of shame: Commentary: Mizoguchi Kenji's final work. Set in a Yoshiwara brothel in Tokyo on the eve of the abolition of the red-light district, this female ensemble piece depicts the joys and sorrows of women who have drifted there with various circumstances. The nonchalant prostitutes, played by a cast of luxurious actresses, exude a peculiar atmosphere, making this film a one-of-a-kind red-light district story.
title_norm:striking rescue: A revenge action film starring Thai action star Tony Jaa, known for 'Ong-Bak' and 'Tom-Yum-Goong'. It depicts a man who lost his family confronting a massive conspiracy, packed with powerful Muay Thai-based hand-to-hand combat and high-speed, hard-hitting action. After his wife and daughter are killed by a mysterious organization, Bai An heads to the Republic of Parivina to uncover the truth and exact revenge. As he investigates on his own, he discovers a giant corporation secretly controlling the drug trade, but behind it swirls a vast conspiracy involving the military and police. The situation becomes intricately tangled with a mad drug lord, corrupt military police, and unexpected trials involving the only daughter of the corporation's owner. Bai An is tossed about but continues to battle the enemies closing in on him. Directed by Cheung Sui-yee. Co-stars include Xing Yu from 'Master Z: Ip Man Legacy', Philip Keung from 'Goldfinger', and Jason Han from 'Overheat: The Final Sanction'.
title_norm:sumiko 22: Directed and written by Fukuoka Sawako of the filmmaking unit "Shidoromodori," which gained attention for "I Still Don't Know You," this drama humorously depicts the relatable struggles of a woman in her twenties, based on her own experiences. Shizuoka Sumiko, 22, realizes that her senses have somehow become vague. Since then, she spends her days having conversations with herself. She realizes that her family's cat is very important to her, that after trying hard to fit into an uncomfortable space she needs to eat delicious chocolate, and that she's bothered by people wearing white skinny jeans that show their underwear. When she tries to remember the previous day while hungover, she ends up remembering things she didn't need to. After quitting the company she joined after graduating university in just four months, Sumiko spends her days in her new life, confirming the things she truly believes. Hori Haruna (from "Hamabe no Game") stars in a lead film role for the first time in five years, with Hamada Satsuki (a member of "Shidoromodori" who also served as assistant director on this film) and Matsuo Shohei (from "Lost Baby Lost") co-starring.
title_norm:summer at grandpas: Taiwanese master Hou Hsiao-hsien crafts a masterpiece drama that vividly portrays the beauty of nature and childhood friendship through the story of a young brother and sister spending a summer in their grandfather's countryside home. After graduating from elementary school in Taipei, Tongtong's mother is hospitalized, so he and his little sister spend summer vacation at their grandfather's house in the countryside. They quickly become friends with the neighborhood children, and Tongtong enjoys a fun summer running through the fields. Meanwhile, his sister Tingting struggles to join the group and passes the time by playing pranks on her brother and his friends, until their father eventually comes from Taipei to pick them up. The father of the siblings is played by filmmaker Edward Yang, known for "The Terrorizers" and "Yi Yi." First released in Japan in 1990. Digital remastered versions were re-released in 2016 and 2025.
title_norm:summer days with coo: Elementary school student Kōichi Uehara finds a large stone buried on a riverbank on his way home. Driven by curiosity, he cracks it open and discovers a dried-up, fossil-like creature inside. It is a baby kappa that has been in a state of suspended animation underground for a long time. Kōichi names it 'Kū' and begins living with it.
title_norm:sun tribe myth from the bakum: Saheiji, left penniless at a Shinagawa pleasure quarter at the end of the Edo period... A masterpiece by Kawashima and Frankie, and a classic in Japanese film history. In this ensemble comedy where late-Edo period patriots and courtesans mingle, Frankie's light and agile movements as he navigates through the chaos are the film's core.
title_norm:sunset boulevard: A film that synchronizes two eras: the silent era of Hollywood, the movie capital, and the 1950s. Billy Wilder stated his intention: 'I wanted to make a film about Hollywood, set in Hollywood.' Unsuccessful screenwriter Gillis stumbles into the home of Norma, a great silent film star. She longs for a comeback to the glamorous world and asks Gillis to polish her script, but... Gloria Swanson's tense performance as Norma is superb. Cecil B. DeMille, known for directing 'Cleopatra' and others, appears as himself.
title_norm:super happy forever: On August 19, 2023, Sano and Miyata visit a seaside resort hotel in Izu. Sano had recently lost his wife Nagi, whom he had met and fallen in love with there five years earlier. Miyata, as a friend, tries to advise Sano, who is clinging to memories of his wife and becoming self-destructive, but Miyata's words, steeped in a certain seminar he is devoted to, do not reach Sano. Exchanging few words, the two visit the now-closed restaurant and sightseeing boat filled with memories, and begin searching for the red hat that was lost long ago.
title_norm:supergirl: A DC Universe film following James Gunn's 2025 "Superman," this hero action movie centers on Supergirl / Kara Zor-El, the cousin of Superman / Clark Kent. In a world after Superman saved Earth, Kara Zor-El, who lost her home planet Krypton, lives quietly with her beloved dog Krypto, her only emotional anchor. One day, a mysterious enemy named Krem suddenly appears and poisons Krypto. To obtain the antidote, Kara embarks on a grand cosmic battle alongside Lucy, an alien girl whose family was also taken by Krem, and a vicious bounty hunter robot. Millie Alcock, the young Australian actor who gained attention for the TV series "House of the Dragon," reprises her role as Supergirl / Kara Zor-El from "Superman." Evey Ridley (Netflix's "3 Body Problem") plays the alien girl Lucy Mary Noelle, and Jason Momoa ("Aquaman," "A Minecraft Movie") co-stars as the bounty hunter robot. Superdog Krypto, who appeared in "Superman," also returns. Produced by James Gunn's DC Studios following "Superman," the film is directed by Craig Gillespie ("I, Tonya," "Cruella").
title_norm:suspiria: 'Never watch it alone—' This famous tagline became a buzzword at the time of release. A masterpiece often talked about to this day, where vivid colors, the eerie sound featuring Goblin, and extreme direction form a trinity that creates a unique tension. It was a hit in Japan in 1977, ranking in the top ten among foreign films released that year. Its influence led to the Japanese release of an unrelated 1975 film by Argento as 'Suspiria Part 2' the following year. For the director, this is the first installment of the 'Three Mothers' trilogy, followed by 'Inferno' and 'Mother of Tears.' Suzy, who has come from America to study at a German ballet school, witnesses a woman disappearing while muttering something on the night she arrives at the dormitory. Shortly after, the woman is killed by someone. After enrolling, Suzy undergoes rigorous training but begins to experience physical abnormalities, fainting, and along with her friend Sara, hears strange groans and footsteps in the dormitory. One night, feeling pursued by someone, Sara flees alone through the dormitory...
title_norm:suzaku: A small village in the mountains of southern Nara Prefecture. Fifteen years have passed since plans to build a railway through this village were proposed, but Kozo Tamura, who was involved in the tunnel construction, loses all motivation upon learning the project has been cancelled. Then one day, Kozo disappears. His remaining family, bewildered, each make their own choices.
title_norm:suzume: Director Makoto Shinkai, of "Your Name." and "Weathering with You," presents a feature animation depicting the adventure and growth of a girl who journeys across ruins throughout Japan to close "doors" that bring disaster. Suzume Iwato, a 17-year-old living in Kyushu, meets Souta Munakata, a young man on a journey searching for doors. Following him to a mountain ruin, Suzume finds an old door standing as if spared from the surrounding collapse, and is drawn to reach for it. Soon, doors begin opening one after another across Japan. As calamities come from beyond the doors, Suzume embarks on a journey to close them. Despite numerous surprises and hardships, Suzume continues forward, but... Nanoka Hara, a young actress known for "The Sound of Sin" and "My Heart Beats for You," was chosen through auditions to voice the protagonist Suzume. Hokuto Matsumura of SixTONES voices Souta, marking his voice acting debut. Also voicing roles are Eri Fukatsu, Shota Someno, Sairi Ito, Kotone Hanase, and Hakuo Matsumoto, with regular Shinkai collaborators Ryunosuke Kamiki and Kana Hanazawa also appearing. Music is again by RADWIMPS, in their third collaboration with Shinkai, alongside composer Kazuma Jinnouchi. Screened in competition at the 73rd Berlin International Film Festival in 2023, marking the first Japanese animated film in competition there in 21 years since "Spirited Away," which won the Golden Bear.
title_norm:swiss army man: An unconventional survival story in which Daniel Radcliffe, of "Harry Potter" fame, plays a corpse, and Paul Dano, known for "Little Miss Sunshine" and "Love & Mercy," plays a young man who attempts to escape a deserted island using the corpse. After being shipwrecked and washing ashore on a deserted island, Hank, a young man, is about to end his life in despair when he discovers a man's corpse washed up on the shore. Noticing that the corpse is emitting gas and has buoyancy, Hank makes a decision and tries to escape the island by straddling the corpse, but... This is the feature debut of directing duo Daniel Kwan and Daniel Scheinert (known as Daniels), who come from a background in commercial directing. The film garnered attention with awards at the Sundance Film Festival and the Sitges Film Festival. Mary Elizabeth Winstead (from "10 Cloverfield Lane") co-stars.
title_norm:taira clan saga: A commentary: In the late Heian period, when warriors rose in place of the aristocracy, Taira no Kiyomori faces various hardships... Mizoguchi depicts the "human" Kiyomori, tormented by the secret of his birth, on an overwhelming scale in this historical drama. A young Raizō, early in his debut, plays the youthful Kiyomori with dashing flair, and the unforgettable performance by Kogure as his sensuous mother lingers in the mind.
title_norm:tange sazen and the pot worth: A commotion over a pot that reveals the hiding place of a large sum of money draws in the swordsman Sanzen... A delightful gem showcasing the talent of Yamanaka, who lightly and skillfully portrays Daigoro's signature role of Sanzen.
title_norm:tange sazen heavenly clouds,: Master director Takashi Kato depicts the process by which Tange Sazen loses his right eye and right arm, with a realism unprecedented in conventional sword-fighting films. Based on the original story by Fumio Hayashi. Ordered by Soma clan lord Nakamura Daizen to steal the famous swords Ken'un and Konryu, Sazen sneaks into the dojo of Onozuka Tessai but only manages to take Ken'un, losing his right eye to Tessai's blade. Hearing this, Daizen abandons Sazen and plots to gather men to attack the dojo again. Enraged by his master's cold treatment, Sazen storms the dojo once more to seize Konryu.
title_norm:tange sazen the million ryo p: Known as a masterpiece by early Showa period master Tomu Uchida, who died at just 28, this period drama stars Denjiro Okochi as the ronin Tange Sazen. Tange Sazen, a ronin living at an archery range and working as a bodyguard, and the proprietress Ofuji take in Chobian, the son of a man stabbed to death at the shop. Chobian carries a certain pot around carefully, using it as a goldfish bowl, but it actually contains a hidden map to a million ryo. This is one of only three surviving films by Uchida, most of whose original prints have been lost. It was remade in 2004 as "Tange Sazen: The Million Ryo Pot" starring Etsushi Toyokawa.
title_norm:taste of cherry: Buddy, a middle-aged man, invites people into his car and makes a strange request: "Tomorrow morning, call out to me lying in a hole. If I answer, help me; if there's no answer, cover me with dirt." Everyone refuses, but the old man he finally picks up begins to tell him about the joy of living...
title_norm:tekkonkinkreet: Based on the popular manga by Taiyo Matsumoto serialized in 'Big Spirits' magazine from 1993 to 1994, this anime film adaptation is directed by Michael Arias, a VFX specialist active in Hollywood known for 'The Animatrix'. Set in the 'Treasure Town' of duty and human emotion, it depicts the exploits of two boys, Kuro and Shiro, who fly freely through the city. The voice cast includes Kazunari Ninomiya, who made his overseas debut in Clint Eastwood's 'Letters from Iwo Jima', and Yu Aoi from 'Hula Girls'.
title_norm:ten dark women: A black comedy directed by Kon Ichikawa and scripted by Natto Wada, weaving together a philandering man, his wife, and nine lovers. TV producer Matsukichi Kazama, despite having a beautiful wife named Futaba, is cheating with nine women. The wife and lovers are vaguely aware of each other's existence and fully know that Matsukichi is a womanizer, yet for some reason they cannot leave him. One day, the wife and a stage actress lover named Ichiko come up with a plan to kill Matsukichi. It is a fictional scheme meant to vent their frustration with him, but timid Matsukichi becomes convinced that his lovers are trying to kill him and consults his wife. The wife readily admits to the plan and then, to eliminate the lovers, suggests staging a fake murder: they gather the lovers for a meeting to denounce Matsukichi, and at that gathering, pretend to shoot him dead with a pistol.
title_norm:that day, on the beach 4k res: Edward Yang × Christopher Doyle! A masterpiece heralding the dawn of Taiwanese New Cinema by these two guiding lights of world cinema!
title_norm:the a care disusebody: Based on the debut novel by physician-author Yo Hisakabe published in 2003, this human suspense film stars Shota Sometani. At the daycare facility 'Ijinzaka Clinic,' an innovative treatment devised by director Kuranosuke Urushibara spreads quietly among the elderly. Aiming for cost-effective care, the treatment involves 'useless limbs' (paralyzed body parts with no hope of recovery), and unexpected 'favorable side effects' have appeared, such as 'feeling lighter in body and mind' and 'a harsh personality softening.' Hearing rumors, editor Yagura senses potential for a revolution in geriatric medicine and proposes publishing a book to Urushibara. However, everything takes a dark turn when an internal whistleblowing about the daycare leaks to a weekly magazine, and a shocking incident occurs at a patient's home. Sometani delivers a haunting performance as Urushibara, a doctor who, in pursuit of his ideals, steps into the gap between rationality and madness. The cast includes Yuki Kitamura as editor Yagura, Naomasa Rokudaira as elderly patient Iwagami who reclaims his life through Urushibara's treatment, and Kumi Takiuchi as Urushibara's wife Kikuko. The film is directed and written by Mitsuki Yoshida, who has gained international attention for works such as 'Family X' and 'Three Lights.'
title_norm:the african queen: Master filmmaker John Huston, known for 'The Maltese Falcon,' adapts the classic adventure novel of the same name by British author C.S. Forester. Africa during World War I. Rose, a British woman, is engaged in missionary work with her brother Samuel, a clergyman, but their village is attacked by German forces, and Samuel dies from the shock. Left alone, Rose is rescued by Charlie, who delivers supplies and mail to the village, and boards his ramshackle steamboat, the 'African Queen.' Charlie had planned to take a break from work until the war ended, but is reluctantly persuaded by the vengeful Rose, and the two of them set out to strike back at the Germans. Humphrey Bogart, of 'Casablanca' and 'The Maltese Falcon,' gives a memorable performance as the rough-hewn captain Charlie, a complete departure from his usual hard-boiled image, winning the Academy Award for Best Actor at the 24th Academy Awards in 1952. Katharine Hepburn, of 'Guess Who's Coming to Dinner' and 'The Philadelphia Story,' plays Rose. In 1990, the tumultuous behind-the-scenes story of this film's production was itself dramatized in 'White Hunter Black Heart,' directed by and starring Clint Eastwood.
title_norm:the beldham: In the house she visits with her young daughter, an eerie presence lurks in the shadows. Her love for her child gradually drives her mad—. The director, Angela Garner, who has appeared in numerous works as an actress and has also blossomed as a screenwriter with works drawing attention for addressing her own experience with eating disorders, makes her feature directorial debut with this film. Known for works with autobiographical elements, she delicately portrays the horror born from the nuances of a mother-daughter relationship and love, based on her own family experiences. Katie Parker, from the Netflix series "The Fall of the House of Usher" and "The Haunting of Hill House," plays the protagonist Harper. She brilliantly portrays a woman desperately protecting her child from the eerie shadows lurking in the house while gradually being consumed by madness. The setting is a suburban house that Harper's mother is preparing to sell. An unidentified black shadow dwells there, but only Harper can perceive its presence... A small sense of unease eventually leads to a truth that overturns expectations. Are Harper's actions, threatened by the eerie presence, born of love? Or madness—? This unpredictable psychological horror accelerates the fear through its masterful story development, leading you to an unprecedented finale.
title_norm:the beldham ベルダム: In the house she visits with her young daughter, an eerie presence lurks in the shadows. Her love for her child gradually drives her mad—. The director, Angela Garner, who has appeared in numerous works as an actress and has also blossomed as a screenwriter with works drawing attention for addressing her own experience with eating disorders, makes her feature directorial debut with this film. Known for works with autobiographical elements, she delicately portrays the horror born from the nuances of a mother-daughter relationship and love, based on her own family experiences. Katie Parker, from the Netflix series "The Fall of the House of Usher" and "The Haunting of Hill House," plays the protagonist Harper.
