Alongside Baisho as Sumire and Kimura as driver Usami, Aoi Yu, making her sixth appearance in a Yamada film since "My Wife is a Rose: Family is Tough III," plays the young Sumire. Takaya Sakaguchi plays Sumire's fiancé Ogawa, and Yuka plays Usami's wife Kaoru. The cast also includes Runa Nakajima, Misuzu Kanno, Lee Jun-young, and Takashi Sasano.
title_norm:tomie: Tsukiko Izumisawa, a girl suffering from memory loss and insomnia due to an accident three years ago, attends a psychiatric clinic. Her doctor, Hosono, probes her memories through hypnotherapy and hears the name "Tomie." However, Tsukiko cannot recall who that name belongs to. Then, strange and terrifying events suddenly begin occurring in Tsukiko's life. One day, a detective from the Metropolitan Police visits Hosono. He is investigating a woman named Tomie Kawakami.
title_norm:tonnerre: A life-affirming drama by rising French director Guillaume Brac, known for 'A Summer's Tale,' depicting an aging, down-and-out musician struggling with a bleak future as he gradually discovers the true meaning of love. Starring Vincent Macaigne, a regular in Brac's films. Maxime, a musician now nearly forgotten by the world, returns to his hometown of Tonnerre in the Burgundy region of France. His single father Claude enjoys outdoor sports, has a vibrant love life, and revels in life, but Maxime, exhausted by city living, has lost his will to live. Then, a young female journalist named Mélodie from a local information magazine comes to interview Maxime. Drawn to her youth and smile, Maxime grows closer to her...
title_norm:tony takitani: A love story adapted from Haruki Murakami's short story of the same name, directed by Jun Ichikawa of 'Tokiwa: The Manga Apartment' and 'Tsugumi,' starring Issey Ogata and Rie Miyazawa. Tony Takitani, born as the son of a trombonist, loses his mother shortly after birth and grows up carrying loneliness. After working at a design company, he becomes an independent illustrator, falls in love with a woman, and marries her. But their happy days are short-lived; his wife dies in an accident. Feeling his loneliness, he hires a woman who closely resembles his late wife as an assistant and tries to get used to her death by having the assistant wear the vast collection of clothes his shopaholic wife left behind... Issey Ogata plays the protagonist Tony Takitani and his father, Rie Miyazawa plays Tony's wife and the woman who resembles her, with Hidetoshi Nishijima providing narration. The music is composed by Ryuichi Sakamoto. The film won the Special Jury Prize, the FIPRESCI Prize, and the Youth Jury Award at the 57th Locarno International Film Festival in 2004. A 4K remastered version was re-released in 2026.
title_norm:top gun maverick: The sequel to the worldwide hit "Top Gun" (1986) that shot Tom Cruise to stardom. Maverick, a legendary pilot, returns to TOPGUN, the U.S. Navy's elite pilot training school, as an instructor. He, who knows the harshness and beauty of the sky better than anyone, teaches the difficulty of protecting and the harshness of fighting, but the trainees are confused and resistant to his unconventional methods. Among them is Rooster, the son of Goose, Maverick's wingman who died during a training flight with him. Rooster resents Maverick and confronts him... Cruise reprises his role as Maverick, with Miles Teller ("Whiplash") and Jennifer Connelly ("A Beautiful Mind") co-starring, and Val Kilmer, who played Maverick's rival Iceman in the previous film, also returns. Directed by Joseph Kosinski ("Oblivion"), with a script by Christopher McQuarrie, known for directing the "Mission: Impossible" series and writing "The Usual Suspects." It was a worldwide blockbuster, grossing over $700 million in North America and over 13.5 billion yen in Japan. Nominated for six Academy Awards at the 95th ceremony including Best Picture, winning Best Sound.
title_norm:topsy turvy journey: Conductor Goichi (Frankie) on the Tohoku Main Line receives passionate advances from his childhood friend, geisha Sakura (Baisho), but secretly has his eye on another woman. The third installment of the 11-film "Travel Series" starring Frankie Sakai, directed by comedy master Segawa.
title_norm:touching the skin of eeriness: A medium-length drama shot by director Hamaguchi Ryusuke, who continues to attract attention with works like 'THE DEPTH' and 'Intimacy,' as a prequel to his planned feature film 'FLOODS.' Chihiro, a boy who has lost his father, comes to live with his half-brother Togo and Togo's lover Misato. Togo and Misato warmly welcome Chihiro, but plagued by loneliness, Chihiro throws himself into dance practice with his same-age friend Naoya. Around them, unsettling events begin to occur... The cast includes talented actors such as Shota Sometani from 'Himizu,' Kiyohiko Shibukawa from 'The Wandering Beast,' and Hotsushi Ishida from 'Canary.'
title_norm:tourist family: A family, fed up with their impoverished life in Sri Lanka, illegally enters India and, armed with 'smiles and a little bit of meddling', sparks small miracles!
title_norm:toy story 5: The fifth installment in Disney and Pixar's beloved 'Toy Story' series, which has always explored the bond between toys and children. It depicts Woody and Buzz joining forces once again to face an unprecedented threat from modern technology. Buzz, Jessie, Forky, and the others living with Bonnie are enjoying their usual daily life. However, everything changes when the latest electronic tablet, the 'Lilypad,' arrives. Seeing Bonnie absorbed in the multi-functional device, the toys begin to doubt their own purpose. As anxiety spreads that 'toys are no longer needed,' Woody receives an SOS from his friends and returns to Bonnie's side, reuniting with Buzz. The legendary duo stands up to a new threat to protect the place of toys. Directed and written by Andrew Stanton, known for 'Finding Nemo' and 'WALL-E,' who has also worked on the 'Toy Story' series as a story and scriptwriter, bringing a new story as a creator who has supported the series. The co-director is Kena Harris, who directed the Pixar short 'Alberto's Letter.' The Japanese dub features the familiar cast including Toshiaki Karasawa as Woody, George Tokoro as Buzz, Yumi Kusaka, and Ryo Ryusei.
title_norm:train to busan: A Korean survival panic action film depicting the terror and chaos caused by the sudden outbreak of a mysterious virus spreading aboard a high-speed train connecting Seoul and Busan. Seok-woo, a fund manager working in Seoul, is separated from his wife and lives with his young daughter Su-an. Su-an insists on going alone to meet her mother in Busan for her birthday, and Seok-woo reluctantly agrees to escort her. They board the KTX high-speed train from Seoul to Busan, but just before departure, a suspicious commotion occurs near Seoul Station. A woman infected with the mysterious virus also boards KTX train 101, the same train as the father and daughter. Alongside the protagonist Seok-woo and his daughter, various passengers—a pregnant woman and her husband, high school baseball players, and a selfish middle-aged businessman—face a life-or-death struggle for survival in a state of extremity where being caught by the infected means certain death, and their individual human dramas unfold. This is the first live-action feature film by Yeon Sang-ho, a rising director who has garnered attention in the Korean animation scene, and the story preceding this film is revealed in the animated feature 'Seoul Station'.
title_norm:trainspottin: A youth film that portrays the cheerful yet miserable lives of young people addicted to drugs, becoming an iconic work of 1990s British pop culture. Renton, a heroin addict living in Edinburgh, Scotland, spends his aimless days hanging out with fellow heroin addicts Sick Boy and Spud, and the violent, alcoholic Begbie. One day, after being arrested for shoplifting, Renton decides to reform, moves to London, and gets a job. However, Begbie and Sick Boy, on the run after a robbery, show up one after another, and Renton gets fired. When they return home, they attend the funeral of their friend Tommy, who turned to drugs after a breakup. Amid overwhelming despair, Renton and the others take a big gamble to change their lives... This is Danny Boyle's second directorial work and the breakout film for Ewan McGregor and Robert Carlyle.
title_norm:travelin band creedence clear: A film documenting and screening the legendary 1970 London performance of the American rock band Creedence Clearwater Revival (CCR). In 1970, at the height of their popularity, CCR embarked on their first and only European tour. The highlight of the tour was their performance at the Royal Albert Hall in London on April 14, where CCR aimed to challenge The Beatles, whose record sales were the highest in the world at the time, by performing in their home territory. However, four days before the performance, news of The Beatles' breakup was reported. Despite this, CCR delivered a powerful, all-or-nothing performance, making the Royal Albert Hall concert one of the greatest live shows in rock history. The complete footage of the London performance, discovered after 50 years, has been restored in 4K, and the film traces their trajectory, interweaving footage capturing the band's daily life, interviews with members, and early live performances. Directed by Bob Smeaton of 'The Beatles Anthology,' with narration by actor Jeff Bridges.
title_norm:trophy: The protagonist is Sohui, a 14-year-old Zainichi Korean girl. She attends a Korean school and devotes herself to Korean dance in her club activities. One day, at an exchange event with a Japanese school, she becomes friends with a Japanese girl named Mirai over their shared love of K-Pop, and Sohui gradually connects with the outside world. To earn money for tickets to their favorite K-Pop idol's concert, the two decide to sell unused items from Sohui's house on a flea market app. Surprisingly, the item that sells for a high price is a North Korean CD owned by Sohui's father, Sanju, who is the principal of the Korean school. Emboldened, Sohui and her friend even sell a "medal" awarded to Sanju by his homeland, North Korea.
title_norm:trouble every day: After becoming a test subject for a new drug, Core (Béatrice Dalle) develops an uncontrollable urge to kill her sexual partners during intercourse. American doctor Shane (Vincent Gallo) travels to France to find her, but...
title_norm:tully: Marlo, a mother of three including a newborn, is given a night nanny by her brother. Initially hesitant, she soon bonds deeply with Tully, a nanny who is thoughtful, surprising, and at times challenging.
title_norm:turbulence: A situational survival thriller set in the inescapable space of a floating hot air balloon, depicting the threats of nature and human conflict. To repair his relationship with his wife Amy, who is grieving a miscarriage, ambitious CEO Zach joins a hot air balloon tour crossing the Italian Dolomites with her. A mysterious woman named Julia joins them, and the flight with the three passengers begins. But high in the sky, Julia suddenly reveals that she had a secret meeting with Zach the previous day, accusing him of infidelity. Zach denies it, but suspicion swirls, and Julia suddenly pulls a knife. During the struggle, the pilot falls out, and the balloon goes out of control. With the radio dead and the balloon reaching an oxygen-thin altitude of 16,000 feet, battered by turbulence and storms, the three are forced into extreme choices with no escape. Directed by Claudio Fae of 'Air Lock: Underwater Emergency Shelter,' with a screenplay by Andy Mason, who wrote and produced 'Air Lock: Underwater Emergency Shelter' and '47 Meters Down.' The cast includes Hera Hilmar of 'Mortal Engines' as Amy, Jeremy Irvine of 'War Horse' as Zach, and Olga Kurylenko, known as a Bond girl from 'Quantum of Solace,' as Julia.
title_norm:turbulence fear takes flight: A situational survival thriller set in the inescapable space of a floating hot air balloon, depicting the threats of nature and human conflict. title_norm:twiggy: A documentary exploring the life and allure of Twiggy, the legendary British model who captivated the world in the 1960s. Debuting at age 16 in 1965, Twiggy quickly rose to stardom, and with her famously slender, twig-like figure and unique fashion sense, she overturned conventional standards of beauty. Becoming an icon of the Swinging London youth culture, she revolutionized the fashion world, sparking a global miniskirt boom. Later, pursuing her own forms of expression, she also found success as an actress and singer, notably starring in Ken Russell's 1971 musical film "The Boy Friend," which drew significant attention. Through Twiggy's own words, rare archival footage, and interviews with those connected to her—including Brooke Shields, Dustin Hoffman, Paul McCartney, and Sienna Miller—the film portrays her life as a woman and mother, her struggles, and her choices. The director is actress Sadie Frost, who also helmed the documentary "Mary Quant: The Legend of Swinging London."
title_norm:twinkle twinkle, killer kane: The directorial debut of William Peter Blatty, known as the author of 'The Exorcist,' who adapted his own novel. Blatty wrote, directed, produced, and scripted this unique human drama set in an old castle used as a psychiatric hospital. In a remote mountain castle serving as a sanatorium, soldiers driven insane by the Vietnam War are gathered and treated. Among them is astronaut Billy Cutshaw, who was committed after going mad just before a rocket launch. One day, Navy psychiatrist Hudson Kane arrives at the facility. Kane listens sympathetically to the patients, but Cutshaw is defiant, and Kane soon begins to be plagued by nightmares. Won the Golden Globe for Best Screenplay. Stars Stacy Keach of 'Roadgames' and 'Escape from L.A.' Although never theatrically released in Japan, it will have its first theatrical screening in 2026 as part of the 'Shinjuku Hardcore Masterpiece Selection 2' special screening (April 17 - May 21, 2026, at CineMart Shinjuku).
title_norm:two zero four six: A sci-fi love story written and directed by Hong Kong master Wong Kar-wai, starring Asian superstars Tony Leung, Takeshi Kaneshiro, and Zhang Ziyi. Set in the 1960s, following "Days of Being Wild" and "In the Mood for Love," it weaves in episodes from those films. In 1967, during Hong Kong's turbulent era, writer Chow, unable to forget a past love and engaging in fleeting relationships with women, begins writing a near-future sci-fi novel titled "2046" at his hotel. The novel's characters board a train where androids serve as stewardesses, heading toward "2046," a place where lost love can be found. Chow reflects his own daily life in the novel, projecting himself onto the male protagonist as he writes. It won Best Actor (Tony Leung) and Best Actress (Zhang Ziyi) at the 24th Hong Kong Film Awards in 2005, and the New York Film Critics Circle Award for Best Foreign Language Film. In 2022, a 4K restored version was screened as part of "WKW4K" at theaters including Cinemart Shinjuku, Grand Cinema Sunshine, and Cinema City.
title_norm:typhoon club: A masterpiece of youth cinema that vividly depicts middle school students who fall into a state of turmoil, showing inexplicable emotional excitement as a typhoon approaches. Directed by Shinji Somai, known for "Sailor Suit and Machine Gun" and "Shonben Rider." In a local city near Tokyo, five students sneak into their private middle school's pool at night to swim. They notice a male student who arrived earlier and play a prank on him, but it goes too far, nearly drowning him. The next morning, the news reports a typhoon approaching. From then on, something gradually begins to go wrong among the students...
title_norm:ugetsu: Commentary: In an age of war, men driven by lust chase illusions even at the cost of sacrificing women... Based on a classic tale of the supernatural, this masterpiece reflects the folly of humans deluded by desire, suspended between reality and fantasy. Winner of the Silver Lion at the Venice Film Festival, it spread Mizoguchi's name worldwide.
title_norm:un homme est mort: A crime suspense film co-produced by France, Italy, and the United States, starring the renowned French actor Jean-Louis Trintignant, known for "A Man and a Woman" and "The Conformist." Lucien, a French hitman, arrives at Los Angeles International Airport. Checking into a Beverly Hills hotel and concealing a pistol, Lucien drives to the upscale residential area where his target, a crime boss, lives. After efficiently eliminating the target, Lucien returns to the hotel only to find that someone has checked him out and his passport and plane ticket are gone. As Lucien becomes paranoid, a hail of bullets suddenly rains down on him from an unknown assassin. Alongside Trintignant as Lucien, the film features a cast of distinctive French, Italian, and American actors including Ann-Margret from "The Hunter" and Roy Scheider from "The French Connection." Directed by Jacques Deray, known for the two "Borsalino" films and "Flic Story." The screenplay is by Jean-Claude Carrière, who worked on numerous masterpieces such as "The Unbearable Lightness of Being" and "The Discreet Charm of the Bourgeoisie." After more than half a century since its production in 1972, it receives its first Japanese release in 2026 in a 4K remastered version.
title_norm:un simple accident: A suspense thriller by Iranian master Jafar Panahi, winner of the Palme d'Or at the 78th Cannes Film Festival in 2025. It thrillingly and humorously depicts people wrongfully imprisoned seeking revenge. Vahid, once unjustly imprisoned, accidentally encounters a man he believes was his torturer guard. He forcibly restrains the man and digs a hole in the wilderness to bury him, but the man's ID card shows a different name. The man claims it's a case of mistaken identity. Blindfolded during imprisonment, Vahid never saw his torturer's face. Unsure if this is the right man, Vahid pauses revenge and visits a friend who was also tortured by the same guard. Panahi, banned from filmmaking by the Iranian government for opposition activities, drew inspiration from his own two imprisonments and the real voices of cellmates. Having won the Golden Lion at Venice for 'The Circle' and 'No Bears', and the Golden Bear at Berlin for 'Taxi', Panahi achieved the feat of winning top prizes at all three major festivals with this film. A French co-production, it was France's entry for Best International Feature Film at the 98th Academy Awards and received a nomination.
title_norm:unchained: Directed by Keisuke Yoshida of "Himeanole" and "Missing," this drama portrays boys who cannot understand pain or common sense, and the adults who continue to confront them head-on. Yoshida wrote the original script based on the juvenile delinquents he encountered during his own sensitive adolescence and the community surrounding them. Nishiken Go, a former half-gray area gangster and ex-convict, runs a full-time residential rehabilitation facility called "Mirai no Sato" in a coastal provincial town. Drawing on his own experiences, Nishiken tackles troubled children with all his might, but his rehabilitation methods, which do not shy away from corporal punishment, are criticized by educators. One day, a middle school teacher named Fuyuko consults him about an uncontrollable student, Kaito, and Yu, who has just been released from a juvenile detention center. Meeting the two, Nishiken instantly sees through Kaito's madness. Kaito's mother, exhausted by his severe domestic violence, decides to entrust her son to "Mirai no Sato." However, Kaito causes trouble with the other residents, escapes, and is arrested for assault. Wataru Ichinose of the Netflix drama "Sanctuary" stars as Nishiken, while the newcomer Hayato Uesaka is cast as the delinquent boy Kaito. Kaho plays middle school teacher Fuyuko, Atsushi Shinohara and Fusako Urabe play Kaito's parents, Iori Wada plays Kaito's delinquent friend Yu, and Nanami Yamazaki and Mansaku Takada play the facility's residents.
title_norm:uncle boonmee who can recall: A fantasy drama by Thai director Apichatpong Weerasethakul, internationally acclaimed for "Tropical Malady," which brought Thailand its first Palme d'Or at the Cannes Film Festival. Boonmee, who is nearing the end of his life in the mountains of Thailand, invites his wife's younger sister Jen to his farm. There, the ghost of Boonmee's wife, who passed away nineteen years earlier, appears, and his missing son also shows up in a transformed state. Eventually, Boonmee ventures with them into the deep forest.
title_norm:under the volcano: A drama by master filmmaker John Huston, known for 'The Treasure of the Sierra Madre' and 'The African Queen,' adapting the novel 'Under the Volcano' by British author Malcolm Lowry. Set in Mexico in the 1930s, it portrays love, loss, and loneliness through a single day in the life of a former British consul succumbing to alcoholism. On the 'Day of the Dead' in 1938, Geoffrey Firmin, a former British consul living in the small Mexican town of Cuernavaca, is in the throes of severe alcoholism, surrendering himself to drink and living a dissolute life. His wife Yvonne, who left him a year earlier but hopes for a reconciliation, suddenly returns. Adding to this, his half-brother Hugh also appears, and the three go out to see the festival and a bullfight... The film masterfully depicts humanity's self-destructive fate within the confines of a single day. Albert Finney, who played the protagonist Geoffrey, received high praise, including a nomination for the Academy Award for Best Actor at the 57th ceremony. The cast also includes Jacqueline Bisset and Anthony Andrews.
title_norm:une belle course: A human drama about a taxi driver who, while driving an elderly lady preparing for the end of her life, gets swept up in a journey across Paris exploring her past. Charles, a grumpy taxi driver on the verge of losing his license with no money or days off, is in the biggest crisis of his life. Then he agrees to drive 92-year-old Madeleine to the opposite side of Paris. Madeleine, who is preparing for her final affairs, asks Charles to make one detour after another. The streets of Paris where she lived her life hold many secrets, and with each detour, Madeleine's surprising past is revealed. This drive gradually transforms both their lives. Dany Boon plays Charles, and French chanson legend Line Renaud plays Madeleine. The film is directed and written by Christian Carion.
title_norm:une femme est une femme: This is Jean-Luc Godard's third feature film, following "Breathless," and a romantic comedy created based on the idea of a "musical comedy in which the characters do not sing." Angela, a cabaret dancer, tells her live-in lover Émile that she wants a child right now. Émile cannot hide his bewilderment at her request. Then a young man named Alfred, who has feelings for Angela, appears... Following Godard's previous film "Le Petit Soldat," Anna Karina plays the heroine, with Jean-Paul Belmondo of "Breathless" as Alfred and Jean-Claude Brialy of "Les Cousins" as Émile. The music is by Michel Legrand, the renowned composer of "The Umbrellas of Cherbourg" and other films.
title_norm:une femme fidèle: An erotic film directed by Roger Vadim, based on the sensual novel 'Les Liaisons Dangereuses'. Set in 19th-century France, it depicts the affair between a playboy count and a married woman. The bewitching performances of two charismatic actresses are captivating.
title_norm:une part manquante: A drama directed by Guillaume Senez, who also teamed up with Romain Duris in 'Our Struggles,' with Duris starring. Set primarily in Japan, it depicts the changing forms of modern families under the universal themes of parent-child bonds and love, against the backdrop of the differences between Japanese and French social systems. Jay, a Frenchman working as a chef in Tokyo, marries a Japanese woman but divorces her. Due to differences in the joint custody systems of Japan and France, he is separated from his beloved daughter Lily. Unable to give up hope, he becomes a taxi driver, wandering the city while searching for traces of his daughter. Nine years later, just as Jay decides to return to France, his daughter Lily, now a grown girl, coincidentally gets into his taxi. Without Lily knowing the driver is her real father, and Jay unable to reveal himself, they spend a brief moment together. The cast includes Judith Chemla, known for 'A Woman's Life' and 'Our Arias for Mother,' Tsu Yu from 'TAXi (2),' Yumi Narita from 'Don't Stop the Camera!' and 'Mari's Story,' as well as Shinnosuke Abe, Toshihiro Yashiba, Moro Agata, and Haruko Uchida.
title_norm:une part manquante また君に会えるまで: A drama directed by Guillaume Senez, who also teamed up with Romain Duris in 'Our Struggles,' with Duris starring. title_norm:until the end of the world: A film that Wim Wenders nurtured for about 13 years before completing. Blending sci-fi elements, it combines a road movie and love story set in a world facing apocalypse. In the winter of 1999, the predicted crash of a nuclear satellite casts the world into anxiety. Claire, traveling by car from Venice, meets Trevor, who is being chased by someone. Though they part ways, she can't stop thinking about him and, with the help of her ex-lover (a writer) and a private detective, follows him to Lisbon, Moscow, and Beijing. Reuniting with Trevor in Tokyo, Claire learns the purpose of his journey.
title_norm:useful ghost: In Bangkok, Thailand, where dust pollution is severe, March (Wisarut Himmarat) spends his days in grief after losing his beloved wife Nat (Davika Hoorne) to a respiratory disease. One day, Nat's soul returns, inhabiting a vacuum cleaner, and the two reaffirm their love. Meanwhile, at the factory run by March's family, the spirit of a deceased employee possesses the machinery, bringing operations to a halt. Rejected by family troubled by the spirit and by society, Nat tries to prove her true love for her husband and her own existence as a 'useful ghost' by helping with the factory's exorcism...
title_norm:uzumaki: "Hey, want to run away with me?" Kirie Goshima is bewildered by the sudden confession from her childhood boyfriend, Shuichi Saito. Lately, Shuichi has been acting listless, as if terrified of something, and Kirie has been worried about him. Eventually, triggered by the incident of a student at Kirie's high school jumping to death from a spiral staircase, Shuichi utters something horrifying. He claims that their town, Kurozu-cho, is possessed by an unknown force of "spirals." Afterward, when Shuichi's father, Toshio, dies a mysterious death, ominous and bizarre spiral phenomena begin to occur one after another around the two of them.
title_norm:vacuum zone: After serving two years in the army prison for stealing an officer's wallet, Kitani returns to his unit. Inside the unit, the squad leader and senior soldiers bully the new recruits. In particular, Private First Class Aita, a university graduate, is subjected to daily violence. Kitani, however, refuses to take part in the bullying. Aita grows fond of Kitani and they become close, but he learns that Kitani has been selected for frontline deployment. Both Kitani's imprisonment and his selection for the front lines were the result of factional infighting.
title_norm:vagabond: A film by renowned French filmmaker Agnès Varda, tracing the steps of a young girl who freezes to death after wandering, which won the Golden Lion, the top prize, at the 42nd Venice International Film Festival in 1985. In winter in southern France, the body of an 18-year-old girl, Mona, is found frozen to death in a roadside ditch in the countryside. The film traces Mona's journey over the final weeks of her life as she hitchhikes aimlessly and continues a solitary journey, through the testimonies of the people she met on the road. Starring Sandrine Bonnaire (from "The Hairdresser's Husband"), with co-stars Macha Méril (from "Belle de Jour"), Stéphane Freiss (from "The Five Senses"), and Yolande Moreau (from "Séraphine"). It recorded over one million admissions in France at the time, becoming Varda's biggest hit.
title_norm:varda by agnès: The final work of the late French master Agnès Varda, who passed away in March 2019. From her debut feature film 'La Pointe Courte' (1955) to her award-winning previous work 'Faces Places', this comprehensive self-portrait sees Varda passionately and humorously recounting her creative career spanning over half a century, looking back with precious footage. It unravels the secrets of her creativity, which was sustained by an insatiable curiosity and passion that kept her active throughout her life.
title_norm:varda par agnès: The final work of the late French master Agnès Varda, who passed away in March 2019. From her debut feature film 'La Pointe Courte' (1955) to her award-winning previous work 'Faces Places', this comprehensive self-portrait sees Varda passionately and humorously recounting her creative career spanning over half a century, looking back with precious footage. It unravels the secrets of her creativity, which was sustained by an insatiable curiosity and passion that kept her active throughout her life.
title_norm:verdens verste menneske: An unconventional love drama directed by Danish filmmaker Joachim Trier, known for "The Worst Person in the World" and "Thelma," which won the Best Actress award at the 74th Cannes Film Festival in 2021 and was nominated for two Academy Awards at the 94th ceremony in 2022—Best International Feature Film and Best Original Screenplay. Julie is approaching the milestone age of 30. Having already squandered several talents, she still hasn't found direction in life. Her older boyfriend Aksel, a successful graphic novelist, has been increasingly eager to settle down. One night, Julie crashes a party she wasn't invited to and meets the young and charming Eivind. Soon after, she leaves Aksel and throws herself into a new romance, hoping to find a new outlook on life—but... Renate Reinsve, who appeared in Trier's "Oslo, August 31st" and other works, plays Julie and won the Best Actress award at the Cannes Film Festival.
title_norm:vertigo: January 2020, just before the coronavirus envelops New York. Poet Gozo Yoshimasu traces the traces of his ally Jonas Mekas (1922–2019), the father of avant-garde cinema, in Manhattan and Brooklyn on the first anniversary of his death, a friendship that had continued since 1985. Wartime study notes left in the studio, a 1945 passport, personal effects arranged by his son Sebastian. In a corner of the bedroom, Yoshimasu becomes dizzy and collapses. Early in the morning of January 23rd, the anniversary of his death, a memorial poem is completed in an instant. Crossing the bridge to the office. Yoshimasu reads it aloud to the waiting Sebastian. Then, a long silence falls.
title_norm:vie privée: Oscar-winning actress Jodie Foster, known for 'The Accused' and 'The Silence of the Lambs', stars in her first French-language film in this mystery. Lilian, a successful American psychoanalyst practicing in Paris, receives news that Paula, a long-time patient, has died. Suspicious of Paula's death, Lilian suspects murder but cannot involve the police due to patient confidentiality. She decides to uncover the truth herself. Meanwhile, since learning of Paula's death, Lilian has been troubled by uncontrollable crying, regardless of the situation, and visits her ex-husband Gabriel, an ophthalmologist. Though the cause of her tears remains unclear, Gabriel agrees to help Lilian investigate Paula's case. As she embarks on a detective-like investigation, Lilian delves into dangerous truths. Foster plays the protagonist, psychoanalyst Lilian, entirely in French. Daniel Auteuil, known for 'La Belle Époque', plays her ex-husband and investigative partner Gabriel. Virginie Efira from 'Suddenly Sick' and Mathieu Amalric from 'Quantum of Solace' co-star. The film is directed by Rebecca Zlotowski, known for 'Grand Central' and 'Planetarium'.
title_norm:vikram: A crime action film produced by and starring Indian national star Kamal Haasan, alongside Vijay Sethupathi from "Jawan" and Fahadh Faasil from "Pushpa: The Rise." It depicts a three-way battle between a drug cartel boss, an unemployed middle-aged man, and a special agent through intense action sequences. Three consecutive terrorist attacks by masked groups occur in Chennai. Special agent Amar suspects Sandhanam, the drug lord who controls the city's gangs, is involved. Meanwhile, Sandhanam is searching for two tons of missing cocaine base that vanished from his territory. As the investigation progresses, Amar becomes strangely preoccupied with Karnan, an unemployed man who was the second victim. Karnan had a police officer son-in-law, who was also killed by the same terrorists. Directed and written by Lokesh Kanagaraj, known for "Master" and "Kaithi," with action choreography by the twin stuntmen Anbariv (Anbumani & Arivumani) active in the Indian film industry.
title_norm:vikram vedha: A crime suspense film starring Hrithik Roshan of "Bang Bang!" and Saif Ali Khan of "Go Goa Gone," adapted as a Hindi remake of a 2017 Tamil-language film. Vikram, an excellent police commissioner who aims to eradicate crime itself rather than boost his record through arrests, sees his convictions shaken when the criminal he was targeting, Veda, surrenders himself, bringing forth a series of mysteries. Eventually, Vikram and Veda, each with their own purposes, are forced to fight together. Hrithik Roshan plays Veda, and Saif Ali Khan plays Vikram.
title_norm:virus: In 1982, the deadly virus MM-88 is stolen from a research institute in East Germany. However, the plane carrying the spy who stole it crashes in the Alps, and the virus spreads across the Earth, wiping out humanity except for a small group of survivors in Antarctica. One of these survivors, earthquake researcher Yoshizumi, realizes an even greater danger is approaching: a massive earthquake could strike the eastern United States, potentially triggering the launch of nuclear missiles.
title_norm:vivre sa vie: This is Jean-Luc Godard's fourth feature film, following "A Woman Is a Woman," and was shot starring Anna Karina, his partner both publicly and privately. Nana, who decides to part ways with her husband after discussing life with him at a café in Paris, falls into a life where she cannot even pay her rent. She begins to proposition men on the street and engage in prostitution. Eventually, Nana becomes numb to having relations with strangers. The music was handled by Michel Legrand, the renowned composer of "The Umbrellas of Cherbourg" and other films.
title_norm:vivre sa vie film en douze ta: This is Jean-Luc Godard's fourth feature film, following "A Woman Is a Woman," and was shot starring Anna Karina, his partner both publicly and privately. title_norm:voice of rain that comes at n: The first feature film directed by Kohei Igarashi, a filmmaker gaining international attention for works like "Oyogisugita Yoru" and "Ikoi no Iki," made while he was a student at Tokyo Zokei University. Young couple Amano and Inaba live together, but life is tough because Inaba has lost his job. Still, Inaba doesn't work, and at night he goes out, meeting friends who treat him, or learning poetry from a cigarette seller. Amano says nothing to Inaba about this, simply watching over him. Then one day, Inaba hears from a friend about "a good job at the hospital"... The film received its theatrical premiere at the "Kohei Igarashi Director Retrospective: Seishun-teki Koto" (from September 20, 2024, at Shimokita-Ekimae-Cinema K2), held in conjunction with the release of Igarashi's feature "SUPER HAPPY FOREVER."
title_norm:voices from the waves kesennu: The second part of the Tohoku documentary trilogy co-directed by Ryusuke Hamaguchi and Ko Sakai, 'Voices from the Waves,' set in Kesennuma. Continuing to film for over a year after completing the previous work 'Tales from the Waves,' which gathered 'dialogues' of people living along the Sanriku coast affected by the tsunami on March 11, 2011, this film records dialogues among 11 people in 7 groups living in Kesennuma City, Miyagi Prefecture. About a year after the disaster, it depicts survivors recalling their memories of the earthquake through conversations with family, friends, and colleagues, and renewing their feelings.
title_norm:voices from the waves shinchi: The second part of the Tohoku documentary trilogy co-directed by Ryusuke Hamaguchi and Ko Sakai, 'Voices from the Waves,' set in Shinchi Town. Following the previous work 'Tales from the Waves,' which captured the 'dialogues' of people affected by the tsunami on March 11, 2011, this film records survivors about a year after the disaster as they talk with family, friends, and colleagues about what happened and how they have been since. While the previous film conducted interviews across a wide area from Iwate to Fukushima Prefectures, this installment focuses specifically on Shinchi Town in Soma District, Fukushima Prefecture, recording dialogues among 10 people in 6 groups.
title_norm:walk slow: A documentary following Namiko Kawamura, an 84-year-old expressive artist who continues to work as a dancer and performer. Directed by Toshiko Rin, known for documentary works such as "Jibun, Maru! Ippo no Hanashi," "Nishi Tenka Chaya Ooishi So," and "Blessed." Kawamura has been familiar with dance since childhood, and from the 1970s onward, she explored a unique form of expression incorporating perception and walking in nature. After participating in a workshop by American dancer Anna Halprin in the 1980s, she established a performance of "slow walking"—a forward-moving gait. This act, both a dance and a way of life, has continued for many years. Set in Okinawa, a place Kawamura had long wished to visit, the film explores the thoughts and memories behind her expression through beach performances and interviews. It records her walking and dancing while confronting the time embedded in a land marked by war memories, observing the journey of a woman who has dedicated her life to dance.
title_norm:walk up: A human drama by Korean master Hong Sang-soo, depicting the interactions of artists in a four-story city apartment building in monochrome imagery. Film director Byeong-su visits the apartment owned by his old friend Heo-ok, an active interior designer, together with his daughter Jeong-su, who aims for a career in interior design. The apartment building has a restaurant on the first floor, a cooking class on the second, rental housing on the third, an atelier for artists on the fourth, and Heo-ok's workspace in the basement. The three chat amiably over wine. Byeong-su leaves briefly for a work call, but when he returns, Jeong-su is nowhere to be found... The story unfolds in four chapters as they ascend each floor of the apartment, and the relationships between Byeong-su and the four women around him develop in unpredictable directions. Kwon Hae-hyo, from "The Day After" and "On the Beach at Night Alone," plays film director Byeong-su. Lee Hye-young from "In Front of Your Face," along with Hong Sang-soo regulars Song Seon-mi and Cho Yun-hee, co-star.
title_norm:wall engravings: The second feature film by Guy Gilles, a director re-evaluated since the 2000s as a 'forgotten master of the French New Wave,' depicting a woman living with the memory of her lover who chose death. The present is shown in black-and-white, and fragments of recollection in color, delicately and melancholically portraying the memory of love and the pain of absence. Jeanne lives with the memory of her deceased lover Jean. Jean rejected social order and the bourgeois world, found no place in the Beat generation, and chose death. Unaware of his death, Jeanne feels him always by her side, existing like a ghost. Masha Meril, known for 'A Time for Loving' and 'Belle de Jour,' plays the protagonist Jeanne, and Patrick Jouané, an actor who met Guy Gilles during the filming of 'Le Rempart des Béguines' and became an irreplaceable presence in his life and work, plays the deceased lover Jean. The film was released in Japanese theaters in April 2026.
title_norm:want to be a shellfish: A small-town barber who has returned from the war unexpectedly finds himself put on trial as a war criminal. This film version, directed by screenwriter Hashimoto himself, is based on a television drama that won an Art Festival Award. A legendary work that portrays the absurdity and cruelty of war, with Frankie's heartfelt performance that shakes the soul.
title_norm:war 2: The second installment in the series following the 2019 Indian spy action blockbuster "War," this is part of the YRF Spy Universe, which shares a world with the "Pathaan" and "Tiger" series. It depicts the fateful battle between two men on a grand, global scale. Kabir, a legendary spy who once betrayed the nation and disappeared, has now transformed into India's greatest threat. To stop the unstoppable Kabir, the government deploys Vikram, an elite Indian army officer. Having lost everything due to a certain incident, Vikram is driven by the sole mission of eliminating Kabir. However, the battle soon turns from a mission into a personal vendetta against Kabir. Hrithik Roshan reprises his role as the legendary agent Kabir from "War," and N.T. Rama Rao Jr. from "RRR" makes his debut in the YRF Spy Universe as the soldier Vikram, who engages in a fierce battle with him. The film is directed by Ayan Mukerji, known for "Brahmastra."
title_norm:war バトル・オブ・フェイト: The second installment in the series following the 2019 Indian spy action blockbuster "War," this is part of the YRF Spy Universe, which shares a world with the "Pathaan" and "Tiger" series. It depicts the fateful battle between two men on a grand, global scale. Kabir, a legendary spy who once betrayed the nation and disappeared, has now transformed into India's greatest threat. To stop the unstoppable Kabir, the government deploys Vikram, an elite Indian army officer. Having lost everything due to a certain incident, Vikram is driven by the sole mission of eliminating Kabir. However, the battle soon turns from a mission into a personal vendetta against Kabir. Hrithik Roshan reprises his role as the legendary agent Kabir from "War," and N.T. Rama Rao Jr. from "RRR" makes his debut in the YRF Spy Universe as the soldier Vikram, who engages in a fierce battle with him. The film is directed by Ayan Mukerji, known for "Brahmastra."
title_norm:warrior of the wind: A samurai yet not a samurai! A shogunate spy who sniffs out darkness and delivers death—he is the Wind Samurai. This suspenseful ninja romance by Ryotaro Shiba weaves together the strange fate and love of Shinzo and Miki, caught in a conspiracy surrounding the phantom land of "Arai" in the Kumano mountains. Sleeping gold, a princess's love, and approaching evil swords! Director Takashi Kato, with ace star Hashizo Okawa, crafts a thrilling ninja suspense epic, connecting Edo and the wilderness with swords and romance.
title_norm:was a stranger: An ensemble drama inspired by the reality that 14 million people were forced to flee abroad to escape the long devastation of the Syrian civil war, depicting families torn apart by conflict and those around them from multiple perspectives. Set across four countries—Syria, Turkey, Greece, and the United States—the story unfolds in five chapters, intersecting the lives of five families. As the civil war between government forces and rebel groups intensifies in Syria's dictatorship, Syrian doctor Amira decides to cross dangerous borders with her daughter to reach safety. Syrian border guard Mustafa distrusts the brutal government forces and struggles between being a soldier who follows orders and a human with a conscience. Turkish smuggler Marwan seeks to earn money by loading refugees onto boats bound for Greece to move his sick son to America. Poet Fathi boards that boat with his wife and child, facing mortal danger. Greek coast guard Stavros discovers refugees navigating stormy seas and strives to save lives. Film producer and humanitarian activist Brandt Andersen, who made the 2020 short film "Refugee" as his starting point, makes his feature directorial, screenwriting, and producing debut with this meticulously researched work. Yasmin Al-Masri reprises her role as doctor Amira from the short, and Omar Sy returns as smuggler Marwan.
title_norm:waterboys: The Tadayono High School swim team is on the verge of disbandment, with only one member left: third-year student Suzuki. Suddenly, a young and beautiful female teacher named Sakuma arrives. When the boys learn of this, they rush to join the team, but Sakuma announces they will be doing 'synchronized swimming.' At that, the boys quickly flee. The only ones who can't escape are five misfits, including Suzuki. Reluctantly, they begin practicing synchronized swimming.
title_norm:we are perfume world tour 3rd: The first documentary film about the techno-pop unit 'Perfume', popular both in Japan and abroad. Formed in Hiroshima in 2000 as a trio of A~chan (Ayaka Nishiwaki), Kashiyuka (Yuka Kashino), and Nocchi (Ayano Omoto), Perfume has gained international popularity through their novel music, refined dance, and live performances utilizing cutting-edge technology. The film centers on footage shot over approximately two months of their overseas activities, including the 'Perfume WORLD TOUR 3rd' held during their anniversary year—marking 15 years since formation and 10 years since major debut—and their stage performance at 'SXSW 2015', a festival of music, film, and interactivity in Texas, USA. It also includes scenes of their hours-long post-performance critique sessions, the members' down-to-earth moments enjoying brief leisure time, and exclusive interviews.
title_norm:we live in time この時を生きて: Director John Crowley (*Brooklyn*) crafts a poignant love story that interweaves the timelines of a couple cherishing the irreplaceable moments of their limited time together. Almut, a rising star chef, and Tobias, a recent divorcee in the depths of despair, fall in love after a fateful encounter. Despite their differing personalities—the free-spirited Almut and the cautious Tobias—they navigate life’s hurdles, eventually building a home and deepening their bond as they welcome a daughter. However, when Almut learns her time is running out, she shares a surprising resolution with Tobias. Florence Pugh (*Midsommar*) and Andrew Garfield (*The Amazing Spider-Man* series) star as Almut and Tobias. The film features a screenplay by Nick Payne (*The Sense of an Ending*) and is executive produced by Benedict Cumberbatch.
title_norm:we shall overcome someday: Set in 1960s Kyoto, this is a youth ensemble drama depicting the love and friendship between Japanese and Zainichi Korean high school students. Based on Takeshi Matsuyama's autobiographical novel "Shonen M no Imujin-gawa," it was directed and written by Kazuyuki Izutsu, known for "Kishiwada Shonen Gurentai" and "Get Up!" In 1968, Kyoto. Kosuke Matsuyama, a second-year student at Furitsu Higashi High School, is ordered by his homeroom teacher to go to a Korean high school, where student conflicts are frequent, to propose a practice soccer match. Reluctantly visiting the Korean school with his friend Norio, Kosuke falls in love at first sight with Kyongja, who is playing the flute in the music room. However, she is the sister of Anson, the boss of the Korean high school. Desperate to get closer to Kyongja, Kosuke diligently studies Korean and buys a guitar at a music store to learn the song "Imujin-gawa" that she was playing... Shioya Shun plays Kosuke, Sawajiri Erika plays Kyongja, and Takaoka Sosuke plays Anson.
title_norm:we who dwell in the mountains: A documentary by the renowned Swiss master Fredi M. Murer, known for 'Höhenfeuer' (Alpine Fire), capturing the mountainous region of his native Canton of Uri. Exploring the lives and spiritual world of mountain people in a changing alpine landscape, the film contains many elements that would later connect to 'Höhenfeuer,' such as folkloric themes and the insularity of communities. It won the International Critics' Prize at the 1974 Locarno International Film Festival. This film, along with 'Höhenfeuer' and 'Green Mountain,' forms the 'Mountain Trilogy.'
title_norm:weathering with you: Director Makoto Shinkai, whose "Your Name." was a historic blockbuster, presents a feature animation depicting a boy and girl in an era of disrupted weather harmony, struggling against fate while choosing their own way of life. Hodaka, a high school student who runs away from a remote island to Tokyo, quickly falls into poverty. After lonely days, he finally lands a job writing for a shady occult magazine. As if foreshadowing his future, rain falls day after day. One day, Hodaka meets a girl named Hina in a corner of the city. Living alone with her younger brother due to circumstances, she possesses a mysterious ability to clear the sky by "praying"... Kotaro Daigo, who appeared in "My Brother Loves Me Too Much," and Nana Mori, with upcoming roles in "Hell Girl" and "Last Letter," voice Hodaka and Hina respectively. Other cast members include Shun Oguri, Tsubasa Honda, Junpei Heisawa, Yuuki Kaji, and Chieko Baisho. Following "Your Name.," Genki Kawamura serves as planner and producer, Masayoshi Tanaka as character designer, and rock band RADWIMPS provides the music. Actress Toko Miura participates as female vocals on the RADWIMPS theme song.
title_norm:weeds on fire: In 1984, Hong Kong before the handover to China. In the suburban new town of Sha Tin, the first youth baseball team in Hong Kong, the 'Sha Yan' team, is formed. In Hong Kong, where baseball is not a major sport, a group of underachieving boys with no baseball experience begin practicing with balls made of rolled-up newspapers, but in their first game, they suffer a crushing defeat against a Taiwanese elementary school team. Nevertheless, guided by their strict yet caring principal Law (played by Liu Kai-chi), the team members gradually grow, centered on the childhood friends—the introverted Lung (played by Lam Yiu-sing) and the impulsive but loyal Wai (played by Tony Wu). The final showdown against their arch-rivals, the Japan Buffaloes, becomes a stage for them to re-examine their 'past' and 'future'—a youth drama based on a true story, set in early 1980s Hong Kong, leaving a quiet resonance that is not reduced to the outcome of the sport.
title_norm:what does that nature say to: Korean master Hong Sang-soo, a multiple award-winner at the Berlin and Cannes film festivals, humorously and realistically depicts the irreparable failures caused by alcohol in this home drama centered on a young poet who ends up spending a day with his girlfriend's family. When poet Dong-ha escorts his girlfriend Juni home, he runs into her father at the front door and unexpectedly spends the day with her family. Initially awkward, Dong-ha gradually grows closer to Juni's family as they show him around their home and neighborhood and engage in conversation. Eventually, at dinner with the family, he drinks as urged, becomes intoxicated, and an uncomfortable atmosphere settles over the table. Ha Seong-guk, who previously played poets in Hong Sang-soo's "The Woman Who Ran" and "In Front of Your Face," takes on the role of Dong-ha, marking his first lead role in a Hong Sang-soo film. The parents welcoming their daughter's boyfriend are played by Hong Sang-soo regulars and real-life couple Kwon Hae-hyo and Cho Yun-hee. Kang So-yi ("In Front of Your Face," "By the Stream") plays Juni, and Park Mi-so ("Introduction") plays Juni's older sister. The film was selected for the competition section of the 75th Berlin International Film Festival in 2025. It will be released in theaters in 2026 as the fifth installment of "Monthly Hong Sang-soo," a project screening new works for five consecutive months to commemorate the director's 30th debut anniversary.
title_norm:what should we have done: Documentary filmmaker Tomoaki Fujino records over 20 years the story of his older sister, who began showing symptoms of schizophrenia, and his parents, who kept her from seeing a psychiatrist. His sister, eight years older, was caring and excellent. Influenced by their parents, she entered medical school to become a doctor. One day, she suddenly started screaming things that weren't true. Schizophrenia was suspected, but her parents—a doctor and a researcher—refused to acknowledge the illness and kept her away from psychiatric care. Doubting their judgment, Fujino tried to persuade them but failed, and left home with a lingering sense of unease. Eighteen years after his sister's onset, Fujino, having studied filmmaking, began recording his family's life whenever he visited home. He filmed family outings and dinner scenes, engaged his parents in conversation, and kept talking to his sister, but her condition worsened. Eventually, his parents installed a chain and padlock on the front door to confine her inside.
title_norm:wheel of fortune and fantasy: Trivial love talk between best friends, a student seeking guidance from a professor, female friends reuniting after 20 years... A first 'short story collection' woven from three tales themed around 'coincidence.' With a small production system ensuring ample rehearsal and shooting time, it carefully captures the actors' light yet delicate expressions. Won the Silver Bear Grand Jury Prize at the 71st Berlin International Film Festival.
title_norm:where is the friends house: An Iranian film that vividly captures a boy's journey to find his friend's house to return a precious notebook he accidentally took home, bringing director Abbas Kiarostami international fame. At a primary school in the village of Koker in northern Iran, Mohammad is severely scolded by his teacher for doing his homework on a piece of paper instead of a notebook and is told he will be expelled if it happens again. However, his best friend Ahmad, who sits next to him, accidentally takes Mohammad's notebook home. Panicked that Mohammad will be expelled without his notebook, Ahmad searches for his friend's house in a distant neighboring village to return it, but struggles to find it... A digital remastered version was screened as part of the special program "And Kiarostami Continues" (from October 16, 2021, at Eurospace in Tokyo and other venues).
title_norm:whisper／小さな祈り: A short film completed after a seven-year production period following director Takashi Miwa's previous work 'a whisper' released in 2017. Miwa, a filmmaker who is also an actor and taught himself stop-motion animation, infuses this work with his own despair and hope for the world, depicting those who continue to pray in a world where things are breaking and being lost, through uniquely original visuals. The film has won numerous awards at film festivals around the world, including Best Inspiration at the WSXA Amsterdam International Film Festival 2025 in the Netherlands and Best Animation in the Short Film category at the Austin International Art Festival 2024 in the USA.
title_norm:why wait, just die: A live-action film adaptation of novelist Kyogoku Natsuhiko's unique mystery novel of the same name set in modern times, starring Nao. A woman named Asami Kashima is murdered. With no clue as to the culprit's identity or motive, a mysterious woman named Eiko Watarai visits those who knew Asami in life, claiming she wants to ask about her. As she follows various testimonies, the outline of Asami's character and her relationship with Eiko gradually emerge. Nao plays Eiko, who goes around asking about Asami. Aoi Ito plays Asami, whose impression changes depending on who is asked; Ko Maehara plays Asami's boss and lover, Hiroyuki Yamazaki; Hikaru Takahashi plays Asami's senior, Kaori Shinomiya; Takuya Kusakawa (from the group Shinkansen) plays Asami's boyfriend, Yuya Sakuma; Tomoko Tabata plays Asami's mother, Naoko Kashima; and Tetsu Hirahara plays the lawyer involved in Asami's case, Riku Gojo. Directed by Junichi Kanai, who previously worked with Nao on "My Daddy," with a screenplay by Kohei Kiyasu (known for "The Kirishima Thing"). The rock band "This is LAST" performs the theme song.
title_norm:wicked for good: Having learned the truth hidden in the land of Oz and walked their separate paths, two witches once again face their irreplaceable former friend. The second part of the timeless musical.
title_norm:winchester 73: The Winchester rifle, a legendary gun said to be one in tens of thousands. A drama of joys and sorrows unfolds around the people who come into possession of this rifle one after another, with all episodes converging into a single finale. A masterfully structured classic Western.
title_norm:wind, woman and road: Ginji, driven from his hometown, returns after ten years... This is a representative work marking the starting point of Tai Kato's unique style, with actors wearing no makeup, low-angle cameras, and simultaneous sound recording.
title_norm:window of memories: A "listening-and-writing film" that makes you remember someone and want to talk about them—the eagerly awaited latest work from director Yui Kiyohara, whose "Our House" and "Remembering Every Night" were acclaimed both in Japan and abroad. Selected for the International Competition at the Yamagata International Documentary Film Festival 2025.
title_norm:wings of desire: A masterpiece fantasy film directed by Wim Wenders ('Paris, Texas'), who took the helm in his home country of Germany for the first time in a decade, winning the Best Director award at the 40th Cannes Film Festival in 1987. Set in Berlin before the fall of the Wall, it poetically and beautifully depicts the fate of an angel who falls in love with a human. Damiel, an angel who listens to the inner voices of humans and comforts their sorrows, meets Marion, a trapeze artist performing in a circus. Strongly drawn to her loneliness, Damiel decides to descend from the heavenly realm to the human world. Bruno Ganz stars, and Peter Falk ('Columbo') appears as himself. The screenplay was contributed by Peter Handke, who would later win the Nobel Prize in Literature. A sequel, 'Faraway, So Close!,' was produced in 1993.
title_norm:wir bergler in den bergen sin: A documentary by the renowned Swiss master Fredi M. Murer, known for 'Höhenfeuer' (Alpine Fire), capturing the mountainous region of his native Canton of Uri. Exploring the lives and spiritual world of mountain people in a changing alpine landscape, the film contains many elements that would later connect to 'Höhenfeuer,' such as folkloric themes and the insularity of communities. It won the International Critics' Prize at the 1974 Locarno International Film Festival. This film, along with 'Höhenfeuer' and 'Green Mountain,' forms the 'Mountain Trilogy.'
title_norm:wise blood: A feature film directed in 1979 by John Huston, the master of American cinema who left behind numerous classics such as 'The Maltese Falcon,' 'The Treasure of the Sierra Madre,' and 'The African Queen.' An unconventional drama that adapts the novel 'Wise Blood' by Flannery O'Connor, a leading figure of Southern literature, vividly portraying the unique atmosphere and spirituality of the American South. When young Hazel Motes is discharged from the U.S. Army and returns home, he finds only a wardrobe and a tombstone left in his family home. In a strange city, he begins preaching the 'Church Without Christ' and encounters a motley cast of characters, including a blind preacher, his daughter, and a simple young man. Eventually, Hazel becomes consumed by madness and despair... Brad Dourif, nominated for an Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor for 'One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest,' plays Hazel. The cast also includes Amy Wright, Harry Dean Stanton, and Ned Beatty. Although it was never theatrically released in Japan, it will have its Japanese theatrical premiere in 2026 as part of the special screening series 'John Huston 120th Anniversary' commemorating the 120th anniversary of his birth.
title_norm:wish: Director Hirokazu Kore-eda of "Nobody Knows" and "Air Doll" depicts a family drama set in Kyushu, which is buzzing with excitement over the full opening of the Kyushu Shinkansen line in March 2010. Starring the comedy brother duo Maeda Maeda's Koki Maeda and Koshiro Maeda. The story follows two brothers, separated by their parents' divorce to live in Kagoshima and Fukuoka respectively, who strive to reunite their broken family, spurred on by the full opening of the bullet train line. Co-stars include regulars from Kore-eda's films such as Yui Natsukawa, Atsushi Abe, Yoshio Harada, and Kirin Kiki.
title_norm:wojna światów następne stulec: One of four dark sci-fi works by Piotr Szulkin, a pioneer of dystopian sci-fi in Poland, who created them during the late 1970s and 1980s under the socialist regime, navigating strict censorship. The film depicts the theme of 'escape from totalitarianism' with a style of intense satire and surrealism taken to its extreme. Martians have attacked Earth. A TV host has been telling people 'there is nothing to fear,' but his apartment is ransacked and his wife is kidnapped. The nightly TV script is also changed, and the reality he sees no longer matches what he tells people every night. The film will have its theatrical premiere in Japan as part of the special screening project 'Polish Dark Sci-Fi: The Four Films of Piotr Szulkin' (starting February 21, 2026, at Theater Image Forum).
title_norm:woman called sada abe: "The outside light bothers me" "His smell is soaked into the futon too..." Sadame closes the storm shutters to keep Kichizō's scent from escaping. How long has it been since the two of them were alone in the small room of the teahouse? Their union seeks ever more unknown pleasures. Sadame, choking Kichizō, says happily, "Kichi-san is twitching inside me." But when Kichizō, whose health is beginning to fail, suggests returning home for a while, Sadame's pure love for him becomes directly linked to pure desire. "I won't let anyone else touch you anymore. No one..."
title_norm:woman is a woman: This is Jean-Luc Godard's third feature film, following "Breathless," and a romantic comedy created based on the idea of a "musical comedy in which the characters do not sing." Angela, a cabaret dancer, tells her live-in lover Émile that she wants a child right now. Émile cannot hide his bewilderment at her request. Then a young man named Alfred, who has feelings for Angela, appears... Following Godard's previous film "Le Petit Soldat," Anna Karina plays the heroine, with Jean-Paul Belmondo of "Breathless" as Alfred and Jean-Claude Brialy of "Les Cousins" as Émile. The music is by Michel Legrand, the renowned composer of "The Umbrellas of Cherbourg" and other films.
title_norm:women of the night: Synopsis: A shocking work depicting the fierce struggle for survival of women who become prostitutes in the burnt-out ruins of Osaka immediately after Japan's defeat. Among the many masterpieces by Tanaka and her ally Mizoguchi, this film leaves a vivid impression with Mizoguchi's cold-hearted direction and Tanaka's passionate performance as a war widow forced into street prostitution.
title_norm:women’s testimonies pioneerin: In 1982, under the sponsorship of socialist researcher Kiyomizu Ishidō, a roundtable discussion was held with pioneering female activists who had participated in the launch of the popular labor movement from the Taishō to Shōwa eras. Those gathered were Setsu Tanno (wife of Masanosuke Watanabe), Utako Nabeyama (wife of Sadachika Nabeyama), Misao Fukuoka (wife of Kyōji Koreeda), and Mina Yamauchi (wife of Naokazu Tachibana). Although they had once worked together in the movement, decades later, after the war, some held different positions, making such a gathering rare. At the request of the host, Mr. Ishidō, who said, 'I want to record this for posterity,' director Haneda filmed the discussion. Time passed without the footage being released, but driven by the director's strong desire to 'preserve the history of these women,' additional filming was done as much as possible to compile the work. In this film, the discrimination and subjugation experienced by these female activists are told in their own words. It is a work that quietly questions what true women's liberation really is.
title_norm:writing hawa: A documentary directed by Najiba Nouri, an Afghan female journalist, who turns the camera on her mother Hawa, who was denied education as a child and forced into marriage at age 13. Hawa lives in Kabul, the capital of Afghanistan, caring for her husband, who is 30 years older and has dementia. Hawa was only 13 when she was forced into marriage; her father kept her from education, and her mother gave her no advice about childbirth. After giving birth to six children, she ensured her daughters received education so they wouldn't follow the same path. Her second daughter, Najiba, lives independently as a journalist. Determined to support her mother, Najiba points the camera at her and listens to her complaints about her husband, secret love, and 'things she wanted to do.' Hawa starts a folk craft business and learns to read and write, but just as her modest dreams begin to take shape, her granddaughter Zahra, who lives with her eldest daughter's ex-husband, flees from her domineering father. Hawa takes in her granddaughter and learns to read and write with her, but Taliban attacks and occupation advance daily, putting Zahra and the family sheltering her in mortal danger. When the Taliban regained power in August 2021, moves to suppress press freedom intensified, and Najiba entrusted the camera to her brother Ali and left her homeland. The film won the Citizens' Prize at the Yamagata International Documentary Film Festival 2025 and numerous awards at film festivals worldwide.
title_norm:ws tragedy: Shizuka Mita is a 20-year-old woman who works hard to become an actress as a trainee at the theater troupe "Sea." Moriguchi, a 26-year-old former troupe member now working at a real estate agency, first notices sincere Shizuka in a park. Shizuka prepares for the lead role audition in the troupe's next production, "The Tragedy of W," but her peer Kaori lands the part, and Shizuka is assigned a minor role with only a single line at the beginning of the story. Downcast after failing the audition, Moriguchi confides in her about his own psychological struggles as an actor. He then proposes marriage on the condition that she never becomes a star, and conversely promises to send a large bouquet to her dressing room as a farewell if she succeeds as an actress.
title_norm:wの悲劇: Shizuka Mita is a 20-year-old woman who works hard to become an actress as a trainee at the theater troupe "Sea."
