It has been nominated for the SKIP City International D-Cinema Festival 2025, the 23rd Ueda Castle Town Film Festival Independent Film Competition, and the 28th Kyoto International Student Film Festival. Lead actor Mao Yoshino passionately plays dual roles: Ichitaro Sahara and his 'ideal self' Sahara. After this film, Yoshino was cast as a main host in 'Love and Rumors Last Seventy-Five Days' (2023, directed by Ririko Shinjo). Satoru Murayama, playing Junji Setoguchi who forms a duo 'Geki Amazu Buta' with Yoshino, portrays his partner while carrying a difficult-to-share secret, and was selected as a main cast member from about 700 applicants for the 2026 film 'Hello My Friend' (2026, directed by Masahide Ichii). Nanami Kitano, playing Sahara's neighbor Suzuka Murii, expresses a delicate distance with Sahara through a transparent performance, and has appeared in many films since. Distribution is handled by GeneHeart, which operates 'GeneTheater,' a streaming service curating only high-quality Japanese short films that stir emotions.
title_norm:お終活3 幸春！人生メモリーズ: The third installment in the human comedy series that explores family dynamics and second chances through the theme of "shukatsu" (end-of-life planning), following "Oshukatsu: Jukushun! Jinsei, Hyakunen Jidai no Sugoshikata" and "Oshukatsu: Saishun! Jinsei Rhapsody." Aya, the eldest daughter of Shinichi and Chikako Ohara, finally decides to marry her fiancé Ryota. However, just before the wedding, a casual remark from Aya causes a rift in their relationship, escalating into a major commotion involving both families. Meanwhile, Shinichi's junior colleague Kato struggles to accept his mother Toyoko's progressing dementia, speaking harshly to her. Chikako gently tells Kato, "Even with dementia, the heart doesn't forget." Continuing from the previous two films, director Hideyuki Kazuki helms this installment, incorporating the latest end-of-life planning trends and knowledge while depicting family bonds with light humor and a warm perspective. The cast reunites familiar faces from the series, including Tsurube Shofukutei as Shinichi Ohara, Junko Takahata as his wife Chikako, Ayame Goriki as their daughter Aya, along with Yuki Matsushita, Masahiko Nishimura, Norika Fujiwara, Renji Ishibashi, Kumiko Fujiyoshi, LiLiCo, Kunikazu Katsumata, and Yoshihiko Hakamada. Guest stars include Keiko Mita as Toyoko, who has dementia, and Fumiyo Kohinata as her son Kato, who supports her despite his own inner conflict.
title_norm:お艶殺し:
A noir romance inspired by Junichiro Tanizaki's 1915 novel *The Murder of Otsuya*. Produced as part of the "TANIZAKI Reimagined" film project commemorating the 140th anniversary of Tanizaki’s birth, the film depicts the warping of love and obsession into violence as a man’s weakness and a woman’s presence become inextricably entwined. 

After serving time for copper wire theft, Shinsuke Abe is released from prison and begins working as a live-in employee at a surveying company. Soon, he is confronted by Santa Tokui, the childhood friend who instigated the crime, and Tsuya Yanagida, Shinsuke’s former lover. Though the theft had been Santa’s idea, Shinsuke had shouldered the full blame and served the sentence alone. While Shinsuke still harbors feelings for Tsuya, she is now involved with Santa. However, their reunion rekindles their mutual attraction, leading them to begin a secret affair behind Santa’s back. Amidst this tension, an irreversible tragedy unfolds.

The film stars Yugo Mikawa (*Cloud*, *Dish Up*), Remi Naoki (TV drama *Sayonara, Teacher*), and Jun Matsuo (*Red Bridge*, *Six Loners*). It is directed by Yoshihiro Tokijo, who previously wrote the screenplay for Toshiki Sato’s *Wandering Bonbon Candy*.
title_norm:お遊さま: A commentary: The man who is a match for the younger sister becomes drawn to the older sister who sits in on the arranged meeting... This is Mizoguchi's first film at Daiei, which produced numerous masterpieces during its golden age. Collaborating for the first time with the renowned cinematographer Miyagawa, it delicately depicts the shifting love triangle between two beautiful sisters and one man with a dreamlike visual beauty.
title_norm:かもめ食堂: A drama depicting the peaceful daily lives of three Japanese women set in a small restaurant in Helsinki, the capital of Finland. Based on the novel of the same name by author Yōko Mure, adapted and directed by Naoko Ogigami, who gained attention with her feature directorial debut "Barber Yoshino." Japanese woman Sachie opens a small restaurant called "Kamome Diner" on a street corner in Helsinki, but no customers come. One day, Sachie happens to meet a Japanese tourist named Midori and asks her to help out at the restaurant. Soon, a variety of colorful characters start coming to Sachie's shop one after another... Satomi Kobayashi, Hairi Katagiri, and Masako Motai play the three Japanese women, with Markku Peltola from "The Man Without a Past" co-starring.
title_norm:きっと青春大革命！カルラ8年の記録: A documentary by transgender director Kani Lapuerta, recording eight years in the life of a transgender elementary school student in Mexico as she grows into a teenager. In Tepoztlán, a town south of Mexico City, 15-year-old Carla talks with director Kani Lapuerta in a secret cocoon. They discuss what kind of film they want to make, and begin to look back on Carla's life chronologically from her elementary school days. The schoolyard where she couldn't line up with either the 'boys' or 'girls,' the bedroom where she endlessly practiced makeup, the morning school reopened during the pandemic, the city hall where she officially changed her name, the slogans she shouted at the Pride March, and the baton club she admired. Watched over by her punk and hippie chef parents, her friends, director Lapuerta, the queer community, and the sacred rocky mountain, Carla encounters various versions of herself. Director Kani Lapuerta also appears in the film, gradually sharing her inner thoughts with Carla like an exchange diary. With comedic touches, it portrays the struggles and fluctuations of adolescence growing up in a small town with strong gender stereotypes.
title_norm:きれっぱしの愛: In a small rural town in Iceland, artist Anna lives with her responsible eldest daughter Ida, her mischievous twin sons Grímur and Þorgils, and her dog Panda, while searching for her path as an artist. Though she married young and is supposedly "no longer a couple" with her ex-husband Magnús, he can't seem to cut ties, constantly finding excuses to visit, share meals, and even join picnics. Before she knows it, they slip back into a daily life as if they were "still a family"—but what comes next?
title_norm:ぐるりのこと。: "Unforgettable masterpieces" return to the screen! Since his directorial debut with "A Touch of Fever" (1993), Ryosuke Hashiguchi—known as a "master of few works" eagerly awaited by film fans both in Japan and abroad—has delivered acclaimed films including "Like Grains of Sand" (1995), which won the Grand Prix at the 25th Rotterdam International Film Festival; "Three Stories of Love" (2015), which swept various film awards including the Kinema Junpo Best Ten Japanese Films No. 1; and his latest work "Motherhood" (2024), released nine years after "Three Stories of Love." "Hush!" depicts a gay couple and a woman—three people who had given up on connecting with others—forming a "new kind of family." "All Around Us" portrays the hope that arises between people through ten years in the life of a married couple. Both films are often cited as "all-time best films" and are known as "unforgettable masterpieces." Now, these two works will be revived in 4K remastered versions! "All Around Us" returns 18 years after its June 2008 release, while "Hush!" returns 25 years after its production in 2001 (released April 2002)—a full quarter-century later. "All Around Us" follows a wife who falls into depression due to her overly serious nature and her husband, a courtroom sketch artist who supports her, tracing their inseparable bond over ten years against the backdrop of various shocking events from the 1990s. The film was screened in the Panorama section of the 2009 Berlin International Film Festival.
title_norm:こころの通訳者たち what a wonderful wo: A documentary capturing people's efforts to convey sign language to those who cannot see. At Cinema Chupki Tabata in Tokyo's Kita Ward, Japan's only universal theater, all screenings include audio guides and subtitles. This documentary records three stage sign language interpreters striving to make theater enjoyable for deaf people. To convey this footage to visually impaired people, a group of unique members begins creating an "audio guide." The thoughts of the stage sign language interpreters eventually overlap with those of the audio guide creators, connecting hearts beyond language and disability. The director is Reo Yamada of "Living in the Margins: The Work of Director Sunao Katabuchi."
title_norm:この世界の（さらにいくつもの）片隅に: An extended version of 'In This Corner of the World,' director Sunao Katabuchi's animated adaptation of Fumiyo Kouno's manga, which achieved an unprecedented long-running hit and high acclaim both domestically and internationally, with new scenes added. In 1944, during the war in Japan, Suzu moves to Kure, Hiroshima Prefecture, after marrying Shusaku and begins a new life surrounded by her husband and his family. As the war situation worsens, life becomes more difficult, but Suzu uses her ingenuity to weave together daily life. One day, Suzu meets a woman named Rin at a brothel she stumbles into. Despite their different circumstances, Suzu connects with Rin, the first woman her age she has met in Kure... Under director Katabuchi, the cast remains unchanged, with Non as the protagonist Suzu and Nanase Iwai as Rin, whose scenes have been added in this version.
title_norm:この場所: A Japan-Philippines co-produced drama set in Rikuzentakata City, Iwate Prefecture, over a decade after the Great East Japan Earthquake, portraying the emotional recovery and identity rebirth of two half-sisters of different cultures and races. Reina Hashimoto, a 20-year-old art student living in Rikuzentakata, suddenly loses her beloved father and is overwhelmed with grief. Then appears Ella, her half-sister seven years older, who arrives from the Philippines. Reina is confused and unable to understand why Ella, who has been out of contact for so long, suddenly shows up after their father's death. The sisters, differing in culture and race, repeatedly clash and seek understanding as they confront their emotional wounds and reconsider their feelings toward family and homeland. Starring Arisa Nakano as Reina, who won the Best Actress award at the 48th Gawad Urian Awards in the Philippines—the first foreign actor to do so—and Filipino actor Gabby Padilla as her sister Ella. The cast also includes Reiko Kataoka, Cheryl Ichikawa, Satoshi Nikaido, and Sho Yakumaru. Directed and written by Filipino filmmaker Jaime Pacena II, who has visited the Tohoku region as a visual artist since 2010 and maintained ties with local communities, in his feature-length directorial debut.
title_norm:この夏の星を見る: A drama based on the award-winning novel by Mizuki Tsujimura, depicting the complex emotions of junior high and high school students during the COVID-19 pandemic, set in Tokyo's Shibuya Ward, Tsuchiura City in Ibaraki Prefecture, and Goto City in Nagasaki Prefecture. In 2020, with school attendance and club activities restricted due to the pandemic, Aya Tanimoto, a second-year student in the astronomy club at Ibaraki Prefectural Sunaura High School, proposes an 'Online Star Catch Contest'—a competition using remote meetings to conduct simultaneous astronomical observations across different locations. The activity, joined by students from the Goto Islands in Nagasaki and central Tokyo, eventually spreads nationwide and sparks a miracle. Hiyori Sakurada, known for 'The Fake Diary,' stars as Aya. Rinataro Mizusawa plays her classmate; Arisa Nakano and Ikoi Hayase play students from Nagasaki; Soiya Kurokawa and Anna Hoshino play students from Tokyo; and Takashi Okabe plays the astronomy club advisor. Tamaki Yamamoto, who gained attention for the 2019 short film 'One Night After' and the streaming drama 'Today You're Restless, You're Burning,' makes his feature-length commercial film debut as director. Mash Morino, known for the drama 'Keke no Hi no Kekeke,' writes the screenplay. Haruka Nakamura, known for 'Look Back,' provides the music.
title_norm:この子は誰: Selected for the Competition section of the 75th Berlin International Film Festival (2025). Screened at "EU Film Days 2026" (Tokyo: May 16–29, 2026 at Theater Image Forum, May 19–24 at the National Film Archive of Japan; Nagoya: June 6–19 at Nagoya Kinema Noi; also held in Hiroshima, Kyoto, and Fukuoka).
title_norm:この星は、私の星じゃない: At the time, many women resonated with Tanaka's sentiment, 'I want to live as myself, rather than living like a woman,' sparking the women's liberation movement across Japan. The women never backed down against the male media who mocked them as 'sour grapes of unpopular women,' retorting, 'The difficulty of women's lives is where lib breathes!' For Tanaka, lib was a world of one versus many. Now, as an acupuncturist facing patients one-on-one, Tanaka says, 'There is a place for that person within me, and there is a place for me within that person.'
title_norm:これからの私たち all shall be well: A drama depicting a long-term lesbian couple facing various problems after one partner's sudden death. Director Ray Yeung, who previously explored the issues of elderly gay couples in "Suk Suk," turns his gaze to the current state of Hong Kong, where prejudice against homosexuality remains deeply rooted, while also highlighting social issues such as severe housing shortages, employment difficulties, and economic disparity. Pat and Angie, a lesbian couple in their 60s, are enjoying a stable and peaceful life both publicly and privately. However, Pat suddenly dies. Angie was close with Pat's relatives, but they clash over the funeral arrangements. Furthermore, under Hong Kong law, Pat's brother, as her relative, inherits her estate. This is an unacceptable reality for Angie, who considered the apartment, filled with memories of Pat, to be their final home. Meanwhile, Pat's financially struggling brother, his wife, and their children also grapple with their own circumstances. The film won the Teddy Award for outstanding LGBTQ cinema at the 74th Berlin International Film Festival in 2024 and received high praise, including five nominations at the 43rd Hong Kong Film Awards, including Best Film. Patra Au, who won the Hong Kong Film Award for Best Supporting Actress for "Suk Suk," plays Angie, earning a Best Actress nomination for this film. Maggie Li, returning to the screen after about 30 years, plays Pat.
title_norm:これって生きてる？: A couple whose smooth-sailing life takes a turn and their marriage falls apart. The disheartened husband, Alex, finds a new purpose in life by turning their marital woes into comedy at a comedy club.
title_norm:さよなら、僕の英雄: Danish director Anders Thomas Jensen, known for writing "Riders of Justice," "The Good Life," and "After the Wedding," delivers a human drama starring his frequent collaborator Mads Mikkelsen. After serving time for a robbery, Anker is released and reunites with his brother Manfred, who hid a large sum of money during the heist, for the first time in 15 years. However, Manfred not only has forgotten the hiding place but also believes he is John Lennon. The two set out on a journey to find the bag of hidden money, but the trip gradually transforms into a journey of self-reflection for both of them. Mikkelsen plays Manfred, who has lost his memory and believes he is John Lennon, embodying this eccentric and unique character. Anker is played by Nikolaj Lie Kaas, another frequent collaborator of Jensen's. The film had its world premiere in the Out of Competition section of the 2025 Venice International Film Festival and became a massive hit in its native Denmark, breaking the country's all-time box office record for a live-action film.
title_norm:さらば、わが愛 覇王別姫: An epic saga depicting the tumultuous lives of two Peking opera actors, this was the first Chinese-language film to win the Palme d'Or at the Cannes Film Festival. It portrays the love, hatred, and lives of two Peking opera performers who play the classic 'Farewell My Concubine,' set against the backdrop of China's turbulent history from 1925 under the Nationalist government through the Cultural Revolution and into the late 1970s. Directed by Chen Kaige, who gained attention with his debut 'Yellow Earth' and became a leading figure of China's Fifth Generation directors with this film's success. In 1925 Beijing, Douzi, abandoned by his prostitute mother, is sent to a Peking opera training school. Shitou protects him like a younger brother and becomes his strong support through harsh training. As they grow up, they become major stars in the Peking opera world... Leslie Cheung plays Cheng Dieyi, a male dan actor who clings to love despite being tossed by the times, and Gong Li appears as a high-class courtesan who becomes his love rival. A 4K version was released in 2023, marking the 30th anniversary of the film's production and 20 years after Leslie Cheung's death.
title_norm:さらば、わが愛／覇王別姫: An epic saga depicting the tumultuous lives of two Peking opera actors, this was the first Chinese-language film to win the Palme d'Or at the Cannes Film Festival. It portrays the love, hatred, and lives of two Peking opera performers who play the classic 'Farewell My Concubine,' set against the backdrop of China's turbulent history from 1925 under the Nationalist government through the Cultural Revolution and into the late 1970s. Directed by Chen Kaige, who gained attention with his debut 'Yellow Earth' and became a leading figure of China's Fifth Generation directors with this film's success. In 1925 Beijing, Douzi, abandoned by his prostitute mother, is sent to a Peking opera training school. Shitou protects him like a younger brother and becomes his strong support through harsh training. As they grow up, they become major stars in the Peking opera world... Leslie Cheung plays Cheng Dieyi, a male dan actor who clings to love despite being tossed by the times, and Gong Li appears as a high-class courtesan who becomes his love rival. A 4K version was released in 2023, marking the 30th anniversary of the film's production and 20 years after Leslie Cheung's death.
title_norm:しあわせな選択: Korean master filmmaker Park Chan-wook, winner of the Grand Prix at Cannes for "Oldboy" and Best Director for "Decision to Leave," directs this suspense drama laced with irony and black humor about a salaryman whose life is turned upside down by a sudden layoff. Park reunites with Lee Byung-hun, who starred in his breakthrough film "Joint Security Area," for the first time in 21 years. Man-su, an ordinary salaryman at a paper company, lives with his wife, two children, and two dogs, believing he has everything he could want. But his life changes drastically when he is suddenly fired from the company he has worked for for 25 years. His job search drags on for over a year, and he is forced to sell his beloved home. Desperate, Man-su walks into a rapidly growing paper company with his resume, only to be flatly rejected. Convinced he is the most qualified person for the company, he makes a decision: if there's no opening, he'll have to create one himself. The film is based on the novel "The Ax" by Donald E. Westlake, which was also adapted into a film by Costa-Gavras. Lee Byung-hun plays the increasingly cornered Man-su, and Son Ye-jin of "Crash Landing on You" plays his wife Mi-ri, who grows stronger as the crisis deepens. The film was selected for the competition section of the 82nd Venice International Film Festival in 2025 and won the newly established International Audience Award (for non-North American films) at the 50th Toronto International Film Festival.
title_norm:すずめの戸締まり: Director Makoto Shinkai, of "Your Name." and "Weathering with You," presents a feature animation depicting the adventure and growth of a girl who journeys across ruins throughout Japan to close "doors" that bring disaster. Suzume Iwato, a 17-year-old living in Kyushu, meets Souta Munakata, a young man on a journey searching for doors. Following him to a mountain ruin, Suzume finds an old door standing as if spared from the surrounding collapse, and is drawn to reach for it. Soon, doors begin opening one after another across Japan. As calamities come from beyond the doors, Suzume embarks on a journey to close them. Despite numerous surprises and hardships, Suzume continues forward, but... Nanoka Hara, a young actress known for "The Sound of Sin" and "My Heart Beats for You," was chosen through auditions to voice the protagonist Suzume. Hokuto Matsumura of SixTONES voices Souta, marking his voice acting debut. Also voicing roles are Eri Fukatsu, Shota Someno, Sairi Ito, Kotone Hanase, and Hakuo Matsumoto, with regular Shinkai collaborators Ryunosuke Kamiki and Kana Hanazawa also appearing. Music is again by RADWIMPS, in their third collaboration with Shinkai, alongside composer Kazuma Jinnouchi. Screened in competition at the 73rd Berlin International Film Festival in 2023, marking the first Japanese animated film in competition there in 21 years since "Spirited Away," which won the Golden Bear.
title_norm:そして人生はつづく: In 1990, a massive earthquake in northern Iran mercilessly struck the village where the 1987 film "Where Is the Friend's Home?" was shot, as well as its residents. After the earthquake, film director Kiarostami, accompanied by his son, heads to the disaster-stricken area to check on the safety of the two brothers who appeared in the film.
title_norm:そして彼女たちは: An ensemble drama by Belgian masters Jean-Pierre and Luc Dardenne, known for "The Child" and "The Kid with a Bike," depicting five young mothers living in a mother-child support facility. The five girls—Jessica, Perla, Ariane, Julie, and Naima—live together in a facility that supports women who became pregnant young. Without anyone to rely on and facing various problems like poverty and violence, they become mothers while confused, troubled, and unable to find a model for the family they should aim for. Struggling not to be swallowed by the overwhelming loneliness, the girls who still wish "to love" sometimes lean on others and choose their own paths to follow. Lukas Dhont, director of "Close," is listed as a co-producer. Screened in the Competition section of the 78th Cannes Film Festival in 2025, it won the Best Screenplay Award and the Ecumenical Jury Prize.
title_norm:そして父になる: Ryota (Fukuyama) is a company employee who has carved out his own life and enjoys smooth sailing. One day, a call from the hospital informs him that the son he has raised with love for six years is actually another couple's child, switched at birth. Through interactions with the family who raised his biological son, his values gradually begin to waver, and he grapples with what family and blood ties truly mean. Winner of the Jury Prize at the 66th Cannes Film Festival.
title_norm:それいけ！アンパンマン パンタンと約束の星: The 37th theatrical film in the beloved national children's anime "Anpanman" based on Takashi Yanase's original work. With "promise" as the story's keyword, it depicts the new character Pantan, a red panda traveler, joining forces with Anpanman, Cream Panda, and other friends he meets on his journey to face challenges. To keep a precious promise made long ago with an adventurer, the red panda Pantan travels in search of a treasure said to be on the Rainbow Star shining in the night sky. During his journey, he is sprayed with Baikinman's baby spray and turned into a child. Helped by Anpanman and his friends, Pantan tells them about his journey and his regret over breaking a precious promise. Hearing this, Uncle Jam encourages him, saying, "What matters is the will to keep a promise," and Pantan decides to set out again with renewed determination. Cream Panda joins Pantan on his journey as they head for their destination, the Rainbow Star... Guest voice actor Tao Tsuchiya plays Pantan. The comedy duo "EXIT" members Rintaro and Daiki Kanekina also appear. Directed by Hiroyuki Yano, who has worked extensively on the TV anime series and theatrical films. The screenplay is by Shoji Yonemura, also a veteran of the TV series and films.
title_norm:ただ空高く舞え: Based on the autobiographical writings of Captain G.R. Gopinath, the founder of India's first low-cost carrier "Air Deccan," this drama depicts the journey of men striving to establish an airline. After being unable to be by his father's side at the time of his death because economy seats were fully booked, Air Force officer Nedumaaran sets out to launch India's first budget airline alongside two of his former comrades. Though many looked down on their passion or mocked their ambition, they remain undeterred by the noise around them, pushing forward toward their dream of founding an airline. Tamil cinema star Suriya takes the lead role, with Sudha Kongara (Final Round) directing.
title_norm:だぁれかさんとアソぼ？: Directed by Takashi Shimizu of the "Ju-On" series, this school horror film stars Suzuka Chinzei of the idol group FRUITS ZIPPER in the lead role. A secret rumor circulates among young people about a forbidden game: if you record a date and name onto a cassette tape on the 13th step of an empty school staircase, that person will die. High school students casually try the game, and their daily lives begin to warp. One by one, those whose names were recorded on the tape die mysteriously on the specified dates. The school takes the situation seriously and asks psychological counselor Koharu Hirase to provide mental care for the students. Koharu counsels a student who witnessed the incidents, but among those who played the game is her younger sister, Nanami. As students are attacked by strange phenomena one after another, Koharu and Nanami are dragged into a chain of terror. Suzuka Chinzei takes on her first solo lead film role and first horror role as counselor Koharu; Anna Hoshino (from "Gold Boy") plays Koharu's sister Nanami; Riku Onishi (from "Water Flows Toward the Sea") plays classmate Jotaro Chiba who looks out for Nanami; and Shota Sometani plays a young man who holds the key to the story.
title_norm:ちびっ子レミと名犬カピ: Based on 'Nobody's Boy.' Even after being sold by his stepfather to traveling performers, young Remi never loses heart. The background art incorporates elements from diverse European masterpieces by Millet and Monet, while Yugo Serikawa's masterful use of dramatic pauses heightens the arduous journey. Frankie Sakai's voice performance as Remi's sidekick Capi, with his playful demeanor, offers a refreshing respite amid the relentless tragedy.
title_norm:てっぺんの向こうにあなたがいる: This drama marks Sayuri Yoshinaga's 124th film appearance and is modeled after Junko Tabei, the first woman to successfully summit the world's highest peak, Mount Everest. It portrays a female mountaineer who staked her entire life on reaching the 'top.' In 1975, as deputy leader and climbing captain of the Japanese Women's Everest Expedition, Junko Tabe became the first woman in the world to summit Everest. Her achievement astonished the world and brought light to herself, her friends, and her family, but it also cast a deep shadow. Her challenges as a mountaineer continued, and in her later years, even while battling illness and after being given a terminal diagnosis, Junko continued to smile, involve those around her, and climb mountains. The cast includes Yoshinaga as Junko Tabe, a character based on Junko Tabei; Koichi Sato as her husband Masaaki; Yuki Amami as Etsuko Kitayama, Junko's ally and Everest climbing partner; and Non as the young Junko. The film is directed by Junji Sakamoto, who previously directed Yoshinaga in 'The Light of the North' and reunites with her after 13 years.
title_norm:とうちゃん:
A short human drama that delicately portrays the emotional shifts of a man marrying a single mother and her young son. Yuta, who is dating single mother Yoko, spends time with her son, Daisuke, on the first night he stays over at her apartment. When Yuta and Yoko tell Daisuke they have decided to get married, he seemingly accepts the news at first, but... The film captures a single day in the life of a family about to take a new step forward at the end of summer.

The film stars Shinji Matsubayashi (*Icchorai*, *GOLDFISH*), Asami Shibuya (*The Kingdom (or About That House)*, *Waiting for the Pianist*), and Sorami (*Good Luck My Road*). It is directed by Ken Nishioka, who continues to create original short works such as *Yellowtail New Year's Eve*. After screening in the Japan Premiere section of the 19th Sapporo International Short Film Festival, the film will have a standalone release at Theater Guild Daikanyama and other venues in 2025. In 2026, it will also be released theatrically as part of "The Ken Nishioka Short Film Special," featuring a triple bill of his short films: *Tochan*, *Yellowtail New Year's Eve*, and *Where the Balloon Goes*.
title_norm:とんがり帽子のメモル／メイプルタウン物語／新メイプルタウン: Episodes marked with ★ will be followed by a talk event (approx. 30 minutes) featuring Junichi Sato (animation director), Hiroki Shibata (animation director), and Daisuke Nishio (animation director).
title_norm:どうすればよかったか？: Documentary filmmaker Tomoaki Fujino records over 20 years the story of his older sister, who began showing symptoms of schizophrenia, and his parents, who kept her from seeing a psychiatrist. His sister, eight years older, was caring and excellent. Influenced by their parents, she entered medical school to become a doctor. One day, she suddenly started screaming things that weren't true. Schizophrenia was suspected, but her parents—a doctor and a researcher—refused to acknowledge the illness and kept her away from psychiatric care. Doubting their judgment, Fujino tried to persuade them but failed, and left home with a lingering sense of unease. Eighteen years after his sister's onset, Fujino, having studied filmmaking, began recording his family's life whenever he visited home. He filmed family outings and dinner scenes, engaged his parents in conversation, and kept talking to his sister, but her condition worsened. Eventually, his parents installed a chain and padlock on the front door to confine her inside.
title_norm:どうぶつ宝島: Young Jim, who dreams of foreign lands and sailing, is left to mind the old inn Benbow Tavern in a port town tonight. But a suspicious cat captain shows up and leaves behind a mysterious map. It seems to indicate the location of treasure hidden by the famous pirate Captain Flint. Jim sets out to sea with his best friend, a mouse named Gran, in his homemade barrel ship, the Pioneer. Their destination: the legendary Treasure Island on the map! However, the Pioneer is sunk by a pirate ship, and the two are quickly taken prisoner. The pirate ship is named the Pork Sauté. Its captain, Silver, was once one of Flint's men, and he too has his eye on the treasure of Treasure Island. Jim and Gran escape and land on Pirate Island. But they are caught by Silver's gang, have the map stolen, and are sold off to slave traders. In the stone prison where they are confined, they find a girl named Cathy already there. It turns out Cathy is Captain Flint's granddaughter and is also looking for the map. Jim and Cathy initially clash but eventually open their hearts to each other and decide to cooperate and head for Treasure Island. Now, the curtain rises on a great adventure across the sea!
title_norm:ながぐつ三銃士: Pero, a cat targeted by a bumbling hitman for saving a mouse, fights villains in the American West! The second theatrical film in the beloved series featuring the cute cat that serves as the symbol of Toei Doga (now Toei Animation).
title_norm:なみのおと: The first installment of the Tohoku documentary trilogy co-directed by Ko Sakai (*Home Sweet Home*) and rising filmmaker Ryusuke Hamaguchi, who garnered acclaim for *PASSION* and *THE DEPTHS*. This documentary gathers the "dialogues" of those affected by the tsunami during the Great East Japan Earthquake. Traveling south from the Taro district of Miyako City in Iwate Prefecture to the town of Shinchi in Fukushima’s Soma District, the film captures family members and friends as they speak with one another about the disaster and its aftermath. By focusing on everyday conversation rather than tragic imagery of the disaster zones, the film distills the raw emotions of the survivors that emerge through their shared words.
title_norm:なみのこえ 新地町: The second part of the Tohoku documentary trilogy co-directed by Ryusuke Hamaguchi and Ko Sakai, 'Voices from the Waves,' set in Shinchi Town. Following the previous work 'Tales from the Waves,' which captured the 'dialogues' of people affected by the tsunami on March 11, 2011, this film records survivors about a year after the disaster as they talk with family, friends, and colleagues about what happened and how they have been since. While the previous film conducted interviews across a wide area from Iwate to Fukushima Prefectures, this installment focuses specifically on Shinchi Town in Soma District, Fukushima Prefecture, recording dialogues among 10 people in 6 groups.
title_norm:なみのこえ 気仙沼: The second part of the Tohoku documentary trilogy co-directed by Ryusuke Hamaguchi and Ko Sakai, 'Voices from the Waves,' set in Kesennuma. Continuing to film for over a year after completing the previous work 'Tales from the Waves,' which gathered 'dialogues' of people living along the Sanriku coast affected by the tsunami on March 11, 2011, this film records dialogues among 11 people in 7 groups living in Kesennuma City, Miyagi Prefecture. About a year after the disaster, it depicts survivors recalling their memories of the earthquake through conversations with family, friends, and colleagues, and renewing their feelings.
title_norm:なんでかね～鶴見 ガーエーにはまだ早い: A drama set in Yokohama's Tsurumi Ward, an area with a large population of people of Okinawan heritage that gained attention as one of the settings for the NHK morning drama "Chimudondon," using the traditional Okinawan performing art of Eisa as a motif. The Tsurumi Eisa group "Shiokaze" is focusing on recruiting new members to further energize their Eisa performances, but they struggle to gather people. Mina, one of the core members, works selling loco moco bowls from a food truck and dreams of one day owning her own live music venue as an artist playing the sanrele, a hybrid of the sanshin and ukulele. One day, Mina meets a young man named Eito, who is from Okinawa. Bonding over their shared Okinawan roots, they chat about their lives. When Mina learns that Eito is from Koza, the heartland of Eisa, she forcefully invites him to join Eisa, saying "Just come watch practice," but... This is the second installment in the series following "That's Why, Tsurumi," which also explored Tsurumi and Okinawa. Directed and written by Atsushi Watanabe, who also worked on the previous film.
title_norm:はじまりの記憶 杉本博司: A documentary that provides the first long-term, in-depth look at Hiroshi Sugimoto, a world-renowned photographer and artist who has won numerous awards in Japan and abroad. The film follows Sugimoto as he works across borders, from his home base in New York to Japan, the South of France, and Sydney. It reveals his true character and what he strives for in his art. Originally broadcast on WOWOW in 2010 as "The Memory of Origins: Contemporary Artist Hiroshi Sugimoto," this theatrical version incorporates newly filmed footage.
title_norm:はなればなれに: A masterpiece from Jean-Luc Godard's early period, this melodrama is based on an American crime novel and depicts in comedic fashion the love triangle and criminal scheme involving two men and one woman. Winter in Paris. Franz and Arthur, best friends with completely opposite personalities, both fall in love at first sight with Odile, a beautiful and shy woman from Scandinavia. One day, they learn that a large sum of money is hidden in Odile's aunt's house, and the three plot to steal it, but the plan takes unexpected twists and turns... This was the first production from "Anouchka Films," the production company founded by Godard and actress Anna Karina, who played Odile and were married at the time. Music by Michel Legrand of "The Umbrellas of Cherbourg." It went unreleased in Japanese theaters for many years before finally premiering in 2001.
title_norm:ひちりん: A human drama written, directed, and starring Yudai Kamishi, known for "Hitokuzu" and "Nebagigi New World." Set in a small yakiniku restaurant in Osaka, it depicts the rebirth of a man burdened by sin and people trying to live again. At a small yakiniku restaurant called "Sashinohana" in a corner of Osaka, Sakurako, who lost her husband, runs the place with support from her elementary school son Ken'nosuke, but she can't match her late husband's flavor, customers dwindle, and she's in a tough spot. One day, a taciturn man named Futoshi Maekawa visits the shop asking to be hired. Having once worked at a yakiniku restaurant in Asakusa, Tokyo, Futoshi has been living on the run from a past incident caused while trying to protect his family. Seeing Sakurako desperately protecting the shop reminds him of his late mother, and as he cuts meat and lights the charcoal grill day by day, he gradually forms a family-like bond with Sakurako and Ken'nosuke. Kamishi also serves as director, screenwriter, producer, and plays Futoshi himself. The cast includes Ai Furukawa, Minatsu Tokutake, Shinzo Hotta, Kazuki Namioka, Naomasa Rokuroku, Mineko Nishikawa, Kanji Tsuda, and Ikkei Watanabe.
title_norm:ひつじ探偵団: An unconventional mystery film starring Hugh Jackman, depicting sheep whose beloved owner is murdered as they struggle to find the culprit. In a peaceful English countryside town, shepherd George lives alone surrounded by his beloved sheep. He reads detective novels to them every night, and the sheep actually understand the stories and look forward to this time. One day, George is found dead. The sheep refuse to believe it was an accident and, led by their smartest leader Lily, launch an investigation. As they follow clues, they discover George had a huge inheritance. Determined to avenge their beloved George, the sheep race to find the killer. Hugh Jackman plays the victimized shepherd George, with Oscar-winning actress Emma Thompson, Nicholas Galitzine from "The Idea of You," and Nicholas Braun from the TV series "Succession" co-starring. Julia Louis-Dreyfus, Patrick Stewart, and Bryan Cranston voice the sheep. Based on the 2005 bestselling novel of the same name by German author Leonie Swann, directed by Kyle Balda of the "Minions" series.
title_norm:ひとしずく:
This drama depicts the struggles and growth of a young woman who moves to Minamiosumi, Kagoshima—the southernmost town on Japan’s mainland—to serve as a member of the Local Revitalization Corps. 24-year-old Kasumi Sakamoto, born and raised in Tokyo, felt stuck in a rut, unsure of what she wanted to do with her life. Drawn by a chance job posting and a longing for rural living, she decides to restart her life by relocating to Minamiosumi. Though initially bewildered by the gap between her ideals and reality, Kasumi gradually begins to take root in the community through tears and laughter.

The film is the theatrical debut of director Daiyu Yamashita, who himself moved to Minamiosumi in 2017 to work in the Local Revitalization Corps. In 2019, Yamashita traveled across all 47 of Japan’s prefectures in a mini-car, interviewing over 200 corps members and local government officials to write the screenplay. Based on his own experiences and the authentic voices he gathered, he portrays the true feelings of people from various walks of life with a warm and empathetic gaze. In addition to professional actors, the film features many local residents.
title_norm:ひとりたび: The third feature film by director Yuho Ishibashi, known for 'Goodbye' and 'When Morning Comes, I Feel Empty.' This human drama follows a woman in her 30s, stuck in her career and love life, as she reexamines her way of living by relying on memories of her first love from her student days. Misaki, a 32-year-old working in Tokyo, feels uncomfortable at the company she has worked for for many years and quits, returning to her family home without any clear prospects for the future. Attending a local class reunion, she learns that her first love from her school days has already passed away. This event gradually reawakens the memories and emotions that had been frozen inside Misaki. The screenplay is written by Naho Uemura, noted for 'Ichiko,' 'Crescent Moon and Cat,' and 'Zakken!' The lead role is played by Rei Okamoto, who is widely active in films like 'Tea Drinking Friends,' as well as dramas, commercials, and stage. The film brings together three women of the same generation—Okamoto (born 1991), Ishibashi (born 1990), and Uemura (born 1988)—to delicately weave a story about the anxieties of a woman in her 30s about the future and her encounter with past memories. The cast also includes Koki Osamura, Akane Sakanoue, Mari Hamada, Hideko Hara, and Mitsuru Hirata.
title_norm:ひなぎく: A landmark film of the 1960s Czech New Wave, this work portrays the wild antics of two uninhibited girls, both named "Marie," using a boldly experimental array of techniques including color shifts, coloring, optical effects, innovative sound design, and abrupt scene transitions. The older sister, with a blonde bob and a daisy wreath, and the younger sister, with dark brown hair in two pigtails, both call themselves "Marie" and pretend to be siblings. They live freely, tricking men into buying them meals only to fake-cry and run away. At home, they do whatever they please—bathing in milk, burning paper, cutting out magazine photos, slicing up bed sheets, and eventually cutting each other's bodies, until the screen itself fragments. Directed and written by Věra Chytilová, a pioneering Czech filmmaker and the most prominent female director of the Czech New Wave. The two leads were played by non-professional actresses selected through auditions: Jitka Cerhová and Ivana Karbanová. Other roles were also filled by non-actors, such as composers and designers. The film had its first official theatrical release in Japan in 1991 at Kichijoji Baus Theater, where it ran for an extended period through word of mouth. It has since gained a cult following, and in March 2026, a 4K restored version will be re-released to commemorate the 60th anniversary of its production and the 35th anniversary of its Japanese release.
title_norm:ひみつのアッコちゃん 海だ! おばけだ!! 夏祭り: Elementary school student Kagami Atsuko can transform into any appearance she desires using a magical mirror. This is the first theatrical film in the second series of "Himitsu no Akko-chan," which captures the transformation wishes of young girls. The story depicts the interaction between "Taishō," who opposes the construction of a building on the children's playground, and his father, who works in construction. Akko transforms into a baton twirler who leads the protest. Kanemori Yoshinori's four-heads-tall characters move energetically across the screen.
title_norm:ひみつのアッコちゃん／ひみつのアッコちゃん 海だ! おばけ: Elementary school student Kagami Atsuko can transform into any appearance she desires using a magical mirror. This is the first theatrical film in the second series of "Himitsu no Akko-chan," which captures the transformation wishes of young girls. The story depicts the interaction between "Taishō," who opposes the construction of a building on the children's playground, and his father, who works in construction. Akko transforms into a baton twirler who leads the protest. Kanemori Yoshinori's four-heads-tall characters move energetically across the screen.
title_norm:ひめゆり: During the final stages of the Pacific War, in Okinawa where fierce battles engulfed even civilians, female students aged 14 to 19 were forced into the battlefield to serve as nurses, and many of them lost their lives. This documentary delves into the truth of the "Himeyuri Student Corps," whose story has been repeatedly told in films and dramas. Through the invaluable testimonies of 22 survivors recorded over 13 years, the harsh fate imposed on these young girls comes to light.
title_norm:ひゃくえむ。: Togashi, born with natural speed, has always used it to gain friends and a place to belong. Meanwhile, transfer student Komiya runs recklessly, trying to forget his painful reality. Togashi teaches Komiya how to run faster, and after school the two practice together. Finding something to devote himself to, Komiya greedily chases new records. Gradually, through the 100-meter dash, their relationship grows into something between rivals and best friends.
title_norm:ひろしま: A high school in Hiroshima. In the third-year class taught by Kitagawa, student Michiko Oba collapses with a nosebleed. It is caused by leukemia from the atomic bomb. In this class, a full one-third of the students are hibakusha (atomic bomb survivors). On that day, Yukiko's sister was exposed to the bomb while working on evacuation duties and died in a river. Endo Yukio's father could not save his wife, who was trapped under a building and engulfed in flames. When radish sprouts appeared in Hiroshima, where it was said no grass would grow for 75 years after the bombing, people found hope in those sprouts.
title_norm:ほかげ: Director Shinya Tsukamoto, known for "Fires on the Plain" and "Killing," depicts the lives of people carrying despair and darkness in the black market just after the end of the war. A woman living alone in a small, surviving izakaya is forced into selling her body and spends her days without the will to resist, overwhelmed by despair. One day, a child who lost their family in an air raid sneaks into the woman's izakaya to steal food. From then on, the child begins to frequent the place, and through her interaction with the child, the woman begins to find a faint glimmer of light. Hikari Mitsushima, known for "Just Remembering," delivers a delicate yet bold performance as the protagonist, the woman. Mirai Moriyama plays a mysterious man with a paralyzed arm, Sōga Tsukao, a child actor known for "The Last 10 Years," plays a war orphan, and Hironori Kōno, known for "Special Actors," plays a young repatriated soldier. It was screened in the Orizzonti section of the 80th Venice International Film Festival in 2023 and won the NETPAC Award (Best Asian Film Award).
title_norm:ほどなく、お別れです: Based on the bestselling novel of the same name by Amone Nagatsuki, winner of the Shogakukan Bunko Novel Award Grand Prize, starring Minami Hamabe and Ren Meguro, directed by Takahiro Miki ("Ao Haru Ride," "Tomorrow I Will Date Yesterday's You"). It depicts a heroine who joins a funeral company and, together with her supervising funeral planner, aims to create the "best possible funeral." Misu Shimizu, struggling with job hunting, has a secret she can't tell anyone: she can hear the voices of the deceased. A fateful encounter changes her life when Reiji Urushibara, a funeral planner who notices her ability, invites her into the world of funeral planning. Guided by something, Misu becomes an intern at the funeral company "Bando Kaikan." Teaming up with Urushibara, she confronts the question "What is a funeral that satisfies not only the surviving family but also the deceased?" through various families' funerals, including a husband who lost his pregnant wife and a couple who lost their young daughter. Eventually, Misu comes to admire Urushibara's sincere dedication to the deceased and their families, and decides to pursue a career as a funeral planner herself. Hamabe plays Misu, Meguro plays Urushibara, with a stellar cast including Mochika Yamada, Ken Mitsuishi, Mirai Shida, Keisuke Watanabe, Kotone Furukawa, and Takumi Kitamura. The script is by Takuro Honda (drama "Lion's Snack"), supervised by Yoshikazu Okada, known for various hit works.
title_norm:ぼくのエリ 200歳の少女: Oscar, a 12-year-old in the prime of playfulness but with not a single friend, falls in love for the first time with Eli, who moves in next door. With messy black hair and a pale face, Eli only ever appears at night, and the more Oscar learns about her, the more mysterious she becomes. Though she claims to be the same age as Oscar, she doesn't even know her own birthday. Around the same time Oscar meets Eli, gruesome murders begin occurring in succession, casting an uneasy air over the town. In the midst of this, Oscar discovers a grave secret: the shocking truth that Eli has been 12 years old for a very long time. Eli is a vampire who has survived for 200 years, moving from town to town and drinking human blood.
title_norm:ぼくらの七日間戦争: At Aoba Junior High, where strict discipline is enforced, eleven boys and girls rise up in pursuit of freedom. They bring food and barricade themselves in an abandoned factory, while the teachers try to disband them strictly according to school rules. The students fend off the teachers using various means, but... A lighthearted youth drama based on the original novel by So Munetari. Screened simultaneously with "Flower's Asuka Gang!".
title_norm:ぼくらの居場所: A Canadian drama that captures the lives of people on the fringes of society with an honest gaze, following three children living in harsh circumstances as they form bonds at a local community education center. In Scarborough, a diverse, multicultural neighborhood in eastern Toronto. Bing, a Filipino boy who fled his mentally ill father's violence to come to this town; Sylvie, a girl of Indigenous heritage living in a shelter with her family of four; and Laura, a girl neglected and tossed about by her parents—these three find a safe haven at the education center run by social worker Hina. Despite their difficult circumstances, they nurture a small but meaningful bond... The lead roles are played by three children making their film debut, and the supporting cast includes non-professional actors from Scarborough. The film is based on Canadian author Catherine Hernandez's debut novel "Scarborough," which she adapted from her own experiences. Directors Shasha Nakai and Rich Williamson, highly acclaimed in the documentary field, made their narrative feature debut with this film. It won eight awards, including Best Picture and Best Director, at the 10th Canadian Screen Awards in 2022.
title_norm:まだ君を知らない: A feature film by the filmmaking unit "Shidoromodori," formed by Fukuoka Sawako and Hamada Satsuki, who met at the Nihon University College of Art. The two, only 22 years old at the time of production, poured their heartfelt, down-to-earth feelings into the film, excited by the chance to meet people living their own lives whom they had yet to know. A lost item is brought to a certain coffee shop. It is an object with an air conditioner remote, a hair dye brush, a myoga (Japanese ginger) food sample, and a wrench attached to it—something whose purpose and creator are unknown. At that coffee shop, part-time worker Ando An writes the lunch menu on the blackboard as usual. Meanwhile, office worker Oshimizu Shizue, unaware of such events, orders fried rice at a ramen shop; Hoshino Genki, who works at a massage parlor, plays video games; and university student Takebe Nagi eats her lover's homemade teriyaki amberjack. Fukuoka and Hamada co-directed, with Fukuoka handling the screenplay. Hamada, who is also an actor, plays Ando An, one of the main characters.
title_norm:みつけた、みつけた 分別と多感: A romantic drama adapting Jane Austen's 1811 novel 'Sense and Sensibility,' relocated to modern-day South India. Directed by Rajiv Menon and featuring music by A. R. Rahman, the duo behind 'Mridangam: The Beat of Passion,' this film was released in 2000. In a prestigious family in Tamil Nadu, South India, the reserved and intelligent elder sister Sowmya works as a school principal, while her free-spirited younger sister Meenakshi, who loves poetry and South Indian classical music, lives in a dreamy haze. After their grandfather's death, the family estate passes to a distant relative, forcing the mother and daughters to start a new life in the bustling city of Chennai. Meenakshi meets a young businessman who loves poetry and a former soldier who lost a leg in war and now grows flowers, while Sowmya encounters a man aspiring to be a film director. Through their respective loves and careers, the sisters gradually discover their own paths in life. Tabu, known for 'The Namesake' and 'Life of Pi,' plays Sowmya; Aishwarya Rai Bachchan, known for 'Robot,' plays Meenakshi; and Ajith Kumar, Mammootty, and Abbas co-star.
title_norm:みんな、おしゃべり！: A comedy about a prideful feud between a deaf Japanese family and a Kurdish family, told through Japanese Sign Language and Kurdish. Natsumi Koga lives with her deaf father and younger brother, who run an electronics shop. One day, their family gets into a minor conflict with a Kurdish family living in the same town. Natsumi, who can hear, and Hiwa, the only member of the Kurdish family who speaks Japanese, are drafted as interpreters for their respective families. As they interpret for each other, a bond of trust grows between Natsumi and Hiwa, but the conflict between the two families only deepens. Then one day, a mysterious drawing by Natsumi's younger brother Shun escalates into an incident that engulfs the entire town. Nagisa Nagashima of "The End of Love" plays the protagonist Natsumi. Kazuyoshi Kezuka, a deaf ramen shop owner in Tokyo's Nishi-Nippori, makes his acting debut as Natsumi's father. Hideaki Nasu of the TV drama "Deaf Voice: Court Sign Language Interpreter" and Akito Imai of "The Two Worlds of My Life" play the father's friends. Shunya Itabashi of "Laughing Kaibutsu" plays a community organizer planning a town revitalization project, and Karin Ono of "Animation x Paralympic: Who Is the Hero?" plays a teacher at a school for the deaf. The film is directed by Ken Kawai, known for works like "Nanno-chan's Second World War" and who is himself a CODA (Child of Deaf Adults).
title_norm:みんなのヴァカンス: A youth film directed by Guillaume Brac, known for 'A Summer's Tale' and 'The Gentle Ones,' which tenderly follows young people enjoying their summer vacation amidst the scenic beauty of Southern France. On a summer night by the Seine, the awkward young man Félix falls in love with Alma and spends a dreamlike time with her. However, the next morning, Alma leaves for vacation with her family. Félix, along with his kind best friend Sheriff and the earnest young man Édouard he met through a ride-sharing app, sets off to chase after Alma to the small rural town of Die in Southern France... Following his 2017 film 'July Tales,' Brac made this work with students from the National Academy of Dramatic Arts in France, casting students appearing in their first feature film. It won the Special Prize of the International Federation of Film Critics in the Panorama section of the 70th Berlin International Film Festival in 2020.
title_norm:めがね: On a break from life, Taeko visits a southern seaside town and stays at a strange inn called Hamada. However, in a small beach town with nothing to see or do, she is pushed around by the overly laid-back residents and, unable to bear it, leaves Hamada—but... From the director Naoko Ogigami and star Satomi Kobayashi of "Kamome Diner," the hit film about slow-living daily life set in a Japanese restaurant in Finland, comes a gentle portrayal of people re-examining their lives, this time set on a southern beach.
title_norm:めぐる面影、今、祖父に会う: The feature directorial debut of Huang Wen-ying, who has served as the production designer for many of director Hou Hsiao-hsien’s works. This family drama follows an art director who returns to her family home to care for her father, reflecting on the life of her grandfather who lived through the Japanese colonial era. Fu-yue, a professional in film production design, temporarily leaves the set to return to her hometown and support her ailing father. As she spends her days there, conversations with an architect she contacted for a set build cause her heart to drift back to the era her grandfather once inhabited. Ariel Lin, who rose to fame in the Taiwanese drama version of "Itazura na Kiss," stars as the protagonist Fu-yue. Vic Chou, known for his role as Hanazawa Rui in "Meteor Garden," plays a dual role as both the architect she is drawn to and her grandfather in his youth. Hou Hsiao-hsien serves as producer.
title_norm:やさしい人: A life-affirming drama by rising French director Guillaume Brac, known for 'A Summer's Tale,' depicting an aging, down-and-out musician struggling with a bleak future as he gradually discovers the true meaning of love. Starring Vincent Macaigne, a regular in Brac's films. Maxime, a musician now nearly forgotten by the world, returns to his hometown of Tonnerre in the Burgundy region of France. His single father Claude enjoys outdoor sports, has a vibrant love life, and revels in life, but Maxime, exhausted by city living, has lost his will to live. Then, a young female journalist named Mélodie from a local information magazine comes to interview Maxime. Drawn to her youth and smile, Maxime grows closer to her...
title_norm:ゆきははなである 新野の雪まつり: A documentary by filmmaker Shinkichi Noda, who continually explored the foundations of people's consciousness in rapidly changing Showa-era Japan. This film captures the "Niino Snow Festival" of Nagano Prefecture, seeking to find the enduring spirit of the people within this festival that has continued since medieval times. The Niino Snow Festival has been held since around the 13th century, centered around Izu Shrine and Suwa Shrine in Niino, Anan Town, Nagano Prefecture. People see the falling winter snow as rice flower blossoms, a harbinger of the harvest, and pray for abundant grain. Throughout the night-long festival, masked and costumed performances like "Kyoman" (horse racing), "Okina" (old man), and "Oni" (demon) appear one after another, and the crowd erupts when the spirit of bounty, "Saiho," makes its entrance. Director Noda attempts to read the everyday wishes of farmers for the coming year's production within this sacred festival space. This film is part of the special screening series "Shinkichi Noda Special: Snow is a Flower" (screening from December 6, 2025, at Pole Pole Higashi-Nakano and other theaters nationwide).
title_norm:ゆっくり あるく 川村浪子、84歳のダンス: A documentary following Namiko Kawamura, an 84-year-old expressive artist who continues to work as a dancer and performer. Directed by Toshiko Rin, known for documentary works such as "Jibun, Maru! Ippo no Hanashi," "Nishi Tenka Chaya Ooishi So," and "Blessed." Kawamura has been familiar with dance since childhood, and from the 1970s onward, she explored a unique form of expression incorporating perception and walking in nature. After participating in a workshop by American dancer Anna Halprin in the 1980s, she established a performance of "slow walking"—a forward-moving gait. This act, both a dance and a way of life, has continued for many years. Set in Okinawa, a place Kawamura had long wished to visit, the film explores the thoughts and memories behind her expression through beach performances and interviews. It records her walking and dancing while confronting the time embedded in a land marked by war memories, observing the journey of a woman who has dedicated her life to dance.
title_norm:ゆっくりあるく 川村浪子、84歳のダンス: A documentary following Namiko Kawamura, an 84-year-old expressive artist who continues to work as a dancer and performer. Directed by Toshiko Rin, known for documentary works such as "Jibun, Maru! Ippo no Hanashi," "Nishi Tenka Chaya Ooishi So," and "Blessed." title_norm:ゆれる:
Directed and written by Miwa Nishikawa, who rose to prominence with her 2002 debut *Wild Berries*, this second feature film explores the psychological conflict between two brothers following a fatal fall in a mountain valley. 

Takeru Hayakawa, a successful and busy photographer living in Tokyo, returns to his hometown for the first time in years to attend the first anniversary of his mother’s death. His older brother, Minoru, lives with their father and works at the family gas station, where their childhood friend Chieko Kawabata works part-time. The three of them visit a remote valley filled with childhood memories. While Takeru is off taking photographs, he spots Minoru and Chieko crossing a suspension bridge in the distance—only for Chieko to fall to her death moments later. As a trial unfolds to determine whether the death was an accident or a crime, Takeru finds himself increasingly unsettled as Minoru begins to reveal a side of himself he has never seen before. 

Starring Joe Odagiri as the younger brother Takeru and Teruyuki Kagawa as the older brother Minoru, with Yoko Maki and Masato Ibu in supporting roles. The film was officially selected for the Directors' Fortnight at the 59th Cannes Film Festival in 2006 and received numerous domestic accolades.
title_norm:よあけの焚き火:
Real-life father and son Motonari and Yasunari Ohkura, Noh performers of the Okura school of Kyogen, star as themselves in their first feature film—a human drama that uses traditional performing arts to explore the universal theme of "passing things down." This marks the feature-length directorial debut of Koichi Doi, who served as an assistant director to Kohei Oguri and has worked extensively in television documentaries.

Born into a Kyogen family with a 650-year legacy, Motonari Ohkura brings his 10-year-old son, Yasunari, to a mountain training hall that he himself visited with his father and brother as a child. Just as his father once did for him, Motonari guides his son through the basics, including cleaning the hall, while subjecting him to rigorous training. Bewildered by his father’s uncharacteristic severity, Yasunari nearly gives up on his practice. One day, a local girl named Sakiko visits the hall. Having lost her parents in a disaster years earlier, Sakiko is captivated by the sight of the younger Yasunari training so earnestly. As Yasunari, carrying the weight of a family history within the unbroken lineage of Kyogen, and Sakiko, who has lost her family, share a quiet connection, a small sense of resolve begins to bloom in both their hearts.
title_norm:よき⾕の物語: A new feature film from director José Luis Guerín, who captivated the world with 'In the City of Sylvia' (2007) and was called 'the most outstanding filmmaker in contemporary Spain' by fellow Spanish director Víctor Erice. Despite his sparse output, Guerín continues to create masterpieces that lightly transcend the boundaries between fiction and documentary. This is his long-awaited new film, his first in ten years since 'The Academy of Muses' (2015), now arriving in Japan. To commemorate the release of 'The Good Valley Story,' the beautiful masterpiece 'In the City of Sylvia' will also be revived. Please enjoy Guerín's world on the big screen. The Vallbona district, located on the outskirts of Barcelona, Spain. This place, named 'The Good Valley,' is surrounded by rivers and railway tracks, an isolated land left behind by development, yet it also seems like an ideal paradise blessed with nature so rich it's hard to believe it's near a big city. Here, families who moved in from the mid-20th century live together with a new generation of immigrants who have arrived recently. Although their cultures and lifestyles differ, the children play together in the river, and everyone eats, drinks, sings, and dances well, finding a moment of peace. A new railway expansion plan is proposed for this urban oasis. A residents' information meeting is held, and some people are forced to relocate...
title_norm:よき谷の物語: A new feature film from director José Luis Guerín, who captivated the world with 'In the City of Sylvia' (2007) and was called 'the most outstanding filmmaker in contemporary Spain' by fellow Spanish director Víctor Erice.
