Winner of the Audience Award at the 2023 Locarno Film Festival, and screened in competition at the 76th Cannes Film Festival.
title_norm:オールド・ボーイ: Oh Dae-su, a man living an ordinary life, regains consciousness to find himself locked in a small, confined room. After 15 years of imprisonment without knowing why, he is suddenly released. Who did this?! For what purpose?! With the help of a young woman named Mi-do, Dae-su vows revenge. A mysterious man named Woo-jin appears before him and proposes a deadly "game": Dae-su must uncover the reason for his imprisonment within five days, with both their lives at stake. An unimaginable and terrifying scheme lies behind it all...
title_norm:オーロラの涙: This human drama depicts the loneliness and division in modern society through the daily life of an immigrant woman working in a massive logistics center in Scotland, ultimately finding a faint glimmer of hope. Aurora, a Portuguese immigrant, works as a picker in a huge logistics center on the outskirts of Scotland. Her days are mostly spent walking through countless aisles following scanner instructions and retrieving items from shelves. Conversations with colleagues are limited to brief breaks, and after her shift, she drags her tired body back to a shared house for immigrant workers. Interactions among residents are superficial, relationships never deepen, and her rootless days continue monotonously. One day, Aurora accidentally breaks her smartphone. Losing this modern necessity—her means of workplace communication and her "companion" for passing time—slowly but surely begins to change her daily life. Portuguese-born, Scotland-based Laura Carreira wrote and directed her first feature film based on her own experiences as an immigrant, winning the Best Director Award at the 72nd San Sebastián International Film Festival in 2024.
title_norm:オー・パン・クぺ: The second feature film by Guy Gilles, a director re-evaluated since the 2000s as a 'forgotten master of the French New Wave,' depicting a woman living with the memory of her lover who chose death. The present is shown in black-and-white, and fragments of recollection in color, delicately and melancholically portraying the memory of love and the pain of absence. Jeanne lives with the memory of her deceased lover Jean. Jean rejected social order and the bourgeois world, found no place in the Beat generation, and chose death. Unaware of his death, Jeanne feels him always by her side, existing like a ghost. Masha Meril, known for 'A Time for Loving' and 'Belle de Jour,' plays the protagonist Jeanne, and Patrick Jouané, an actor who met Guy Gilles during the filming of 'Le Rempart des Béguines' and became an irreplaceable presence in his life and work, plays the deceased lover Jean. The film was released in Japanese theaters in April 2026.
title_norm:オー・パン・クペ: The second feature film by Guy Gilles, a director re-evaluated since the 2000s as a 'forgotten master of the French New Wave,' depicting a woman living with the memory of her lover who chose death. The present is shown in black-and-white, and fragments of recollection in color, delicately and melancholically portraying the memory of love and the pain of absence. Jeanne lives with the memory of her deceased lover Jean. Jean rejected social order and the bourgeois world, found no place in the Beat generation, and chose death. Unaware of his death, Jeanne feels him always by her side, existing like a ghost. Masha Meril, known for 'A Time for Loving' and 'Belle de Jour,' plays the protagonist Jeanne, and Patrick Jouané, an actor who met Guy Gilles during the filming of 'Le Rempart des Béguines' and became an irreplaceable presence in his life and work, plays the deceased lover Jean. The film was released in Japanese theaters in April 2026.
title_norm:カインド・ハート: A suspense comedy that follows the trail of a serial murder spree by a young man burning with ambition and a thirst for revenge, laced with biting black humor. One of the 'Ealing Comedies,' a series of comedy films produced at Ealing Studios in the UK from the late 1930s to the mid-1950s, directed by Robert Hamer, known for 'It Always Rains on Sunday.' The story is told in flashback form as Louis, a young man of aristocratic blood from the D'Ascoyne family, writes his memoirs in his prison cell, recounting how he systematically murders his relatives to avenge his mother's disownment and reclaim his status. The renowned actor Alec Guinness, known for his role as Obi-Wan Kenobi in 'Star Wars' and 'The Bridge on the River Kwai,' plays all eight members of the D'Ascoyne family who are killed by Louis. Dennis Price plays the protagonist Louis, and Joan Greenwood leaves a strong impression as the cold, calculating heroine. This film is part of the special screening series 'The Golden Age of British Ealing Comedies' (June 20–July 17, 2026, at Shinjuku K's Cinema).
title_norm:カウント・ベイシー: A documentary exploring the life and music of Count Basie, the American jazz pianist who built the golden age of swing jazz. Starting his career as a jazz pianist in his twenties, Count Basie met many top musicians in Kansas City, Missouri, joined the Blue Devils in 1928, and later honed his skills with the Bennie Moten Orchestra before forming his own Basie Orchestra. Fusing jazz and blues and revolutionizing rhythm, he was hailed as the 'King of Swing' and remains beloved by jazz fans and musicians across generations in Japan. The film focuses not only on his public triumphs but also on his private life, which Basie rarely discussed. Through home videos, photo albums, and letters from his family, it reveals his love for his daughter Diane, born with cerebral palsy, and his wife Catherine, who supported the African American civil rights movement. Featuring interviews with current Basie Orchestra members, friends like Quincy Jones and Annie Ross, and archival materials, the documentary traces his legacy and the turbulent social history of 20th-century America. Directed by British filmmaker Jeremy Marre, known for many music documentaries including 'Roots Rock Reggae.'
title_norm:カニングハム: A documentary commemorating the 100th anniversary of the birth of Merce Cunningham, who fundamentally redefined the concept of dance. Active as a choreographer and dancer in the United States from the late 1930s, Merce Cunningham shocked the world with performances that opened up new frontiers in dance, through his groundbreaking philosophy that 'music and choreography exist independently' and his incorporation of chance into choreography. The film explores Cunningham's philosophy and voice through never-before-seen archival footage, and delves into the behind-the-scenes collaborations with his lifelong partner, avant-garde music master John Cage, and 20th-century representative artists such as Robert Rauschenberg and Andy Warhol. Furthermore, 14 representative works created over approximately 30 years, from his unknown days in 1944 to his establishment of fame in 1972, are re-staged by contemporary dancers. It captures the dynamism of space and body in extraordinary locations such as building rooftops and forests. The film will have its first theatrical release in Japan as part of the special screening project 'Performance Art: A Film Festival Around Body and Space' (starting August 1, 2026, at Eurospace and other theaters nationwide).
title_norm:カミング・ホーム: A human drama starring the acclaimed actor Ben Kingsley, humorously depicting a lonely elderly man who, after getting caught up in a bizarre commotion with his neighbors, rediscovers the joy of life. Milton, a 79-year-old man living in a small town in western Pennsylvania, continues to live alone despite his daughter Denise worrying about his early symptoms of dementia. One night, an unidentified flying object from the sky crashes into Milton's yard, shaking his peaceful daily life. When no one around him takes him seriously, Milton shares the secret of the flying object with his neighbors Sandy and Joyce, who are around his age and also witnessed it. The three, each carrying their own loneliness, rediscover the forgotten joys of life and face their futures. Harriet Sansom Harris ("The Bodybuilder") plays Sandy, Jane Curtin ("Coneheads") plays Joyce, and Zoe Winters (series "Succession") plays Milton's daughter Denise. The director is Mark Turtletaub, known as a producer for "Little Miss Sunshine" and "Loving."
title_norm:カラオケ行こ！: Okasatomi, the choir club president, is suddenly invited to karaoke by yakuza member Narita Kyoji, who asks for singing lessons. To avoid the 'terror' that awaits whoever comes in last at the gang's karaoke contest, Kyoji must improve at all costs. His chosen song is X JAPAN's 'Kurenai.' Satomi reluctantly agrees to coach him, but in time, their relationship begins to change... What fate awaits Satomi? And can Kyoji escape the bottom spot?
title_norm:カルロス・カイザー サッカー史上最も奇妙な成功者: A documentary exploring the life of Carlos Henrique Raposo, known as "Kaiser," who was dubbed "the greatest footballer who never played football." In the 1980s and 90s, before information was readily available on the internet, Kaiser, despite being a poor footballer, used his cunning conversational skills and connections to continually secure contracts with Brazilian and foreign clubs, building a career as a professional player. Once signed, he would consistently avoid playing in official matches by faking injuries or causing trouble during training. He further deceived those around him for years by using fake mobile phones to simulate offers from overseas clubs and agents. After ending his 26-year career in 2003, Kaiser began telling his story in 2010, but astonishingly, no coach, player, or reporter had ever exposed his lies. The film recounts Kaiser's many anecdotes through testimonies from Kaiser himself and football figures from that era, along with archival footage, photographs, and reenactments. The director is British documentary filmmaker Louis Myles.
title_norm:カーンターラ 神の降臨: A legendary suspense-action film set in South India, centered on the ancient ritual of 'Bhuta Kola' (spirit worship). It powerfully depicts the strange fate of a land protected by divine grace and became a long-running hit in India. About 170 years ago, a vast forest was granted to the indigenous people by the oracle of the god Panjuruli. The village of Kadu Bettur has long performed the Bhuta Kola ritual and maintained peace through divine protection, even when landlords tried to reclaim the land. However, the newly appointed forest officer Murali attempts to incorporate the villagers' land into a state-designated protected forest. As the village faces a crisis of survival, Shiva, a buffalo race champion whose father was a Bhuta Kola performer, opposes the forest department to protect the village's peace, leading to an incident. Rishab Shetty, who has an unusual background of juggling jobs in water vending and real estate before entering the film industry, directed, wrote, and starred in the film, passionately playing Shiva, the village's biggest rogue.
title_norm:ガガ 英雄たちに栄光あれ: One of four dark sci-fi works by Piotr Szulkin, a pioneer of dystopian science fiction in Poland, created under the strict censorship of the socialist regime in the late 1970s and 1980s. With a style blending fierce satire and extreme surrealism, the film depicts the miserable existence of people living under corrupt power and bureaucracy. A man trapped on a giant space station is forced, like other prisoners, to volunteer for exploration of a distant planet. Landing on Planet Australia 458, he is welcomed as a hero, but soon realizes that freedom comes at a high price. His violent life is broadcast live for the entertainment of the planet's inhabitants. The film had its Japanese theatrical premiere in 2026 as part of the special screening series "Polish Dark Sci-Fi: The End of Civilization Tetralogy" (starting February 21, 2026, at Theater Image Forum).
title_norm:ガザからの声 episode1 「アハマドの物語」／ガザか: Ahmad al-Gharban, from Beit Lahia in northern Gaza, survived an Israeli military attack on March 22, but lost both his legs and his fingers. His twin brother Muhammad, his uncle, and his six-year-old cousin were killed. Ahmad had dreamed of becoming a performer, having studied at a circus school alongside his late brother. The displacement camp where the family now lives is situated on the former site of the Islamic University of Gaza, a place where drones circle overhead day and night.
title_norm:ガタカ: A sci-fi suspense film starring Ethan Hawke, Uma Thurman, and Jude Law. In a near future where 'valids' born through genetic engineering dominate society, Vincent, born naturally, lives a life of discrimination as an 'invalid.' He has dreamed of becoming an astronaut since childhood, but it is a profession only permitted for valids. One day, through a DNA broker, Vincent purchases the valid identity of Jerome, a former swimmer now paralyzed from the waist down. Posing as Jerome, Vincent joins the space corporation 'Gattaca' and, through sheer effort, is eventually selected as an astronaut for a Titan exploration mission, but... This is the directorial and screenwriting debut of Andrew Niccol.
title_norm:ガリバーの宇宙旅行: Toei Animation's first sci-fi feature. It is also the first feature-length film solely directed by Kuroda Yoshiro, whose highly designed compositions and musical style highlight the allegorical world. Ambitious meta-cinematic structures are employed, marking a breakthrough for a new generation at Toei Animation. The princess's secret revealed at the end carries a critique of civilization, an idea proposed by then-animator Hayao Miyazaki.
title_norm:ガーゴイル: After becoming a test subject for a new drug, Core (Béatrice Dalle) develops an uncontrollable urge to kill her sexual partners during intercourse. American doctor Shane (Vincent Gallo) travels to France to find her, but...
title_norm:キッスで殺せ！: One night, private detective Mike Hammer picks up a woman named Christina and lets her into his car, but is suddenly attacked by three men and loses consciousness. When he comes to, Mike finds himself in a hospital bed. According to his secretary Velda, Mike and Christina were driven into a river along with the car, and Christina died. Sensing something behind it all, Mike begins to investigate Christina's background.
title_norm:キャット・ピープルの呪い: The directorial debut of Robert Wise, the master behind "West Side Story" and "The Sound of Music," made in 1944. This is a sequel to the cult horror film "Cat People" directed by Jacques Tourneur. A lonely, imaginative girl named Amy finds a beautiful ring in a dilapidated old house in her neighborhood. When she returns home and makes a wish on the ring, a beautiful woman named Irena appears before her. Amy becomes friends with Irena, whom only she can see, but...
title_norm:キャトルミューティ玲子: A comedy entertainment that depicts human foolishness through the figure of a private detective, shy in love, who falls for a woman during an investigation. Arata Yamaguchi, an actor who has also directed short films, serves as director, screenwriter, editor, and lead actor. Private detective Suzuya takes on jobs such as searching for runaway pets and investigating infidelity. One day, Suzuya receives a strange request and proceeds with the investigation, but is toyed with by a friend behaving inexplicably, a carefree boss, and the irresistible charm of a woman named Reiko. The "Cattle Mutilation" in the title is taken from the strange phenomenon "cattle mutilation," in which livestock believed to have been taken by UFOs are found with their internal organs and blood removed. Although never theatrically released, it won the Audience Award with the highest score among the 16 films screened at the event "CINEMA JAM vol.1" (August 16-22, 2025, at K's cinema in Tokyo), which screened energetic works on a daily rotation. This earned it the right to a solo theatrical release at the mini theater "Stranger" in Kikukawa, Tokyo, where it was released in September 2025. In August 2026, it will be released sequentially nationwide at K's cinema and other venues.
title_norm:キュア: A masterpiece of psychological suspense in Japanese film history, directed by the brilliant Kiyoshi Kurosawa and starring Kōji Yakusho. A series of bizarre murders occur one after another. While the perpetrators of each case have no connection, the victims all have an X-shaped cut from their neck to their chest, all the assailants are arrested near the crime scene immediately after the incident, and none of the killers had a clear intent to murder just before the act. Detective Takabe, whose wife suffers from a mental illness, is assigned to the investigation but struggles to find a common thread among the perpetrators. Around the same time, a murder with the same modus operandi occurs on a beach near Tokyo, and a young man named Mamiya, who has no memory of being near the scene, is taken into custody. Takabe discovers that Mamiya is a former medical student and realizes he has been using hypnosis to trigger the series of events, but...
title_norm:キラークイーン phantom school:
This is the sequel to the indie sci-fi action film "Killer Queen Beyond School," which followed the battles of a high school girl whose hands were transformed into tentacles by a parasitic alien. Introducing the new element of the multiverse, the film depicts the next chapter in protagonist Reina’s fight.

Reina Gouriki, who gained special powers after an encounter with an extraterrestrial, and her best friend Anzu Mikawa find themselves visiting entrepreneur Annie Tachibana after a streamer friend leaks footage of Reina in combat. However, Annie is secretly researching the artificial creation of multiverses, and the three are accidentally pulled into an alternate dimension. There, they learn of a "phantom school" that may hold the key to returning home, but during their search, Anzu becomes possessed by the vengeful spirit of Annie's deceased lover.

Saraha returns to the lead role alongside Aiko and other original cast members, joined by a new supporting cast. Director Yusuke Takahashi—who also serves as screenwriter, cinematographer, editor, and VFX supervisor—further deepens the unique "tentacles x youth x sci-fi" world established in the first film.
title_norm:キラー・オブ・シープ: The feature debut of Charles Burnett, a filmmaker who quietly revolutionized American cinema by depicting the daily lives and humanity of African Americans, released in 1977. It portrays the everyday existence of African American workers living on the fringes of Los Angeles with a realistic gaze and poetic visual beauty. Set in the Watts district of Los Angeles in the early 1970s, still bearing the scars of the Watts riots. Stan works at a sheep slaughterhouse to support his wife and two children, living an empty daily life. Exhausted physically and mentally by labor and poverty, he withdraws into himself, while his wife grows increasingly lonely. Directed by Burnett as his graduate thesis film while a student at UCLA Film School, it was shot in Watts using a mostly amateur cast of people he knew. Long unreleased due to music copyright issues, it finally had a theatrical release in the US in 2007. The 4K restoration completed in 2025 replaces the music in the final scene with Dinah Washington's "Unforgettable," as Burnett originally intended. It won the FIPRESCI Prize at the Forum section of the 31st Berlin International Film Festival in 1981. In Japan, it will have its first theatrical release in the 4K restored version as part of the special screening series "Charles Burnett: Everyday Blues" (starting February 7, 2026, at Theater Image Forum).
title_norm:キングダム 魂の決戦: Set during China's Spring and Autumn period, this is the fifth live-action film adaptation of Yasuhisa Hara's popular manga series 'Kingdom,' depicting the grand story of Shin, a boy who dreams of becoming the world's greatest general, and the young king Ying Zheng, who aims to unify China. This film adapts the beloved 'Coalition Army Arc' from the original manga, where Qin clashes with the six other states. Three years after the Battle of Mayang, where Qin lost the great general Wang Qi, Shin, who has inherited Wang Qi's will and continued to grow, has been promoted to commander of a thousand men. Meanwhile, under the strategy of Zhao's prime minister Li Mu, all states except Qin unite to form a 'Coalition Army' of 500,000 troops, launching an invasion of Qin. At the capital city of Xianyang's palace, Ying Zheng and his court scramble to respond, but faced with an unprecedented force, Qin is pushed to the brink of national collapse. Shin, along with fellow young generals Meng Tian and Wang Ben, heads to Hangu Pass, the gateway to Qin, where representative Qin generals such as Biao Gong, Meng Wu, Teng, Wang Jian, and Huan Qi gather. On the other side, the Coalition Army, led by Lord Chunshen of Chu, assembles powerful warriors from various states, including the fierce Zhao general Wan Ji, who harbors a grudge against Qin for trampling his homeland. Familiar series cast members return, including Kento Yamazaki as Shin, Ryō Yoshizawa as Ying Zheng, and Shun Oguri as Li Mu. New additions to the lavish cast include Jun Shison as Meng Tian, Fūju Kamio as Wang Ben, Kenji Sakaguchi as Huan Qi, and Takumi Saitō as Lord Chunshen. Director Shinsuke Sato, who has helmed all previous films in the series, returns, and original manga author Yasuhisa Hara, who has been involved in the script since the first film, also wrote the screenplay for this installment.
title_norm:キン肉マン 晴れ姿! 正義超人／キン肉マン ニューヨーク危: The fifth theatrical film of the TV anime in which Kinnikuman, prince of Kinniku Planet, battles evil choujins in pro wrestling. When lightning suddenly strikes Toei Uzumasa Movie Village, Kinnikuman time-travels to the Edo period, and to save a princess, he and the Seigi Choujins face off against Shuten Doji. Directed by Takenori Kawata, who also served as series director in the middle of the series, this work is heavy on comedy packed with period drama gags.
title_norm:キートン将軍: Comedy king Buster Keaton produced, directed, and starred in this action comedy inspired by a real train robbery during the American Civil War era. Engineer Johnny Gray deeply loves both his locomotive, "The General," and his beloved Annabelle. One day, however, "The General" is stolen by Union spies, and Annabelle is trapped in the boxcar. Johnny pursues the General on another locomotive, but unwittingly finds himself deep in Union territory... Also known under the Japanese titles "Keaton's Great Train Chase" and "Keaton's Great Train Robbery."
title_norm:ギデンズ・コーの功夫: A wuxia fantasy action film directed by Taiwanese director Giddens Ko of 'The Secrets in the Lattice' and 'You Are the Apple of My Eye,' starring Ko Chen-tung, who collaborated with Ko on those two previous films. Director Giddens Ko, also active as a novelist, adapts his own internet-published novel 'Kung Fu' for the screen, weaving in homages to Hong Kong and Taiwanese wuxia films from the 1980s and 90s throughout. Underachieving high school student Yuan Zai and his best friend A Yi encounter a mysterious drifter, Huang Jun, who has awakened from a 500-year slumber. Witnessing Huang Jun's overwhelming martial arts prowess as a kung fu master, Yuan Zai and A Yi become his disciples. Their classmate Yi Jing, on whom Yuan Zai has a secret crush, also joins their training. They soon learn of the centuries-old feud between Huang Jun and his junior disciple Lan Jin, and uncover a momentous secret hidden within 'kung fu' that could shake heaven and earth. Ko Chen-tung plays Yuan Zai, Berant Zhu of 'Black Education' plays A Yi, Wang Jing of 'The Secrets in the Lattice' and 'The Return of the Condor Heroes' plays Yi Jing, veteran actor Tai Li-len plays the mysterious kung fu master Huang Jun, and Liu Kuan-ting of 'The Girl Who Robbed Time' plays Huang Jun's nemesis Lan Jin.
title_norm:ギデンズ・コーの功夫（カンフー）: A wuxia fantasy action film directed by Taiwanese director Giddens Ko of 'The Secrets in the Lattice' and 'You Are the Apple of My Eye,' starring Ko Chen-tung, who collaborated with Ko on those two previous films. Director Giddens Ko, also active as a novelist, adapts his own internet-published novel 'Kung Fu' for the screen, weaving in homages to Hong Kong and Taiwanese wuxia films from the 1980s and 90s throughout. Underachieving high school student Yuan Zai and his best friend A Yi encounter a mysterious drifter, Huang Jun, who has awakened from a 500-year slumber. Witnessing Huang Jun's overwhelming martial arts prowess as a kung fu master, Yuan Zai and A Yi become his disciples. Their classmate Yi Jing, on whom Yuan Zai has a secret crush, also joins their training. They soon learn of the centuries-old feud between Huang Jun and his junior disciple Lan Jin, and uncover a momentous secret hidden within 'kung fu' that could shake heaven and earth. Ko Chen-tung plays Yuan Zai, Berant Zhu of 'Black Education' plays A Yi, Wang Jing of 'The Secrets in the Lattice' and 'The Return of the Condor Heroes' plays Yi Jing, veteran actor Tai Li-len plays the mysterious kung fu master Huang Jun, and Liu Kuan-ting of 'The Girl Who Robbed Time' plays Huang Jun's nemesis Lan Jin.
title_norm:クニコからはじまる話: A woman armed with a knife breaks into the office of a paranormal documentary production company. After injuring an employee, she reveals her motive: to "save humanity." She is apparently obsessed with a conspiracy theory claiming that "unless a certain videotape is returned to its rightful place, the human race will perish." The production crew tracks down the man spreading these theories online. He reveals that the video was once submitted to the "Shi-gazo" series and is a clip so terrifying it surpasses even the legendary "Kuniko." The crew unearths the tape and sets out to uncover the true identity of what is captured on screen. However, this was merely the entrance to a labyrinth with no exit, where countless horrors writhe in the shadows...
title_norm:クベーラ:
Set in a Mumbai swirling with greed, this Indian crime action thriller depicts a homeless young man caught in a conspiracy as he stands up against a national-level evil. To monopolize the vast oil rights lying in the Bay of Bengal, wealthy Mumbai businessman Neeraj Mithra teams up with former CBI (Central Bureau of Investigation) ace investigator Deepak Tej to plot a massive money-laundering scheme. As their cover, they choose the nameless homeless—those abandoned by society. Deva Kallam, a simple-hearted young man living as a beggar in the slums, unknowingly finds himself burdened with immense wealth, becoming a target for the organization's assassins. Driven into a corner, he plunges into a brutal battle for survival.

Director Sekhar Kammula, previously acclaimed for his delicate human and romantic dramas, delivers a profound and thrilling portrayal of the dark underbelly of a society ruled by violence and greed. Internationally active actor Dhanush, known for *The Gray Man* and *The Extraordinary Journey of the Fakir*, stars in the lead role, delivering a powerful performance as Deva, the simple young man living in the shadows of society. Nagarjuna Akkineni of *Brahmāstra* plays former CBI agent Deepak, while Rashmika Mandanna of the *Pushpa* duology portrays the heroine Samaira, who holds the key to the story. The title "Kubera" refers to the god of wealth and treasure in Indian mythology.
title_norm:クリーデンス・クリアウォーター・リヴァイヴァル トラヴェリ: A film documenting and screening the legendary 1970 London performance of the American rock band Creedence Clearwater Revival (CCR). In 1970, at the height of their popularity, CCR embarked on their first and only European tour. The highlight of the tour was their performance at the Royal Albert Hall in London on April 14, where CCR aimed to challenge The Beatles, whose record sales were the highest in the world at the time, by performing in their home territory. However, four days before the performance, news of The Beatles' breakup was reported. Despite this, CCR delivered a powerful, all-or-nothing performance, making the Royal Albert Hall concert one of the greatest live shows in rock history. The complete footage of the London performance, discovered after 50 years, has been restored in 4K, and the film traces their trajectory, interweaving footage capturing the band's daily life, interviews with members, and early live performances. Directed by Bob Smeaton of 'The Beatles Anthology,' with narration by actor Jeff Bridges.
title_norm:クルージング: A crime suspense film directed by William Friedkin, who won an Academy Award for "The French Connection" and had a worldwide hit with "The Exorcist," released in 1980, set against the backdrop of New York City's underground gay culture at the time. A series of murders targeting only gay men occurs in New York at night. Police detective Burns, given a secret mission, goes undercover in S&M clubs frequented by gay men, pretending to be homosexual. Wandering the depths of male sexuality night after night, Burns wears himself down both physically and mentally, finally finding a clue to the killer... Based on actual murders of gay men that occurred between 1973 and 1979, Friedkin wrote the script after experiences including meeting with a suspect who had also appeared in "The Exorcist." Considered the first Hollywood film to openly depict male same-sex S&M sex, it faced protests from the time of its announcement through its release for allegedly promoting homophobia, and was not a commercial success. However, since the 2000s, it has been re-evaluated as a valuable record of gay culture before the global spread of HIV.
title_norm:グリム童話 金の鳥: A classic fairy tale produced for theatrical release after a long absence. The story follows three princes in search of a golden bird, with the addition of a witch and robots. Directed by Hirata Toshio with character designs by Ōhashi Manabu, both former Toei Dōga staff, the actual production was handled by Madhouse. The rounded, line-suppressed characters and soft art style make it approachable, and the musical animation by Nankei Kōji is also enjoyable.
title_norm:グレイ・ミッション: To confront the dictator Salazar, who vanished after stealing one billion dollars, sharp lawyer Rachel hires two professionals: the brilliant Sid (Henry Cavill), a former Royal Marine, and Bronco (Jake Gyllenhaal), a fighting machine from the U.S. Navy. The team uses strategic warfare to bring down the dictator's empire, but just as the mission is about to succeed, Rachel is kidnapped by Salazar. Sid and Bronco infiltrate the isolated island controlled by Salazar and face a dangerous battle—.
title_norm:グレン・ミラー物語: Young trombonist Glenn Miller was always in search of a new sound. He joined a prestigious orchestra but left to focus on arranging. The turning point in his music came from his beloved wife Helen. Following her advice, he formed his own band and eventually achieved unprecedented popularity and fame. However, when World War II began, he volunteered for the Air Force. In late 1944, the plane carrying Glenn Miller disappeared over the English Channel... An emotional musical film, with numerous hit songs coloring the love and bond between the couple played by James Stewart and June Allyson!
title_norm:コット、はじまりの夏: Set in early 1980s Ireland, this human drama depicts a special summer vacation experienced by a 9-year-old girl. It won the Grand Prix in the International Generation section for films starring children at the 72nd Berlin International Film Festival and was nominated for the International Feature Film Award at the 95th Academy Awards. In 1981, in a rural Irish town, a quiet girl named Cott, who lives silently within a large family, spends her summer vacation at the lush green farm of the Kinsella couple. Initially confused by the unfamiliar life, Cott receives abundant love from Sean and Eileen and, as she carefully experiences each moment, comes to feel a joy in living she had never known before. Catherine Clinch, in her debut role, delicately portrays the protagonist Cott with overwhelming transparency and presence, winning the IFTA Award (Irish Film & Television Academy Award) for Best Actress at the youngest age of 12. Based on the novel "Foster" by Irish writer Claire Keegan, this is the first feature-length fiction film directed and written by Colm Bairéad, who has previously focused on children's perspectives and family bonds in his documentary works.
title_norm:コードギアス 亡国のアキト 最終章「愛シキモノタチヘ」: The final chapter of "Code Geass: Akito the Exiled," a side story to the hit anime "Code Geass: Lelouch of the Rebellion." The final battle unfolds, featuring the "Alexander Liberté," an upgraded version of the Type-01 Knightmare Frame piloted by the protagonist Akito. Although Yukiya’s bomb successfully reduced the Euro Britannian forces by a third, the wZERO unit remains at a severe disadvantage, besieged at Castle Weisswolf. With Ashley—a former enemy—now fighting by his side, Akito prepares for the ultimate showdown against his rampaging brother, Shin. Facing the final conflict, Akito cuts his hair as a sign of his resolve and entrusts it to Leila.
title_norm:ゴジラ: A landmark tokusatsu kaiju film produced and released by Toho in 1954. Ships are sinking one after another in the Pacific Ocean. The few survivors report sightings of a giant monster. An investigation team formed by paleontologist Dr. Yamane, his daughter and assistant Emiko, and her fiancé Hideto Ogata, head of a salvage company, is dispatched to Odo Island near the incident site, where the monster eventually appears. Named "Godzilla" after an old island legend, the monster is believed to be an ancient creature that survived in secret, awakened by the radiation from repeated hydrogen bomb tests, and countermeasures are devised. However, humans are helpless against its immense power, and Godzilla lands in Tokyo, turning the city into a sea of fire. Meanwhile, Dr. Yamane's beloved student, scientist Serizawa, has realized a terrible invention that could be effective against Godzilla. Fearing its future misuse, Serizawa hesitates to use it... A Hollywood version directed by Roland Emmerich was also produced in 1998. To commemorate the 60th anniversary in 2014 and the production/release of the second Hollywood version "GODZILLA" (directed by Gareth Edwards), this original film was revived as the "Godzilla 60th Anniversary Digital Remastered Version."
title_norm:ゴダール・ソシアリスム: A visual poem by French master Jean-Luc Godard, depicting modern Europe with overwhelming visual beauty and masterful editing. It is Godard's first feature film shot entirely in digital, his first in six years since 'Our Music.' Set on a luxury cruise ship touring the Mediterranean, it consists of three movements: the first movement 'Such Things' depicts human drama over gold lost during the Spanish Civil War; the second movement 'Where to, Europe' is a political comedy about a family living in the French countryside; and the third movement 'We Humans' explores history and culture across six locations related to human history, using countless quotations and collages. Utilizing various video formats and freely incorporating images, words, sounds, and even digital noise, it is depicted with overwhelming density and speed, full of rebellious spirit. Musician Patti Smith, guitarist Lenny Kaye, and philosopher Alain Badiou appear as themselves. Screened as part of the special screening series 'Jean-Luc Godard in the 21st Century: Our Films 2001-2010' (starting June 20, 2026, at Theater Image Forum Shibuya and other locations nationwide).
title_norm:ゴーイング マイ ホーム 第1話 第2話: The first continuous TV drama (10 episodes) helmed by Kore-eda, who considers TV dramas a more formative experience than films. It includes devices that suggest connections to his past films, such as casting and character settings. It was screened at the International Film Festival Rotterdam in 2013.
title_norm:ゴーイング マイ ホーム 第3話 第4話: Ryota, troubled by the small triangular hat he found in the forest, discovers a notebook that appears to have been written by Eisuke. It is a notebook recording the places where Kuna is said to appear. Guided by his father's words, Ryota walks around town and hears an unexpected fact from Naho, whom he meets by chance.
title_norm:ゴーイング マイ ホーム 第5話 第6話: Ryota has returned to work, but his own project is progressing smoothly under his subordinate's leadership, and he is increasingly losing his presence. Meanwhile, as Eisuke diligently pursues rehabilitation, Toshiko grows more suspicious about the relationship between her husband and Naho's mother.
title_norm:ゴーイング マイ ホーム 第7話 第8話: Eisuke is discharged from the hospital and returns home. The family gathers around the dinner table for the first time in a while to celebrate his homecoming. Amid this, Ryota confronts Eisuke about a photo of a plot of land for sale that was tucked inside a notebook, but he is confused and angered by his father's response.
title_norm:ゴーイング マイ ホーム 第9話 第10話: On the day of the event to search for Kuna, as the group searches for her in the forest, the feelings each of them has been harboring gradually come to the surface. As the event draws to a close, Ryota receives a phone call from Toshiko.
title_norm:ゴースト・オブ・ウエノ: Set in Ueno Park in Tokyo, this human mystery, a Japan-China-Korea co-production, explores human connections while focusing on "disappearance" as a way of life. A homeless man known as "Gojo" in Ueno has died. No one knows his real name, what he did in life, or why he ended up in a tent in the park. Satsuki, a social worker, with the help of Toshi, a man living in the park after losing his wife, searches through the homeless network to uncover Gojo's identity, using his diary as a clue. Eventually, the existence of a woman comes to light, and it's revealed that Gojo had cut ties with his family. This fact also profoundly shakes Satsuki's own life. Kadowaki Mugi stars as Satsuki, a social worker carrying a certain loss from her own past, and Takenaka Naoto co-stars as Toshi, a homeless man who accompanies Satsuki. The director and screenwriter is Wang Qii, who spent his childhood in Japan and studied filmmaking in the UK. Wayne Wang, known for directing "Smoke" and "The Joy Luck Club," is credited as co-writer and project planner.
title_norm:ゴールデンカムイ 網走監獄襲撃編: The second film in the live-action adaptation of Satoru Noda's popular manga "Golden Kamuy," serving as a sequel to the 2024 film and the WOWOW drama series "Golden Kamuy: The Hunt of the Tattooed Prisoners in Hokkaido." Former soldier Saichi Sugimoto, known as "Immortal Sugimoto," learns of a vast gold hoard stolen from the Ainu people. The mysterious culprit, "Noppera-bo," hid the gold before his capture, tattooing the locations on the bodies of prisoners and engineering their escape. The tattoos form a single code when combined across 24 men. Sugimoto meets Ainu girl Asirpa, whose father was killed by the gold thief, and they join forces. Meanwhile, Lieutenant Tsurumi of the Imperial Japanese Army's 7th Division, who aims to conquer Hokkaido, and Toshizo Hijikata, who should have died in the Boshin War, also seek the gold, sparking a fierce battle for the tattooed prisoners. The stage moves to Abashiri Prison, where Noppera-bo is incarcerated. Returning cast members include Kento Yamazaki as Sugimoto and Anna Yamada as Asirpa, with new additions: Yu Inaba as Private Usami of the 7th Division, Sohma Wada as Chief Guard Kadokura, and Jun Kunimura as Navy Rear Admiral Heiji Koido, father of "Satsuma's Prince" Otonoshin Koido. Directed by Kenji Katagiri, who helmed episodes 3 and 5-8 of the drama series.
title_norm:サイボーグ009怪獣戦争: During the early days of TV anime, orders were unstable, so to secure steady theatrical commissions, a medium-length film series called "B Works" was planned (conventional feature-length films were called "A Works"). Based on Shotaro Ishinomori's popular sci-fi manga, the film employed TV anime staff such as Keiichiro Kimura, the animation director of "Rainbow Sentai Robin," and utilized TV production efficiency techniques. While there were changes from the original manga, such as turning one of the characters into a child, the battles unfold across land, sea, and air, offering high entertainment value, and the composition shows awareness of widescreen framing.
title_norm:サイボーグ009／サイボーグ009 怪獣戦争: During the early days of TV anime, orders were unstable, so to secure steady theatrical commissions, a medium-length film series called "B Works" was planned (conventional feature-length films were called "A Works"). Based on Shotaro Ishinomori's popular sci-fi manga, the film employed TV anime staff such as Keiichiro Kimura, the animation director of "Rainbow Sentai Robin," and utilized TV production efficiency techniques. While there were changes from the original manga, such as turning one of the characters into a child, the battles unfold across land, sea, and air, offering high entertainment value, and the composition shows awareness of widescreen framing.
title_norm:サイボーグ００９ 怪獣戦争: During the early days of TV anime, orders were unstable, so to secure steady theatrical commissions, a medium-length film series called "B Works" was planned (conventional feature-length films were called "A Works"). Based on Shotaro Ishinomori's popular sci-fi manga, the film employed TV anime staff such as Keiichiro Kimura, the animation director of "Rainbow Sentai Robin," and utilized TV production efficiency techniques. While there were changes from the original manga, such as turning one of the characters into a child, the battles unfold across land, sea, and air, offering high entertainment value, and the composition shows awareness of widescreen framing.
title_norm:サスペリア: 'Never watch it alone—' This famous tagline became a buzzword at the time of release. A masterpiece often talked about to this day, where vivid colors, the eerie sound featuring Goblin, and extreme direction form a trinity that creates a unique tension. It was a hit in Japan in 1977, ranking in the top ten among foreign films released that year. Its influence led to the Japanese release of an unrelated 1975 film by Argento as 'Suspiria Part 2' the following year. For the director, this is the first installment of the 'Three Mothers' trilogy, followed by 'Inferno' and 'Mother of Tears.' Suzy, who has come from America to study at a German ballet school, witnesses a woman disappearing while muttering something on the night she arrives at the dormitory. Shortly after, the woman is killed by someone. After enrolling, Suzy undergoes rigorous training but begins to experience physical abnormalities, fainting, and along with her friend Sara, hears strange groans and footsteps in the dormitory. One night, feeling pursued by someone, Sara flees alone through the dormitory...
title_norm:サスペリアpart2: The splendid murder aesthetics of Dario Argento, the emperor of Italian horror, explode throughout the film. In Japan, after the huge success of 'Suspiria' (1977) with the clever tagline 'Never watch it alone,' this film was given a Japanese title to ride on that wave and was released in theaters, but it is actually unrelated in content and was made before that film. A shocking work that weaves the mystery of a series of gruesome murders with Argento's signature gorgeous and shocking visual beauty. Starring David Hemmings from 'Blow-Up' and Daria Nicolodi, Argento's good partner both publicly and privately. At the European Parapsychology Conference held in Rome, a telepathic woman named Helga, while demonstrating her abilities on stage, senses someone's murderous intent and becomes hysterical. She declares that a person who has committed brutal murders is in the audience. Later, Helga is brutally murdered in her room. Mark, a British pianist who happens to arrive at the scene and witnesses the murder and a suspect, teams up with journalist Jenna to investigate the mystery, but the truth they ultimately uncover is beyond imagination.
title_norm:サナトリウム: Screening at EU Film Days 2026 (Tokyo: May 16–29 at Theater Image Forum, May 19–24 at the National Film Archive of Japan; Nagoya: June 6–19 at Nagoya Kinema Noi; also held in Hiroshima, Kyoto, and Fukuoka).
title_norm:サムライ 4kレストア: Hitman Jeff carries out his usual assignment, but as he leaves the scene, a pianist catches a glimpse of his face—a film noir depicting the life of a lone-wolf killer.
title_norm:サムライ（1967）: A film noir masterpiece from French director Jean-Pierre Melville starring Alain Delon, depicting the life of a lone wolf hitman. Clad in a fedora and trench coat, the solitary killer Jef secures an alibi from his call-girl lover, Jane, before heading out on a hit. Jef successfully assassinates his target—a nightclub owner—but as he flees the scene, his face is seen by the club's singer, Valérie. Jef is hauled in during a police sweep, but he is released after Valérie provides false testimony during the lineup. Nevertheless, the suspicious detective puts a tail on him. Co-starring François Périer of "Nights of Cabiria" and Nathalie Delon, who was married to Delon at the time.
title_norm:サヨナラの引力: Summer 2008, Seoul. University students Uno and Jeong-won meet fatefully on a long-distance bus. Uno, who dreams of becoming a game creator, and Jeong-won, who aspires to be an architect. Supporting each other through their urban days filled with dreams and anxieties, they eventually fall in love, deeply and truly. However, faced with the harshness of reality that youth cannot resist, they choose to part ways. Ten years later, in the summer of 2024, they coincidentally reunite on a flight to Seoul. As they look back on their memories, Uno asks Jeong-won a question he has kept buried deep in his heart: 'What if, back then...'
title_norm:サンキュー、チャック: A human mystery film adaptation of Stephen King's 2020 short story "The Life of Chuck," directed by Mike Flanagan of "Doctor Sleep." As massive natural and man-made disasters strike the Earth one after another, the world is nearing its end. With no internet or social media, mysterious advertisements suddenly appear everywhere on street signs, TVs, and radios, reading: "Thanks to Charles Krantz. For 39 great years, thanks, Chuck." When high school teacher Marty rushes out of his house to see his ex-wife Felicia, the deserted city is filled with Chuck's ads. As Marty and Felicia, who have safely reunited, gaze at the stars, feeling the apocalypse approaching, and hold hands, the scene shifts to the perspective of the man in the ads, Chuck, and a story tracing his life unfolds through beautiful imagery. Tom Hiddleston of the "Avengers" series plays the protagonist Chuck, with Chiwetel Ejiofor of "12 Years a Slave," Karen Gillan of the "Guardians of the Galaxy" series, Jacob Tremblay of "Wonder," and Mark Hamill of the "Star Wars" series co-starring. Mandy Moore, choreographer of "La La Land," choreographs the dance scenes. It won the Audience Award, the top prize, at the 2024 Toronto International Film Festival.
title_norm:サンセット大通り: A film that synchronizes two eras: the silent era of Hollywood, the movie capital, and the 1950s. Billy Wilder stated his intention: 'I wanted to make a film about Hollywood, set in Hollywood.' Unsuccessful screenwriter Gillis stumbles into the home of Norma, a great silent film star. She longs for a comeback to the glamorous world and asks Gillis to polish her script, but... Gloria Swanson's tense performance as Norma is superb. Cecil B. DeMille, known for directing 'Cleopatra' and others, appears as himself.
title_norm:サンタクロースたちの休暇:
The first theatrical feature from director Keiichi Shibuya—leader of the independent film unit "Sangazu" and winner of the Special Jury Prize at the 3rd Horror Film Awards for his short "Kodoku."

Aiko, having lost both parents, survives by collecting spare change left in city vending machines. Her solitary life is interrupted when a runaway woman named Agatha moves in. They are soon joined by Bob, a man harboring a desperate yearning, and the three begin their winter days together. As they lean on one another, each carrying their own burdens and prayers, a Santa Claus who has finished his Christmas duties watches over them.

Themed as "a winter vacation movie set in Japan," the film captures the preciousness of "time spent cherishing someone"—a feeling so easily forgotten—through quirky characters and a whimsical, offbeat atmosphere. The film received the Tomoyuki Furumaya Prize (Special Jury Prize) at the 29th Ueda Jokamachi Film Festival’s 23rd Independent Film Contest and the Theater Seven/Nanagei Prize at the Juso Shitamachi Film Festival 2025.
title_norm:ザッケン！: A youth story based on the manga 'Zakken!' (published by Shogakukan), which was developed from a real club activity, the 'Weed Research Club,' at Tokyo Metropolitan Hibiya High School, by screenwriter and film director Naho Uemura and the scenario creation team 'Monogatari Lab,' with Uemura herself writing and directing the film adaptation. It delicately and freshly depicts a teenage girl lost and unsure of herself, who discovers her own identity through the weeds growing at her feet, which she had never paid attention to before. Spring of her first year of high school. Sugano Yukari, an ordinary girl who isn't passionate about anything and just goes through the motions, meets her classmate Tokuda Mimi, nicknamed 'Dokudami-chan,' who loves weeds and is fascinated by their vitality. Slightly eccentric but with a straightforward and pure heart, Yukari gradually opens up to her. Dokudami-chan dreams of reviving the 'Zakken,' or 'Weed Research Club,' and Yukari, while hesitant about her enthusiasm, begins activities with her aimed at reviving the club, but... Luna Nakajima, who has starred in films like 'A Town of Old Houses' and 'Tore!' and won the Japan Academy Prize for Newcomer for 'Tokyo Taxi,' plays Sugano Yukari, and Miyu Oshima, known for the NHK morning drama 'Omusubi' and the drama 'Bokutachi nchi,' plays Tokuda Mimi, taking on the lead roles.
title_norm:ザ・コラール 希望を紡ぐ歌:
Starring Ralph Fiennes (*Conclave*), this moving human drama follows a choir on the brink of collapse during wartime as they find new hope through an unprecedented endeavor. 

Set in Northern Yorkshire during World War I, a choir decimated by conscription attempts to rebuild by welcoming local youth and townspeople. Dr. Henry Guthrie, a physician who had been practicing in enemy Germany, is appointed as their conductor. Burdened by prejudice and suspicion, he confronts a ragtag ensemble of veterans, prostitutes, devout volunteers, and boys awaiting the draft, working to restore lost connections and hope. Together, they embark on a daring, world-first challenge. However, as new conscription notices arrive, their hard-won peace is once again threatened by the shadows of war. 

Ralph Fiennes portrays Dr. Henry Guthrie, embodying the complex inner life of a strict yet eccentric man. He is joined by a talented British supporting cast including Roger Allam and Mark Addy. Directed by Nicholas Hytner (*The Madness of King George*).
title_norm:ザ・スーパーマリオギャラクシー・ムービー: The second film in the series of "The Super Mario Bros. Movie", which animated the world of Nintendo's "Super Mario" game series and became a massive hit in 2023, grossing over $13 billion worldwide. Twin plumbers Mario and Luigi, while helping Princess Peach in the Mushroom Kingdom, take care of the captured King Koopa and solve everyone's problems. One day, they meet a new partner, Yoshi. Then, triggered by Princess Peach's birthday party, they embark on a new adventure across space to thwart the evil ambitions of Koopa's son, Bowser Jr. In addition to familiar faces from the first film like Mario, Luigi, Princess Peach, Koopa, and Toad, new characters from the original game series appear, including Yoshi, Rosalina, and Bowser Jr. Produced jointly by Chris Meledandri of Illumination (known for the "Minions" and "Sing" series) and Nintendo's Shigeru Miyamoto. Directors Aaron Horvath and Michael Jelenic, and screenwriter Matthew Fogel return, along with the original voice cast including Chris Pratt, Anya Taylor-Joy, Charlie Day, and Jack Black, as well as the Japanese dub cast including Mamoru Miyano, Ayasa Shida, Yu Hatakeyama, Kenta Miyake, and Tomokazu Seki.
title_norm:ザ・セル: The Campbell Institute on the outskirts of Chicago. Young psychologist Catherine is researching technology to enter the human subconscious and dreams. She receives a request to look inside the mind of a serial killer who derives sexual pleasure from watching a woman drown while trapped in a glass cell.
title_norm:ザ・ピーナッツバター・ファルコン: A human drama depicting the adventure of three people—a down-on-his-luck fisherman, a young man with Down syndrome who escapes from a care facility, and a nurse from the facility—as they journey to fulfill the young man's dream. Zack, a young man with Down syndrome living in a group home, escapes to enroll in a professional wrestling school, a dream he has had since childhood. Tyler, a fisherman living a lonely life after the death of his brother, tries to flee on his boat after being caught stealing someone else's catch. Zack happens to meet Tyler, and Eleanor, the nurse who came looking for Zack, joins them. The three head to a destination for Zack's sake. Shia LaBeouf plays Tyler, Dakota Johnson plays Eleanor, and Zack Gottsagen, who inspired the film's creation, plays Zack. John Hawkes and Thomas Haden Church round out the supporting cast. The film marks the feature directorial debut of Tyler Nilson and Michael Schwartz.
title_norm:ザ・フー アメイジング・ジャーニー:
Produced in 2007, this music documentary chronicles over 40 years of the legendary British rock band The Who. After debuting in 1965, The Who shot to stardom as the definitive icons of the Mod movement, and in 1969, they pioneered the "rock opera" genre with their landmark double concept album *Tommy*. Yet, behind the scenes, the band grappled with internal strife, creative pressure, and substance abuse, eventually facing the threat of dissolution following the death of genius drummer Keith Moon in 1978.

Directed by Murray Lerner (*Message to Love: The Isle of Wight Festival 1970*), the film examines the band from multiple perspectives, looking back on their tumultuous career through testimonies from members, family, and associates. It features rare archival material, including the earliest known live footage from just before their debut and previously unreleased performances from the classic *Live at Leeds*. Renowned musicians such as Sting, Eddie Vedder (Pearl Jam), Noel Gallagher (Oasis), The Edge (U2), and Steve Jones (Sex Pistols) also appear to speak passionately about the enduring impact of The Who.
title_norm:ザ・フー キッズ・アー・オールライト: Alongside The Beatles and The Rolling Stones, The Who led the golden age of British rock and continued to innovate the genre as a superband. This rock documentary masterpiece features live performances of their greatest hits from 1964 to 1978—a period when they were unable to tour Japan at their peak—along with promotional films and interviews. Among the many historic scenes, the film notably features Keith Moon, the legendary genius drummer, in his final full-bodied performance, filmed at Shepperton Studios in May 1978 specifically for this production—a truly precious treasure.
title_norm:ザ・レイジ: A revenge action film starring Thai action star Tony Jaa, known for 'Ong-Bak' and 'Tom-Yum-Goong'. It depicts a man who lost his family confronting a massive conspiracy, packed with powerful Muay Thai-based hand-to-hand combat and high-speed, hard-hitting action. After his wife and daughter are killed by a mysterious organization, Bai An heads to the Republic of Parivina to uncover the truth and exact revenge. As he investigates on his own, he discovers a giant corporation secretly controlling the drug trade, but behind it swirls a vast conspiracy involving the military and police. The situation becomes intricately tangled with a mad drug lord, corrupt military police, and unexpected trials involving the only daughter of the corporation's owner. Bai An is tossed about but continues to battle the enemies closing in on him. Directed by Cheung Sui-yee. Co-stars include Xing Yu from 'Master Z: Ip Man Legacy', Philip Keung from 'Goldfinger', and Jason Han from 'Overheat: The Final Sanction'.
title_norm:シネマ歌舞伎 らくだ: The seventh installment of 'Cinema Kabuki,' which screens kabuki stage performances in theaters. It is a double feature with the classic rakugo story 'Rakuda' by Okura Kitaro. Based on a masterpiece of classical rakugo, it depicts the commotion caused by the duo of Kyuroku, played by Nakamura Kanzaburo, and Hanji, played by Bando Mitsugoro. It is screened as a double feature with 'Renjishi,' directed by Yamada Yoji.
title_norm:シネマ歌舞伎 京鹿子娘二人道成寺: The third installment in the "Cinema Kabuki" series, which brings live Kabuki stage performances to the big screen. This film is a digital cinema adaptation of the legendary February 2006 performance of "Kyokanoko Musume Ninin Dojoji" (The Maiden at Dojoji Temple) at the Kabuki-za, starring Bando Tamasaburo and Onoe Kikunosuke. At Dojoji Temple in Kii Province, a dedication ceremony for a new temple bell is being held. The temple’s original bell was destroyed by Kiyohime, who, consumed by her intense passion for her lover Anchin, transformed into a giant serpent and incinerated the bell that had hidden him. A beautiful shirabyoshi dancer named Hanako appears and is granted permission to join the service on the condition that she performs a dance. However, her true identity is the vengeful spirit of Kiyohime.
title_norm:シネマ歌舞伎 女殺油地獄（2011）: The 13th installment of the "Cinema Kabuki" series, which presents digital screenings of live Kabuki stage performances. The film depicts the pathos and madness of Yohei, the son of the Kawachiya oil merchant in Tenma, Osaka, who leads a dissolute life due to a complex family environment. It portrays his feelings for Okichi, the wife of fellow merchant Teshimaya Shichizaemon, as well as the deep affection of his stepfather Tokubei and biological mother Osawa. Based on a joruri play by Chikamatsu Monzaemon, this production was staged in June 2009 as part of the farewell performances for the fourth-generation Kabuki-za.
title_norm:シネマ歌舞伎 曽根崎心中:
Chikamatsu Monzaemon’s masterpiece "The Love Suicides at Sonezaki," a tragic tale based on a real-life incident, has long been a staple of both puppet theater and Kabuki. This iconic play, which also featured in a pivotal scene of the blockbuster film "National Treasure," is now brought to the big screen as part of the "Cinema Kabuki" series—digital screenings of live Kabuki performances. This production captures the April 2009 performance at the Kabukiza Theatre, starring Living National Treasure Sakata Tojuro IV, who portrayed the courtesan Ohatsu more than 1,400 times in his lifetime, alongside his eldest son Nakamura Ganjiro (who also served as the Kabuki consultant for the film "National Treasure") as her lover Tokube.

The courtesan Ohatsu and the merchant Tokube are deeply in love. One day, Tokube is betrayed by a friend and swindled out of the money he was meant to return to his uncle. As Tokube falls into despair over his tarnished honor, Ohatsu’s faith in him never wavers. While Tokube hides beneath the floorboards, Ohatsu asks him if he is prepared to prove his innocence with his very life. Tokube responds with a firm resolve to die. To clear their names and be united in the afterlife, the two lovers slip away under the cover of night toward the woods of Sonezaki.
title_norm:シネマ歌舞伎『曽根崎心中』: Ohatsu, a courtesan, and Tokube'e, a merchant, are deeply in love. However, Tokube'e is betrayed by a friend and swindled out of the money he was meant to return to his uncle. Desperate and with his honor tarnished, Tokube'e finds solace in Ohatsu, who remains steadfast in her belief in him. When Ohatsu asks Tokube'e—who is hiding beneath the floorboards—if he is prepared to prove his innocence with his life, he signals his resolve to die. To be united in the afterlife, the two slip away under the cover of night toward the woods of Sonezaki.
title_norm:シムシャー: Screening at EU Film Days 2026 (Tokyo: May 16–29, 2026 at Theater Image Forum, May 19–24 at the National Film Archive of Japan; Nagoya: June 6–19 at Nagoya Kinema Noi; also to be held in Hiroshima, Kyoto, and Fukuoka).
title_norm:シャオ・メイ ローマ大決戦: Italian visionary director Gabriele Mainetti, who gained international acclaim for *They Call Me Jeeg*, delivers an Italian kung fu action film depicting a Chinese woman’s quest for revenge against a criminal organization in the Roman underworld. Xiao Mei, a young Chinese woman who travels to Rome to search for her missing sister, ventures into a dangerous immigrant district where prostitution and human trafficking are rampant. After meeting Marcello, a local diner owner, Mei enlists his help to take on a ruthless trafficking ring headquartered in a high-end Chinese restaurant called "The Forbidden City." Liu Yaxi—who served as the lead stunt double in Disney’s live-action *Mulan* and performed stunts in numerous action films such as *Detective Dee: The Four Heavenly Kings* and *Vanguard*—makes her feature film starring debut, portraying the protagonist Xiao Mei with extraordinary physical prowess. The film co-stars Marco Giallini (*Perfect Strangers*, *God Willing*) and features stunt supervision by Yang Liang (*Deadpool & Wolverine*). It won Best Feature Film in the Orbita section at the 2025 Sitges Film Festival and Best Director at the Italian Golden Globes.
title_norm:シャドウズ・エッジ: A battle action film starring Jackie Chan, depicting the fight between a police force led by a tracking expert and a cybercrime group led by a former assassin. In Macau, a series of clever heists by an elusive cybercrime group occur. With the surveillance system hijacked and the investigation stalled, the police seek help from Huang Dezhong, a retired tracking expert, as their trump card. Teaming up with young elite police officers, Huang Dezhong uses old-school investigative techniques and the latest technology to pursue the cybercrime group led by a former assassin known as 'Shadow.' Leon Ka-Fai, known for 'The Lover' and 'Cold War,' plays the former assassin leader of the criminal group, reuniting with Jackie Chan for the first time in about 20 years since 'The Myth.' JUN, a member of the popular K-POP group SEVENTEEN who also works as an actor, takes on his first villain role as a member of the criminal group. Zhang Zifeng, from 'Sister Summer's Farewell,' and Zusha, from the TV drama 'Mountain and River Shadows,' also appear. The film is directed and written by Larry Yang, who previously worked with Jackie Chan on 'Ride On.'
title_norm:シャーズ51: Director Minoru Kawasaki, known for delivering numerous bizarre films such as "Ika Resurā" and "Nihon Igai Zenbu Chinbotsu," created this shark movie for the 3rd Tokyo International Shark Film Festival in 2026. The title "Shāzu" is a coined term combining "shark" and "Jaws," and the film pays respect, homage, and parody to Steven Spielberg's work while depicting a battle between a shark that emerges from the forest and humans. In Takeshima, Aichi Prefecture, a young woman is attacked by something and goes missing, later found dead. Police chief Majima suspects a shark attack and tries to close the island but is opposed by local influential figures. Days later, a boy becomes a shark victim in front of a crowd, revealing the presence of a man-eating shark to the town. Biologist Funabashi, dispatched for investigation, points out from the boy's wounds that the culprit is a mutant shark that came ashore and inhabits the forest. Majima and Funabashi, along with professional shark hunter Kujō, set out to eliminate it but are driven into a corner by the shark's tremendous power. Veteran actor Ryōsuke Nogi stars, with former kickboxing world champion Satoshi Kobayashi, comedian Eiji Ukulele, pro wrestler Andy Wu, and Gorō Ibuki from the drama series "Mito Kōmon" co-starring. Idol group "Mitsubachi Girls" appears and also performs the insert song. Shark movie "Ouija Shark 2" director John Miliore and manga artist Mayumi Kurata make cameo appearances, with actor Tamotsu Ishibashi in a special appearance.
title_norm:ショパン、ショパン！: Screening at the "Polish Film Festival 2025" (November 14–20, 2025 / YEBISU GARDEN CINEMA). Screening at "EU Film Days 2026" (Tokyo: May 16–29, 2026 at Theater Image Forum, May 19–24 at National Film Archive of Japan; Nagoya: June 6–19 at Nagoya Cinema Neu; also held in Hiroshima, Kyoto, and Fukuoka).
title_norm:ションベン・ライダー: Jojo, Bruce, and Jisho, a trio of middle schoolers, are constantly bullied by the neighborhood bully Debnaga. Determined to get revenge on Debnaga today, the three are psyched up, but right before their eyes, Debnaga is kidnapped. From there, the three are drawn into a yakuza conflict involving stimulant drugs...
title_norm:シラート: This road movie, blending a fantastical story with cool dance music, follows a father and son's journey through a desert rave party in search of a missing daughter, sparking buzz across Spain and Europe. Luis drives with his son Esteban from the Moroccan mountains deep into the desert to find his daughter, who disappeared after attending a desert rave. They reach an outdoor rave site where reality and hallucination blur, but she is not there. The father and son chase a group of ravers, heading to the next rave site where they believe she went. Sergi López ("Pan's Labyrinth") plays father Luis. Directed and written by Oliver Laxe ("Fire Will Come"), the film is produced by renowned Spanish master Pedro Almodóvar. The title "Siraat" means "path" in Arabic and, in a religious sense, symbolizes the narrow bridge over heaven and hell on Judgment Day. Screened in the Competition section of the 78th Cannes Film Festival in 2025, it won four awards including the Jury Prize. It was nominated for the Academy Awards for Best International Feature Film and Best Sound at the 98th Academy Awards.
title_norm:シルビアのいる街で: This film follows a young aspiring painter wandering through places of memory, searching for traces of Sylvia, a woman he loved six years ago. It constructs an obsessive love story reminiscent of Alfred Hitchcock's 'Vertigo' (1958) with meticulously calculated sound and imagery, resulting in a groundbreaking work unlike anything seen before. The film was shot entirely on location in Strasbourg, France, an ancient city where medieval streetscapes and cutting-edge railways coexist without dissonance, creating a stateless atmosphere. The masterful sound design, which orchestrates the city's noises—the murmur of people, the passing of trams—like a symphony, and the beautiful, luminous chain of images captured through glass reflections and tram windows, transport the viewer into an unknown, otherworldly space.
title_norm:シング・ストリート 未来へのうた: A semi-autobiographical work by director John Carney of "Begin Again" and "Once," this youth drama depicts the love and friendship of a boy who forms a band to impress a girl he likes, set to 1980s British sounds. In 1985 Dublin, Ireland, struggling through a severe recession, 14-year-old Conor is forced to transfer to a rough public school after his father loses his job. At home, his parents constantly fight, pushing the family to the brink of collapse. Conor's only solace in his miserable days is watching music videos from neighboring London on TV with his music-obsessed older brother. One day, captivated by the mature charm of a girl named Raphina he sees on the street, Conor invites her to appear in a music video for his band. Hurriedly forming a band, Conor begins intense training to create a video that will amaze the London music scene...
title_norm:シンシン アンド ザ マウス: A human drama based on a story from Banana Yoshimoto's short story collection 'Mitten and Fubin', co-produced by Japan and Taiwan. It quietly depicts a woman carrying loss who, through encounters in a foreign land, gradually finds renewal. Chizumi is a woman living each day with deep grief after losing her mother. As time passes without filling the void in her heart, she is invited by a friend to visit Taiwan. There, she meets Shin-shin, a young man with a Taiwanese mother and a Japanese father. The unfamiliar cityscapes and the accumulation of casual conversations slowly begin to move her frozen heart, and Chizumi, while still carrying her lingering sense of loss, discovers small warmth. Yukino Kishii ('Small, Slow but Steady', 'Just the Two of Us') plays the protagonist Chizumi, and popular young Taiwanese actor Tseng Jing-hua (known for 'The Soul of the Prisoner', 'Your Name Engraved Herein') plays Shin-shin, the young man she meets in Taiwan. The cast also includes Tokio Fujiwara, Seina Nakata, Tokio Emoto, Kayo Ise, Kisuke Iida, and Kimiko Yo. Directed and scripted by Yukinori Makabe ('I Am a Monk.', 'Scoop!').

It quietly depicts a woman carrying loss who, through encounters in a foreign land, gradually finds renewal. Chizumi is a woman living each day with deep grief after losing her mother. As time passes without filling the void in her heart, she is invited by a friend to visit Taiwan. There, she meets Shin-shin, a young man with a Taiwanese mother and a Japanese father. title_norm:シンプル・アクシデント 偶然: A suspense thriller by Iranian master Jafar Panahi, winner of the Palme d'Or at the 78th Cannes Film Festival in 2025. It thrillingly and humorously depicts people wrongfully imprisoned seeking revenge. Vahid, once unjustly imprisoned, accidentally encounters a man he believes was his torturer guard. He forcibly restrains the man and digs a hole in the wilderness to bury him, but the man's ID card shows a different name. The man claims it's a case of mistaken identity. Blindfolded during imprisonment, Vahid never saw his torturer's face. Unsure if this is the right man, Vahid pauses revenge and visits a friend who was also tortured by the same guard. Panahi, banned from filmmaking by the Iranian government for opposition activities, drew inspiration from his own two imprisonments and the real voices of cellmates. Having won the Golden Lion at Venice for 'The Circle' and 'No Bears', and the Golden Bear at Berlin for 'Taxi', Panahi achieved the feat of winning top prizes at all three major festivals with this film. A French co-production, it was France's entry for Best International Feature Film at the 98th Academy Awards and received a nomination.

title_norm:シーシュポスたちのまなざし: A youth suspense film depicting the struggles and growth of a university student working on a documentary about an incident that occurred in a certain local city. University student Mayu Kuroda is tasked with creating a documentary for a class project based on her own high school experience. Back then, rumors spread that a male teacher, Nitta, had engaged in inappropriate sexual acts with her senior in the broadcasting club, Nojima, whom she admired. Articles in weekly magazines and social media posts drastically changed Nojima's life. Feeling this situation was unjust, Mayu intended to create a work that would serve as a warning about the information society by reflecting on that time. However, as she proceeds with research and filming alongside her university classmates, she is confronted with the reality that the local community is not welcoming the reopening of the case. Furthermore, facts she didn't know at the time and the various intentions of those involved and related parties come to light. Director Hiroki Inoue, highly acclaimed domestically and internationally for the short film 'Aza' and the VR live-action film 'Nagisa ni te', depicts social issues such as bullying, reputational damage via social media, and the insularity of local communities through an original script. Luna Toyota, in her first lead film role, naturally and delicately portrays the protagonist Mayu. Co-stars include Koshu Hirano from the special effects drama 'Ultraman Z', Kohei Yamashita from 'Toritsukushima', Yu Takaoka from the short film 'Tsunagaru', and Yuri Some no from 'Keep Your Hands Off Eizouken!'.
title_norm:ジェイムズ・ブッカー 愛すべきピアノ・ジャンキー: Real name: James Carroll Booker III. The solitary genius who taught organ to Dr. John, prompting the latter to call him "the best black, gay, one-eyed junkie piano genius New Orleans ever produced." A virtuoso whose technique effortlessly bridged classical, jazz, R&B, and rock, he was as much a gifted vocalist as he was a master of the keys. Yet, he was also a man of many burdens—a minority figure struggling with drug and alcohol addiction, his sexuality, and mental illness. With a litany of eccentric rumors and a criminal record to his name, he was an indisputable wreck of a human being. But the moment he sat at the piano, his performance radiated a divine brilliance that transcended all boundaries. His playful personality showed not a trace of the pathos usually found in self-destructive souls. Turning his handicap into a signature style, his look—always sporting a sharp eyepatch—is just one of his many lovable charms.
title_norm:ジェイムズ・ブッカー／愛すべきピアノ・ジャンキー:
If the music is great, that alone is enough. This is the untold "human" non-fiction story of a brilliant, drug-addicted pianist. While New Orleans has produced countless legendary artists, the name James Booker remains relatively unknown to many. Born James Carroll Booker III, he was the solitary genius who taught the organ to Dr. John—the man who famously described him as "the best black, gay, one-eyed junkie piano genius New Orleans ever produced."

Despite being a virtuoso who effortlessly bridged classical, jazz, R&B, and rock, and a gifted vocalist to boot, Booker was a man plagued by demons: drug and alcohol addiction, mental illness, and the struggles of his identity. With endless rumors of eccentric behavior and a history of institutionalization, he was, by all accounts, an undeniable mess of a human being. Yet, the moment he sat at the piano, his playing radiated a divine brilliance that transcended genre with ease. His mischievous personality showed none of the tragic gloom typically associated with self-destructive souls. Turning his physical handicap into a trademark, his look—always sporting a stylish eyepatch—became one of his most endearing charms.

This eccentric musical "human" non-fiction uncovers the life of this obscure, singular musician who dedicated his short 43 years to his hometown of New Orleans, featuring a wealth of emotional performance footage. He may not have had a flashy, chart-topping career, but this film makes you believe from the bottom of your heart: "If the music is great, that alone is enough."
title_norm:ジェニー・ペンはご機嫌ななめ: A psychological thriller set in a care home that should be a place of peace, depicting elderly residents driven into a nightmare with no escape by a cruel resident who dominates them. Stefan Mortensen, a principled and proud judge who has worked for years upholding the law, is forced into a wheelchair by illness and enters a suburban care home. There, he encounters the evil resident Dave Creeley, who uses a finger puppet named 'Jenny Pen' for doll therapy to dominate the elderly through insidious bullying. Stefan, opposing him, becomes a target, and Dave's unreasonable, humiliating harassment escalates. Having fought for justice all his life, Stefan throws himself into one final, brutal battle. John Lithgow ('Conclave') plays the dominating Dave, and Geoffrey Rush ('The King's Speech') plays the former judge Stefan who confronts him. Both won Best Actor awards together at the 57th Sitges Film Festival in 2024. Paul Lewis, the puppet creator behind 'M3GAN', designed Jenny Pen.
title_norm:ジャパン・ロボット: A featured film of "Indian Movie Week 2020" (September 11 – October 9, 2020, at Kineka Omori; from September 25, 2020, at Shinjuku Piccadilly).
title_norm:ジャンヌ・ディエルマン ブリュッセル1080、コメルス河畔: A masterpiece drama by Belgian female director Chantal Akerman, who left many works earnestly examining women's lives in society and daily life, carefully capturing a housewife's frustrations and details while tracing how cracks emerge in ordinary routine. Jeanne lives alone with her adolescent son in a Brussels apartment. Boiling water, peeling potatoes, going shopping—she leads an "ordinary" life, but... Starring Delphine Seyrig, known for "Last Year at Marienbad" and "The Discreet Charm of the Bourgeoisie." Screened at the "Chantal Akerman Film Festival" (April 29 - May 12, 2022, Human Trust Cinema Shibuya).
title_norm:ジョン・クランコ: A film about the life of genius choreographer John Cranko, who elevated the Stuttgart Ballet from a small regional company in Germany to world-class status, made with the full cooperation of the ballet company. It depicts the untold story behind the creation of his masterpiece "Onegin" and his true face, cut short by an untimely death at the age of 45, all colored by spectacular dance performances by current star dancers. John Cranko, an up-and-coming choreographer active in England, is prosecuted for homosexual acts after a police sting operation. Forced to leave London in 1960, he becomes a guest artist with the Stuttgart Ballet through connections. Finding a place in the company that accepts him without prejudice, he becomes artistic director the following year in 1961, creating works and a company that express beauty and passion with free-thinking ideas. In 1969, the ballet company is invited to the Metropolitan Opera House in New York and rises to the top of the world overnight. Sam Riley, known for "Maleficent" and "Control," stars, passionately portraying Cranko, a man overflowing with passion and innovative talent but who sometimes hurts others due to being too pure in his pursuit of art. Directed and written by Joachim A. Lang, known for "The Man Who Produced Hitler" and who has covered the Stuttgart Ballet for many years.

title_norm:ジョン・バージャーと4つの季節: A documentary produced by Tilda Swinton, exploring the later years of British writer John Berger, who profoundly influenced her. From his debut in the late 1950s until his death in 2017, John Berger engaged in creative expression across diverse fields including art criticism, poetry, plays, and novels. Known for his Booker Prize-winning novel "G." and the worldwide bestseller "Ways of Seeing," his works have been increasingly translated and acclaimed in South Korea and Japan in recent years. Swinton, who admired Berger and deepened their friendship from the 1980s, conceived this film in 2009 in collaboration with the London-based experimental production company Derek Jarman Lab. The film depicts Swinton, her two children, and artists who cherished Berger, visiting him in the French Alpine village of Quincy, engaging in dialogues about memories of war, humans and animals, politics and art, and passing on legacies to the next generation, structured across four chapters following Quincy's four seasons. Screened at the 66th Berlin International Film Festival in 2016.
title_norm:ジョン・バージャー生誕100年記念：映画『ジョン・バージャ: A documentary produced by Tilda Swinton, exploring the later years of British writer John Berger, who deeply influenced her. From his debut in the late 1950s until his death in 2017, John Berger engaged in creative expression across diverse fields including art criticism, poetry, plays, and novels. Known for the Booker Prize-winning novel 'G.' and the worldwide bestseller 'Ways of Seeing', his works have been increasingly translated and acclaimed in South Korea and Japan in recent years.
