title_norm:友だちの恋人: The sixth film in Éric Rohmer's "Comedies and Proverbs" series. Set in a new town on the outskirts of Paris, it lightly depicts the romantic affairs of four men and women. Blanche, a shy woman working at city hall, and Léa, a pragmatic female student, hit it off and become friends. Léa lives with her boyfriend Fabien, but their relationship isn't going well. Meanwhile, Blanche develops feelings for Alexandre, a playboy and friend of Fabien's, but her timid nature prevents her from confessing. Eventually, Fabien finds himself drawn to Blanche... The colorful 1980s fashion is also a highlight.
title_norm:友よ、静かに瞑れ: After learning that his old friend Sakaguchi had attacked the president of Shimogata Construction and been arrested, Shindo returned to a small port town in Okinawa. Shimogata Construction was in charge of the town's redevelopment and had been harassing and threatening Sakaguchi to force him to sell his hotel. Shindo stayed at the hotel, the "Free Inn," and began investigating the incident. Meeting Shimogata's development chief Takabatake and Detective Tokuda, who was colluding with Shimogata, Shindo uncovered the truth: Sakaguchi had stormed Shimogata Construction to rescue his kidnapped son, Ryuta. Shindo also learned that Sakaguchi was suffering from cancer and had only a few months to live.
title_norm:叛逆のサウンドトラック: A staggering documentary that delivers an unprecedented experience to audiences! A jazz rhapsody that digs into the darkness of history, built entirely from archival footage! Satchmo, Malcolm X, Gillespie, Khrushchev, Coltrane, Castro, Nina Simone, Nehru, Nasser, and Sukarno too... Witness a historical farce swirling with conspiracy!
title_norm:口に関するアンケート: A film adaptation of the bestselling novel 'A Survey About the Mouth' by author Senkin, who sparked the mockumentary horror boom with 'About a Certain Place in the Kinki Region.' Published in 2024, the palm-sized, 60-page story became a huge sensation on social media for delivering a solid scare in such a short format. Directed by Takashi Shimizu of the 'Ju-On' series, it marks Rihito Itagaki's first solo lead role in a live-action film. A group of university students hear a rumor about a 'cursed tree' in a cemetery known as a haunted spot and visit it for a test of courage. The next day, one of the group members mysteriously disappears. Since then, inexplicable phenomena begin to occur around the students who visited the cemetery, and they are gradually driven into a corner. Guided by the baffling testimonies of the five students, a terrifying truth emerges. Rihito Itagaki plays Shota Murai, one of the university students. The cast also includes Keito Tsuna as Tatsuya, Ai Yoshikawa as An, MOMONA (ME:I) as Mirei, Shuto Mori (BUDDiiS) as Horita, a student who visits the cemetery for fun, Tomoki Nishiyama (TAGRIGHT) as Kawase, who is forcibly taken to the cemetery by Horita, Shido Nakamura as Detective Kusabe, who pursues the missing student, and Tokio Emoto as journalist Nishi.
title_norm:口蹄疫から生きのびた豚:
A dark fantasy anime inspired by the mass culling of pigs during the 2010 foot-and-mouth disease outbreak in South Korea. The film allegorically depicts the intersection of two fates—a pig that survived the cull and a man driven to despair by human society—weaving in social issues such as the spread of disease, environmental destruction, bullying, lookism, and generational divides through a variety of expressive styles.

In modern South Korea, as countless pigs are slaughtered following an outbreak of foot-and-mouth disease, a single pig with an extraordinary instinct for survival rises from a mass grave where it was buried alive. The pig longs to become human: "To survive, I want to become a 'human'—a creature of absolute power. I will stop at nothing to achieve it." Meanwhile, Choi Jong-seok, a man who has endured brutal bullying since childhood, wishes for the opposite: "I want to cast aside my life as a human and become a 'beast' instead." These two destinies, never meant to meet, intertwine like a spiral, leading them toward an unimaginable transformation.

The film is directed by South Korea's Huh Bum-wook, marking his second feature-length work.
title_norm:台湾ハリウッド:
Set against the backdrop of the Taiwanese film industry between 1955 and 1981—a period that saw the production of numerous "B-movies"—this comedy portrays the filmmakers of the era who staked their dreams on the silver screen. 

An 18-year-old grandson cares for his grandmother, who is living with dementia. His grandfather, a screenwriter, tells
title_norm:台風クラブ: A masterpiece of youth cinema that vividly depicts middle school students who fall into a state of turmoil, showing inexplicable emotional excitement as a typhoon approaches. Directed by Shinji Somai, known for "Sailor Suit and Machine Gun" and "Shonben Rider." In a local city near Tokyo, five students sneak into their private middle school's pool at night to swim. They notice a male student who arrived earlier and play a prank on him, but it goes too far, nearly drowning him. The next morning, the news reports a typhoon approaching. From then on, something gradually begins to go wrong among the students...
title_norm:名探偵コナン ハイウェイの堕天使: The 29th theatrical film in the nationally hit series "Detective Conan", based on the manga by Gosho Aoyama. Conan, Ran, Sonoko, and Kogoro, along with motorcycle enthusiast Sera Masumi, encounter a mysterious black motorcycle speeding out of control while on their way to the "Kanagawa Motorcycle Festival" in Yokohama's Minato Mirai district. Kanagawa Prefectural Police traffic officer Hagiwara Chiharu chases the black bike but narrowly misses catching it. Conan and the others arrive at the festival venue, where a new white motorcycle called "Angel" equipped with cutting-edge technology is being unveiled. News then arrives that the runaway black bike has appeared in Tokyo. After evading the Metropolitan Police Department's pursuit, the black bike, whose body closely resembles the "Angel", is dubbed the "Black Angel" or "Lucifer", and the chase continues. In Chiharu's mind, memories of her younger brother Hagiwara Kenji and his colleague Matsuda Jinpei flash by. Hagiwara Chiharu, praised by Ran as the "Goddess of the Wind" for her driving skills, makes her first appearance in a theatrical film, engaging in intense motorcycle action against the mysterious black bike "Lucifer". Chiharu is voiced by Miyuki Sawashiro, who took over the role from Atsuko Tanaka, who passed away in August 2024. Guest voice actors Ryusei Yokohama and Mei Hata make their voice acting debuts. Directed by Takahiro Hasui, who handled direction for "Detective Conan: Black Iron Submarine".
title_norm:名無し: A film adaptation of the psycho-violent manga "Nanashi" by Sato Jiro—who is active not only as an actor but also as a screenwriter and film director—marking his first work based on a manga. Sato stars and wrote the script, with Hideo Shijo of "Bad Summer" directing. A brutal murder occurs at a family restaurant in the afternoon. Security cameras capture a bald middle-aged man who appears to be the culprit, but he holds no weapon. The footage records the bizarre sight of people spurting blood and collapsing just from the man approaching and lightly touching them. Investigating police identify the bald man as "Taro Yamada," who was questioned for shoplifting 11 years earlier. When investigators rush to Yamada's home address, they find a decomposed female corpse. Sato plays the protagonist, serial killer Yamada. Takaya Kamikawa plays Teruo, the patrol officer who becomes the namesake for the nameless orphaned young Yamada. MEGUMI plays Hanako Yamada, who grew up with Yamada in the same children's home and lives with him. Kuroudo Yashima plays Detective Kunieda, who works tirelessly to stop Yamada.
title_norm:君と僕の5分: Set in early 2000s South Korea, when Japanese pop culture was restricted, this coming-of-age drama tenderly follows a shy transfer student and a popular class president who bond over J-Pop. In 2001, Gyung-hwan transfers to a high school in Daegu, Korea's most conservative city. A huge fan of then-taboo Japanese music and anime, he secretly listens to Japanese songs on his MP3 player during lunch. Teased as an 'otaku' by classmates, he discovers that his deskmate, class president Jae-min, also secretly loves Japanese culture. Sharing earphones on the bus after school while listening to J-Pop, they gradually grow closer. One day, Gyung-hwan confesses a secret to Jae-min, but afterward, Jae-min's attitude suddenly changes. Making his feature debut, director Eom Ha-nul wrote the script based on his own teenage experiences as a fan of Japanese culture, weaving in diverse Japanese pop culture from the 1990s. Shim Hyun-seo, a child actor known for 'The King of Pigs', plays transfer student Gyung-hwan, and Hyun Woo-seok, from 'The School Nurse Files', plays class president Jae-min. Gong Min-jung ('Kim Ji-young: Born 1982') and Lee Dong-hwi ('The Roundup: Punishment') co-star.
title_norm:君と僕の５分: Set in early 2000s South Korea, when Japanese pop culture was restricted, this coming-of-age drama tenderly follows a shy transfer student and a popular class president who bond over J-Pop. In 2001, Gyung-hwan transfers to a high school in Daegu, Korea's most conservative city. title_norm:君と花火と約束と: A youth romance anime film adaptation of the novel of the same name by Madoroka. Set against the backdrop of the 'Nagaoka Festival Grand Fireworks Display' in Nagaoka City, Niigata Prefecture, one of Japan's three major fireworks festivals that attracts hundreds of thousands of visitors annually, it depicts a promise that transcends time and a summer in the lives of high school students. One day shortly after entering high school, Makoto Natsume meets his classmate Akira Hayama. Since childhood, Akira has been told by her great-grandmother that she would 'one day meet Makoto Natsume,' and she holds a single painting of fireworks. As they investigate the secret of the painting, which Makoto has no memory of, the two discover the existence of 'a certain promise' made in the past. Eventually, the meaning of a fate connected across time becomes clear. The voice of the protagonist, Makoto, is played by Shōri Satō, a member of the popular group 'timelesz,' in his first lead role in an anime film. The heroine, Akira, is voiced by Nanoka Hara, known for playing the protagonist Suzume Iwato in 'Suzume.' The director is Kei Suzuki of the TV anime 'Tower of God.' The project is produced by Shin-Ei Animation, with animation production jointly handled by SynergySP and Answer Studio.
title_norm:君のクイズ: An adaptation of the 2022 bestselling mystery novel "Your Quiz" by Naoki Prize-winning author Satoshi Ogawa. The stage is the grand finale of "Q-1 Grand Prix," a live quiz show with a 10-million-yen prize. As the nation watches with bated breath, Reo Mishima, the "Absolute King of Quizzes," and Kizuna Honjo, "The Man Who Saved the World in His Head," are both one step away from victory. On the final buzzer question, Honjo presses his button before a single character of the question has even been read. To the shock of the audience, he correctly identifies the answer and claims the championship. Unable to hide his bewilderment at this impossible feat, Mishima launches his own investigation to uncover how Honjo achieved a "zero-character correct answer." Tomoya Nakamura stars as the protagonist Reo Mishima, a man of vast knowledge and logical thinking; Ryunosuke Kamiki portrays the enigmatic genius player Kizuna Honjo; and Tsuyoshi Muro plays Yasuhiko Sakata, the show’s producer who will stop at nothing to create a spectacle. Directed by Kohei Yoshino (*Anime Supremacy!*, *The Silent Service*), the film utilizes stylish VFX to depict the labyrinthine thought processes unfolding within a quiz player's mind.
title_norm:君の名は。: Director Makoto Shinkai, known for delicately portraying the nuances of male-female emotions against beautiful landscapes in works like "The Place Promised in Our Early Days" and "5 Centimeters Per Second," delivers his first original feature in three years since "The Garden of Words." Character design by Masayoshi Tanaka of "Anohana: The Flower We Saw That Day" fame, animation direction by Masashi Ando, known for his work on Studio Ghibli films like "Princess Mononoke" and "Spirited Away," and music including the theme song by popular rock band RADWIMPS. The film remained in the top 10 of domestic box office rankings for 29 consecutive weeks, achieving historic blockbuster success with over 25 billion yen in revenue. It won the Award for Best Screenplay at the 40th Japan Academy Prize, a first for an animated work. One month before a comet approaches for the first time in 1000 years, Mitsuha Miyamizu, a high school girl living in a mountainous rural town, dreams she is a male high school student in Tokyo. Mitsuha, who feels cramped by her small town and longs for the city, enjoys city life in her dream. Meanwhile, Taki Tachibana, a male high school student in Tokyo, dreams he is a high school girl in a mountain town he's never visited. As the body-swapping phenomenon continues and they become aware of each other, Taki and Mitsuha eventually discover an unexpected truth. Voice cast includes Ryunosuke Kamiki as Taki and Mone Kamishiraishi as Mitsuha, with Masami Nagasawa and Etsuko Ichihara among others.
title_norm:君の見る世界をなぞる: Set in sun-drenched Southern France, this is a fresh and vivid youth drama about the inner conflicts and love of an adolescent boy living in the complex modern era. Enzo, a 16-year-old raised in a wealthy family in Southern France, struggles to fit in at school and works at a construction site. He becomes drawn to Vlad, a young Ukrainian man he meets there, but Vlad must go to war for his military service. Distrust towards his seemingly comfortable family, anxiety about the future, and the reality of war taking away those close to him. Unable to control his emotions, Enzo's summer passes quietly. Originally a project launched by director Laurent Cantet, known for "The Class," his ally Robin Campillo, known for "BPM (Beats Per Minute)," took over and completed the film after Cantet passed away in 2024 while battling cancer. Newcomer actor Eloi Poy, a former competitive swimmer, delicately portrays Enzo's inner turmoil. Pierfrancesco Favino, known for "The Traitor," and Élodie Bouchez, known for "The Dreamed Path," co-star as Enzo's parents. Amateur actor Maxime Slivinsky, who actually worked on construction sites, was cast as Vlad, the worker Enzo has a faint crush on.
title_norm:君は映画: A youth comedy directed by Makoto Ueda, head of the theater group "Europe Kikaku," known for writing screenplays for numerous hit films like "Summer Time Machine Blues" and "River, Don't Flow On." This is his feature directorial debut, set in the real-life building "Shelbo Shimokitazawa" in Shimokitazawa, employing innovative gimmicks. At the cinema Tollywood on the second floor of "Shelbo Shimokitazawa," Madoka, a playwright from Shimokitazawa, and Kazuma, a band musician from Sangenjaya, each go to see a movie. An impossible structure emerges where each other's events are projected onto the screen as a film. Meanwhile, problems arise at the shops adjacent to the cinema, "Good Heavens" and "Mikazuki Rock." Madoka and Kazuma try to solve the problems using this structure, but their films influence each other, and the situation spirals in unexpected directions. Starring Maria Ito ("Summer Film ni Notte") as Madoka the playwright and Kai Inowaki ("Musicophilia") as Kazuma the band musician. The cast also includes Oshiro Maeda and Hinako Kikuchi as members of Madoka's theater troupe, Suzuyuki Kaneko and Yusuke Mikawa as members of Kazuma's band, Takafumi Imai as a semi-delinquent who frequents "Mikazuki Rock," and the comedy duo "The Geese" as a pair of detectives. Additionally, members of Europe Kikaku, including Gota Ishida, Shintaro Kanamaru, and Riko Fujitani, play unique characters.
title_norm:君は行く先を知らない: A car races across the desolate landscape of Iran. In the back seat, the father entertains his exuberant younger son; in the passenger seat, the mother sways to an old pop song; and in the driver's seat, the eldest son stares silently ahead. While the younger son, unaware of the purpose of the trip, frolics innocently, the family arrives near the Turkish border...
title_norm:君も出世ができる: The pinnacle of Japanese musicals, depicting a salaryman struggling in the battle for foreign tourists in Tokyo just before the Olympics. Throughout the film, talented performers sing and dance, and Frankie's astonishing physical abilities leave you in awe. The grand group dance in 'Man Alone' is especially breathtaking.
title_norm:唯心: The short film collection "Yuishin"—comprising four works starting with "20db" (produced and released in 2019), the second film "breath," the third "Sky, White, Waves, and Mother," and the fourth "Blue and White"—will be screened at Kichijoji Uplink for one week from Friday, June 5 to Thursday, June 11, 2026!
title_norm:喜劇 ・日本列島震度0: A female fortune teller predicts a major earthquake, a tabi craftsman in downtown Tokyo urges evacuation, and a shady loan shark schemes to make a quick profit... Fifty years after the Great Kanto Earthquake, this earthquake frenzy comedy wildly laughs at a Japan caught up in the 'Japan Sinks' boom. The duo of Frankie and Zaitsu is simply the best!
title_norm:喜劇 ・男の子守唄: A former war orphan lives with the child of the prostitute who took him in... A heartwarming comedy woven by a man who, even 25 years after the war, still carries the scars of burnt ruins and black markets in his heart. Frankie gives a poignant performance as a man working hard as a street performer and at a host club.
title_norm:喜劇 逆転旅行: Conductor Goichi (Frankie) on the Tohoku Main Line receives passionate advances from his childhood friend, geisha Sakura (Baisho), but secretly has his eye on another woman. The third installment of the 11-film "Travel Series" starring Frankie Sakai, directed by comedy master Segawa.
title_norm:喜劇 駅前漫画: The 15th installment of the 'Ekimaé Series,' which produced 24 films starring Frankie, Morishige, and Bando. Riding the unprecedented manga boom, this film features Frankie as a manga artist and is a legendary oddity, with appearances by 'Obake no Q-taro' and 'Osomatsu-kun' within the story.
title_norm:嗚呼!! 花の応援団: The first film adaptation in 20 years of the hit 1976 series "Aa!! Hana no Ōendan." At the Minami Kawachi University cheerleading squad, an annual alumni gathering is planned, but they discover a hole in their precious team flag. The members hurriedly take part-time jobs to earn repair money, but the workplace is run by yakuza who refuse to pay and threaten them. However, Sekidō Aota appears and beats the yakuza to a pulp. Ken'ichi Nagira reprises his role as senior Yakutsuji from the previous series, and Junko Miyashita also appears.
title_norm:噂の女: A commentary: A daughter returns to Kyoto's Shimabara pleasure district, wounded after a broken engagement, and strongly resists her mother, who runs the long-established geisha house "Izutsuya." This masterpiece centers on the mother-daughter conflict, portraying the sorrow of women who have no choice but to live in the flower and willow world. The art direction by Hiroshi Mizutani, who long supported Mizoguchi's films from before the war, is also stunning.
title_norm:四つのいのち: Italian filmmaker Michelangelo Frammartino tells the story of four lives that are born and die. Based on the Pythagorean concept of "four transmigrations," the film presents humans, animals, plants, and minerals with equal weight from a fundamentally egalitarian perspective that does not center the human world. After an elderly shepherd quietly dies in a mountain village in Calabria, southern Italy, his young goat dies beside a large fir tree. The tree is cut down for a village festival and eventually becomes charcoal. With no dialogue and long takes, the film captures nature as it is. In Japan, it screened in the natural TIFF section of the 23rd Tokyo International Film Festival in 2010 and was released theatrically in 2011. It will be released in 2026 as part of the special screening series "The Amazing World of Michelangelo Frammartino."
title_norm:四十九 seek: Shane Kosugi, son of action star Sho Kosugi who sparked the ninja boom in Hollywood and brother of Kane Kosugi, makes his feature directorial debut with this action film themed around ninjas believed to be extinct. Chinese martial arts world champion Kansuke Asano, who became a world champion in his teens, stars and produces, with Kane Kosugi also appearing. Ninjas living in modern-day Japan have changed their names and appearances, secretly carrying out missions as agents of the non-governmental organization 'Shiju-ku (49)'. Kyōhei Aizawa, one of the most skilled agents in history, loses his beloved lover, the only person he truly trusted, in a plane crash. As he contemplates the meaning of life in solitude, Kyōhei is assigned an infiltration mission into the Japanese yakuza group Takatsuki-gumi. After Kyōhei successfully completes the mission, the Takatsuki-gumi, learning of his existence, begins eliminating people around him by any means necessary for a certain purpose. Realizing that his loved ones are disappearing because of him, Kyōhei confronts the Takatsuki-gumi alone. Asano plays the protagonist Kyōhei, with Seiki Miura and Nanana among the cast.
title_norm:四月の余白: Directed by Keisuke Yoshida of "Himeanole" and "Missing," this drama portrays boys who cannot understand pain or common sense, and the adults who continue to confront them head-on. Yoshida wrote the original script based on the juvenile delinquents he encountered during his own sensitive adolescence and the community surrounding them. Nishiken Go, a former half-gray area gangster and ex-convict, runs a full-time residential rehabilitation facility called "Mirai no Sato" in a coastal provincial town. Drawing on his own experiences, Nishiken tackles troubled children with all his might, but his rehabilitation methods, which do not shy away from corporal punishment, are criticized by educators. One day, a middle school teacher named Fuyuko consults him about an uncontrollable student, Kaito, and Yu, who has just been released from a juvenile detention center. Meeting the two, Nishiken instantly sees through Kaito's madness. Kaito's mother, exhausted by his severe domestic violence, decides to entrust her son to "Mirai no Sato." However, Kaito causes trouble with the other residents, escapes, and is arrested for assault. Wataru Ichinose of the Netflix drama "Sanctuary" stars as Nishiken, while the newcomer Hayato Uesaka is cast as the delinquent boy Kaito. Kaho plays middle school teacher Fuyuko, Atsushi Shinohara and Fusako Urabe play Kaito's parents, Iori Wada plays Kaito's delinquent friend Yu, and Nanami Yamazaki and Mansaku Takada play the facility's residents.
title_norm:国宝: A human drama depicting the tumultuous life of a man born into a yakuza family who dedicates his life to the path of art as a Kabuki actor. A talked-about sensation that has taken the Japanese film world by storm, finally screening!
title_norm:國分玲: A time-leap suspense film inspired by the urban legend passed down on social media of "Kokubun Rei, a time traveler from 2058," depicting human drama surrounding time machine research. Starring Tetsuya Funeyama, who works as an actor, singer, and writer, and Minami Mitou, an actress and model. University professor Kokubun Rei has devoted his life to time machine research while struggling with funding shortages. One day, a mysterious woman named Kitayama Hana leaves the words "Please return it in the future" and transfers 350 billion yen into Rei's account. Rei, along with inventor Furuta, investigates inexplicable phenomena occurring in the basement of an abandoned building, becoming convinced that this place is the key to transcending time. Meanwhile, a girl named Kazuko who had been sleeping for seven years miraculously awakens, and the events she witnesses gradually begin to intersect with the fates of Rei and the others. Funeyama plays the protagonist Kokubun Rei, Mitou plays Kitayama Hana who holds the key to the story, with Amisa Miyazaki, Tomohiro Furuya, and Hidemasa Mase in supporting roles. The director is Roger D. Cohen, who served as an assistant director on "Shukuzan" and makes his commercial film directorial debut with this work.
title_norm:土を喰らう十二ヵ月: A human drama starring Kenji Sawada, based on the culinary essay "Days of Eating Earth: My Twelve Months of Shojin" by writer Tsutomu Minakami. Directed and written by Yuji Nakae of "Nabi no Koi" fame, the film crafts an original story inspired by the rich worldview of the source material. Tsutomu, a writer living alone in a remote mountain cabin in Nagano, spends his days cooking wild berries, mushrooms, and vegetables from his garden, feeling the changing seasons as he writes. His editor and much younger lover, Machiko, occasionally visits him from Tokyo. For the two, cooking and eating seasonal ingredients together is a special time. Though Tsutomu lives a carefree life, he has been unable to enshrine the ashes of his wife, who passed away 13 years ago. Takako Matsu plays Tsutomu's lover Machiko. Cooking researcher Yoshiharu Doi created the many dishes that appear in the film.
title_norm:土曜日の男:
This unique action film follows a man struggling with anger management who unleashes his fury only once a week—on Saturdays—as he takes a stand against a corrupt police officer abusing his power. 

Raised in a coastal town in Andhra Pradesh, India, Surya has been quick-tempered since childhood. His worried mother taught him to record his anger in a notebook rather than acting on it immediately, advising him that if the feeling persists after time has passed, then the anger is truly justified. Even after his mother’s passing, Surya maintains this habit, but with a personal twist: he designates Saturday as the day he finally lets out a week’s worth of pent-up rage. 

Now an adult working as an insurance agent in Hyderabad, Surya leads a seemingly ordinary life, yet his ritualistic Saturday outbursts continue. His path eventually crosses with Inspector Dayanand, a man who treats the local citizens with utter brutality... 

Starring Nani (*Eega*) as Surya, the film features S.J. Suryah, a renowned character actor in Tamil cinema, as the villainous Inspector Dayanand.
title_norm:在日ミャンマー人: Following the 2021 military coup, this film follows the struggles and activism of young Myanmar nationals living in Japan. Through demonstrations in Japan, support for displaced persons, and investigations into interest groups, it sheds light on the dire situation in their homeland.
title_norm:地底への旅: Director Michelangelo Frammartino, whose "Four Lives" depicting the cycle of life earned high praise at the Cannes Film Festival, questions the meaning of humanity's venture into the unknown against the historical context of Italy's economic boom. This film won the Special Jury Prize in the Competition section of the 78th Venice International Film Festival in 2021. Young explorers descend 683 meters underground without maps, using acetylene lamps to measure and map the cave structure. Above ground, an elderly shepherd on the Pollino Plateau prepares for a quiet death amidst vast nature, suffering from illness. The shepherd's death coincides with the explorers reaching the deepest abyss, creating a grand cycle of life and death, time and space. The cinematographer is the renowned Renato Berta, known for collaborations with masters like Jean-Luc Godard, Éric Rohmer, Daniel Schmid, and Manoel de Oliveira. In Japan, it screened under the title "Cave" in the World Focus section of the 34th Tokyo International Film Festival. It will have its theatrical premiere in Japan in 2026 under the title "Journey to the Depths of the Earth" as part of the special screening series "The Amazing World of Michelangelo Frammartino."
title_norm:地方記者: A pollution issue arises in a town in the Tohoku region, and the media war heats up... An excellent film in which Frankie plays a newspaper reporter, depicting the struggles of journalists who, while grappling with the difficulties of maneuvering in a rural setting, burn with passion for producing community-focused articles.
title_norm:地獄の英雄: Billy Wilder parted ways with his long-time screenwriting partner Charles Brackett and brought in a new writer for this film. Jack, kicked out of a New York newspaper, witnesses a man buried alive in a cave. Desperate to return to a top-tier paper, he manipulates information using the scoop. A journalist who stops at nothing for his own ambition is ultimately judged by public opinion, making for a compelling watch. There is also an anecdote that the studio changed the title from 'Ace in the Hole' to 'The Big Carnival' due to poor public reception.
title_norm:地球の静止する日: A flying saucer suddenly arrives in Washington. An alien named Klaatu lands and, concerned for Earth's future, demands that humanity abandon nuclear weapons. He declares that if his demand is not accepted, he will shut down all energy on Earth...
title_norm:墮落天使: Director Wong Kar-wai of 'Chungking Express' crafts a pop-infused ensemble drama about the poignant romantic entanglements of five men and women in the neon-lit streets of Hong Kong. This film completes an episode originally planned as part of 'Chungking Express' as an independent work. A lonely hitman and the woman who acts as his agent. Their rule is to keep personal feelings out of work, but their relationship begins to waver. Meanwhile, a mute young man named Mo sneaks into other people's shops every night and runs them without permission. One day, Mo meets a woman who has just been heartbroken and falls for her. The hitman is played by Leon Lai of 'The City of Sadness,' the agent by Michelle Lee of 'Flowers of Shanghai,' and Mo by Takeshi Kaneshiro of 'Chungking Express.' Cinematography is by Christopher Doyle, who worked on many of Wong Kar-wai's films. First released in Japan in 1996. In 2022, a 4K restored version was screened as part of 'WKW4K' (from August 19, 2022, at Cine Mart Shinjuku, Grand Cinema Sunshine, Cinema City, etc.).
title_norm:声をあげるということ 性犯罪 刑法改正の記録: A documentary recording the five-year struggle of sexual violence survivors who courageously raised their voices. In 2019, four acquittals in sexual crime cases were handed down one after another across Japan. Despite acknowledging that the women were in situations where they could not resist, the courts repeatedly delivered verdicts favorable to the perpetrators, citing reasons such as 'the perpetrator mistakenly believed there was consent,' 'there was no clear resistance from the woman,' or 'she could have resisted but didn't.' People who could no longer tolerate the ongoing disregard for sexual violence victims stood up and began to speak about their sadness, anger, and suffering in their own words. The realities that had never been put into words—such as women suffering from trauma and PTSD due to sexual abuse by their biological fathers, a single mother unable to fight against repeated sexual harassment at work, the victimization of sexual minorities overlooked by the system, and male victims—gradually became shared and spread nationwide. Their voices swelled into a major movement, driving society to amend the Penal Code in 2023. The director is Saki Hamachi, who has worked on numerous television documentaries. After producing a documentary program on the subject, Director Hamachi, who had been covering people working on the Penal Code reform for sexual crimes since 2019, decided to preserve the record of the struggle as a feature film, conducting further interviews to complete this work.
title_norm:夏の夜の人々: Screened as part of the special program "Finnish Films Loved by Aki Kaurismäki" (November 25 – December 1, 2017, at Eurospace in Shibuya, Tokyo).
title_norm:夏の終わりの訪問者: Screened at "EU Film Days 2026" (Tokyo: May 16–29, 2026 at Theater Image Forum, May 19–24 at National Film Archive; Nagoya: June 6–19 at Nagoya Cinema Neu; also held in Hiroshima, Kyoto, and Fukuoka).
title_norm:夜に現れた女: To be screened at EU Film Days 2026 (Tokyo: May 16–29, 2026 at Theater Image Forum, May 19–24 at National Film Archive; Nagoya: June 6–19 at Nagoya Kinema Noi; also to be held in Hiroshima, Kyoto, and Fukuoka).
title_norm:夜のまにまに:
Set in Osaka, this youth romance depicts the relationship between a serious, melancholic young man and an unconventional, proactive woman. Shinpei, a part-time worker who has just broken up with his girlfriend Saki, hits it off with Kasumi after meeting her at a movie theater, and they spend the night wandering the city together. Later, Kasumi unexpectedly begins working at the same cafe as Shinpei. Surprised by the reunion, Shinpei ends up playing amateur detective when Kasumi asks for his help investigating her boyfriend’s infidelity. Despite being swept up in Kasumi’s assertive pace, Shinpei gradually finds himself drawn to her.

Amon Kabe (*Being Good*, *Chihayafuru* series) stars as Shinpei, with Nairu Yamamoto (*The Cat Escaped*) playing Kasumi. The supporting cast includes Hisao Kurozumi (*Manji*), Miru Nagase (*The Last Judgment*), Nagiko Tsuji (*Nagi’s Blues*), and Masatoshi Kihara (*Tokyo Disaster*). The film is directed by Teppei Isobe (*Cornflakes*, *Nagi’s Blues*).
title_norm:夜のストレンジャー: In a corner of the city, Kawamura Kiriko lives a lonely life as a late-night taxi driver. Bound by a past with a criminal record, she continues to reject connections with others—until suddenly, someone targets her life. Who is the attacker? And what is the reason—!? A mysterious Land Cruiser, its driver unseen, roars as it attacks! But with the police refusing to take her seriously, she decides to fight alone. If she can do that, she can make a fresh start...
title_norm:夜のストレンジャー 恐怖: In a corner of the city, Kawamura Kiriko lives a lonely life as a late-night taxi driver. Bound by a past with a criminal record, she continues to reject connections with others—until suddenly, someone targets her life. Who is the attacker? And what is the reason—!? A mysterious Land Cruiser, its driver unseen, roars as it attacks! But with the police refusing to take her seriously, she decides to fight alone. If she can do that, she can make a fresh start...
title_norm:夜の女たち: Synopsis: A shocking work depicting the fierce struggle for survival of women who become prostitutes in the burnt-out ruins of Osaka immediately after Japan's defeat. Among the many masterpieces by Tanaka and her ally Mizoguchi, this film leaves a vivid impression with Mizoguchi's cold-hearted direction and Tanaka's passionate performance as a war widow forced into street prostitution.
title_norm:夜は短し歩けよ乙女: An animated film adaptation of "The Night is Short, Walk on Girl," an early bestseller by popular author Tomihiko Morimi, known for "The Tatami Galaxy" and "Uchoten Kazoku," which humorously depicts the story of an unremarkable university student who pines for a black-haired maiden. Directed by Masaaki Yuasa, popular for his uniquely expressive animation works including the TV anime "The Tatami Galaxy," "Mind Game," and "Ping Pong The Animation." The screenplay is by Makoto Ueda of the theater troupe Europe Kikaku, who also worked on "The Tatami Galaxy." Singer-songwriter and actor Gen Hoshino, also popular for his role in the drama "We Married as a Job," voices the protagonist. The university student "Senpai," who harbors feelings for "the black-haired maiden," a junior in his club, spends his days executing the "Nakame Strategy" aimed at "getting her to notice him as much as possible." The seasons turn as he gets swept up in strange incidents caused by his colorful friends, but his relationship with the black-haired maiden only progresses around the edges without making real headway...
title_norm:夜中のポップコーン: A single-location comedy about an awkward, movie-loving girls' night that unfolds when three women gather for a TV broadcast of a B-movie. It won the Kinemaister Award at the 19th Tanabe-Benkei Film Festival, known as a gateway for independent films. One Friday night, three women gather at Misawa's home to watch a TV broadcast of "The Growth," a cult-favorite B-movie monster panic film. Nagata and Matsuno, invited by the host Misawa, are meeting for the first time, but due to Misawa's unexpected absence, they end up spending an awkward viewing party together. However, as time passes, they begin to open up to each other, and as they share memories related to movies, the connections and regrets binding the three of them on this day come to light. The director is Takumi Fujimoto, who also works as a stage director and made his feature-length film debut in 2021 with "Home Security Guard and Housework Fairy." The screenplay is by Saku Tanikaze, who works as an actor while also planning, writing, and directing stage productions. The film will be screened in theaters as part of the "Tanabe-Benkei Film Festival Selection 2026" (May 8–28, 2026 at Theatre Shinjuku / June 13–18, 2026 at Theatre Umeda), which showcases award-winning works from the festival.
title_norm:夜来風雨の声: The first feature film directed by Kohei Igarashi, a filmmaker gaining international attention for works like "Oyogisugita Yoru" and "Ikoi no Iki," made while he was a student at Tokyo Zokei University. Young couple Amano and Inaba live together, but life is tough because Inaba has lost his job. Still, Inaba doesn't work, and at night he goes out, meeting friends who treat him, or learning poetry from a cigarette seller. Amano says nothing to Inaba about this, simply watching over him. Then one day, Inaba hears from a friend about "a good job at the hospital"... The film received its theatrical premiere at the "Kohei Igarashi Director Retrospective: Seishun-teki Koto" (from September 20, 2024, at Shimokita-Ekimae-Cinema K2), held in conjunction with the release of Igarashi's feature "SUPER HAPPY FOREVER."
title_norm:夢の涯てまでも: A film that Wim Wenders nurtured for about 13 years before completing. Blending sci-fi elements, it combines a road movie and love story set in a world facing apocalypse. In the winter of 1999, the predicted crash of a nuclear satellite casts the world into anxiety. Claire, traveling by car from Venice, meets Trevor, who is being chased by someone. Though they part ways, she can't stop thinking about him and, with the help of her ex-lover (a writer) and a private detective, follows him to Lisbon, Moscow, and Beijing. Reuniting with Trevor in Tokyo, Claire learns the purpose of his journey.
title_norm:夢の涯てまでも ディレクターズカット・: A film that Wim Wenders nurtured for about 13 years before completing. Blending sci-fi elements, it combines a road movie and love story set in a world facing apocalypse. In the winter of 1999, the predicted crash of a nuclear satellite casts the world into anxiety. Claire, traveling by car from Venice, meets Trevor, who is being chased by someone. Though they part ways, she can't stop thinking about him and, with the help of her ex-lover (a writer) and a private detective, follows him to Lisbon, Moscow, and Beijing. Reuniting with Trevor in Tokyo, Claire learns the purpose of his journey.
title_norm:夢は牛のお医者さん: A documentary film adaptation of a 26-year chronicle following one girl's dream from its beginning to the present day, originally produced by TeNY Television Niigata, a local TV station in Niigata Prefecture. The story gained attention when it was featured on Nippon Television network programs such as "Zoom In!! Morning!" and "NNN Documentary." In 1987, three calves arrive at a small elementary school in the mountains of Niigata. A third-grade girl at the time dreams of becoming a "cow doctor" through caring for the calves. After parting with the cows she had grown attached to, and with support from her family and those around her, she overcomes difficult hurdles to become a veterinarian for "livestock," not pets. Through her continued dedication to invaluable lives every day—now as a married mother—the film explores the importance of having dreams, as well as themes of family, hometown, work, and the harshness of reality. Yui Yokoyama of AKB48 takes on her first narration role.
title_norm:夢物語 the living dragon: Bruce Lee, Jackie Chan, Jet Li, Donnie Yen... Yasuaki Kurata is the one and only active action actor who has engaged in fierce battles with countless legends. Now 80 years old and celebrating 60 years as an action actor, this legend takes on a new challenge! Directors Koichi Sakamoto, Kenji Tanigaki, and Yuji Shimomura—three currently active talents who are graduates of the Kurata Action Club—have taken the helm. Filming also took place in Hong Kong, resulting in a historic reunion on screen with Sammo Hung! The miraculous film 'Dream Story' follows a man who has dedicated his life to action. Be sure to see its full scope on the big screen!
title_norm:大丈夫、大丈夫、大丈夫！: A human drama set in a Seoul arts troupe in Korea, depicting the heartwarming connection between a high school girl who lost her mother and a perfectionist teacher. In-yeon, a member of the dance department at the Seoul International Arts Troupe, receives news of her mother's death. Raised in a single-parent household, she is evicted for unpaid rent and begins secretly sleeping in the troupe's practice room. Amid intense training for the troupe's 60th-anniversary performance, the cold-hearted artistic director Sora, known as the "witch," discovers In-yeon's living situation and takes her in as a live-in guest. Despite their differences in age, personality, and lifestyle, the two gradually open their hearts to each other as they spend time together. Meanwhile, problems arise within the team when Nari, the troupe's ace who is hostile toward In-yeon, falters, causing the feelings of In-yeon and the other members to diverge from Sora's. Lee Re from "Hope" plays the protagonist In-yeon, Jin Seo-yeon from "Believer" plays the teacher Sora called the "witch," and Son Seok-koo from "The Roundup" co-stars. Directed by Kim Hye-young, known for the TV drama "Be Melodramatic," in her feature-length debut. It won the Crystal Bear (Best Film) in the Generation Kplus section at the 74th Berlin International Film Festival in 2024, the first Korean film to do so.
title_norm:大丈夫であるように: A documentary born from a letter sent to Kore-eda by singer Cocco. Interweaving her journey across Japan, singing as if in prayer, with the song 'Jugon no Mieru Oka' inspired by the sight of a dugong appearing in the sea at the planned relocation site for the US military base in Henoko, Okinawa, and her daily life in her hometown of Okinawa. The film records the sincere figure of Cocco, celebrating her 10th debut anniversary, as she resonates with the pain of the land and devotes herself to singing.
title_norm:大丈夫と約束して: Official Selection, Competition Section of the 37th Tokyo International Film Festival (2024).
title_norm:大乗の國: Following the enactment of the Film Law in October 1939, the government mandated the nationwide screening of "culture films" the following year. Within Toho’s Culture Film Department, the Toho National Policy Film Association was established, with auditor Hirohisa Ikenaga serving as its chairman. This film was produced by the association as a follow-up to *Kodo Nippon* (The Imperial Way of Japan, 1939, dir. Taisuke Aoki). It depicts the introduction of Buddhism to Japan and its subsequent spread and development, interweaving footage of temples and artworks from across the country. The script was written by film historian Junichiro Tanaka, with Eiji Tsuburaya handling cinematography and composition. It was released to the public at the Toho 4th Floor Theater, which opened that same year. Although the Toho National Policy Film Association ceased operations after producing only these two films, Masaru Takamura of the publicity department, who had been instrumental in the production, hid the film after the war, allowing it to escape confiscation by the occupation forces.
title_norm:大濛: Directed by Taiwan's Yu-Hsun Chen, known for "The Girl Who Leapt Through Time" and "The Tropical Fish," this is a story of hope and rebirth set against the backdrop of the "White Terror" era in 1950s Taiwan, when many citizens were arrested and executed on suspicion of being anti-government. In the 1950s, under martial law in Taiwan. A young girl named A-Yue, living in Chiayi, learns that her brother, captured as an anti-government element, has been executed in Taipei. With a small amount of money and her brother's keepsake watch in hand, she heads to Taipei alone, only to find that a hefty fee is required to claim his body. At her wit's end, she is tricked by a suspicious man and nearly sold into a brothel, but is rescued by a rickshaw puller named Zhao Gongdao. Originally from Guangdong, China, he came to Taiwan as a soldier for the Nationalist army and has been unable to return home, living hand-to-mouth ever since. Having lost his army comrades to the White Terror and finding no direction in life, Gongdao is moved by A-Yue's determination and decides to lend her a hand. Caitlin Fang ("A Girl from America") plays A-Yue, Will Or ("The Staggering Girl") plays Zhao Gongdao, and popular Taiwanese singer and actor 9m88 co-stars. The film won four awards, including Best Feature Film, at the 62nd Golden Horse Awards in 2025.
title_norm:大統領のケーキ: Lamia, chosen as the 'honorable' cake maker, goes out to town with her grandmother and friend the rooster to search for cake ingredients──
title_norm:天井 ／ 袋いっぱいの蚤: A screening of two rare works by Věra Chytilová, the standard-bearer of the Czech New Wave renowned for *Daisies* (1966). *Ceiling*, her graduation project from the Film and TV School of the Academy of Performing Arts in Prague (FAMU), employs cinéma vérité-style cinematography to portray the inner void felt by a woman who transitions from a medical student to a successful model, trading her glamorous lifestyle for a series of imposed constraints. Her subsequent film, *A Bagful of Fleas*, also utilizes a cinéma vérité approach to vividly capture the everyday lives of girls in a dormitory.
title_norm:天使たち: Set in Shinjuku's Kabukicho, this film portrays two girls working at a girls' bar alongside women from various backgrounds. As they continue to sell their youth and perform the roles demanded of them, they gradually lose sight of what they truly want. The film won the Movie.com Award at the 18th Tanabe Benkei Film Festival, a gateway for new directors. Naru, 19, starts working at a girls' bar after high school to leave her parents' home. Maria, 21, works at the same bar while attending university to repay her student loans. Bathed in the neon lights of the night town, Naru wishes to become someone special, while Maria longs to be a normal college student. One day, Naru meets a host on the streets of Kabukicho, and Maria is approached by a customer for an off-the-books deal. The director and screenwriter is Naima Kimura, for whom this is her second directorial work and first feature film. Kimura drew inspiration from her own experience working at a girls' bar as a student. The film was screened in theaters as part of the "Tanabe Benkei Film Festival Selection 2024" (May 9–June 5, 2024 at Theatre Shinjuku; June 20–26, 2024 at Theatre Umeda).
title_norm:天使の涙: Director Wong Kar-wai of 'Chungking Express' crafts a pop-infused ensemble drama about the poignant romantic entanglements of five men and women in the neon-lit streets of Hong Kong. This film completes an episode originally planned as part of 'Chungking Express' as an independent work. A lonely hitman and the woman who acts as his agent. Their rule is to keep personal feelings out of work, but their relationship begins to waver. Meanwhile, a mute young man named Mo sneaks into other people's shops every night and runs them without permission. One day, Mo meets a woman who has just been heartbroken and falls for her. The hitman is played by Leon Lai of 'The City of Sadness,' the agent by Michelle Lee of 'Flowers of Shanghai,' and Mo by Takeshi Kaneshiro of 'Chungking Express.' Cinematography is by Christopher Doyle, who worked on many of Wong Kar-wai's films. First released in Japan in 1996. In 2022, a 4K restored version was screened as part of 'WKW4K' (from August 19, 2022, at Cine Mart Shinjuku, Grand Cinema Sunshine, Cinema City, etc.).
title_norm:天外者: A historical ensemble drama starring Haruma Miura, depicting the life of Tomoatsu Godai, a visionary who built the foundations of modern Japan's economy and was hailed as a 'Tengaramon' (a person of extraordinary talent). Written by Eriko Komatsu and directed by Mitsutoshi Tanaka, the film presents an original story. In the late Edo period, Japan is shocked by Perry's arrival. Young samurai Saisuke Godai (later Tomoatsu), sensing the dawn of a new era, ignores internal conflicts over expulsion or opening of the country and looks to the world. After meeting the courtesan Haru, he is driven by the desire for 'free dreams' and joins forces with Ryoma Sakamoto, Yataro Iwasaki, Hirobumi Ito, and others to build a nation where everyone can dream. Shohei Miura plays Ryoma Sakamoto, Godai's ally; Takanori Nishikawa plays Yataro Iwasaki, who later founded the Mitsubishi conglomerate; Yuki Morinaga plays a young Hirobumi Ito, who becomes the first Prime Minister; and Mei Nagano plays the courtesan Haru.

title_norm:天気の子: Director Makoto Shinkai, whose "Your Name." was a historic blockbuster, presents a feature animation depicting a boy and girl in an era of disrupted weather harmony, struggling against fate while choosing their own way of life. Hodaka, a high school student who runs away from a remote island to Tokyo, quickly falls into poverty. After lonely days, he finally lands a job writing for a shady occult magazine. As if foreshadowing his future, rain falls day after day. One day, Hodaka meets a girl named Hina in a corner of the city. Living alone with her younger brother due to circumstances, she possesses a mysterious ability to clear the sky by "praying"... Kotaro Daigo, who appeared in "My Brother Loves Me Too Much," and Nana Mori, with upcoming roles in "Hell Girl" and "Last Letter," voice Hodaka and Hina respectively. Other cast members include Shun Oguri, Tsubasa Honda, Junpei Heisawa, Yuuki Kaji, and Chieko Baisho. Following "Your Name.," Genki Kawamura serves as planner and producer, Masayoshi Tanaka as character designer, and rock band RADWIMPS provides the music. Actress Toko Miura participates as female vocals on the RADWIMPS theme song.
title_norm:太福 daifuku: A short documentary by British youth Theo Barnes, who came to Japan to study animation, recording the final days of 'Daifuku,' a set meal restaurant that operated for over half a century on 'Star Road,' a shopping street near Asagaya Station on the Chuo Line. In a corner of the 'Star Road' shopping street at the north exit of Tokyo's Asagaya Station, 'Daifuku' had supported people's meals since the period of high economic growth. It was not just a place serving home-style cooking, but a small community where regulars gathered and exchanged words. In February 2026, the restaurant's closing day approaches. The steaming kitchen, laughter echoing at the counter, the resilient figure of the mama-san protecting her shop—no major events occur, but the lives of people built up over time are palpably alive. The director is 20-year-old British youth Theo Barnes, who came to Asagaya to study animation. Stumbling into this shop by chance, he became captivated by traditional Japanese living culture and, from a foreigner's unique perspective, captured the fading Showa-era scenery.
title_norm:太陽の王子 ホルスの大冒険: Director Isao Takahata's feature-length debut, made in 1968 during his time at Toei Animation. Based on the puppet play 'The Sun on the Spring Elm' by Kazuo Fukazawa, it depicts the brave boy Hols, entrusted with the Sun Sword, confronting a demon. Hols lives with his father in a remote natural setting. Rescued from a wolf attack by the rock giant Moog, Hols receives the Sun Sword embedded in Moog's shoulder. After losing his father, Hols follows his father's dying wish and sets out for a village where people live, but is captured by the terrifying demon Grunwald and thrown off a cliff. Washing up in a village, Hols defeats a giant pike that has been plaguing the villagers and becomes a hero. One day, he meets a lonely girl named Hilda in a ruined village and brings her back, but... Scene design, art design, and key animation were handled by Hayao Miyazaki, animation direction by Yasuo Otsuka, and key animation by Koji Mori. It was released as part of the 'Toei Manga Parade' (Toei Manga Festival) in the summer of 1968.

title_norm:太陽（ティダ）の運命: Director Tadahiko Sako, known for "Kamejiro: The Man the U.S. Military Feared Most," delves into modern Okinawan history through the lives of two governors who fiercely confronted the national government. Masahide Ota (the 4th governor after Okinawa's reversion to Japan, serving 1990–98) and Takeshi Onaga (the 7th governor, serving 2014–18) held opposing political positions, yet both garnered broad support from the people and managed the prefecture by transcending the traditional conservative-liberal divide. Ota fought the state in court in 1995 over his refusal to sign for the forced use of military land, while Onaga did the same in 2015 regarding the revocation of the Henoko landfill approval; their battles brought to light the nature of democracy, local autonomy, and the contradictions of the nation. Incorporating testimonies from many who were involved in their lives, the film highlights their personal charisma and depicts the indomitable struggle of two men who lived by their convictions. The title "Tida" means "Sun" in the Okinawan dialect, a word that anciently referred to a chief or leader.
title_norm:失われた週末: A serious drama acclaimed worldwide, winning four Academy Awards and the Grand Prix at the Cannes Film Festival. Don, a struggling writer living in New York, drowns his days in alcohol. Desperate for drink money, he steals from his brother and even tries to sell his typewriter. Ray Milland delivers a powerful performance as Don wandering the depths of despair, earning him an Oscar for Best Actor. Director Wilder met his second wife, Audrey Young, during the making of this film.
title_norm:失楽園: Kuki, once a sharp editor at a publishing house but now relegated to a dead-end position, meets Rinko, a married woman who teaches calligraphy at a culture center run by a friend, and continues an adulterous affair with her. Their love only deepens, and Kuki eventually rents an apartment in Tokyo to serve as their love nest. But Rinko's husband hires a private detective and learns of her infidelity, while Kuki's wife pressures him for a divorce. Yet the more they are cornered by those around them, the more fiercely Kuki and Rinko's love burns.
title_norm:奇跡: Director Hirokazu Kore-eda of "Nobody Knows" and "Air Doll" depicts a family drama set in Kyushu, which is buzzing with excitement over the full opening of the Kyushu Shinkansen line in March 2010. Starring the comedy brother duo Maeda Maeda's Koki Maeda and Koshiro Maeda. The story follows two brothers, separated by their parents' divorce to live in Kagoshima and Fukuoka respectively, who strive to reunite their broken family, spurred on by the full opening of the bullet train line. Co-stars include regulars from Kore-eda's films such as Yui Natsukawa, Atsushi Abe, Yoshio Harada, and Kirin Kiki.
title_norm:女たちの庭: Soichiro Ishizuka, the head of Kikumaru Textiles—a venerable establishment in Nihonbashi—has three daughters, Hatsuko, Yuko, and Izumi, with his wife Ayako. Hatsuko has taken Yoshio as her husband to serve as the family heir, and the parents are now searching for a suitable match for Yuko. One day, Soichiro’s old schoolmate Furusawa arrives with news that another classmate, Mayama—a potter living in Imari, Kyushu—is rumored to be terminally ill with cancer...
title_norm:女たちの証言 －「労働運動のなかの先駆的女性たち」: In 1982, under the sponsorship of socialist researcher Kiyomizu Ishidō, a roundtable discussion was held with pioneering female activists who had participated in the launch of the popular labor movement from the Taishō to Shōwa eras. Those gathered were Setsu Tanno (wife of Masanosuke Watanabe), Utako Nabeyama (wife of Sadachika Nabeyama), Misao Fukuoka (wife of Kyōji Koreeda), and Mina Yamauchi (wife of Naokazu Tachibana). Although they had once worked together in the movement, decades later, after the war, some held different positions, making such a gathering rare. At the request of the host, Mr. Ishidō, who said, 'I want to record this for posterity,' director Haneda filmed the discussion. Time passed without the footage being released, but driven by the director's strong desire to 'preserve the history of these women,' additional filming was done as much as possible to compile the work. In this film, the discrimination and subjugation experienced by these female activists are told in their own words. It is a work that quietly questions what true women's liberation really is.
title_norm:女たちの証言－労働運動のなかの先駆的な女性たち－: In 1982, under the sponsorship of socialist researcher Kiyomizu Ishidō, a roundtable discussion was held with pioneering female activists who had participated in the launch of the popular labor movement from the Taishō to Shōwa eras. title_norm:女ともだち: The third feature film by Italian master Michelangelo Antonioni, known for the 'trilogy of arid love' including L'Avventura, La Notte, and L'Eclisse, made in 1955. Set in Turin, it depicts the unstable relationships of five women who meet by chance through his distinctive visual style, winning the Silver Lion at the 16th Venice International Film Festival. Clelia, who works at a high-end dress shop based in Rome, arrives in Turin as the manager of a new branch opening there. One night, in the hotel room next to her lodging, she discovers Rosetta unconscious after a suicide attempt. Through this incident, Clelia deepens her friendship with Rosetta and her friend Momina... Based on Cesare Pavese's novel "Among Women Only." Starring Eleonora Rossi Drago from "The Golden Coach," Gabriele Ferzetti from L'Avventura, and Valentina Cortese from "Day for Night," among others. First released in Japanese theaters in 1964. A 2K restored version will be shown in August 2026 at the retrospective "Michelangelo Antonioni Retrospective: Arid Love, Wandering Souls," featuring five of Antonioni's early works.
title_norm:女と男のいる舗道: This is Jean-Luc Godard's fourth feature film, following "A Woman Is a Woman," and was shot starring Anna Karina, his partner both publicly and privately. Nana, who decides to part ways with her husband after discussing life with him at a café in Paris, falls into a life where she cannot even pay her rent. She begins to proposition men on the street and engage in prostitution. Eventually, Nana becomes numb to having relations with strangers. The music was handled by Michel Legrand, the renowned composer of "The Umbrellas of Cherbourg" and other films.
title_norm:女は女である: This is Jean-Luc Godard's third feature film, following "Breathless," and a romantic comedy created based on the idea of a "musical comedy in which the characters do not sing." Angela, a cabaret dancer, tells her live-in lover Émile that she wants a child right now. Émile cannot hide his bewilderment at her request. Then a young man named Alfred, who has feelings for Angela, appears... Following Godard's previous film "Le Petit Soldat," Anna Karina plays the heroine, with Jean-Paul Belmondo of "Breathless" as Alfred and Jean-Claude Brialy of "Les Cousins" as Émile. The music is by Michel Legrand, the renowned composer of "The Umbrellas of Cherbourg" and other films.
title_norm:女鹿: Centering on the intense and mysterious relationship between two women—one dominant, one submissive, almost like doppelgängers—this masterpiece from Chabrol's 'peak period' exudes a powerful allure with the film itself baring love and hatred. One day, Frédérique, a bourgeois woman, spots Hoïe, a girl drawing on the pavement of the Pont des Arts bridge over the Seine. Hoïe comes to live at Frédérique's mansion and is drawn to Paul, a guest, but Paul also has a relationship with Frédérique... A sensual work filled with the complex and ambiguous hearts of women. In this film, Stéphane Audran, who was already Chabrol's wife, co-stars with her former husband Jean-Louis Trintignant. (1968) *All films screened in digitally remastered versions.
title_norm:妻の病 レビー小体型認知症: This documentary captures the ten-year journey and the profound bond between Dr. Koichi Ishimoto, a pediatrician in Nankoku City, Kochi Prefecture, and his wife, Yayoi, as they navigate her battle with dementia. After being diagnosed with schizophrenia in 2004, it was discovered three years later that Yayoi actually had early-onset Lewy body dementia. Since then, Dr. Ishimoto has meticulously recorded his wife’s daily life, utilizing the keen observational eye unique to a physician. Director Shinichi Ise, who first met Dr. Ishimoto during the production of his pediatric cancer documentary "Kaze no Katachi," provides a warm portrayal of the doctor caring for Yayoi with deep affection while supported by family and the local community. Through the story of a couple whose bond deepens through illness, the film asks what is truly important when a loved one—or oneself—is faced with dementia.
title_norm:宇宙からのメッセージ: A bandwagon film made by Kinji Fukasaku during the Star Wars boom. Though the story is simplistic, borrowing from the Tale of the Eight Dog Warriors, it generated buzz with the casting of Vic Morrow and the construction of a full-scale replica of the Riave ship. While the special effects fall short compared to Star Wars, the chase scenes created without compositing were highly praised overseas. The planet Jirusia in the Andromeda Galaxy has been transformed into a "Planet Fortress" by the invading Gabanas Empire, led by Emperor Roxeia XII. Jirusia's Great Chief Kido seeks a hero of miraculous salvation, releasing eight "Sacred Riave Fruits" into space and instructing his granddaughter Emeralida and two warriors, Urokko, to pursue the fruits and retrieve the hero. However, Roxeia launches pursuit warships without delay. The Riave fruits reach five individuals on the Earth Federation colony planet Miraseria: Galda, a former general who resigned in disillusionment; Shiro and Aron, young space bikers; Jack, a thug; and Meia, a wealthy heiress. The youths find Emeralida's damaged ship while collecting "Space Fireflies" and rescue her and Urokko, but are bewildered by their mission. Galda returns the fruit and declines to join. Shiro and the others, keeping Meia in the dark, lie about introducing other heroes and sell Emeralida to an old woman seeking a bride for her son. The old woman and Emeralida are later captured by Gabanas pursuit forces. Meia, furious upon learning of their actions, inspires the repentant youths to prepare for Jirusia's rescue. They modify Meia's space boat to carry Shiro and Aron's small craft and head for Jirusia. Along the way, they are joined by Hans, a Gabanas man who holds a Riave fruit and is the rightful heir to the Gabanas throne, usurped by Roxeia. Meanwhile, Gabanas, captivated by Earth's beauty, demands unconditional surrender from the Earth Federation. Amid the chaos, Shiro and his six companions, now reunited with Galda, infiltrate the Gabanas fortress to destroy the planet fortress and rescue Emeralida. Gathering the remaining two allies, the eight confront Roxeia.
title_norm:宇宙戦争 次の世紀: One of four dark sci-fi works by Piotr Szulkin, a pioneer of dystopian sci-fi in Poland, who created them during the late 1970s and 1980s under the socialist regime, navigating strict censorship. The film depicts the theme of 'escape from totalitarianism' with a style of intense satire and surrealism taken to its extreme. Martians have attacked Earth. A TV host has been telling people 'there is nothing to fear,' but his apartment is ransacked and his wife is kidnapped. The nightly TV script is also changed, and the reality he sees no longer matches what he tells people every night. The film will have its theatrical premiere in Japan as part of the special screening project 'Polish Dark Sci-Fi: The Four Films of Piotr Szulkin' (starting February 21, 2026, at Theater Image Forum).
title_norm:安寿と厨子王丸: Summoned by Toei's top brass seeking a weighty drama, screenwriter Sumie Tanaka was brought on board. The story follows aristocratic siblings reduced to slavery, overcoming their suffering through social advancement. Animators strongly objected to the narrative's obliviousness to societal power structures, yet the breathtakingly beautiful Yamato-e style visuals, where backgrounds and characters harmonize perfectly, captivate the viewer.
title_norm:完全版 ザ・レンチキュラーズ a b: "Rakkun" has a crush on his classmate "Sawaki-san." After a simple exchange of work gloves brings them closer together, Rakkun is walking on air—until he remembers a rumor that she had a boyfriend in middle school. Director Akira Amemiya of the SSSS.GRIDMAN series presents a relatable, slice-of-life youth romantic comedy.
title_norm:宝島: A documentary by Guillaume Brac, director of 'A Summer's Tale' and 'The Gentle Ones,' capturing a summer at the leisure facility 'Leisure Island' in Cergy-Pontoise, a suburb of Paris. Known as the setting for Éric Rohmer's 'My Girlfriend's Boyfriend,' and a place Brac himself frequently visited as a child, Leisure Island is filled with vacationers but has no flashy attractions, only expanses of water and greenery. Under beautiful sunlight, the film captures the natural moments of various people: boys trying to sneak into the facility, young men hitting on women, an elderly man reminiscing about the past, and employees managing and guarding the place.
title_norm:実録阿部定: "The outside light bothers me" "His smell is soaked into the futon too..." Sadame closes the storm shutters to keep Kichizō's scent from escaping. How long has it been since the two of them were alone in the small room of the teahouse? Their union seeks ever more unknown pleasures. Sadame, choking Kichizō, says happily, "Kichi-san is twitching inside me." But when Kichizō, whose health is beginning to fail, suggests returning home for a while, Sadame's pure love for him becomes directly linked to pure desire. "I won't let anyone else touch you anymore. No one..."
title_norm:宮古島物語ふたたヴィラ かんかかりゃの願い: The third chapter of the "Miyako Island Story: Futatavilla" series, a human drama exploring the bonds and rebirth of people set against the backdrop of a small hotel on Okinawa's Miyako Island. Directed, written by, and starring Yudai Uanishi (known for "Hitokuzu" and "Goro's 400 Million Yen"), the film centers on a small villa called "Futatavilla," where it is said that staying will grant the reunion one truly desires. A couple who lost their daughter to bullying, a man pursued by debt and guilt, and friends burdened by their pasts—each carrying their own pain and prayers—are drawn to the island as if guided by the wind, eventually discovering a glimmer of new hope. The cast includes Katsuya Shibayama, chairman of Resort Life Co., Ltd., which operates hotels in Miyako Island and throughout Japan, alongside returning regulars Yudai Uanishi, Chieko Matsubara, Ai Furukawa, Mika Tokutake, and Ruby Moreno. Guest stars include Ryo Tamura and Tamotsu Ishibashi.
title_norm:家からの手紙: A documentary by Belgian director Chantal Akerman, who revolutionized cinema with 'Jeanne Dielman, 23 quai du Commerce, 1080 Bruxelles,' a portrait of an ordinary housewife's daily routine. In this film, she reads letters from her mother over footage capturing the landscapes of 1970s New York. By layering her mother's affectionate words over the bleak cityscapes of New York—alleyways, cars on avenues, people waiting for trains on station platforms, and underground passages—the film highlights the alienation of urban life and the distance from family far away. In Japan, it received its theatrical premiere at the 'Chantal Akerman Film Festival 2023' (April 7–27, 2023, Human Trust Cinema Shibuya), screened together with 'Saute ma ville.'
title_norm:家族という病: Writer Shimojo Akiko's 2015 essay, which questioned the concept of 'family worship' and became a bestseller with 600,000 copies, is adapted into a film by director-screenwriter Oyama Chikako of 'My Name is Lucia.' This ensemble piece, laced with black humor, depicts the absurdity and madness of people clinging to normalcy. Bestselling mystery novelist Tahara Junichiro has his life controlled by his intense wife Mariko, leaving his true talent dormant. Former elite salaryman Matsubara Yuji, unable to betray his mother's expectations even after retirement, continues to play the role of a fake executive while dealing with his hikikomori son. High school girl Kuroki Maria is driven into a corner when rumors spread that her mother is an AV actress. Appearing before these three families is Fujita Shin, an up-and-coming writer who won a literary award for a work themed around nudity. Additionally, a homeless woman living freely in the park appears as a completely different presence. Starring Fujimoto Takahiro, Tomochika, Watanabe Eri, Koide Keisuke, Teraishi Ken, Sakakibara Ai, and Hiroi Wakana.
title_norm:富江: Tsukiko Izumisawa, a girl suffering from memory loss and insomnia due to an accident three years ago, attends a psychiatric clinic. Her doctor, Hosono, probes her memories through hypnotherapy and hears the name "Tomie." However, Tsukiko cannot recall who that name belongs to. Then, strange and terrifying events suddenly begin occurring in Tsukiko's life. One day, a detective from the Metropolitan Police visits Hosono. He is investigating a woman named Tomie Kawakami.
title_norm:富江 tomie: Tsukiko Izumisawa, a girl suffering from memory loss and insomnia due to an accident three years ago, attends a psychiatric clinic. title_norm:寝ても覚めても: The commercial film debut of director Ryusuke Hamaguchi, who gained attention for "Happy Hour," a film that meticulously depicted the daily lives and friendships of four women over more than five hours and won major awards at numerous international film festivals including Locarno and Nantes. This film was entered into the Competition section of the 71st Cannes International Film Festival. It is an adaptation of the award-winning love novel of the same name by Akutagawa Prize-winning author Tomoka Shibasaki, starring Masahiro Higashide and Erika Karata. Asako, a 21-year-old living in Osaka, meets Baku and falls into a fateful love, but one day, Baku suddenly disappears from her life. Two years later, having moved from Osaka to Tokyo, Asako meets Ryohei, who has a face identical to Baku's. Unable to forget Baku, Asako tries to avoid Ryohei, but he develops feelings for her. Despite her hesitation, Asako finds herself drawn to Ryohei. Higashide plays the dual roles of Baku and Ryohei, while Karata plays Asako.
