title_norm:寝る映画:
A film featuring a screenplay generated by ChatGPT, with its ethereal visuals and music also brought to life through AI. As the characters experience a virtual world while asleep, they discover a profound connection to the film's core themes: "seeing with the heart" and "touching with sound."

Yuki is blind, and her husband Ken is deaf. Despite their bond, a certain distance lingers between them. One day, the couple joins a clinical trial premised on the idea that "disabilities can be overcome within an AI-generated virtual reality." While their bodies sleep in the physical world, they awaken in a virtual realm where their sight and hearing have been restored. Amidst the strange occurrences of this world, they begin to sense each other’s presence more deeply than ever before.

Positioned as "unconscious immersive cinema" designed to be experienced while the viewer sleeps, this experimental film attempts to reach the subconscious by layering poetic phrases, music, and subtitled imagery throughout. It is directed by Tsuyoshi Sone, widely known as the cinematographer of "One Cut of the Dead."
title_norm:尋秦記 バック・トゥ・ザ・パスト: A historical sci-fi action film and sequel to the 2001 TV series 'A Step into the Past', based on a popular Hong Kong novel. After time-traveling to the Warring States period and deeply influencing history, former Hong Kong police VIP protection officer Xiang Shaolong lives quietly in seclusion with his wife and child. His former disciple, the King of Qin, whom Xiang helped ascend the throne, remains wary of his master, their conflict smoldering. Meanwhile in modern Hong Kong, Ken, the time machine inventor imprisoned for 20 years for Xiang's failure to return, is released. Having lost everything, he plots to seize the Qin throne and become the First Emperor himself, traveling back to the Warring States with his daughter Gary and others. Attacked by Ken, the King of Qin flees and ends up at Xiang Shaolong's refuge. Louis Koo and Raymond Lam, who also starred together in the 2024 hit 'Twilight of the Warriors: Walled In', reprise their roles as Xiang Shaolong and the King of Qin, also performing the theme song. Alongside original TV series cast members, the film features Michael Miu ('White Storm'), Bai Baihe ('Monster Hunt'), and Wu Yue ('Ip Man: The Finale'). Hong Kong action star Sammo Hung serves as action director.
title_norm:小さな恋のメロディ: A coming-of-age love story about the first love of an 11-year-old boy and girl, which became a huge hit in Japan along with the theme song 'Melody Fair' by the Bee Gees. Daniel, a shy boy attending a London public school, is best friends with his rambunctious classmate Tom, and they always play together. One day after school, while peeking at the girls' ballet practice, Daniel's heart is captured by a girl named Melody. They are drawn to each other and eventually promise to get married... The screenplay was written by Alan Parker, who later directed films such as 'Midnight Express' and 'Mississippi Burning.' A digital remastered version was re-released in June 2019.
title_norm:小川のほとりで: Korean master Hong Sang-soo directs an ensemble drama set at a women's university in Seoul, depicting the romantic entanglements of students and adults surrounding a theater festival. At a women's university in Seoul, with the theater festival approaching, textile artist Jon-hee, who works as a lecturer, invites her uncle Si-on, a famous actor and stage director, as a temporary director to fill a gap caused by a love scandal on campus. As they begin creating a short play for the festival, various events unfold over ten days, including the aftermath of the students' love affairs and the budding romance between a senior professor and Si-on. Actress Kim Min-hee, Hong Sang-soo's partner in both public and private life, stars as Jon-hee and won the Best Performance Award at the 77th Locarno International Film Festival in 2024. The cast also includes regulars from Hong Sang-soo's films: Kwon Hae-hyo as Jon-hee's uncle Si-on, Cho Yun-hee as the professor who admires Si-on, and Ha Seong-guk as the fired director who was dating three people. In Japan, it was screened under the title 'Suyuchon' at the 25th Tokyo Filmex in 2024. It was theatrically released in 2025 as the second film in the 'Monthly Hong Sang-soo' project, a series of five consecutive monthly new releases celebrating the director's 30th debut anniversary.
title_norm:小春日和 indian summer:
This human drama depicts a troubled and isolated nursing assistant searching for her own way of life through a series of encounters. The film was planned and produced by Tomoko Kusube, a psychiatrist and actress, who drew from her own experience battling cancer to convey the importance of living a positive life.

Koharu Sakaguchi, burdened by worries she cannot share with anyone, flees her home after a clash with her father. Unable to return due to her feelings of guilt, she begins working as a nursing assistant at a hospital. Through her interactions with patients facing their illnesses in their own ways—such as "The Cancers," a trio of women living brightly despite their battle with cancer, and Yuki Yamamoto, who chooses to be discharged to spend her remaining days at home—Koharu gradually begins to confront her own life. One day, she suddenly recalls a precious message from her beloved grandmother, Suzuko, and makes a firm resolution.

Misaki Mizumura (*Move Forward as You Are*) stars as Koharu Sakaguchi, with Yura Chihara as Hiyori Sakaguchi, Kaoru Yumi as Grandmother Suzuko, Rie Shibata as cancer patient Yuki Yamamoto, Kappa Kunikida as Yuki’s husband Takashi, and Shiro Sano as Dr. Hiroshi Ueda. The film is directed by Isao Matsumoto (*Let’s Meet at Angie’s Bar*).
title_norm:少佐と少女: Billy Wilder's second directorial work, which was never theatrically released in Japan. This was his highly anticipated first Hollywood film, successfully casting the era's star Ginger Rogers. To save money on train fare to Iowa, Susan disguises herself as a 12-year-old girl. A faint affection begins to blossom between her and Colonel Philip, who happens to be on the same train... Although the film touches on the theme of attraction to a minor, it was produced 12 years before the publication of the bestselling novel "Lolita."
title_norm:少女ムシェット: Master filmmaker Robert Bresson's eighth feature, made right after his masterpiece "Au Hasard Balthazar." Based on a novel by French author Georges Bernanos, it starkly and realistically depicts the tragic fate of a young girl through rigorous framing and the actors' minimally restrained performances. 14-year-old Mouchette lives in the French countryside, forced to run the household for her alcoholic father and ill mother, while being cruelly treated by classmates and teachers at school. The unfortunate girl's fate takes a turn for the worse when, one rainy night, she encounters a poacher in the forest, sending her spiraling into further misery and ruin. Nadine Nortier, discovered for this role, plays the protagonist Mouchette, a girl standing on the brink of despair yet harboring a rebellious spirit. Produced in 1967, it was first released in Japan in 1974 by Equipe de Cinema, and again in 1995 by France Eiga Sha. A 4K restored digital remastered version had a revival release in October 2020. Another revival release is scheduled for 2026 as part of the "Robert Bresson Masterpiece Selection."
title_norm:少年ジャックと魔法使い: Directed by Yasuji Yabushita with animation direction by Akira Daikuhara for Toei Animation's 10th anniversary film. Based on the heroic epic 'Beowulf,' this version features Jack driving a car, a witch arriving by helicopter, and a struggle to rescue comrades turned into demons in the witch's castle. Seiichiro Uno's cheerful music won the Mainichi Film Concours Music Award.
title_norm:少年猿飛佐助: The second feature-length animation produced against the backdrop of the flourishing Toei period drama genre. For the sword-fighting scenes, Reijiro Adachi, a top action choreographer at Toei Kyoto Studio, was brought in, and Daikuhara Akira, known for dynamic action, handled both direction and key animation. Newcomers including Isao Takahata, Hiroshi Ikeda, Masao Kuroda, and Yoichi Kotabe participated in production for the first time. It is also Japan's first feature-length animation in CinemaScope.
title_norm:山の焚火: A 1985 film by the master Fredi M. Murer, known as a pioneer of New Swiss Cinema, which won the Golden Leopard, the top prize at the Locarno International Film Festival. A family of four lives a nearly self-sufficient life surrounded by the majestic Alps. The teenage younger brother, who is deaf-mute, grows up healthily, sometimes frustrated by his disability but loved by his parents and older sister. One day, angered by a broken lawnmower, he throws it away, incurring his father's wrath. Running away from home, he begins living alone in a mountain hut. His worried sister brings him food, and they spend happy times together around a campfire on the mountain peak. Eventually, the sister's pregnancy is discovered... The film was first released in Japanese theaters in 1986. A digitally remastered version was revived in February 2020.
title_norm:山口くんはワルくない: A youth romance live-action film adaptation of the shōjo manga of the same name by Yu Saiki, serialized in Kodansha's 'Bessatsu Friend,' starring Kyōhei Takahashi of the idol group 'Naniwa Danshi.' It depicts the romantic journey of Satsuki, an ordinary high school girl who dreams of love, and Yamaguchi-kun, a transfer student with a scary-looking face and a Kansai dialect. Yamaguchi-kun, who transfers to Satsuki's school, has blonde hair and piercings, giving him a menacing look, and rumors circulate that he's a yakuza. After a certain incident brings her close to Yamaguchi-kun, Satsuki learns about his shy and kind true nature and gradually becomes drawn to him. Satsuki tries to keep Yamaguchi-kun's hidden charms all to herself, but a handsome classmate, Ishizaki, who inexplicably has a grudge against Yamaguchi-kun, stands in her way. It turns out Ishizaki also harbors special feelings for Yamaguchi-kun, suddenly emerging as Satsuki's romantic rival. The love triangle of these three takes an unexpected turn. Kyōhei Takahashi plays Yamaguchi-kun, who has a kind and pure heart beneath his scary appearance; Hikaru Takahashi ('Romantic Killer') plays the heroine Satsuki, who grows close to Yamaguchi-kun; and Yōji Iwase ('The Girl and the Guard Dog') plays Ishizaki, the classmate who stirs up trouble between Yamaguchi-kun and Satsuki. The film is directed by Kentarō Moriya ('PRINCE OF LEGEND,' 'Seaside Motel').
title_norm:山椒大夫: Commentary: In the Heian period, Zushio and Anju, separated from their parents, are sold into slavery... A film adaptation of Ogai's short story based on a medieval folktale, this timeless masterpiece won the Silver Lion at the Venice International Film Festival. The visual beauty captured by the renowned cinematographer Miyagawa is also awe-inspiring.
title_norm:岡本万太: The protagonist, Manta Okamoto (Sojiro Sanada), is a 26-year-old part-timer. Plagued by mounting irritation over life’s minor inconveniences, he lives in constant fear of whether he can suppress his own impulses. For Manta is a man of uncontrollable rage. Once a month, his stress reaches a breaking point—his "Limit Day." To cope, he locks himself away at home, strapped to a bed with restraints. Because these days strike without warning, he frequently misses work, leading to a cycle of being fired and drifting from one job to the next. One day, Nakamura (Masaki Miura), a former senior colleague from a publishing house that let him go, approaches him with a new opportunity. The job is simple: store some cardboard boxes for a few days in exchange for a large sum of money. But...
title_norm:左利きの少女: Taipei, a night market noodle stall. Five-year-old Yi-jin (Nina Yeh), along with her single mother Shue-fen (Janel Tsai) who is burdened with debt, and her teenage sister Yi-an (Ma Shih-yuan), returns from the countryside to rebuild their lives. One day, her old-fashioned grandfather denounces her dominant left hand as the "devil's hand," and Yi-jin begins to feel guilt. That devil's hand, inadvertently, brings to light the "sins" that each family member has been hiding.
title_norm:左撇子女孩: Taipei, a night market noodle stall. Five-year-old Yi-jin (Nina Yeh), along with her single mother Shue-fen (Janel Tsai) who is burdened with debt, and her teenage sister Yi-an (Ma Shih-yuan), returns from the countryside to rebuild their lives. One day, her old-fashioned grandfather denounces her dominant left hand as the "devil's hand," and Yi-jin begins to feel guilt. That devil's hand, inadvertently, brings to light the "sins" that each family member has been hiding.
title_norm:市民ケーン: A human drama produced, directed, co-written, and starring the 25-year-old prodigy Orson Welles, hailed as a masterpiece in film history. Based on real-life newspaper magnate William Randolph Hearst, it depicts the tumultuous life of a wealthy tycoon through innovative visual techniques and narrative structure. The wealthy newspaper magnate Kane dies, leaving behind the mysterious word "Rosebud." A newsreel editor assigned to investigate the meaning of the word interviews people who knew Kane in life, including his ex-wife and business partners. What emerges is the lonely life of a man who had everything. The film won the Academy Award for Best Original Screenplay at the 14th Academy Awards in 1942.
title_norm:帰って来たドラゴン: In the late Qing dynasty, the villainous Im Kun-ho rules over Gold Sand Village, a place rife with all kinds of crime and violence, including drugs and human trafficking. The Dragon group, traveling while punishing evil, and at the same time, the legendary female martial artist Eagle, arrive in this village. They are both searching for a treasure called the 'Silver Pearl', said to have been stolen from a Tibetan temple. Then, the ruthless killer karate practitioner Black Jaguar also appears, and fierce battles unfold among the powerful fighters over the Silver Pearl. This is the Japan comeback film for Yasuaki Kurata, who was active primarily in Hong Kong.
title_norm:幕末ヒポクラテスたち: A period drama set at the end of the Edo period, when traditional Chinese medicine doctors and Western-trained Dutch medicine doctors coexisted, starring Kuranosuke Sasaki as the village Dutch medicine doctor Daisuke Okura. In a village on the outskirts of Kyoto at the end of the Edo period, Daisuke Okura is a tolerant, curious Dutch medicine doctor who saves common people regardless of wealth or status. He is constantly engaged in fierce arguments with the Chinese medicine doctor Gensai, his sworn enemy. One day, Okura saves a hot-tempered young man named Shinsa through surgery, an event that drastically changes both their lives. Director Kazuki Omori, known for the ensemble drama 'Hippocrates' about Kyoto medical students, conceived this film based on the 1960 film 'Fundoshi Doctor,' which depicted a warm-hearted doctor and his wife, setting it in Kyoto at the end of the Edo period to portray the dawn of modern Japanese medicine. When Omori passed away in 2022 while preparing for filming, the project nearly became a phantom, but Akira Ogata, director of 'The Independent Teenage Chorus' and a former assistant director to Omori, carried on his will and brought it to completion. Kuranosuke Sasaki plays Okura. Takeshi Naito, who made his film debut in 'Hippocrates,' plays Okura's rival Gensai, and Akira Emoto, who played a resident doctor in 'Hippocrates,' appears as the mysterious samurai Danzo. Additionally, Shizuka Muroi, who made her film debut in Omori's 'Hear the Wind Sing,' provides narration, and Takuya Nishioka, who has known Omori since the 1970s, wrote the screenplay, with many cast and crew members associated with Kazuki Omori participating.
title_norm:幕末太陽傳: Saheiji, left penniless at a Shinagawa pleasure quarter at the end of the Edo period... A masterpiece by Kawashima and Frankie, and a classic in Japanese film history. In this ensemble comedy where late-Edo period patriots and courtesans mingle, Frankie's light and agile movements as he navigates through the chaos are the film's core.
title_norm:幸せの、忘れもの。: A Spanish film that delicately portrays the story of a woman living in a world without sound and her family. Ángela, who is deaf, and her husband Héctor, who gently supports her, communicate through the irreplaceable language of sign language. Ángela works in a pottery workshop, surrounded by the comforting smell of clay and trusted colleagues, living a quiet and peaceful life. However, a certain 'happy event' begins to gradually shatter her daily life. As she wavers in her sense of alienation, Ángela tries to grasp the 'true happiness' that flickers between the silent world and the world outside... Directed by emerging filmmaker Eva Libertad, who also works as a playwright and sociologist, this film is based on her highly acclaimed 2021 short film 'Sorda.' Starring Miriam Garlo, a deaf actress and Libertad's real sister, the film reflects the director and her sister's long-standing personal experiences, capturing the subtle misunderstandings between deaf and hearing people and the different feelings of alienation each holds. It won the Panorama Audience Award and the Art Cinema Award at the 75th Berlin International Film Festival in 2025, as well as the Golden Biznaga (Best Film), Audience Award, Best Actress, and Best Actor at the 28th Málaga Film Festival in Spain.
title_norm:幸福（しあわせ）: One of the representative works of Agnès Varda, a leading female director of the French New Wave, this human drama depicts the ironic fate that befalls an ordinary couple in search of happiness. François lives a peaceful and happy life surrounded by his beautiful wife Thérèse and their adorable children. One day, while visiting a nearby town, François meets Émilie, a woman who works at the post office, and falls in love with her. At the same time, François truly loves his wife Thérèse. One day, while on a picnic with his family, François confesses his infidelity to Thérèse... The film won the Silver Bear at the 1965 Berlin International Film Festival.
title_norm:幻の光: Having witnessed grief work in his TV documentary 'However... In an Age of Welfare Cuts,' Kore-eda tackles this theme head-on in his first theatrical feature, based on the novel of the same name by Teru Miyamoto. Yumiko (Esumi), who carries childhood trauma, loses her husband to suicide in the midst of a happy marriage. Years later, she lives a peaceful life with a new family, but a lingering unease never fully fades. Against the backdrop of Noto's nature captured in long shots, the quiet rebirth of a woman's heart is depicted with a serene gaze.
title_norm:幻を見るひと: A documentary depicting Yoshimasu Gozo, a leading contemporary Japanese poet, as he visits Kyoto, a city rich with groundwater, questions the meaning of life through dialogue with 'water' and the changing seasons, and ultimately creates a poem. Witnessing the tsunami damage from the Great East Japan Earthquake in 2011, Yoshimasu was struck speechless by the impact of water that strips everything away. Seeking a new meaning for water, he visits Kyoto, known for its abundant groundwater. In Kyoto, a basin surrounded by deep mountains, Yoshimasu travels tracing the 'water' of the city, visiting places like Ryukyoin, where Kawabata Yasunari wrote 'The Old Capital,' as well as Daigo-ji, Myoshin-ji, Daitoku-ji, and Kifune Shrine. The film captures Yoshimasu's sensibility, which remains virginal even as he approaches 80, and his precious creative process.
title_norm:幻を見るひと〜京都の吉増剛造〜: The film opens with footage of the tsunami from the Great East Japan Earthquake (courtesy of the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism). The new work by Gozo Yoshimasu, 'A Water Tree Stands on the Planet,' born at the climax of this film, was completed after the poet's long struggle. Yoshimasu had been unable to write poetry since the 2011 Great East Japan Earthquake. 'At the beginning of human life, there is amniotic fluid and bathwater; at the end, there is the water of the dying that moistens the lips,' says Yoshimasu. 'Water,' the source of life for humanity, has been an important theme for poets throughout history. However, the poet who directly witnessed the scars of the great tsunami lost his words to the impact of water that strips everything away. Instead of writing poetry, Yoshimasu began daily copying the poems of the Showa-era philosopher Takaaki Yoshimoto in rice-grain-sized characters, like a sutra transcription. The camera captures this strange and fascinating scene. 'Beside the Poem,' written over four years and which he calls 'Monster-kun,' is a massive work of nearly 700 pages. Within it, the actual voice of the representative Japanese poet Akiko Yosano (1878–1942) resounds, sanukite stones ring, and finally, an eerie scene unfolds as he flings ink onto paper like Jackson Pollock (USA, 1912–1956), the founder of action painting. Deviating from the act of writing, time accumulates on a single sheet of paper, creating an object-like state. This becomes a 'practice writing book' over a long period, leading to the gestation of a new work. One day, learning that Kyoto has as much groundwater as Lake Biwa (Japan's largest lake), the poet seeks a new path for poetic creation in Kyoto's water veins. The poet's tentacles begin to reach the water of Kyoto, which holds a giant cradle of water. Then, before Yoshimasu appears the phantom of Yasunari Kawabata, winner of the Nobel Prize in Literature. Resonating with the talent of seeing phantoms in Kawabata, who stayed in Kyoto and devoted himself to creative work, the poet gropes for the thread of his own poetic creation. What the poet's senses finally touch is the great Eastern spirit, the water god, the dragon. Yoshimasu hears the voice of water's destiny and takes up his brush. The story of Gozo Yoshimasu depicted in this film shows the path of a poet, standing at the abyss of creative despair, 'gaining new life.' The backdrop, like Kawabata's masterpiece 'The Old Capital' which earned him the Nobel Prize, is vividly colored by Kyoto's four seasons, Zen temples, and karesansui (dry landscape gardens).
title_norm:幻魔大戦: The destroyer of the universe, "Genma," was approaching Earth. Luna, a princess of Transylvania and an esper, received a message from the cosmic consciousness "Froi" and began a battle to protect Earth alongside Vega, a cyborg soldier also fighting Genma. Luna decided to gather psychics from around the world to counter Genma. Among them was high school student Azuma Higashi, who was unaware of his own abilities until Vega's provocations awakened his psychic powers. However, emotionally immature, he closed his heart to Luna's pleas to join the fight to save the universe. Even so, the enemy appeared before him without mercy.
title_norm:床一面こんな感じ: A drama about two women who are close friends but growing increasingly dissatisfied with their shared living situation, as they struggle to clean their filthy apartment over the course of one night. Yabuki Kotori is curious and takes long trips to the toilet, while Mimori Suzuka is a fermented food enthusiast who is bad at housework. The best friends share a house, but something feels off. One day, their dream man, Kurita-san, is coming to visit, but their apartment is unbelievably dirty. With a deadline of 10 a.m., Kotori and Suzuka start a big cleanup together, but... Created by the filmmaking unit "Shidoromodori," known for "Sumiko 22" and "I Still Don't Know You," consisting of Hamada Satsuki and Fukuoka Sawako, based on their own shared-house experiences. Hamada directs, and Fukuoka handles the script and editing. Seto Riko (from "Kekkyoku Kohi") stars as Yabuki Kotori, and Sono Rin (from "Otona ni Naritakunaremasu you ni") stars as Mimori Suzuka, with Matsuzaki Shohei, Shinpo Yuki, and Kudo Haruka in a special appearance supporting the cast. The project "chill the gambler" and "kiss the gambler" by singer-songwriter Kana-fan provides the music and theme song.
title_norm:廃用身: Based on the debut novel by physician-author Yo Hisakabe published in 2003, this human suspense film stars Shota Sometani. At the daycare facility 'Ijinzaka Clinic,' an innovative treatment devised by director Kuranosuke Urushibara spreads quietly among the elderly. Aiming for cost-effective care, the treatment involves 'useless limbs' (paralyzed body parts with no hope of recovery), and unexpected 'favorable side effects' have appeared, such as 'feeling lighter in body and mind' and 'a harsh personality softening.' Hearing rumors, editor Yagura senses potential for a revolution in geriatric medicine and proposes publishing a book to Urushibara. However, everything takes a dark turn when an internal whistleblowing about the daycare leaks to a weekly magazine, and a shocking incident occurs at a patient's home. Sometani delivers a haunting performance as Urushibara, a doctor who, in pursuit of his ideals, steps into the gap between rationality and madness. The cast includes Yuki Kitamura as editor Yagura, Naomasa Rokudaira as elderly patient Iwagami who reclaims his life through Urushibara's treatment, and Kumi Takiuchi as Urushibara's wife Kikuko. The film is directed and written by Mitsuki Yoshida, who has gained international attention for works such as 'Family X' and 'Three Lights.'
title_norm:從今以後: A drama depicting a long-term lesbian couple facing various problems after one partner's sudden death. Director Ray Yeung, who previously explored the issues of elderly gay couples in "Suk Suk," turns his gaze to the current state of Hong Kong, where prejudice against homosexuality remains deeply rooted, while also highlighting social issues such as severe housing shortages, employment difficulties, and economic disparity. Pat and Angie, a lesbian couple in their 60s, are enjoying a stable and peaceful life both publicly and privately. However, Pat suddenly dies. Angie was close with Pat's relatives, but they clash over the funeral arrangements. Furthermore, under Hong Kong law, Pat's brother, as her relative, inherits her estate. This is an unacceptable reality for Angie, who considered the apartment, filled with memories of Pat, to be their final home. Meanwhile, Pat's financially struggling brother, his wife, and their children also grapple with their own circumstances. The film won the Teddy Award for outstanding LGBTQ cinema at the 74th Berlin International Film Festival in 2024 and received high praise, including five nominations at the 43rd Hong Kong Film Awards, including Best Film. Patra Au, who won the Hong Kong Film Award for Best Supporting Actress for "Suk Suk," plays Angie, earning a Best Actress nomination for this film. Maggie Li, returning to the screen after about 30 years, plays Pat.
title_norm:復活の日: In 1982, the deadly virus MM-88 is stolen from a research institute in East Germany. However, the plane carrying the spy who stole it crashes in the Alps, and the virus spreads across the Earth, wiping out humanity except for a small group of survivors in Antarctica. One of these survivors, earthquake researcher Yoshizumi, realizes an even greater danger is approaching: a massive earthquake could strike the eastern United States, potentially triggering the launch of nuclear missiles.
title_norm:心と体と シネマカリテと また逢える: A slaughterhouse on the outskirts of Budapest. Mária, who struggles to fit in at work, and Endre, her boss who takes an interest in her. Though the two are socially awkward and out of sync, they are drawn together when a company-wide counseling session reveals they have been sharing the exact same dream—but...
title_norm:心のパズル:
A drama that explores the multifaceted nature of the human psyche through the lens of Dissociative Identity Disorder (multiple personality disorder). Former stage actor Kimihiko Yuasa, unable to control a violent "other self" within him, once struck the director he admired, Kiyoshi Yanagimoto, during a rehearsal. Now, while grappling with his own inner turmoil, Yuasa works as a private investigator. One day, he is approached by Takayama—who, like Yuasa, was a victim of Yanagimoto’s abuse of power—with a request: "He must have multiple personalities; find the evidence." As Yuasa begins his investigation, he encounters a version of Yanagimoto who seems like a completely different person.

The film marks the directorial debut of Shigeharu Kadowaki. Coming from the food and beverage industry, Kadowaki turned to filmmaking
title_norm:心をつないで 思いを紡いで: Screening at EU Film Days 2026 (Tokyo: May 16–29, 2026 at Theater Image Forum, May 19–24 at National Film Archive; Nagoya: June 6–19 at Nagoya Kinema Noi; also to be held in Hiroshima, Kyoto, and Fukuoka).
title_norm:心平、: A brother who cannot fit into society, a father who has given up on the future, and a sister bound to the home. This is a story of the small steps the three of them take forward. One day, the Great East Japan Earthquake suddenly upends their peaceful daily lives. Not only the earthquake and tsunami, but also the nuclear accident forced many people to lose their homes and jobs, leaving Fukushima behind. This is the story of a family living in the aftermath, three years later, in a deeply scarred Fukushima.
title_norm:心耳 耳を澄まさぬ表現者たち: This documentary focuses on "Sign Language Kyogen," a subject that Tetsuko Kuroyanagi has devoted over 40 years to, capturing the efforts of deaf individuals who take on classical performing arts through sign language. The Sign Language Kyogen project was initiated by Tetsuko Kuroyanagi in the 1980s with the "Japan Deaf Theatre Company." Over four decades, their performances have become so popular that tickets are constantly sold out, and they have also performed abroad, spreading Japanese traditional arts worldwide. Through rare footage of the overseas performance of "Uri Nusubito" (The Melon Thief), testimonies from those involved, scenes of rigorous training, and behind-the-scenes moments, the film explores the appeal of Sign Language Kyogen, its differences from traditional Kyogen, and how it is received globally. Interview footage features Tetsuya Izaki, a founding member of the troupe who has supported Sign Language Kyogen alongside Kuroyanagi; Satoshi Ezoe, the troupe's representative; and Chikashige Miyake, a Kyogen performer of the Izumi school who instructs the troupe using sign language. Tetsuko Kuroyanagi serves as executive producer, and director Shugo Fujii, known for "ONPAKU" and "Chō Gitaiteki Ningen," completed this as his first documentary work.
title_norm:心耳～耳を澄まさぬ表現者たち: There are deaf people spreading Japanese traditional performing arts to the world. Driven by this fact, director Hidetake Fujii's impulse that "this must be conveyed to the world" became the catalyst for making this film. Tetsuko Kuroyanagi's passion, having devoted 40 years to sign language and sign language Kyogen. Through meeting her, the significance of sign language as a "language" comes into view. But the story does not end as a mere record of inspiration. What they arrive at is one pressing question. This film is by no means simply a movie to promote the appeal of sign language.
title_norm:急に具合が悪くなる: Director Ryusuke Hamaguchi ("Drive My Car," "Evil Does Not Exist") portrays the spiritual encounter of two women with the same-sounding name in Paris. Based on the exchange of 20 letters between philosopher Makiko Miyano, who survived cancer metastasis, and anthropologist Maho Isono, titled "Suddenly Feeling Ill," the film depicts the connection between two women who meet by chance and their confrontation with the world. Marie-Lou Fontaine, director of the care facility "Garden of Freedom" on the outskirts of Paris, struggles with staff shortages and misunderstanding while striving for humane care. She meets Japanese stage director Mari Morisaki, who is battling cancer, and draws courage from her theater work. Guided by the coincidence of their similar-sounding names, Marie-Lou and Mari begin a friendship. But one day, Mari suddenly falls ill. As her illness progresses, their bond deepens, and their souls connect. Virginie Efira ("Benedetta") plays Marie-Lou, and Tao Okamoto, a global fashion model who has appeared in Hollywood films like "The Wolverine," plays Mari. Kyozo Nagatsuka ("Enemy") plays Goro Seimiya, an actor in Mari's play, and Koyo Kuroki ("The Generation of the Looking-Ahead") plays Tomoki Kubodera, Goro's grandson. Screened in the Competition section of the 79th Cannes Film Festival in 2026, Virginie Efira and Tao Okamoto jointly won the Best Actress award. Okamoto became the first Japanese person to win the Cannes Best Actress award.
title_norm:怪奇タクシー 布告を知らぬ者達に: A live-action film adaptation of Tatsuya Morino's popular manga "Kaiki Taxi," created by the artist who studied under Shigeru Mizuki and specializes in yokai (supernatural creatures) stories. The film consists of three episodes: "Curve's Man-Eating Car," where a TV crew investigating rumors of a mysterious accident involving a couple's car on a hilltop date spot curve is drawn into a terrifying experience, guided by the enigmatic taxi driver Takerō Kiboku; "Illegal Parking Critic," which reveals the truth behind a tragedy where an ambulance couldn't reach the hospital in time due to traffic caused by illegally parked cars, resulting in a death; and "Mystery Tour," depicting various strange occurrences during a bus tour attended by a man with a secret. The cast includes Yumi Okada, Taisei Kido, Koji Matoba, Emiri Nakayama, Taiyo Sugiura, Seiji Chihara, Ryūya Nagayama, and Makoto Ogawa. Hideo Okamoto, who also wrote the screenplay for the film adaptation "Kaiki Taxi: Beware the Windy Night Road" and is known as a designer for various special effects and anime works, directed the film.
title_norm:怪奇タクシー布告を知らぬ者達に: This film is a live-action adaptation of the cult-favorite work 'Kaiki Taxi' by yokai manga artist Tatsuya Morino. Screened at the Hiroshima International Film Festival 2025 and the Kyoto Machinaka Film Festival 2026, it has stirred the occult film scene and finally hits theaters. Three horror tales spanning genres like occult, urban legend, and human terror are woven together: 'Curve's Man-Eating Car,' where a TV crew investigating a curve prone to mysterious accidents encounters terror guided by an unidentified monstrous taxi driver named Takerō Kaiki; 'Illegal Parking Critic,' depicting the tragedy born from illegal parking and a further chilling truth; and 'Mystery Tour,' the nightmare of a man with a secret who joins a certain bus tour. The cast brings together a luxurious and diverse lineup, including Yumi Okada, Taisei Kido, Yu Kamimura, Dai Hirayama ('Curve's Man-Eating Car'), Koji Matoba, Emiri Nakayama, Taiyo Sugiura, Seiji Chihara ('Illegal Parking Critic'), Ryuya Nagayama, Makoto Ogawa, and Mirai Takikita ('Mystery Tour'). The director is Hideo Okamoto, who has long been active in special effects, anime, and design. Expanding the original work's worldview, it has been developed into a more layered, full-fledged horror. Occult? Human terror? Genre-defying, this eerie and exhilarating horror, where fantasy and reality intermingle, races through this summer!
title_norm:怪奇！死肉の男: A full AI-produced film adaptation (with all dialogue in English) of horror manga artist Hino Hideshi's terrifying yet moving story 'Horror! The Man of Dead Flesh.' One day, a 'living corpse' suddenly appears in the city—his body is rotting and squishy, maggots crawl from his eyes, and his heart isn't beating, yet somehow he is alive! After being taken into police custody, the man is sent to a university hospital's isolation ward. Growing sick of the repeated human experiments, he finally attempts to escape... Who is he, and where is he headed? A poignant and sorrowful man of dead flesh. His fate begins with death. What awaits him beyond?
title_norm:怪物: Directed by Hirokazu Kore-eda, winner of the Palme d'Or at the Cannes Film Festival for "Shoplifters," this human drama is based on an original screenplay by Yuji Sakamoto, the popular screenwriter known for films like "We Made a Beautiful Bouquet" and the TV drama "The Days of Natsume." The music was composed by Ryuichi Sakamoto, who became the first Japanese to win an Academy Award for Best Original Score for "The Last Emperor" and passed away in March 2023. In a suburban town by a large lake, a single mother who loves her son, a caring schoolteacher, and innocent children live peaceful daily lives. One day, a fight breaks out at school. It seems like an ordinary scuffle between kids, but the accounts of those involved conflict, gradually escalating into a major incident that draws in society and the media. Then, on a stormy morning, the children suddenly vanish. What is the "monster"? This collaboration among leading Japanese creators—Hirokazu Kore-eda, Yuji Sakamoto, and Ryuichi Sakamoto—depicts the conclusion reached through a search for the "monster" from each character's perspective. Alongside Soya Kurokawa and Hinata Hiiragi, who play the two central boys, the film features a stellar cast including Sakura Ando, Eita Nagayama, Mitsuki Takahata, Akihiro Kakuta, Shido Nakamura, and Yuko Tanaka. It was screened in the Competition section of the 76th Cannes Film Festival in 2023, winning the Best Screenplay Award. It also received the Queer Palm, awarded to films dealing with LGBT and queer themes.
title_norm:怪速急行■■行き: A mystery horror from South Korea that follows the fate of a video creator investigating the truth behind a station rumored to make people disappear. Da-gyeong, a female horror content creator struggling with low view counts, posts a video about the urban legend of 'Gwangnim Station,' a subway station where people have been going missing, in a bid to turn things around. The video goes viral, skyrocketing to the top of the rankings overnight. Consumed by her desire for views, Da-gyeong steps into an inescapable darkness to uncover the truth behind the rumors. Directed by rising South Korean filmmaker Tak Seung, the film depicts how a familiar place like a subway station transforms into something terrifying. Ju Hyeon-yeong (known for dramas like 'A Gentle Woman' and 'Extraordinary Attorney Woo') makes her feature film debut as the protagonist Da-gyeong. Jung Bae-su (from 'Queen of Tears') plays the station master who tells Da-gyeong about the strange rumors, and Choi Bo-min (from 'Spirit Fingers') plays Woo-jin, the producer at the content production company Da-gyeong works for.
title_norm:恋する惑星: A stylish ensemble love story set in Hong Kong that depicts the intersecting romantic entanglements of young people, catapulting director Wong Kar-wai to international fame. Cop 223, heartbroken on April Fool's Day, buys a can of pineapple every day until his birthday a month later. Determined to forget his lover by falling for a woman he meets that night, he encounters a blonde woman in sunglasses at a bar he stumbles into. Meanwhile, fast-food worker Faye is given a letter by her boss for regular customer Cop 633. It's a letter from Cop 633's ex-girlfriend, containing the key to his apartment. Faye, harboring a crush on him, uses the key to sneak into his room... Cop 223 is played by Takeshi Kaneshiro, and Cop 633 by Tony Leung. It won three awards including Best Picture at the 14th Hong Kong Film Awards. First released in Japan in 1995. In 2022, a 4K restored version was screened as part of 'WKW4K' (from August 19, 2022, at Cine Mart Shinjuku, Grand Cinema Sunshine, Cinema City, etc.).
title_norm:恋文: From naval academy to the skies of the South Seas, and now having survived to set foot on his homeland's soil, Reikichi's only thought has been his beloved Michiko. Through rumors, he heard she had lost her husband to death and moved to Tokyo. Reikichi moves to Tokyo and stays in the apartment of his younger brother Yo, a book broker, and while working as a ghostwriter of love letters for mistresses through the help of his war comrade Yamaji, he searches for Michiko's whereabouts. The day that compressed five years into an instant finally arrives. Michiko comes to him to request ghostwriting of a love letter, just like any other 'panpan' girl. Reikichi, who had cherished the image of pure Michiko, lashes out with harsh words at the Michiko before him. From then on, Reikichi spends days of drunken agony torn between love and hatred for Michiko. Yo, who vaguely senses his brother's feelings, consults Yamaji and meets Michiko. After her husband's death in the war, unable to stay in her stepmother's home, she worked with the occupation forces in Yokohama, and out of loneliness began living with a kind foreign officer—but she was not living a dissolute life like so-called 'panpan' girls, and had since parted with that officer. Yo and Yamaji arrange for Michiko and Reikichi to meet, but Reikichi refuses. Knowing Reikichi's heart that will not forgive her, Michiko throws herself into oncoming traffic amid tangled headlights. Told by police of her serious injury, Reikichi realizes that regardless of her past mistakes, she is precious to him. In the car racing to the hospital, Reikichi sobs and prays to God for Michiko's life.
title_norm:恐怖份子: With the release of 'A One and a Two (4K Restored)', the screening of Edward Yang's representative work 'A Brighter Summer Day (Digital Remastered)' has also been confirmed!
title_norm:恐怖分子: With the release of 'A One and a Two (4K Restored)', the screening of Edward Yang's representative work 'A Brighter Summer Day (Digital Remastered)' has also been confirmed!
title_norm:息を殺して: This is the graduation work from Kohei Igarashi's master's program at Tokyo University of the Arts. Igarashi, who studied under Nobuhiro Suwa and Kiyoshi Kurosawa, received high international praise for his first feature film, "The Voice of Wind and Rain," made while he was still a student. It is December 30, 2017, about two years before the Tokyo Olympics, and the constitution has been revised and a National Defense Force established. A stray dog wanders into a garbage processing plant. Tani-chan, who works in the office, searches for the dog but can't find it. Ken, who finished his night shift, plays video games with Go, who is off duty that day. Adachi-san refuses to go home, while Yan-san is busy putting up New Year's decorations. The workers at the plant each grapple with similar problems: pregnancy, infidelity, family, and friends who died in the war. Amidst this, Tani-chan, troubled by her affair with Adachi-san, begins to feel that her late father, the former plant manager, might be present in this place.
title_norm:息子のまなざし: The Dardenne brothers, directors of 'Rosetta' and 'The Promise,' sincerely and ambitiously tackle a profound motif that could be called humanity's eternal challenge in civilized society. They depict the extreme inner turmoil of a protagonist burdened with complex emotions in a stripped-down, understated style. Olivier Gourmet won the Best Actor award at the 2003 Cannes Film Festival. One day, a boy named Francis enters a vocational training center. He wants to join the woodworking class, but the instructor, Olivier, turns him away, saying he's too busy. Yet, Olivier finds himself strangely preoccupied with Francis. Eventually, Olivier accepts Francis into his class...
title_norm:悪は存在しない: In Mizuhiki Town, Nagano Prefecture, blessed with abundant nature. Takumi and his only daughter Hana have lived modestly there for generations, but one day a plan emerges to build a glamping site nearby, and its repercussions gradually reach their lives. A feature film born alongside "GIFT," a silent live concert film by Eiko Ishibashi, who composed the music for "Drive My Car." Winner of the Silver Lion (Grand Jury Prize) at the 80th Venice International Film Festival.
title_norm:悪は存在しない濱⼝⻯介監督特集上映突然、偶然、必然: In Mizuhiki Town, Nagano Prefecture, blessed with abundant nature. Takumi and his only daughter Hana have lived modestly there for generations, but one day a plan emerges to build a glamping site nearby, and its repercussions gradually reach their lives. A feature film born alongside "GIFT," a silent live concert film by Eiko Ishibashi, who composed the music for "Drive My Car." Winner of the Silver Lion (Grand Jury Prize) at the 80th Venice International Film Festival.
title_norm:悲しくて美しい世界 this is sparklehors: This documentary explores the enigmatic life and music of Mark Linkous, the central figure of the American act Sparklehorse, who emerged during the mid-1990s alternative rock boom and earned a devoted following for his singular musicality. Sparklehorse released their debut album, *Vivadixiesubmarinetransmissionplot*, in 1995, garnering critical acclaim across the West for its inventive sound. The band gained further prominence as the opening act for Radiohead and R.E.M., but during a European tour with Radiohead, Linkous suffered a near-fatal alcohol and drug overdose. Though he survived, the lasting effects of the incident cast a long shadow over his life, and in 2010, while working on his sixth album, he took his own life. Through interviews recorded shortly before his death and testimonies from fellow musicians and filmmaker David Lynch, this film unravels the reality of Linkous’s existence and his music.
title_norm:情事: Sandro, his lover Anna, and her friend Claudia go sailing on a yacht. When they land on a certain island, Anna suddenly disappears. Sandro and Claudia search for her, but gradually find themselves drawn to each other, giving in to their desires despite their guilt.
title_norm:惊天大营救: A revenge action film starring Thai action star Tony Jaa, known for 'Ong-Bak' and 'Tom-Yum-Goong'. It depicts a man who lost his family confronting a massive conspiracy, packed with powerful Muay Thai-based hand-to-hand combat and high-speed, hard-hitting action. After his wife and daughter are killed by a mysterious organization, Bai An heads to the Republic of Parivina to uncover the truth and exact revenge. As he investigates on his own, he discovers a giant corporation secretly controlling the drug trade, but behind it swirls a vast conspiracy involving the military and police. The situation becomes intricately tangled with a mad drug lord, corrupt military police, and unexpected trials involving the only daughter of the corporation's owner. Bai An is tossed about but continues to battle the enemies closing in on him. Directed by Cheung Sui-yee. Co-stars include Xing Yu from 'Master Z: Ip Man Legacy', Philip Keung from 'Goldfinger', and Jason Han from 'Overheat: The Final Sanction'.
title_norm:惑星ソラリス: When communication is lost with the space station Prometheus, which is exploring the ocean-and-cloud-covered planet Solaris, psychologist Kris is sent to investigate. Upon arriving at the Prometheus, Kris witnesses the suicide of a friend, traces of people who shouldn't be there, and a series of inexplicable phenomena caused by the sentient organic ocean.
title_norm:愛と殺意: The feature-length debut by Italy's master filmmaker Michelangelo Antonioni, released in 1950. A noir-toned drama of love and hatred woven between a capitalist's wife and her former lover. Milan capitalist Enrico hires a detective to investigate the past conduct of his beautiful wife Paola. Ironically, this investigation leads Paola to reunite with her former lover Guido. Bored with her loveless marriage, she rediscovers passion in her relationship with Guido. As her husband's investigation progresses, the two gradually step into a dangerous affair. Paola is played by Milan-born actress Lucia Bosè, who appeared in "Lumière" and "Last Harem." The role of former lover Guido is played by Massimo Girotti, known for his appearances in Luchino Visconti works such as "The Postman Always Rings Twice" and "Summer Storm." In this work, Antonioni—who continually examined modern loneliness and the futility of love between men and women—already depicts the alienation in human relationships that would carry through his later films. In Japan, it will receive its theatrical premiere in a 4K restored version at the special screening series "Michelangelo Antonioni Retrospective: The Futility of Love, Wandering Souls" in August 2026.
title_norm:愛のコリーダ: In the 11th year of the Showa era (1936). Sadako, a maid at a Japanese inn, becomes infatuated with the inn's master and begins an affair. When the affair is discovered by the man's wife, the two decide to elope. As they indulge in days of pleasure, Sadako becomes unwilling to ever let him go, and eventually strangles him to death to keep him for herself, then cuts off his genitals.
title_norm:愛の世紀: A drama by Jean-Luc Godard, the master who led the French New Wave, centered on the theme of 'love.' Edgar, a young artist in Paris, conceives a new work depicting four moments related to love—'encounter, passion, separation, reconciliation'—using three couples. The heroine Edgar considers ideal for this project is a woman he met two years ago. She is the granddaughter of an elderly couple who were once involved in the Resistance, whom Edgar met while researching the history of the Resistance in Brittany. Searching for her, Edgar revives his memories of Brittany two years ago. The first half depicts present events in richly shaded black-and-white 35mm film, while the second half shows protagonist Edgar's flashbacks in vivid color using digital video. The 4K restored version will be screened in Japan for the first time as part of the special screening series 'Jean-Luc Godard in the 21st Century: Our Films 2001-2010' (starting June 20, 2026, at Theater Image Forum Shibuya and other locations nationwide).
title_norm:愛の新世界: Ray is an actress in a small theater troupe. By day, she devotes herself to rehearsals with her friends, and by night, she works as a dominatrix at an SM club in Shibuya. One evening, Ray becomes friendly with Ayumi, a hotel escort girl she occasionally sees in the elevator of the building where the club is located. Ayumi is a shrewd girl living with Kenji, a ronin studying for medical school entrance exams. The two hit it off and head out into the nightlife. After drinking, dancing, and partying, they part ways, promising to go see the sea at dawn together someday. Finally, the day of Ray's theater troupe's performance arrives. With Ayumi and Ray's client Sawatari watching, Ray's play is a success, met with thunderous applause. Ray is moved by the satisfaction of accomplishing something. Ayumi is also moved seeing Ray like this. The two head out to the coast at dawn in a car driven by a man they picked up.
title_norm:愛の言葉: A love story starring Sungmo and Jihyuk of the popular K-pop group "Supernova," set against the rich natural backdrop of Chuncheon City, also known as a filming location for "Winter Sonata." It depicts a young man who has lost his words meeting a loved one and finding hope to live again. Teo, a piano tuner with a speech disorder caused by aftereffects of brain tumor surgery, meets Inha, a former popular singer who has lost her sight due to retinitis pigmentosa and is recuperating in a small village in Chuncheon. Unable to speak, Teo plays the piano to accompany Inha's singing, which leads Inha to open her heart to him. However, Inha's ex-lover Romy appears to take her back, and Inha ends up returning to Seoul. The director is Han Sang-hee, who directed "First Snow's Love: Virgin Snow" starring Lee Joon-gi and Aoi Miyazaki.
title_norm:愛妻記: A film adaptation of the autobiographical novel by Ozaki, who won the Akutagawa Prize for "Norakuro Megane," with his wife as the model. This endearing film depicts the poor but happy days of a quirky writer husband (Frankie), who calls his wife by the pet name "Yoshihyoe," and his simple, charming wife (Kishi).
title_norm:我々のものではない世界: Screened in the International Competition section of the Yamagata International Documentary Film Festival 2013, where it won the Grand Prize.
title_norm:我ら山人たち: A documentary by the renowned Swiss master Fredi M. Murer, known for 'Höhenfeuer' (Alpine Fire), capturing the mountainous region of his native Canton of Uri. Exploring the lives and spiritual world of mountain people in a changing alpine landscape, the film contains many elements that would later connect to 'Höhenfeuer,' such as folkloric themes and the insularity of communities. It won the International Critics' Prize at the 1974 Locarno International Film Festival. This film, along with 'Höhenfeuer' and 'Green Mountain,' forms the 'Mountain Trilogy.'
title_norm:我在這裡等你: A road movie set in Hong Kong and Taiwan, depicting a midsummer miracle connected by a single letter. Against the beautiful, shimmering landscapes of Taiwan, it portrays a time-spanning bond between a wounded writer and a lonely young man. Tianyu, a popular Hong Kong writer, faces fierce public backlash after accusations of plagiarism. Deeply hurt, he travels alone to Taiwan in search of the 'Whale's Vanished Cove,' a place said to lead to heaven, which a boy he once corresponded with told him about. After being cheated in an unfamiliar country and getting drunk in the bustling streets of Taipei, Tianyu is helped by Ashang, a local thug. When Tianyu reveals the purpose of his journey, Ashang, claiming to know the 'Whale's Vanished Cove,' offers to take him there, and their summer journey begins... Terence Lau, known for 'Twilight Warriors: Final Battle in the Kowloon Walled City,' delicately portrays the gentle and pure writer Tianyu, while Fandy Fan, from 'Destiny Matchup,' co-stars as the thug Ashang.
title_norm:戦いの向こう 侍たちの記録 2026 world base: A documentary providing an intimate behind-the-scenes look at Samurai Japan, the Japanese national baseball team, during the 6th World Baseball Classic (WBC) held in March 2026. Having vowed to "discard admiration and surpass it" to win the world championship in a hard-fought battle at the 2023 WBC, the team entered this tournament under the immense pressure of being the reigning champions, facing the inescapable burden of "having to remain the winning champions." The film explores what the players felt and how they fought during their quest to remain on top, and how they came to terms with the result of losing in the quarterfinals. Through the lens of the only camera granted exclusive access to the team for this tournament, the documentary gets to the heart of the action behind the scenes. The director is Shintaro Miki, who has previously made documentaries closely following Samurai Japan, such as "Unity, Beyond: The Warriors' Anguish and Hope" and "The Samurai Who Surpassed Admiration: Record of Becoming World No. 1." Narration is provided by Kazunari Ninomiya, and the theme song is performed by Koshi Inaba. It began streaming on Netflix on April 20, 2026, and had a limited theatrical release nationwide in Japan starting August 14, 2026, including at Aeon Cinema Itabashi.

title_norm:戦国自衛隊: Led by Lieutenant Yoshiaki Iba, 21 members of the Japan Ground Self-Defense Force, armed with modern weapons, suddenly time-slip along with their supply depot to the Sengoku period while en route to an exercise. As they stand bewildered, Nagao Heizo Kagetora arrives with his retainers to meet them. Upon first seeing Iba, Kagetora takes an instant liking to him, calling him "a kindred spirit," and is drawn to their unfamiliar clothing and weapons, hoping to recruit them. Iba and his soldiers struggle to accept the reality of their time slip. However, after encountering Kagetora and being attacked by guerrilla forces of a rival feudal lord—resulting in a comrade's death—and witnessing Kagetora's battle firsthand, they are forced to come to terms with having arrived in the Sengoku period.
title_norm:打ち上げ花火、下から見るか？横から見るか？: Summer vacation. Norimichi, an elementary school student, is invited by his classmate Nazuna—who is set to transfer schools after the summer due to her parents' divorce—to go to the fireworks festival with her that night. However, Nazuna is planning to run away from home, and Norimichi finds himself being dragged along. Meanwhile, Norimichi's friends, including Junichi, have decided to go to the festival to see for themselves whether fireworks look round or flat when viewed from the side. Nazuna remains determined to carry out her plan to run away.
title_norm:拳銃 兵士の休暇: Vijay, a star of the Indian Tamil-language film industry known for films like "Master" and "Leo: Bloody Sweet," stars in this 2012 crime action film. Jagadish, a Tamilian living in Mumbai who serves as a soldier in Kashmir, encounters a bomb attack targeting a bus while home on leave. Investigating on his own, he uncovers clues to a larger, coordinated terrorist plot and, along with his colleagues, takes action to prevent it. Jagadish soon finds himself in a tense battle of wits against the enemy commander. This is the first collaboration between Vijay and director A.R. Murugadoss, known for "Kaththi" and "Sarkar." Upon its release in India in 2012, it became the highest-grossing Tamil film of that year and won numerous awards.
title_norm:捕风追影: A battle action film starring Jackie Chan, depicting the fight between a police force led by a tracking expert and a cybercrime group led by a former assassin. In Macau, a series of clever heists by an elusive cybercrime group occur. With the surveillance system hijacked and the investigation stalled, the police seek help from Huang Dezhong, a retired tracking expert, as their trump card. Teaming up with young elite police officers, Huang Dezhong uses old-school investigative techniques and the latest technology to pursue the cybercrime group led by a former assassin known as 'Shadow.' Leon Ka-Fai, known for 'The Lover' and 'Cold War,' plays the former assassin leader of the criminal group, reuniting with Jackie Chan for the first time in about 20 years since 'The Myth.' JUN, a member of the popular K-POP group SEVENTEEN who also works as an actor, takes on his first villain role as a member of the criminal group. Zhang Zifeng, from 'Sister Summer's Farewell,' and Zusha, from the TV drama 'Mountain and River Shadows,' also appear. The film is directed and written by Larry Yang, who previously worked with Jackie Chan on 'Ride On.'
title_norm:探偵物語: This was a highly anticipated comeback film for Yakusho, who had taken a break from acting to prepare for university entrance exams after the massive hit of her starring movie "Sailor Suit and Machine Gun" (1981). The story follows a pampered college girl, played by Yakusho, who is bodyguarded by a private detective played by Matsuda. Director Negishi Kichitaro and the staff devised various strategies to help Yakusho grow as an actress, and she rose to the occasion. It was first released as a double feature with "The Girl Who Leapt Through Time" starring Harada Tomoyo. College student Arai Naomi is set to leave for America, where her father awaits, in one week. Invited by her admired senior Nagai, she heads to a hotel, but a man claiming to be her uncle bursts in and drives Nagai away. The man is a private detective named Tsujiyama Shuichi, hired by her father's former secretary to protect her until her departure. One day, Tsujiyama's ex-wife Sachiko shows up at his apartment, saying she is suspected of stabbing Kazuya, the heir to the Okazaki gang, at a hotel. Naomi suggests to Tsujiyama that they search for the real culprit together.
title_norm:撃たれた自由の声を撮れ: A documentary recording the daily struggles of women who continue to seek freedom in Afghanistan under Taliban rule. In August 2021, the Taliban seized control of nearly all of Afghanistan, collapsing the two-decade democratic government. With the Taliban's return to power, women were once again barred from working outside the home, deprived of educational opportunities, and girls were forced into marriages with much older men and confined to their houses. Sisters Rashmin and Nastaran, along with other women, take to the streets to raise their voices against countless inequalities. Undaunted even by armed men, they hide smartphones under their scarves to film and broadcast the current situation in Afghanistan. They continue their resistance while moving from one relative's home to another, but in a patriarchal society, their father despises the women participating in demonstrations, and they are forced to live in fear of neighbors informing on them. Despite such harsh circumstances, Rashmin, driven by the desire not to make the next generation experience the same suffering, rushes out into the streets. The director is Zainab Entezar, an Afghan-born female filmmaker, producer, and writer who, while living in exile, continues to broadcast the voices of the women of her homeland to the world.
title_norm:敗北者たち: The second feature film by Italian master Michelangelo Antonioni, known for "L'Avventura" and "Red Desert," made in 1953. An omnibus ensemble drama depicting young people who commit crimes, set in cities across France, Italy, and England. Paris, Rome, London. In each city, driven by greed for money, vanity, or unfulfilled boredom, young people turn to crimes such as murder and smuggling. Against the backdrop of postwar prosperity regaining its wealth, the spiritual emptiness of a younger generation that has lost its way, and shifting values, quietly come to the surface. Antonioni handled direction, original story, and screenplay, with Suso Cecchi D'Amico, a leading Italian screenwriter known for Visconti works like "White Nights" and "The Leopard," and writer Giorgio Bassani co-writing the script. His gaze, calmly observing the alienation and apathy behind crime, carries forward into his later works. In Japan, it will receive its theatrical premiere in a 2K restored version at the special screening "Michelangelo Antonioni Retrospective: The Futility of Love, Wandering Souls" in August 2026.
title_norm:教授と美女: At the Totten Foundation in New York, eight scholars are putting the finishing touches on an encyclopedia, but when grammar professor Potts overhears a slang term, he realizes their work has been isolated from the real world and ventures into the city to investigate. There, he seeks the help of O'Shea, a nightclub singer... Although the film was a hit in the U.S. upon release, it was never imported due to the times. Billy Wilder contributed to the script on the condition that he be allowed to observe Hawks' direction. He made his directorial debut the following year, having used this as preparation.
title_norm:敵:
Director Daihachi Yoshida (*The Kirishima Thing*, *Kiba: The Fangs of Fiction*) adapts Yasutaka Tsutsui’s novel of the same name into a monochrome cinematic experience. It tells the story of an elderly man living a tranquil, solitary life who is suddenly confronted by an "enemy."

Gisuke Watanabe, 77, is a retired university professor and widower living alone in the traditional Japanese house he inherited from his grandfather. He wakes at the same hour every morning, prepares his own meals, and treats every item he owns—from his clothing to his stationery—with meticulous care. Occasionally, he shares drinks with a few close friends or hosts dinner for a former student. His days pass in peace as he calculates how many more years his savings will sustain this lifestyle. However, into this quiet existence comes a disturbing message, flashing across his computer screen: "The enemy is coming."

Kyozo Nagatsuka takes on his first leading film role in 12 years as Gisuke. He is joined by Kumi Takiuchi as his former student, Asuka Kurosawa as his late wife, and Yuumi Kawai as a university student he meets at a bar, with Satoru Matsuo, Takashi Matsuo, Shinsuke Kato, and Ayumu Nakajima rounding out the supporting cast. The film competed at the 37th Tokyo International Film Festival in 2024, where it achieved a triple crown: the Tokyo Grand Prix / The Governor of Tokyo Award, Best Director (Daihachi Yoshida), and Best Actor (Kyozo Nagatsuka).
title_norm:新・平家物語: A commentary: In the late Heian period, when warriors rose in place of the aristocracy, Taira no Kiyomori faces various hardships... Mizoguchi depicts the "human" Kiyomori, tormented by the secret of his birth, on an overwhelming scale in this historical drama. A young Raizō, early in his debut, plays the youthful Kiyomori with dashing flair, and the unforgettable performance by Kogure as his sensuous mother lingers in the mind.
title_norm:新作歌舞伎 風の谷のナウシカ 前編: The first part of "New Kabuki: Nausicaä of the Valley of the Wind," a kabuki adaptation of all seven volumes of Hayao Miyazaki's manga version of "Nausicaä of the Valley of the Wind." The story is set in a world where industrial civilization was destroyed by a war known as the "Seven Days of Fire," and most of the land is covered by the "Sea of Corruption," a forest that emits giant insects and toxic miasma. Nausicaä, the daughter of the chieftain of the small "Valley of the Wind," where people who control the wind live, is not afraid of the feared Sea of Corruption or its insects and seeks to unravel the mystery of its origin. One day, a stone containing the power to revive the "God Warrior," which burned the world in the Seven Days of Fire, is discovered in the small kingdom of Pejite, and the powerful empire of Tolmekia moves to seize it. This first part includes three of the seven acts: Act I "The One in Blue Garments Stands in a Golden Field," Act II "The Revival of the Devil's Law," and Act III "The White Witch Marches on the Bloody Path." This is a recorded video of the stage performance held at Shinbashi Enbujo Theatre from December 6 to 25, 2019, screened as a delayed viewing in February 2020 at Togeki, Shinjuku Piccadilly, and other venues (Part 1: February 14–20, 2020 / Part 2: February 28–March 5, 2020, each for a limited one-week run).
title_norm:新作歌舞伎 風の谷のナウシカ 後編: The second part of the "New Kabuki: Nausicaä of the Valley of the Wind," a kabuki adaptation of Hayao Miyazaki's manga version of "Nausicaä of the Valley of the Wind." This kabuki adaptation covers the entire epic story of the original seven-volume manga, which was not depicted in the anime film directed by Miyazaki himself. The stage production was performed at the Shinbashi Enbujō Theatre as a daytime (first part) and evening (second part) continuous performance, and this is a filmed recording of that acclaimed stage. Kikunosuke Onoe plays the protagonist Nausicaä, and Shichinosuke Nakamura plays Princess Kushana, Nausicaä's adversary. The script was written by Keiko Niwa, who has worked on many Studio Ghibli films such as "Tales from Earthsea" and "The Secret World of Arrietty." Direction was handled by G2, who also directed "New Kabuki: NARUTO." This second part includes Act 4 "Great Tsunami," Act 5 "Forest of Purification," Act 6 "Awakening of the God Warrior," and the Grand Finale "Secrets of the Shrine of Shuwa" from the total of seven acts. The stage performance at Shinbashi Enbujō from December 6 to 25, 2019, was filmed and screened as a delay viewing at Tōgeki, Shinjuku Piccadilly, and other venues in February 2020 (first part: February 14–20, 2020; second part: February 28–March 5, 2020, each for a limited one-week run).
title_norm:新凱旋門物語: The Grande Arche, a monumental cube-shaped building in the La Défense district west of Paris, stands on the "Paris historical axis" stretching straight from the glass pyramid of the Louvre. Behind its completion lies the unknown story of an anonymous architect whose fate was shaken. Based on historical fact, this human drama immerses viewers in the bizarre life of an architect who challenged a national project while being tossed about by ideals and political maneuvering. An ensemble of talented actors lends the film credibility, earning it a selection in the Un Certain Regard section of the 78th Cannes Film Festival and eight César Award nominations. This architectural drama resonates with debates surrounding Japan's National Stadium and the Osaka Expo. In 1983 Paris, President Mitterrand envisioned a new monument to celebrate the bicentennial of the French Revolution. The international design competition selected the unknown Danish architect Johan Otto von Spreckelsen. His bold plan—a cube-shaped arch of Italian Carrara marble with a cloud-like roof floating at its base—captured the president's heart and made him an overnight sensation. However, budget constraints, political pressure, and the expectations of those around him stood in the way of his pursuit of perfection. Should he stick to his ideals or compromise with reality? Caught in the vortex of a massive project, what "certain decision" will one architect make?
title_norm:新劇場版☆ケロロ軍曹 復活して速攻地球滅亡の危機であります: As part of the 20th-anniversary project for the TV anime "Sergeant Keroro," based on the manga by Mine Yoshizaki serialized in "Monthly Shonen Ace" since 1999, this theatrical anime is the first in 16 years since "Keroro Gunso the Super Movie: Creation! Ultimate Keroro, Wonderous Time-Space Island!!" in 2010. It depicts the Keroro Platoon, who were supposed to invade Earth, fighting to protect the planet from a new invader. Sergeant Keroro and his platoon members, who came to Earth to invade but now spend their days idly at their host family's home, encounter mysterious phenomena occurring across the country. Feeling a sense of crisis, the Keroro Platoon rises to the challenge, putting their pride as invaders on the line, but they encounter mysterious letters wherever they go. The screenplay and general direction are handled by Yuichi Fukuda, known for directing the live-action "Gintama" series. The staff includes key members who have supported the series, with Satoshi Ozaki as director, Satoshi Koike as character designer, and BN Pictures handling animation production. Jesse from SixTONES voices the theatrical original characters, the brothers Aruru and Deruru, playing both roles.
title_norm:新喜劇之王: Mo dreams of becoming a movie actress. But she remains a perpetual extra, and the only roles that come her way are bit parts where her face never even appears, or corpse roles. One day, her minor cosmetic surgery for a role catches the eye of a staff member, and she is selected for the blockbuster "Snow White: Bloody Chinatown," starring former star actor Ma. But Ma is the absolute worst in both acting and personality—a troublemaker clinging to past glory. A washed-up actor Ma, and Mon, fighting to climb out from the bottom. Before long, this encounter will drastically change both of their lives—!!

title_norm:新感染 ファイナル・エクスプレス: A Korean survival panic action film depicting the terror and chaos caused by the sudden outbreak of a mysterious virus spreading aboard a high-speed train connecting Seoul and Busan. Seok-woo, a fund manager working in Seoul, is separated from his wife and lives with his young daughter Su-an. Su-an insists on going alone to meet her mother in Busan for her birthday, and Seok-woo reluctantly agrees to escort her. They board the KTX high-speed train from Seoul to Busan, but just before departure, a suspicious commotion occurs near Seoul Station. A woman infected with the mysterious virus also boards KTX train 101, the same train as the father and daughter. Alongside the protagonist Seok-woo and his daughter, various passengers—a pregnant woman and her husband, high school baseball players, and a selfish middle-aged businessman—face a life-or-death struggle for survival in a state of extremity where being caught by the infected means certain death, and their individual human dramas unfold. This is the first live-action feature film by Yeon Sang-ho, a rising director who has garnered attention in the Korean animation scene, and the story preceding this film is revealed in the animated feature 'Seoul Station'.
title_norm:旅立ちのラストダンス: A human drama reuniting Hong Kong comedy king Michael Hui, popular in Japan for the 'Mr. Boo!' series, and Dayo Wong, a top Hong Kong comedian and actor ('A Witness Out of the Blue'), after 32 years. It became a massive hit, breaking Hong Kong's all-time box office record. Set in Hong Kong's funeral industry, it carefully explores universal themes of family, tradition, and views on life and death. Wedding planner To-sang, burdened with debt from the pandemic, reluctantly switches to the funeral business but faces difficulties as weddings and funerals are vastly different. To-sang, focused on profit, constantly clashes with the strict Taoist priest Master Man, who values tradition. However, as To-sang interacts with Master Man and his daughter Man-yuet, his resentment gradually fades. He begins to understand the true meaning of the traditional Taoist ritual 'Breaking Hell' that Master Man performs at funerals. Dayo Wong plays funeral director To-sang, and Michael Hui plays Taoist Master Man. Director Anselm Chan, a screenwriter making his third feature, helmed the film. It won five awards at the 43rd Hong Kong Film Awards in 2025, including Best Actress (Michelle Wai). At the 37th Tokyo International Film Festival's World Focus section, a 126-minute version was screened under the title 'The Last Dance'. The theatrical release is a 140-minute director's cut.

title_norm:无名: Set in Shanghai during World War II, this spy noir depicts the back-and-forth battle of nameless spies among the Chinese Communist Party, the Kuomintang, and the Japanese military. Starring Hong Kong superstar Tony Leung, who won the Best Actor award at the 53rd Cannes International Film Festival for 'In the Mood for Love' (2000) and has recently gained attention from younger generations for his role in 'Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings' (21). The other lead is Wang Yibo, who debuted as a member of the China-Korean joint unit 'UNIQ' and later broke out as an actor in the TV drama 'The Untamed' (19), now one of the most sought-after young actors in China. This film marks his first leading role in a movie, and he has since starred in multiple films, winning the Best Actor award at the 20th Film Channel Media Awards for his second lead role in 'Born to Fly' (23) alongside this film. The intense, stunt-free action sequences performed by the two leads captivate with overwhelming tension and unparalleled beauty. Directed by Chen Er, who previously helmed 'Once Upon a Time in Shanghai' (16). Chen also wrote and edited this film, and Tony Leung was so impressed by the script—only Chen's fourth feature—that he agreed to star. Nominated for eight awards including Best Picture and Best Actor at the 36th China Film Golden Rooster Awards, the highest honor in Chinese cinema, held in November last year. Wang Yibo, making his film debut, was nominated for Best Supporting Actor. Tony Leung won Best Actor, and director Chen Er won Best Director and Best Editing, achieving a triple crown.
title_norm:日動短篇集: The origins of Toei Animation trace back to Nihon Dōga, founded by pre-war animation artists Masaoka Kenzo and Yamamoto Sanae. After releasing the "Tora-chan" series, which reflected the social conditions immediately following Japan's defeat in the war, the studio was renamed Nichidō Eiga and began producing animations commissioned by the Toei Education Film Division. The first commissioned work was "Ukare Violin," directed by Yabushita Taiji (also known as Yabushita Taiji). The positive reception of this work led Toei to decide on acquiring Nichidō Eiga, which in turn led to the establishment of Toei Dōga. Notably, Yabushita had experience shooting and directing cultural and documentary films as a commissioned staff member of the Ministry of Education's Film Section, and he would go on to play a central role as a director at Toei Dōga.
title_norm:日本のいちばん長い日: The film depicts the 24 hours from noon on August 14, 1945 (Showa 20), when the Showa Emperor and cabinet ministers decided to surrender at an Imperial Conference, to noon on August 15, when the acceptance of the Potsdam Declaration was announced to the public via the radio broadcast of the Emperor's Jewel Voice (Gyokuon-hoso) through NHK.
title_norm:日本鬼子（リーベン・クイズ） 日中15年戦争・元皇軍兵士の: This documentary interviews 14 former Japanese soldiers who carried out acts of aggression against China during the 15-year Sino-Japanese War, which began with the Manchurian Incident in 1931, and records their confessions of the atrocities they committed. The interviewees include military doctors and Unit 731 members who repeatedly performed vivisections and bacterial experiments, military police who conducted torture and mass executions for their own achievements and honor, and soldiers who were drilled into the Japanese military's unique structure through private punishment of lower ranks by superiors, losing their humanity. These witnesses, with diverse upbringings, educations, occupations, and military careers, speak of the horrific facts they themselves carried out, driven by a poignant desire to convey the madness-like acts humans are capable of, their weaknesses, and the true nature of war. Produced and released in 2001. A DCP version was re-screened at Theater Image Forum in Tokyo in August 2019.
title_norm:日泰小食: Set in a small diner on Cheung Chau, an outlying island of Hong Kong, this documentary observes a changing world through the islanders who gather there. Located about 30 minutes southwest of Hong Kong Island by ferry, Cheung Chau is a small island known as a fishing village, where colorful boats bob in the harbor and time flows gently. The 'Yat Tai' diner on the island is always bustling with locals who gather to play cards and mahjong with a beer in hand. However, societal changes and the fervor of citizens reach this island far from Hong Kong, and the diner's regulars cannot remain indifferent. From the owner staring at the TV to young people eagerly seeking information, each person grapples with the tides of the era from their own perspective and distance. Eventually, the pandemic that engulfs the world also has a major impact on this diner. The director is Frankie Shin, for whom this is his first feature-length documentary. Shin, a native of Cheung Chau who was also a regular at the Yat Tai diner, carefully captures how the people he treated like family faced the changing times and continued their daily lives. The film won the Best Documentary Award at the 29th Busan International Film Festival in 2024.
