title_norm:星の時: "I am a typist, a virgin, and I like Coke and hot dogs." Based on the novel by Clarice Lispector, known as 'Brazil's Virginia Woolf,' this film shines with an unforgettable brilliance in the history of Brazilian cinema. After 40 years, it receives its first theatrical release in Japan.
title_norm:星を追う子ども: Makoto Shinkai, the animation artist known for delicate psychological portrayals and meticulous visual beauty in works like 'Voices of a Distant Star' and 'The Place Promised in Our Early Days,' returns with his first original feature in five years since '5 Centimeters per Second.' This juvenile animation follows a girl named Asuna who, triggered by mysterious music heard through a mineral radio left by her father, embarks on a grand adventure. The familiar staff supporting Shinkai's works, including art director Takumi Tanji and composer Tenmon, come together for this film.
title_norm:映画 hugっと！プリキュア♡ふたりはプリキュア オールス: Cure Black, Cure White, and Shiny Luminous defeat a monster rampaging through the city. However, a mysterious monster named Miden appears and transforms Luminous into a child. Miden steals memories from all the previous Pretty Cures and turns them into baby Cures. Miden also appears before Hana and the others, and Hana fights alongside Black and White, who rush to help, but Cure Ange, Cure Etoile, Cure Macherie, Cure Amour, and even White are all reduced to toddlers. Hana, sinking into grief and despair before her young companions who have forgotten everything about themselves, and Nagisa, who cannot transform into a Pretty Cure without Honoka, find themselves in an utterly desperate crisis.
title_norm:映画 えんとつ町のプペル 〜約束の時計台〜: The sequel to the 2020 anime film 'Poupelle of Chimney Town,' based on the picture book of the same name by Akihiro Nishino. Based on the 2019 picture book 'Tick Tock: The Promised Clock Tower,' it is adapted on a much larger scale, depicting the story of the boy Rubitch meeting his dear friend Poupelle, who went far away in the previous film, once again. One year has passed since the miracle night when Chimney Town was enveloped in a starry sky. The boy Rubitch, who lost his dear best friend Poupelle, continued to believe in their reunion but eventually gives up to move forward. One day, Rubitch wanders into a mysterious otherworld that controls time, the 'Millennium Fortress.' In this world, clocks that no longer tell time are disposed of, but there is a mysterious clock tower that, though not broken, has stopped at 11:59. The mission Rubitch is given to return to his original world is to get this stopped clock tower moving again. Rubitch meets a man who has kept a promise and waited for 100 years, and regains the courage to believe. Continuing from the previous film, Akihiro Nishino serves as executive producer, original creator, and screenwriter, Yusuke Hirota directs, and STUDIO4°C handles the animation production. Yuzuna Nagase, a child actor known for the TV drama series 'Asa ga Kita,' voices the protagonist Rubitch, and Masataka Kubota, who voiced Poupelle in the previous film, reprises his role.

title_norm:映画 それいけ！アンパンマン パンタンと約束の星: The key word in the film 'Anpanman: Pantan and the Star of Promise' is 'promise.' The central character in this work is a new character, a red panda traveler named Pantan. Pantan embarks on a grand adventure to find a treasure said to be on the Rainbow Star shining in the night sky, in order to keep a precious promise made long ago with a certain adventurer! Along the way, Pantan meets Anpanman, Cream Panda, and other friends, and together they join forces to face one challenge after another! What kind of adventure awaits Pantan and the others? And will they be able to obtain the treasure...? Enjoy a thrilling, suspenseful, and epic story! Long ago, the red panda Pantan was traveling to keep a precious promise made with a certain adventurer. However, during the journey, he was hit by Baikinman's baby spray and turned into a child! Helped by Anpanman and the others, he tells everyone about the reason for his journey and his regret over breaking that important promise. Jam Uncle encourages him, saying, 'Isn't the important thing the feeling of wanting to keep a promise?' Renewing his resolve to 'keep the promise this time,' Pantan sets off for the Rainbow Star with Cream Panda. Cream Panda promises Pantan, 'I will never give up!' and joins the adventure, but is nearly discouraged by many crises. Meanwhile, Baikinman and his gang, who secretly boarded the plane, also come after the treasure... Pantan and the others keep trying, determined never to give up no matter what! When the Rainbow Star shines again, what they see at the promised place is... Can Pantan keep his promise this time? A story of precious promises and friendship.
title_norm:映画 デジモンアドベンチャー: The first theatrical film in the "Digimon" series. From a midnight computer screen, a strange creature named "Botamon" is born! While Tai is uneasy, his little sister Kari is overjoyed. Botamon evolves into Agumon! Suddenly, the Digital World, home to digital monsters, appears. A bird-like monster charges at Agumon. But then, another change occurs in Agumon's body... Evolution into the giant monster "Greymon" begins! Two colossal monsters clash—what will be the outcome of this fierce battle?
title_norm:映画 プリキュアオールスターズdx3 未来にとどけ！世界を: The 10th theatrical film in the "Precure" series, which has enjoyed immense popularity among girls since its broadcast began in 2004. Hibiki Hōjō and Kanade Minamino visit a huge shopping mall and, while searching for the lost fairy Hamy, crash into Tsubomi's fashion show. Suddenly, fairies descend from the sky, and buildings from the "Toy Country" and giant sweets from the "Dessert Kingdom" appear one after another. Furthermore, the formidable enemies the Precures have fought in the past are resurrected.

Childhood friends Hibiki Hojo and Kanade Minamino, along with the fairy Hummy, visit a massive shopping mall on its opening day, but they lose sight of Hummy along the way. They manage to find her, but end up crashing into a fashion show hosted by Erika Kurumi. Amidst this, buildings and residents from other worlds, such as the Toy Kingdom and the Dessert Kingdom, suddenly appear. Furthermore, powerful enemies who once tormented the Pretty Cures are revived by the dark power of a black hole, plotting to wither the miracle flower connecting worlds, the "Prism Flower," and plunge the world into darkness. The Pretty Cures are sent to different worlds by the enemies' scheme, separated from their usual partners and allies, and each is invited into the worlds created by their formidable foes.

title_norm:映画『それいけ！アンパンマン パンタンと約束の星』: Pantan, a red panda, is traveling to keep a precious promise made with an adventurer. However, during the journey, he gets sprayed with Baikinman's baby spray and turns into a child! Pantan had long regretted breaking a promise in the past, but Uncle Jam encourages him, saying, 'What matters is the will to keep a promise.' Determined to keep the promise this time, he sets off with Cream Panda toward the Rainbow Star. When the Rainbow Star shines once more, what do they see at the promised place?
title_norm:映画『仮面ライダーゼッツ さよならのミッション』 映画『超: "Kamen Rider Zetts" (Sundays 9:00-9:30 AM on TV Asahi) follows the story of Yorozu Baku, a good-natured young man who dreams of becoming an invincible agent, who transforms using the first-ever "chest-mounted transformation belt (Zetts Driver)"! To save humanity from the nightmare monsters known as "Nightmares," he carries out missions. His sister Miro is actually an agent with no blood relation to Baku, and her real father is...?! The movie for Kamen Rider Zetts, which is entering a turbulent second chapter in the TV series, makes its grand debut this summer! Don't miss a world unique to cinema where dreams and reality intertwine!
title_norm:映画ちいかわ 人魚の島のひみつ: Based on the original manga serialized on X (formerly Twitter) since 2020 by illustrator Nagano, the massively popular "Chiikawa" franchise—winner of the Japan Character Grand Prix three times, with its 2022 TV anime's catch-up streams on YouTube surpassing 400 million views—gets an animated film adaptation. Under the complete supervision of creator Nagano, the film adapts the particularly popular long-form "Siren Arc" from the original manga series, depicting a grand adventure of Chiikawa and friends on a mysterious island through epic music and powerful visuals. One day, while Chiikawa and Hachiware are relaxing in the square, a rabbit with a flyer stuck to its face appears. Hachiware reads the flyer, which turns out to be an invitation to a "special island." Tempted by promises of "easy monster subjugation on the island for 100x rewards" and "limited island ramen, limited sweets—sweet and spicy stuff all practically free," Chiikawa and friends decide to join the island camp. Along with a skeptical otter, they board a ship and land on the island, but... CygamesPictures, known for "Umamusume: Pretty Derby - Beginning of a New Era," handles the animation production.
title_norm:映画クレヨンしんちゃん 奇々怪々！オラの妖怪バケ～ション: The 33rd theatrical film in the 'Crayon Shin-chan' TV anime series. It depicts the Nohara family's great adventure after they wander into a land of yokai (supernatural creatures), a strangely nostalgic and bizarre world. One summer day, strange phenomena are reported across Japan, causing a stir. Amid this, the Nohara family plans to visit Hiroshi's parents in Akita Prefecture. While preparing for the trip, a suspicious shadow peeks from behind a garden bush at Shin-chan, who is cheerfully playing a yokai game. Arriving in Akita, the Noharas spend a peaceful time at Grandpa Ginnosuke's house, but the next morning, a strange incident occurs: flyers for 'Obake-shon Village' are scattered in the room where Shin-chan and the others slept. At Shin-chan's request, the family heads to Obake-shon Village, but on the way, they wander into a strange space deep in a remote mountain. It is the entrance to the 'Land of Yokai,' forbidden to humans. Masaki Watanabe, who has directed the TV anime 'Crayon Shin-chan' since 2022, makes his film directorial debut, with screenplay by Yoshiko Nakamura, who has written for the TV series. Actress Sairi Ito voices the nine-tailed fox yokai 'Yako,' who guides Shin-chan and the others in the yokai land, and comedy duo 'Mayurika' members Sakamoto and Nakatani appear as guest voice actors.
title_norm:映画史特別編 選ばれた瞬間: A special edition of the monumental video monument 'Histoire(s) du cinéma' by Jean-Luc Godard, the master of the French New Wave, re-edited by Godard himself. 'Histoire(s) du cinéma' is an epic work completed by Godard over ten years from 1988 to 1998, spanning 8 chapters and totaling 5 hours. This video art, weaving together a rich tapestry of images and sounds while freely quoting films, music, literature, and art from around the world that Godard loved, garnered significant attention, particularly in Europe. This film is a reconstruction of the original digital video version, re-edited by Godard in 2002 with new arguments and his unique perspective, and produced on 35mm film for theatrical release. It was given a special screening at the 58th Cannes Film Festival in 2005. In Japan, it will be screened in theaters for the first time as part of the special screening series 'Jean-Luc Godard in the 21st Century: Our Films 2001-2010' (starting June 20, 2026, at Theater Image Forum Shibuya and other locations nationwide).
title_norm:春光乍洩: A love story directed by Wong Kar-wai of 'Days of Being Wild,' starring Leslie Cheung and Tony Leung as lovers, depicting the poignant romance and human relationships between two men set in Argentina. Ho Po-wing and Lai Yiu-fai, who have loved intensely but repeatedly broken up, head to Iguazu Falls to repair their relationship, but get lost, argue, and part on bad terms. Later, a wounded Ho Po-wing shows up at the apartment of Lai Yiu-fai, who is working as a doorman at a tango bar in Buenos Aires. Lai Yiu-fai reluctantly lets him stay, but after recovering, Ho Po-wing starts going out while Lai Yiu-fai is away. Meanwhile, Lai Yiu-fai changes jobs to work at a Chinese restaurant and becomes close with a young coworker named Chang. It won the Best Director award at the 50th Cannes International Film Festival. Released in theaters in 1997. In February 2018, it had a special screening at Bunkamura Le Cinema to coincide with the release of the digital remaster of Wong Kar-wai's 'Days of Being Wild.' In 2022, a 4K restored version was screened as part of 'WKW4K' (from August 19, 2022, at Cine Mart Shinjuku, Grand Cinema Sunshine, Cinema City, etc.).
title_norm:春树:
Winner of the Best Director Award and Best Actor Award in the Competition Section of the 38th Tokyo International Film Festival.

A woman who has lost her mother tongue returns home. Dreams, love, memories, and the time of cinema gently unravel—

Chunshu, 37, has lost her way as an aspiring actress and is stuck in her love life. Returning to Chengdu, her former hometown she left twenty years ago, she visits her old acting instructor, Zhang Mei. But Zhang Mei has dementia and is gradually losing her speech. Unable to find a place anywhere, Chunshu is quietly accompanied by Dongdong, Zhang Mei's son who has returned from Shanghai to care for his mother. Like the decaying national film studio that remains in ruins, past glories, teachings, and lessons are gradually forgotten in the flow of time, and days pass quietly beside people stuck in stagnation.

Released simultaneously with its sister film "Twilight in Luomu," shot consecutively with the same cast.

title_norm:昭和元禄落語心中 “与太郎放浪篇”ディレクターズカット版: Haruko Kumota’s popular manga series "Showa Genroku Rakugo Shinju," which explores the true nature and deep-seated karma of storytellers set against the backdrop of the Showa-era rakugo world, receives an animated adaptation. This theatrical release compiles the two-part original animation DVD (OAD) "Yotaro Wandering Arc"—previously bundled with the special editions of the manga’s 7th and 8th volumes—into a single feature, screening ahead of the January 2016 television broadcast. For its theatrical run, the film features newly enhanced sound effects, heightening the immersive atmosphere of the rakugo performances delivered by the characters on stage.
title_norm:是枝裕和初期tvドキュメンタリー作品集: A collection of TV documentaries researched and directed by Hirokazu Kore-eda during his time at Television Man Union. This program screens the first two works that Kore-eda himself has said 'directed my path afterward.'
title_norm:時々、私は考える:
Daisy Ridley (the "Star Wars" series) stars in and produces this human drama about an awkward woman who discovers the beauty of life through a new romance and connections with her colleagues.

Set in the quiet port town of Astoria, Oregon—famously known as the setting for "The Goonies"—the story follows Fran, a socially awkward woman who leads a solitary life, simply commuting between her office and her home. With no friends or romantic partners, her sole comfort lies in indulging in surreal daydreams of her own death. Her stagnant routine begins to slowly shift following a series of small interactions with a friendly new coworker named Robert. But even as her dates with Robert progress smoothly, Fran finds herself unable to break free from the emotional barriers holding her back.

Director Rachel Lambert, who was named one of IndieWire’s "28 Rising Female Directors to Watch" in 2023, brings this feature-length adaptation of Stephanie Abel Horowitz’s 2019 short film of the same name to the screen.
title_norm:時をかける少女: The first anime adaptation of Yasutaka Tsutsui's classic novel, previously adapted into TV dramas and films. A youth sci-fi drama depicting high school girl Makoto, who gains the power of "time leap" to travel to the past by chance, and realizes the preciousness of irreplaceable moments in life as she repeatedly redoes the past. Second-year high school student Makoto Konno gains the power to "time leap" back to the past after accidentally cracking a walnut found in the school science lab. Using this power, Makoto fully enjoys her carefree daily life, singing karaoke as much as she wants with her male friends Chiaki Mamiya and Kosuke Tsuda, and making spectacular plays in baseball. No matter what happens, she can go back in time and reset as many times as she wants. But this fun everyday life was supposed to continue... Directed by Mamoru Hosoda, who had worked on theatrical versions of "Digimon Adventure" and "ONE PIECE" and later became a leading Japanese animation director with films like "Summer Wars," "The Boy and the Beast," and "Mirai." Character design by Yoshiyuki Sadamoto ("Neon Genesis Evangelion"), animation production by Madhouse. Riisa Naka voices the protagonist Makoto, and Sachie Hara made her voice acting debut as Makoto's aunt, Kazuko Yoshiyama. Initially released in only 6 theaters in 2006, it gained popularity through word-of-mouth and achieved a long run exceeding 8 months. In 2021, it was re-released with the immersive 4DX system as part of a project commemorating the 10th anniversary of Hosoda's production company, Studio Chizu.

title_norm:曦曦: This documentary, the feature debut of Taiwanese director Wu Fan, captures the bond she forms with the unique Chinese dancer XiXi, whom she met by chance in Berlin, portraying the vibrant lives of two women. While studying in Europe from Taiwan, director Wu Fan meets XiXi, a Chinese contemporary dancer, in Berlin. Deeply drawn to XiXi, who dances like a free bird, Wu Fan begins filming her daily life. XiXi's journey, wandering Europe as a dancer in search of a free soul, appears beautiful to Wu Fan's eyes, like a wild bird unafraid to take flight. At the same time, XiXi lavishes love on her daughter Nina, whom she is allowed to see occasionally while staying in touch with her ex-husband Mederic. Eventually, Wu Fan's camera begins to capture the deep wounds hidden in XiXi's past. This becomes a catalyst for Wu Fan herself to confront her own family trauma. The film won the Emerging International Filmmaker Award at the Hot Docs Canadian International Documentary Festival 2024.
title_norm:書かれた顔: This film approaches Kabuki actor Bandō Tamasaburō and, through the existence of the onnagata (female-role specialist), brings into relief a traditional Japanese feminine ideal as a construct of fiction. An unconventional work that blends fiction and reality and depicts its subject in a fantastical manner.
title_norm:書を捨てよ町へ出よう: A grandmother who is a habitual shoplifter, a father who is a war criminal, and a sister with an obsessive love for rabbits. Raised in a dysfunctional family, "I" am always thinking of running away from home, while "he" is placed in a privileged environment. Burdened by a restless, pent-up passion with nowhere to go, "I" encounters strange people and wanders through a city where fantasy and memory blend together.
title_norm:最初の半歩: In 1984, Hong Kong before the handover to China. In the suburban new town of Sha Tin, the first youth baseball team in Hong Kong, the 'Sha Yan' team, is formed. In Hong Kong, where baseball is not a major sport, a group of underachieving boys with no baseball experience begin practicing with balls made of rolled-up newspapers, but in their first game, they suffer a crushing defeat against a Taiwanese elementary school team. Nevertheless, guided by their strict yet caring principal Law (played by Liu Kai-chi), the team members gradually grow, centered on the childhood friends—the introverted Lung (played by Lam Yiu-sing) and the impulsive but loyal Wai (played by Tony Wu). The final showdown against their arch-rivals, the Japan Buffaloes, becomes a stage for them to re-examine their 'past' and 'future'—a youth drama based on a true story, set in early 1980s Hong Kong, leaving a quiet resonance that is not reduced to the outcome of the sport.
title_norm:最後通告: A 1998 fantasy film by Swiss filmmaker Fredi M. Murer, known for 'Höhenfeuer' and 'We, the Mountain People,' which allegorically depicts the mass disappearance of children. Through the form of fantasy, it portrays social issues still relevant today, such as the runaway collective psychology fueled by uncertain information and miscommunication within families. One morning after a full moon, ten-year-old children vanish across Switzerland: six boys and six girls, evenly selected from the four language regions. With police and media unable to find solid leads, the incident develops into an inexplicable situation. Reflecting the contradictions and anxieties lurking in society, the story moves toward the next full moon. Directed and written by Murer, with cinematography by Pio Corradi ('Höhenfeuer') and music by Mario Beretta. Starring Hanspeter Müller, Lilo Bauer, and Benedikt Freitag. It won the Grand Prix at the 1998 Montreal World Film Festival. Released in Japan in 2000, it will receive a special 35mm film screening in 2026 to coincide with the final Japanese screenings of Murer's documentary trilogy, the 'Mountain Trilogy.'
title_norm:月に囚われた男: Sam takes a job that requires him to stay alone on the moon for three years to mine a necessary energy source for Earth. Direct communication with Earth is not permitted, and his only conversation partner is a single artificial intelligence computer. But one day, with only two weeks left until the end of his mission, Sam encounters a person with the same face as his own.
title_norm:月の犬:
Starring Masato Hagiwara, this noir drama depicts the existential despair of two men who would never have met if not for one woman taking an interest in them. Having failed to notice his long-time wife’s illness and living in regret after her death, Higashijima leaves the yakuza underworld behind. He drifts into an unfamiliar town and meets a woman named Saori at a bar. Intrigued by him, Saori begins to entrust him with work. Meanwhile, Minami, a member of a criminal organization, finds himself unable to endure the monotony of his daily life. Upon learning of Higashijima’s existence through Saori, Minami hopes the man will change the scenery of his world and assigns him to look after a young boy named Shogo. Higashijima carries out his duties in silence, but after discovering Shogo’s secret, he defies his orders and takes the boy outside...

Masato Hagiwara plays Higashijima, Tomoka Kurotani plays Saori, and Motoki Fukami plays Minami, supported by a cast including Soraji Shibuya, Kyosuke Yabe, Eriko Nakamura, Suzuka Ohgo, Hideko Hara, and Susumu Terajima. The film is directed by Kenji Yokoi, who won the
title_norm:月老: From Giddens Ko, director of "Mon Mon Mon Monsters!" and "You Are the Apple of My Eye," comes a pure love fantasy inspired by the Taiwanese folk deity "Yue Lao" (the God of Matchmaking) and the concept of reincarnation. After being struck by lightning and brought to the underworld, Xiao Lun, along with Pinky who also arrives there, returns to the mortal world as the Taiwanese matchmaking god "Yue Lao" to tie the fates of people together. One day, a dog appears before them, triggering Xiao Lun to recover his lost memories of his past life. He remembers a promise he made to his first love, Xiao Mi, which he was unable to fulfill due to his sudden death. Starring popular Taiwanese actors: Ku Chen-dong ("You Are the Apple of My Eye") as Xiao Lun, Vivian Sung ("Our Times") as Xiao Mi, and Wang Jing ("The Soul of the Banquet," "My Ghost Friend") as Pinky.
title_norm:月老〜また会う日まで〜: From Giddens Ko, director of "Mon Mon Mon Monsters!" and "You Are the Apple of My Eye," comes a pure love fantasy inspired by the Taiwanese folk deity "Yue Lao" (the God of Matchmaking) and the concept of reincarnation. title_norm:未来: A mystery drama based on the acclaimed novel by best-selling author Kanae Minato, considered her magnum opus, directed by Takahisa Zeze ('The Last 10 Years', 'Those Who Were Not Protected'). Shinomiya Mayuko fulfills her grandmother's expectations and becomes a teacher despite her complicated family background. One day, her student Saeki Akiko receives a letter from someone claiming to be 'Me, 20 years from now'. Half-doubtful, Akiko writes back, enduring the grief of losing her father and the lonely days with her withdrawn mother. But violence from her mother's boyfriend, bullying, and an unbelievable truth push her to the edge. In deep despair, Akiko and her only friend Arisa hatch a forbidden plan: 'kill the parents'. Mayuko tries to save Akiko, reaching out even as she herself is crushed by society's injustices. Yuna Kuroshima plays Mayuko, the teacher who tries to support children despite her own complicated past. Nanami Yamazaki plays Akiko, the girl struggling to survive harsh reality. Tori Matsuzaka and Kitagawa Keiko play Akiko's parents Ryota and Fumino. Ryuta Bando plays Mayuko's lover Haruki Yuki. Kanata Hosoda and Hana Kondo play Hirota Higuchi and Shinju Morimoto, who deeply influence the lives of Mayuko and Akiko.
title_norm:東京物語: A timeless masterpiece by the master Yasujiro Ozu, this film depicts the changing family relationships in post-war Japan through the story of an elderly couple visiting their children in Tokyo. Using his signature "Ozu style"—characterized by low camera angles and static shots—he meticulously portrays the parent-child dynamic. Shukishi and Tomi, an elderly couple living in Onomichi, travel to Tokyo for the first time in a while to visit their children. However, their eldest son, Koichi, a doctor, and their eldest daughter, Shige, who runs a beauty salon, are both too busy with their own lives to pay much attention to their parents. Only Noriko, the widow of their second son who died in the war, shows them genuine kindness and consideration.
title_norm:東京裁判: A feature-length documentary that records the proceedings of the International Military Tribunal for the Far East, which determined the course of Japan's future after its defeat in the Pacific War. Released 25 years after the trial, it was edited over a five-year period from over 500,000 feet of film footage provided by the U.S. Department of Defense.
title_norm:東映動画短篇集: Toei Dōga's first work was the gem of a short film "Koneko no Rakugaki," brimming with the primal joy of "pictures moving." From its sequel "Koneko no Studio" through "Mogura no Motoro," the animals brought to life by Mori Yasuji's animation possess a special charm, and it is clear that the expression of animal characters, a Toei Dōga specialty, was already refined at this early stage. Until TV animation production began, these shorts served as a valuable platform for young talent, with Shirakawa Daisaku and Ikeda Hiroshi making their directorial debuts.
title_norm:栄光のバックホーム: This film traces the life of former professional baseball player Shintaro Yokota, who was drafted second by the Hanshin Tigers and expected to have a bright future, but was forced to retire at age 21 after being diagnosed with a brain tumor. It stars Taya Matsutani and Kyoka Suzuki. In the 2013 draft, 18-year-old Shintaro Yokota was selected second by the Hanshin Tigers. In the opening game of 2016, he was chosen as a starter for the first team and recorded his first hit, with everyone holding great expectations for his future. However, soon after, Shintaro began experiencing double vision. The doctor's diagnosis was a brain tumor, a harsh reality for a 21-year-old. Nevertheless, supported by his family, mentors, and teammates, Shintaro fought against his illness. At his retirement game in September 2019, he performed a miraculous throw home, moving the stadium to tears. But Shintaro's story didn't end there. Matsutani, a former high school baseball player, plays Yokota, and Suzuki plays his mother, Manami. The director is Jun Akiyama of "20 Years Old Soul."
title_norm:根本敬の映像夜間中学＜同窓会＞: Principal Nemoto continues to be active and well in the fields of manga, art, music, education, and others even after the school's closure. On the day, we plan to gather nostalgic footage along with new works, and spend a pleasant time watching them together with everyone. Of course, there will also be plenty of updates on Principal Nemoto's unusual current situation, as only a special manga artist can provide.
title_norm:桜桃の味: Buddy, a middle-aged man, invites people into his car and makes a strange request: "Tomorrow morning, call out to me lying in a hole. If I answer, help me; if there's no answer, cover me with dirt." Everyone refuses, but the old man he finally picks up begins to tell him about the joy of living...
title_norm:森に聴く: A nature documentary that travels from the foothills of Mount Oakan in Hokkaido to Iriomote Island in Okinawa, visiting various locations with researchers, venturing into ancient forests, and exploring the mysteries of their intelligence.
title_norm:楊貴妃: A commentary: Emperor Xuanzong of Tang, grieving the loss of his beloved consort, sets his sights on a young woman... Mizoguchi's first color film, a co-production with Hong Kong, is a courtly tapestry portraying the love and tragic fate of Yang Guifei, the beauty who toppled an empire. The restrained color palette that highlights the exotic costumes and art direction is striking.
title_norm:機動戦士ガンダム 閃光のハサウェイ キルケーの魔女: The second part of a three-part animated film adaptation of Yoshiyuki Tomino's three-volume novel "Mobile Suit Gundam: Hathaway's Flash," originally published in 1989-90. Set 12 years after "Mobile Suit Gundam: Char's Counterattack," it depicts the struggle of Hathaway Noah, a young man who rebels against the corrupt Earth Federation government. In Universal Century 105 (U.C.0105), 12 years after the Second Neo-Zeon War, also known as "Char's Rebellion," the anti-Earth Federation organization "Mafty" begins its resistance through the assassination of high-ranking government officials. The leader, Mafty Navue Erin, is revealed to be Hathaway Noah, the son of Bright Noah, who fought alongside Amuro Ray in the One Year War. Hathaway, though bewildered by the words of the mysterious girl Gigi Andalusia, continues his path to fulfill his mission as Mafty. Meanwhile, Federation Colonel Kenneth Sleg, who is pursuing Mafty, is offered a secret deal by Handley Yoksan of the criminal police agency. As Hathaway and Kenneth each move for their own purposes, Gigi also departs for Hong Kong to fulfill her role. Main cast members including Kensho Ono (Hathaway), Reina Ueda (Gigi), and Junichi Suwabe (Kenneth) reprise their roles from the first film. Main staff, including director Shukou Murase, screenwriter Yasuyuki Muto, and composer Hiroyuki Sawano, also return.
title_norm:機動警察パトレイバー ezy file 2: During an internal audit at headquarters, Kurumi from the maintenance team notices that one live round for the revolver cannon is missing. She consults Kikkyo, and one by one, the other squad members get drawn into the situation. Unaware of this, Towa and Saki begin to suspect the attitudes of Kikkyo and the others...
title_norm:欲望の翼: Director Wong Kar-wai's second feature film from 1990, this youth ensemble drama depicts the romantic entanglements of young people in 1960s Hong Kong with a sense of rushing visual beauty, catapulting Wong Kar-wai to international fame. Yuddy approaches Su, who works as a vendor at a soccer stadium, and they fall in love. However, Yuddy is troubled by not knowing his biological mother. After breaking up with Su, Yuddy spends a night with Mimi, a dancer at a nightclub. Leaving the room, Mimi encounters Yuddy's best friend Zeb, who falls in love with her at first sight. Tide, a policeman on night patrol, has feelings for Su, but she cannot forget Yuddy. The cast features Hong Kong cinema's biggest stars, including Leslie Cheung, Maggie Cheung, Carina Lau, Tony Leung, Andy Lau, and Jacky Cheung. First released in Japan in 1992. A digital remastered version was released in February 2018 at Bunkamura Le Cinema and other venues. A 4K restored version was released in December 2023 as part of the special screening "Wong Kar-wai: The Beginning."

title_norm:歌舞伎役者 片岡仁左衛門 第1巻「若鮎の巻」:
This is the first volume of an epic six-part documentary, totaling 10 hours and 46 minutes, that chronicles the life of the legendary actor Kataoka Nizaemon XIII from age 84 to 90. Nizaemon was a mainstay of the Kabuki world from the late Showa to early Heisei eras. In 1987, as the "Wakaayu-no-kai"—a study group for young Kamigata Kabuki actors—prepared for its eighth independent performance, the camera follows Nizaemon XIII as he provides supervision and acting instruction. The featured plays are "Ichijo Okura Monogatari" from *Kiichi Hogen Sanryaku no Maki* and "Domomata" from *Keisei Hangonko*, with the film tracking the process from the rehearsal room to the final stage performance. The rehearsal footage captures Nizaemon meticulously instructing on every detail, from pronunciation to physical movement, conveying the raw intensity of the practice space. 

The film is directed by Sumiko Haneda, a documentary filmmaker renowned for works such as *Akiko: Portrait of a Dancer* and *The Ode to Hayachine*. Due to its immense length, theatrical screenings have been rare, and with no home video release or online streaming available, the film has long been difficult to view. title_norm:歌舞伎役者 片岡仁左衛門 第2巻「人と芸の巻 上巻」:
The second volume of a monumental six-part documentary totaling 10 hours and 46 minutes, recording the life of the legendary actor Kataoka Nizaemon XIII—who supported the Kabuki world from the late Showa to early Heisei eras—from the age of 84 to 90. This is the first half of the "The Man and His Art" segment, following Nizaemon over a four-year period from age 84 to 88, capturing his occasional discourses on his craft, his stage performances, and his daily life.

The film includes footage of rehearsals and performances from 1987, featuring "Numazu" from *Iga-goe Dochu Sugoroku* (Nakaza, Osaka), "Daimonjiya" from *Kamiko Jitate Ryomen Kagami* (National Theatre, Tokyo), and *Kotobuki Soga no Taimen* (Minamiza, Kyoto). The latter was a milestone performance marking his 35th consecutive appearance at the Minamiza’s *Kaomise* festival, and the camera captures Nizaemon as he receives commendations and interviews. Furthermore, it depicts his daily routine
title_norm:歌舞伎役者 片岡仁左衛門 第3巻「人と芸の巻 中巻」:
The third volume of a monumental six-part documentary series totaling 10 hours and 46 minutes, capturing the legendary actor Kataoka Nizaemon XIII—who sustained the Kabuki world from the late Showa to early Heisei eras—between the ages of 84 and 90. This is the middle installment of the "Man and Art" section, which turns the camera toward Nizaemon’s artistic discourse, stage performances, and personal life over a four-year period from age 84 to 88.

The film features his 1988 performances at Tokyo’s Kabuki-za, including the "Gakumonjo" and "Domyoji" scenes from *Sugawara Denju Tenarai Kagami* and the "Hanawatashi" scene from *Imoseyama Onna Teikin*. It further captures a "Gathering to Hear Artistic Talks" with his patrons; rehearsal footage for his role as Okina in *Kotobuki Shiki Sanbaso* for the opening of Omiya Sonic City; a gathering of supporters in Matsumoto, Nagano; reflections on a short story he wrote at age 23; his passion for trains; a scene of him plucking a shamisen at a Gion teahouse; and the Kataoka family’s Obon traditions.

The film is directed by Sumiko Haneda, a documentary filmmaker renowned for works such as *Akiko: Portrait of a Dancer*. Due to its immense length, theatrical screenings have been rare, and because it has never been released on home video or streaming platforms, the film has long been difficult to view. However, in 2026, to commemorate the 33rd anniversary of Kataoka Nizaemon XIII’s passing and the centenary of director Sumiko Haneda’s birth, all six volumes will receive their first Japanese theatrical screening in 17 years.
title_norm:歌舞伎役者 片岡仁左衛門 第4巻「人と芸の巻 下巻」: The fourth volume of a monumental six-part documentary totaling 10 hours and 46 minutes, this film chronicles the life of the legendary actor Nizaemon Kataoka XIII—a pillar of the Kabuki world from the late Showa to early Heisei eras—from the age of 84 to 90. This installment serves as the second half of the "Man and His Art
title_norm:歌舞伎役者 片岡仁左衛門 第5巻「孫右衛門の巻」: The fifth volume of a monumental six-part documentary, totaling 10 hours and 46 minutes, which captures the life of Kataoka Nizaemon XIII—the legendary actor who sustained the Kabuki world from the late Showa to early Heisei eras—from the age of 84 to 90. The camera focuses on the rehearsals and stage performances of the "Fuin-giri" and "Ninokuchi-mura" scenes from *Koi Bikyaku Yamato Orai* (The Love Messenger on the Yamato Highway) held at the Kabukiza Theatre in Tokyo in 1989. During dress rehearsals, a red lamp was placed at the edge of the *hanamichi* runway to serve as a marker for Nizaemon, whose eyesight had weakened, yet he could no longer see even that guide. On stage, Nizaemon performed the role of Magoemon, with Kataoka Takao as Chubei and Nakamura Jakuemon as Umekawa. The beginning of this volume also includes interview footage from the 1988 publication of Nizaemon’s photo book *Fushi*, featuring the master himself alongside his sons Gato, Hidetaro, and Takao. The film is directed by Sumiko Haneda, a documentary filmmaker renowned for works such as *Akiko: Portrait of a Dancer* and *The
title_norm:歌舞伎役者 片岡仁左衛門 第6巻「登仙の巻」:
The sixth volume of a comprehensive six-part, 10-hour and 46-minute documentary following the life of Kataoka Nizaemon XIII—a master actor who sustained the Kabuki world from the late Showa to early Heisei eras—from the age of 84 to 90. Capturing Nizaemon’s final years from age 88 to 90, the film records performances including "Sanmon" from *The Golden Gate and the Paulownia Crest* (1991, Minamiza, Kyoto), "Arakawa no Sakichi" from *Eight Views of Ryogoku* (1992, Minamiza), "Lord Tsunatoyo at the Mihama Pavilion" from *The Treasury of Loyal Retainers of the Genroku Era* (1992, Misonoza, Nagoya), "The Carriage Pull" from *Sugawara and the Secrets of Calligraphy* (1992, Minamiza), *The Auspicious Sanbaso* (1993, Meijiza reopening, Tokyo), *The Felicitous Soga Confrontation* (1993, Meijiza), "The Inner Garden" from *Kiichi Hogen’s Book of Strategy* (1993, Minamiza), and his final stage appearance in "The State Barge on the Lake" from *The Eight-Array Guardian Castle* (1993, Minamiza), portraying a man dedicated to his craft until the very end. 

In the "Artistic Discussion" segment, he reflects on "Lord Tsunatoyo at the Mihama Pavilion" and recalls seeing Matsumoto Koshiro in "The Inner Garden" at the Imperial Theatre 70 years earlier. The film also features their 62nd wedding anniversary celebration and interviews with his wife, Kiyoko, his second daughter, Yuko, and his fifth daughter, Shizuka. Directed by Sumiko Haneda, known for works such as *Akiko: Portrait of a Dancer*. Due to its immense length, opportunities for theatrical screenings have been limited, and with no home video release or online streaming available, the film has long been difficult to view. However, in 2026, to commemorate the 33rd anniversary of Kataoka Nizaemon XIII’s passing and the centenary of director Sumiko Haneda’s birth, all six volumes will be screened in Japanese theaters for the first time in 17 years.
title_norm:正義廻廊: A courtroom dark thriller based on the real 'Parents Murder and Dismemberment Case' that occurred in Tai Kok Tsui, Hong Kong in March 2013, and the subsequent trial. Henry Chong, a young man with deep resentment towards his parents, conspires with his friend Angus Tong to murder them, dismembering and disposing of their bodies. The two are soon arrested, and the crime seems certain, but when the trial begins, Angus denies the murder, testifying that Henry killed his parents and that he was threatened into dismembering the bodies. Henry, on the other hand, insists they killed them together, directly contradicting Angus's testimony. As everything begins to unravel, the trial descends into a labyrinth, with intense battles between defense and prosecution, and the jurors' ethics and emotions sway, until the time for the verdict arrives. The actual trial concluded in 2015, and the perpetrator is serving time. The film depicts this case, which is said to still hold lingering mysteries about whether the verdict was correct. Due to some graphic depictions, it received an R18 rating in Hong Kong (R15+ in Japan) but was a huge hit. It garnered attention, winning Best Actor at the Hong Kong International Film Festival and Best New Director and Best Editing at the Hong Kong Film Awards.
title_norm:正義迴廊: A courtroom dark thriller based on the real 'Parents Murder and Dismemberment Case' that occurred in Tai Kok Tsui, Hong Kong in March 2013, and the subsequent trial. Henry Chong, a young man with deep resentment towards his parents, conspires with his friend Angus Tong to murder them, dismembering and disposing of their bodies. The two are soon arrested, and the crime seems certain, but when the trial begins, Angus denies the murder, testifying that Henry killed his parents and that he was threatened into dismembering the bodies. Henry, on the other hand, insists they killed them together, directly contradicting Angus's testimony. As everything begins to unravel, the trial descends into a labyrinth, with intense battles between defense and prosecution, and the jurors' ethics and emotions sway, until the time for the verdict arrives. The actual trial concluded in 2015, and the perpetrator is serving time. The film depicts this case, which is said to still hold lingering mysteries about whether the verdict was correct. Due to some graphic depictions, it received an R18 rating in Hong Kong (R15+ in Japan) but was a huge hit. It garnered attention, winning Best Actor at the Hong Kong International Film Festival and Best New Director and Best Editing at the Hong Kong Film Awards.
title_norm:歩いても 歩いても: Director Hirokazu Kore-eda of "Nobody Knows" and "Maborosi" quietly captures the scene of a family gathering at their elderly parents' home for the first time in a while, bringing out the joys and sorrows of life in this home drama. One summer day, the second son, Ryota, and the eldest daughter, Chinami, bring their respective families to the home where former doctor Kyohei Yokoyama and his wife Toshiko live alone. The Yokoyama family spends a casual time together, but this day happens to be the anniversary of the death of their eldest son, Junpei, who passed away 15 years ago.
title_norm:死ねばいいのに: A live-action film adaptation of novelist Kyogoku Natsuhiko's unique mystery novel of the same name set in modern times, starring Nao. A woman named Asami Kashima is murdered. With no clue as to the culprit's identity or motive, a mysterious woman named Eiko Watarai visits those who knew Asami in life, claiming she wants to ask about her. As she follows various testimonies, the outline of Asami's character and her relationship with Eiko gradually emerge. Nao plays Eiko, who goes around asking about Asami. Aoi Ito plays Asami, whose impression changes depending on who is asked; Ko Maehara plays Asami's boss and lover, Hiroyuki Yamazaki; Hikaru Takahashi plays Asami's senior, Kaori Shinomiya; Takuya Kusakawa (from the group Shinkansen) plays Asami's boyfriend, Yuya Sakuma; Tomoko Tabata plays Asami's mother, Naoko Kashima; and Tetsu Hirahara plays the lawyer involved in Asami's case, Riku Gojo. Directed by Junichi Kanai, who previously worked with Nao on "My Daddy," with a screenplay by Kohei Kiyasu (known for "The Kirishima Thing"). The rock band "This is LAST" performs the theme song.
title_norm:死亡遊戯で飯を食う。 44 cloudy beach: A sequel to the 2026 TV anime 'Death Game de Meshi o Kū,' based on the popular light novel by Yūshi Ukai, this theatrical anime adapts the original 'Cloudy Beach' arc. A deadly murder game where survival earns you prize money. Allies you encouraged yesterday can become enemies today, and even with full preparation, you can lose your life. The girl Yūki aims to clear this life-or-death game 99 times, making a living from the prize money she wins. Overcoming the 'Wall of Thirty'—a jinx where player survival rates drop drastically—she continues forward and takes on her 44th game, 'Cloudy Beach.' Among the eight players gathered on a remote island, Yūki spots a familiar veteran. Continuing from the TV anime, Sōda Ueno of 'Stepsister Life' directs, with animation production by Studio Deen.
title_norm:死神バーバー: A human fantasy set in a mysterious beauty salon run by Death, where a woman who must spend her final days there reexamines her life through various encounters and farewells. Based on a proposal by Yoichi Umeki submitted for a Nihon University College of Art class assignment, with a screenplay by Kohei Taniguchi ('This Video Cannot Be Played THE MOVIE') and directed by Shinji Imaoka ('Reiko Iruka'). Hairdresser Miho Saeki, frustrated by troubles at work and in her private life, slips on stairs. Waking up, she is led by rookie Death Sakuma to a suspicious salon 'Meikup' (Makeup), where Death hairdressers touch up the deceased to connect them with loved ones for one last day. However, Miho's actual death is days away, and Sakuma jumped the gun. She stays at the salon until her death. Hinako Sakurai plays Miho, KANON from dance & vocal group STARGLOW plays Sakuma. Okabe Dai (comedy trio Hanako) plays the salon owner, Hirai Amon plays Miho's boyfriend, Inuzuka Kenta plays her salon manager, and Miho Jun plays her mother.
title_norm:残されたヘッドライン:
A documentary film compiling Japanese newsreel footage that has been lost to history. Behind the evolution of news from newspapers and radio into visual media were the "newsreels" once screened in cinemas. This work features a careful selection of footage across various fields filmed from the Meiji era to the early 1950s, with a primary focus on the early Showa period. Produced with the cooperation of Chunichi Eigasha—a company that created theatrical newsreels during the Showa era—the film weaves together culture, politics, entertainment, social customs, and incidents that have faded with time. 

Categorized into "War," "Disasters and Accidents," "Infrastructure," and "Culture and Customs," the film presents rare footage, including some being shown for the first time in Japan. Highlights include the threat of the dictator Hitler, a legendary snake-handling nude dancer, the enforcement of the Prostitution Prevention Act, and the personal effects, final letters, and hidden stories of the Kamikaze Special Attack Units. The narration is provided by Yuichi Mayama, the Nippon TV news anchor who brought the news into living rooms across the nation throughout the Showa and Heisei eras.
title_norm:残響のメロディ 魂の放浪者ニコ、最後の旅路: A musical biopic depicting the later years of Nico, the German-born chanteuse of the American rock band The Velvet Underground and muse of pop art pioneer Andy Warhol, who dominated the 1960s scene. Focusing on the two years before her death in 1988 at age 49, it interweaves her stage presence with personal struggles, realistically portraying the loneliness and rebirth behind the glamorous legend. In 1986, Nico, in her late 40s and living alone in England, distances herself from past fame and embarks on a European tour with her new manager Richard and her band. But the journey is harsh, forcing her to confront her unstable psyche, drug addiction, and conflicts with those around her. Burdened by regret and conflict as a mother, she retrieves her son Ari, who is in a French rehabilitation facility for drug addiction and a suicide attempt, and brings him along on tour... Trine Dyrholm (from "Into Eternity") stars as Nico and performs the songs herself. John Gordon Sinclair ("Gregory's Girl") plays manager Richard, and Anamaria Marinca ("4 Months, 3 Weeks and 2 Days") plays violinist Sylvia. Directed by Italian filmmaker Susanna Nicchiarelli, known for "Miss Marx." It won the Best Film award in the Orizzonti section at the 74th Venice International Film Festival in 2017.
title_norm:殺しの分け前 ポイント・ブランク: A hard-boiled action film directed by British master John Boorman in 1967, early in his career, starring Hollywood legend Lee Marvin ('The Dirty Dozen,' 'The Professionals'). Based on Richard Stark's crime novel 'The Hunter' (featuring the character Parker), it depicts a man's revenge against his betrayers, blending avant-garde New Wave techniques with the psychedelic culture of the American West Coast. Walker, at the request of his friend Reese, robs a criminal organization's deal at the abandoned Alcatraz prison and steals a large sum of money. However, Reese betrays Walker, shooting him and fleeing with his $93,000 share and Walker's wife, Lyn. As his consciousness fades, memories and fantasies swirl through Walker's mind. Surviving, Walker sets out to recover his share and exact revenge, tracking Reese down. Marvin delivers a powerful performance as the ruthless avenger Walker, with Angie Dickinson ('Rio Bravo') and John Vernon ('Dirty Harry') co-starring.
title_norm:殺し屋1: A violent action film based on the popular manga of the same name by Hideo Yamamoto, directed by Takashi Miike. Set in a yakuza apartment building in Shinjuku's Kabukicho district, it depicts a surreal battle between insane men with thorough violence. The boss of the Anjo-gumi yakuza group, based in Kabukicho, suddenly disappears. Kakihara, a masochist who loved the violence given by the boss, persistently searches the city. Eventually, he learns of a hitman named Ichi, and upon witnessing his deranged killing style, feels an excitement akin to love. Tadanobu Asano plays Kakihara, with bleached hair and a face full of scars, and Nao Omori plays Ichi, a weak-willed man who turns into a crying killing machine. The cast includes Shinya Tsukamoto, Suzuki Matsuo, SABU, and Jun Kunimura. The screenplay is by Sakichi Sato, known for 'The Golden Grasslands.' A 4K remastered version will be re-released in May 2026.
title_norm:殺し屋のプロット: Directed by, starring, and produced by Michael Keaton, this crime noir follows an aging hitman losing his memory as he attempts one final perfect crime. John Knox is a contract killer with an unconventional past, holding two PhDs and having served as a former Army reconnaissance officer. Upon being diagnosed with a rapidly progressing form of dementia that will erase his memory within weeks, he resolves to retire from the trade. But just as he prepares to walk away, his estranged son, Miles, appears on his doorstep. Miles tearfully confesses to murdering the man who raped his daughter and begs his father to help cover up the crime. Racing against his own fading mind, Knox sets out to pull off one last perfect crime for the sake of his son. Alongside Keaton as Knox, the film stars Al Pacino as his confidant Xavier, Academy Award winner Marcia Gay Harden (Pollock) as his ex-wife Ruby, and James Marsden (X-Men series) as Miles.
title_norm:殺し屋１ ４k:
The boss of the Anjo-gumi has suddenly vanished, along with 300 million yen of the gang's funds. Kakihara (Tadanobu Asano), an ultimate masochist who lived for the violence inflicted upon him by his boss, believes the man has been abducted but is still alive, and begins a relentless search through Kabukicho. Eventually, he learns of the existence of a killer named Ichi (Nao Omori) and feels a thrill akin to love at the sight of his brutal handiwork. "I want to meet Ichi soon." "I want to taste the despair before I'm killed." Despite their paths crossing without meeting time and again, Kakihara’s heart races at the prospect of their encounter. Now, the moment of their meeting draws closer with every passing second...

*Screening in 2K at this theater.
title_norm:母と暮せば: On August 9, 1948, at a midwife's home in Nagasaki, Nobuko is visited by her son Koji, who she had lost three years earlier in the atomic bombing. Stunned by the impossibility, she watches as her already-dead son begins to appear frequently. Koji, who had been aiming to become a doctor, had a fiancée named Machiko with whom he had promised a future.
title_norm:母べえ: In the 15th year of the Showa era, as global tensions rise, German literature scholar Shigeru (Mitsugoro Bando) is arrested for advocating against the war. His grieving mother Kayo (Sayuri Yoshinaga) and two daughters (Mirai Shida, Mirai Sato) are supported by his former students, relatives, and neighbors, and strive to live brightly and strongly.
title_norm:気狂いピエロ: A masterpiece by Jean-Luc Godard, released in 1965 and revered as a cornerstone of the French New Wave. Ferdinand, called 'Pierrot,' is driven by an urge to escape his boring married life and spends a night with his former lover Marianne, whom he meets by chance. The next morning, finding a dead stranger, the two go on the run, but Marianne eventually tires of Ferdinand and betrays him by colluding with gangsters. A digitally remastered version with a new translation by Jiro Terao was released in 2016. A 2K restored version was released in 2022 and 2026.
title_norm:気狂いピエロ pierrot le fou: Freedom! Provocation! Headlong rush! A dizzying flood of quotations and colors. Loquacious poetry and suffocating romanticism. Karina, Godard's muse but recently divorced from him, and Belmondo, who became a huge star in 'Breathless' and would part ways with Godard through this film. A miraculous masterpiece where each burned out at the critical point of their careers! [STORY] Ferdinand is bored with his life with his wealthy wife and driven by an urge to escape. One night, a babysitter arrives for their young daughter as the couple heads to a party. She turns out to be his former lover, Marianne. Ferdinand slips out of the party, returns home alone, drives her home, and spends the night with her. Waking up the next morning, he finds a dead man with scissors stuck in his neck in her apartment. In contrast to his shock, Marianne calmly makes breakfast and sings. Ferdinand, leaving Paris with only the clothes on his back, follows her as she promises to explain later, heading to the south of France where her brother lives...
title_norm:水の中で深呼吸: Directed by Shoji Yasui, who won the International Jury Special Award at the 30th Kineko International Film Festival for 'Sweet', this coming-of-age drama follows a high school student grappling with unspoken feelings, captured through fresh, vivid imagery. Aoi, a first-year high school student on the swimming team, endures unreasonable harassment from upperclassmen while silently dedicating herself to practice. She harbors a secret she cannot share with anyone: her growing attraction to her classmate and fellow swimmer, Hina. One day, unable to bear the harassment directed at Hina, Aoi finally stands up to the upperclassmen, triggering a relay race between the first-years and the seniors. Overwhelmingly outmatched, the first-years face criticism, and Aoi ends up embarrassing Hina. Encouraged by her childhood friend and fellow swimmer Masaki, Aoi finds solace in his presence, yet also realizes she is developing feelings for him that go beyond friendship. Torn between love, friendship, and her own identity, Aoi struggles to understand herself. Runa Ishikawa, known for 'Let's Meet in Sarugakucho' and 'Umibe no Onnanoko', stars as Aoi. Runa Nakajima from 'Ninety Years Old. What a Joy.' plays Hina, with supporting performances from Moe Kurata, Yuka Sasaki, Rin Matsumiya, and Zohjin Hachijoin.
title_norm:水俣一揆 一生を問う人々: Director Noriaki Tsuchimoto, who brought global attention to Minamata disease with *Minamata: The Victims and Their World*, returns to the subject in this feature-length documentary. On March 20, 1973, the Kumamoto District Court ruled in favor of the patients, ordering Chisso Corporation to pay damages and establishing its legal liability for the disaster. Following the verdict, direct negotiations unfolded at Chisso’s headquarters as patients sought compensation for lifelong medical care and living expenses. This film closely follows the actions of the patients involved in these talks. Utilizing synchronized sound recording, the film captures the raw intensity of the negotiations, providing a meticulous record of the patients' struggle.
title_norm:氷血: Minoru (Hiromitsu Kitayama) and Yuki (Chihiro Kato) move with their young son Akira to Minoru's family home in a heavy snowfall area. The couple wishes for a peaceful life, but Minoru's father Shigeru, who has dementia, is inexplicably terrified of Yuki and calls out his deceased wife's name. One morning, Shigeru dies grotesquely in an abnormal state. From that moment on, the family is plagued by suspicion and fear. Soon, eerie 'white women' begin appearing in the house one after another, encroaching on their daily lives. Minoru, as if losing his mind, keeps drawing pictures of the 'white woman,' while young Akira's view of his mother gradually begins to reflect 'something else.' One by one, the family members break down. Minoru, captivated by snowflakes and losing his reason; Yuki, being eroded; and Akira, placed in danger. Is this a curse, an illusion, or reality? When the snowy plains are stained with fresh blood, an unknown 'white terror' appears and runs amok with brutality.
title_norm:汚れた英雄: The International A-Class 500cc final (All-Japan Road Race Championship, Round 8) is held at the UGO Circuit. The fateful showdown between bike racers Akio Kitano and Keishi Oki ends just before the finish line when Oki overtakes Kitano, pushing the decisive battle to the final round. Kitano uses his handsome looks and sexual prowess to secure funding from multiple patrons to maintain his team. When Christine Adams, heir to a billion-dollar fortune and owner of an international conglomerate, arrives in Japan, Kitano quickly approaches her and successfully secures funding. Finally, Kitano faces the final race, but...
title_norm:決断するとき: Starring Cillian Murphy of "Oppenheimer," this film adapts the bestselling novel "Small Things Like These" by Irish author Claire Keegan. Set against the backdrop of the real-life human rights abuses at Ireland's Magdalene laundries, it depicts the inner conflict and decision of a man who discovers a truth society has long ignored. In 1985, in a small Irish town, coal merchant Bill Furlong lives modestly with his family. One day before Christmas, while delivering coal to a local convent, a girl confined there begs him, "Please get me out of here." Confronted with the reality of young women suffering with no way out, Bill understands it would be wise to look the other way, but his conscience torments him, leading him to make a fateful decision. Emily Watson of "Breaking the Waves" plays the convent's Mother Superior, Sister Mary, winning the Silver Bear for Best Supporting Performance at the 74th Berlin International Film Festival in 2024. Eileen Walsh of "The Magdalene Sisters" plays Bill's wife, Eileen. Murphy, who fell in love with the original novel, personally pushed for the film adaptation and served as a producer for the first time. Directed by Tim Mielants of "Peaky Blinders," the film also features Matt Damon as a producer and Ben Affleck as an executive producer.
title_norm:沓掛時次郎 遊侠一匹: Tokijiro sets out on a journey with the wife and child of a man he killed out of obligation to the underworld. This eighth film adaptation of a classic play, directed by Tai Kato, crystallizes supreme lyricism into a poignant love story, resulting in a masterpiece.
title_norm:沖縄狂想曲: A documentary that spotlights various issues occurring in Okinawa, delving into the reality of Okinawa and Japan. Directed by Takafumi Ota, known for social issue works such as "The House of the Rising Sun" and "Documentary: The Battle of Okinawa - Unknown Memories of Sorrow," the film investigates numerous problems facing Okinawa, including the Henoko base issue, the International University helicopter crash, Osprey noise and crash incidents, as well as historical events like the Koza riot and the Yumiko-chan incident. Experts including former major newspaper editorial board members, prominent university professors, a former mayor, and former prefectural government executives thoroughly explain realities that major media cannot report. Furthermore, the film introduces the challenges of former Okinawa Governor Masahide Ota, the true intent behind former Prime Minister Yukio Hatoyama's statement "at least outside the prefecture," and a parliamentary question by Taro Yamamoto of Reiwa Shinsengumi.
title_norm:沢田美由紀のガマランドにお邪魔します:
Set in the mysterious amusement park "Gamaland," this medium-length horror film employs a found-footage format to depict an inexplicable story surrounding Miyuki Sawada. Gamaland was a real-life location once symbolized by its iconic, giant toad statue. A VHS tape recorded there, steeped in the atmosphere of the early Heisei era, captures a date between a couple, Kohei Shimizu and Miyuki Sawada—but the footage gradually transforms into something deeply unsettling.

The film is directed by Koki Nishii, the filmmaker behind the YouTube channel "Filmest TV," which specializes in recreating modern subjects with a 1980s and 90s aesthetic. Nishii, who also made waves with the September 2024 YouTube drama *Tomochika Suspense Theater: Sotoyu Meguri Mystery - Dogo Striptease Girl Serial Murders*, served as screenwriter and editor, and appears in the film under the name "Nishii." The cast features Tsubasa Nakahara (Masashi Yamamoto’s *DUDE*) as Miyuki Sawada and Takeo Gozu (Netflix’s *Tokyo Swindlers*). The film is produced by NOTHING NEW, a label garnering attention for horror works such as *Chilled* (winner of the FIPRESCI Prize at the Berlin International Film Festival), the short film anthology *NN4444*, and the medium-length horror *Shiki*.
title_norm:河内山宗俊: To save the daughter of an amazake shop owner from a dire situation, two rogues throw themselves into the fray. A masterpiece showcasing perfect chemistry between the renowned actors of Zenshinza and director Yamanaka. The beauty of a 15-year-old Setsuko Hara is captivating.
title_norm:河童のクゥと夏休み: Elementary school student Kōichi Uehara finds a large stone buried on a riverbank on his way home. Driven by curiosity, he cracks it open and discovers a dried-up, fossil-like creature inside. It is a baby kappa that has been in a state of suspended animation underground for a long time. Kōichi names it 'Kū' and begins living with it.
title_norm:泳ぎすぎた夜: A co-directed work by young French and Japanese filmmakers Damien Manivel of "The Young Poet" and Kohei Igarashi of "Hold Your Breath," born from their meeting at the 2014 Locarno International Film Festival. It depicts the small adventure of a boy living in wintry Aomori. In Aomori, covered entirely in snow in winter, a fishmonger father wakes in the middle of every night to head to the city market. His six-year-old son wakes as his father leaves and finds himself unable to fall back asleep. While the family sleeps soundly, the boy draws a picture, and the next morning on his usual way to school, he wanders off course, boards a train, and heads to the fish market to deliver his drawing to his father.
title_norm:浪華悲歌: Synopsis: Ayako (Yamada), a telephone operator, enters into a lover's contract with a married company president to cover her father's debts after he loses his job due to embezzlement suspicions... Considered one of Mizoguchi's masterpieces from before the war, the lively streets of Osaka and Yamada's modern fashion are also highlights.
title_norm:海よりもまだ深く: Director Hirokazu Kore-eda of "Our Little Sister" and "Like Father, Like Son" teams up with Atsushi Abe for the third time, following "Still Walking" and "I Wish," in this human drama centered on a man who can't grow up and his aging mother, portraying a family living a present different from the future they once dreamed of. Ryota is a middle-aged man who won a literary prize 15 years ago but hasn't been successful since, still chasing his dream of becoming a writer. He currently works at a detective agency to make ends meet, but makes excuses to himself and others that it's "research for his novel." Still hung up on his ex-wife, Kyoko, he is shocked to discover she has a new boyfriend while "staking out" her apartment. One day, Ryota, Kyoko, and their 11-year-old son Shingo gather at the apartment of his mother, Toshiko, who lives alone in a housing complex. Stranded by a typhoon, they end up spending the night together. Kirin Kiki delivers a wonderful performance as the protagonist's mother, with a stellar supporting cast including Yoko Maki, Satomi Kobayashi, and Lily Franky.
title_norm:海灘的一天: Edward Yang × Christopher Doyle! A masterpiece heralding the dawn of Taiwanese New Cinema by these two guiding lights of world cinema!
title_norm:海街diary: A story spanning one year in the lives of three sisters (Ayase, Nagasawa, Kaho) who, after the death of their father who left home 15 years ago and with whom they had lost touch, come to live with their half-sister Suzu (Hirose), who has lost her own family. Based on the best-selling manga by Yoshida Akimi, it carefully depicts the town of Kamakura, where the story is set, and the changing seasons, while bringing to light the love and sorrows of women of different generations.
title_norm:海辺のポーリーヌ: The third film in Éric Rohmer's "Comedies and Proverbs" series. It depicts the romantic entanglements of six men and women at a seaside villa, seen through the eyes of adolescent girl Pauline. Fifteen-year-old Pauline comes to Normandy for a vacation with her older cousin Marion. When they go to the beach, they meet Marion's ex-boyfriend Pierre. Pierre still harbors feelings for Marion, but Marion falls for Henri, a playboy acquaintance of Pierre's. Meanwhile, Pauline grows close to Sylvain, a boy windsurfing at the beach... The film won the Silver Bear and the FIPRESCI Prize at the Berlin International Film Festival.
title_norm:海辺の一日: Edward Yang × Christopher Doyle! A masterpiece heralding the dawn of Taiwanese New Cinema by these two guiding lights of world cinema!
title_norm:海辺の彼女たち: This is the second feature film by director Akiro Fujimoto, whose first feature 'Where I Belong'—a Japan-Myanmar co-production—won the Grand Prize in the 'Asian Future' section of the 30th Tokyo International Film Festival and received high acclaim both in Japan and abroad. Following his previous film, which dramatized the true story of a Myanmar family torn between Japan and Myanmar, this work again tackles the realities of Asian residents in Japan, depicting the plight of young women who come to Japan as technical intern trainees. Three Vietnamese women, who fled their workplaces after being mistreated, become undocumented. Relying on brokers to find new jobs, they end up in a snowy northern port town... Fujimoto met a female technical intern trainee online who later disappeared after grueling daily labor; he interviewed women in similar situations and wrote an original script.
title_norm:海辺の恋:
The 1963 feature debut of Guy Gilles—a director currently being rediscovered as a "forgotten master of the Nouvelle Vague"—is an autobiographical work that captures the fleeting love of youth. On a summer shore, Geneviève and Daniel, a sailor, find love in each other's arms. But when the vacation ends, he returns to the port city of Brest while she goes back to Paris. Hoping for a reunion, they continue to write to one another. Their story expands with the arrival of Guy, another sailor returning from the Algerian War, as the paths and emotions of the three quietly interweave. 

Starring Daniel Moosmann and Geneviève Thénier, the film also features director Guy Gilles himself as the sailor Guy, with a supporting cast of legendary actors including Jean-Pierre Léaud, Jean-Claude Brialy, Alain Delon, and Juliette Gréco. Impressed by Gilles’ 1959 short *Au biseau des baisers*, the master Jean-Pierre Melville provided partial funding for the film. A winner of the Critics’ Prize at the Locarno Film Festival, it will be released in Japanese theaters in April 2026.
title_norm:消えない光: Screening at the "Finland Film Festival 2025" (November 8–14, 2025 / Eurospace, Tokyo). Screening at "EU Film Days 2026" (Tokyo: May 16–29, 2026 at Theater Image Forum, May 19–24 at National Film Archive of Japan; Nagoya: June 6–19 at Nagoya Kinema Noi; also held in Hiroshima, Kyoto, and Fukuoka).
title_norm:深夜の告白: An early work by Billy Wilder and a masterpiece of film noir suspense. Insurance salesman Walter is approached by a married woman who wants to take out an accident insurance policy on her husband without his knowledge. Sensing something amiss, he initially refuses, but captivated by the beautiful wife, he descends into becoming an accomplice in the husband's murder. The murder scene creates indirect realism by holding on the expressions of those present. The supporting characters surrounding the pair are also superb.
title_norm:済州島四・三事件 ハラン: Based on the 'Jeju April 3 Incident,' a massacre in which nearly 30,000 people are said to have been killed but which was covered up for a long time, this drama depicts the flight of a mother and daughter desperately trying to survive while being driven into a corner by unreasonable violence. On April 3, 1948, the 'Jeju April 3 Incident' began when some islanders on Jeju Island, opposed to interference by foreign forces, staged an armed uprising. From October of the same year, the government designated areas more than 5 kilometers from the coastline as 'hostile zones' and issued a proclamation stating, 'Anyone entering or leaving will be shot without condition.' To escape disaster, the villagers head for Hallasan Mountain, which rises in the center of Jeju Island. A-jin, a woman who has to leave the village temporarily, is extremely worried about her 6-year-old daughter Hye-sen, whom she left behind. Meanwhile, in the village, the South Korean army is mercilessly shooting the elderly. Surviving, Hye-sen heads into the mountains alone to find her mother. After miraculously reuniting, the mother and daughter embark on a life-or-death escape to survive. Directed and written by Ha Myeong-mi, who built her career as a screenwriter for commercial films, it vividly portrays the nameless people tossed about by state power. Kim Hyang-gi, known for 'Along with the Gods' and 'Innocent Witness,' stars as A-jin.
title_norm:湖中の女: A beautiful female editor visits private detective Philip Marlowe, asking him to find the missing wife of a magazine publisher. This experimental film is shot entirely from Marlowe's point of view, using the camera as his eyes.
title_norm:満月の夜: The fourth film in Éric Rohmer's 'Comedies and Proverbs' series. Louise, an interior designer, lives with her architect boyfriend Rémi in a suburban Paris apartment. The serious Rémi and the free-spirited Louise are constantly bickering. Feeling stifled in her life with Rémi, Louise rents her own room in Paris and starts going out with her married best friend Octave... The film delicately portrays a woman's emotions as she wavers between two men and two homes. Lead actress Pascale Ogier won the Best Actress award at the Venice Film Festival for this role, but tragically died shortly after at the young age of 25. The cast also includes Fabrice Luchini from 'Claire's Knee' and Tchéky Karyo from 'Nikita.'
title_norm:火山のもとで: A drama by master filmmaker John Huston, known for 'The Treasure of the Sierra Madre' and 'The African Queen,' adapting the novel 'Under the Volcano' by British author Malcolm Lowry. Set in Mexico in the 1930s, it portrays love, loss, and loneliness through a single day in the life of a former British consul succumbing to alcoholism. On the 'Day of the Dead' in 1938, Geoffrey Firmin, a former British consul living in the small Mexican town of Cuernavaca, is in the throes of severe alcoholism, surrendering himself to drink and living a dissolute life. His wife Yvonne, who left him a year earlier but hopes for a reconciliation, suddenly returns. Adding to this, his half-brother Hugh also appears, and the three go out to see the festival and a bullfight... The film masterfully depicts humanity's self-destructive fate within the confines of a single day. Albert Finney, who played the protagonist Geoffrey, received high praise, including a nomination for the Academy Award for Best Actor at the 57th ceremony. The cast also includes Jacqueline Bisset and Anthony Andrews.
title_norm:火葬人: Set in Prague, Czechoslovakia on the eve of World War II, this dark comedy depicts how an ordinary citizen working at a funeral home is influenced by his pro-Nazi friend and the social climate, driving him toward a disastrous solution. Karel Kopfrkingl, who works as a cremator at a small Prague funeral home, is an ordinary man who loves his family. One day, he reunites with a war buddy from World War I, who has become a member of the Nazi Party. Persuaded by his friend to monitor the local Jewish community, Karel gradually becomes influenced by his friend and the social situation... The film portrays how an utterly ordinary person becomes a perpetrator, using beautiful yet eerie expressionistic imagery. This work, which exposes the terror of totalitarian ideology, was banned in its home country of Czechoslovakia and could not be shown until the fall of the communist regime in 1990. It won the Grand Prize at the 5th Sitges - Catalonian International Film Festival. In Japan, it will have its theatrical premiere in April 2026 as part of "Czech Film Masterpieces," a series featuring classics of the Czech New Wave.
title_norm:災 劇場版: A psychological suspense film directed, written, and edited by Yutaro Seki and Kentaro Hirase of the filmmaking collective "May," who gained domestic and international attention for their 2022 feature debut "Miyamatsu to Yamashita." It stars Kōji Yakusho, who also collaborated with them on that previous film. This is the theatrical version of the WOWOW drama series "Wazawai" (Disaster), broadcast from April to May 2025. It boldly restructures the six-episode series into a single film, depicting the calamity brought by a single man who infiltrates the everyday lives of six unrelated people. A high school girl troubled by family and her future, a deliveryman with a past, a shopping mall cleaner and a barber, the manager of a debt-ridden inn, and an ordinary housewife. The modest daily lives of these six people are suddenly struck by inexplicable disasters. The police dismiss them all as suicides or accidents, but Detective Dōmoto senses something strange and pursues the truth. Lurking around the edges of these six disasters is a single man. Changing his personality and appearance, he appears before the six as completely different people, bringing calamity upon them. Detective Dōmoto is played by Anne Nakamura, his colleague by Pistol Takehara and Kaito Miyakuni, and the people struck by disaster by Sena Nakajima, Ryuhei Matsuda, Megumi Uchida, Shunki Fujiwara, Jiro (Shisonne), and Maki Sakai.
title_norm:炎のごとく: The turbulent life of gambler Senkichi, who continues to love one woman. Set in Kyoto at the end of the Edo period, this powerful portrayal of unadorned love between a man and a woman stands as Tai Kato's final, crowning live-action film.
title_norm:炎上: Director Makoto Nagahisa, known for "We Are Little Zombies" and "And So We Put Goldfish in the Pool," casts Nana Mori in a drama set in Shinjuku's Kabukicho, depicting a "flame war" incident started by a girl. Born into a family of cult followers, Kobayashi Kurie is raised under strict discipline alongside her younger sister. The sisters pray to God daily for their painful days to end and for their education-obsessed father to disappear. Years later, their prayers are answered when their father dies, but their mother continues the harsh upbringing. Unable to bear it any longer, Kurie runs away from home, leaving her sister behind. Following a message on social media, she arrives at a square in Kabukicho where young people gather. There, she is given the name "Juju," a place to sleep, food, a smartphone, and a job. Experiencing the world for the first time and meeting various people, she finally begins to develop her own will. She dreams of taking her sister away from their mother and living together, but... Nagahisa wrote the original script and filmed on location in Kabukicho, capturing the raw reality of the neighborhood and the young people living there. Mori plays the protagonist Kurie, with Aoi Yamada ("Perfect Days"), Ryosuke Soda ("The Liar and His Lover"), and Wataru Ichinose (Netflix's "Sanctuary") co-starring.
title_norm:無こその存在 あるいは鮎子の人生:
A social drama depicting the darkness of a crumbling Japan through the story of a young woman living at the bottom of a stratified society who dreams of terrorism, and the mysterious Italian man who helps her. 

Ayuko Amami, a woman in her 20s, commits repeated acts of fraud and theft using matching apps. Her accomplice is Otoya Yamaguchi, whom she met on an app a year ago; they are "comrades in terrorism," a bond that is neither friendship nor romance. The two plan a large-scale terrorist attack targeting the Ministry of Finance, but unable to even find a route to acquire firearms, they continue their fraudulent activities. One day, they are caught in an undercover sting operation led by Detective Sasaki. While Otoya is arrested on the spot, Ayuko manages to escape. During her flight, she is rescued by Leo, a foreign tour guide who happens to be passing by. Upon learning of Ayuko’s terrorist plot, Leo introduces her to Manjiro Haruki, a high-profile wanted terrorist, but...

Ayumi Sakuma (Fast Break) stars as Ayuko, with Diego Martina—a multi-talented scholar of Japanese literature, translator, poet, and illustrator—playing Leo, and Naoya Serizawa (NHK’s Hanbun, Aoi) as Otoya. The film is written and directed by Gen Takahashi, known for works such as Confessions of a Dog and GOTH.
title_norm:無名: Set in Shanghai during World War II, this spy noir depicts the back-and-forth battle of nameless spies among the Chinese Communist Party, the Kuomintang, and the Japanese military. Starring Hong Kong superstar Tony Leung, who won the Best Actor award at the 53rd Cannes International Film Festival for 'In the Mood for Love' (2000) and has recently gained attention from younger generations for his role in 'Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings' (21). The other lead is Wang Yibo, who debuted as a member of the China-Korean joint unit 'UNIQ' and later broke out as an actor in the TV drama 'The Untamed' (19), now one of the most sought-after young actors in China. This film marks his first leading role in a movie, and he has since starred in multiple films, winning the Best Actor award at the 20th Film Channel Media Awards for his second lead role in 'Born to Fly' (23) alongside this film. The intense, stunt-free action sequences performed by the two leads captivate with overwhelming tension and unparalleled beauty. Directed by Chen Er, who previously helmed 'Once Upon a Time in Shanghai' (16). Chen also wrote and edited this film, and Tony Leung was so impressed by the script—only Chen's fourth feature—that he agreed to star. Nominated for eight awards including Best Picture and Best Actor at the 36th China Film Golden Rooster Awards, the highest honor in Chinese cinema, held in November last year. Wang Yibo, making his film debut, was nominated for Best Supporting Actor. Tony Leung won Best Actor, and director Chen Er won Best Director and Best Editing, achieving a triple crown.
