title_norm:花緑青が明ける日に: This animated film marks the feature directorial and screenwriting debut of Yoshitoshi Shinomiya, who has worked across genres primarily as a Nihonga (Japanese-style) painter. It is a Japan-France co-production with the cutting-edge French studio Miyu Productions. The 330-year-old Tategami Fireworks Factory, nestled in the woods, is facing eviction due to town redevelopment. Keitaro Tategami, who grew up there, has barricaded himself in the factory for four years, striving to complete the legendary "Shuhari" firework in place of his missing father, Eitaro. Meanwhile, Keitaro's childhood friend Kaoru Shikimori left their hometown for Tokyo after a past incident. Contacted by Keitaro's older brother Sentaro, who works at the city office, Kaoru visits the Tategami family on the last day of summer, the day before the eviction deadline, reuniting with Keitaro for the first time in four years. As they clash, trying to reclaim lost time and broken bonds, they hatch a surprising plan to uncover the secret of the phantom firework. The key lies in a beautiful blue pigment called "hanaryokusei" (copper acetoarsenite). Actors Rihito Noda and Kotone Furukawa make their voice acting debuts as Keitaro and Kaoru respectively, with voice actor Miyu Irino as Keitaro's brother Sentaro and actor Takashi Okabe as their father Eitaro. The film was selected for the Competition section of the 78th Berlin International Film Festival in 2026.
title_norm:芸術家、ただいま迷走中: Screened at EU Film Days 2026 (Tokyo: May 16–29 at Theater Image Forum, May 19–24 at the National Film Archive of Japan; Nagoya: June 6–19 at Nagoya Cinema Neu; also to be held in Hiroshima, Kyoto, and Fukuoka).
title_norm:華麗なる一族: A socially conscious drama centered on a wealthy banking family, depicting human ambition, love, and hatred over wealth and power spanning political and financial circles. Director Yamamoto Satsuo's epic adaptation of Yamasaki Toyoko's novel of the same name. Daisuke Manpai, president of Hanshin Bank. The Manpai family, renowned in Kansai financial circles, expands its influence by marrying off its children one after another to major figures in politics and finance, solidifying its power. These maneuvers are orchestrated not by Daisuke's naive aristocratic wife, Neiko, but by Aiko Takasu, who has long served as both a tutor and housekeeper. However, the family's gears gradually begin to grind out of sync...
title_norm:華麗な関係: An erotic film directed by Roger Vadim, based on the sensual novel 'Les Liaisons Dangereuses'. Set in 19th-century France, it depicts the affair between a playboy count and a married woman. The bewitching performances of two charismatic actresses are captivating.
title_norm:萌の朱雀: A small village in the mountains of southern Nara Prefecture. Fifteen years have passed since plans to build a railway through this village were proposed, but Kozo Tamura, who was involved in the tunnel construction, loses all motivation upon learning the project has been cancelled. Then one day, Kozo disappears. His remaining family, bewildered, each make their own choices.
title_norm:落下音: Four girls from different eras, spanning from the 1910s to the present day, experience inexplicable events on a farm in northern Germany. A century-spanning visual epic where their anxieties resonate with one another.
title_norm:蒸発: A documentary co-directed by German filmmaker Andreas Hartmann and Berlin/Tokyo-based video artist Arata Mori, exploring the Japanese phenomenon of "evaporation" (disappearance). In Japan, approximately 80,000 people go missing each year, with thousands vanishing completely. Known as "evaporated people," their reasons range from relationship troubles and debt to yakuza threats. Some, with the help of so-called "night escape artists," abandon all ties and start new lives elsewhere. "Evaporation," intersecting deep loss and the hope of starting over, has been a motif in literature and film. This work uses immersive imagery to delve into the unknown work of "night escape artists" and the emotional conflicts and paths to reconciliation for both the disappeared and those left behind. It garnered attention at film festivals worldwide, winning Best Documentary at the 39th Munich International Documentary Film Festival.
title_norm:蘇える金狼: Legendary popular actor Yusaku Matsuda stars as a lone wolf with two faces—a salaryman and an outlaw—in this hit Kadokawa action film based on the novel of the same name by Haruhiko Oyabu, which was a huge success upon its release. Following his explosive popularity in the pioneering TV drama 'Taiyo ni Hoero!', Matsuda teams up again with director Tohru Murakawa and cinematographer Seizo Sengen—who also worked with him on the 'Game' film series and the drama 'Daitokai PARTII'—to break new ground in domestic hard-action cinema. A must-see film, Matsuda enhanced his wild charisma by experiencing live-fire shooting abroad for his role. Murakawa's signature long-take cinematography brings unique intensity to the gunfight scenes, and the final line is said to be an ad-lib by Matsuda himself, not in the script. Tetsuya Asakura appears to be an ordinary salaryman by day, but by night he trains his body and plots to take over a massive corporation. One day, he uses drugs he obtained to seduce his boss's mistress, Kyoko Nagai. Soon after, he discovers that a man named Sakurai is blackmailing company executives over an embezzlement scandal. Asakura skillfully manipulates Sakurai and the company to successfully become engaged to the president's daughter, Eriko. Meanwhile, burning with jealousy, Kyoko makes a fateful decision.
title_norm:蘇える金狼（1979）: A hard-boiled action film reuniting actor Yusaku Matsuda and director Toru Murakawa—the duo behind *The Most Dangerous Game* and *The Execution Game*—to adapt Haruhiko Oyabu’s novel of the same name. Tetsuya Asakura is a 29-year-old ordinary salaryman, but by night, he hones his physique at a boxing gym, driven by a burning ambition to seize control of Towa Yushi, the conglomerate where he is employed. After successfully robbing an armored car of 90 million yen, Asakura uses narcotics obtained during the money-laundering process to manipulate Kyoko, his boss’s mistress. Armed with Kyoko’s insider information on the company’s corrupt inner workings, Asakura begins eliminating his rivals one by one, but...
title_norm:血を吸うスマトラオオコンニャク: Set in Malaysia, this demon-combining exorcism gore horror film takes on the Islamic exorcism rites of the state religion and Southeast Asia's most enigmatic flower, the titan arum. A boy apprentice exorcist, who inherited spiritual powers from his mother, engages in a deadly struggle against the forbidden curse dwelling within the "corpse flower." Iqbal, raised under the wing of Norman, a Muslim exorcist, possesses rare spiritual abilities inherited from his mother Dina. One day, Dina is possessed and killed by an evil spirit while shielding Iqbal, who was targeted because of the strength of his powers. Grief-stricken, Iqbal resents his own overwhelming power, and his father Norman, worried about his son's future, seals away part of his abilities. Crawling toward the wounded family are a series of tragedies brought by the curse of the "corpse flower." Can Iqbal overcome his sorrow and exorcise a curse steeped in mystery and taboo?
title_norm:街の上で: Arakawa Ao (Ryuya Wakaba), who works at a vintage clothing store in Shimokitazawa, can't forget his ex-girlfriend who cheated on him and dumped him. His life, mostly spent alone—occasionally going to live shows or his usual bar—is self-contained within the Shimokitazawa area. One day, a female director attending art school invites him to appear in her independent film.
title_norm:街の灯（1931）: A timeless masterpiece written, directed by, and starring the King of Comedy, Charles Chaplin, depicting the struggles of a man who falls in love with a blind flower girl through a blend of humor and pathos. Defying the rising tide of "talkies," the film was intentionally produced as a sound film without dialogue. Charlie, a homeless and jobless tramp, falls for a blind girl selling flowers on a street corner. Mistaken for a wealthy gentleman, he attempts to earn money for her by working as a street sweeper and competing in boxing matches, but success is hard to come by. In the midst of his efforts, Charlie befriends a drunken millionaire and receives a large sum of money from him, but...
title_norm:裏窓: After breaking his leg, photographer Jeff is confined to a wheelchair and bed rest. To stave off boredom, he makes a daily habit of watching the residents of the apartment building across the way through his window. One day, however, he notices that the bedridden wife who had been arguing with her salesman husband has disappeared. Enlisting the help of his girlfriend Lisa and his nurse Stella, he begins his investigation through the rear window. Piece by piece, he gathers circumstantial evidence suggesting the man murdered his wife, and his suspicion gradually hardens into certainty…
title_norm:裸の拍車: Like 'The Naked Spur,' this is a Technicolor Western directed by Anthony Mann and starring James Stewart, produced by William H. Wright of 'Violent Behavior' in 1953. The screenplay was written by up-and-coming radio and TV writing team Sam Rolfe and Harold Jack Bloom, cinematography by William C. Mellor of 'Cross Missouri,' and music by Bronisław Kaper of 'The Wolf of the North.' Co-stars include Janet Leigh of 'Blood Fight,' Robert Ryan of 'The Three Bad Men of the Wilderness,' newcomer Ralph Meeker of 'The Four Jeeps,' and Millard Mitchell of 'Singin' in the Rain.'
title_norm:西游·降魔篇: Young monster hunter Xuanzang uses his "Three Hundred Nursery Rhymes" as a weapon to try to awaken the good hearts of monsters, but always fails. One day, in a riverside village attacked by a half-fish, half-beast monster, he works with the villagers to haul the creature ashore, where it transforms into human form. The nursery rhymes Xuanzang sings have no effect at all, and when he is attacked instead, he is saved by a female monster hunter named Duan.
title_norm:西游记·女儿国: Continuing their westward journey to India, Sanzo and his companions Son Goku, Cho Hakkai, and Sha Gojyo are attacked by a giant fish while traveling by boat on a river. The four are swept through a mysterious hole in the sky and land in a strange land—the "Land of Women," where only women live. The queen and Sanzo develop mutual affection. Soon, the four are sentenced to execution under the land's laws, but they manage to escape thanks to the queen's intervention. However, they have no idea how to return from the Land of Women to their original world...
title_norm:西遊記: A rousing entertainment masterpiece based on Osamu Tezuka's "My Son Goku," bringing together the energy of young artists during the first golden age of Toei Animation. It is noteworthy that Osamu Tezuka himself took the lead in drawing the storyboards, and the on-site staff included a large number of talented individuals who would later carry the future of Japan's animation industry. In other words, it is one of the origins of Japanese animated films, a monumental work that greatly envisioned the future of the medium from an entertainment perspective. Winner of the Special Grand Prize at the Venice International Children's Film Festival.
title_norm:西遊記 はじまりのはじまり: Young monster hunter Xuanzang uses his "Three Hundred Nursery Rhymes" as a weapon to try to awaken the good hearts of monsters, but always fails. One day, in a riverside village attacked by a half-fish, half-beast monster, he works with the villagers to haul the creature ashore, where it transforms into human form. The nursery rhymes Xuanzang sings have no effect at all, and when he is attacked instead, he is saved by a female monster hunter named Duan.
title_norm:西遊記 女人国の戦い: Continuing their westward journey to India, Sanzo and his companions Son Goku, Cho Hakkai, and Sha Gojyo are attacked by a giant fish while traveling by boat on a river. The four are swept through a mysterious hole in the sky and land in a strange land—the "Land of Women," where only women live. The queen and Sanzo develop mutual affection. Soon, the four are sentenced to execution under the land's laws, but they manage to escape thanks to the queen's intervention. However, they have no idea how to return from the Land of Women to their original world...
title_norm:西遊記 孫悟空 vs 白骨夫人: Five hundred years after the violent Son Goku was imprisoned under Five Elements Mountain, he is freed from his seal by the monk Sanzo, who is heading to India, and joins the journey as Sanzo's bodyguard. Along the way, the group gains new companions, but they are confronted by the demoness Hakukotsu-fujin, who seeks to kill Sanzo in order to maintain her own eternal beauty. Using various schemes, Hakukotsu-fujin finally captures Sanzo.
title_norm:西遊記之孫悟空三打白骨精: Five hundred years after the violent Son Goku was imprisoned under Five Elements Mountain, he is freed from his seal by the monk Sanzo, who is heading to India, and joins the journey as Sanzo's bodyguard. Along the way, the group gains new companions, but they are confronted by the demoness Hakukotsu-fujin, who seeks to kill Sanzo in order to maintain her own eternal beauty. Using various schemes, Hakukotsu-fujin finally captures Sanzo.
title_norm:西遊記～はじまりのはじまり～: Young monster hunter Xuanzang uses his "Three Hundred Nursery Rhymes" as a weapon to try to awaken the good hearts of monsters, but always fails. One day, in a riverside village attacked by a half-fish, half-beast monster, he works with the villagers to haul the creature ashore, where it transforms into human form. The nursery rhymes Xuanzang sings have no effect at all, and when he is attacked instead, he is saved by a female monster hunter named Duan.
title_norm:見はらし世代: Set in rapidly redeveloping Tokyo's Shibuya, this drama portrays the relationship between a father and son left behind after the mother's death. It marks the film debut of Koyo Kurozaki, who gained attention for his acting debut in the NHK morning drama "Boogie Woogie." This is the feature debut of Yuiga Dansuka, based on his original script; he previously directed the short "I Want to Go Far Away" as part of the Agency for Cultural Affairs' young filmmaker development project "ndjc (New Directions in Japanese Cinema)." Ren, a young man working as a Phalaenopsis orchid delivery driver in Shibuya, became estranged from his father, Hajime, a landscape designer, after losing his mother, Yumiko, as a child. One day, Ren coincidentally meets his father during a delivery and tells his sister Emi, but she remains indifferent, quietly preparing for her own wedding. Amidst this, Ren tries to reassess his distance from his family. Kurozaki plays the protagonist Ren, Kenichi Endo (an indispensable supporting actor in Japanese cinema) plays his father Hajime, Haru Ikewaki (active as an actress and model) plays the deceased mother Yumiko, and Maso Kuryu (a talented actress from "Chrysanthemum and Guillotine" and "The Lies of the Suzuki Family") plays his sister Emi. The film was selected for the Directors' Fortnight at the 78th Cannes Film Festival in 2025.
title_norm:親切なクムジャさん: Director Park Chan-wook's final installment of his "Revenge Trilogy," following "Sympathy for Mr. Vengeance" and "Oldboy," is a suspense drama about a woman wrongfully imprisoned who exacts revenge. Lee Geum-ja is imprisoned after a man takes her daughter hostage and forces her to take the blame for his child kidnapping and murder. During her sentence, she never loses her gentle smile, earning the nickname "Kind Geum-ja." After serving 13 years, she is released and begins her revenge against the true culprit who framed her. She retrieves her daughter, who was adopted abroad, and with the help of former inmates who have already been released, corners the man. Starring Lee Young-ae ("JSA," "Last Present") and co-starring Choi Min-sik ("Oldboy"), with cameos by Kang Hye-jung, Yoo Ji-tae, Song Kang-ho, and Shin Ha-kyun.
title_norm:親密さ: Spanning approximately four hours, this feature-length work originated as a project for the acting course graduation at ENBU Seminar, a vocational school for film, theater, and actor training. It is composed of two parts: a narrative film depicting the process of creating a play titled "Intimacies," and a recording of the actual stage performance, with fiction and reality intertwining in each. With the premiere of their new production drawing near, directors Reiko and Ryohei find the limits of their collaborative partnership beginning to show...
title_norm:親密さ濱⼝⻯介監督特集上映突然、偶然、必然: A project that started as a graduation work for the film acting course at ENBU Seminar. A masterpiece youth ensemble drama depicted in two parts: the first half, where the process of creating a play called "Intimacy" is performed as fiction, and the second half, which records the actual performance and composes it as a film. Reality and fiction continue to intertwine complexly, and the core of reality on the other side of the real and the fictional stirs the heart.
title_norm:言の葉の庭: From the director Makoto Shinkai, known for delicate drama and visual beauty in works like 'The Place Promised in Our Early Days' and '5 Centimeters per Second,' comes a love story set for the first time in modern Tokyo. Takao, a high school student aiming to become a shoemaker, skips school on rainy days to sketch shoes in a park's Japanese garden. One such day, he meets a mysterious older woman named Yukino, and the two grow closer through meetings that happen only on rainy days. For Yukino, who says she has lost her place in the world, Takao tries to craft shoes that make her want to walk more, but... The main staff for character design, art, and music features new faces different from Shinkai's previous works. The short film 'Dareka no Manazashi' is shown as a double feature.
title_norm:記憶の解凍: A film by director Anju Niwata from Hiroshima Prefecture, expressing her nine-year project "Memory Thawing" through documentary and animation. "Memory Thawing" recreates the "colors of memory" by colorizing black-and-white photos capturing daily life before and after the atomic bombing, combining dialogue with war survivors and AI technology. Through conversations based on the colorized photos, frozen sad memories transform into memories of happy pre-war daily life. The film conveys precious "narratives" from records of dialogues with over 30 people in Japan and abroad, including former residents of Nakajima-honmachi, a once-thriving entertainment district in the area now home to the Hiroshima Peace Memorial Park. The animation part depicts the protagonist Anji, who travels through time in a time machine to restore the colors of a lost everyday life. Director Niwata drew the illustrations for the animation part, which was produced under the supervision of Sunao Katabuchi, director of the animated film "In This Corner of the World," with participation from video artist Kenta Nomura and others. Composer and pianist Kanako Hara handled the music, composing the theme song "Heiwa Iro no Shashin" after visiting the Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum and Peace Memorial Park and speaking with atomic bomb survivors. Director Niwata wrote the lyrics, and HIPPY, a singer-songwriter active in passing down the atomic bomb experience, performed the song.
title_norm:許されざる者: The Zachary family runs a ranch on the Texas plains. Rumors spread that their adopted daughter, Rachel, is a Kiowa girl. Ben, the eldest son who manages the ranch, tries to uncover the truth. The facts eventually come to light through the mother, but the Zacharys become isolated, and the Kiowa attack to reclaim Rachel. Ben and his family fight back. This is Audrey Hepburn's first and only Western film.
title_norm:許されざる者（1960）: The Zachary family runs a ranch on the Texas plains. Rumors spread that their adopted daughter, Rachel, is a Kiowa girl. Ben, the eldest son who manages the ranch, tries to uncover the truth. The facts eventually come to light through the mother, but the Zacharys become isolated, and the Kiowa attack to reclaim Rachel. Ben and his family fight back. This is Audrey Hepburn's first and only Western film.
title_norm:詩人iidabii ある宗教2世の記録: A documentary capturing the spoken-word poet iidabii, a so-called 'second-generation religious believer' raised under a specific faith, as he bares his past, wounds, and inner conflicts. iidabii unleashes the power of words and the cry of his soul with his entire being. Growing up in a religion practiced by his parents, he spent a childhood where even questioning was forbidden, until he encountered 'poetry.' For him, burdened with a complex background and a stutter, poetry became a weapon to shout his emotions in silence and a means to redefine himself. His poetry resonates deeply with those living on the fringes of society. This film records iidabii's life journey and creative process over three years, weaving a story about faith, family, language, and freedom. Directed by Matsui Shuhiro and Tsuda Tomomi, who have worked on numerous television documentary programs.
title_norm:誓い 建築家 b・v・ドーシ: A documentary about the world-renowned Indian architect Balkrishna Doshi. Balkrishna Vithaldas Doshi, who in 2018 became the first Indian to win the Pritzker Prize, considered the Nobel Prize of architecture, passed away in 2023 at the age of 95. Beginning his career under Le Corbusier in Paris in the 1950s, he oversaw the implementation of Corbusier's projects in Ahmedabad, western India, and later collaborated with Louis Kahn after India's independence. Influenced by Corbusier and Kahn, Doshi incorporated sustainable and ecological ideas into his architecture early on, establishing a unique style that fused modernism with Indian tradition, climate, and spirituality. He aimed for architecture that contributes to society and the environment, a 'people's architecture' rooted in daily life. This film delves into Doshi's inner world in his final years, visiting the buildings he collaborated on with Corbusier and Kahn, as well as his own works, as he discusses his architectural philosophy, creative process, and career spanning 70 years. Screened as part of the special program 'Le Corbusier and Doshi: Indian Modernism' (starting May 1, 2026, at Eurospace in Tokyo and other theaters nationwide).
title_norm:誓い 建築家b・v・ドーシ: A documentary about the world-renowned Indian architect Balkrishna Doshi. title_norm:誰がために憲法はある: This documentary re-examines the meaning of the Constitution of Japan, based on the stage monologue "Kenpo-kun" (Mr. Constitution) performed for years by comedian Hiro Matsumoto. In 1980, 35 years after the war, actress Misako Watanabe learned that her first love had died in the atomic bombing of Hiroshima while evacuated. As a central member of a group of veteran actresses, she spent 33 years performing atomic bomb reading dramas across Japan, a project that came to a close in 2019. The film records the personal reflections of these actresses who toured the country in a spirit of requiem. It also captures Misako Watanabe, aged 87 in 2019, as she delivers a soul-stirring performance of "Kenpo-kun"—a personification of the Constitution used to convey its importance—pouring her heart into the role to ensure the tragedy of war never happens in this country again. The film is directed by Junichi Inoue, who wrote the screenplay for "Dare to Stop Us" and directed the documentary "Inherit the Earth."
title_norm:誰も知らない: Keiko (YOU) and four children, including Akira (Yagira), live in a single apartment room under false pretenses. When Keiko eventually stops coming home, the children are left to fend for themselves, but their financial situation gradually becomes dire. Inspired by a real-life child abandonment case, the film delicately portrays modern social issues such as neglect, young carers, and those who fall through the cracks of the welfare system, earning high international acclaim.
title_norm:谷口善太郎 たたかう小説: A documentary depicting the little-known struggles of Zen-taro Taniguchi—a politician affectionately known as "Tanizen" in the post-war era—during his years as a proletarian novelist. In 1931, Taniguchi entered the literary world under the pen name Hajime Sui. His debut work, "Episode of the March 15th Incident," followed by his
title_norm:貸間あり: In a large rundown house overlooking the Tsutenkaku Tower in Osaka, a group of eccentric lodgers live... Frankie, in his famous partnership with Kawashima, plays a laid-back jack-of-all-trades who works as a ghostwriter and konnyaku maker. With unique supporting actors like Naniwa and Ozawa, this is a brilliant ensemble comedy that leaves a lasting impression.
title_norm:赤い砂漠: The first color film by Italian master Michelangelo Antonioni, this psychological drama won the Golden Lion at the 25th Venice International Film Festival in 1964. In Ravenna, an industrial coastal city lined with sterile factories, Giuliana lives with her husband and son but remains unable to recover from the shock of a car accident years earlier, spending her days in emotional instability. One day, her husband introduces her to his friend Corrado. Giuliana is drawn to Corrado, who carries a loneliness similar to her own, and gradually the two grow closer... Monica Vitti, known as Antonioni's muse, plays Giuliana, with British star Richard Harris as Corrado. A 4K restored version will be released in August 2026 as part of the retrospective program "Michelangelo Antonioni Retrospective: Arid Love, Wandering Souls," featuring five of Antonioni's early works.
title_norm:赤い糸 輪廻のひみつ: From Giddens Ko, director of "Mon Mon Mon Monsters!" and "You Are the Apple of My Eye," comes a pure love fantasy inspired by the Taiwanese folk deity "Yue Lao" (the God of Matchmaking) and the concept of reincarnation. After being struck by lightning and brought to the underworld, Xiao Lun, along with Pinky who also arrives there, returns to the mortal world as the Taiwanese matchmaking god "Yue Lao" to tie the fates of people together. One day, a dog appears before them, triggering Xiao Lun to recover his lost memories of his past life. He remembers a promise he made to his first love, Xiao Mi, which he was unable to fulfill due to his sudden death. Starring popular Taiwanese actors: Ku Chen-dong ("You Are the Apple of My Eye") as Xiao Lun, Vivian Sung ("Our Times") as Xiao Mi, and Wang Jing ("The Soul of the Banquet," "My Ghost Friend") as Pinky.
title_norm:赤い風車: A biographical film by master filmmaker John Huston, known for 'The Maltese Falcon' and 'The African Queen,' depicting the short life of the late 19th-century French painter Toulouse-Lautrec. Paris, Montmartre, at the end of the 19th century. The painter Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec frequents the cabaret 'Moulin Rouge,' symbolized by the red windmill on its roof, spending his days sketching the dancers and drunk patrons. Born into an aristocratic family, his leg growth stopped due to the effects of consanguineous marriage and a childhood accident. He finds purpose in life by leaving his stifling home to live in Montmartre and painting its scenes. One night, Henri helps a prostitute named Marie and begins living with her, but their relationship gradually falls apart. Based on the biographical novel 'Moulin Rouge' by Pierre La Mure, the screenplay was co-written by Huston and Anthony Veiller, known for 'The Night of the Iguana' and 'The Killers.' José Ferrer, of 'The Caine Mutiny,' stars, playing both Toulouse-Lautrec and his father in a dual role. The film won the Academy Awards for Best Art Direction and Best Costume Design at the 25th Academy Awards in 1953.
title_norm:赤線地帯: Commentary: Mizoguchi Kenji's final work. Set in a Yoshiwara brothel in Tokyo on the eve of the abolition of the red-light district, this female ensemble piece depicts the joys and sorrows of women who have drifted there with various circumstances. The nonchalant prostitutes, played by a cast of luxurious actresses, exude a peculiar atmosphere, making this film a one-of-a-kind red-light district story.
title_norm:赫い髪の女: Based on Kenji Nakagami's short story "Akagami" (Red Hair), with a screenplay by the young Haruhiko Arai, vividly brought to the screen by director Kōji Wakamatsu. A masterpiece passionately remembered as one of Nikkatsu Roman Porno's representative works. The story follows Kōzō, a dump truck driver at a construction company, and a red-haired woman he picks up on the street, depicting the sordid waves of lust, the stagnant relationship between a man and a woman unfolding in a closed-off town. And on the other side, a man and a woman who begin seeking an escape from it all...
title_norm:超時空英雄伝エイリアノイド part1：神剣激突 & pa: Across time and space, the fates of heroes collide—the ultimate chronoverse entertainment is born! From CJ ENM, the studio behind the Oscar-winning "Parasite," comes an unprecedented scale of time-spanning entertainment blockbuster. Five years in the making, 387 days of shooting—a grand adventure that carves a new monument in Korean film history now begins. An ancient cosmic punishment: aliens have been imprisoning prisoners inside human bodies. In modern-day Korea, android guards Gado and Thunder pursue rampaging aliens, while in the late Goryeo Dynasty 630 years ago, Taoist sorcerer Muruk and a mysterious woman named Ian who controls lightning engage in a fateful battle over the legendary "Divine Sword." And at the moment when time and space intersect, a battle beyond imagination begins. Directed by Choi Dong-hoon, the hitmaker behind "The Thieves" and "Assassination," each drawing over 10 million viewers. He has assembled a stellar cast including Ryu Jun-yeol, Kim Woo-bin, Kim Tae-ri, as well as So Ji-sub, Yeom Jung-ah, Jo Woo-jin, and Lee Ha-nui. Transcending time, those guided by destiny now clash for the future of humanity. In 2026, an unprecedented realm of imagination is unleashed on screen.
title_norm:身土不二（しんどふじ）: A documentary focusing on organic farming in Atsushio Kano Town, Fukushima Prefecture, and its school lunches that achieved a 100% local consumption rate. The former Atsushio Kano Village in Kitakata City, Fukushima, was once called the 'Village of Organic Farming.' Starting organic farming in 1980, their specially cultivated rice 'Himesayuri Rice,' grown with minimal pesticides and chemical fertilizers, became the village's main specialty. Organic cultivation expanded to vegetables, and these rice and vegetables were used in school lunches, gaining national attention as 'nearly 100% locally sourced lunches.' However, the wave of declining birthrates and aging population has reached the town, threatening the continuation of school lunches amid the consolidation of schools and the aging of local farmers. The film documents over three and a half years the reality of the 'Atsushio Kano Method' lunches, the passion of the 'Magokoro Vegetable Association' farmers for growing vegetables, and the children happily eating those lunches. Through the interactions between local farmers who continue to provide lunches through organic farming and the children, it highlights the issues of declining birthrates, aging, global environmental problems facing agriculture today, and the origins of organic farming. Directed by Abiko Wataru, known for 'Decision: The 3.11 Mother-Child Evacuation That Changed Destiny,' who moved his base to Fukushima after the 2011 Great East Japan Earthquake to produce documentary films.
title_norm:身土不二（しんどふじ）～日本一の学校給食と有機農業～: Food is truly the 'staff of life' for humans. Agriculture is the 'industry of life,' as proclaimed by Mr. Yoshimasa Kobayashi (a agricultural cooperative employee). In 1980, organic agriculture began in Atsushio Kano Village. Soon, through the efforts of residents who wanted to raise their children on local organic vegetables and rice, a newly assigned nutritionist, and Mr. Kobayashi, school lunches using 'Magokoro Vegetables' (heartfelt vegetables) were born. This initiative, known as the 'Atsushio Kano Method' of school lunches, became a topic of discussion, drawing a flood of media coverage and study visits from across the country. However, the wave of declining birthrates and an aging population reached this 'Organic Village,' leading to the closure of the junior high school and the merger of two elementary schools. Amid concerns about becoming a 'marginal settlement,' the very continuation of the school lunch program is threatened. This film explores the origins of organic agriculture through school lunches with a nearly 100% local consumption rate and a lifestyle attuned to the village's natural environment.
title_norm:軋み kishimi:
A single-location drama depicting the human drama that unfolds within the apartment of a popular manga artist. Jun Sakashita has spent three years without a job, relying on his wife, Yumiko, a successful manga artist. One day, Jun is confronted with a scene in his living room: his wife, an editor, and the corpse of Hitomi—Jun’s mistress, whom Yumiko killed on impulse. Between an editor desperate to cover up the murder, an assistant who drops by unaware of the situation, and a mysterious man searching for Hitomi, a web of conflicting motives intersects within the walls of the apartment.

Mami Yamasaki (*Love Like...*) stars as the protagonist Yumiko, while Akiyoshi Shibata (*Agito: Psychic Wars*) plays her husband, Jun. They are supported by Ren Yagami, Ryusuke Komakine, and Takashi Shigematsu. The film is directed by Kei Morikawa, who won the Grand Prix at the Yubari International Fantastic Film Festival for *Make Room*, which also depicted a single-location commotion in an adult video set's makeup room. The original story and screenplay are by Brazily Anne Yamada, leader of the theater troupe "Gekidan Brazil" and screenwriter for *RAILWAYS* and *Stigmatized Properties*.
title_norm:軍服を着た神様: A documentary exploring the mystery of "Japanese gods" found across Taiwan. In Taiwan, once a Japanese colony, there are over fifty locations where Japanese men in military uniforms are enshrined as deities. Cultural anthropologist Yohei Fujino and documentary filmmaker Kyo Endo spent six years, including the COVID-19 pandemic, traveling across Taiwan to visit these "Japanese gods." As they trace the mystery, the fact that each Japanese god truly existed as an individual human being comes to light, revealing their extraordinary fates, the nature of Taiwanese folk beliefs, and the lingering traces of war Japan left in Taiwan. Through the souls of Japanese people wandering in a foreign land after death, the Taiwanese who soothe these souls and enshrine them as gods, and the Japanese descendants who reconnect with their deified ancestors, the film portrays an unknown exchange between Japan and Taiwan born from the heart of mourning and honoring the dead. Directed by Kyo Endo, who specializes in folkloric motifs and won the 73rd Mainichi Film Award for Best Documentary for "Meguri Kagura." Music and animation are by Tetsutaro Take, a member of the music unit "Bakurocho Band" who also works as an artist.
title_norm:近松物語: A commentary: Osan, the young wife of a Kyoto paper merchant, is suspected of adultery with the clerk Mohei due to a chance incident... Based on a Chikamatsu puppet play, this celebrated film depicts a man and woman who awaken to true love through a life-or-death escape, rendered with rigorous yet flowing brushstrokes. The dignified beauty of Kagawa as Osan is not to be missed.
title_norm:遊歩 ノーボーダー: A documentary tracing the journey and present life of Yuho Asaka, one of Japan's pioneers of peer counseling. Born in Fukushima City, Fukushima Prefecture in 1956, Yuho Asaka has a condition characterized by brittle bones. From a young age, she was forced to give up on learning and grew angry at a society that discriminates and excludes based on disability and gender. Always searching for her place in the world, Asaka connected with the cerebral palsy activist group "Fukushima Prefecture Aoi Shiba no Kai" and, drawing on the independent living movement and feminism she encountered while studying in the U.S., helped establish Japan's first independent living center. She also participated in international conferences and helped spark changes to the Eugenic Protection Law. The film follows Asaka's relentless pursuit of freedom, while also depicting her sister Aiko, who was caught in the turbulent relationship between their father and Yuho; her daughter Sora, who was born with the same condition and works at an overseas institute advocating for the rights of people with disabilities while attending graduate school; and the young caregivers who share daily life with her in a free-spirited relationship. Yumiko Asano, producer of "What Could Have Been?," makes her directorial debut, with Tomoaki Fujino, director of that same film, handling cinematography, editing, and production.

title_norm:遠来 トモベのコトバ: Filmmaker Shinichi Ise, known for documentary works such as the "Nao-chan" series and "PascaLs: Something Like Happiness," presents a human documentary chronicling the long journey of musician and poet Masato Tomobe in New York. Born in Tokyo in 1950, Tomobe began singing on the streets of Nagoya after graduating high school and made his recording debut in 1972 with the album "Osaka e Yatte Kita" (I've Come to Osaka). To date, he has released 26 original albums and published numerous collections of poetry and essays. Filming for this project began about ten years ago when Director Ise, a friend of Tomobe for 30 years, went to visit him while he was living in New York. The film gathers the unstructured moments of Tomobe’s ongoing journey in search of words, bringing them to the screen alongside his songs and poetry.
title_norm:遺愛: A horror film directed by Yoshizo Sakai of "Fictional" and "Counselor," planned and produced by Tokio Omori, a TV Tokyo producer who brought forth "The Missing Exhibit" and "Searching for Kikue Ishinaga." Rio Yamashita, who starred in the 2025 long-running hit "Yukiko a.k.a." primarily in mini-theaters over about a year, plays the lead role of a woman tormented by paranoid fear through caring for her mother. After her father's death, Kana returns to her childhood home and begins caring for her mother, who has dementia. She devotes herself to caregiving as if trying to reclaim time with her mother, but her mother's inexplicable behavior gradually becomes increasingly bizarre, and Kana begins to feel uneasy about strange occurrences around her. Eventually, possessed by the sensation that something has entered her mother's inner being, Kana is driven mad by the presence of an unearthly "something." In addition to Rio Yamashita as the protagonist Kana, An Ogawa, who has starred in successive films including "There Is a Stone" and "Song of the Beyond," plays Kana's younger sister Anri, who rushes to the family home after hearing Kana's pleas, and Sports Makita plays psychiatrist Kumagai, who becomes acquainted with Kana and Anri's family through a certain incident.
title_norm:里見八犬伝: Kinji Fukasaku directs this adaptation of Toshio Kamata's legendary novel "Shin Satomi Hakkenden," a fresh take on Bakin Takizawa's classic "Nanso Satomi Hakkenden." Starring the glamorous duo Hiroko Yakushimaru and Hiroyuki Sanada, it became a massive hit characteristic of Kadokawa Films, which dominated the era and breathed new life into Japanese cinema. Tamazusa, who once married into the Hikita domain and indulged in debauchery and tyranny before being destroyed by the Satomi clan, returns as a demon queen to exact revenge. She orders her son Motofuji Hikita and his retainers to attack the Satomi's Tateyama Castle. The Satomi clan is annihilated, but Princess Shizu and a few retainers escape, pursued by Tamazusa's forces. The eight warriors, each possessing a jewel inscribed with one of the virtues—benevolence, righteousness, propriety, wisdom, loyalty, faith, filial piety, and brotherly love—scattered from Princess Fuse's body, live their separate lives. Guided by fate, they gather around Princess Shizu and rise to battle, aiming to crush Tamazusa's ambitions.
title_norm:重慶森林: A stylish ensemble love story set in Hong Kong that depicts the intersecting romantic entanglements of young people, catapulting director Wong Kar-wai to international fame. Cop 223, heartbroken on April Fool's Day, buys a can of pineapple every day until his birthday a month later. Determined to forget his lover by falling for a woman he meets that night, he encounters a blonde woman in sunglasses at a bar he stumbles into. Meanwhile, fast-food worker Faye is given a letter by her boss for regular customer Cop 633. It's a letter from Cop 633's ex-girlfriend, containing the key to his apartment. Faye, harboring a crush on him, uses the key to sneak into his room... Cop 223 is played by Takeshi Kaneshiro, and Cop 633 by Tony Leung. It won three awards including Best Picture at the 14th Hong Kong Film Awards. First released in Japan in 1995. In 2022, a 4K restored version was screened as part of 'WKW4K' (from August 19, 2022, at Cine Mart Shinjuku, Grand Cinema Sunshine, Cinema City, etc.).
title_norm:野性の証明: A massacre occurs deep in the Tohoku mountains, killing most of a village's residents. A self-defense force special unit member, Misawa, who was training in the mountains, happens upon the scene, kills the perpetrator, and rescues the sole survivor—a village girl named Yoriko. Later, after retiring, Misawa adopts Yoriko and works as an insurance salesperson. One day, he rescues a female journalist named Tomoko from an attacker, but she is being targeted because she tried to expose the corruption of a local businessman, Oba. Meanwhile, Detective Kitano, who suspects Misawa of being the massacre killer, continues to shadow him.
title_norm:野火: An anti-war film adapted from Shōhei Ōoka's novel of the same name, scripted by Kazuo Wada and directed by Kon Ichikawa. Abandoned by both the hospital and his unit, Tamura wanders the island of Leyte on the Philippine front. He reunites with fellow retreating soldiers in front of a hospital, but when the hospital comes under shelling, Tamura flees alone. With no food and having lost his comrades, Tamura survives by eating grass. Eventually he reunites with his former comrades Nagamatsu and Yasuda, who had been separated from him. The two call the soldiers they killed 'monkeys' and have been eating their flesh...
title_norm:金子文子 何が私をこうさせたか: This biographical drama centers on Fumiko Kaneko, a nihilist and anarchist who fiercely resisted Japan's state power about 100 years ago, depicting the 121 days from her death sentence to her suicide in prison. Directed by female filmmaker Sachi Hamano (known for "Yukiko-san no Ashioto"), the film draws on tanka poems that convey Kaneko's own voice to portray her solitary struggle. Born in 1903, Kaneko grew up as a "non-registered person" because her father never filed her birth registration. At age nine, she was sent to live with her grandmother and aunt in Korea, where she suffered abuse akin to slavery from a family that exploited the colonized Korean villagers. In 1919, she witnessed the March First Independence Movement in Korea. Sent back to her mother's home in Yamanashi at 16, she later struggled through poverty in Tokyo, moving ideologically from Christianity to socialism, anarchism, and finally nihilism. She eventually met Park Yeol, a Korean independence activist who had fled to Japan. Becoming comrades and lovers, they campaigned against Japanese imperialism and colonialism, but were arrested during the 1923 Great Kanto Earthquake and sentenced to death. After her sentence was commuted to life imprisonment through amnesty, Kaneko was sent to Tochigi Women's Prison, where she continued her solitary fight behind bars. Nanana stars as Kaneko, embodying the soulful cry of a woman who defied state power to the end. Katsuya Kobayashi plays Park Yeol, with supporting performances by Masaki Miura, Yoko Horaguchi, and Kazuko Yoshiyuki.
title_norm:鉄コン筋クリート: Based on the popular manga by Taiyo Matsumoto serialized in 'Big Spirits' magazine from 1993 to 1994, this anime film adaptation is directed by Michael Arias, a VFX specialist active in Hollywood known for 'The Animatrix'. Set in the 'Treasure Town' of duty and human emotion, it depicts the exploits of two boys, Kuro and Shiro, who fly freely through the city. The voice cast includes Kazunari Ninomiya, who made his overseas debut in Clint Eastwood's 'Letters from Iwo Jima', and Yu Aoi from 'Hula Girls'.
title_norm:銀河鉄道999: The first theatrical film in the classic sci-fi anime series "Galaxy Express 999," based on Leiji Matsumoto's manga of the same name. Based on the "Andromeda Arc" from the original manga, it features character designs different from the TV series. In a future where humans can achieve eternal life by replacing their bodies with machines, the mechanical bodies are expensive and unaffordable for the poor. Rumors spread that riding the Galaxy Express 999 can take you to a planet where you can get a free mechanical body. The boy Tetsurō Hoshino heads to the metropolis Megalopolis, where the 999 stops, with his mother, but they are attacked by the Mechanical Count's human hunt, and his mother is killed. Living in the slums of Megalopolis, Tetsurō one day receives a pass for the 999 from the mysterious beauty Maetel and embarks on a journey into space with her. The theme song by Godiego was also a huge hit.
title_norm:鍵: A bold, original film adaptation of Junichiro Tanizaki's novel 'The Key', which explores the depths of sexuality through the alternating diaries of a married couple. Starring Mitsuru Fukikoshi, it lays bare a dying man's obsessive attachment and pure love for his younger wife. Kenzo Kenmochi, who runs a construction company, is told by his doctor he has only six months to live. Worried about his much younger wife Ikuko, he schemes to push her into an affair with his subordinate Kimura. As Kimura and Ikuko grow closer, things go according to plan, but Kenzo cannot let go of his feelings for Ikuko. Despite his physical decline, his jealousy intensifies. When he secretly reads Ikuko's diary, he finds her feelings of strong attraction to Kimura's body. Mitsuru Fukikoshi humorously plays the clumsy, jealousy-consumed Kenzo. Kei Kanno plays his wife Ikuko, and Keisuke Koide plays Kimura. The film is directed and written by Shinji Imaoka, known for scripting 'The Zombie Child' and directing 'Reiko and the Dolphin', with Minoru Matsumoto co-writing the screenplay.
title_norm:長江七號: Ti, who lost his wife to illness, works at a construction site to send his only son Dicky to a prestigious private elementary school. While retrieving a pair of sneakers Dicky wanted from the garbage dump, Ti finds a green ball. Dicky begins keeping the creature (or is it an object of unknown nature?) that is born from the ball Ti brought home, naming it Miracle 7.
title_norm:長靴をはいたネコ ８０日間世界一周: Péro, a restaurant waiter in a certain town, gets into an argument with the arrogant Lord Groumon and makes a bet: "I'll travel around the world in eighty days. If I fail, I'll become Groumon's slave." Pursued by time, Péro continues his arduous journey with a father-and-son mouse duo and Carter, the restaurant's cook, but is obstructed by Dr. Garigari, Lord Groumon's henchman, and the mysterious beauty Susanna.
title_norm:長靴をはいた猫: Hundreds of years ago, in a certain country, lived a kind-hearted boy named Pierre and a brave cat named Pero who wore boots. Pierre was raised in a wealthy home, but after his father died, his greedy brothers, after his inheritance, drove him out. Pero was ostracized after helping a mouse. They became friends while taking shelter from the rain at the same farm one rainy day and decided to travel together. Crossing fields, mountains, rivers, and lakes, they arrived at a castle where Pierre was delighted to see a wonderful notice. It stated that the richest and most valiant young man in the world would become Princess Rosa's husband. However, princes and knights from all over the world flocked there, using every means to win the princess's favor, and even the demon king Lucifer tried to become her husband using his magic. But when Rosa refused his proposal, he turned the castle into ruins, transformed the king into a pig, and left, saying he would return for the princess on the night of the full moon. Sneaking into the hall and witnessing everything, Pero realized that if they defeated the demon king, Pierre would become the bridegroom. Around that time, Pero rescued a lost baby mouse. Grateful, the mice became Pero's loyal servants and helped him, allowing Pierre to meet the princess. On the night of the full moon, Pierre revealed his true identity, and the princess was captivated by this pure and gallant young man, but she was taken away by the demon king who appeared exactly on time. Pierre, along with Pero and the mouse servants, went to the demon king's castle. The demon king was in high spirits at his wedding feast with the princess. Flattered by Pero's compliments, he showed off by transforming into various animals. But when the demon king realized Pierre and the others were after his magic pendant, he trapped them in a cave. The princess, bargaining for everyone's lives by agreeing to become the demon king's queen, seized a moment to grab the pendant and throw it into the cave. Pierre escaped to the castle tower and held the pendant high. At that moment, the sun rose from behind the mountains, and the pursuing demon king disintegrated along with the castle. Thus, in the castle restored to peace, Pierre and the princess were wed, and they lived happily ever after with Pero.
title_norm:長靴をはいた猫 80日間世界一周: Péro, a restaurant waiter in a certain town, gets into an argument with the arrogant Lord Groumon and makes a bet: "I'll travel around the world in eighty days. If I fail, I'll become Groumon's slave." Pursued by time, Péro continues his arduous journey with a father-and-son mouse duo and Carter, the restaurant's cook, but is obstructed by Dr. Garigari, Lord Groumon's henchman, and the mysterious beauty Susanna.
title_norm:開戦前夜: Four months before the attack on Pearl Harbor—what they saw was the conclusion: 'Japan's inevitable defeat.' In April 1941, there existed an organization called the 'Total War Research Institute,' where elites from across Japan were secretly gathered. The 'best and brightest' of the next generation, selected from bureaucrats, the military, and the private sector, were tasked with 'predicting' the outcome of a war with the United States and other foreign powers. After accumulating vast amounts of data and repeatedly running simulations with anguish and passion, what they saw was a shocking scenario of Japan's 'overwhelming defeat'—one that predicted almost everything except the atomic bombings. Not a single bullet is fired. But here lies the harshest battlefield, where the mind is the weapon. Why did Japan charge into a war it knew it would lose? Now, the 'inconvenient truth' buried in history bares its fangs on the screen.
title_norm:阿飛正傳: Director Wong Kar-wai's second feature film from 1990, this youth ensemble drama depicts the romantic entanglements of young people in 1960s Hong Kong with a sense of rushing visual beauty, catapulting Wong Kar-wai to international fame. Yuddy approaches Su, who works as a vendor at a soccer stadium, and they fall in love. However, Yuddy is troubled by not knowing his biological mother. After breaking up with Su, Yuddy spends a night with Mimi, a dancer at a nightclub. Leaving the room, Mimi encounters Yuddy's best friend Zeb, who falls in love with her at first sight. Tide, a policeman on night patrol, has feelings for Su, but she cannot forget Yuddy. The cast features Hong Kong cinema's biggest stars, including Leslie Cheung, Maggie Cheung, Carina Lau, Tony Leung, Andy Lau, and Jacky Cheung. First released in Japan in 1992. A digital remastered version was released in February 2018 at Bunkamura Le Cinema and other venues. A 4K restored version was released in December 2023 as part of the special screening "Wong Kar-wai: The Beginning."
title_norm:隣人たち: In 1960s America, best friends Celine and Alice live next door to each other in a suburban neighborhood. Both come from wealthy families and each has an only son the same age, living a perfect, happy life. But one day, Celine's son is involved in a tragic accident, and their relationship changes completely. Consumed by loss, Celine gradually begins to grow close to Alice's son, Theo. Alice starts to grow suspicious. Is she trying to take my family away? Or is it all just a misunderstanding... Alice's behavior escalates step by step, and soon both women are swallowed into a vortex of madness and delusion.
title_norm:雨月物語: Commentary: In an age of war, men driven by lust chase illusions even at the cost of sacrificing women... Based on a classic tale of the supernatural, this masterpiece reflects the folly of humans deluded by desire, suspended between reality and fantasy. Winner of the Silver Lion at the Venice Film Festival, it spread Mizoguchi's name worldwide.
title_norm:雪之丞変化: This adaptation of the same-named period novel by Otaguro Mikami was scripted by Daisuke Ito and Teinosuke Kinugasa, with a screenplay by Natsuto Wada, and directed by Kon Ichikawa. Kazuo Hasegawa, who starred in the 1935 version, again plays the dual roles of Yukinojo Nakamura and Yami Taro. The cast also includes Fujiko Yamamoto, Ayako Wakao, Raizo Ichikawa, and Shintaro Katsu, among other luminaries. This film commemorates Hasegawa's 300th appearance. In Edo, Yukinojo Nakamura, a female-role actor of Kamigata kabuki performing in the city, spots Sanzai Tsuchibe and Kaimiya, the men who framed his father on false charges and drove him to suicide. Sanzai's daughter, Namiji, falls in love with Yukinojo, and he uses her to avenge his father. Kawaguchiya, who had been hoarding rice during the Edo famine, is thwarted by Kaimiya—instigated by Yukinojo—and goes bankrupt, after which Kaimiya sets fire to his shop. Enraged, Kaimiya strangles Kawaguchiya but is stabbed by Namiji, whom he had tried to abduct.
title_norm:雲と大地のはざまで: A Peruvian film that, through the eyes of a boy living under the vast Andes Mountains caring for alpacas, depicts the prayers embedded in the lives of the people there and the conflict surrounding mining development. In a small Peruvian village surrounded by the majestic Andes Mountains over 4,000 meters high, 8-year-old Feliciano makes it his daily routine to take his alpacas grazing with his loyal dog Rambo. His family makes a living by shearing and selling the wool from the alpacas they care for. In the year before the FIFA World Cup, Feliciano dreams of the Peruvian national team qualifying and advancing to the finals in Russia, listening excitedly to radio broadcasts. He believes this peaceful daily life will last forever, but soon a conflict arises between the villagers and mining companies threatening nature, and one day a major incident engulfs the entire village. Around the same time, a young alpaca named Ronaldo, whom Feliciano especially adored, disappears. The director is Franco García Becerra, for whom this is his second feature film. The role of the protagonist Feliciano is played by Alberto Merma, selected through open auditions and workshops. The film won the Special Prize in the Generation Kplus section and the Special Jury Prize in the Ibero-American Film section at the 74th Berlin International Film Festival in 2024.
title_norm:雲のむこう、約束の場所: Makoto Shinkai, who rose to prominence with his fully digital personal animation "Voices of a Distant Star" in 2002, makes his feature-length directorial debut. Set in post-war Japan divided north and south by the Tsugaru Strait, it depicts boys struggling to save a girl burdened with the world's mysteries. In Japan under US military rule, middle school students Hiroki Fujisawa and Takuya Shirakawa in Aomori admire a giant tower standing across the strait in Hokkaido, and secretly work on assembling an airplane at an abandoned station site, dreaming of one day reaching that tower. One summer vacation, they confide their airplane secret to their classmate Sayuri Sawatari, another object of their admiration. The three share the dream of reaching the tower together, enjoying a brief period of happiness, but in the summer of their third year of middle school, Sayuri transfers away without explanation. The dream of reaching the tower by plane fades, and three years pass. Hiroki and Takuya, having gone their separate ways, reunite when dark clouds gather over the world situation and the tower's secrets gradually come to light. Voice cast includes actors Hidetaka Yoshioka and Masato Hagiwara.
title_norm:雲のむこう、約束の場所 the place promise: Makoto Shinkai, who rose to prominence with his fully digital personal animation "Voices of a Distant Star" in 2002, makes his feature-length directorial debut.
