title_norm:霧のごとく: Directed by Taiwan's Yu-Hsun Chen, known for "The Girl Who Leapt Through Time" and "The Tropical Fish," this is a story of hope and rebirth set against the backdrop of the "White Terror" era in 1950s Taiwan, when many citizens were arrested and executed on suspicion of being anti-government. In the 1950s, under martial law in Taiwan. A young girl named A-Yue, living in Chiayi, learns that her brother, captured as an anti-government element, has been executed in Taipei. With a small amount of money and her brother's keepsake watch in hand, she heads to Taipei alone, only to find that a hefty fee is required to claim his body. At her wit's end, she is tricked by a suspicious man and nearly sold into a brothel, but is rescued by a rickshaw puller named Zhao Gongdao. Originally from Guangdong, China, he came to Taiwan as a soldier for the Nationalist army and has been unable to return home, living hand-to-mouth ever since. Having lost his army comrades to the White Terror and finding no direction in life, Gongdao is moved by A-Yue's determination and decides to lend her a hand. Caitlin Fang ("A Girl from America") plays A-Yue, Will Or ("The Staggering Girl") plays Zhao Gongdao, and popular Taiwanese singer and actor 9m88 co-stars. The film won four awards, including Best Feature Film, at the 62nd Golden Horse Awards in 2025.
title_norm:霸王别姬: An epic saga depicting the tumultuous lives of two Peking opera actors, this was the first Chinese-language film to win the Palme d'Or at the Cannes Film Festival. It portrays the love, hatred, and lives of two Peking opera performers who play the classic 'Farewell My Concubine,' set against the backdrop of China's turbulent history from 1925 under the Nationalist government through the Cultural Revolution and into the late 1970s. Directed by Chen Kaige, who gained attention with his debut 'Yellow Earth' and became a leading figure of China's Fifth Generation directors with this film's success. In 1925 Beijing, Douzi, abandoned by his prostitute mother, is sent to a Peking opera training school. Shitou protects him like a younger brother and becomes his strong support through harsh training. As they grow up, they become major stars in the Peking opera world... Leslie Cheung plays Cheng Dieyi, a male dan actor who clings to love despite being tossed by the times, and Gong Li appears as a high-class courtesan who becomes his love rival. A 4K version was released in 2023, marking the 30th anniversary of the film's production and 20 years after Leslie Cheung's death.
title_norm:青い春: At an all-boys high school. Kyujo (Ryuhei Matsuda) and his five friends, now third-years in the new term, stand outside the railing on the rooftop, playing the 'Balcony Game'—competing to see who can clap the most times before falling. Kyujo sets a new record in this game, where failure means a straight drop to the schoolyard, and as the winner, gains the right to rule the school. But for him, both the 'game' and 'ruling the school' are meaningless and trivial. As Kyujo and the others drift through their aimless days, lost about where they belong, the reality of choosing their future paths is eventually thrust upon them...
title_norm:青春残酷物語: High school girls Makoto and Yoko always hitch rides home from town with men who have cars, getting them to drive them home. But one day, a middle-aged man in a foreign car tries to take Makoto to a hotel. A college student named Kiyoshi appears, knocks the man down, and saves Makoto, but their encounter leads them toward destruction... The shocking intensity of the love scenes and raw depictions gave rise to the term 'Shochiku Nouvelle Vague,' and this second feature film by director Nagisa Oshima was a huge box office hit.
title_norm:青髭8人目の妻: At a department store in the French resort of Riviera, American businessman Michael Brandon (Gary Cooper) insists on buying only the top half of a pair of pajamas. Conveniently appearing to take just the bottoms is Nicole (Claudette Colbert), the daughter of a poor aristocrat. Instantly smitten by her spirited nature, Brandon pursues her relentlessly and secures an engagement. However, on their wedding day, Nicole discovers Brandon has been married seven times and flies into a rage. They manage to marry only on the condition that Brandon pays Nicole a huge alimony if they divorce. Naturally, the relationship fails, and frustrated by his wife's indifference, Brandon resorts to a desperate measure.
title_norm:青髭八人目の妻: At a department store in the French resort of Riviera, American businessman Michael Brandon (Gary Cooper) insists on buying only the top half of a pair of pajamas. Conveniently appearing to take just the bottoms is Nicole (Claudette Colbert), the daughter of a poor aristocrat. Instantly smitten by her spirited nature, Brandon pursues her relentlessly and secures an engagement. However, on their wedding day, Nicole discovers Brandon has been married seven times and flies into a rage. They manage to marry only on the condition that Brandon pays Nicole a huge alimony if they divorce. Naturally, the relationship fails, and frustrated by his wife's indifference, Brandon resorts to a desperate measure.
title_norm:響け！情熱のムリダンガム: A youth music film about a young man's struggle to become a player of the mridangam, a traditional Indian percussion instrument. Peter, the son of a mridangam craftsman living in Chennai, India, is inspired to become a player himself after seeing a master perform on a mridangam his father made. Apprenticing under the master and training diligently, Peter faces various challenges including caste discrimination, conflicts over preserving traditional arts, and generational differences, but confronts them with passion and respect. The music is composed by A. R. Rahman, who won an Academy Award for 'Slumdog Millionaire.' G. V. Prakash Kumar, Rahman's nephew and a renowned film music composer, plays the protagonist Peter. Screened under the title 'The World Is Full of Rhythms' in the World Focus section of the 31st Tokyo International Film Festival in 2018. For its theatrical release in October 2022, the film was distributed by 'Nandori,' a South Indian restaurant in Tokyo's Arakawa Ward that fell in love with the film.
title_norm:風たちの午後: Mitsu's birthday. Natsuko buys matching Virgo necklaces and a rose. However, a white handkerchief is hanging in the apartment window. It's the signal that Mitsu's lover, Hideo, is there. Natsuko, who has secretly fallen in love with Mitsu, approaches Hideo in order to have Mitsu all to herself... On a midsummer afternoon, a shocking ending that will shake the world.
title_norm:風と女と旅鴉: Ginji, driven from his hometown, returns after ten years... This is a representative work marking the starting point of Tai Kato's unique style, with actors wearing no makeup, low-angle cameras, and simultaneous sound recording.
title_norm:風の武士: A samurai yet not a samurai! A shogunate spy who sniffs out darkness and delivers death—he is the Wind Samurai. This suspenseful ninja romance by Ryotaro Shiba weaves together the strange fate and love of Shinzo and Miki, caught in a conspiracy surrounding the phantom land of "Arai" in the Kumano mountains. Sleeping gold, a princess's love, and approaching evil swords! Director Takashi Kato, with ace star Hashizo Okawa, crafts a thrilling ninja suspense epic, connecting Edo and the wilderness with swords and romance.
title_norm:風琴 あるリードオルガン修復家のあしあと: A documentary following Teruo Wakui, a restorer of reed organs. Once a common sight in school classrooms, these wooden reed organs (pump organs) were known as "fukin" (wind instruments) during the Meiji era. By pumping the foot pedals, an airflow is created, causing air to vibrate small metal pieces called reeds inside the instrument to produce sound. Imported from Europe and the United States in the late 19th century, they were eventually produced by numerous Japanese manufacturers as well. They became a staple not only in churches and schools but also in private homes during the mid-Showa period. Today, however, there are no manufacturers left in the world that produce reed organs. Teruo Wakui, a tuner and restorer living in Nagano Prefecture, is one of the few individuals capable of repairing and maintaining these complex instruments. He is involved in the restoration of organs from both Japan and abroad, including historically significant masterpieces. This film follows Wakui’s restoration projects across Japan while exploring the history of the reed organ and the various people who sustain its enduring charm.
title_norm:風船の行方:
A 2006 short film by director Ken Nishiyasu, whose works—produced in a signature style where he handles everything from production and screenwriting to editing and cinematography—have been screened at various film festivals. This human drama focuses on a mother and daughter, depicting the subtle nuances of their fluctuating emotions through delicate direction.

In a family restaurant at night, Michiko and her daughter, Mana, sit facing each other. Having raised her daughter alone while overwhelmed by the demands of daily life, Michiko carries a deep sense of fatigue and loneliness. Eventually, these emotions are directed toward Mana, and she impulsively leaves the restaurant.

The film was released theatrically as part of "The Ken Nishiyasu Short Film Special," a triple feature showcasing three of his works: *To-chan*, *Buri no Omisoka*, and *Fusen no Yukue*.
title_norm:香港四徑大步走: The Hong Kong Four Trails Ultra Challenge, commonly known as HK4TUC, requires runners to consecutively complete four trail courses in Hong Kong and reach the finish line within a time limit of 72 hours (3 days). The total course length is 298 km, comparable to the distance between Tokyo and Nagoya, with a cumulative elevation gain of 14,500 m, equivalent to seven full marathons or two ascents of Mount Everest. Furthermore, participants must procure their own water and food from shops along the way, and strict rules prohibit the use of poles or portable music players, which would be advantageous on the undulating mountain paths. It is an event of extreme physical and mental challenge. This film captures 18 runners who took on the HK4TUC pushing their limits, set against the beautiful natural landscapes of Hong Kong, rarely seen before. The director is Robin Lee, a British director born and raised in Hong Kong. The film began a limited release in Hong Kong at the end of 2024, but word-of-mouth spread rapidly and the number of screens increased sharply. It gained further attention when the major star Chow Yun-fat, known for the 'A Better Tomorrow' series and 'Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon', highly praised it, saying 'every Hong Kong person should watch it'. Supported not only by sports enthusiasts but also by general film fans, it became the biggest surprise hit of 2025, attracting 150,000 viewers. Additionally, it has won numerous awards, including the Best New Director Award at the 43rd Hong Kong Film Awards, the Audience Award at the 22nd Hong Kong Asian Film Festival, the Recommended Film Award at the 31st Hong Kong Film Critics Society Awards, and the Jury Special Award at the 2025 Hong Kong Directors' Guild Awards, earning high praise as a documentary.
title_norm:香港四徑大歩走 英題：four trails: A surprise smash hit that ranked in Hong Kong's box office top ten for eight weeks! Highly praised by Chow Yun-fat ("A Better Tomorrow" series)! An unimaginably grueling drama about runners! The Hong Kong Four Trails Ultra Challenge, commonly known as HK4TUC, requires runners to consecutively complete four trail courses in Hong Kong and reach the finish line within a time limit of 72 hours (3 days). The total course length is 298 km, comparable to the distance between Tokyo and Nagoya, with a cumulative elevation gain of 14,500 m, equivalent to seven full marathons or two ascents of Mount Everest. Furthermore, runners must procure their own water and food from shops along the way, and strict rules prohibit the use of poles (advantageous on undulating mountain paths) and portable music players, making it an event of extreme physical and mental hardship. This film captures 18 runners competing in the HK4TUC as they push their limits, set against the beautiful natural landscapes of Hong Kong rarely seen before.
title_norm:骨までしゃぶる: In the late Meiji period, a poor farmer's daughter is sold as a prostitute to the Suzaki pleasure quarters. A fierce masterpiece of women's cinema by Tai Kato, depicting the sorrow and resilience of women exploited to the bone.
title_norm:骨を掘る男: A documentary following Ryusho Gushiken, who has spent over 40 years collecting the remains of those who died in the Battle of Okinawa. It is said that nearly 3,000 sets of remains—of local residents, former Japanese soldiers, American soldiers, and people from the Korean Peninsula and Taiwan—still lie in southern Okinawa Island, the site of fierce fighting. Gushiken, now 70, began collecting remains at age 28 and has found approximately 400 sets. From fragments he gathers—crushed and scattered small bones, pieces of teacups, shrapnel, and traces of flamethrowers—he infers whether the remains are those of soldiers or civilians, how they met their end, and offers his thoughts and prayers. Film director Katsuya Okuma, who himself lost a great-aunt in the Battle of Okinawa, accompanies Gushiken on his collection efforts, searching for traces of his great-aunt's life. Interweaving archival footage of the Battle of Okinawa, the film illuminates Okinawa's history and present.
title_norm:魁!! 男塾: Depicts the extreme training and battles at 'Otokojuku,' a school that raises men among men. Invited to the 'Big Battle August' tournament where representatives from around the world compete for supremacy during summer vacation, the first-year students fight their way through Hawaii, Niagara Falls, Alaska, and New York, culminating in a decisive battle against the American team. The appeal lies in the massive physiques and dynamic storytelling.
title_norm:魁!!男塾: Depicts the extreme training and battles at 'Otokojuku,' a school that raises men among men. Invited to the 'Big Battle August' tournament where representatives from around the world compete for supremacy during summer vacation, the first-year students fight their way through Hawaii, Niagara Falls, Alaska, and New York, culminating in a decisive battle against the American team. The appeal lies in the massive physiques and dynamic storytelling.
title_norm:鯨が消えた入り江: A road movie set in Hong Kong and Taiwan, depicting a midsummer miracle connected by a single letter. Against the beautiful, shimmering landscapes of Taiwan, it portrays a time-spanning bond between a wounded writer and a lonely young man. Tianyu, a popular Hong Kong writer, faces fierce public backlash after accusations of plagiarism. Deeply hurt, he travels alone to Taiwan in search of the 'Whale's Vanished Cove,' a place said to lead to heaven, which a boy he once corresponded with told him about. After being cheated in an unfamiliar country and getting drunk in the bustling streets of Taipei, Tianyu is helped by Ashang, a local thug. When Tianyu reveals the purpose of his journey, Ashang, claiming to know the 'Whale's Vanished Cove,' offers to take him there, and their summer journey begins... Terence Lau, known for 'Twilight Warriors: Final Battle in the Kowloon Walled City,' delicately portrays the gentle and pure writer Tianyu, while Fandy Fan, from 'Destiny Matchup,' co-stars as the thug Ashang.
title_norm:鰤の大晦日:
A 2014 short film by director Ken Nishioka, who built his filmmaking career in the United States and has had his independent works screened at festivals both in Japan and abroad. This slice-of-life drama, set amidst the frantic atmosphere of the year-end, explores a couple's relationship and their sense of distance from those around them.

New Year's Eve in Tokyo. Shiho and her husband Junpei receive a whole yellowtail as a year-end gift, but they are at a loss as to how to handle it, unable to fillet the fish themselves. As they contact friends and acquaintances to find someone to take it, they not only struggle to find a recipient but also face insensitive remarks about their lack of children. Carrying a sense of displacement, Shiho remembers an uncle she has long been estranged from and heads out into the city with her husband.

The film won the Encouragement Award at the 16th Nagaoka Indie Movie Competition and was an official selection at the 9th Sapporo International Short Film Festival. It was released theatrically as part of the "Ken Nishioka Short Film Special," a triple feature including *Tochan*, *Yellowtail New Year's Eve*, and *Where the Balloon Goes*.
title_norm:麗しのサブリナ: A romantic comedy directed by Billy Wilder, starring Audrey Hepburn in the year following "Roman Holiday." Sabrina, the daughter of a chauffeur serving the wealthy Larrabee family, falls in love with the family's younger son. To make her forget this hopeless love, her father and fellow servants send Sabrina to Paris. Two years later, Sabrina returns as a refined lady, and her transformation is so complete that the younger son and his brother fail to recognize her as the chauffeur's daughter. In 2013, a digitally remastered version was released as part of the special screening series "Screen Beauties Vol. 1: Audrey Hepburn."
title_norm:麻雀放浪記: In Ueno just after Japan's defeat in the war. One day, a young man named Tetsu unexpectedly runs into Joshu Tora, who once taught him how to gamble. Led by Tora into the Chinchiro slums, Tetsu bets his last bit of money on a game run by Dosa Ken, a professional gambler. He wins a considerable amount, but most of it is taken by Dosa Ken as a coaching fee.
title_norm:黒い十人の女: A black comedy directed by Kon Ichikawa and scripted by Natto Wada, weaving together a philandering man, his wife, and nine lovers. TV producer Matsukichi Kazama, despite having a beautiful wife named Futaba, is cheating with nine women. The wife and lovers are vaguely aware of each other's existence and fully know that Matsukichi is a womanizer, yet for some reason they cannot leave him. One day, the wife and a stage actress lover named Ichiko come up with a plan to kill Matsukichi. It is a fictional scheme meant to vent their frustration with him, but timid Matsukichi becomes convinced that his lovers are trying to kill him and consults his wife. The wife readily admits to the plan and then, to eliminate the lovers, suggests staging a fake murder: they gather the lovers for a meeting to denounce Matsukichi, and at that gathering, pretend to shoot him dead with a pistol.
title_norm:黒い家: Director Morita Yoshimitsu, known for '39 Criminal Law Article 39,' adapts the novel of the same name by Kishi Yusuke, which won the 4th Japan Horror Novel Award. Wakatsuki Shinji, who works at an insurance company, encounters the hanged body of a woman's son when he visits her home to explain insurance payouts. The police rule it a suicide, and the insurance money is paid out accordingly. However, sensing something suspicious in the parents' attitude, Wakatsuki begins his own investigation, doubting the suicide verdict. Gradually, the couple's abnormal behavior concerning the insurance money comes to light.
title_norm:黒い雨: Shizuma Shigematsu, living with his family in a village near Fukuyama City, was in Hiroshima with his wife and niece. The atomic bombing was a tragedy that mercilessly took the lives of thousands and forever etched the harsh existence of the survivors.
title_norm:黒の牛: A visual poem co-produced by Japan, Taiwan, and the United States, inspired by the "Ten Ox Herding Pictures," which depict the path to enlightenment in Zen using ten images of oxen. Directed and written by Tetsuichiro Tsuta, who gained domestic and international attention for "The Ravine of Goodbye," the film took eight years to complete. A hunter, forced to wander as he loses his mountain home in a rapidly changing era, encounters a majestic black ox in the mountains. He forcibly brings the resisting ox back and begins living with it in a remote house. The man and the ox till the land to survive, but they cannot see eye to eye in the face of nature's fury. However, an encounter with a Zen monk gradually brings the man and the ox to understand each other. Taiwanese acclaimed actor Lee Kang-sheng, known for his frequent roles in Tsai Ming-liang's films like "Stray Dogs," stars, with dancer Min Tanaka, also active as an actor, co-starring as the Zen monk. The entire film was shot on film, with some portions using 70mm film, a first for a Japanese feature film. The music uses compositions by Ryuichi Sakamoto, who had expressed his intention to participate in the project before his death. After its premiere at the "Asian Future" section of the 37th Tokyo International Film Festival in 2024, it won the top prize, the Firebird Award, at the 49th Hong Kong International Film Festival in 2025.
title_norm:黒川の女たち: A documentary that investigates the reality of sexual violence euphemistically called "entertainment" inflicted on the women of the Kurokawa settlement group in Manchuria during wartime. As part of the Japanese government's national policy in the 1930s-40s, the Manchuria-Mongolia settlement groups were sent from across Japan to Manchuria, China. As Japan's defeat became imminent, the Soviet army invaded Manchuria in August 1945, plunging the settlers into dire circumstances. To survive and return to Japan, the Kurokawa settlement group from Gifu Prefecture offered 15 women aged 18 and older (by traditional count) as sexual partners to the enemy Soviet army in exchange for help. After returning to Japan, the women faced discrimination and prejudice. Their voices, physically and mentally scarred, were silenced, and the truth was concealed for many years. However, about 70 years after the war, in 2013, the women of Kurokawa joined hands and began to speak publicly about the layers of harm they suffered. Director Fumie Matsubara, known for "Hama no Don," carefully weaves together these women's oral stories. Actress Shinobu Otake provides narration.
title_norm:黒牢城: Acclaimed director Kiyoshi Kurosawa ("Wife of a Spy," "Creepy") takes on his first period film, adapting the mystery novel of the same name by Honobu Yonezawa, which won both the 166th Naoki Prize and the 12th Yamaneko Prize. Murashige Araki rebels against Nobunaga Oda's tyrannical methods and holes up in Arioka Castle. Surrounded by the Oda army and isolated, Murashige struggles to control his hot-blooded retainers while relying on his wife, Chiyo, for emotional support, striving to protect the castle and its people. Amidst this, a boy is murdered inside the castle, followed by a series of strange incidents. With the suspects being the retainers and family members trapped inside the sealed-off castle, and the enemy outside, everyone falls into suspicion and paranoia. Cornered, Murashige seeks help from the genius military strategist Kanbei Kuroda, who was imprisoned after being sent as Nobunaga's envoy to persuade him, and sets out to solve the case. Starring Masahiro Motoki as Lord Murashige Araki, Masaki Suda as the genius strategist Kanbei Kuroda, Yuriko Yoshitaka as Murashige's wife Chiyo, Takao Aoki as Murashige's trusted retainer Kyusaemon Araki, Ryota Miyate (Snow Man) as the young retainer Saburo Inui, Tasuku Emoto as the skilled sniper Sagari Saika who witnesses the events, and Joe Odagiri as Juemon Kori, who operates in the shadows as Murashige's hidden blade. The film was selected for the Cannes Premiere section at the 79th Cannes Film Festival in 2026.
title_norm:點五步: In 1984, Hong Kong before the handover to China. In the suburban new town of Sha Tin, the first youth baseball team in Hong Kong, the 'Sha Yan' team, is formed. In Hong Kong, where baseball is not a major sport, a group of underachieving boys with no baseball experience begin practicing with balls made of rolled-up newspapers, but in their first game, they suffer a crushing defeat against a Taiwanese elementary school team. Nevertheless, guided by their strict yet caring principal Law (played by Liu Kai-chi), the team members gradually grow, centered on the childhood friends—the introverted Lung (played by Lam Yiu-sing) and the impulsive but loyal Wai (played by Tony Wu). The final showdown against their arch-rivals, the Japan Buffaloes, becomes a stage for them to re-examine their 'past' and 'future'—a youth drama based on a true story, set in early 1980s Hong Kong, leaving a quiet resonance that is not reduced to the outcome of the sport.
title_norm:黴の花: An unconventional romance film starring Kim Jae-kyung, former leader of the South Korean girl group RAINBOW who now works as an actress. Based on the short story 'Flowers of Mold' by Ha Seong-nan, an award-winning author in Korean literary circles, the film depicts a woman who tries to understand others through 'trash,' the most private and defenseless traces of a person. Ji-su, who carries deep romantic trauma, secretly collects and files away other people's trash, believing that 'one's true self appears in what they throw away.' One day, she finds a trash bag that has been carefully sorted and discarded, and upon discovering it belongs to her neighbor, a man named U-je, she approaches him using fragmentary information gleaned from the trash. The two gradually open their hearts to each other, but one night, U-je witnesses Ji-su entering her apartment with a trash bag and discovers her secret. Kim Jae-kyung passionately portrays the protagonist Ji-su, who cannot trust others due to past relationship experiences, with Hyun-woo from the TV drama 'Law School' co-starring as the neighbor U-je. Directed by Sim Hye-jung, who gained attention for her previous work 'A Bedsore,' the film won the CGV Award and the Watcha's Pick Feature Film Award at the Jeonju International Film Festival 2023.
title_norm:그 자연이 네게 뭐라고 하니: Korean master Hong Sang-soo, a multiple award-winner at the Berlin and Cannes film festivals, humorously and realistically depicts the irreparable failures caused by alcohol in this home drama centered on a young poet who ends up spending a day with his girlfriend's family. When poet Dong-ha escorts his girlfriend Juni home, he runs into her father at the front door and unexpectedly spends the day with her family. Initially awkward, Dong-ha gradually grows closer to Juni's family as they show him around their home and neighborhood and engage in conversation. Eventually, at dinner with the family, he drinks as urged, becomes intoxicated, and an uncomfortable atmosphere settles over the table. Ha Seong-guk, who previously played poets in Hong Sang-soo's "The Woman Who Ran" and "In Front of Your Face," takes on the role of Dong-ha, marking his first lead role in a Hong Sang-soo film. The parents welcoming their daughter's boyfriend are played by Hong Sang-soo regulars and real-life couple Kwon Hae-hyo and Cho Yun-hee. Kang So-yi ("In Front of Your Face," "By the Stream") plays Juni, and Park Mi-so ("Introduction") plays Juni's older sister. The film was selected for the competition section of the 75th Berlin International Film Festival in 2025. It will be released in theaters in 2026 as the fifth installment of "Monthly Hong Sang-soo," a project screening new works for five consecutive months to commemorate the director's 30th debut anniversary.
title_norm:기생충: The fourth collaboration between director Bong Joon-ho ('Memories of Murder,' 'The Host,' 'Snowpiercer') and lead actor Song Kang-ho, this film won the Palme d'Or at the 72nd Cannes Film Festival in 2019, the first for a Korean film. It also garnered global attention by winning four awards at the 92nd Academy Awards, including Best Picture—the first for a foreign language film—as well as Best Director, Best Original Screenplay, and Best International Feature Film. The Kim family is all unemployed and living in poverty, scraping by day to day. One day, the eldest son, Ki-woo, goes to the lavish home of IT CEO Mr. Park for a tutoring job interview. Following him, his sister Ki-jeong also sets foot in the mansion. The encounter between these two families from opposite worlds accelerates into a tragicomedy beyond imagination at breakneck speed... Co-starring Lee Sun-kyun ('A Hard Day'), Cho Yeo-jeong ('The Concubine'), and Choi Woo-shik ('Train to Busan').
title_norm:너를 줍다: An unconventional romance film starring Kim Jae-kyung, former leader of the South Korean girl group RAINBOW who now works as an actress. Based on the short story 'Flowers of Mold' by Ha Seong-nan, an award-winning author in Korean literary circles, the film depicts a woman who tries to understand others through 'trash,' the most private and defenseless traces of a person. Ji-su, who carries deep romantic trauma, secretly collects and files away other people's trash, believing that 'one's true self appears in what they throw away.' One day, she finds a trash bag that has been carefully sorted and discarded, and upon discovering it belongs to her neighbor, a man named U-je, she approaches him using fragmentary information gleaned from the trash. The two gradually open their hearts to each other, but one night, U-je witnesses Ji-su entering her apartment with a trash bag and discovers her secret. Kim Jae-kyung passionately portrays the protagonist Ji-su, who cannot trust others due to past relationship experiences, with Hyun-woo from the TV drama 'Law School' co-starring as the neighbor U-je. Directed by Sim Hye-jung, who gained attention for her previous work 'A Bedsore,' the film won the CGV Award and the Watcha's Pick Feature Film Award at the Jeonju International Film Festival 2023.
title_norm:너와 나의 5분: Set in early 2000s South Korea, when Japanese pop culture was restricted, this coming-of-age drama tenderly follows a shy transfer student and a popular class president who bond over J-Pop. In 2001, Gyung-hwan transfers to a high school in Daegu, Korea's most conservative city. A huge fan of then-taboo Japanese music and anime, he secretly listens to Japanese songs on his MP3 player during lunch. Teased as an 'otaku' by classmates, he discovers that his deskmate, class president Jae-min, also secretly loves Japanese culture. Sharing earphones on the bus after school while listening to J-Pop, they gradually grow closer. One day, Gyung-hwan confesses a secret to Jae-min, but afterward, Jae-min's attitude suddenly changes. Making his feature debut, director Eom Ha-nul wrote the script based on his own teenage experiences as a fan of Japanese culture, weaving in diverse Japanese pop culture from the 1990s. Shim Hyun-seo, a child actor known for 'The King of Pigs', plays transfer student Gyung-hwan, and Hyun Woo-seok, from 'The School Nurse Files', plays class president Jae-min. Gong Min-jung ('Kim Ji-young: Born 1982') and Lee Dong-hwi ('The Roundup: Punishment') co-star.
title_norm:되살아나는 목소리: A documentary co-directed by Park Soo-nam, a second-generation Zainichi Korean filmmaker who turns 90 in 2025, and her daughter Park Ma-i, depicting the stories of the voiceless buried in history. Park Soo-nam, a second-generation Zainichi Korean born in Mie Prefecture in March 1935, gained attention for her correspondence with Lee Jin-woo, a second-generation Zainichi Korean juvenile death row inmate in the 1958 Komatsugawa Incident, published as "Sin, Death, and Love." She subsequently published collections of testimonies uncovering the voices of Zainichi Koreans forcibly conscripted under colonial rule and those exposed to the atomic bombs in Hiroshima and Nagasaki. Switching from pen to camera, she made her directorial debut in 1986 with the documentary "Another Hiroshima" about Korean A-bomb victims. She has since produced documentary works such as "Song of Ariran: Testimony from Okinawa," "Nuchigafu (Life's Blessing): Testimony from the Place of Mass Death," and "Silence: The Rising Comfort Women." This film refocuses on the realities and contemporary challenges of Korean A-bomb victims, a lifework for Park Soo-nam, and is based on 16mm film she has been shooting for about 40 years. It depicts the voiceless stories of Koreans affected by the atomic bombs in Hiroshima and Nagasaki, forced laborers taken to Nagasaki's Battleship Island (Gunkanjima), former Korean civilian employees in the Battle of Okinawa, and women forced into Japanese military sexual slavery.
title_norm:만약에 우리: Summer 2008, Seoul. University students Uno and Jeong-won meet fatefully on a long-distance bus. Uno, who dreams of becoming a game creator, and Jeong-won, who aspires to be an architect. Supporting each other through their urban days filled with dreams and anxieties, they eventually fall in love, deeply and truly. However, faced with the harshness of reality that youth cannot resist, they choose to part ways. Ten years later, in the summer of 2024, they coincidentally reunite on a flight to Seoul. As they look back on their memories, Uno asks Jeong-won a question he has kept buried deep in his heart: 'What if, back then...'
title_norm:만약에 우리／once we were us: Summer 2008, Seoul. University students Uno and Jeong-won meet fatefully on a long-distance bus. Uno, who dreams of becoming a game creator, and Jeong-won, who aspires to be an architect. Supporting each other through their urban days filled with dreams and anxieties, they eventually fall in love, deeply and truly. However, faced with the harshness of reality that youth cannot resist, they choose to part ways. Ten years later, in the summer of 2024, they coincidentally reunite on a flight to Seoul. As they look back on their memories, Uno asks Jeong-won a question he has kept buried deep in his heart: 'What if, back then...'
title_norm:박하사탕: A human drama that traces twenty years in the life of a man against the backdrop of modern Korean history, winning five major awards including Best Picture at the Grand Bell Awards, South Korea's equivalent of the Oscars. This is the second feature film by director Lee Chang-dong, made in 1999, known for "Oasis" and "Secret Sunshine." Spring, 1999. Kim Yeong-ho, at the depths of despair after losing his job and family, shows up at a picnic with old friends wearing an out-of-place suit. It is the same place he visited twenty years earlier with his first love, Sunim. Standing on the railroad tracks, Yeong-ho shouts "I want to go back!" at an oncoming train, and his life begins to rewind. We see his self-destructed marriage to his wife Hong-ja, his love for Sunim that drew them together but was never fulfilled, and the Gwangju Uprising he witnessed as a soldier. Yeong-ho's journey through memory eventually arrives at the time twenty years ago when his life was most beautiful and pure. The film was released in a 4K-restored digital remaster in 2019 to coincide with the release of Lee Chang-dong's "Burning." A 4K restoration was also screened in 2023 as part of the special retrospective "Lee Chang-dong Retrospective 4K."
title_norm:부산행: A Korean survival panic action film depicting the terror and chaos caused by the sudden outbreak of a mysterious virus spreading aboard a high-speed train connecting Seoul and Busan. Seok-woo, a fund manager working in Seoul, is separated from his wife and lives with his young daughter Su-an. Su-an insists on going alone to meet her mother in Busan for her birthday, and Seok-woo reluctantly agrees to escort her. They board the KTX high-speed train from Seoul to Busan, but just before departure, a suspicious commotion occurs near Seoul Station. A woman infected with the mysterious virus also boards KTX train 101, the same train as the father and daughter. Alongside the protagonist Seok-woo and his daughter, various passengers—a pregnant woman and her husband, high school baseball players, and a selfish middle-aged businessman—face a life-or-death struggle for survival in a state of extremity where being caught by the infected means certain death, and their individual human dramas unfold. This is the first live-action feature film by Yeon Sang-ho, a rising director who has garnered attention in the Korean animation scene, and the story preceding this film is revealed in the animated feature 'Seoul Station'.
title_norm:브로커: A road movie that won two awards at the 75th Cannes Film Festival, featuring a Korean production team and cast. Two male brokers who kidnap an infant from a 'baby hatch' and the mother who once abandoned her child. Bound by a strange sense of solidarity, they journey to find adoptive parents, quietly pursued by two female detectives. This film returns to Kore-eda's signature theme of 'quasi-family,' depicting certain hope beyond the moral dilemmas surrounding the salvation of unwanted lives.
title_norm:사랑만의 언어: A love story starring Sungmo and Jihyuk of the popular K-pop group "Supernova," set against the rich natural backdrop of Chuncheon City, also known as a filming location for "Winter Sonata." It depicts a young man who has lost his words meeting a loved one and finding hope to live again. Teo, a piano tuner with a speech disorder caused by aftereffects of brain tumor surgery, meets Inha, a former popular singer who has lost her sight due to retinitis pigmentosa and is recuperating in a small village in Chuncheon. Unable to speak, Teo plays the piano to accompany Inha's singing, which leads Inha to open her heart to him. However, Inha's ex-lover Romy appears to take her back, and Inha ends up returning to Seoul. The director is Han Sang-hee, who directed "First Snow's Love: Virgin Snow" starring Lee Joon-gi and Aoi Miyazaki.
title_norm:사잇소리: A Korean suspense thriller about floor noise and a cult religion, depicting the fate of a female writer who strives to uncover the truth behind the noise coming from the upstairs neighbor. Eun-su, an aspiring writer living in apartment 401, has been applying to numerous writing contests but faces a string of rejections. Meanwhile, for about a month, she has been tormented by unbearable noise coming from unit 501 above. Deciding to use this situation as material for her work, Eun-su, along with her friend Ji-seong, begins observing Ho-gyeong, a middle-aged man living in 501. Even after he notices her excessive stalking, she relentlessly pursues him for the sake of her writing. Eventually, Eun-su arrives at a shocking truth hidden behind the noise, but at the same time, she finds herself backed into a dangerous situation. Director Kim Jeong-uk, who has crafted many stories candidly depicting the human psyche, portrays with intense suspense the psychological anxiety born from trivial troubles lurking in daily life. Ryu Hwa-young, known as a former member of the K-pop group T-ARA, stars in her first lead film role, passionately playing Eun-su, a writer whose obsession with writing blurs the line between reality and delusion. Veteran actor Park Jin-woo, known for the Netflix drama "Squid Game," plays the mysterious upstairs resident Ho-gyeong.
title_norm:수유천: Korean master Hong Sang-soo directs an ensemble drama set at a women's university in Seoul, depicting the romantic entanglements of students and adults surrounding a theater festival. At a women's university in Seoul, with the theater festival approaching, textile artist Jon-hee, who works as a lecturer, invites her uncle Si-on, a famous actor and stage director, as a temporary director to fill a gap caused by a love scandal on campus. As they begin creating a short play for the festival, various events unfold over ten days, including the aftermath of the students' love affairs and the budding romance between a senior professor and Si-on. Actress Kim Min-hee, Hong Sang-soo's partner in both public and private life, stars as Jon-hee and won the Best Performance Award at the 77th Locarno International Film Festival in 2024. The cast also includes regulars from Hong Sang-soo's films: Kwon Hae-hyo as Jon-hee's uncle Si-on, Cho Yun-hee as the professor who admires Si-on, and Ha Seong-guk as the fired director who was dating three people. In Japan, it was screened under the title 'Suyuchon' at the 25th Tokyo Filmex in 2024. It was theatrically released in 2025 as the second film in the 'Monthly Hong Sang-soo' project, a series of five consecutive monthly new releases celebrating the director's 30th debut anniversary.
title_norm:아가씨: Directed by Park Chan-wook of 'Oldboy' fame, this suspense drama is based on Sarah Waters' novel 'Fingersmith' but transposed to 1930s Japanese-occupied Korea. Sook-hee, a girl raised by a gang of swindlers in a slum, is approached by a con man known as Count Fujiwara with a plan: seduce Lady Hideko, an heiress to a vast fortune, marry her, then commit her to an asylum and steal her wealth. Agreeing to take part, Sook-hee begins working as a maid named Ok-ju at a remote mansion where Hideko lives with her domineering, Japanophile uncle Kouzuki. But as devoted Sook-hee gradually opens Hideko's heart, Sook-hee herself finds herself drawn to the woman she is supposed to betray. Kim Min-hee plays Hideko, while newcomer Kim Tae-ri was cast as Sook-hee through auditions. Ha Jung-woo plays the Count, and Cho Jin-woong plays Uncle Kouzuki.
title_norm:악마가 이사왔다: A romantic comedy from director Lee Sang-geun, who previously scored a massive hit in Korea with 'EXIT' and reunites with Im Yoon-ah. It follows a woman possessed by a demon who shows completely different faces by day and night, and the kind-hearted young man who falls for her. On leave from work, Gil-gu falls in love at first sight with Seon-ji, a baker who moves in downstairs. But when he encounters her late that night, she is entirely different. Her father Jang-su explains that Seon-ji is gentle and bright by day, but at 2 AM a demon awakens, transforming her. Gil-gu agrees to Jang-su's odd request to watch over Seon-ji at night. She drags him out every night, running wild and selfishly bossing him around. Im Yoon-ah, a Girls' Generation member known for films like 'EXIT' and drama 'The King's Chef', plays Seon-ji. Ahn Bo-hyun, from the drama 'Spring Fever', plays Gil-gu. Song Dong-il, known for the 'Reply' series, plays Seon-ji's protective father Jang-su.
title_norm:어쩔수가없다: Korean master filmmaker Park Chan-wook, winner of the Grand Prix at Cannes for "Oldboy" and Best Director for "Decision to Leave," directs this suspense drama laced with irony and black humor about a salaryman whose life is turned upside down by a sudden layoff. Park reunites with Lee Byung-hun, who starred in his breakthrough film "Joint Security Area," for the first time in 21 years. Man-su, an ordinary salaryman at a paper company, lives with his wife, two children, and two dogs, believing he has everything he could want. But his life changes drastically when he is suddenly fired from the company he has worked for for 25 years. His job search drags on for over a year, and he is forced to sell his beloved home. Desperate, Man-su walks into a rapidly growing paper company with his resume, only to be flatly rejected. Convinced he is the most qualified person for the company, he makes a decision: if there's no opening, he'll have to create one himself. The film is based on the novel "The Ax" by Donald E. Westlake, which was also adapted into a film by Costa-Gavras. Lee Byung-hun plays the increasingly cornered Man-su, and Son Ye-jin of "Crash Landing on You" plays his wife Mi-ri, who grows stronger as the crisis deepens. The film was selected for the competition section of the 82nd Venice International Film Festival in 2025 and won the newly established International Audience Award (for non-North American films) at the 50th Toronto International Film Festival.
title_norm:올드보이: Oh Dae-su, a man living an ordinary life, regains consciousness to find himself locked in a small, confined room. After 15 years of imprisonment without knowing why, he is suddenly released. Who did this?! For what purpose?! With the help of a young woman named Mi-do, Dae-su vows revenge. A mysterious man named Woo-jin appears before him and proposes a deadly "game": Dae-su must uncover the reason for his imprisonment within five days, with both their lives at stake. An unimaginable and terrifying scheme lies behind it all...
title_norm:우리의 하루: The 30th feature film by Korean master Hong Sang-soo, who continues to release works in his unique style, distanced from large-scale commercial cinema. It depicts a day in the lives of a resting actor and an elderly poet living in seclusion, whose paths almost cross but never quite do. Sang-won, an actor on hiatus staying at a friend's house, and Hong Ui-ju, an elderly poet living alone in a small apartment, receive visits from young guests burdened with anxiety about the future, who ask various questions: What is necessary for acting? How does one become an actor or poet? Why did you start writing poetry? The topics the young people raise gradually develop into important conversations about life. Meanwhile, a friend's cat suddenly goes missing... Through two alternating locations and times, and the comedic dialogue that unfolds, the film discovers dramatic moments hidden in everyday life. Kim Min-hee, an indispensable presence in Hong Sang-soo's works, plays the actor Sang-won, and Ki Joo-bong, who won the Best Actor award at the Locarno International Film Festival for "Hotel by the River," plays the poet Hong Ui-ju. The film will be released in theaters in 2026 as the fourth installment of "Monthly Hong Sang-soo," a project screening new works for five consecutive months to commemorate the director's 30th debut anniversary.
title_norm:친절한 금자씨: Director Park Chan-wook's final installment of his "Revenge Trilogy," following "Sympathy for Mr. Vengeance" and "Oldboy," is a suspense drama about a woman wrongfully imprisoned who exacts revenge. Lee Geum-ja is imprisoned after a man takes her daughter hostage and forces her to take the blame for his child kidnapping and murder. During her sentence, she never loses her gentle smile, earning the nickname "Kind Geum-ja." After serving 13 years, she is released and begins her revenge against the true culprit who framed her. She retrieves her daughter, who was adopted abroad, and with the help of former inmates who have already been released, corners the man. Starring Lee Young-ae ("JSA," "Last Present") and co-starring Choi Min-sik ("Oldboy"), with cameos by Kang Hye-jung, Yoo Ji-tae, Song Kang-ho, and Shin Ha-kyun.
title_norm:탑: A human drama by Korean master Hong Sang-soo, depicting the interactions of artists in a four-story city apartment building in monochrome imagery. Film director Byeong-su visits the apartment owned by his old friend Heo-ok, an active interior designer, together with his daughter Jeong-su, who aims for a career in interior design. The apartment building has a restaurant on the first floor, a cooking class on the second, rental housing on the third, an atelier for artists on the fourth, and Heo-ok's workspace in the basement. The three chat amiably over wine. Byeong-su leaves briefly for a work call, but when he returns, Jeong-su is nowhere to be found... The story unfolds in four chapters as they ascend each floor of the apartment, and the relationships between Byeong-su and the four women around him develop in unpredictable directions. Kwon Hae-hyo, from "The Day After" and "On the Beach at Night Alone," plays film director Byeong-su. Lee Hye-young from "In Front of Your Face," along with Hong Sang-soo regulars Song Seon-mi and Cho Yun-hee, co-star.
title_norm:한란: Based on the 'Jeju April 3 Incident,' a massacre in which nearly 30,000 people are said to have been killed but which was covered up for a long time, this drama depicts the flight of a mother and daughter desperately trying to survive while being driven into a corner by unreasonable violence. On April 3, 1948, the 'Jeju April 3 Incident' began when some islanders on Jeju Island, opposed to interference by foreign forces, staged an armed uprising. From October of the same year, the government designated areas more than 5 kilometers from the coastline as 'hostile zones' and issued a proclamation stating, 'Anyone entering or leaving will be shot without condition.' To escape disaster, the villagers head for Hallasan Mountain, which rises in the center of Jeju Island. A-jin, a woman who has to leave the village temporarily, is extremely worried about her 6-year-old daughter Hye-sen, whom she left behind. Meanwhile, in the village, the South Korean army is mercilessly shooting the elderly. Surviving, Hye-sen heads into the mountains alone to find her mother. After miraculously reuniting, the mother and daughter embark on a life-or-death escape to survive. Directed and written by Ha Myeong-mi, who built her career as a screenwriter for commercial films, it vividly portrays the nameless people tossed about by state power. Kim Hyang-gi, known for 'Along with the Gods' and 'Innocent Witness,' stars as A-jin.
title_norm:헤어질 결심: From Park Chan-wook, director of 'Oldboy' and 'The Handmaiden', comes a suspense drama about a detective investigating a murder and the victim's wife, a suspect to whom he finds himself drawn. When a man falls to his death from a mountain peak, Detective Hae-joon suspects it may be murder rather than an accident. He focuses on the victim's mysterious wife, Sore, but she has an alibi. As the investigation proceeds, Hae-joon finds himself attracted to Sore, and she develops special feelings for him too. Just when a lead emerges and the case seems solved... Park Hae-il plays Hae-joon, Tang Wei plays Sore, with Lee Jung-hyun and Go Kyung-pyo in supporting roles. The film won the Best Director award at the 75th Cannes Film Festival in 2022.
title_norm:８ 1／2: The undisputed representative work of director F. Fellini. Film director Guido dreams one day of his body falling through the air. To heal the various mental and physical fatigue associated with his daily life, he goes to a spa for rest and recuperation, but even there he cannot escape from work and life. And finally, he begins to hallucinate that he is among the elderly spending their remaining years at the spa... This film is an autobiographical work by Fellini himself, and its depiction is superb, portraying reality and fantasy in parallel! A must-see!!
title_norm:＜アイルランド映画祭2026＞『ニュー・ボーイ／クリスティ:
◆ **Christy**
Original Title: Christy
Director: Brendan Canty
Cast: Danny Power, Diarmuid Noyes, Emma Willis
Story: After being kicked out of his foster home, 17-year-old Christy seeks refuge with his estranged older brother, Shane, and his family. However, their relationship is strained, and Christy begins running with his delinquent cousins. Shane tries desperately to save his younger brother, but... Set in the impoverished district of Knocknaheeny, this film explores the bond between brothers struggling with aimless anger and frustration. Despite being Director Canty's debut feature, it received critical acclaim at the Berlin International Film Festival and other festivals worldwide, winning numerous awards. (2025)

◆ **Co-feature: New Boy (Short Film)**
Original Title: An Buachaill Nua
Director: Diarmuid Timmons
Cast: Diarmuid de Faoite, Michael Redahan, Finn O'Hara, Noah Guller
Story: 1970s Ireland. Set in Sligo, the home of poet W.B. Yeats known for its beautiful rural landscapes, this film offers a fresh depiction of the interaction between a transfer student who arrives late on his first day and the local boys. It was an official selection at the 79th BAFTA Awards, the Toronto Irish Film Festival, and numerous other film festivals. (2025)
title_norm:＜アイルランド映画祭2026＞『三人の女強盗』トークイベン: An attempted bank robbery occurs in a rural town, perpetrated by three women who seem the least likely to commit such a crime. As the story explores why they turned to crime, the pasts that haunt them are gradually revealed. The film features a narrative where various issues intertwine and unravel like a jigsaw puzzle, alongside a brilliant ensemble cast of Ireland’s leading actresses, including Carrie Crowley (The Quiet Girl) and Bríd Brennan (Brooklyn). (2025)
title_norm:＜アイルランド映画祭2026＞イン・タイム ドーナル・ラニ: This documentary offers a multi-faceted look at the life of Dónal Lunny, a leading figure in Irish music, through his own words, testimonials from fellow musicians, and live performance footage. Having formed numerous bands and collaborated with a wide array of artists since the 1960s, the film explores Lunny’s unwavering devotion to the music of his homeland, his deep ties to Japan, and his journey of overcoming tragedy to find the inspiration that drives him today. (2025)

title_norm:＜アイルランド映画祭2026＞フィルム／まずは踊れ:
<<Commemorating the 120th Anniversary of Playwright Samuel Beckett>>

◆ Dance First
Director: James Marsh
Cast: Gabriel Byrne, Fionn O'Shea, Sandrine Bonnaire
Story: The life of Samuel Beckett is brought to the screen in elegant monochrome. From his childhood in Dublin and his time in the Resistance during the war to his encounters with his wife Suzanne and James Joyce, the film meticulously examines the light and shadow of the Nobel Prize-winning author's life. Two Irish actors portray Beckett: Gabriel Byrne (*The Usual Suspects*) as the older Beckett, and Fionn O'Shea (*Dating Amber*) as his younger self. (2023)

◆ Double Feature: Film
Director: Alan Schneider
Cast: Buster Keaton
Story: A man flees into an apartment room while hiding his face. As if fearing the gaze of others, he drives out the dogs and cats, tears down the portraits on the walls, and covers the mirrors... This is the only film screenplay Beckett ever wrote, an intense silent short praised by Gilles Deleuze as "the greatest Irish film." Buster Keaton, in his later years, plays the protagonist whose face is rarely shown; his physical performance is a must-see. (1965)
title_norm:＜アイルランド映画祭2026＞父の祈りを: 1974. Gerry is arrested as a suspect in a bombing believed to have been carried out by the IRA (Irish Republican Army). Before long, the authorities set their sights on his father, Giuseppe, and under torture, the two are coerced into confessing to crimes they did not commit... A dramatic, socially conscious human drama based on a shocking real-life case of wrongful conviction in the midst of the Northern Ireland conflict. Featuring brilliant performances by three-time Academy Award winner Daniel Day-Lewis and Pete Postlethwaite (The Usual Suspects). (1993)
title_norm:＜エッセンシャル・ヌーヴェルヴァーグ＞ 女と男のいる舗道: This is Jean-Luc Godard's fourth feature film, following "A Woman Is a Woman," and was shot starring Anna Karina, his partner both publicly and privately. Nana, who decides to part ways with her husband after discussing life with him at a café in Paris, falls into a life where she cannot even pay her rent. She begins to proposition men on the street and engage in prostitution. Eventually, Nana becomes numb to having relations with strangers. The music was handled by Michel Legrand, the renowned composer of "The Umbrellas of Cherbourg" and other films.
title_norm:＜エッセンシャル・ヌーヴェルヴァーグ＞ 女は女である: This is Jean-Luc Godard's third feature film, following "Breathless," and a romantic comedy created based on the idea of a "musical comedy in which the characters do not sing." Angela, a cabaret dancer, tells her live-in lover Émile that she wants a child right now. Émile cannot hide his bewilderment at her request. Then a young man named Alfred, who has feelings for Angela, appears... Following Godard's previous film "Le Petit Soldat," Anna Karina plays the heroine, with Jean-Paul Belmondo of "Breathless" as Alfred and Jean-Claude Brialy of "Les Cousins" as Émile. The music is by Michel Legrand, the renowned composer of "The Umbrellas of Cherbourg" and other films.
title_norm:＜ロックの時間＞ ザ・フー キッズ・アー・オールライト: Alongside The Beatles and The Rolling Stones, The Who led the golden age of British rock and continued to innovate the genre as a superband. This rock documentary masterpiece features live performances of their greatest hits from 1964 to 1978—a period when they were unable to tour Japan at their peak—along with promotional films and interviews. Among the many historic scenes, the film notably features Keith Moon, the legendary genius drummer, in his final full-bodied performance, filmed at Shepperton Studios in May 1978 specifically for this production—a truly precious treasure.
title_norm:＜東学祭＞ 愛のコリーダ: In the 11th year of the Showa era (1936). Sadako, a maid at a Japanese inn, becomes infatuated with the inn's master and begins an affair. When the affair is discovered by the man's wife, the two decide to elope. As they indulge in days of pleasure, Sadako becomes unwilling to ever let him go, and eventually strangles him to death to keep him for herself, then cuts off his genitals.
title_norm:ｗの悲劇: Shizuka Mita is a 20-year-old woman who works hard to become an actress as a trainee at the theater troupe "Sea." Moriguchi, a 26-year-old former troupe member now working at a real estate agency, first notices sincere Shizuka in a park. Shizuka prepares for the lead role audition in the troupe's next production, "The Tragedy of W," but her peer Kaori lands the part, and Shizuka is assigned a minor role with only a single line at the beginning of the story. Downcast after failing the audition, Moriguchi confides in her about his own psychological struggles as an actor. He then proposes marriage on the condition that she never becomes a star, and conversely promises to send a large bouquet to her dressing room as a farewell if she succeeds as an actress.
title_norm:𥇥 の母: Bannosuke Chutaro continues his journey searching for his long-lost mother... A masterpiece among masterpieces, with unforgettable scenes between Kinnosuke, longing for his mother, and the great actresses Kogure, Natsukawa, Naniwa, and Sawamura that bring tears to the eyes.
tmdb:1001026:
The madness of this nation has culminated in a human hunt. 
The long-lost, somber masterpiece once thought impossible to view is finally unleashed again.
Directed by Peter Collinson (*The Italian Job*)
Starring Peter Fonda (*Easy Rider*)
Guest Star: William Holden

<50th Anniversary of Japanese Release>
*Open Season* (Japanese Title: *Dirty Hunter*)
Confirmed for a nationwide theatrical rollout starting January 2, 2026 (Fri) at Cinemart Shinjuku and other theaters.

Ken, Greg, and Art are three Vietnam veterans who have each married, had children, and enjoyed success in society, achieving a picture-perfect life of happiness. But they harbor a hobby they can tell no one about: human hunting. On the weekend the "season" opens, the three pack their bags and head for the hunting grounds in search of prey.

Based on the novel *Open Season* by David Osborn, *Dirty Hunter* is a terrifying suspense-action film directed by the British maverick Peter Collinson—known for *The Italian Job* (1969)—and starring Peter Fonda of *Easy Rider* (1969) fame. Since its 1975 theatrical release in Japan and a few subsequent television broadcasts, the film was never released on home video and became a "phantom" movie nearly impossible to watch worldwide. Now, after half a century, it finally returns to the big screen.

While it utilizes the "human hunting" premise found in many survival-action horror films, it eschews "Battle Royale" style entertainment. Instead, it highlights the darkness of America and humanity itself through the abnormal behavior of men who have completely lost their sense of ethics and morality—a vividness that remains undiminished today. The film possesses a grimness reminiscent of a fusion between Sam Peckinpah’s *Straw Dogs* (1971) and John Boorman’s *Deliverance* (1972). While it shares thematic similarities with films depicting the anguish of Vietnam veterans like *Soldier Blue* (1972), *Taxi Driver* (1976), and *Rolling Thunder* (1977), this Spanish production radiates a texture unlike any of them.

From start to finish, the film offers no sense of catharsis, featuring a succession of events that betray any hope and long sequences of the hunters psychologically cornering their "prey." It is a masterpiece of traumatic cinema that wears down the viewer's nerves.

Peter Fonda plays one of the human hunters; it is said he decided to take the role only after carefully rereading the original treatment multiple times. He is joined by John Phillip Law (*Barbarella*, 1967) and Richard Lynch (*Scarecrow*, 1973). Cornelia Sharpe (*Serpico*, 1973) and Alberto de Mendoza (*Horror Express*, 1972)—winner of the Argentine Film Critics Association Award—play the couple subjected to horrific psychological torment. Furthermore, Academy Award-winning legend William Holden appears as a guest star. The circumstances of why such a massive star appeared in this film remain unknown. In later years, Fonda remarked: "I really enjoyed that movie. It was the first time I played a real villain. I wish that movie would come out on VHS. I really love it."

The newly released teaser trailer shows Fonda and the other two hunters capturing and tormenting the couple. Despite committing the loathsome act of "human hunting," the sight of the three enjoying it as a leisure activity is terrifying. However, at the end, another hunter appears before
tmdb:1002470: A human drama by Korean master Hong Sang-soo, depicting the interactions of artists in a four-story city apartment building in monochrome imagery. Film director Byeong-su visits the apartment owned by his old friend Heo-ok, an active interior designer, together with his daughter Jeong-su, who aims for a career in interior design. The apartment building has a restaurant on the first floor, a cooking class on the second, rental housing on the third, an atelier for artists on the fourth, and Heo-ok's workspace in the basement. The three chat amiably over wine. Byeong-su leaves briefly for a work call, but when he returns, Jeong-su is nowhere to be found... The story unfolds in four chapters as they ascend each floor of the apartment, and the relationships between Byeong-su and the four women around him develop in unpredictable directions. Kwon Hae-hyo, from "The Day After" and "On the Beach at Night Alone," plays film director Byeong-su. Lee Hye-young from "In Front of Your Face," along with Hong Sang-soo regulars Song Seon-mi and Cho Yun-hee, co-star.
tmdb:1005251: A courtroom dark thriller based on the real 'Parents Murder and Dismemberment Case' that occurred in Tai Kok Tsui, Hong Kong in March 2013, and the subsequent trial. Henry Chong, a young man with deep resentment towards his parents, conspires with his friend Angus Tong to murder them, dismembering and disposing of their bodies. The two are soon arrested, and the crime seems certain, but when the trial begins, Angus denies the murder, testifying that Henry killed his parents and that he was threatened into dismembering the bodies. Henry, on the other hand, insists they killed them together, directly contradicting Angus's testimony. As everything begins to unravel, the trial descends into a labyrinth, with intense battles between defense and prosecution, and the jurors' ethics and emotions sway, until the time for the verdict arrives. The actual trial concluded in 2015, and the perpetrator is serving time. The film depicts this case, which is said to still hold lingering mysteries about whether the verdict was correct. Due to some graphic depictions, it received an R18 rating in Hong Kong (R15+ in Japan) but was a huge hit. It garnered attention, winning Best Actor at the Hong Kong International Film Festival and Best New Director and Best Editing at the Hong Kong Film Awards.
tmdb:1008038: Set in 1990s Canada, this drama weaves the bond between a Korean immigrant mother and her son through beautiful 16mm film imagery. Soyoung, who became an unwed mother after losing her lover, moves with her infant son Donghyun to a suburb of Vancouver, Canada. Starting work at a factory, Soyoung faces language and cultural barriers as well as racial discrimination, but raises her son with determination. When Donghyun turns 16, he goes by the English name "David" and has fully adapted to life in Canada, but deep down he yearns to know his roots and the father he has never met. Then one day, receiving shocking news, the mother and son return to Korea for the first time, confronting a painful past. Director and screenwriter Anthony Shim, who himself immigrated from Korea to Canada at age eight, powerfully yet delicately portrays the fluidity of immigrant identity and the conflict and renewal between parent and child. Choi Seung-yoon, active in Korea as a dancer, choreographer, and actor, plays mother Soyoung, and Ethan Hwang of the drama "The Umbrella Academy" plays the teenage Donghyun.
tmdb:1012310: A human drama depicting the natural beauty of Shimane and the bond between father and son, centered around the motif of traditional Tatara steelmaking.
tmdb:1013701:
A documentary capturing the present state of the "Beautiful Island" of Taiwan, documenting the research process of the film collective Kuzoku—acclaimed for works such as *Saudade*, *Bangkok Nites*, and *TENZO*—as they prepare for their upcoming feature. Known for their method of conducting exhaustive location research before filming, Kuzoku plans to shoot their next project in Taiwan in 2026. Since 2020, they have made repeated visits to the island, continuing their fieldwork even amidst the pandemic. 

Guided by the music echoing through the streets, they journey to the villages of Taiwan’s indigenous peoples: the Amis settlement of Tafalong in Hualien County; the Seediq villages reached by crossing the 3,000-meter peaks of the Central Mountain Range; and the Paiwan villages at the island’s southernmost tip. As they connect with the people they meet—youth rapping in endangered indigenous tongues and artists updating traditional melodies into contemporary sounds—they also confront a history of invasion and colonization by various nations, including Japan.
tmdb:1015079: Set in Malaysia, this demon-combining exorcism gore horror film takes on the Islamic exorcism rites of the state religion and Southeast Asia's most enigmatic flower, the titan arum. A boy apprentice exorcist, who inherited spiritual powers from his mother, engages in a deadly struggle against the forbidden curse dwelling within the "corpse flower." Iqbal, raised under the wing of Norman, a Muslim exorcist, possesses rare spiritual abilities inherited from his mother Dina. One day, Dina is possessed and killed by an evil spirit while shielding Iqbal, who was targeted because of the strength of his powers. Grief-stricken, Iqbal resents his own overwhelming power, and his father Norman, worried about his son's future, seals away part of his abilities. Crawling toward the wounded family are a series of tragedies brought by the curse of the "corpse flower." Can Iqbal overcome his sorrow and exorcise a curse steeped in mystery and taboo?
tmdb:101664: One year after the whirlwind of romantic opportunities that came to the penniless and girlfriend-less Yukiyo Fujimoto—his 'Moteki' (sudden popularity with women)—his relationships with the four girls have ended. But new girls begin approaching him again, and a 'Second Moteki' is about to arrive.
tmdb:1017417: A love story directed by Rikiya Imaizumi (known for "Ai ga Nanda") starring Goro Inagaki, based on an original screenplay. Freelance writer Shigeki Ichikawa realizes that his wife, editor Sae, is having an affair with the popular young writer she handles, but he can't bring himself to confront her. At the same time, Shigeki is troubled by a certain feeling that sprouted within him when he learned of the affair. One day, at a literary award ceremony, Ichikawa meets high school writer Rea Kubo and is drawn to the content of her award-winning novel "La France." He asks if there is a real-life model for the story and if he can meet them. Sae, Ichikawa's wife, is played by Yuri Nakamura; high school writer Kubo by Tina Tamashiro; Shigeki's friend Masatsugu Arisaka by Ryuya Wakaba; Arisaka's wife Yukino by Mirai Shida; and Sae's lover Madoka Arakawa by Shion Sasaki.
tmdb:1018: One midnight, a car crash occurs on Mulholland Drive. The sole survivor, a dark-haired woman, manages to make her way to the streets of Hollywood and slips into an empty residence. It turns out to be the home of famous actress Ruth, where she is soon discovered by Ruth’s niece, Betty. Betty initially assumes the woman—who impulsively calls herself Rita—is a friend of her aunt, but she soon realizes they are total strangers. Rita confesses that she can remember nothing. The only clues are a large sum of cash and a mysterious blue key found in her bag. Out of both sympathy and curiosity, Betty offers to help Rita recover her memories, but...
tmdb:10180:
A legendary masterpiece and a historic box-office smash, often called the greatest film in Danish cinema history.

Four supremely unlucky rogues, each haunted by absurd childhood traumas. Despite their different ages and backgrounds, they plot a massive heist to turn around their lives of constant failure. After surviving a fierce shootout and making their escape, what lies ahead for them is...

This is the role Mads plays! Arne, a gun-obsessed brute who solves every problem with violence and is constantly on edge. A young Mads’s ripped physique and mischievous sex appeal are simply irresistible...!
tmdb:1018061: A music documentary tracing the journeys and bonds of four session musicians who supported the American West Coast sound. In the early 1970s, musicians Danny Kortchmar (guitar), Waddy Wachtel (guitar), Leland Sklar (bass), and Russ Kunkel (drums) participated in recordings for artists like Carole King, James Taylor, Jackson Browne, and Linda Ronstadt, who lived around Laurel Canyon in Los Angeles. Later called the supergroup "The Immediate Family," their solid playing and musical understanding contributed to the birth of many classic songs, continually supporting the artists' expressions. Through interviews with the four musicians themselves and the renowned artists they made music with, the film reveals moments of creation in the studio's closed space and the deep bonds between musicians. It also explores projects each participated in solo, depicting their rise to becoming popular musicians. Directed by Denny Tedesco, who also directed the music documentary "The Wrecking Crew" about the session musicians who supported the American music scene of the 1960s and 70s.
tmdb:1019185:
“I always felt like an outsider.”
“Now I know—the world can be changed, and I can find a place where I belong.”

Lawan is a Kurdish boy who was born deaf. Concerned about his future in Iraq, his parents decide to seek asylum in the United Kingdom. After spending a year in a refugee camp, the family enters the UK through the efforts of a supporter, and Lawan enrolls at the Royal School for the Deaf Derby. Learning sign language for the first time, he begins to communicate with his teachers and peers, showing remarkable growth that astonishes everyone around him. But then, Lawan’s family is suddenly ordered to be deported by the British government...
tmdb:1021643: A drama directed by Guillaume Senez, who also teamed up with Romain Duris in 'Our Struggles,' with Duris starring. Set primarily in Japan, it depicts the changing forms of modern families under the universal themes of parent-child bonds and love, against the backdrop of the differences between Japanese and French social systems. Jay, a Frenchman working as a chef in Tokyo, marries a Japanese woman but divorces her. Due to differences in the joint custody systems of Japan and France, he is separated from his beloved daughter Lily. Unable to give up hope, he becomes a taxi driver, wandering the city while searching for traces of his daughter. Nine years later, just as Jay decides to return to France, his daughter Lily, now a grown girl, coincidentally gets into his taxi. Without Lily knowing the driver is her real father, and Jay unable to reveal himself, they spend a brief moment together. The cast includes Judith Chemla, known for 'A Woman's Life' and 'Our Arias for Mother,' Tsu Yu from 'TAXi (2),' Yumi Narita from 'Don't Stop the Camera!' and 'Mari's Story,' as well as Shinnosuke Abe, Toshihiro Yashiba, Moro Agata, and Haruko Uchida.
tmdb:1023: A human drama written and directed by Anders Thomas Jensen, the acclaimed screenwriter of *Open Hearts* and *Brothers*, starring Mads Mikkelsen (*The Hunt*). Drawing motifs from the Old Testament’s "Book of Job" and the fable of Adam’s apples, the film uses dark humor to depict the eccentric characters inhabiting a rural church. Adam, a neo-Nazi skinhead on parole, is sent to a countryside church that doubles as a rehabilitation center. When his mentor, the priest Ivan, asks him to set a goal, Adam dismissively replies that he will bake an apple cake using fruit from the garden. The residents of the church are all peculiar, including Ivan himself, who uses blind faith to shield himself from a harsh reality. As Adam relentlessly attempts to strip away Ivan’s self-deception, a series of bizarre calamities begins to plague him. Ulrich Thomsen (*In a Better World*) stars as Adam, with Mikkelsen portraying Ivan.
tmdb:1024298: A human drama starring Kenji Sawada, based on the culinary essay "Days of Eating Earth: My Twelve Months of Shojin" by writer Tsutomu Minakami. Directed and written by Yuji Nakae of "Nabi no Koi" fame, the film crafts an original story inspired by the rich worldview of the source material. Tsutomu, a writer living alone in a remote mountain cabin in Nagano, spends his days cooking wild berries, mushrooms, and vegetables from his garden, feeling the changing seasons as he writes. His editor and much younger lover, Machiko, occasionally visits him from Tokyo. For the two, cooking and eating seasonal ingredients together is a special time. Though Tsutomu lives a carefree life, he has been unable to enshrine the ashes of his wife, who passed away 13 years ago. Takako Matsu plays Tsutomu's lover Machiko. Cooking researcher Yoshiharu Doi created the many dishes that appear in the film.
tmdb:1025029: A film documenting and screening the legendary 1970 London performance of the American rock band Creedence Clearwater Revival (CCR). In 1970, at the height of their popularity, CCR embarked on their first and only European tour. The highlight of the tour was their performance at the Royal Albert Hall in London on April 14, where CCR aimed to challenge The Beatles, whose record sales were the highest in the world at the time, by performing in their home territory. However, four days before the performance, news of The Beatles' breakup was reported. Despite this, CCR delivered a powerful, all-or-nothing performance, making the Royal Albert Hall concert one of the greatest live shows in rock history. The complete footage of the London performance, discovered after 50 years, has been restored in 4K, and the film traces their trajectory, interweaving footage capturing the band's daily life, interviews with members, and early live performances. Directed by Bob Smeaton of 'The Beatles Anthology,' with narration by actor Jeff Bridges.
tmdb:1026103: A Korean suspense thriller about floor noise and a cult religion, depicting the fate of a female writer who strives to uncover the truth behind the noise coming from the upstairs neighbor. Eun-su, an aspiring writer living in apartment 401, has been applying to numerous writing contests but faces a string of rejections. Meanwhile, for about a month, she has been tormented by unbearable noise coming from unit 501 above. Deciding to use this situation as material for her work, Eun-su, along with her friend Ji-seong, begins observing Ho-gyeong, a middle-aged man living in 501. Even after he notices her excessive stalking, she relentlessly pursues him for the sake of her writing. Eventually, Eun-su arrives at a shocking truth hidden behind the noise, but at the same time, she finds herself backed into a dangerous situation. Director Kim Jeong-uk, who has crafted many stories candidly depicting the human psyche, portrays with intense suspense the psychological anxiety born from trivial troubles lurking in daily life. Ryu Hwa-young, known as a former member of the K-pop group T-ARA, stars in her first lead film role, passionately playing Eun-su, a writer whose obsession with writing blurs the line between reality and delusion. Veteran actor Park Jin-woo, known for the Netflix drama "Squid Game," plays the mysterious upstairs resident Ho-gyeong.
tmdb:10293: The third film in Éric Rohmer's "Comedies and Proverbs" series. It depicts the romantic entanglements of six men and women at a seaside villa, seen through the eyes of adolescent girl Pauline. Fifteen-year-old Pauline comes to Normandy for a vacation with her older cousin Marion. When they go to the beach, they meet Marion's ex-boyfriend Pierre. Pierre still harbors feelings for Marion, but Marion falls for Henri, a playboy acquaintance of Pierre's. Meanwhile, Pauline grows close to Sylvain, a boy windsurfing at the beach... The film won the Silver Bear and the FIPRESCI Prize at the Berlin International Film Festival.
tmdb:1030205: A biographical drama starring Kazunari Ninomiya as real-life Japanese prisoner of war Yamamoto Hanao, held in a Siberian labor camp (Laguerre). Based on Jun Henmi's nonfiction novel "The Last Letter from the Laguerre," directed by Takahisa Zeze, known for "Those Who Were Not Protected" and "The Thread." In 1945, after World War II, Japanese POWs in Siberian camps faced brutal conditions—temperatures dropping to -40°C, minimal food, and forced heavy labor, with many dying. Amid this, Yamamoto Hanao believes he will return to his wife and children in Japan, encouraging those around him. His selfless actions and strong faith ignite a flame of hope in many prisoners' hearts. Kitagawa Keiko plays Yamamoto's wife Mojimi, with a star-studded cast including Matsuzaka Tori, Nakajima Kento, Kiryū Kentarō, and Yasuda Ken as fellow prisoners.
tmdb:1033148: Director Lynne Ramsay ("We Need to Talk About Kevin," "You Were Never Really Here") presents a psychological drama starring Jennifer Lawrence and Robert Pattinson, depicting a couple torn between love and madness. It was screened in the Competition section of the 78th Cannes Film Festival and nominated for the Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Drama. Grace, a writer who moves to a countryside town with her husband Jackson, begins a new life. Peaceful days are shattered after childbirth: her writing stalls, and the pressure and loneliness of childcare, along with fragmentary hallucinations, gradually distort her reality. As the boundary between reality and fantasy blurs, Grace's mind quietly but surely collapses. Jennifer Lawrence, who won the Academy Award for Best Actress for "Silver Linings Playbook," plays Grace and also serves as a producer, drawing on her own childbirth experience to embody the loneliness and anxiety of a postpartum woman. Robert Pattinson ("The Batman") plays Jackson. The film is based on the novel "Die, My Love" by Ariana Harwicz, with Martin Scorsese as a producer.
tmdb:10341: A film that Wim Wenders nurtured for about 13 years before completing. Blending sci-fi elements, it combines a road movie and love story set in a world facing apocalypse. In the winter of 1999, the predicted crash of a nuclear satellite casts the world into anxiety. Claire, traveling by car from Venice, meets Trevor, who is being chased by someone. Though they part ways, she can't stop thinking about him and, with the help of her ex-lover (a writer) and a private detective, follows him to Lisbon, Moscow, and Beijing.
