The Japanese voice cast includes Megumi Han as Kent, Shizuka Ishigami as Chase, Mako Komatsu as Marshall, Shiori Izawa as Skye, Sōma Saitō as Rubble, Miyuki Kobori as Rocky, and Sayuri Yahagi as Zuma, all reprising their roles from previous series. Guest voice actors include Yūko Ōshima and the comedy duo "Rainbow" members Takao Jumbo and Naoto Ikeda. The theme song is a new track written by the Backstreet Boys titled "Bottle Up."
tmdb:1185957: Set in a small diner on Cheung Chau, an outlying island of Hong Kong, this documentary observes a changing world through the islanders who gather there. Located about 30 minutes southwest of Hong Kong Island by ferry, Cheung Chau is a small island known as a fishing village, where colorful boats bob in the harbor and time flows gently. The 'Yat Tai' diner on the island is always bustling with locals who gather to play cards and mahjong with a beer in hand. However, societal changes and the fervor of citizens reach this island far from Hong Kong, and the diner's regulars cannot remain indifferent. From the owner staring at the TV to young people eagerly seeking information, each person grapples with the tides of the era from their own perspective and distance. Eventually, the pandemic that engulfs the world also has a major impact on this diner. The director is Frankie Shin, for whom this is his first feature-length documentary. Shin, a native of Cheung Chau who was also a regular at the Yat Tai diner, carefully captures how the people he treated like family faced the changing times and continued their daily lives. The film won the Best Documentary Award at the 29th Busan International Film Festival in 2024.
tmdb:1188968: Documentary filmmaker Tomoaki Fujino records over 20 years the story of his older sister, who began showing symptoms of schizophrenia, and his parents, who kept her from seeing a psychiatrist. His sister, eight years older, was caring and excellent. Influenced by their parents, she entered medical school to become a doctor. One day, she suddenly started screaming things that weren't true. Schizophrenia was suspected, but her parents—a doctor and a researcher—refused to acknowledge the illness and kept her away from psychiatric care. Doubting their judgment, Fujino tried to persuade them but failed, and left home with a lingering sense of unease. Eighteen years after his sister's onset, Fujino, having studied filmmaking, began recording his family's life whenever he visited home. He filmed family outings and dinner scenes, engaged his parents in conversation, and kept talking to his sister, but her condition worsened. Eventually, his parents installed a chain and padlock on the front door to confine her inside.
tmdb:11898: A suspense comedy that follows the trail of a serial murder spree by a young man burning with ambition and a thirst for revenge, laced with biting black humor. One of the 'Ealing Comedies,' a series of comedy films produced at Ealing Studios in the UK from the late 1930s to the mid-1950s, directed by Robert Hamer, known for 'It Always Rains on Sunday.' The story is told in flashback form as Louis, a young man of aristocratic blood from the D'Ascoyne family, writes his memoirs in his prison cell, recounting how he systematically murders his relatives to avenge his mother's disownment and reclaim his status. The renowned actor Alec Guinness, known for his role as Obi-Wan Kenobi in 'Star Wars' and 'The Bridge on the River Kwai,' plays all eight members of the D'Ascoyne family who are killed by Louis. Dennis Price plays the protagonist Louis, and Joan Greenwood leaves a strong impression as the cold, calculating heroine. This film is part of the special screening series 'The Golden Age of British Ealing Comedies' (June 20–July 17, 2026, at Shinjuku K's Cinema).
tmdb:11906: 'Never watch it alone—' This famous tagline became a buzzword at the time of release. A masterpiece often talked about to this day, where vivid colors, the eerie sound featuring Goblin, and extreme direction form a trinity that creates a unique tension. It was a hit in Japan in 1977, ranking in the top ten among foreign films released that year. Its influence led to the Japanese release of an unrelated 1975 film by Argento as 'Suspiria Part 2' the following year. For the director, this is the first installment of the 'Three Mothers' trilogy, followed by 'Inferno' and 'Mother of Tears.' Suzy, who has come from America to study at a German ballet school, witnesses a woman disappearing while muttering something on the night she arrives at the dormitory. Shortly after, the woman is killed by someone. After enrolling, Suzy undergoes rigorous training but begins to experience physical abnormalities, fainting, and along with her friend Sara, hears strange groans and footsteps in the dormitory. One night, feeling pursued by someone, Sara flees alone through the dormitory...
tmdb:1191585: A documentary by filmmaker Shinkichi Noda, who continually explored the foundations of people's consciousness in rapidly changing Showa-era Japan. This film captures the "Niino Snow Festival" of Nagano Prefecture, seeking to find the enduring spirit of the people within this festival that has continued since medieval times. The Niino Snow Festival has been held since around the 13th century, centered around Izu Shrine and Suwa Shrine in Niino, Anan Town, Nagano Prefecture. People see the falling winter snow as rice flower blossoms, a harbinger of the harvest, and pray for abundant grain. Throughout the night-long festival, masked and costumed performances like "Kyoman" (horse racing), "Okina" (old man), and "Oni" (demon) appear one after another, and the crowd erupts when the spirit of bounty, "Saiho," makes its entrance. Director Noda attempts to read the everyday wishes of farmers for the coming year's production within this sacred festival space. This film is part of the special screening series "Shinkichi Noda Special: Snow is a Flower" (screening from December 6, 2025, at Pole Pole Higashi-Nakano and other theaters nationwide).
tmdb:1192992: An animated film that visualizes an astonishing true story from 1990s Hungary in Eastern Europe, incorporating documentary materials. In 1990s Hungary, after the fall of the Iron Curtain opened the door to Western Europe, foreign travel was liberalized, and many people turned their eyes to the outside world. However, international train tickets were expensive and out of reach for ordinary people. Amidst this, three young men—intellectual Akos, fearless Pecha, and swimming enthusiast Laci—find a way to forge tickets. They dissolve the blue carbon ink "Pelikan Blue" from the company Pelikan, used on the tickets, with household detergent and rewrite the destinations. After enjoying overseas trips with forged tickets, they decide to distribute "tickets to freedom" to other young people in similar situations. The plan seems to go smoothly, but eventually, a police investigation begins, escalating into a major uproar that shakes the nation. Directed by László Csáki, known for his distinctive animation style, who conducted meticulous research over ten years and blends documentary materials like archival footage and interview audio with hand-drawn animation.
tmdb:1193128: An ensemble drama inspired by the reality that 14 million people were forced to flee abroad to escape the long devastation of the Syrian civil war, depicting families torn apart by conflict and those around them from multiple perspectives. Set across four countries—Syria, Turkey, Greece, and the United States—the story unfolds in five chapters, intersecting the lives of five families. As the civil war between government forces and rebel groups intensifies in Syria's dictatorship, Syrian doctor Amira decides to cross dangerous borders with her daughter to reach safety. Syrian border guard Mustafa distrusts the brutal government forces and struggles between being a soldier who follows orders and a human with a conscience. Turkish smuggler Marwan seeks to earn money by loading refugees onto boats bound for Greece to move his sick son to America. Poet Fathi boards that boat with his wife and child, facing mortal danger. Greek coast guard Stavros discovers refugees navigating stormy seas and strives to save lives. Film producer and humanitarian activist Brandt Andersen, who made the 2020 short film "Refugee" as his starting point, makes his feature directorial, screenwriting, and producing debut with this meticulously researched work. Yasmin Al-Masri reprises her role as doctor Amira from the short, and Omar Sy returns as smuggler Marwan.
tmdb:1194915:
This unique action film follows a man struggling with anger management who unleashes his fury only once a week—on Saturdays—as he takes a stand against a corrupt police officer abusing his power. 

Raised in a coastal town in Andhra Pradesh, India, Surya has been quick-tempered since childhood. His worried mother taught him to record his anger in a notebook rather than acting on it immediately, advising him that if the feeling persists after time has passed, then the anger is truly justified. Even after his mother’s passing, Surya maintains this habit, but with a personal twist: he designates Saturday as the day he finally lets out a week’s worth of pent-up rage. 

Now an adult working as an insurance agent in Hyderabad, Surya leads a seemingly ordinary life, yet his ritualistic Saturday outbursts continue. His path eventually crosses with Inspector Dayanand, a man who treats the local citizens with utter brutality... 

Starring Nani (*Eega*) as Surya, the film features S.J. Suryah, a renowned character actor in Tamil cinema, as the villainous Inspector Dayanand.
tmdb:1197306: Former special forces operative Levon Cade (Jason Statham) has left his dangerous past behind, now working as a construction foreman with a "safety first" motto. While Levon hopes to lead a quiet life and be a good father to his daughter, his world is upended when Jenny—the daughter of his boss and benefactor—suddenly disappears. As he searches for her, Levon uncovers a massive criminal organization specializing in human trafficking. Forced to unleash his long-dormant skills, he plunges into a fierce and relentless battle.
tmdb:1208348: Brendan Fraser, winner of the Academy Award for Best Actor for "The Whale," stars in this human drama shot entirely in Japan. Directed by Japanese filmmaker HIKARI, who gained attention for her feature debut "37 Seconds" and the drama series "Beef," the film follows a down-on-his-luck actor living in Tokyo who rediscovers himself through working for a rental family service. Philip, an American actor who once dominated toothpaste commercials but has since been largely forgotten, lives in Tokyo, eking out a living in the acting world and blending into the city. One day, he is hired by Tada, who runs a rental family company. The job involves playing the role of a cherished "family member" for clients in exchange for payment. Initially hesitant about delving into others' lives, Philip begins to change as he interacts with the people he meets through his work. Takehiro Hira plays Tada, the rental family company owner; Mari Yamamoto plays Aiko, an actress working for the company; and Akira Emoto plays Kikuo, an aging actor.
tmdb:12101: Directed by Richard Fleischer of "Fantastic Voyage" fame, this 1973 near-future sci-fi film adapts Harry Harrison's novel "Make Room! Make Room!" and depicts various social issues such as overpopulation, extreme weather, food shortages, resource depletion, ecological collapse, and poverty. In 2022, New York City is suffering from explosive population growth, leaving people homeless and food shortages commonplace, while rapid climate change has subjected the city to heat waves. In a world of extreme inequality, most people spend their days idly waiting for the weekly government ration of the nutrient food "Soylent." Amidst this, a murder occurs: Simonsohn, an executive of the Soylent Corporation who just announced the new product "Soylent Green" as the ultimate nutrition, is killed. Homicide detective Thorn takes on the investigation... Charlton Heston of "Ben-Hur" stars as Detective Thorn, with Edward G. Robinson of "Little Caesar" co-starring. A digitally remastered version was revived in theaters in May 2024.
tmdb:12102: Manhattan, New York. Ted Kramer, a businessman in his eighth year of marriage, leads a busy life, but one day his wife Joanna, determined to find her independence, suddenly walks out on him. Ted is forced to care for their seven-year-old son, Billy, on his own, but balancing work and parenting proves harder than he ever imagined. Eventually, Joanna takes the matter to court to claim custody of Billy, but Ted refuses to yield. The legal battle of Kramer vs. Kramer begins.
tmdb:1212271: Actress Scarlett Johansson makes her feature directorial debut with this lighthearted drama about the friendship between a powerful elderly woman and a motherless student, sparked by a lie, set against the backdrop of her own Jewish cultural roots. Based on a script by first-time feature screenwriter Tory Kamen, drawing on her own grandmother's and family history, Johansson directs with humor and wit. Eleanor, an elderly woman living in New York, feels a void after losing her longtime friend Bessie. One day, intending to attend a tea party, she accidentally wanders into a support group for Holocaust survivors. There, she improvises a story about Bessie's life, recounting her Holocaust memories. Inspired by the dramatic story, journalism student Nina approaches Eleanor, and a new friendship blossoms. But Eleanor's lie takes on a life of its own, sparking a major uproar. June Squibb ("Thelma") plays the unconventional Eleanor, and Erin Kellyman ("Solo: A Star Wars Story") plays Nina. Rita Zohar, herself a Holocaust survivor, plays Eleanor's late friend Bessie.
tmdb:1212461: Acclaimed at the Sundance Film Festival! Rescue your beloved dog, whisked away into the world of a PC game! An extraordinary sci-fi fantasy from visionary director Albert Birney!! [A Movies from the Uncharted Zone 2026 Selection] In theaters Friday, January 16.
tmdb:1214266: A road movie set in Hong Kong and Taiwan, depicting a midsummer miracle connected by a single letter. Against the beautiful, shimmering landscapes of Taiwan, it portrays a time-spanning bond between a wounded writer and a lonely young man. Tianyu, a popular Hong Kong writer, faces fierce public backlash after accusations of plagiarism. Deeply hurt, he travels alone to Taiwan in search of the 'Whale's Vanished Cove,' a place said to lead to heaven, which a boy he once corresponded with told him about. After being cheated in an unfamiliar country and getting drunk in the bustling streets of Taipei, Tianyu is helped by Ashang, a local thug. When Tianyu reveals the purpose of his journey, Ashang, claiming to know the 'Whale's Vanished Cove,' offers to take him there, and their summer journey begins... Terence Lau, known for 'Twilight Warriors: Final Battle in the Kowloon Walled City,' delicately portrays the gentle and pure writer Tianyu, while Fandy Fan, from 'Destiny Matchup,' co-stars as the thug Ashang.
tmdb:1214499: Shiori Ito, a journalist and survivor of sexual violence, pursues the truth of her case and challenges the structures of power. This documentary is composed of a vast archive of audio and video footage recorded by Ito and those around her.
tmdb:1214539: A staggering documentary that delivers an unprecedented experience to audiences! A jazz rhapsody that digs into the darkness of history, built entirely from archival footage! Satchmo, Malcolm X, Gillespie, Khrushchev, Coltrane, Castro, Nina Simone, Nehru, Nasser, and Sukarno too... Witness a historical farce swirling with conspiracy!
tmdb:1217411:
Director Yuki Horiuchi—who earned high praise at various domestic indie film festivals, including winning the Grand Prix at a student film festival for the dialogue-driven drama *At the End of the Night*, which depicted the end of summer for youths struggling to grow up—returns with an ensemble piece about those who don't go to the festival on the day of a summer celebration.

A man in a coffee shop tries to persuade the school's "Madonna" to star in his independent film. People at a bus stop wait endlessly for a bus that shows no sign of coming. Someone, enraged that the festival's fireworks display was canceled, steals fireworks to set them off themselves. Two girls wake up hungover to find their air conditioner remote missing and search for it while retracing their memories of the night before. A girl works her shift at a cafe. On the day of the festival, the ordinary summer lives of these people who aren't attending begin to intertwine.

The film won the Special Jury Prize at the 24th TAMA NEW WAVE competition. It stars Masahiro Mera, who also appeared in *At the End of the Night*.
tmdb:1219388: This documentary follows the struggles of four high school students in Shimane Prefecture and their teacher as they experience theater for the first time. At the Kakeya Branch of Mitoya High School—the smallest prefectural high school in Shimane with just 70 students—four teenagers begin their journey into drama. Each a novice to the stage, they grapple with their own insecurities—from social anxiety to a lack of academic focus or passion—as they gradually devote themselves to the craft. Under the guidance of their advisor, Yoshihiro Kameo, they select Osamu Dazai’s classic "Run, Melos!" and head to the regional competition with high hopes. However, they are soon overwhelmed by the high level of the main Mitoya High School campus, and the COVID-19 pandemic results in a competition held behind closed doors. Though they fail to advance to the prefectural level and fear their efforts will go unseen, their youth takes an unexpected turn. The film has earned high praise at various festivals, winning four awards including the Special Jury Prize and Audience Award at the 14th Shimokitazawa Film Festival, and was an official selection at the Tokyo Documentary Film Festival 2022.
tmdb:12197: The feature directorial debut of Joachim Trier, a Danish director distantly related to Lars von Trier who studied film in Denmark and England, released in 2006. This is the first work of the "Oslo Trilogy," which also includes his later films "Oslo, August 31st" and "The Worst Person in the World." Philip and Erik are childhood friends who have dreamed of becoming writers since they were kids. One day, they both send manuscripts to a publisher, but only Philip's is accepted. Philip becomes a suddenly famous author, but soon begins to suffer mental instability. Meanwhile, Erik continues writing novels without giving up... Anders Danielsen Lie, who stars in all three films of the "Oslo Trilogy," plays Philip. Selected as Norway's entry for the 79th Academy Awards for Best Foreign Language Film, it received high praise, winning the Grand Prix (Best Film), Best Director, and Best Screenplay at the Amanda Awards, Norway's equivalent of the Academy Awards. It received its first theatrical release in Japan as part of the special screening series "Joachim Trier: The Oslo Trilogy" (starting February 13, 2026, at Bunkamura Le Cinéma Shibuya Miyashita and other venues in Tokyo).
tmdb:1220515:
Set in early 1990s Poland, this road movie follows a Holocaust survivor and his New York-born-and-raised daughter as they journey to trace their family history, told with a humorous and warm perspective. Directed by Julia von Heinz, known for *And Tomorrow the Entire World*, the film is an adaptation of the novel *Too Many Men* by Australian author Lily Brett, based on her own experiences.

In 1991, New York native Ruth arrives in Warsaw, Poland—her parents' homeland—with her father, Edek. While it is Ruth’s first time visiting, for her father, it is his first return home in about 50 years. Ruth hopes to explore her roots during the trip, but her free-spirited father constantly thwarts her plans, leading to her growing frustration. Even after visiting the Auschwitz-Birkenau concentration camp and hearing the horrific memories from her father’s own lips for the first time, the rift between them remains. Just as Ruth finally decides to leave her father and return to New York
tmdb:1221061: Four girls from different eras, spanning from the 1910s to the present day, experience inexplicable events on a farm in northern Germany. A century-spanning visual epic where their anxieties resonate with one another.
tmdb:1225624: This human drama depicts the loneliness and division in modern society through the daily life of an immigrant woman working in a massive logistics center in Scotland, ultimately finding a faint glimmer of hope. Aurora, a Portuguese immigrant, works as a picker in a huge logistics center on the outskirts of Scotland. Her days are mostly spent walking through countless aisles following scanner instructions and retrieving items from shelves. Conversations with colleagues are limited to brief breaks, and after her shift, she drags her tired body back to a shared house for immigrant workers. Interactions among residents are superficial, relationships never deepen, and her rootless days continue monotonously. One day, Aurora accidentally breaks her smartphone. Losing this modern necessity—her means of workplace communication and her "companion" for passing time—slowly but surely begins to change her daily life. Portuguese-born, Scotland-based Laura Carreira wrote and directed her first feature film based on her own experiences as an immigrant, winning the Best Director Award at the 72nd San Sebastián International Film Festival in 2024.
tmdb:1226141: A human drama reuniting Hong Kong comedy king Michael Hui, popular in Japan for the 'Mr. Boo!' series, and Dayo Wong, a top Hong Kong comedian and actor ('A Witness Out of the Blue'), after 32 years. It became a massive hit, breaking Hong Kong's all-time box office record. Set in Hong Kong's funeral industry, it carefully explores universal themes of family, tradition, and views on life and death. Wedding planner To-sang, burdened with debt from the pandemic, reluctantly switches to the funeral business but faces difficulties as weddings and funerals are vastly different. To-sang, focused on profit, constantly clashes with the strict Taoist priest Master Man, who values tradition. However, as To-sang interacts with Master Man and his daughter Man-yuet, his resentment gradually fades. He begins to understand the true meaning of the traditional Taoist ritual 'Breaking Hell' that Master Man performs at funerals. Dayo Wong plays funeral director To-sang, and Michael Hui plays Taoist Master Man. Director Anselm Chan, a screenwriter making his third feature, helmed the film. It won five awards at the 43rd Hong Kong Film Awards in 2025, including Best Actress (Michelle Wai). At the 37th Tokyo International Film Festival's World Focus section, a 126-minute version was screened under the title 'The Last Dance'. The theatrical release is a 140-minute director's cut.
tmdb:1226863: The second film in the series of "The Super Mario Bros. Movie", which animated the world of Nintendo's "Super Mario" game series and became a massive hit in 2023, grossing over $13 billion worldwide. Twin plumbers Mario and Luigi, while helping Princess Peach in the Mushroom Kingdom, take care of the captured King Koopa and solve everyone's problems. One day, they meet a new partner, Yoshi. Then, triggered by Princess Peach's birthday party, they embark on a new adventure across space to thwart the evil ambitions of Koopa's son, Bowser Jr. In addition to familiar faces from the first film like Mario, Luigi, Princess Peach, Koopa, and Toad, new characters from the original game series appear, including Yoshi, Rosalina, and Bowser Jr. Produced jointly by Chris Meledandri of Illumination (known for the "Minions" and "Sing" series) and Nintendo's Shigeru Miyamoto. Directors Aaron Horvath and Michael Jelenic, and screenwriter Matthew Fogel return, along with the original voice cast including Chris Pratt, Anya Taylor-Joy, Charlie Day, and Jack Black, as well as the Japanese dub cast including Mamoru Miyano, Ayasa Shida, Yu Hatakeyama, Kenta Miyake, and Tomokazu Seki.
tmdb:1228710: The first theatrical feature film in about seven years from the globally popular sci-fi saga "Star Wars". It depicts on a grand scale the story of the lone bounty hunter Mandalorian and the young Force-sensitive being Grogu, as portrayed in the drama series "The Mandalorian". Set in the galaxy after "Star Wars: Return of the Jedi", the era is chaotic, with the New Republic's rule incomplete and outlaws and Imperial remnants running rampant. Amidst this, the orphan Grogu, who possesses immense Force power, is pursued by those who covet his strength. The bounty hunter Din Jarin, aka the Mandalorian, decides to protect him, and as they travel through a dangerous galaxy, they gradually develop a father-son bond. The film shows a grown Grogu using the Force powers he honed under Luke Skywalker's training, and features intense, fast-paced battles against Imperial remnants, delivering the large-scale action unique to the "Star Wars" series. A new character, Colonel Ward, is played by the renowned actress Sigourney Weaver. Dave Filoni, Lucasfilm's Chief Creative Officer, serves as executive producer, and Jon Favreau directs, bringing together the creators behind "The Mandalorian" series.
tmdb:1230368: Rock legend Bruce Springsteen. In 1982, in the shadow of fame, he was grappling with deep loneliness and inner conflict. This film depicts the behind-the-scenes creation of the legendary masterpiece "Nebraska" and his spiritual journey.
tmdb:1233413: A survival thriller directed by Ryan Coogler ('Black Panther,' 'Creed'), starring Michael B. Jordan, with whom Coogler has frequently collaborated on feature films. In the 1930s, in a devout small town in the American South, twin brothers Smoke and Stack open a dance hall in their former hometown, serving illegal alcohol and music in pursuit of a fortune. On opening night, the crowd revels in a night of swirling desires, but the arrival of uninvited guests changes everything. The dance hall is consumed by senseless despair, and a night of chaos beyond human comprehension begins. Jordan plays the dual role of the twin brothers. The cast includes Hailee Steinfeld ('Bumblebee'), Jack O'Connell ('Ferrari'), and Delroy Lindo ('Da 5 Bloods'). Coogler also wrote and produced the film, reuniting the 'Black Panther' team including production designer Hannah Beachler, composer Ludwig Göransson, and costume designer Ruth E. Carter. At the 98th Academy Awards, it received a record-tying 16 nominations, including Best Picture and Best Director, winning four awards: Best Actor (Michael B. Jordan), Best Original Screenplay, Best Cinematography, and Best Original Score.
tmdb:123365: Directed by Yasuji Yabushita with animation direction by Akira Daikuhara for Toei Animation's 10th anniversary film. Based on the heroic epic 'Beowulf,' this version features Jack driving a car, a witch arriving by helicopter, and a struggle to rescue comrades turned into demons in the witch's castle. Seiichiro Uno's cheerful music won the Mainichi Film Concours Music Award.
tmdb:1235870: Known as a masterpiece by early Showa period master Tomu Uchida, who died at just 28, this period drama stars Denjiro Okochi as the ronin Tange Sazen. Tange Sazen, a ronin living at an archery range and working as a bodyguard, and the proprietress Ofuji take in Chobian, the son of a man stabbed to death at the shop. Chobian carries a certain pot around carefully, using it as a goldfish bowl, but it actually contains a hidden map to a million ryo. This is one of only three surviving films by Uchida, most of whose original prints have been lost. It was remade in 2004 as "Tange Sazen: The Million Ryo Pot" starring Etsushi Toyokawa.
tmdb:123867: Mimiko-chan, Pan-chan, and Papanda lived happily together every day. Then, one day, while Mimiko-chan and the others were out, two suspicious characters showed up... When Mimiko-chan returned, she was delighted, saying, "It's my first time seeing burglars!" but the pair ran away in a flash. Mimiko-chan was a little disappointed that the seemingly interesting guests had gone, but Pan-chan noticed that his food had been eaten. Pan-chan sniffed around the house searching. Crawling into Pan-chan's bed and sleeping soundly was... a tiger cub! Both of them were so surprised they ran around the house making a huge commotion...
tmdb:1239041: A Hong Kong youth film vividly depicting the changes and growth of three young people with hearing impairments. Sophie, in her 20s, lost her hearing at age 3 and uses a cochlear implant to live a "normal" life as a "hearing person." Jason, born deaf, lives proudly as a sign language user. Alan, also a cochlear implant user, is bilingual in sign and spoken language. Jason and Alan met at a deaf school that banned sign language and promoted oral education; despite recognizing their different circumstances, they remained close friends into adulthood. When Alan and Sophie meet as ambassadors promoting cochlear implants, Jason becomes furious at Sophie's statement at a promotion event: "If science advances, there will be no deaf people in this world." John Shiuin, known for "Aspiring Lyricist" and "Kill the Twilight," plays Sophie and also wrote the lyrics for Panther Chan's theme song "What If." Directed by Adam Wong, highly acclaimed for "The Way We Dance" and "The Way We Keep Dancing." Won Best Leading Actress (John Shiuin) at the 61st Golden Horse Awards in 2024, and received a Special Mention at the 20th Osaka Asian Film Festival in 2025.
tmdb:1241436:
"Civil War" director Alex Garland joins forces with co-director Ray Mendoza—a former U.S. Special Forces member and military advisor on Garland’s previous film—for this visceral war action drama. Based on Mendoza’s real-life experiences during the Iraq War, the film recreates the extreme conditions of the front lines with unflinching realism.

2006, Ramadi, Iraq. An eight-man U.S. Special Forces platoon is tasked with the surveillance and sniping of a high-ranking Al-Qaeda operative. However, the enemy detects their presence sooner than anticipated and launches a preemptive strike, triggering a full-scale urban confrontation. With their escape route cut off, the platoon is completely surrounded as casualties mount. The situation descends into absolute chaos: some abandon their command, others lose contact with headquarters, and screams fill the air. As the shell-shocked soldiers struggle to drag their wounded comrades to safety, a relentless hail of gunfire continues to rain down upon them.
tmdb:1242015: An ensemble drama by Belgian masters Jean-Pierre and Luc Dardenne, known for "The Child" and "The Kid with a Bike," depicting five young mothers living in a mother-child support facility. The five girls—Jessica, Perla, Ariane, Julie, and Naima—live together in a facility that supports women who became pregnant young. Without anyone to rely on and facing various problems like poverty and violence, they become mothers while confused, troubled, and unable to find a model for the family they should aim for. Struggling not to be swallowed by the overwhelming loneliness, the girls who still wish "to love" sometimes lean on others and choose their own paths to follow. Lukas Dhont, director of "Close," is listed as a co-producer. Screened in the Competition section of the 78th Cannes Film Festival in 2025, it won the Best Screenplay Award and the Ecumenical Jury Prize.
tmdb:1245255: Directed and written by Fukuoka Sawako of the filmmaking unit "Shidoromodori," which gained attention for "I Still Don't Know You," this drama humorously depicts the relatable struggles of a woman in her twenties, based on her own experiences. Shizuoka Sumiko, 22, realizes that her senses have somehow become vague. Since then, she spends her days having conversations with herself. She realizes that her family's cat is very important to her, that after trying hard to fit into an uncomfortable space she needs to eat delicious chocolate, and that she's bothered by people wearing white skinny jeans that show their underwear. When she tries to remember the previous day while hungover, she ends up remembering things she didn't need to. After quitting the company she joined after graduating university in just four months, Sumiko spends her days in her new life, confirming the things she truly believes. Hori Haruna (from "Hamabe no Game") stars in a lead film role for the first time in five years, with Hamada Satsuki (a member of "Shidoromodori" who also served as assistant director on this film) and Matsuo Shohei (from "Lost Baby Lost") co-starring.
tmdb:1249236: A documentary co-directed by German filmmaker Andreas Hartmann and Berlin/Tokyo-based video artist Arata Mori, exploring the Japanese phenomenon of "evaporation" (disappearance). In Japan, approximately 80,000 people go missing each year, with thousands vanishing completely. Known as "evaporated people," their reasons range from relationship troubles and debt to yakuza threats. Some, with the help of so-called "night escape artists," abandon all ties and start new lives elsewhere. "Evaporation," intersecting deep loss and the hope of starting over, has been a motif in literature and film. This work uses immersive imagery to delve into the unknown work of "night escape artists" and the emotional conflicts and paths to reconciliation for both the disappeared and those left behind. It garnered attention at film festivals worldwide, winning Best Documentary at the 39th Munich International Documentary Film Festival.
tmdb:125217: Saheiji, left penniless at a Shinagawa pleasure quarter at the end of the Edo period... A masterpiece by Kawashima and Frankie, and a classic in Japanese film history. In this ensemble comedy where late-Edo period patriots and courtesans mingle, Frankie's light and agile movements as he navigates through the chaos are the film's core.
tmdb:125251: Set in Mukojima, Tokyo, during the Taisho era. Siblings Gen and Aoiro live with their writer father and stepmother. Gen takes care of Aoiro, covering for their sick stepmother, but Aoiro starts hanging out with a bad crowd. They protect each other at times and have big fights at others, living together as siblings, until Aoiro falls ill with tuberculosis.
tmdb:1253000: From Steven Kostanski, the mad genius director of "Psycho Goreman" (2020) and member of Canada's notorious effects collective Astron-6, who has contributed special effects to Hollywood blockbusters like "Resident Evil: Retribution" (2012) and "Pacific Rim" (2013). His two latest films, "Frankie Freako" and "Deathstalker," will be released sequentially in Japan starting July 3rd at Cinemart Shinjuku and other theaters nationwide. Kostanski, who wrote and directed both films, is known for his unique creature designs reminiscent of classics like "E.T." (1982), "Gremlins" (1984), and "The Goonies" (1985), blending 80s-style monster panic with absurdist black humor, creating a devoted fanbase. These new films bring his signature style to Japan. "Deathstalker" is a reboot of the 1984 cult classic "Deathstalker" (executive produced by Roger Corman). It reconstructs the sword-and-sorcery world with Kostanski's signature nightmarish horror and gore, infused with comedy and darkness. Daniel Bernhardt ("The Matrix Reloaded," "John Wick") stars as the titular Deathstalker. Slash, guitarist of Guns N' Roses, contributes to production and music. Synopsis: In a chaotic world ruled by sword and sorcery, the kingdom of Abraxion suffers under attacks from the sudden appearance of the crimson knight order, the Dread Knights, and is in decline. Unsettling rumors spread that this war is a precursor to the resurrection of the ancient sorcerer Necromemnon. Amidst this, the insolent wandering warrior Deathstalker comes into possession of a cursed amulet, making him a target for the Dread Knight's assassins. To break the curse and repel the approaching evil, Deathstalker embarks on a perilous journey, eventually being drawn into a battle that will decide the fate of the world.
tmdb:125368: A black comedy directed by Kon Ichikawa and scripted by Natto Wada, weaving together a philandering man, his wife, and nine lovers. TV producer Matsukichi Kazama, despite having a beautiful wife named Futaba, is cheating with nine women. The wife and lovers are vaguely aware of each other's existence and fully know that Matsukichi is a womanizer, yet for some reason they cannot leave him. One day, the wife and a stage actress lover named Ichiko come up with a plan to kill Matsukichi. It is a fictional scheme meant to vent their frustration with him, but timid Matsukichi becomes convinced that his lovers are trying to kill him and consults his wife. The wife readily admits to the plan and then, to eliminate the lovers, suggests staging a fake murder: they gather the lovers for a meeting to denounce Matsukichi, and at that gathering, pretend to shoot him dead with a pistol.
tmdb:1254808: From the director of "Boyhood" and the "Before" series, Richard Linklater, comes a film that goes behind the scenes of Jean-Luc Godard's "Breathless"—a landmark work of the French New Wave, the revolutionary film movement that emerged in the late 1950s. It depicts the young people who sparked a revolution in film history, along with their vibrant interactions with the leading filmmakers of French cinema. In 1959, France. Jean-Luc Godard, a 28-year-old critic writing for the film magazine "Cahiers du Cinéma," begins production on his feature directorial debut, "Breathless," starring French up-and-coming actor Jean-Paul Belmondo and American starlet Jean Seberg. Those around him are thrown off by Godard's innovative and freewheeling shooting methods, but the set, fueled by a shared passion for filmmaking, is filled with energy. Following the style of "Breathless," the film is shot in black and white in the Academy ratio (1:1.37), almost entirely in French, and the cast, except for Zoey Deutch as Jean Seberg, is made up of mostly unknown actors. Guillaume Marbeck, who worked as a photographer and model, was cast as the protagonist Godard. The film was selected for the Competition section of the 78th Cannes Film Festival in 2025.
tmdb:1257009: A survival action film depicting a deadly battle between dinosaurs that suddenly appear in the jungles of the Vietnam War and the U.S. military. In 1968, amidst the intense Vietnam War, the elite 'Viper Squad' of the U.S. Army Green Berets, on a special mission, goes missing in the jungle. The U.S. 'Vulture Platoon,' dispatched to search for them, encounters deep in the jungle a horde of dinosaurs, including Tyrannosaurus and Triceratops. Facing attacks from land, river, and air, the Vulture Platoon members engage in a fierce battle against the dinosaurs. Directed by Luke Sparke, an up-and-coming Australian filmmaker who single-handedly handled the script, production, editing, and art direction. Dale Dye, a retired Marine who served in the Vietnam War and appeared in 'Platoon' and 'Saving Private Ryan,' supervised the script, adding realism to the war film.
tmdb:1257374: Set in a supermarket after closing, this film depicts complex human relationships through a continuous stream of idle chatter. Actor Jun Hosoi planned, directed, and starred in the project, with Nanami Hidaka also serving as planner and co-star. They are joined by a talented supporting cast including An Ogawa, Ryohei Higashino, and Seiichi Kohinata. The film won the Audience Award in the Japanese Short Film Competition at the SKIP City International D-Cinema Festival 2024. Following a double Acting Award win (Jun Hosoi and Nanami Hidaka) and a positive reception at MOOSIC LAB 2025, the film has now been set for a one-week solo theatrical release.
tmdb:1258490: A love story starring Sungmo and Jihyuk of the popular K-pop group "Supernova," set against the rich natural backdrop of Chuncheon City, also known as a filming location for "Winter Sonata." It depicts a young man who has lost his words meeting a loved one and finding hope to live again. Teo, a piano tuner with a speech disorder caused by aftereffects of brain tumor surgery, meets Inha, a former popular singer who has lost her sight due to retinitis pigmentosa and is recuperating in a small village in Chuncheon. Unable to speak, Teo plays the piano to accompany Inha's singing, which leads Inha to open her heart to him. However, Inha's ex-lover Romy appears to take her back, and Inha ends up returning to Seoul. The director is Han Sang-hee, who directed "First Snow's Love: Virgin Snow" starring Lee Joon-gi and Aoi Miyazaki.
tmdb:1258509: In a small rural town in Iceland, artist Anna lives with her responsible eldest daughter Ida, her mischievous twin sons Grímur and Þorgils, and her dog Panda, while searching for her path as an artist. Though she married young and is supposedly "no longer a couple" with her ex-husband Magnús, he can't seem to cut ties, constantly finding excuses to visit, share meals, and even join picnics. Before she knows it, they slip back into a daily life as if they were "still a family"—but what comes next?
tmdb:126150: Péro, a restaurant waiter in a certain town, gets into an argument with the arrogant Lord Groumon and makes a bet: "I'll travel around the world in eighty days. If I fail, I'll become Groumon's slave." Pursued by time, Péro continues his arduous journey with a father-and-son mouse duo and Carter, the restaurant's cook, but is obstructed by Dr. Garigari, Lord Groumon's henchman, and the mysterious beauty Susanna.
tmdb:1263012: Tony Kiritsis (Bill Skarsgård), a middle-aged single man living in Indianapolis, believing he was swindled out of his entire life savings by the mortgage company Meridian Mortgage, breaks into their office and takes the president's son and executive, Dick Hall (Dacre Montgomery), hostage. Using a device called a "dead man's wire"—a shotgun and wire rigged to his and the hostage's necks so that any sudden movement would trigger the gun—he demands an apology and compensation from the company. With the local police completely unable to act, Tony calls a popular radio show to expose Meridian Mortgage's wrongdoing, involving the show's DJ Fred Temple (Coleman Domingo) to broadcast his claims. The mortgage company's representative issues a statement on TV accepting Tony's demands, but Tony refuses, insisting that the president, M.L. Hall, must apologize in person first. As the situation shows no sign of improvement, the FBI arrives and begins profiling Tony, while police prepare for a raid. Suspicion of a bomb on the scene brings in a bomb squad, tightening the net around Tony. Meanwhile, Tony's next move is to call in the three major US networks and other media to the scene, holding a press conference with the dead man's wire still pointed at Dick. Tony's appeal through the media divides public opinion and throws America into chaos.
tmdb:1264805: Summer 2008, Seoul. University students Uno and Jeong-won meet fatefully on a long-distance bus. Uno, who dreams of becoming a game creator, and Jeong-won, who aspires to be an architect. Supporting each other through their urban days filled with dreams and anxieties, they eventually fall in love, deeply and truly. However, faced with the harshness of reality that youth cannot resist, they choose to part ways. Ten years later, in the summer of 2024, they coincidentally reunite on a flight to Seoul. As they look back on their memories, Uno asks Jeong-won a question he has kept buried deep in his heart: 'What if, back then...'
tmdb:1265692: This documentary, the feature debut of Taiwanese director Wu Fan, captures the bond she forms with the unique Chinese dancer XiXi, whom she met by chance in Berlin, portraying the vibrant lives of two women. While studying in Europe from Taiwan, director Wu Fan meets XiXi, a Chinese contemporary dancer, in Berlin. Deeply drawn to XiXi, who dances like a free bird, Wu Fan begins filming her daily life. XiXi's journey, wandering Europe as a dancer in search of a free soul, appears beautiful to Wu Fan's eyes, like a wild bird unafraid to take flight. At the same time, XiXi lavishes love on her daughter Nina, whom she is allowed to see occasionally while staying in touch with her ex-husband Mederic. Eventually, Wu Fan's camera begins to capture the deep wounds hidden in XiXi's past. This becomes a catalyst for Wu Fan herself to confront her own family trauma. The film won the Emerging International Filmmaker Award at the Hot Docs Canadian International Documentary Festival 2024.
tmdb:1266127: The sequel to the survival horror "Ready or Not," in which bride Grace, targeted for death in a traditional wedding-night game, flees the mansion of a wealthy family. The stage expands further, depicting Grace being drawn into a power struggle among the ultra-rich who secretly control the world. Grace survived the blood-soaked game, but the nightmare wasn't over. Her survival catches the attention of the rulers who secretly manipulate the world, and she is once again chosen as a target. The stage is the forbidden realm known as the Council, where chosen noble families vie for supremacy. Representatives of six noble families, bound by a pact with the demon Le Bail, attack Grace with their ancestral weapons, tasked with killing her by dawn. Her only ally is her long-estranged sister Faith, but the two are chained together and unable to move freely. In this extreme situation, their family bond is put to the test as they fight to survive. Samara Weaving reprises her role as Grace. Kathryn Newton ("Abigail") joins as sister Faith, along with new cast members Sarah Michelle Gellar, David Cronenberg, and Elijah Wood. As with the previous film, directing duties were handled by Matt Bettinelli-Olpin and Tyler Gillett of the filmmaking unit Radio Silence.
tmdb:1266781:
France in the 1960s. Natasha is a free-spirited, slightly clumsy woman who dreams of becoming a flight attendant. However, it was an era when airlines demanded nothing less than physical perfection and submissiveness from women. Despite failing one recruitment test after another, she refuses to give up on her dream of taking to the skies. One day, while working as a temporary staff member for an art transport service, she unexpectedly finds herself assigned to a special flight carrying the legendary *Mona Lisa*. But when an unforeseen incident occurs mid-flight, Natasha is thrust into the greatest adventure of her life.

Starring Camille Lou, who brings a charming touch to the role of the lovable, dream-chasing heroine, the film features a stellar cast of legendary French actors, including Isabelle Adjani and Fabrice Luchini. A heartwarming comedy brimming with laughter, spirit, and courage that reminds us all of the "wings" we carry within—prepare for takeoff!

[Featured in "Movies We Haven't Experienced 2026"]
In theaters from Friday, January 16.
tmdb:1267905: Ivy and Theo are a picture-perfect couple who seem to have it all: stellar careers, a loving marriage, and gifted children. But behind the scenes, a domestic war is brewing. As Theo’s career takes a nosedive, Ivy’s true ambitions are laid bare. A biting black comedy where the hidden competitiveness and resentment of a "happy" couple finally explode.
tmdb:126863: A representative work of "structural film" that uses the early comedy *Tom, Tom, the Piper's Son* (1905)—which depicted the chaos of a festive crowd—as source material for re-photography. Through various visual effects such as zooming, panning, and high- and low-speed playback, it deconstructs the original meaning of the work, drawing the viewer’s eye toward the polysemic details and the materiality of the image. This critical interpretation of Billy Bitzer’s original version by Ken Jacobs (1933–2025), who relentlessly challenged the possibilities of cinematic expression, sparked international debate regarding the re-evaluation of early cinema.
tmdb:1269644: In 1945, at the end of World War II, the island of Amrum in northern Germany remained in a strange, paradise-like stillness even as bombers flew overhead toward the mainland. Naning, a 12-year-old boy evacuated there, supports his pregnant mother and family by helping with farm work in place of his father, who has not returned from the front. However, when his mother Hille, who is devoted to Hitler, collapses both mentally and physically upon receiving news of his death, Naning's daily life is transformed. Hille, drained of vitality and refusing food, desires only one thing: white bread generously spread with butter and honey.
tmdb:1272405: A wuxia fantasy action film directed by Taiwanese director Giddens Ko of 'The Secrets in the Lattice' and 'You Are the Apple of My Eye,' starring Ko Chen-tung, who collaborated with Ko on those two previous films. Director Giddens Ko, also active as a novelist, adapts his own internet-published novel 'Kung Fu' for the screen, weaving in homages to Hong Kong and Taiwanese wuxia films from the 1980s and 90s throughout. Underachieving high school student Yuan Zai and his best friend A Yi encounter a mysterious drifter, Huang Jun, who has awakened from a 500-year slumber. Witnessing Huang Jun's overwhelming martial arts prowess as a kung fu master, Yuan Zai and A Yi become his disciples. Their classmate Yi Jing, on whom Yuan Zai has a secret crush, also joins their training. They soon learn of the centuries-old feud between Huang Jun and his junior disciple Lan Jin, and uncover a momentous secret hidden within 'kung fu' that could shake heaven and earth. Ko Chen-tung plays Yuan Zai, Berant Zhu of 'Black Education' plays A Yi, Wang Jing of 'The Secrets in the Lattice' and 'The Return of the Condor Heroes' plays Yi Jing, veteran actor Tai Li-len plays the mysterious kung fu master Huang Jun, and Liu Kuan-ting of 'The Girl Who Robbed Time' plays Huang Jun's nemesis Lan Jin.
tmdb:1275240: A youth drama written and directed by Yoko Yamanaka, highly acclaimed for her directorial debut 'Amiko,' which made her the youngest director ever invited to the Forum section of the Berlin International Film Festival. Starring Yuumi Kawai from 'The Girl in the Photograph,' it sharply portrays the love lives and struggles of contemporary Japanese youth. It won the FIPRESCI Prize at the Directors' Fortnight of the 77th Cannes Film Festival in 2024. For 21-year-old Kana, thinking about the future is too boring, and she doesn't even know what she wants out of life. She has no passion for anything, and even love is just a way to kill time. Her live-in boyfriend Honda tries to please her by paying rent and cooking, but as Kana grows closer to the confident creator Hayashi, she begins to feel Honda is a burden. Daikei Kaneko from 'See You at the Jogasaki Cart' and 'Summer Film' plays Hayashi, and Kanichiro from 'Okiku and the World' and 'Promised Land' plays Honda. The cast also includes Yuzumi Shintani, Ayumu Nakajima, Erika Karata, and Shiku Shibuya.
tmdb:1277872: Set in sun-drenched Southern France, this is a fresh and vivid youth drama about the inner conflicts and love of an adolescent boy living in the complex modern era. Enzo, a 16-year-old raised in a wealthy family in Southern France, struggles to fit in at school and works at a construction site. He becomes drawn to Vlad, a young Ukrainian man he meets there, but Vlad must go to war for his military service. Distrust towards his seemingly comfortable family, anxiety about the future, and the reality of war taking away those close to him. Unable to control his emotions, Enzo's summer passes quietly. Originally a project launched by director Laurent Cantet, known for "The Class," his ally Robin Campillo, known for "BPM (Beats Per Minute)," took over and completed the film after Cantet passed away in 2024 while battling cancer. Newcomer actor Eloi Poy, a former competitive swimmer, delicately portrays Enzo's inner turmoil. Pierfrancesco Favino, known for "The Traitor," and Élodie Bouchez, known for "The Dreamed Path," co-star as Enzo's parents. Amateur actor Maxime Slivinsky, who actually worked on construction sites, was cast as Vlad, the worker Enzo has a faint crush on.
tmdb:1279865: This animated film marks the feature directorial and screenwriting debut of Yoshitoshi Shinomiya, who has worked across genres primarily as a Nihonga (Japanese-style) painter. It is a Japan-France co-production with the cutting-edge French studio Miyu Productions. The 330-year-old Tategami Fireworks Factory, nestled in the woods, is facing eviction due to town redevelopment. Keitaro Tategami, who grew up there, has barricaded himself in the factory for four years, striving to complete the legendary "Shuhari" firework in place of his missing father, Eitaro. Meanwhile, Keitaro's childhood friend Kaoru Shikimori left their hometown for Tokyo after a past incident. Contacted by Keitaro's older brother Sentaro, who works at the city office, Kaoru visits the Tategami family on the last day of summer, the day before the eviction deadline, reuniting with Keitaro for the first time in four years. As they clash, trying to reclaim lost time and broken bonds, they hatch a surprising plan to uncover the secret of the phantom firework. The key lies in a beautiful blue pigment called "hanaryokusei" (copper acetoarsenite). Actors Rihito Noda and Kotone Furukawa make their voice acting debuts as Keitaro and Kaoru respectively, with voice actor Miyu Irino as Keitaro's brother Sentaro and actor Takashi Okabe as their father Eitaro. The film was selected for the Competition section of the 78th Berlin International Film Festival in 2026.
tmdb:1284120: Nordic gothic body horror has arrived! After premiering at the 41st Sundance Film Festival and sparking a "mass walkout" shockwave with its unpredictable plot and relentless, grotesque imagery, *Ugly Sister* is finally coming to theaters. A massive hit in its native Norway, where it spent four consecutive weeks in the Top 10, the film has been officially selected for
tmdb:128722: To save the daughter of an amazake shop owner from a dire situation, two rogues throw themselves into the fray. A masterpiece showcasing perfect chemistry between the renowned actors of Zenshinza and director Yamanaka. The beauty of a 15-year-old Setsuko Hara is captivating.
tmdb:1287819: A period comedy depicting a late-Edo period samurai who time-travels to a modern-day period drama studio and struggles as a sword-falling extra. In Kyoto at the end of the Edo period, Kosaka Shinzaemon, a retainer of the Aizu domain, receives a secret order from the chief retainer to kill a Choshu domain samurai, but at the moment his blade meets his target's, he is struck by lightning and loses consciousness. When he wakes up, he finds himself in a modern period drama studio. Shinzaemon causes commotions wherever he goes, and is stunned to learn that the Tokugawa shogunate fell 140 years ago. Resigned to death at first, he is helped by kind-hearted people and regains his will to live. Eventually, relying only on his polished swordsmanship, he knocks on the studio's door and decides to live as a sword-falling extra. Starring Makiya Yamaguchi, who has appeared in numerous period dramas including the TV series "Kenkaku Shobai," with Norimasa Tomiya and Yuno Sakura co-starring. Directed and written by Junichi Yasuda ("Gohan," "Kenju to Medamayaki"), it was completed with special cooperation from Toei Kyoto Studio despite being an independent production. Released exclusively at Ikebukuro Cinema Rosa on August 17, 2024 (a "Deluxe Version" with added scenes began screening at Kawasaki Cinecitta from August 30), word of mouth spread, and from September 13 of the same year, with Gaga as co-distributor, it expanded to over 100 theaters nationwide including Shinjuku Piccadilly and Toho Cinemas Hibiya. It became an unprecedented hit for an independent film and achieved the feat of winning the Best Picture award at the 48th Japan Academy Film Prize.
tmdb:1288072: A horror film directed by Osgood Perkins of "Longlegs" fame, depicting extreme terror closing in on a woman brought to a mountain lodge by her lover, rendered in a mysterious, nightmarish world. Liz, an artist living in the city, is invited to a mountain lodge owned by her boyfriend Malcolm. Malcolm is a wealthy but somewhat enigmatic doctor, and for Liz, who wants to confirm his true feelings, this weekend trip to mark their first anniversary is supposed to be special. The lodge, reached by car driven by Malcolm, is in a remote area surrounded by dense forest. Nearby is another lodge owned by Malcolm's cousin Darren, who visits with his young lover Minka, but Liz feels repulsed by Darren's crude and intrusive manner. Encouraged by Malcolm, Liz eats a chocolate cake said to be a gift from the caretaker, and is plagued by strange nightmares and hallucinations. The next day, Malcolm is called away to the hospital for an emergency, leaving Liz alone at the lodge. Gripped by a vague unease, Liz is beset by one abnormal event after another, losing the boundary between reality and nightmare, and is threatened by the presence of something unknown stirring within the lodge. Tatiana Maslany, who also appeared in Perkins' previous film "The Monkey," plays the protagonist Liz, and Rossif Sutherland from "Orphan: First Kill" plays her boyfriend Malcolm.
tmdb:1290424: The Grande Arche, a monumental cube-shaped building in the La Défense district west of Paris, stands on the "Paris historical axis" stretching straight from the glass pyramid of the Louvre. Behind its completion lies the unknown story of an anonymous architect whose fate was shaken. Based on historical fact, this human drama immerses viewers in the bizarre life of an architect who challenged a national project while being tossed about by ideals and political maneuvering. An ensemble of talented actors lends the film credibility, earning it a selection in the Un Certain Regard section of the 78th Cannes Film Festival and eight César Award nominations. This architectural drama resonates with debates surrounding Japan's National Stadium and the Osaka Expo. In 1983 Paris, President Mitterrand envisioned a new monument to celebrate the bicentennial of the French Revolution. The international design competition selected the unknown Danish architect Johan Otto von Spreckelsen. His bold plan—a cube-shaped arch of Italian Carrara marble with a cloud-like roof floating at its base—captured the president's heart and made him an overnight sensation. However, budget constraints, political pressure, and the expectations of those around him stood in the way of his pursuit of perfection. Should he stick to his ideals or compromise with reality? Caught in the vortex of a massive project, what "certain decision" will one architect make?
tmdb:1290432: Oscar-winning actress Jodie Foster, known for 'The Accused' and 'The Silence of the Lambs', stars in her first French-language film in this mystery. Lilian, a successful American psychoanalyst practicing in Paris, receives news that Paula, a long-time patient, has died. Suspicious of Paula's death, Lilian suspects murder but cannot involve the police due to patient confidentiality. She decides to uncover the truth herself. Meanwhile, since learning of Paula's death, Lilian has been troubled by uncontrollable crying, regardless of the situation, and visits her ex-husband Gabriel, an ophthalmologist. Though the cause of her tears remains unclear, Gabriel agrees to help Lilian investigate Paula's case. As she embarks on a detective-like investigation, Lilian delves into dangerous truths. Foster plays the protagonist, psychoanalyst Lilian, entirely in French. Daniel Auteuil, known for 'La Belle Époque', plays her ex-husband and investigative partner Gabriel. Virginie Efira from 'Suddenly Sick' and Mathieu Amalric from 'Quantum of Solace' co-star. The film is directed by Rebecca Zlotowski, known for 'Grand Central' and 'Planetarium'.
tmdb:1291712: Based on the global bestseller "The Taster" written from the testimony of German woman Margot Wolk, this drama portrays the fate of women forced by the Nazis to be Hitler's food tasters. It captures the horrors of war from a female perspective and the shifting relationships among the women who share their daily lives as tasters. In 1943, near the end of World War II, Rosa flees the bombing of Berlin and waits for her husband's return from the front in a Polish village, close to the forest where Hitler's Wolf's Lair headquarters is located. One day, Rosa is ordered to taste Hitler's food before he eats, and along with other young women, she is forced under SS guard at gunpoint to consume the meals. They endure the torment of sampling the finest dishes prepared for Hitler in a life-threatening situation. In July 1944, a coup attempt to assassinate Hitler at the Wolf's Lair plunges the war into further chaos. Elisa Schlott, star of the Netflix series "The Empress," plays Rosa, with Max Riemelt of "The Matrix Resurrections" co-starring as an SS officer. Italian director Silvio Soldini, known for "Emma's Eyes" and "Love in Venice," directs.
tmdb:12924: Makoto Shinkai, who rose to prominence with his fully digital personal animation "Voices of a Distant Star" in 2002, makes his feature-length directorial debut. Set in post-war Japan divided north and south by the Tsugaru Strait, it depicts boys struggling to save a girl burdened with the world's mysteries. In Japan under US military rule, middle school students Hiroki Fujisawa and Takuya Shirakawa in Aomori admire a giant tower standing across the strait in Hokkaido, and secretly work on assembling an airplane at an abandoned station site, dreaming of one day reaching that tower. One summer vacation, they confide their airplane secret to their classmate Sayuri Sawatari, another object of their admiration. The three share the dream of reaching the tower together, enjoying a brief period of happiness, but in the summer of their third year of middle school, Sayuri transfers away without explanation. The dream of reaching the tower by plane fades, and three years pass. Hiroki and Takuya, having gone their separate ways, reunite when dark clouds gather over the world situation and the tower's secrets gradually come to light. Voice cast includes actors Hidetaka Yoshioka and Masato Hagiwara.
tmdb:1293858: The second feature from Belgian director Laura Wandel, who gained attention with her 2021 debut 'Playground', is a human suspense drama depicting one night's events surrounding a 4-year-old boy hospitalized in a pediatric ward and his mother, told from the perspective of a nurse trying to support them. Four-year-old Adam is admitted to a pediatric center with a broken left arm. Malnourished and underdeveloped, his bones are brittle. The court rules that Rebecca, an immigrant single mother, has not been providing Adam with proper nutrition and issues an order restricting her visits. Nurse manager Lucie, herself a single mother, tries to support Rebecca, who fears losing custody and being separated from her son. But Rebecca's reckless actions and pressure from superiors and colleagues push Lucie into a corner. Léa Drucker ('Close') plays nurse Lucie, torn between her desire to save the mother and child and the judicial system the hospital must follow. Anamaria Vartolomei ('Happening') plays isolated single mother Rebecca. The film is produced by Belgian masters Jean-Pierre and Luc Dardenne. It opened the Critics' Week at the 2025 Cannes Film Festival.
tmdb:1293968: A documentary by Guillaume Brac, director of 'A Summer's Tale' and 'The Gentle Ones,' capturing a summer at the leisure facility 'Leisure Island' in Cergy-Pontoise, a suburb of Paris. Known as the setting for Éric Rohmer's 'My Girlfriend's Boyfriend,' and a place Brac himself frequently visited as a child, Leisure Island is filled with vacationers but has no flashy attractions, only expanses of water and greenery. Under beautiful sunlight, the film captures the natural moments of various people: boys trying to sneak into the facility, young men hitting on women, an elderly man reminiscing about the past, and employees managing and guarding the place.
tmdb:1295026: Togashi, born with natural speed, has always used it to gain friends and a place to belong. Meanwhile, transfer student Komiya runs recklessly, trying to forget his painful reality. Togashi teaches Komiya how to run faster, and after school the two practice together. Finding something to devote himself to, Komiya greedily chases new records. Gradually, through the 100-meter dash, their relationship grows into something between rivals and best friends.
tmdb:1295035: On August 19, 2023, Sano and Miyata visit a seaside resort hotel in Izu. Sano had recently lost his wife Nagi, whom he had met and fallen in love with there five years earlier. Miyata, as a friend, tries to advise Sano, who is clinging to memories of his wife and becoming self-destructive, but Miyata's words, steeped in a certain seminar he is devoted to, do not reach Sano. Exchanging few words, the two visit the now-closed restaurant and sightseeing boat filled with memories, and begin searching for the red hat that was lost long ago.
tmdb:1295400: Danish director Anders Thomas Jensen, known for writing "Riders of Justice," "The Good Life," and "After the Wedding," delivers a human drama starring his frequent collaborator Mads Mikkelsen. After serving time for a robbery, Anker is released and reunites with his brother Manfred, who hid a large sum of money during the heist, for the first time in 15 years. However, Manfred not only has forgotten the hiding place but also believes he is John Lennon. The two set out on a journey to find the bag of hidden money, but the trip gradually transforms into a journey of self-reflection for both of them. Mikkelsen plays Manfred, who has lost his memory and believes he is John Lennon, embodying this eccentric and unique character. Anker is played by Nikolaj Lie Kaas, another frequent collaborator of Jensen's. The film had its world premiere in the Out of Competition section of the 2025 Venice International Film Festival and became a massive hit in its native Denmark, breaking the country's all-time box office record for a live-action film.
tmdb:129713: Set in 1960s Kyoto, this is a youth ensemble drama depicting the love and friendship between Japanese and Zainichi Korean high school students. Based on Takeshi Matsuyama's autobiographical novel "Shonen M no Imujin-gawa," it was directed and written by Kazuyuki Izutsu, known for "Kishiwada Shonen Gurentai" and "Get Up!" In 1968, Kyoto. Kosuke Matsuyama, a second-year student at Furitsu Higashi High School, is ordered by his homeroom teacher to go to a Korean high school, where student conflicts are frequent, to propose a practice soccer match. Reluctantly visiting the Korean school with his friend Norio, Kosuke falls in love at first sight with Kyongja, who is playing the flute in the music room. However, she is the sister of Anson, the boss of the Korean high school. Desperate to get closer to Kyongja, Kosuke diligently studies Korean and buys a guitar at a music store to learn the song "Imujin-gawa" that she was playing... Shioya Shun plays Kosuke, Sawajiri Erika plays Kyongja, and Takaoka Sosuke plays Anson.
tmdb:1299655: From director Richard Linklater, known for the 'Before' trilogy beginning with 'Before Sunrise' and the six-time Oscar-nominated 'Boyhood,' this conversation piece stars his longtime collaborator Ethan Hawke and depicts a night spent at a party attended by legendary Broadway lyricist Lorenz Hart. On the evening of March 31, 1943, the night of the premiere of the musical 'Oklahoma!,' created by his longtime composing partner Richard Rodgers with a new collaborator, Lorenz Hart—the lyricist behind hits like 'The Lady Is a Tramp' and 'My Funny Valentine'—was invited to a party at the Broadway restaurant Sardi's. Over the course of that night, Hart confronts his own swirling emotions of love, jealousy, anxiety, and longing. Ethan Hawke plays Lorenz Hart, alongside Margaret Qualley as Elizabeth, the woman Hart pines for; Andrew Scott as his former partner Richard Rodgers; and Bobby Cannavale as Eddie, the bartender Hart trusts as a confidant. The film was screened in the competition section of the 75th Berlin International Film Festival in 2025, where Andrew Scott won the Silver Bear for Best Supporting Actor. It was nominated for Best Original Screenplay and Best Actor (Ethan Hawke) at the 98th Academy Awards.
tmdb:1301421: An unconventional mystery film starring Hugh Jackman, depicting sheep whose beloved owner is murdered as they struggle to find the culprit. In a peaceful English countryside town, shepherd George lives alone surrounded by his beloved sheep. He reads detective novels to them every night, and the sheep actually understand the stories and look forward to this time. One day, George is found dead. The sheep refuse to believe it was an accident and, led by their smartest leader Lily, launch an investigation. As they follow clues, they discover George had a huge inheritance. Determined to avenge their beloved George, the sheep race to find the killer. Hugh Jackman plays the victimized shepherd George, with Oscar-winning actress Emma Thompson, Nicholas Galitzine from "The Idea of You," and Nicholas Braun from the TV series "Succession" co-starring. Julia Louis-Dreyfus, Patrick Stewart, and Bryan Cranston voice the sheep. Based on the 2005 bestselling novel of the same name by German author Leonie Swann, directed by Kyle Balda of the "Minions" series.
tmdb:130279: In the late Qing dynasty, the villainous Im Kun-ho rules over Gold Sand Village, a place rife with all kinds of crime and violence, including drugs and human trafficking. The Dragon group, traveling while punishing evil, and at the same time, the legendary female martial artist Eagle, arrive in this village. They are both searching for a treasure called the 'Silver Pearl', said to have been stolen from a Tibetan temple. Then, the ruthless killer karate practitioner Black Jaguar also appears, and fierce battles unfold among the powerful fighters over the Silver Pearl. This is the Japan comeback film for Yasuaki Kurata, who was active primarily in Hong Kong.
tmdb:1303613: A Spanish film that delicately portrays the story of a woman living in a world without sound and her family. Ángela, who is deaf, and her husband Héctor, who gently supports her, communicate through the irreplaceable language of sign language. Ángela works in a pottery workshop, surrounded by the comforting smell of clay and trusted colleagues, living a quiet and peaceful life. However, a certain 'happy event' begins to gradually shatter her daily life. As she wavers in her sense of alienation, Ángela tries to grasp the 'true happiness' that flickers between the silent world and the world outside... Directed by emerging filmmaker Eva Libertad, who also works as a playwright and sociologist, this film is based on her highly acclaimed 2021 short film 'Sorda.' Starring Miriam Garlo, a deaf actress and Libertad's real sister, the film reflects the director and her sister's long-standing personal experiences, capturing the subtle misunderstandings between deaf and hearing people and the different feelings of alienation each holds. It won the Panorama Audience Award and the Art Cinema Award at the 75th Berlin International Film Festival in 2025, as well as the Golden Biznaga (Best Film), Audience Award, Best Actress, and Best Actor at the 28th Málaga Film Festival in Spain.
tmdb:1306400: A filmed recording of the Broadway musical 'Merrily We Roll Along,' which won four Tony Awards, screened in theaters. Based on the play of the same name by George S. Kaufman and Moss Hart, this musical, which premiered in 1981, features music by the legendary Stephen Sondheim, creator of numerous masterpieces including 'Sweeney Todd.' The story depicts the tumultuous 30-year relationship between Frank, a successful Hollywood producer; Mary, a former best-selling author; and Charlie, a Pulitzer Prize-winning playwright, told in reverse chronological order. This recording captures the 2023–24 Broadway production starring Maria Friedman, which was a huge hit. Jonathan Groff, known for the Netflix series 'Mindhunter' and as the voice of Kristoff in Disney's 'Frozen,' plays producer Frank; Daniel Radcliffe of the 'Harry Potter' series plays playwright Charlie; and Lindsay Mendez, a veteran of numerous Broadway musicals, plays former best-selling author Mary. At the 2024 Tony Awards, the production won Best Revival of a Musical, Best Actor in a Musical (Jonathan Groff), Best Featured Actor in a Musical (Daniel Radcliffe), and Best Orchestrations.
tmdb:1314245: The first feature film directed by Kohei Igarashi, a filmmaker gaining international attention for works like "Oyogisugita Yoru" and "Ikoi no Iki," made while he was a student at Tokyo Zokei University. Young couple Amano and Inaba live together, but life is tough because Inaba has lost his job. Still, Inaba doesn't work, and at night he goes out, meeting friends who treat him, or learning poetry from a cigarette seller. Amano says nothing to Inaba about this, simply watching over him. Then one day, Inaba hears from a friend about "a good job at the hospital"... The film received its theatrical premiere at the "Kohei Igarashi Director Retrospective: Seishun-teki Koto" (from September 20, 2024, at Shimokita-Ekimae-Cinema K2), held in conjunction with the release of Igarashi's feature "SUPER HAPPY FOREVER."
tmdb:1314481: A sequel to the 2006 hit film "The Devil Wears Prada," based on the bestselling novel of the same name by American author Lauren Weisberger, set 20 years later. Miranda rules the fashion world as the charismatic editor-in-chief of New York's top fashion magazine "Runway." Andrea, who was once hired as her assistant and endured grueling days under her strict perfectionism, now works as a news reporter. One day, learning that Miranda and her right-hand man Nigel are facing a crisis, Andrea returns to "Runway" as a features editor. She also reunites with her former assistant colleague Emily, who has become an executive at a luxury brand and holds the key to "Runway's" survival. As their dreams and ambitions clash, events take an unexpected turn. The cast reunites from the previous film, including Meryl Streep as Miranda, Anne Hathaway as Andrea, Emily Blunt as Emily, and Stanley Tucci as Nigel. David Frankel returns as director, and Aline Brosh McKenna as screenwriter.
tmdb:1315054: Part 2 is suffering. No money. Money stolen. It’s enough to break your heart. The Lunar New Year is fast approaching. China. Zhili, the town of children's clothing. The story of the young people unfolding in its garment factories grows increasingly dramatic. Yun keeps making mistakes; his colleagues are fed up, and he no longer wants to work. Wanxiang has lost the ledger, and the boss tells him he cannot pay his wages. He saw the boss beating a business partner. At another factory, the owner has absconded with all the assets. Days of bitter negotiations follow. The youths return to their hometowns to celebrate the Lunar New Year. Here, the fate of a generation emerges—one that even fellow Chinese living in cities like Beijing or Shanghai know nothing about.
tmdb:1315057: Korean master Hong Sang-soo directs an ensemble drama set at a women's university in Seoul, depicting the romantic entanglements of students and adults surrounding a theater festival. At a women's university in Seoul, with the theater festival approaching, textile artist Jon-hee, who works as a lecturer, invites her uncle Si-on, a famous actor and stage director, as a temporary director to fill a gap caused by a love scandal on campus. As they begin creating a short play for the festival, various events unfold over ten days, including the aftermath of the students' love affairs and the budding romance between a senior professor and Si-on. Actress Kim Min-hee, Hong Sang-soo's partner in both public and private life, stars as Jon-hee and won the Best Performance Award at the 77th Locarno International Film Festival in 2024. The cast also includes regulars from Hong Sang-soo's films: Kwon Hae-hyo as Jon-hee's uncle Si-on, Cho Yun-hee as the professor who admires Si-on, and Ha Seong-guk as the fired director who was dating three people. In Japan, it was screened under the title 'Suyuchon' at the 25th Tokyo Filmex in 2024. It was theatrically released in 2025 as the second film in the 'Monthly Hong Sang-soo' project, a series of five consecutive monthly new releases celebrating the director's 30th debut anniversary.
tmdb:1315477: Based on the 'Jeju April 3 Incident,' a massacre in which nearly 30,000 people are said to have been killed but which was covered up for a long time, this drama depicts the flight of a mother and daughter desperately trying to survive while being driven into a corner by unreasonable violence. On April 3, 1948, the 'Jeju April 3 Incident' began when some islanders on Jeju Island, opposed to interference by foreign forces, staged an armed uprising. From October of the same year, the government designated areas more than 5 kilometers from the coastline as 'hostile zones' and issued a proclamation stating, 'Anyone entering or leaving will be shot without condition.' To escape disaster, the villagers head for Hallasan Mountain, which rises in the center of Jeju Island. A-jin, a woman who has to leave the village temporarily, is extremely worried about her 6-year-old daughter Hye-sen, whom she left behind. Meanwhile, in the village, the South Korean army is mercilessly shooting the elderly. Surviving, Hye-sen heads into the mountains alone to find her mother. After miraculously reuniting, the mother and daughter embark on a life-or-death escape to survive. Directed and written by Ha Myeong-mi, who built her career as a screenwriter for commercial films, it vividly portrays the nameless people tossed about by state power. Kim Hyang-gi, known for 'Along with the Gods' and 'Innocent Witness,' stars as A-jin.
tmdb:1315772: The third installment in the 'Minions' animated film series, an adventure comedy featuring the popular characters born from Illumination's 'Despicable Me' franchise as the main protagonists. The Minions, continuing their quest for the most powerful and evil boss, arrive in Hollywood, the city of dreams. Getting into a movie studio by chance, they eagerly decide to make their own monster movie and attempt to summon a real monster. The first to appear is an unexpectedly small green monster, but soon, extremely dangerous monsters are unleashed upon the city one after another, throwing Hollywood into chaos. Adding to the mayhem, a rift forms among the Minions themselves, putting them in an unprecedented crisis. Directed by Pierre Coffin, known for the 'Minions' and 'Despicable Me' series. The screenplay is co-written by Brian Lynch, who worked on Illumination's 'Pets' series, and Coffin. In the Japanese dub, Matsudaira Ken voices film director Max, Chiba Yudai voices the new boss candidate Dott, Suzuki Airi voices Debbie, who falls in love with Dott, and Yamadera Koichi voices the mysterious monster Goomy. Comedy duo 'Batterys' members Ace and Ie are cast as the unique monsters Phillips and Howard, marking their voice acting debut. Additionally, singer LiSA joins the dub cast as a Hollywood actress.
