tmdb:1317288: A drama starring Timothée Chalamet, set in 1950s New York, inspired by the life of real-life table tennis player Marty Reisman. Marty Mauser, who dreams of becoming the world's number one table tennis player in America where the sport has low popularity, works at a relative's shoe store to raise funds to participate in the World Championships. After losing to Japanese player Endo at the World Championships held in London, Marty aims to compete in the next World Championships in Japan. With his mistress Rachel pregnant, his player eligibility revoked by the table tennis association, and his funds running out, Marty tries every possible way to raise money for the trip... Gwyneth Paltrow plays Kay, a retired famous actress; Grammy-winning artist Tyler Okonma, known as Tyler, The Creator, plays Marty's friend; Odessa A'zion plays Marty's girlfriend; Kevin O'Leary plays Milton, Kay's husband and president of an ink company; and Japanese Deaflympics table tennis representative Kōto Kawaguchi plays Japanese player Endo. Directed by Josh Safdie ("Uncut Gems," "Good Time"), the film was nominated for nine Academy Awards at the 98th ceremony, including Best Picture, Best Director, and Best Actor.
tmdb:1319196: Part 3: Homecoming. Returning home. Holding weddings. Living on. The sheer enormity of living. As the Lunar New Year holiday approaches, the garment factories of Zhili grow quiet. The few remaining workers head home, everyone seeking to celebrate the Spring Festival in their birthplace. Some hold weddings during the break. But there is no work in the hometown. In Mingyan’s home province of Yunnan, it is cold; even indoors, breath turns white and hands grow numb. When the holiday ends, the workers return to the factories. Some find their places of employment gone. The youthful voices of boys and girls echo—a new generation of young migrant workers has arrived at the factories. Here, the fate of a generation entirely unknown even to fellow Chinese living in cities like Beijing and Shanghai comes into focus.
tmdb:132148: Part 2 opens with the attempted coup of June 29, 1973, which was introduced at the end of Part 1. It was clear that this "attempted coup" served as a useful dress rehearsal for the military, and everyone began to realize that the "real thing" was only a matter of time. The left becomes divided over strategy, while the right steadily prepares for the military's seizure of power. Finally, on the morning of September 11, 1973, the coup is set in motion, and the presidential palace is bombed and destroyed by the military. After addressing the Chilean people via radio, Allende dies in what is believed to be a suicide. That same evening, members of the military junta, chaired by Augusto Pinochet, appear on television to announce the establishment of a new military regime.
tmdb:132150: The film follows ordinary workers and peasants as they collaborate to organize countless local groups collectively known as "Popular Power." They distribute food, occupy, manage, and guard factories and farmland, combat the profiteering black market, and coordinate with neighborhood social service organizations. These activities were initially launched as a means to counter strikes by anti-Allende factory owners, retailers, and professional associations. Eventually, "Popular Power" gradually transforms into Soviet-style socialist organizations that demand the government take a resolute stand against the right wing.
tmdb:1322562: The concluding chapter of the theatrical trilogy based on the TV anime "Mononoke," itself a spin-off from the "Bakeneko" segment of the 2006 Fuji TV Noitamina omnibus anime "Ayakashi." It delves into the greatest secret long hidden within the Ooku (the shogun's harem) and depicts the fierce battle between the protagonist, the Medicine Seller, and the most fearsome mononoke of all, the Serpent God, which threatens to shake the Ooku to its foundations. After a deadly struggle with the Medicine Seller, who carries a exorcism sword, and a Tengu umbrella, followed by a decisive battle with the Fire Rat, peace finally seems to have returned to the Ooku. However, the Medicine Seller senses a lingering presence and remains on guard. Around this time, the shogun's official wife, Sachiko, gives birth to a long-awaited son, but the infant soon dies. Sachiko, who had hoped to change her formal marriage to the shogun by bearing an heir, is physically and emotionally exhausted and becomes entangled in a conspiracy that could overturn the Ooku's very existence. Hokuto Mizorogi, the priest of the "Mizusama" faith within the Ooku, watches the events unfold with a solemn expression. At the same time, unnatural earthquakes, as if a giant creature is crawling, occur frequently within the Ooku, and bizarre incidents happen where maids are twisted and crushed to death. Before the Medicine Seller, who rushes to the scene, appears the mononoke Serpent God, taking the form of a giant snake.
tmdb:1325734: Charlie and Emma, who meet by fate at a Boston café, are living the happiest of days. On the night just seven days before their wedding, during dinner with their best friend couple who are also their attendants, they confess their worst past deeds. It starts as a lighthearted game, but everyone is utterly put off by Emma's 'worst secret.' Charlie begins to fear that Emma may have another side beyond his imagination. Their peak of happiness plummets into the depths of suspicion and paranoia, but there is no way to stop the wedding preparations, and the day finally arrives—.
tmdb:1326056: Set in early 2000s South Korea, when Japanese pop culture was restricted, this coming-of-age drama tenderly follows a shy transfer student and a popular class president who bond over J-Pop. In 2001, Gyung-hwan transfers to a high school in Daegu, Korea's most conservative city. A huge fan of then-taboo Japanese music and anime, he secretly listens to Japanese songs on his MP3 player during lunch. Teased as an 'otaku' by classmates, he discovers that his deskmate, class president Jae-min, also secretly loves Japanese culture. Sharing earphones on the bus after school while listening to J-Pop, they gradually grow closer. One day, Gyung-hwan confesses a secret to Jae-min, but afterward, Jae-min's attitude suddenly changes. Making his feature debut, director Eom Ha-nul wrote the script based on his own teenage experiences as a fan of Japanese culture, weaving in diverse Japanese pop culture from the 1990s. Shim Hyun-seo, a child actor known for 'The King of Pigs', plays transfer student Gyung-hwan, and Hyun Woo-seok, from 'The School Nurse Files', plays class president Jae-min. Gong Min-jung ('Kim Ji-young: Born 1982') and Lee Dong-hwi ('The Roundup: Punishment') co-star.
tmdb:1326354:
Winner of the Best Short Film Award at the 2025 New Zealand Screen Awards. Reckless young Mac decides to give his late friend's beat-up car, "Rochelle," one last moment in the spotlight. He heads to the local junk car race. At first his friends are exasperated, but soon they are moved by Mac's dream and begin to cheer him on in earnest...
■ Ticket price: 1,000 yen flat rate (Free tickets, invitation tickets, and other discounts are not applicable.)
■ Same-day discount at the box office: Present a ticket for another film viewed on the same day to receive 100 yen off. (Limited to tickets purchased at the box office on the day.)
Making movie theaters a more casual option. "20 Minute Cinema" is a new initiative screening short films of 15–20 minutes in theaters. A 20-minute stop you can drop into like a café between shopping or after work. Masterpieces from around the world you won't find on streaming services will add vibrant color to your daily life.
tmdb:1328409: A youth ensemble drama featuring all fourth-generation members of the popular idol group Hinatazaka46. Directed by the renowned Kumakiri Kazuyoshi, known for 'My Man' and '#Manhole,' it follows eleven unique high school girls on a school trip to Tokyo as they race through the big city to enjoy everything it has to offer. High school student Ikezono, visiting Tokyo on a school trip, meticulously plans a perfect itinerary to tour famous spots, intending to lead her group. However, on the long-awaited free day, the group inexplicably splits up, and Ikezono finds herself alone at the base of Tokyo Skytree. Determined to complete her plan, she sets out to explore Tokyo, but unbeknownst to her, her group members each have their own agendas for being in Tokyo. Shogenji Yoko, who served as center for Hinatazaka46's single 'Kimi wa Honeydew,' stars as the protagonist Ikezono, with all eleven fourth-generation members appearing. The screenplay is by Fukuda Shohei of the 'HiGH&LOW THE MOVIE' series and Tsuchiya Ryoichi of the film 'Osomatsu-san.' From the planning stage, they directly interviewed all eleven members, gathering memories from their school days, pre-idol stories, and feelings about Tokyo, crafting an original script woven from their real-life stories.
tmdb:13310: Oscar, a 12-year-old in the prime of playfulness but with not a single friend, falls in love for the first time with Eli, who moves in next door. With messy black hair and a pale face, Eli only ever appears at night, and the more Oscar learns about her, the more mysterious she becomes. Though she claims to be the same age as Oscar, she doesn't even know her own birthday. Around the same time Oscar meets Eli, gruesome murders begin occurring in succession, casting an uneasy air over the town. In the midst of this, Oscar discovers a grave secret: the shocking truth that Eli has been 12 years old for a very long time. Eli is a vampire who has survived for 200 years, moving from town to town and drinking human blood.
tmdb:133160: Near the end of the war, 100 middle-aged soldiers are called up. Their postings are decided by their superior officer's lottery. Realizing he won't return alive after being assigned to the Philippines, Morikawa Teizo asks Matsuyama Keita to deliver a postcard to his wife, Tomoko, and tell her he read it. After the war ends, only six soldiers, including Keita, survive. Based on the postcard, they visit Tomoko's house, but...
tmdb:1336502: A documentary following Ryusho Gushiken, who has spent over 40 years collecting the remains of those who died in the Battle of Okinawa. It is said that nearly 3,000 sets of remains—of local residents, former Japanese soldiers, American soldiers, and people from the Korean Peninsula and Taiwan—still lie in southern Okinawa Island, the site of fierce fighting. Gushiken, now 70, began collecting remains at age 28 and has found approximately 400 sets. From fragments he gathers—crushed and scattered small bones, pieces of teacups, shrapnel, and traces of flamethrowers—he infers whether the remains are those of soldiers or civilians, how they met their end, and offers his thoughts and prayers. Film director Katsuya Okuma, who himself lost a great-aunt in the Battle of Okinawa, accompanies Gushiken on his collection efforts, searching for traces of his great-aunt's life. Interweaving archival footage of the Battle of Okinawa, the film illuminates Okinawa's history and present.
tmdb:1337447: A brother who cannot fit into society, a father who has given up on the future, and a sister bound to the home. This is a story of the small steps the three of them take forward. One day, the Great East Japan Earthquake suddenly upends their peaceful daily lives. Not only the earthquake and tsunami, but also the nuclear accident forced many people to lose their homes and jobs, leaving Fukushima behind. This is the story of a family living in the aftermath, three years later, in a deeply scarred Fukushima.
tmdb:1353263: A documentary that delves into the corruption allegations against Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Following the October 7, 2023, attack on Israel by the Islamic fundamentalist organization Hamas, the Israeli military began its assault on the Gaza Strip, leading to the seemingly endless Gaza-Israel conflict with massive loss of life. A key figure in this conflict is Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, a charismatic leader whose hardline political stance is controversial. He is also the first sitting Israeli prime minister to be criminally indicted. In 2017, as the corruption investigation progressed, parts of police interrogation records of Netanyahu and his associates were secretly leaked to the film's production team. These records documented collusion with business and media circles, bribery, and provision of benefits. The film features testimonies from former Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Olmert, a former head of the domestic intelligence agency Shin Bet, Netanyahu's former spokesperson, and prominent investigative journalists. It exposes how corruption led to national decay, and how Netanyahu colluded with far-right forces to maintain his long-term rule and avoid conviction, pushing democracy into crisis. Netanyahu himself sought to stop the film's release and threatened legal action; it was banned from screening in Israel. Alex Gibney, known for 'Taxi to the Dark Side' and 'Enron: The Smartest Guys in the Room,' served as executive producer, and Alexis Bloom, director of 'Anita: Speaking Truth to Power,' directed the film.
tmdb:1356670: A social human drama that depicts the relentless hard work and unexpected troubles constantly falling on nurses in an understaffed, full hospital ward, which became a huge hit in Switzerland. Directed by Swiss screenwriter and filmmaker Petra Volpe, it realistically and thrillingly portrays the urgent, universal problem of hospital realities. Florie, a dedicated and highly professional nurse working in a state hospital, faces an even busier late shift than usual because a colleague is out sick. The ward is full, and she also has to train nursing students. Despite the situation, Florie treats patients with anxiety and loneliness sincerely, but she falls into an unmanageable situation and eventually faces a major trial. Leonie Benesch, known for 'The Teachers' Lounge' and 'September 5,' stars.
tmdb:1359916: A live-action film adaptation of Makoto Shinkai's 2007 theatrical anime "5 Centimeters Per Second," directed by Shinkai of "Your Name." and "Suzume," starring Hokuto Matsumura of SixTONES. Spring 1991. Takaki Tono and Akari Shinohara, who meet at an elementary school in Tokyo, connect through their shared loneliness, but Akari moves away upon graduation. In the winter of their first year of middle school, they reunite on a snowy night in Iwafune, Tochigi, and promise beneath a cherry tree standing in the snow to meet again at the same place on March 26, 2009. Time passes to 2008. Takaki, now working as a systems engineer in Tokyo and approaching 30, realizes a part of himself remains left behind in a distant time. Akari, too, lives her quiet daily life with those memories. Mitsuki Takahata plays Akari Shinohara, the heroine who connects with Takaki; Nana Mori plays Kanae Sumita, a high school classmate who has feelings for Takaki; Yuzu Aoki plays Takaki in high school; and Asa Kimura plays Risa Mizuno, Takaki's coworker. Also starring Aoi Miyazaki and Hidetaka Yoshioka. Directed by visual artist and photographer Yoshiyuki Okuyama, who gained attention with "At the Bench," with a screenplay by Fumiko Suzuki of "Love At Least."
tmdb:1364904: In Bangkok, Thailand, where dust pollution is severe, March (Wisarut Himmarat) spends his days in grief after losing his beloved wife Nat (Davika Hoorne) to a respiratory disease. One day, Nat's soul returns, inhabiting a vacuum cleaner, and the two reaffirm their love. Meanwhile, at the factory run by March's family, the spirit of a deceased employee possesses the machinery, bringing operations to a halt. Rejected by family troubled by the spirit and by society, Nat tries to prove her true love for her husband and her own existence as a 'useful ghost' by helping with the factory's exorcism...
tmdb:1365683: A drama based on the true story of composer Vivaldi's appointment as a violin teacher at the Ospedale della Pietà in Venice in the early 18th century, depicting the growth of a lonely girl whose talent blossoms under his guidance, and Vivaldi's inner ambition, craving recognition for his own genius. Venice, 1716, at the Ospedale della Pietà. Cecilia, raised without knowing her mother's presence or love, secretly slips out of bed every night to write letters to her mother with no address. To leave the Pietà and live in the outside world, her mother must come for her, or she must marry a nobleman. Amidst this, Antonio Vivaldi, arriving as a violin teacher, discovers Cecilia's exceptional violin skill and appoints her as the leader of the first violins. Under Vivaldi, Cecilia endures rigorous practice, hones her violin skills, and they gradually grow close. However, the officer the Pietà has chosen as Cecilia's husband returns from war, and an incident soon occurs. Tekla Insolia, noted for the Italian TV drama 'The Art of Joy,' plays Cecilia, and Michele Riondino of 'The Sleeping Beauty' plays Vivaldi. The film is directed and written by Damiano Michieletto, a leading Italian opera director who served as creative director for the opening and closing ceremonies of the Milan Cortina Winter Olympics.
tmdb:13688: Ti, who lost his wife to illness, works at a construction site to send his only son Dicky to a prestigious private elementary school. While retrieving a pair of sneakers Dicky wanted from the garbage dump, Ti finds a green ball. Dicky begins keeping the creature (or is it an object of unknown nature?) that is born from the ball Ti brought home, naming it Miracle 7.
tmdb:1370545: A human drama based on a story from Banana Yoshimoto's short story collection 'Mitten and Fubin', co-produced by Japan and Taiwan. It quietly depicts a woman carrying loss who, through encounters in a foreign land, gradually finds renewal. Chizumi is a woman living each day with deep grief after losing her mother. As time passes without filling the void in her heart, she is invited by a friend to visit Taiwan. There, she meets Shin-shin, a young man with a Taiwanese mother and a Japanese father. The unfamiliar cityscapes and the accumulation of casual conversations slowly begin to move her frozen heart, and Chizumi, while still carrying her lingering sense of loss, discovers small warmth. Yukino Kishii ('Small, Slow but Steady', 'Just the Two of Us') plays the protagonist Chizumi, and popular young Taiwanese actor Tseng Jing-hua (known for 'The Soul of the Prisoner', 'Your Name Engraved Herein') plays Shin-shin, the young man she meets in Taiwan. The cast also includes Tokio Fujiwara, Seina Nakata, Tokio Emoto, Kayo Ise, Kisuke Iida, and Kimiko Yo. Directed and scripted by Yukinori Makabe ('I Am a Monk.', 'Scoop!').
tmdb:1371185: A musical drama starring Hugh Jackman and Kate Hudson in their first collaboration, based on the true story of a married couple who performed as a tribute band to American national singer Neil Diamond. Mike, who once dreamed of a music career, now can only get on stage by imitating someone else's singing, hitting rock bottom in life. One day, he meets Claire, a woman with the same passion, and they form a tribute band to their beloved Neil Diamond. Starting from a small garage, their voices gradually capture the hearts of the people in their town. But then, a sudden tragedy strikes them. Jackman and Hudson deliver powerful performances of Neil Diamond's classic songs, including 'Sweet Caroline.' The cast includes Michael Imperioli from 'The Sopranos,' Ella Anderson from 'The Glass Castle,' and singer-songwriter King Princess. Based on the 2008 documentary of the same name, Craig Brewer, director of 'Hustle & Flow,' wrote and directed the film. Hudson was nominated for Best Actress at the 98th Academy Awards.
tmdb:1372044: This documentary chronicles the struggle of Iwao Hakamada, who spent 47 years on death row. Convicted for the 1966 murder-arson of a miso company executive’s family in Shizuoka Prefecture, Hakamada was suddenly released in March 2014 after 47 years and seven months of imprisonment. Arrested at the age of 30 after spending his youth as a professional boxer, his pleas of innocence were ignored by both the courts and the public. He endured decades of terror, living each day with the fear that his execution might be carried out the next morning, and was 78 years old by the time of his release. Amidst dramatic media coverage of the unprecedented decision to release a death row inmate pending a retrial, director Chiaki Kasai—who has followed Hakamada for 22 years—records the story behind the headlines. The camera captures the daily lives of Hakamada and his sister, Hideko, reunited after being torn apart for nearly half a century, and through their dialogues, delves deep into Hakamada’s inner psyche.
tmdb:13754: Based on the popular manga by Taiyo Matsumoto serialized in 'Big Spirits' magazine from 1993 to 1994, this anime film adaptation is directed by Michael Arias, a VFX specialist active in Hollywood known for 'The Animatrix'. Set in the 'Treasure Town' of duty and human emotion, it depicts the exploits of two boys, Kuro and Shiro, who fly freely through the city. The voice cast includes Kazunari Ninomiya, who made his overseas debut in Clint Eastwood's 'Letters from Iwo Jima', and Yu Aoi from 'Hula Girls'.
tmdb:1378051: Called the 'Voice of Brazil,' Milton Nascimento, affectionately known as Bituca, led MPB (Brazilian popular music post-bossa nova) alongside contemporaries Gilberto Gil, Caetano Veloso, and Chico Buarque, and collaborated with countless international musicians. This documentary film traces Milton's life and music while following his global farewell concert tour, announced upon turning 80 in 2022. In the first half, Milton's troupe tours Europe and the Americas, receiving ecstatic welcomes. Pat Metheny, Spike Lee, Quincy Jones, and Wayne Shorter speak about Milton, and there are scenes of collaboration with Esperanza Spalding and Herbie Hancock. Milton reflects on his childhood raised as an adopted son, converses with his own adopted child on the road, and shares memories of his benefactor, singer Elis Regina. The second half begins with the landscapes of Minas Gerais, the highland region of inland Brazil that is Milton's home and musical origin. Friends like Chico, Caetano, and Gil, collaborating poets like Márcio Borges and Ronaldo Bastos, and younger musicians who admire Milton, discuss the appeal and depths of his music. Inescapable negative histories, such as racism and Brazil's 20-year military dictatorship starting in 1964, are also revealed. Then, the farewell concert finale approaches: the concert at Mineirão, the football stadium in Belo Horizonte, the capital of Minas Gerais. Members of Clube da Esquina (Corner Club), the title of a landmark 1972 album and the name for the family of Minas musicians centered around Milton—Lô Borges, Beto Guedes, Wagner Tiso, and Toninho Horta—share behind-the-scenes stories and perform together.
tmdb:1379266: A human drama depicting the tumultuous life of a man born into a yakuza family who dedicates his life to the path of art as a Kabuki actor. A talked-about sensation that has taken the Japanese film world by storm, finally screening!
tmdb:1381512: A youth drama about a girl who, after learning her late mother loved visual kei bands, discovers herself and grows through encounters with music and visual kei culture. Maria, a high school student raised by a single mother, suddenly loses her mother. While sorting through her belongings, she finds CDs, photos, and a diary from her mother's youth, along with an unplayable demo tape named 'MARIA'—the same as her own name. To uncover her mother's secrets, Maria visits a live house and encounters visual kei music. Hina Kikuchi, a model and actor known for 'Oshi no Ko' and 'The Suicide Note,' stars in her first solo lead film role. Masataka Fujishige co-stars as Kanata, a former visual kei musician; Sahel Rosa as Kyoko, Maria's mother's friend; and Tomoko Fujita as Miki, Maria's grandmother. Directed by Daisuke Miyazaki ('Yamato (California),' 'VIDEOPHOBIA'). Filmed at the iconic live house 'Meguro Rokumeikan,' a mecca for visual kei bands, the film also features 1990s visual kei CDs, posters, and fans (bangyaru).
tmdb:1381564: Living in poverty, bothered by noisy neighbors. Frustrated with an absurd reality, middle school student Kenta struggles to support his mother Asako and younger brother Yuji. And then there's the mysterious "pokapon" sound echoing around him. Watching over this family quietly is the housing complex manager, Shunichi. Eventually, Kenta and Shunichi begin to understand each other, but rumors start to circulate that the perpetrator of a series of child murders that once shocked the nation is hiding in this housing complex...
tmdb:1382406: A revenge action film starring Thai action star Tony Jaa, known for 'Ong-Bak' and 'Tom-Yum-Goong'. It depicts a man who lost his family confronting a massive conspiracy, packed with powerful Muay Thai-based hand-to-hand combat and high-speed, hard-hitting action. After his wife and daughter are killed by a mysterious organization, Bai An heads to the Republic of Parivina to uncover the truth and exact revenge. As he investigates on his own, he discovers a giant corporation secretly controlling the drug trade, but behind it swirls a vast conspiracy involving the military and police. The situation becomes intricately tangled with a mad drug lord, corrupt military police, and unexpected trials involving the only daughter of the corporation's owner. Bai An is tossed about but continues to battle the enemies closing in on him. Directed by Cheung Sui-yee. Co-stars include Xing Yu from 'Master Z: Ip Man Legacy', Philip Keung from 'Goldfinger', and Jason Han from 'Overheat: The Final Sanction'.
tmdb:13828: Based on the novel "Sono Keitai wa XX de" by Nobuyuki Jōkō, directed by Kenta Fukasaku of "Battle Royale II: Requiem" and scripted by Tetsuya Ōishi of "Death Note." Shiyori and Aiko visit the remote hot spring village "Agari Village" and split up after a trivial quarrel. That night, a phone rings near Shiyori in her room. A mysterious voice warns her to "run or your legs will be cut off," and as she is bewildered, the villagers begin attacking her one after another. Starring Nao Matsushita and Ami Suzuki.
tmdb:1385199:
A touching human drama that follows a boy who lost his younger sister in a disaster and the people around him, told through a warm and compassionate lens.

Kazuki Morimoto, a fifth-grader who lost his sister in an earthquake several years ago, has moved to a new town with his single father, Yosuke, who runs a ramen shop. However, Kazuki struggles to fit in at school and with his new surroundings. One day, after learning about the existence of fairies called "Brownies," Kazuki begins to truly believe that his sister didn't die, but was instead spirited away by them. He sets out on a quest to find the Brownies. While those around him are bewildered by his behavior, his classmate Toko Izumi decides to help him, joined by her relative, a translator named Daisuke Izumi. Eventually, sparked by a lie from a "young carer" named Sota, Kazuki embarks on a journey to find the Brownies. Toko, Sota, and a truant boy named Masato follow after him.

Ayaki Hirano, known for the NHK morning drama series *The Tiger and Her Wings*, stars as the protagonist Kazuki. Junnosuke Taguchi plays Daisuke, the translator who holds the key to the story, while comedian Akira 100% portrays Kazuki’s father, Yosuke. The screenplay is written by Yuiko Miura (*Memories of Tomorrow*), and director Yuta Soma, who has created numerous short films centered on the theme of "children and social issues," makes his feature film directorial debut.
tmdb:1388366: A horror film based on the popular cartoon character 'Popeye,' created by American cartoonist Elzie Crisler Segar in 1929. Produced after the original copyright expired in January 2025, entering the public domain, it depicts the righteous sailor Popeye awakening as a brutal murderer, armed with his familiar can of spinach and powerful forearms. College student Dexter is making a documentary about a local legend in a small port town: a sailor who wanders the docks every night in search of prey. One night, Dexter brings along Olivia, whom he has long had a crush on, and their friends to sneak into an abandoned factory near the port for investigation. As they proceed in a somewhat playful mood, the smell of pipe tobacco begins to drift from somewhere, and soon the legendary sailor emerges from the darkness. As his companions are brutally killed one after another, Dexter and Olivia desperately flee, following clues left in the factory to uncover the sailor's true identity.
tmdb:1397201: The second film in the live-action adaptation of Satoru Noda's popular manga "Golden Kamuy," serving as a sequel to the 2024 film and the WOWOW drama series "Golden Kamuy: The Hunt of the Tattooed Prisoners in Hokkaido." Former soldier Saichi Sugimoto, known as "Immortal Sugimoto," learns of a vast gold hoard stolen from the Ainu people. The mysterious culprit, "Noppera-bo," hid the gold before his capture, tattooing the locations on the bodies of prisoners and engineering their escape. The tattoos form a single code when combined across 24 men. Sugimoto meets Ainu girl Asirpa, whose father was killed by the gold thief, and they join forces. Meanwhile, Lieutenant Tsurumi of the Imperial Japanese Army's 7th Division, who aims to conquer Hokkaido, and Toshizo Hijikata, who should have died in the Boshin War, also seek the gold, sparking a fierce battle for the tattooed prisoners. The stage moves to Abashiri Prison, where Noppera-bo is incarcerated. Returning cast members include Kento Yamazaki as Sugimoto and Anna Yamada as Asirpa, with new additions: Yu Inaba as Private Usami of the 7th Division, Sohma Wada as Chief Guard Kadokura, and Jun Kunimura as Navy Rear Admiral Heiji Koido, father of "Satsuma's Prince" Otonoshin Koido. Directed by Kenji Katagiri, who helmed episodes 3 and 5-8 of the drama series.
tmdb:1398359: A family, fed up with their impoverished life in Sri Lanka, illegally enters India and, armed with 'smiles and a little bit of meddling', sparks small miracles!
tmdb:1401281: A biographical musical film chronicling the tumultuous life of Ann Lee, a real-life religious leader who founded the utopian "Shaker" sect in the 18th century, starring Amanda Seyfried of "Mamma Mia!" and "Les Misérables." Born into a poor blacksmith's family in 18th-century England, Ann grows up as a devout woman. After the heartbreaking experience of bearing four children, all of whom die, she receives a revelation that she is the female reincarnation of Christ. Her way of life, preaching equality of gender and race, attracts many followers but also invites persecution from those who resent or fear her. Eventually, she crosses to America with just eight followers, seeking a utopia where they can realize an ideal life based on gender and racial equality, but further hardships await her there. Co-stars include Lewis Pullman of "Top Gun: Maverick" and Thomasin McKenzie of "Last Night in Soho." Directed by Mona Fastvold, who co-wrote the script with her partner, director Brady Corbet of "The Brutalist." The film was presented in the competition section of the 82nd Venice International Film Festival in 2025.
tmdb:1401778: A situational survival thriller set in the inescapable space of a floating hot air balloon, depicting the threats of nature and human conflict. To repair his relationship with his wife Amy, who is grieving a miscarriage, ambitious CEO Zach joins a hot air balloon tour crossing the Italian Dolomites with her. A mysterious woman named Julia joins them, and the flight with the three passengers begins. But high in the sky, Julia suddenly reveals that she had a secret meeting with Zach the previous day, accusing him of infidelity. Zach denies it, but suspicion swirls, and Julia suddenly pulls a knife. During the struggle, the pilot falls out, and the balloon goes out of control. With the radio dead and the balloon reaching an oxygen-thin altitude of 16,000 feet, battered by turbulence and storms, the three are forced into extreme choices with no escape. Directed by Claudio Fae of 'Air Lock: Underwater Emergency Shelter,' with a screenplay by Andy Mason, who wrote and produced 'Air Lock: Underwater Emergency Shelter' and '47 Meters Down.' The cast includes Hera Hilmar of 'Mortal Engines' as Amy, Jeremy Irvine of 'War Horse' as Zach, and Olga Kurylenko, known as a Bond girl from 'Quantum of Solace,' as Julia.
tmdb:1404777: A massive hit released in Vietnam in 2025, drawing approximately 2.56 million viewers and earning around 1.2 billion yen at the box office, ranking among the country's top 10 highest-grossing films of all time. Its universal themes of love, money, family, and life choices resonated with audiences across generations. To reclaim a lost family home filled with memories, Van reluctantly follows a plan devised by her sister Kieu and best friend Thien, approaching two wealthy suitors who are pursuing her. One is a man with calm, mature charm and warmth. The other is young, unconventional, and a playboy. Van eventually discovers her true feelings, but also learns that both men have their own hidden motives for approaching her. Thu Tran, who has been active as a Vietnamese actor and producer, makes her directorial debut while also starring and producing.
tmdb:1406829: A human drama depicting the inner lives of children wavering amidst the awakening of self, set against the backdrop of "Kodomo Kabuki" (Children's Kabuki) performed at the Nagahama Hikiyama Festival in Shiga Prefecture, a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage. Eleven-year-old Ibuki visits his father’s hometown of Nagahama for the first time with his Taiwanese mother, Yaohua, to deliver the remains of his father, Shuichi, who passed away a year ago. Nagahama is in the midst of preparations for its annual festival, and Ibuki is cast in the *onnagata* (female role) once performed by his father in the festival's Children's Kabuki. Struggling with the unfamiliar environment and the difficult phrasing of Kabuki, Ibuki becomes isolated, but he begins to slowly open up after meeting Hana, a young girl who feels a sense of dissonance
tmdb:14069: The first anime adaptation of Yasutaka Tsutsui's classic novel, previously adapted into TV dramas and films. A youth sci-fi drama depicting high school girl Makoto, who gains the power of "time leap" to travel to the past by chance, and realizes the preciousness of irreplaceable moments in life as she repeatedly redoes the past. Second-year high school student Makoto Konno gains the power to "time leap" back to the past after accidentally cracking a walnut found in the school science lab. Using this power, Makoto fully enjoys her carefree daily life, singing karaoke as much as she wants with her male friends Chiaki Mamiya and Kosuke Tsuda, and making spectacular plays in baseball. No matter what happens, she can go back in time and reset as many times as she wants. But this fun everyday life was supposed to continue... Directed by Mamoru Hosoda, who had worked on theatrical versions of "Digimon Adventure" and "ONE PIECE" and later became a leading Japanese animation director with films like "Summer Wars," "The Boy and the Beast," and "Mirai." Character design by Yoshiyuki Sadamoto ("Neon Genesis Evangelion"), animation production by Madhouse. Riisa Naka voices the protagonist Makoto, and Sachie Hara made her voice acting debut as Makoto's aunt, Kazuko Yoshiyama. Initially released in only 6 theaters in 2006, it gained popularity through word-of-mouth and achieved a long run exceeding 8 months. In 2021, it was re-released with the immersive 4DX system as part of a project commemorating the 10th anniversary of Hosoda's production company, Studio Chizu.
tmdb:141: As the second installment of THE RIVER's original program 'REVIVAL by THE RIVER,' which brings back beloved Western films from the 2000s for revival screenings, the legendary cult film 'Donnie Darko' will be screened once again. An emergency revival screening will take place at Human Trust Cinema Shibuya for a limited weekend on August 22 (Sat) and 23 (Sun), 2026. It returns to Japanese screens to mark the 25th anniversary of its U.S. release. Middlesex, Massachusetts. Donnie Darko, 17. Ever since a plane engine fell onto his house, a silver rabbit has appeared before him. The rabbit tells him [28:06:42:12]. The beautiful transfer student, Dr. Hawking, the basement door... Everything surrounding him is telling him about "it." What awaits him in the world 28 days later? Flat rate of 1,600 yen (various discount services not applicable).
tmdb:1418429: An adaptation of Masuji Ibuse’s novel of the same name, this comedy depicts the joys and sorrows of common people while incorporating the local color of Western Japan. The screenplay was written by Toshio Shiina, one of the co-writers of *The Embraced Bride*, and directed by Noboru Nakamura of *Cloudburst*. The cinematography is by Toshio Ubukata (*The Embraced Bride*). The film stars Keiji Sada and Mariko Okada (both of *Zero Fish Today*), leading an ensemble cast that includes Toshiko Kobayashi, Achako Hanabishi, Yunosuke Ito, Tony Tani, Toshiyuki Ichimura, Chieko Seki, and Hisao Toake. Filmed in Eastman Shochiku Color.
tmdb:1418515: A documentary exploring the creative life of 83-year-old legendary New York-based artist Meredith Monk. Living in a TriBeCa loft with a turtle, the woman with trademark braids, Meredith Monk, was born on November 20, 1942, and raised in New York. She has worked as a composer, singer, director, choreographer, and performance artist creating various music-theatre works, films, and installations, influencing many musicians. A pioneer of contemporary artistic expression, she treats her voice—spanning over three octaves—as an instrument, continuously pursuing original, genre-transcending expression. The film weaves together extensive archival footage of Monk's stage and performance works with interviews from admirers like Björk and David Byrne, connecting fragments of her 60-year career like a concept album to depict her unique expression and life. It highlights her strong, resilient, and charming persona, having started her career in the male-dominated 1960s and continued her own path despite occasional critical scorn.
tmdb:1418516: A human drama about a young man who could only feel himself through committing crimes, and how he finds meaning in life through his encounter with a couple running an okonomiyaki restaurant. Directed and written by Toshizo Fujiwara, who has acted in films such as "A Scene at the Sea," the film was selected for the Panorama section of the 75th Berlin International Film Festival in 2025. Hiroyuki and Sonoko Kiuchi, a couple running an okonomiyaki shop, hire former prisoners and juvenile detention center graduates to help them reintegrate into society. However, since an incident involving a former employee a year ago, they have been plagued by online harassment. During an interview at a juvenile detention center, the Kiuchis meet 18-year-old Yuto Nishimura, who pleads to start his life over, and they hire him as a new employee. Yuto begins working earnestly, but after a certain event, he reconnects with his old friends and becomes strongly drawn to Yukiha, a dancer he meets at a club. The script was written based on extensive research at various sites, including an okonomiyaki shop in Osaka that actually supports the employment of former prisoners and juvenile detainees, and incorporates Fujiwara's own experiences. Daiki Ido stars in his first leading role as Yuto, Fujiwara plays Hiroyuki, Rino Tsuneishi plays Sonoko, with supporting roles by Tomoko Fujita and Jiei Kabira.
tmdb:1418569: A documentary depicting an Israeli-American family's desperate efforts to rescue their daughter abducted by Hamas, crossing divides. On the morning of October 7, 2023, the agricultural community of Nir Oz in southwestern Israel was attacked by Hamas militants, with a quarter of its roughly 400 residents killed or taken hostage. Yehuda, the father of hostage Liat Beinin Atzili and her husband Aviv, along with his family, begins a frantic mission to save them. Because Liat holds American citizenship, Yehuda travels to the US as part of a delegation urging the American government to secure the hostages' release, but is shocked to realize that the hostages' plight is being used to justify the Israeli government's continuation of the war. While Yehuda, critical of Netanyahu's administration, accuses the prime minister of prolonging the war to avoid imprisonment, some family members and associates push back, arguing that rescue should take priority over criticism. Through the urgent perspective of those longing for the safe return of their loved ones, the film illuminates the complex interplay of politics, history, and divided values. The production includes Darren Aronofsky, director of 'Black Swan,' among its team. It won the Best Documentary Award at the 75th Berlin International Film Festival in 2025.
tmdb:1418849: Korean master Hong Sang-soo, a multiple award-winner at the Berlin and Cannes film festivals, humorously and realistically depicts the irreparable failures caused by alcohol in this home drama centered on a young poet who ends up spending a day with his girlfriend's family. When poet Dong-ha escorts his girlfriend Juni home, he runs into her father at the front door and unexpectedly spends the day with her family. Initially awkward, Dong-ha gradually grows closer to Juni's family as they show him around their home and neighborhood and engage in conversation. Eventually, at dinner with the family, he drinks as urged, becomes intoxicated, and an uncomfortable atmosphere settles over the table. Ha Seong-guk, who previously played poets in Hong Sang-soo's "The Woman Who Ran" and "In Front of Your Face," takes on the role of Dong-ha, marking his first lead role in a Hong Sang-soo film. The parents welcoming their daughter's boyfriend are played by Hong Sang-soo regulars and real-life couple Kwon Hae-hyo and Cho Yun-hee. Kang So-yi ("In Front of Your Face," "By the Stream") plays Juni, and Park Mi-so ("Introduction") plays Juni's older sister. The film was selected for the competition section of the 75th Berlin International Film Festival in 2025. It will be released in theaters in 2026 as the fifth installment of "Monthly Hong Sang-soo," a project screening new works for five consecutive months to commemorate the director's 30th debut anniversary.
tmdb:1419406: A battle action film starring Jackie Chan, depicting the fight between a police force led by a tracking expert and a cybercrime group led by a former assassin. In Macau, a series of clever heists by an elusive cybercrime group occur. With the surveillance system hijacked and the investigation stalled, the police seek help from Huang Dezhong, a retired tracking expert, as their trump card. Teaming up with young elite police officers, Huang Dezhong uses old-school investigative techniques and the latest technology to pursue the cybercrime group led by a former assassin known as 'Shadow.' Leon Ka-Fai, known for 'The Lover' and 'Cold War,' plays the former assassin leader of the criminal group, reuniting with Jackie Chan for the first time in about 20 years since 'The Myth.' JUN, a member of the popular K-POP group SEVENTEEN who also works as an actor, takes on his first villain role as a member of the criminal group. Zhang Zifeng, from 'Sister Summer's Farewell,' and Zusha, from the TV drama 'Mountain and River Shadows,' also appear. The film is directed and written by Larry Yang, who previously worked with Jackie Chan on 'Ride On.'
tmdb:1422404: Master filmmaker Yoji Yamada, directing his 91st film, brings together Baisho Chieko and Kimura Takuya as leads in this human drama about the joys of life, based on the 2022 French film "A Taxi for Paris." Taxi driver Koji Usami is tasked with driving 85-year-old Sumire Takano from Tokyo's Shibamata to a nursing home in Hayama, Kanagawa. Sumire asks him, "For my last look at Tokyo, there are a few places I'd like to stop by," and Usami follows her instructions, driving her around various locations. As they share the journey, Sumire gradually opens up and reveals her surprising past. The chance encounter between a taxi driver and his passenger sets both their hearts and lives in motion. Alongside Baisho as Sumire and Kimura as driver Usami, Aoi Yu, making her sixth appearance in a Yamada film since "My Wife is a Rose: Family is Tough III," plays the young Sumire. Takaya Sakaguchi plays Sumire's fiancé Ogawa, and Yuka plays Usami's wife Kaoru. The cast also includes Runa Nakajima, Misuzu Kanno, Lee Jun-young, and Takashi Sasano.
tmdb:1422562: A film conceived by global musician Charli XCX, who also stars, depicting the turbulent behind-the-scenes world of show business involving top stars and industry insiders. In 2024, pop star Charli XCX became a global sensation with her album "brat," sparking a social phenomenon called "Brat Summer" and becoming an icon of the era. Bold and unapologetic, she daily pursues her authentic self. However, her music label, manager, and social media handlers, using the slogan "Brat Summer Forever," try to forcibly prolong the movement, intervening in live performances and promotions with backing from Amazon, pushing Charli into a clichéd star image. Overwhelmed by her busy schedule, Charli escapes to Ibiza for a vacation just days before a live show, throwing the production into chaos. Directed by Aidan Zamiri, who has directed music videos for Billie Eilish and others. The cast includes Alexander Skarsgård, Rosanna Arquette, and Kylie Jenner.
tmdb:1425905: Shane Kosugi, son of action star Sho Kosugi who sparked the ninja boom in Hollywood and brother of Kane Kosugi, makes his feature directorial debut with this action film themed around ninjas believed to be extinct. Chinese martial arts world champion Kansuke Asano, who became a world champion in his teens, stars and produces, with Kane Kosugi also appearing. Ninjas living in modern-day Japan have changed their names and appearances, secretly carrying out missions as agents of the non-governmental organization 'Shiju-ku (49)'. Kyōhei Aizawa, one of the most skilled agents in history, loses his beloved lover, the only person he truly trusted, in a plane crash. As he contemplates the meaning of life in solitude, Kyōhei is assigned an infiltration mission into the Japanese yakuza group Takatsuki-gumi. After Kyōhei successfully completes the mission, the Takatsuki-gumi, learning of his existence, begins eliminating people around him by any means necessary for a certain purpose. Realizing that his loved ones are disappearing because of him, Kyōhei confronts the Takatsuki-gumi alone. Asano plays the protagonist Kyōhei, with Seiki Miura and Nanana among the cast.
tmdb:1425909: A documentary tracing the journey and present life of Yuho Asaka, one of Japan's pioneers of peer counseling. Born in Fukushima City, Fukushima Prefecture in 1956, Yuho Asaka has a condition characterized by brittle bones. From a young age, she was forced to give up on learning and grew angry at a society that discriminates and excludes based on disability and gender. Always searching for her place in the world, Asaka connected with the cerebral palsy activist group "Fukushima Prefecture Aoi Shiba no Kai" and, drawing on the independent living movement and feminism she encountered while studying in the U.S., helped establish Japan's first independent living center. She also participated in international conferences and helped spark changes to the Eugenic Protection Law. The film follows Asaka's relentless pursuit of freedom, while also depicting her sister Aiko, who was caught in the turbulent relationship between their father and Yuho; her daughter Sora, who was born with the same condition and works at an overseas institute advocating for the rights of people with disabilities while attending graduate school; and the young caregivers who share daily life with her in a free-spirited relationship. Yumiko Asano, producer of "What Could Have Been?," makes her directorial debut, with Tomoaki Fujino, director of that same film, handling cinematography, editing, and production.
tmdb:1427396:
Directed by Katsuyuki Motohiro of the "Bayside Shakedown" series, this youth sci-fi comedy is a film adaptation of the popular stage play by the theater group Europe Kikaku. Set during a sweltering summer vacation, the story follows a group of college students who trigger a series of chaotic events when they use a time machine to retrieve an air conditioner remote before it broke.

In the clubroom of a university's Sci-Fi Research Society, five male students and two female members of the photography club are languishing in the oppressive heat. Their air conditioner's remote control broke the previous day, leaving them to suffer through the summer. Suddenly, a time machine appears before them. What starts as a joke turns into a discovery: the machine is real. Caught up in the excitement, three members decide to travel back to yesterday to fetch the working remote. However, a junior from the year 2030 suddenly appears before those left behind, leading the group to realize the grave dangers of altering the past...

The screenplay was penned by Europe Kikaku’s own Makoto Ueda. Eita, who rose to prominence in "Water Boys," makes his film-starring debut as Komoto, the student at the heart of the commotion. Juri Ueno, known for "Swing Girls" and "Turtles Are Surprisingly Fast Swimmers," plays Shibata, the photography club member and object of Komoto's affection.
tmdb:1437156:
This feature film serves as the sequel to the 2023 television drama *Last Man: The Blind Investigator*, which followed a blind FBI agent and a solitary detective as they teamed up to tackle a series of complex cases.

FBI Special Agent Hiromi Minami (Masaharu Fukuyama) lost his sight in a past incident, yet earned the moniker "Last Man" for his uncanny ability to bring every investigation to a definitive close. During an exchange program with the Tokyo Metropolitan Police Department, he was assigned an attendant in Shintaro Godo (Yo Oizumi), a lone-wolf detective who stops at nothing to make an arrest. After forging an invincible partnership and discovering the shocking truth that they are biological brothers, the two were bound by an even deeper bond before Minami eventually returned to the United States.

Two years later, Minami returns to Japan and summons Godo to join him on a case in Hokkaido. There, they encounter Nagisa Ivanova (Rie Miyazawa), Minami’s first love. Teaming up once again to protect her from a mysterious organization, Minami and Godo join forces with a joint task force comprising the FBI, CIA, and Hokkaido Prefectural Police. However, lurking behind the case is a conspiracy capable of shaking the world.

The film features returning cast members Ren Nagase, Mio Imada, Tae Kimura, Yo Yoshida, and Takaya Kamikawa, with Rie Miyazawa joining the ensemble as the pivotal character Nagisa Ivanova.
tmdb:144: A masterpiece fantasy film directed by Wim Wenders ('Paris, Texas'), who took the helm in his home country of Germany for the first time in a decade, winning the Best Director award at the 40th Cannes Film Festival in 1987. Set in Berlin before the fall of the Wall, it poetically and beautifully depicts the fate of an angel who falls in love with a human. Damiel, an angel who listens to the inner voices of humans and comforts their sorrows, meets Marion, a trapeze artist performing in a circus. Strongly drawn to her loneliness, Damiel decides to descend from the heavenly realm to the human world. Bruno Ganz stars, and Peter Falk ('Columbo') appears as himself. The screenplay was contributed by Peter Handke, who would later win the Nobel Prize in Literature. A sequel, 'Faraway, So Close!,' was produced in 1993.
tmdb:1443: Sofia Coppola, daughter of the master Francis Ford Coppola, made her feature directorial debut with this 1999 film. Based on the novel "The Virgin Suicides" by American author Jeffrey Eugenides, it depicts the emotional fluctuations of adolescent girls harboring a sense of danger with fresh, vivid visual beauty. In a 1970s American suburban town. The Lisbon house has five sisters, aged 13 to 17, each born a year apart, and the neighborhood boys are infatuated with them. One June day when dragonflies are swarming, the youngest daughter, Cecilia, attempts suicide. A few days later, the family throws a party to cheer her up, but during the party, she throws herself out of a window... Kirsten Dunst, who gained attention in "Interview with the Vampire," plays the fourth daughter Lux, while James Woods and Kathleen Turner play the sisters' parents. The French electronic duo AIR composed the music. A 4K restored version was released in May 2025 as part of the "12 Months of Cinema Relay 2024-2025."
tmdb:1443397: Director Tadahiko Sako, known for "Kamejiro: The Man the U.S. Military Feared Most," delves into modern Okinawan history through the lives of two governors who fiercely confronted the national government. Masahide Ota (the 4th governor after Okinawa's reversion to Japan, serving 1990–98) and Takeshi Onaga (the 7th governor, serving 2014–18) held opposing political positions, yet both garnered broad support from the people and managed the prefecture by transcending the traditional conservative-liberal divide. Ota fought the state in court in 1995 over his refusal to sign for the forced use of military land, while Onaga did the same in 2015 regarding the revocation of the Henoko landfill approval; their battles brought to light the nature of democracy, local autonomy, and the contradictions of the nation. Incorporating testimonies from many who were involved in their lives, the film highlights their personal charisma and depicts the indomitable struggle of two men who lived by their convictions. The title "Tida" means "Sun" in the Okinawan dialect, a word that anciently referred to a chief or leader.
tmdb:1445363: A visual work by director Baz Luhrmann, who helmed the 2022 biographical film "Elvis," using cutting-edge technology to revive Elvis Presley in the modern era. Elvis Presley, hailed as the "King of Rock and Roll" for his innovative music and charismatic stage performances, lived a 42-year life as a darling of the times. During the production of the biopic "Elvis," director Baz Luhrmann and his team discovered a treasure trove in Warner Bros.' vault: footage shot for "Elvis: That's the Way It Is" (covering his August 1970 Las Vegas engagement) and "Elvis on Tour" (recording his 1972 nationwide tour), as well as unreleased 8mm film and unheard audio of Elvis discussing his career. This film centers on the legendary Las Vegas shows and iconic performances from the nationwide tour, restoring countless precious images over more than two years using state-of-the-art restoration/remastering technology. Using over 70 songs including hits like "Can't Help Falling in Love" and "Suspicious Minds" as well as rare performances like "Oh Happy Day," it synchronizes Elvis's overwhelming vocals with his own words, delicately and boldly reconstructing the footage for an immersive cinematic experience.
tmdb:1447567: A documentary by transgender director Kani Lapuerta, recording eight years in the life of a transgender elementary school student in Mexico as she grows into a teenager. In Tepoztlán, a town south of Mexico City, 15-year-old Carla talks with director Kani Lapuerta in a secret cocoon. They discuss what kind of film they want to make, and begin to look back on Carla's life chronologically from her elementary school days. The schoolyard where she couldn't line up with either the 'boys' or 'girls,' the bedroom where she endlessly practiced makeup, the morning school reopened during the pandemic, the city hall where she officially changed her name, the slogans she shouted at the Pride March, and the baton club she admired. Watched over by her punk and hippie chef parents, her friends, director Lapuerta, the queer community, and the sacred rocky mountain, Carla encounters various versions of herself. Director Kani Lapuerta also appears in the film, gradually sharing her inner thoughts with Carla like an exchange diary. With comedic touches, it portrays the struggles and fluctuations of adolescence growing up in a small town with strong gender stereotypes.
tmdb:14485: Depicts the extreme training and battles at 'Otokojuku,' a school that raises men among men. Invited to the 'Big Battle August' tournament where representatives from around the world compete for supremacy during summer vacation, the first-year students fight their way through Hawaii, Niagara Falls, Alaska, and New York, culminating in a decisive battle against the American team. The appeal lies in the massive physiques and dynamic storytelling.
tmdb:1448792: Set in Shinjuku's Kabukicho, this film portrays two girls working at a girls' bar alongside women from various backgrounds. As they continue to sell their youth and perform the roles demanded of them, they gradually lose sight of what they truly want. The film won the Movie.com Award at the 18th Tanabe Benkei Film Festival, a gateway for new directors. Naru, 19, starts working at a girls' bar after high school to leave her parents' home. Maria, 21, works at the same bar while attending university to repay her student loans. Bathed in the neon lights of the night town, Naru wishes to become someone special, while Maria longs to be a normal college student. One day, Naru meets a host on the streets of Kabukicho, and Maria is approached by a customer for an off-the-books deal. The director and screenwriter is Naima Kimura, for whom this is her second directorial work and first feature film. Kimura drew inspiration from her own experience working at a girls' bar as a student. The film was screened in theaters as part of the "Tanabe Benkei Film Festival Selection 2024" (May 9–June 5, 2024 at Theatre Shinjuku; June 20–26, 2024 at Theatre Umeda).
tmdb:1449997: A film themed around the 'quarter-life crisis,' a psychological state common among people in their late twenties to thirties who feel vague anxiety and restlessness about the future, unable to live the life they imagined. Directed by and starring Reimi Miyamori, it won the Actor Award at the 18th Tanabe Benkei Film Festival, a gateway for independent films. Nozomi, a 25-year-old woman who moved to Tokyo to become a novelist, is struggling and going nowhere. In her mind, 18-year-old Nozomi, living a rural high school life, asks her if she has truly followed through on her words and made it big in Tokyo. While resisting a frustrating life where she wants to change but cannot, the 25-year-old Nozomi confronts her 18-year-old self and begins to notice various things she had never faced before. This is the debut feature film of Reimi Miyamori, a graduate of the Nihon University College of Art's Film Department who began making films during the COVID-19 pandemic. She served as director, screenwriter, producer, and lead actress. It was screened in theaters as part of the 'Tanabe Benkei Film Festival Selection 2024' (May 9 – June 5, 2024 at Theatre Shinjuku / June 20–26, 2024 at Theatre Umeda).
tmdb:145075: A documentary by internationally acclaimed Iranian director Abbas Kiarostami ('Where Is the Friend's Home?'), focusing on homework and school education. Feeling that Iranian children are always overwhelmed by homework, Kiarostami himself acts as interviewer, asking elementary school students and their parents a series of questions about 'homework.' Through the interviews, the complex family circumstances of each child emerge, revealing the problems within Iran's education system. Kiarostami vividly captures the children's diverse expressions and words while sounding an alarm to society. A digital remastered version was screened as part of the special program 'And Kiarostami Continues' (from October 16, 2021, at Eurospace in Tokyo and other venues).
tmdb:1453589: An animated film based on the novel 'Nihonjin' by Oscar Nakazato, which won the 'Jabuti Prize' in 2012, the most prestigious literary award in Brazil's publishing world, depicting the rich human drama of three generations of Japanese immigrants living in Brazil. Inspired by the visual world of contemporary artist Oscar Oiwa, who expresses sweeping, allegorical perspectives with meticulous detail, it was brought to the screen by the Brazilian animation studio PINGUIM CONTENT. Noboru, a 10-year-old boy who is a third-generation Japanese-Brazilian, is given a school assignment to research his cultural identity and visits his grandfather Hideo. The taciturn Hideo has avoided confronting his past, but begins to tell his life story to Noboru. In the 1920s, 20-year-old Hideo arrived in Brazil after a two-month voyage and struggled daily on an unfamiliar coffee plantation. As Noboru delves deeper into his family's history, he learns of an uncle, Haruo, whom he has never met. Ken Kaneko, a painter and first-generation Japanese immigrant from Yokohama, voices the grandfather Hideo, and Pietro Takeda, an 11-year-old with several years of voice acting experience, voices the grandson Noboru.
tmdb:1453778: STORY: In the dark city of East Asia, Shinjuku's Kabukicho district. A man walks with a swagger, cutting through the wind: Aiba Shiro, a rookie detective at the Shinjuku Central Police Station. Born and raised in Kabukicho, Aiba, a former bōsōzoku gang leader, is always causing trouble due to his physical strength and hot-blooded nature. One day, Korean National Police Agency detective Choi Si-woo arrives in Japan, pursuing a heinous internationally wanted criminal syndicate. From day one, the two clash and are on the verge of conflict, but with information that the wanted criminals are hiding in Kabukicho, they form an impromptu partnership and begin a joint investigation. As they investigate while remaining at odds, a certain group robbery incident triggers a massive conflict between a violent yakuza group and Kabukicho's largest host club group. Furthermore, the criminal syndicate joins the fray, and Shinjuku, transformed into a battlefield, is enveloped in chaotic darkness. And lurking behind it all is a vast conspiracy involving state power.
tmdb:1454699: Set in Shizuoka during the 1970s and 80s, this human drama portrays a single mother navigating a turbulent era, searching for her own way to live while walking forward with strength. In 1977, during a fierce storm that causes a blackout at the hospital, Fujiko gives birth to her daughter Mari. But her joy as a new mother is short-lived; she suffers unreasonable treatment from her husband's family, and her infant daughter Mari is taken away by her mother-in-law and sister-in-law. With the help of her own mother Chiyo, Fujiko manages to get Mari back and, defying opposition from those around her, decides to raise Mari as a single mother. Buffeted by the waves of the times, she refuses to be defeated by society, seeks freedom, and desperately fights to survive with the support of those around her. Yuki Katayama ('The Burning of the Crimson') stars as Fujiko. YOU plays the spiteful mother-in-law Toshiko, Lily Franky plays Sasaki, whom Fujiko meets through her insurance sales job, Tsuyoshi Ujiki plays Fujiko's ailing father, Keiko Takeshita plays Hatayama, the director of the daycare center Fujiko turns to, Issey Ogata plays Oishi, an old friend of Fujiko's father who runs a soba shop, Kayoko Kishimoto plays Fujiko's mother Chiyo, and MEGUMI plays Nagura, the owner of the coffee shop where Fujiko works. Directed and based on an original story by Taichi Kimura, who has directed numerous music videos and commercials and gained attention with his 2023 feature debut 'AFTERGLOWS'. MEGUMI handled planning and production.
tmdb:1454836: Ryuichi Sakamoto performed with a full orchestra in Japan for the first time in 16 years at the acclaimed concert "Playing the Orchestra 2013." As an updated version, the 2014 Tokyo concert, which he conducted himself, became "Ryuichi Sakamoto | Playing the Orchestra 2014." At this concert, Sakamoto played the piano while conducting all pieces, performing a diverse repertoire—from YMO-era classics to masterpieces like "Merry Christmas, Mr. Lawrence" and "The Last Emperor," as well as his film scores—with the Tokyo Philharmonic Orchestra.
tmdb:14551: The Winchester rifle, a legendary gun said to be one in tens of thousands. A drama of joys and sorrows unfolds around the people who come into possession of this rifle one after another, with all episodes converging into a single finale. A masterfully structured classic Western.
tmdb:1456349: A suspense thriller by Iranian master Jafar Panahi, winner of the Palme d'Or at the 78th Cannes Film Festival in 2025. It thrillingly and humorously depicts people wrongfully imprisoned seeking revenge. Vahid, once unjustly imprisoned, accidentally encounters a man he believes was his torturer guard. He forcibly restrains the man and digs a hole in the wilderness to bury him, but the man's ID card shows a different name. The man claims it's a case of mistaken identity. Blindfolded during imprisonment, Vahid never saw his torturer's face. Unsure if this is the right man, Vahid pauses revenge and visits a friend who was also tortured by the same guard. Panahi, banned from filmmaking by the Iranian government for opposition activities, drew inspiration from his own two imprisonments and the real voices of cellmates. Having won the Golden Lion at Venice for 'The Circle' and 'No Bears', and the Golden Bear at Berlin for 'Taxi', Panahi achieved the feat of winning top prizes at all three major festivals with this film. A French co-production, it was France's entry for Best International Feature Film at the 98th Academy Awards and received a nomination.
tmdb:1457842: A new feature film from director José Luis Guerín, who captivated the world with 'In the City of Sylvia' (2007) and was called 'the most outstanding filmmaker in contemporary Spain' by fellow Spanish director Víctor Erice. Despite his sparse output, Guerín continues to create masterpieces that lightly transcend the boundaries between fiction and documentary. This is his long-awaited new film, his first in ten years since 'The Academy of Muses' (2015), now arriving in Japan. To commemorate the release of 'The Good Valley Story,' the beautiful masterpiece 'In the City of Sylvia' will also be revived. Please enjoy Guerín's world on the big screen. The Vallbona district, located on the outskirts of Barcelona, Spain. This place, named 'The Good Valley,' is surrounded by rivers and railway tracks, an isolated land left behind by development, yet it also seems like an ideal paradise blessed with nature so rich it's hard to believe it's near a big city. Here, families who moved in from the mid-20th century live together with a new generation of immigrants who have arrived recently. Although their cultures and lifestyles differ, the children play together in the river, and everyone eats, drinks, sings, and dances well, finding a moment of peace. A new railway expansion plan is proposed for this urban oasis. A residents' information meeting is held, and some people are forced to relocate...
tmdb:1464639: The sequel to the 2020 anime film 'Poupelle of Chimney Town,' based on the picture book of the same name by Akihiro Nishino. Based on the 2019 picture book 'Tick Tock: The Promised Clock Tower,' it is adapted on a much larger scale, depicting the story of the boy Rubitch meeting his dear friend Poupelle, who went far away in the previous film, once again. One year has passed since the miracle night when Chimney Town was enveloped in a starry sky. The boy Rubitch, who lost his dear best friend Poupelle, continued to believe in their reunion but eventually gives up to move forward. One day, Rubitch wanders into a mysterious otherworld that controls time, the 'Millennium Fortress.' In this world, clocks that no longer tell time are disposed of, but there is a mysterious clock tower that, though not broken, has stopped at 11:59. The mission Rubitch is given to return to his original world is to get this stopped clock tower moving again. Rubitch meets a man who has kept a promise and waited for 100 years, and regains the courage to believe. Continuing from the previous film, Akihiro Nishino serves as executive producer, original creator, and screenwriter, Yusuke Hirota directs, and STUDIO4°C handles the animation production. Yuzuna Nagase, a child actor known for the TV drama series 'Asa ga Kita,' voices the protagonist Rubitch, and Masataka Kubota, who voiced Poupelle in the previous film, reprises his role.
tmdb:1464829: Set in rapidly redeveloping Tokyo's Shibuya, this drama portrays the relationship between a father and son left behind after the mother's death. It marks the film debut of Koyo Kurozaki, who gained attention for his acting debut in the NHK morning drama "Boogie Woogie." This is the feature debut of Yuiga Dansuka, based on his original script; he previously directed the short "I Want to Go Far Away" as part of the Agency for Cultural Affairs' young filmmaker development project "ndjc (New Directions in Japanese Cinema)." Ren, a young man working as a Phalaenopsis orchid delivery driver in Shibuya, became estranged from his father, Hajime, a landscape designer, after losing his mother, Yumiko, as a child. One day, Ren coincidentally meets his father during a delivery and tells his sister Emi, but she remains indifferent, quietly preparing for her own wedding. Amidst this, Ren tries to reassess his distance from his family. Kurozaki plays the protagonist Ren, Kenichi Endo (an indispensable supporting actor in Japanese cinema) plays his father Hajime, Haru Ikewaki (active as an actress and model) plays the deceased mother Yumiko, and Maso Kuryu (a talented actress from "Chrysanthemum and Guillotine" and "The Lies of the Suzuki Family") plays his sister Emi. The film was selected for the Directors' Fortnight at the 78th Cannes Film Festival in 2025.
tmdb:1464883: Lamia, chosen as the 'honorable' cake maker, goes out to town with her grandmother and friend the rooster to search for cake ingredients──
tmdb:1465560: In 2024, as the Israeli attacks on Gaza continued, Iranian filmmaker Sepideh Farsi felt an urgent need to share the voices of the local people. However, with Gaza under blockade, entry was impossible. She decided to produce a film centered on video calls with Fatma Hassouna, a 24-year-old Palestinian photojournalist living in northern Gaza whom she had met.
tmdb:1466682: This biographical drama centers on Fumiko Kaneko, a nihilist and anarchist who fiercely resisted Japan's state power about 100 years ago, depicting the 121 days from her death sentence to her suicide in prison. Directed by female filmmaker Sachi Hamano (known for "Yukiko-san no Ashioto"), the film draws on tanka poems that convey Kaneko's own voice to portray her solitary struggle. Born in 1903, Kaneko grew up as a "non-registered person" because her father never filed her birth registration. At age nine, she was sent to live with her grandmother and aunt in Korea, where she suffered abuse akin to slavery from a family that exploited the colonized Korean villagers. In 1919, she witnessed the March First Independence Movement in Korea. Sent back to her mother's home in Yamanashi at 16, she later struggled through poverty in Tokyo, moving ideologically from Christianity to socialism, anarchism, and finally nihilism. She eventually met Park Yeol, a Korean independence activist who had fled to Japan. Becoming comrades and lovers, they campaigned against Japanese imperialism and colonialism, but were arrested during the 1923 Great Kanto Earthquake and sentenced to death. After her sentence was commuted to life imprisonment through amnesty, Kaneko was sent to Tochigi Women's Prison, where she continued her solitary fight behind bars. Nanana stars as Kaneko, embodying the soulful cry of a woman who defied state power to the end. Katsuya Kobayashi plays Park Yeol, with supporting performances by Masaki Miura, Yoko Horaguchi, and Kazuko Yoshiyuki.
tmdb:14696: Commentary: In an age of war, men driven by lust chase illusions even at the cost of sacrificing women... Based on a classic tale of the supernatural, this masterpiece reflects the folly of humans deluded by desire, suspended between reality and fantasy. Winner of the Silver Lion at the Venice Film Festival, it spread Mizoguchi's name worldwide.
tmdb:1476614: Director Ryusuke Hamaguchi ("Drive My Car," "Evil Does Not Exist") portrays the spiritual encounter of two women with the same-sounding name in Paris. Based on the exchange of 20 letters between philosopher Makiko Miyano, who survived cancer metastasis, and anthropologist Maho Isono, titled "Suddenly Feeling Ill," the film depicts the connection between two women who meet by chance and their confrontation with the world. Marie-Lou Fontaine, director of the care facility "Garden of Freedom" on the outskirts of Paris, struggles with staff shortages and misunderstanding while striving for humane care. She meets Japanese stage director Mari Morisaki, who is battling cancer, and draws courage from her theater work. Guided by the coincidence of their similar-sounding names, Marie-Lou and Mari begin a friendship. But one day, Mari suddenly falls ill. As her illness progresses, their bond deepens, and their souls connect. Virginie Efira ("Benedetta") plays Marie-Lou, and Tao Okamoto, a global fashion model who has appeared in Hollywood films like "The Wolverine," plays Mari. Kyozo Nagatsuka ("Enemy") plays Goro Seimiya, an actor in Mari's play, and Koyo Kuroki ("The Generation of the Looking-Ahead") plays Tomoki Kubodera, Goro's grandson. Screened in the Competition section of the 79th Cannes Film Festival in 2026, Virginie Efira and Tao Okamoto jointly won the Best Actress award. Okamoto became the first Japanese person to win the Cannes Best Actress award.
tmdb:14784:
Four years in the making, spanning over 13 World Heritage sites and 24 countries.
Visual beauty like peering into a kaleidoscope; the power of a story that resonates with the soul.
tmdb:1479653: The eighth installment of the 2025-26 season of "MET Live Viewing," which records and screens the latest opera performances at the Metropolitan Opera House in New York. Based on Mexican painters Frida Kahlo and Diego Rivera, this production reverses the setting of the classic Italian opera "Orfeo ed Euridice," depicting a deceased wife returning from the underworld to her husband for just one day in "Frida and Diego: The Last Dream" (recording of the performance staged on May 30, 2026). In 1957, on Mexico's Day of the Dead. Diego, who lost his wife Frida three years earlier, is tormented by age and grief, longing to reunite with her. Meanwhile, Frida, freed from suffering in the underworld, is told by La Catrina, the guardian of the dead, that she should accompany Diego at the end of his life, and reluctantly agrees to return to the earthly world for only 24 hours. Diego and Frida have a moving reunion, but Frida is bound by a rule that she must not touch the living.
tmdb:1480382: January 29, 2024. Based on the true tragedy the world watched from the sidelines—a soul-shaking true-life drama. On January 29, 2024, a volunteer team from the Palestinian humanitarian organization Palestine Red Crescent Society receives an emergency call. It is from Hind Rajab, a 6-year-old girl trapped in a car under gunfire in the Gaza Strip. The Red Crescent volunteer team keeps the line open with Rajab and exhausts every possible means to rescue her— Directed and written by acclaimed Tunisian filmmaker Kaouther Ben Hania, who continues to explore the boundary between fiction and documentary.
tmdb:1480504: The feature directorial debut of Terrence Malick, director of "Days of Heaven" and "The Thin Red Line," released in 1973. Based on a series of real murders that occurred in the late 1950s in America, it vividly and poetically depicts the flight of a young couple who commit a series of unplanned crimes. In 1959, in a small town in South Dakota. Holly, a 15-year-old girl who is not very noticeable at school, meets Kit, a young garbage collector, and falls in love. However, when Kit shoots and kills Holly's father, who disapproves of their relationship, the two embark on a aimless journey of escape. They live a reckless life, staying carefree in a treehouse and breaking into a rich man's mansion. Holly can only watch as Kit kills people one after another... Martin Sheen, known for "Apocalypse Now," plays Kit, and Sissy Spacek, known for "Carrie," plays Holly. In Japan, it was broadcast on TV in 1980 under the title "Jigoku no Tōhikō," and was released in theaters for the first time in March 2025 under the title "Badlands."
tmdb:1482884: Centering on the intense and mysterious relationship between two women—one dominant, one submissive, almost like doppelgängers—this masterpiece from Chabrol's 'peak period' exudes a powerful allure with the film itself baring love and hatred. One day, Frédérique, a bourgeois woman, spots Hoïe, a girl drawing on the pavement of the Pont des Arts bridge over the Seine. Hoïe comes to live at Frédérique's mansion and is drawn to Paul, a guest, but Paul also has a relationship with Frédérique... A sensual work filled with the complex and ambiguous hearts of women. In this film, Stéphane Audran, who was already Chabrol's wife, co-stars with her former husband Jean-Louis Trintignant. (1968) *All films screened in digitally remastered versions.
tmdb:1484359:
A concert film capturing the live performance held to commemorate the 15th anniversary of the six-member South Korean boy group INFINITE. Since their debut in 2010, INFINITE has garnered global acclaim for their catchy tracks and perfectly synchronized choreography. Their world tour, "2024 - 2025 INFINITE 15th ANNIVERSARY CONCERT ‘LIMITED EDITION’"—held in honor of their 15th anniversary in 2025—was met with rave reviews, proving the group's enduring popularity and powerful presence.

This film features the full recording of the Seoul stop of the tour, held at the KSPO DOME in December 2024. In addition to their spectacular stage performances and overwhelming vocal prowess, the film includes exclusive behind-the-scenes footage and member interviews that can only be seen here. From the crowd-pleasing "The Chaser" to the first-ever live performance of "AIR"—brought to the stage by passionate requests from fans worldwide—and the solo stages into which each member poured their heart and soul, the magic of the concert is brought back to life on the big screen.
tmdb:1487961: The first film adaptation in 20 years of the hit 1976 series "Aa!! Hana no Ōendan." At the Minami Kawachi University cheerleading squad, an annual alumni gathering is planned, but they discover a hole in their precious team flag. The members hurriedly take part-time jobs to earn repair money, but the workplace is run by yakuza who refuse to pay and threaten them. However, Sekidō Aota appears and beats the yakuza to a pulp. Ken'ichi Nagira reprises his role as senior Yakutsuji from the previous series, and Junko Miyashita also appears.
