Yeon-su Ha, who moved her base of operations from Korea to Japan and appeared in the NHK morning drama 'The Tiger's Wing,' plays Kim Juri, the part-time worker who initially keeps her distance from George due to her free-spirited nature. Yusuke Mikawa, known for 'Cloud,' co-stars as Iwakura, another part-time employee who watches over the two.
tmdb:1603232: A documentary depicting the 25-year culmination of the three-member music unit 'Perfume,' which announced a 'cold sleep' (hiatus) in 2025. Formed in Hiroshima in 1999, Perfume gained attention not only in Japan but worldwide after the huge breakout success of their 2007 single 'Polyrhythm.' Having raced through 25 years, they announced a hiatus from 2026, termed a 'cold sleep,' on September 21, 2025, the 20th anniversary of their major debut. This film looks back at their journey from formation to the present, including live performances—especially their last concert before the cold sleep and first Tokyo Dome show in five years, 'Perfume ZO/Z5 Anniversary "Nebula Romance" Episode TOKYO DOME' held on September 22 and 23—along with unreleased footage. It also closely follows the behind-the-scenes after the cold sleep announcement and features exclusive interviews with the three members. The three, who have grown both as artists and as people over 25 years, explore what has changed and what remains constant, as well as their feelings about the cold sleep. The director is Taketoshi Sado, who also directed the 2015 Perfume documentary film 'WE ARE Perfume WORLD TOUR 3rd DOCUMENT.'
tmdb:1605972: A heartwarming comedy that became a massive hit in France, depicting the chaos that ensues when a father-and-son jewel thief duo hide out at a summer camp for people with disabilities. Paulo and his father rob a jewelry store, but when their getaway car is towed, they are left with no means of escape. Stranded on the street, they are mistaken for new arrivals by staff from a care facility about to depart for a summer camp. Taking advantage of the confusion, they pose as a resident and his caregiver to sneak into the camp. The lively days spent with the vibrant residents gradually begin to soften the hearts of the father and son. Popular French comedian, actor, and writer Artus serves as director and screenwriter while starring as Paulo, joined by veteran actor Clovis Cornillac (Paris 36) as the father. The fellow campers are played by 11 amateur actors who actually have disabilities.
tmdb:1607600:
A youth music film reuniting director Tomorowo Taguchi and screenwriter Kankuro Kudo of *Iden & Tity*. Based on the autobiographical essay *Street Kingdom* by photographer Yuichi Jibiki—who served as the group's photographer and manager—the film depicts the "Tokyo Rockers," a movement of young people who forged Japan's first homegrown punk rock scene.

In 1978, Yuichi, a young photographer who moved to Tokyo driven by the sounds of the Sex Pistols on the radio, visits a live house after discovering a small rock zine called *Rockin' Doll*. There, he finds a space overflowing with raw energy where music, bands, and audiences are free from all restraint. Blown away by a performance from the band TOKAGE, led by vocalist Momo, Yuichi captures the moment in a frenzy of shutter clicks.

Officially hired as their photographer, Yuichi grows closer to the band. Their music soon ignites a fire among the youth, evolving into the "Tokyo Rockers" movement that would redefine the landscape of Japanese rock.

Kazunobu Mineta stars as Yuichi alongside Ryuya Wakaba as Momo. The ensemble cast includes Riho Yoshioka, Taiga Nakano, Shotaro Mamiya, Nao Omori, Shido Nakamura, and Sena Nakajima. Yoshihide Otomo (*Iden & Tity*) provides the film's music.
tmdb:1608471: Satoshi Kimura, director of 'Strange Lovers from Another Planet' and 'The Melancholic After-School of Yoyogi Johnny', takes on the classic French genre of 'vacation film' with this dialogue-driven drama. At the start of summer, Yuka, freshly divorced from Haruki after three years together, visits a seaside town on vacation with her best friend Shina and Shina's boyfriend Dazai. Yuka and Dazai were once in love, and reuniting with him rekindles her feelings. Meanwhile, Shina finds herself drawn to Tenma, a poet living in the seaside town. The film creates '1:1' scenes where characters enter the frame in pairs, unfolding the story through a chain of different combinations. The emotion of 'liking' determines each character's formation, shifting relationships as they cross paths. Yu Imari ('Soirée', 'A Janitor') plays Yuka, Ei Adachi ('If Tokugawa Ieyasu Became Prime Minister') plays Dazai, Yuki Shinho ('YOUNG&FINE') plays Shina, Takeo Yamaguchi ('BADBOYS THE MOVIE') plays Tenma, and Ryo Igarashi ('Before Dawn') plays Haruki.
tmdb:1613385:
The classic drama series "Oretachi no Tabi," a quintessential symbol of youth in the Showa era, receives its first-ever film adaptation. Since its debut as a serial drama on the Nippon TV network in 1975, the series has continued through special episodes produced at various milestones in the protagonists' lives. This sequel, arriving 20 years after the last installment, marks the directorial debut of lead actor Masatoshi Nakamura.

Kosuke Tsumura (nicknamed "Kasuke"), his college classmate Takao Kanzaki ("Omeda"), and his elementary school senior Shinroku Kumazawa ("Guzu-roku") have now reached their 70s, their friendship spanning over 50 years. Kasuke runs a small local factory, Omeda serves as the mayor of Yonago City in Tottori Prefecture, and Guzu-roku is the chairman of a nursing care facility—each living out their peaceful daily lives.

One day, Omeda visits Kasuke's factory, but he appears deeply troubled
tmdb:1616908: At a convenience store called AnyMart in a corner of Tokyo, the assistant manager Sakai (Sosuke Ikematsu) has spent most of his twenties working there since his student days. Register work. Stocking shelves. Disposal. Mobile games. Dating apps. Just repeating the same things every day. The owner (Masahiko Nishimura) rules the store within the convenience store system, allowing no deviation. However, the arrival of a new part-time worker, Ogawa (Erika Karata), begins to quietly disrupt the store's equilibrium. Eventually, this distortion silently and surely transforms the convenience store into an extreme space.
tmdb:1620313: Acclaimed director Kiyoshi Kurosawa ("Wife of a Spy," "Creepy") takes on his first period film, adapting the mystery novel of the same name by Honobu Yonezawa, which won both the 166th Naoki Prize and the 12th Yamaneko Prize. Murashige Araki rebels against Nobunaga Oda's tyrannical methods and holes up in Arioka Castle. Surrounded by the Oda army and isolated, Murashige struggles to control his hot-blooded retainers while relying on his wife, Chiyo, for emotional support, striving to protect the castle and its people. Amidst this, a boy is murdered inside the castle, followed by a series of strange incidents. With the suspects being the retainers and family members trapped inside the sealed-off castle, and the enemy outside, everyone falls into suspicion and paranoia. Cornered, Murashige seeks help from the genius military strategist Kanbei Kuroda, who was imprisoned after being sent as Nobunaga's envoy to persuade him, and sets out to solve the case. Starring Masahiro Motoki as Lord Murashige Araki, Masaki Suda as the genius strategist Kanbei Kuroda, Yuriko Yoshitaka as Murashige's wife Chiyo, Takao Aoki as Murashige's trusted retainer Kyusaemon Araki, Ryota Miyate (Snow Man) as the young retainer Saburo Inui, Tasuku Emoto as the skilled sniper Sagari Saika who witnesses the events, and Joe Odagiri as Juemon Kori, who operates in the shadows as Murashige's hidden blade. The film was selected for the Cannes Premiere section at the 79th Cannes Film Festival in 2026.
tmdb:1621777: A psycho-horror film self-remade by director Taro Miyaoka, known for "The Fallen" and "Last Summer Wars," based on his own independent film "Chain"—which won the Special Jury Prize at the 21st Tokyo Student Film Festival—after more than 15 years. Exploring the boundary between love and obsession, it thrillingly depicts human madness. Tatsuki, a 23-year-old who has never had a girlfriend, meets Erica, a beautiful woman working at a café, and is captivated by her kindness. Their relationship deepens, but Erica's suggestive words and actions, along with inexplicable events around Tatsuki, gradually cast an unsettling shadow over his daily life. Eventually, Erica's abnormal obsession and madness are revealed, dragging Tatsuki into an inescapable fate. Starring Ayumu Mochizuki, who rose to fame with the two-part film "Solomon's Perjury." The heroine Erica is played by Mei Hayashi, who has worked as a model since elementary school and made her acting debut in the 2024 drama "Goodbye, Teacher." The cast also includes Hayato Takao, Kurea Hatsuki, Moeka Koizumi, and Itsuki Fujiwara. The screenplay was written by Tete Inoue of "Initiation Love."
tmdb:1622621: A youth romance anime film adaptation of the novel of the same name by Madoroka. Set against the backdrop of the 'Nagaoka Festival Grand Fireworks Display' in Nagaoka City, Niigata Prefecture, one of Japan's three major fireworks festivals that attracts hundreds of thousands of visitors annually, it depicts a promise that transcends time and a summer in the lives of high school students. One day shortly after entering high school, Makoto Natsume meets his classmate Akira Hayama. Since childhood, Akira has been told by her great-grandmother that she would 'one day meet Makoto Natsume,' and she holds a single painting of fireworks. As they investigate the secret of the painting, which Makoto has no memory of, the two discover the existence of 'a certain promise' made in the past. Eventually, the meaning of a fate connected across time becomes clear. The voice of the protagonist, Makoto, is played by Shōri Satō, a member of the popular group 'timelesz,' in his first lead role in an anime film. The heroine, Akira, is voiced by Nanoka Hara, known for playing the protagonist Suzume Iwato in 'Suzume.' The director is Kei Suzuki of the TV anime 'Tower of God.' The project is produced by Shin-Ei Animation, with animation production jointly handled by SynergySP and Answer Studio.
tmdb:1623075:
This cinematic experience fuses footage from large-scale music live events with animation, following the expansive worldview of LDH JAPAN’s next-generation comprehensive entertainment project, "BATTLE OF TOKYO." Set in the fictional future city of "Super Tokyo," the project reimagines real-life LDH artists as fictional characters, depicting a narrative that traverses both real and virtual worlds. Between 2019 and 2024, massive live events featuring GENERATIONS, THE RAMPAGE, FANTASTICS, BALLISTIK BOYZ, and PSYCHIC FEVER (2023/2024 only) were held, drawing a cumulative audience of 500,000 people. 

This film features a re-edited mix of carefully selected live performance footage and music videos, with audio remastered in 5.1ch surround sound. The animated segments vividly and dramatically portray the final chapter of the story—originally depicted in the novel "BATTLE OF TOKYO" by Soki Tsukishima—revolving around the battles and bonds of five teams of youths possessing special skills. The film features voice acting by Yuki Kaji, Yuma Uchida, and Tomokazu Sugita. EXILE HIRO serves as the project producer, with Norihisa Hiranuma ("HiGH&LOW THE WORST X") directing and Dai Sato ("Ghost in the Shell: Stand Alone Complex") writing the screenplay.
tmdb:1623376: A live-action film adaptation of the soccer manga 'Blue Lock', serialized in Kodansha's 'Weekly Shonen Magazine' since 2018, which has gained popularity both domestically and internationally for its innovative premise, unique and egotistical characters, and unpredictable story development. To overcome the Japanese national team's chronic lack of goal-scoring ability, a top-secret project, the 'Blue Lock (Blue Prison)', is launched. Three hundred high school strikers are gathered and subjected to numerous trials, with only the final survivor earning the right to become the world's greatest striker. However, there's a cruel condition: those eliminated are permanently banned from ever representing Japan. Yoichi Isagi, an unknown high school player who dreams of becoming the national team's ace striker and winning the World Cup, decides to participate to change his life. Lacking the outstanding physical abilities of the other 299 participants, Isagi relies on his exceptional spatial awareness to survey the entire pitch and his strong will to pursue the goal, taking on the fierce survival battle. Takahashi Fumiya stars as Yoichi Isagi. The cast includes Sakurai Kaito as Meguru Bachira (Team Z), Takahashi Kyohei (Naniwa Danshi) as Hyoma Chigiri, Nomura Kota as Rensuke Kunigami, K (&TEAM) as Seishiro Nagi (the undefeated champion Team V), Tsunahiro Keito as Reo Mikage, Kubota Masataka as Jinpachi Ego (the project's supreme leader), and Hatakeyama Mei as Anri Teieri (Ego's right hand). The Japan Football Association and J.League fully cooperated with the filming, and former Japanese national team player Matsui Daisuke served as soccer supervisor.
tmdb:1624755:
**Introduction**
Fifteen years after the Great East Japan Earthquake. A Self-Defense Force member who lost his wife and child, and a boy who lost his parents. This is a story of rebirth for two individuals as they begin to walk forward alongside their experiences of loss.

Director Yuji Kakizaki, who earned high acclaim for his previous work *The Sun Falls*—a profound human drama focusing on the resolve of a samurai’s wife and the bond of a married couple—now takes on a new challenge: a story of "loss" and "rebirth."

The film stars Yasuyuki Maekawa, who left an unforgettable impression in the director's previous work. He breathes life into Third Lieutenant Kasuga, a JSDF member who continues his duties despite losing his wife and young daughter in the tsunami, through a performance imbued with quiet strength. Set in the disaster-stricken areas of the Great East Japan Earthquake, Kasuga spends his days providing support at evacuation centers, facing people head-on while carrying his own deep pain. It is there that he meets Kazuki Yoshimura, a boy who has
tmdb:1624812: A crime drama about three women who have drifted through life, who deepen their bond through gold smuggling and reclaim their respective lives. Director Chihiro Amano ("Mrs. Noisy") was inspired by a real 2017 incident in which housewives were arrested for gold smuggling at Chubu Centrair International Airport. She co-wrote the original script with Madoka Kumagai, with whom she also worked on "Sato-san and Sato-san." Large-scale location shooting was conducted in Singapore, depicting the glamorous yet perilous journey of gold smuggling. Wakako, a mother of two living a peaceful life, learns that her husband has been fired from his company for embezzlement. To pay off her husband's debts, she becomes involved in gold smuggling in Singapore, where she meets Kiyoe, a non-regular researcher struggling with student loan repayments, and Mayu, an unmarried pregnant woman with zero savings. After successfully smuggling gold and getting a taste for it, the three decide to start smuggling on their own. For the first time, they gain money, freedom, and the joy of living authentically, spending a magical time together—but... Kasumi Arimura plays Wakako, the mother of two who learns of her husband's embezzlement; Haru Kuroki plays Kiyoe, the indebted researcher; Sara Minami plays Mayu, the unmarried pregnant woman; Akihisa Shiono plays Wakako's husband Takashi; Yuzu Aoki plays Kiyoe's colleague Shiina; and Takumi Saito plays Takashi's boss Tanoue.
tmdb:1626: This is Jean-Luc Godard's fourth feature film, following "A Woman Is a Woman," and was shot starring Anna Karina, his partner both publicly and privately. Nana, who decides to part ways with her husband after discussing life with him at a café in Paris, falls into a life where she cannot even pay her rent. She begins to proposition men on the street and engage in prostitution. Eventually, Nana becomes numb to having relations with strangers. The music was handled by Michel Legrand, the renowned composer of "The Umbrellas of Cherbourg" and other films.
tmdb:1630435: Based on the debut novel by physician-author Yo Hisakabe published in 2003, this human suspense film stars Shota Sometani. At the daycare facility 'Ijinzaka Clinic,' an innovative treatment devised by director Kuranosuke Urushibara spreads quietly among the elderly. Aiming for cost-effective care, the treatment involves 'useless limbs' (paralyzed body parts with no hope of recovery), and unexpected 'favorable side effects' have appeared, such as 'feeling lighter in body and mind' and 'a harsh personality softening.' Hearing rumors, editor Yagura senses potential for a revolution in geriatric medicine and proposes publishing a book to Urushibara. However, everything takes a dark turn when an internal whistleblowing about the daycare leaks to a weekly magazine, and a shocking incident occurs at a patient's home. Sometani delivers a haunting performance as Urushibara, a doctor who, in pursuit of his ideals, steps into the gap between rationality and madness. The cast includes Yuki Kitamura as editor Yagura, Naomasa Rokudaira as elderly patient Iwagami who reclaims his life through Urushibara's treatment, and Kumi Takiuchi as Urushibara's wife Kikuko. The film is directed and written by Mitsuki Yoshida, who has gained international attention for works such as 'Family X' and 'Three Lights.'
tmdb:16306: A singular fantasy masterpiece, this film adapts the novel by French sci-fi author Stefan Wul through the distinct visual artistry of illustrator Roland Topor. Set on the wild planet Ygam, it depicts the conflict and eventual cooperation between the humanoid Oms and the giant Draags, who treat them like slaves. The film’s staggering sci-fi imagination and unique animation style are truly a sight to behold.
tmdb:1631314: A youth comedy directed by Makoto Ueda, head of the theater group "Europe Kikaku," known for writing screenplays for numerous hit films like "Summer Time Machine Blues" and "River, Don't Flow On." This is his feature directorial debut, set in the real-life building "Shelbo Shimokitazawa" in Shimokitazawa, employing innovative gimmicks. At the cinema Tollywood on the second floor of "Shelbo Shimokitazawa," Madoka, a playwright from Shimokitazawa, and Kazuma, a band musician from Sangenjaya, each go to see a movie. An impossible structure emerges where each other's events are projected onto the screen as a film. Meanwhile, problems arise at the shops adjacent to the cinema, "Good Heavens" and "Mikazuki Rock." Madoka and Kazuma try to solve the problems using this structure, but their films influence each other, and the situation spirals in unexpected directions. Starring Maria Ito ("Summer Film ni Notte") as Madoka the playwright and Kai Inowaki ("Musicophilia") as Kazuma the band musician. The cast also includes Oshiro Maeda and Hinako Kikuchi as members of Madoka's theater troupe, Suzuyuki Kaneko and Yusuke Mikawa as members of Kazuma's band, Takafumi Imai as a semi-delinquent who frequents "Mikazuki Rock," and the comedy duo "The Geese" as a pair of detectives. Additionally, members of Europe Kikaku, including Gota Ishida, Shintaro Kanamaru, and Riko Fujitani, play unique characters.
tmdb:1633438: This documentary captures the life of Shigeru Endo, who, despite being confined to his bed by cerebral palsy, interacts with young caregivers and composes numerous tanka poems from his bedside. The film is directed by Shinichi Ise, a friend of Endo since their student days, who previously helmed the 1999 documentary *Entoko*, which also followed Endo’s daily life. Despite his physical limitations, Endo organized his own caregiver network called "Entoko" (meaning both "where Endo is" and "a place of connections"). As his disability progressed over more than 35 years in bed, Endo began writing tanka in his late 50s, using poetry to give voice to the cries of his soul. Through the deep emotional connection between Endo and his caregivers, the film portrays people living in a way that honors and sustains life exactly as it is.
tmdb:1633790: During an internal audit at headquarters, Kurumi from the maintenance team notices that one live round for the revolver cannon is missing. She consults Kikkyo, and one by one, the other squad members get drawn into the situation. Unaware of this, Towa and Saki begin to suspect the attitudes of Kikkyo and the others...
tmdb:1634021:
The fourth installment of the "Our Recipe Book Series," a youth film project centered on the themes of community, food, and high school life. Set in Kiyose City, Tokyo, the film humorously depicts a summer spent by high school film club members with an alien they encounter by chance.

Hayate, a high school sophomore living in Kiyose, is a massive sci-fi fan. He secretly dreamed of filming an alien movie with his club, but had lost his nerve after his previous work was panned by critics. However, one day just before summer break, something crashes into the woods of Kiyose, and Hayate and his fellow film club members encounter a real alien there. Alongside this extraterrestrial visitor and a group of unique friends—including his handsome, movie-loving childhood friend Hinata; the cheerful and brainy "Bon-chan"; and the easygoing, music-loving Wakamizu—Hayate sets out to make his movie.

The film is directed by Masahide Ichii, known for "Haruchika: Bring on the Melody," "The Family of Typhoon," and "What to Do with My Husband: Oh My Charlie."
tmdb:1634820: A full AI-produced film adaptation (with all dialogue in English) of horror manga artist Hino Hideshi's terrifying yet moving story 'Horror! The Man of Dead Flesh.' One day, a 'living corpse' suddenly appears in the city—his body is rotting and squishy, maggots crawl from his eyes, and his heart isn't beating, yet somehow he is alive! After being taken into police custody, the man is sent to a university hospital's isolation ward. Growing sick of the repeated human experiments, he finally attempts to escape... Who is he, and where is he headed? A poignant and sorrowful man of dead flesh. His fate begins with death. What awaits him beyond?
tmdb:1637456: Starring Tasuku Emoto, this drama explores themes of family memory and records. Yuta, who lives with his wife and daughter in Tokyo, travels to a rural town in Kyushu to care for his father-in-law Makoto, who has broken his leg, until he recovers. While helping out at Makoto's old-fashioned photo studio, Yuta exchanges videos taken on his smartphone with his wife and daughter back in Tokyo. Even without major events, the accumulation of daily trivial records and memories quietly and vividly reveals the long span of a family's life. Moka Kamishiraishi ("Shōgun," "Girl Encounters") plays Yuta's wife Yuki, who continues working and raising their child in Tokyo. Issey Ogata plays Makoto, the taciturn father-in-law, and Yū Kashii plays a character symbolizing precious family memories. Director Miu Sakanishi, who gained attention for short films while at Kyoto University of Art and Design and later worked as an assistant director for Yūya Ishii and a making-of cameraman for Yūichirō Doi, makes her feature-length directorial debut.
tmdb:1637635: Directed by Keisuke Yoshida of "Himeanole" and "Missing," this drama portrays boys who cannot understand pain or common sense, and the adults who continue to confront them head-on. Yoshida wrote the original script based on the juvenile delinquents he encountered during his own sensitive adolescence and the community surrounding them. Nishiken Go, a former half-gray area gangster and ex-convict, runs a full-time residential rehabilitation facility called "Mirai no Sato" in a coastal provincial town. Drawing on his own experiences, Nishiken tackles troubled children with all his might, but his rehabilitation methods, which do not shy away from corporal punishment, are criticized by educators. One day, a middle school teacher named Fuyuko consults him about an uncontrollable student, Kaito, and Yu, who has just been released from a juvenile detention center. Meeting the two, Nishiken instantly sees through Kaito's madness. Kaito's mother, exhausted by his severe domestic violence, decides to entrust her son to "Mirai no Sato." However, Kaito causes trouble with the other residents, escapes, and is arrested for assault. Wataru Ichinose of the Netflix drama "Sanctuary" stars as Nishiken, while the newcomer Hayato Uesaka is cast as the delinquent boy Kaito. Kaho plays middle school teacher Fuyuko, Atsushi Shinohara and Fusako Urabe play Kaito's parents, Iori Wada plays Kaito's delinquent friend Yu, and Nanami Yamazaki and Mansaku Takada play the facility's residents.
tmdb:1638776: The sequel and conclusion to the 2023 blockbuster 'Till We Meet Again on the Lily Hill', a live-action adaptation of Shiomi Natsue's best-selling novel, which depicted the poignant love between a high school girl who time-travels from the present to 1945 and a kamikaze pilot. Based on the sequel novel 'I Want to Meet You Again on That Starry Hill', it follows the story of Yuri, the protagonist, after she wakes up in the present day, having lost her beloved in a senseless manner. Seven years have passed since her parting with Akira, the kamikaze pilot. Yuri has become a high school teacher, a dream of Akira's, and leads a busy life, but her heart remains left behind on that lily-covered hill in 1945. A young man named Ryo, who bears a resemblance to Akira, appears before her. He is a temporary teacher assigned as the deputy homeroom teacher for Yuri's class. Yuri is swayed by Ryo's straightforward affection, but she cannot bring herself to embrace a new love, feeling it would betray Akira. Amidst her inner conflict, Yuri meets Chiyo, an elderly woman spending her peaceful final days in a hospice. It's another form of love that Chiyo walked after losing Ishimaru. And what Chiyo entrusts to Yuri is a book left by Akira just before his sortie, addressed to the future Yuri. The cast reunites members from the previous film, including Fukuhara Haru as Yuri, Deguchi Natsuki, and Ito Kentaro. Additionally, Hosoda Kanata plays Ryo, the young man with Akira's likeness, and Baisho Chieko plays the elderly Chiyo. Directed by Niinobe Katsuhiko of '366 Days', with the theme song performed by Fukuyama Masaharu, continuing from the previous film.
tmdb:1639386: A documentary depicting the life of activist Teishiro Minami, who organized Japan's first Pride Parade in 1994. Today, Pride Parades are held in over 40 locations in Japan, and partnership systems are spreading nationwide. At the starting point of this progress were the grassroots activities of pioneers who forged a path from "zero" to "one." Born in Karafuto (Sakhalin) in 1931 and raised in Akita Prefecture, Teishiro Minami moved to Tokyo at age 22, constantly searching for a way to live authentically. In 1984, he began the gay liberation movement, immersing himself in activism and following his passion. Then, in 1994, he launched Japan's first Pride Parade. The activities Minami spearheaded became the foundation of the pride movement in Japan, but he gradually became fixated on his own beliefs, deepening the rift with those around him. By the third parade, he faced significant backlash and was forced to step back from the front lines of the movement. What did Minami, driven by justice and swept along by the times, find in the end of his fervor? Tracing his tumultuous path through his own testimony, interviews with people involved at the time, news reports, photos, and videos, the film depicts the origins of the pride movement in Japan. Directed by Hiroaki Matsuoka ("Okinawa Coming Out Story").
tmdb:1642802:
An original work from the creative duo behind the *Thus Spoke Kishibe Rohan* series, director Kazutaka Watanabe and star Issey Takahashi. Inspired by the "Sunekosuri" (shin-rubber) folklore of Okayama Prefecture, this film is set deep within a forest to tell a mysterious, beautiful, and cruel tale of love.

Deep in a forest far from civilization, a young man with an injured leg is led by a woman’s sweet singing voice to an ancient shrine. Living there are a mysterious man and his young, beautiful wife, Sayuri. Nursed back to health, the young man spends a dreamlike time where it feels as though time itself has stopped. These peaceful, repeating days seem as if they might last forever, but...

Director Watanabe personally visited the forests of Okayama, drawing inspiration from local legends to pen this original screenplay. Filming took place in the cities of Takahashi and Niimi in Okayama Prefecture. Issey Takahashi stars as the mysterious man, while rising star Nijiko Aoto, in her second film role, plays Sayuri, the mysterious woman living deep in the woods. Koudai Kurosaki, who garnered attention for his lead role in *The Miharashi Generation* (selected for the 78th Cannes Film Festival Directors' Fortnight), portrays the injured young man who wanders into the forest.
tmdb:1645545:
Twenty-two-year-old Iroha lives at home, dissatisfied with her current self and facing an uncertain future. One day, her older sister Karen returns for the first time in five years. Karen is free-spirited and lives for romance—a woman who, unlike Iroha, has always made bold choices in life. But the reality she carries with her is this: "I'm pregnant. But I don't know who the father is."

There are three possibilities: a wealthy heir, an older man with a violent streak, and an ex-boyfriend burdened by debt. In each relationship, there remains an ambiguity that falls short of being called "love." Why does Karen keep repeating romances she knows will only end in pain? Dragged along on the search for the father, Iroha travels across Nagasaki Prefecture with her sister, witnessing the loneliness and the desperate need for validation that lie beneath the surface of romance.

The sister who seemed so strong was, in truth, longing to be loved more than anyone else. Contrary to her glamorous exterior, she had been constantly entrusting her self-worth to others. At the same time, Iroha realizes that she herself had been running away from being hurt by avoiding love altogether.

More important than being chosen by someone else is acknowledging yourself. Before being loved by another, you must accept yourself. Clashing and baring their true feelings, the sisters finally come to understand each other's weaknesses. Carrying their love without answers and their own imperfect selves... the sisters' journey continues.
tmdb:1647782: A bold, original film adaptation of Junichiro Tanizaki's novel 'The Key', which explores the depths of sexuality through the alternating diaries of a married couple. Starring Mitsuru Fukikoshi, it lays bare a dying man's obsessive attachment and pure love for his younger wife. Kenzo Kenmochi, who runs a construction company, is told by his doctor he has only six months to live. Worried about his much younger wife Ikuko, he schemes to push her into an affair with his subordinate Kimura. As Kimura and Ikuko grow closer, things go according to plan, but Kenzo cannot let go of his feelings for Ikuko. Despite his physical decline, his jealousy intensifies. When he secretly reads Ikuko's diary, he finds her feelings of strong attraction to Kimura's body. Mitsuru Fukikoshi humorously plays the clumsy, jealousy-consumed Kenzo. Kei Kanno plays his wife Ikuko, and Keisuke Koide plays Kimura. The film is directed and written by Shinji Imaoka, known for scripting 'The Zombie Child' and directing 'Reiko and the Dolphin', with Minoru Matsumoto co-writing the screenplay.
tmdb:1649900: A documentary following Namiko Kawamura, an 84-year-old expressive artist who continues to work as a dancer and performer. Directed by Toshiko Rin, known for documentary works such as "Jibun, Maru! Ippo no Hanashi," "Nishi Tenka Chaya Ooishi So," and "Blessed." Kawamura has been familiar with dance since childhood, and from the 1970s onward, she explored a unique form of expression incorporating perception and walking in nature. After participating in a workshop by American dancer Anna Halprin in the 1980s, she established a performance of "slow walking"—a forward-moving gait. This act, both a dance and a way of life, has continued for many years. Set in Okinawa, a place Kawamura had long wished to visit, the film explores the thoughts and memories behind her expression through beach performances and interviews. It records her walking and dancing while confronting the time embedded in a land marked by war memories, observing the journey of a woman who has dedicated her life to dance.
tmdb:1651162: A film adaptation of the novel "Iwaiyama" by Nanami Kamon, an author known for works on folklore and the occult, based on her own experiences, starring Ai Hashimoto. Directed and written by Shingo Takeda, a filmmaker who has won awards at film festivals for his horror works, marking his feature-length theatrical debut. Horror novelist Minami Kano, suffering from writer's block, receives a letter from her middle school classmate Asako Yaguchi. The letter describes unexplainable phenomena that have been occurring ever since she went on a dare to visit a ruin known as a haunted spot. Seeking material for her new work, Minami reunites with Asako and their old friends, and becomes entangled in mysterious events. As the investigation progresses, it emerges that behind the series of strange occurrences lies the forbidden mountain "Iwaiyama" they once set foot on. Ai Hashimoto plays the protagonist Minami Kano, marking her first horror film role in ten years since "Zan: The Haunted Room." The cast also includes Ren Ishikawa, Sayu Kubota, Takuya Kusakawa, Yuya Matsuura, and Go Riju.
tmdb:1651166: A live-action film adaptation of novelist Kyogoku Natsuhiko's unique mystery novel of the same name set in modern times, starring Nao. A woman named Asami Kashima is murdered. With no clue as to the culprit's identity or motive, a mysterious woman named Eiko Watarai visits those who knew Asami in life, claiming she wants to ask about her. As she follows various testimonies, the outline of Asami's character and her relationship with Eiko gradually emerge. Nao plays Eiko, who goes around asking about Asami. Aoi Ito plays Asami, whose impression changes depending on who is asked; Ko Maehara plays Asami's boss and lover, Hiroyuki Yamazaki; Hikaru Takahashi plays Asami's senior, Kaori Shinomiya; Takuya Kusakawa (from the group Shinkansen) plays Asami's boyfriend, Yuya Sakuma; Tomoko Tabata plays Asami's mother, Naoko Kashima; and Tetsu Hirahara plays the lawyer involved in Asami's case, Riku Gojo. Directed by Junichi Kanai, who previously worked with Nao on "My Daddy," with a screenplay by Kohei Kiyasu (known for "The Kirishima Thing"). The rock band "This is LAST" performs the theme song.
tmdb:1651171: A youth story based on the manga 'Zakken!' (published by Shogakukan), which was developed from a real club activity, the 'Weed Research Club,' at Tokyo Metropolitan Hibiya High School, by screenwriter and film director Naho Uemura and the scenario creation team 'Monogatari Lab,' with Uemura herself writing and directing the film adaptation. It delicately and freshly depicts a teenage girl lost and unsure of herself, who discovers her own identity through the weeds growing at her feet, which she had never paid attention to before. Spring of her first year of high school. Sugano Yukari, an ordinary girl who isn't passionate about anything and just goes through the motions, meets her classmate Tokuda Mimi, nicknamed 'Dokudami-chan,' who loves weeds and is fascinated by their vitality. Slightly eccentric but with a straightforward and pure heart, Yukari gradually opens up to her. Dokudami-chan dreams of reviving the 'Zakken,' or 'Weed Research Club,' and Yukari, while hesitant about her enthusiasm, begins activities with her aimed at reviving the club, but... Luna Nakajima, who has starred in films like 'A Town of Old Houses' and 'Tore!' and won the Japan Academy Prize for Newcomer for 'Tokyo Taxi,' plays Sugano Yukari, and Miyu Oshima, known for the NHK morning drama 'Omusubi' and the drama 'Bokutachi nchi,' plays Tokuda Mimi, taking on the lead roles.
tmdb:1653724:
Set in Shinjuku’s Kabukicho district following the closure of the "Toyoko" area, this suspenseful drama follows four displaced youths over the course of a single night as their fates collide in a desperate escape. Marking the feature film debut of 24-year-old rising talent Ren Akiba, the film is a feature-length adaptation of his own short film which won the Grand Prix at the 2nd Tokyo Independent Film Festival. Akiba penned the original screenplay based on his own personal experiences in Kabukicho.

Asuka, a high school student who feels she has no place at home or school, travels to Kabukicho drawn by "Tokyo Escape," an autobiographical web novel written by a girl living in Toyoko. There, she happens to meet the author, Hiyori, and the two form an immediate bond. Asuka is introduced to Edo, a protector of the drifters in Toyoko, and Merio, a leader among the local youth. However, after attending a meeting led by Merio and witnessing a shocking reality, Asuka grabs Hiyori’s hand and flees. Their escape earns them the ire of a "han-gure" criminal group, leaving them hunted. Meanwhile, Edo fights to preserve the youths' sanctuary, while Merio makes increasingly dangerous choices in his pursuit of the girls. As the police become involved, the situation spirals toward a rapid climax.

The film stars Rio Teramoto as Asuka, Akana Ikeda as Hiyori, Keito Tsuna as Edo, and Nao Takahashi as Merio, supported by Yuya Matsuura, Motoki Fukami, and Honami Sato. Michihito Fujii, director of *The Strangers* and *The Journalist*, serves as executive producer.
tmdb:1654395: A youth romance live-action film adaptation of the shōjo manga of the same name by Yu Saiki, serialized in Kodansha's 'Bessatsu Friend,' starring Kyōhei Takahashi of the idol group 'Naniwa Danshi.' It depicts the romantic journey of Satsuki, an ordinary high school girl who dreams of love, and Yamaguchi-kun, a transfer student with a scary-looking face and a Kansai dialect. Yamaguchi-kun, who transfers to Satsuki's school, has blonde hair and piercings, giving him a menacing look, and rumors circulate that he's a yakuza. After a certain incident brings her close to Yamaguchi-kun, Satsuki learns about his shy and kind true nature and gradually becomes drawn to him. Satsuki tries to keep Yamaguchi-kun's hidden charms all to herself, but a handsome classmate, Ishizaki, who inexplicably has a grudge against Yamaguchi-kun, stands in her way. It turns out Ishizaki also harbors special feelings for Yamaguchi-kun, suddenly emerging as Satsuki's romantic rival. The love triangle of these three takes an unexpected turn. Kyōhei Takahashi plays Yamaguchi-kun, who has a kind and pure heart beneath his scary appearance; Hikaru Takahashi ('Romantic Killer') plays the heroine Satsuki, who grows close to Yamaguchi-kun; and Yōji Iwase ('The Girl and the Guard Dog') plays Ishizaki, the classmate who stirs up trouble between Yamaguchi-kun and Satsuki. The film is directed by Kentarō Moriya ('PRINCE OF LEGEND,' 'Seaside Motel').
tmdb:1654870: A comedy starring Hiroshi Tachi, depicting a 70-year-old movie star caught up in a major uproar over surrendering his driver's license. Nanjo Hiroshi, who has enjoyed a smooth acting career and recently won numerous film awards for art films, secretly longs to appear in action movies. When his longtime actor friend Ozaki Makoto gets into a motorcycle accident, Nanjo is asked by the media for comment as a fellow actor of the same generation. His remarks admonishing Ozaki unexpectedly attract public attention, and the narrative takes on a life of its own, involving his manager and family, and being interpreted in ways far from his original intent. Although Nanjo wants to continue performing action scenes with cars and motorcycles, those around him expect him to surrender his license, plunging him into the biggest crisis of his life. Hiroshi Tachi comically plays actor Nanjo Hiroshi, the same name as the character he played in the 1994 film "License!". Nishino Nanase plays his manager Kawauna Mai, who is thrown into chaos by Nanjo; Kurokawa Sooya plays young man Kugami Ryo, whose life changes dramatically after meeting Nanjo; Yoshida Kotaro plays Mita Atsushi, the president of Nanjo's talent agency; and Uzaki Ryudo plays Ozaki Makoto, an actor friend who built an era alongside Nanjo. Directed by Kawai Yuji of "Kaguya-sama: Love Is War" fame, with screenplay by Hayashi Tamio of "From the Land of Love to the Land of Sorrow".
tmdb:1656442:
Set in the mysterious amusement park "Gamaland," this medium-length horror film employs a found-footage format to depict an inexplicable story surrounding Miyuki Sawada. Gamaland was a real-life location once symbolized by its iconic, giant toad statue. A VHS tape recorded there, steeped in the atmosphere of the early Heisei era, captures a date between a couple, Kohei Shimizu and Miyuki Sawada—but the footage gradually transforms into something deeply unsettling.

The film is directed by Koki Nishii, the filmmaker behind the YouTube channel "Filmest TV," which specializes in recreating modern subjects with a 1980s and 90s aesthetic. Nishii, who also made waves with the September 2024 YouTube drama *Tomochika Suspense Theater: Sotoyu Meguri Mystery - Dogo Striptease Girl Serial Murders*, served as screenwriter and editor, and appears in the film under the name "Nishii." The cast features Tsubasa Nakahara (Masashi Yamamoto’s *DUDE*) as Miyuki Sawada and Takeo Gozu (Netflix’s *Tokyo Swindlers*). The film is produced by NOTHING NEW, a label garnering attention for horror works such as *Chilled* (winner of the FIPRESCI Prize at the Berlin International Film Festival), the short film anthology *NN4444*, and the medium-length horror *Shiki*.
tmdb:1657017: The protagonist is Sohui, a 14-year-old Zainichi Korean girl. She attends a Korean school and devotes herself to Korean dance in her club activities. One day, at an exchange event with a Japanese school, she becomes friends with a Japanese girl named Mirai over their shared love of K-Pop, and Sohui gradually connects with the outside world. To earn money for tickets to their favorite K-Pop idol's concert, the two decide to sell unused items from Sohui's house on a flea market app. Surprisingly, the item that sells for a high price is a North Korean CD owned by Sohui's father, Sanju, who is the principal of the Korean school. Emboldened, Sohui and her friend even sell a "medal" awarded to Sanju by his homeland, North Korea.
tmdb:1657504: Actor Tsuyoshi Rishu, who has directed films such as 'Chloe' and 'Goodbye Debussy', takes the director's chair for a feature film for the first time in 13 years, with Issei Takahashi in the lead role. This human drama humorously depicts a man who has avoided social interactions, whose life takes an unexpected turn when he discovers he has been unknowingly registered as married to a woman he doesn't know. Mikio Natsuno, a slightly naive man who never gets angry, goes to get a copy of his family register to renew his passport and is shocked to find the words 'Relationship: Wife' for a woman he has absolutely no memory of. Learning that a woman named 'Shigeko' has registered herself as his wife without his knowledge, Mikio begins searching for this mysterious woman. He eventually finds Shigeko at a small flower shop on a street corner, but she is an unconventional woman who destroys everything she touches. Though Mikio is tossed around by Shigeko, this strange encounter gradually brings unexpected changes to both their lives. Issei Takahashi plays the kind-hearted and sensitive protagonist Mikio, and Kumi Goshima (NHK morning drama 'Manpuku') plays the enigmatic heroine Shigeko who bewilders everyone around her. Okihiko Serizawa and Chizuru Ikewaki co-star, and director Rishu also appears as a key character. World-renowned jazz pianist Junko Onishi provides the music.
tmdb:1658226: Directed by Takashi Shimizu of the "Ju-On" series, this school horror film stars Suzuka Chinzei of the idol group FRUITS ZIPPER in the lead role. A secret rumor circulates among young people about a forbidden game: if you record a date and name onto a cassette tape on the 13th step of an empty school staircase, that person will die. High school students casually try the game, and their daily lives begin to warp. One by one, those whose names were recorded on the tape die mysteriously on the specified dates. The school takes the situation seriously and asks psychological counselor Koharu Hirase to provide mental care for the students. Koharu counsels a student who witnessed the incidents, but among those who played the game is her younger sister, Nanami. As students are attacked by strange phenomena one after another, Koharu and Nanami are dragged into a chain of terror. Suzuka Chinzei takes on her first solo lead film role and first horror role as counselor Koharu; Anna Hoshino (from "Gold Boy") plays Koharu's sister Nanami; Riku Onishi (from "Water Flows Toward the Sea") plays classmate Jotaro Chiba who looks out for Nanami; and Shota Sometani plays a young man who holds the key to the story.
tmdb:1658268: Minoru (Hiromitsu Kitayama) and Yuki (Chihiro Kato) move with their young son Akira to Minoru's family home in a heavy snowfall area. The couple wishes for a peaceful life, but Minoru's father Shigeru, who has dementia, is inexplicably terrified of Yuki and calls out his deceased wife's name. One morning, Shigeru dies grotesquely in an abnormal state. From that moment on, the family is plagued by suspicion and fear. Soon, eerie 'white women' begin appearing in the house one after another, encroaching on their daily lives. Minoru, as if losing his mind, keeps drawing pictures of the 'white woman,' while young Akira's view of his mother gradually begins to reflect 'something else.' One by one, the family members break down. Minoru, captivated by snowflakes and losing his reason; Yuki, being eroded; and Akira, placed in danger. Is this a curse, an illusion, or reality? When the snowy plains are stained with fresh blood, an unknown 'white terror' appears and runs amok with brutality.
tmdb:1659338: A sequel to the 2026 TV anime 'Death Game de Meshi o Kū,' based on the popular light novel by Yūshi Ukai, this theatrical anime adapts the original 'Cloudy Beach' arc. A deadly murder game where survival earns you prize money. Allies you encouraged yesterday can become enemies today, and even with full preparation, you can lose your life. The girl Yūki aims to clear this life-or-death game 99 times, making a living from the prize money she wins. Overcoming the 'Wall of Thirty'—a jinx where player survival rates drop drastically—she continues forward and takes on her 44th game, 'Cloudy Beach.' Among the eight players gathered on a remote island, Yūki spots a familiar veteran. Continuing from the TV anime, Sōda Ueno of 'Stepsister Life' directs, with animation production by Studio Deen.
tmdb:1662803: A rare directorial effort from Isamu Kosugi—the star actor of Nikkatsu’s contemporary dramas—produced during his time at Toyoko Eiga. Ryosuke (Haida) and Kinuko (Hidaka) are engaged but unable to take the plunge into marriage due to the post-war housing shortage. When they finally secure a new home through a housing lottery, Ryosuke’s benefactor Kawakami (Furukawa), a repatriate from Manchuria, moves in unannounced, throwing their new life into unexpected chaos. The film vibrantly depicts the couple as they navigate Kawakami’s inconsiderate behavior, striving to overcome their troubles with songs and laughter.
tmdb:1663038: The third installment in the human comedy series that explores family dynamics and second chances through the theme of "shukatsu" (end-of-life planning), following "Oshukatsu: Jukushun! Jinsei, Hyakunen Jidai no Sugoshikata" and "Oshukatsu: Saishun! Jinsei Rhapsody." Aya, the eldest daughter of Shinichi and Chikako Ohara, finally decides to marry her fiancé Ryota. However, just before the wedding, a casual remark from Aya causes a rift in their relationship, escalating into a major commotion involving both families. Meanwhile, Shinichi's junior colleague Kato struggles to accept his mother Toyoko's progressing dementia, speaking harshly to her. Chikako gently tells Kato, "Even with dementia, the heart doesn't forget." Continuing from the previous two films, director Hideyuki Kazuki helms this installment, incorporating the latest end-of-life planning trends and knowledge while depicting family bonds with light humor and a warm perspective. The cast reunites familiar faces from the series, including Tsurube Shofukutei as Shinichi Ohara, Junko Takahata as his wife Chikako, Ayame Goriki as their daughter Aya, along with Yuki Matsushita, Masahiko Nishimura, Norika Fujiwara, Renji Ishibashi, Kumiko Fujiyoshi, LiLiCo, Kunikazu Katsumata, and Yoshihiko Hakamada. Guest stars include Keiko Mita as Toyoko, who has dementia, and Fumiyo Kohinata as her son Kato, who supports her despite his own inner conflict.
tmdb:1663041: Director Taichi Kazama, known for the TV drama "Silent," adapts manga artist Akari Tamura's comic into a live-action film, a love story about the first crushes of "supporting characters" who have quietly lived on the fringes of society. Shy and reserved college student Nobuko Tanaka identifies with the term "mob," meaning crowd, extra, or non-major character, and has lived her life watching from afar as other protagonists shine. Then, she notices Hiroki Irie, a young man working part-time at the same supermarket. Touched by Irie's natural thoughtfulness, Nobuko gradually becomes drawn to him. Through her encounter with Irie, she begins to struggle to break free from the shell that has bound her, and while sometimes confronted with harsh realities, she perseveres with the support of her coworkers. Meanwhile, Irie also notices Nobuko's quiet kindness and looks straight at her. The accumulation of small, everyday moments eventually gives them both the strength to take a step forward. Hiyori Sakurada ("The Diary of a Substitute Lie") plays Nobuko, aka Mobuko, and Taisei Kido ("Yukite Kaeranu") plays Hiroki Irie, the object of her first love. The cast also includes Ikoi Hayase as Nobuko's junior coworker Abe, Erika Karata as senior coworker Shinozaki, Takuya Kusakawa as fellow part-timer and Irie's friend Kaneko, Tsubasa Araki as new part-timer Ono, and Kanji Furutachi as store manager Orihara.
tmdb:1663504: A film version serving as a sequel to the TV dramas 'Chaser Game W: My Ex-Girlfriend is My Harassing Boss' and 'Chaser Game W2: The Beautiful Celestial Maidens,' which delicately portrayed the realities of the game industry and a romance between women. Set seven years after the drama, it depicts the relationship evolving over time and the two women confronting life choices. Itsuki and Fuyu live in Ito City, Shizuoka Prefecture, with their daughter Tsuki, now a middle school student. As they become consumed by housework, childcare, and work, their time together becomes routine. Over the seven years, their relationship shifts from lovers to family, and they gradually begin to drift apart. Though they maintain a peaceful home while being disturbed by each other's casual words and attitudes, their daughter Tsuki senses the unease between her parents. One day, Tsuki gets into trouble and is helped by a taxi driver named Kozue. This encounter prompts Itsuki and Fuyu to confront each other's true feelings for the first time and re-examine the form of love they have lost sight of. Continuing from the drama series, Sugai Yuka stars as Itsuki, Nakamura Yurika as Fuyu, Okamoto Mirai as their middle-school-aged daughter Tsuki, Ito Ayumi as taxi driver Kozue, and Kurotani Tomoka as Department Chief Ro. Directed by Ota Isamu, who also worked on the drama series, with a screenplay by Asada Atsushi.
tmdb:16664: In a provincial city, middle school student Yuichi becomes close with the honor student Hoshino, but a summer trip changes the dynamics among their friends. When the new semester begins, Hoshino defeats the class's worst delinquent in a fight and gradually turns into a tyrant himself. As his actions escalate—assault, shoplifting, and forcing classmates into prostitution—Yuichi, who has become a target of bullying, is also made complicit. Turning his eyes away from reality, Yuichi creates a fan site for his idolized artist, Lily Chou-Chou.
tmdb:1671640: The second installment of the omnibus film 'The Bastard and the Beautiful World,' released in 2018 and starring Goro Inagaki, Tsuyoshi Kusanagi, and Shingo Katori of 'New Map.' Directed and written by Kenji Yamauchi, who also participated in the previous film and is known for his work in theater and commercials, as well as directing films like 'I Like My Friend's Dad' and 'Unique Countries of Asia.' In an age where information and answers are instantly available and people try to find meaning in everything, this film invites Inagaki, Kusanagi, and Katori into a story that runs counter to 'meaning,' with the concept of enjoying not knowing things as they are. The cast includes First Summer Uika, who is active not only in variety shows but also in films and taiga dramas; Shuri, who starred in the NHK morning drama 'Boogie Woogie'; and veteran actors such as Kanji Furutachi, Seiyo Uchino, and Mitsuru Fukikoshi.
tmdb:1674644: A documentary providing an intimate behind-the-scenes look at Samurai Japan, the Japanese national baseball team, during the 6th World Baseball Classic (WBC) held in March 2026. Having vowed to "discard admiration and surpass it" to win the world championship in a hard-fought battle at the 2023 WBC, the team entered this tournament under the immense pressure of being the reigning champions, facing the inescapable burden of "having to remain the winning champions." The film explores what the players felt and how they fought during their quest to remain on top, and how they came to terms with the result of losing in the quarterfinals. Through the lens of the only camera granted exclusive access to the team for this tournament, the documentary gets to the heart of the action behind the scenes. The director is Shintaro Miki, who has previously made documentaries closely following Samurai Japan, such as "Unity, Beyond: The Warriors' Anguish and Hope" and "The Samurai Who Surpassed Admiration: Record of Becoming World No. 1." Narration is provided by Kazunari Ninomiya, and the theme song is performed by Koshi Inaba. It began streaming on Netflix on April 20, 2026, and had a limited theatrical release nationwide in Japan starting August 14, 2026, including at Aeon Cinema Itabashi.
tmdb:1677118: A documentary produced to commemorate the 60th anniversary of the landmark special-effects drama series 'Ultraman.' The special-effects TV drama 'Ultraman,' which first aired in 1966, achieved a peak viewership rating of 42.8% and sparked a social phenomenon. Even over 60 years since its birth, Tsuburaya Productions continues to release new Ultraman series works, beloved across generations and borders. This film is planned by filmmaker Kore-eda Hirokazu, known for 'Monsters' and 'Shoplifters,' and features numerous leading creators from film, special effects, and design. Filmmakers Guillermo del Toro, Kore-eda Hirokazu, and Nicolas Winding Refn, game creator Kojima Hideo, anime director Anno Hideaki, and special effects/film director Higuchi Shinji, among others active at the forefront of their fields both in Japan and abroad, offer their unique perspectives to unravel the question, 'What is Ultraman?' The film explores the worldview where the protagonist is a hero yet carefully depicts the background of the kaiju, and the strong appeal of the designs of both Ultraman and the monsters, while also shedding light on the ideas and work of Tsuburaya Eiji and the staff of that era, tracing the journey of how Ultraman spread across the world.
tmdb:1677894: A youth suspense film depicting the struggles and growth of a university student working on a documentary about an incident that occurred in a certain local city. University student Mayu Kuroda is tasked with creating a documentary for a class project based on her own high school experience. Back then, rumors spread that a male teacher, Nitta, had engaged in inappropriate sexual acts with her senior in the broadcasting club, Nojima, whom she admired. Articles in weekly magazines and social media posts drastically changed Nojima's life. Feeling this situation was unjust, Mayu intended to create a work that would serve as a warning about the information society by reflecting on that time. However, as she proceeds with research and filming alongside her university classmates, she is confronted with the reality that the local community is not welcoming the reopening of the case. Furthermore, facts she didn't know at the time and the various intentions of those involved and related parties come to light. Director Hiroki Inoue, highly acclaimed domestically and internationally for the short film 'Aza' and the VR live-action film 'Nagisa ni te', depicts social issues such as bullying, reputational damage via social media, and the insularity of local communities through an original script. Luna Toyota, in her first lead film role, naturally and delicately portrays the protagonist Mayu. Co-stars include Koshu Hirano from the special effects drama 'Ultraman Z', Kohei Yamashita from 'Toritsukushima', Yu Takaoka from the short film 'Tsunagaru', and Yuri Some no from 'Keep Your Hands Off Eizouken!'.
tmdb:1678: A landmark tokusatsu kaiju film produced and released by Toho in 1954. Ships are sinking one after another in the Pacific Ocean. The few survivors report sightings of a giant monster. An investigation team formed by paleontologist Dr. Yamane, his daughter and assistant Emiko, and her fiancé Hideto Ogata, head of a salvage company, is dispatched to Odo Island near the incident site, where the monster eventually appears. Named "Godzilla" after an old island legend, the monster is believed to be an ancient creature that survived in secret, awakened by the radiation from repeated hydrogen bomb tests, and countermeasures are devised. However, humans are helpless against its immense power, and Godzilla lands in Tokyo, turning the city into a sea of fire. Meanwhile, Dr. Yamane's beloved student, scientist Serizawa, has realized a terrible invention that could be effective against Godzilla. Fearing its future misuse, Serizawa hesitates to use it... A Hollywood version directed by Roland Emmerich was also produced in 1998. To commemorate the 60th anniversary in 2014 and the production/release of the second Hollywood version "GODZILLA" (directed by Gareth Edwards), this original film was revived as the "Godzilla 60th Anniversary Digital Remastered Version."
tmdb:168040: After his cheesemaker father passes away, 18-year-old Totone is left to shoulder the family business and care for his seven-year-old sister. This film vividly depicts his daily life as he clumsily yet earnestly strives to carve out a path for himself.
tmdb:1680559: Novelist Jotaro Izumi (Sojiro Yoshimura) made a spectacular debut after winning the Bungei Prize. However, his success was short-lived; now, he spends his days in depravity, borrowing money from his editor, Eiji Matsumura (Kohshu Hirano), on the condition that he write. Pursued relentlessly by photographer Ranko Kijima (Aika Yukihira), he drifts into a relationship and moves into her home, yet the twisted desires writhing within him remain unfulfilled. It is then that Matsumura introduces him to a research subject: Anna Unabara (Suika Yamasaki), a woman once dubbed the "Beautiful Criminal" for swindling 30 million yen through sugar dating. Beneath her quiet and submissive facade lurks an inexplicable strangeness—and Jotaro begins to feel that she may be the one who can finally satisfy his desires.
tmdb:1683000: Set against the chaotic nightscape of Tokyo, this human drama delicately portrays young people living with loneliness and unspoken anguish on the fringes of the city, tackling the extreme subject of a mass suicide event held at a nightclub. Directed and written by Yuto Shimizu, who gained attention with his debut feature 'The Fireworks That Bloomed Inside Me.' A young man named Amenashi loses his sister Anna, who changed after witnessing a classmate's suicide in high school and later took her own life. Burdened by guilt over her death, Amenashi continues to chase her shadow. One night, he learns of a secret mass suicide event held in a corner of Tokyo's neon-lit streets and, drawn to it, steps into the nightclub venue. His friends Notsu and Hattori, suspicious of his actions, follow him and infiltrate the club. In this closed space filled with despairing youth, the three try to escape but are forced to confront the emotions buried deep within their hearts. Amenashi is played by Iori Abe, and his sister Anna by Utano Aoi, both reuniting with director Shimizu after 'The Fireworks That Bloomed Inside Me.' The cast also includes Kosuke Tanaka and Taiga Hironaka, with rappers Kan a.k.a. GAMI, Bontou, and Isaac among the diverse supporting roles. The producer is Ken Ochiai of 'Uzumasa Limelight.'
tmdb:1687841: A short documentary following a boy on a ventilator as he takes on an adventure to a deserted island. Ten-year-old Sota Yoshihara, who requires advanced medical care, and his mother Sumiyo decide to join a tour that takes children with disabilities to a remote island in Okinawa. For Sota, who relies on a ventilator and needs electricity and medical care daily, a trip to an island with no electricity or water is far from safe—one wrong step could be life-threatening. Doctors initially say the tour is too difficult, but Sota's earnest wish to 'go on an adventure to a deserted island' ultimately moves a doctor to accompany the tour himself, making the journey possible. On the day of the tour, with the help of many people, Sota crosses the sea on a small fishing boat and sets foot on the deserted island. The film captures how one boy's small courage and challenge move those around him to fulfill his wish, and reveals moments that remind everyone of what is truly important in their own lives. Directed by Takehiro Noguchi, known for directing NHK's morning drama 'Anpan' and 'Yell' as well as the taiga drama 'What Will Ieyasu Do?', in his documentary directorial debut.
tmdb:1688584: Set in Ueno Park in Tokyo, this human mystery, a Japan-China-Korea co-production, explores human connections while focusing on "disappearance" as a way of life. A homeless man known as "Gojo" in Ueno has died. No one knows his real name, what he did in life, or why he ended up in a tent in the park. Satsuki, a social worker, with the help of Toshi, a man living in the park after losing his wife, searches through the homeless network to uncover Gojo's identity, using his diary as a clue. Eventually, the existence of a woman comes to light, and it's revealed that Gojo had cut ties with his family. This fact also profoundly shakes Satsuki's own life. Kadowaki Mugi stars as Satsuki, a social worker carrying a certain loss from her own past, and Takenaka Naoto co-stars as Toshi, a homeless man who accompanies Satsuki. The director and screenwriter is Wang Qii, who spent his childhood in Japan and studied filmmaking in the UK. Wayne Wang, known for directing "Smoke" and "The Joy Luck Club," is credited as co-writer and project planner.
tmdb:1694409: A human fantasy set in a mysterious beauty salon run by Death, where a woman who must spend her final days there reexamines her life through various encounters and farewells. Based on a proposal by Yoichi Umeki submitted for a Nihon University College of Art class assignment, with a screenplay by Kohei Taniguchi ('This Video Cannot Be Played THE MOVIE') and directed by Shinji Imaoka ('Reiko Iruka'). Hairdresser Miho Saeki, frustrated by troubles at work and in her private life, slips on stairs. Waking up, she is led by rookie Death Sakuma to a suspicious salon 'Meikup' (Makeup), where Death hairdressers touch up the deceased to connect them with loved ones for one last day. However, Miho's actual death is days away, and Sakuma jumped the gun. She stays at the salon until her death. Hinako Sakurai plays Miho, KANON from dance & vocal group STARGLOW plays Sakuma. Okabe Dai (comedy trio Hanako) plays the salon owner, Hirai Amon plays Miho's boyfriend, Inuzuka Kenta plays her salon manager, and Miho Jun plays her mother.
tmdb:1694487: A woman armed with a knife breaks into the office of a paranormal documentary production company. After injuring an employee, she reveals her motive: to "save humanity." She is apparently obsessed with a conspiracy theory claiming that "unless a certain videotape is returned to its rightful place, the human race will perish." The production crew tracks down the man spreading these theories online. He reveals that the video was once submitted to the "Shi-gazo" series and is a clip so terrifying it surpasses even the legendary "Kuniko." The crew unearths the tape and sets out to uncover the true identity of what is captured on screen. However, this was merely the entrance to a labyrinth with no exit, where countless horrors writhe in the shadows...
tmdb:1694504: A youth ensemble drama set on Wakasa Wada Beach in Takahama Town, Fukui Prefecture, the first beach in Asia to receive the international environmental certification "Blue Flag," depicting a young man lost and without dreams who meets lifeguards and grows through challenging trials. Yuki Otomo, a university junior, has no motivation for job hunting and is lost in life. Plagued by loneliness at being left behind by those around him and a sense of futility about the future, he is invited by his uncle to spend summer vacation in Fukui. One day, Yuki tries to save a drowning person but ends up drowning himself, and is rescued by members of the "Wakasa Wada Lifesaving Club." Witnessing their love for the sea and their courage to act for others, a passionate feeling begins to stir in the apathetic Yuki's heart. Deciding to become a lifeguard, Yuki trains hard alongside his peers, but... Model and actor Nose Rin, who made his screen debut in "About a Place in the Kinki Region," makes his film lead debut as Yuki. Satoshi Tokushige plays the leader of the Wakasa Wada Lifesaving Club, Hina Irei plays a club member, Toru Kazama plays Yuki's uncle, and Tokuma Nishioka plays the chairman of the Takahama Town Water Rescue Association. Directed and written by Yoshihisa Kodama, known for "Oshorin," with the ending theme performed by singer-songwriter Hana Sekitori.
tmdb:1696868: An unconventional home drama depicting the daily life of a new father (Frankie), who works from home and is run ragged by his mischievous toddler yet raises him with abundant love. His chemistry with his on-screen wife Ikeuchi is excellent, and Bando and Miki are amusing as hopeless fathers.
tmdb:1697876: A short black comedy written and directed by Kuruma Takahira of the comedy duo 'Reiwa Roman' as his directorial debut. It depicts an incident that occurs on a congested highway late at night, entirely from the perspective of dashcams. Six cars are driving on the highway. Inside each vehicle, excuses, pride, probing, work anxiety, someone being chased, reckless challenges to boost video views, and trivial conversations unfold. Only the dashcams inside the cars record everything. Tomohiro Kodama of the comedy duo 'Sarugorira' stars, with a stellar supporting cast including Joe Odagiri, Kengo Kora, Aoi Morikawa, and Oshiro Maeda. It was released in theaters after a special screening at 'Short Shorts Film Festival & Asia 2026'. A making-of documentary titled 'KURUMA: The Road to BREAK SHOT' was also produced, delving into the behind-the-scenes production.
tmdb:1701409: A love story starring Nakajima Kento and Nagahama Neru as the heroine, set on the set of a romantic comedy drama. Popular actor Kanzaki Reiji, hailed as a '360-degree handsome man,' has starred in numerous romantic comedies. Turning 30, he yearns to be recognized as an actor in more serious works, but receives another offer for a typical rom-com. He resists upon learning his co-star is Minakaze Misato, a member of the idol group 'Pyon Pyon Fruits,' but this encounter will drastically change his life. The polar opposites, Reiji and Misato, are imperfect, leading them to hesitate and clash, yet they grow with the support of those around them. The cast includes Itaya Yuka as producer Shuto Asami, Shiono Akihisa as rival actor Fuchigami Soma, Honda Riki as director Nihei Sanpei, Mitsuishi Ken as senior actor Yamamura Kenji, Zaizen Naomi as veteran screenwriter Hashitani Kinako, and Mitsuishi Kotono as Misato's mother Mariko. Directed by Kamitani Kaede of the TV drama 'She Was Pretty,' with a screenplay by Okita Haruka of the 'Radiation House' series.
tmdb:170657: Young monster hunter Xuanzang uses his "Three Hundred Nursery Rhymes" as a weapon to try to awaken the good hearts of monsters, but always fails. One day, in a riverside village attacked by a half-fish, half-beast monster, he works with the villagers to haul the creature ashore, where it transforms into human form. The nursery rhymes Xuanzang sings have no effect at all, and when he is attacked instead, he is saved by a female monster hunter named Duan.
tmdb:1706714: Four months before the attack on Pearl Harbor—what they saw was the conclusion: 'Japan's inevitable defeat.' In April 1941, there existed an organization called the 'Total War Research Institute,' where elites from across Japan were secretly gathered. The 'best and brightest' of the next generation, selected from bureaucrats, the military, and the private sector, were tasked with 'predicting' the outcome of a war with the United States and other foreign powers. After accumulating vast amounts of data and repeatedly running simulations with anguish and passion, what they saw was a shocking scenario of Japan's 'overwhelming defeat'—one that predicted almost everything except the atomic bombings. Not a single bullet is fired. But here lies the harshest battlefield, where the mind is the weapon. Why did Japan charge into a war it knew it would lose? Now, the 'inconvenient truth' buried in history bares its fangs on the screen.
tmdb:1719557: Bruce Lee, Jackie Chan, Jet Li, Donnie Yen... Yasuaki Kurata is the one and only active action actor who has engaged in fierce battles with countless legends. Now 80 years old and celebrating 60 years as an action actor, this legend takes on a new challenge! Directors Koichi Sakamoto, Kenji Tanigaki, and Yuji Shimomura—three currently active talents who are graduates of the Kurata Action Club—have taken the helm. Filming also took place in Hong Kong, resulting in a historic reunion on screen with Sammo Hung! The miraculous film 'Dream Story' follows a man who has dedicated his life to action. Be sure to see its full scope on the big screen!
tmdb:1722720: A concert film that reconstructs the immersive live experience of the popular K-pop group ATEEZ for theaters. Following their 2025 theatrical release "ATEEZ WORLD TOUR [TOWARDS THE LIGHT : WILL TO POWER] IN CINEMAS," this is their second theatrical release, based on the immersive experience that toured various locations from 2025 by the VR concert platform AMAZE, reconfigured in native 8K resolution and 5.1ch surround sound. One day, a mysterious message arrives for ATEEZ, who are spending a peaceful time at their hideout. From that moment, everything begins to change, and their fans "ATINY" disappear. As if under a spell, ATEEZ wander through a dreamlike wilderness, a world engulfed in flames and collapsing, and a "Dark City" shrouded in deep fog. While pursued by an unidentified force, they launch a counterattack to find ATINY. Featuring Hongjoong, Seonghwa, Yunho, Yeosang, San, Mingi, Wooyoung, and Jongho, the film brings performances of hit songs like "INCEPTION," "BOUNCY (K-HOT CHILLI PEPPERS)," and "Ice On My Teeth" to the big screen. It also includes 20 minutes of unreleased behind-the-scenes footage.
tmdb:17234: Elementary school student Kōichi Uehara finds a large stone buried on a riverbank on his way home. Driven by curiosity, he cracks it open and discovers a dried-up, fossil-like creature inside. It is a baby kappa that has been in a state of suspended animation underground for a long time. Kōichi names it 'Kū' and begins living with it.
tmdb:1728113: KATSEYE: WILD HEARTS offers an intimate look at the group's bold new era and serves as a tribute to the fans who have supported their journey. Through never-before-seen footage, fan videos created by the fandom EYEKONS, and candid interviews with the members, the film portrays the strong bond between KATSEYE and their global fandom. A love letter to the EYEKONS who have helped build the KATSEYE movement, the film reflects that this group's story is only just beginning. The documentary also captures the highs, setbacks, sacrifices, and breakthrough moments KATSEYE experienced on their path to becoming global pop stars—from the intense pressure of the HYBE and Geffen Records audition program The Debut: Dream Academy to topping the charts. Praised by media outlets including The New York Times, Vogue, Rolling Stone, and Billboard, KATSEYE has solidified its global presence as one of the most exciting new-generation global acts in pop through relentless effort and stunning live performances. The team behind Netflix's documentary series Pop Star Academy: KATSEYE returns for this film, produced by Interscope Films and Boardwalk Pictures in partnership with HYBE x GEFFEN. Nadia Hallgren, who also directed the series, serves as director.
tmdb:173: In the 1860s, a series of shipwrecks caused by a mysterious sea monster occur across the globe. Marine biologist Professor Aronnax and his companions are dispatched by the U.S. government to investigate. One night, their vessel collides with a mysterious object: the Nautilus, a versatile submarine commanded by Captain Nemo, a brilliant scientist who harbors a deep hatred for authority and war. Invited by the captain, the professor and his group embark on an extraordinary journey to the depths of the ocean.
tmdb:1730:
Film director David Lynch passed away on January 15, 2025, at the age of 78. Since his 1976 debut *Eraserhead*, the master filmmaker captivated creators and audiences worldwide as the "King of Cult." He left behind only ten feature films, the final of which—2006’s *Inland Empire*—has been 4K remastered under Lynch’s own supervision. This is his most concentrated work, with Lynch himself handling everything from directing and screenwriting to cinematography, music, and editing. Starring Laura Dern as an actress who lands a lead role, the film depicts a nightmarish, absurdist drama where the boundaries between reality and cinema gradually blur. Regarding its alluringly inscrutable content, the director left only one explanation: "about a woman in trouble." This mystery-laden tale sparked polarized reactions upon its release and continues to be spoken of as a legend today.

【STORY】
Hollywood actress Nikki Grace (Laura Dern) is cast in *On High in Blue Tomorrows*, a remake of an unfinished Polish film titled *47*. Before long, she falls into an affair with her co-star Devon Berk (Justin Theroux)—mirroring the film's plot—and the movie's narrative begins to intertwine with her own life. As the boundary between reality and fiction dissolves, Nikki’s psyche is driven toward a total collapse.
tmdb:17431: Sam takes a job that requires him to stay alone on the moon for three years to mine a necessary energy source for Earth. Direct communication with Earth is not permitted, and his only conversation partner is a single artificial intelligence computer. But one day, with only two weeks left until the end of his mission, Sam encounters a person with the same face as his own.
tmdb:1747405: An ensemble drama depicting the lives of three couples at crossroads in life. A former restaurant manager facing mandatory retirement after 25 years and grappling with loneliness, a painter struggling under his father's shadow and on the verge of divorce, and a young man captivated by a mysterious hotel guest. When their seemingly unrelated daily lives intersect, heartwarming "little miracles" unfold alongside unexpected events.
tmdb:175: Jacques (Jean-Marc Barr) and Enzo (Jean Reno) grew up together as childhood friends on a Greek island. Years later, when they reunite on the Côte d'Azur for the first time in twenty years, Enzo invites Jacques to compete in a free-diving world championship held in Sicily, Italy. Meanwhile, Johanna (Rosanna Arquette), who had a chance encounter with Jacques in the Andes, travels from New York to Sicily under the pretext of a business trip.
tmdb:17729: Young trombonist Glenn Miller was always in search of a new sound. He joined a prestigious orchestra but left to focus on arranging. The turning point in his music came from his beloved wife Helen. Following her advice, he formed his own band and eventually achieved unprecedented popularity and fame. However, when World War II began, he volunteered for the Air Force. In late 1944, the plane carrying Glenn Miller disappeared over the English Channel... An emotional musical film, with numerous hit songs coloring the love and bond between the couple played by James Stewart and June Allyson!
tmdb:177945: Ryota (Fukuyama) is a company employee who has carved out his own life and enjoys smooth sailing. One day, a call from the hospital informs him that the son he has raised with love for six years is actually another couple's child, switched at birth. Through interactions with the family who raised his biological son, his values gradually begin to waver, and he grapples with what family and blood ties truly mean. Winner of the Jury Prize at the 66th Cannes Film Festival.
tmdb:17962: A fantasy drama by Hirokazu Kore-eda of "Maborosi" fame, depicting the seven days between death and reaching heaven. Twenty-two deceased people arrive at a facility shrouded in mist. The staff waiting for them instruct them to choose the single most important memory from their lives within the seven days before they go to heaven. Some choose a memory immediately, while others struggle to decide. But the final day, when a screening will be held, steadily approaches. Starring ARATA in his film debut.
tmdb:18030: One night, private detective Mike Hammer picks up a woman named Christina and lets her into his car, but is suddenly attacked by three men and loses consciousness. When he comes to, Mike finds himself in a hospital bed. According to his secretary Velda, Mike and Christina were driven into a river along with the car, and Christina died. Sensing something behind it all, Mike begins to investigate Christina's background.
tmdb:18148: A timeless masterpiece by the master Yasujiro Ozu, this film depicts the changing family relationships in post-war Japan through the story of an elderly couple visiting their children in Tokyo. Using his signature "Ozu style"—characterized by low camera angles and static shots—he meticulously portrays the parent-child dynamic.
