Shukishi and Tomi, an elderly couple living in Onomichi, travel to Tokyo for the first time in a while to visit their children. However, their eldest son, Koichi, a doctor, and their eldest daughter, Shige, who runs a beauty salon, are both too busy with their own lives to pay much attention to their parents. Only Noriko, the widow of their second son who died in the war, shows them genuine kindness and consideration.
tmdb:18311: Director Wong Kar-wai's second feature film from 1990, this youth ensemble drama depicts the romantic entanglements of young people in 1960s Hong Kong with a sense of rushing visual beauty, catapulting Wong Kar-wai to international fame. Yuddy approaches Su, who works as a vendor at a soccer stadium, and they fall in love. However, Yuddy is troubled by not knowing his biological mother. After breaking up with Su, Yuddy spends a night with Mimi, a dancer at a nightclub. Leaving the room, Mimi encounters Yuddy's best friend Zeb, who falls in love with her at first sight. Tide, a policeman on night patrol, has feelings for Su, but she cannot forget Yuddy. The cast features Hong Kong cinema's biggest stars, including Leslie Cheung, Maggie Cheung, Carina Lau, Tony Leung, Andy Lau, and Jacky Cheung. First released in Japan in 1992. A digital remastered version was released in February 2018 at Bunkamura Le Cinema and other venues. A 4K restored version was released in December 2023 as part of the special screening "Wong Kar-wai: The Beginning."
tmdb:18329: A love story directed by Wong Kar-wai of 'Days of Being Wild,' starring Leslie Cheung and Tony Leung as lovers, depicting the poignant romance and human relationships between two men set in Argentina. Ho Po-wing and Lai Yiu-fai, who have loved intensely but repeatedly broken up, head to Iguazu Falls to repair their relationship, but get lost, argue, and part on bad terms. Later, a wounded Ho Po-wing shows up at the apartment of Lai Yiu-fai, who is working as a doorman at a tango bar in Buenos Aires. Lai Yiu-fai reluctantly lets him stay, but after recovering, Ho Po-wing starts going out while Lai Yiu-fai is away. Meanwhile, Lai Yiu-fai changes jobs to work at a Chinese restaurant and becomes close with a young coworker named Chang. It won the Best Director award at the 50th Cannes International Film Festival. Released in theaters in 1997. In February 2018, it had a special screening at Bunkamura Le Cinema to coincide with the release of the digital remaster of Wong Kar-wai's 'Days of Being Wild.' In 2022, a 4K restored version was screened as part of 'WKW4K' (from August 19, 2022, at Cine Mart Shinjuku, Grand Cinema Sunshine, Cinema City, etc.).
tmdb:18352: Set in Prague, Czechoslovakia on the eve of World War II, this dark comedy depicts how an ordinary citizen working at a funeral home is influenced by his pro-Nazi friend and the social climate, driving him toward a disastrous solution. Karel Kopfrkingl, who works as a cremator at a small Prague funeral home, is an ordinary man who loves his family. One day, he reunites with a war buddy from World War I, who has become a member of the Nazi Party. Persuaded by his friend to monitor the local Jewish community, Karel gradually becomes influenced by his friend and the social situation... The film portrays how an utterly ordinary person becomes a perpetrator, using beautiful yet eerie expressionistic imagery. This work, which exposes the terror of totalitarian ideology, was banned in its home country of Czechoslovakia and could not be shown until the fall of the communist regime in 1990. It won the Grand Prize at the 5th Sitges - Catalonian International Film Festival. In Japan, it will have its theatrical premiere in April 2026 as part of "Czech Film Masterpieces," a series featuring classics of the Czech New Wave.
tmdb:1841: A beautiful female editor visits private detective Philip Marlowe, asking him to find the missing wife of a magazine publisher. This experimental film is shot entirely from Marlowe's point of view, using the camera as his eyes.
tmdb:185354: One of four dark sci-fi works by Piotr Szulkin, a pioneer of dystopian sci-fi in Poland, who created them during the late 1970s and 1980s under the socialist regime, navigating strict censorship. The film depicts the theme of 'escape from totalitarianism' with a style of intense satire and surrealism taken to its extreme. Martians have attacked Earth. A TV host has been telling people 'there is nothing to fear,' but his apartment is ransacked and his wife is kidnapped. The nightly TV script is also changed, and the reality he sees no longer matches what he tells people every night. The film will have its theatrical premiere in Japan as part of the special screening project 'Polish Dark Sci-Fi: The Four Films of Piotr Szulkin' (starting February 21, 2026, at Theater Image Forum).
tmdb:1859: A romantic comedy featuring the divinely beautiful Greta Garbo in a comedic performance. The Soviets try to sell jewels confiscated from aristocrats, while the aristocrats are determined to stop them. The man and woman who become their respective agents end up falling in love.
tmdb:185987: Shizuma Shigematsu, living with his family in a village near Fukuyama City, was in Hiroshima with his wife and niece. The atomic bombing was a tragedy that mercilessly took the lives of thousands and forever etched the harsh existence of the survivors.
tmdb:18872: Having witnessed grief work in his TV documentary 'However... In an Age of Welfare Cuts,' Kore-eda tackles this theme head-on in his first theatrical feature, based on the novel of the same name by Teru Miyamoto. Yumiko (Esumi), who carries childhood trauma, loses her husband to suicide in the midst of a happy marriage. Years later, she lives a peaceful life with a new family, but a lingering unease never fully fades. Against the backdrop of Noto's nature captured in long shots, the quiet rebirth of a woman's heart is depicted with a serene gaze.
tmdb:18910: The directorial debut of William Peter Blatty, known as the author of 'The Exorcist,' who adapted his own novel. Blatty wrote, directed, produced, and scripted this unique human drama set in an old castle used as a psychiatric hospital. In a remote mountain castle serving as a sanatorium, soldiers driven insane by the Vietnam War are gathered and treated. Among them is astronaut Billy Cutshaw, who was committed after going mad just before a rocket launch. One day, Navy psychiatrist Hudson Kane arrives at the facility. Kane listens sympathetically to the patients, but Cutshaw is defiant, and Kane soon begins to be plagued by nightmares. Won the Golden Globe for Best Screenplay. Stars Stacy Keach of 'Roadgames' and 'Escape from L.A.' Although never theatrically released in Japan, it will have its first theatrical screening in 2026 as part of the 'Shinjuku Hardcore Masterpiece Selection 2' special screening (April 17 - May 21, 2026, at CineMart Shinjuku).
tmdb:190060: Mekas established his unique "diary film" method with his first feature, *Walden* (1968). This work serves as a sequel of sorts, woven from 124 film sketches of friends he socialized with in New York between 1969 and 1984—the period surrounding the founding of Anthology Film Archives. It also stands as a precious record of the figures behind "Fluxus," the art movement that shaped the SoHo district. A deeper understanding of this context can be gained by referring to the book *Mekas no Yujin Nikki* (Mekas’s Diary of Friends), compiled by Mekas himself following the film's completion (published in 1989 by Shobunsha).
tmdb:19105: Iron Maiden is the definitive band of the New Wave of British Heavy Metal (NWOBHM) movement that emerged in the UK in the early 1980s. They made their debut in 1980 with the self-titled album *Iron Maiden*. Following the release of *Killers* the next year, Bruce Dickinson joined as the band's second lead singer. Their 1982 release, *The Number of the Beast*, became a massive global hit, selling over two million copies. They continued their ascent to the pinnacle of the heavy metal world with a succession of iconic albums, including *Piece of Mind* (1983) and *Powerslave* (1984). After several lineup changes, the band’s roster stabilized in the late 1990s. In 2008, they embarked on the "Somewhere Back in Time Tour," an unprecedented world tour that sent metalheads across the globe into a frenzy.
tmdb:1923: FBI Special Agent Chet Desmond vanishes mysteriously while investigating the murder of local waitress Teresa Banks. One year later, the evil entities lurking throughout the town begin to target the high school queen, Laura Palmer. At the same time, Special Agent Dale Cooper, who has taken over the investigation into the Teresa Banks case, resolves to unravel the profound mystery by drawing upon his unique gift—a sharp sixth sense.
tmdb:194395: Pero, a cat targeted by a bumbling hitman for saving a mouse, fights villains in the American West! The second theatrical film in the beloved series featuring the cute cat that serves as the symbol of Toei Doga (now Toei Animation).
tmdb:196929: Two years after the worldwide acclaim of "Freeze Die Come to Life," protagonist Valerka is now fifteen. As he prepares to bid farewell to his boyhood, the adult world has taken on an even more tragic aspect. His only emotional refuge is Valya, Galya’s younger sister. When Valerka is expelled from school and leaves town alone, Valya continues to send him letters, but...
tmdb:198375: From the director Makoto Shinkai, known for delicate drama and visual beauty in works like 'The Place Promised in Our Early Days' and '5 Centimeters per Second,' comes a love story set for the first time in modern Tokyo. Takao, a high school student aiming to become a shoemaker, skips school on rainy days to sketch shoes in a park's Japanese garden. One such day, he meets a mysterious older woman named Yukino, and the two grow closer through meetings that happen only on rainy days. For Yukino, who says she has lost her place in the world, Takao tries to craft shoes that make her want to walk more, but... The main staff for character design, art, and music features new faces different from Shinkai's previous works. The short film 'Dareka no Manazashi' is shown as a double feature.
tmdb:20108: The 7th feature film by master director Robert Bresson, known for "L'Argent," "Pickpocket," and "The Trial of Joan of Arc," released in 1966. Inspired by an episode from Dostoevsky's novel "The Idiot," it portrays the strange fate of a donkey and a young girl. In a small Pyrenean village, little Marie names a newborn donkey Balthazar and cherishes him. Ten years later, Balthazar is used for hard labor by a blacksmith but escapes the suffering and returns to Marie. The grown Marie rejoices at their reunion and takes Balthazar with her, but Gérard, who has feelings for her, becomes jealous and torments the donkey. Through the silent perspective of the donkey, the film calmly depicts human folly and ugliness, winning the Special Jury Prize at the Venice International Film Festival and earning acclaim as a masterpiece. Starring Anne Wiazemsky, who later appeared in many Godard films including "La Chinoise," in her film debut. First theatrically released in Japan in 1970, and again in 1995 distributed by France Eigasha. Revived in October 2020 in a 4K restored digital remaster. Also revived in 2026 as part of "Robert Bresson Masterpiece Selection."
tmdb:20126: The splendid murder aesthetics of Dario Argento, the emperor of Italian horror, explode throughout the film. In Japan, after the huge success of 'Suspiria' (1977) with the clever tagline 'Never watch it alone,' this film was given a Japanese title to ride on that wave and was released in theaters, but it is actually unrelated in content and was made before that film. A shocking work that weaves the mystery of a series of gruesome murders with Argento's signature gorgeous and shocking visual beauty. Starring David Hemmings from 'Blow-Up' and Daria Nicolodi, Argento's good partner both publicly and privately. At the European Parapsychology Conference held in Rome, a telepathic woman named Helga, while demonstrating her abilities on stage, senses someone's murderous intent and becomes hysterical. She declares that a person who has committed brutal murders is in the audience. Later, Helga is brutally murdered in her room. Mark, a British pianist who happens to arrive at the scene and witnesses the murder and a suspect, teams up with journalist Jenna to investigate the mystery, but the truth they ultimately uncover is beyond imagination.
tmdb:203612: A documentary about the Sagrada Família, the century-spanning architectural project conceived by Catalan architect Antoni Gaudí, under construction since 1882 for over 130 years. Registered as a World Heritage Site in 2005, the Sagrada Família continues to captivate over three million visitors annually from around the world. As construction continues towards a projected completion in 2026, computers have been introduced on site, and staff repeatedly experiment to determine how to best reproduce Gaudí's vision with current technology. Incorporating footage from inside the site, inaccessible to outsiders, and interviews with architectural staff, the film unravels the project surrounding the Sagrada Família, including how the construction period, once said to require '300 years until completion,' has been shortened to a projected completion in 2026.
tmdb:20442: Like 'The Naked Spur,' this is a Technicolor Western directed by Anthony Mann and starring James Stewart, produced by William H. Wright of 'Violent Behavior' in 1953. The screenplay was written by up-and-coming radio and TV writing team Sam Rolfe and Harold Jack Bloom, cinematography by William C. Mellor of 'Cross Missouri,' and music by Bronisław Kaper of 'The Wolf of the North.' Co-stars include Janet Leigh of 'Blood Fight,' Robert Ryan of 'The Three Bad Men of the Wilderness,' newcomer Ralph Meeker of 'The Four Jeeps,' and Millard Mitchell of 'Singin' in the Rain.'
tmdb:20525: In the 15th year of the Genroku era. A young samurai (Okada) burdened by the duty to avenge his father travels from Shinshu to Edo and hides out in a tenement slum. The film depicts how his resolve begins to waver as he interacts with the residents of the tenement. While weaving the story of the Ako Ronin's raid into the background, director Kore-eda turns it on its head, aiming for 'a story where the weak are affirmed as they are.' This ambitious work marks Kore-eda's first deep dive into a narrative world, having previously been conscious of the distance between fiction and nonfiction in his live-action films.
tmdb:20532: Commentary: In the Heian period, Zushio and Anju, separated from their parents, are sold into slavery... A film adaptation of Ogai's short story based on a medieval folktale, this timeless masterpiece won the Silver Lion at the Venice International Film Festival. The visual beauty captured by the renowned cinematographer Miyagawa is also awe-inspiring.
tmdb:2061: Frank, a highly skilled drug pusher, makes money with his partner Tony by carrying out jobs for drug kingpin Milo. After taking a huge loan from Milo for a large deal, a police raid causes the deal to fail, and Frank loses the money, facing relentless pressure from his boss to repay the debt. A crime action drama that depicts a man spiraling into a hellish debt trap in the underworld of rampant drug trafficking, pushed to his absolute limits, all rendered in dark, stylish visuals. This is Nicolas Winding Refn's landmark debut film, hailed as the Danish film that first achieved worldwide success as a gangster movie.
tmdb:20874: A deadpan sci-fi comedy made in Soviet-era Georgia in 1986, which became a huge hit in the USSR at the time. One day, a student named Gedevan asks construction engineer Mashkov for help, looking troubled, saying, 'There are some men over there who claim to be aliens.' Mashkov, who doesn't believe in aliens, presses a button on a space travel device the men were holding, and in the next instant, Mashkov and Gedevan are warped to the planet Pluke in the Kin-Dza-Dza Nebula, far from Earth. There, for some reason, Earth matches are extremely valuable, and the two try to use the value of matches to somehow return to Earth... Culturally popular in Japan as well, it was first introduced at the 'Soviet SF Film Festival' held in Tokyo in 1989, later released in a new print in 2001 and a digital remaster in August 2016. In May 2021, to coincide with the release of the animated version 'Ku! Kin-Dza-Dza,' the live-action film had its fourth theatrical release.
tmdb:208837: A life-affirming drama by rising French director Guillaume Brac, known for 'A Summer's Tale,' depicting an aging, down-and-out musician struggling with a bleak future as he gradually discovers the true meaning of love. Starring Vincent Macaigne, a regular in Brac's films. Maxime, a musician now nearly forgotten by the world, returns to his hometown of Tonnerre in the Burgundy region of France. His single father Claude enjoys outdoor sports, has a vibrant love life, and revels in life, but Maxime, exhausted by city living, has lost his will to live. Then, a young female journalist named Mélodie from a local information magazine comes to interview Maxime. Drawn to her youth and smile, Maxime grows closer to her...
tmdb:21036: This animation was planned following the panda boom in Japan sparked by China's gift of pandas to Ueno Zoo in 1972 as part of Japan-China friendship. Mimiko sends her grandmother off to a memorial service and will be living alone for a while. But when she returns home, there is a child panda who understands human speech. Then the father panda also appears. This panda father and child were lured by the bamboo grove near Mimiko's home. Mimiko treats the father panda, Papanda, as her own father and the child panda, Pan, as her child, and begins living together with them. One day, a policeman visiting Mimiko's house is startled to see the panda pair. In fact, Papanda and Pan had escaped from the zoo. The zoo director, alerted by the police, tries to take them back, but Pan gets lost, and a search begins. Pan is found swept away in a river, with a sluice-gate waterfall beyond—a major crisis. Can they rescue Pan? And can Mimiko and the panda pair live together again?
tmdb:212162: The third film in the theatrical series of "Puella Magi Madoka Magica," which aired on TV from January to April 2011 and received high acclaim and popularity, including winning the Grand Prize in the Animation Division at the 15th Agency for Cultural Affairs Media Arts Festival. Following the "Beginning Story" and "Eternal Story" films, which recompiled the 12-episode TV series, this is a completely new feature-length work with newly written script and animation. In a new world where Madoka Kaname freed magical girls from the chain of cruel fate, Homura Akemi, left behind unable to fulfill her feelings for Madoka, continues to fight alone, believing she can meet Madoka again. New magical girl Nagisa Momoe appears as a new character alongside Madoka and Homura.
tmdb:226860: After learning that his old friend Sakaguchi had attacked the president of Shimogata Construction and been arrested, Shindo returned to a small port town in Okinawa. Shimogata Construction was in charge of the town's redevelopment and had been harassing and threatening Sakaguchi to force him to sell his hotel. Shindo stayed at the hotel, the "Free Inn," and began investigating the incident. Meeting Shimogata's development chief Takabatake and Detective Tokuda, who was colluding with Shimogata, Shindo uncovered the truth: Sakaguchi had stormed Shimogata Construction to rescue his kidnapped son, Ryuta. Shindo also learned that Sakaguchi was suffering from cancer and had only a few months to live.
tmdb:22984: Alongside The Beatles and The Rolling Stones, The Who led the golden age of British rock and continued to innovate the genre as a superband. This rock documentary masterpiece features live performances of their greatest hits from 1964 to 1978—a period when they were unable to tour Japan at their peak—along with promotional films and interviews. Among the many historic scenes, the film notably features Keith Moon, the legendary genius drummer, in his final full-bodied performance, filmed at Shepperton Studios in May 1978 specifically for this production—a truly precious treasure.
tmdb:238937: Tokijiro sets out on a journey with the wife and child of a man he killed out of obligation to the underworld. This eighth film adaptation of a classic play, directed by Tai Kato, crystallizes supreme lyricism into a poignant love story, resulting in a masterpiece.
tmdb:239366: The theatrical film version of the TV anime "Mouretsu Pirates," which aired from January to June 2012, based on Yuichi Sasamoto's popular SF light novel "Mini-Skirt Space Pirates." Marika Kato, a high school girl who is a legitimate space pirate holding a government-issued "privateer's license," leads a busy life juggling her studies, club activities in the space yacht club, a part-time job at a café, and her role as captain of the space pirate ship "Bentenmaru." One day during spring break, just before she is about to advance to her third year, Marika takes on a pirate business job aboard a luxury liner and meets Kanata Mugen, the son of the renowned subspace diver, Dr. Mugen. The opening theme, following the TV series, is "Mouretsu Uchuu Koukyoukyoku Dainanagakushou 'Mugen no Ai'" by Momoiro Clover Z. The director is Tatsuo Sato, known for "Martian Successor Nadesico."
tmdb:24128: A live documentary of the rock band Talking Heads. Capturing their 1983 stage performance at the Pantages Theatre with various camera angles, it conveys the raw energy and excitement directly.
tmdb:24183: Fifteen-year-old Igor works in an auto repair shop, helping his father who trades in illegal foreign workers. One day, a worker named Amidou causes an accident. Fearing the police will discover his illegal labor, Igor's father refuses to take Amidou to the hospital. Amidou dies, entrusting Igor with a message for his wife and children. Igor's father makes him help bury the body and lies to Amidou's wife, Assita...
tmdb:25050: Director Hirokazu Kore-eda of "Nobody Knows" and "Maborosi" quietly captures the scene of a family gathering at their elderly parents' home for the first time in a while, bringing out the joys and sorrows of life in this home drama. One summer day, the second son, Ryota, and the eldest daughter, Chinami, bring their respective families to the home where former doctor Kyohei Yokoyama and his wife Toshiko live alone. The Yokoyama family spends a casual time together, but this day happens to be the anniversary of the death of their eldest son, Junpei, who passed away 15 years ago.
tmdb:25051: Four men and women, all family members of the perpetrators of a murder case committed by a cult three years earlier, meet once a year to pay their respects at the lake where the ashes were scattered. That year, their car goes missing as they try to return from the lake. Stranded, they end up spending the night at a lodge where the cult members once lived, along with a former cult member who also lost his motorcycle. Directed by Hirokazu Kore-eda of "After Life" fame. Starring ARATA, Yusuke Iseya, Susumu Terajima, Tadanobu Asano, and others.
tmdb:25053: Based on a short manga by Yoshiie Gouda, this allegorical work uses the love story of a sentient love doll to lead viewers into philosophical contemplation about the emptiness and life of modern people. With cinematographer Mark Lee Ping-bing and art director Yohei Taneda on board, the fictional setting is brilliantly visualized using analog special effects.
tmdb:2517: Keiko (YOU) and four children, including Akira (Yagira), live in a single apartment room under false pretenses. When Keiko eventually stops coming home, the children are left to fend for themselves, but their financial situation gradually becomes dire. Inspired by a real-life child abandonment case, the film delicately portrays modern social issues such as neglect, young carers, and those who fall through the cracks of the welfare system, earning high international acclaim.
tmdb:25364: Billy Wilder parted ways with his long-time screenwriting partner Charles Brackett and brought in a new writer for this film. Jack, kicked out of a New York newspaper, witnesses a man buried alive in a cave. Desperate to return to a top-tier paper, he manipulates information using the scoop. A journalist who stops at nothing for his own ambition is ultimately judged by public opinion, making for a compelling watch. There is also an anecdote that the studio changed the title from 'Ace in the Hole' to 'The Big Carnival' due to poor public reception.
tmdb:25538: A family drama by Edward Yang, the master of Taiwanese New Cinema known for 'A Brighter Summer Day' and 'The Terrorizers,' which quietly observes the life changes that befall each member of a five-person family living in Taipei. Yang won the Best Director award at the 53rd Cannes Film Festival in 2000 for this film. Elementary school student Yang-yang lives a comfortable life in a luxury apartment with his father NJ, who runs a computer company, his mother Min-min, his high school sister Ting-ting, and his gentle grandmother. They seem like a picture-perfect happy family, but troubles begin after the wedding of the mother's younger brother. The grandmother falls into a coma from a stroke, the father is shaken by a reunion with his first love, and the mother seeks solace in a new religion. To save his company from bankruptcy, the father travels to Japan to secure a contract with a genius game designer named Ota. Meanwhile, the sister starts dating the boyfriend of her neighbor Li-li... Issey Ogata appears as the game designer Ota. As director Yang passed away in 2007, this became his final completed feature film. A 4K restoration was screened as the opening film of the Cannes Classics section at the 78th Cannes Film Festival in 2025.
tmdb:25656: On a break from life, Taeko visits a southern seaside town and stays at a strange inn called Hamada. However, in a small beach town with nothing to see or do, she is pushed around by the overly laid-back residents and, unable to bear it, leaves Hamada—but... From the director Naoko Ogigami and star Satomi Kobayashi of "Kamome Diner," the hit film about slow-living daily life set in a Japanese restaurant in Finland, comes a gentle portrayal of people re-examining their lives, this time set on a southern beach.
tmdb:25657: A drama depicting the peaceful daily lives of three Japanese women set in a small restaurant in Helsinki, the capital of Finland. Based on the novel of the same name by author Yōko Mure, adapted and directed by Naoko Ogigami, who gained attention with her feature directorial debut "Barber Yoshino." Japanese woman Sachie opens a small restaurant called "Kamome Diner" on a street corner in Helsinki, but no customers come. One day, Sachie happens to meet a Japanese tourist named Midori and asks her to help out at the restaurant. Soon, a variety of colorful characters start coming to Sachie's shop one after another... Satomi Kobayashi, Hairi Katagiri, and Masako Motai play the three Japanese women, with Markku Peltola from "The Man Without a Past" co-starring.
tmdb:25746: In the 15th year of the Showa era, as global tensions rise, German literature scholar Shigeru (Mitsugoro Bando) is arrested for advocating against the war. His grieving mother Kayo (Sayuri Yoshinaga) and two daughters (Mirai Shida, Mirai Sato) are supported by his former students, relatives, and neighbors, and strive to live brightly and strongly.
tmdb:26039: A hard-boiled action film directed by British master John Boorman in 1967, early in his career, starring Hollywood legend Lee Marvin ('The Dirty Dozen,' 'The Professionals'). Based on Richard Stark's crime novel 'The Hunter' (featuring the character Parker), it depicts a man's revenge against his betrayers, blending avant-garde New Wave techniques with the psychedelic culture of the American West Coast. Walker, at the request of his friend Reese, robs a criminal organization's deal at the abandoned Alcatraz prison and steals a large sum of money. However, Reese betrays Walker, shooting him and fleeing with his $93,000 share and Walker's wife, Lyn. As his consciousness fades, memories and fantasies swirl through Walker's mind. Surviving, Walker sets out to recover his share and exact revenge, tracking Reese down. Marvin delivers a powerful performance as the ruthless avenger Walker, with Angie Dickinson ('Rio Bravo') and John Vernon ('Dirty Harry') co-starring.
tmdb:261558: After serving two years in the army prison for stealing an officer's wallet, Kitani returns to his unit. Inside the unit, the squad leader and senior soldiers bully the new recruits. In particular, Private First Class Aita, a university graduate, is subjected to daily violence. Kitani, however, refuses to take part in the bullying. Aita grows fond of Kitani and they become close, but he learns that Kitani has been selected for frontline deployment. Both Kitani's imprisonment and his selection for the front lines were the result of factional infighting.
tmdb:26275: A youth comedy set in Shimotsuma City, Ibaraki Prefecture, depicting the friendship between two girls with completely opposite values: a Lolita and a Yankee. Based on the novel of the same name by Novala Takemoto, directed and adapted by Tetsuya Nakashima. In Shimotsuma City, Ibaraki, surrounded by endless rice fields, 17-year-old Momoko is a super laid-back girl who adores Rococo-era France. She dresses in her beloved Lolita fashion and commutes to Daikanyama, where the flagship store of her worshipped brand is located. One day, she starts selling counterfeit famous brands to earn money for clothes, and a girl her age named Ichigo, a member of a local biker gang, appears before her. Ichigo takes a liking to the gutsy Momoko and begins frequently visiting her home. Momoko the Lolita girl is played by Kyoko Fukada, and Ichigo the Yankee girl is played by Anna Tsuchiya. In 2024, marking the 20th anniversary of its release, it was converted to Digital Cinema Package (DCP) and screened in revival.
tmdb:263232: An erotic film directed by Roger Vadim, based on the sensual novel 'Les Liaisons Dangereuses'. Set in 19th-century France, it depicts the affair between a playboy count and a married woman. The bewitching performances of two charismatic actresses are captivating.
tmdb:26347: A feature film by French master Jean-Luc Godard, shot in the war-torn city of Sarajevo as a prayer for world peace. Based on Dante's epic poem 'The Divine Comedy,' it is structured in three parts: 'Hell,' 'Purgatory,' and 'Paradise.' Visiting Sarajevo for a lecture, Godard finds a historical crossroads in the rebuilding city, which is also a history of human conflict and massacre. Using the asymmetry between Israel and Palestine, and Judaism and Islam as examples, Godard discusses the dominant structures of conflict in the world. 'Hell' is composed of montages of war footage; 'Purgatory' depicts the interaction between Godard, invited to Sarajevo for a lecture, and a female student named Olga; and 'Paradise' shows the peaceful world Olga reaches after her death. Godard appears as himself, along with Palestinian poet Mahmoud Darwish and Spanish novelist Juan Goytisolo, who appear under their real names. The 4K restored version will be screened in Japan for the first time as part of the special screening series 'Jean-Luc Godard in the 21st Century: Our Films 2001-2010' (starting June 20, 2026, at Theater Image Forum Shibuya and other locations nationwide).
tmdb:26356: Directed by Pier Paolo Pasolini, the Italian polymath known as a poet, writer, and filmmaker, this film adapts the Greek tragedy 'Medea' starring Maria Callas, the iconic 20th-century soprano. Jason, the orphaned son of the King of Iolcus, demands the return of the throne from his uncle Pelias, who usurped it. Pelias sets the condition that Jason must retrieve the Golden Fleece from the barbaric land of Colchis. On his journey, Jason wins the heart of Medea, the daughter of the King of Colchis, and brings back the fleece. However, the promise of the throne is broken, and Jason flees with Medea to neighboring Corinth. There, favored by the king, Jason abandons Medea and becomes engaged to the king's daughter. Betrayed, Medea vows revenge. In March 2022, the film had a revival screening as part of the special program 'Pasolini Film Speciale 1 & 2' (at Human Trust Cinema Yurakucho, Shinjuku Musashino Hall, and others).
tmdb:26638: The first color film by Italian master Michelangelo Antonioni, this psychological drama won the Golden Lion at the 25th Venice International Film Festival in 1964. In Ravenna, an industrial coastal city lined with sterile factories, Giuliana lives with her husband and son but remains unable to recover from the shock of a car accident years earlier, spending her days in emotional instability. One day, her husband introduces her to his friend Corrado. Giuliana is drawn to Corrado, who carries a loneliness similar to her own, and gradually the two grow closer... Monica Vitti, known as Antonioni's muse, plays Giuliana, with British star Richard Harris as Corrado. A 4K restored version will be released in August 2026 as part of the retrospective program "Michelangelo Antonioni Retrospective: Arid Love, Wandering Souls," featuring five of Antonioni's early works.
tmdb:266598: A puppy named Rock rises up with stray dogs to defeat Killer the tiger, who killed his mother. Drawing on 'Chushingura' and Sazanami Iwaya's children's literature 'Koganemaru,' this film more consciously adopts Disney's style compared to earlier feature-length works. The stateless urban depictions and the action in a snow-covered amusement park, inspired by an idea from Osamu Tezuka, exude a chic and modern sensibility.
tmdb:2671: Reiko Asakawa, a TV station director, is investigating an urban legend when she notices that a man and woman rumored to have been involved with a 'cursed videotape' that kills viewers within a week died at the exact same date and time as her niece, Tomoko Oishi, who had died strangely a few days earlier. As her investigation progresses, Reiko discovers that Tomoko and the other three who died simultaneously were acquaintances, that they had stayed at a rental villa in Izu called 'Izu Pacific Land' a week prior, and that the faces of the four in film photos taken at that time are eerily distorted. Seeking to uncover the mystery of their deaths, Reiko visits the villa in question, watches the suspicious tape that was rented there, and immediately receives an eerie silent phone call. From that point on, Reiko's own photos also begin to show her face distorted, just like the four deceased.
tmdb:26868: A massacre occurs deep in the Tohoku mountains, killing most of a village's residents. A self-defense force special unit member, Misawa, who was training in the mountains, happens upon the scene, kills the perpetrator, and rescues the sole survivor—a village girl named Yoriko. Later, after retiring, Misawa adopts Yoriko and works as an insurance salesperson. One day, he rescues a female journalist named Tomoko from an attacker, but she is being targeted because she tried to expose the corruption of a local businessman, Oba. Meanwhile, Detective Kitano, who suspects Misawa of being the massacre killer, continues to shadow him.
tmdb:26886: Yuji Nimura spends a quiet, monotonous daily life with his coworker Mamoru Arida at the same moist towel factory. Yuji is reckless and struggles to get along with others. Seeing this, Mamoru one day proposes two signals that only the two of them can understand and tries to enforce them. Around that time, Yuji begins to take an interest in the highly venomous 'sea wasp' jellyfish that Mamoru keeps. One day, Mamoru entrusts the jellyfish to Yuji and suddenly disappears. Mamoru is imprisoned as a suspect in the murder of the factory owner and his wife. From then on, Yuji, though bewildered, begins caring for the jellyfish as if possessed by something.
tmdb:26895: "Unforgettable masterpieces" return to the big screen! Since his directorial debut with "Twenty Years' Micro Heat" (1993), Ryosuke Hashiguchi—a "master of few works" eagerly awaited by film fans worldwide—has won the Grand Prix at the 25th Rotterdam International Film Festival for "Like Grains of Sand" (1995), swept various film awards including the Kinema Junpo Best Ten Japanese Films No. 1 for "Three Stories of Love" (2015), and released his latest film "Motherhood" (2024) nine years after "Three Stories of Love." "Hush!" depicts a gay couple and a woman who proposes having a child through sperm donation—"not dating or marriage, but I want a child"—and the "new form of family" the three of them create. "All Around Us" portrays the hope that arises between people over the course of a decade in a married couple's life. Both films are often cited as "all-time best movies" and are known as "unforgettable masterpieces." Now, these two works are getting a revival release in 4K remastered versions! "All Around Us" returns 18 years after its June 2008 release, and "Hush!" returns a full quarter-century after its production in 2001 (released April 2002). "Hush!" was screened at the 2001 Cannes Film Festival Directors' Fortnight.
tmdb:269: Jean-Luc Godard's first feature-length directorial work. Produced with techniques that broke the conventions of theatrical cinema at the time, such as improvisational direction and handheld street shooting, it is a landmark film of the French New Wave that greatly influenced the later film industry. The original idea was by François Truffaut, and Claude Chabrol also participated as a technical advisor. Michel, a car thief who kills a policeman and flees to Paris, enjoys a free relationship with Patricia, an American student selling newspapers. To test Michel's love, Patricia informs the police of his whereabouts and tells Michel what she has done... A digitally remastered version with a new translation by Jiro Terao was released in 2016. In 2022, a 4K restored version created to commemorate the 60th anniversary of its release was shown. In 2026, a 4K restored version will be revived in conjunction with the release of Richard Linklater's film 'Nouvelle Vague,' which depicts the production process of 'Breathless.'
tmdb:270055: From naval academy to the skies of the South Seas, and now having survived to set foot on his homeland's soil, Reikichi's only thought has been his beloved Michiko. Through rumors, he heard she had lost her husband to death and moved to Tokyo. Reikichi moves to Tokyo and stays in the apartment of his younger brother Yo, a book broker, and while working as a ghostwriter of love letters for mistresses through the help of his war comrade Yamaji, he searches for Michiko's whereabouts. The day that compressed five years into an instant finally arrives. Michiko comes to him to request ghostwriting of a love letter, just like any other 'panpan' girl. Reikichi, who had cherished the image of pure Michiko, lashes out with harsh words at the Michiko before him. From then on, Reikichi spends days of drunken agony torn between love and hatred for Michiko. Yo, who vaguely senses his brother's feelings, consults Yamaji and meets Michiko. After her husband's death in the war, unable to stay in her stepmother's home, she worked with the occupation forces in Yokohama, and out of loneliness began living with a kind foreign officer—but she was not living a dissolute life like so-called 'panpan' girls, and had since parted with that officer. Yo and Yamaji arrange for Michiko and Reikichi to meet, but Reikichi refuses. Knowing Reikichi's heart that will not forgive her, Michiko throws herself into oncoming traffic amid tangled headlights. Told by police of her serious injury, Reikichi realizes that regardless of her past mistakes, she is precious to him. In the car racing to the hospital, Reikichi sobs and prays to God for Michiko's life.
tmdb:27102: The fourth film in Éric Rohmer's 'Comedies and Proverbs' series. Louise, an interior designer, lives with her architect boyfriend Rémi in a suburban Paris apartment. The serious Rémi and the free-spirited Louise are constantly bickering. Feeling stifled in her life with Rémi, Louise rents her own room in Paris and starts going out with her married best friend Octave... The film delicately portrays a woman's emotions as she wavers between two men and two homes. Lead actress Pascale Ogier won the Best Actress award at the Venice Film Festival for this role, but tragically died shortly after at the young age of 25. The cast also includes Fabrice Luchini from 'Claire's Knee' and Tchéky Karyo from 'Nikita.'
tmdb:27197: This adaptation of the same-named period novel by Otaguro Mikami was scripted by Daisuke Ito and Teinosuke Kinugasa, with a screenplay by Natsuto Wada, and directed by Kon Ichikawa. Kazuo Hasegawa, who starred in the 1935 version, again plays the dual roles of Yukinojo Nakamura and Yami Taro. The cast also includes Fujiko Yamamoto, Ayako Wakao, Raizo Ichikawa, and Shintaro Katsu, among other luminaries. This film commemorates Hasegawa's 300th appearance. In Edo, Yukinojo Nakamura, a female-role actor of Kamigata kabuki performing in the city, spots Sanzai Tsuchibe and Kaimiya, the men who framed his father on false charges and drove him to suicide. Sanzai's daughter, Namiji, falls in love with Yukinojo, and he uses her to avenge his father. Kawaguchiya, who had been hoarding rice during the Edo famine, is thwarted by Kaimiya—instigated by Yukinojo—and goes bankrupt, after which Kaimiya sets fire to his shop. Enraged, Kaimiya strangles Kawaguchiya but is stabbed by Namiji, whom he had tried to abduct.
tmdb:27337: A refreshing youth drama set in high school, depicting the struggles of a girls' band. Starring Bae Doona of 'Barking Dogs Never Bite' and 'Tube', Aki Maeda of the 'Battle Royale' series, Yuu Kashii of 'Lorelei', and Shiori Sekine, bassist of the rock band Base Ball Bear. Directed by Nobuhiro Yamashita of 'A Gentle Breeze in the Village'. It delicately portrays the subtle emotional shifts and excitement in the hearts of teenage girls. At a local high school, an emergency strikes Kyoko, Megumi, and Nozomi of the same band. They had even prepared an original song for the school festival, but guitarist Moyu injured her finger, and the furious vocalist Rinko quit the band. However, after listening to 'Linda Linda' by The Blue Hearts, which they happen to hear, Kyoko and the others decide to form a cover band of The Blue Hearts. They invite Song, a Korean exchange student, to be the vocalist, and she agrees. The four practice hard toward the final day of the school festival, but...
tmdb:273433: A high school in Hiroshima. In the third-year class taught by Kitagawa, student Michiko Oba collapses with a nosebleed. It is caused by leukemia from the atomic bomb. In this class, a full one-third of the students are hibakusha (atomic bomb survivors). On that day, Yukiko's sister was exposed to the bomb while working on evacuation duties and died in a river. Endo Yukio's father could not save his wife, who was trapped under a building and engulfed in flames. When radish sprouts appeared in Hiroshima, where it was said no grass would grow for 75 years after the bombing, people found hope in those sprouts.
tmdb:27432: The feature debut of Charles Burnett, a filmmaker who quietly revolutionized American cinema by depicting the daily lives and humanity of African Americans, released in 1977. It portrays the everyday existence of African American workers living on the fringes of Los Angeles with a realistic gaze and poetic visual beauty. Set in the Watts district of Los Angeles in the early 1970s, still bearing the scars of the Watts riots. Stan works at a sheep slaughterhouse to support his wife and two children, living an empty daily life. Exhausted physically and mentally by labor and poverty, he withdraws into himself, while his wife grows increasingly lonely. Directed by Burnett as his graduate thesis film while a student at UCLA Film School, it was shot in Watts using a mostly amateur cast of people he knew. Long unreleased due to music copyright issues, it finally had a theatrical release in the US in 2007. The 4K restoration completed in 2025 replaces the music in the final scene with Dinah Washington's "Unforgettable," as Burnett originally intended. It won the FIPRESCI Prize at the Forum section of the 31st Berlin International Film Festival in 1981. In Japan, it will have its first theatrical release in the 4K restored version as part of the special screening series "Charles Burnett: Everyday Blues" (starting February 7, 2026, at Theater Image Forum).
tmdb:275: An unconventional crime suspense film by the Coen Brothers, laced with black humor. In snow-covered Fargo, Minnesota, car salesman Jerry, drowning in debt, plots to have his wife Jean kidnapped to extort a ransom from her wealthy father. But when the two hired kidnappers shoot a police officer and a witness, the case spirals out of control. Winner of multiple film awards, including the Academy Awards for Best Original Screenplay and Best Actress.
tmdb:2767:
A love story from French visionary Leos Carax, following *Boy Meets Girl* and *Bad Blood*, this film serves as the final chapter of his trilogy centered on a young man named Alex. On the Pont-Neuf, the oldest and most beautiful bridge in Paris, a street performer named Alex encounters Michèle, an art student wandering the streets while suffering from the pain of a broken heart and a seemingly incurable eye disease. Before long, the two begin living together on the bridge, deepening their bond amidst their shared loneliness. Michèle struggles with lingering feelings for a cellist named Julien and the fear of losing her sight as an artist, while Alex has lived his life without ever knowing a true connection to others. Gradually, a profound love blossoms between them. However, Michèle eventually learns that her parents are searching for her and that a cure for her eye disease has been found...

Denis Lavant returns to play the protagonist Alex, following his roles in *Boy Meets Girl* and *Bad Blood*, while Juliette Binoche portrays Michèle. Produced in 1991 and released in Japan in 199
tmdb:2786: A masterpiece by Jean-Luc Godard, released in 1965 and revered as a cornerstone of the French New Wave. Ferdinand, called 'Pierrot,' is driven by an urge to escape his boring married life and spends a night with his former lover Marianne, whom he meets by chance. The next morning, finding a dead stranger, the two go on the run, but Marianne eventually tires of Ferdinand and betrays him by colluding with gangsters. A digitally remastered version with a new translation by Jiro Terao was released in 2016. A 2K restored version was released in 2022 and 2026.
tmdb:27958: A crime suspense film directed by William Friedkin, who won an Academy Award for "The French Connection" and had a worldwide hit with "The Exorcist," released in 1980, set against the backdrop of New York City's underground gay culture at the time. A series of murders targeting only gay men occurs in New York at night. Police detective Burns, given a secret mission, goes undercover in S&M clubs frequented by gay men, pretending to be homosexual. Wandering the depths of male sexuality night after night, Burns wears himself down both physically and mentally, finally finding a clue to the killer... Based on actual murders of gay men that occurred between 1973 and 1979, Friedkin wrote the script after experiences including meeting with a suspect who had also appeared in "The Exorcist." Considered the first Hollywood film to openly depict male same-sex S&M sex, it faced protests from the time of its announcement through its release for allegedly promoting homophobia, and was not a commercial success. However, since the 2000s, it has been re-evaluated as a valuable record of gay culture before the global spread of HIV.
tmdb:28276: In a suburban housing complex, several families live side by side like in a row house. The Hayashi family's sons Minoru (Kōji Shidō) and Isamu (Masahiko Shimazu) beg their parents for a television, but their request is denied. The children go on strike, refusing to speak until their demand is met, and eventually, their parents give in and buy one.
tmdb:28436: The directorial debut of Robert Wise, the master behind "West Side Story" and "The Sound of Music," made in 1944. This is a sequel to the cult horror film "Cat People" directed by Jacques Tourneur. A lonely, imaginative girl named Amy finds a beautiful ring in a dilapidated old house in her neighborhood. When she returns home and makes a wish on the ring, a beautiful woman named Irena appears before her. Amy becomes friends with Irena, whom only she can see, but...
tmdb:28580: A serious drama acclaimed worldwide, winning four Academy Awards and the Grand Prix at the Cannes Film Festival. Don, a struggling writer living in New York, drowns his days in alcohol. Desperate for drink money, he steals from his brother and even tries to sell his typewriter. Ray Milland delivers a powerful performance as Don wandering the depths of despair, earning him an Oscar for Best Actor. Director Wilder met his second wife, Audrey Young, during the making of this film.
tmdb:287765: A black man is murdered in an elevator at a luxury hotel in Tokyo, leaving behind the word 'Stoha' and a poetry collection by Saijo Yaso. Fashion designer Kyoko Yasugi and her son appear and disappear along the investigative trail. Detective Muneyori travels to the United States to trace the black man's past. The unexpected relationship between Kyoko and the black man, as well as the connection between the American detective and Detective Muneyori, comes to light.
tmdb:290098: Directed by Park Chan-wook of 'Oldboy' fame, this suspense drama is based on Sarah Waters' novel 'Fingersmith' but transposed to 1930s Japanese-occupied Korea. Sook-hee, a girl raised by a gang of swindlers in a slum, is approached by a con man known as Count Fujiwara with a plan: seduce Lady Hideko, an heiress to a vast fortune, marry her, then commit her to an asylum and steal her wealth. Agreeing to take part, Sook-hee begins working as a maid named Ok-ju at a remote mansion where Hideko lives with her domineering, Japanophile uncle Kouzuki. But as devoted Sook-hee gradually opens Hideko's heart, Sook-hee herself finds herself drawn to the woman she is supposed to betray. Kim Min-hee plays Hideko, while newcomer Kim Tae-ri was cast as Sook-hee through auditions. Ha Jung-woo plays the Count, and Cho Jin-woong plays Uncle Kouzuki.
tmdb:2912: Directed by Claude Chabrol, a leading figure of the French New Wave known for numerous suspense and mystery masterpieces, this crime drama is set in a peaceful rural village. It quietly and sharply delves into the darkness of the human psyche through a series of murders committed by a lonely butcher and the female teacher who is loved by him. Hélène, a primary school teacher in a small village in southwestern France, meets Paul, a war veteran burdened with loneliness, and they gradually grow close. Meanwhile, a series of murders of women shakes the village's calm daily life. One day, during a picnic with her students, Hélène discovers a brutally murdered body; beside it lies a lighter identical to one she had given Paul. Stéphane Audran, who was married to Chabrol at the time, stars as Hélène, the same character name as in 'Les Biches'. Jean Yanne plays the butcher Paul. Although never theatrically released in Japan, the film will have its Japanese theatrical premiere as part of the 'Claude Chabrol Masterpiece Selection' (starting February 13, 2026, at Cinema Rise and Morc Asagaya, among others), featuring three of Chabrol's suspense films from the late 1960s to 1970.
tmdb:292674: This was a highly anticipated comeback film for Yakusho, who had taken a break from acting to prepare for university entrance exams after the massive hit of her starring movie "Sailor Suit and Machine Gun" (1981). The story follows a pampered college girl, played by Yakusho, who is bodyguarded by a private detective played by Matsuda. Director Negishi Kichitaro and the staff devised various strategies to help Yakusho grow as an actress, and she rose to the occasion. It was first released as a double feature with "The Girl Who Leapt Through Time" starring Harada Tomoyo. College student Arai Naomi is set to leave for America, where her father awaits, in one week. Invited by her admired senior Nagai, she heads to a hotel, but a man claiming to be her uncle bursts in and drives Nagai away. The man is a private detective named Tsujiyama Shuichi, hired by her father's former secretary to protect her until her departure. One day, Tsujiyama's ex-wife Sachiko shows up at his apartment, saying she is suspected of stabbing Kazuya, the heir to the Okazaki gang, at a hotel. Naomi suggests to Tsujiyama that they search for the real culprit together.
tmdb:29269: A love story adapted from Haruki Murakami's short story of the same name, directed by Jun Ichikawa of 'Tokiwa: The Manga Apartment' and 'Tsugumi,' starring Issey Ogata and Rie Miyazawa. Tony Takitani, born as the son of a trombonist, loses his mother shortly after birth and grows up carrying loneliness. After working at a design company, he becomes an independent illustrator, falls in love with a woman, and marries her. But their happy days are short-lived; his wife dies in an accident. Feeling his loneliness, he hires a woman who closely resembles his late wife as an assistant and tries to get used to her death by having the assistant wear the vast collection of clothes his shopaholic wife left behind... Issey Ogata plays the protagonist Tony Takitani and his father, Rie Miyazawa plays Tony's wife and the woman who resembles her, with Hidetoshi Nishijima providing narration. The music is composed by Ryuichi Sakamoto. The film won the Special Jury Prize, the FIPRESCI Prize, and the Youth Jury Award at the 57th Locarno International Film Festival in 2004. A 4K remastered version was re-released in 2026.
tmdb:293:
Robert Redford’s third directorial feature is an adaptation of the autobiographical debut novel by former professor Norman Maclean, written at the age of 74 (and nominated for the 1977 Pulitzer Prize). Set amidst the natural splendor of Montana, the film portrays the enduring bonds of family through luminous cinematography (winner of the Best Cinematography Oscar at the 65th Academy Awards), a lyrical score, and a superb ensemble cast.

In the 1910s, in the small town of Missoula, Montana, brothers Norman and Paul are the sons of a Presbyterian minister. Though their personalities are polar opposites—Norman is serious and studious while Paul is free-spirited and reckless—they are united by their shared devotion to fly fishing. After leaving home for university, Norman returns years later as a young man. He finds that Paul has become a newspaper reporter and an even more skilled fisherman, but has also become dangerously entangled in high-stakes poker. Norman watches over his brother with growing concern, but...
tmdb:298467: The pinnacle of Japanese musicals, depicting a salaryman struggling in the battle for foreign tourists in Tokyo just before the Olympics. Throughout the film, talented performers sing and dance, and Frankie's astonishing physical abilities leave you in awe. The grand group dance in 'Man Alone' is especially breathtaking.
tmdb:298621: The second feature film by Guy Gilles, a director re-evaluated since the 2000s as a 'forgotten master of the French New Wave,' depicting a woman living with the memory of her lover who chose death. The present is shown in black-and-white, and fragments of recollection in color, delicately and melancholically portraying the memory of love and the pain of absence. Jeanne lives with the memory of her deceased lover Jean. Jean rejected social order and the bourgeois world, found no place in the Beat generation, and chose death. Unaware of his death, Jeanne feels him always by her side, existing like a ghost. Masha Meril, known for 'A Time for Loving' and 'Belle de Jour,' plays the protagonist Jeanne, and Patrick Jouané, an actor who met Guy Gilles during the filming of 'Le Rempart des Béguines' and became an irreplaceable presence in his life and work, plays the deceased lover Jean. The film was released in Japanese theaters in April 2026.
tmdb:29884: At the Totten Foundation in New York, eight scholars are putting the finishing touches on an encyclopedia, but when grammar professor Potts overhears a slang term, he realizes their work has been isolated from the real world and ventures into the city to investigate. There, he seeks the help of O'Shea, a nightclub singer... Although the film was a hit in the U.S. upon release, it was never imported due to the times. Billy Wilder contributed to the script on the condition that he be allowed to observe Hawks' direction. He made his directorial debut the following year, having used this as preparation.
tmdb:2998: Italian master Michelangelo Antonioni, who won top prizes at all three major film festivals (Berlin, Venice, Cannes) in the 1960s, made this film after moving to America in 1970. Set in Los Angeles and Death Valley, it depicts the psychological landscape of love between a man and a woman. In the late 1960s, amidst the peak of counterculture, with university protests raging and students clashing with armed police, Mark grows tired of futile debates at student gatherings. He grabs a gun and confronts the police officers cracking down on campus, but misses his chance to fire and flees. He then steals a Cessna at an airfield and takes to the sky. Meanwhile, Daria, a secretary at a Los Angeles real estate company, is driving across the vast desert to attend a meeting. The two meet by chance and arrive at Zabriskie Point, overlooking Death Valley... The leads are newcomers Mark Frechette and Daria Halprin, whom Antonioni scouted on the streets. The soundtrack effectively features music by Pink Floyd, Jerry Garcia of the Grateful Dead, Kaleidoscope, John Fahey, The Rolling Stones, and The Youngbloods. Released in Japan in 1970, it also had a late-show release in 1996. A revival release is scheduled for 2026, the first in 30 years.
tmdb:30020: Buddy, a middle-aged man, invites people into his car and makes a strange request: "Tomorrow morning, call out to me lying in a hole. If I answer, help me; if there's no answer, cover me with dirt." Everyone refuses, but the old man he finally picks up begins to tell him about the joy of living...
tmdb:300590: Ginji, driven from his hometown, returns after ten years... This is a representative work marking the starting point of Tai Kato's unique style, with actors wearing no makeup, low-angle cameras, and simultaneous sound recording.
tmdb:303629: The turbulent life of gambler Senkichi, who continues to love one woman. Set in Kyoto at the end of the Edo period, this powerful portrayal of unadorned love between a man and a woman stands as Tai Kato's final, crowning live-action film.
tmdb:303638: This is the graduation work from Kohei Igarashi's master's program at Tokyo University of the Arts. Igarashi, who studied under Nobuhiro Suwa and Kiyoshi Kurosawa, received high international praise for his first feature film, "The Voice of Wind and Rain," made while he was still a student. It is December 30, 2017, about two years before the Tokyo Olympics, and the constitution has been revised and a National Defense Force established. A stray dog wanders into a garbage processing plant. Tani-chan, who works in the office, searches for the dog but can't find it. Ken, who finished his night shift, plays video games with Go, who is off duty that day. Adachi-san refuses to go home, while Yan-san is busy putting up New Year's decorations. The workers at the plant each grapple with similar problems: pregnancy, infidelity, family, and friends who died in the war. Amidst this, Tani-chan, troubled by her affair with Adachi-san, begins to feel that her late father, the former plant manager, might be present in this place.
tmdb:304027: At Madame Lily's brothel, life-or-death gambling takes place amidst decadent plumes of purple smoke. The patrons are intoxicated by the company of young prostitutes and beautiful boys. The brothel's celebrated chanteuse, Viola—also known as "La Paloma" (Ingrid Caven)—appears on stage singing "Shanghai." A male patron gazes intently at her alluring figure. This man, named Isidore (Peter Kern), visits La Paloma's dressing room day after day with a yellow rose, but is fiercely rejected by her, drowned in alcohol.
tmdb:30497: A giant man wearing human skin wanders with a chainsaw in hand... Just how much human blood has soaked into his filthy apron? A horror film inspired by a real-life killer from Wisconsin. In rural Texas, five young people are on a road trip. When they run out of gas and stop at a farmhouse to rest, they are swept into a gruesome “festival.” Facing the masked man “Leatherface” and his sinister family—amidst inescapable despair, a night of terror begins.
tmdb:305588: A cheerful young man moves to Tokyo to help at a relative's milk shop and struggles to outdo his business rivals. A film adaptation of a popular radio drama, this is an early representative work of Frankie Sakai, known as a hidden gem of slapstick comedy.
tmdb:30617: Kamen Rider Decade, aka Kadoya Tsukasa, arrives in a "certain world." In this world, for some reason, the photos Tsukasa takes do not distort the image. Suddenly, a certain Western-style mansion comes to mind. Following faint memories, Tsukasa reaches the mansion, where he meets a girl who calls herself his sister, Kadoya Sayo. Tsukasa becomes convinced this is his own world. However, even in this world, the "collapse of worlds" is progressing. Sayo's servant, Tsukikage Nobuhiko, claims that the cause of the world's collapse lies in the Riders born in each world, and declares that to stop it, they must decide on a single "strongest Rider."
tmdb:3082: A classic comedy masterpiece by Charles Chaplin, who directed, wrote, produced, composed the music for, and starred in it, offering a scathing satire of industrial civilization and capitalist society. Charlie, working in a large factory, goes mad from performing monotonous tasks with the same machine every day and is sent to a hospital. After being discharged, he is mistaken for the leader of a protest march and imprisoned. When proven innocent and freed, he starts working at a shipyard but is quickly fired, leading him to consider ways to return to prison. Eventually, he is arrested for eating without paying and meets a young girl who stole bread in the police van. The heroine is played by Paulette Goddard, Chaplin's partner at the time. This was the first film in which Chaplin spoke on screen and sang his own composition, "Titina." The famous song "Smile" played during the final scene also leaves a lasting impression.
tmdb:30839: The Tadayono High School swim team is on the verge of disbandment, with only one member left: third-year student Suzuki. Suddenly, a young and beautiful female teacher named Sakuma arrives. When the boys learn of this, they rush to join the team, but Sakuma announces they will be doing 'synchronized swimming.' At that, the boys quickly flee. The only ones who can't escape are five misfits, including Suzuki. Reluctantly, they begin practicing synchronized swimming.
tmdb:313297: Long ago in Japan. A boy named Kubo, who lost his left eye, lives with his ailing mother. Playing a magical shamisen inherited from his mother, he earns a living by telling the story of a samurai named Hanzo in the village. On the night of the Bon festival, two 'Sisters of the Dark' who claim to be his mother's sisters appear and attack Kubo, but his mother tells him to gather his father's 'sword, armor, and helmet' and magically sends Kubo far away. Beginning his journey, Kubo makes allies of a female monkey and a male stag beetle while searching for the 'sword, armor, and helmet'.
tmdb:313369: A musical film directed by Damien Chazelle, who gained attention with "Whiplash," starring Ryan Gosling and Emma Stone. It depicts the romance between a struggling actress and a jazz pianist through gorgeous and romantic song and dance reminiscent of classic musical films. Mia, an aspiring actress dejected after failing an audition, has a terrible first encounter with Sebastian, a pianist, at a jazz bar she enters drawn by the sound of piano. Later, Mia reunites with Sebastian at a party, where he's sullenly playing 80s pop by the poolside. Though they clash during their first conversation, they fall in love as they're drawn to each other's talents and dreams. J.K. Simmons, who won the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor for "Whiplash," also appears. Emma Stone won Best Actress at the 73rd Venice International Film Festival, and the film won a record seven awards at the 74th Golden Globe Awards including Best Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy. At the 89th Academy Awards, it received 14 nominations, tying the record for most nominations, with Chazelle becoming the youngest Best Director winner in history, and winning six Oscars total including Best Actress for Emma Stone.
tmdb:314186: During the early days of TV anime, orders were unstable, so to secure steady theatrical commissions, a medium-length film series called "B Works" was planned (conventional feature-length films were called "A Works"). Based on Shotaro Ishinomori's popular sci-fi manga, the film employed TV anime staff such as Keiichiro Kimura, the animation director of "Rainbow Sentai Robin," and utilized TV production efficiency techniques. While there were changes from the original manga, such as turning one of the characters into a child, the battles unfold across land, sea, and air, offering high entertainment value, and the composition shows awareness of widescreen framing.
tmdb:314223: Inspired by Hans Christian Andersen's words, 'My life is a fairy tale,' this musical drama weaves together tales like 'The Red Shoes' and 'Thumbelina' while depicting Andersen's boyhood. The night sky sparkles with colorful stars, and the orchestra's melodies envelop the story. The art by Reiji Koyama and the music by Seiichiro Uno sweetly bring this fairy-tale world to life.
tmdb:31427: An anti-war film adapted from Shōhei Ōoka's novel of the same name, scripted by Kazuo Wada and directed by Kon Ichikawa. Abandoned by both the hospital and his unit, Tamura wanders the island of Leyte on the Philippine front. He reunites with fellow retreating soldiers in front of a hospital, but when the hospital comes under shelling, Tamura flees alone. With no food and having lost his comrades, Tamura survives by eating grass. Eventually he reunites with his former comrades Nagamatsu and Yasuda, who had been separated from him. The two call the soldiers they killed 'monkeys' and have been eating their flesh...
tmdb:314400: A Gothic fantasy film by Italian master Marco Bellocchio, released in 2015 and winner of the FIPRESCI Prize at the 72nd Venice International Film Festival. The story intertwines the 17th century and the modern era, depicted with eerily beautiful imagery. In 17th-century Bobbio, northern Italy, young soldier Federico visits an old monastery to uncover the truth behind the death of his twin brother Fabrizio, a priest. It is said that Fabrizio was seduced by a nun named Benedetta, betrayed his faith, and lost his life. Seeking to restore his brother's honor, Federico tries to make Benedetta confess her guilt, but gradually becomes captivated by her, even as she is accused of witchcraft. The story then shifts to the modern day, centuries later. The former monastery lies in ruins, and a sale to a wealthy Russian is being negotiated. A man appears, but the ruins are haunted by a mysterious old count who only shows himself at night. Benedetta is played by Lidia Lieberman, Federico (living in both past and present) by Pier Giorgio Bellocchio, and the mysterious old count by Roberto Herlitzka. A cover of Metallica's "Nothing Else Matters" is used prominently in the film.
tmdb:31522: This is Jean-Luc Godard's third feature film, following "Breathless," and a romantic comedy created based on the idea of a "musical comedy in which the characters do not sing." Angela, a cabaret dancer, tells her live-in lover Émile that she wants a child right now. Émile cannot hide his bewilderment at her request. Then a young man named Alfred, who has feelings for Angela, appears... Following Godard's previous film "Le Petit Soldat," Anna Karina plays the heroine, with Jean-Paul Belmondo of "Breathless" as Alfred and Jean-Claude Brialy of "Les Cousins" as Émile. The music is by Michel Legrand, the renowned composer of "The Umbrellas of Cherbourg" and other films.
tmdb:315846: A story spanning one year in the lives of three sisters (Ayase, Nagasawa, Kaho) who, after the death of their father who left home 15 years ago and with whom they had lost touch, come to live with their half-sister Suzu (Hirose), who has lost her own family. Based on the best-selling manga by Yoshida Akimi, it carefully depicts the town of Kamakura, where the story is set, and the changing seasons, while bringing to light the love and sorrows of women of different generations.
tmdb:31996: At a department store in the French resort of Riviera, American businessman Michael Brandon (Gary Cooper) insists on buying only the top half of a pair of pajamas. Conveniently appearing to take just the bottoms is Nicole (Claudette Colbert), the daughter of a poor aristocrat. Instantly smitten by her spirited nature, Brandon pursues her relentlessly and secures an engagement. However, on their wedding day, Nicole discovers Brandon has been married seven times and flies into a rage. They manage to marry only on the condition that Brandon pays Nicole a huge alimony if they divorce. Naturally, the relationship fails, and frustrated by his wife's indifference, Brandon resorts to a desperate measure.
tmdb:32568: A social satire comedy that depicts the fate of a scientist obsessed with developing a 'miracle fiber' that never gets dirty, delving into the fundamental contradictions of capitalism. One of the 'Ealing Comedies,' a series of comedy films produced at Ealing Studios in the UK from the late 1930s to the mid-1950s, directed by Alexander Mackendrick, known for 'The Ladykillers.' Sidney, a scientist working in the British textile industry, spends his days experimenting to develop a fiber that never gets dirty and never frays, no matter how much it's washed. He builds strange contraptions in a corner of the factory, remaining expressionless and unfazed by the lack of understanding around him. With the backing of the company president and his daughter Daphne, Sidney finally completes the 'miracle fiber,' but... The lead role of the scientist Sidney is played by the renowned actor Alec Guinness, known for 'Star Wars' and 'The Bridge on the River Kwai.' This film is part of the special screening series 'The Golden Age of British Ealing Comedies' (June 20–July 17, 2026, at Shinjuku K's Cinema).
tmdb:326598: Shizuka Mita is a 20-year-old woman who works hard to become an actress as a trainee at the theater troupe "Sea." Moriguchi, a 26-year-old former troupe member now working at a real estate agency, first notices sincere Shizuka in a park. Shizuka prepares for the lead role audition in the troupe's next production, "The Tragedy of W," but her peer Kaori lands the part, and Shizuka is assigned a minor role with only a single line at the beginning of the story. Downcast after failing the audition, Moriguchi confides in her about his own psychological struggles as an actor. He then proposes marriage on the condition that she never becomes a star, and conversely promises to send a large bouquet to her dressing room as a farewell if she succeeds as an actress.
tmdb:328083: Ogasawara Shibuki meets Daito Shima Ken, who is training in magic, and decides to go on a trip in his car. Shibuki's destination is Osaka, and Ken's is Okinawa. The two don't get along and argue constantly during the trip. In Hamamatsu, Ken's uncle has a magic show, and Shibuki ends up helping out. However, during the show, Ken meets with a jazz singer named Ise Masayo. Seeing Ken so smitten with Masayo, Shibuki feels jealous. The car arrives in Osaka, and the two part ways. But Shibuki can't stop thinking about Ken and sets off for Okinawa, where her sister and brother-in-law live.
tmdb:32924: Ann (Jodie Foster), a contemporary artist in Los Angeles, accidentally witnesses a mafia murder. Her boyfriend Bob (Charlie Sheen) is killed, and Ann goes into hiding. Professional hitman Milo (Dennis Hopper), hired by the mafia, pursues Ann but inexplicably begins to fall in love with her. Milo gives Ann an ultimatum: "Die or become my woman." Forced to comply, Ann gradually finds herself drawn to Milo's pure feelings... <Screening Overview> Period: Friday, July 17 – Thursday, July 23, limited one-week screening. Admission: Flat rate of 1,300 yen (no discounts applicable, no complimentary tickets or T-tickets accepted). *Screening material is DVD.
tmdb:32961: A crime comedy that depicts, with ironic humor, how two men's gold bullion heist plan takes an unexpected turn. One of the 'Ealing Comedies,' a series of comedy films produced at Ealing Studios in the UK from the late 1930s to the mid-1950s, directed by Charles Crichton, who was later nominated for an Academy Award for Best Director for 'A Fish Called Wanda.' Henry, a serious man who has worked as a bank security guard for 20 years, conspires with his friend Pendlebury, a souvenir shop owner, to steal a shipment of gold bullion. After successfully pulling off the heist, they process the gold into miniature Eiffel Towers to smuggle it abroad, but in a lounge at the Eiffel Tower in Paris, they accidentally sell them to a group of schoolchildren on a trip from England... Alec Guinness of 'Star Wars' fame plays Henry, and Stanley Holloway of 'My Fair Lady' plays Pendlebury. A young Audrey Hepburn appears in a single scene. The film won the Academy Award for Best Original Screenplay at the 25th Academy Awards in 1953. This film is part of the special screening series 'The Golden Age of British Ealing Comedies' (June 20–July 17, 2026, at Shinjuku K's Cinema).
tmdb:331322: An entertainment film based on Arima Yorichika's original work "Kisaburo Ichidai," adapted by Kikushima Ryuzo and directed by Masumura Yasuzo. Its success led to a series of nine films. The dynamic duo of the outrageous protagonist played by Katsu Shintaro and the intellectual officer played by Tamura Takahiro are the highlight.
tmdb:33170: Kamijo struggles to scrape together tribute money for the yakuza while harboring ambitions of one day surpassing them. Then, a man named Koya appears—a man who kills yakuza without so much as a flicker of expression. Koya fills a sports bag with knives and goes around stabbing anyone who calls himself a yakuza, one after another.
tmdb:33320: Director Satoshi Kon of 'Perfect Blue' crafts an original feature-length animation depicting an actress who has cherished a man for decades, transcending time and space. Tachibana, the president of a small video production company, visits the secluded estate of Chiyoko Fujiwara, a legendary Showa-era actress who once dominated the silver screen, to produce a documentary about her. Chiyoko, who vanished from cinema thirty years ago and has lived in seclusion, begins to recount her memories upon seeing a single key Tachibana brings. Her narrative soon blurs the lines between reality and film episodes, unfolding into a tumultuous tale. At the 5th Agency for Cultural Affairs Media Arts Festival, it won the Grand Prize in the animation division alongside Hayao Miyazaki's 'Spirited Away.' It also received the Best Asian Film award at the 33rd Sitges Film Festival, earning high acclaim domestically and internationally, and was distributed worldwide by DreamWorks.
tmdb:33333: At an all-boys high school. Kyujo (Ryuhei Matsuda) and his five friends, now third-years in the new term, stand outside the railing on the rooftop, playing the 'Balcony Game'—competing to see who can clap the most times before falling. Kyujo sets a new record in this game, where failure means a straight drop to the schoolyard, and as the winner, gains the right to rule the school. But for him, both the 'game' and 'ruling the school' are meaningless and trivial. As Kyujo and the others drift through their aimless days, lost about where they belong, the reality of choosing their future paths is eventually thrust upon them...
tmdb:33441: Produced during the mid-1980s when original video animation was booming, this omnibus work pushes forward the director's individuality. Katsuhiro Otomo handles the opening and ending, packing the essence of his animation into a short time. The English title logo features a building drawn in meticulous detail so its structure is discernible. The composition of it running as a machine, and the imagery of a toy-box-like, amusement-park-like interior collapsing carefully step by step, truly feels like a microcosm of 'Steamboy'. While other directors develop unique worlds around the theme of 'robots', Otomo creates a short film that is more relaxed and visually driven.
tmdb:338371: Mitsu's birthday. Natsuko buys matching Virgo necklaces and a rose. However, a white handkerchief is hanging in the apartment window. It's the signal that Mitsu's lover, Hideo, is there. Natsuko, who has secretly fallen in love with Mitsu, approaches Hideo in order to have Mitsu all to herself... On a midsummer afternoon, a shocking ending that will shake the world.
tmdb:339: On the planet Earth, in five cities—Los Angeles, New York, Paris, Rome, and Helsinki—five taxi drivers pick up passengers. Five stories unfolding simultaneously on the same night. This film features the strange humor and brilliantly sharp dialogue common to Jarmusch’s work, and the underlying sense of desolate emptiness remains as potent as ever. While his films often polarize audiences due to their unique atmosphere, this entry is relatively accessible and crafted to be enjoyed by a wide range of people. The New York segment and the Paris segment starring Roberto Benigni are particularly recommended.
tmdb:342737: From director Mike Mills, who drew on his own gay father for "Beginners," comes a story now centered on his mother. Set in Santa Barbara in 1979, it depicts a special summer for 15-year-old Jamie, his single mother Dorothea, and the people around them. Dorothea, a single mother struggling with how to raise her adolescent son Jamie, asks her roommate, photographer Abbie, and Jamie's childhood friend Julie, who lives nearby, to help him out. Starring as the mother Dorothea, Annette Bening was nominated for the Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy. Elle Fanning ("Maleficent") plays Julie, and Greta Gerwig ("Frances Ha") plays Abbie.
tmdb:342774: A documentary film adaptation of a 26-year chronicle following one girl's dream from its beginning to the present day, originally produced by TeNY Television Niigata, a local TV station in Niigata Prefecture. The story gained attention when it was featured on Nippon Television network programs such as "Zoom In!! Morning!" and "NNN Documentary."
