In 1987, three calves arrive at a small elementary school in the mountains of Niigata. A third-grade girl at the time dreams of becoming a "cow doctor" through caring for the calves. After parting with the cows she had grown attached to, and with support from her family and those around her, she overcomes difficult hurdles to become a veterinarian for "livestock," not pets. Through her continued dedication to invaluable lives every day—now as a married mother—the film explores the importance of having dreams, as well as themes of family, hometown, work, and the harshness of reality. Yui Yokoyama of AKB48 takes on her first narration role.
tmdb:34375: A film adaptation of Nagano Mamoru's work of the same name, centered on episodes from the original first volume. In the star cluster year 2988, on the planet Adler, the unveiling of a new Fatima created by the renowned scientist Balanche is approaching. Headliners confident in their skills gather from across the star cluster, vying to be chosen as the master of the Fatima made by the master craftsman, when Balanche's friend, Radios Sopp, arrives on Adler.
tmdb:347031: An unconventional survival story in which Daniel Radcliffe, of "Harry Potter" fame, plays a corpse, and Paul Dano, known for "Little Miss Sunshine" and "Love & Mercy," plays a young man who attempts to escape a deserted island using the corpse. After being shipwrecked and washing ashore on a deserted island, Hank, a young man, is about to end his life in despair when he discovers a man's corpse washed up on the shore. Noticing that the corpse is emitting gas and has buoyancy, Hank makes a decision and tries to escape the island by straddling the corpse, but... This is the feature debut of directing duo Daniel Kwan and Daniel Scheinert (known as Daniels), who come from a background in commercial directing. The film garnered attention with awards at the Sundance Film Festival and the Sitges Film Festival. Mary Elizabeth Winstead (from "10 Cloverfield Lane") co-stars.
tmdb:34834: Young Jim, who dreams of foreign lands and sailing, is left to mind the old inn Benbow Tavern in a port town tonight. But a suspicious cat captain shows up and leaves behind a mysterious map. It seems to indicate the location of treasure hidden by the famous pirate Captain Flint. Jim sets out to sea with his best friend, a mouse named Gran, in his homemade barrel ship, the Pioneer. Their destination: the legendary Treasure Island on the map! However, the Pioneer is sunk by a pirate ship, and the two are quickly taken prisoner. The pirate ship is named the Pork Sauté. Its captain, Silver, was once one of Flint's men, and he too has his eye on the treasure of Treasure Island. Jim and Gran escape and land on Pirate Island. But they are caught by Silver's gang, have the map stolen, and are sold off to slave traders. In the stone prison where they are confined, they find a girl named Cathy already there. It turns out Cathy is Captain Flint's granddaughter and is also looking for the map. Jim and Cathy initially clash but eventually open their hearts to each other and decide to cooperate and head for Treasure Island. Now, the curtain rises on a great adventure across the sea!
tmdb:348882: The third part of the Tohoku documentary trilogy co-directed by Ryusuke Hamaguchi ('PASSION') and Ko Sakai ('Home Sweet Home'). Following the first two works that collected dialogues of Great East Japan Earthquake survivors, this documentary records folk tales passed down in the Tohoku region. With folk tale researcher Kazuko Ono as the listener, three storytellers with richly inflected dialects perform their tales. The unique atmosphere that arises between storyteller and listener is brought to the screen through creative camerawork.
tmdb:348885: The second part of the Tohoku documentary trilogy co-directed by Ryusuke Hamaguchi and Ko Sakai, 'Voices from the Waves,' set in Shinchi Town. Following the previous work 'Tales from the Waves,' which captured the 'dialogues' of people affected by the tsunami on March 11, 2011, this film records survivors about a year after the disaster as they talk with family, friends, and colleagues about what happened and how they have been since. While the previous film conducted interviews across a wide area from Iwate to Fukushima Prefectures, this installment focuses specifically on Shinchi Town in Soma District, Fukushima Prefecture, recording dialogues among 10 people in 6 groups.
tmdb:348886: The second part of the Tohoku documentary trilogy co-directed by Ryusuke Hamaguchi and Ko Sakai, 'Voices from the Waves,' set in Kesennuma. Continuing to film for over a year after completing the previous work 'Tales from the Waves,' which gathered 'dialogues' of people living along the Sanriku coast affected by the tsunami on March 11, 2011, this film records dialogues among 11 people in 7 groups living in Kesennuma City, Miyagi Prefecture. About a year after the disaster, it depicts survivors recalling their memories of the earthquake through conversations with family, friends, and colleagues, and renewing their feelings.
tmdb:35172: The Dardenne brothers, directors of 'Rosetta' and 'The Promise,' sincerely and ambitiously tackle a profound motif that could be called humanity's eternal challenge in civilized society. They depict the extreme inner turmoil of a protagonist burdened with complex emotions in a stripped-down, understated style. Olivier Gourmet won the Best Actor award at the 2003 Cannes Film Festival. One day, a boy named Francis enters a vocational training center. He wants to join the woodworking class, but the instructor, Olivier, turns him away, saying he's too busy. Yet, Olivier finds himself strangely preoccupied with Francis. Eventually, Olivier accepts Francis into his class...
tmdb:354433: It's Laura's birthday. Hamtaro has prepared a present, but Laura ignores him, and in frustration he runs away from home. Seeing this, the Ham-Hams are about to help Hamtaro run away when a mysterious fairy hamster appears and takes everyone to Ham-Ham Land, a dream world where only hamsters live. But Hamtaro can't stop thinking about Laura. Hearing from the fairy hamster about 'magic sunflower seeds' that allow hamsters to talk to humans, Hamtaro sets out on an adventure to find them. But what awaits?
tmdb:354570: A small-town barber who has returned from the war unexpectedly finds himself put on trial as a war criminal. This film version, directed by screenwriter Hashimoto himself, is based on a television drama that won an Art Festival Award. A legendary work that portrays the absurdity and cruelty of war, with Frankie's heartfelt performance that shakes the soul.
tmdb:354759: Starring four women with no acting experience, this film portrays the anxieties and worries of ordinary women in their late 30s through a tense 317-minute drama. Directed by Ryusuke Hamaguchi, known for challenging works like the 4-hour-plus epic "Intimacies" (using film school students) and the Tohoku documentary trilogy ("The Sound of the Waves," "Voices from the Waves," "Singing in the Dark"), the film won the Best Actress award for its four leads at the 68th Locarno International Film Festival in Switzerland. Akari, Sakurako, Fumi, and Jun, all in their late 30s, thought they were best friends who could tell each other anything. However, it is revealed that Jun had been hiding her year-long divorce negotiations. Shaken by this, the four women take a trip to Arima Onsen for a brief escape and enjoy a fun time together, but...
tmdb:3549:
Academy Award nominee for Best Foreign Language Film. An emotional human drama that inspired a Hollywood remake.

Jacob, a Danish man dedicated to helping orphans in India, receives an offer for a massive donation from Jørgen, a businessman back in his home country. Returning home, Jacob finalizes the deal with Jørgen, only to be invited to his daughter's wedding. There, an unexpected reunion leads him to a shocking discovery...

Mads plays this role:
Jacob, a naive idealist with a secret who runs an orphanage in India. Beloved by the children, he is a gentle soul who evokes a sense of tenderness, yet he harbors a hidden past...
tmdb:355135: Hamtaro had a dream. It was a dream of a beautiful hamster princess... 'Help me... Please... Come here quickly...' The princess was trapped inside a soap bubble, tears in her eyes. Even after waking up, Hamtaro can't stop worrying about the princess from his dream. So, he and the Ham-Hams decide to go rescue her. They arrive at the 'Hamja Kingdom,' the homeland of hamsters with a history of 8686 in the Ham Calendar, surrounded by desert. The sky is dark, and the hamsters living there seem downcast. No wonder—Princess Shera of the Hamja Kingdom, who was engaged to Prince Hamuha of the neighboring country, has been kidnapped by a mysterious cat that suddenly appeared and trapped her just like in Hamtaro's dream. That cat wants to marry Princess Shera and take over the kingdom! At this rate, the princess and the kingdom are in danger! Can Hamtaro and the Ham-Hams save the princess and protect the hamsters' homeland? An adventure of love and courage begins now.
tmdb:355345: Based on 'Nobody's Boy.' Even after being sold by his stepfather to traveling performers, young Remi never loses heart. The background art incorporates elements from diverse European masterpieces by Millet and Monet, while Yugo Serikawa's masterful use of dramatic pauses heightens the arduous journey. Frankie Sakai's voice performance as Remi's sidekick Capi, with his playful demeanor, offers a refreshing respite amid the relentless tragedy.
tmdb:35648: In the near future, to cope with an aging society, the Ministry of Health and Welfare develops a sixth-generation computer with self-replicating functions, the elderly care machine 'Unit Z001.' However, this computer absorbs the elderly selected as samples and goes on a rampage, causing a huge uproar involving volunteer female college students and the media.
tmdb:35717: The fourth feature film by French wunderkind Leos Carax, released eight years after 'The Lovers on the Bridge.' An adaptation of the novel 'Pierre' by 19th-century American author Herman Melville, written the year after his masterpiece 'Moby-Dick.' Shifting the setting to modern-day Paris, it uses emotional imagery and sound to depict the intense, racing love of a man and woman swept up by fate and drawn into despair. Pierre, a young novelist living in a Norman castle, enjoys a wealthy, contented rural life with his mother Marie and fiancée Lucie. One day, Isabelle, a Bosnian refugee claiming to be Pierre's half-sister, appears. Drawn to Isabelle's charm, Pierre abandons everything and heads to Paris with her. Guillaume Depardieu, son of Gérard Depardieu, passionately plays Pierre, and Katerina Golubeva, known for 'Paris at Night,' plays Isabelle. Catherine Deneuve co-stars as Pierre's mother Marie. Cinematography is by Éric Gautier, known for 'My King,' and music is by singer-songwriter Scott Walker. A 4K restored version will be re-released in February 2026.
tmdb:35861: A commentary: Osan, the young wife of a Kyoto paper merchant, is suspected of adultery with the clerk Mohei due to a chance incident... Based on a Chikamatsu puppet play, this celebrated film depicts a man and woman who awaken to true love through a life-or-death escape, rendered with rigorous yet flowing brushstrokes. The dignified beauty of Kagawa as Osan is not to be missed.
tmdb:360179: A socially conscious drama centered on a wealthy banking family, depicting human ambition, love, and hatred over wealth and power spanning political and financial circles. Director Yamamoto Satsuo's epic adaptation of Yamasaki Toyoko's novel of the same name. Daisuke Manpai, president of Hanshin Bank. The Manpai family, renowned in Kansai financial circles, expands its influence by marrying off its children one after another to major figures in politics and finance, solidifying its power. These maneuvers are orchestrated not by Daisuke's naive aristocratic wife, Neiko, but by Aiko Takasu, who has long served as both a tutor and housekeeper. However, the family's gears gradually begin to grind out of sync...
tmdb:36095: A masterpiece of psychological suspense in Japanese film history, directed by the brilliant Kiyoshi Kurosawa and starring Kōji Yakusho. A series of bizarre murders occur one after another. While the perpetrators of each case have no connection, the victims all have an X-shaped cut from their neck to their chest, all the assailants are arrested near the crime scene immediately after the incident, and none of the killers had a clear intent to murder just before the act. Detective Takabe, whose wife suffers from a mental illness, is assigned to the investigation but struggles to find a common thread among the perpetrators. Around the same time, a murder with the same modus operandi occurs on a beach near Tokyo, and a young man named Mamiya, who has no memory of being near the scene, is taken into custody. Takabe discovers that Mamiya is a former medical student and realizes he has been using hypnosis to trigger the series of events, but...
tmdb:361743: The sequel to the worldwide hit "Top Gun" (1986) that shot Tom Cruise to stardom. Maverick, a legendary pilot, returns to TOPGUN, the U.S. Navy's elite pilot training school, as an instructor. He, who knows the harshness and beauty of the sky better than anyone, teaches the difficulty of protecting and the harshness of fighting, but the trainees are confused and resistant to his unconventional methods. Among them is Rooster, the son of Goose, Maverick's wingman who died during a training flight with him. Rooster resents Maverick and confronts him... Cruise reprises his role as Maverick, with Miles Teller ("Whiplash") and Jennifer Connelly ("A Beautiful Mind") co-starring, and Val Kilmer, who played Maverick's rival Iceman in the previous film, also returns. Directed by Joseph Kosinski ("Oblivion"), with a script by Christopher McQuarrie, known for directing the "Mission: Impossible" series and writing "The Usual Suspects." It was a worldwide blockbuster, grossing over $700 million in North America and over 13.5 billion yen in Japan. Nominated for six Academy Awards at the 95th ceremony including Best Picture, winning Best Sound.
tmdb:366331:
<Director’s Statement>

I felt a desire to record this event. I am a historian and a sociologist. I believed that what I must do now is to document this and preserve it for future generations.

I had never made a film before. I had never even been interested in filmmaking. However, gathering fragments of historical records and weaving them into a single world is exactly what I have done in my previous writings. Whether the medium I handled was text or video was of no consequence in this instance.

It goes without saying that this is not a work I created alone. The people who filmed on-site at the time and those who sat for interviews all cooperated without compensation.

Above all, the protagonists of this film are every single person who appears in it. they are diverse in gender, generation, social status, nationality, origin, and ideology. I found the sight of such varied people gathering in a single place to be both a rare occurrence and something profoundly powerful and beautiful.

Such miraculous moments rarely visit a nation or a society. As a historian, I know this to be true. What I have done—what I set out to do—is simply to record such a moment, and nothing more.

I believe this is a film that can be interpreted in many ways. After viewing it, I hope you will share your honest thoughts with the person sitting next to you. It is the audience, and society as a collective, that gives meaning to a film. From that dialogue, I believe something new will be born, both for you and for society.
tmdb:367196: In 1984, Hong Kong before the handover to China. In the suburban new town of Sha Tin, the first youth baseball team in Hong Kong, the 'Sha Yan' team, is formed. In Hong Kong, where baseball is not a major sport, a group of underachieving boys with no baseball experience begin practicing with balls made of rolled-up newspapers, but in their first game, they suffer a crushing defeat against a Taiwanese elementary school team. Nevertheless, guided by their strict yet caring principal Law (played by Liu Kai-chi), the team members gradually grow, centered on the childhood friends—the introverted Lung (played by Lam Yiu-sing) and the impulsive but loyal Wai (played by Tony Wu). The final showdown against their arch-rivals, the Japan Buffaloes, becomes a stage for them to re-examine their 'past' and 'future'—a youth drama based on a true story, set in early 1980s Hong Kong, leaving a quiet resonance that is not reduced to the outcome of the sport.
tmdb:36832: A science fiction film set in a near-future New York ten years after a social-democratic liberation revolution. Now hailed as a classic of feminist cinema, the film uses a documentary-style approach to depict women uniting across lines of gender, race, and class to confront the oppression that persists even in the post-revolutionary era.
tmdb:36895: A small village in the mountains of southern Nara Prefecture. Fifteen years have passed since plans to build a railway through this village were proposed, but Kozo Tamura, who was involved in the tunnel construction, loses all motivation upon learning the project has been cancelled. Then one day, Kozo disappears. His remaining family, bewildered, each make their own choices.
tmdb:369086: A war drama depicting the tragedy of the 'Himeyuri Student Corps,' mobilized as nursing staff during the Battle of Okinawa at the end of the Pacific War. Director Toshio Masuda brings together Nikkatsu's golden couple Sayuri Yoshinaga and Mitsuo Hamada to adapt Keiichiro Ishino's novel of the same name. In 1943, in Okinawa, still untouched by the shadow of war, Yonamine Kazuko, a student at the Okinawa Normal School for Girls, enjoys a sports day with her classmates and meets Nishizato Junichiro, a student from the men's normal school. By 1944, the war situation worsens. As Okinawa itself is about to become a battlefield, Kazuko and Junichiro, now engaged in building fortifications, begin to develop feelings for each other. Soon, Saipan falls. Kazuko's mother Hatsu, an elementary school teacher, boards a transport ship to accompany the schoolchildren who have been ordered to evacuate to the mainland, but the ship is sunk and she never returns. In October, the air raids finally begin. A state of total emergency is declared across the island. Female students are sent to the Haebaru Army Hospital as temporary nurses, while male students join the army as part of the Blood and Iron Student Corps.
tmdb:369557: A semi-autobiographical work by director John Carney of "Begin Again" and "Once," this youth drama depicts the love and friendship of a boy who forms a band to impress a girl he likes, set to 1980s British sounds. In 1985 Dublin, Ireland, struggling through a severe recession, 14-year-old Conor is forced to transfer to a rough public school after his father loses his job. At home, his parents constantly fight, pushing the family to the brink of collapse. Conor's only solace in his miserable days is watching music videos from neighboring London on TV with his music-obsessed older brother. One day, captivated by the mature charm of a girl named Raphina he sees on the street, Conor invites her to appear in a music video for his band. Hurriedly forming a band, Conor begins intense training to create a video that will amaze the London music scene...
tmdb:37165: A comedy-drama depicting a man whose entire life is broadcast live on a reality TV show. Truman, a man born and raised on the isolated island town of Seahaven, works at an insurance company and lives a peaceful daily life with his dependable wife Meryl. However, there is a shocking fact that only he doesn't know. In reality, since his birth, every moment of Truman's life has been broadcast live 24 hours a day on the TV show 'The Truman Show.' The town he lives in is a massive set, and all the residents, including his wife and best friend, are actors. Beginning to feel that something is off about the world he lives in, he frantically tries to uncover the truth... Jim Carrey plays the protagonist Truman, and Ed Harris plays the show's producer. The film won Best Actor and Best Supporting Actor at the 56th Golden Globe Awards. Directed by Peter Weir ('Witness'), with a screenplay by Andrew Niccol ('Gattaca').
tmdb:37169: Dr. Josef Heiter, a German who was once a renowned surgeon for separating conjoined twins, harbors a secret desire to do the opposite of his previous operations: to connect a human's mouth to another's anus and create a "Human Centipede." One day, two American women traveling, Lindsay and Jenny, get a flat tire while driving and seek help at Dr. Heiter's house. To fulfill his desire, Heiter welcomes the unsuspecting pair warmly and begins work on creating a human centipede, adding Katsuro, a Japanese man he had already captured, to the mix.
tmdb:372058: Director Makoto Shinkai, known for delicately portraying the nuances of male-female emotions against beautiful landscapes in works like "The Place Promised in Our Early Days" and "5 Centimeters Per Second," delivers his first original feature in three years since "The Garden of Words." Character design by Masayoshi Tanaka of "Anohana: The Flower We Saw That Day" fame, animation direction by Masashi Ando, known for his work on Studio Ghibli films like "Princess Mononoke" and "Spirited Away," and music including the theme song by popular rock band RADWIMPS. The film remained in the top 10 of domestic box office rankings for 29 consecutive weeks, achieving historic blockbuster success with over 25 billion yen in revenue. It won the Award for Best Screenplay at the 40th Japan Academy Prize, a first for an animated work. One month before a comet approaches for the first time in 1000 years, Mitsuha Miyamizu, a high school girl living in a mountainous rural town, dreams she is a male high school student in Tokyo. Mitsuha, who feels cramped by her small town and longs for the city, enjoys city life in her dream. Meanwhile, Taki Tachibana, a male high school student in Tokyo, dreams he is a high school girl in a mountain town he's never visited. As the body-swapping phenomenon continues and they become aware of each other, Taki and Mitsuha eventually discover an unexpected truth. Voice cast includes Ryunosuke Kamiki as Taki and Mone Kamishiraishi as Mitsuha, with Masami Nagasawa and Etsuko Ichihara among others.
tmdb:374671: Director Hirokazu Kore-eda of "Our Little Sister" and "Like Father, Like Son" teams up with Atsushi Abe for the third time, following "Still Walking" and "I Wish," in this human drama centered on a man who can't grow up and his aging mother, portraying a family living a present different from the future they once dreamed of. Ryota is a middle-aged man who won a literary prize 15 years ago but hasn't been successful since, still chasing his dream of becoming a writer. He currently works at a detective agency to make ends meet, but makes excuses to himself and others that it's "research for his novel." Still hung up on his ex-wife, Kyoko, he is shocked to discover she has a new boyfriend while "staking out" her apartment. One day, Ryota, Kyoko, and their 11-year-old son Shingo gather at the apartment of his mother, Toshiko, who lives alone in a housing complex. Stranded by a typhoon, they end up spending the night together. Kirin Kiki delivers a wonderful performance as the protagonist's mother, with a stellar supporting cast including Yoko Maki, Satomi Kobayashi, and Lily Franky.
tmdb:37726: Tsukiko Izumisawa, a girl suffering from memory loss and insomnia due to an accident three years ago, attends a psychiatric clinic. Her doctor, Hosono, probes her memories through hypnotherapy and hears the name "Tomie." However, Tsukiko cannot recall who that name belongs to. Then, strange and terrifying events suddenly begin occurring in Tsukiko's life. One day, a detective from the Metropolitan Police visits Hosono. He is investigating a woman named Tomie Kawakami.
tmdb:37959: High school senior Sugihara has South Korean nationality, but usually doesn't think about it. He starts dating a girl named Sakurai and thinks he must confess his nationality to her someday, when a tragedy befalls a close friend of the same nationality. Based on the Naoki Prize-winning novel "GO" by Kinichi Kaneshiro. Directed by Isao Yukisada, who won the International Critics' Award at the previous year's Busan Film Festival for "Himawari." Screenplay by Kankuro Kudo of the TV series "Ikebukuro West Gate Park." Co-starring popular young actors including Yosuke Kubozuka from that show and Ko Shibasaki from "Battle Royale."
tmdb:38010: Directed by Yoshihiro Nakamura, who helmed the film adaptation of Kotaro Isaka's "A Duck and a Coin Locker," this film adapts another of Isaka's short stories of the same name. It's an ensemble drama depicting how a song that received almost no attention upon its release transcends time to save the world from extinction. In the 1970s, the ahead-of-its-time punk band "Gekirin" disbanded, leaving behind the song "FISH STORY," which was not understood by the world. Years later, in the 1980s, a timid college student who happens upon the record takes desperate action to save a woman attacked by thugs. Further in time, in the 2000s, a ferry cook aspiring to be a hero saves a high school student caught up in a sea-jacking during a school trip. And in 2012, as humanity faces extinction from a comet collision, a record shop owner also holds "FISH STORY" in his hands. Ito Atsushi and Kora Kengo play the members of the band "Gekirin," Hamada Gaku plays the timid college student, Tabe Mikako plays the high school student caught in the sea-jacking, Moriyama Mirai plays the cook, and Omori Nao plays the record shop owner. The screenplay is by Tamio Hayashi, who later worked with Nakamura on "Golden Slumber." Music production was handled by Kazuyoshi Saito. In 2026, 17 years after its 2009 release, it will be digitally re-released.
tmdb:38013: 'Conceal nothing, create no taboos, and share everything as much as possible.' That is the rule of the Kyobashi family, decided by Eriko as a reaction against her mother Satoko, who never did anything motherly—Eriko is determined to maintain a smiling, happy household. But contrary to Eriko's wishes, each family member harbors secrets. Her husband Takashi shuttles between two lovers, Asako and Mina; her daughter Mana refuses to go to school; and her son Ko, a shut-in with an interest in architecture, unknowingly hires Mina—his father's lover—as his tutor. One day, Eriko throws a joint birthday party for Satoko and Mina. However, thanks to a drunken Mina, the family's secrets are exposed one after another, and the home Eriko built crumbles. Yet on her own birthday, a birthday call from Satoko dissolves her resentment, and Eriko is able to be reborn, warmly welcoming her family home with gifts in hand.
tmdb:380341: On August 9, 1948, at a midwife's home in Nagasaki, Nobuko is visited by her son Koji, who she had lost three years earlier in the atomic bombing. Stunned by the impossibility, she watches as her already-dead son begins to appear frequently. Koji, who had been aiming to become a doctor, had a fiancée named Machiko with whom he had promised a future.
tmdb:38047: Directed by Kiyoshi Aoyama of 'Helpless,' this human drama depicts the journey of recovery for people traumatized by a bus-jacking incident. It won the FIPRESCI Prize and the Ecumenical Jury Prize at the 53rd Cannes International Film Festival in 2000. A bus-jacking occurs in a regional city in Kyushu, and many passengers are killed. The only survivors are the driver, Sawai, and two siblings: junior high school student Naoki and elementary school student Kozue. All three are deeply scarred. Two years later, Sawai, who had disappeared leaving his family behind, returns to town. Around the same time, a series of murders occur in the area, and suspicion falls on Sawai. Learning that the siblings are living alone, Sawai visits their home and begins living with them. Joined by the siblings' cousin, Akihiko, the four set out on a journey in a bus driven by Sawai... Kōji Yakusho plays Sawai, while real-life siblings Shō Miyazaki and Aoi Miyazaki play Naoki and Kozue. Following director Kiyoshi Aoyama's death in March 2022, a digital master complete version was released in theaters that May as a memorial screening.
tmdb:381902: Five hundred years after the violent Son Goku was imprisoned under Five Elements Mountain, he is freed from his seal by the monk Sanzo, who is heading to India, and joins the journey as Sanzo's bodyguard. Along the way, the group gains new companions, but they are confronted by the demoness Hakukotsu-fujin, who seeks to kill Sanzo in order to maintain her own eternal beauty. Using various schemes, Hakukotsu-fujin finally captures Sanzo.
tmdb:381920: A medium-length drama shot by director Hamaguchi Ryusuke, who continues to attract attention with works like 'THE DEPTH' and 'Intimacy,' as a prequel to his planned feature film 'FLOODS.' Chihiro, a boy who has lost his father, comes to live with his half-brother Togo and Togo's lover Misato. Togo and Misato warmly welcome Chihiro, but plagued by loneliness, Chihiro throws himself into dance practice with his same-age friend Naoya. Around them, unsettling events begin to occur... The cast includes talented actors such as Shota Sometani from 'Himizu,' Kiyohiko Shibukawa from 'The Wandering Beast,' and Hotsushi Ishida from 'Canary.'
tmdb:382170: Nanami Minagawa, a temporary teacher in Tokyo, meets Tetsuya on social media and marries him. She hires Amaru, a jack-of-all-trades, to provide stand-in guests for the wedding ceremony. However, Tetsuya's affair soon comes to light. Then Nanami is accused by her mother-in-law of having an affair herself and is forced to leave the house. Amaru introduces Nanami to jobs as a stand-in wedding guest and as a live-in maid with a monthly salary of 1 million yen. There she meets her fellow maid, the unconventional and free-spirited Mashiro Satonaka.
tmdb:38368: A fantasy drama by Thai director Apichatpong Weerasethakul, internationally acclaimed for "Tropical Malady," which brought Thailand its first Palme d'Or at the Cannes Film Festival. Boonmee, who is nearing the end of his life in the mountains of Thailand, invites his wife's younger sister Jen to his farm. There, the ghost of Boonmee's wife, who passed away nineteen years earlier, appears, and his missing son also shows up in a transformed state. Eventually, Boonmee ventures with them into the deep forest.
tmdb:384024: The debut feature film by Lizzie Borden (b. 1958) examines a New York feminist collective. After being screened only a few times following its production, the film remained shelved for nearly 40 years due to the dissatisfaction of its cast members. Permission was finally granted in 2016, leading to a 4K restoration by Anthology Film Archives in 2022. Utilizing a documentary style, the film explores the dynamics of female collectivity that would later be further developed in *Born in Flames* (1983) and *Working Girls* (1986).
tmdb:38804: A musical film sprinkled with comedic elements, including a parody of trademarked dogs and Freudian psychoanalysis of a dog. An American phonograph salesman arrives in Vienna. His rare phonograph is mistaken for a bomb, and he falls in love at first sight with an aristocrat's daughter, dragging his pet dog into a series of mishaps. Bing Crosby's expansive singing voice is a delight to hear. However, this became Billy Wilder's only musical film, as he later said he lacked the talent to make musicals.
tmdb:39107: At Enma's palace, where he usually manages heaven and hell, a young psychedelic demon forgets to replace the tank of the spirit laundering device that purifies souls bound for hell. Evil energy leaks from the now-full tank, and using the psychedelic demon's body as a medium, it transforms into the monster Janemba. At the same time, Enma's palace is sealed off by a barrier, throwing the order of the afterlife and the living world into chaos. In the living world, villains previously defeated, such as Frieza, are revived, causing great turmoil. Son Gohan, Son Goten, and Trunks fight back, but they are at a loss for a fundamental solution. Around the same time, during the finals of the Other World Tournament being held again as a rematch of the previous one, a mysterious crystal suddenly appears. Sensing something wrong in the Enma realm, Goku and Pikkon head to Enma's location and attempt to destroy the barrier, but fail. Enma tells them that the one who created the barrier is Janemba, who is above, and with Janemba himself calling him out, Goku takes on the fight. Janemba looks foolish at first glance, but he freely manipulates magical, bizarre techniques and is skilled at reading his opponent's movements, so Goku struggles somewhat. Finally, Goku transforms into Super Saiyan 3 for the second time since his battle with Majin Buu and lands a full-force blow on Janemba. However, Janemba, who seemed to have been killed, instantly regenerates his body and, now in a more combat-oriented form, attacks Goku. Janemba's power is too much even for Goku's Super Saiyan 3, and Goku finds himself in dire straits. Just then, Vegeta, who has regained his original body due to the disturbance in the afterlife's order, rushes to Goku's aid. Vegeta fights bravely on his own, but he cannot match Janemba, and after being shown the clear difference in power, he realizes that even in death, he still falls short of Goku, and is disheartened. Then, Goku proposes the fusion technique as a last resort. To restore the order of the afterlife and the living world, Goku and Vegeta attempt to fuse in the face of the powerful enemy Janemba.
tmdb:391327: Goro and Sachino first met on the Third Keihin Expressway. Sachino, thrown out of a white Mustang, was rescued by Goro, who was riding a motorcycle. The two begin living together. Meanwhile, the middle-aged man who was driving the Mustang is also leading a strange cohabitation. Sachino starts working at a snack bar called Queen Elizabeth. Goro gets into a fight and quits his part-time job. When Goro leaves home, Sachino decides to meet the middle-aged man.
tmdb:393091: Kyoko, a nun at St. Saffron Church on Mount Rokko, plays hymns on the organ. Haruhiko Tenryu, the second-generation head of the Tenryu-gumi yakuza clan, is deeply in love with Kyoko because of her refined beauty, and has even forced his underlings to be baptized as Christians. Also harboring feelings for Kyoko is Detective Jindai, whose family runs a Tendai sect temple, presenting another formidable obstacle. However, Kyoko herself secretly harbors feelings for Eiji, whom she met fatefully one stormy day. As the feelings of those around her intertwine, Kyoko's destiny begins to move in an unexpected direction.
tmdb:396535: A Korean survival panic action film depicting the terror and chaos caused by the sudden outbreak of a mysterious virus spreading aboard a high-speed train connecting Seoul and Busan. Seok-woo, a fund manager working in Seoul, is separated from his wife and lives with his young daughter Su-an. Su-an insists on going alone to meet her mother in Busan for her birthday, and Seok-woo reluctantly agrees to escort her. They board the KTX high-speed train from Seoul to Busan, but just before departure, a suspicious commotion occurs near Seoul Station. A woman infected with the mysterious virus also boards KTX train 101, the same train as the father and daughter. Alongside the protagonist Seok-woo and his daughter, various passengers—a pregnant woman and her husband, high school baseball players, and a selfish middle-aged businessman—face a life-or-death struggle for survival in a state of extremity where being caught by the infected means certain death, and their individual human dramas unfold. This is the first live-action feature film by Yeon Sang-ho, a rising director who has garnered attention in the Korean animation scene, and the story preceding this film is revealed in the animated feature 'Seoul Station'.
tmdb:39871: Billy Wilder's second directorial work, which was never theatrically released in Japan. This was his highly anticipated first Hollywood film, successfully casting the era's star Ginger Rogers. To save money on train fare to Iowa, Susan disguises herself as a 12-year-old girl. A faint affection begins to blossom between her and Colonel Philip, who happens to be on the same train... Although the film touches on the theme of attraction to a minor, it was produced 12 years before the publication of the bestselling novel "Lolita."
tmdb:39951: Toei Animation's first sci-fi feature. It is also the first feature-length film solely directed by Kuroda Yoshiro, whose highly designed compositions and musical style highlight the allegorical world. Ambitious meta-cinematic structures are employed, marking a breakthrough for a new generation at Toei Animation. The princess's secret revealed at the end carries a critique of civilization, an idea proposed by then-animator Hayao Miyazaki.
tmdb:400033:
"I want to film a documentary on Ryuichi Sakamoto for a French television program." In 1983, director Elizabeth Lennard visited Sakamoto in Berlin—where he was attending a David Sylvian recording session—to make this proposal. In May 1984, just as Sakamoto began work on his fourth solo album, *Ongaku Zukan*, filming took place in Tokyo over a brief span of only one week. The five-member French crew, led by Lennard, captured a vivid record of Japan, the city of Tokyo, and the musician Ryuichi Sakamoto.

Following its 1985 completion and French TV broadcast, the film screened at international festivals in Rotterdam, Locarno, and São Paulo. In Japan, it premiered at the inaugural Tokyo International Film Festival on June 9th of that year. While the subsequent VHS and DVD releases were long out of print and difficult to obtain, the original 16mm film was recently discovered in a warehouse and has been digitally restored.

Within its 60-minute runtime, the film captures a 30-something Sakamoto in the studio and in interviews, discussing his upbringing, values, musical philosophy, and culture. It also features footage from Nagisa Oshima’s *Merry Christmas, Mr. Lawrence* (1983), YMO’s "scatter" concerts, and music videos, while projecting the vibrant energy of 1980s Tokyo—from the Shibuya Scramble to Shinjuku Alta—onto the screen. This legendary documentary, an immersion into the "Sounds of Tokyo" as seen through Sakamoto’s eyes and portrait, finally makes its theatrical debut after nearly 40 years.
tmdb:400579: Marlo, a mother of three including a newborn, is given a night nanny by her brother. Initially hesitant, she soon bonds deeply with Tully, a nanny who is thoughtful, surprising, and at times challenging.
tmdb:404:
73-year-old Alvin Straight (Richard Farnsworth) lives with his daughter Rose (Sissy Spacek) in Laurens, Iowa. One day, he suffers a fall and is forced to go to the hospital. The doctor advises him to undergo treatment and use a walker, but he refuses. Accepting only the use of two canes, he promptly returns home. He is a stubborn man. On a stormy night, news arrives that his 76-year-old brother Lyle (Harry Dean Stanton), from whom he has been long estranged, has collapsed from a heart attack. It is 560 kilometers to Mount Zion, Wisconsin, where Lyle lives. By car, it would be a day’s journey, but Alvin does not have a driver’s license. Determined to see his brother on his own terms, Alvin ignores the opposition of those around him and sets out alone on a tractor traveling at just 8 km/h. All for the chance to gaze at the starry sky with his brother once more.

*Note: This theater will be screening a 2K converted version.
tmdb:40723: After becoming a test subject for a new drug, Core (Béatrice Dalle) develops an uncontrollable urge to kill her sexual partners during intercourse. American doctor Shane (Vincent Gallo) travels to France to find her, but...
tmdb:41089: A drama by master filmmaker John Huston, known for 'The Treasure of the Sierra Madre' and 'The African Queen,' adapting the novel 'Under the Volcano' by British author Malcolm Lowry. Set in Mexico in the 1930s, it portrays love, loss, and loneliness through a single day in the life of a former British consul succumbing to alcoholism. On the 'Day of the Dead' in 1938, Geoffrey Firmin, a former British consul living in the small Mexican town of Cuernavaca, is in the throes of severe alcoholism, surrendering himself to drink and living a dissolute life. His wife Yvonne, who left him a year earlier but hopes for a reconciliation, suddenly returns. Adding to this, his half-brother Hugh also appears, and the three go out to see the festival and a bullfight... The film masterfully depicts humanity's self-destructive fate within the confines of a single day. Albert Finney, who played the protagonist Geoffrey, received high praise, including a nomination for the Academy Award for Best Actor at the 57th ceremony. The cast also includes Jacqueline Bisset and Anthony Andrews.
tmdb:41245: A human drama that traces twenty years in the life of a man against the backdrop of modern Korean history, winning five major awards including Best Picture at the Grand Bell Awards, South Korea's equivalent of the Oscars. This is the second feature film by director Lee Chang-dong, made in 1999, known for "Oasis" and "Secret Sunshine." Spring, 1999. Kim Yeong-ho, at the depths of despair after losing his job and family, shows up at a picnic with old friends wearing an out-of-place suit. It is the same place he visited twenty years earlier with his first love, Sunim. Standing on the railroad tracks, Yeong-ho shouts "I want to go back!" at an oncoming train, and his life begins to rewind. We see his self-destructed marriage to his wife Hong-ja, his love for Sunim that drew them together but was never fulfilled, and the Gwangju Uprising he witnessed as a soldier. Yeong-ho's journey through memory eventually arrives at the time twenty years ago when his life was most beautiful and pure. The film was released in a 4K-restored digital remaster in 2019 to coincide with the release of Lee Chang-dong's "Burning." A 4K restoration was also screened in 2023 as part of the special retrospective "Lee Chang-dong Retrospective 4K."
tmdb:415073: Set in 1950, in Kokura, Northern Kyushu, under U.S. occupation just after the war. To resolve the escalating yakuza conflict between the Okagen and Hashiden gangs, the police chief proposes a peaceful solution: a yakuza baseball tournament instead of a turf war. The protagonist, Kasuke of the Okagen gang, uses his wits to suppress Hashiden's offense, but the impatient Hashiden brings in their secret weapon, Ginji. A pitcher who became a yakuza after having his fingers severed over a woman, his magical pitches turn the tide, putting Okagen in a tough spot.
tmdb:415379:
Depicting a world of female passion filled with deep-seated grudges and a blood-stained drama of love and hate, Mio Saito’s novel—winner of the inaugural Yokomizo Seishi Prize—was brought to the screen by master director Yasuzo Masumura (*Black Express*, *Nakano Spy School*, *Idiot’s Love*, *The Wife of Seishu Hanaoka*, *Artery of the Archipelago*). Boasting a magnificent cast including Shima Iwashita, Jinpachi Nezu, and Kyoko Kishida, the film is a visual masterpiece defined by a unique color palette rich in shadows; it would ultimately serve as Masumura’s final directorial work. The musical score by Yuji Ohno, renowned for the *Lupin III* series, is another standout feature.

The brutally murdered body of Ryoko Ikehata (Yoko Hatanaka) is discovered. She had been a frequent visitor to the home of Kazuki Hata (Kunio Murai), a secretary to a cabinet minister with ambitions for the premiership. Koichi Moda (Naoki Sugiura), a reportage writer who had been in contact with Ryoko to expose political corruption, begins investigating Seiga (Mari Henmi), a fortune teller and Hata’s common-law wife. Moda enlists the help of his junior colleague, Sudo (Jinpachi Nezu). During the investigation, Moda finds himself drawn to a bar hostess named Yukiko (Shima Iwashita), and the two begin a series of secret trysts. However, just as Moda uncovers Seiga’s true identity, he meets a mysterious death. Taking Moda’s place to uncover the truth, Sudo heads to Aizu, where he witnesses...
tmdb:41948: The Soviet Union, shortly after World War II. In Suchan, a small coal-mining town turned labor camp zone, 12-year-old Valerka constantly acts out in rebellion against his single mother. Galya, a girl of the same age, is always looking out for him, appearing like a guardian angel to rescue him whenever he is in trouble. One day, after a prank goes too far and causes a locomotive to derail, Valerka flees the town alone, fearing arrest.
tmdb:41972: In 1982, the deadly virus MM-88 is stolen from a research institute in East Germany. However, the plane carrying the spy who stole it crashes in the Alps, and the virus spreads across the Earth, wiping out humanity except for a small group of survivors in Antarctica. One of these survivors, earthquake researcher Yoshizumi, realizes an even greater danger is approaching: a massive earthquake could strike the eastern United States, potentially triggering the launch of nuclear missiles.
tmdb:42076: The destroyer of the universe, "Genma," was approaching Earth. Luna, a princess of Transylvania and an esper, received a message from the cosmic consciousness "Froi" and began a battle to protect Earth alongside Vega, a cyborg soldier also fighting Genma. Luna decided to gather psychics from around the world to counter Genma. Among them was high school student Azuma Higashi, who was unaware of his own abilities until Vega's provocations awakened his psychic powers. However, emotionally immature, he closed his heart to Luna's pleas to join the fight to save the universe. Even so, the enemy appeared before him without mercy.
tmdb:42112: The 13th feature film by French master director Robert Bresson, who left behind masterpieces such as "Resistance: From the Prisoner's Diary" and "Mouchette." Bresson, already over 80 at the time of filming, passed away in 1999, making this his final work. Based on the novella "The Forged Coupon" by Russian literary giant Leo Tolstoy, it depicts the life of Yvon, a young fuel delivery man who, after unknowingly using a counterfeit bill that falls into his hands, triggers a family massacre and spirals downward. The title "L'argent" means "money" in French. First released in Japan in 1986. Revived in 2011 as part of "Cinema Masterpiece Selection III: The Art of Robert Bresson" with new prints. In 2026, it will be revived again in a 2K restored version as part of "Robert Bresson Masterpiece Selection."
tmdb:42179: A feature film directed in 1979 by John Huston, the master of American cinema who left behind numerous classics such as 'The Maltese Falcon,' 'The Treasure of the Sierra Madre,' and 'The African Queen.' An unconventional drama that adapts the novel 'Wise Blood' by Flannery O'Connor, a leading figure of Southern literature, vividly portraying the unique atmosphere and spirituality of the American South. When young Hazel Motes is discharged from the U.S. Army and returns home, he finds only a wardrobe and a tombstone left in his family home. In a strange city, he begins preaching the 'Church Without Christ' and encounters a motley cast of characters, including a blind preacher, his daughter, and a simple young man. Eventually, Hazel becomes consumed by madness and despair... Brad Dourif, nominated for an Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor for 'One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest,' plays Hazel. The cast also includes Amy Wright, Harry Dean Stanton, and Ned Beatty. Although it was never theatrically released in Japan, it will have its Japanese theatrical premiere in 2026 as part of the special screening series 'John Huston 120th Anniversary' commemorating the 120th anniversary of his birth.
tmdb:422: The undisputed representative work of director F. Fellini. Film director Guido dreams one day of his body falling through the air. To heal the various mental and physical fatigue associated with his daily life, he goes to a spa for rest and recuperation, but even there he cannot escape from work and life. And finally, he begins to hallucinate that he is among the elderly spending their remaining years at the spa... This film is an autobiographical work by Fellini himself, and its depiction is superb, portraying reality and fantasy in parallel! A must-see!!
tmdb:422956: Murayama Takashi, who suffered from a serious illness since early childhood, discovers shogi during repeated hospitalizations and, at age 15, becomes a disciple of Mori Nobuo. Ten years later, Takashi moves to Tokyo to fulfill his dream of becoming a Meijin champion. Supported by those around him, he devotes himself fully to shogi, and after reaching the rank of 7-dan, he develops a fierce rivalry with Habu Yoshiharu, who won the Meijin title in the same generation. Takashi immerses himself even deeper in shogi, but cancer gradually consumes his body...
tmdb:424694: A biographical drama depicting Freddie Mercury, the vocalist of the world-famous rock band Queen, who passed away in 1991 at the young age of 45. Queen's current members Brian May and Roger Taylor served as music producers, and the film's soundtrack primarily uses Freddie's own vocals. It recreates the moments of birth of classics like "Bohemian Rhapsody" and "We Will Rock You," as well as legendary performances in music history such as the stunning performance at "Live Aid," the largest charity concert of the 20th century, while also portraying the untold stories behind his glamorous career. Rami Malek, known for "Night at the Museum," delivers a passionate performance as Freddie. Bryan Singer, known for the "X-Men" series, is credited as director, but he left during production, and Dexter Fletcher, known for "Sunshine on Leith" and "Eddie the Eagle," completed the film, handling the remaining shooting and post-production. Despite the production troubles, it was embraced by audiences worldwide, and in Japan, it became a massive hit, surpassing 13 billion yen at the box office, the highest for a film released in 2018. It won Best Motion Picture – Drama and Best Actor – Drama at the 76th Golden Globe Awards. It was nominated for five Academy Awards at the 91st Academy Awards, including Best Picture, and won four, including Best Actor.
tmdb:42632: A music documentary recording the 'Monterey International Pop Festival' held in 1967. In June 1967, in the midst of the hippie movement, the 'Monterey International Pop Festival,' which would usher in a new era of rock and roll, was held in Monterey, California. The festival launched the careers of Jimi Hendrix, Janis Joplin, and Otis Redding, and featured numerous artists including Jefferson Airplane, Simon & Garfunkel, The Mamas & the Papas, and The Who, serving as a pioneer of large-scale rock festivals. Directed by D. A. Pennebaker, known for numerous music documentaries such as 'Don't Look Back' and 'Ziggy Stardust,' the film captures legendary moments including Pete Townshend smashing his guitar, Jimi Hendrix burning his guitar, and Cass Elliot being overwhelmed by Janis Joplin's performance.
tmdb:429845: Director Takashi Kato presents an unconventional period action film depicting the story of the Sanada Ten Braves, who fought in the Winter and Summer Sieges of Osaka, with fantastical fun and excitement! Affected by the radiation of a meteorite that fell from space, the Warring States street urchin Sasuke gains mysterious abilities. Growing up, he calls himself Sarutobi Sasuke and, along with the flying squirrel Okiri, becomes a subordinate of the cool commander Sanada Yukimura, rampaging through the rigged Winter and Summer Sieges of Osaka!
tmdb:42994: An epic theatrical omnibus animation consisting of three stories, with Katsuhiro Otomo serving as executive producer and general director. "Magnetic Rose" is a sci-fi drama set aboard a distressed spacecraft, adapted by Satoshi Kon from Otomo’s manga of the same name. "Stink Bomb" is a black comedy depicting the massive panic triggered by a man who accidentally swallows an experimental drug. "Cannon Fodder," directed by Otomo himself, chronicles the daily life of a boy living in a city built entirely for the purpose of firing cannons. Each segment is characterized by a unique, strange flavor imbued with a profound sense of wonder.
tmdb:430: A slapstick comedy filmed in Germany. McNamara, the head of Coca-Cola's Berlin branch, is tasked by a company executive with babysitting his daughter. However, this girl is a troublesome handful who defies easy handling. The protagonist's mindset of doing anything for career advancement echoes Billy Wilder's previous film "The Apartment." The rapid-fire exchange of gags in the dialogue is quintessentially Wilder. The film also showcases the full comedic charm of James Cagney, who also worked as a director.
tmdb:430214: An animated film adaptation of "The Night is Short, Walk on Girl," an early bestseller by popular author Tomihiko Morimi, known for "The Tatami Galaxy" and "Uchoten Kazoku," which humorously depicts the story of an unremarkable university student who pines for a black-haired maiden. Directed by Masaaki Yuasa, popular for his uniquely expressive animation works including the TV anime "The Tatami Galaxy," "Mind Game," and "Ping Pong The Animation." The screenplay is by Makoto Ueda of the theater troupe Europe Kikaku, who also worked on "The Tatami Galaxy." Singer-songwriter and actor Gen Hoshino, also popular for his role in the drama "We Married as a Job," voices the protagonist. The university student "Senpai," who harbors feelings for "the black-haired maiden," a junior in his club, spends his days executing the "Nakame Strategy" aimed at "getting her to notice him as much as possible." The seasons turn as he gets swept up in strange incidents caused by his colorful friends, but his relationship with the black-haired maiden only progresses around the edges without making real headway...
tmdb:431339: The world's oceans are overflowing with massive amounts of plastic waste. This documentary investigates the hidden impacts of marine pollution on animals, the environment, and humanity.
tmdb:43255: Commentary: Mizoguchi Kenji's final work. Set in a Yoshiwara brothel in Tokyo on the eve of the abolition of the red-light district, this female ensemble piece depicts the joys and sorrows of women who have drifted there with various circumstances. The nonchalant prostitutes, played by a cast of luxurious actresses, exude a peculiar atmosphere, making this film a one-of-a-kind red-light district story.
tmdb:433702: In present-day Japan, the giant demonic monster Orochi appears on a coast. Hibiki and Asumu rush to fight it, but Hibiki is defeated by Orochi and falls into a coma. Asumu seeks clues to save Hibiki in the Takeshi's ancient documents describing Orochi, but there he finds the name "Asumu," the same as his own, along with the stories of Oni... The ancient document tells of a village in the Sengoku period. There, Orochi demanded a human sacrifice every year. When Asumu's acquaintance Hitoe is chosen as the sacrifice, Asumu consults Tobei Tachibana to find a way to save her. Following the idea of asking an Oni for help, Asumu and the others set out to search for an Oni.
tmdb:434775: Lawyer Shigemori (Fukuyama) takes on the defense of Misumi (Yakusho), who has been arrested on suspicion of murdering the president of the company where he worked. Misumi had previously been sentenced to life imprisonment for a robbery-murder committed 30 years ago and was on parole. Misumi's testimony shifts back and forth repeatedly. Eventually, an unexpected connection emerges between the victim's daughter, Sakie (Hirose), and Misumi... This film, framed as a courtroom suspense, questions ethical issues that lie outside legal judgment.
tmdb:435421: The 23rd work in Stan Brakhage’s (1933–2003) 8mm silent “Song” series, this film was created as a direct response to the Vietnam War. Interweaving historical footage of war, death, violence, and mobilization with psalms and scenes of everyday life, Brakhage employs his signature mythopoetic structure to deliver a clear message to his contemporaries.
tmdb:437543: Continuing their westward journey to India, Sanzo and his companions Son Goku, Cho Hakkai, and Sha Gojyo are attacked by a giant fish while traveling by boat on a river. The four are swept through a mysterious hole in the sky and land in a strange land—the "Land of Women," where only women live. The queen and Sanzo develop mutual affection. Soon, the four are sentenced to execution under the land's laws, but they manage to escape thanks to the queen's intervention. However, they have no idea how to return from the Land of Women to their original world...
tmdb:437961: The first documentary film about the techno-pop unit 'Perfume', popular both in Japan and abroad. Formed in Hiroshima in 2000 as a trio of A~chan (Ayaka Nishiwaki), Kashiyuka (Yuka Kashino), and Nocchi (Ayano Omoto), Perfume has gained international popularity through their novel music, refined dance, and live performances utilizing cutting-edge technology. The film centers on footage shot over approximately two months of their overseas activities, including the 'Perfume WORLD TOUR 3rd' held during their anniversary year—marking 15 years since formation and 10 years since major debut—and their stage performance at 'SXSW 2015', a festival of music, film, and interactivity in Texas, USA. It also includes scenes of their hours-long post-performance critique sessions, the members' down-to-earth moments enjoying brief leisure time, and exclusive interviews.
tmdb:43877: Synopsis: Ayako (Yamada), a telephone operator, enters into a lover's contract with a married company president to cover her father's debts after he loses his job due to embezzlement suspicions... Considered one of Mizoguchi's masterpieces from before the war, the lively streets of Osaka and Yamada's modern fashion are also highlights.
tmdb:43963: Legendary popular actor Yusaku Matsuda stars as a lone wolf with two faces—a salaryman and an outlaw—in this hit Kadokawa action film based on the novel of the same name by Haruhiko Oyabu, which was a huge success upon its release. Following his explosive popularity in the pioneering TV drama 'Taiyo ni Hoero!', Matsuda teams up again with director Tohru Murakawa and cinematographer Seizo Sengen—who also worked with him on the 'Game' film series and the drama 'Daitokai PARTII'—to break new ground in domestic hard-action cinema. A must-see film, Matsuda enhanced his wild charisma by experiencing live-fire shooting abroad for his role. Murakawa's signature long-take cinematography brings unique intensity to the gunfight scenes, and the final line is said to be an ad-lib by Matsuda himself, not in the script. Tetsuya Asakura appears to be an ordinary salaryman by day, but by night he trains his body and plots to take over a massive corporation. One day, he uses drugs he obtained to seduce his boss's mistress, Kyoko Nagai. Soon after, he discovers that a man named Sakurai is blackmailing company executives over an embezzlement scandal. Asakura skillfully manipulates Sakurai and the company to successfully become engaged to the president's daughter, Eriko. Meanwhile, burning with jealousy, Kyoko makes a fateful decision.
tmdb:44012: A masterpiece drama by Belgian female director Chantal Akerman, who left many works earnestly examining women's lives in society and daily life, carefully capturing a housewife's frustrations and details while tracing how cracks emerge in ordinary routine. Jeanne lives alone with her adolescent son in a Brussels apartment. Boiling water, peeling potatoes, going shopping—she leads an "ordinary" life, but... Starring Delphine Seyrig, known for "Last Year at Marienbad" and "The Discreet Charm of the Bourgeoisie." Screened at the "Chantal Akerman Film Festival" (April 29 - May 12, 2022, Human Trust Cinema Shibuya).
tmdb:44018: A film by renowned French filmmaker Agnès Varda, tracing the steps of a young girl who freezes to death after wandering, which won the Golden Lion, the top prize, at the 42nd Venice International Film Festival in 1985. In winter in southern France, the body of an 18-year-old girl, Mona, is found frozen to death in a roadside ditch in the countryside. The film traces Mona's journey over the final weeks of her life as she hitchhikes aimlessly and continues a solitary journey, through the testimonies of the people she met on the road. Starring Sandrine Bonnaire (from "The Hairdresser's Husband"), with co-stars Macha Méril (from "Belle de Jour"), Stéphane Freiss (from "The Five Senses"), and Yolande Moreau (from "Séraphine"). It recorded over one million admissions in France at the time, becoming Varda's biggest hit.
tmdb:441660: Sengoku once took the world by storm with performances using his ability to read residual thoughts, but the mental toll eventually drove him to retire from show business and seek a quiet life. One day, a high school pianist named Ami approaches him with a request for the "Mighties" to find her missing music teacher, Yukie. Though initially reluctant, Sengoku eventually teams up with his former partner, Mighty Maruyama, to pursue the mystery of the case.
tmdb:444208: A socially conscious drama based on Yamasaki Toyoko's novel of the same name, depicting the shadowy maneuvers of trading companies and their collusion with political and financial circles over the selection of the main fighter jet for the second defense buildup. Kinki Shoji is locked in a bloody battle with other trading companies over the selection of the main fighter jet for the second defense buildup, which is said to involve a total budget exceeding one trillion yen. Before long, the conflict inevitably escalates into a war of 'live ammunition' attacks on the political world.
tmdb:446173: A documentary by director Frederick Wiseman capturing the behind-the-scenes world of the New York Public Library, one of the world's greatest temples of knowledge and a dream destination for librarians everywhere. The New York Public Library, boasting a collection of 60 million items in its main Beaux-Arts building from the early 19th century and 92 branches, is also known for its thorough service to local residents and researchers. Wiseman, a documentary master who received an Academy Honorary Award in 2016, handled direction, sound, editing, and production, recording the librarians and volunteers working with pride and love for the materials and activities, as well as the behind-the-scenes areas tourists never see. By showing why the library is the most famous in the world, the film illuminates what the public sphere means and what democracy supporting American society is. Numerous celebrities appear, including Dr. Richard Dawkins, Elvis Costello, and Patti Smith. Winner of the International Critics' Week Award at the 74th Venice International Film Festival.
tmdb:44686: Sean Boyd, a former police officer turned truck driver, lives with his only daughter, Cassie, following a divorce from his wife. It was supposed to be the start of another peaceful, ordinary day for the two of them; after celebrating Cassie’s 15th birthday, Boyd drops her off at Central Park on her way to school. However, without warning, Cassie is suddenly dragged into a mysterious car. Having witnessed his daughter’s kidnapping right before his eyes, a desperate Boyd gives chase, but he is rushed to the hospital after his vehicle flips in a violent accident...
tmdb:454639: A new live-action film adaptation of the popular "Masters of the Universe" series, based on the action figures created by Mattel in 1981, which have been expanded across comics, animation, and other media, and previously adapted into the 1987 live-action film "Masters of the Universe" starring Dolph Lundgren. Prince Adam of the planet Eternia is sent to Earth as a child to protect him from war, and grows up hiding his identity. Fifteen years later, guided by the legendary Power Sword he accidentally discovers, he returns to his homeworld and learns that Eternia is under the control of his archenemy Skeletor. To save Eternia and its people, Adam transforms into the warrior He-Man and plunges into a deadly battle against the forces of evil. Directed by Travis Knight ("Bumblebee", "Kubo and the Two Strings"), with a screenplay by Chris Butler ("Missing Link"). Nicholas Galitzine, who has gained attention for roles in "Red, White & Royal Blue" and "The Idea of You", plays the lead role of Adam/He-Man. Camila Mendes ("The Revenge Swap", "Upgraded") plays the warrior Teela, who fights alongside He-Man; Jared Leto ("Tron: Ares") plays the villain Skeletor; and Idris Elba plays Man-At-Arms, a father figure to He-Man, in a star-studded cast.
tmdb:4550: Director Park Chan-wook's final installment of his "Revenge Trilogy," following "Sympathy for Mr. Vengeance" and "Oldboy," is a suspense drama about a woman wrongfully imprisoned who exacts revenge. Lee Geum-ja is imprisoned after a man takes her daughter hostage and forces her to take the blame for his child kidnapping and murder. During her sentence, she never loses her gentle smile, earning the nickname "Kind Geum-ja." After serving 13 years, she is released and begins her revenge against the true culprit who framed her. She retrieves her daughter, who was adopted abroad, and with the help of former inmates who have already been released, corners the man. Starring Lee Young-ae ("JSA," "Last Present") and co-starring Choi Min-sik ("Oldboy"), with cameos by Kang Hye-jung, Yoo Ji-tae, Song Kang-ho, and Shin Ha-kyun.
tmdb:45987: A commentary: In the late Heian period, when warriors rose in place of the aristocracy, Taira no Kiyomori faces various hardships... Mizoguchi depicts the "human" Kiyomori, tormented by the secret of his birth, on an overwhelming scale in this historical drama. A young Raizō, early in his debut, plays the youthful Kiyomori with dashing flair, and the unforgettable performance by Kogure as his sensuous mother lingers in the mind.
tmdb:45993: A commentary: A daughter returns to Kyoto's Shimabara pleasure district, wounded after a broken engagement, and strongly resists her mother, who runs the long-established geisha house "Izutsuya." This masterpiece centers on the mother-daughter conflict, portraying the sorrow of women who have no choice but to live in the flower and willow world. The art direction by Hiroshi Mizutani, who long supported Mizoguchi's films from before the war, is also stunning.
tmdb:46043: A commentary: The man who is a match for the younger sister becomes drawn to the older sister who sits in on the arranged meeting... This is Mizoguchi's first film at Daiei, which produced numerous masterpieces during its golden age. Collaborating for the first time with the renowned cinematographer Miyagawa, it delicately depicts the shifting love triangle between two beautiful sisters and one man with a dreamlike visual beauty.
tmdb:461674: A documentary about Hans and Margret Rey, the couple who created the beloved children's book series "Curious George," cherished worldwide. Hans and Margret, originally from Hamburg, Germany, were living in Paris and creating children's books when they invented the character Curious George, who would become the protagonist of their future bestseller. When World War II began, the Jewish couple fled Paris on bicycles to escape the Nazi invasion, carrying the original illustrations for "Curious George" with them. After the war, they continued their writing careers in New York, protecting the character of George for the rest of their lives. The film portrays their tumultuous lives using a wealth of archival footage, precious original artwork, and handwritten animation. This is the feature-length directorial debut of Ema Yamazaki, acclaimed in Japan and abroad for works like "Elementary School: A Small Society" and "Koshien: Field of Dreams," completed in 2017. It was released in theaters in 2018 as part of the Shinjuku Cinema Qualite special program "Caricolle 2018 / Qualite Fantastic! Cinema Collection 2018." A Japanese dubbed version with narration by Yuuimi Kawai is scheduled for release in 2026.
tmdb:463257: A human drama depicting the adventure of three people—a down-on-his-luck fisherman, a young man with Down syndrome who escapes from a care facility, and a nurse from the facility—as they journey to fulfill the young man's dream. Zack, a young man with Down syndrome living in a group home, escapes to enroll in a professional wrestling school, a dream he has had since childhood. Tyler, a fisherman living a lonely life after the death of his brother, tries to flee on his boat after being caught stealing someone else's catch. Zack happens to meet Tyler, and Eleanor, the nurse who came looking for Zack, joins them. The three head to a destination for Zack's sake. Shia LaBeouf plays Tyler, Dakota Johnson plays Eleanor, and Zack Gottsagen, who inspired the film's creation, plays Zack. John Hawkes and Thomas Haden Church round out the supporting cast. The film marks the feature directorial debut of Tyler Nilson and Michael Schwartz.
tmdb:466000: A classic fairy tale produced for theatrical release after a long absence. The story follows three princes in search of a golden bird, with the addition of a witch and robots. Directed by Hirata Toshio with character designs by Ōhashi Manabu, both former Toei Dōga staff, the actual production was handled by Madhouse. The rounded, line-suppressed characters and soft art style make it approachable, and the musical animation by Nankei Kōji is also enjoyable.
tmdb:468: A youth road movie directed early in the career of Gus Van Sant, one of American cinema's leading masters, and notable for the collaboration of River Phoenix and Keanu Reeves. Mike, who suffers from narcolepsy and suddenly loses consciousness when tense, was abandoned by his mother at age 12 and left his hometown of Idaho to live on the streets of Portland, selling his body. Scott, raised without want as the son of Portland's mayor, grew disgusted with his superficial family and ran away from home. After meeting on the streets, the two head to Mike's hometown of Idaho to search for his missing mother, but eventually their paths diverge. River Phoenix, who played Mike, won the Volpi Cup (Best Actor) at the 48th Venice International Film Festival. The film is inspired by William Shakespeare's plays "Henry IV, Part 1," "Henry IV, Part 2," and "Henry V."
tmdb:46919: A landmark film of the 1960s Czech New Wave, this work portrays the wild antics of two uninhibited girls, both named "Marie," using a boldly experimental array of techniques including color shifts, coloring, optical effects, innovative sound design, and abrupt scene transitions. The older sister, with a blonde bob and a daisy wreath, and the younger sister, with dark brown hair in two pigtails, both call themselves "Marie" and pretend to be siblings. They live freely, tricking men into buying them meals only to fake-cry and run away. At home, they do whatever they please—bathing in milk, burning paper, cutting out magazine photos, slicing up bed sheets, and eventually cutting each other's bodies, until the screen itself fragments. Directed and written by Věra Chytilová, a pioneering Czech filmmaker and the most prominent female director of the Czech New Wave. The two leads were played by non-professional actresses selected through auditions: Jitka Cerhová and Ivana Karbanová. Other roles were also filled by non-actors, such as composers and designers. The film had its first official theatrical release in Japan in 1991 at Kichijoji Baus Theater, where it ran for an extended period through word of mouth. It has since gained a cult following, and in March 2026, a 4K restored version will be re-released to commemorate the 60th anniversary of its production and the 35th anniversary of its Japanese release.
tmdb:46938: The only fairy tale adaptation directed by Nishizawa Nobutaka. What is the mission entrusted to the younger sister Elisa to turn her brothers, who were transformed into swans by a witch's daughter, back into humans? Elisa's pitiful yet steady hands as she weaves nettle shirts lend a powerful realism to this fantastical story. Miyazaki Kyōko, an actress also known as the wife of Nakadai Tatsuya, wrote the screenplay under the name Takaba.
tmdb:47104: A young couple who married a few days after the earthquake appeared in one scene of 'And Life Goes On.' However, the young man who played the husband had actually proposed to the woman playing the wife before and been rejected. When director Kiarostami learned of their past, he decided to make a film based on this episode.
tmdb:473262: A musical biopic depicting the later years of Nico, the German-born chanteuse of the American rock band The Velvet Underground and muse of pop art pioneer Andy Warhol, who dominated the 1960s scene. Focusing on the two years before her death in 1988 at age 49, it interweaves her stage presence with personal struggles, realistically portraying the loneliness and rebirth behind the glamorous legend. In 1986, Nico, in her late 40s and living alone in England, distances herself from past fame and embarks on a European tour with her new manager Richard and her band. But the journey is harsh, forcing her to confront her unstable psyche, drug addiction, and conflicts with those around her. Burdened by regret and conflict as a mother, she retrieves her son Ari, who is in a French rehabilitation facility for drug addiction and a suicide attempt, and brings him along on tour... Trine Dyrholm (from "Into Eternity") stars as Nico and performs the songs herself. John Gordon Sinclair ("Gregory's Girl") plays manager Richard, and Anamaria Marinca ("4 Months, 3 Weeks and 2 Days") plays violinist Sylvia. Directed by Italian filmmaker Susanna Nicchiarelli, known for "Miss Marx." It won the Best Film award in the Orizzonti section at the 74th Venice International Film Festival in 2017.
tmdb:47370: The film depicts the 24 hours from noon on August 14, 1945 (Showa 20), when the Showa Emperor and cabinet ministers decided to surrender at an Imperial Conference, to noon on August 15, when the acceptance of the Potsdam Declaration was announced to the public via the radio broadcast of the Emperor's Jewel Voice (Gyokuon-hoso) through NHK.
tmdb:473702: A documentary by the renowned Swiss master Fredi M. Murer, known for 'Höhenfeuer' (Alpine Fire), capturing the mountainous region of his native Canton of Uri. Exploring the lives and spiritual world of mountain people in a changing alpine landscape, the film contains many elements that would later connect to 'Höhenfeuer,' such as folkloric themes and the insularity of communities. It won the International Critics' Prize at the 1974 Locarno International Film Festival. This film, along with 'Höhenfeuer' and 'Green Mountain,' forms the 'Mountain Trilogy.'
tmdb:47578: Kinji Fukasaku directs this adaptation of Toshio Kamata's legendary novel "Shin Satomi Hakkenden," a fresh take on Bakin Takizawa's classic "Nanso Satomi Hakkenden." Starring the glamorous duo Hiroko Yakushimaru and Hiroyuki Sanada, it became a massive hit characteristic of Kadokawa Films, which dominated the era and breathed new life into Japanese cinema. Tamazusa, who once married into the Hikita domain and indulged in debauchery and tyranny before being destroyed by the Satomi clan, returns as a demon queen to exact revenge. She orders her son Motofuji Hikita and his retainers to attack the Satomi's Tateyama Castle. The Satomi clan is annihilated, but Princess Shizu and a few retainers escape, pursued by Tamazusa's forces. The eight warriors, each possessing a jewel inscribed with one of the virtues—benevolence, righteousness, propriety, wisdom, loyalty, faith, filial piety, and brotherly love—scattered from Princess Fuse's body, live their separate lives. Guided by fate, they gather around Princess Shizu and rise to battle, aiming to crush Tamazusa's ambitions.
tmdb:47794: A police inspector from the Montreal Police Department solves a murder case using clues obtained from the victim's diary.
tmdb:479844: Set in Japan and Myanmar, this drama is based on a true story about a Myanmar family living in Japan. Kane lives in a small Tokyo apartment with her two young sons. After her husband Aise is detained by immigration authorities, Kane must support the family alone. Since her children grew up in Japan and cannot speak their native language, Kane pours all her love into them using her imperfect Japanese, but the brothers, stressed by their father's absence, fight daily. Growing anxious about their future, Kane increasingly longs to return to Myanmar, where she was born and raised. This is director Akiro Fujimoto's feature-length debut. The film was screened in the 'Asian Future' section of the 30th Tokyo International Film Festival in 2017, where it won both the section's Best Picture Award and the Japan Foundation Asia Center Special Prize.
tmdb:48153: A crime suspense film co-produced by France, Italy, and the United States, starring the renowned French actor Jean-Louis Trintignant, known for "A Man and a Woman" and "The Conformist." Lucien, a French hitman, arrives at Los Angeles International Airport. Checking into a Beverly Hills hotel and concealing a pistol, Lucien drives to the upscale residential area where his target, a crime boss, lives. After efficiently eliminating the target, Lucien returns to the hotel only to find that someone has checked him out and his passport and plane ticket are gone. As Lucien becomes paranoid, a hail of bullets suddenly rains down on him from an unknown assassin. Alongside Trintignant as Lucien, the film features a cast of distinctive French, Italian, and American actors including Ann-Margret from "The Hunter" and Roy Scheider from "The French Connection." Directed by Jacques Deray, known for the two "Borsalino" films and "Flic Story." The screenplay is by Jean-Claude Carrière, who worked on numerous masterpieces such as "The Unbearable Lightness of Being" and "The Discreet Charm of the Bourgeoisie." After more than half a century since its production in 1972, it receives its first Japanese release in 2026 in a 4K remastered version.
tmdb:48207: A coming-of-age love story about the first love of an 11-year-old boy and girl, which became a huge hit in Japan along with the theme song 'Melody Fair' by the Bee Gees. Daniel, a shy boy attending a London public school, is best friends with his rambunctious classmate Tom, and they always play together. One day after school, while peeking at the girls' ballet practice, Daniel's heart is captured by a girl named Melody. They are drawn to each other and eventually promise to get married... The screenplay was written by Alan Parker, who later directed films such as 'Midnight Express' and 'Mississippi Burning.' A digital remastered version was re-released in June 2019.
