He created outstanding designs and numerous masterpieces of architecture, including the timeless classic "Stool 60," the iconic "Aalto Vase," and the "Maison Louis Carré" with its exquisite harmony with nature. What drove Alvar Aalto's life as a designer was a single woman—
tmdb:685550: Synopsis: Early Taisho era. This film depicts the growth of a boy raised by an elderly woman in a mountain village on the Izu Peninsula. A masterpiece of literary drama, it was adapted and filmed by master director Keisuke Kinoshita from the autobiographical novel by the literary giant Yasushi Inoue. Incidentally, "Shirobamba" refers to the snow bug. Ashikawa plays the role of the boy’s fleeting "Madonna."
tmdb:68606: Kuki, once a sharp editor at a publishing house but now relegated to a dead-end position, meets Rinko, a married woman who teaches calligraphy at a culture center run by a friend, and continues an adulterous affair with her. Their love only deepens, and Kuki eventually rents an apartment in Tokyo to serve as their love nest. But Rinko's husband hires a private detective and learns of her infidelity, while Kuki's wife pressures him for a divorce. Yet the more they are cornered by those around them, the more fiercely Kuki and Rinko's love burns.
tmdb:687163: A film adaptation of the bestselling science fiction novel by Andy Weir, author of "The Martian" (the basis for the Oscar-nominated "The Martian"). It depicts a middle school science teacher entrusted with the fate of Earth on the brink of extinction, who encounters an unknown life form with the same purpose at the edge of the universe, and together they risk their lives to save their home planets. An unexplained anomaly occurs where the sun's energy is being drained. If this continues, Earth will freeze and humanity will perish. It is discovered that the same phenomenon is happening not only to the sun but to countless stars scattered across the universe, and a single intact star is found 11.9 light-years away. Humanity's only remaining option is to travel to that star in a spaceship and solve the mystery to save the sun and humanity. Sent into space for this "Hail Mary" project is Grace, a brilliant scientist who left academia and now works as a humble middle school teacher. Alone in the vastness of space far from Earth, he relies on his scientific knowledge to tackle the mission, where he meets Rocky, an alien also struggling to save his home planet. Despite their different forms and languages, the two use science as a common language to face challenges, developing a friendship along the way. Ryan Gosling of "La La Land" and "Barbie" plays the protagonist middle school teacher Grace, with Sandra Hüller of "Anatomy of a Fall" and "The Zone of Interest" co-starring. Drew Goddard, who also worked on "The Martian," wrote the screenplay, and Phil Lord & Christopher Miller, known for producing and writing the "Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse" series, directed.
tmdb:690: Michel, a poor university student, discovers by chance that he has a talent for pickpocketing. Though once caught by a detective, he is released due to lack of evidence and soon targets others' wallets again. Eventually, his methods become organized as he brings in accomplices. In 'A Man Escaped,' Bresson realistically and thrillingly depicted a prison break; here, he turns his focus to pickpocketing, introducing actual techniques while portraying a lonely young man distrustful of others. A gripping masterpiece where the realism born from amateur actors and the suspense created by various pickpocketing scenes blend seamlessly.
tmdb:69013: "The outside light bothers me" "His smell is soaked into the futon too..." Sadame closes the storm shutters to keep Kichizō's scent from escaping. How long has it been since the two of them were alone in the small room of the teahouse? Their union seeks ever more unknown pleasures. Sadame, choking Kichizō, says happily, "Kichi-san is twitching inside me." But when Kichizō, whose health is beginning to fail, suggests returning home for a while, Sadame's pure love for him becomes directly linked to pure desire. "I won't let anyone else touch you anymore. No one..."
tmdb:701387: The eccentric genius Yorgos Lanthimos, known for 'Poor Things' and 'The Favourite', directs this kidnapping suspense film starring Emma Stone in their fifth collaboration. Ari Aster, director of 'Welcome to Eddington' and 'Midsommar', serves as producer. It is a remake of the 2003 Korean film 'Save the Green Planet!'. Michelle, the charismatic CEO of a globally renowned pharmaceutical company, is kidnapped by Teddy, a conspiracy theorist who firmly believes she is an alien set on invading Earth, and his devoted cousin Don. They imprison her in a basement and demand she abandon her plans for Earth. Michelle dismisses their absurd demands and tries to talk her way out, but the tug-of-war takes unexpected turns. As Teddy's hidden past comes to light, the absurd kidnapping plot veers in unforeseen directions. Emma Stone appears with a shaved head, passionately playing Michelle. Jesse Plemons and newcomer Aiden Delvis, cast through auditions, play the two kidnappers. The film was presented in the competition section of the 82nd Venice International Film Festival in 2025 and was nominated for four Academy Awards at the 98th ceremony, including Best Picture and Best Actress.
tmdb:70520: Alibaba XXXIII, descendant of the original Alibaba and now king, indulges in pleasure and uses the lamp's genie to oppress his people. The descendant of a thief, Al-Hack, teams up with one mouse and 38 cats, riding a flying carpet into the castle. Akira Daikuhara's challenge is evident in the round, deformed characters. Hack is voiced by Nobuyo Oyama, and the shadow-puppet flashback scenes were handled by the theater troupe Kakashiza. This was the last film credited to Toei president Hiroshi Okawa, who passed away suddenly that year.
tmdb:705866: At the time, many women resonated with Tanaka's sentiment, 'I want to live as myself, rather than living like a woman,' sparking the women's liberation movement across Japan. The women never backed down against the male media who mocked them as 'sour grapes of unpopular women,' retorting, 'The difficulty of women's lives is where lib breathes!' For Tanaka, lib was a world of one versus many. Now, as an acupuncturist facing patients one-on-one, Tanaka says, 'There is a place for that person within me, and there is a place for me within that person.'
tmdb:705996: From Park Chan-wook, director of 'Oldboy' and 'The Handmaiden', comes a suspense drama about a detective investigating a murder and the victim's wife, a suspect to whom he finds himself drawn. When a man falls to his death from a mountain peak, Detective Hae-joon suspects it may be murder rather than an accident. He focuses on the victim's mysterious wife, Sore, but she has an alibi. As the investigation proceeds, Hae-joon finds himself attracted to Sore, and she develops special feelings for him too. Just when a lead emerges and the case seems solved... Park Hae-il plays Hae-joon, Tang Wei plays Sore, with Lee Jung-hyun and Go Kyung-pyo in supporting roles. The film won the Best Director award at the 75th Cannes Film Festival in 2022.
tmdb:71: A coming-of-age drama set in a 1980s British mining town, following a boy's struggle to become a ballet dancer and the bonds of family. In 1984, in a mining town in northeast England, 11-year-old Billy, who has lost his mother, is forced by his coal miner father to attend boxing classes. One day, intrigued by a ballet class he stumbles upon, he joins the girls in their lessons. Ballet teacher Mrs. Wilkinson discovers Billy's talent as a dancer, and under her passionate guidance, he improves rapidly. Jamie Bell, chosen from over 2,000 auditionees, delivers a powerful performance as Billy. Julie Walters of "Educating Rita" plays Mrs. Wilkinson, earning an Academy Award nomination for Best Supporting Actress. Gary Lewis of "My Name Is Joe" plays Billy's father. World-renowned ballet dancer Adam Cooper makes a special appearance. The film marks the feature directorial debut of stage director Stephen Daldry, who later helmed "The Hours."
tmdb:71933: One of four dark sci-fi works by Piotr Szulkin, a pioneer of dystopian science fiction in Poland, created under the socialist regime in the late 1970s and 1980s. With a style blending fierce satire and extreme surrealism, the film explores the theme of "escape from totalitarianism." In a world devastated by nuclear war, the planet is frozen, and radiation kills anyone who ventures outside the dome. A man who controls the last surviving humans walks among the crowds, preventing morale from collapsing, seducing prostitutes, suppressing rebellions, and occasionally feeding the hungry. But as the true evil nature of the dome becomes clear, he begins to question whether humanity is worth saving. The film had its Japanese theatrical premiere in 2026 as part of the special screening series "Polish Dark Sci-Fi: The End of Civilization Tetralogy" (starting February 21, 2026, at Theater Image Forum).
tmdb:72592: Takemoto (Sakurai Sho), a student at Hama Art University, one day finds himself falling for Hagumi (Aoi Yu), a girl who paints with complete absorption. She is a transfer student rumored to be a prodigy and a relative of university professor Hanamoto (Sakai Masato). Takemoto cannot get Hagumi out of his head, but the presence of the extraordinary senior Morita (Iseya Yusuke), who also cares for her, stirs up Takemoto's feelings.
tmdb:730251: Directed by Neo Sora, known for "Ryuichi Sakamoto | Opus," in his feature fiction film debut, this youth film depicts the precariousness of friendship in a possible future, using unique sound and emotional visual beauty. In Japan, XX years from now. Yuta and Ko, childhood best friends, spend their days listening to music and goofing around with their friends. One night in their senior year of high school, they sneak into school, and Yuta comes up with a crazy prank. The next day, the principal, enraged upon discovering the prank, escalates the situation by introducing an AI surveillance system into the school. This event prompts Ko, who is about to go to university, to think deeply about his future and identity, creating a rift between him and Yuta, who just wants to keep having fun. Sōta Kurihara and Yukito Hidaka, both cast through auditions and making their screen debuts, play the protagonists Yuta and Ko respectively. Yūta Hayashi from "Lost Summer" and Kirara Inori from "Summer Film ni Notte" co-star. The film was screened in the Orizzonti Competition section at the 81st Venice International Film Festival in 2024.
tmdb:736240: This is the second feature film by director Akiro Fujimoto, whose first feature 'Where I Belong'—a Japan-Myanmar co-production—won the Grand Prize in the 'Asian Future' section of the 30th Tokyo International Film Festival and received high acclaim both in Japan and abroad. Following his previous film, which dramatized the true story of a Myanmar family torn between Japan and Myanmar, this work again tackles the realities of Asian residents in Japan, depicting the plight of young women who come to Japan as technical intern trainees. Three Vietnamese women, who fled their workplaces after being mistreated, become undocumented. Relying on brokers to find new jobs, they end up in a snowy northern port town... Fujimoto met a female technical intern trainee online who later disappeared after grueling daily labor; he interviewed women in similar situations and wrote an original script.
tmdb:736732: A road movie that won two awards at the 75th Cannes Film Festival, featuring a Korean production team and cast. Two male brokers who kidnap an infant from a 'baby hatch' and the mother who once abandoned her child. Bound by a strange sense of solidarity, they journey to find adoptive parents, quietly pursued by two female detectives. This film returns to Kore-eda's signature theme of 'quasi-family,' depicting certain hope beyond the moral dilemmas surrounding the salvation of unwanted lives.
tmdb:73990: Led by Lieutenant Yoshiaki Iba, 21 members of the Japan Ground Self-Defense Force, armed with modern weapons, suddenly time-slip along with their supply depot to the Sengoku period while en route to an exercise. As they stand bewildered, Nagao Heizo Kagetora arrives with his retainers to meet them. Upon first seeing Iba, Kagetora takes an instant liking to him, calling him "a kindred spirit," and is drawn to their unfamiliar clothing and weapons, hoping to recruit them. Iba and his soldiers struggle to accept the reality of their time slip. However, after encountering Kagetora and being attacked by guerrilla forces of a rival feudal lord—resulting in a comrade's death—and witnessing Kagetora's battle firsthand, they are forced to come to terms with having arrived in the Sengoku period.
tmdb:743563: A crime action film produced by and starring Indian national star Kamal Haasan, alongside Vijay Sethupathi from "Jawan" and Fahadh Faasil from "Pushpa: The Rise." It depicts a three-way battle between a drug cartel boss, an unemployed middle-aged man, and a special agent through intense action sequences. Three consecutive terrorist attacks by masked groups occur in Chennai. Special agent Amar suspects Sandhanam, the drug lord who controls the city's gangs, is involved. Meanwhile, Sandhanam is searching for two tons of missing cocaine base that vanished from his territory. As the investigation progresses, Amar becomes strangely preoccupied with Karnan, an unemployed man who was the second victim. Karnan had a police officer son-in-law, who was also killed by the same terrorists. Directed and written by Lokesh Kanagaraj, known for "Master" and "Kaithi," with action choreography by the twin stuntmen Anbariv (Anbumani & Arivumani) active in the Indian film industry.
tmdb:74581: A commentary: A masterpiece that gazes with a penetrating eye at two contrasting geisha sisters living in Kyoto's Gion pleasure district. The older sister, old-fashioned and easily swayed by emotion, and the younger sister, modern and pragmatic... You can't take your eyes off the 19-year-old Yamada, who plays the younger sister rebelling against her submissive elder sibling and trying to toy with men, exuding a remarkable presence.
tmdb:74617: A theatrical version of the TV anime "Mazinger Z," featuring a piloted giant robot as the protagonist. Director Nobutaka Nishizawa heightened the drama by entrusting the robot with the protagonist's worries and pain, depicting the invincible Mazinger Z fighting while battered and broken. The surprise appearance of the successor Great Mazinger, ahead of the TV series, astonished children. "Mazinger Z" achieved strong revenue from merchandise licensing, sparking a trend of incorporating merchandising into projects from the planning stage onward.
tmdb:746257: A historical ensemble drama starring Haruma Miura, depicting the life of Tomoatsu Godai, a visionary who built the foundations of modern Japan's economy and was hailed as a 'Tengaramon' (a person of extraordinary talent). Written by Eriko Komatsu and directed by Mitsutoshi Tanaka, the film presents an original story. In the late Edo period, Japan is shocked by Perry's arrival. Young samurai Saisuke Godai (later Tomoatsu), sensing the dawn of a new era, ignores internal conflicts over expulsion or opening of the country and looks to the world. After meeting the courtesan Haru, he is driven by the desire for 'free dreams' and joins forces with Ryoma Sakamoto, Yataro Iwasaki, Hirobumi Ito, and others to build a nation where everyone can dream. Shohei Miura plays Ryoma Sakamoto, Godai's ally; Takanori Nishikawa plays Yataro Iwasaki, who later founded the Mitsubishi conglomerate; Yuki Morinaga plays a young Hirobumi Ito, who becomes the first Prime Minister; and Mei Nagano plays the courtesan Haru.
tmdb:749004: Directed and written by Céline Sciamma of "Portrait of a Lady on Fire," this film weaves a story of loss and healing connecting three generations: daughter, mother, and grandmother. Eight-year-old Nelly, grieving her beloved grandmother, is taken by her parents to clean out the forest house where her grandmother lived. But her mother, who spent her own childhood there, is overwhelmed by memories at every turn and eventually leaves. Left behind, Nelly wanders the woods and meets another eight-year-old girl who calls herself Marion—the same name as Nelly's mother. The girl invites Nelly to her home, which turns out to be "grandma's house." Sisters Joséphine and Gabrielle Sanz, making their film debut, play Nelly and Marion. Nina Meurisse ("A Woman's Life") and Margot Abascal ("Sagan") co-star. The film was presented in the competition section of the 71st Berlin International Film Festival in 2021.
tmdb:74997: Screening dates: August 22 (Sat), 24 (Mon), 26 (Wed). Synopsis: In the dead of night in London. Martin, a young man working as a security guard in an underground parking garage, feels an abnormal excitement towards the film 'The Human Centipede' and becomes obsessed with the desire to create his own 'Human Centipede'. He plans to connect 12 people... and intends to place an actress from 'The Human Centipede' at the front. He kidnaps men and women one after another and confines them in a huge warehouse. Then, Martin, who has no medical knowledge whatsoever, begins his gruesome surgery using carpentry tools and no anesthesia...
tmdb:75233: The second feature film by director Joachim Trier (known for "The Worst Person in the World"), released in 2011. A bold adaptation of Pierre Drieu La Rochelle's novel "Le Feu Follet" (also the basis for Louis Malle's film "The Fire Within"), it sensitively portrays the pain and despair of a young man addicted to drugs, set in modern-day Oslo. Anders, undergoing a drug addiction treatment program at a facility in the suburbs, is plagued by suicidal thoughts. As his rehabilitation nears its end, he receives a leave pass and returns to his hometown of Oslo to reunite with friends. However, conversations are strained, and a job interview goes poorly. Eventually, he goes to a party but fails to fit in, and after a long period of abstinence, he starts drinking alcohol and then turns to drugs. This is the second film in what is called the "Oslo Trilogy," which includes Trier's 2006 debut "Reprise" and his 2021 film "The Worst Person in the World." Anders Danielsen Lie, who also starred in "Reprise," plays the protagonist Anders. The film was screened in the Un Certain Regard section at the 64th Cannes Film Festival in 2011. It received its first Japanese theatrical release as part of the special program "Joachim Trier: The Oslo Trilogy" (from February 13, 2026, at Bunkamura Le Cinéma Shibuya Miyashita in Tokyo and other venues).
tmdb:752867: A found footage horror film that uses avant-garde visuals and storytelling to depict four men and women visiting a desert who encounter unimaginable terror. Three memory cards are discovered in the Mojave Desert, containing horrifying footage. One day, Robbie, Angela, Scott, and Michelle come to the Mojave Desert in California to shoot a music video. But when night falls, strange sounds, lights, and inexplicable phenomena begin to occur. Soon, the four are swallowed by a rift in reality, and the camera captures the nightmare that befalls them. Robbie Banfitch, a multi-talented filmmaker, screenwriter, actor, and musician from New Jersey, makes his feature-length directorial and screenwriting debut, also starring in the lead role.
tmdb:755136: Starring Kumi Takiuchi of 'A Balance' and directed by Yujiro Harumoto of 'To the Ends of the Earth,' this drama confronts the problems and contradictions of the information society head-on. Yūko, a documentary filmmaker, pursues the truth behind a high school girl's suicide due to bullying that occurred three years ago. She is committed to shedding light on issues that need to be brought before the public, even if it means clashing with the production side. Meanwhile, she helps run the cram school managed by her father, Masashi, and has lived happily with him, working as a team. However, an unexpected action by Masashi forces Yūko into an ultimate choice that shakes her convictions. Takiuchi plays the protagonist Yūko, and Ken Mitsuishi plays her father Masashi, with supporting roles by Tomohiro Umeda and Yūmi Kawai. The film was screened in the Panorama section of the 71st Berlin International Film Festival in 2021.
tmdb:758866: Inheriting the original story of a man's loss and hope after losing his wife, this is a remarkable narrative where the story and the play within the film resonate contrapuntally, boldly incorporating theatrical elements from timeless works like 'Uncle Vanya' and 'Waiting for Godot.' It won four awards including Best Screenplay at the 74th Cannes Film Festival and won the Academy Award for Best International Feature Film at the 94th Academy Awards.
tmdb:760329: The untold story of mixed martial artist Mark Kerr, who rose to fame during the early days of the "PRIDE" tournament that captivated all of Japan, is brought to film by Dwayne Johnson—also known as the wrestler The Rock—who stars and produces. Making his MMA debut in 1997, Mark Kerr rose undefeated to the top. After consecutive wins in the UFC, he also made a stunning run in Japan's PRIDE, becoming feared as "the strongest man in the hominidae family," but the pressure quietly eroded his mind. Kerr gradually became dependent on painkillers, and his relationship with his girlfriend Dawn deteriorated. After experiencing his first defeat, he finally confronts his own weakness and decides to step back into the ring to rebuild his life. Dwayne Johnson, inspired by the 2002 documentary of the same name, personally secured the film rights and carefully portrays the vulnerable side of a tough man. Emily Blunt plays Kerr's girlfriend Dawn, and Japanese actors including Tadanobu Asano, Satoshi Ishii, Yasuko Mitsuura, and Tomoyasu Hotei also appear. Benny Safdie, highly acclaimed for his co-directed works with his brother Josh such as "Uncut Gems," makes his solo directorial debut with this film, winning the Silver Lion for Best Director at the 82nd Venice International Film Festival in 2025. A team led by Japanese makeup artist Kazuhiro Tsuji handled the special effects makeup, earning a nomination for the Academy Award for Best Makeup and Hairstyling at the 98th Academy Awards.
tmdb:761344: Arakawa Ao (Ryuya Wakaba), who works at a vintage clothing store in Shimokitazawa, can't forget his ex-girlfriend who cheated on him and dumped him. His life, mostly spent alone—occasionally going to live shows or his usual bar—is self-contained within the Shimokitazawa area. One day, a female director attending art school invites him to appear in her independent film.
tmdb:76715: The will of the old family patriarch Saibee Inugami is made public, but it states that the heir to the vast fortune is the one who marries Tamayo Nonomiya, the granddaughter of Saibee's mentor. Saibee's three grandsons each scheme to claim Tamayo for themselves, but this soon escalates into a series of murders...
tmdb:76721: A rousing entertainment masterpiece based on Osamu Tezuka's "My Son Goku," bringing together the energy of young artists during the first golden age of Toei Animation. It is noteworthy that Osamu Tezuka himself took the lead in drawing the storyboards, and the on-site staff included a large number of talented individuals who would later carry the future of Japan's animation industry. In other words, it is one of the origins of Japanese animated films, a monumental work that greatly envisioned the future of the medium from an entertainment perspective. Winner of the Special Grand Prize at the Venice International Children's Film Festival.
tmdb:77056: Three stories about love and chance, all centered around a date in Paris.
tmdb:782: A sci-fi suspense film starring Ethan Hawke, Uma Thurman, and Jude Law. In a near future where 'valids' born through genetic engineering dominate society, Vincent, born naturally, lives a life of discrimination as an 'invalid.' He has dreamed of becoming an astronaut since childhood, but it is a profession only permitted for valids. One day, through a DNA broker, Vincent purchases the valid identity of Jerome, a former swimmer now paralyzed from the waist down. Posing as Jerome, Vincent joins the space corporation 'Gattaca' and, through sheer effort, is eventually selected as an astronaut for a Titan exploration mission, but... This is the directorial and screenwriting debut of Andrew Niccol.
tmdb:783111: The 1979 presidential assassination trial. Told through the perspectives of those who defend, those on trial, and those pulling the strings from the shadows, this shocking suspense thriller reveals the truth behind the worst political trial in South Korean history.
tmdb:783263: High school student Momoko (Ashikawa) nurtures a tender romance while dreaming of her future at university. Set against a backdrop of breathtaking lakeside scenery, this impactful film vividly portrays the sometimes cruel reality of youth. Experience Ashikawa’s legendary appearance in a sailor uniform on the big screen.
tmdb:783740: From Giddens Ko, director of "Mon Mon Mon Monsters!" and "You Are the Apple of My Eye," comes a pure love fantasy inspired by the Taiwanese folk deity "Yue Lao" (the God of Matchmaking) and the concept of reincarnation. After being struck by lightning and brought to the underworld, Xiao Lun, along with Pinky who also arrives there, returns to the mortal world as the Taiwanese matchmaking god "Yue Lao" to tie the fates of people together. One day, a dog appears before them, triggering Xiao Lun to recover his lost memories of his past life. He remembers a promise he made to his first love, Xiao Mi, which he was unable to fulfill due to his sudden death. Starring popular Taiwanese actors: Ku Chen-dong ("You Are the Apple of My Eye") as Xiao Lun, Vivian Sung ("Our Times") as Xiao Mi, and Wang Jing ("The Soul of the Banquet," "My Ghost Friend") as Pinky.
tmdb:78450: With the release of 'A One and a Two (4K Restored)', the screening of Edward Yang's representative work 'A Brighter Summer Day (Digital Remastered)' has also been confirmed!
tmdb:784524:
From Briarcliff Entertainment, the bold distributor of *The Apprentice*, and the production team behind *Nightcrawler* comes a descent into madness. Featuring brutal workout scenes and a performance brimming with a chilling intensity that overwhelms the viewer, this film set social media ablaze and sparked a massive sensation across the U.S. immediately upon the trailer's release. Its imagery—at once beautiful and destructively ominous—and its relentless psychological depth have earned rave reviews from major international media, with *The Guardian* praising its "Joker-like sharpness" and *IndieWire* declaring that it "surpasses Travis Bickle from Taxi Driver."

The film is written and directed by Elijah Bynum, one of Hollywood’s most watched young talents, who made a striking debut with *Hot Summer Nights* starring Timothée Chalamet and Maika Monroe. It is produced by Jennifer Fox (*Nightcrawler*, *We Need to Talk About Kevin*) and Dan Gilroy (*Nightcrawler*). These masters of thrilling human drama, known for pushing the boundaries of morality, have teamed up to take the audience beyond a new kind of "extreme." In the lead role, Jonathan Majors underwent a grueling physical transformation to showcase a physique that rivals professional bodybuilders. He pours his heart and soul into portraying a protagonist who possesses both a titan’s strength and a fragile, dangerous psyche—a character that evokes both terror and profound empathy.

"I will become the world's best bodybuilder—"
A lonely man dreaming of glory pushes his body and mind to their absolute limits. With brutal workout scenes and a performance of overwhelming intensity, this film ignited social media and created a whirlwind of excitement across America the moment the trailer was unveiled. Its beautiful yet ruinous atmosphere and its merciless dive into the depths of the human heart have been hailed by major critics, earning comparisons to the sharpness of *Joker* and the legendary Travis Bickle of *Taxi Driver*.

Writer-director Elijah Bynum, who burst onto the scene with *Hot Summer Nights*, has solidified his status with this, his second feature—a film he describes as the moment he "realized what I truly wanted to film." Produced by the powerhouse duo of Jennifer Fox and Dan Gilroy, these experts in provocative, boundary-pushing drama have formed a formidable tag team to show audiences what lies beyond the edge. Jonathan Majors delivers a tour-de-force performance, embodying a man of immense physical power and haunting vulnerability.

The Japanese subtitles were supervised by Hidetada Yamagishi, an IFBB (International Federation of Bodybuilding and Fitness) Pro bodybuilder. Through the cooperation of Yamagishi—a world-renowned athlete who has achieved immense success in numerous competitions and remains active primarily in the U.S.—this film offers a "strongest-tier" cinematic experience that captures the raw reality of the American bodybuilding world.

Killian Maddox lives in rural America, caring for his ailing grandfather. Living a life of isolation with a low income and no friends or lovers, he holds onto one unwavering dream: to become a world-class bodybuilder and grace the cover of a magazine with his sculpted physique. He sacrifices everything to a regime of grueling training and strict dieting, but as his body screams in pain, the injustices of society and his own isolation begin to erode his sanity. Following a specific incident, his pure dream begins to transform into total madness.
tmdb:785542: Twenty-nine-year-old Rona (Saoirse Ronan) returns to her childhood home in Scotland’s Orkney Islands for the first time in a decade. Having lost herself in the chaos of London while studying biology, she spent years escaping into addiction, but has finally managed to break the cycle. Now sober and seeking a fresh start, Rona finds herself still haunted by fragments of memory—the rift she caused with her lover and the many troubles she left in her wake. Amidst the freezing seas and wild winds, she learns to embrace the past she tried to escape and reaches out for a vibrant tomorrow. A song of beginnings; a journey back to herself.
tmdb:790999: Produced for PBS as a tribute to Chuck Berry (1926–2017)—the founder of rock and roll who transcended barriers of race and generation to exert a profound influence on future artists, culture, and society. This documentary brings together rare footage of Berry’s signature songs performed by the man himself and the rock legends he inspired, including The Beatles, The Rolling Stones, Jimi Hendrix, Keith Richards, Paul McCartney, and Bruce Springsteen. These performances were collected with the permission of the artists and their estates, with many of them digitally remastered. The film is narrated by Danny Glover, star of *The Color Purple* and the *Lethal Weapon* series.
tmdb:79382: Director Hirokazu Kore-eda of "Nobody Knows" and "Air Doll" depicts a family drama set in Kyushu, which is buzzing with excitement over the full opening of the Kyushu Shinkansen line in March 2010. Starring the comedy brother duo Maeda Maeda's Koki Maeda and Koshiro Maeda. The story follows two brothers, separated by their parents' divorce to live in Kagoshima and Fukuoka respectively, who strive to reunite their broken family, spurred on by the full opening of the bullet train line. Co-stars include regulars from Kore-eda's films such as Yui Natsukawa, Atsushi Abe, Yoshio Harada, and Kirin Kiki.
tmdb:795052: Starring the "Grand Prix actress" Machiko Kyo. On a Christmas night filled with the sound of hymns, a woman surrenders her purity to a man who is little more than a passing stranger, leading her down a sorrowful path into a world of betrayal and sin. Throwing away her irreplaceable youth into a quagmire and crying out in anguish, the film depicts the heartbreaking poignancy of a love that unexpectedly blossomed in a woman’s heart.
tmdb:795811: Trivial love talk between best friends, a student seeking guidance from a professor, female friends reuniting after 20 years... A first 'short story collection' woven from three tales themed around 'coincidence.' With a small production system ensuring ample rehearsal and shooting time, it carefully captures the actors' light yet delicate expressions. Won the Silver Bear Grand Jury Prize at the 71st Berlin International Film Festival.
tmdb:79707: Makoto Shinkai, the animation artist known for delicate psychological portrayals and meticulous visual beauty in works like 'Voices of a Distant Star' and 'The Place Promised in Our Early Days,' returns with his first original feature in five years since '5 Centimeters per Second.' This juvenile animation follows a girl named Asuna who, triggered by mysterious music heard through a mineral radio left by her father, embarks on a grand adventure. The familiar staff supporting Shinkai's works, including art director Takumi Tanji and composer Tenmon, come together for this film.
tmdb:800513: Legendary Broadway icon Lillian Hall is struck by a sudden illness. Struggling against memory loss, she stakes everything on what may be her final stage performance. Will the play successfully reach its opening night? A moving masterpiece and an ode to life that powerfully conveys the joy of living.
tmdb:804370: The adventure of Iris, a girl living in a near future devastated by climate change, and Arco, a rainbow-colored boy who 'fell from the sky.' A poetically rich animation by a rising French director, depicted in vivid colors.
tmdb:805379: Master director Takashi Kato depicts the process by which Tange Sazen loses his right eye and right arm, with a realism unprecedented in conventional sword-fighting films. Based on the original story by Fumio Hayashi. Ordered by Soma clan lord Nakamura Daizen to steal the famous swords Ken'un and Konryu, Sazen sneaks into the dojo of Onozuka Tessai but only manages to take Ken'un, losing his right eye to Tessai's blade. Hearing this, Daizen abandons Sazen and plots to gather men to attack the dojo again. Enraged by his master's cold treatment, Sazen storms the dojo once more to seize Konryu.
tmdb:805627: This is the first original feature-length film by the popular theater troupe 'Europe Kikaku,' known for works like 'Summer Time Machine Blues,' rebooting their short film 'Howling.' On the second floor of a certain mixed-use building, Kato hears a voice from the TV and looks at the screen to see his own face. The Kato on the screen speaks to him, saying 'I'm you from two minutes in the future.' It seems that the second-floor room where Kato is and the first-floor café are connected with a two-minute time difference. The friends who learn of the 'Time TV' become desperate to find out more about the future by facing two TVs towards each other... The film stars troupe members including Kazunari Tosa as the protagonist Kato, along with Aki Asakura and Riko Fujitani. The original concept and screenplay are by the troupe's leader, Makoto Ueda, and the director is the troupe's video director, Junta Yamaguchi.
tmdb:8073: A masterpiece from Jean-Luc Godard's early period, this melodrama is based on an American crime novel and depicts in comedic fashion the love triangle and criminal scheme involving two men and one woman. Winter in Paris. Franz and Arthur, best friends with completely opposite personalities, both fall in love at first sight with Odile, a beautiful and shy woman from Scandinavia. One day, they learn that a large sum of money is hidden in Odile's aunt's house, and the three plot to steal it, but the plan takes unexpected twists and turns... This was the first production from "Anouchka Films," the production company founded by Godard and actress Anna Karina, who played Odile and were married at the time. Music by Michel Legrand of "The Umbrellas of Cherbourg." It went unreleased in Japanese theaters for many years before finally premiering in 2001.
tmdb:811941: A sea battle entertainment film starring NTR Jr. from "RRR." In 1996, on the eve of the Cricket World Cup, the Indian police headquarters, under high alert, receives intelligence about a sabotage plot by a massive criminal organization. Special investigation officer Shivam pursues the organization's leader to Ratnagiri in South India. A settlement of four villages in the region known as the "Red Sea" is feared as a den of vicious smugglers. Disguising himself as a smuggler to gather information, Shivam learns from the elder Singappa about a brutal conflict that began 12 years ago and the bloody legend of the Red Sea's hero, Devaraj, and his son Vara. NTR Jr. plays dual roles as the legendary hero Devaraj and his son Vara. Saif Ali Khan from "Vikram Vedha" plays Devaraj's nemesis Bhaira, and Janhvi Kapoor from "Gunjan Saxena: The Kargil Girl" plays the heroine. The film is directed and written by Koratala Siva, known for "Mirchi" and "Janatha Garage."
tmdb:819277: Brian Epstein spent his days busy at the furniture store founded by his grandfather. Within two years, the record department he added had grown into the shop's flagship division. One day, at Liverpool’s Cavern Club, he encounters a fledgling local four-piece band: The Beatles. Unexpectedly captivated by their sound, he offers to manage them. He polishes their stage presence and refines their look, from their suits to their hair. After pitching to major labels, they finally secure a debut through EMI’s Parlophone, and the band quickly becomes a global phenomenon. While Epstein is overjoyed by their success, beneath his public persona as their manager lies a sense of personal unfulfillment that no one else can see.
tmdb:823: A film adaptation of Mamoru Oshii's manga "Kerberos Panzer Cop," part of the "Kerberos Saga" that also includes Oshii's live-action films "The Red Spectacles" and "StrayDog: Kerberos Panzer Cops." Set in an alternate 1960s Japan, it depicts the love, hatred, and tragic romance between an elite special forces officer and a guerrilla girl. In the Tokyo metropolitan area, emerging from post-war chaos, the "Capital Police" is formed to combat escalating armed conflicts. Kazuki Fuse, a member of the Special Assault Team, encounters a girl carrying a bomb during a riot suppression. Hesitating to pull the trigger, the girl detonates the bomb and kills herself. Fuse is sent back to training school for failing his mission, but one day he meets a woman who looks exactly like the girl. This is the directorial debut of animator Hiroyuki Okiura, known for key animation on "Akira" and "Patlabor," and it received high praise at the Berlin International Film Festival. In March 2026, a 4K remastered and Dolby Atmos version will be released for revival screenings and home video to mark the 25th anniversary.
tmdb:828: A flying saucer suddenly arrives in Washington. An alien named Klaatu lands and, concerned for Earth's future, demands that humanity abandon nuclear weapons. He declares that if his demand is not accepted, he will shut down all energy on Earth...
tmdb:8286: Praised by many critics and hailed not only as one of Chabrol's best works but also as his own greatest confidence piece. Charles, an executive at an insurance company, lives happily with his wife Hélène and son, but one day discovers that Hélène is having an affair with a writer named Pegala. Visiting Pegala's house, Charles initially maintains his composure, but gradually succumbs to rage... A masterpiece thriller capturing Agnès Varda's 'Happiness', Jacques Demy's 'The Umbrellas of Cherbourg', and the sophisticated visual beauty of Jean Rabier, who shot all three films including this one, along with performances by renowned actors, exquisitely delicate psychological portrayal, and startling violence. (1969) *All films screened in digitally remastered versions.
tmdb:829549:
Ahaan, a young man with Down syndrome, lives in the Indian metropolis of Mumbai with his loving parents. Though he leads a comfortable life, his parents' overprotective "consideration"—born from their concern about how others perceive him—keeps him confined to their home. Deep down, Ahaan harbors a growing, earnest desire to become independent, find a job, and marry a wonderful woman.

Meanwhile, Ozzy, a cantankerous middle-aged man, has been left alone after his wife, Anu, finally had enough of his rigid self-imposed rules and obsessive cleanliness. It is then that Ahaan, who is close friends with Anu, pays a visit to Ozzy’s home. Ozzy hits upon the idea of using Ahaan as a way to get his hands on his wife’s home cooking, and a strange partnership begins to form with Ahaan, who longs for the freedom to go outside...
tmdb:83091: Warriors clad in constellational armor, the 'Saints,' fight for the goddess Athena. With beautifully exaggerated bodies designed by Shingo Araki and Michi Himeno, special moves accompanied by lavish screen effects like transmitted light, fast-paced action, emotional direction, and an orchestral score, it became a representative action anime of the 1980s. The first theatrical film was directed by TV series director Toshio Morishita and depicts the resurrection of the evil god Eris.
tmdb:83761: In 1990, a massive earthquake in northern Iran mercilessly struck the village where the 1987 film "Where Is the Friend's Home?" was shot, as well as its residents. After the earthquake, film director Kiarostami, accompanied by his son, heads to the disaster-stricken area to check on the safety of the two brothers who appeared in the film.
tmdb:838154: A car races across the desolate landscape of Iran. In the back seat, the father entertains his exuberant younger son; in the passenger seat, the mother sways to an old pop song; and in the driver's seat, the eldest son stares silently ahead. While the younger son, unaware of the purpose of the trip, frolics innocently, the family arrives near the Turkish border...
tmdb:838240: The first feature-length animated film by Spanish director Pablo Berger, known for 'Blancanieves.' Based on the graphic novel of the same name by American author Sara Varon, it depicts the friendship between a dog and a robot in 1980s New York, where anthropomorphic animals live, entirely without dialogue or narration. In Manhattan, New York. Dog, deeply lonely, builds a robot to be his friend, and they deepen their bond. In summer, Dog and Robot go to the beach, but Robot rusts and becomes immobile. Dog tries everything to repair Robot, but the beach closes for the off-season with Robot left behind, and the two are separated. Nominated for Best Animated Feature at the 96th Academy Awards in 2024.
tmdb:84155: Childhood friends Hibiki Hojo and Kanade Minamino, along with the fairy Hummy, visit a massive shopping mall on its opening day, but they lose sight of Hummy along the way. They manage to find her, but end up crashing into a fashion show hosted by Erika Kurumi. Amidst this, buildings and residents from other worlds, such as the Toy Kingdom and the Dessert Kingdom, suddenly appear. Furthermore, powerful enemies who once tormented the Pretty Cures are revived by the dark power of a black hole, plotting to wither the miracle flower connecting worlds, the "Prism Flower," and plunge the world into darkness. The Pretty Cures are sent to different worlds by the enemies' scheme, separated from their usual partners and allies, and each is invited into the worlds created by their formidable foes.
tmdb:84237: The final work of renowned early Showa period director Tomu Uchida, who died of illness at just 28, this is a humanistic period drama. In the Edo period, Shinzo, a barber living in a poor tenement, runs a gambling den and catches the eye of yakuza. Strapped for cash, he tries to pawn his barber tools but is refused. Meanwhile, Matajuro, a ronin living in the same tenement, seeks employment with a samurai his father once served, but is completely ignored. One day, Shinzo accidentally kidnaps the pawnshop owner's daughter and brings her back to the tenement... An adaptation of Kawatake Mokuami's kabuki play "Kamiyui Shinzo."
tmdb:842924: A human mystery film adaptation of Stephen King's 2020 short story "The Life of Chuck," directed by Mike Flanagan of "Doctor Sleep." As massive natural and man-made disasters strike the Earth one after another, the world is nearing its end. With no internet or social media, mysterious advertisements suddenly appear everywhere on street signs, TVs, and radios, reading: "Thanks to Charles Krantz. For 39 great years, thanks, Chuck." When high school teacher Marty rushes out of his house to see his ex-wife Felicia, the deserted city is filled with Chuck's ads. As Marty and Felicia, who have safely reunited, gaze at the stars, feeling the apocalypse approaching, and hold hands, the scene shifts to the perspective of the man in the ads, Chuck, and a story tracing his life unfolds through beautiful imagery. Tom Hiddleston of the "Avengers" series plays the protagonist Chuck, with Chiwetel Ejiofor of "12 Years a Slave," Karen Gillan of the "Guardians of the Galaxy" series, Jacob Tremblay of "Wonder," and Mark Hamill of the "Star Wars" series co-starring. Mandy Moore, choreographer of "La La Land," choreographs the dance scenes. It won the Audience Award, the top prize, at the 2024 Toronto International Film Festival.
tmdb:843: A romantic drama directed by Wong Kar-wai of 'Days of Being Wild' and 'Happy Together,' starring Tony Leung and Maggie Cheung, depicting the adulterous love between a married man and woman. Hong Kong, 1962. Chow, a newspaper editor, and Chan, a secretary at a trading company, move into the same apartment building on the same day and become neighbors. They soon discover their respective spouses are having an affair and begin spending time together. Hesitant yet strongly drawn to each other, Chow and Chan... Some settings and the worldview are carried over from 'Days of Being Wild,' and the story connects to the 2004 film '2046.' It won the Best Actor award and the Technical Grand Prize at the 53rd Cannes Film Festival. Released in Japanese theaters in 2001. In February 2018, it had a special screening at Bunkamura Le Cinéma alongside the digital remastered release of Wong Kar-wai's 'Days of Being Wild.' In August 2022, the 4K restored version was screened as part of 'WKW4K: Wong Kar-wai 4K.' In May 2026, a revival release titled 'In the Mood for Love 25th Anniversary Special Edition' is scheduled, screened simultaneously with the short film 'In the Mood for Love 2021.'
tmdb:844: A sci-fi love story written and directed by Hong Kong master Wong Kar-wai, starring Asian superstars Tony Leung, Takeshi Kaneshiro, and Zhang Ziyi. Set in the 1960s, following "Days of Being Wild" and "In the Mood for Love," it weaves in episodes from those films. In 1967, during Hong Kong's turbulent era, writer Chow, unable to forget a past love and engaging in fleeting relationships with women, begins writing a near-future sci-fi novel titled "2046" at his hotel. The novel's characters board a train where androids serve as stewardesses, heading toward "2046," a place where lost love can be found. Chow reflects his own daily life in the novel, projecting himself onto the male protagonist as he writes. It won Best Actor (Tony Leung) and Best Actress (Zhang Ziyi) at the 24th Hong Kong Film Awards in 2005, and the New York Film Critics Circle Award for Best Foreign Language Film. In 2022, a 4K restored version was screened as part of "WKW4K" at theaters including Cinemart Shinjuku, Grand Cinema Sunshine, and Cinema City.
tmdb:84480: The sixth feature-length anime from Toei Animation, this adventure fantasy humorously explores Japanese mythology. In the age of the gods long ago, Prince Susanoo, born to Izanagi and Izanami, enjoys happy days on Onogoro Island. One day, his mother Izanami dies. Unable to accept her death, Susanoo sets out with a rabbit named Akahana on a journey to Yomi-no-Kuni, the land of the dead where his mother is said to be. After adventures in the Night Land ruled by his brother Tsukuyomi and Takamagahara ruled by his sister Amaterasu, Susanoo arrives in Izumo Province. There, to save the princess Kushinada, he decides to fight the Yamata-no-Orochi. This was the directorial debut of Yugo Serikawa, later known for the 'Cyborg 009' series, with original animation direction by Koji Mori. The Orochi battle scene, which took Yasuo Otsuka and Sadao Tsukioka six months to complete, is celebrated as one of the greatest moments in Japanese animation history. The music was composed by Akira Ifukube, known for 'Godzilla'.
tmdb:846279: Elementary school student Kagami Atsuko can transform into any appearance she desires using a magical mirror. This is the first theatrical film in the second series of "Himitsu no Akko-chan," which captures the transformation wishes of young girls. The story depicts the interaction between "Taishō," who opposes the construction of a building on the children's playground, and his father, who works in construction. Akko transforms into a baton twirler who leads the protest. Kanemori Yoshinori's four-heads-tall characters move energetically across the screen.
tmdb:848950:
The fifth feature film from Patricia Mazuy—editor of Agnès Varda’s *Vagabond* and director of films such as *Paul Sanchez Is Back!*—this neo-noir exposes the evil lurking within modern society through a series of murders surrounding half-brothers who inherit a bowling alley.

Armand wanders the streets, living out of strangers' cars parked outside "Le Cargo," the club where he occasionally works. One day, his half-brother Guillaume, a police officer, appears to inform him of the death of their father, a hunter. Seeking to reconcile with his estranged brother, Guillaume offers Armand the chance to manage "Bowling Saturne," the bowling alley their father left behind. However, after taking over, Armand begins causing friction, even demanding that his father’s old associates stay away. Meanwhile, the hunters are provoked by animal rights activist Xuan in the media and nearly erupt into violence before Guillaume intervenes. As Guillaume falls in love with Xuan after a chance encounter, the bodies of several young women are discovered in a local cemetery, revealing that a
tmdb:851488: On August 6, 1945, the atomic bomb was dropped on Hiroshima, and Japan's defeat became all but certain. The Prime Minister's secretary, Nakajima, sounds out senior statesmen about accepting the Potsdam Declaration. But this peace faction's moves provoke the resistance-minded military officers. Unable to persuade the army and out of options, the Prime Minister petitions for an Imperial Conference to be held.
tmdb:851783: A crime suspense film starring Hrithik Roshan of "Bang Bang!" and Saif Ali Khan of "Go Goa Gone," adapted as a Hindi remake of a 2017 Tamil-language film. Vikram, an excellent police commissioner who aims to eradicate crime itself rather than boost his record through arrests, sees his convictions shaken when the criminal he was targeting, Veda, surrenders himself, bringing forth a series of mysteries. Eventually, Vikram and Veda, each with their own purposes, are forced to fight together. Hrithik Roshan plays Veda, and Saif Ali Khan plays Vikram.
tmdb:85399: Toei Animation's first departure from traditional Japanese or Chinese settings follows a young sailor's romantic voyage. The screenplay was an unusual collaboration between Morio Kita, a recent Akutagawa Prize winner with experience as a ship's doctor, and Osamu Tezuka. Staff went to great lengths to depict waves, sometimes painting as many as 300 polka dots on a single cel, and the resulting animation—over 10,000 drawings—imbues the ocean adventure with remarkable realism.
tmdb:85474: Portuguese visionary director Pedro Costa, acclaimed for *In Vanda's Room* and *Colossal Youth*, follows the musical career of French actress Jeanne Balibar (*My Sex Life... or How I Got into an Argument*, *Va savoir*) in this documentary. From vocal lessons and album recordings to rehearsals and live concerts, the film moves from France to Tokyo, capturing Balibar’s multifaceted expressions through stunning black-and-white cinematography.
tmdb:855136: A Canadian drama that captures the lives of people on the fringes of society with an honest gaze, following three children living in harsh circumstances as they form bonds at a local community education center. In Scarborough, a diverse, multicultural neighborhood in eastern Toronto. Bing, a Filipino boy who fled his mentally ill father's violence to come to this town; Sylvie, a girl of Indigenous heritage living in a shelter with her family of four; and Laura, a girl neglected and tossed about by her parents—these three find a safe haven at the education center run by social worker Hina. Despite their difficult circumstances, they nurture a small but meaningful bond... The lead roles are played by three children making their film debut, and the supporting cast includes non-professional actors from Scarborough. The film is based on Canadian author Catherine Hernandez's debut novel "Scarborough," which she adapted from her own experiences. Directors Shasha Nakai and Rich Williamson, highly acclaimed in the documentary field, made their narrative feature debut with this film. It won eight awards, including Best Picture and Best Director, at the 10th Canadian Screen Awards in 2022.
tmdb:855483: Set in Shanghai during World War II, this spy noir depicts the back-and-forth battle of nameless spies among the Chinese Communist Party, the Kuomintang, and the Japanese military. Starring Hong Kong superstar Tony Leung, who won the Best Actor award at the 53rd Cannes International Film Festival for 'In the Mood for Love' (2000) and has recently gained attention from younger generations for his role in 'Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings' (21). The other lead is Wang Yibo, who debuted as a member of the China-Korean joint unit 'UNIQ' and later broke out as an actor in the TV drama 'The Untamed' (19), now one of the most sought-after young actors in China. This film marks his first leading role in a movie, and he has since starred in multiple films, winning the Best Actor award at the 20th Film Channel Media Awards for his second lead role in 'Born to Fly' (23) alongside this film. The intense, stunt-free action sequences performed by the two leads captivate with overwhelming tension and unparalleled beauty. Directed by Chen Er, who previously helmed 'Once Upon a Time in Shanghai' (16). Chen also wrote and edited this film, and Tony Leung was so impressed by the script—only Chen's fourth feature—that he agreed to star. Nominated for eight awards including Best Picture and Best Actor at the 36th China Film Golden Rooster Awards, the highest honor in Chinese cinema, held in November last year. Wang Yibo, making his film debut, was nominated for Best Supporting Actor. Tony Leung won Best Actor, and director Chen Er won Best Director and Best Editing, achieving a triple crown.
tmdb:858024: A drama by Chloé Zhao, director of "Nomadland," that blends fiction with the tragic love story behind the creation of Shakespeare's classic play "Hamlet." Based on the 2020 novel of the same name by Northern Irish author Maggie O'Farrell, which won the Women's Prize for Fiction and the National Book Critics Circle Award. In a small 16th-century English village, Agnes Shakespeare, who possesses knowledge of herbs and mysterious powers, lives with her three children while her husband William works as a writer in London. Agnes struggles to protect her children during a plague outbreak, but tragedy strikes when her 11-year-old son Hamnet dies, plunging the family into deep grief. Jessie Buckley ("Women Talking") plays Agnes, and Paul Mescal ("Aftersun") plays William, with Emily Watson ("Breaking the Waves") and Joe Alwyn ("The Brutalist") co-starring. Steven Spielberg and Sam Mendes are among the producers. Nominated for eight Academy Awards at the 98th ceremony, including Best Picture, Jessie Buckley won the Best Actress award.
tmdb:85844: Synopsis: A shocking work depicting the fierce struggle for survival of women who become prostitutes in the burnt-out ruins of Osaka immediately after Japan's defeat. Among the many masterpieces by Tanaka and her ally Mizoguchi, this film leaves a vivid impression with Mizoguchi's cold-hearted direction and Tanaka's passionate performance as a war widow forced into street prostitution.
tmdb:858485: A legendary suspense-action film set in South India, centered on the ancient ritual of 'Bhuta Kola' (spirit worship). It powerfully depicts the strange fate of a land protected by divine grace and became a long-running hit in India. About 170 years ago, a vast forest was granted to the indigenous people by the oracle of the god Panjuruli. The village of Kadu Bettur has long performed the Bhuta Kola ritual and maintained peace through divine protection, even when landlords tried to reclaim the land. However, the newly appointed forest officer Murali attempts to incorporate the villagers' land into a state-designated protected forest. As the village faces a crisis of survival, Shiva, a buffalo race champion whose father was a Bhuta Kola performer, opposes the forest department to protect the village's peace, leading to an incident. Rishab Shetty, who has an unusual background of juggling jobs in water vending and real estate before entering the film industry, directed, wrote, and starred in the film, passionately playing Shiva, the village's biggest rogue.
tmdb:859910: In 1982, under the sponsorship of socialist researcher Kiyomizu Ishidō, a roundtable discussion was held with pioneering female activists who had participated in the launch of the popular labor movement from the Taishō to Shōwa eras. Those gathered were Setsu Tanno (wife of Masanosuke Watanabe), Utako Nabeyama (wife of Sadachika Nabeyama), Misao Fukuoka (wife of Kyōji Koreeda), and Mina Yamauchi (wife of Naokazu Tachibana). Although they had once worked together in the movement, decades later, after the war, some held different positions, making such a gathering rare. At the request of the host, Mr. Ishidō, who said, 'I want to record this for posterity,' director Haneda filmed the discussion. Time passed without the footage being released, but driven by the director's strong desire to 'preserve the history of these women,' additional filming was done as much as possible to compile the work. In this film, the discrimination and subjugation experienced by these female activists are told in their own words. It is a work that quietly questions what true women's liberation really is.
tmdb:86241: Composer Carol returns from Europe to Los Angeles, where her wealthy father, Carl, lives. Carol becomes involved with various women... An ensemble drama set in Los Angeles, depicting the tangled romantic entanglements and loneliness of various men and women. Directed by Alan Rudolph and produced by Robert Altman, with whom Rudolph collaborated on *Nashville* and *Buffalo Bill and the Indians*.
tmdb:864692: A spy action film starring Indian cinema superstar Shah Rukh Khan, known for films like "My Name Is Khan" and "Om Shanti Om." When the Indian government revokes the autonomy of the Kashmir region spanning India and Pakistan, an enraged Pakistani General Qadir teams up with former Indian soldier Jim to plan a terrorist attack. Pathaan, an agent of India's intelligence agency RAW (Research and Analysis Wing), moves to stop Jim's planned biological weapon attack. However, it is discovered that a biological weapon has been planted on a plane flying over Delhi. With only six minutes left in a desperate situation, Pathaan, India's top agent, fights to protect his homeland. It has become a talking point that Tiger, the spy played by Salman Khan in the film "Tiger: The Legendary Spy"—which also features the same Indian intelligence agency RAW—is set as a colleague of the protagonist Pathaan in this film. Directed by Siddharth Anand of "War" and "Bang Bang!" Deepika Padukone, who has co-starred with Shah Rukh Khan in films like "Om Shanti Om" and "Chennai Express," plays the heroine Rubai.
tmdb:86814: A documentary by Belgian director Chantal Akerman, who revolutionized cinema with 'Jeanne Dielman, 23 quai du Commerce, 1080 Bruxelles,' a portrait of an ordinary housewife's daily routine. In this film, she reads letters from her mother over footage capturing the landscapes of 1970s New York. By layering her mother's affectionate words over the bleak cityscapes of New York—alleyways, cars on avenues, people waiting for trains on station platforms, and underground passages—the film highlights the alienation of urban life and the distance from family far away. In Japan, it received its theatrical premiere at the 'Chantal Akerman Film Festival 2023' (April 7–27, 2023, Human Trust Cinema Shibuya), screened together with 'Saute ma ville.'
tmdb:86829: The Coen brothers, directors of "No Country for Old Men" and "True Grit," won the Grand Prix at the 66th Cannes Film Festival in 2013 with this film. Loosely based on the life of Dave Van Ronk, a musician who represented the 1960s folk scene, it humorously depicts a week in the life of a struggling young folk singer. In the winter of 1960s New York, singer-songwriter Llewyn keeps performing at live houses but can't seem to make it big. On the verge of giving up on making a living through music, he still manages to get by with the help of his friends. Oscar Isaac, who appeared in "Robin Hood" and "Drive," plays Llewyn and also performs the songs. The music is by T Bone Burnett of "O Brother, Where Art Thou?" and "Crazy Heart."
tmdb:869626: A talked-about film that adapts short films sequentially released by amateur filmmaker Dean Fleischer-Camp into a feature-length movie. It depicts the adventures of Marcel, a small shell, in a mockumentary style combining live-action and stop-motion animation.
tmdb:872906: A thrilling action film from the 'King of Bollywood', Shah Rukh Khan, in his first collaboration with a young Tamil film crew. It depicts the righteous struggle of subway hijackers who steal a ransom from arms dealers.
tmdb:873797: A romantic comedy from director Lee Sang-geun, who previously scored a massive hit in Korea with 'EXIT' and reunites with Im Yoon-ah. It follows a woman possessed by a demon who shows completely different faces by day and night, and the kind-hearted young man who falls for her. On leave from work, Gil-gu falls in love at first sight with Seon-ji, a baker who moves in downstairs. But when he encounters her late that night, she is entirely different. Her father Jang-su explains that Seon-ji is gentle and bright by day, but at 2 AM a demon awakens, transforming her. Gil-gu agrees to Jang-su's odd request to watch over Seon-ji at night. She drags him out every night, running wild and selfishly bossing him around. Im Yoon-ah, a Girls' Generation member known for films like 'EXIT' and drama 'The King's Chef', plays Seon-ji. Ahn Bo-hyun, from the drama 'Spring Fever', plays Gil-gu. Song Dong-il, known for the 'Reply' series, plays Seon-ji's protective father Jang-su.
tmdb:883:
Alfred Molina is desperate to meet Steve Coogan, who has just arrived in L.A. When Alfred presses him, saying, "How about a vacation? Just the two of us," and "Give me your home phone number," Steve is left wondering what his true intentions are... (From "Cousins?")
<A collection of short films themed around coffee and cigarettes, filmed by director Jim Jarmusch over the course of 18 years. Across 11 shorts, a total of 24 performers appear, including Cate Blanchett, Bill Murray, Steve Buscemi, and Roberto Benigni. The third segment, "Somewhere in California," was awarded the Short Film Palme d'Or at the Cannes Film Festival. This is a work where the director's trademark musical taste and humor can be enjoyed from start to finish.>
tmdb:8843: The Campbell Institute on the outskirts of Chicago. Young psychologist Catherine is researching technology to enter the human subconscious and dreams. She receives a request to look inside the mind of a serial killer who derives sexual pleasure from watching a woman drown while trapped in a glass cell.
tmdb:88527: High school girls Makoto and Yoko always hitch rides home from town with men who have cars, getting them to drive them home. But one day, a middle-aged man in a foreign car tries to take Makoto to a hotel. A college student named Kiyoshi appears, knocks the man down, and saves Makoto, but their encounter leads them toward destruction... The shocking intensity of the love scenes and raw depictions gave rise to the term 'Shochiku Nouvelle Vague,' and this second feature film by director Nagisa Oshima was a huge box office hit.
tmdb:88529: Toshio, a university student, drives a luxury car through the office district. Together with his friends Jun, Morishita, and Fujieda, he forces his father's company secretary, Ikuko, into the car and robs her. After savoring a brief thrill, they return the money and let her go, but days later they contact her again and forcibly take her to a party.
tmdb:88931: Based on Kenji Nakagami's short story "Akagami" (Red Hair), with a screenplay by the young Haruhiko Arai, vividly brought to the screen by director Kōji Wakamatsu. A masterpiece passionately remembered as one of Nikkatsu Roman Porno's representative works. The story follows Kōzō, a dump truck driver at a construction company, and a red-haired woman he picks up on the street, depicting the sordid waves of lust, the stagnant relationship between a man and a woman unfolding in a closed-off town. And on the other side, a man and a woman who begin seeking an escape from it all...
tmdb:8899: The Dardenne brothers, directors of 'The Son' and 'The Child,' craft a moving human love story centered on an immigrant woman who enters a sham marriage to obtain citizenship. With a bold structure, they suspensefully portray the conflict that arises when unexpected feelings develop within the false marriage, and the protagonist's growing desperation as she is cornered by her inescapable ties to the criminal underworld. Starring newcomer Arta Dobroshi, with Jérémie Renier from 'The Child.' Lorna, a woman from Albania, comes to Belgium. Dreaming of opening a bar with her fellow countryman lover, she enters a sham marriage with a drug-addicted young man, Claudy, arranged by a shady broker, Fabio, to gain citizenship. Initially finding him annoying, Lorna gradually develops special feelings for Claudy as he struggles to quit drugs and earnestly seeks her affection...
tmdb:893372: A human drama about a taxi driver who, while driving an elderly lady preparing for the end of her life, gets swept up in a journey across Paris exploring her past. Charles, a grumpy taxi driver on the verge of losing his license with no money or days off, is in the biggest crisis of his life. Then he agrees to drive 92-year-old Madeleine to the opposite side of Paris. Madeleine, who is preparing for her final affairs, asks Charles to make one detour after another. The streets of Paris where she lived her life hold many secrets, and with each detour, Madeleine's surprising past is revealed. This drive gradually transforms both their lives. Dany Boon plays Charles, and French chanson legend Line Renaud plays Madeleine. The film is directed and written by Christian Carion.
tmdb:896670: Japan in the near future. The Japan Ground Self-Defense Force (JGSDF) is deployed to a conflict zone in Eastern Europe. A tragedy born on a brutal battlefield ignites a chain of further devastation. A retired former officer defies his organization’s orders to embark on a final mission for a subordinate left deeply scarred by war. Carrying the weight of a hidden truth, he stands against a
tmdb:905: A sensual melodrama based on the play of the same name by F. Wedekind, which gave L. Brooks, who moved from Hollywood to Germany, the nickname 'Lulu' after her character. Lulu, a dancer in a seedy dive, becomes the mistress of Dr. Schön, a newspaper publisher, through the skills of her foster father Schigolch. She rises to perform in top theaters, and when Schön tries to break up with her, she turns the tables and forces him to marry her. Schön has a son of marriageable age, Alwa, who is also his secretary, and Lulu seduces him as if enjoying tearing the father and son apart. When Schön learns of her numerous affairs and the decisive truth, he threatens to kill Lulu and then himself, but in the struggle, she shoots him. Although captured, she escapes during the trial with the help of her foster father and Alwa. She lives a life of pleasure on a gambling ship in a port town, introduced by her lover, the strongman Rodrigo. But when Rodrigo sells her, a fight breaks out over her, and Lulu, her foster father, and Alwa secretly enter London. Reduced to extreme poverty in the slums, Lulu decides to become a prostitute, bringing a man into her room while the two men wait outside, unaware that the effeminate man is the infamous Jack the Ripper...
tmdb:90715: An avant-garde Western by Robert Downey Sr. (1936–2021), the New York-based independent filmmaker whose anti-establishment works exerted a profound influence on directors like Jonathan Demme and Paul Thomas Anderson. When a strange man (Arbus) parachutes into a small frontier town ruled by the tyrannical Seaweedhead Greasers (Henderson), he begins to bestow healing upon the people through his mysterious powers. Restored by Anthology in 2025.
tmdb:910850: The second part of a three-part animated film adaptation of Yoshiyuki Tomino's three-volume novel "Mobile Suit Gundam: Hathaway's Flash," originally published in 1989-90. Set 12 years after "Mobile Suit Gundam: Char's Counterattack," it depicts the struggle of Hathaway Noah, a young man who rebels against the corrupt Earth Federation government. In Universal Century 105 (U.C.0105), 12 years after the Second Neo-Zeon War, also known as "Char's Rebellion," the anti-Earth Federation organization "Mafty" begins its resistance through the assassination of high-ranking government officials. The leader, Mafty Navue Erin, is revealed to be Hathaway Noah, the son of Bright Noah, who fought alongside Amuro Ray in the One Year War. Hathaway, though bewildered by the words of the mysterious girl Gigi Andalusia, continues his path to fulfill his mission as Mafty. Meanwhile, Federation Colonel Kenneth Sleg, who is pursuing Mafty, is offered a secret deal by Handley Yoksan of the criminal police agency. As Hathaway and Kenneth each move for their own purposes, Gigi also departs for Hong Kong to fulfill her role. Main cast members including Kensho Ono (Hathaway), Reina Ueda (Gigi), and Junichi Suwabe (Kenneth) reprise their roles from the first film. Main staff, including director Shukou Murase, screenwriter Yasuyuki Muto, and composer Hiroyuki Sawano, also return.
tmdb:912480: A Canadian psychological thriller depicting the madness of a woman captivated by a brutal serial killer, this film won Best Screenplay, Best Feature, and Best Score at the 2023 Fantasia International Film Festival. Ludovic Chevalier is a serial killer arrested on suspicion of kidnapping, imprisoning, and torturing young girls, filming their deaths to be streamed on the deep web (known as "RED ROOMS"). For Kelly-Anne, a successful fashion model, attending the trial of the man whose heinous crimes have shocked the world has become a quiet daily routine. Starring as the protagonist obsessed with the gruesome case is Juliette Gariépy, who balances a modeling career with filmmaking. The film is written and directed by Pascal Plante, whose 2020 film *Nadia, Butterfly* was an Official Selection at the 73rd Cannes Film Festival.
tmdb:91426: A commentary: Emperor Xuanzong of Tang, grieving the loss of his beloved consort, sets his sights on a young woman... Mizoguchi's first color film, a co-production with Hong Kong, is a courtly tapestry portraying the love and tragic fate of Yang Guifei, the beauty who toppled an empire. The restrained color palette that highlights the exotic costumes and art direction is striking.
tmdb:916224: Director Makoto Shinkai, of "Your Name." and "Weathering with You," presents a feature animation depicting the adventure and growth of a girl who journeys across ruins throughout Japan to close "doors" that bring disaster. Suzume Iwato, a 17-year-old living in Kyushu, meets Souta Munakata, a young man on a journey searching for doors. Following him to a mountain ruin, Suzume finds an old door standing as if spared from the surrounding collapse, and is drawn to reach for it. Soon, doors begin opening one after another across Japan. As calamities come from beyond the doors, Suzume embarks on a journey to close them. Despite numerous surprises and hardships, Suzume continues forward, but... Nanoka Hara, a young actress known for "The Sound of Sin" and "My Heart Beats for You," was chosen through auditions to voice the protagonist Suzume. Hokuto Matsumura of SixTONES voices Souta, marking his voice acting debut. Also voicing roles are Eri Fukatsu, Shota Someno, Sairi Ito, Kotone Hanase, and Hakuo Matsumoto, with regular Shinkai collaborators Ryunosuke Kamiki and Kana Hanazawa also appearing. Music is again by RADWIMPS, in their third collaboration with Shinkai, alongside composer Kazuma Jinnouchi. Screened in competition at the 73rd Berlin International Film Festival in 2023, marking the first Japanese animated film in competition there in 21 years since "Spirited Away," which won the Golden Bear.
tmdb:916405: Set in early 1980s Ireland, this human drama depicts a special summer vacation experienced by a 9-year-old girl. It won the Grand Prix in the International Generation section for films starring children at the 72nd Berlin International Film Festival and was nominated for the International Feature Film Award at the 95th Academy Awards. In 1981, in a rural Irish town, a quiet girl named Cott, who lives silently within a large family, spends her summer vacation at the lush green farm of the Kinsella couple. Initially confused by the unfamiliar life, Cott receives abundant love from Sean and Eileen and, as she carefully experiences each moment, comes to feel a joy in living she had never known before. Catherine Clinch, in her debut role, delicately portrays the protagonist Cott with overwhelming transparency and presence, winning the IFTA Award (Irish Film & Television Academy Award) for Best Actress at the youngest age of 12. Based on the novel "Foster" by Irish writer Claire Keegan, this is the first feature-length fiction film directed and written by Colm Bairéad, who has previously focused on children's perspectives and family bonds in his documentary works.
tmdb:91691: One of four dark sci-fi works by Piotr Szulkin, a pioneer of dystopian science fiction in Poland, created under the strict censorship of the socialist regime in the late 1970s and 1980s. With a style blending fierce satire and extreme surrealism, the film depicts the miserable existence of people living under corrupt power and bureaucracy. A man trapped on a giant space station is forced, like other prisoners, to volunteer for exploration of a distant planet. Landing on Planet Australia 458, he is welcomed as a hero, but soon realizes that freedom comes at a high price. His violent life is broadcast live for the entertainment of the planet's inhabitants. The film had its Japanese theatrical premiere in 2026 as part of the special screening series "Polish Dark Sci-Fi: The End of Civilization Tetralogy" (starting February 21, 2026, at Theater Image Forum).
tmdb:91735: A director's cut, completed in 2007 through re-editing, of Charles Burnett's second feature film from 1983. Burnett, an influential figure in American independent cinema who consistently depicts the daily lives and humanity of African Americans, presents a tragicomedy of a working-class young man torn between family, friendship, and identity. It quietly reveals class differences within the Black community, psychological gaps between generations, and the frustration of young people left behind by social success, all from the gaps in everyday life. Pierce, a 30-year-old helping his parents run their dry-cleaning shop, drifts aimlessly through his days with no clear future. His childhood friends are either in prison or already dead. When his brother, a lawyer, marries a woman from a wealthy family, Pierce's discomfort and feelings of inferiority grow. Around this time, Pierce reunites with his best friend Soldier, just released from prison, and finds himself caught between his sense of duty to his family and his loyalty to his friend, forced to make a choice. In Japan, this 4K restored version will have its theatrical premiere at the special screening series 'Charles Burnett: Everyday Blues' (from February 7, 2026, at Theater Image Forum).
tmdb:918983: A war film depicting the fleeting youth of kamikaze pilots who perished in vain at the end of the Pacific War. This is the directorial debut of Yoshio Inoue, based on a script by Kimiyuki Hasegawa (known for "The Squirrel and the American: Gunshot in the Ruins"). Yoshio Inoue was born in Tokyo in 1926, graduated from Urawa High School's humanities track, joined Daiei in February 1938, and studied under Seiji Hisamatsu, Kon Ichikawa, and Yasuzo Masumura. Cinematography by Toru Watanabe (known for "The White Path Across the River").
tmdb:922087: This Indian sci-fi action film comically and eccentrically depicts a gangster's son who obtains a phone that allows him to talk to people in the past and tries to rewrite fate. In 1975, mad scientist Chiranjeevi invents a telephone that can call people in the past. Using it, he can avert disasters about to befall his past self or loved ones, or make choices that lead to profit. However, Chiranjeevi gets caught in a gang war at a bar while celebrating, and the phone goes missing. Twenty years later, auto mechanic Mark stumbles upon the phone and learns its special abilities and how to use it. This phone eventually sparks a massive upheaval involving Mark's foster father, gang boss Jackie; Jackie's son Madan; and Mark's deceased father, Antony. In Japan, Vishal plays dual roles as mechanic Mark and his gangster father Antony, while S. J. Surya, known for "Jigarthanda Double X," co-stars as Antony's partner Jackie.
tmdb:927291: A pollution issue arises in a town in the Tohoku region, and the media war heats up... An excellent film in which Frankie plays a newspaper reporter, depicting the struggles of journalists who, while grappling with the difficulties of maneuvering in a rural setting, burn with passion for producing community-focused articles.
tmdb:9277: A blockbuster hit from director George Roy Hill, who reunited with stars Paul Newman and Robert Redford after 'Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid.' Chicago in the 1930s. Young con man Hooker, whose partner was killed by a powerful gangster, teams up with gambler Gondorff to pull off the ultimate scheme for revenge. A brilliant crime drama with a twist-filled plot and crisp pacing. Won 7 Academy Awards in 1973, including Best Picture, the most of any film that year.
tmdb:92989: Taiwanese master Hou Hsiao-hsien crafts a masterpiece drama that vividly portrays the beauty of nature and childhood friendship through the story of a young brother and sister spending a summer in their grandfather's countryside home.
