After graduating from elementary school in Taipei, Tongtong's mother is hospitalized, so he and his little sister spend summer vacation at their grandfather's house in the countryside. They quickly become friends with the neighborhood children, and Tongtong enjoys a fun summer running through the fields. Meanwhile, his sister Tingting struggles to join the group and passes the time by playing pranks on her brother and his friends, until their father eventually comes from Taipei to pick them up. The father of the siblings is played by filmmaker Edward Yang, known for "The Terrorizers" and "Yi Yi." First released in Japan in 1990. Digital remastered versions were re-released in 2016 and 2025.
tmdb:9344: Photographer Larry Clark, known for his photo book "Tulsa" and for continuously capturing the real lives of teenagers, made his directorial debut with this 1995 film. It vividly depicts the reality of teenagers living on the streets in the 1990s—sex, drugs, violence, HIV—in a documentary-like style, sparking nationwide controversy in America. On a hot summer afternoon in New York, Telly is hanging out with his friends as usual, bragging about having bagged a virgin girl. Meanwhile, at Ruby's house, Jenny and four other girls are also talking only about sex. Ruby, who enjoys experienced and unprotected sex, gets excited sharing her own stories. Jenny is angry at Telly, who took her virginity and then never contacted her again. Worried about HIV infection, Ruby suggests Jenny get tested and goes with her to hear the results. Jenny had only ever had sex with Telly, and the test result is positive. Having received a death sentence from just one sexual encounter with one person, Jenny tries to tell Telly the truth. But Telly, unaware that he is an HIV carrier, is out having fun luring a new virgin. The screenplay was written by Harmony Korine, then 19 years old. Cinematography is by Eric Edwards, the renowned cameraman of "My Own Private Idaho." Music is by Lou Barlow of the alternative rock band Dinosaur Jr. Gus Van Sant served as executive producer. Chloë Sevigny, who had no acting experience at the time, played Jenny, and Rosario Dawson played Ruby.
tmdb:934584: A thriller dripping with black humor that depicts the collapse of capitalist society following the outbreak of a mysterious disease called "Rich Flu" that only infects the wealthy. Directed and written by Galder Gaztelu-Urrutia of the "The Platform" series, which sharply depicted social inequality, it thrillingly portrays the chaos brought about by a reversal of values. Laura, a high-ranking producer at a streaming platform company, prioritizes her career over her family and is on the verge of success in the glamorous film industry. But just then, a mysterious disease called "Rich Flu" suddenly spreads worldwide, killing wealthy people one after another. As wealth transforms from a symbol of success into a "mark of elimination," capitalist society collapses and the world descends into chaos. In this extreme situation, Laura makes a decision. Mary Elizabeth Winstead, known for films like "Gemini Man" and "Birds of Prey," plays the career-driven Laura who neglects her family. Raf Spall, who has appeared in major works like "Life of Pi" and "Jurassic World: Fallen Kingdom," plays Tony, her husband who is exasperated with her yet gets caught up in the unprecedented pandemic alongside her. Timothy Spall, known for the "Harry Potter" series and "Mr. Turner," plays the billionaire Sebastian Snail.
tmdb:936075: A biographical film depicting the life of Michael Jackson, the "King of Pop," beloved across eras and borders for his overwhelming vocal ability and innovative dance performances. Directed by Antoine Fuqua of "Training Day" and "The Equalizer" series, it portrays Michael's story—how he transcended music to greatly impact the world—alongside his many hit songs. Michael Jackson, under his ambitious father Joseph's strict training, achieved early success as a member of the Jackson 5. Meeting legendary producer Quincy Jones, he created numerous historic hits as a solo artist and quickly became the darling of his era. But behind the glory lay the loneliness of a precocious genius, the shackles of his authoritarian father, and the struggle between his love for his family and the visions overflowing within him. The film stars Michael's real-life nephew Jaafar Jackson as Michael, with Juliano Krue Valdi as young Michael, Colman Domingo as father Joseph, Nia Long as mother Katherine, Kendrick Sampson as Quincy Jones, and Miles Teller as longtime lawyer John Branca. The screenplay was written by John Logan of "Gladiator," and the film was produced by Graham King of "Bohemian Rhapsody."
tmdb:94365: Screening dates: August 23 (Sun), 25 (Tue), 27 (Thu). Synopsis: Prison warden Bill Boss has a problem. His prison has the highest rates of riots, medical costs, and staff turnover in the nation, and the state governor, having seen enough, gives him an ultimatum: 'If this continues, you're fired.' Then, one day, Bill's right-hand man Dwight proposes a dream-like idea that could save billions of dollars. It's an idea inspired by the movie 'The Human Centipede'—literally making the prisoners 'kneel' and giving them the ultimate punishment and deterrent! Once connected, food costs are just one portion! Bill and Dwight set out to connect 500 prisoners and create a centipede prison...
tmdb:94655: Bestselling author Tyvian Jones is living a leisurely life in Venice, Italy. But his life is turned upside down when he unexpectedly meets the bewitching French woman Eva Olivier. Despite being already engaged to Francesca Ferrara, he loses his heart to Eva at first sight. However, winning Eva's love is no easy task—she is more interested in money than love. Still, Tyvian cannot let go of his obsession, pursuing Eva with a passion that threatens to destroy his life.
tmdb:948549: Lou, a gym employee, and Jackie, a drifting bodybuilder, meet and fall in love, only to be pulled into the darkness of Lou’s family... An unconventional queer romance thriller.
tmdb:95240: A near-future drama by director Shinji Aoyama of "EUREKA," depicting people striving to find hope for the future in a world ravaged by a mysterious deadly virus, through the symbol of hope—"sound"—and beautiful imagery. In 2015, "Lemming Disease," which is transmitted through images and inevitably leads to death, has spread worldwide, and people live in despair. Amid this, the only method to suppress the onset of the disease is discovered: listening to the "sound" performed by Mizui and Asuhara. One day, a wealthy man appears before them, asking them to save his granddaughter Hana, who has been infected with Lemming Disease. Mizui is played by Tadanobu Asano, Hana by Aoi Miyazaki, Asuhara by musician Masaya Nakahara, and Hana's grandfather by author Yasutaka Tsutsui. The title "Eri Eri Rema Sabakutani" refers to the last words of Jesus Christ, Hebrew for "My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?" Screened in the Un Certain Regard section at the 58th Cannes Film Festival in 2005.
tmdb:9539:
Pain and salvation. Rejection and worship. Despair, and then ecstasy. The world's fastest theatrical release—you will become a "witness" to film history. Since its French release in 2008, 'Martyrs' has sparked controversy with its brutally intense depictions, while leading audiences to an unpredictable conclusion that borders on the sublime, igniting fierce debate worldwide. The pinnacle of the "French horror" movement that dominated an era, and the masterpiece of the eccentric genius director Pascal Laugier, now revived in the Reiwa era with a 4K digital remaster in the world's fastest theatrical release. The origin of Laugier's consistent portrayal of women with the conviction to face despair, this film pushes terror and philosophical depth to their absolute limits, venturing into realms beyond human comprehension. Even 18 years later, it remains undimmed, continuing to exert immense influence on contemporary French filmmakers including Coralie Fargeat's 'The Substance' and Julia Ducournau's 'TITANE'. What awaits beyond the pain swirling with conflicting emotions is an unknown realm no other film has ever reached. *Please note: This theater will screen the 2K version.
France in the early 1970s. A missing girl named Lucie is found wandering the streets, battered and emaciated. She had been imprisoned, tortured, and abused by someone for a long time, and escaped on her own. However, there were no signs of sexual abuse, and the motive for the crime remained unknown... 15 years later, one morning, a doorbell suddenly rings at a peaceful family home surrounded by forest. When the homeowner opens the door, Lucie (Mylène Jampanoï) stands there with a hunting rifle. Convinced she has finally found the person who abused her, she pulls the trigger of revenge. Anna (Morjana Alaoui), Lucie's best friend, receives a phone call from her and rushes to the house, turning away in horror at the carnage. The two set about disposing of the bodies and preparing to leave. But then, they are confronted with an unimaginable truth.
Admission: General/Student/Senior 1,700 yen, HC discount 1,000 yen. *Other discounts, various invitation and courtesy tickets, and T-tickets cannot be used.
tmdb:95600: The life of Johann Sebastian Bach as seen through the eyes of his second wife, Anna Magdalena Bach. Directed and written by the duo Jean-Marie Straub and Danièle Huillet, with cinematography by Ugo Piccone, Saverio Diamante, and Giovanni Canfarelli, and music by Leo Leonius. Starring Gustav Leonhardt and Christiane Lang-Drewanz. The film is composed of just over one hundred shots. Only the musicians performing appear on screen, while Anna Magdalena's (Christiane Lang-Drewanz) narration recounts Bach's (Gustav Leonhardt) life from age 35 until his death. The Bach works performed on screen include the Brandenburg Concerto No. 5 BWV 1050, 1st movement Allegro; Prelude No. 8 BWV 854 from the Clavier-Büchlein for Wilhelm Friedemann Bach; Minuet from French Suite No. 1 BWV 812; Viola da Gamba Sonata No. 2 BWV 1028, 1st movement Adagio; Organ Trio No. 2 BWV 526, 2nd movement Largo; Magnificat BWV 243, movements 11 and 12; Tempo di Gavotta from Partita No. 6 BWV 830; Cantata BWV 205 "Zerreißet, zersprenget, zertrümmert die Gruft," movements 2 and 3 (Bass Recitative and Aria); Cantata BWV 198 "Trauer-Ode," final chorus; Funeral Music for Prince Leopold BWV 244a, Soprano Aria; St. Matthew Passion BWV 244, opening chorus; Cantata BWV 42 "Am Abend aber desselbigen Sabbats," opening Sinfonia and Tenor Recitative; and 24 other pieces. In 1722, Anna Magdalena is taken in as Bach's second wife. Over the 29 years until her death in 1756, Bach's creative struggles and his attitude towards Anna and their children at home are narrated in the order the music was composed.
tmdb:961: Comedy king Buster Keaton produced, directed, and starred in this action comedy inspired by a real train robbery during the American Civil War era. Engineer Johnny Gray deeply loves both his locomotive, "The General," and his beloved Annabelle. One day, however, "The General" is stolen by Union spies, and Annabelle is trapped in the boxcar. Johnny pursues the General on another locomotive, but unwittingly finds himself deep in Union territory... Also known under the Japanese titles "Keaton's Great Train Chase" and "Keaton's Great Train Robbery."
tmdb:965150: A human drama that recounts a summer vacation spent with a father, 20 years later from the perspective of the daughter who has now reached the same age her father was then, as she discovers a new side of her father she never knew at the time. During the summer when she was 11, adolescent Sophie visits a rustic Turkish resort with her 31-year-old father Calum, from whom she lives apart. Under the blazing sun, they point a video camera Calum obtained at each other, spending intimate time together. 20 years later, Sophie, now the same age as Calum was then, looks back at the nostalgic footage shot at that time, reviving memories of her beloved father. Paul Mescal, who broke out with the TV drama "Normal People," plays the loving yet sensitive father Calum, earning a nomination for the 95th Academy Award for Best Actor. The role of Sophie is played by newcomer Frankie Corio, selected through auditions. The director and screenwriter is Scottish newcomer Charlotte Wells, making her feature-length debut with this film.
tmdb:9662: The feature directorial debut of bande dessinée artist and animator Sylvain Chomet, this animated film humorously depicts a grandmother's desperate quest to rescue her kidnapped grandson. Minimizing dialogue and featuring stylized characters on a jaunty jazz-infused soundtrack, this adventure earned high international acclaim, becoming the first French film nominated for the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature. The grandmother learns that her shy, lonely grandson, Champion, is interested in bicycles. To help him become a cyclist, the grandmother trains with him, and he eventually grows up to compete in the world's greatest bicycle race, the Tour de France. However, during the race, Champion is kidnapped by mysterious figures. The grandmother sets off on an adventure with her loyal dog Bruno to rescue her kidnapped grandson. With the help of three legendary triplet musician old ladies, and armed with her life experience, wisdom, and humor, she overcomes numerous obstacles. Besides Best Animated Feature, the film was also nominated for the Academy Award for Best Original Song. In Japan, it was praised by Isao Takahata of Studio Ghibli and was first released in theaters in 2004. A revival screening was held in 2021 as a pre-20th anniversary project.
tmdb:967941: Having learned the truth hidden in the land of Oz and walked their separate paths, two witches once again face their irreplaceable former friend. The second part of the timeless musical.
tmdb:9696: A violent action film based on the popular manga of the same name by Hideo Yamamoto, directed by Takashi Miike. Set in a yakuza apartment building in Shinjuku's Kabukicho district, it depicts a surreal battle between insane men with thorough violence. The boss of the Anjo-gumi yakuza group, based in Kabukicho, suddenly disappears. Kakihara, a masochist who loved the violence given by the boss, persistently searches the city. Eventually, he learns of a hitman named Ichi, and upon witnessing his deranged killing style, feels an excitement akin to love. Tadanobu Asano plays Kakihara, with bleached hair and a face full of scars, and Nao Omori plays Ichi, a weak-willed man who turns into a crying killing machine. The cast includes Shinya Tsukamoto, Suzuki Matsuo, SABU, and Jun Kunimura. The screenplay is by Sakichi Sato, known for 'The Golden Grasslands.' A 4K remastered version will be re-released in May 2026.
tmdb:969681: The fourth installment of Tom Holland's 'Spider-Man' series, part of the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU). Set four years after the previous film 'Spider-Man: No Way Home,' it depicts a new battle for Peter Parker—Spider-Man—who has been erased from people's memories. To protect his loved ones, Peter Parker chose to erase all memory of his existence from the world. Living a lonely life in New York, where no one knows him, he spends his days fighting crime as Spider-Man and dedicating himself to protecting the city's people. But as public expectations of Spider-Man rise, the pressure threatens his very existence, causing life-threatening physical mutations. At the same time, mysterious crimes occur frequently in the city, and an unprecedented threat looms over Spider-Man. Co-stars include Zendaya as MJ, Jacob Batalon as Ned, and other familiar faces from the previous three films, plus Jon Bernthal as Frank Castle/The Punisher from the MCU series 'Daredevil' and 'The Punisher,' and Mark Ruffalo as Bruce Banner/The Hulk from 'The Avengers.' The director is Destin Daniel Cretton of 'Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings,' replacing Jon Watts, who directed the previous three films.
tmdb:970348: British master Ken Loach delivers the final chapter of his 'North East England Trilogy', following 'I, Daniel Blake' and 'Sorry We Missed You'. Set in a former mining town in Northern England, 'The Old Oak' is the last remaining pub cherished by locals. About 30 years after the town's vibrant heyday, it now faces harsh times, but owner TJ Ballantine struggles to keep it going through trial and error. However, when the town begins accepting Syrian refugees, the pub—once a place of solace—turns into a battleground for belonging. Wrestling with the pub's uncertain future, TJ meets Yara, a Syrian woman with a camera, and unexpectedly forms a friendship. Scripted by Paul Laverty, Loach's longtime collaborator, the film is portrayed with warmth and realism. Dave Turner, who appeared in 'I, Daniel Blake' and 'Sorry We Miss You', plays pub owner TJ. Winner of the Audience Award at the 2023 Locarno Film Festival, and screened in competition at the 76th Cannes Film Festival.
tmdb:972662: Aboard an express train from Tokyo to Osaka, waitress Sayoko (Dan) pressures kitchen assistant Kiichi (Frankie) to marry her. An adaptation of a popular novel by Bunroku Shishi, this ensemble comedy depicts the chaos stirred up by a group of eccentric passengers sharing the dining car.
tmdb:974576: The Catholic Church is the largest Christian denomination in the world, with over 1.4 billion faithful. Its supreme leader and the head of state of Vatican City, the Pope, has died. With no time to mourn, Cardinal Lawrence is tasked with presiding over the Conclave to elect a successor. As more than 100 powerful candidates from across the globe gather, secret voting begins behind the closed doors of the Sistine Chapel. Amidst a split vote, Lawrence’s turmoil deepens as he uncovers a web of conspiracy, discrimination, and scandal simmering beneath the surface. Then, on the verge of a new Pope being named, a major incident erupts, shaking the high-security Vatican to its core...
tmdb:974950: Lawyer Rita receives a top-secret request from Manitas, a Mexican drug cartel boss: "Prepare a new life for me as a woman." Through Rita’s flawless plan, Manitas successfully disappears. Years later, while Rita is leading a new life in the UK, Emilia Pérez appears before her, now living as a completely different person... As past and present, sin and redemption, and love and hate intertwine, their lives begin to move once again.
tmdb:97787: The first theatrical film in the "Digimon" series. From a midnight computer screen, a strange creature named "Botamon" is born! While Tai is uneasy, his little sister Kari is overjoyed. Botamon evolves into Agumon! Suddenly, the Digital World, home to digital monsters, appears. A bird-like monster charges at Agumon. But then, another change occurs in Agumon's body... Evolution into the giant monster "Greymon" begins! Two colossal monsters clash—what will be the outcome of this fierce battle?
tmdb:987409: Conductor Goichi (Frankie) on the Tohoku Main Line receives passionate advances from his childhood friend, geisha Sakura (Baisho), but secretly has his eye on another woman. The third installment of the 11-film "Travel Series" starring Frankie Sakai, directed by comedy master Segawa.
tmdb:99002: In the port city of Marseille in southern France. Young Boni works at a pizzeria, spending his days belonging nowhere. One day, his long-estranged younger sister Nenette suddenly appears and crashes at his place. Having nowhere to go, Nenette carries a secret: she is pregnant. But she never reveals this fact to Boni. In their awkward cohabitation, the two spend time maintaining a distance they cannot cross. Boni develops feelings for a woman who works at a bakery, but cannot turn those feelings into reality. Nenette confronts her own body and tries to choose her future. In a cruel world, desire and tenderness quietly transform their relationship. Unspoken emotions slowly seep through.
tmdb:996: An early work by Billy Wilder and a masterpiece of film noir suspense. Insurance salesman Walter is approached by a married woman who wants to take out an accident insurance policy on her husband without his knowledge. Sensing something amiss, he initially refuses, but captivated by the beautiful wife, he descends into becoming an accomplice in the husband's murder. The murder scene creates indirect realism by holding on the expressions of those present. The supporting characters surrounding the pair are also superb.
tmdb:996846: A human drama that portrays the pure love between a woman facing early-onset dementia and a young man who has lived his life obeying his parents, while incorporating social themes such as dementia, young caregivers, and human dignity. Kazuya, a 27-year-old office worker, is a so-called obedient child who always listens to his parents. He lives a stable life meeting their expectations, but feels a sense of emptiness somewhere in his heart. One day, he happens to visit a "dementia café" and meets Reiko, a woman 20 years his senior. Despite suffering from early-onset dementia, Reiko's smile lights up those around her, and Kazuya is captivated. Witnessing Reiko facing her loneliness, he is drawn to her strength and human vulnerability. This encounter frees Kazuya from the rails laid by his parents, and for the first time in his life, he discovers true love. Directed and written by Etsuo Kato, whose 2023 film "Three Souls" was screened and won awards at numerous film festivals including the Tanabe-Benkei Film Festival. Minehiro Kinomoto and Shinobu Tsuji, who also appeared in "Three Souls," play Kazuya and Reiko respectively. Winner of the Grand Prix at the 20th Nakajima Film Festival.
tmdb:999075: Taipei, a night market noodle stall. Five-year-old Yi-jin (Nina Yeh), along with her single mother Shue-fen (Janel Tsai) who is burdened with debt, and her teenage sister Yi-an (Ma Shih-yuan), returns from the countryside to rebuild their lives. One day, her old-fashioned grandfather denounces her dominant left hand as the "devil's hand," and Yi-jin begins to feel guilt. That devil's hand, inadvertently, brings to light the "sins" that each family member has been hiding.
tmdb:999693: January 2020, just before the coronavirus envelops New York. Poet Gozo Yoshimasu traces the traces of his ally Jonas Mekas (1922–2019), the father of avant-garde cinema, in Manhattan and Brooklyn on the first anniversary of his death, a friendship that had continued since 1985. Wartime study notes left in the studio, a 1945 passport, personal effects arranged by his son Sebastian. In a corner of the bedroom, Yoshimasu becomes dizzy and collapses. Early in the morning of January 23rd, the anniversary of his death, a memorial poem is completed in an instant. Crossing the bridge to the office. Yoshimasu reads it aloud to the waiting Sebastian. Then, a long silence falls.
